\title[Sketches for three-dimensional Yang--Mills theory]{Sketches for three-dimensional Yang--Mills theory}
\date{}
\hypersetup{pdftitle={Sketches for three-dimensional Yang--Mills theory},pdfauthor={}}
\begin{document}
\begin{abstract}
We give detailed sketches for extensions of the scalar construction of
three-dimensional lattice Yang--Mills theory. Each section develops one
main result, including curvature tensors, short-distance laws, compact
gauge groups, Wilson loops, local nets, dynamics and a confinement
criterion. We explain the constructions and estimates, retain their
technical arguments, and specify the estimates and limit passages
required by the sketches.
\end{abstract}
\maketitle
\tableofcontents

\section{Introduction}\label{sec:supplement-introduction}

The curvature-bilinear manuscript \cite{YM3main} constructs the
Euclidean correlations of three-dimensional $\mathrm{SU}(2)$
Yang--Mills theory and proves their Osterwalder--Schrader axioms
on Schwartz tests flat at coincidences. We develop further
consequences and extensions of that construction. The first
concerns local fields in real time.

\begin{theoremzero}[Real-time tensor fields, sketched]
Every clustering component of the curvature-bilinear correlations
admits a reconstruction by local tempered tensor fields in
$1+2$ dimensions. Their energy-momentum spectrum lies in the
closed forward cone, and each component has a cyclic vacuum
unique among translation-invariant vectors.
\end{theoremzero}

The precise setting and reconstruction are given in
\S\ref{sec:realtime}. The Euclidean construction, stress
conservation and rotation argument are used from
\cite{YM3main}; their proofs are not repeated here.

The remaining sections each develop one principal result.
Point splitting relates a close pair of scalar insertions
to a curvature tensor. Weighted backgrounds describe
anisotropic variations. The two-term short-distance law
and its lattice coefficient determine a correction to
natural scaling. Other sketches concern compact gauge
groups, Wilson loops, centre flux, latent heat, infrared
bounds, a Haag net, and stochastic and deterministic
dynamics. The final section gives a finite-size
confinement criterion.

The arguments are drawn from \cite{YMM2}. We explain their
reductions and estimates, and retain the technical reasoning
for the additional results. Each statement headed
\emph{Sketch} gives the intended conclusion and the route to it.
The general-group construction and continuum gradient flow
require the uniform estimates and limiting identifications
specified in their sketches; these steps are not proved here.
The confinement criterion assumes its stated box inequality
along the continuum trajectory.

We use the scalar construction of \cite{YMM1} and the
curvature-bilinear theory of \cite{YM3main}. Lattice spacing
is $a_K=L^{-K}$, with odd $L\ge13$, and the physical
inverse-coupling label is $b=a_K\beta_K$. Thus a fixed-label
sequence has $\beta_K=L^Kb$. The reference coupling that
controls the renormalization steps is distinct from
$b^{-1/2}$. We recall the necessary conventions where
each sketch uses them. Full convergence on a fixed torus,
subsequential infinite-volume convergence, and selection
of a clustering component have different meanings;
their order is specified in each argument.


\section{Tensor correlations on a fixed torus}\label{sec:fixed-torus}

The curvature main manuscript constructs tensor correlations by taking
subsequences and then constructs their Osterwalder--Schrader spaces.
Here the volume is fixed. Comparing two consecutive lattice cutoffs
gives a summable error, and hence a limit along the full sequence.
The same comparison identifies several lattice representatives of a
tensor insertion and controls changes in the physical coupling label.
The detailed comparisons below retain the supplied proof sketches;
the following statement collects the conclusions they are intended
to establish.

Write $T_\ell=(\mathbb R/\ell\mathbb Z)^3$,
$a_K=L^{-K}$, and $\Lambda_{K,\ell}=a_K\mathbb Z^3/\ell\mathbb Z^3$,
where the blocking factor $L$ is odd. The physical label is
$\mathsf b=a_K\beta$; thus a fixed label means Wilson measures at
$\beta=L^K\mathsf b$. Initially use the reference regime
$0<g\le\gamma_W^{\rm ref}$ and
\[
 \mathsf b\in I(g)=(g^{-2}+\bar B,X_g-\bar B],
 \qquad \ell\in\mathfrak L(g)=\{2L^m:m\ge m_{\mathfrak L}(g)\}.
\]
Here $B_\sharp$ is the fixed error bound in the main manuscript's
first-passage construction,
$\bar B=B_\sharp L/(L-1)$, $X_g=L(g^{-2}+B_\sharp)$, and
$m_{\mathfrak L}(g)$ is its admitted-side threshold. In this regime
$(K,L^K\mathsf b)$ is a first-passage datum for every $K\ge1$.
An exact dilation, described below, removes this initial restriction
on the positive label and on the side $2L^m$.

Let $V=\operatorname{Sym}_3(\mathbb R)$ and let $O_K^T(H)$ be the
main manuscript's lattice representative of
$\frac12\int\operatorname{tr}(HT)\,\mathrm{d}x$. Its diagonal terms are the three
plaquette-plane forms, and its off-diagonal terms are the three bond
forms. For a matrix weight set
\begin{gather*}
 |H|=\sup_x\max_{i,j}|H_{ij}(x)|,\qquad
 \|H\|_{\rm Lip}=|H|+\operatorname{Lip}_\infty H,\\
 \mathcal S_{n;K}(H_1,\ldots,H_n)
 =\langle O_K^T(H_1);\ldots;O_K^T(H_n)\rangle_{K,\ell,L^K\mathsf b}.
\end{gather*}
The Lipschitz seminorm uses the sup distance on the torus, entry by
entry. Support separations in this overview use that distance.
For bounded Borel weights, $\bar O_K^T(H)$ uses the cell means
\[
 H^{(K)}(x)=a_K^{-3}
       \int_{x+a_K[-1/2,1/2)^3}H(y)\,\mathrm{d}y
\]
at the least corner $x$ of the plaquette or bond. This specifies the
sampling convention even when point values have no meaning.

We also need to compare insertions built from different plaquette
corners. For an ordered pair of signed directions
$l=(\alpha,\alpha')$, $\alpha'\ne\pm\alpha$, let $W_{x,l}$ be its
plaquette loop, $\lambda(l)$ its normal direction, and
$s(l)=\operatorname{sgn}(\alpha)\operatorname{sgn}(\alpha')
\varepsilon_{\lambda(l)|\alpha||\alpha'|}$ its orientation. Put
\begin{gather*}
 w(U)=\frac{U-U^{-1}}{2i},\qquad
 Q_x(l,l')=\frac12\operatorname{tr}[w(W_{x,l})w(W_{x,l'})],\\
 \mathcal Q_{l,l';\xi}(\phi)
       =a_K^{-1}\sum_x\phi(x+a_K\xi)Q_x(l,l'),
 \qquad |\xi|_\infty\le\frac12.
\end{gather*}
A class insertion $\mathcal E$ is a finite sum of these corner
forms and of plane forms
$\mathcal O_\lambda(\phi)=O_K^T(\phi E_{\lambda\lambda})$,
with real Lipschitz weights. Here $E_{ij}$ are the matrix units.
Its quadratic symbol $\mathrm{Sym}\,\mathcal E$ is the sum of
\[
 \phi E_{\lambda\lambda},\qquad
 \phi s(l)s(l')
       (E_{\lambda(l)\lambda(l')}+E_{\lambda(l')\lambda(l)}),
\]
respectively; its norm $\|\mathcal E\|$ is the sum of
$\sup|\phi|+\operatorname{Lip}_\infty\phi$ over its terms.
In particular $\mathrm{Sym}\,O_K^T(H)=H$.

\begin{sketch}[Full fixed-torus limit]
\label{supp:fixed-torus}
Fix $n\ge2$ and $d>0$. Suppose the weights $H_a$ vanish off closed
sets $\Sigma_a\subset T_\ell$ with pairwise sup distances at least
$d$. For Lipschitz weights, there are $C,p,K_1$ such that
\begin{gather*}
 |\mathcal S_{n;K+1}(H_1,\ldots,H_n)-\mathcal S_{n;K}(H_1,\ldots,H_n)|
 \le C\ell^{3(n+1)}K^pL^{-\theta_nK}\prod_a\|H_a\|_{\rm Lip},\\
 \theta_n=\frac1{1260n(8n+3)},\qquad K\ge K_1.
\end{gather*}
Consequently $\mathcal S_n^{\ell,\mathsf b}=\lim_K\mathcal S_{n;K}$
exists along the full sequence, with the tail bounded by the sum of
the displayed right-hand side over $K'\ge K$. For $\bar O_K^T$ the
same assertions hold for bounded Borel weights, with
$\prod_a|H_a|$ and a possibly different constant. The two limits
agree for Lipschitz weights.

Class insertions $\mathcal E_a,\mathcal E'_a$ over these sets with
equal symbols have cumulants differing by at most
\[
 C^{\rm u}K^pL^{-\theta_nK}
                   \prod_a(\|\mathcal E_a\|+\|\mathcal E'_a\|).
\]
Their common limit is
$\mathcal S_n^{\ell,\mathsf b}
 (\mathrm{Sym}\,\mathcal E_1,\ldots,\mathrm{Sym}\,\mathcal E_n)$.
The Lipschitz seminorms in this comparison can be omitted when
the representatives carry the same weights at the same sites.

The cutoff estimates are uniform for $\mathsf b$ in any compact
interval $J\subset I(g)$. The limits are continuous in the label;
if $\mathsf b$ is an interior point of $I(g)$ and
$a_K\beta_K\to\mathsf b$, the full cutoff sequence at $\beta_K$
has the same limit. Exact dilation extends these conclusions to
every $\mathsf b>0$ and every side $2L^m$, $m\ge0$.
\end{sketch}

\subsection{Comparing two cutoffs through one block field}

The new estimate concerns the relation between the measures at
$K$ and $K+1$. Bounds on each measure separately would only provide
compactness. The comparison instead evaluates their insertions over
one block field at a common depth. This introduces three errors:
replacing each insertion by its value at a background, comparing the
two background values, and comparing the two laws of the block field.
Prop.~\ref{C-355-36} gives this argument for plane and bond
forms; Lem.~\ref{sf-cut} includes corner forms. Expanding a tensor
insertion into its six entries then gives $6^n$ terms.

The two depths have different purposes. Set
\[
 \sigma=\left\lfloor\frac K{1260n}\right\rfloor,
 \qquad s=\left\lfloor\frac\sigma{8n+3}\right\rfloor.
\]
At depth $s$ the supports are far enough apart for the separated-source
calculus. Each insertion has size at most a constant times
$\ell^3L^{4s}$ times its weight norm. Replacing it by the first
source member evaluated at the background of the depth-$\sigma$
block field leaves a large-field error, a loss-of-memory error
decaying like a polynomial times $L^{-(\sigma-s)/2}$, and a
connecting-polymer error decaying exponentially in $L^sd$.
The inequality $\sigma-s\ge(8n+2)s$ pays for the growth
$L^{4ns}$ of a product of $n$ insertions. After that cost, the
slowest decay is $L^{-s}$.

The background comparison is the substantive local step. In a
suitable gauge the fine plaquette variables are curls of a small
Lie-algebra-valued field to second order; the coarse variables are
their block averages. The variance about an average is controlled
by the defect in Jensen's inequality. Summing that defect relates
it to the action lost in averaging. The comparison of background
actions controls this loss, and the minimality of the coarse
background controls the difference between that background and
the averaged fine background. This gives, for one insertion,
a defect bounded by a constant times
\[
 \ell^3L^{4\sigma}K^{1/2}L^{-(K-\sigma)/2}
       (\sup|\phi|+L^{-\sigma}\operatorname{Lip}_\infty\phi).
\]
Finally, the two block-field laws differ by at most a constant
times $\ell^3K^{\mathsf p_0}L^{-K/10}$ on bounded gauge-invariant
functions. Here $\mathsf p_0$ denotes the fixed polynomial exponent of
that comparison. The small choice of $\sigma$ pays for the
$L^{4n\sigma}$ growth in both of these errors: their remaining
decays are at least $L^{-K/3}$ and $L^{-K/11}$, respectively.
Thus $s\ge\theta_nK-2$ gives the stated summable rate.

\subsection{Sampling, symbols, and changes of label}

Cell means remove the regularity cost at its source. The cell of a
coarse site $y$ is the union of the cells of its $L^3$ fine sites
$B(y)$, so
\[
 \phi^{(K)}(y)=L^{-3}
                 \sum_{x\in B(y)}\phi^{(K+1)}(x).
\]
The weights therefore match exactly across one averaging step.
Point sampling introduces a mismatch of order
$a_K\operatorname{Lip}_\infty\phi$ instead. The uniform sup-norm
bound of Lem.~\ref{sf-sym}(b) makes this mismatch vanish in the
limit. Uniform convergence on sup-norm balls also transfers bounded
pointwise continuity from the finite-cutoff cell means to the
limit. In each argument separately, the resulting functional is
a countably additive measure, vanishes on Lebesgue null sets, and
has an $L^1$ density. This is the precise measure-theoretic conclusion
for separated weights.

Equality of quadratic symbols is stronger than agreement of a
formal leading expression. To prove it, the comparison replaces
each loop by a canonical loop in the same plane, with its orientation
sign. Moving its anchor costs
$O(a_K\operatorname{Lip}_\infty\phi)$. The plane insertion is
reduced to corner products by the exact identity
\[
 a_p=\frac12Q_x(l,l)+\frac12a_p^2.
\]
The last term is fourth order at the backgrounds and lies within
the comparison error. The resulting canonical form depends only
on the symbol. Thus bond averages, clovers, and individual corners
produce the same separated continuum field, with a quantified
error before taking the limit.

Uniformity in the label requires tracking where it enters the
comparison. Let $\Theta_\star$ be the fixed threshold for comparing
the two backgrounds. On $J\subset I(g)$ the block-law constants
and their threshold are common; the background-radius bounds are
common; and $L^\sigma\mathsf b\ge\Theta_\star$ holds throughout
$J$ once it holds at its least label. At fixed $K$
the compact-group integral is continuous in $\beta=L^K\mathsf b$.
Uniform cutoff convergence therefore gives a continuous limit in
$\mathsf b$. For $\mathsf b_K=a_K\beta_K\to\mathsf b$, split the
error into the uniform cutoff tail at $\mathsf b_K$ and continuity
of the limiting function at $\mathsf b$.

For an initially inadmissible side or label, dilation replaces
$(\ell,\mathsf b,K)$ by $(L^z\ell,L^z\mathsf b,K-z)$,
keeps the underlying graph and bare coupling unchanged, and
multiplies an $n$-fold cumulant by $L^{zn}$. For sufficiently
large $z$, the reference coupling
$g'=(L^z\mathsf b/2)^{-1/2}$ admits this new side and places the
new label in the interior of $I(g')$. This is the exact transfer
used in Thm.~\ref{sf-tori}.

The same theorem retains translations, signed-permutation
covariance, coordinate-plane reflection positivity, and the
separated fixed-torus stress identity. Derivatives in that identity
act on periodic continuum test functions. Its two-point refinements
are stated with their own scale restrictions. Extensions through
coinciding supports, their contact ambiguity, and stronger rates
under weaker separation are separate tasks below; they are not
consequences of the separated-support convergence estimate.

\emph{Sources.} Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8} follows an insertion through the levels as a source under a majorant. A \emph{majorant} on $\Lambda_{K,\ell}$ is a pair $(\mathsf s,S)$ of a number $\mathsf s\ge0$, its \emph{size}, and a set $S$ of plaquettes; its weight is the plaquette source $\mathsf s\mathbf 1_S$, and $\mathsf m_j=12M^3\alpha_0^2L^{K-j}\mathsf s$, $j\ge0$, are the numbers that the calculus of Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8} attaches to that weight at the level $j$, $\alpha_0\in(0,1]$ a basic constant of the calculus. A \emph{source under $(\mathsf s,S)$} is a triple of: a \emph{first member} $F$, a continuous function of the configurations of $\Lambda_{K,\ell}$, invariant under the gauge transformations, with $|F(U)|\le a_K^{-1}\mathsf s\sum_{p\in S}a_p(U)$; a local family at the level $0$ of norm at most $\mathsf c^\flat\mathsf m_0$, $\mathsf c^\flat$ a basic number of the calculus; and local families at the levels $j\ge1$ of norms at most $\frac12\mathsf m_j$; each family vanishes at the regions of its level that hold no plaquette of $S$, and each sums at its level to $F$, up to the value at the trivial field.

A \emph{source system under majorants} is a tuple of sources under majorants $(\mathsf s_a,S_a)$; all the numbers of the calculus are then formed at the weights $\mathsf s_a\mathbf 1_{S_a}$. A source under $(\mathsf s,S)$ is a source under every $(\mathsf s',S')$ with $\mathsf s'\ge\mathsf s$ and $S'\supset S$, the majorant entering only the right members of three inequalities and the two clauses of vanishing; the sum of two sources, member by member, is a source under the sum of the sizes and the union of the sets, and $c$ times a source is one under $|c|$ times the size. For the value at short distance the calculus reads besides, of a real source, the kernel $\mathsf t(p,p')=\mathsf t(p',p)$ of its first member to the second order at a small field, vanishing unless $p,p'\in S$, with $2\sum_{p'}|\mathsf t(p,p')|\le\mathsf s$.

{\cite[Lem.~C.4]{YMM2}} says which insertions are sources.


\begin{proposition}[Two consecutive cutoffs on one torus for the plaquette forms of one plane and the bond forms]\label{C-355-36}
Let $0<g\le\gamma^{\rm ref}_W$, $b\in I(g)$, $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$, $n\ge2$ and $\mathsf d>0$; by Cor.~\YMMref{118.4}{815} the pairs $(K,L^Kb)$ are first-passage data at $g$ with label $b$. For a bounded Borel function $\psi$ on $T_\ell$ and $x\in\Lambda_{K,\ell}$ put $\psi^{(K)}(x)=a_K^{-3}\int_{x+a_K[-\frac12,\frac12)^3}\psi$. A \emph{cell insertion} at the cutoff $K$ is one of the following: the plaquette form $\mathcal O(w)$ of one plane $\{\kappa,\kappa'\}$, with $w(p)=\psi^{(K)}(x)$ at the plaquette $p$ spanned at $x$ by $a_Ke_\kappa$, $a_Ke_{\kappa'}$ and $w=0$ at the plaquettes of the two other planes; the sum of the three, the action density with the weight $\psi^{(K)}$; and the bond form $Y[\mathsf w]$ of one direction $\mu$, with $\mathsf w(\langle x,x+a_Ke_\mu\rangle)=\psi^{(K)}(x)$ and $\mathsf w=0$ at the bonds of the two other directions. Let $\mathcal E_1,\dots,\mathcal E_n$ be cell insertions, of any kinds, whose functions $\psi_a$ are real and vanish off closed sets at pairwise sup distances $\ge\mathsf d$, and $\kappa_K=\langle\mathcal E_1;\dots;\mathcal E_n\rangle_{K,\ell,L^Kb}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] There are numbers $C$, $p$, formed from the constants, $n$ and $b$, and a cutoff $K_1$, formed besides from $g$, $\ell$ and $\mathsf d$, such that for $K\ge K_1$
\[|\kappa_{K+1}-\kappa_K|\le C\,\ell^{3(n+1)}K^pL^{-\theta_nK}\prod_a\sup|\psi_a|,\qquad\theta_n=\frac1{1260\,n(8n+3)} .\]
So $\kappa_K$ converges along the full sequence $K\to\infty$, and the limit is $n$-linear and symmetric. The same holds, with $\sup|\psi_a|+{\rm Lip}_\infty\psi_a$ in the place of $\sup|\psi_a|$, for the forms of the three kinds whose weights are real functions $\psi_a$ with ${\rm Lip}_\infty\psi_a<\infty$ read at the barycentres of the plaquettes and at the midpoints of the bonds, $w(p)=\psi_a(x(p))$, $\mathsf w(\mathfrak b)=\psi_a(x_{\mathfrak b})$, under the same separation of the supports; and for such weights the two limits agree.
\item[(b)] In this clause the separation of the head is replaced by a weaker one. Let $\psi_1,\dots,\psi_n$ be real Lipschitz functions on $T_\ell$, none of them $0$, let $\mathcal E_1=Y[\mathsf w]$ be the bond form of one direction $\mu$ with $\mathsf w(\mathfrak b)=\psi_1(x_{\mathfrak b})$ at the bonds $\mathfrak b$ of the direction $\mu$ and $\mathsf w=0$ at the others, let $\mathcal E_a=\mathcal O(w_a)$, $w_a(p)=\psi_a(x(p))$, $2\le a\le n$, be action densities, and let $\kappa_K$ be the joint cumulant of these $n$ forms. If the $n$ supports have no common point and their spread is at least $\mathsf d_0>0$ (the definition preceding Lem.~\YMMref{114.6}{805}), then from a cutoff on $|\kappa_{K+1}-\kappa_K|\le C\,K^pL^{-K/120}\prod_a\|\psi_a\|_\sharp$, $\|\psi\|_\sharp=\max\{\sup|\psi|,40M{\rm Lip}\,\psi\}$, with $C$, $p$ and the cutoff formed from the constants, $n$, $\ell$, $b$ and $\mathsf d_0$.
\item[(c)] If all the $\mathcal E_a$ are action densities with real Lipschitz weights read at the barycentres, $\mathcal E_a=\mathcal O(w_a)$, $w_a(p)=\psi_a(x(p))$, and $\kappa_K$ is their joint cumulant, the convergence is given by Thm.~\YMMref{AR}{810}, equation~\YMMref{(2203)}{810}, Cor.~\YMMref{117.1}{812} and Cor.~\YMMref{118.4}{815}: from a cutoff on, $|\kappa_{K+1}-\kappa_K|\le C\,\ell^{3(n+1)}K^{p}L^{-K/10}\prod_a\|\psi_a\|_\sharp$.
\end{enumerate}
Clauses (a) and (b) carry the convergence of Thm.~\YMMref{AR}{810} over to the plaquette form of one plane, to the bond form and to weights that are means over the lattice cubes; clause (c) is that theorem for the action density.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(a) At the two cutoffs $K$ and $K+1$, at the one label $b$ on the one torus, put
\[\sigma=\lfloor K/(1260\,n)\rfloor,\qquad s=\lfloor\sigma/(8n+3)\rfloor;\]
then $\sigma\le\lceil K/1260\rceil$, $\sigma-s\ge(8n+2)s$, $s\ge\theta_nK-2$ and $4n\sigma\le K/315$. Every insertion is the first member of a source under a majorant at both cutoffs ({\cite[Lem.~2.11]{YMM2}}, which holds on every side with (Sd.1), so on every $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$ by Prop.~\YMMref{74.1}{615}): under $(\mathsf s_a,S_a)$ with $\mathsf s_a=\sup|\psi_a|$ for a plaquette form or an action density and $\mathsf s_a=59\sup|\psi_a|$ for a bond form, $S_a$ the plaquettes whose corners lie within $\frac32a_K$ of the closed set off which $\psi_a$ vanishes; a source under a majorant is one under every larger majorant, so that these majorants serve, and corners of plaquettes of different $S_a$ are at sup distance $\ge\mathsf d-3a_K\ge\mathsf d/2$ once $6a_K\le\mathsf d$. The two cumulants are compared through three errors, each bounded by a number formed from the constants and $n$ times the factors written.

(i) \emph{One cutoff.} By Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8}, on the small fields, the chain with the sources is run up to the level $K-s$, at which the $n$ insertions have sizes at most $4\ell^3L^{4s}\mathsf s_a$; each insertion is replaced by its \emph{read-out}, its first member read at the background of the block field of the depth $\sigma$, a function of that block field alone. The cumulant of the $n$ insertions and the cumulant of their $n$ read-outs differ by at most
\[\Bigl[2L^{4n}V_\ell\,L^{-(4n+2)s}+n\,\epsilon(\sigma-s)+2e^{3-L^s\mathsf d/(2M)}\Bigr]\prod_a4\ell^3L^{4s}\mathsf s_a .\]
The first term is the large-field term (Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{115.2}{806}}), $V_\ell=4M^{-3}\ell^3e^{\mathsf B(X_g)\ell^3}$ times a number formed from the constants and $n$. The second is the loss of memory of the progression with sources between the depths $s$ and $\sigma$: the sources switched on at the level $K-\sigma$ in the place of the level $0$ change the effective terms of the level $K-s$ by at most $\epsilon(\sigma-s)$ times their sizes, $\epsilon(\nu)=C_{\rm m}(\nu+1)^{2\mathfrak p_0+2}L^{-\nu/2}$ with a number $C_{\rm m}$ of the constants, because the linearised steps contract on the small fields, as the flows of Props.~\YMMref{114.2}{801}, \YMMref{114.3}{803} forget their start. The third bounds the polymers that join two supports, whose linear size is at least $L^s\mathsf d/(2M)-2$ in the units of the level $K-s$.

(ii) \emph{The tie at the depth $\sigma$.} The read-outs of the two cutoffs are functions of one block field $V$ of the depth $\sigma$, vanishing where $V$ has large fields, of sizes at most $\frac32B_3^2\ell^3L^{4\sigma}\mathsf s_a$; over one such $V$ they differ by at most
\[\tau_a=C_{\rm t}\,\ell^3L^{4\sigma}K^{1/2}L^{-(K-\sigma)/2}\sup|\psi_a|\]
for weights that are means over the lattice cubes, and by the same with $\sup|\psi_a|+L^{-\sigma}{\rm Lip}_\infty\psi_a$ in the place of $\sup|\psi_a|$ for a weight read at the points of the two lattices, $C_{\rm t}$ a number of the constants; so, under one law of $V$, the cumulants of the read-outs of the two cutoffs differ by at most $\sum_a\tau_a\prod_{b\ne a}\frac32B_3^2\ell^3L^{4\sigma}\mathsf s_b$. The tie is a statement of its own, the counterpart of equation~\YMMref{(2156)}{795} for the products of two plaquette loops at a site. Let $(t,\varepsilon_{\rm r},V)$ be data of the comparison (the setting preceding Lem.~\YMMref{113.8}{794}), $t=K-\sigma$, $U^{\rm A}$, $U^{\rm B}$ the backgrounds over $V$ of the bare lattices $\Lambda_{K,\ell}$, $\Lambda_{K+1,\ell}$, and $N_t=\ell^3L^{3\sigma}$ the number of the sites of the level $t$; for two loops $l$, $l'$ at a site $x$ let $Q_x(l,l')=\langle w(W_{x,l}),w(W_{x,l'})\rangle$, $\langle X,Y\rangle=\frac12\operatorname{tr}XY$, $W_{x,l}$ the plaquette loop of $l$ at $x$. Then for $\xi\in[-1,1]^3$ and a complex function $\phi$ on $T_\ell$ with ${\rm Lip}_\infty\phi<\infty$,
\[\Bigl|L^{t+1}\!\!\sum_{x\in\Lambda_{K+1,\ell}}\!\!\phi(x+a_{K+1}\xi)\,Q_x(l,l')(U^{\rm B})-L^t\!\!\sum_{y\in\Lambda_{K,\ell}}\!\!\phi(y+a_K\xi)\,Q_y(l,l')(U^{\rm A})\Bigr|\le C_{\rm t}\,\|\phi\|_{(t)}\,\varepsilon_{\rm r}^2N_t\,t^{1/2}L^{-t/2},\]
$\|\phi\|_{(t)}$ the norm in equation~\YMMref{(2154)}{795}; and for a weight $\mathsf v_{\rm f}$ on the sites of $\Lambda_{K+1,\ell}$ and its block mean $\mathsf v_{\rm c}(y)=L^{-3}\sum_{x\in B(y)}\mathsf v_{\rm f}(x)$ on $\Lambda_{K,\ell}$, $B(y)$ the $L^3$ sites of the block of $y$, the same holds with $\mathsf v_{\rm f}$, $\mathsf v_{\rm c}$ in the place of the two readings of $\phi$ and $\sup|\mathsf v_{\rm f}|$ in the place of $\|\phi\|_{(t)}$. The proof follows that of Prop.~\YMMref{113.9}{795}: in a gauge on a box about a site of the coarse lattice the background is $e^{ia}$ with a small 1-form $a$ with values in the Lie algebra, the plaquette variables $w(W_{x,l})$ of the fine lattice are the curls of $a$ up to the second order, and those of the coarse lattice their averages (one averaging step with values in the Lie algebra); the variance of the curls about their averages, plaquette by plaquette, is bounded by the defect of Jensen's inequality, whose sum over the plaquettes is $2L^{-2}$ times the difference $L\sum_pa_p-\sum_{p'}a_{p'}$ of the actions of the fine background and of its block average, a difference bounded through the comparison of the two background actions, equation~\YMMref{(2155)}{795}, and the minimality of the background of the coarse lattice; and the background of the coarse lattice is compared with the block average of the fine background, a nearly minimal competitor, through its excess of action.

The bond density is a sum of four such products, $q_{\mathfrak b}=\frac14\sum_{\varepsilon,\varepsilon'=\pm}\varepsilon\varepsilon'\,Q_x((\mu,\varepsilon\lambda),(\mu,\varepsilon'\lambda'))$ at $\xi=\frac12e_\mu$, and the plaquette density of one plane is one such product up to $a_p^2$, by $a_p=\frac12Q_x(l,l)+\frac12a_p^2$ at the loop $l$ of the plane, $a_p^2$ being of the fourth order in the field at the backgrounds; the action density is equation~\YMMref{(2156)}{795} itself. With $a_K^{-1}=L^\sigma L^t$ and $\varepsilon_{\rm r}\le1$, $t\le K$, this gives $\tau_a$; for means over the lattice cubes the weights of the two cutoffs are tied by the block mean, $\psi^{(K)}(y)=L^{-3}\sum_{x\in B(y)}\psi^{(K+1)}(x)$, since the cell of $y$ is the union of the cells of the $x\in B(y)$, and the tie asks no regularity.

(iii) \emph{The laws.} The laws of the block field of the depth $\sigma\le\lceil K/1260\rceil$ at the two cutoffs differ, on the bounded gauge-invariant functions, by at most $\mathsf C_{\rm bf}\ell^3K^{\mathsf p_0}L^{-K/10}$ times their sup norm for $K\ge K_{\rm bf}$ (Cor.~\textup{\ref{IV-62-66}}), with the numbers $\mathsf C_{\rm bf}$, $K_{\rm bf}$ of Def.~\textup{\ref{IV-62-62}}~(5) at the label $b$ and $\mathsf p_0=2\mathfrak p_0+\frac12$; for the cumulant of the read-outs this costs $\mathsf C_{\rm bf}\ell^3K^{\mathsf p_0}L^{-K/10}\prod_a\frac32B_3^2\ell^3L^{4\sigma}\mathsf s_a$.

\emph{The balance.} In (i), $\sigma-s\ge(8n+2)s$ gives $L^{4ns}\epsilon(\sigma-s)\le C_{\rm m}(\sigma+1)^{2\mathfrak p_0+2}L^{-s}$; and from a cutoff on $L^{4n}V_\ell L^{-s}\le1$ and $2e^{3-L^s\mathsf d/(2M)}L^{(4n+1)s}\le1$; so (i) is at most $(4\ell^3)^n[3+nC_{\rm m}(\sigma+1)^{2\mathfrak p_0+2}]L^{-s}\prod_a\mathsf s_a$. In (ii) and (iii), $4n\sigma\le K/315$ gives $L^{4n\sigma}L^{-(K-\sigma)/2}\le L^{-K/3}$ and $L^{4n\sigma}L^{-K/10}\le L^{-K/11}$. As $L^{-s}\le L^2L^{-\theta_nK}$, $\theta_n<\frac1{11}$, $\sigma+1\le K$ and $\mathsf s_a\le59\sup|\psi_a|$, the three errors give (a) with $p=2\mathfrak p_0+2$; the factor $\ell^{3(n+1)}$ comes from the $n$ sizes and the law, and $C$ is formed from the constants, $n$ and $\mathsf C_{\rm bf}$, so from the constants, $n$ and $b$.

The cutoff $K_1$ is the least from which $K\ge K_{\rm bf}$, $s\ge1$, $L^s\mathsf d\ge6M$, $6a_K\le\mathsf d$, $L^\sigma b\ge\Theta_\star$ (the number of equation~\YMMref{(2148)}{794}), the two inequalities above and the thresholds of the chain of $n$ sources at the depth $s$ hold; through $V_\ell$, the distance and $K_{\rm bf}$ it reads besides $g$, $\ell$ and $\mathsf d$, while $C$ and $p$ read neither. The Lipschitz numbers enter at one place, the tie, with the factor $L^{-\sigma}$. The two readings of a Lipschitz weight, at the points and through the means over the lattice cubes, differ by at most $a_K{\rm Lip}_\infty\psi_a$, the size of the weight of a source; the bound of the moments of first members of sources at one fixed depth then makes the two cumulants at the cutoff $K$ differ by at most a number formed from the constants, $n$, $g$, $\ell$ and $\mathsf d$ times $a_K\sum_a{\rm Lip}_\infty\psi_a\prod_{b\ne a}\sup|\psi_b|$, which tends to $0$; so the two limits agree.

Since $\sum_KK^pL^{-\theta_nK}<\infty$, $\kappa_K$ converges along the full sequence; multilinearity and symmetry pass to the limit.

(b) Only the bond form needs a tie: the cumulant is the mixed derivative at $0$, in the parameters of the action densities, of the mean of the bond form under the measure with these densities as sources; along the chain the derivative of the bond form obeys a linear recursion, whose sizes are those of a member of the level $j$ and of what a step creates, so that no disc in a parameter of the bond form is needed; the polymers that meet all the $n$ supports, which make the contact terms, have at a depth $u$ a linear size of at least $\mathsf d_0L^u/M-2$ in the units of their level, as in the polymer estimate in Thm.~\YMMref{AR}{810}, so that the spread, and no pairwise distance, enters; and the comparison of the bond forms of the two backgrounds over one block field, the tie of (ii), gives the rate $L^{-K/120}$. (c) is Thm.~\YMMref{AR}{810}, equation~\YMMref{(2203)}{810} with Cor.~\YMMref{117.1}{812} and Cor.~\YMMref{118.4}{815}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The pointwise source identity}

We use the actual sourced history of
\cite[Thm.~D, Prop.~5.59, \S7.2]{YM3main}, with its admitted
torus, coupling range, source ball and fixed analytic radii.
The coefficient sequence is
$x_j=L^{-1}x_{j-1}-e_j$; the counterterms $e_j$ are fixed
independently of the sources. For two plaquette weights put
$w_\lambda=\lambda_1w_1+\lambda_2w_2$, and let
$E_\lambda^{(j)}$ be the effective action at height $j$
for these same source parameters. The new point here is an
identity at every admitted real chart point, with the whole
source parameter left in its exponential, rather than only
an almost-everywhere identity for the pushed-forward measure.

We recall the size conventions used in that identity. Set
$\omega_n=(n+1)L^{-(n-1)}$. At height $j$ the source-size
recursion and the remaining analytic room are
\begin{gather*}
 s_j=(1+\beta_{\rm s})\delta(x_j)/\alpha_0,
 \qquad \theta_j=K_{\mathbf M}s_j,
 \qquad N_{\star,j}=w_\star/(4K_\Lambda s_j),\\
 m_{j,a}=12M^3\alpha_0^2L^{K-j}|w_a|_\infty,\qquad
 c^\flat=81C_P^2C_{\mathcal A}^2/K_\Lambda,\\
 d_{1,a}=c^\flat\theta_0m_{0,a},\qquad
 n_{j,a}=m_{j,a}+\sum_{i=1}^j\omega_{j+1-i}d_{i,a},
 \qquad d_{j+1,a}=\theta_jn_{j,a},\\
 N_j^{\rm rm}=N_{\star,j}
    -\left(\sum_{n=1}^j\omega_n\right)
                      (E_0+\tfrac32\alpha_0^2B_\sharp).
\end{gather*}
All constants and radii in these formulas are those of the
fixed weighted source construction just cited. The admitted
parameter domains are the successive intersections
\begin{equation}\label{eq:weighted-progression-domain}
\begin{split}
 \Lambda^{\rm w}_0
 &=\{\lambda:c^\flat\sum_a|\lambda_a|m_{0,a}<N_{\star,0}\},\\
 \Lambda^{\rm w}_j
 &=\{\lambda\in\Lambda^{\rm w}_{j-1}:
                    \sum_a|\lambda_a|n_{j,a}<N_j^{\rm rm}\}.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
We write $\Lambda^{\rm w}=\Lambda^{\rm w}_{K-1}$ for the
common admitted domain through the required heights.
The norm $N_i(g)$ below is the bare-array norm at height $i$;
the map $\mathbb V'[g]^{\rm tot}(P;B)$ is the sum of its
local evaluations in the fourth source slot of the actual
step, over its finite domain set $\mathcal D_i$.

For clarity, write $w_i(P,B)$ for the fluctuation density
of this step, including the interaction and the chart
Jacobian, on its real cutoff domain $\mathsf{Rg}_{x_i}$.
Its normalizer and normalized measure are
\[
 \Xi(x_i;P)=\int_{\mathsf{Rg}_{x_i}}w_i(P,B)\,\mathrm{d}B,
 \qquad
 \nu_i[P](\mathrm{d}B)
       =\Xi(x_i;P)^{-1}w_i(P,B)\,\mathrm{d}B.
\]
For complex $P$ this measure need not be positive.
The normalization and insertion identities below first
control its total variation; positivity is then used
only on the specified real chart class. The regular
backgrounds and enlarged cubes are those of
\cite[\S7.2, eq.~7.xxvi]{YM3main}, including the stated
range $d_*\ge3$ of the background estimate.

\paragraph{Evaluation radii in the remaining sketches.}
Write $\ell=2L^m$ and $\eta_T=L^{-T}$. Here $K$ is the bare cutoff,
$T$ is a regularity level of a real bare configuration $U$, and
$1\le j\le T$ is the level of the pointed local family being evaluated.
Regularity at radius $\varepsilon$ means
$|\partial U-1|<\varepsilon\eta_T^2$ and
$|J^{(T)}(U)|<\varepsilon$, with the lattice current of the main
construction. Applying the detailed calculations with the radius of the
main manuscript requires an admission check. The calculations use
\[
 d_*^{\rm old}(j;T,\varepsilon)
 =\min\left\{\frac{c_A\alpha_0L^{2(T-j)}}{M\varepsilon},
              \frac{L^{m+K-j}-4}{2M}\right\}-1,
\]
whereas the regular-family estimate in the main manuscript uses
\[
 d_*^{\rm main}(j;T,\varepsilon)
 =\min\left\{\frac{c_A\alpha_0L^{2(T-j)}}{M\varepsilon},
              \frac{L^{m+K-j}-5}{2M}\right\}-2.
\]
The source's automatic admission calculation gives a lower bound of
$4$ for the minimum before the final subtraction, and thereby gives
$d_*^{\rm old}\ge3$. That calculation does not give
$d_*^{\rm main}\ge3$. One must verify admission of the working and upper levels with
$d_*^{\rm main}$, then use this radius in the flat-top and
regular-background estimates. The calculations below describe these
comparisons, but the displayed bound alone does not supply that
admission check.



At the canonical source choice we retain the following numerical
part of the choice explicitly. Put
\begin{equation}\label{eq:canonical-source-quarter-room}
 \begin{gathered}
 N_1=\frac{L}{L-1}(E_0+\tfrac32\alpha_0^2B_\sharp),\qquad
 N_\star\ge\frac{2L-1}{L-1}N_1,\qquad
 K_\Lambda^\omega=(1+\beta_{\rm s})^4K_\Lambda,\\
 K_{\mathbf M}(K_\Lambda^\omega)
 \left(\delta(\gamma^{-2})+s_\gamma N_1
                 +e^{-\gamma_2\mathfrak b(\gamma^{-2})^2/2}\right)
                                      \le E_0/4,\\
 s_\gamma\le\frac{w_\star}{4K_\Lambda^\omega N_\star},
 \qquad 8K_Ps_\gamma\le w_\star.
 \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
The allowance $N_\star$ is chosen after $E_0,B_\sharp$ and before
$\gamma$. The last three requirements are upper bounds tending
to zero with $\gamma$, with all other quantities already fixed.
They can therefore be retained in the ordered common choice of
Prop.~\YMMref{69.1}{595}. They are the source-room
conditions also imposed in \S\ref{sec:cutoff-calibration}
and Lem.~\ref{C-363-23}; a half-size bound alone is not used in
the source induction.

\begin{lemma}[Normalized step integrals]
\label{lem:weighted-step-integrals}
At an actual step of height $i$ in
{\cite[Def.~B.16]{YMM2}}, let
$P\in\mathcal U^\circ_{i+1}(T_\ell;\alpha_0,\alpha_1)$.
The integral defining $\Xi(x_i;P)$ is absolutely convergent and
nonzero. Its normalized measure $\nu_i[P]$ has finite total
variation and mass one. For every bare array $g$ through level
$i$, the function $B\mapsto\mathbb V'[g]^{\rm tot}(P;B)$ is
bounded and continuous on $\mathsf{Rg}_{x_i}$, with
\begin{equation}\label{eq:weighted-total-bound}
 |\mathbb V'[g]^{\rm tot}(P;B)|
       \le\#\mathcal D_i\,K_\Lambda s_iN_i(g).
\end{equation}
The first and mixed insertion identities are
equation~\YMMref{(2298)}{837}. For a real chart point of norm
less than $r_\alpha$, the normalized measure is a probability
measure by Prop.~\YMMref{124.5}{836}.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The rule sending an array to the fourth potential bounds each
of its local members by $K_\Lambda s_iN_i(g)$ on the step
domain. Summing over the finitely many domains gives
\eqref{eq:weighted-total-bound}. Each member is holomorphic
in the fluctuation field there, hence continuous on the real box.
To evaluate the normalization, insert $\mu g$ in the source
slot and restrict $\mu$ so that its array norm is smaller
than the remaining room. The whole-torus identity of
Thm.~\YMMref{V}{416}, equation~\YMMref{(902)}{417},
expresses the integral as the exponential
of the sum of the localized output, so it is nonzero and
absolutely convergent. Here $\tau=1$ removes the additional
quadratic potential. At $\mu=0$, division by this nonzero
integral gives mass one and finite total variation. The bound
\eqref{eq:weighted-total-bound} justifies differentiation
of the normalized integral; the first derivative of its
logarithm is the mean of the inserted total, and the mixed
derivative is its covariance. This is precisely the argument
for equation~\YMMref{(2298)}{837}. Positivity is asserted only
at the real chart points covered by
Prop.~\YMMref{124.5}{836}.
\end{proof}

For the tower identity we use the real two-source frame of
Lem.~\ref{C-352-11}(a), retaining its actual canonical places,
flat-top hypotheses and weighted progression. The chart, lowering
map and chain classes are those of Section~\YMMref{124}{832}.
In particular, a member of $\mathsf{Cc}_n(r)$ is a real bare
potential $A$ satisfying
\begin{equation}\label{eq:weighted-chain-class}
 \|v_A^{[n]}\|\le r,\qquad
 v_A^{[n]}=(A,J^{(n)}(e^{i\eta_nA})),\qquad
 e^{i\eta_nA}=U^u,\quad
 U\in\mathcal C(\mathbf B_n,W),\quad
 \varpi(W)<\varepsilon_{\mathcal W}\alpha_0.
\end{equation}
Thus the norm condition is accompanied by an actual background
condition. The two radii in equation~\YMMref{(2285)}{833} are
denoted here by $\varrho_{\rm ch}$ and $\varrho_{\rm fl}$.

\begin{lemma}[The domains of a chain background]
\label{lem:weighted-chain-background}
In this frame, let $1\le n\le K$, $r\ge0$ and
$A\in\mathsf{Cc}_n(r)$. The array actions through level $n$
are defined at $\widetilde U=e^{i\eta_nA}$. If, in addition,
$r<r'\le\varrho_{\rm ch}$, then $\widetilde U$ is regular
of level $n$ at radius $3r'$, and
\[
 P[v_A^{[n]}]\in\mathcal U^\circ_n(T_\ell;\alpha_0,\alpha_1),
 \qquad 0\le a_p(\widetilde U)<\tfrac92(r')^2\eta_n^4.
\]
If $r=0$, then $A=0$ and $\widetilde U=\mathbf1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Under the additional radius condition the chart norm is at most
$r<r'$. Its image lies in the simple domain with radii
$(3r',r',r')$, and in the core because
$r'\le r_\alpha$. This is the usable-chart construction in
equation~\YMMref{(933)}{427} and the domain verification
preceding equation~\YMMref{(2287)}{834}. Hence
\[
 |\partial\widetilde U-\mathbf1|<3r'\eta_n^2,
 \qquad |J^{(n)}(\widetilde U)|<r',
\]
which gives regularity. To check the earlier array actions, use
the background $U$ and block field $W$ in
\eqref{eq:weighted-chain-class}. The small-plaquette clause of
Prop.~\YMMref{52.3}{433} puts $W$ in the actual step
domain. At height $n-1$ the canonical sum rule has its array
actions defined at every representative of this orbit. This
gives all levels through $n-1$; at level $n$ the plain-core
clause in the proof of the same proposition supplies the
remaining pairs. At $n=1$ there are no earlier levels to check.
The trivial pairs lie in their cores as well. These are exactly
the domain conditions for the absolute array actions. Their
domains are gauge invariant, so they hold also at $U^u=
\widetilde U$.

For an $SU(2)$ plaquette,
$a_p(\widetilde U)=\tfrac12|\partial\widetilde U(p)-\mathbf1|^2$;
the regularity bound gives the asserted estimate. Finally the
chart norm dominates $|A|$, so $r=0$ forces $A=0$.
\end{proof}

Write $\mathsf{Sum}[f](U)$ for the finite sum over the domains
and base points of the family $f$, evaluated at the pairs of $U$.
For $w_\lambda=\lambda_1w_1+\lambda_2w_2$ and
$\lambda\in\Lambda^{\rm w}=\Lambda^{\rm w}_{K-1}$, set
\begin{equation}\label{eq:weighted-relative-functions}
\begin{gathered}
 D_i^\lambda(U)=\mathcal O(w_\lambda)(U)
       +\sum_{j=1}^i\mathsf{Sum}[E^{(j)}_\lambda-E^{(j)}](U),
 \qquad \mathcal O(w)(U)=L^K\sum_pw(p)a_p(U),\\
 \Phi_{a,i}=\partial_aD_i^\lambda|_0,
 \qquad \mathsf F_i=\partial_1\partial_2D_i^\lambda|_0,\\
 \Phi^{\rm ir}_{a,i}(U)=\sum_{j=1}^i
       \bigl(\mathsf{Sum}[\dot E^{(j)}_a](U)
                       -\mathsf{Sum}[\dot E^{(j)}_a](\mathbf1)\bigr).
\end{gathered}
\end{equation}
These functions are defined when the array actions through level
$i$ are defined at $U$. Then the relative exponent is holomorphic
in $\lambda$ and $D_i^0=0$, by
{\cite[Prop.~B.8]{YMM2}}.

\begin{proposition}[The two-source tower]
\label{prop:weighted-pair-tower}
In the frame just specified, let $1\le i<K$ and $r\ge0$ satisfy
\begin{equation}\label{eq:weighted-tower-smallness}
 r<\varrho_{\rm ch},\qquad
 \delta_i<\varrho_{\rm fl},\qquad
 6L^{-2}r+8C_{\rm db}\delta_i<\varepsilon_{\mathcal W}\alpha_0.
\end{equation}
For $A\in\mathsf{Cc}_{i+1}(r)$ put
$\widetilde U=e^{i\eta_{i+1}A}$, $v=v_A^{[i+1]}$,
$P=P[v]$ and $\nu=\nu_i[P]$. For
$B\in\mathsf{Rg}_{x_i}$ put
\[
 \widetilde U^{\rm lw}(B)
        =e^{i\eta_iA^{\rm lw}(v,g_iB)}.
\]
Then $\nu$ is a probability measure. The relative exponents and
their derivatives in \eqref{eq:weighted-relative-functions} are
defined at $\widetilde U$ through level $i+1$ and at
$\widetilde U^{\rm lw}(B)$ through level $i$. Their latter
values, as well as $\mathcal O(w_a)(\widetilde U^{\rm lw}(B))$,
are bounded continuous functions of $B$. For every
$\lambda\in\Lambda^{\rm w}$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:weighted-pair-tower}
 e^{D_{i+1}^\lambda(\widetilde U)}
     =\int e^{D_i^\lambda(\widetilde U^{\rm lw}(B))}\,\mathrm{d}\nu(B).
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:weighted-pair-tower-derivatives}
\begin{split}
 \Phi_{a,i+1}(\widetilde U)
    &=\int\Phi_{a,i}(\widetilde U^{\rm lw})\,\mathrm{d}\nu,\\
 \mathsf F_{i+1}(\widetilde U)
    &=\int\mathsf F_i(\widetilde U^{\rm lw})\,\mathrm{d}\nu
       +\big\langle\Phi_{1,i}(\widetilde U^{\rm lw});
                         \Phi_{2,i}(\widetilde U^{\rm lw})\big\rangle_\nu.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Prop.~\YMMref{124.2}{834} applies under
\eqref{eq:weighted-tower-smallness}. It gives
\[
 A^{\rm lw}(v,g_iB)\in
  \mathsf{Cc}_i(L^{-1}r+\tfrac{11}{10}c_{\mathfrak h}\delta_i),
\]
and Lem.~\ref{lem:weighted-chain-background} puts $P$ in
the level-$(i+1)$ core and verifies the array actions at both
backgrounds. Restriction to earlier
levels preserves this definedness: it retains a subset of the
required core conditions. The chart point is real and has norm
less than $r_\alpha$, so Prop.~\YMMref{124.5}{836} gives
the asserted positivity and normalization of $\nu$.

The source enters only through the bare array. At height $i$,
the difference $g_\lambda=f_{\lambda,i}-f_{0,i}$ has zero
counterterms and equals
\[
 g_\lambda=((E^{(j)}_\lambda-E^{(j)},0)_{j\le i},\emptyset)
                 \sqcup\mathsf W_{L^{K-i}w_\lambda}.
\]
Indeed $E^{(j)}_0=E^{(j)}$ and the counterterms were kept fixed.
The action of a zero-counterterm array is the sum of its pointed
totals minus their values at $\mathbf1$. Its weight member adds
$\eta_i^{-1}\sum_pL^{K-i}w_\lambda(p)a_p(U)=\mathcal O(w_\lambda)(U)$.
Since the plaquette action vanishes at $\mathbf1$, this gives
\[
 S[g_\lambda](U)=D_i^\lambda(U)-D_i^\lambda(\mathbf1).
\]
Apply the array sum rule, equation~\YMMref{(2289)}{834}, to
$g_\lambda$. The constant at $\mathbf1$ cancels, yielding
\begin{equation}\label{eq:weighted-tower-action}
 \mathbb V'[g_\lambda]^{\rm tot}(P;B)
      =D_i^\lambda(\widetilde U^{\rm lw}(B))
                            -D_i^\lambda(\widetilde U).
\end{equation}
The same calculation for the first and mixed derivatives of
$g_\lambda$, and for its weight member alone, gives the analogous
identities for $\Phi_{a,i}$, $\mathsf F_i$ and $\mathcal O(w_a)$.
Lem.~\ref{lem:weighted-step-integrals} makes these potential
totals bounded and continuous on the fluctuation box; hence
so are the listed functions. Finally
$\Phi^{\rm ir}_{a,i}=\Phi_{a,i}-\mathcal O(w_a)
-\sum_{j\le i}\mathsf{Sum}[\dot E^{(j)}_a](\mathbf1)$,
which gives the remaining continuity assertion.

Let $\Xi_\lambda(P)$ be the step integral with array
$f_{\lambda,i}$ and with all other data unchanged. The finite-source
estimate puts this array in the admitted norm ball. The actual
one-step theorem therefore gives an absolutely convergent integral
and the identity
\begin{equation}\label{eq:weighted-tower-integral}
 \Xi_\lambda(P)
   =\exp\mathsf{Sum}[\mathsf{St}_i(f_{\lambda,i})](P)\ne0.
\end{equation}
Here the calibration equals the running coefficient, so $\tau=1$
and the additional quadratic potential, bounded by a constant times
$|1-\tau|$, is zero. The whole torus is an admitted localization
domain, and the output radii are $(\alpha_0,\alpha_1)$. These are
the hypotheses for the whole-torus identity of Thm.~\YMMref{V}{416};
the same specialization is used in
{\cite[Prop.~B.8]{YMM2}}.

At zero source this integral is precisely the normalization of
$\nu_i[P]$, equation~\YMMref{(2293)}{836}. The provision is linear
in its bare array, so division of the two integrals and
\eqref{eq:weighted-tower-action} give
\[
 \frac{\Xi_\lambda(P)}{\Xi_0(P)}
  =e^{-D_i^\lambda(\widetilde U)}
       \int e^{D_i^\lambda(\widetilde U^{\rm lw}(B))}\,\mathrm{d}\nu(B).
\]
On the other hand the recursion
{\cite[eq.~200]{YMM2}} and
\eqref{eq:weighted-tower-integral} give
\[
 \frac{\Xi_\lambda(P)}{\Xi_0(P)}
   =\exp\mathsf{Sum}[E^{(i+1)}_\lambda-E^{(i+1)}](P)
   =\exp\bigl(D_{i+1}^\lambda(\widetilde U)
                                  -D_i^\lambda(\widetilde U)\bigr).
\]
The sum at $P$ equals the sum at its pair, which is the pair of
$\widetilde U$. Comparing the two quotients proves
\eqref{eq:weighted-pair-tower}.

To differentiate this identity, the pointwise holomorphy in the
sources needs a bound uniform in the fluctuation field. Define the
finite numbers
\[
 K_{i,a}=2L^K\sum_p|w_a(p)|
       +\sum_{j\le i}\sum_{X\in\mathcal D_j}
                         \#(X\cap\mathbb T^{(j)})d_{j,a},
\]
where $d_{j,a}$ are the Lipschitz bounds in
{\cite[eq.~196]{YMM2}}. All pairs entering the
lowered array actions lie in their cores. The family norm bounds
each of their values, and $0\le a_p(U)\le2$ on real configurations.
Consequently
\[
 |D_i^\lambda(\widetilde U^{\rm lw}(B))|
                  \le\sum_{a=1}^2|\lambda_a|K_{i,a}
 \quad(\lambda\in\Lambda^{\rm w},\ B\in\mathsf{Rg}_{x_i}).
\]
Thus the exponential is uniformly bounded on each compact source
set, independently of $B$. Cauchy's formula and integration against
the probability measure justify differentiation. Since $D_i^0=0$,
the first derivatives give the first identity in
\eqref{eq:weighted-pair-tower-derivatives}. The mixed derivative
gives the integral of
$\mathsf F_i+\Phi_{1,i}\Phi_{2,i}$. Subtracting the product
of the two first-derivative identities leaves the covariance
in its second identity.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{The calibrated cutoff comparison}\label{sec:cutoff-calibration}

We record the choices used in the comparison of two successive cutoffs.
They must be made before fixing the torus or its physical coupling.
The setting has three parts, denoted by \textup{(Th1)}--\textup{(Th3)}.

In \textup{(Th1)}, choose the real construction constants and canonical
auxiliary data as in Lem.~\YMMref{118.1}{812}. Impose the global
background, response, localization and actual-domain hypotheses of
Section~\YMMref{113}{786}, and the source and recursion hypotheses of
Section~\YMMref{114}{799}. In particular the fixed pair radii are
$(\alpha_0,\alpha_1)$, $\alpha_0\le a_{\rm H}$, the lag weights are
$L^{-(j-i)}$, and
\[
 E_0^{\rm s}=E_0,\qquad
 N_\star^{\rm s}=\frac L{L-1}
                 (E_0+\tfrac32\alpha_0^2B_\sharp).
\]
The constants $K_{\rm Q}^\vee,K_{\rm L}^\vee,\mu_\star,
\sigma_{\rm src}$ and the three smallness inequalities are those
in equations~\YMMref{(2170)}{801} and the surrounding source construction.
Take
\[
 \varrho=\min\left\{
 \frac{20\mu_\star}{\sqrt3K_{\rm L}^\vee\gamma},
 \frac{\sigma_{\rm src}}2(\gamma^{-2}-\bar B)\right\}>0,
 \qquad
 \mathsf{Src}=\mathsf{Src}_{\mathsf{Bc}}(2\varrho,2\varrho).
\]
Thus the coupling sequence, Gaussian structures, auxiliary data and
pair cores are independent of the source.

In \textup{(Th2)}, fix $0<\eth<1$ before decreasing $\gamma$, and use
the tail calibration of Section~\YMMref{115}{805}:
\[
 c'=(1-\eth)c_\star,\qquad
 C_{\rm maj}^{\Sigma}=C_{\rm maj}+(6L^3+1)\log2,\qquad
 C_{\rm low}(x)=c_{\rm low}+\tfrac92\log x.
\]
The ceiling $\gamma$ is chosen so that $\log\gamma^{-2}$ exceeds
both the case-II history threshold and the summability threshold
specified there. These thresholds, the source smallness conditions,
and the background and response conditions are part of the
calibration. The proof of Lem.~\YMMref{118.1}{812} verifies that they
can be imposed simultaneously. None depends on the finite lattice.

For later use put $c_{\log}=\log L/\log\gamma^{-2}$ and
\[
 c_\rho=\max\left\{2B_3,
       \frac{C_HA_1}{(1-L^{-3/2})A_0}\right\}.
\]
We write $\mathsf t_\natural$ for the fixed calibration denoted by
$\tau_\natural$ in equation~\YMMref{(2134)}{790}. It is the least
$\tau\ge\gamma^{-2}$ at which
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 2c_\rho\varepsilon(\tau)
 \le\min\{\varepsilon_{\mathcal W}\alpha_0,c_2^{\rm SO},
                                  \varepsilon_{\rm v}/4\},\\
 \delta(\tau)\le\varepsilon_{\mathcal W},\qquad
 4C_{\rm db}\delta(\tau)
       \le\min\{1,r_{\rm B},r_{\rm B}^{\rm s}/2\}.
 \end{gathered}
\]
The thresholds are continuous, decreasing and tend to zero;
their positive fixed ceilings therefore make this minimum finite.
All three inequalities persist at larger $\tau$.

In \textup{(Th3)}, fix
\[
 K\ge2,\quad \mathsf b'\ge\gamma^{-2},\quad m\in\mathbb N,\quad
 MR(\mathsf b')\le L^m,\quad \ell=2L^m,\quad
 x_j=L^{K-j}\mathsf b'\quad(0\le j\le K).
\]
Choose an integer top level $1\le t_*\le K-1$ such that
$x_{t_*}\ge\mathsf t_\natural$. These are precisely the
finite-lattice data in Section~\YMMref{115}{805}. The setting
\textup{(E)} retains \textup{(Th1)}, \textup{(Th2)}, the label and
the side, allowing $K$ to vary. A compact label interval
$J=[b_-,b_+]$ is admissible on this side when
$b_-\ge\gamma^{-2}$ and $MR(b_+)\le L^m$, as in
equation~\YMMref{(2201)}{810}.

For a comparison involving $n$ insertions, the depths are
$u=\lceil K/[180(3n+4)]\rceil$ and $s=\lceil K/9\rceil$.
The errors and smallness conditions are those in
Section~\YMMref{116}{807}; the additional support condition is
$d_\infty(\underline f)L^u\ge6M$ when $n\ge2$.
For bounded functions of block fields one takes $n=1$ and omits
this support condition. \S\ref{sec:block-field-laws} displays
all the resulting errors and conditions \textup{(k0)}--\textup{(k4)},
\textup{(k6)}.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:cutoff-admissible-labels}
Let $0<g\le\gamma$ and $\ell=2L^m\in\mathfrak L(g)$. Then
\[
 J_g=[g^{-2}+B_\sharp-L^{-1}\bar B,\ X_g+\bar B]
\]
is an admissible label interval on $T_\ell$, and it contains $I(g)$
and every first-passage label at $g$. The larger interval
$\mathsf J_g=[\gamma^{-2},L(X_g+\bar B)]$ is also admissible
on $T_\ell$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The lower endpoint is at least $\gamma^{-2}$, since
$B_\sharp-L^{-1}\bar B=B_\sharp(L-2)/(L-1)\ge0$.
The side floor in equation~\YMMref{(1528)}{615} gives
$L^m\ge LM R(X_g+\bar B)$, and hence the required room
$MR(\max J_g)\le L^m$. The containment of $I(g)$ follows from
its endpoints. The first-passage label bound is
equation~\YMMref{(1531)}{615}.
For the larger interval, the radius scaling inequality in the proof
of Prop.~\YMMref{74.1}{615} gives
$R(LX)\le LR(X)$ for $X\ge\gamma^{-2}$. Apply it at
$X=X_g+\bar B$ and use the same side floor to obtain
$MR(\max\mathsf J_g)\le LMR(X_g+\bar B)\le L^m$.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{The laws of the block fields}\label{sec:block-field-laws}

The cutoff comparison also controls bounded functions of a fixed block
field. We prove the resulting total-variation convergence here. We use
the calibrated small-field setting of Section~\YMMref{115}{805}: all constants,
auxiliary data, source radii and tail thresholds are fixed before the
cutoff, with $E_0^{\rm s}=E_0$,
$N_\star^{\rm s}=L(E_0+3\alpha_0^2B_\sharp/2)/(L-1)$,
$\mathsf b\ge\gamma^{-2}$, $MR(\mathsf b)\le L^m$ and $\ell=2L^m$.
This is the setting denoted by \textup{(E)}. The precise calibration,
including the source and tail smallness conditions, is that of
Prop.~\YMMref{115.2}{806}, not merely the displayed lower bound on
$\mathsf b$.

At cutoffs $K$ and $K+1$ use the same physical depth, and put
\[
 u=\lceil K/1260\rceil,\qquad s=\lceil K/9\rceil,
 \qquad t_1=K-u,\qquad t_0=K-s.
\]
\[
 x_{[d]}=L^d\mathsf b,\qquad N_{[d]}=\ell^3L^{3d},
 \qquad y_{[d]}=(\log x_{[d]})^{2\mathfrak p_0}.
\]
The errors in Prop.~\YMMref{116.1}{808} and the discarded mass in
Prop.~\YMMref{115.2}{806} are
\begin{align*}
 \epsilon_{\rm fg}&=C_{\rm old}C_{\rm fg}\frac L{L-1}E_0
                           N_{[u]}L^{-(s-u)},\\
 \epsilon_{\rm cl}&=4\mathsf K_{\rm w}c_\rho^2A_0^2
    (1+2\varrho/\mathsf b)y_{[K]}N_{[s]}\sqrt K L^{-(K-s)/2},\\
 \epsilon_{\rm sh}&=3(s-u)N_{[s]}
    \exp[C_{\rm sh}-\kappa_{\rm b}A_1^2y_{[u]}/4],\\
 \mathsf R_{t_1}&=2M^{-3}N_{[u]}
    \exp[-c'A_0^2y_{[u]}+(\mathsf C^\Sigma_{\rm maj}+2
                                      +C_{\rm low}(\mathsf b))\ell^3].
\end{align*}
Here $c'=(1-\eth)c_\star>0$, with the fixed $0<\eth<1$ of that
calibration. We retain the following names for the comparison conditions:
\begin{gather*}
 \textup{(k0)}\quad1\le u<s<K,\qquad
 \textup{(k1)}\quad L^u\mathsf b\ge\Theta_\star,\\
 \textup{(k2)}\quad\epsilon_{\rm fg}\le1/8,\qquad
 \textup{(k3)}\quad\epsilon_{\rm cl},\epsilon_{\rm sh}\le1/20,\\
 \textup{(k4)}\quad256\mathsf K_uc_\rho^2A_0^2N_{[s]}L^{-(K-s)}
                         \le\gamma_{\rm r}A_1^2,\qquad
 \textup{(k6)}\quad\mathsf R_{t_1}\le1/2.
\end{gather*}
There is no support-separation condition in this measure statement.
The constants $\Theta_\star$, $\mathsf K_u$, $\mathsf K_{\rm w}$
and the other comparison constants are those in
Sections~\YMMref{116}{807} and~\YMMref{115}{805}, with identical level
units. In particular the block lattice at depth $d$ is
$\Lambda_{d,\ell}$ on both cutoffs.

For uniformity in $\mathsf b$, let
$\mathsf J=[\mathsf b_-,\mathsf b_+]$ satisfy
$\mathsf b_-\ge\gamma^{-2}$ and $MR(\mathsf b_+)\le L^m$.
Define $\bar\epsilon_{\rm sh}$ by replacing $\mathsf b$ by
$\mathsf b_-$ in $y_{[u]}$, and define $\bar{\mathsf R}$ by that
same replacement in its negative exponent and by replacing
$C_{\rm low}(\mathsf b)$ with $C_{\rm low}(\mathsf b_+)$.
They dominate their unbarred counterparts. The uniform threshold
$K_0$ in Thm.~\YMMref{AR}{810}, taken at $n=1$, makes (k0)--(k4) and
(k6) valid for all $K\ge K_0$. Its proof shows that
$K^ae^{a'K}(\bar{\mathsf R}+\bar\epsilon_{\rm sh})\to0$
for every fixed real $a,a'$. The reason is
$u\ge K/1260$ and $2\mathfrak p_0\ge2$ in the negative exponents.

We first record the measure-theoretic passage to the limit.

\begin{lemma}[A summable sequence of probability measures]\label{IV-62-61}
Let $(\Omega,\mathfrak B)$ be a measurable space, let $K_*\in\mathbb N$, and let $\mu^K$, $K\ge K_*$, be probability measures on $\mathfrak B$. Let $q_K\ge0$ be numbers with $\sum_{K\ge K_*}q_K<\infty$ and
\[
\sup_{E\in\mathfrak B}\bigl|\mu^{K+1}(E)-\mu^K(E)\bigr|\le q_K\qquad(K\ge K_*).
\]
Then $\mu(E):=\lim_{K\to\infty}\mu^K(E)$ exists for every $E\in\mathfrak B$,
\[
\sup_{E\in\mathfrak B}\bigl|\mu^K(E)-\mu(E)\bigr|\le\sum_{k\ge K}q_k\qquad(K\ge K_*),
\]
and $\mu$ is a probability measure on $\mathfrak B$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\emph{Step 1: the limit and the bound.} For $K'>K\ge K_*$ and $E\in\mathfrak B$,
\[
\bigl|\mu^{K'}(E)-\mu^K(E)\bigr|\le\sum_{k=K}^{K'-1}q_k\le\sum_{k\ge K}q_k ,
\]
and the right-hand side tends to $0$ as $K\to\infty$. Hence $(\mu^K(E))_K$ is a Cauchy sequence, and its limit $\mu(E)$ exists. Letting $K'\to\infty$ in the display gives the asserted bound, uniformly in $E$.

\emph{Step 2: elementary properties.} As limits of the corresponding properties of the $\mu^K$, we have $\mu(E)\ge0$ for all $E\in\mathfrak B$, $\mu(\emptyset)=0$, $\mu(\Omega)=1$, and $\mu$ is finitely additive.

\emph{Step 3: $\sigma$-additivity.} Let $E_1,E_2,\dots\in\mathfrak B$ be pairwise disjoint and put $R_N:=\bigcup_{i>N}E_i$. By finite additivity,
\[
\mu\Bigl(\bigcup_iE_i\Bigr)=\sum_{i\le N}\mu(E_i)+\mu(R_N).
\]
Let $\eta>0$, and choose $K\ge K_*$ with $\sum_{k\ge K}q_k\le\eta$. By Step~1, $\mu(R_N)\le\mu^K(R_N)+\eta$ for every $N$. Since $\mu^K$ is a measure and $R_N$ decreases to $\emptyset$, we have $\mu^K(R_N)\to0$ as $N\to\infty$; hence $\limsup_N\mu(R_N)\le\eta$. As $\eta>0$ is arbitrary and $\mu(R_N)\ge0$, $\mu(R_N)\to0$, and $\mu(\bigcup_iE_i)=\sum_i\mu(E_i)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[The laws of the block fields]\label{IV-62-62}
Assume (E), with label $\mathsf b$ and side $\ell=2L^m$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)] At cutoff $K$ set $\beta=L^K\mathsf b$ and
\[
 \rho_0(U)=e^{-A^{a_K}(\mathsf b,U)},\qquad
 Z_K=\int\rho_0\,\mathrm{d}U>0,\qquad
 \langle H\rangle_K=Z_K^{-1}\int H\rho_0\,\mathrm{d}U.
\]
Here $dU$ is product Haar probability measure and
$A^{a_K}(\mathsf b,U)=\beta\sum_pa_p(U)$ is the Wilson action.
\item[(2)] For $K\ge\max\{d,1\}$ the law at depth $d$ is
\begin{equation}\label{IV-62-63}
 \mu_d^K(E)=\langle\mathbf1_E(\mathcal M^{K-d}U)\rangle_K
 \qquad(E\subset\mathcal V(\Lambda_{d,\ell})\text{ Borel}).
\end{equation}
The averaging map is Borel and gauge covariant. Its map from
$\Lambda_{d+1,\ell}$ to $\Lambda_{d,\ell}$ is independent of the
bare cutoff: its definition uses precisely these two lattices.
These properties are proved in Prop.~\YMMref{4.5}{20}.
Thus $\mu_d^K$ is a Borel probability measure.
\item[(3)] Write $\mathfrak B_d$ for the sigma-algebra of invariant
Borel sets in $\mathcal V(\Lambda_{d,\ell})$. Gauge transformations
are bijections, so complements and countable unions of invariant
sets remain invariant. The map $\mathcal M$ in the consistency
identity below is the fixed map from depth $d+1$ to depth $d$.
\item[(4)] For $K\ge2$, use the errors above and set
\begin{equation}\label{IV-62-64}
 \mathfrak o_K=8\mathsf R_{t_1}+12\epsilon_{\rm fg}
                          +8\epsilon_{\rm cl}+12\epsilon_{\rm sh}.
\end{equation}
\item[(5)] For an interval $\mathsf J=[\mathsf b_-,\mathsf b_+]$
as above, put
\begin{equation}\label{IV-62-65}
\mathsf C_{\mathrm{bf}}:=2\Bigl[1+12\,C_{\mathrm{old}}C_{\mathrm{fg}}\tfrac L{L-1}E_0\,L^4+32\,\mathsf K_{\mathrm w}c_\rho^2A_0^2\bigl(1+\tfrac{2\varrho}{\mathsf b_-}\bigr)\bigl(\log(L\mathsf b_+)\bigr)^{2\mathfrak p_0}L^{7/2}\Bigr]
\end{equation}
and
\[
K_{\mathrm{bf}}:=\min\Bigl\{k\in\mathbb Z:\ k\ge K_0,\ \text{and }\ 8\,\bar{\mathsf R}+12\,\bar\epsilon_{\mathrm{sh}}\le\tfrac12\,\mathsf C_{\mathrm{bf}}\,\ell^3K^{\mathsf p_0}L^{-K/10}\ \text{ at all integers }K\ge k\Bigr\},
\]
where $\mathsf p_0=2\mathfrak p_0+1/2$ and $K_0$ is the uniform
threshold specified above. This minimum exists: the bracket defining
$\mathsf C_{\rm bf}$ is at least $1$, and the barred errors decay
faster than every exponential in $K$. Its dependencies are only
$\ell$, the endpoints of $\mathsf J$ and the fixed constants.
\end{enumerate}
\end{definition}

The comparison of the two lattices made above also controls the laws of Def.~\ref{IV-62-62}, and Lem.~\ref{IV-62-61} turns this control into their convergence as the cutoff tends to infinity.

\begin{corollary}[Convergence of the laws of the block fields]\label{IV-62-66}
Assume the setting (E), and take $u,s,t_1,t_0$ and the comparison errors defined above.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textup{(a)}] Let $K\ge2$ be an integer at which the conditions (k0), (k1), (k2), (k3), (k4) and (k6) hold. Then, for every integer $0\le d\le u$ and every bounded Borel function $F:\mathcal V(\Lambda_{d,\ell})\to\mathbb C$ invariant under the gauge transformations of $\Lambda_{d,\ell}$,
\begin{equation}\label{IV-62-67}
\Bigl|\bigl\langle F(\mathcal M^{K+1-d}U)\bigr\rangle_{K+1}-\bigl\langle F(\mathcal M^{K-d}U)\bigr\rangle_K\Bigr|\ \le\ \mathfrak o_K\,\sup|F| .
\end{equation}
If moreover $\mathsf J$ is an interval of labels under (Tor) on the side $\ell$ with $\mathsf b\in\mathsf J$, then at every integer $K\ge K_{\mathrm{bf}}$ the conditions (k0)--(k4) and (k6) hold, and
\begin{equation}\label{IV-62-68}
\mathfrak o_K\ \le\ \mathsf C_{\mathrm{bf}}\,\ell^3\,K^{\mathsf p_0}\,L^{-K/10};
\end{equation}
here $\mathsf C_{\mathrm{bf}}$ and $K_{\mathrm{bf}}$ are the numbers of Def.~\ref{IV-62-62}(5), which depend on the label $\mathsf b$ only through $\mathsf J$.
\item[\textup{(b)}] Let $K_{\mathrm{bf}}$ be taken at $\mathsf J=\{\mathsf b\}$. For every integer $d\ge0$ and every $E\in\mathfrak B_d$ the limit $\mu_d(E):=\lim_{K\to\infty}\mu^K_d(E)$ exists, and
\begin{equation}\label{IV-62-69}
\sup_{E\in\mathfrak B_d}\bigl|\mu^K_d(E)-\mu_d(E)\bigr|\ \le\ \sum_{K'\ge K}\mathfrak o_{K'}<\infty\qquad\text{for every integer }K\ge K_{\mathrm{bf}}\text{ with }\lceil K/1260\rceil\ge d .
\end{equation}
The set function $\mu_d$ is a probability measure on $\mathfrak B_d$. The family $(\mu_d)_{d\ge0}$ is consistent: if $E\in\mathfrak B_d$, then $\mathcal M^{-1}(E)\in\mathfrak B_{d+1}$ and
\begin{equation}\label{IV-62-70}
\mu_{d+1}\bigl(\mathcal M^{-1}E\bigr)=\mu_d(E),
\end{equation}
where $\mathcal M:\mathcal V(\Lambda_{d+1,\ell})\to\mathcal V(\Lambda_{d,\ell})$ is the averaging map of Def.~\ref{IV-62-62}(3).
\item[\textup{(c)}] For every integer $d\ge0$, every integer $K\ge\max\{d,1\}$ and every Borel set $E\subset\mathcal V(\Lambda_{d,\ell})$,
\begin{equation}\label{IV-62-71}
\mu^K_d(E)=\int\bar{\mathbf 1}_E\,\mathrm{d}\mu^K_d,\qquad\bar{\mathbf 1}_E(V):=\int\mathbf 1_E(V^v)\,\mathrm{d}v,
\end{equation}
where $dv$ is the product of one Haar probability measure of $G$ for each site of $\Lambda_{d,\ell}$, a measure on the group of the gauge transformations $v$ of $\Lambda_{d,\ell}$.
The function $\bar{\mathbf 1}_E$ is Borel, takes its values in $[0,1]$ and is gauge invariant.
Consequently the limit in (b), the bound \eqref{IV-62-69} and the identity \eqref{IV-62-70} hold for all Borel sets: $\mu^K_d\to\mu_d$ in total variation, that is, uniformly on the Borel subsets of $\mathcal V(\Lambda_{d,\ell})$; $\mu_d$ is a Borel probability measure on $\mathcal V(\Lambda_{d,\ell})$ that is gauge invariant; and the image of $\mu_{d+1}$ under $\mathcal M$ is $\mu_d$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
We first compare the normalized means at depth $u$. On either lattice
$\bullet\in\{\mathrm A,\mathrm B\}$, let $\Lambda_0^\bullet$
be the full unnormalized law at that depth, $\Lambda_1^\bullet$ its
small-field chain restricted to $\mathsf{In}_{[u]}$, and
$\Lambda_2^\bullet$ the chain restarted from the classical action at
depth $s$, again restricted to $\mathsf{In}_{[u]}$. We regard them as
functionals on bounded gauge-invariant Borel functions $F$ of the
depth-$u$ field. These are precisely the chain and classical-start
measures used in Props.~\YMMref{115.2}{806} and~\YMMref{116.1}{808}, with source
zero. All three functionals are positive and have strictly positive
mass. For the full law this is immediate. The chain is the image of
the nonnegative small-field weight times the bare density, by
Prop.~\YMMref{115.2}{806}. For the classical start, the initial density
is positive, the chart kernels preserve positivity, and the final
exponential density does not vanish on the open set
$\mathsf{In}_{[u]}$ containing the trivial configuration; these are
the positivity statements in the proof of Prop.~\YMMref{116.1}{808}.

We use the following elementary normalization bound. If positive
functionals $P,Q$ satisfy $P(1)>0$ and
\[
 |Q(F)-P(F)|\le\epsilon\|F\|_\infty P(1),
 \qquad0\le\epsilon\le1/2,
\]
then $Q(1)\ge(1-\epsilon)P(1)>0$, and subtraction of the two normalized
fractions gives
\[
 \left|\frac{Q(F)}{Q(1)}-\frac{P(F)}{P(1)}\right|
 \le\frac{2\epsilon}{1-\epsilon}\|F\|_\infty
 \le4\epsilon\|F\|_\infty.
\]

The discarded-mass estimate in Prop.~\YMMref{115.2}{806} gives
$0\le\Lambda_0^\bullet-\Lambda_1^\bullet$ on this algebra and
\[
 (\Lambda_0^\bullet-\Lambda_1^\bullet)(1)
            \le\mathsf R_{t_1}\Lambda_0^\bullet(1).
\]
Consequently their normalized means differ by at most
$4\mathsf R_{t_1}\|F\|_\infty$.

Forgetting the early array changes the final exponent by at most
$\epsilon_{\rm fg}$, by equation~\YMMref{2180}{803} and the definition of
$\epsilon_{\rm fg}$ above. Write the two final densities as
$p_1=e^{c^\bullet+\Phi^\bullet}$ and
$p_2=e^{\hat c^\bullet+\hat\Phi^\bullet}$ on
$\mathsf{In}_{[u]}$. Positivity gives $p_1=|p_1|$ almost everywhere
and $p_2=|p_2|>0$ there. Thus, with
$\varkappa=|e^{c^\bullet-\hat c^\bullet}|$,
\[
 \frac{p_1}{p_2}\in
 \varkappa[e^{-\epsilon_{\rm fg}},e^{\epsilon_{\rm fg}}]
 \quad\hbox{almost everywhere}.
\]
Since $\epsilon_{\rm fg}\le1/8$,
$e^{\epsilon_{\rm fg}}-1\le(5/4)\epsilon_{\rm fg}\le1/2$.
Apply the normalization bound to
$P=\varkappa\Lambda_2^\bullet$, $Q=\Lambda_1^\bullet$.
The factor $\varkappa$ cancels, and these two normalized means differ
by at most $5\epsilon_{\rm fg}\|F\|_\infty$.

The two classical starts can be written on the common depth-$s$
configuration space as $k^\bullet\hat F_0^\bullet\,\mathrm{d}W$, followed
by the same block averaging down to depth $u$. The final
total-variation estimate in the proof of Prop.~\YMMref{116.1}{808} is
\[
 \int|k^{\mathrm A}\hat F_0^{\mathrm A}
             -k^{\mathrm B}\hat F_0^{\mathrm B}|\,\mathrm{d}W
 \le(2\epsilon_{\rm cl}+3\epsilon_{\rm sh})
                           \Lambda_2^{\mathrm A}(1).
\]
We will also use the relative version of the mismatch bound. For every
bounded nonnegative gauge-invariant function $H$ of the final block field,
the proof of Prop.~\YMMref{116.1}{808} gives
\[
 \int H(\mathcal M^{s-u}W)\,k^\bullet
           \mathbf1_{\{k^\circ=0\}}\hat F_0^\bullet\,\mathrm{d}W
       \le\epsilon_{\rm sh}\Lambda_2^\bullet(H).
\]
Indeed, at a mismatching test some fluctuation of lattice $\bullet$
exceeds half its threshold. Prop.~\YMMref{114.4}{803} bounds the
marked next measure by
\[
 \exp(C_{\rm sh}-\kappa_{\rm b}\mathfrak b(x_{(k)})^2/4)
\] times the
ordinary next measure. Each later positive cut and image operation
preserves this order. Sum over at most $s-u$ steps and $3N_{[s]}$
bonds at each step, and use
$\mathfrak b(x_{(k)})^2\ge A_1^2y_{[u]}$ to obtain the displayed bound.
This proves an inequality of measures before testing against $H$.

The total-variation proof bounds separately the mass where a fluctuation
test differs and the difference of the classical action on the common cut. Inserting
$F$ in this inequality costs only $\|F\|_\infty$.
By (k3), $2\epsilon_{\rm cl}+3\epsilon_{\rm sh}\le1/4$,
so normalization gives an error
$(8\epsilon_{\rm cl}+12\epsilon_{\rm sh})\|F\|_\infty$.
Adding the five comparisons
\[
 \Lambda_0^{\mathrm A},\ \Lambda_1^{\mathrm A},\
 \Lambda_2^{\mathrm A},\ \Lambda_2^{\mathrm B},\
 \Lambda_1^{\mathrm B},\ \Lambda_0^{\mathrm B}
\]
bounds the difference of the normalized full laws by
\[
 [8\mathsf R_{t_1}+10\epsilon_{\rm fg}
                   +8\epsilon_{\rm cl}+12\epsilon_{\rm sh}]
               \|F\|_\infty\le\mathfrak o_K\|F\|_\infty.
\]
For $d\le u$, apply this to $F\circ\mathcal M^{u-d}$.
Block averaging is Borel and gauge covariant, and its maps at equal
physical depth coincide. Hence this composition remains bounded and
gauge invariant, with no increase of its supremum norm. This proves
\eqref{IV-62-67}.

For the rate, the ceiling inequalities in Thm.~\YMMref{AR}{810} give
$4u-s\le-K/10+4$ and $(7s-K)/2\le-K/9+7/2$.
Therefore
\[
 12\epsilon_{\rm fg}\le
 12C_{\rm old}C_{\rm fg}\frac L{L-1}E_0L^4\ell^3L^{-K/10},
\]
and, since $\log(L^K\mathsf b_+)\le K\log(L\mathsf b_+)$,
\[
 8\epsilon_{\rm cl}\le
 32\mathsf K_{\rm w}c_\rho^2A_0^2
 (1+2\varrho/\mathsf b_-)(\log(L\mathsf b_+))^{2\mathfrak p_0}
 L^{7/2}\ell^3K^{2\mathfrak p_0+1/2}L^{-K/9}.
\]
Their sum is at most half the right side of \eqref{IV-62-68};
the other half bounds $8\mathsf R_{t_1}+12\epsilon_{\rm sh}$
by the choice of $K_{\rm bf}$. This proves the uniform rate.

For (b), fix $d$ and let $K_*$ be the least $K\ge K_{\rm bf}$
with $\lceil K/1260\rceil\ge d$. For every invariant Borel set $E$,
apply (a) to $F=\mathbf1_E$. The resulting differences of the
probability measures are bounded by the summable sequence
$\mathfrak o_K$, since a fixed power of $K$ times $L^{-K/10}$ is
summable. Lem.~\ref{IV-62-61} gives the limit, the rate and countable
additivity. Gauge covariance makes $\mathcal M^{-1}E$ invariant,
and the exact finite-cutoff identity
\[
 \mu^K_{d+1}(\mathcal M^{-1}E)=\mu^K_d(E)
\]
passes to the limit. This proves consistency.

For (c), invariance of the Wilson density and Haar measure makes the
bare law gauge invariant. Gauge covariance of block averaging and
extension of a coarse site gauge to the fine sites give the same
invariance for $\mu^K_d$. The action $(V,v)\mapsto V^v$ is continuous,
so Fubini's theorem shows that $\bar{\mathbf1}_E$ is Borel.
Right invariance of Haar measure gives
\[
 \bar{\mathbf1}_E(V^{v'})
 =\int\mathbf1_E(V^{vv'})\,\mathrm{d}v=\bar{\mathbf1}_E(V).
\]
Integrating the invariance of $\mu^K_d$ over $v$ proves
\eqref{IV-62-71}. Now apply (a) to this function, whose values lie
in $[0,1]$. The same summable bound holds for every Borel set $E$,
so Lem.~\ref{IV-62-61} applies on the full Borel sigma-algebra.
The finite-cutoff consistency and gauge invariance pass to these
limits. For invariant $E$, $\bar{\mathbf1}_E=\mathbf1_E$, so this
extension agrees with the measure in (b).
\end{proof}


\subsubsection{Notation and hypotheses}

\emph{Notation.} All constants depend only on the basic constants (a common real choice as in Prop.~\YMMref{69.1}{595}, among them $\mathfrak p_0$, $A_0$, $M=L^{m'}$, $C_{\rm lat}$ and the last, $\gamma$) and on the arguments shown; a constant is called basic if it depends on the basic constants alone. The blocking factor $L$ is odd; $a_K=L^{-K}$, $\mathbb L_K=a_K\mathbb Z^3$; $T_\ell$ is the torus of side $\ell=2L^m$ and $\Lambda_{K,\ell}$ its lattice of spacing $a_K$; $\langle\cdot\rangle_{K,\ell,\beta}$ is Wilson's measure on $\Lambda_{K,\ell}$, $\langle\mathcal A_1;\dots;\mathcal A_n\rangle$ a cumulant, $\mathcal G_{K,\beta}$ the set of the periodic Gibbs states on $\mathbb L_K$ at $\beta$, that is, of the Gibbs states of Wilson's weight $e^{-\beta\sum_pa_p}$ that are invariant under the translations of a subgroup of finite index of $a_K\mathbb Z^3$ ({\cite[\S{}K.1]{YMM2}}); by Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{103.4}{758}} every $\nu\in\mathcal G_{K,\beta}$ is invariant under $a_K\mathbb Z^3\rtimes W_3$ and reflection positive at the lattice mirrors $\{n\cdot x=c\}$, $n\in\{e_\mu,e_\mu\pm e_\lambda\}$, of the nine families.

On $\mathbb R^3$ and on $T_\ell$, $|x|$ is the Euclidean norm and $|x|_\infty=\max_\mu|x_\mu|$ the sup norm; the balls $B(x,r)$ (open) and $\bar B(x,r)$ (closed), the distances $|x-y|$ of points and the distance $\mathrm{dist}$ of sets are Euclidean. Where sets or supports are said to be pairwise $\ge\delta$ apart, to have a diameter $\le\varrho$, or where a weight vanishes within $\delta$ of a set, the sup distance $\mathrm{dist}_\infty$ is meant, unless the Euclidean distance is named, as in Thm.~\ref{sf-coin}(a), (c). In Lems.~{\cite[Lem.~C.15]{YMM2}} and~{\cite[Lem.~C.16]{YMM2}}, in {\cite[Thm.~BV]{YMM2}}(e) and in Thm.~\ref{sf-coin}(c), (d) the separations of sets are read with the Euclidean distance $\mathrm{dist}(A,B)=\inf_{x\in A,y\in B}|x-y|$, which these statements name; the factor $1/\sqrt3$ between it and the sup distance is paid inside their proofs.

The depth at the level $k$ of the renormalisation is $s=K-k$ ({\cite[result~G.2]{YMM2}}); the depth of a distance $d$ is the least $s=s(d)\ge0$ with $L^sd\ge C_W(s)$, where $C_W(s)=c_W(\log\bar x_s)^{2\mathfrak p_0}$, $\bar x_s=L^{s+1}(g^{-2}+\bar B)$ and $c_W$ is basic; it depends on $g$, it does not decrease as $d$ falls or as $g^{-2}$ grows, and $s(d)\to\infty$ as $d\to0$; if $s(d)\ge1$, then $C_W(s)\le L^sd<LC_W(s)$ at $s=s(d)$, so that $d$ is about $C_W(s)$ units of the level of that depth, and, for $0<d<1$, $Y_{s(d)}:=\log\bar x_{s(d)}\le2\log\frac1d+C(g)$. The reference coupling $g>0$ is that of~\YMMref{74}{614}, $\mathfrak d(g)$ is the set of its first-passage data $(K,\beta)$ (\YMMref{74}{614}, \YMMref{74}{614}), $g_t$ is the running coupling at the level $t$, and $\mathsf b=a_K\beta$ is the label ({\cite[result~G.2]{YMM2}}). $B_\sharp$ bounds $|L^{-1}x_{j-1}-x_j|$ as in {\cite[\S{}G.2]{YMM2}}, $\bar B=B_\sharp L/(L-1)$, $X_g=L(g^{-2}+B_\sharp)$ as in \YMMref{(1526)}{615}, $I(g)=(g^{-2}+\bar B,X_g-\bar B]$ as in \YMMref{(1527)}{615}, and $\mathfrak L(g)=\{2L^m:m\ge m_{\mathfrak L}(g)\}$ (\YMMref{(1528)}{615}, \YMMref{(1528)}{615}) is the set of the sides at $g$, $\ell_g$ its least member.

Every $(K,\beta)\in\mathfrak d(g)$ has $g^{-2}<a_K\beta\le L(g^{-2}+\bar B)$, and $(K,L^K\mathsf b)\in\mathfrak d(g)$ for every integer $K\ge1$ if $\mathsf b\in I(g)$. (H) is the condition $0<g\le\gamma^{\rm ref}_W$, where $\gamma^{\rm sd}_W\le\gamma^{\rm ref}_W\le\gamma$ are the thresholds of the choices in equations~\YMMref{(2326)--(2327)}{845}; (T) is (H) together with $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$ and $\mathsf b\in I(g)$, and then $\langle\cdot\rangle_K:=\langle\cdot\rangle_{K,\ell,L^K\mathsf b}$.

\emph{The field.} $V=\mathrm{Sym}_3(\mathbb R)=V_A\oplus V_E\oplus V_T$, the multiples of $\mathbf 1$, the traceless diagonal matrices and the matrices with zero diagonal, is the splitting under the group $W_3$ of the $48$ signed permutation matrices; $V_{\mathbb C}=\mathrm{Sym}_3(\mathbb C)$; $E_{\lambda\lambda'}$ are the matrix units and $e_{ij}=E_{ij}+E_{ji}$. As $F_{\mu\nu}=\varepsilon_{\mu\nu\lambda}B_\lambda$ in three dimensions, the six fields are the entries of $T_{\lambda\lambda'}=\langle B_\lambda,B_{\lambda'}\rangle$. A weight is a bounded Borel function $H$ on $\mathbb R^3$ (or on $T_\ell$) with values in $V$ or $V_{\mathbb C}$ and compact support, $|H|=\sup_x\max_{\lambda\lambda'}|H_{\lambda\lambda'}(x)|$; an isometry $rx=Rx+v$ acts by $(rH)(x)=RH(r^{-1}x)R^t$, so that a reflection acts on points and on indices.

At a site $x$ the $24$ plaquette loops are $W_{x,l}$, $l=(\alpha,\alpha')$ an ordered pair of signed directions with $\alpha'\ne\pm\alpha$; $\lambda(l)$ is the normal of the plane of $l$ and $s(l)=\mathrm{sgn}\,\alpha\,\mathrm{sgn}\,\alpha'\,\varepsilon_{\lambda(l)|\alpha||\alpha'|}$ its orientation. With $w(U)=\frac{U-U^{-1}}{2i}$, $Q_x(l,l')=\frac12\mathrm{tr}\,w(W_{x,l})w(W_{x,l'})$, $a_p=1-\frac12\mathrm{tr}\,U(\partial p)$, and, for a bond $b=\langle x,x+a_Ke_\mu\rangle$ with $\lambda_b<\lambda'_b$ the two other directions, $q_b=\frac14\sum_{\epsilon,\epsilon'=\pm}\epsilon\epsilon'Q_x((\mu,\epsilon\lambda_b),(\mu,\epsilon'\lambda'_b))$, the lattice form of $\frac12\int\mathrm{tr}(HT)$ is
{\cite[eq.~1]{YMM2}}
($x(p)$, $x_b$ the midpoints, $\lambda(p)$ the normal of $p$). $O^T_K(f\mathbf 1)=\mathcal O(f)$ is the action density, and $\mathcal O_\lambda(\phi)=O^T_K(\phi E_{\lambda\lambda})=a_K^{-1}\sum_{\lambda(p)=\lambda}\phi(x(p))a_p$ are the three plane fields. $\bar O^T_K(H)$ is {\cite[eq.~1]{YMM2}} with $H(x(p))$, $H(x_b)$ replaced by the mean of $H$ over the cell $x+a_K[-\frac12,\frac12)^3$, $x$ the least corner of $p$, resp.\ of $b$. A corner field is $\mathcal Q_{l,l';\xi}(\phi)=a_K^{-1}\sum_x\phi(x+a_K\xi)Q_x(l,l')$, $|\xi|_\infty\le\frac12$; a site form is $a_K^{-1}\sum_x\sum_{l,l'}v(x;l,l')Q_x(l,l')$, of norm $\|v\|=\sup_x\sum_{l,l'}|v(x;l,l')|$; a mixed source is a pair $\mathfrak s=(w,\mathsf w)$ of real weights of the plaquettes and of the bonds, with the lattice form $\mathcal O^T(\mathfrak s)=a_K^{-1}[\sum_pw(p)a_p-\sum_b\mathsf w(b)q_b]$ and $|\mathfrak s|=\sup|w|+8\sup|\mathsf w|$. $\mathfrak S(O)$ is the set of the tuples $X=(H_1,\dots,H_n)$, $n\ge0$, of continuous weights with pairwise disjoint supports in an open set $O$, and $\mathfrak F(O)$ its complex span; $rX$, $\theta F$, $\tau_vF$ and $\bar F$ act entry by entry, $F'\cdot F$ concatenates, and $A^{\nu'}_K(X)=\prod_a[O^T_K(H_a)-\nu'(O^T_K(H_a))]$, $A^\nu[\mathcal A]=\mathcal A-\nu(\mathcal A)$. A pair at scale $d$ is a pair of real weights vanishing off closed balls $\bar B(x_0,d_-)$, $\bar B(y_0,d_-)$, $0<d_-<d$.

\emph{Free values and the stress tensor.} Let
\begin{equation}\label{sf-free}
\mathcal W(H_1,H_2)=\tfrac32\iint\mathrm{tr}[H_1(x)K_3(x-y)H_2(y)K_3(x-y)]\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y,\qquad K_3(u)=\frac{3\hat u\hat u^t-\mathbf 1}{4\pi|u|^3}.
\end{equation}
The free values are the separated connected Wick contractions, with no contraction within one insertion, as in {\cite[Thm.~V]{YMM2}}(f)(i). Use three independent colors with off-diagonal covariance $\langle B^c_\lambda(x)B^d_\mu(y)\rangle=\delta^{cd}\mathsf b^{-1}K_3(x-y)_{\lambda\mu}$ for $x\ne y$. The cumulants of the smeared bilinears formally denoted by $\frac12\int\mathrm{tr}(H_aT^{\rm free})$, $T^{\rm free}=\sum_cB^c(B^c)^t$, at separated supports are: $\mathsf b^{-2}\mathcal W(H_1,H_2)$ at two points; the kernel $3\mathsf b^{-3}k_3$, $k_3(x,y,z)=\mathrm{tr}[K_3(x-y)K_3(y-z)K_3(z-x)]$, for three action densities and $3\mathsf b^{-4}k_4$, $k_4$ the sum over the three rings $(x_{\varsigma(1)},\dots,x_{\varsigma(4)})$ of $\mathrm{tr}\prod_lK_3(x_{\varsigma(l)}-x_{\varsigma(l+1)})$, for four; and $3\mathsf b^{-n}K^{(n)}_{\underline\lambda}(\phi)$ for $n$ plane fields $\mathcal O_{\lambda_a}(\phi_a)$.
