On the lattice, $3\mathsf b^{-n}K^{(n)}_K(w_1,\dots,w_n)$ is the cumulant of the plaquette forms $a_K^{-1}\sum_pw_a(p)a_p$ for three free lattice photon fields, that is with $a_p$ replaced by $\frac12\sum_c(F^c_p)^2$, the $F^c$ independent Gaussian plaquette variables of covariance $\beta^{-1}C^{\rm free}$, $C^{\rm free}$ the free lattice covariance; likewise, for mixed sources the free lattice value of the cumulant of $\mathcal O^T(\mathfrak s_1)$, $\mathcal O^T(\mathfrak s_2)$ is the cumulant obtained when every $a_p$ and every $Q_x(l,l')$ is replaced by its quadratic part in three such independent fields; it is $\frac32\mathsf b^{-2}\mathrm{Tr}(\mathsf W_1C^{\rm free}\mathsf W_2C^{\rm free})$, $\mathsf W_a$ the symmetric matrix with $\mathcal O^T(\mathfrak s_a)=(2a_K)^{-1}\sum_cF^{c\,t}\mathsf W_aF^c$ after this replacement. $\mathsf w_0=\frac1{12}388^{-6}$.

For $\eta\in C^2_c(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ put $H^{\rm cons}[\eta]=(\nabla\cdot\eta)\mathbf 1-\nabla\eta-(\nabla\eta)^t$, $(\nabla\eta)_{ij}=\partial_i\eta_j$, and $\|\eta\|_{C^2}=\sup|\eta|+\sup|\nabla\eta|+\sup|\nabla^2\eta|$; then $\frac12\mathrm{tr}(H^{\rm cons}[\eta]T)=\sum_{ij}\partial_i\eta_j\Theta_{ij}$ with the stress tensor $\Theta_{ij}=\frac12\delta_{ij}\mathrm{tr}\,T-T_{ij}$: insertions of $H^{\rm cons}[\eta]$ express the conservation of $\Theta$, and $\frac12\mathrm{tr}(s_{ij}T)=\Theta_{ij}$ for $s_{ij}=\delta_{ij}\mathbf 1-e_{ij}$. For a unit vector $n$, $\Theta_n=\mathbf 1-2nn^t$.

\emph{Chessboards and limits.} A board of side $\mathsf l=L^{-i}$, $i\in\mathbb Z$, divides space into cubes, its cells, by bond mirrors, its walls; for $\ell'\in\mathfrak L(g)$, $\ell'\ge2\mathsf l$, and $D$ a function of the bonds of one cell, $\|D\|_{{\rm ch},\ell'}$ is the $N$-th root of $|\langle\prod_\kappa D_\kappa\rangle_{K,\ell',\beta}|$, the $D_\kappa$ being the $N=(\ell'/\mathsf l)^3$ mirror images of $D$ in the cells of $T_{\ell'}$, conjugated after an odd number of reflections as in the main chessboard convention. A Gibbs sequence at $g$ is $(K_j,\beta_j,\nu_j)$ with $(K_j,\beta_j)\in\mathfrak d(g)$, $K_j\to\infty$, $\nu_j\in\mathcal G_{K_j,\beta_j}$; a limit at $g$ is $\sigma(X)=\lim_j\nu_j(A^{\nu_j}_{K_j}(X))$, $X\in\mathfrak S(\mathbb R^3)$, along a Gibbs sequence with $a_{K_j}\beta_j\to\mathsf b$, its label.

Its trace part $\sigma_0(f_1,\dots,f_n)=\sigma(f_1\mathbf 1,\dots,f_n\mathbf 1)$ is a scalar limit, to which Thm.~\YMMref{AP}{780} (the scalar action density on $\mathbb R^3$), with Thm.~\YMMref{AL}{746} applies, with a canonical decomposition $(\mathsf X_0,\lambda_0,(\sigma_{0,\zeta})_{\zeta\in\mathsf X_0})$. With $\theta$ the reflection in $\{x_3=0\}$, $\mathcal H(\sigma)$ is the Hilbert space of the form $\langle[F'],[F]\rangle=\sigma(\theta\bar F'\cdot F)$ on $\mathfrak F(\{x_3>0\})$, and $\Omega=[\emptyset]$. More generally, let $\sigma$ have the properties of {\cite[Thm.~BV]{YMM2}}(c), as every limit at $g$ has, and let $u$ be a unit vector at which $\sigma$ is reflection positive: $\sigma(\theta_u\bar F\cdot F)\ge0$ for $F\in\mathfrak F(\{u\cdot x>0\})$, $\theta_u$ the reflection in $\{u\cdot x=0\}$, acting on points and on indices by $E\mapsto\Theta_uE\Theta_u$.

The \emph{picture of $u$} is formed in the same way: the Hilbert space $\mathcal H_u$ of the form $\langle[F'],[F]\rangle_u=\sigma(\theta_u\bar F'\cdot F)$ on $\mathfrak F(\{u\cdot x>0\})$, $\Omega_u=[\emptyset]_u$, the self-adjoint $H_u\ge0$ with $e^{-tH_u}[F]_u=[\tau_{tu}F]_u$, $t\ge0$, the unitary group $\mathcal U^u(v)[F]_u=[\tau_vF]_u$, $v\in u^\perp$, which commutes with it, and their joint spectral measure $\mathcal P_u$ on $[0,\infty)\times u^\perp$, with $e^{-tH_u}\mathcal U^u(v)=\int e^{-tE+iv\cdot q}\,\mathrm{d}\mathcal P_u(E,q)$; the picture of $e_3$ is $(\mathcal H(\sigma),H,\mathcal U,\mathcal P)$ of {\cite[Thm.~BW]{YMM2}}(a). On a torus, $\mathcal S_{n;K}(X)=\langle O^T_K(H_1);\dots;O^T_K(H_n)\rangle_K$.

\begin{theorem}[The tori]\label{sf-tori}
Assume \textup{(T)}, $n\ge2$, $d>0$, $\theta_n=1/(1260n(8n+3))$, and let the supports of $X=(H_1,\dots,H_n)$ be pairwise $\ge d$ apart.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] There are an exponent $\mathsf p$ depending only on the basic constants (one may take $\mathsf p=2\mathfrak p_0+2$), a number $C^{\rm od}$ depending only on $n$ and on the constant $C_{\rm bf}$ of the comparison of two cutoffs at the label $\mathsf b$, and a threshold $K_1$ depending besides on $g$, $\mathsf b$, $\ell$, $d$, on the threshold $K_{\rm bf}$ of that comparison and on the number $\Theta_\star$ ($C_{\rm bf}$, $K_{\rm bf}$ of Def.~\textup{\ref{IV-62-62}}(5), formed at a compact interval $J\subset I(g)$ that holds $\mathsf b$, so that they read the label only through $J$ (Cor.~\textup{\ref{IV-62-66}}(a)), $\Theta_\star$ of Section~\YMMref{113}{786}), such that for $K\ge K_1$ and Lipschitz weights
\begin{equation}\label{sf-rate}
|\mathcal S_{n;K+1}(X)-\mathcal S_{n;K}(X)|\le6^nC^{\rm od}\ell^{3(n+1)}K^{\mathsf p}L^{-\theta_nK}\prod_a(|H_a|+\mathrm{Lip}\,H_a).
\end{equation}
So $\mathcal S_n=\mathcal S^{\ell,\mathsf b}_n=\lim_K\mathcal S_{n;K}$ exists along the full sequence of cutoffs, with $|\mathcal S_{n;K}(X)-\mathcal S_n(X)|\le6^nC^{\rm od}\ell^{3(n+1)}\sum_{K'\ge K}K'^{\mathsf p}L^{-\theta_nK'}\prod_a(|H_a|+\mathrm{Lip}\,H_a)$; it is $n$-linear and symmetric, $|\mathcal S_n(X)|\le60^nK^{\rm ub}_n(g,\ell,\frac d2)\prod_a|H_a|$ with the number of Lem.~\ref{sf-sym}(b), and the centred moments converge to $\sigma^{\ell,\mathsf b}(X)=\sum_\pi\prod_{B\in\pi}\mathcal S_{|B|}(X_B)$, the sum over the partitions $\pi$ of the entries without singletons; $\sigma^{\ell,\mathsf b}(\emptyset)=1$, $\sigma^{\ell,\mathsf b}((H))=0$. With $\bar O^T_K$, \eqref{sf-rate} holds for bounded Borel weights vanishing off closed sets $\Sigma_a$ pairwise $\ge d$ apart, with $\prod_a|H_a|$ on the right and a number $C^{\rm av}$ of the same kind as $C^{\rm od}$; the limit extends $\mathcal S_n$, and in each argument $A\mapsto\mathcal S_n(\dots,1_AE,\dots)$, $E\in V$, is a countably additive measure on $\Sigma_a$ vanishing on Lebesgue null sets, so it is given by a density in $L^1(\Sigma_a;V)$.
\item[(b)] $\mathcal S_n(rX)=\mathcal S_n(X)$ for $rx=Rx+v$, $R\in W_3$, $v\in\mathbb R^3$; $\sigma^{\ell,\mathsf b}(\theta\bar F\cdot F)\ge0$ for the reflection $\theta$ in a plane $\{x_\mu=c\}$, acting on points and indices, and $F\in\mathfrak F(\{c<x_\mu<c+\frac\ell2\})$; at $H_a=f_a\mathbf 1$, $\mathcal S_n$ is the limit of the truncated functions of the action density.
\item[(c)] A class insertion over a closed set $\Sigma$ is a finite sum $\mathcal E$ of terms $\mathcal O(\phi1_\lambda)=a_K^{-1}\sum_{\lambda(p)=\lambda}\phi(x(p))a_p$ and $\mathcal Q_{l,l';\xi}(\phi)$ with real Lipschitz $\phi$ supported in $\Sigma$; its symbol $\mathrm{Sym}\,\mathcal E$ is the sum of the weights $\phi E_{\lambda\lambda}$, resp.\ $\phi\,s(l)s(l')(E_{\lambda(l)\lambda(l')}+E_{\lambda(l')\lambda(l)})$, of its terms, and $\|\mathcal E\|$ is the sum of their numbers $\sup|\phi|+\mathrm{Lip}\,\phi$. There is $C^{\rm u}$ depending only on $n,g,\ell,d$ such that for $K\ge K_1+1$ and class insertions $\mathcal E_a$, $\mathcal E'_a$ over closed sets pairwise $\ge d$ apart with $\mathrm{Sym}\,\mathcal E_a=\mathrm{Sym}\,\mathcal E'_a$,
\[|\langle\mathcal E_1;\dots;\mathcal E_n\rangle_K-\langle\mathcal E'_1;\dots;\mathcal E'_n\rangle_K|\le C^{\rm u}K^{\mathsf p}L^{-\theta_nK}\prod_a(\|\mathcal E_a\|+\|\mathcal E'_a\|),\]
and the Lipschitz numbers drop out of the bound if $\mathcal E_a$, $\mathcal E'_a$ carry the same weights at the same sites. So $\lim_K\langle\mathcal E_1;\dots;\mathcal E_n\rangle_K=\mathcal S_n(\mathrm{Sym}\,\mathcal E_1,\dots,\mathrm{Sym}\,\mathcal E_n)$: the bond form, the clover form and the single corners give one field, and $\mathrm{Sym}\,O^T_K(H)=H$.
\item[(d)] Let $(H_1,H_2)$ be a pair at scale $d<1$ with $3d\le|x_0-y_0|\le\frac\ell4$. There are a threshold $s_1(g,\ell)$ on the depth and a number $\mathsf e^T_{g,\ell}(d)$, tending to $0$ like $(\log\frac1d)^{-2\mathfrak p_0}$, such that if $s(d)\ge s_1(g,\ell)$, then for Lipschitz pairs, and for bounded ones with $\bar O^T_K$,
\begin{equation}\label{sf-two}
|\mathcal S_2(H_1,H_2)-\mathsf b^{-2}\mathcal W(H_1,H_2)|\le\mathsf e^T_{g,\ell}(d)\,\mathsf b^{-2}|H_1||H_2|,
\end{equation}
and the same holds for class insertions over the two balls, with $\mathrm{Sym}\,\mathcal E_a$ for $H_a$. At finite cutoff, for $(K,\beta)\in\mathfrak d(g)$ with $K\ge s(d)+2$ and $4a_K\le d-d_-$, and for continuous pairs, \eqref{sf-two} holds for $\langle O^T_K(H_1);O^T_K(H_2)\rangle_{K,\ell,\beta}$ with $a_K\beta$ for $\mathsf b$ and the further error $\mathsf b^{-2}[c_K|H_1||H_2|+\frac98\mathrm{rm}_K(H_1,H_2)]$, where $c_K=28000\,C_{\rm lat}(1+C_{\mathsf k})(a_K/d)^2$ with $C_{\mathsf k}$ basic, and $\mathrm{rm}_K\ge0$ depends only on $K$, $d$, the two weights and the choice of $O^T_K$ or $\bar O^T_K$, and tends to $0$ as $K\to\infty$. One may take $s_1(g,\ell)\le\hat s(g,\ell):=\max\{s_\flat(g),\lceil2\Lambda_\ell/\log L\rceil\}$, with a depth $s_\flat(g)$ depending only on $g$ and $\Lambda_\ell=(12\log\ell/(c'A_0^2))^{1/(2\mathfrak p_0)}$, $c'$ basic; from this depth on, the error of the finite-cutoff law against the lattice Wick value of {\cite[Lem.~C.10]{YMM2}} is independent of $\ell$. Further, under the same conditions on $d$:
(i) $|\mathcal S_2(rH_1,rH_2)-\mathcal S_2(H_1,H_2)|\le10\,\mathsf e^T_{g,\ell}(d)\mathsf b^{-2}|H_1||H_2|$ for $rx=x_0+R(x-x_0)$, $R\in O(3)$;
(ii) for the reflection $\theta$ in a plane $\{x_\mu=c\}$, a point $z$ at distance $\frac32d$ from it, a Lipschitz function $\phi$ with $1_{B(z,d/128)}\le\phi\le1_{B(z,d/64)}$ and $E\in V$: $\mathcal S_2(\theta(\phi E),\phi E)\ge(\mathsf w_0-\mathsf e^T_{g,\ell}(d))\mathsf b^{-2}\mathrm{tr}\,E^2$; so no non-zero real combination of the six fields vanishes.
And at every $d$: (iii) for $0<d_-<d<1$, $\frac32d\le c-x_{0,\mu}\le\frac\ell2-\frac32d$ and real Lipschitz $H$ vanishing off $\bar B(x_0,d_-)$, $0\le\mathcal S_2(\theta H,H)\le3600\,C^*_3(g,\ell)\mathsf b^{-2}|H|^2$, with $C^*_3(g,\ell)\le c_3(g)(1+\log\ell)^8e^{16\Lambda_\ell}$ independent of $d$.
\item[(e)] For $q\ge2$, $\eta\in C^2(T_\ell;\mathbb R^3)$ and Lipschitz $H_2,\dots,H_q$, the $q$ supports pairwise $\ge d$ apart: $\mathcal S_q(H^{\rm cons}[\eta],H_2,\dots,H_q)=0$, and $\sigma^{\ell,\mathsf b}((H^{\rm cons}[\eta])\cdot X')=0$ for $X'\in\mathfrak S(T_\ell)$ off $\mathrm{supp}\,\eta$. There are $C,\mathsf p,K_0$ depending only on $g,\ell,q,d$ such that for all $(K,\beta)\in\mathfrak d(g)$ with $K\ge K_0$ and all bounded $H_a$,
\[|\langle O^T_K(H^{\rm cons}[\eta]);O^T_K(H_2);\dots;O^T_K(H_q)\rangle_{K,\ell,\beta}|\le CK^{\mathsf p}L^{-K/56}\|\eta\|_{C^2}\prod_{a\ge2}|H_a|,\]
also with $\bar O^T_K$; the bound is uniform in the label, and it stays true, with another $C$, if $O^T_K(H^{\rm cons}[\eta])$ is changed by a site form plus a plaquette form, carried within $2a_K$ of $\mathrm{supp}\,\eta$, whose weights are at most $36a_K\|\eta\|_{C^2}$. At $H_a=h_a\mathbf 1$ this is the conservation of the stress tensor among action densities.
\item[(f)] The numbers $\mathsf p$, $C^{\rm od}$, $C^{\rm av}$ and $K_1$ of (a) may be taken the same at all the labels of a compact interval $J\subset I(g)$ (Lem.~\ref{sf-cut}(b)), and $\mathsf b\mapsto\mathcal S^{\ell,\mathsf b}_n(X)$ is continuous on $I(g)$. For Lipschitz weights, and for bounded ones with $\bar O^T_K$: if $\mathsf b$ is an inner point of $I(g)$ and $a_K\beta_K\to\mathsf b$, then $\langle O^T_K(H_1);\dots;O^T_K(H_n)\rangle_{K,\ell,\beta_K}\to\mathcal S^{\ell,\mathsf b}_n(X)$ along the full sequence of cutoffs.
\end{enumerate}
By {\cite[Lem.~C.8]{YMM2}}, (a)--(f) hold on every torus of side $2L^m$, $m\ge0$, and at every label $\mathsf b>0$, with the constants of a triple $(g',L^z\mathsf b,L^z\ell)$ with \textup{(T)}, taken at the distance $L^zd$, and powers of $L^z$; for large $z$ one may take $g'=(L^z\mathsf b/2)^{-1/2}$, and then $L^z\mathsf b$ is an inner point of $I(g')$.
\end{theorem}

\paragraph{The remaining estimate for overlapping sources.}\label{sf-overlap-input}
In the setting \textup{(T)}, consider the source derivatives of the step maps on their admitted analytic domains, with the weighted local-family norms and source sizes of the construction. For two bond forms $Y_a,Y_b$ whose weights overlap, one still needs to show that the derivative of order two created at depth $u$ decomposes into a local part $\mathfrak l$ of norm at most $cL^u$ and a remainder of norm at most $cK^{\mathsf p}L^{u/2}$, in the units of the two source sizes. The local part vanishes at the trivial background. At the real background $U_{u'}$ of a small block field of a coarser level, of depth $u'\le u$, one also needs the evaluated sum estimate
\[
 \left|\sum_{X,z}\mathfrak l(X,U_{u'},z)\right|
 \le K^{\mathsf p}\mathsf b^{-2}N L^{-2(u-u')},
\]
where the sum runs over every polymer and base point and $N$ is the number of sites of that coarser level. The family-norm bounds on the decomposition hold on the admitted analytic domains; the last estimate is required at these real backgrounds. The constants may depend on the number of derivatives, the fixed torus and a compact label interval, but not on the cutoff or the depths. The sources in the overlapping cases are the off-diagonal bond forms in clause \textup{(b)} below.


The cancellation behind the evaluated sum estimate concerns the linear parts of the two insertions in the fluctuation field. If these parts have coefficient vectors $r_a,r_b$, their pairing through the fluctuation covariance $C_u$ satisfies
\[
 |\langle r_a,C_ur_b\rangle|
 \le \|C_u\|_{2\to2}\|r_a\|_2\|r_b\|_2.
\]
Thus a uniform covariance bound and the estimates
\[
 \|r_a\|_2^2\le CK^{\mathsf p}\mathsf b^{-2}N
 L^{-2(u-u')}\|\phi_a\|_\sharp^2
\]
give the required estimate, after absorbing fixed constants and the two source sizes. The proposed gain comes from writing the linear curvature response as a discrete curl and summing by parts: a difference then falls on the product of the weight and the background curvature. Over one lattice spacing at depth $u$, the local gauge bounds at depth $u'$ give the factor $L^{-(u-u')}$ in the $L^2$ norm, whose square gives the displayed gain. To complete this argument for the actual off-diagonal step insertions, one still needs the quantitative decomposition above and the identification and bounds of its linear coefficient vectors, including the remaining nonlinear terms. These are the additional input here; the local gauge estimate and the step-map Cauchy estimate alone do not supply that identification.

\begin{theorem}[Coinciding points, overlapping insertions, more points]\label{sf-coin}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[beginpenalty=10000]
\item[(a)] Assume \textup{(H)}, $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$, $(K,\beta)\in\mathfrak d(g)$, $0<d<1$ and $s_{\rm th}(n,g)\le s(d)\le K$, $s_{\rm th}$ a threshold depth depending on $n$ and $g$. For complex weights whose supports lie within the Euclidean distance $0.87d$ of points $x_a$ and are at pairwise Euclidean distances $\ge1.26d$, with no bound on their mutual distances,
\[|\langle O^T_K(H_1);\dots;O^T_K(H_n)\rangle_{K,\ell,\beta}|\le60^nC_n(g,\ell)\big[2\log\tfrac1d+C(g)\big]^{8n\mathfrak p_0}\mathsf b^{-n}\prod_a|H_a|:\]
the power counting $d^{-3}$ of an entry, the dimension of $\mathrm{tr}\,FF$, up to logarithms. On a side that is small over the canonical sequence of $(K,\beta)$ (equation~\YMMref{(2312)}{841}), for $g\le\gamma^{\rm sd}_W$ the least side $\ell_g$ (Lem.~\YMMref{126.3}{846}), the number $C_n(g,\ell)$ is free of $\ell$; on every other $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$ it carries the factor $\max\{1,\mathsf c(\ell)\}^n$, $\mathsf c(\ell)=2\ell^3e^{\mathsf B(\bar x_0)\ell^3}/(c'A_0^2)$, with the function $\mathsf B$ and the number $c'$ of equation~\YMMref{(2311)}{841}. Read at the reference coupling $\gamma^{\rm sd}_W$ after a dilation, the bound takes a scale-covariant form: let $\delta_\star=[L((\gamma^{\rm sd}_W)^{-2}+\bar B)]^{-1}$ and $\beta>X_{\gamma^{\rm sd}_W}$, let $z\in\mathbb Z$ be fixed by the first-passage window of $\beta$ at $\gamma^{\rm sd}_W$, so that $\delta_\star\mathsf b\le L^{-z}<(\gamma^{\rm sd}_W)^2\mathsf b$, and let $L^z\ell$ be the least side at $\gamma^{\rm sd}_W$; then for every $d<\delta_\star\mathsf b$ with $s_{\rm th}(n,\gamma^{\rm sd}_W)\le s(L^zd)\le K-z$, the depth and the threshold being formed at $\gamma^{\rm sd}_W$, the bound holds with $[2\log\frac{\mathsf b}d+C]^{8n\mathfrak p_0}$ in the place of $[2\log\frac1d+C(g)]^{8n\mathfrak p_0}$ and numbers depending only on $n$ and the basic constants, and this statement is invariant under $(K,\ell,\mathsf b,d)\mapsto(K-1,L\ell,L\mathsf b,Ld)$.

For supports only at pairwise Euclidean distances $\ge d$ the bound holds at $d''=\min\{\frac34d,L^{-s_{\rm th}(n,g)}\}$, for $K\ge s(d'')$, with $\sum_Q\sup_Q|H_a|$ in the place of $|H_a|$ and $\mathsf b^{-n}$ kept, $Q$ running through the boxes of a partition of $T_\ell$ into at most $(2\ell/d'')^3$ boxes of sides $\le\frac{99}{100}d''$: each box lies within the Euclidean distance $0.87d''$ of its centre and pieces of two weights are at Euclidean distances $\ge d\ge1.26d''$, so every product of the pieces $H_a\mathbf 1_Q$ has the geometry of the first display at $d''$. In the amalgam norm $d''^3\sum_Q\sup_Q|H_a|$ this is the bound with $\mathsf bd''^3$ in the place of $\mathsf b$: the power $d^{-3}$ of an entry.

At $n=2$ and for $g\le\gamma^{\rm sd}_W$ the off-diagonal components need no logarithm and no number of the side: for every $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$, $(K,\beta)\in\mathfrak d(g)$, $h>0$ with $1.31h<1$ and $s(1.31h)\le K$, and complex weights $\mathsf w_1,\mathsf w_2$ of the bonds with $x_b$ in closed cubes $Q_1,Q_2$ of side $\frac32h$ at a sup distance $\ge\frac52h$ wherever $\mathsf w_i(b)\ne0$, no bound being asked on the distance of the cubes, the bond forms $Y_i=a_K^{-1}\sum_b\mathsf w_i(b)q_b$ have $|\langle Y_1;Y_2\rangle_{K,\ell,\beta}|\le36\,C_\infty(g)\,\mathsf b^{-2}\sup|\mathsf w_1|\sup|\mathsf w_2|$, with the number $C_\infty(g)$ of {\cite[Lem.~C.7]{YMM2}}, which depends on $g$ alone; so the off-diagonal part of $\mathcal S^{\ell,\mathsf b}_2$ has the power counting of {\cite[Prop.~C.22]{YMM2}} with $q=0$ and a number $A$ free of $\ell$.

The bound passes to $\mathcal S^{\ell,\mathsf b}_n$ for weights vanishing off closed sets in balls of radius $0.86d$ at pairwise Euclidean distances $\ge1.27d$, with a number depending on $\ell$. So $\mathcal S^{\ell,\mathsf b}_n$ has the power counting of {\cite[Prop.~C.22]{YMM2}} with $q=8n\mathfrak p_0$, a number $A=A_n(g,\ell)\mathsf b^{-n}$ and $h_0\in\ell2^{-\mathbb N}$ with $h_0\le\min\{\frac\ell{64n},\frac12L^{-s_{\rm th}(n,g)}\}$: it extends over all the diagonals to a distribution $\tilde{\mathcal S}_n$ of order $\le3n-2$ with the same power counting and one more logarithm. The lattice functionals $\tilde u_K$ formed from the cumulants at the cutoff $K$ with the subtractions of {\cite[Prop.~C.22]{YMM2}}, the sum running over the products of Whitney cubes of the sides $h$ with $s(1.52h)\le K$ alone, obey $|\tilde u_K(F)|\le C_EA\,\mathfrak l(\lambda)^{8n\mathfrak p_0+1}\|F\|_{(\lambda),3n-2}$, one number for all $K$, for $8h_K\le\lambda\le h_0$, $h_K\le2C_W(K)a_K$ the least side admitted at the cutoff $K$, and every $F$ supported in a product of closed cubes of side $2\lambda$, wherever their centres lie; and $\tilde u_K(F)\to\tilde{\mathcal S}_n(F)$ for every smooth $F$.

Within this power counting the extension is unique exactly up to the sums $\sum_{\pi,\alpha}\partial^\alpha\delta_\pi\otimes T_{\pi,\alpha}$ over the partitions $\pi$ into at most $n-1$ blocks and $|\alpha|\le3|\pi|$. At two points the real, exchange-symmetric, translation-invariant contact terms in $\mathfrak E_2(0)$ form a twelve-dimensional space under $W_3$ on $\mathbb R^3$ or $T_\ell$, and a six-dimensional space under $O(3)$ on $\mathbb R^3$, by Lem.~\ref{C-355-34}(f). $\mathcal S_2$ is no measure across the diagonal.
\item[(b)] The convergence rates in this clause remain targets until the actual step insertions satisfy the overlapping-source estimates described in \S\ref{sf-overlap-input}. Under \textup{(T)} let $r\ge2$ tensor entries $O^T_K(\phi_aE_a)$, $E_a\in V$, and $n$ action densities $\mathcal O(f_i)$ be given, all with Lipschitz weights, and let $d>0$. Their joint cumulants $\kappa_K$ converge as $K\to\infty$ at a rate: $|\kappa_{K+1}-\kappa_K|\le CK^{\mathsf p}L^{-cK}\prod_a\|\phi_a\|_\sharp|E_a|\prod_i\|f_i\|_\sharp$ in the norms $\|\phi\|_\sharp=\max\{\sup|\phi|,40M\,\mathrm{Lip}\,\phi\}$, $|E|$ the largest modulus of the entries of $E$, for $K$ beyond a threshold, with $C,\mathsf p$ depending on $r$, $n$, $\ell$ and a compact interval of labels about $\mathsf b$ and the threshold depending besides on the geometry of the supports (on $d$ in the cases where $d$ is named), in the following cases:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]

\item $c=\frac1{120r}$ also if $\phi_a\phi_b=0$ for $a\ne b$, the tensor weights not overlapping (their supports may touch), provided that of any $r+n$ points, one from each support, the supports of the $f_i$ included, two are $\ge d$ apart, so that no point is common to all the supports (at $n=0$ the numbers $C,\mathsf p$ depend on $d$ as well)
\item $c=\frac1{360r}$ for off-diagonal $E_a$, $r\ge3$, if no three tensor supports share a point, nothing being asked of the $f_i$
\item $c=\frac1{864}$ for $r=2$, off-diagonal $E_a$ and $n\ge1$, the two tensor supports overlapping at will, if of any $n+2$ points, one from each support, two are $\ge d$ apart.

\item[(c)] The arbitrary-order interacting conclusion remains a target.
It requires the remainder estimate described in
\S\ref{hyp:quantitative-torus}, with its real plaquette weights,
first-creation bound, numerical ranges and error $\mathsf e_n$.
Keep $36d<\ell$. The cyclic formula is exact for three free lattice
photon fields; the corresponding interacting conclusion is the following.
For the plane fields, with real Lipschitz $\phi_a$ in the open balls $B(x_a,d)$, these in a ball of radius $\le\frac\ell4$, $\mathrm{Lip}\,\phi_a\le|\phi_a|/(\vartheta_0d)$ and $|x'-y'|\ge d$ for $x'\in\mathrm{supp}\,\phi_a$, $y'\in\mathrm{supp}\,\phi_b$, $a\ne b$ (Euclidean distances, as for the $w_a$): $|\langle\mathcal O_{\lambda_1}(\phi_1);\dots;\mathcal O_{\lambda_n}(\phi_n)\rangle_{K,\ell,\beta}-3\mathsf b^{-n}K^{(n)}_{\underline\lambda}(\phi)|\le[\mathsf e_n+C_n(\frac{a_K}{\vartheta_0d}+\frac{d^3}{\ell^3})]\mathsf b^{-n}\prod_a|\phi_a|$, $C_n=\frac32n![6^nC_{\rm lat}(1+3C_{\rm lat})^{n-1}+43\cdot11^n]$; the same with $3^nC_n$ for real combinations $\sum_\lambda k_{a,\lambda}\mathcal O_\lambda(\phi_a)$, $k_a\in[-1,1]^3$, among them the diagonal entries $\mathcal O(\phi)-2\mathcal O_m(\phi)=O^T_K(\phi s_{mm})$ of the stress tensor.

For $2\le n\le7$ and $g\le\min\{\gamma_n,\gamma^{\rm sd}_W\}$, with $d$ below a threshold depending on $n$ and $g$ and the balls $B(x_a,d)$ in one ball of radius $9d$, the lattice inequality in \S\ref{hyp:quantitative-torus}, with $\mathcal K^{(n)}_K$ formed on $T_{\ell_g}$ and with $\varepsilon^{\rm rt}_n(g,d)$ of {\cite[Lem.~C.16]{YMM2}}\textup{(a)} added to $\mathsf e_n$, holds also in every periodic Gibbs state and on every torus of $\mathfrak L(g)$; $\varepsilon^{\rm rt}_n(g,d)$ tends to $0$ with $d$ like a positive power of $d$ times a power of $\log\frac1d$.
\item[(d)] Let $g$ be below a basic threshold. On $T_{\ell_g}$ almost everywhere, and for every limit at $g$ and every re-centred component at every such triple of points, the kernel $s_3$ of three action densities obeys
\[
\begin{multlined}
|s_3-3\mathsf b^{-3}k_3|\le\varepsilon_A(g,d)\,\mathsf b^{-3}r^{-3}d^{-6}\quad\text{for }0<|x-y|=r\le d=\mathrm{dist}(z,\{x,y\})\le d_A(g), \\
\varepsilon_A\le C(g)\Big[\big(\log\tfrac1d\big)^{39\mathfrak p_0+2}d^{1/2}+\Big(\frac d{\ell_g}\Big)^3\Big],

uniformly in $\frac rd\in(0,1]$, $d_A(g)>0$ depending on $g$. At a cutoff the same law holds for narrow weights, in every periodic Gibbs state and on $T_{\ell_g}$: for real plaquette weights $w_1,w_2,w_3$ carried by sets $S_a\subset B(x_a,\rho)$ with $\mathrm{dist}(S_1,S_2)\ge r$, $|x_1-x_2|\le8r$, $\mathrm{dist}(S_a,S_3)\ge d$ and $|x_a-x_3|\le18d$ for $a=1,2$, where $0<\rho\le r\le d$, $d$ below a threshold depending on $g$, and $s(\rho)\le K$ (the geometry of {\cite[Lem.~C.15]{YMM2}}(c)), the third cumulant of the forms $a_K^{-1}\sum_pw_a(p)a_p$ is $3\mathsf b^{-3}K^{(3)}_K(w_1,w_2,w_3)$ up to $[C(g)Y^{39\mathfrak p_0+2}d^{1/2}+C(g)d^{3/2}]\rho^9r^{-3}d^{-6}\mathsf b^{-3}\prod_a|w_a|$, $Y=\log\bar x_{s(d)}$; for Lipschitz bumps $w_a=f_a\circ x$ with $\mathrm{Lip}\,f_a\le|f_a|/(\vartheta\rho)$, $0<\vartheta\le1$, the same holds against $3\mathsf b^{-3}\int k_3\prod_af_a$ with $C(g)(\frac{a_K}{\vartheta\rho}+(\frac d{\ell_g})^3)$ more in the bracket. Four action densities at two scales are free in the same sense, on the torus and at a cutoff: on $T_{\ell_g}$, for $r\le|x_1-x_2|,|x_3-x_4|\le2r$ and $r\le d=\mathrm{dist}(\{x_1,x_2\},\{x_3,x_4\})\le d'_A(g)$, the kernel $s_4$ of the truncated four-point function of the action density has $|s_4-3\mathsf b^{-4}k_4|\le\varepsilon_4(g,d)\mathsf b^{-4}r^{-6}d^{-6}$ almost everywhere, $\varepsilon_4\le C(g)[(\log\frac1d)^{47\mathfrak p_0+2}d^{1/2}+(\frac d{\ell_g})^3]$, uniformly in $\frac rd\in(0,1]$; and at a cutoff, in every periodic Gibbs state and on $T_{\ell_g}$, for real plaquette weights $w_1,\dots,w_4$ in two such narrow pairs $\{1,2\}$, $\{3,4\}$, with $\mathrm{dist}(S_3,S_4)\ge r$, $|x_3-x_4|\le8r$, $\mathrm{dist}(S_a,S_b)\ge d$ and $|x_a-x_b|\le18d$ for $a\le2<b$, $d$ below a threshold depending on $g$, the fourth cumulant of the plaquette forms is $3\mathsf b^{-4}K^{(4)}_K(w_1,\dots,w_4)$ up to $[C(g)Y^{47\mathfrak p_0+2}d^{1/2}+C(g)d^{3/2}]\rho^{12}r^{-6}d^{-6}\mathsf b^{-4}\prod_a|w_a|$.

\begin{corollary}[A tensor against the action density]\label{sf-ode}
Let $\sigma$ be a limit at $g$ under \textup{(H)}, or a re-centred component $\sigma^c_\xi$. There are real-analytic functions $A,B$ on $(0,\infty)$ with $s_2(x,y;e,\mathbf 1)=\mathrm{tr}\big(e\,[A(r)\mathbf 1+B(r)\hat u\hat u^t]\big)$, $u=x-y$, $r=|u|$, for all $e\in V$; $F=3A+B$ is the kernel of two action densities, and
\[B'(r)+\frac3rB(r)=\frac14F'(r),\qquad\text{so}\qquad B(r)=r^{-3}\Big(c+\frac14\int_1^rt^3F'(t)\,\mathrm{d}t\Big)\]
for one real number $c$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{lemma}[Exact symmetries; separated insertions]\label{sf-sym}
\textup{(a)} Let $rx=Rx+v$, with $R\in W_3$, $Re_\mu=s_\mu e_{\pi(\mu)}$, and $v\in a_K\mathbb Z^3$, act on configurations by moving the bonds. Then $rO^T_K(H)=O^T_K(rH)$ for every complex weight, on $\Lambda_{K,\ell}$ and on $\mathbb L_K$; in components $ra_p=a_{rp}$ and $rq_b=s_{\lambda_b}s_{\lambda'_b}q_{rb}$. Under a law $\nu$ invariant under these maps, as the torus measures and the periodic Gibbs states are (Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{103.4}{758}}), $\nu(q_b)=0$ and $\nu(a_p)=e_\nu$ does not depend on $p$, so that $\nu(O^T_K(H))=e_\nu a_K^{-1}\sum_pH_{\lambda(p)\lambda(p)}(x(p))$: the off-diagonal components need no subtraction; moments and cumulants are invariant. $O^T_K(H)$ depends only on the bonds within $a_K$ of a point where $H\ne0$.

\textup{(b)} Assume \textup{(H)}, $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$, $q\ge2$, $\delta>0$. In the calculus of sources of Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8} let $C_{(m)}$, $m\ge1$, be the numbers, depending only on $m$, with which the mixed derivative families of order $m$ of a source system under majorants are bounded at the level $t$ by $C_{(m)}L^{4m(T-t)}$ times the product of the sizes of the sources, $T$ the working level; put $K_r=\sum_{\pi}\prod_{B\in\pi}C_{(|B|)}$, the sum over the partitions of $\{1,\dots,r\}$; and let $h_q(s)$ be the largest left member, at the depth $s$, of the smallness conditions that this calculus asks of the families of the orders $2,\dots,q$ for majorants at least $3M$ units of the working level apart, a function of the depth depending only on $q$ and $g$ and tending to $0$ as $s\to\infty$.

Let $s_q(\delta)$ be the least $s\ge0$ with $L^s\delta\ge3M$ and $h_q(s)\le1$; at $s=s_q(\delta)$ put $M_r=K_r[1+L^{4r}V_\ell(4q)L^{-(4q+1)s}]$, where $V_\ell(b)=4M^{-3}\ell^3e^{\mathsf B(X_g)\ell^3}\mathsf C_{\rm ag}(b+1,\eth)$, with the function $\mathsf B$ and the number $\mathsf C_{\rm ag}$ of equation~\eqref{eq:ward-volume-constants} at a fixed $\eth\in(0,1)$, so that $K_rL^{4r}V_\ell(b)L^{-(b+1)s}$, $b\ge4r$, bounds, in units of the sizes, the part of a centred mean of $r$ first members that is carried by the histories in which a large field is created below the working level (Prop.~\ref{prop:ward-fixed-volume-rarity}); and
\[K^{\rm ub}_q(g,\ell,\delta)=(4\ell^3L^{4s})^q\sum_\pi(|\pi|-1)!\prod_{B\in\pi}M_{|B|},\]
the sum over all partitions of $\{1,\dots,q\}$. Let $(K,\beta)\in\mathfrak d(g)$ with $K\ge s_q(\delta)+2$ and $3a_K\le\delta$, and let each $\mathcal F_a$ be one of: $O^T_K(H_a)$ or $\bar O^T_K(H_a)$ with $H_a$ vanishing off a closed set $\Sigma_a$ (size $\mathsf s_a=60|H_a|$); a site form with weights at the sites within $\frac12a_K$ of $\Sigma_a$ (size $23\|v_a\|$); $\mathcal O(w_a)$ with $w_a(p)=0$ unless $x(p)$ is within $a_K$ of $\Sigma_a$ (size $|w_a|$); or a sum of two of these (the sum of the sizes); the $\Sigma_a$ being pairwise $\ge2\delta$ apart. Then
\[|\langle\mathcal F_1;\dots;\mathcal F_q\rangle_{K,\ell,\beta}|\le K^{\rm ub}_q(g,\ell,\delta)\prod_a\mathsf s_a.\]
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(a) $\mathrm{tr}\,U^{-1}=\mathrm{tr}\,U$ on $SU(2)$ gives $ra_p=a_{rp}$, and $w(U^{-1})=-w(U)$ gives the signs in $rq_b$; inserted into {\cite[eq.~1]{YMM2}} they give $rO^T_K(H)=O^T_K(rH)$, as $(rH)_{\pi\lambda,\pi\lambda'}(rx)=s_\lambda s_{\lambda'}H_{\lambda\lambda'}(x)$. The reflection through $b$ normal to $\lambda_b$ lies in the group, fixes $b$ and reverses $q_b$; the group is transitive on the plaquettes. (b) By {\cite[Lem.~C.4]{YMM2}} each $\mathcal F_a$ is the first member of a source, in the calculus of Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8}, under the majorant made of its size and of the plaquettes of its form (for $O^T_K(H)$ the size is $1+59$, for its plaquette and its bond part), and so, the notion being monotone in the majorant, under the majorant made of its size and of the plaquettes whose corners lie within $\frac32a_K$ of $\Sigma_a$; as $3a_K\le\delta$, corners of plaquettes of different majorants are $\ge\delta$ apart. At the depth $s=s_q(\delta)$, $L^s\delta$ exceeds the range of the block terms, and the mean of a centred product of $r$ first members is at most $M_r\prod_a4\ell^3L^{4s}\mathsf s_a$, up to constants common to all the subproducts, which cancel in cumulants; the M\"obius formula for cumulants gives $K^{\rm ub}_q$; the number grows with $\ell$ and as $\delta\to0$, since only the sizes of the sources enter.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Two successive cutoffs]\label{sf-cut}
Assume \textup{(T)}. An entry is one of $\mathcal O(w)$, $\mathcal O(w1_\lambda)$, 
\[
a_K^{-1}\sum_{b\parallel\mu}w(x_b)q_b
\]
 and $\mathcal Q_{l,l';\xi}(w)$, with a real function $w$ read at every cutoff at the barycentres of the plaquettes, at the midpoints of the bonds, resp.\ at the shifted sites.
\textup{(a)} \eqref{sf-rate} holds for $n$ entries with supports pairwise $\ge d$ apart, without the factor $6^n$ and with $|w_a|$ for $|H_a|$; and for entries whose weights are the cell means of bounded Borel functions, with $\prod_a|w_a|$ on the right.
\textup{(b)} Every compact interval $J\subset I(g)$ is an interval of labels under (Tor) on every side $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$ (\S\ref{sec:cutoff-calibration}): its labels exceed $g^{-2}\ge\gamma^{-2}$, and $MR(x)\le L^{m_{\mathfrak L}(g)-1}$ for $x\le L(g^{-2}+\bar B)$ by \YMMref{(1528)}{615}. With $C_{\rm bf}$ and $K_{\rm bf}$ formed at $J$ (Def.~\textup{\ref{IV-62-62}}(5)), which serve the comparison of Cor.~\textup{\ref{IV-62-66}}(a) at every label of $J$, the numbers $\mathsf p$, $C^{\rm od}$ and $C^{\rm av}$ of Thm.~\ref{sf-tori}(a) serve all labels of $J$, and so does $K_1$, formed with $K_{\rm bf}$ of $J$ and at the least label of $J$.
\textup{(c)} Let $(t,\varepsilon_r,V)$ be data of the comparison of the cutoffs $K$ and $K+1$ (the setting preceding Lem.~\YMMref{113.8}{794}): a level $1\le t\le K$ of the cutoff $K$ with $L^{K-t}\mathsf b\ge\Theta_\star$, the radius 
\[
\varepsilon_r=2c_\rho\varepsilon(L^{K-t}\mathsf b)
\]
 of that Definition, and a block field $V$ of the depth $K-t$ with $\varpi(V)<\varepsilon_r$; let $U^A$ and $U^B$ be its backgrounds at the level $t$ of the cutoff $K$ and at the level $t+1$ of the cutoff $K+1$, and $\eta_t=L^{-t}$, $N_t=\ell^3L^{3(K-t)}$. The \emph{corner form} of a weight $v$ on the sites and of loops $l,l'$ at a configuration $U$ of a lattice is $\eta^{-1}\sum_xv(x)Q_x(l,l')(U)$, with $\eta=\eta_{t+1}$ on $\Lambda_{K+1,\ell}$ at $U^B$ and $\eta=\eta_t$ on $\Lambda_{K,\ell}$ at $\mathcal MU^B$ and at $U^A$; as $a_K^{-1}=L^{K-t}\eta_t^{-1}$ and 
\[
a_{K+1}^{-1}=L^{K-t}\eta_{t+1}^{-1},
\]
an entry is $L^{K-t}$ times a corner form, and $L^{K-t}N_t=\ell^3L^{4(K-t)}$ gives the factor $L^{4\sigma}$ below, $\sigma=K-t$. $B_3$ is the fixed background regularity constant of Thm.~\YMMref{E}{10}; its bound at these data is $B_3\varepsilon_r$, as used in the comparison preceding Lem.~\YMMref{113.8}{794}. For loops $l,l'$ and $l_1,l'_1$ in the same planes and complex $v$ on the sites,
\[\Big|\eta_{t+1}^{-1}\sum_xv(x)\big[s(l)s(l')Q_x(l,l')-s(l_1)s(l'_1)Q_x(l_1,l'_1)\big](U^B)\Big|\le2K^{\rm cf}_0\sup|v|\,\varepsilon_r^2N_tL^{-t/2},\]
$K^{\rm cf}_0$ basic: at a background the corner forms depend, in the mean, on their planes and signs alone.
\textup{(d)} Let $U^A$ be the background of the coarser lattice and $\mathcal MU^B$ the block average of $U^B$. For weights $v_f$, $v_c$ on the sites of the fine and of the coarse lattice, with $v_{\max}=\max\{\sup|v_f|,\sup|v_c|\}$ and the mismatch $m=\max_y|L^{-3}\sum_{x\in B(y)}v_f(x)-v_c(y)|$, $B(y)$ the block of $y$:
\[\Big|\eta_{t+1}^{-1}\sum_xv_f(x)Q_x(l,l')(U^B)-\eta_t^{-1}\sum_yv_c(y)Q_y(l,l')(\mathcal MU^B)\Big|\le\big[4B_3^2m+K^{\rm cf}_0v_{\max}L^{-t/2}\big]\varepsilon_r^2N_t;\]
and $\mathcal MU^B$, a nearly minimal competitor at the level $t$, has $|\eta_t^{-1}\sum_xv(x)[Q_x(l,l')(\mathcal MU^B)-Q_x(l,l')(U^A)]|\le12\sup|v|\,(C\,t\,A\,\Delta A)^{1/2}$, $A$ its action and $\Delta A$ its excess. So an entry with a Lipschitz weight, read at the two cutoffs, changes over one block field of depth $\sigma$ by at most $C\ell^3L^{4\sigma}K^{1/2}L^{-(K-\sigma)/2}(\sup|w|+L^{-\sigma}\mathrm{Lip}\,w)$, and an entry whose weights at the two cutoffs are tied by the block mean by the same with $\sup|w|$ alone.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(a) The entries are first members of sources under majorants ({\cite[Lem.~C.4]{YMM2}}), of the sizes $\sup|w|$, $59\sup|w|$, resp.\ $23\sup|w|$, and the corners of the plaquettes of two majorants are $\ge d-3a_K\ge d'=\frac d2$ apart. \emph{First link, at one cutoff.} By Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8} a source system of $n$ members is carried by its first members read at the backgrounds of the block field of a depth $\sigma$ up to the error
\[2\mathfrak K'_n\big[2L^{4n}V_\ell(b)L^{-(b+1)s}+n\,\epsilon_{\rm fg}(\sigma-s)+2e^{3-L^sd'/M}\big](4\ell^3L^{4s})^n\prod_a\mathsf s_a\]
at a second depth $s<\sigma$, for every real $b\ge4n$, with $V_\ell$ and $M_r$ of Lem.~\ref{sf-sym}(b) formed at the depth $s$ and $\mathfrak K'_n=\sum_\pi|\pi|!\prod_{B\in\pi}M_{|B|}$: the first term is carried by the histories in which a large field is created below the working level of the depth $s$ (Prop.~\ref{prop:ward-fixed-volume-rarity}); the second is the forgetting of what the members of the sources make below the level $K-\sigma$, $\epsilon_{\rm fg}(\nu)=C_{\rm fg}(\nu+1)^{2\mathfrak p_0+2}L^{-\nu/2}$ with $C_{\rm fg}$ basic; the third is the decay over the distance $d'$ in the units of the working level; no number of it reads $K$ or $\beta$. \emph{Second link, between the cutoffs.} The laws of the block field of the depth $\sigma$ at the cutoffs $K$ and $K+1$ differ in total variation by at most $C_{\rm bf}\ell^3K^{\mathsf p_0}L^{-K/10}$, $\mathsf p_0=2\mathfrak p_0+\frac12$ the exponent of Def.~\textup{\ref{IV-62-62}}(5) (Cor.~\textup{\ref{IV-62-66}}(a)); over one block field an entry read at the two backgrounds changes by the defect of (d); and a first member read at a background is at most $\frac32B_3^2\ell^3L^{4\sigma}$ times its size.

With $\sigma=\lfloor K/(1260n)\rfloor$, $s=\lfloor\sigma/(8n+3)\rfloor$ and $b=4n+1$ the three errors are at most $L^2L^{-\theta_nK}$, $L^{-K/3}$ and $L^{-K/11}$ times the sizes, up to powers of $K$ and of $\ell$: the first as $\sigma-s\ge(8n+2)s$ makes each term of the bracket at most a power of $K$ times $L^{-(4n+1)s}$, and $L^{-s}\le L^2L^{-\theta_nK}$; the second as $L^{4n\sigma}L^{-(K-\sigma)/2}\le L^{-K/3}$; the third as $L^{4n\sigma}L^{-K/10}\le L^{-K/11}$: this is $\theta_n$. A Lipschitz weight read at the points of two lattices has the mismatch $m\le\frac32a_K\mathrm{Lip}\,w$, whence the term $L^{-\sigma}\mathrm{Lip}\,w$; cell means have $m=0$, as the cell of a coarse site is the union of the cells of the sites of its block, whence sup norms. (b) The first link reads the label only through the data of the depth $s$ of $(K,L^K\mathsf b)$, whose numbers are uniform on the compact $J$, the numbers of its error being free of the label.

Otherwise the label enters the proof of (a) only through $C_{\rm bf}$ and $K_{\rm bf}$, which depend on it only through $J$ (Cor.~\textup{\ref{IV-62-66}}(a)), through the condition $L^\sigma\mathsf b\ge\Theta_\star$ of the data of the comparison at the depth $\sigma$, which holds at every label of $J$ once it holds at the least one, and through the radius $\varepsilon_r$ of the backgrounds, which the calibration conditions in equation~\YMMref{(2148)}{794} bound at the levels where $L^\sigma\mathsf b\ge\Theta_\star$, and of which the defects of (c), (d) read only $\varepsilon_r\le1$. (c) Over a block, in a suitable gauge, each loop at the background is $\pm$ one plaquette variable of the block, depending only on the plane of the loop, up to $O(\varpi^2)$, $\varpi$ the size of the background; the variance of the plaquette variables of a block is bounded, plaquette by plaquette, by the defect of Jensen's inequality, whose sum is the action that one averaging step loses, and this is controlled by the weighted actions of the backgrounds (Prop.~\YMMref{113.9}{795}). (d) The first display is (c) carried across one averaging step, the block mean tying the weights; for the second, $\mathcal MU^B$ is nearly minimal at the level $t$ (Props.~\YMMref{113.5}{792}, \YMMref{113.7}{793}), and a nearly minimal competitor has nearly the corner forms of the background, by its energy; this gives the factor $t^{1/2}$ and, with $t\le K$, the defect.
\end{proof}


\emph{Step 1: the tori, \textup{(a)}--\textup{(c)} and \textup{(f)}.} By {\cite[eq.~1]{YMM2}}, $O^T_K(H)=\sum_\lambda\mathcal O(H_{\lambda\lambda}1_\lambda)+\sum_{\lambda<\lambda'}O^{\rm od}_{\lambda\lambda'}(H_{\lambda\lambda'})$, $O^{\rm od}_{\lambda\lambda'}(\phi)=-a_K^{-1}\sum_{b\parallel\mu}\phi(x_b)q_b$ for $\mu$ the third direction, with weights supported in $\mathrm{supp}\,H$, of sup norm $\le|H|$ and Lipschitz number $\le\mathrm{Lip}\,H$; so a cumulant of the $O^T_K(H_a)$ is a sum of $6^n$ cumulants of entries. Lem.~\ref{sf-cut}(a) gives \eqref{sf-rate}, and summing over $K'\ge K$ the limit with its rate; the bound of $\mathcal S_n$ is Lem.~\ref{sf-sym}(b) at $\delta=\frac d2$; the formula for the centred moments holds at every $K$.

With $\bar O^T_K$ the cumulant at fixed $K$ is a polynomial in finitely many cell means of the $H_a$, each continuous under bounded pointwise convergence, and the rate is uniform on balls of the sup norm: so the limit is continuous under bounded pointwise convergence, which makes it countably additive in each argument, and it vanishes when all the cell means vanish, in particular on null sets; the theorem of Radon--Nikodym gives the density. For (b), Lem.~\ref{sf-sym}(a) gives the invariance under $a_K\mathbb Z^3\rtimes W_3$ at every cutoff; a real and a lattice translation of a weight differ by a weight of sup norm $\le a_K\mathrm{Lip}\,H$, and the bounds are in sup norms. As $L$ is odd, $\{x_\mu=c\}$ with $c\in a_{K_0}(\mathbb Z+\frac12)$ is a bond mirror of all the lattices with $K\ge K_0$, at which Wilson's measure is reflection positive (Cor.~\YMMref{85.3}{679}, Prop.~\YMMref{91.4}{700}) and $\theta O^T_K(H)=O^T_K(\theta H)$; such $c$ are dense, and the reflection at another $c$ is conjugate to one of these by a translation.

At $H_a=f_a\mathbf 1$, $O^T_K(f_a\mathbf 1)=\mathcal O(f_a)$. For (c): every class insertion is, at the rate, its standard form, built from the corner fields with the loops $l_\lambda=(\kappa,\kappa')$, $\kappa<\kappa'$ the two directions other than $\lambda$, at the sites. The shift $\xi$ costs a site form of norm $\le\frac12a_K\mathrm{Lip}\,\phi$, bounded by Lem.~\ref{sf-sym}(b); loops in one plane are exchanged, with the sign $s(l)s(l')$, inside the rate of Lem.~\ref{sf-cut}(a), the difference being tied at the depth $\sigma$ with the defect of Lem.~\ref{sf-cut}(c); and $a_p=\frac12Q_x(l_\lambda,l_\lambda)+\frac12a_p^2$, whose second term is of fourth order at the backgrounds. The standard form depends on the symbol alone; $O^T_K(\mathrm{Sym}\,\mathcal E)$ is a class insertion with the same symbol, and (a) gives the limit; with the same weights at the same sites no shift and no Lipschitz number occur.

For (f), take the numbers $C_{\rm bf}$, $K_{\rm bf}$ of Def.~\textup{\ref{IV-62-62}}(5) at a compact interval $J\subset I(g)$ that holds $\mathsf b$ in its interior: by Cor.~\textup{\ref{IV-62-66}}(a) they read the label only through $J$, and the comparison of the block fields of two successive cutoffs holds with them at every label of $J$. The rate of (a) reads the label at these places alone: $C_{\rm bf}$ and $K_{\rm bf}$; the condition $L^\sigma\mathsf b\ge\Theta_\star$, which is monotone in the label; the radius of the backgrounds, which the calibration conditions in equation~\YMMref{(2148)}{794} bound at the levels where $L^\sigma\mathsf b\ge\Theta_\star$; and the data of the depth $s$ of $(K,L^K\mathsf b)$, whose numbers are uniform on the compact $J$.

So, by Lem.~\ref{sf-cut}(b), one exponent $\mathsf p$, one $C^{\rm od}$, one $C^{\rm av}$ and one threshold $K_1$ serve all labels of $J$, for the entries and for the cell means. At a fixed $K$, $\mathcal S_{n;K}$ is continuous in the label, an integral over a compact group against a density continuous in $\beta=L^K\mathsf b$; so $\mathcal S^{\ell,\cdot}_n$ is a uniform limit on $J$ of functions continuous in the label, hence continuous on $J$; with $\mathsf b_K=a_K\beta_K\in J$ for large $K$,
\[|\mathcal S_{n;K}(\mathsf b_K)-\mathcal S_n(\mathsf b)|\le|\mathcal S_{n;K}(\mathsf b_K)-\mathcal S_n(\mathsf b_K)|+|\mathcal S_n(\mathsf b_K)-\mathcal S_n(\mathsf b)|\to0,\]
as in Cor.~\YMMref{117.1}{812}; with $\bar O^T_K$ the same.

\emph{Step 2: every label and side; all of \textup{(H)}.} {\cite[Lem.~C.8]{YMM2}}(a) gives
\[\langle O^T_K(H_1);\dots;O^T_K(H_n)\rangle_{K,\ell_*,L^K\mathsf b_*}=L^{zn}\langle O^T_{K-z}(H^{(z)}_1);\dots;O^T_{K-z}(H^{(z)}_n)\rangle_{K-z,L^z\ell_*,L^{K-z}(L^z\mathsf b_*)},\]
which carries Thm.~\ref{sf-tori} to every label and side, with $L^zd$ for $d$; with $g'=(L^z\mathsf b/2)^{-1/2}$ the label $L^z\mathsf b$ is an inner point of $I(g')$, which carries (f). Lems.~{\cite[Lem.~C.12]{YMM2}} and~{\cite[Lem.~C.13]{YMM2}}, {\cite[Prop.~C.21]{YMM2}} for its limits and its growth, and Steps~6, 7 and 10--13 of the proof of \cite[Thms.~BU--BX]{YMM2} are first carried out at couplings $g\le\gamma^{\rm sd}_W$; {\cite[Lem.~C.8]{YMM2}}(b) carries the data, the states, the limits, the Hilbert spaces, the semigroups, {\cite[eq.~263]{YMM2}} and the decomposition to all of (H), and $\sigma=L^{nz}\sigma_z(X^{(z)})$ carries the bounds of {\cite[Prop.~C.21]{YMM2}}(b), (c) and its growth, the powers of $L^z$ entering $C_G$ and $C$; the count of {\cite[Prop.~C.21]{YMM2}}(a) at a cutoff holds on all of (H) with the numbers set in its statement. In particular one may take $d_0(g)=L^{-z}\min_id_0(g'_i)$, with the error $\max_i\mathsf e^\infty_{g'_i}(L^zd)$ at $d$, for $z$ large enough at $g$.

\emph{Step 3: two points on one torus.} By {\cite[Lem.~C.10]{YMM2}}(a) and $|K_3(u)_{\lambda\lambda'}|\le(2\pi|u|^3)^{-1}$, $|u|\ge d$ on the supports, the Wick value is a Riemann sum of $\mathcal W$: with $a_K^3\sum_{p,p'}|\mathfrak t_H(p,p')|\le45d^3|H|$, by the row sums $2\sum_{p'}|\mathfrak t_H(p,p')|\le3|H|$ of the kernel of $O^T_K(H)$ (Step~14(a)) and the counts of the plaquettes and the bonds in a ball,
\[\Big|6\sum\mathfrak t_1\mathfrak t_2CC-\mathcal W(H_1,H_2)\Big|\le12150\,E_1\big(\tfrac1\pi+E_1\big)|H_1||H_2|+\mathrm{rm}_K(H_1,H_2),\]
where $\mathrm{rm}_K$ is the difference between a Riemann sum over the anchors, that is the barycentres, the midpoints or the sites of the cells, and the integral $\mathcal W$; it depends only on $K$, $d$ and the weights, and it tends to $0$, by the uniform continuity of $K_3$ on the two balls, for continuous weights and for cell means. With $|\mathcal W|\le54|H_1||H_2|$ ({\cite[Lem.~C.9]{YMM2}}(a)) and the bounds on $v^2$, \eqref{sf-two} follows at finite cutoff with
\[\mathsf e^T_{g,\ell}(d)=\tfrac98\big[3600\,\varepsilon^e_{g,\ell}(s)+12150\,E^\infty\big(\tfrac1\pi+E^\infty\big)\big]+162\bar Bg^2L^{2-s},\qquad E^\infty=E_1-C_{\rm lat}(a_K/d)^2,\]
and $\frac98\cdot12150\,[E_1(\frac1\pi+E_1)-E^\infty(\frac1\pi+E^\infty)]\le c_K$; the term $162\bar Bg^2L^{2-s}$ is $54$ times $3\bar Bg^2L^{2-s}$. As $K\to\infty$, (a) gives \eqref{sf-two}; $\mathsf e^T\to0$ like $(\log\frac1d)^{-2\mathfrak p_0}$ because $Y_s^{2\mathfrak p_0}\varepsilon^e_{g,\ell}(s)$ is bounded and $t=L^sd\ge C_W(s)\to\infty$. The class: (c) at $n=2$. The bound on $s_1(g,\ell)$ and the independence of $\ell$: {\cite[Lem.~C.10]{YMM2}}(b). (i): $\mathcal W$ is invariant ({\cite[Lem.~C.9]{YMM2}}(a)) and $|rH|\le3|H|$, so the law at $(H_1,H_2)$ and at $(rH_1,rH_2)$ gives $(1+9)\mathsf e^T$. (ii): {\cite[Lem.~C.9]{YMM2}}(b) and the law at the pair $(\theta(\phi E),\phi E)$, whose centres are $3d$ apart, with $|\phi E|^2\le\mathrm{tr}\,E^2$. (iii): {\cite[Lem.~C.10]{YMM2}}(c) at $c\in a_{K_0}(\mathbb Z+\frac12)$ and the limit; a general $c$ by (b).

\emph{Step 4: conservation on the torus.} Cut $\eta$ by a partition of unity into pieces of diameter $<1$; by multilinearity it suffices to treat one piece. In its slot, by {\cite[eq.~264]{YMM2}}, $\mathsf bO^T_K(H^{\rm cons}[\eta])=\mathrm{St}_K[\eta]-\Delta_K[\eta]$, and $\mathrm{St}_K[\eta]$ may be replaced by $-\mathrm{Rm}_K[\eta]$, the null terms $\mathcal N_\eta$, $\mathcal N'_\eta$ vanishing against the far entries. This leaves the remainders of {\cite[Prop.~C.17]{YMM2}}(a): the cubic one $\mathcal S[\mathsf b\eta]$, the five local forms of $J_\eta$, the form $\frac32a_K\mathcal O(w_\eta)$ and the forms of $\Delta_K[\eta]$, each with a conditional mean, given the block field of depth $\phi K$, that is constant on $T_\ell$ up to $K^{\mathsf p}L^{-(\frac1{28}-3\phi)K}\|\eta\|_{C^2}$: by {\cite[Prop.~C.17]{YMM2}}(c) for the cubic one; by power counting at the backgrounds of the level $K-\phi K$, as in the proof of {\cite[Prop.~C.17]{YMM2}}(b), for the local forms, those of the order $2$ (the three of $J_\eta$, with weights at most $(3+5\mathsf b)\|\eta\|_{C^2}$, the form $\frac32a_K\mathcal O(w_\eta)$ and the two forms of $\Delta_K[\eta]$ with weights at most $60\mathsf ba_K\sup|\nabla^2\eta|$) having oscillations at most $CK^{2\mathfrak p_0}L^{4\phi K-K}\|\eta\|_{C^2}$, and the two of the orders $3$ and $4$ of $J_\eta$, with weights at most $L^K\mathsf b\sup|\nabla\eta|$, oscillations at most $CK^{3\mathfrak p_0}L^{4\phi K-\frac K2}\|\eta\|_{C^2}$; and by the cut at the level $K-\lceil K/14\rceil$ for the form of vanishing symbol of $\Delta_K[\eta]$ alone.

A joint cumulant of entries far apart is at most the product of the oscillations of their conditional means at that level, a spectator costing $L^{4\phi K}$; at $\phi=1/(56(4q-1))$ the exponent is $-\frac1{28}+(4q-1)\phi=-\frac1{56}$. (a) gives the limit, and the moments vanish, being sums of products of cumulants of which one holds the slot of $H^{\rm cons}[\eta]$. The estimate of {\cite[Prop.~C.17]{YMM2}}(c) is uniform on the interval of labels, which gives the uniformity in the label; $\bar O^T_K$ as in Step~1; a change by forms with weights $\le36a_K\|\eta\|_{C^2}$ costs, by Lem.~\ref{sf-sym}(b), $a_K$ times a number independent of $K$. At $H_a=h_a\mathbf 1$ the spectators are action densities.

The rate $L^{-K/36}$ also holds by the argument of \cite[proof of Thms.~BU--BX, Step~8]{YMM2} on $T_\ell$.

\emph{Step 14: coinciding points, overlaps and more points.} (a): $O^T_K(H)$ is the first member of a source of Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8} under a majorant of size $60|H|$, carried by the plaquettes $p$ with $H_{\lambda(p)\lambda(p)}(x(p))\ne0$ and by the plaquettes through the bonds $b$ with $H_{\lambda_b\lambda'_b}(x_b)\ne0$ (Lem.~\ref{sf-sym}(b)): its plaquette part has the size $|H|$, and its bond part $-a_K^{-1}\sum_bH_{\lambda_b\lambda'_b}(x_b)q_b$ the size $59|H|$. Indeed $q_b$ is a bilinear form in the vector parts $w(W_{x,(\mu_b,\alpha)})$, $\alpha\in\{\pm\lambda_b,\pm\lambda'_b\}$, of the four plaquette loops at the bond $b=\langle x,x+a_Ke_{\mu_b}\rangle$; for a form $-a_K^{-1}\sum_b\mathsf w(b)q_b$ the members at the height $0$ and at every level are carried by the at most six cubes with a common corner that hold the four plaquettes through $b$, and they are bounded there as those of a plaquette source of the weight $59\sup|\mathsf w|$ on these plaquettes; to the second order at a small field the form is $a_K^{-1}$ times the quadratic form $-\sum_b\mathsf w(b)\langle\mathsf u_{b,\lambda_b},\mathsf u_{b,\lambda'_b}\rangle$ in the plaquette variables, $\mathsf u_{b,\lambda}$ linear forms with the coefficients $0,\pm\frac12$, whose symmetric kernel has the row sums $2\sum_{p'}|\mathfrak t(p,p')|\le2\sup|\mathsf w|$, so that the kernel $\mathfrak t_H$ of $O^T_K(H)$ has $2\sum_{p'}|\mathfrak t_H(p,p')|\le3|H|$.

So at the depth $s(d)$ an insertion of size $d$ is a source of size $v|H|$ in the units of the working level, and Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8} bounds the cumulant of $n$ such sources, wherever they lie, by $60^nk'_n(g,s)\mathsf b^{-n}\prod_a|H_a|$ on a side that is small over the canonical sequence of $(K,\beta)$ (equation~\YMMref{(2312)}{841}), for $g\le\gamma^{\rm sd}_W$ the least side $\ell_g$ (Lem.~\YMMref{126.3}{846}), the bound reading only the sizes of the sources; $k'_n(g,s)\le C_n(g)Y_s^{8n\mathfrak p_0}$, of the $8\mathfrak p_0$ of one entry $2\mathfrak p_0$ coming from the supremum of the plaquette action, in units of the working level, on the small fields, and $6\mathfrak p_0$ from the number $(LC_W(s))^3$ of the unit cubes of the working level in a ball of radius $d$; and $Y_{s(d)}\le2\log\frac1d+C(g)$.

On every other side $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$ the histories with a large field on $T_\ell$, summed against their weights (Prop.~\ref{prop:ward-fixed-volume-rarity}), add the factor $\max\{1,\mathsf c(\ell)\}^n$, $\mathsf c(\ell)=2\ell^3e^{\mathsf B(\bar x_0)\ell^3}/(c'A_0^2)$, with the function $\mathsf B$ and the number $c'$ of equation~\YMMref{(2311)}{841}, as $V_\ell$ does in Lem.~\ref{sf-sym}(b): this is the $\ell$ of $C_n(g,\ell)$. The scale-covariant form is the same bound read at the coupling $\gamma^{\rm sd}_W$ after the dilation of {\cite[Lem.~C.8]{YMM2}} by $L^z$: $(K-z,\beta)$ is a first-passage datum at $\gamma^{\rm sd}_W$ with the label $L^z\mathsf b\in((\gamma^{\rm sd}_W)^{-2},L((\gamma^{\rm sd}_W)^{-2}+\bar B)]$, which gives $\delta_\star\mathsf b\le L^{-z}<(\gamma^{\rm sd}_W)^2\mathsf b$, so that $\log\frac1{L^zd}$ differs from $\log\frac{\mathsf b}d$ by at most a basic number, and the factor $L^{zn}$ of the dilation turns $(L^z\mathsf b)^{-n}$ into $\mathsf b^{-n}$; the depth and the threshold are those of the dilated distance at $\gamma^{\rm sd}_W$, and the shift $(K,\ell,\mathsf b,d)\mapsto(K-1,L\ell,L\mathsf b,Ld)$ is one more step of the dilation.

Supports only at pairwise Euclidean distances $\ge d$ are cut into the boxes $Q$ of sides $\le\frac{99}{100}d''$ of a partition of $T_\ell$ into at most $(2\ell/d'')^3$ boxes, $d''=\min\{\frac34d,L^{-s_{\rm th}(n,g)}\}$: a piece $H_a1_Q$ lies within the Euclidean distance $\frac{\sqrt3}2\cdot\frac{99}{100}d''<0.8574\,d''\le0.87\,d''$ of the centre of $Q$, and pieces of different entries are at Euclidean distances $\ge d\ge\frac43d''\ge1.26\,d''$; the bound at the distance $d''$ for each product of pieces, summed by the $n$-linearity, the sum of the products being the product of the sums, gives $\prod_a\big(\sum_Q\sup_Q|H_a|\big)$ in the place of $\prod_a|H_a|$, at the same $\mathsf b^{-n}$: that is $(\mathsf bd''^3)^{-n}$ times the product of the norms $d''^3\sum_Q\sup_Q|H_a|$, a factor $d''^{-3}$ for each entry.

At $n=2$, for $g\le\gamma^{\rm sd}_W$, every $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$, $1.31h<1$ and $s(1.31h)\le K$, two off-diagonal bond forms $Y[\mathsf w_\iota]=-a_K^{-1}\sum_b\mathsf w_\iota(b)q_b$ whose bonds have their midpoints in cubes of side $\frac32h$ at the sup distance $\ge\frac52h$ have $|\langle Y[\mathsf w_1];Y[\mathsf w_2]\rangle_{K,\ell,\beta}|\le36\,C_\infty(g)\mathsf b^{-2}\sup|\mathsf w_1|\sup|\mathsf w_2|$, with the number $C_\infty(g)$ of {\cite[Lem.~C.7]{YMM2}}, of $g$ alone. This rests on {\cite[Lem.~C.7]{YMM2}}, applied at $d=1.31h$: at every $0<d<1$ with $s(d)\le K$, two real bond forms of one direction each, with $|x_b-x_\iota|\le d-2a_K$ on $\mathrm{supp}\,\mathsf w_\iota$ and $|x_1-x_2|_\infty\ge3d+a_K$, with no upper bound on that distance, have $|\langle Y[\mathsf w_1];Y[\mathsf w_2]\rangle_{K,\ell,\beta}|\le C_\infty(g)\mathsf b^{-2}\sup|\mathsf w_1|\sup|\mathsf w_2|$.

The means vanish, by Lem.~\ref{sf-sym}(a); a bond mirror parts the two forms at the distance $\ge\frac32d$ from both points, and reflection positivity there (Cor.~\YMMref{85.3}{679}, Prop.~\YMMref{91.4}{700}), that is Schwarz's inequality for the positive form, bounds the cumulant by the square roots of the two mirror pairs $\langle\theta Y[\mathsf w_\iota];Y[\mathsf w_\iota]\rangle$. By the transfer operator of the normal direction, positive by reflection positivity, a mirror pair is, as a function of the distance $t$ of the form from the mirror, a sum of exponentials with positive coefficients, symmetric under $t\mapsto\frac\ell2-t$, as the reflection fixes a second plane of the torus at the distance $\frac\ell2$; so on $[\frac32d,\frac\ell2-\frac32d]$ it is largest at $t=\frac32d$, where the form and its image are at the distance $3d$.

The proof of {\cite[Lem.~C.7]{YMM2}} bounds such a mirror pair on every torus of $\mathfrak L(g)$ and at every $K\ge s(d)$ by a number of $g$ alone times $\mathsf b^{-2}$ and the sizes, the cutoffs $K=s(d)$ and $K=s(d)+1$ among them; for $d<d_0(g)$ and $K\ge s(d)+2$ this is also the range of {\cite[Lem.~C.12]{YMM2}}: on every torus of $\mathfrak L(g)$ the pair has its Wick value of {\cite[Lem.~C.10]{YMM2}}(a) on $T_{\ell_g}$ up to a number of $g$ alone times $v^2$ and the sizes, and the Wick value of two entries of size $d$ at the distance $3d$ is at most a basic multiple of $v^2\le\frac98\mathsf b^{-2}$ times the sizes, by $|C(p,q)|\le Ca_K^3d^{-3}$ and $a_K^3\sum_{p,p'}|\mathfrak t_H(p,p')|\le45d^3|H|$, as in {\cite[Lem.~C.10]{YMM2}}(c); for $d\ge d_0(g)$ the forms are cut into pieces of a size below $d_0(g)$, whose pairs are bounded so, in a number that depends on $g$ alone; and where $K$ lies below the depth that these pieces ask, the crude bound $c\,a_K^{-4}$ of a form serves, as in {\cite[Lem.~C.10]{YMM2}}(c).

At $d=1.31h$, $x_\iota$ the centres of the cubes: $|x_b-x_\iota|\le1.2991h\le d-2a_K$ and $|x_1-x_2|_\infty\ge4h\ge3d+a_K$; and a complex weight of the bonds is the sum of six weights, each $i^\epsilon$ times a real weight carried by the bonds of one direction, of sup norm at most that of the weight: thirty-six pairs. The bound passes to $\mathcal S_n$ by Thm.~\ref{sf-tori}(a) for $\bar O^T_K$ and continuity, which gives the power counting of {\cite[Prop.~C.22]{YMM2}} with $q=8n\mathfrak p_0$ and $h_0\in\ell2^{-\mathbb N}$ with $h_0\le\min\{\frac\ell{64n},\frac12L^{-s_{\rm th}(n,g)}\}$; {\cite[Prop.~C.22]{YMM2}} gives the extension and the contact terms; the same subtractions made at each cutoff, with the products of cubes restricted to those of a side $h$ with $s(1.52h)\le K$, give lattice functionals that are bounded uniformly in $K$ and converge to the extension.

The counts at two points are those of Lem.~\ref{C-355-34}(f): take real, exchange-symmetric, translation-invariant contact terms in $\mathfrak E_2(0)$. They are $\sum_{|\alpha|\le3}\partial^\alpha\delta(x-y)\,c_\alpha(e,e')$ with bilinear $c_\alpha$, symmetric under the exchange of the two entries; under $O(3)$ on $\mathbb R^3$, which contains $-\mathbf 1$, the odd orders drop, and there remain $\mathrm{tr}\,e\,\mathrm{tr}\,e'$ and $\mathrm{tr}(ee')$ at the order $0$ and the contractions of $\partial_i\partial_j$ with $\delta_{ij}\mathrm{tr}\,e\,\mathrm{tr}\,e'$, $\delta_{ij}\mathrm{tr}(ee')$, $e_{ij}\mathrm{tr}\,e'+e'_{ij}\mathrm{tr}\,e$ and $(ee'+e'e)_{ij}$ at the order $2$: six; under $W_3$, on $\mathbb R^3$ or $T_\ell$, there are twelve. $\mathcal S_2$ is no measure across the diagonal: at the scale $d$ a unit cube holds $\gtrsim d^{-3}$ disjoint mirror pairs of balls, each of mass $\ge(\mathsf w_0-\mathsf e^T)\mathsf b^{-2}\mathrm{tr}\,E^2$ by Thm.~\ref{sf-tori}(d)(ii). (b): the action densities stay in the exponent: their weights form the source $w_z=\sum_iz_if_i$ of the sourced bare density $\rho^{w_z}_0=\exp[-\beta A_K+\sum_iz_i\mathcal O(f_i)]$ of equation~\YMMref{(10)}{14}, which Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8} carries through all the levels as a source at the plaquettes; the tensor entries, in the third and fourth cases the bond forms $Y_a=-a_K^{-1}\sum_{b\parallel\mu_a}\phi_a(x_b)q_b$ of the off-diagonal labels $E_a$, enter through their sources of Lem.~\ref{sf-sym}(b) and are derivatives at the strength $0$: $\kappa_K=\partial_{z_1}\cdots\partial_{z_n}\partial_{\tau_1}\cdots\partial_{\tau_r}\log\int\exp[\sum_a\tau_aY_a]\,\rho^{w_z}_0\,\mathrm{d}U$ at $z=0$, $\tau=0$; and likewise, in the first two cases, where the tensor weights do not overlap, for diagonal labels with the plaquette forms $Y_a=a_K^{-1}\sum_p\phi_a(x(p))(E_a)_{\lambda(p)\lambda(p)}a_p$, and for every $E_a\in V$ with $Y_a=O^T_K(\phi_aE_a)$, by {\cite[eq.~1]{YMM2}} the plaquette form of the diagonal part of $E_a$ plus the bond forms of its off-diagonal part.

Differentiated at the strength $0$ along the tensor entries, the step maps of Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8} give a recursion for the members of each order, each derivative of a step being bounded by Cauchy's estimate in the strengths. The input of \S\ref{sf-overlap-input} is used at order two: for two bond forms $Y_a$, $Y_b$ whose weights overlap, one renormalisation step at the depth $u$ creates a part $\mathfrak l$ bounded by $cL^u$ and a remainder bounded by $cK^{\mathsf p}L^{u/2}$ in the units of the sizes, and $\mathfrak l$, read at a background of a lower depth $u'$, is at most $K^{\mathsf p}\mathsf b^{-2}NL^{-2(u-u')}$, $N$ the number of the sites of the level of that depth: the arrays of order two born above a depth are forgotten below it, and this carries the case of two overlapping entries.

The remaining step is to establish this second-derivative estimate, including its stated forgetting bound, for these bond forms; and it is here that the third and fourth cases use that the labels $E_a$ are off-diagonal. Where the tensor supports are $\ge d$ apart, a member of order $\ge2$ vanishes unless its polymer reaches across the distance $d$; where only $\phi_a\phi_b=0$, the arrays of order $m\ge2$ are at most $K^{\mathsf p}L^{-mu/2}$ in the units of the sizes, the weights not overlapping, and with the condition on the $r+n$ supports this gives the same rate. For $r\ge3$ off-diagonal entries of which any two may overlap and no three supports share a point, each overlapping pair is carried by its arrays of order two, which are forgotten below their depth as for two entries; an array of order $m\ge3$ joins $m$ entries whose supports have no common point, so, the supports being compact, its polymer must cross a positive distance fixed by their geometry, and it is bounded as where the supports are apart; the depths proportional to $K$ then give $c=\frac1{360r}$.

Two cutoffs are then compared as in Lem.~\ref{sf-cut}, at depths proportional to $K$, which gives the rates. (c), with Euclidean distances between sets, here and in (d): at the depth $s(d)$ the $n$-th cumulant of the quadratic insertions in the Gaussian part is the sum over the cyclic orders, $3\mathsf b^{-n}K^{(n)}_K$, the value for three free lattice photon fields, for which the left member vanishes identically; the uniform interacting remainder is the estimate still to be established in \S\ref{hyp:quantitative-torus}, with its explicit first-creation term bounded by the weights $\varpi_t$; for the plane fields the free lattice cumulants differ from $3\mathsf b^{-n}K^{(n)}_{\underline\lambda}$ by at most $\frac13C_n(\frac{a_K}{\vartheta_0d}+\frac{d^3}{\ell^3})\prod_a|\phi_a|$, by the comparison of the lattice kernel with the free kernel (equations~\YMMref{(2245)--(2246)}{824}).

Every periodic Gibbs state and every torus of $\mathfrak L(g)$, for $2\le n\le7$: establishing the remainder estimate on $T_{\ell_g}$ and {\cite[Lem.~C.16]{YMM2}}(a), the weights being bounded functions of the plaquettes in balls of radius $d$ within one ball of radius $9d$, give the lattice inequality in \S\ref{hyp:quantitative-torus} with $\varepsilon^{\rm rt}_n(g,d)$ added to $\mathsf e_n$, and $\varepsilon^{\rm rt}_n(g,d)\to0$ with $d$ since some $\sigma\in(0,1)$ has $4-\frac n2-3\sigma>0$ exactly when $n\le7$. (d): {\cite[Lem.~C.15]{YMM2}}(c) gives the laws at a cutoff on $T_{\ell_g}$, the large fields being bounded as in {\cite[Lem.~C.15]{YMM2}}(a), and the comparison of the free lattice cycles with $k_3$, $k_4$, by equations~\YMMref{(2245)--(2246)}{824}, gives the terms $(d/\ell_g)^3$; {\cite[Lem.~C.16]{YMM2}}(c) carries the laws to every periodic Gibbs state, at three points with the further $C(g)d^{3/2}\rho^9r^{-3}d^{-6}\prod_a|w_a|$ and at four with $C(g)d^{3/2}\rho^{12}r^{-6}d^{-6}\prod_a|w_a|$, $d^{3/2}$ times the natural sizes; first passing to a continuum subsequential limit at fixed positive widths, then letting the widths tend to $0$ and using Lebesgue's differentiation theorem gives the kernels, with estimates uniform in the states, those of the truncated functions; the law of four points is that on the torus and at a cutoff; for limits and re-centred components $\sigma^c_\xi$, {\cite[Lem.~C.14]{YMM2}} and {\cite[Thm.~BW]{YMM2}}(d), (f), the kernels being continuous, and for a limit the third centred moment being the third cumulant; the point-split law follows from the three-point law, {\cite[Lem.~C.9]{YMM2}}(d) and the kernels of {\cite[Thm.~BV]{YMM2}}(e), the constant $2.7$ covering $2.66$ and the passage from $\mathrm{dist}(z,\{x,y\})$ to $|c-z|$.

\emph{Proof of Cor.~\ref{sf-ode}.} By {\cite[Thm.~BW]{YMM2}}(c), (d) the kernel $s_2(x,y;e,\mathbf 1)$ is real-analytic, a function of $u=x-y$, and linear in $e$, so $s_2(x,y;e,\mathbf 1)=\mathrm{tr}(e\,\tau(u))$ with $\tau(u)\in V$; invariance under $O(3)$ gives $\tau(Ru)=R\tau(u)R^t$, so $\tau(u)$ commutes with the stabiliser of $\hat u$ and is $A(r)\mathbf 1+B(r)\hat u\hat u^t$, and $\mathrm{tr}\,\tau=3A+B=F$. Conservation against one action density, $\sigma((H^{\rm cons}[\eta]),(f\mathbf 1))=0$ for $\mathrm{supp}\,\eta$ off $\mathrm{supp}\,f$, reads $\iint[(\nabla\cdot\eta)(x)F(x-y)-2\sum_{ij}\partial_i\eta_j(x)\tau_{ij}(x-y)]f(y)\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y=0$; integration by parts in $x$, for all such $\eta$ and $f$, gives $2\sum_i\partial_i\tau_{ij}=\partial_jF$ off $u=0$, that is $2(A'+B'+\frac2rB)=F'$, as $\sum_i\partial_i(B\hat u_i\hat u_j)=(B'+\frac2rB)\hat u_j$. With $A=\frac13(F-B)$ this is $B'+\frac3rB=\frac14F'$, and $(r^3B)'=\frac14r^3F'$. $\square$

\begin{remark}
The limits on $\mathbb R^3$ are taken along subsequences of Gibbs sequences, and each theorem speaks of the limit of the sequence chosen; the label, the bounds and the laws at short distance are the same for all of them. The uniqueness of the vacuum in {\cite[Thm.~BW]{YMM2}}\textup{(f)} is that of each component $\sigma_\xi$, and the vacuum of $\mathcal H(\sigma)$ is unique exactly when the index space $\mathsf X$ is a point. {\cite[Thm.~BW]{YMM2}} concerns limits through periodic Gibbs states; of the limits along growing tori {\cite[Thm.~BV]{YMM2}}\textup{(c)} is asserted, with positivity at the coordinate mirrors alone. The laws at short distance are laws to leading order, with errors that tend to $0$ with the distance, and Thm.~\ref{sf-tori} and Thm.~\ref{sf-coin}\textup{(a)}, \textup{(b)} concern one torus at a time, with constants that depend on its side.
\end{remark}


\subsubsection{Notation and hypotheses}

\emph{Data.} The radius, the constants and the data are those of the main theorems (Prop.~\YMMref{69.1}{595} and Section~\YMMref{82}{665}; the constants chosen in the order of that proof; the uniform free-response geometry, radius and decay conditions in Section~\YMMref{52.6}{426}, retained in Section~\YMMref{120.3}{820}; $c_\star$ by equation~\YMMref{(1429)}{582}): $L$ odd, $M$ a power of $L$, $A_0$, $A_1$, $P=2\mathfrak p_0\ge18$, $\eth\in(0,1)$, $c'=(1-\eth)c_\star$, the last constant $\gamma$, and the ceilings $\gamma_1=\gamma^{\rm sd}_W\le\gamma_2=\gamma^{\rm ref}_W\le\gamma$ of the choices in equations~\YMMref{(2326)--(2327)}{845}. $B_\sharp\ge0$ is the flow bound: $|L^{-1}x_{j-1}-x_j|\le B_\sharp$ at every step ({\cite[\S{}G.2]{YMM2}}), and $\bar B=B_\sharp L/(L-1)$ (Section~\YMMref{74}{614}); both are numbers of the constants alone. $T_\ell$, $\ell=2L^m$, is the torus of side $\ell$, $\Lambda_{K,\ell}$ its lattice of spacing $a_K=L^{-K}$, $\mathbb L_K=a_K\mathbb Z^3$; $|\cdot|$ and $|\cdot|_\infty$ are the Euclidean and the maximum norm, on a torus minimised over lifts; $\hat u=u/|u|$.

A first-passage datum $(K,\beta)$ at the reference coupling $g$ (\YMMref{74.2}{616}, \YMMref{74.1}{615}) has the running couplings $x_0=\beta,\dots,x_K$, with $|L^{-1}x_{t-1}-x_t|\le B_\sharp$ for $1\le t\le K$ (Prop.~\YMMref{74.1}{615}), so that, the differences telescoping, $|L^{-z}x_{K-z}-x_K|\le B_\sharp\sum_{0\le i<z}L^{-i}\le\bar B$ for $0\le z\le K$; $y_t=\log x_t$, $g_t=x_t^{-1/2}$, the large-field threshold $p_0(g_t)^2=A_0^2y_t^P$; the first passage $x_K\le X_g<x_{K-1}$ \YMMref{74}{614} at $X_g=L(g^{-2}+B_\sharp)$, so that $X_g+\bar B=L(g^{-2}+\bar B)$ \YMMref{(1526)}{615}; and the label $b=a_K\beta\in I^{\rm lab}(g):=[g^{-2},\bar x_0]$, $\bar x_0=L(g^{-2}+\bar B)=X_g+\bar B$; for $\mathsf b$ in the interval $I(g)=(g^{-2}+\bar B,X_g-\bar B]\subset I^{\rm lab}(g)$ of Section~\YMMref{74}{614}, $X_g-\bar B=L(g^{-2}+\bar B)-2\bar B$, $(K,L^K\mathsf b)$ is a first-passage datum for every integer $K\ge1$. $\mathfrak L(g)=\{2L^m:m\ge m_{\mathfrak L}(g)\}$ is the family of the sides at $g$ (equation~\YMMref{(1528)}{615}), $\ell'=2\mathsf l$, $\mathsf l=L^{m_{\mathfrak L}(g)}$, its least member, $\mathsf l\ge LM$.

A side $\ell=2L^m$ is \emph{admissible} if $MR(x_K)\le L^m$, $R(x)$ the least power of $L$ that is at least $(\log x)^r$, $r$ a constant; it is \emph{small} if it is small over the running couplings in the sense of equation~\YMMref{(2312)}{841}: admissible, $LM\le L^m$, $\ell\ge N_{\mathsf H}$, the lower bound of condition (H), and $\mathsf B(x_K)\ell^3\le\frac12c'p_0(g_K)^2$, $\mathsf B$ the function equation~\YMMref{(2311)}{841} of the volume factor $e^{\mathsf B\ell^3}$ (equation~\eqref{eq:ward-volume-constants}); for $g\le\gamma_1$ the side $\ell'$ is small for every datum (Lem.~\YMMref{126.3}{846}). As $R$ does not decrease, $x_K\le X_g<\bar x_0$ and $L^{m_{\mathfrak L}(g)}\ge LMR(\bar x_0)$ \YMMref{(1528)}{615}, every side $2L^m\in\mathfrak L(g)$ has $LMR(x_K)\le L^m$ for every datum at $g$: the sides of $\mathfrak L(g)$ are admissible.

\emph{Depth.} $Y_s=(s+1)\log L+\log(g^{-2}+\bar B)=\log\bar x_s$, $\bar x_s=L^{s+1}(g^{-2}+\bar B)$ and $C_W(s)=C_{W,0}A_0^2Y_s^P$ as in equation~\YMMref{(2321)}{843}, with the room constant $C_{W,0}=\max\{1,4L^2M/A_0^2\}$ (equation~\YMMref{(2320)}{843}), so that $C_W(s)\ge4L^2MY_s^P$ and $L^{-2}C_W(s)\ge4MY_s^P\ge M$; $\mathsf{Lm}_s=L^2C_W(s)Y_s^{3\mathfrak p_0}$, $x^-_s=4L^{s-2}g^{-2}/(5\mathsf{Lm}_s)$. For $0<d<1$, $s(d)$ is the least $s$ with $L^sd\ge C_W(s)$; so $Y_{s(d)}\le2\log\frac1d+C(g)$. At the working level $\mathsf k=\max\{K-s(d),2\}$: $y=y_{\mathsf k}$, $\hat d=d/a_{K-\mathsf k}$, $\upsilon^{-1}=a_{K-\mathsf k}x_{\mathsf k}$, and $\upsilon^2\le\frac98b^{-2}$; if $s(d)\le K$, then $\hat d\ge L^{s(d)-2}d\ge L^{-2}C_W(s(d))\ge M$ and $d\ge C_W(s(d))a_{s(d)}\ge4L^2Ma_K\ge676a_K$.

The free template of Section~\YMMref{120}{817} has, for $0\le n\le K$, the orthogonal projection $\Pi_n=\Pi^{\rm tp}_n$ onto the background space of the level $n$ of the exact curvatures, with its kernel $\Pi_n(p,q)$ on the plaquettes (Section~\YMMref{120}{817}); the free kernel is $\Pi_0$, the background kernel of the depth $s'$ is $C^{\rm bg}_{K,s'}=\Pi_{K-s'}$, $0\le s'\le K$, and the slice of the step $j$ is $\mathcal C_{(j)}=\Pi_{j-1}-\Pi_j$, $1\le j\le K$ \YMMref{(2227)}{818}. So $\Pi_0=\Pi_n+\sum_{1\le j\le n}\mathcal C_{(j)}$ for every $n$, and $\Pi_k-\Pi_T=\sum_{k<j\le T}\mathcal C_{(j)}$ for $k\le T$ \YMMref{(2227)}{818}; in particular the free kernel is the sum of the background kernel $\Pi_K$ of the top level and of all the slices.

With $\eta_n=L^{-n}$ and $\mathsf r=|x(p)-x(q)|_\infty$, $|\Pi_n(p,q)|\le C^{\rm bg}_{\rm tp}\eta_n^3$ and $|\mathcal C_{(j)}(p,q)|\le C_{\rm tp}\eta_{j-1}^3e^{-\delta_{\rm tp}\mathsf r/a_{K-j+1}}$ (Props.~\YMMref{120.5}{821} and~\YMMref{120.6}{821}). The background kernel of the working level is $C^{\rm bg}=C^{\rm bg}_{K,K-\mathsf k}=\Pi_{\mathsf k}$, and the free kernel is $C^{\rm bg}$ plus the slices $\mathcal C_{(j)}$, $j\le\mathsf k$, the slice $\mathcal C_{(j)}$ decaying exponentially beyond the scale $a_{K-j+1}$. $K_3(u)=(3\hat u\hat u^{\rm T}-\mathbf1)/(4\pi|u|^3)$.

\emph{Large fields; the chain.} The chain has the levels $0\le j\le K$, $\eta_j=L^{-j}$, local families with the sizes of \YMMref{(759)}{375}, the geometry of Prop.~\YMMref{45.1}{353} and {\cite[Lem.~O.1]{YMM2}}, and the contraction numbers $\theta^{[j]}$. A history is a sequence of large-field regions up to a step; $Z_t(h)$ is its region at the level $t$, $\tilde\nu_K(h)=Z^{-1}\int\mathfrak w_h\rho_0\,\mathrm{d}U$ the law of the histories; $\mathsf w_t$ is the probability that the first large field is created at the step $t$, so that $\sum_{t'\le t}\mathsf w_{t'}=\tilde\nu_K(\{Z_t\ne\emptyset\})$; $\mathsf W_T=\sum_{t\le T}\mathsf w_t$. $\Phi^{(t)}[X]$ is the conditional mean of $X$ given the block field of the level $t$ on the history without large fields. For sources with majorants (Lem.~\ref{bil:forms}) $\mathsf D_j$ is the least sup distance, in units of $a_{K-j}$, of corners of plaquettes of different sets $S_a$. For two sources at the working level, $\mathsf k<j_1\le T$ are the middle and the upper level that go with $(\mathsf k,\hat d,y)$ (equation~\YMMref{(2316)}{842}), $n_T=T-\mathsf k$, $L^{n_T}\ge\hat dy^{3\mathfrak p_0}$; for $\mathsf L\ge0$, $c>0$,
\[
{\rm sm}^{\mathsf L,c}_T=\max\Bigl\{x_T^{-1/2},\ x_{\mathsf k}e^{-d_*(T)},\ x_{\mathsf k}e^{-(\mathsf D_{\mathsf k}/M-2)},\ \max_{\mathsf k\le i<T}(\delta_i+\varepsilon^{\rm co}_i),\ x_{\mathsf k}^2\mathsf LL^{3(K-\mathsf k)}e^{-cp_0(g_T)^2}\Bigr\},
\]
and ${\rm sm}_T$ is its value at $c=\frac12c'$ and $\mathsf L=\mathsf L_\ell:=2M^{-3}\ell^3$, the number of the weights of a small side: by the rarity of large fields on one torus (Prop.~\ref{prop:ward-fixed-volume-rarity}), $\mathsf w_t\le\tilde\nu_K(\{Z_t\ne\emptyset\})\le2M^{-3}\ell^3L^{3(K-t)}e^{-c'p_0(g_t)^2}e^{\mathsf B(x_K)\ell^3}$ for $1\le t\le K$, for $g\le\gamma_2$, $K\ge3$ and every admissible side, and on a small side $\mathsf B(x_K)\ell^3\le\frac12c'p_0(g_K)^2\le\frac12c'p_0(g_t)^2$, as $x_t\ge x_K$; so $\mathsf w_t\le\mathsf L_\ell L^{3(K-t)}e^{-\frac12c'p_0(g_t)^2}$ and $\mathsf W_T\le\mathsf L_\ell L^{3(K-T)}e^{-\frac12c'p_0(g_T)^2}$ there. The symbols $\alpha_0,\beta_s,\kappa,K_M,K_\Lambda,C_{\mathcal A}$ retain their meanings in the common choice of Prop.~\YMMref{69.1}{595} and Section~\YMMref{82}{665} and $C_P$ is the number of Def.~\YMMref{51.2}{390}; $\delta(t)=A_1t^{-1/2}(\log t)^{\mathfrak p_0}$ and $\delta_i=\delta(x_i)$; $\varepsilon^{\rm co}_i$ is the error $e_i^{\rm co}$ defined before equation~\YMMref{(2302)}{837}, $d_*$ that of equation~\YMMref{(2262)}{828}, $M_{\rm pl}$ that of equation~\YMMref{(2285)}{833}; $\mathsf c_X$, $\mathsf c_I$, $\mathsf C_{\mathsf M}$, $\mathsf C_i$, $\mathsf c_{\rm sb}$ and $\mathsf c_{\rm tl}$ are fixed in \eqref{eq:short-distance-constants}--\eqref{eq:short-distance-collected-constants} and the preceding paragraph; $\mathsf p_0$ is the exponent of Cor.~\textup{\ref{IV-62-66}}; $C_{\rm tp}$, $C^{\rm bg}_{\rm tp}$, $\delta_{\rm tp}$ are the numbers of Props.~\YMMref{120.5}{821} and~\YMMref{120.6}{821}, $C_{\rm lat}$ that of equation~\YMMref{(2245)}{824}, and $C^{\rm fl}_\star$, $C^{\rm tm}_\flat$ those of equation~\eqref{eq:ward-template-constants}; $c_\theta$ and $\mathsf S_3$ are numbers of the constants alone.

The short-distance estimates use the constants of
Lems.~\YMMref{125.2}{840} and~\YMMref{125.5}{842}.
We write these constants with the font used here:
$\mathsf C_{\rm sz}=C_{\rm sz}$,
$\mathsf C_{\mathsf M}=C_{\mathsf M}$,
$\mathsf c_{\rm up}=c_{\rm up}$, $\mathsf c_I=c_I$ and
$\mathsf C_i=C_i$, with the same convention for $C'_3,C''_3$.
In particular $\mathsf c_X=405B_3^2A_0^2/2$.
Fix these choices before the source, lattice and levels, and put
\begin{equation}\label{eq:short-distance-constants}
 \mathsf c_{\mathfrak p}=\sup_{a\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}}
                  (a+2)^{4\mathfrak p_0}L^{-a},\qquad
 \mathsf c_{\rm sb}=\mathsf C_{\rm sz}+\mathsf c_{\rm up},\qquad
 \mathsf c_{\rm tl}=2L^8\mathsf c_{\mathfrak p}+1.
\end{equation}
The supremum is finite because exponential decay dominates the
fixed power of $a$. For $\vartheta\in\{1,2\}$ define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:short-distance-collected-constants}
\begin{split}
 \mathsf C_B^{(\vartheta)}={}&\mathsf C_{\mathsf M}
       +4\mathsf c_X\mathsf c_I+6\mathsf c_I^2\\
 &+\mathsf c_{\rm tl}\bigl[\mathsf C_{\mathsf M}
   +(2+\vartheta^2+\vartheta^2\mathsf c_{\rm tl})
       \mathsf c_{\rm sb}^2
   +2\vartheta\mathsf c_{\rm sb}(\mathsf c_X+\mathsf c_I)\bigr],\\
 \mathsf C_{\rm B}={}&\mathsf C_7+2(1+A_1)^4\mathsf C_5
       +\mathsf C'_3+\mathsf C''_3+\mathsf C_6
       +\mathsf C_B^{(1)},\\
 \mathsf C'_B={}&\mathsf C_B^{(2)},\qquad
 \mathsf C^e_B=\mathsf C_7+2(1+A_1)^4\mathsf C_5
       +\mathsf C'_3+\mathsf C''_3+\mathsf C_6+\mathsf C'_B.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
These are fixed numbers, and $\mathsf C_{\rm B}\le\mathsf C^e_B$.

\begin{lemma}[The coefficient of the collected error]
\label{lem:short-distance-collected-constant}
Under the hypotheses of Cor.~\YMMref{125.6}{843},
the coefficient $C_B$ in its estimate may be chosen to be
$\mathsf C_{\rm B}$ in
\eqref{eq:short-distance-collected-constants}.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Use the notation of that corollary:
$p=\mathfrak p_0$, $q=\widehat d_{\mathsf k}$,
$y=y_{\mathsf k}$, $n=T-\mathsf k\ge1$, and $s_T\le1$.
Divide the errors by $\widehat m_1\widehat m_2$, and write
$\mathfrak m=n^4q^6y^{15p}$.
The first four terms in equation~\YMMref{(2319)}{843}
are the direct terms of the seven-error estimate.
Its remaining terms are bounded by
\[
 [\mathsf C_7+2(1+A_1)^4\mathsf C_5
             +\mathsf C'_3+\mathsf C''_3+\mathsf C_6]
                  \mathfrak m s_T.
\]
Indeed $x_T^{-1}\le s_T^2\le s_T$, $W_T\le t_T\le s_T$,
and $1+A_1y^p\le(1+A_1)y^p$.

In the remainder of equation~\YMMref{(2315)}{842}, use
$i_T\le\mathsf c_Iq^3y^{3p}s_T$ and
$z_T\le\mathsf c_Xy^{-7p}+i_T$.
The separated-support term costs
$\mathsf C_{\mathsf M}\mathfrak m s_T$.
The cross terms cost
$(4\mathsf c_X\mathsf c_I+2\mathsf c_I^2)\mathfrak m s_T$,
and the top term is at most
\[
 2z_T^2\le4\mathsf c_X^2y^{-14p}
                   +4\mathsf c_I^2\mathfrak m s_T.
\]
For its last line, the size and tail bounds give
\[
 2L^8\mathsf c_{\mathfrak p}+n\le\mathsf c_{\rm tl}n,
 \qquad b_0\le\mathsf c_{\rm sb}nq^3x_{\mathsf k}y^{2p},
 \qquad x_{\mathsf k}^2t_T\le s_T.
\]
Consequently the bracket in that line is at most
\[
 [\mathsf C_{\mathsf M}+(3+\mathsf c_{\rm tl})\mathsf c_{\rm sb}^2
       +2\mathsf c_{\rm sb}(\mathsf c_X+\mathsf c_I)]
                  n^3q^6y^{5p}x_{\mathsf k}^2.
\]
Multiplication by its remaining factor, at most
$\mathsf c_{\rm tl}nt_T$, gives the last part of
$\mathsf C_B^{(1)}\mathfrak m s_T$.
Adding these coefficients proves the assertion.
\end{proof}

We use this admissible value of the collected coefficient in
the depth error of equation~\YMMref{(2330)}{846}.
We use the following names for its auxiliary functions:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:short-distance-envelope-names}
 \mathsf{Lm}_s=\mathsf L_s=L^2C_W(s)Y_s^{3\mathfrak p_0},\qquad
 \mathsf{sm}_g(s)=\sigma_g(s).
\end{equation}
Here $\mathsf L_s$ is defined in equation~\YMMref{(2322)}{844},
and $\sigma_g$, $\epsilon_g$, $Y_s^-$, $x_s^-$ and $s_1(g)$
are the functions and threshold of
equations~\YMMref{(2328)--(2332)}{846}.
The proof there gives $s^a\mathsf{sm}_g(s)\to0$ for every
$a\ge0$ and boundedness of $Y_s^{2\mathfrak p_0}\epsilon_g(s)$.
Changing the fixed collected coefficient to the admissible value
above preserves that proof: its only additional occurrence is
a fixed multiple of a polynomial times $\mathsf{sm}_g(s)$.

\emph{Laws.} $\langle\cdot\rangle_\ell=\langle\cdot\rangle_{K,\ell,\beta}$ is the Wilson measure on $T_\ell$, $\tilde\mu_\ell$ its periodic extension to $\mathbb L_K$, $\mathcal G^{\rm per}_{K,\beta}$ the set of the periodic Gibbs states on $\mathbb L_K$; a \emph{law} at $(K,\beta)$ is a member of $\mathcal G^{\rm per}_{K,\beta}$ or a $\tilde\mu_\ell$, $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$, and for the latter distances are those of $T_\ell$. $\langle X_1;\dots;X_n\rangle_\nu$ is the joint cumulant (complex multilinear), $\nu(X;Y)=\langle X;Y\rangle_\nu$, $A[F]=A^\nu[F]=F-\nu(F)$; for a tuple $X=(H_1,\dots,H_n)$, $A^\nu(X)=\prod_aA^\nu[O^T_K(H_a)]$, extended linearly to combinations of tuples; along a sequence of laws $\nu_j$, $A_j=A^{\nu_j}$, and $A(X)=A^\rho(X)$ for the law $\rho$ at hand. $p_\ell=\ell^{-3}\log Z_{K,\ell,\beta}$ is the pressure, and $G_g=C_S+C_g+2C_{\rm tt}C'_{\rm tt}E_0$ is formed with the constants of {\cite[\S{}N]{YMM2}}, with which the canonical source energies form a system of localised source energies ({\cite[Lem.~N.1]{YMM2}}).

A \emph{mirror} $\theta$ is the reflection in a coordinate plane through midpoints of bonds; it acts on points, on functions of the field by $(\theta F)(U)=F(\theta U)$, and on tensor labels.
