The \emph{nine families} are the planes whose normals are $e_\mu$ or $(e_\mu\pm e_\lambda)/\sqrt2$, $\mu\ne\lambda$ (eighteen unit normals); every periodic Gibbs state is invariant under the lattice isometries and reflection positive, in the sense of the reflection form below, at the lattice planes of the nine families (Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{103.4}{758}}). For a mirror $\theta_c$ in $\{x_{\mu_0}=c\}$ and a law $\nu$, $\|F\|_{\nu,c}=\nu(\overline{\theta_cF}F)^{1/2}$ on the functions of the field on $\{x_{\mu_0}>c\}$.

\emph{Boards.} A board of $\mathbb L_K$ has a side $\mathsf l_0=a_i$, $i\le K-1$ an integer (negative $i$ admitted, so that $\mathsf l=L^{m_{\mathfrak L}(g)}$ is a side of a board), and an offset $o\in a_K\mathbb Z^3$; it is the partition of $\mathbb R^3$ into the cubes $o+\mathsf l_0\mathbf n+[-\frac12\mathsf l_0,\frac12\mathsf l_0)^3$, $\mathbf n\in\mathbb Z^3$, its \emph{cells}, so that the offset is the centre of a cell, and its \emph{walls} are the planes $\{x_\mu=o_\mu+\mathsf l_0(t+\frac12)\}$, $t\in\mathbb Z$, $\mu=1,2,3$. As $\mathsf l_0/a_K=L^{K-i}$ is odd, the walls lie in $a_K(\mathbb Z+\frac12)$ and pass through midpoints of bonds: they are planes of mirrors. A \emph{function of a cell} is a function of the variables of the bonds with both ends in the open cell; its images under successive reflections in the walls are its \emph{copies}, with complex conjugation after an odd number of reflections. For a side $\ell_0\in2\mathsf l_0\mathbb N$ the chessboard seminorm $\|\Phi\|_{{\rm ch},\ell_0}\ge0$ of a bounded function $\Phi$ of a cell has as its $N_0$-th power, $N_0=(\ell_0/\mathsf l_0)^3$, the $\tilde\mu_{\ell_0}$-mean of the product of the $N_0$ copies of $\Phi$ in a period box.

\emph{Field and label conventions.} The field is $O_K^T$ of {\cite[eq.~1]{YMM2}}, with the same $w(G)$, $a_p$, $q_b$ and midpoint convention. We use $\langle X,Y\rangle=\frac12\operatorname{tr}(XY)$ and the sup norm $|H|_\infty$. In this section $E_{\lambda\lambda'}$ denotes the symmetric label with entries $1$ at $(\lambda,\lambda')$ and $(\lambda',\lambda)$, rather than a matrix unit. A loop is a pair $l=(\alpha,\alpha')$, $\alpha,\alpha'\in\{\pm1,\pm2,\pm3\}$, $|\alpha|\ne|\alpha'|$; $W_x(l)$ is the holonomy from $x$ along $e_\alpha$, then $e_{\alpha'}$, around the plaquette $p(x,l)$, and $\sigma(l)=\mathrm{sgn}\,\alpha\,\mathrm{sgn}\,\alpha'\,\mathrm{sgn}(|\alpha'|-|\alpha|)$. 
We write $S_n^T[\nu](H_1,\ldots,H_n)$ for the joint cumulant of the $O_K^T(H_a)$ under $\nu$. The free covariance is $\mathcal W$ in \eqref{sf-free}. The test norm used here is
\[
 N(H)=\max_{\lambda\lambda'}\bigl(|H_{\lambda\lambda'}|_\infty+d\,\operatorname{Lip}H_{\lambda\lambda'}\bigr).
\]

\emph{Forms.} A \emph{cell} is a plaquette, a positively oriented bond with the four loops that start along it, or a site with all its $24$ loops. A \emph{form} is $F=a_K^{-1}\sum_ph(p)a_p$ or $F=a_K^{-1}\sum_{\mathsf c}\sum_{l,l'}v(\mathsf c,l,l')\langle w(W_l),w(W_{l'})\rangle$, the cells $\mathsf c$ being bonds, resp. sites, with real weights of finite support (complex weights where this is said); its \emph{size} $|F|_\star$ is $\sup|h|$, $59\|v\|$, resp. $23\|v\|$, $\|v\|=\sup_{\mathsf c}\sum_{l,l'}|v(\mathsf c,l,l')|$; its \emph{carrier} is the set of the centres of the cells of its support, $S[F]$ the set of the plaquettes of these cells; its \emph{kernel} is $\mathsf t_F(p,p')=\frac12h(p)\delta_{pp'}$, resp. $\mathsf t_F(p',p'')=\frac12\sum v(\mathsf c,l,l')\sigma(l)\sigma(l')[\delta_{p'p(l)}\delta_{p''p(l')}+\delta_{p'p(l')}\delta_{p''p(l)}]$. For a weight $\mathsf w$ of the bonds, $Y[\mathsf w]=-a_K^{-1}\sum\mathsf w(\mathsf e)q_{\mathsf e}$ is a bond form of size $59\sup|\mathsf w|$; $O^T_K(H)$ is a sum of six forms, each on the plaquettes of one normal or on the bonds of one direction, of total size at most $180|H|_\infty$. The \emph{Gaussian value} of two forms is
\[
G(F_1,F_2)=6\upsilon^2\sum\mathsf t_{F_1}(p,p')\,\mathsf t_{F_2}(q,q')\,C^{\rm bg}(p,q)\,C^{\rm bg}(p',q'),
\]
Wick's value for three free photon fields, $2(N^2-1)=6$ at $N=2$.

\emph{Limits.} $S$ denotes a volume-first limit, or a continuum limit along growing tori, of the action density, with its defining sequence ({\cite[\S{}K.1]{YMM2}}). A tuple is \emph{separated} if its supports are pairwise disjoint. Along a sequence of laws at which all $S^T_n[\nu_j](X)$ converge, $\sigma^T(X)=\sum_\pi\prod_{I\in\pi}S^T_{\#I}(X_I)$, the sum over the partitions into blocks of at least two, is the limit of the means of the products of the insertions centred in the states, and $\sigma^T(\emptyset)=1$. A \emph{limit through periodic Gibbs states} is a limit along $\nu_j\in\mathcal G^{\rm per}_{K_j,\beta_j}$, $K_j\to\infty$, that converges at all separated tuples in $C^1_c(\mathbb R^3;V)$; $H,P_1,P_2,\Omega$ are the Hamiltonian, the momenta and the vacuum reconstructed from $\sigma^T$ at $\{x_3=0\}$ (Prop.~\YMMref{94.1}{720}; classes $[F]$ of combinations $F$ of tuples in $\{x_3>0\}$, $\langle[F'],[F]\rangle=\sigma^T(\theta\bar F'\cdot F)$), with $e^{-tH}[F]=[\tau_{te_3}F]$, the unitary group $\mathcal U(v)[F]=[\tau_{(v,0)}F]$, $v\in\mathbb R^2$, of the horizontal translations, and the joint spectral measure $\mathcal P$ of $(H,P_1,P_2)$; and alike at a plane of each of the nine families: the \emph{nine pictures}. $\tau_v$ is the translation by $v$.

\emph{Numbers.} Each symbol $C_\cdot$, $c_\cdot$, $k_\cdot$, $s_\cdot(g)$, and each error function $\varepsilon_\cdot,\omega_\cdot,o_\cdot,e_\cdot,{\rm Df}_\cdot$ of $s$, is a function of the constants, of $g$ and of the arguments shown alone; it does not depend on $K$, $\beta$, $\ell$, the law, a weight or a position unless these are shown, and error functions tend to $0$ as $s\to\infty$. $s_1(g)$ is the first depth of the envelopes of equations~\YMMref{(2328)--(2336)}{846}, with the notation in \eqref{eq:short-distance-envelope-names}, $s_p(g)$ ($p$ even) that of Lem.~\ref{bil:far}.


\begin{theorem}\label{thm:bil}
Let $(K,\beta)$ be a first-passage datum at $g$ and $b=a_K\beta$.

\textbf{(A)} Let $0<g\le\gamma_2$ and let $\ell$ be small. Then the following hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(A1)] For $n\ge2$, $0<d<1$, $K\ge K_0'(n,d)$ and forms $F_1,\dots,F_n$ on $\Lambda_{K,\ell}$, with complex weights allowed at bonds and sites, whose carriers are pairwise at distance $\ge d$,
\[
|\langle F_1;\dots;F_n\rangle_\ell|\le k^\circ(n,d)\,b^{-n}\prod_a|F_a|_\star,
\]
where $d''=\min\{\frac34d,L^{-s_{\rm th}(n)}\}$, $K_0'(n,d)=s(d'')$, $k^\circ(n,d)=(2\ell_{\max}/d'')^{3n}k'_n(g,s(d''))$, $\ell_{\max}^3=\frac12c'A_0^2Y_{s(d'')}^P$, with $s_{\rm th}$, $k'_n$ of Lem.~\ref{bil:nsrc}: the power $d^{-3}$ for each entry, times a power of $\log\frac1d$. No upper bound on the distances is asked.
\item[(A2)] Let $s_1(g)\le s(d)\le K$, $3d\le|x_1-x_2|\le4d$, and let the carrier of $F_i$ lie within $d-2a_K$ of $x_i$. Then $|\langle F_1;F_2\rangle_\ell-G(F_1,F_2)|\le\varepsilon^\natural_g(s(d))\,\upsilon^2|F_1|_\star|F_2|_\star$, $\varepsilon^\natural_g$ of Lem.~\ref{bil:two}. For complex tensor weights $H_i$ supported within $d-2a_K$ of $x_i$ the same holds for $O^T_K(H_1)$, $O^T_K(H_2)$, the Gaussian value being formed with their kernels (Lem.~\ref{bil:forms}) and the error being $4\cdot60^2\varepsilon^\natural_g(s(d))\upsilon^2|H_1|_\infty|H_2|_\infty$. If $H_i=\varphi_iE_{\lambda_i\lambda_i'}$, $\varphi_i$ real and Lipschitz with support in $B(x_i,d-2a_K)$, and $\lambda_1\ne\lambda_1'$, then
\[
|\langle O^T_K(H_1);O^T_K(H_2)\rangle_\ell-b^{-2}\mathcal W(H_1,H_2)|\le e^{\rm od}\,b^{-2}N(H_1)N(H_2),
\]
with the number $e^{\rm od}$ of Step~2, at most $\bar e^{\rm od}_g(s(d))$, $\bar e^{\rm od}_g$ an error function.
\item[(A3)] Let $s_1(g)\le s(d)\le K$, and let the carrier of $Y=Y[\mathsf w]$, $\mathsf w$ real on the bonds of one direction, lie within $d-2a_K$ of a point at a distance between $\frac32d$ and $2d$ from the plane of a mirror $\theta$. Then
\[
0\le\langle\theta Y;Y\rangle_\ell\le C^\circ_{\rm od}(g)\,b^{-2}\sup|\mathsf w|^2,\qquad C^\circ_{\rm od}(g)=\tfrac98\bigl[600C_{\mathsf k}^2+59^2\bar\varepsilon^\natural_g\bigr],\quad\bar\varepsilon^\natural_g=\sup_{s\ge s_1(g)}\varepsilon^\natural_g(s),
\]
$C_{\mathsf k}$ of Lem.~\ref{bil:ker}. For a real form $F$ at bonds, resp. sites, with the weight $v$, placed in the same way, $0\le\langle\theta F;F\rangle_\ell\le\frac98[6N^2C_{\mathsf k}^2+c^2\bar\varepsilon^\natural_g]\,b^{-2}\|v\|^2$, $(N,c)=(30,59)$, resp. $(10,23)$. For real tensor weights $H_i$ as in (A2), $|\langle O^T_K(H_1);O^T_K(H_2)\rangle_\ell|\le\frac98[12150C_{\mathsf k}^2+60^2\bar\varepsilon^\natural_g]\,b^{-2}|H_1|_\infty|H_2|_\infty$.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{(B)} Let $g\le\gamma_1$, $s_8(g)\le s(d)\le K$, let $\theta'_1,\theta'_2,\theta'_3$ be mirrors of $T_{\ell'}$, $\theta'_\mu$ normal to $e_\mu$, and let $Y$ be as in (A3), carried within $d-2a_K$ of a point at a distance between $\frac32d$ and $2d$ from a plane of $\theta'_{\mu_0}$ and, up to $a_K/2$, midway between the planes of the two other mirrors. With $\theta'^\eta=\theta'^{\eta_1}_1\theta'^{\eta_2}_2\theta'^{\eta_3}_3$,
\[
\begin{multlined}
0\le M_8=\Bigl\langle\prod_{\eta\in\{0,1\}^3}\theta'^\eta Y\Bigr\rangle_{\ell'}\le C_8\,b^{-8}\sup|\mathsf w|^8,\qquad0\le M_8-\langle\theta'_{\mu_0}Y;Y\rangle_{\ell'}^4 \\
\le(\tfrac98)^459^8\omega^\sharp_{g,8}(s(d))\,b^{-8}\sup|\mathsf w|^8,
\end{multlined}
\]
$C_8=(\frac98)^4[(106C'^2_{\mathsf k})^4+59^8\bar\omega_{g,8}]$, $\bar\omega_{g,8}=\sup_{s\ge s_8(g)}\omega_{g,8}(s)$, with $C'_{\mathsf k}$ of Lem.~\ref{bil:ker} and $\omega_{g,8}$, $\omega^\sharp_{g,8}$ of Lem.~\ref{bil:far}.

\textbf{(C)} Let $g\le\gamma_1$ and let $\nu,\nu'$ be laws at $(K,\beta)$.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(C1)] For $n\ge2$, $d,R>0$, every $K$, and forms $F_1,\dots,F_n$ on $\mathbb L_K$ whose carriers lie in balls of radius $R$ and are pairwise at distance $\ge d$: $|\langle F_1;\dots;F_n\rangle_\nu|\le C^T_n(d;R)\,b^{-n}\prod_a|F_a|_\star$, with $C^T_n$ of Step~4; complex weights cost a factor $2^n$. So 
\[
|S^T_n[\nu](H_1,\dots,H_n)|\le60^nC^T_n(d;R)\,b^{-n}\prod_a|H_a|_\infty
\]
 for supports in such balls at mutual distance $\ge d$, and $|\nu(F)-\nu'(F)|\le2C^T_1(R)\,b^{-1}|F|_\star$.
\item[(C2)] If $s(d)\le K$, $\mathrm{supp}\,H_i\subset B(x_i,d-3a_K)$ and $|x_1-x_2|_\infty\ge3d+a_K$ (on a torus for all lifts): 
\[
|S^T_2[\nu](H_1,H_2)|\le180^2C^\diamond_\infty(g)\,b^{-2}|H_1|_\infty|H_2|_\infty,
\]
$C^\diamond_\infty$ of Step~5. For $Y[\mathsf w_i]$, $\mathsf w_i$ real on the bonds of one direction, carried within $d-2a_K$ of $x_i$: 
\[
|\nu(Y[\mathsf w_1];Y[\mathsf w_2])|\le C^{\rm per}_\infty(g)\,b^{-2}\sup|\mathsf w_1|\sup|\mathsf w_2|,
\]
with a number $C^{\rm per}_\infty\ge e^{2G_g\mathsf l^3}C_8^{1/4}$.
\item[(C3)] Let $s_{16}(g)\le s=s(d)\le K$, $3d\le|x_1-x_2|\le4d$, let the carriers of real forms $F_i$ lie within $d-2a_K$ of $x_i$, $\hat m=\upsilon^2|F_1|_\star|F_2|_\star$, and let $F_i'$ be the forms on $T_{\ell'}$ with the weights of $F_i$ on the board of side $\mathsf l$ whose cell holds the pair in its middle. Then
\[
\begin{multlined}
|\nu(F_i)-\tilde\mu_{\ell'}(F_i)|\le e^{G_g\mathsf l^3}o_{g,16}(s)^{1/8}\upsilon|F_i|_\star,\quad|\nu(F_1;F_2)-\tilde\mu_{\ell'}(F_1;F_2)|\le{\rm Df}_g(s)\,\hat m, \\
|\nu(F_1;F_2)-G(F_1',F_2')|\le[\omega'_{g,16}+{\rm Df}_g](s)\,\hat m,
\end{multlined}
\]
the Gaussian value being formed on $T_{\ell'}$ and ${\rm Df}_g$ given in Step~5; the error function and the first depth are the same for all the laws. The same holds for $F_i=O^T_K(H_i)$, $H_i$ real tensor weights supported within $d-2a_K$ of $x_i$, with $60|H_i|_\infty$ in the place of $|F_i|_\star$.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{(D)} Let $g\le\gamma_1$, let $(K_j,\beta_j)$ be first-passage data at $g$ and $\nu_j$ laws at $(K_j,\beta_j)$: all periodic Gibbs states, or all $\tilde\mu_{\ell_j}$ with $\ell_j\to\infty$. Tuples $X=(H_1,\dots,H_n)$ are in $C_c(\mathbb R^3;V)$ with pairwise disjoint supports.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(D1)] Along a subsequence ($K_j\to\infty$ is not asked) $a_{K_j}\beta_j\to\mathsf b\in I^{\rm lab}(g)$ and $S^T_n[\nu_j](X)\to S^T_n(X)$ for all $n\ge2$ and all $X$; $S^T_n$ is symmetric, multilinear, bounded as in (C1) with $\mathsf b$ for $b$, and in each entry a $V^*$-valued Radon measure off the other supports. For laws $\nu'_j$ at the same data, $\lim(\nu_j-\nu'_j)(O^T_{K_j}(H))$ exists along a further subsequence, of modulus $\le120C^T_1(R)\mathsf b^{-1}|H|_\infty$ if $\mathrm{supp}\,H$ lies in a ball of radius $R$. If each $\nu_j$ is a weak limit of measures $\tilde\mu_\ell$ at $(K_j,\beta_j)$, then for any numbers $\Lambda_j$ there are sides $\ell_j\ge\max\{\Lambda_j,j\}$ in $\mathfrak L(g)$ with $S^T_n[\tilde\mu_{\ell_j}](X)\to S^T_n(X)$ along the full sequence: a limit through limit states of the tori is a limit along growing tori.
\item[(D2)] Over every volume-first limit $S$ and every continuum limit along growing tori there is such an $S^T$, with $S^T_n(f_1\mathbf1,\dots,f_n\mathbf1)=S_n(f_1,\dots,f_n)$, $f_i\in C^1_c$.
\item[(D3)] If $K_j\to\infty$: $S^T_n(rX)=S^T_n(X)$ for $rx=Ax+y$, $A\in W_3$; and for every coordinate plane $\{x_\mu=c\}$, with its reflection $\theta$ acting on points and on indices, all finitely many tuples $X_i$ (the empty one included) with supports in $\{x_\mu>c\}$ and all complex $c_i$: $\sum_{i,k}\bar c_ic_k\sigma^T(\theta X_i\cdot X_k)\ge0$. For limits through periodic Gibbs states the same holds at the planes with the normals $e_\mu\pm e_\lambda$, the Hilbert space is separable, and $H\ge|P_1|$, $H\ge|P_2|$. The numbers $\mathfrak c_j=a_{K_j}^{-4}(\nu_j(a_p)-\tilde\mu_{\ell'}(a_p))$, the same at all plaquettes, obey $|\mathfrak c_j|\le C(g)\mathsf b^{-1}$ for all large $j$; along a further subsequence $\mathfrak c_j\to\mathfrak c$, and along it the moments centred at the means of $\tilde\mu_{\ell'}$ in the place of those of the $\nu_j$ converge too, to $\sum_B\prod_{i\in B}(\mathfrak c\int\mathrm{tr}\,H_i)\,\sigma^T(X_{B^c})$, the sum over the subsets $B$ of the entries, a functional with the same properties whose one-point function is $\mathfrak c\int\mathrm{tr}\,H$.
\item[(D4)] For $\mathsf b\in I(g)$, $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$ and continuous $H_a:T_\ell\to V$ with disjoint supports, $S^{T,(\ell,\mathsf b)}_n(H)=\lim_K\langle O^T_K(H_1);\dots;O^T_K(H_n)\rangle_{K,\ell,L^K\mathsf b}$ exists along the full sequence of cutoffs (for $g\le\gamma_2$) and obeys the bound of (D1). Along a subsequence of every $\ell_i\to\infty$ these limits converge, and the limit is also the limit of $S^T_n[\tilde\mu_{\ell_i}]$ at suitable cutoffs $K_i\to\infty$: a limit along growing tori, with the properties of (D3) for these limits.
\item[(D5)] Let $K_j\to\infty$, $s(d)\ge s_{16}(g)$, $3d\le|x_1-x_2|\le4d$, and $H_i$ Lipschitz with compact support in the open ball $B(x_i,d)$. Then
\[
|S^T_2(H_1,H_2)-\mathsf b^{-2}\mathcal W(H_1,H_2)|\le36\,\bar e_g(s(d))\,\mathsf b^{-2}N(H_1)N(H_2),
\]
the function $\bar e_g$ being the same for all sequences; the same holds for the limits of (D4), on every $\ell$. At $H_i=f_i\mathbf1$ the leading term is $\frac9{16\pi^2}\mathsf b^{-2}\iint f_1(x)f_2(y)|x-y|^{-6}\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y$, the scalar leading coefficient in Thm.~\YMMref{AW}{852}.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{(E)} Let $g\le\gamma_2$, $K\ge3$, and let $\ell=2L^m$ be admissible.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(E1)] With $\tilde\nu_K$ the law of the histories and $Z_t$ the large-field region of the level $t$, for $1\le t\le K$:
\[
0\le\mathsf w_t\le\tilde\nu_K(\{Z_t\ne\emptyset\})\le C_\flat M^{-3}\ell^3L^{3(K-t)}\exp\bigl[-\tfrac34c_\star p_0(g_t)^2\bigr];
\]
$C_\flat$ is a function of the constants at two admissible sets of values alone, and does not depend on $g$, $K$, $\beta$, $\ell$, $t$; $\frac34c_\star\ge\frac12c'$, and $\frac34c_\star\ge c'$ if $\eth\ge\frac14$. The same holds with $(c^\natural_2,C_\natural)$ for $(\frac34c_\star,C_\flat)$, $c^\natural_2$ the constant of Def.~\ref{def:rarity-choices} with which Prop.~\ref{prop:local-large-field-rarity} bounds the rarity of a large field at a point, and $C_\natural$ a function of the constants.
\item[(E2)] Let $(c,C)$ be a pair for which (E1) holds with $(c,C)$ for $(\frac34c_\star,C_\flat)$, as $(\frac12c',C_\flat)$, $(\frac34c_\star,C_\flat)$ and $(c^\natural_2,C_\natural)$ do; $\sigma_c=\frac2{\log L}(\frac6{cA_0^2})^{1/P}$, $\hat s(g,\ell)=\max\{s_\flat(g),\lceil\sigma_c(\log\ell)^{1/P}\rceil\}$, the numbers below being formed at $(c,C)$ and $s_\flat(g)$ being the first depth of the envelopes at $(c,C)$, chosen so that also $2c\mathfrak p_0A_0^2y^{P-1}\ge13$ at the working level. Let $\hat s\le s(d)\le K$, $|x_1-x_2|\ge3d$ (no upper bound), and let $F_i$ be sums of forms within $d-2a_K$ of $x_i$, of size the sum of the sizes. Then
(i) $|\langle F_1;F_2\rangle_\ell-G(F_1,F_2)|\le\varepsilon^\circ_g(s(d))\upsilon^2|F_1|_\star|F_2|_\star$, with $Y_s^P\varepsilon^\circ_g(s)$ bounded;
(ii) $|\langle F_1;F_2\rangle_\ell|\le C^\circ_\star(g)b^{-2}|F_1|_\star|F_2|_\star$;
(iii) if $x_1$ is at a distance $\ge\frac32d$ from both planes of $\theta$, $0\le\langle\theta F_1;F_1\rangle_\ell\le C^\circ_\star(g)b^{-2}|F_1|_\star^2$;
(iv) for all $d$ with $s(d)\le K$ and $F$ placed as in (iii), $0\le\langle\theta F;F\rangle_\ell\le C^\circ_3(g,\ell)b^{-2}(|F|_\star/59)^2$, which is $C^\circ_3b^{-2}\sup|\mathsf w|^2$ at $F=Y[\mathsf w]$, $\mathsf w$ real on the bonds of one direction, and $C^\circ_3(g,\ell)\le c_3(g)(1+\log\ell)^8\exp[16(\frac{6\log\ell}{cA_0^2})^{1/P}]$, so that $\ell^{-\epsilon}C^\circ_3(g,\ell)$ is bounded for every $\epsilon>0$;
(v) if all points of the carriers of $F_1$ and $F_2$ are $\ge r$ apart and $K\ge s(\min\{\frac r8,L^{-\hat s}\})$: $|\langle F_1;F_2\rangle_\ell|\le(\ell\max\{\frac8r,L^{\hat s}\}+1)^6C^\circ_\star(g)b^{-2}|F_1|_\star|F_2|_\star$.
On the sides with $\log\ell\le(s_\flat(g)/\sigma_c)^P$ the first depth is $\hat s=s_\flat(g)$, free of $\ell$.
\item[(E3)] Let $\mathsf L<\infty$ and $c''\ge\frac12c'$ be numbers with $\mathsf w_t\le\mathsf LL^{3(K-t)}e^{-c''p_0(g_t)^2}$ for $1\le t\le K$. Then: (i) Lem.~\ref{bil:nsrc}, for sources under majorants, holds on $T_\ell$ with $\max\{1,M^3\mathsf L/(c'A_0^2)\}^nk'_n$ for $k'_n$, under its hypotheses $n\ge2$ and $s_{\rm th}(n)\le s(d)\le K$ and in its geometry: $|\langle F_1;\dots;F_n\rangle_\ell|\le\max\{1,M^3\mathsf L/(c'A_0^2)\}^nk'_n(g,s(d))\,b^{-n}\prod_a\mathsf s_a$, with no factor of a covering; (ii) from (i), by the covering of Step~1, (A1) holds on $T_\ell$ with $2\ell$ for $2\ell_{\max}$ and $\max\{1,M^3\mathsf L/(c'A_0^2)\}^nk'_n$ for $k'_n$. Two such pairs are had on every admissible side: $\mathsf L=2M^{-3}\ell^3e^{\mathsf B(\bar x_0)\ell^3}$, $c''=c'$, by the rarity of large fields on one torus (Prop.~\ref{prop:ward-fixed-volume-rarity}), as $\mathsf B$ increases and $x_K\le X_g<\bar x_0$; and the pair of (E1), $\mathsf L=C_\flat M^{-3}\ell^3$, $c''=\frac34c_\star\ge\frac12c'$. So (i) and (ii) hold on every admissible side with $\max\{1,c(\ell)\}^nk'_n$ for $k'_n$, (ii) with $2\ell$ for $2\ell_{\max}$, where $c(\ell)=2\ell^3e^{\mathsf B(\bar x_0)\ell^3}/(c'A_0^2)$, the number $M^3\mathsf L/(c'A_0^2)$ at the first pair; with the weights of (E1), $c(\ell)$ may be replaced by $C_\flat\ell^3/(c'A_0^2)$, a power of $\ell$.
\end{itemize}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Contact extensions and mirror bounds]\label{bil:lim}
Let $g\le\gamma_1$ unless another range is given, and let
$\sigma=\sigma^T$, with cumulants $S_n^T$, be a limit through
periodic Gibbs states.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(F8)] (\emph{Coinciding points.}) Let $g\le\gamma_2$, $\mathsf b\in I(g)$, $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$, $n\ge2$. $S^{T,(\ell,\mathsf b)}_n$ extends to a symmetric, translation invariant distribution $\tilde S_n$ on $T_\ell^n$ of order $\le3n-2$ with
\[
|\tilde S_n(F)|\le C\mathsf b^{-n}\bigl(1+\log\tfrac{h_0}\lambda\bigr)^{8n\mathfrak p_0+1}\max_{|\gamma|\le3n-2}\lambda^{|\gamma|}\sup|\partial^\gamma F|
\]
for $F$ supported in a product of closed sup-balls of radius $\lambda\le h_0$ about any points, coinciding or not ($C,h_0$ of $g,\ell,n$); the lattice cumulants with their Taylor parts at the diagonals subtracted (Lem.~\ref{bil:ext}) obey this bound for all $K$ and all $8h_K\le\lambda\le h_0$, $h_K\le2C_W(K)a_K$ the least scale at the cutoff $K$, with one number for all cutoffs, and they converge to $\tilde S_n$ at every smooth $F$; two extensions with this bound differ by a sum $\sum_{|\pi|\le n-1}\sum_{|\alpha|\le3|\pi|}\partial^\alpha_\xi\delta_\pi\otimes T_{\pi,\alpha}$ of contact terms, and every such sum may be added; at $n=2$ the translation invariant, real, symmetric contact terms covariant under the cubic group form a space of dimension twelve, under $O(3)$ on $\mathbb R^3$ one of dimension six.

The reconstruction (the Hilbert space, the semigroup, the momenta and the kernels of {\cite[Lem.~D.13]{YMM2}}) uses the values of $\sigma$ at separated tuples alone, so no choice of the extension and no contact term enters it; beyond the separated tuples it rests on the insertion bound of \cite[Thm.~BZ(F2)(vi)]{YMM2}. For $g\le\gamma_1$ every limit point of $\langle Y[\varphi_1];Y[\varphi_2]\rangle_{K,\ell,\beta}$ as $K,\ell\to\infty$, $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$, in any order, is bounded at separated cubes by $36C^{\rm od}_\infty(g)(\inf b)^{-2}\sup|\varphi_1|\sup|\varphi_2|$, with no power of the distance and no logarithm, and so extends to $\mathbb R^6$ as a distribution of order $\le4$.
\item[(F9)] (\emph{Mirror bound in every state; the power $6$.}) Let $s(d)\le K$. If $X=A[O^T_K(H)]$ is carried in $B(x_0,d-2a_K)$ and $x_0$ is at a distance $\ge\frac32d$ from the plane of $\theta$, then $0\le\nu(\theta X\cdot X)\le C_\infty(g)\,b^{-2}|H|_\infty^2$ in every periodic Gibbs state $\nu$, $C_\infty(g)$ defined in \eqref{eq:bil-mirror-constants}; for a bond form $Y=Y[\mathsf w]$ with a complex weight carried there, $\nu(Y)=0$ and $0\le\nu(\overline{\theta Y}Y)\le36C^{\rm od}_\infty(g)b^{-2}|\mathsf w|_\infty^2$, with $C^{\rm od}_\infty(g)$ alone for real weights of one direction. For $H_1,H_2\in C_c(\mathbb R^3;V)$ with disjoint supports and off-diagonal values,
\[
\begin{multlined}
|\sigma(H_1,H_2)|\le A_6C^{\rm od}_\infty(g)\,\mathsf b^{-2}\iint\|H_1(x)\|_1\|H_2(y)\|_1\min\{|x-y|_\infty,3\}^{-6}\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y,\qquad\|E\|_1 \\
=\sum_{\lambda<\lambda'}|E_{\lambda\lambda'}|,
\end{multlined}
\]
$A_6=64\cdot36\cdot((8/\pi^3)32^3)^2$; for the whole tensor the same holds with a pure number $A$ in the place of $A_6$, with $C_\infty(g)$ in the place of $C^{\rm od}_\infty(g)$ and with $\|E\|_1=\sum_{\lambda\le\lambda'}|E_{\lambda\lambda'}|$; by (D5) the power $6$ is the true one.
\end{itemize}
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Matrices and corner forms]\label{bil:mat}
(a) For complex $2\times2$ matrices, with the operator norm: $|\langle X,Y\rangle|\le|X||Y|$; if $\det V=\det V'=1$ and $T$ is invertible, then $w(TVT^{-1})=Tw(V)T^{-1}$, $w(V^{-1})=-w(V)$, $|V^{-1}-\mathbf1|=|V-\mathbf1|$ and $|V^{-1}-V'^{-1}|=|V-V'|$; so $|w(V)|\le|V-\mathbf1|$ and $|w(V)-w(V')|\le|V-V'|$.

(b) For loops $l,l'$ of one cell the corner form $Q=\langle w(W_l),w(W_{l'})\rangle$ is a polynomial in the bond variables, $0$ at the trivial configuration, gauge invariant, and real at $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ configurations, where $|Q|\le a_{p(l)}+a_{p(l')}$. Let $\eta,b_0,b_1>0$ be arbitrary. At complex configurations with $|U(\mathsf e)|\le e^{\eta b_1}$ on the bonds of the cell and $|\partial U(p)-\mathbf1|<b_0\eta^2$ at its two plaquettes, $|Q|\le4e^{4t\eta b_1}b_0^2\eta^4$, $t=1$ at bonds and $t=2$ at sites. If $|U(\mathsf e)|\le e^{1/13}$ at the bonds of $p=p(l)$, $p'=p(l')$ and at their reverses, $|\partial U(p)-\mathbf1|\le\zeta_0$ and $|\partial U(p')-\mathbf1|\le\zeta_0$ with $e^{4/13}\zeta_0\le1$, and $B'$ is a $1$-form with $\rho=\max|B'|\le\frac1{128}$, then $|Q(e^{iB'}U)-Q(U)|\le784\rho^2+112e^{2t/13}\rho\zeta_0$. At the small points of a chart of height $i$, $|Q-\sigma(l)\sigma(l')\langle\mathrm{ang}_{p(l)},\mathrm{ang}_{p(l')}\rangle|\le12M_{\rm pl}^2\eta_i^4\mathsf{rt}^{-3}$, where $\mathrm{ang}_p$ is the angle of $p$ and $\mathsf{rt}\ge2$ is the quotient of the radii of the chart over the point (Lem.~\YMMref{124.4}{835}).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(a) The trace of a $2\times2$ matrix is the sum of two entries, each at most the norm. For $\det V=1$, $V^{-1}=(\mathrm{tr}\,V)\mathbf1-V$; so $V^{-1}-\mathbf1=(\mathrm{tr}\,E)\mathbf1-E$ with $E=V-\mathbf1$, and $V^{-1}-V'^{-1}=(\mathrm{tr}\,E)\mathbf1-E$ with $E=V-V'$; for $2\times2$ matrices $(\mathrm{tr}\,E)\mathbf1-E=JE^{\rm T}J^{-1}$ with the unitary $J=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}$, and $|E^{\rm T}|=|E|$; finally $w(V)=[(V-\mathbf1)-(V^{-1}-\mathbf1)]/2i$. (b) For $V=\exp(i\phi\,n\cdot\sigma)\in\mathrm{SU}(2)$, $w(V)=\sin\phi\;n\cdot\sigma$ and $\langle w(V),w(V)\rangle=\sin^2\phi\le2(1-\cos\phi)$, which with the Schwarz inequality for $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ gives $|Q|\le a_{p(l)}+a_{p(l')}$. The complex bounds follow from (a) applied to the holonomies of the two plaquettes; the bound on a shift and the second order follow from the expansion of the holonomy in the $1$-form and in the chart, $w(W_l)=\sigma(l)\,\mathrm{ang}_{p(l)}$ to the first order; every bound of a vector part at a complex configuration goes through (a).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Forms are sources]\label{bil:forms}
(a) Let $\bar k\ge1$ be an integer, the \emph{top index}. Call $F$ a \emph{source of top index $\bar k$ under the majorant} $(\mathsf s,S)$, $\mathsf s\ge0$ a number and $S$ a set of plaquettes, if $F$ is continuous, gauge invariant, $|F|\le L^K\mathsf s\sum_{p\in S}a_p$, and $F$ is the sum, at height $0$, of a family in the fourth place over a point (\S\ref{sec:step-input-conventions}) of size $\le c^\flat\mathsf m_0$, $c^\flat=81C_P^2C_{\mathcal A}^2/K_\Lambda$, and, at each height $1\le j\le\bar k$, of a family without base point (Def.~\YMMref{49.5}{375}) of size $\le\frac12\mathsf m_j$, $\mathsf m_j=12M^3\alpha_0^2L^{K-j}\mathsf s$, both vanishing on the regions that miss $S$. The top index is that of the data of the chain at which the source is used: the working level $\mathsf k$ for $n$ sources (Lems.~\ref{bil:nsrc} and~\ref{bil:prod}, where the chain runs up to the level $\mathsf k+1$), and $T-1$, $T$ the upper level, for two sources and for far pairs (Lems.~\ref{bil:two} and~\ref{bil:far}), where the one-step covariance of the level $j$, $\mathsf k<j\le T$, is formed with the members of the height $j-1$; since $n_T\ge2$, there $T-1>\mathsf k$.

A source is a source of the top index of the data at hand. Call it \emph{quadratic}, with the kernel $\mathsf t$, if besides $\mathsf t$ is a real symmetric function on $S\times S$ with $2\sum_{p'}|\mathsf t(p,p')|\le\mathsf s$ such that $|a_KF-\sum\mathsf t(p,p')\langle\mathrm{ang}_p,\mathrm{ang}_{p'}\rangle|\le M_{\rm pl}^2\eta_i^4\mathsf{rt}^{-3}(\#S)\mathsf s$ at the small points of the chart of height $i$. Then every form $F$ is a source under $(|F|_\star,S[F])$ of every top index, since it has its member at every height $j\ge1$ of the chain, linearly in its weights, and it is quadratic with the kernel $\mathsf t_F$ if it is real; a plaquette form with the weight $h$ is one under $(\sup|h|,\mathrm{supp}\,h)$, with $\mathsf t=\frac12h\delta$; for real weights at bonds or sites $2\sum_{p'}|\mathsf t_F(p,p')|\le8\|v\|$; $O^T_K(H)$ is one under $(60|H|_\infty,S_H)$, $S_H$ the plaquettes of its six forms, with $2\sum_{p'}|\mathsf t_H(p,p')|\le3|H|_\infty$.

Under sums the sizes add and the sets unite, and a source under $(\mathsf s,S)$ is one under $(\mathsf s',S)$ for every $\mathsf s'\ge\mathsf s$.

(b) The proof of the two-point law of the action density on a torus of small side (Thm.~\YMMref{AU}{847}), and the proofs of the statements on which it rests (Thm.~\YMMref{AT}{839}, Prop.~\YMMref{125.1}{838}, Lems.~\YMMref{125.2}{840}, \YMMref{125.4}{841} and~\YMMref{125.5}{842}; the weighted progression of Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{122.1}{826}}; the first step and the term of the history without large-field regions, the first-step part of {\cite[Lem.~B.19]{YMM2}} and Prop.~\YMMref{123.1}{829}; the quotients of the sources and of a step, their tower and the reduction of the covariance to one-step covariances, Prop.~\YMMref{123.1}{829} and equation~\YMMref{(2268)}{829}, the quotient definitions in {\cite[\S{}B.9]{YMM2}}, the quotient identities preceding equation~\YMMref{(2273)}{830}, equation~\YMMref{(2273)}{830}, {\cite[Lem.~B.20]{YMM2}} and Prop.~\YMMref{123.2}{830}; the carried family and the flat top, Prop.~\YMMref{123.3}{832}, equation~\YMMref{(2283)}{832}; and the sum over the level of the first creation, equation~\eqref{eq:ward-first-creation}), use the source only through the properties of (a) and its boundedness; they therefore apply to every source in the sense of (a) whose top index is that of the data of the statement applied, and to every quadratic source where the kernel is used.

(c) The step map and its Lipschitz bound hold for forms: for weights $v$, $v'$ at the cells the outputs of one step differ by at most $\theta^{[j]}8n_{\mathfrak c}e^{4t_{\mathfrak c}/13}M^3\alpha_0^2\|v-v'\|$ in the norms of the families of Def.~\YMMref{49.5}{375}, a pure number times the number for plaquette weights ($n_{\mathfrak c}=18$, $t_{\mathfrak c}=1$ at bonds; $n_{\mathfrak c}=7$, $t_{\mathfrak c}=2$ at sites); the step map depends only on its input array.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(a) The cubes of the partition of height $k$ that hold a corner of a plaquette of a cell form a connected region of at most $6$ (bond) or $7$ (site) cubes with a common corner, and a region of height $k$ serves at most $n_{\mathfrak c}M^3\eta_k^{-3}$ cells. At height $0$, with $\mathbf U$ the configuration of the bond variables and $B'$ the $1$-form in the fourth place, of which the family is a function, the family $\sum_{X_0(\mathsf c)=Y}[f_{\mathsf c}(e^{iB'}\mathbf U)-f_{\mathsf c}(\mathbf U)]$, $f_{\mathsf c}=\sum_{l,l'}v(\mathsf c,l,l')\langle w(W_l),w(W_{l'})\rangle$, $X_0(\mathsf c)$ the region of the cell, is holomorphic and gauge covariant, and Lem.~\ref{bil:mat}(b) bounds it at complex configurations; with the count, $n_{\mathfrak c}\cdot3138/(81\cdot12)\le59$, resp. $23$, it gives the size $c^\flat\mathsf m_0$ with the factor $59$, resp. $23$, of $|F|_\star$.

At height $j\ge1$ the member over a region $X$ is $\eta_j^{-1}\sum_{X_j(\mathsf c)=X}f_{\mathsf c}$, of size $\le\frac12\mathsf m_j$ by the same count. To second order $w(W_l)=\sigma(l)\,\mathrm{ang}_{p(l)}$, whence $\sum\mathsf t_F(p,p')\langle\Phi_p,\Phi_{p'}\rangle=\sum v(\mathsf c,l,l')\sigma(l)\sigma(l')\langle\Phi_{p(l)},\Phi_{p(l')}\rangle$, with the error of Lem.~\ref{bil:mat}(b). Finally $O^T_K(H)=a_K^{-1}\sum_pw_H(p)a_p+Y[\mathsf w_H]$ with the plaquette weight $w_H(p)=H_{\lambda(p)\lambda(p)}(x(p))$ and the bond weight $\mathsf w_H(\mathsf e)=H_{\lambda\lambda'}(x_{\mathsf e})$: a plaquette form of size $\le|H|_\infty$ and a bond form of size $\le59|H|_\infty$, whose sizes add to $60|H|_\infty$. (b) The source enters these proofs at four places.

First, through the clause on $F$ itself: its continuity and its gauge invariance in the first step, where the Wilson density is multiplied by $e^{F_\lambda}$, $F_\lambda=\sum_a\lambda_aF_a$ (the first-step part of {\cite[Lem.~B.19]{YMM2}}), and in the sum over the level of the first creation (equation~\eqref{eq:ward-first-creation}); its pointwise majorant, which bounds $F$ at the backgrounds of the small fields of the level $t$ by $L^K\mathsf s\sum_{p\in S}\sup a_p$, the supremum over these backgrounds, that is by the size of the source at the level $t$, and by $2L^K\mathsf s\,\#S$ at the height $0$, in the quotients, their tower, the reduction and the identity of the quotients (Prop.~\YMMref{123.1}{829} and equation~\YMMref{(2268)}{829}, the quotient identities preceding equation~\YMMref{(2273)}{830}, equation~\YMMref{(2273)}{830} and Prop.~\YMMref{123.2}{830}); it is the source of the power $2\mathfrak p_0$ of Lem.~\ref{bil:nsrc}.

Second, at the height $0$, through its family in the fourth place over a point and the size of that family (the height-zero part of {\cite[Prop.~B.8]{YMM2}}; here the clause of the height $0$ of (a)). Third, at the heights $1\le j\le\bar k$, through its families without base point, their sizes and the action formula ({\cite[Lem.~P.6]{YMM2}}), the one-step covariance of the level $j+1$ being formed with the member of the height $j$ ({\cite[Lem.~B.20]{YMM2}}); here the clause of the heights of (a), up to the top index. Fourth, at the second order at the small points of a chart, through its kernel (Lem.~\YMMref{124.4}{835}), in the carried family and the flat top (Props.~\YMMref{125.1}{838} and~\YMMref{123.3}{832}, equation~\YMMref{(2283)}{832}); here the kernel $\mathsf t$ of (a).

Every other step of these proofs is stated there for arbitrary bare arrays and local families, for bounded Borel functions of the field, or for numbers. (c) The step map is formed from its input array alone; its Lipschitz constant for the arrays of plaquette weights, with the count of (a) and Lem.~\ref{bil:mat}(b), gives the factor $8n_{\mathfrak c}e^{4t_{\mathfrak c}/13}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The kernel]\label{bil:ker}
Let $s'\le K$, $d\ge a_{s'}$, $\hat d=d/a_{s'}$, and $|u|=|x(p)-x(q)|\ge d$. Then
\[
|C^{\rm bg}_{K,s'}(p,q)-\epsilon_p\epsilon_qa_K^3K_3(u)_{\lambda(p)\lambda(q)}|\le(a_K/d)^3E_1,\qquad E_1=C_{\rm lat}[(a_K/d)^2+(d/\ell)^3]+C^{\rm fl}_\star\hat d^3e^{-\delta_{\rm tp}L\hat d/\sqrt3},
\]
$\epsilon_p=\pm1$ the orientation of $p$; so $|C^{\rm bg}(p,q)|\le C_{\mathsf k}(a_K/d)^3$, $C_{\mathsf k}=1+3C_{\rm lat}+C^{\rm fl}_\star C^{\rm tm}_\flat$, and in the form in which far pairs use it the same holds with $C'_{\mathsf k}=3^{3/2}C_{\rm tp}\mathsf S_3+C^{\rm bg}_{\rm tp}$. If $8a_K\le d$ and $4d<\ell$, a ball of radius $d$ holds at most $10(d/a_K)^3$ sites, at most as many centres of bonds of one direction, and as many centres of plaquettes of one normal.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The free kernel is the background kernel plus the fluctuation kernel $C^{\rm fl}_{K,s'}=\Pi_0-\Pi_{K-s'}$, the sum of the slices of the scales below $a_{s'}$ \YMMref{(2227)}{818}. The comparison of the lattice free kernel with $a_K^3K_3$, with the number $C_{\rm lat}$ of equation~\YMMref{(2245)}{824}, gives the first term of $E_1$, and the exponential decay of the fluctuation kernel beyond the scale $a_{s'}$, $|C^{\rm fl}_{K,s'}(p,q)|\le C^{\rm fl}_\star(a_K/a_{s'})^3e^{-\delta_{\rm tp}L\mathsf r/a_{s'}}$ for $\mathsf r=|x(p)-x(q)|_\infty\ge a_{s'}/\sqrt3$ (Prop.~\YMMref{120.6}{821} at $t_0=3^{-1/2}$), with $\mathsf r\ge d/\sqrt3$, gives the second; condition (H) fixes the constants, and $|K_3(u)_{\lambda\lambda'}|\le(2\pi)^{-1}|u|^{-3}$. The count is a count of lattice points in a ball.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[$n$ sources on a small torus]\label{bil:nsrc}
Let $0<g\le\gamma_2$, $n\ge2$, let $\ell$ be small, and let $s_{\rm th}(n)\le s(d)\le K$, where $s_{\rm th}(n)$ is the least integer $s\ge3$ with $2T_n(3)\theta(L^{s-2}g^{-2})\le1$, $\theta(t)=K_M(1+\beta_s)\delta(t)/\alpha_0$, which does not increase on $[e^P,\infty)$, $\delta(t)=A_1t^{-1/2}(\log t)^{\mathfrak p_0}$, and $T_n$ is the series {\cite[eq.~3]{YMM2}}. Let $(\mathsf s_a,S_a)$ be majorants with points $x_a$, $|x(p)-x_a|\le\frac78d$ on $S_a$, $|x(p)-x(q)|\ge\frac54d$ for $p\in S_a$, $q\in S_{a'}$, $a\ne a'$, and let $F_a$ be (complex) sources of top index $\mathsf k$, the working level, under them. Then
\[
|\langle F_1;\dots;F_n\rangle_\ell|\le k'_n(g,s(d))\,b^{-n}\prod_a\mathsf s_a,\qquad k'_n(g,s)\le C_n(g)Y_s^{8n\mathfrak p_0},
\]
so $k'_n(g,s(d))\le C_n(g)[2\log\frac1d+C(g)]^{8n\mathfrak p_0}$. No upper bound on the distances is asked.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Insert $F_\lambda=\sum_a\lambda_aF_a$ as the source into the weighted progression of {\cite[eq.~200]{YMM2}} (Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{122.1}{826}}). A chain rule for the step map in any number of parameters (Cauchy estimates on polydiscs) and locality give, for every set $\beta$ of $r=\#\beta\ge2$ sources: the mixed derivative $E^{(j)}_\beta=\partial_\beta E^{(j)}_\lambda|_0$ of the local family of level $j$ vanishes on the polymers that miss some $S_a$, $a\in\beta$, so that its norm is at most $e^{-4\beta_s\kappa[\mathsf D_j/M-2]_+}$ times its size $\mathsf d_{j,\beta}$; splitting into the top block and the rest, by induction on $r$ and on $j$, $\mathsf d_{j+1,\beta}\le c_\theta\hat G_r\prod_{a\in\beta}\hat g_{j,a}$, $\hat G_r$ given by a recursion in $r$ and $\hat g_{j,a}$ the sizes of the sources at the level $j$, as long as $\theta^{[j]}T_n(\mathsf D_j/M)\le\frac12$; the threshold $s_{\rm th}(n)$ gives this for $1\le j\le\mathsf k$, since $\mathsf D_j/M\ge3$ and $x_j>L^{s-2}g^{-2}$ there.

The chain runs up to the level $\mathsf k+1$, and its top index is the working level $\mathsf k$, so that the sources need their families without base point at the heights $1\le j\le\mathsf k$ alone. On the history without large fields, with $e^\Psi$ the density of the level $t\le\mathsf k$, $\Psi$ formed with the source $F_\lambda$, the identity $\partial_Be^\Psi=e^\Psi\sum_\pi\prod_{\beta\in\pi}\partial_\beta\Psi$ gives, almost everywhere and for any complex constants $c_a$,
\[
\Phi^{(t)}\Bigl[\prod_{a\in B}(F_a-c_a)\Bigr]=\sum_{\pi\in{\rm Part}(B)}\prod_{\beta\in\pi}\varkappa^{(t)}_\beta,\qquad\varkappa^{(t)}_{\{a\}}=\partial_a\Psi|_0-c_a,\qquad\varkappa^{(t)}_\beta=\partial_\beta\Psi|_0\quad(\#\beta\ge2),
\]
since the constants multiply the density by $e^{-\sum_a\lambda_ac_a}$; the blocks of two or more elements do not depend on the $c_a$, and all the blocks are bounded by the sizes \YMMref{(759)}{375}. The sum over the level $t$ of the first creation (equation~\eqref{eq:ward-first-creation}) adds the weights $\mathsf w_t\le2M^{-3}\ell^3L^{3(K-t)}e^{-\frac12c'p_0(g_t)^2}$ (Lem.~\YMMref{125.3}{841}), and on a small side $2M^{-3}\ell^3\le M^{-3}c'A_0^2Y_s^P$; the Gaussian decay in $K-t$ makes the sum converge. M\"obius inversion gives the cumulant from the moments of the $F_a-c_a$. These steps alone give a power of $\frac1d$: the sizes of the blocks hold the factor $x_{\mathsf k}^{r/2}\le\bar x_s^{r/2}$, and the sum over $t$ the factor $L^{3s}$.

Three estimates remove both factors. (i) $\hat d\ge4MY_s^P$ (Lem.~\YMMref{126.1}{844}, equation~\YMMref{(2323)}{844}), and corners of plaquettes of different sets $S_a$ are at the sup distance $\ge\frac5{4\sqrt3}d-a_K$; so $\mathsf D_{\mathsf k}/M\ge2Y_s^P$, as in Lem.~\YMMref{126.1}{844}, and a block of an order $r\ge2$ at the working level is at most a number times $\hat d^3(x_{\mathsf k}^{1/2}y^{\mathfrak p_0})^re^{-(\mathsf D_{\mathsf k}/M-2)}\prod_{a\in\beta}\upsilon\mathsf s_a$, in which $e^{2-2Y_s^P}\bar x_s^{r/2}=e^{2-2Y_s^P+rY_s/2}$ is bounded for $r\le n$ (at the levels $t<\mathsf k$ the blocks are larger by $L^{(3+r/2)(\mathsf k-t)}(\mathsf k-t+2)^{r\mathfrak p_0}$, and they enter the sum over $t$ alone). (ii) In the sum over $t$, $y_{\mathsf k-m}\ge y+m\log\frac{3L}4$ for $m\ge0$, $(y+u)^P\ge y^P+u^P$, and $u^P\ge u^2$ at $u=m\log\frac{3L}4$ give $e^{-\frac12c'p_0(g_{\mathsf k-m})^2}\le e^{-\frac12c'A_0^2y^P}e^{-\frac12c'A_0^2(m\log\frac{3L}4)^2}$; the first factor is kept, and as $y>Y^-_s=Y_s-\log(2L^3)$ (Lem.~\YMMref{126.1}{844}, equation~\YMMref{(2324)}{844}, equations~\YMMref{(2328)--(2336)}{846}, with the notation in \eqref{eq:short-distance-envelope-names}) it is at most $e^{-\frac12c'A_0^2(Y^-_s)^P}$, against which $L^{3s}\bar x_s^r$ is bounded. (iii) Take for $c_a$ the constant part of the first order of $F_a$ at the working level, $c_a=\sum_{i\le\mathsf k}\sum_{(X,z)}\dot E^{(i)}_a(X,\mathbf 1,z)$, $\dot E^{(i)}_a$ the derivative in $\lambda_a$ at $0$ of the local family of the level $i$.

Then the singleton $\varkappa^{(\mathsf k)}_{\{a\}}$ is the first-order part of $F_a$ at the block field of that level, at most its supremum over the small fields, the size $\mathsf X_{\mathsf k,a}\le\mathsf c_Xy^P\hat d^3\upsilon\mathsf s_a$ of the size definitions preceding and in Prop.~\YMMref{123.2}{830} (Lem.~\YMMref{125.2}{840}, equation~\YMMref{(2310)}{840}, at each pair of the majorants), plus an irrelevant part, smaller by a factor that tends to $0$ as $s\to\infty$; neither holds a factor $x_{\mathsf k}$. So the leading term of a moment is the product of the singletons, at most $\prod_aC\,Y_s^P(LC_W(s))^3\upsilon\mathsf s_a$; the partitions with a block of an order $\ge2$ and the sum over $t$ add at most a number of $n$ and $g$ times this, and with $\upsilon^2\le\frac98b^{-2}$ M\"obius inversion gives $k'_n(g,s)\le C_n(g)Y_s^{8n\mathfrak p_0}$.

Of the power $8\mathfrak p_0$ for each entry, $2\mathfrak p_0$ come from the supremum of $x_{\mathsf k}a_p$ over the small fields, of order $A_0^2y^{2\mathfrak p_0}$, and $6\mathfrak p_0$ from the number $\hat d^3<(LC_W(s))^3$ of the unit cubes of the working level in a ball of radius $d$. Of the side the proof reads the settings of the chain at the $n$ majorants, the conditions of the sum over the level of the first creation and the bound on the weights $\mathsf w_t$, which serves only to bound that sum. The weights enter only the tail term of each block of the M\"obius inversion, the sum over the level of the first creation in the moment of that block: linearly in their prefactor, and through the Gaussian sum of the estimate (ii) above, in which $e^{-c''p_0(g_t)^2}$ with $c''\ge\frac12c'$ may stand for $e^{-\frac12c'p_0(g_t)^2}$.

As the settings and the conditions hold on every admissible side for $K\ge3$ (Step~14), the lemma holds on every admissible side, for $K\ge3$ and weights $\mathsf w_t\le\mathsf LL^{3(K-t)}e^{-c''p_0(g_t)^2}$, $1\le t\le K$, $c''\ge\frac12c'$, with the factor $\max\{1,M^3\mathsf L/(c'A_0^2)\}^n$ on $k'_n$: as $Y_s\ge1$, each block gains at most the factor $\max\{1,M^3\mathsf L/(c'A_0^2)\}$ over the tail of a small side, and there are at most $n$ blocks (Thm.~\ref{thm:bil}(E3)).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[As many sources as unit cubes]\label{bil:prod}
Let $0<g'\le\gamma_2$, $(K',\beta)$ a first-passage datum at $g'$, $\ell$ a side small over its running couplings, $0<d<1$ with $s=s(d)\le K'$, the depth, the working level and $\upsilon$ being formed at $g'$, and let $n$ be an integer with $2\le n\le\ell^3$. Let $(\mathsf s_a,S_a)$, $1\le a\le n$, be majorants placed as in Lem.~\ref{bil:nsrc} and $F_a$ sources of top index $\mathsf k$, the working level, under them, and suppose
\[
2Y_s^P\ge u_*(n),\qquad y_{K'}\ge2\log L+\mathfrak p_0\log3,\qquad L^{3s}\le x_{K'}^{20},
\]
where $u_*(n)=\max\{4,(2/A_\kappa)(n[c_1+\log(c^*n)]+\log3)\}\le Cn\log(en)$, $A_\kappa=4\beta_s\kappa$, $c^*=\max\{4,\frac12c^\flat\}$, $c_1$ a number of the constants. Then there are complex numbers $c_a$ such that for every nonempty $B\subset\{1,\dots,n\}$
\[
\Bigl|\Bigl\langle\prod_{a\in B}(F_a-c_a)\Bigr\rangle_{K',\ell,\beta}\Bigr|\le\prod_{a\in B}\mathsf A_n(s)\upsilon\mathsf s_a,\qquad\mathsf A_n(s)\le Cn^{4+\mathfrak p_0}(LC_W(s))^3\bar x_sY_s^P .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
It is the proof of Lem.~\ref{bil:nsrc} with two changes. First, the mixed derivative families of every order $r\le n$ are bounded with the numbers $(c^*r)^r$ in the place of $\hat G_r$, by Cauchy estimates on polydiscs of radii proportional to $1/r$; for this it suffices that $T_m(u)(c^*m)^m\le1$ for $2\le m\le n$ at $u=\mathsf D_j/M$, which holds as soon as $u\ge4$ and $\frac12A_\kappa u\ge m[c_1+\log(c^*m)]+\log3$, so for $u\ge u_*(n)$, and the first hypothesis gives $\mathsf D_j/M\ge u_*(n)$. Second, the moments are bounded directly, from the conditional cumulants at the upper level and the sum over the partitions, and not through the cumulants of the sources; the sum over the level of the first creation (equation~\eqref{eq:ward-first-creation}) is bounded by the count of the cubes of a small side, through the last two hypotheses. Hence a bound in product form, with no factorial in $n$ beyond the power in $\mathsf A_n(s)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Two sources at one scale]\label{bil:two}
(a) Let $g\le\gamma_2$, $\ell$ small, $s_1(g)\le s(d)\le K$, $3d\le|x_1-x_2|\le4d$, and let $(F_a,\mathsf t_a)$ be real quadratic sources of top index $T-1$ under $(\mathsf s_a,S_a)$ in the sense of Lem.~\ref{bil:forms}(a), with their families without base point at the heights $1\le j\le T-1$, $T$ the upper level (forms have a member at every height $j\ge1$), $S_a$ within $d-a_K$ of $x_a$. Then
\[
\begin{multlined}
\Bigl|\langle F_1;F_2\rangle_\ell-6\upsilon^2\sum\mathsf t_1(p,p')\mathsf t_2(q,q')C^{\rm bg}(p,q)C^{\rm bg}(p',q')\Bigr|\le\varepsilon^\natural_g(s(d))\upsilon^2\mathsf s_1\mathsf s_2,\qquad|\langle F_1;F_2\rangle_\ell| \\
\le C^\sharp_g(s(d))\upsilon^2\mathsf s_1\mathsf s_2,
\end{multlined}
\]
where $\varepsilon^\natural_g(s)=\varepsilon^\flat_g(s)+2(1+A_1)^4\mathsf C_5s^2(LC_W(s))^6Y_s^{2P}{\rm sm}_g(s)$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon^\flat_g(s)={}&(\mathsf C_2+\mathsf C_3)(Y^-_s)^{-2\mathfrak p_0}+\mathsf C_3\,s\,(Y^-_s)^{-5\mathfrak p_0}\\
&+\mathsf C_6(Y^-_s)^{-6\mathfrak p_0}+\mathsf C_8\bigl((LC_W(s))^3+1\bigr)(Y^-_s)^{-9\mathfrak p_0}\\
&+4\mathsf c_X^2(Y^-_s)^{-14\mathfrak p_0}\\
&+(\mathsf C'_B+\mathsf C_7+\mathsf C'_3+\mathsf C''_3+\mathsf C_6)\,s^4(LC_W(s))^6Y_s^{11\mathfrak p_0}{\rm sm}_g(s),
\end{aligned}
\]
$Y^-_s=Y_s-\log(2L^3)$ and ${\rm sm}_g$ the functions of equations~\YMMref{(2328)--(2336)}{846}, with the notation in \eqref{eq:short-distance-envelope-names}, $\mathsf C_i$ the constants of Lem.~\YMMref{125.5}{842}, with the convention in \eqref{eq:short-distance-constants}--\eqref{eq:short-distance-collected-constants}: $\varepsilon^\flat_g$ bounds all the errors of the proof but those of the Gaussian values at the flat top, which the second summand bounds, and both tend to $0$ as $s\to\infty$ (the decay argument preceding equation~\YMMref{(2332)}{846}); and 
\[
C^\sharp_g(s)=\mathsf C_2(LC_W(s))^6Y_s^{2P}+4\mathsf c_X^2+\mathsf C'_Bs^4(LC_W(s))^6Y_s^{6\mathfrak p_0}{\rm sm}_g(s)\le C(g)Y_s^{16\mathfrak p_0}.
\]


(b) Let $\ell$ be admissible, $K\ge3$, $s=s(d)\le K$, $\mathsf{Lm}_s\le L^{s-3}$, $x^-_s\ge e^P$; then the settings of the chain hold at the levels $\mathsf k<j_1\le T\le K-2$, with $n_T\le s$, $676a_K\le d$, $20d<\ell$, $M\le\hat d<LC_W(s)$. Let $|x_1-x_2|\ge3d$, $|L^{-1}x_{t-1}-x_t|\le B_\sharp$ for all $t$, $B_\sharp$ the flow bound of the running couplings and $\bar B=LB_\sharp/(L-1)$ (Section~\YMMref{74}{614}), $y_K\ge2\log(1+\bar B)$; let $\mathsf L\ge0$, $c>0$ with $\mathsf w_t\le\mathsf LL^{3(K-t)}e^{-cp_0(g_t)^2}$ ($t\le T$), $\mathsf W_T\le\mathsf LL^{3(K-T)}e^{-cp_0(g_T)^2}$, $2c\mathfrak p_0A_0^2y^{P-1}\ge13$, and ${\rm sm}^{\mathsf L,c}_T\le1$. Then on $T_\ell$ the error in (a) is at most
\[
\bigl\{(\mathsf C_2+\mathsf C_3)y^{-2\mathfrak p_0}+\mathsf C_3n_Ty^{-5\mathfrak p_0}+\mathsf C_6y^{-6\mathfrak p_0}+\mathsf C_8(\hat d^3+1)y^{-9\mathfrak p_0}+4\mathsf c_X^2y^{-14\mathfrak p_0}+\mathsf C^e_Bn_T^4\hat d^6y^{15\mathfrak p_0}{\rm sm}^{\mathsf L,c}_T\bigr\}\upsilon^2\mathsf s_1\mathsf s_2,
\]
and the remainder ${\rm Rest}'_T$ of the proof of (a) obeys $|{\rm Rest}'_T|\le\bigl[4\mathsf c_X^2y^{-14\mathfrak p_0}+\mathsf C'_Bn_T^4\hat d^6y^{6\mathfrak p_0}{\rm sm}^{\mathsf L,c}_T\bigr]\upsilon^2\mathsf s_1\mathsf s_2$; for two plaquette weights $\mathsf C^{(1)}_B$ may replace $\mathsf C'_B$.

(c) In the setting of (a), almost everywhere at the upper level $T$ and for all the quotients,
\[
\bigl|\Phi^{(T)}[F_1F_2]-\Phi^{(T)}[F_1]\,\Phi^{(T)}[F_2]-G\bigr|\le\varepsilon_g(s(d))\,\upsilon^2\mathsf s_1\mathsf s_2,
\]
$G=6\upsilon^2\sum\mathsf t_1(p,p')\mathsf t_2(q,q')C^{\rm bg}(p,q)C^{\rm bg}(p',q')$ the Gaussian value of (a) and $\varepsilon_g=\epsilon_g$ the error function in equation~\YMMref{(2330)}{846}, with the coefficient fixed in Lem.~\ref{lem:short-distance-collected-constant}; and almost everywhere at every level $j\le T$ the conditional covariance $\Phi^{(j)}[F_1F_2]-\Phi^{(j)}[F_1]\Phi^{(j)}[F_2]$ is at most the crude size $\mathsf M'_j$ of the size definitions preceding and in Prop.~\YMMref{123.2}{830}, formed at the majorants, which Lem.~\YMMref{125.2}{840} bounds by $[\mathsf m_\star L^{4n}(n+1)^{2\mathfrak p_0}+2n_T\mathsf{sb}_0^2]\upsilon^2\mathsf s_1\mathsf s_2$, $n=[\mathsf k-j]_+$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(a) The covariance is a sum of one-step covariances plus a rest, $\langle F_1;F_2\rangle=\sum_{\mathsf k<j\le T}{\rm qm}_j+{\rm Rest}'_T$, ${\rm qm}_j=\int{\rm Qt}_j[X_{j-1,1};X_{j-1,2}]\,\mathrm{d}\mathsf m_{j|T}$, with the step quotients ${\rm Qt}_j$ of the quotient definitions in {\cite[\S{}B.9]{YMM2}}, their measures $\mathsf m_{j|T}$ and the first-order parts $X_{j-1,a}$ of the sources (Prop.~\YMMref{123.2}{830}, which holds for these sources by Lem.~\ref{bil:forms}(b)). The steps $j_1<j\le T$ are bounded crudely, by $2\mathsf X_{j-1,1}\mathsf X_{j-1,2}$ each: the error $\mathsf{Er}_2$ of equation~\YMMref{(2307)}{839}. For $\mathsf k<j\le j_1$ the one-step covariance is almost everywhere the total of the mixed derivative family $\mathsf K^{(j)}$ of the step $j$ ({\cite[Lem.~B.20]{YMM2}}); carried to the upper level $T$ (Prop.~\YMMref{123.3}{832}) and evaluated at the trivial background it is the number $\mathsf{sum}^{(j)}_T$, up to the error $\mathsf{Ft}^{(j)}_T$ of the flat top, which holds at every point of the small-field set of the level $T$ (Prop.~\YMMref{123.3}{832}, equation~\YMMref{(2283)}{832}, in its sup-norm form); the mass $1-\mathsf W_T$ of $\mathsf m_{T|T}$ costs $\mathsf W_T(\bar{\mathsf n}^{\rm G}_j+\mathsf e_{j,T})$; and $\mathsf{sum}^{(j)}_T$ is the Gaussian number $\mathsf n^{\rm G}_{j,T}$ up to the error $\mathsf e_{j,T}$ of equations~\YMMref{(2303)--(2305)}{838} (Prop.~\YMMref{125.1}{838}).

With kernels $\mathsf t_a$ in the place of $\frac12w_a\delta$ this proof reads the source at three places alone: the covariance of one step at a triple is the covariance of the first-order variations of the two sources under the fluctuation measure of that step; the second order of a source at a small point of the chart is the quadratic form of its kernel; and the forms of the slices are built with the kernels. So it gives the Gaussian numbers $2(N^2-1)\upsilon_j^2\sum\mathsf t_1(p,p')\mathsf t_2(q,q')\mathcal C_{(j)}(p,q)\mathcal C_{(j)}(p',q')+4(N^2-1)\sum_{j<i'\le T}\upsilon_j\upsilon_{i'}\sum\mathsf t_1(p,p')\mathsf t_2(q,q')\mathcal C_{(j)}(p',q')\mathcal C_{(i')}(p,q)$, with the same errors $\mathsf e_{j,T}$ and the same constants, for every real quadratic source, the bond forms under $(59\sup|\mathsf w|,S[\mathsf w])$ among them (Lem.~\ref{bil:forms}(a)).

The Gaussian numbers sum to $6\upsilon^2\sum\mathsf t_1\mathsf t_2DD$, $D=\sum_{\mathsf k<j\le T}\mathcal C_{(j)}=\Pi_{\mathsf k}-\Pi_T$, since the slices telescope and the terms $(j,i')$, $(i',j)$ agree under the symmetry of the kernels, and $C^{\rm bg}=\Pi_{\mathsf k}$; the Gaussian numbers above $j_1$, the replacing of the couplings $\upsilon_j$ of the steps by $\upsilon$ and the dropping of $\Pi_T$, with $|\Pi_T(p,q)|\le C^{\rm bg}_{\rm tp}\eta_T^3$ (Prop.~\YMMref{120.5}{821}), cost the errors $\mathsf{Er}_6$, $\mathsf{Er}_7$, $\mathsf{Er}_8$ of equation~\YMMref{(2307)}{839}. With the deposit inequality $L^{3a}\mathsf e_{\mathsf k-a}\le L^{-10a}\mathsf e_{\mathsf k}$, $\mathsf e_k=e^{-\frac12c'p_0(g_k)^2}$ (the proof of Lem.~\YMMref{125.4}{841}; its hypotheses
hold by equation~\YMMref{(2326)}{845} and the logarithmic
floors immediately following that equation),
\[
|{\rm Rest}'_T|\le\bigl[4\mathsf c_X^2y^{-14\mathfrak p_0}+\mathsf C'_Bn_T^4\hat d^6y^{6\mathfrak p_0}{\rm sm}_T\bigr]\upsilon^2\mathsf s_1\mathsf s_2 .
\]
Collected, the left member of (a) is at most $|{\rm Rest}'_T|+\mathsf{Er}_2+\sum_{\mathsf k<j\le j_1}\mathsf{Ft}^{(j)}_T+\mathsf W_T\sum_{\mathsf k<j\le j_1}\bar{\mathsf n}^{\rm G}_j+2\sum_{\mathsf k<j\le j_1}\mathsf e_{j,T}+\mathsf{Er}_6+\mathsf{Er}_7+\mathsf{Er}_8$. By the bounds of the errors at the attached levels (Lem.~\YMMref{125.5}{842}), with $Y^-_s<y\le Y_s$ (Lem.~\YMMref{126.1}{844}, equation~\YMMref{(2324)}{844}), $1\le n_T\le s$, $\hat d<LC_W(s)$ and ${\rm sm}_T\le{\rm sm}_g(s)$, all these terms but the sum of the $\mathsf e_{j,T}$ are together at most $\varepsilon^\flat_g(s)\upsilon^2\mathsf s_1\mathsf s_2$, and $2\sum_{\mathsf k<j\le j_1}\mathsf e_{j,T}\le2(1+A_1)^4\mathsf C_5s^2(LC_W(s))^6Y_s^{2P}{\rm sm}_g(s)\upsilon^2\mathsf s_1\mathsf s_2$.

The crude bound is the same sum with the Gaussian numbers bounded by their sizes. (b) In the proof of (a) the side enters only through the weights $\mathsf w_t$ and the sum over the level of the first creation (equation~\eqref{eq:ward-first-creation}), and the distance only through a lower bound; the factor $e^{-cp_0(g_t)^2}$ is used at three places alone: in the deposit inequality at $c$, in its monotonicity in $t$,
and in the bound on $\mathsf w_t$. For the first, the proof of
Lem.~\YMMref{125.4}{841} applies with $c'/2$ replaced by $c$.
To make this substitution explicit, put $P=2\mathfrak p_0$,
$y=y_{\mathsf k}$ and
$\Delta=y_{\mathsf k-a}-y$ for $1\le a\le\mathsf k$.
The flow bound and $y_K\ge2\log(1+\bar B)$ give
\[
 \Delta\ge a\log L+\log(1-\bar B/x_{\mathsf k})>2a,
 \qquad
 y(a\log L-\Delta)
 \le\frac8{3e}\frac{\bar B}{1+\bar B}<1.
\]
Keeping the linear and quadratic terms of the power gives
\[
 (y+\Delta)^P-y^P
 \ge Py^{P-1}a\log L
   +Py^{P-2}\left[\frac{P-1}{2}\Delta^2
                         -y(a\log L-\Delta)\right]
 \ge Py^{P-1}a\log L.
\]
Thus, for $\mathsf e_j=e^{-cp_0(g_j)^2}$,
\[
 L^{3a}\mathsf e_{\mathsf k-a}
 \le L^{-(2c\mathfrak p_0A_0^2y^{P-1}-3)a}
               \mathsf e_{\mathsf k}
 \le L^{-10a}\mathsf e_{\mathsf k}.
\]
The case $a=0$ is immediate. This uses exactly the rate condition
$2c\mathfrak p_0A_0^2y^{P-1}\ge13$ in (b), at the working
level $\mathsf k$; no stronger rate condition at $K$ is needed. The settings follow from the arithmetic of the working level under the two depth conditions, the flow bound and the lower bound on $y_K$. (c) A block of two is the conditional covariance $\Phi^{(n)}_{12}=\Phi^{(n)}[F_1F_2]-\Phi^{(n)}[F_1]\Phi^{(n)}[F_2]$.

Almost everywhere, by the tower of the quotients (equation~\YMMref{(2273)}{830}), $\Phi^{(n)}_{12}={\rm Qt}_n[\Phi^{(n-1)}_{12}]+{\rm Qt}_n[\Phi^{(n-1)}[F_1];\Phi^{(n-1)}[F_2]]$, and $\Phi^{(n-1)}[F_a]$ is a constant plus the first-order part $X_{n-1,a}$ plus an irrelevant part (equation~\YMMref{(2267)}{829} and Prop.~\YMMref{123.1}{829}); this gives the crude bound at every level (the proof of Prop.~\YMMref{123.2}{830}, through Lem.~\ref{bil:forms}(b)). For $\mathsf k<j\le j_1$ the one-step covariance ${\rm Qt}_j[X_{j-1,1};X_{j-1,2}]$ is almost everywhere the total $\mathsf F^{(j)}_j$ of the family $\mathsf K^{(j)}$ ({\cite[Lem.~B.20]{YMM2}}), and ${\rm Qt}_{i+1}[\mathsf F^{(j)}_i]=\mathsf F^{(j)}_{i+1}$ almost everywhere (the proof of Prop.~\YMMref{123.3}{832}).

So, by induction on $n$ from $\mathsf k$ to $T$, the remainder $R_n=\Phi^{(n)}_{12}-\sum_{\mathsf k<j\le\min\{n,j_1\}}\mathsf F^{(j)}_n$ is almost everywhere at most $\mathsf M_{\mathsf k}$, plus twice the products of the sizes of the first-order and of the irrelevant parts at the levels $\mathsf k\le j<n$, plus twice the products of the sizes of the first-order parts at the steps above $j_1$. At $n=T$ the measure $\mathsf m_T$ is carried by the small-field set of the level $T$, at every point of which $\mathsf F^{(j)}_T$ is within $\mathsf{Ft}^{(j)}_T$ of the number $\mathsf{sum}^{(j)}_T$ (Prop.~\YMMref{123.3}{832}, equation~\YMMref{(2283)}{832}, before any integration); $\mathsf{sum}^{(j)}_T$ is $\mathsf n^{\rm G}_{j,T}$ up to $\mathsf e_{j,T}$, and the Gaussian numbers give $G$ up to $\mathsf{Er}_6+\mathsf{Er}_7+\mathsf{Er}_8$, as in (a).

No sum over the levels of the first creation enters, so that there are no tails and no weight $\mathsf W_T$: the error is at most the bracket of Cor.~\YMMref{125.6}{843} times $\upsilon^2\mathsf s_1\mathsf s_2$, and with $Y^-_s<y\le Y_s$, $n_T\le s$, $\hat d<LC_W(s)$ and ${\rm sm}_T\le{\rm sm}_g(s)$ this bracket is at most $\varepsilon_g(s)$, term by term.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Symmetries and copies]\label{bil:sym}
(a) For a lattice isometry $r$ with $re_\mu=s_\mu e_{\pi(\mu)}$: $q_{(r\mathsf e)^+}(rU)=s_\lambda s_{\lambda'}q_{\mathsf e}(U)$, $\lambda<\lambda'$ the directions other than that of $\mathsf e$; so $rO^T_K(H)=O^T_K(rH)$, and there is a linear bijection $r^\sharp$ of the weights, with $\|r^\sharp v\|=\|v\|$, real weights kept real and carriers and sets $S[\cdot]$ carried by $r$, such that the image of a form is the form of the same kind with the weight $r^\sharp v$; in particular $Y[r^\sharp\mathsf w](rU)=Y[\mathsf w](U)$ and $\theta Y[\mathsf w]=Y[\theta^\sharp\mathsf w]$.

(b) A law that is invariant under the reflections in the site planes has $\nu(q_{\mathsf e})=0$; all laws are such, so $\nu(Y[\mathsf w])=0$.

(c) For a board of side $\mathsf l_0$ and $\ell_0=2\mathsf l_0$, a form whose carrier lies in a cell at a distance $\ge\rho>a_K$ from the walls is a function of the cell; its copies on $T_{\ell_0}$ are forms of the same kind, size and mean, with the mirror images as carriers; copies in different cells of a period box are $\ge2\rho$ apart, two in one cell at the original distance.

(d) If $3d\le|x_0-y_0|\le4d$, the midpoint is within $\frac{a_K}2$ of the offset of the board of side $\mathsf l$ in each coordinate, and the weights are carried within $d-2a_K$ of $x_0$, $y_0$, then the corners of their plaquettes lie within the sup distance $3d$ of the centre of the cell, and the sixteen copies on $T_{\ell'}$ form eight pairs, partners $3d$ to $4d$ apart, different pairs at sup distance $\ge\mathsf l-6d\ge11M$, the suprema of the weights kept; the same holds for tensor weights and arbitrary majorants.

(e) For majorants with plaquettes within $d-a_K$ of $x_0$, $y_0$, $3d\le|x_0-y_0|\le4d$, the tents $\tilde f_a=\mathsf s_a\sum_{p\in S_a}\max\{0,1-2a_K^{-1}|u-x(p)|_\infty\}$ are Lipschitz, equal $\mathsf s_a\mathbf1_{S_a}$ at the barycentres, have their supports in $B(x_a,d)$, and $d\le{\rm dist}(\mathrm{supp}\,\tilde f_1,\mathrm{supp}\,\tilde f_2)\le6d$. Let besides $0<g\le\gamma_2$, $(K,\beta)$ a first-passage datum at $g$, $\ell$ small, $0<d<1$ and $s_1(g)\le s=s(d)\le K$, so that $\mathsf{Lm}_s\le L^{s-3}$ and $x^-_s\ge e^P$ (equation~\YMMref{(2331)}{846}). Then $s\ge3$, $2\le\mathsf k\le K-1$, $M\le L^{-2}C_W(s)\le\hat d<LC_W(s)$, $\mathsf D_{\mathsf k}\ge3M$ for the pair, $20d\le\ell$, and the middle and the upper level have $\mathsf k<j_1\le T\le K-2$, $1\le n_T\le s$, $L^{n_T}<\mathsf{Lm}_s$, $x_T>x^-_s$.

Let $n\ge1$ pairs of such majorants be given, $p=2n$, the corners of plaquettes of different pairs at the sup distance $\ge11M$. Then $\mathsf D_{\mathsf k}$, the least over all $a\ne a'$, is $\ge3M$: partners give $3M$, members of different pairs $11ML^{K-\mathsf k}$. The settings of the chain for the $p$ sources hold with the top index $T-1$, with the smallness conditions at the heights $0,\dots,T-1$ and $d_*(t)\ge3$ for $1\le t\le T$; the levels, the lattices, the histories, the measures and the quotients of the chain are the same for all pairs, and for the chain of each pair alone, and do not depend on the sources; and $\theta^{[j]}T_p(\mathsf D_j/M)\le\frac12$ for $1\le j<T$ as soon as
\[
{\rm th}_{g,p}(s)=2s^{2+p\mathfrak p_0}\mathsf{Lm}_s^{p/2-1}T^+_p\,\theta(x^-_s)\le1,\qquad T^+_p=T_p(3)+(\tfrac43)^{p/2}L,
\]
$\theta$ the function of Lem.~\ref{bil:nsrc}; ${\rm th}_{g,p}(s)$ tends to $0$ as $s\to\infty$, being a power of $s$ times $L^{-s/2}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(a) $r$ carries the loops at $\mathsf e$ to those at $r\mathsf e$; reversal sends $w(V)$ to $w(V^{-1})=-w(V)$, conjugation keeps $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$, and the sign is the product of the signs of the two vectors $u_\lambda$, $u_{\lambda'}$. (b) The reflection in the site plane through $x_{\mathsf e}$ normal to $\lambda$ flips $s_\lambda$ alone, so that it changes the sign of $q_{\mathsf e}$; torus measures are invariant under it, periodic Gibbs states by Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{103.4}{758}}. (c) Each coordinate of a copy lies between two consecutive walls, at a distance $\ge\rho$ from both, and the mean is kept by the invariance of $\tilde\mu_{\ell_0}$ under the lattice isometries. (d) The corners lie within the sup distance $3d$ of the centre of the cell, and $\mathsf l\ge LM$. (e) A tent is carried within $\frac{\sqrt3}2a_K$ of its barycentre and vanishes at the other barycentres; the supports need not come near the centres, which is why only $d\le{\rm dist}\le6d$ holds, and nothing uses an upper bound on the distance.

The settings and the numbers come from the arithmetic of the working level (Lem.~\YMMref{126.1}{844}) and from Lem.~\YMMref{126.2}{845}, by which the objects of the construction satisfy the settings of the chain; neither involves a source, and of the majorants the settings for the $p$ sources read the weights $\mathsf s_a\mathbf 1_{S_a}$ and the bound $\mathsf D_{\mathsf k}\ge3M$ alone. \emph{The threshold.} $T_p(u)=\sum_{n'\ge1}(\frac43)^{p/2}(n'+1)^{1+p\mathfrak p_0}L^{1+(p/2-1)n'}e^{-4\beta_s\kappa[L^{n'-1}u-2]_+}$ does not increase. If $L^qu\ge3$, $q\ge1$, the $q$ terms with $n'\le q$ are each at most $(\frac43)^{p/2}(q+1)^{1+p\mathfrak p_0}L^{1+(p/2-1)q}$, and the term of the index $n'=q+n''$ is at most $(q+1)^{1+p\mathfrak p_0}L^{(p/2-1)q}$ times the term of the index $n''$ of $T_p(3)$, as $n'+1\le(q+1)(n''+1)$ and $L^{n'-1}u\ge3L^{n''-1}$; so $T_p(u)\le(q+1)^{2+p\mathfrak p_0}L^{(p/2-1)q}T^+_p$.

For $1\le j\le\mathsf k$, $\mathsf D_j/M\ge3$ and $T_p(\mathsf D_j/M)\le T_p(3)\le T^+_p$; for $\mathsf k<j<T$, $q=j-\mathsf k\le n_T-1$ has $L^q\mathsf D_j/M=\mathsf D_{\mathsf k}/M\ge3$, $q+1\le n_T\le s$ and $L^{(p/2-1)q}<\mathsf{Lm}_s^{p/2-1}$. And $\theta^{[j]}=\theta(x_j)\le\theta(x^-_s)$, since $x_j\ge x_T>x^-_s\ge e^P$ and $\theta$ does not increase on $[e^P,\infty)$. So $\theta^{[j]}T_p(\mathsf D_j/M)\le\frac12{\rm th}_{g,p}(s)\le\frac12$ for $1\le j<T$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Far pairs; centred sources]\label{bil:far}
Let $0<g\le\gamma_2$, $\ell$ small, $n\ge1$, $p=2n$, $s=s(d)\le K$. For pairs $\tau\le n$ let $3d\le|z_{(\tau,1)}-z_{(\tau,2)}|\le4d$, let the majorants have their plaquettes within $d-a_K$ of $z_a$, and let corners of plaquettes of different pairs be at sup distance $\ge11M$; let $(F_a,\mathsf t_a)$ be real quadratic sources of top index $T-1$ under the majorants, with their families without base point at the heights $1\le j\le T-1$ (as forms have them), $\tilde F_a=F_a-\langle F_a\rangle_\ell$, $\tilde P_J=\prod_{\tau\in J}\tilde F_{(\tau,1)}\tilde F_{(\tau,2)}$, $G_\tau$ the Gaussian value of the pair, $\hat m_a=\upsilon\mathsf s_a$, $\hat m_\tau=\hat m_{(\tau,1)}\hat m_{(\tau,2)}$, $\hat m_J=\prod_{\tau\in J}\hat m_\tau$. For $s\ge s_p(g)$, a first depth $\ge s_1(g)$, and all nonempty $J$ and $B$:
\[
|\langle\tilde P_J\rangle_\ell-\textstyle\prod_JG_\tau|\le\omega'_{g,p}(s)\hat m_J,\qquad|\langle\tilde P_J\rangle_\ell-\prod_J\langle\tilde P_\tau\rangle_\ell|\le\omega'^\sharp_{g,p}(s)\hat m_J,\qquad|G_\tau|\le g_0\hat m_\tau;
\]
if $N_2$ pairs lie in $B$ and $N_1$ meet it in one element,
\[
\Bigl|\Bigl\langle\prod_B\tilde F_a\Bigr\rangle_\ell\Bigr|\le\bigl[e_g(s)^{N_1}(g_0+\delta_g(s))^{N_2}+\mathrm{Bl}(p){\rm far}_{g,p}(s)(1+g_0+\varepsilon_g(s))^n+{\rm tl}_{g,p}(s)\bigr]\prod_B\hat m_a,
\]
so that this mean is $\le o_{g,p}(s)\prod_B\hat m_a$, $o_{g,p}=e_g+\mathrm{Bl}(p){\rm far}_{g,p}(1+g_0+\varepsilon_g)^n+{\rm tl}_{g,p}$, if $B$ holds no pair, and $\le{\rm Mo}_{g,p}(s)\prod_B\hat m_a$ in every case, $\sup_{s\ge s_p(g)}{\rm Mo}_{g,p}(s)<\infty$; $Y_s^P\omega'^\sharp_{g,p}(s)$ is bounded. Here
\[
\begin{multlined}
\omega'_{g,p}=n\delta_g(1+g_0+\delta_g)^{n-1}+\mathrm{Bl}(p){\rm far}_{g,p}(1+g_0+\varepsilon_g)^n+{\rm sm}_g(1+g_0)^n+{\rm tl}_{g,p},\qquad\omega'^\sharp_{g,p} \\
=\omega'_{g,p}\bigl[1+n(1+g_0+\omega'_{g,p})^{n-1}\bigr],
\end{multlined}
\]
with $g_0=\frac32 81^2C'^2_{\mathsf k}$ for arbitrary majorants and $g_0=422C'^2_{\mathsf k}$ for majorants of bond weights of one direction. For bond forms $Y[\mathsf w_a]$ with real weights on the bonds of one direction, whose means vanish, $|G_\tau|\le106C'^2_{\mathsf k}\upsilon^2\sup|\mathsf w_{(\tau,1)}|\sup|\mathsf w_{(\tau,2)}|$, and the same functions at $g_0=106C'^2_{\mathsf k}/59^2$, written $\omega_{g,p}$, $\omega^\sharp_{g,p}$, serve in units of $\hat m_a=59\upsilon\sup|\mathsf w_a|$. Here ${\rm far}_{g,p}(s)=C^{\rm far}_p(LC_W(s))^3\bar x_s^{p/2}Y_s^{p\mathfrak p_0}e^{-11L^{s-2}/\mathsf{Lm}_s}$, $\varepsilon_g$ is the error function of equations~\YMMref{(2328)--(2336)}{846}, with the notation in \eqref{eq:short-distance-envelope-names} for a close pair, $\delta_g=\varepsilon_g+e_g^2$, $e_g$ and ${\rm tl}_{g,p}$ are the error functions of the singletons and of the tails,
\[
\begin{gathered}
e_g(s)=2\mathsf c_X(Y^-_s)^{-7\mathfrak p_0}+2(\mathsf c_I+\mathsf c_{\rm tl}\mathsf c_{\rm sb})\,s^2(LC_W(s))^3Y_s^{3\mathfrak p_0}{\rm sm}_g(s),\\
{\rm tl}_{g,p}(s)=\mathrm{Bl}(p)\,\mathsf c_\sigma^p\mathsf c_{\rm sb}^p(1+S^{\rm tl}_p)\,s^{1+3p/2}(LC_W(s))^{3p}Y_s^{2p\mathfrak p_0}\,M^{-3}c'A_0^2Y_s^PL^{3s}\bar x_s^p\,e^{-\frac12c'A_0^2(\log x^-_s)^P},
\end{gathered}
\]
$\mathsf c_\sigma=4+\mathsf C_{\mathsf M}^{1/2}/\mathsf C_{\rm sz}+\sqrt2$, $\mathsf C_{\rm sz}$ of Lem.~\YMMref{125.2}{840} and the constant convention preceding \eqref{eq:short-distance-constants}, $S^{\rm tl}_p=\sum_{a\ge0}L^{(3+4p)a+4p}(a+2)^{2p\mathfrak p_0}e^{-\frac12c'A_0^2(a\log\frac{3L}4)^2}$, ${\rm Mo}_{g,p}=(1+g_0+\delta_g)^n+\mathrm{Bl}(p){\rm far}_{g,p}(1+g_0+\varepsilon_g)^n+{\rm tl}_{g,p}$, $\mathrm{Bl}(p)$ is the number of partitions of $p$ elements, and $s_p(g)$ is the least integer $\ge s_1(g)$ from which ${\rm th}_{g,p}$ of Lem.~\ref{bil:sym}(e), ${\rm far}_{g,p}$ and $e_g$ are at most $1$ and $2\mathsf c_{\rm tl}s\,{\rm sm}_g(s)\le1$; it exists, since these four functions tend to $0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
By Lem.~\ref{bil:sym}(e) all pairs share one working level, one upper level $T$ and one tower of quotients, and, as ${\rm th}_{g,p}(s)\le1$ for $s\ge s_p(g)$, $\theta^{[j]}T_p(\mathsf D_j/M)\le\frac12$ for $1\le j<T$, so that the mixed derivative families of every order $\le p$ are bounded up to the level $T$ (the bound of the proof of Lem.~\ref{bil:nsrc}). At $T$, almost everywhere, $\Phi^{(T)}[\prod_B\tilde F_a]=\sum_\pi\prod_{\beta\in\pi}\varkappa^{(T)}_\beta$ (the identity of the proof of Lem.~\ref{bil:nsrc}, which holds at every level of the chain in use, here up to $T$, at $c_a=\langle F_a\rangle_\ell$); the conditional cumulants of order $\ge2$ do not depend on the centring constants.

A block that links two pairs is at most ${\rm far}_{g,p}(s)\prod\hat m_a$: by the vanishing of mixed derivatives on polymers that miss a support it is exponentially small in the distance $11M$ measured in units of the level $T$, that is in $L^{K-T}>L^{s-2}/\mathsf{Lm}_s$. A block of one pair is the conditional covariance $\Phi^{(T)}[F_{(\tau,1)}F_{(\tau,2)}]-\Phi^{(T)}[F_{(\tau,1)}]\Phi^{(T)}[F_{(\tau,2)}]$, the quotients being those of the chain of that pair alone (Lem.~\ref{bil:sym}(e)); by Lem.~\ref{bil:two}(c) it is almost everywhere within $\varepsilon_g(s)\hat m_\tau$ of $G_\tau$. A singleton obeys, by the sum over the level of the first creation (equation~\eqref{eq:ward-first-creation}) applied to $F_a$ minus its flat-top constant,
\[
|\Phi^{(T)}[F_a]-\langle F_a\rangle_\ell|\le2\mathsf Y_{T,a}+\rho'_a\le e_g(s)\hat m_a,
\]
$\mathsf Y_{T,a}$ the size of $F_a$ at the level $T$ and $\rho'_a$ its first-creation sum; for bond forms the mean is $0$, and the bound is used only in its last line, so that centring replaces the vanishing of the mean. So the partitions of $B$ without a linking block add up to the product, over the pairs that meet $B$, of $\varkappa^{(T)}_{\{(\tau,1),(\tau,2)\}}+\varkappa^{(T)}_{\{(\tau,1)\}}\varkappa^{(T)}_{\{(\tau,2)\}}=G_\tau+O(\delta_g(s))\hat m_\tau$ if both members lie in $B$, and of a singleton if one does. Crude bounds of the conditional moments at all the levels $t\le T$ (for a block of one pair, the crude clause of Lem.~\ref{bil:two}(c)), multiplied by $\mathsf w_t$ and summed, give the tails ${\rm tl}_{g,p}$.

Summing over the at most $\mathrm{Bl}(p)$ partitions gives the bounds of the lemma, and $\langle\tilde P_\tau\rangle=G_\tau+O(\delta_g)\hat m_\tau$ gives the second from the first. \emph{The size of $G_\tau$.} For plaquettes $p\in S_{(\tau,1)}$, $q\in S_{(\tau,2)}$, $|x(p)-x(q)|\ge3d-2(d-a_K)>d$; so $|C^{\rm bg}(p,q)|\le C'_{\mathsf k}(a_K/d)^3$ (Lem.~\ref{bil:ker}), and $|G_\tau|\le6C'^2_{\mathsf k}(a_K/d)^6(\sum|\mathsf t_{(\tau,1)}|)(\sum|\mathsf t_{(\tau,2)}|)\upsilon^2$. The two sums are counted by volume. The midpoints of the bonds of one direction form a translate of $a_K\mathbb Z^3$. Let $\mathsf w$ be a weight on the bonds of one direction with $S[\mathsf w]$ within $d-a_K$ of $z_a$.

A bond of its support has its four plaquettes in $S[\mathsf w]$, and its midpoint is the midpoint of the centres of two of them, opposite in one plane, so that it lies within $d-a_K$ of $z_a$; the open cubes of side $a_K$ about these midpoints are disjoint and lie within $d-a_K+\frac{\sqrt3}2a_K<d$ of $z_a$, in $B(z_a,d)$, a Euclidean ball as $20d\le\ell$; so the support of $\mathsf w$ has at most $\frac{4\pi}3(d/a_K)^3$ bonds. For a bond form $Y[\mathsf w]$ on the bonds of one direction, $q_b$ being a quarter of a signed sum of four corner forms, $\sum_{p,p'}|\mathsf t(p,p')|\le\sum_b|\mathsf w(b)|\le\frac{4\pi}3(d/a_K)^3\sup|\mathsf w|$, and $6(\frac{4\pi}3)^2<106$. For a majorant of such a form, $\#S\le4\cdot\frac{4\pi}3(d/a_K)^3$, each bond lying in four plaquettes, and $\sum|\mathsf t|\le\frac12(\#S)\mathsf s$, as $2\sum_{p'}|\mathsf t(p,p')|\le\mathsf s$; so $6(\frac{8\pi}3)^2<422$.

For an arbitrary majorant, $\#S\le81(d/a_K)^3$ (the plaquette count following equation~\YMMref{(2300)}{837}) and $\sum|\mathsf t|\le\frac12(\#S)\mathsf s$ give $6(\frac{81}2)^2=\frac32 81^2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Pressure, domination, boards, extraction]\label{bil:press}
(a) For $0<g\le\gamma$, $\ell_1\le\ell_2$ in $\mathfrak L(g)$ and every datum, $0\le p_{\ell_1}-p_{\ell_2}\le G_g$; from Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8} alone, $0\le p_{\ell_1}-p_{\ell_2}\le G^F_g=C_g+C_{\rm maj}+2+2C_{\rm tt}C'_{\rm tt}E_0\le2C_g+2C_{\rm tt}C'_{\rm tt}E_0$.

(b) Let $K$, $\beta>0$, a board of side $\mathsf l_0$, a side $\ell_0\ge2\mathsf l_0$ and $G$ with $p_{\ell_0}-p_\ell\le G$ on an unbounded set of sides be given. For bounded functions $\Phi_{\mathbf k}$ of distinct cells and every $\nu\in\mathcal G^{\rm per}_{K,\beta}$ (and for $\tilde\mu_\ell$ if the cells are distinct modulo the period): $|\nu(\prod\Phi_{\mathbf k})|\le\prod e^{G\mathsf l_0^3}\|\Phi_{\mathbf k}\|_{{\rm ch},\ell_0}$. No reflection invariance of $\nu$ is used.

(c) Let $h>0$ with $\mathsf l_0\in h\mathbb N$, as $h=a_K$, or $h=a_{K-t}$ for a level $t$. If $n(r+2\rho+h)<\mathsf l_0$, any $n$ cubes of side $r$ admit an offset in $h\mathbb Z^3$ with all their points at a distance $\ge\rho$ from the walls, also after translations by $\mathsf l_0\mathbb Z^3$; at $h=a_{K-t}$ the walls lie along faces of the blocks of the level $t$.

(d) Let functionals $\Lambda^{(j)}_n$ on tuples in $C_c(\mathbb R^3;V)$ with disjoint supports be linear in each entry on the tuples in $B(0,R')$ from an index $j_0(n,d,R,R')$ on, and bounded there by $c_n(d;R)\prod|H_a|_\infty$ at the tuples of type $(d;R)$ (supports in balls of radius $R$, at mutual distance $\ge d$). Then every subsequence has a subsequence that converges at all tuples, to multilinear limits with the same bounds.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(a) At the source $0$ the localised source energies of {\cite[Lem.~N.1]{YMM2}} give $E/\ell^3-C_g\le p_\ell\le E/\ell^3+C_S$ and $|E_\ell/\ell^3-E_{\ell'}/\ell'^3|\le2C_{\rm tt}C'_{\rm tt}E_0$, and $p_\ell$ does not increase with $\ell$ by the chessboard estimate (Cor.~\YMMref{86.6}{683}). Without Thms.~\YMMref{AJ}{673} and~\YMMref{AD}{607}, $\tilde Z(0)=e^{-E}Z$ with $e^{-C_g\ell^3}\le\tilde Z(0)\le e^{(C_{\rm maj}+2)\ell^3}$ gives $G^F_g$. (b) The chessboard estimate on $T_\ell$ (Prop.~\YMMref{86.3}{681}) gives $|\langle\prod\Phi_{\mathbf k}\rangle_\ell|\le\prod\|\Phi_{\mathbf k}\|_{{\rm ch},\ell}$, and comparing $Z_\ell$ with $Z_{\ell_0}$ cell by cell gives $\|\Phi\|_{{\rm ch},\ell}\le e^{\mathsf l_0^3(p_{\ell_0}-p_\ell)}\|\Phi\|_{{\rm ch},\ell_0}$ (Cor.~\YMMref{86.6}{683}).

For every periodic Gibbs state $\nu$ and every unbounded set of sides, the domination theorem (Prop.~\YMMref{91.9}{705}) gives $|\nu(\prod\Phi_{\mathbf k})|\le\liminf_\ell\prod\|\Phi_{\mathbf k}\|_{{\rm ch},\ell}$, the lower limit taken along the sides of the set; along the sides with $p_{\ell_0}-p_\ell\le G$ the comparison bounds the right member by $\prod e^{G\mathsf l_0^3}\|\Phi_{\mathbf k}\|_{{\rm ch},\ell_0}$. (c) In each direction there are $\mathsf l_0/h$ offsets modulo $\mathsf l_0$, and fewer than $n((r+2\rho)/h+1)<\mathsf l_0/h$ of them are bad. (d) The bound gives the equicontinuity $|\Lambda(X)-\Lambda(X')|\le c_n\sum_a|H_a-H_a'|_\infty\prod_{a'\ne a}\max\{|H_{a'}|_\infty,|H'_{a'}|_\infty\}$; a countable set of Lipschitz functions is dense with control of the supports; a diagonal sequence converges on it, hence everywhere.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The rate on a fixed torus]\label{bil:rate}
Let $g\le\gamma_2$, $\mathsf b\in I(g)$, $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$, $q\ge2$, $d>0$, $\theta_q=1/(1260q(8q+3))$, $\mathsf p=\max\{2\mathfrak p_0+2,\mathsf p_0,1\}$, where $\mathsf C_{\rm bf}\ell^3K^{\mathsf p_0}L^{-K/10}$, $K\ge K_{\rm bf}$, is the comparison of the laws of the block fields at two cutoffs of Cor.~\textup{\ref{IV-62-66}}. There are $C$, of the constants, $q$ and $\mathsf C_{\rm bf}$, and $K_1$, besides of $g,\mathsf b,\ell,d$, such that for $K\ge K_1$ and $G_K=\langle\mathcal E_1;\dots;\mathcal E_q\rangle_{K,\ell,L^K\mathsf b}$, the $\mathcal E_a$ any of $\mathcal O_K(\varphi)=O^T_K(\varphi\mathbf 1)$, $O^T_K(\varphi E_{\lambda\lambda})$ (the plaquettes of the plane normal to $\lambda$ alone) and $O^T_K(\varphi E_{\lambda\lambda'})$, $\lambda\ne\lambda'$, read at the centres of the plaquettes and the bonds, with real $\varphi_a$, Lipschitz in $|\cdot|_\infty$, whose supports are pairwise at sup distance $\ge d$:
\[
|G_{K+1}-G_K|\le C\ell^{3(q+1)}K^{\mathsf p}L^{-\theta_qK}\prod_a(\sup|\varphi_a|+\mathrm{Lip}\,\varphi_a).
\]
So $\lim_KG_K$ exists, with the tail of the series as the error; any number of the entries may be off-diagonal, and one pair $(C,K_1)$ serves a compact interval of labels. The same holds with $\prod_a\sup|\psi_a|$ for bounded Borel functions $\psi_a$ that vanish off closed sets at pairwise sup distances $\ge d$, entered through their cell means: at a site $x$ of $\Lambda_{K,\ell}$ the mean $\psi_a^{(K)}(x)=a_K^{-3}\int_{x+a_K[-\frac12,\frac12)^3}\psi_a$ is the weight of the plaquette with the corner $x$ and the edges $a_Ke_\kappa$, $a_Ke_{\kappa'}$, for the component $\lambda\lambda$, $\{\kappa,\kappa',\lambda\}=\{1,2,3\}$, and of the bond $\langle x,x+a_Ke_\mu\rangle$, for the component $\lambda\lambda'$, $\lambda\ne\lambda'$, $\mu$ the third direction, for all six components.

As $L$ is odd, the cells of $\Lambda_{K+1,\ell}$ at the sites of the block $B(y)$ of a site $y$ of $\Lambda_{K,\ell}$ make up the cell of $y$, so that $\psi^{(K)}(y)=L^{-3}\sum_{x\in B(y)}\psi^{(K+1)}(x)$: the weights of two cutoffs are tied exactly. So the limit exists for test functions of no regularity and agrees with that for Lipschitz functions. For one function evaluated at the points of the lattices of two cutoffs no bound of this kind by the sup norms holds. For one off-diagonal entry among action densities the rate is free of their number: if $n\ge1$, $\lambda\ne\lambda'$, and $\varphi,f_1,\dots,f_n$ are real Lipschitz functions on $T_\ell$, none of them $0$, whose $n+1$ supports have no common point, then $\kappa_K=\langle O^T_K(\varphi E_{\lambda\lambda'});\mathcal O_K(f_1);\dots;\mathcal O_K(f_n)\rangle_{K,\ell,L^K\mathsf b}$ obeys
\[
|\kappa_{K+1}-\kappa_K|\le CK^pL^{-K/120}(\sup|\varphi|+\mathrm{Lip}\,\varphi)\prod_{i=1}^n(\sup|f_i|+\mathrm{Lip}\,f_i)\qquad(K\ge K_2),
\]
with $C,p,K_2$ of the constants, $n$, $\ell$, the end points of a compact interval of labels that holds $\mathsf b$ and the spread $\mathsf d_\infty$ of the $n+1$ supports (the definition preceding Lem.~\YMMref{114.6}{805}).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Let $s<\sigma'\le\lceil K/1260\rceil$ be depths, the second at most the depth up to which Cor.~\textup{\ref{IV-62-66}} compares the laws of the block fields, and $\sigma'\ge(8q+3)s$. At each of the cutoffs $K$, $K+1$ the cumulant is, up to three errors, the cumulant of the first members of the sources, that is of the functions $\mathcal E_a$ themselves and not of their families at the heights, evaluated at the background of the block field of the depth $\sigma'$: the progression with the sources switched on at the level $K-\sigma'$ forgets what lies below, with the error $\epsilon(\sigma'-s)$, $\epsilon(\nu)=C(\nu+1)^{2\mathfrak p_0+2}L^{-\nu/2}$; the large fields cost $L^{-(b'+1)s}$, for any $b'\ge4q$; and the distance of the supports costs $e^{3-L^sd/M}$.

Each of the three multiplies $(4\ell^3L^{4s})^q\prod_a(\sup|\varphi_a|+\mathrm{Lip}\,\varphi_a)$, the bound of the entries at the depth $s$; as $L^{4qs}L^{-(\sigma'-s)/2}\le L^{-s}$ for $\sigma'-s\ge(8q+2)s$ and $L^{4qs}L^{-(b'+1)s}\le L^{-s}$ for $b'\ge4q$, together they are of the order $K^{2\mathfrak p_0+2}L^{-s}$. Over one block field $V$ of the depth $\sigma'$, with $t=K-\sigma'$, the background $U^{\rm A}$ on $\Lambda_{K,\ell}$ and the background $U^{\rm B}$ on $\Lambda_{K+1,\ell}$ are compared in three links. (1) $U'=\mathcal M(U^{\rm B})$, $U^{\rm B}$ averaged once, is a configuration of the coarse lattice over the same block field, a competitor whose excess energy over $U^{\rm A}$ is at most $C\varepsilon_{\rm r}^2\eta_tN_t$, $\varepsilon_{\rm r}$ the radius of the small fields of the depth $\sigma'$ and $N_t$ the number of the cubes of the level $t$: its energy is at least that of $U^{\rm A}$, by the minimality of $U^{\rm A}$, and at most that of $U^{\rm B}$ up to a number of the same order, by the inequality of Jensen of (2); and the energy of $U^{\rm B}$ exceeds that of $U^{\rm A}$ by at most a number of the same order, since the prolongation of $U^{\rm A}$ to the fine lattice is a competitor of $U^{\rm B}$ whose energy exceeds that of $U^{\rm A}$ by at most such a number.
