(2) The fine background against its average: for a bilinear form of the loops at one site or at one bond, the defect of Jensen's inequality $\sum_p\mathsf W(p',p)|g_p|^2\ge L^{-2}|G'_{p'}|^2$, with the averaging kernel $\mathsf W$, $g_p$ the fine and $G'_{p'}$ the averaged curvature, is the variance of the fine curvature on the block of $p'$, and its sum over the blocks is the difference of the two energies; so the curvature is nearly constant in mean square under the shifts of a plaquette in its own plane within a block, with the error $L^{-t/2}$, and the weights enter only through the mismatch of their block means, which is $0$ for cell means and at most $\frac32a_K\mathrm{Lip}\,\varphi$ for one function read at the centres on the two lattices. (3) The competitor against $U^{\rm A}$: along the $t$ consecutive levels each pair of backgrounds differs by one gauge transformation and one small $1$-form $A_k$, with $\sum_kL^{t-k}\|A_k\|^2$ at most a number times the excess, which costs $(t\eta_t)^{1/2}$.

So the corner fields $a_K^{-1}\sum_x\varphi(x+a_K\xi)Q_x(l,l')$, $Q_x(l,l')$ the corner forms of Lem.~\ref{bil:mat}(b), of which $O^T_K(\varphi E_{\lambda\lambda'})$ is a sum of four with the coefficients $\pm\frac14$, agree at the two backgrounds up to $C\ell^3L^{4\sigma'}K^{1/2}L^{-(K-\sigma')/2}(\sup|\varphi|+L^{-\sigma'}\mathrm{Lip}\,\varphi)$ for Lipschitz weights, and up to the same number with $\sup|\psi|$ for weights tied by the cell mean; for one function evaluated at the points of two lattices the mismatch of the block means is not small in the sup norm, and there the Lipschitz number pays. The block-field laws at $K$ and $K+1$ differ by $\mathsf C_{\rm bf}\ell^3K^{\mathsf p_0}L^{-K/10}$ (Cor.~\textup{\ref{IV-62-66}}(a), whose numbers read the label only through an interval that holds it).

With $\sigma'=\lfloor K/(1260q)\rfloor$ and $s=\lfloor\sigma'/(8q+3)\rfloor$ the four errors give the rate $\theta_q$. For one off-diagonal entry among action densities whose supports have no common point another road keeps the action densities as sources in the exponent of the progression, as in the comparison of two cutoffs with sources (Thm.~\YMMref{AR}{810}), and passes the one off-diagonal entry alone to the block field as a bounded function: it is put into the chain as a member whose tower is split at the depth $\lceil K/36\rceil$; what it creates below the level $K-\lceil K/36\rceil$ is born at a small coupling, and above it the member is carried along the run and forgotten.

No factor $L^{4q\sigma'}$ enters, the rate is free of $n$, and it is $L^{-K/120}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[What the properties of the limits do not decide]\label{bil:zeta}
Let $\sigma$ be a limit through periodic Gibbs states, $g\le\gamma_1$, and for real $\zeta$ let $\Lambda_\zeta$ be the linear map of $V$ that is $1$ on the diagonal and $\zeta$ on the off-diagonal matrices, $\sigma^\zeta(X)=\sigma(\Lambda_\zeta X)$.

(a) $\sigma^\zeta$ is a real symmetric functional, bounded as in (D1) with the factor $\max\{1,|\zeta|\}^n$, invariant under translations and $W_3$, reflection positive at the nine families; $[F]\mapsto[\Lambda_\zeta F]$ is an isometry of its Hilbert space into that of $\sigma$ that intertwines the semigroups, the translations and the vacua; so $\sigma^\zeta$ has the cone of \cite[Thm.~BZ(F4)]{YMM2}, the insertion bound of \cite[Thm.~BZ(F2)]{YMM2} with the factor $\max\{1,|\zeta|\}$ for each entry, and the plateau of \cite[Thm.~BZ(F6)]{YMM2}.

(b) For $\zeta\ne1$, $\sigma^\zeta$ is not invariant under the rotations about $e_3$; it is reflection positive at no plane outside the nine families; and it does not obey the free law of \cite[Thm.~BZ(F1)]{YMM2} at any label.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(a) $\Lambda_\zeta$ commutes with $\rho(w)$ for $w\in W_3$, since a signed permutation carries diagonal matrices to diagonal and off-diagonal to off-diagonal ones, and the mirrors of the nine families act on the labels by elements of $W_3$; the rest follows from the isometry. (b) Let $D=E_{11}-E_{22}$ and $O=E_{12}$, the symmetric matrix with the entries $1$ at $(1,2)$ and $(2,1)$, so that $\rho(R_t)D=\cos2t\,D+\sin2t\,O$, $\rho(R_t)O=-\sin2t\,D+\cos2t\,O$ for the rotations $R_t$ about $e_3$, and let $C=E_{33}$. If $\sigma$ and $\sigma^\zeta$ were both invariant under the $R_t$, the mixed kernel would obey $(\zeta-1)\sin2t\;\mathcal G(R_tu)(O,C)=0$, so $\mathcal G(\cdot)(O,C)\equiv0$; but by \cite[Thm.~BZ(F1)]{YMM2} at short distance $\mathcal G(u)(O,C)$ is close to $\mathsf b^{-2}$ times the mixed free kernel $3K_3(u)_{13}K_3(u)_{23}$, which does not vanish identically.

By {\cite[Prop.~D.16]{YMM2}}(b) $\sigma^\zeta$ is then positive at no further plane. If $\sigma^\zeta$ obeyed the free law at a label $\mathsf b'$, the law at two diagonal entries, where $\sigma^\zeta=\sigma$, would give $\mathsf b'=\mathsf b$; and the mixed law depends on $\zeta$ with its sign, $\sigma^\zeta(H_1,H_2)=\zeta\sigma(H_1,H_2)$ for $H_1$ off-diagonal and $H_2$ diagonal, while the mixed free covariance does not vanish identically; so $\zeta=1$. In the proof of {\cite[Prop.~D.15]{YMM2}} every input but conservation holds for $\sigma^\zeta$: it is conservation that excludes it at all distances, and the mixed free law at short distance.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Extension over coinciding points]\label{bil:ext}
Let $\mathsf M=\mathbb R^3$ or $T_\ell$, $n\ge2$, $A,h_0>0$, $q\ge0$, and let $u$ be a functional of $n$ entries, $n$-linear on $\prod_aC^\infty_c(O_a;V_{\mathbb C})$ for open $O_a$ with pairwise disjoint closures, with the bound
\[
|u(f_1,\dots,f_n)|\le A\,\bigl(1+\log\tfrac{h_0}h\bigr)^q\prod_a\sup|f_a|
\]
for $0<h\le h_0$ and all $f_a$ supported in closed cubes of side $\frac32h$, wherever they lie, at pairwise sup distances $\ge\frac52h$; on $T_\ell$ the number $h_0$ lies in $\ell2^{-\mathbb N}$ and $h_0\le\ell/(64n)$.

(a) There is a distribution $\tilde u$ on $\mathsf M^n$ of order $\le3n-2$ that agrees with $u$ on separated tensor products and has
\[
|\tilde u(F)|\le C_{\rm ex}A\bigl(1+\log\tfrac{h_0}\lambda\bigr)^{q+1}\max_{|\gamma|\le3n-2}\lambda^{|\gamma|}\sup|\partial^\gamma F|
\]
for every $F$ supported in a product of closed sup-balls of radius $\lambda\le h_0$ about any points, $C_{\rm ex}$ depending only on $n$ and $q$, with the label norm and auxiliary smooth cutoffs fixed; if $u$ is invariant under permutations of the entries, translations and a closed subgroup of $O(3)$ that maps $\mathsf M$ to itself, $\tilde u$ can be chosen invariant.

(b) Two extensions with this bound differ by $\sum_{|\pi|\le n-1}\sum_{|\alpha|\le3|\pi|}\partial^\alpha_\xi\delta_\pi\otimes T_{\pi,\alpha}$, $\pi$ the partitions of the entries, $\delta_\pi$ the diagonal of $\pi$, $\xi$ the differences of the points in the blocks, and $T_{\pi,\alpha}$ distributions on $\mathsf M^{|\pi|}$ with the bound of (a) at the power $\lambda^{|\alpha|}$; and every such sum can be added. A distribution with the bound of (a) at a power $\lambda^{\kappa'}$, $\kappa'>3k$, on $\mathsf M^k$ is $0$.

(c) At $n=2$ the translation invariant terms of (b) are $\sum_{|\alpha|\le3}\int\mathsf c_\alpha(\partial^\alpha f_1(x),f_2(x))\,\mathrm{d}x$ with bilinear forms $\mathsf c_\alpha$; the real ones that are symmetric in the two entries and covariant under $O(3)$ on $\mathbb R^3$ form a space of dimension six, spanned in Fourier space by $\mathrm{tr}\,H\,\mathrm{tr}\,H'$, $\mathrm{tr}\,HH'$, $p^2\mathrm{tr}\,H\,\mathrm{tr}\,H'$, $p^2\mathrm{tr}\,HH'$, $(p\cdot Hp)\mathrm{tr}\,H'+(p\cdot H'p)\mathrm{tr}\,H$, $(Hp)\cdot(H'p)$; covariant under the cubic group on $T_\ell$, they form a space of dimension twelve.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(a) Apply Lem.~\ref{C-355-34}(a)--(d) at $\kappa=r=0$, with the stated torus convention. Its construction reads as follows. $\mathsf M^n$ minus the big diagonal is the union of the admissible products of dyadic cubes of sides $h_j=2^{-j}h_0$, pairwise at sup distances $\ge3h_j$, that lie in no larger admissible product (on $T_\ell$ the dyadic cubes tile the torus, as $h_0\in\ell2^{-\mathbb N}$, and each cluster lies in a sup ball of radius $13nh_0<\frac\ell4$, which lifts to $\mathbb R^3$ and defines the differences within that cluster); there is a partition of unity $\varphi_{\mathbf Q}$ with $|\partial^\gamma\varphi_{\mathbf Q}|\le c_\gamma h(\mathbf Q)^{-|\gamma|}$, and on each product $u$ extends to the smooth functions with the bound, by an absolutely convergent expansion in products.

The cubes of a product at mutual distances $\le12h$ form its clusters, a partition $\pi(\mathbf Q)$ with $k$ blocks, where $k\le n-1$ below the coarsest side $h_0$; put $\tilde u(F)=\sum_{\mathbf Q}u_{\mathbf Q}(\varphi_{\mathbf Q}(F-P_{\mathbf Q}F))$, $P_{\mathbf Q}F$ the Taylor polynomial of order $3k$ averaged over the piece of size $h$ of the stratum $\Delta_{\pi(\mathbf Q)}$ next to $\mathbf Q$ when $k\le n-1$, and $P_{\mathbf Q}=0$ otherwise. On the products with $k\le n-1$ the remainder is of order $(h/\lambda)^{3k+1}$, the number of products of side $h$ near a given point is of order $(\lambda/h)^{3k}$, and the sum over the scales converges with one more logarithm; the order of the extension is $3(n-1)+1=3n-2$. Choose the grid partition and the Taylor averages covariantly under $h_0\mathbb Z^3$. Average the resulting extension over the parameters $t\in[0,h_0)^3$ with normalized Lebesgue measure; periodicity in $t$ makes this mean invariant under every translation. Then average over permutations and the compact orthogonal subgroup, as in Lem.~\ref{C-355-34}(d). Its support-radius comparison and the fixed-scale localization in part~(c) preserve the stated bound, with a constant depending on $n,q$. (b) A distribution supported on the big diagonal with the bound of (a) is, stratum by stratum, a sum of transversal derivatives of order $\le3|\pi|$ of $\delta_\pi$; the vanishing for $\kappa'>3k$ is the scaling of the bound. (c) A translation invariant contact term at $n=2$ is a polynomial of order $\le3$ in the relative momentum $p$; $-\mathbf1\in O(3)$ acts trivially on $V$ and changes the sign of $p$, so only the orders $0$ and $2$ remain, and the invariant theory of $O(3)$ on symmetric matrices gives two forms at the order $0$ and four at the order $2$; under the cubic group $3+9$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Thms.~\ref{thm:bil} and~\ref{bil:lim}]
\emph{Step 1: (A1).} Cut $T_\ell$ into at most $(2\ell/d'')^3$ boxes of radius $\le0.86\,d''$, and each form into its pieces on these boxes. A choice of nonzero pieces, one of each form, has the geometry of Lem.~\ref{bil:nsrc} at $d''$, with the majorants of Lem.~\ref{bil:forms}: the pieces lie within $\frac78d''$ of points, and the plaquettes of pieces of different forms are at least $d-2a_K\ge\frac54d''$ apart, as $d\ge\frac43d''$; $s(d'')\ge s_{\rm th}(n)$ since $L^{s(d'')}\ge1/d''$, and $\ell\le\ell_{\max}$ on a small side. Multilinearity gives
\[
|\langle F_1;\dots;F_n\rangle_\ell|\le(2\ell_{\max}/d'')^{3n}k'_n(g,s(d''))\,b^{-n}\prod_a|F_a|_\star .
\]

\emph{Step 2: (A2), (A3).} (A2) is Lem.~\ref{bil:two}(a) with Lem.~\ref{bil:forms}(a): a real form is a real quadratic source under $(|F|_\star,S[F])$ with the kernel $\mathsf t_F$, and its plaquettes lie within $d-a_K$ of $x_i$ when its cells lie within $d-2a_K$; for complex tensor weights the real and imaginary parts give four real pairs, and $O^T_K(H)$ is a source under $(60|H|_\infty,S_H)$. For the continuum form, Lem.~\ref{bil:ker} gives $C^{\rm bg}(p,q)=\epsilon_p\epsilon_qa_K^3K_3(x(p)-x(q))_{\lambda(p)\lambda(q)}+O((a_K/d)^3E_1)$; the sums over plaquettes and bonds are Riemann sums of the integral, with an error $(6/\pi)(a_K/d)$ for each factor at Lipschitz weights; $\upsilon^2$ against $b^{-2}$ costs $8\bar Bg^2L^{2-s}$; and
\[
\begin{aligned}\tfrac32\mathrm{tr}[E_{\lambda_1\lambda_1'}KE_{\lambda_2\lambda_2'}K]&=3[K_{\lambda_1\lambda_2}K_{\lambda_1'\lambda_2'}+K_{\lambda_1\lambda_2'}K_{\lambda_1'\lambda_2}],\quad(\lambda_1\ne\lambda_1',\ \lambda_2\ne\lambda_2'),\\\tfrac32\mathrm{tr}[E_{\lambda\lambda'}KE_{\gamma\gamma}K]&=3K_{\lambda\gamma}K_{\lambda'\gamma}\quad(\lambda\ne\lambda')\end{aligned}
\]
identify the Gaussian value with $b^{-2}\mathcal W$. So, with $s=s(d)$,
\[
e^{\rm od}=\tfrac98\bigl[59^2\varepsilon^\natural_g(s)+600E_2(\tfrac1\pi+E_2)+636/C_W(s)\bigr]+8\bar Bg^2L^{2-s},\qquad E_2=E_1+\tfrac6\pi\tfrac{a_K}d,
\]
which is at most an error function of $s$, since $a_K/d\le C_W(s)^{-1}$, $d<LC_W(s)L^{-s}$ and $M\le L^{-2}C_W(s)\le\hat d<LC_W(s)$ (Lem.~\ref{bil:sym}(e)), so that also the term $C^{\rm fl}_\star\hat d^3e^{-\delta_{\rm tp}L\hat d/\sqrt3}$ of $E_1$ is at most an error function of $s$. For (A3) apply (A2) to $(\theta Y,Y)$, whose points are $3d$ to $4d$ apart. By Lem.~\ref{bil:ker} and its count, at most $10(d/a_K)^3$ centres of bonds of one direction in a ball of radius $d$,
\[
|G(\theta Y,Y)|\le6C_{\mathsf k}^2(a_K/d)^6\Bigl(\sum|\mathsf t|\Bigr)^2\upsilon^2\le600C_{\mathsf k}^2\upsilon^2\sup|\mathsf w|^2,
\]
and with $\upsilon^2\le\frac98b^{-2}$, $|Y|_\star=59\sup|\mathsf w|$ the bound follows. Since $\langle Y\rangle_\ell=0$ (Lem.~\ref{bil:sym}(b)), $\langle\theta Y;Y\rangle_\ell=\langle\theta Y\cdot Y\rangle_\ell\ge0$ by reflection positivity at a plane through midpoints of bonds (Cor.~\YMMref{85.3}{679}); for other forms the centred form $F-\langle F\rangle_\ell$ gives the sign. For forms at bonds and sites the count gives $\sum|\mathsf t|\le N(d/a_K)^3\|v\|$, $N=30$, resp. $10$, and for $O^T_K(H)$ the same count gives the number $12150=6\cdot45^2$, with $60^2\bar\varepsilon^\natural_g$ from the size $60|H|_\infty$.

\emph{Step 3: (B).} By Lem.~\ref{bil:sym}(a) the copies $\theta'^\eta Y$ are bond forms of the same size; by Lem.~\ref{bil:sym}(d) partners across the plane of $\theta'_{\mu_0}$ are $3d$ to $4d$ apart and other pairs $\ge11M$; their means vanish by Lem.~\ref{bil:sym}(b). Lem.~\ref{bil:far} with $n=4$, for bond forms, gives $M_8\le(g_0^4+\bar\omega_{g,8})\hat m_J$ with $\hat m_J=59^8\upsilon^8\sup|\mathsf w|^8$ and $59^2g_0=106C'^2_{\mathsf k}$, so $M_8\le C_8b^{-8}\sup|\mathsf w|^8$; and $|M_8-\prod_\tau\langle P_\tau\rangle|\le\omega^\sharp_{g,8}\hat m_J$ with $\langle P_\tau\rangle=\langle\theta'_{\mu_0}Y;Y\rangle_{\ell'}$ for all four pairs. The signs come from reflection positivity: $M_8$ is a mean of mirror copies, and the chessboard estimate gives $\langle\theta'_{\mu_0}Y\cdot Y\rangle_{\ell'}\le M_8^{1/8}M_8^{1/8}$ times the seminorms $1$ of the six other cells.

\emph{Step 4: (C1).} With $\delta=\min\{d,\frac12,\mathsf l/(4n)\}$ cut each form into its pieces on the cubes of side $\delta$ (at most $(2R/\delta+2)^{3n}$ tuples of pieces); only the boundedness of the weights is used. For each tuple of pieces Prop.~\ref{bil:press}(c) gives a board of side $\mathsf l$ with all pieces at distance $\frac\delta2$ from the walls; on a torus, pieces are first moved by periods into one period box. Centre by $c_a=\tilde\mu_{\ell'}(F_a)$, write the cumulant through moments, and dominate each moment by Prop.~\ref{bil:press}(b). The eighth power of the seminorm of a product of centred pieces in one cell is a centred moment of at most $8m$ forms on $T_{\ell'}$ at mutual distance $\ge\delta$ (Lem.~\ref{bil:sym}(c)), bounded by (A1):
\[
\Bigl\|\prod_a(F_a-c_a)\Bigr\|_{{\rm ch},\ell'}\le\mathrm{Bl}_{8m}^{1/8}\prod_ab^{-1}|F_a|_\star,\qquad\mathrm{Bl}_N=\sum_{\pi\in{\rm Part}_2(N)}\prod_{I\in\pi}k^\circ(\#I,\delta),
\]
${\rm Part}_2(N)$ the partitions into blocks of at least two. So 
\[
C^T_n(d;R)=\max\{(2R/\delta+2)^{3n}\mathsf f_ne^{nG_g\mathsf l^3}\mathsf{Bm}_n^n,\ \relax C^{\rm cr}_n(d;R)\},
\]
$\mathsf f_n=\sum_\pi(\#\pi-1)!$, $\mathsf{Bm}_n=\max_{m\le n}\max\{1,\mathrm{Bl}^{1/8}_{8m}\}$; below the cutoff $K_n=\max_{r\le8n}K'_0(r,\delta)$ bounds by suprema give $C^{\rm cr}_n(d;R)=\mathsf f_n[6\bar x_0L^{K_n}(2RL^{K_n}+1)^3]^n$. The one-point number $C^T_1(R)$ is the case $n=1$. Complex weights: real and imaginary parts.

\emph{Step 5: (C2), (C3).} For (C2) let $D=|x_1-x_2|_\infty$, on a torus minimised over the lifts, be attained in the coordinate $\mu_0$. If $D>3$, the supports lie in balls of radius $1$ more than $1$ apart, and (C1) at $(\frac12;1)$ bounds the covariance. Let $D\le3$. One board of side $\mathsf l$ serves both insertions: it has a wall normal to $e_{\mu_0}$ at the midpoint of $x_{1,\mu_0}$ and $x_{2,\mu_0}$, up to $\frac{a_K}2$, and its offset $o$ at $\frac12(x_{1,\nu}+x_{2,\nu})$, up to $\frac{a_K}2$, in the two coordinates $\nu\ne\mu_0$. The distance $t_i$ of $x_i$ to the wall lies in $[\frac D2-\frac{a_K}2,\frac D2+\frac{a_K}2]\subset[\frac32d,2)$, and $|x_{i,\nu}-o_\nu|<2$, so that the corners of the plaquettes of either insertion lie within $3$ of the middle of its cell in the coordinates $\nu\ne\mu_0$.

Of the eight copies of one insertion on $T_{\ell'}$, the partners across the wall are $2t_i\in[3d',4d']$ apart, $d'=\max\{d,\frac{t_i}2\}$, and copies that differ in a reflection normal to an $e_\nu$, $\nu\ne\mu_0$, are at least $\mathsf l-6\ge11M$ apart ($\mathsf l\ge LM$, $M\ge3$); the carriers lie within $d'-2a_K$ of their points, and $s(d')\le s(d)\le K$. So Lem.~\ref{bil:far} with $n=4$ at the distance $d'$, for bond forms, whose means vanish, bounds the eighth power of the seminorm of a bond insertion by $(g_0^4+\bar\omega_{g,8})\hat m_J=C_8b^{-8}\sup|\mathsf w|^8$, as in Step~3, on this board, which the two insertions fix together, and its centred one-direction case bounds the seminorm of each of the forms of a tensor insertion; domination bounds the covariance by the product of the two seminorms; if $s(d')<s_8(g)$, (A1) is used at the distance $d_\flat=L^{-s_8(g)}$.

This gives
\[
\begin{multlined}
C^\diamond_\infty=\max\{2(c^\diamond_\infty)^2,C^T_2(\tfrac12;1)\},\qquad c^\diamond_\infty=e^{G_g\mathsf l^3}\max\bigl\{(\tfrac98)^{1/2}((422C'^2_{\mathsf k})^4+\bar\omega^{\rm o}_{g,8})^{1/8},\ \relax \mathrm{Bl}_8(d_\flat)^{1/8}, \\
\ \relax 12\bar x_0L^{K_\flat}(2L^{K_\flat}+1)^3\bigr\},
\end{multlined}
\]
$\bar\omega^{\rm o}_{g,8}$ the supremum of the error of Lem.~\ref{bil:far} for majorants of one direction, $\mathrm{Bl}_8(d_\flat)$ the number of Step~4 at the distance $d_\flat$ and $K_\flat$ its cutoff. For bond forms the mean vanishes in every law, and $C^{\rm per}_\infty$ is formed in the same way with $C_8^{1/4}$; complex weights of all three directions cost the factor $36$. For (C3) place the pair in the middle of a cell (Lem.~\ref{bil:sym}(d)) and use Lem.~\ref{bil:far} with $n=8$ for the sixteen copies (in its proof the blocks of one pair rest on the clause of Lem.~\ref{bil:two}(c), almost everywhere at the upper level): for $X_i=F_i-c_i$, $c_i=\tilde\mu_{\ell'}(F_i)$, and $m=\tilde\mu_{\ell'}(X_1X_2)=\tilde\mu_{\ell'}(F_1;F_2)$,
\[
\|X_1X_2-m\|_{{\rm ch},\ell'}^8=\sum_J(-m)^{8-\#J}\langle\tilde P_J\rangle_{\ell'}\le\omega'^\sharp_{g,16}(s)(|m|+\hat m)^8,
\]
since $\langle\tilde P_J\rangle$ replaced by $m^{\#J}$ gives $(m-m)^8=0$ and $|\langle\tilde P_J\rangle-m^{\#J}|\le\omega'^\sharp_{g,16}\hat m^{\#J}$. For one point, $\|X_i\|^8_{{\rm ch},\ell'}$ is a centred moment of eight of the sixteen forms, one from each pair, a set that holds no pair, so it is at most $o_{g,16}(s)(\upsilon|F_i|_\star)^8$. Domination now gives the three bounds of (C3), with
\[
{\rm Df}_g(s)=e^{G_g\mathsf l^3}[\omega'^\sharp_{g,16}(s)]^{1/8}(1+g_0+\omega'_{g,16}(s))+e^{2G_g\mathsf l^3}o_{g,16}(s)^{1/4},
\]
since $|m|\le(g_0+\omega'_{g,16})\hat m$, and $|m-G(F_1',F_2')|\le\omega'_{g,16}\hat m$ by Lem.~\ref{bil:far} at one pair. For $O^T_K(H_i)$ the same, with the majorants $(60|H_i|_\infty,S_{H_i})$.

\emph{Step 6: (D1)--(D3).} (C1), Prop.~\ref{bil:press}(d), the compactness of $I^{\rm lab}(g)$ and the theorem of F.~Riesz give (D1); the second clause is (C1) at $n=1$; for the third, the local functions $O^T_K(H)$ and the weak convergence give some $\ell_j\ge\max\{\Lambda_j,j\}$ in $\mathfrak L(g)$ at which the first $j$ tuples of a dense countable family are matched within $\frac1j$. $O^T_K(f\mathbf1)=\mathcal O_K(f)$ gives (D2), along a subsequence of the defining sequence of $S$. Lem.~\ref{bil:sym}(a) gives $rO^T_K(H)=O^T_K(rH)$; the invariance and the reflection positivity of the laws at the lattice mirrors pass to the limits, since lattice isometries approximate the real ones and the bounds are equicontinuous; periodic Gibbs states are positive at the nine families.

The semigroup of symmetric contractions $[F]\mapsto[\tau_{te_3}F]$ is $e^{-tH}$, Stone's theorem gives the momenta and the joint spectral measure, and the lattice energy--momentum inequality (Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{99.3}{739}}) gives $H\ge|P_k|$. Centred at the means of $\tilde\mu_{\ell'}$, the moments in $\nu_j$ are $\sum_B\prod_{i\in B}(\nu_j-\tilde\mu_{\ell'})(O^T_{K_j}(H_i))\,\nu_j(A_j(X_{B^c}))$. The bond parts have mean $0$ in both laws, and all plaquettes have one mean in each law (Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{103.4}{758}}), so that $(\nu_j-\tilde\mu_{\ell'})(O^T_{K_j}(H))=\mathfrak c_j\,a_{K_j}^3\sum_pH_{\lambda(p)\lambda(p)}(x(p))$, a Riemann sum of $\mathfrak c_j\int\mathrm{tr}\,H$, with $\mathfrak c_j=a_{K_j}^{-4}(\nu_j(a_p)-\tilde\mu_{\ell'}(a_p))$; (C1) at $n=1$, applied to a plaquette form, bounds $|\mathfrak c_j|$ by $C(g)\mathsf b^{-1}$ for large $j$.

So the $\mathfrak c_j$ converge along a further subsequence, to $\mathfrak c$, and along it the recentred moments converge to the functional of (D3), whose one-point function is $\mathfrak c\int\mathrm{tr}\,H$; it is reflection positive, since the means of $\tilde\mu_{\ell'}$ are invariant under the lattice mirrors.

\emph{Step 7: (D4).} For Lipschitz entries Lem.~\ref{bil:rate} makes the cumulants Cauchy in $K$, and its form for cell means gives the same for bounded Borel weights; continuous entries are approximated by Lipschitz ones uniformly in $K$, by the torus form of (C1); Prop.~\ref{bil:press}(d) applies in $\ell$ to periodised tuples, which are defined and linear once $\ell$ is large against the supports; a diagonal choice of the cutoffs gives the limits along growing tori.

\emph{Step 8: (D5) and \cite[Thm.~BZ(F1)]{YMM2}.} On $T_{\ell'}$, (C3) and the continuum form of Step~2, with $\frac32\mathrm{tr}[E_{\lambda\lambda}KE_{\gamma\gamma}K]=\frac32K_{\lambda\gamma}^2$, give the law for all $36$ pairs of components; then $j\to\infty$. For two off-diagonal components the error is $\bar e^{\rm od}_g+\frac98 59^2{\rm Df}_g$, for an off-diagonal and a diagonal one $\bar e^{\rm od}_g+\frac98 59\,{\rm Df}_g$, for two diagonal ones $\frac98[\omega'_{g,16}+{\rm Df}_g+150\bar E_1(\frac1\pi+\bar E_1)+159/C_W(s)]+2\bar Bg^2L^{2-s}$, $\bar E_1$ the bound of $E_1$ by a function of $s$ ((C3) being used with the majorants of the respective kinds); $\bar e_g$ is their maximum. At $H_i=f_i\mathbf1$, $\frac32\mathrm{tr}\,K_3(u)^2=\frac9{16\pi^2}|u|^{-6}$; the leading term is covariant under $O(3)$. For (F1), Lem.~\ref{bil:far} with arbitrary majorants, centred, at $n=8$ bounds the means, $|\nu(O^T_K(H))-\tilde\mu_{\ell'}(O^T_K(H))|\le60e^{G_g\mathsf l^3}{\rm mn}_g(s)\upsilon|H|_\infty$, where ${\rm mn}_g=[e_g^8+\mathrm{Bl}(16){\rm far}_{g,16}(1+g_0+\varepsilon_g)^8+{\rm tl}_{g,16}]^{1/8}\le o_{g,16}^{1/8}$ comes from its moment bound at $N_1=8$, so sup norms suffice, and the law holds at a finite cutoff for continuous weights, the Riemann sums of continuous weights giving $r_K\to0$ and the lattice term of $E_1$ the term $C(g)(a_K/d)^2$; letting $j\to\infty$,
\[
\begin{multlined}
e^\infty_g(d)=\tfrac98\Bigl\{3600\bigl[\omega'_{g,16}+e^{G_g\mathsf l^3}(\omega'^\sharp_{g,16})^{1/8}(1+g_0+\omega'_{g,16})+e^{2G_g\mathsf l^3}{\rm mn}_g^2\bigr](s)+12150E^\infty_1(\tfrac1\pi \\
+E^\infty_1)\Bigr\}+162\bar Bg^2L^{2-s},\qquad s=s(d),
\end{multlined}
\]
$E^\infty_1=E_1-C_{\rm lat}(a_K/d)^2$. The errors are powers of $Y_{s(d)}^{-1}$, the worst the root $[\omega'^\sharp_{g,16}]^{1/8}$, and $Y_{s(d)}\sim\log\frac1d$. This root can be avoided: in Step~5 the eighth power of the seminorm of $X_1X_2-m$ is an alternating sum of means of products of the sixteen copies, and at the upper level the parts of these means without a block that links two pairs recombine to $\prod_\tau(\Psi_\tau-m)$, $\Psi_\tau$ the conditional means of the pairs, with $|\Psi_\tau-m|\le(\delta_g+\omega'_{g,16})\hat m$ almost everywhere at the upper level (the blocks of one pair by Lem.~\ref{bil:two}(c), the singletons as in the proof of Lem.~\ref{bil:far}, and $|G(F_1',F_2')-m|\le\omega'_{g,16}\hat m$ as in Step~5); so the seminorm itself is at most a multiple of $(\delta_g+\omega'_{g,16})\hat m$ plus the eighth roots of the terms ${\rm far}$ and ${\rm tl}$, which decay faster than every power of $Y_s^{-1}$, and the means are bounded with ${\rm mn}_g$, so that the second term of ${\rm Df}_g$ may be taken $e^{2G_g\mathsf l^3}{\rm mn}_g^2$; as $\varepsilon_g$, $\omega'_{g,16}$ and $1/C_W(s)$ are of order $Y_s^{-2\mathfrak p_0}$ and ${\rm mn}_g^2$ is of smaller order, the error is at most $C(g)(\log\frac1d)^{-2\mathfrak p_0}$; by {\cite[Lem.~D.19]{YMM2}} the same holds for $g\le\gamma_2$, as $(\log\frac1{L^zd})^{-2\mathfrak p_0}\le2^{2\mathfrak p_0}(\log\frac1d)^{-2\mathfrak p_0}$ for $d\le L^{-2z}$.

On the tori of $\mathfrak L(g)$ the torus limits of (D4) are limits along cutoffs at the labels $L^K\mathsf b$, and the same bound passes to them. The law fixes $\mathsf b$, since $\mathcal W\ne0$. Since $\mathcal W$ is invariant under $O(3)$ and $|rH|_\infty\le3|H|_\infty$, the law gives $|\sigma(rH_1,rH_2)-\sigma(H_1,H_2)|\le(9+1)e^\infty_g\mathsf b^{-2}|H_1|_\infty|H_2|_\infty$. Non-degeneracy: $\mathcal W(\theta(\varphi E),\varphi E)\ge w_0\,\mathrm{tr}\,E^2$ for this bump.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[The mirror bound and the power-six kernel estimate]
(F9). In a periodic Gibbs state $\nu$, $\langle F',F\rangle_{\nu,c}=\nu(\overline{\theta_cF'}F)$ is a positive semi-definite Hermitian form on the local functions on $\{x_{\mu_0}>c\}$, the translation by $a_Ke_{\mu_0}$ is a contraction for it, and so the mirror may be moved away: $\|F\|_{\nu,c}\le\|F\|_{\nu,c'}$ for $c\le c'$, $c'-c\in a_K\mathbb Z$. It therefore suffices that $x_0$ lies at a distance between $\frac32d$ and $2d$ from the plane. There the plane is a wall of a board of side $\mathsf l$, $\theta X$ is the copy of $X$ in the neighbouring cell, and, as $\nu(\theta X\cdot X)=\nu(\theta(F-c)\cdot(F-c))-(\nu(F)-c)^2$ for $F=O^T_K(H)$ and $c$ its mean on $T_{\ell'}$, domination by $T_{\ell'}$ gives $\nu(\theta X\cdot X)\le e^{2G_g\mathsf l^3}\|F-c\|^2_{{\rm ch},\ell'}$, the eighth power of the seminorm being the mean of eight copies. For bond forms (B) bounds it, and for the whole tensor Lem.~\ref{bil:far} with arbitrary majorants, centred, at $n=4$; if $s(d)<s_8(g)$, (C1) at the distance $L^{-s_8(g)}$ bounds the covariance directly. So
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bil-mirror-constants}
\begin{multlined}
C^{\rm od}_\infty(g)=\max\{e^{2G_g\mathsf l^3}C_8^{1/4},\,59^2C^T_2(L^{-s_8(g)};1)\},\qquad C_\infty(g)=\max\{e^{2G_g\mathsf l^3}(C'_8)^{1/4}, \\
\,60^2C^T_2(L^{-s_8(g)};1)\},
\end{multlined}
\end{equation}
$C'_8=(\frac98)^460^8[g_0^4+\bar\omega'_{g,8}]$, $g_0=\frac32 81^2C'^2_{\mathsf k}$; complex weights of all directions cost $36$. For the kernel bound at off-diagonal entries, {\cite[Prop.~D.15]{YMM2}}(a) bounds the two-point kernel at $u$ by $\Gamma(|u|/2\sqrt3)$, and the mirror bound for bond forms applied to bumps at the height $t$ bounds $\Gamma(t)$ by a multiple of $C^{\rm od}_\infty(g)\mathsf b^{-2}\max\{1,t^{-1}\}^6$; the holomorphy of the two-point function in the relative position and the mean value inequality on a polydisc of radius proportional to $|x-y|$ turn this bound for bumps at the scale $|x-y|$ into the pointwise bound $A_6C^{\rm od}_\infty(g)\mathsf b^{-2}\min\{|x-y|_\infty,3\}^{-6}$ of the kernel. For the whole tensor the same steps, with the mirror bound for $X=A[O^T_K(H)]$ and its number $C_\infty(g)$, give the bound with a pure number $A$ in the place of $A_6$. By (D5) the kernel is of order $|x-y|^{-6}$ at short distance, so the power is the true one.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Contact extensions on tori and the mirror bound]
(F8). Every side $\ell=2L^m\in\mathfrak L(g)$ is admissible over the run of every datum at $g$: $LM\,R(x_K)\le L^m$ (equation~\YMMref{(1533)}{615}, as in the paragraph \emph{Data} of the Setting).

On $T_\ell$ the clause (i) of (E3), on Lem.~\ref{bil:nsrc} (the bound of that Lemma on an admissible side with $\max\{1,c(\ell)\}^nk'_n$ for $k'_n$, without the factor of the covering), at the geometry of Lem.~\ref{bil:nsrc} at $d=1.52h$ (a cube of side $\frac32h$ lies within $1.3h\le\frac78d$ of its centre, and cubes at sup distance $\ge\frac52h$ are more than $\frac54d$ apart), bounds the cumulants of $n$ entries at the cubes of side $\frac32h$ at sup distances $\ge\frac52h$, for $0<h\le h_0$, where $h_0\in\ell2^{-\mathbb N}$ and $h_0\le\min\{\ell/(64n),\frac12L^{-s_{\rm th}(n)}\}$, so that $1.52h\le1.52h_0<L^{-s_{\rm th}(n)}$, by $60^n\max\{1,c(\ell)\}^nC_n(g)[2\log\frac1{1.52h}+C(g)]^{8n\mathfrak p_0}\,b^{-n}\prod|H_a|_\infty$ uniformly in the cutoff, which is at most $C(1+\log\frac{h_0}h)^{8n\mathfrak p_0}b^{-n}\prod|H_a|_\infty$; through the cell means of Lem.~\ref{bil:rate} the bound passes to the limits of (D4), and Lem.~\ref{bil:ext} gives the extension, its bound, the contact terms and the counts.

At a cutoff the same construction, with the products of the cubes restricted to the scales $h$ with $s(1.52h)\le K$, gives subtracted lattice cumulants with the bound for all $\lambda\ge8h_K$, $h_K\le2C_W(K)a_K$ the least scale, uniformly in $K$; by Lem.~\ref{bil:rate} they converge to $\tilde S_n$; their difference to the lattice cumulants depends on $F$ only through the derivatives of the orders $\le3k$ on the strata of $k$ blocks and the values at distances $<6h_K$. On $\mathbb R^3$: let two cubes of side $\frac32h$ lie at sup distance $\ge\frac52h$, $d=1.31h$, $s(d)\le K$. Their centres are at sup distance $\ge4h\ge3d+a_K$, the cubes lie within $d-2a_K$ of their centres, and a mirror plane $\{x_{\mu_0}=c\}$ between them, normal to a coordinate in which the centres are $\ge4h$ apart, has each centre at a distance $\ge2h-\frac{a_K}2\ge\frac32d$.

On a torus $T_\ell$, $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$, the mirror $\theta$ has the second plane $\{x_{\mu_0}=c+\frac\ell2\}$, at a distance $\ge\frac\ell4-\frac{a_K}2\ge2h-\frac{a_K}2\ge\frac32d$ from each centre, as the sup distance $\ge4h$ of the centres on $T_\ell$ is at most $\frac\ell2$. For a bond form $Y$ with a complex weight of all directions, carried within $d-2a_K$ of a point at a distance $\ge\frac32d$ from both planes, and $\tau$ the translation by $a_Ke_{\mu_0}$, the invariance of the torus measure gives $\psi(k):=\langle\overline{\theta\tau^kY}\,\tau^kY\rangle_\ell=\langle\theta\bar Y\,\tau^{2k}Y\rangle_\ell$, and the Schwarz inequality for the positive form of $\theta$ on the half torus between the two planes (Cor.~\YMMref{85.3}{679}) gives $\psi(k)^2\le\psi(k-1)\psi(k+1)$ as long as the translates keep the distance $\ge\frac32d$ from both planes.

A non-negative sequence with this property takes its largest value at an end of its range, and there the point lies at a distance between $\frac32d$ and $2d$ from one of the two planes. That plane is a wall of a board of side $\mathsf l$, $\frac\ell2$ being a multiple of $\mathsf l$, the cells are distinct modulo the period, and domination by $T_{\ell'}$ with (B), or (C1) at the distance $L^{-s_8(g)}$ if $s(d)<s_8(g)$, bounds $\psi$ there as in (F9); so the mirror bound of (F9) for bond forms with complex weights of all directions, $0\le\langle\overline{\theta Y}Y\rangle_\ell\le36C^{\rm od}_\infty(g)b^{-2}|\mathsf w|_\infty^2$, holds on the tori of $\mathfrak L(g)$. With the Schwarz inequality for the positive form of that mirror, the means of bond forms being $0$, this mirror bound gives $|\langle Y[\mathsf w_1];Y[\mathsf w_2]\rangle_{K,\ell,\beta}|\le36C^{\rm od}_\infty(g)b^{-2}|\mathsf w_1|_\infty|\mathsf w_2|_\infty$ on every $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$: the bound of Lem.~\ref{bil:ext} with $q=0$ and a number free of the side, which every limit point inherits.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[First-creation and tail refinements]
\emph{Step 14: (E1)--(E3).} (E1): $\tilde\nu_K(\{Z_t\ne\emptyset\})=\sum_{t'\le t}\mathsf w_{t'}$, the weights of the first creations, and the run may be stopped at the level $t$ without changing this number. A first creation forces the failure of a local test in some test cube of the step; averaging the test over the gauge variables of its cube with the density of the gauge fixing of the step gives Borel functions $0\le F\le1$ that are local, gauge invariant and covariant under the lattice isometries, and the average is undone exactly inside the sum over the histories of any admissible set of values with the same $A_0$; so $\mathsf w_t$ is at most a sum of means of such functions, two for each test cube, its plaquette test and its averaged witness test, and at $t=1$ one for each density cube too: at most $2N_\tau+N_\delta$ for each cell of the level $t$, $N_\tau$ the number of the test cubes and $N_\delta$ that of the density cubes of a cell ($N_\delta$ entering at $t=1$ alone), and at most $(2N_\tau+N_\delta)M^{-3}\ell^3L^{3(K-t)}$ in all.

These means pass to a second admissible set of values with $\frac{93}{100}A_1$ for $A_1$ and the other constants that enter $c_\star$ kept, whose deposit constant $c_\star''$ has $(\frac{93}{100})^2c_\star\le c_\star''\le c_\star$: a product of test functions with disjoint supports is dominated by the probability, at the second set of values, that all the centres lie in the large-field region. Let $s_t$ be the side of a cell of the level $t$. If the torus has at least $2L^2$ cells of the level $t$ along a side, take the board of side $L^2s_t$ whose offset is the centre of the test function $F$, its \emph{witness}; the chessboard estimate with the mirrors in the walls of this board bounds $\langle F\rangle$ by the $N$-th root of the mean of the product of the copies of $F$ in its $N$ cells on the torus, and this product asks a large field in every cell of the board.

A creation reaches less than $49s_t<L^2s_t$ and so serves one cell alone: such a history has at least $N$ creations. Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8}, which bounds the density of these histories from above by $\exp[-\frac9{10}c''_\star p_0(g_t)^2N]$, at the fraction $\frac9{10}$ of the deposit, and that of the empty history from below, with the volume term $Cy_t(L^2MR(x_t))^3N$, which $\frac1{40}c_\star p_0(g_t)^2N$ pays, gives $\langle F\rangle\le\exp[-\frac34c_\star p_0(g_t)^2]$, as $\frac9{10}(\frac{93}{100})^2-\frac1{40}\ge\frac34$; with fewer cells of the level $t$ Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8} is used without mirrors, at the first set of values; a threshold on $y_K$ is removed by stopping the couplings at the last level above it.

The union bound over the cells gives $C_\flat$. The pair $(c^\natural_2,C_\natural)$: if $Z_t\ne\emptyset$, some cell of the level $t$ has its centre in $Z_t$, and the rarity at a point of Prop.~\ref{prop:local-large-field-rarity} with the union bound over the at most $M^{-3}\ell^3L^{3(K-t)}$ cells gives the bound. (E2): Lem.~\ref{bil:two}(b) with $\mathsf L=CM^{-3}\ell^3$; half of the exponent $cp_0(g_t)^2$ pays $\ell^3$ once $\frac12cA_0^2(\frac12s\log L)^P\ge3\log\ell$, which is $s\ge\sigma_c(\log\ell)^{1/P}$; the other half pays $\log C+3s\log L+2Y_s$ and the envelopes from $s_\flat(g)$ on; the depth condition $2c\mathfrak p_0A_0^2y^{P-1}\ge13$ is the rate condition of the deposit lemma at $c$. For (iv) there are three cases.

If $s(d)\ge\hat s$, (iv) is (iii). If $s(d)<\hat s$, then $d\ge L^{-s(d)}\ge L^2d'$, $d'=L^{-\hat s-1}$; let $s'=s(d')\ge\hat s$. If besides $K\ge s'$, cover by balls of radius $d'$, at which (ii) and (iii) hold; this costs the factor $(4/d'+2)^6\le5^6L^{6\hat s+6}$. If $K<s'$, the suprema of the forms give the number $100L^{8s'}\bar x_0^2$. So $C^\circ_3$ is the larger of $(4/d'+2)^6$ times the number of (ii) and (iii), in the units of (iv), and of $100L^{8s'}\bar x_0^2$; as $s'\le\hat s+1+\lceil\log_LC_W(2\hat s+2)\rceil$, $L^{8s'}\le L^{8\hat s+16}C_W(2\hat s+2)^8$, and with $L^{\hat s}\le L^{s_\flat(g)+1}\exp[2(\frac{6\log\ell}{cA_0^2})^{1/P}]$ this gives the bound of (iv), whose factor $(1+\log\ell)^8\exp[16(\frac{6\log\ell}{cA_0^2})^{1/P}]$ comes from the third case, the covering costing less; for (v) cover by balls of radius $\min\{\frac r8,L^{-\hat s}\}$. (E3): let $\ell=2L^m$ be admissible, $K\ge3$, and $s_{\rm th}(n)\le s(d)\le K$.

The proof of Lem.~\ref{bil:nsrc} reads the side at the following places, and each of them holds on an admissible side. The arithmetic of the working level (Lem.~\YMMref{126.1}{844}) asks nothing of the side. Lem.~\YMMref{126.2}{845} asks (Sd.1) alone, $MR(x_K)\le L^m$, and gives the frame, the order $x_0>x_1>\dots>x_K$ of the run (so $y_K\le y$), (Sd.2) and (Sd.3) ($LM\le L^m$, $\ell\ge N_{\mathsf H}$), the data of the construction at every level $\le K$, and the settings of the chain at the levels $\mathsf k<j_1=T=\mathsf k+1$ at every pair of the majorants; the setting of the chain for $n$ sources ({\cite[Prop.~B.21]{YMM2}} at $p=n$) asks these data and the frame alone, and the threshold $s_{\rm th}(n)$ reads no side.

The sum over the level of the first creation (equation~\eqref{eq:ward-first-creation}) holds at all the levels $\le K$ (Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8} and Cor.~\YMMref{69.4}{604}, as in the proof of Lem.~\YMMref{126.2}{845}), and the rarity on one torus, Prop.~\ref{prop:ward-fixed-volume-rarity} at the level $K$, whose hypotheses hold by that canonical construction, bounds the weights before any smallness of the side is used:
\[
\mathsf w_t\le\tilde\nu_K(\{Z_t\ne\emptyset\})\le2M^{-3}\ell^3e^{\mathsf B(x_K)\ell^3}L^{3(K-t)}e^{-c'p_0(g_t)^2},\qquad\mathsf B(x_K)\le\mathsf B(\bar x_0).
\]
From there on the side enters the proof only through this number $2M^{-3}\ell^3e^{\mathsf B(\bar x_0)\ell^3}$, in the tail of the sum over the level of the first creation, where a small side has $2M^{-3}\ell^3\le M^{-3}c'A_0^2Y_s^P$, and through the number of the boxes of the covering. As $Y_s\ge1$ the quotient of the two numbers is at most $c(\ell)$, each block of a partition takes at most the factor $\max\{1,c(\ell)\}$, and there are at most $n$ blocks: the bound of Lem.~\ref{bil:nsrc} holds on every admissible side with $\max\{1,c(\ell)\}^nk'_n(g,s(d))$ for $k'_n(g,s(d))$, which is (E3)(i) at this pair; the covering of Step~1, with $2\ell$ for $2\ell_{\max}$, gives (E3)(ii). The same argument serves every pair $(\mathsf L,c'')$ of (E3): the weights enter only the tail term of each block, linearly in $\mathsf L$ and through a Gaussian sum in which $c''\ge\frac12c'$ may stand for $\frac12c'$, and no smallness of $\mathsf w_t$ is used; so, as $Y_s\ge1$, each block takes at most the factor $\max\{1,M^3\mathsf L/(c'A_0^2)\}$, which is $\max\{1,c(\ell)\}$ at the pair above, and (E3)(i) and (ii) hold with it. The weights of (E1), $\mathsf w_t\le C_\flat M^{-3}\ell^3L^{3(K-t)}e^{-\frac12c'p_0(g_t)^2}$, give $C_\flat\ell^3/(c'A_0^2)$ in the place of $c(\ell)$.
\end{proof}

\section{Real-time tensor fields}\label{sec:realtime}

Let $V=\operatorname{Sym}_3(\mathbb R)$. The gauge-invariant
curvature tensor $T=(T_{ij})$ is normalized by
\[
 \mathcal T(H)=\frac12\int\operatorname{tr}(H(x)T(x))
                                    \,\mathrm{d}x,
 \qquad H\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;V_{\mathbb C}).
\]
This notation denotes a smeared bilinear, rather than a
pointwise product of separately constructed gauge-dependent
curvatures. Its trace gives the action density
$\mathcal O(f)=\mathcal T(f\mathbf1)$. An orthogonal matrix
$R$ acts on tensor labels by $\rho(R)E=RER^{\mathsf T}$.
Reflections act on these labels as well as on the points.

Fix a clustering component $\sigma$ of the Euclidean
correlations. Reflection in $x_3=0$ gives a Hilbert space
$\mathcal H$, the vacuum $\Omega$, a positive generator
$H$ of Euclidean time translations, and spatial momenta
$P_1,P_2$. These objects and the analytic insertion bounds
are supplied by \cite[\S\S6,8]{YM3main}. The purpose here
is to obtain operator-valued tempered distributions on
Minkowski space, including their tensor covariance and
locality. The Euclidean theorem on flat tests alone is
not being quoted as a theorem about distributions on all
ordinary Euclidean tests.

\begin{sketch}[Reconstruction of the tensor fields]
\label{supp:realtime-fields}
The component $\sigma$ reconstructs a covariant local
tensor field on $\mathbb R^{1+2}$, defined on a common
invariant domain and tempered in its real-time test
functions. Its translation spectrum lies in the closed
forward cone. The vacuum is cyclic and unique among
translation-invariant vectors. Multiplying a component
with $r$ Euclidean-time indices by $i^r$ gives its
Hermitian real-time component. Their separated Euclidean correlations agree
with $\sigma$.
\end{sketch}

\subsection{What the continuation must accomplish}

The input consists of separated Euclidean insertions.
Their analytic continuation must do more than assign
numbers to imaginary times: it must produce distributions
with a common domain, identify adjoints in a real tensor
frame, and make products commute at spacelike separation.
The bounded insertion operators give a route to these
tasks. They keep positive Euclidean time gaps while the
spatial and temporal arguments are continued, and their
power bounds control removal of those gaps.

The main manuscript has already constructed bounded slab
insertions and analytic point kernels. We use those
objects without repeating their lattice estimates or the
proof of rotation covariance. A slab insertion between
two positive time gaps is a bounded operator. Concentrating
its test near a point gives the regularized point
operators; the uniform $L^1$ insertion bound controls
their dependence on the regularization. Their products,
with positive gaps left between consecutive factors,
give holomorphic vector-valued kernels.

The spectrum controls the permitted complex translations.
For $z\in\mathbb C^3$, the tube
\[
 \operatorname{Re}z_3>
          |(\operatorname{Im}z_1,\operatorname{Im}z_2)|
\]
keeps the translation operator bounded. Consecutive
differences of insertion points must lie in this tube;
the absolute positions alone do not specify a product's
analytic domain. Rotation covariance identifies the
continuations obtained from different choices of the
Euclidean time direction. Reflection supplies the
adjoint relation. The tensor action in that relation
is essential for selecting the Hermitian real-time
components.

At the boundary of the tube, the point kernels need
not have pointwise limits. Their polynomial bounds give
distributional boundary values. Smearing those boundary
values defines the fields and their products on the
vacuum domain. The same bounds give temperateness and
the energy-domain extensions in the detailed argument.
Locality follows by comparing the continuations in the
two orders on a region of spacelike separation and
taking their boundary values there. The conclusion
concerns the common invariant domain; passing to a net
of bounded local operators is the separate task in
\S\ref{supp:C-363-1}.

There is also a Euclidean extension issue. The theory
on tests flat at coincidences does not select contact
terms supported on the diagonals. The additional
extension discussion below describes the freedom left
by the separated correlations. It does not assert
that an arbitrary choice of such terms inherits
reflection positivity on ordinary Euclidean tests.


For an open set $O$, let $\mathfrak S_V(O)$ denote the tuples of
$C^1_c(O;V)$ entries with pairwise disjoint supports, including the
empty tuple, and let $\mathbb C\mathfrak S_V(O)$ be their complex
linear span. We also write $\mathfrak S^1_V(O)$ for this space of
tuples when distinguishing it from tuples of continuous entries.
Put $\mathbb E_+=\{x_3>0\}$ and $V_0=\mathbb R\mathbf1$.
The stress tensor is $\Theta_{ij}=\frac12\delta_{ij}\operatorname{tr}T-T_{ij}$;
its labels are
$\mathsf m_{ij}=\delta_{ij}\mathbf1-e_ie_j^{\mathsf T}-e_je_i^{\mathsf T}$,
so $\frac12\operatorname{tr}(\mathsf m_{ij}T)=\Theta_{ij}$.
The notation $\mathcal T_K(H)$ below is another name for $O_K^T(H)$.
Isometries and linear maps of $V$ act entry by entry. Put
$\mathcal D_{n,c}=\mathbb C\mathfrak S_V(\{n\cdot x>c\})$,
$\Theta_n=1-2nn^{\mathsf T}$, and
$(\theta_{n,c}H)(x)=\Theta_nH(\theta_{n,c}x)\Theta_n$, where
$\theta_{n,c}x=x-2(n\cdot x-c)n$. Positivity at $(n,c)$ means
$\sigma(\theta_{n,c}\bar F\cdot F)\ge0$ for $F\in\mathcal D_{n,c}$.


\begin{definition}[Data with labels; real time; the frame]\label{C-355-5}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[beginpenalty=10000]
\item[(1)] A \emph{symmetric functional on labelled tuples} is a map $\sigma$ on $\mathfrak S^1_V(\mathbb R^3)$ with $\sigma(\varnothing)=1$, invariant under the permutations of the entries and $n$-linear on $\prod_aC^1_c(O_a;V)$ for open sets $O_a$ with pairwise disjoint closures; it is continued linearly to $\mathbb C\mathfrak S^1_V$. It is \emph{reconstruction data with labels} with the numbers $C_V,p_V\ge0$, $c_0\in(0,\frac12]$, if: $(\mathrm{Rec1})_V$ $\sigma(\mathsf rX)=\sigma(X)$ for every isometry $\mathsf r$; $(\mathrm{Rec2})_V$ $\sigma(\theta\bar F\cdot F)\ge0$ on $\mathbb C\mathfrak S^1_V(\mathbb E_+)$, the space $\mathcal H(\sigma)$ is separable, and $H$, $\mathcal U$, $\mathcal P$ are formed as in {\cite[Def.~2.2]{YMM2}}~(3); $(\mathrm{Rec3})_V$ $\mathcal P(\{E<|q|\})=0$; $(\mathrm{Rec4})_V$ for $\eta\in(0,1]$, $F,F'\in\mathbb C\mathfrak S^1_V(\{x_3>\eta\})$ and $h\in C^1_c(\{|x_3|<c_0\eta\};V)$,
\[|\sigma(\theta\bar F\cdot(h)\cdot F')|\le C_V\eta^{-p_V}\|h\|_{L^1}\,\|[\tau_{-\eta e_3}F]\|\,\|[\tau_{-\eta e_3}F']\| .\]
(Rec5) is the condition $\ker H=\mathbb C\Omega$; it is not part of the data.
\item[(2)] A point of $\mathbb R^{1+2}$ is $x=(t,\vec x)$; $U(x)=e^{itH}\mathcal U(\vec x)$; $\mathcal D_\infty=\bigcap_j\operatorname{dom}H^j$; $\mathcal S_V=\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{1+2};V_{\mathbb C})$ and $f^*=\rho(\theta)\bar f$. $\iota(t,\vec x)=(\vec x,-it)$; $\mathcal L$ is the restricted Lorentz group of $\mathbb R^{1+2}$, and $\hat\Lambda=\iota\Lambda\iota^{-1}\in\mathrm{SO}(3,\mathbb C)$. For $\mathfrak z\in\mathbb C^3$, $d_\square(\mathfrak z)=\operatorname{Re}\mathfrak z_3-|\operatorname{Im}\mathfrak z_1|-|\operatorname{Im}\mathfrak z_2|$ and $d_\circ(\mathfrak z)=\operatorname{Re}\mathfrak z_3-|(\operatorname{Im}\mathfrak z_1,\operatorname{Im}\mathfrak z_2)|$.
\item[(3)] The \emph{frame} (M1)--(M5) concerns a tensor carrying one label on a space with a scalar field $\phi(f)$, $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{1+2})$, a unique vacuum and a representation $U$ of $\mathbb R^{1+2}\rtimes\mathcal L$; with $\vartheta_1=\vartheta_2=1$, $\vartheta_3=-1$: (M1) sesquilinear forms $\mathfrak q_{ij}=\mathfrak q_{ji}$ on $\mathcal D_\infty\times\mathcal D_\infty$ with $|\mathfrak q_{ij}(\psi',\psi)|\le c_T\|(1+H)^l\psi'\|\,\|(1+H)^l\psi\|$, $\overline{\mathfrak q_{ij}(\psi',\psi)}=\vartheta_i\vartheta_j\mathfrak q_{ij}(\psi,\psi')$, $\mathfrak q_{ij}(\Omega,\Omega)=0$, and the operators $T^E_{ij}(F)$ they define, with the real-time components $T_{00}=-T^E_{33}$, $T_{0j}=-iT^E_{3j}$, $T_{jk}=T^E_{jk}$; (M2) continuous kernels $\mathsf s_{ij}(x;y_1,\dots,y_m)$ of one tensor entry among $m$ scalar entries, covariant under $\mathrm O(3)$ and the translations, $\mathsf s_{ij}(\mathsf Rx+b;\mathsf Ry+b)=\mathsf R_{ii'}\mathsf R_{jj'}\mathsf s_{i'j'}(x;y)$, related to the forms by the product formula of two point operators at different heights, $\mathsf s^{F',G}_{ij}(x,y)=\mathfrak q_{ij}(\psi'_x,\psi_x)$ as written out in the proof of Lem.~\ref{C-355-31}~(c); (M3) $T^E_{ij}(F_1)\phi(f)\psi=\phi(f)T^E_{ij}(F_1)\psi$ on the span $\mathcal D_0$ of $\Omega$ and the vectors $\phi(f_1)\cdots\phi(f_n)\Omega$, for spacelike separated supports; (M4)~(a) $T_{0\nu}(\partial_0F)\psi=\sum_{k=1,2}T_{k\nu}(\partial_kF)\psi$ on $\mathcal D_0$; (M5) $U(\Lambda)T[a,b](F)\Omega=T[\Lambda a,\Lambda b](F\circ\Lambda^{-1})\Omega$, $T[a,b]=a^\mu b^\nu T_{\mu\nu}$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Covariance, reconstruction, locality]\label{C-355-10}
Let $0<g\le\gamma^{\rm sd}_W$ and let $\sigma$ be a tensor limit at $g$ with label $b_*$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] $\sigma(\mathsf RX)=\sigma(X)$ for every $\mathsf R\in\mathrm O(3)$ and every $X\in\mathfrak S_V(\mathbb R^3)$.
\item[(b)] $\sigma(\theta_{n,c}\bar F\cdot F)\ge0$ for every unit vector $n$, every $c\in\mathbb R$ and every $F\in\mathbb C\mathfrak S_V(\{n\cdot x>c\})$, where $(\theta_{n,c}H)(x)=\Theta_nH(x-2(n\cdot x-c)n)\Theta_n$ and $\Theta_n=1-2nn^{\rm T}$.
\item[(c)] $\sigma^1$ is reconstruction data with labels at $V=\mathrm{Sym}_3(\mathbb R)$ with the invariant norm, with $c_0=\frac12$, every $p_V>\frac{17}2$ and $C_V=2^{p_V}C_{p_V}b_*^{-1}\le2^{p_V}C_{p_V}g^2$; its invariance holds at all tuples of continuous entries. The map $[F]_{\sigma^1}\mapsto[F]_\sigma$ extends to a unitary map of $\mathcal H(\sigma^1)$ onto $\mathcal H(\sigma)$ that carries $\Omega$, $H$, $\mathcal U$, $\mathcal P$ to $\Omega$, $H$, $\mathcal U$, $\mathcal P$.
\item[(d)] (i) For every $n$ there is exactly one continuous function $\mathsf s_n(x;e)$ on the non-coinciding configurations, $n$-linear in $e\in V^n$, with $\sigma(H_1,\dots,H_n)=\int\mathsf s_n(x;H_1(x_1),\dots,H_n(x_n))\,\mathrm{d}x$ for all $X\in\mathfrak S_V(\mathbb R^3)$; it is real-analytic, symmetric when points and labels are permuted together, $\mathsf s_n(\mathsf rx_1,\dots,\mathsf rx_n;\rho(\mathsf R)e_1,\dots,\rho(\mathsf R)e_n)=\mathsf s_n(x;e)$ for every isometry $\mathsf rx=\mathsf Rx+v$, and $|\mathsf s_n(x;e)|\le\bigl(C_V(2n^2/\min\{1,\mathsf d(x)\})^{p_V}\bigr)^n\prod_a|e_a|$ at every point, $\mathsf d(x)=\min_{a\ne b}|x_a-x_b|$; so $|\sigma(X)|\le(C_V(2n^2/d)^{p_V})^n\prod_a\|H_a\|_{L^1}$ at pairwise distances $\ge d$, $0<d\le1$, and $|\mathsf S_n(\varphi)|\le(8\pi^23^{\lceil p_V\rceil+2}(2e^2)^{p_V}C_V)^n(n!)^{2p_V}|\varphi|_{(\lceil p_V\rceil+4)n}$. (ii) There is a strongly continuous unitary representation $U$ of $\mathbb R^{1+2}\rtimes\mathcal L$ on $\mathcal H(\sigma)$ with $U(x,1)=e^{itH}\mathcal U(\vec x)$, $U(a,\Lambda)\Omega=\Omega$, $U(a,\Lambda)\mathcal D_0=\mathcal D_0$, the joint spectrum in the closed forward cone, and
\[U(a,\Lambda)T(f)U(a,\Lambda)^{-1}=T\bigl(\hat\Lambda f(\Lambda^{-1}(\cdot-a))\hat\Lambda^{\rm T}\bigr)\quad\text{on }\mathcal D_0 ,\]
with the transpose, not the adjoint. (iii) $T(f)T(f')\psi=T(f')T(f)\psi$ for $\psi\in\mathcal D_0$ whenever $f,f'\in\mathcal S_V$ have spacelike separated supports: all six components are local with respect to all six.
\item[(e)] Let $0<g\le\gamma$. Every sequence of first-passage data at $g$ with $K_j\to\infty$ and periodic Gibbs states has a subsequence along which the tensor limit exists. Every such limit $\sigma$ satisfies (a), (b) and the conclusion of {\cite[Thm.~E]{YMM2}}~(c), and $\sigma^1$ is reconstruction data with labels with $c_0=\frac12$, every $p_V>\frac{17}2$ and
\[C_V=3^{p_V}L^{4z}\max_{k=1,2}2^{p_V}C_{p_V}[g'_k]\,g'^2_k ,\]
where $z$ is the least integer $\ge1$ with $L^zg^{-2}\ge2(\gamma^{\rm sd}_W)^{-2}$, $g'^{-2}_1=L^zg^{-2}/2$, $g'^{-2}_2=L^{z+1}g^{-2}/4$, and $C_p[g']$ is the number $C_p$ of {\cite[Thm.~C]{YMM2}}~(c) at the coupling $g'$: a number formed from the constants, $g$ and $p_V$, one triple for all the tensor limits at $g$; so (c) and (d) hold for it.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Components and Wightman tensor fields]\label{C-355-13}
Let $\sigma$ be the tensor limit of a sequence $(K_j,\beta_j,\nu_j)$ of first-passage data and periodic Gibbs states at $g$, and $A^\nu_K(X)=\prod_a[\mathcal T_K(H_a)-\nu(\mathcal T_K(H_a))]$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] \emph{(Decomposition; $0<g\le\gamma^{\rm ref}_W$.)} There are a compact metrisable space $\mathsf X$, a Borel probability measure $\lambda$ on $\mathsf X$ with support $\mathsf X$, and real symmetric functionals $\sigma_\xi$, $\xi\in\mathsf X$, on labelled tuples, with $\xi\mapsto\sigma_\xi(X)$ continuous and $\xi\mapsto\sigma_\xi$ injective, such that $\sigma$ has iterated plateaux in the sense of {\cite[Def.~2.2]{YMM2}}~(5) at every $(X^1,\dots,X^q)$, $q\ge1$, $X^i\in\mathfrak S_V(\mathbb R^3)$, and its iterated plateau there is $\int\prod_i\sigma_\xi(X^i)\,\mathrm{d}\lambda(\xi)$.
\item[(b)] \emph{(Each component; $0<g\le\gamma^{\rm ref}_W$.)} For every $\xi\in\mathsf X$: (i) there are translation-invariant events $E_j$ with $\nu_j(E_j)>0$ such that $\rho_j=\nu_j(\cdot\,|\,E_j)\in\mathcal G^{\rm per}_{K_j,\beta_j}$ and $\sigma_\xi(X)=\lim_j\rho_j(A^{\nu_j}_{K_j}(X))$ along the full sequence, indeed $\|E_{\rho_j}[A^{\nu_j}_{K_j}(X)\,|\,\mathcal I]-\sigma_\xi(X)\|_{L^\infty(\rho_j)}\to0$, $\mathcal I$ the invariant $\sigma$-field; (ii) $\sigma_\xi((H))=\frac{c_{\pi(\xi)}}3\int\operatorname{tr}H$ with a real number $c_{\pi(\xi)}$, and the recentred functional $\sigma^c_\xi(X)=\sum_{J\subset\{1..n\}}\prod_{a\notin J}(-\sigma_\xi((H_a)))\,\sigma_\xi(X_J)$ is the tensor limit of $(K_j,\beta_j,\rho_j)$; so it has all the properties of a tensor limit, and $[F]\mapsto[\mathsf S_\xi F]$, $\mathsf S_\xi X=\sum_J\prod_{a\notin J}\sigma_\xi((H_a))X_J$, is a unitary map of $\mathcal H(\sigma_\xi)$ onto $\mathcal H(\sigma^c_\xi)$ that carries $\Omega_\xi$ to $\Omega$ and intertwines $H$ and $\mathcal P$; (iii) $\ker H_\xi=\mathbb C\Omega_\xi$; (iv) there is exactly one map $\pi$ of $\mathsf X$ onto the space $\mathsf X_0$ of the canonical decomposition $(\mathsf X_0,\lambda_0,(\sigma_{0,\zeta}))$ of the scalar part $\sigma|_{V_0}$ with $\sigma_\xi(f_1\mathbf 1,\dots,f_n\mathbf 1)=\sigma_{0,\pi(\xi)}(f_1,\dots,f_n)$; it is continuous and onto, and $\pi_*\lambda=\lambda_0$.
\item[(c)] \emph{(Wightman fields; $0<g\le\gamma^{\rm sd}_W$.)} For every $\xi$, the restriction of $\sigma^c_\xi$ to $C^1_c$ entries is reconstruction data with labels with $c_0=\frac12$, every $p_V>\frac{17}2$ and the numbers of Thm.~\ref{C-355-10}~(c), and it has (Rec5). Its reconstruction is a Wightman tensor field of six components in $1+2$ dimensions: the fields $T(f)$, $f\in\mathcal S_V$, on $\mathcal D_0$ are tempered; $\langle\psi,T(f)\psi'\rangle=\langle T(f^*)\psi,\psi'\rangle$, so that $T_{33}$ and $T_{jk}$, $j,k\le2$, are Hermitian and $T_{3j}$ is Hermitian after the factor $i$; $U(a,\Lambda)T(f)U(a,\Lambda)^{-1}=T(\hat\Lambda f(\Lambda^{-1}(\cdot-a))\hat\Lambda^{\rm T})$; the joint spectrum lies in the closed forward cone; $\Omega_\xi$ is the only invariant vector and is cyclic; all components are local with respect to all. The growth condition of {\cite[Thm.~C]{YMM2}}~(h) holds with the same numbers for all components. The given limit $\sigma$ is the integral over $\lambda$ of its components in the sense of (a).
\item[(d)] \emph{(The frame over a component; $0<g\le\gamma^{\rm sd}_W$.)} On the scalar subspace of $\mathcal H(\sigma^c_\xi)$ the frame (M1)--(M5) holds for the tensor formed at the label matrices $\mathsf m_{ij}$ of the stress tensor, with the forms $q_0(\cdot,\cdot;\mathsf m_{ij})$, the kernels $\mathsf s_{ij}(x;y)=\mathsf s_{1+m}(x,y;\mathsf m_{ij},\mathbf 1,\dots,\mathbf 1)$, the scalar field $\phi(f)=T(f\mathbf 1)$ and the restriction to the scalar subspace of the representation $U$ of Thm.~\ref{C-355-10}~(d)~(ii) for $\sigma^c_\xi$. The scalar subspace reduces $U(a,\Lambda)$: $\phi(f)$ keeps it; $U(a,\Lambda)\phi(f)U(a,\Lambda)^{-1}=\phi(f(\Lambda^{-1}(\cdot-a)))$ on $\mathcal D_0$, since $\hat\Lambda\mathbf 1\hat\Lambda^{\rm T}=\mathbf 1$; $U(a,\Lambda)\Omega=\Omega$; and $\Omega$ with the vectors $\phi(f_1)\cdots\phi(f_n)\Omega$ spans a dense subspace of it, by Prop.~\ref{C-355-25}~(a)~(v) for the restriction of $\sigma^c_\xi$ to the tuples with entries in $V_0$, whose space is the scalar subspace and whose fields are the restrictions of the $T(f\mathbf 1)$. In particular the real-time stress tensor is conserved, (M4)~(a).
\item[(e)] \emph{(The frame on $\mathcal H_0$; $0<g\le\gamma^{\rm sd}_W$.)} For $\sigma$ itself, (M1) holds, the kernels $\mathsf s_{ij}(x;y)$ of one tensor entry among scalar entries are covariant as in (M2) and continuous at all non-coinciding points, $[T^E_{ij}(F),\phi(f)]=0$ between scalar vectors at spacelike separation as in (M3), and $\langle\Omega,\phi(f_1)\cdots\phi(f_n)T[t](F)\Omega\rangle$ is invariant under $(f,t,F)\mapsto(f\circ\Lambda^{-1},\Lambda t,F\circ\Lambda^{-1})$ as in (M5).
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proposition}[Covariance at one label suffices]\label{C-355-14}
Let $0<g\le\gamma^{\rm sd}_W$ and let $\sigma$ be a tensor limit at $g$. If $\sigma(\mathsf RX)=\sigma(X)$ for all $\mathsf R\in\mathrm O(3)$ at the tuples with exactly one entry outside $V_0$, then the kernels of (M2) are covariant at all non-coinciding points and (M3), (M5) hold on $\mathcal H_0$.
\end{proposition}

By Thm.~\ref{C-355-10}~(a) every tensor limit at $g$ satisfies the condition of Prop.~\ref{C-355-14}, and its conclusion is contained in Thm.~\ref{C-355-13}~(e). Its proof uses rotational covariance only for tuples with exactly one entry outside $V_0$. It follows the proofs of Props.~\YMMref{108.3}{771}, \YMMref{110.2}{777} and~\YMMref{110.1}{776}, with one labelled insertion.

\begin{proposition}[Reconstruction for data with labels]\label{C-355-25}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[beginpenalty=10000]
\item[(a)] Let $\sigma$ be reconstruction data with labels with the numbers $C_V$, $p=p_V$, $c_0$; (Rec5) is not supposed. Then $\mathcal H(\sigma)$ is separable, and there are a strongly continuous unitary representation $U$ of $\mathbb R^{1+2}\rtimes\mathcal L$ with $U(x,1)=e^{itH}\mathcal U(\vec x)$, operators $\phi(f)$, $f\in\mathcal S_V$, on the span $\mathcal D_0$ of $\Omega$ and of the vectors $\phi(f_1)\cdots\phi(f_n)\Omega$, functions $\mathbf W_n(\mathfrak z;e)$ holomorphic on $\{d_\circ>0\}^{n-1}$ and $n$-linear in $e$, and vectors $\Psi_n(z;e)$ with $[X]=\int\Psi_n(x;h_1(x_1),\dots,h_n(x_n))\,\mathrm{d}x$ for the tuples in $\mathbb E_+$ ordered in the third coordinate, such that: (i) the spectral measure of $U(\cdot,1)$ is carried by the closed forward cone and $U(a,\Lambda)\Omega=\Omega$; with (Rec5), the invariant vectors are the multiples of $\Omega$; (ii) $\phi(f)\mathcal D_0\subset\mathcal D_0$, $U(a,\Lambda)\mathcal D_0=\mathcal D_0$, $f\mapsto\langle\psi,\phi(f)\psi'\rangle$ is tempered, and $\langle\psi,\phi(f)\psi'\rangle=\langle\phi(f^*)\psi,\psi'\rangle$; (iii) $U(a,\Lambda)\phi(f)U(a,\Lambda)^{-1}=\phi(D(\Lambda)f(\Lambda^{-1}(\cdot-a)))$ on $\mathcal D_0$, where $D(\Lambda)=\rho_{\mathbb C}(\hat\Lambda)$ and $\rho_{\mathbb C}$ is the holomorphic continuation of $\rho|_{\mathrm{SO}(3)}$ to $\mathrm{SO}(3,\mathbb C)$; at $V=\mathrm{Sym}_3(\mathbb R)$, $D(\Lambda)A=\hat\Lambda A\hat\Lambda^{\rm T}$; (iv) $\phi(f)\phi(f')\psi=\phi(f')\phi(f)\psi$ on $\mathcal D_0$ at spacelike separated supports, for all components; (v) $\mathcal D_0$ is dense; (vi) $|\mathbf W_n(\mathfrak z;e)|\le(C_V\eta^{-p})^n\prod_k|e_k|$ for $e\in V^n$, $d_\circ(\mathfrak z_k)\ge2\eta$, $0<\eta\le1$; $\langle\Omega,\phi(f_1)\cdots\phi(f_n)\Omega\rangle=\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}\int\mathbf W_n(\iota(x_2-x_1+i\epsilon\alpha_1),\dots;f_1(x_1),\dots,f_n(x_n))\,\mathrm{d}x$ for all $\alpha_k$ in the open forward cone; $\sigma(X)=\int\mathbf W_n(x_2-x_1,\dots;h_1(x_1),\dots)\,\mathrm{d}x$ at the tuples ordered in the third coordinate; (vii) there is exactly one function $\mathbf S_n$, holomorphic on the union of the tubes $\{d_\circ(\mathsf R^{-1}(z_{\varsigma(k+1)}-z_{\varsigma(k)}))>0,\ 1\le k<n\}$ over $\mathsf R\in\mathrm{SO}(3)$ and the permutations $\varsigma$, which on each of them is $\mathbf W_n$ written in the frame $\mathsf R$ at the labels $\rho(\mathsf R)^{-1}e_{\varsigma(k)}$; its restriction $\mathsf s_n$ to the real non-coinciding configurations is real-analytic, is the only continuous kernel of $\sigma$, is symmetric in points and labels together, and is invariant under every isometry; (viii) $\Omega$ and the vectors $\Psi_n(x;e)$ at real $x$ with $0<x_{13}<\dots<x_{n3}$ are total, and so are $\Omega$ and the classes of the tuples whose entries lie in disjoint slabs.

Clauses (i)--(vi) hold as well for complex symmetric functionals invariant under the orientation-preserving isometries, with $\overline{\sigma(W)}=\sigma(\theta\bar W)$ and with $(\mathrm{Rec2})_V$--$(\mathrm{Rec4})_V$.
\item[(b)] For data as in (a) the two-fold plateau $m_2(X,Y)=\lim_{|v|\to\infty}\sigma(X\cdot\tau_vY)$ exists, and $\sigma$ has a Hermitian canonical decomposition: a compact metrisable $\mathsf X$, a Borel probability measure $\lambda$ with support $\mathsf X$, and complex symmetric functionals $\sigma_\xi$ with $\overline{\sigma_\xi(X)}=\sigma_\xi(\theta X)$, continuous and injective in $\xi$, such that the iterated plateaux of $\sigma$ ({\cite[Def.~2.2]{YMM2}}~(5)) are $\int\prod_i\sigma_\xi(X^i)\,\mathrm{d}\lambda$; it is unique up to exactly one homeomorphism, and its components are real, so that it is a canonical decomposition, if and only if $m_2(F,F)\ge0$ for the real combinations $F$ of tuples.

Every component has $(\mathrm{Rec2})_V$--$(\mathrm{Rec4})_V$ with the numbers of $\sigma$ and (Rec5), is reflection positive at every mirror, and $|\sigma_\xi(X\cdot\tau_vY)-\sigma_\xi(X)\sigma_\xi(Y)|\le K(X,Y)|v|^{-1}$ for $|v|\ge r(X,Y)$, with $K$, $r$ formed from $C_V$, $p$, $c_0$ and the two tuples, the same for all $\xi$. Let $V_0$ be a subrepresentation such that the classes of the tuples with entries in $V_0$ are total, and let $(\mathsf X_0,\lambda_0,(\sigma_{0,\zeta}))$ be the Hermitian canonical decomposition of $\sigma|_{V_0}$, which is reconstruction data with labels in $V_0$ with the numbers of $\sigma$. There is exactly one map $\pi:\mathsf X\to\mathsf X_0$ with $\sigma_\xi|_{V_0}=\sigma_{0,\pi(\xi)}$ for every $\xi$; it is continuous and onto, $\pi_*\lambda=\lambda_0$, and $g\mapsto g\circ\pi$ is a unitary map of $L^2(\mathsf X_0,\lambda_0)$ onto $L^2(\mathsf X,\lambda)$.

So for every tuple $X$ there is a bounded Borel function $g_X$ on $\mathsf X_0$ with $\sigma_\xi(X)=g_X(\pi(\xi))$ for $\lambda$-almost every $\xi$, and the iterated plateaux of $\sigma$ are $\int\prod_ig_{X^i}\,\mathrm{d}\lambda_0$: the decomposition of $\sigma|_{V_0}$ bears that of $\sigma$ as measure spaces. The map $\pi$ is a homeomorphism if and only if every $g_X$ agrees $\lambda_0$-almost everywhere with a continuous function, in particular if $\dim\ker H<\infty$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(a) On the circular cone $|e^{-\mathfrak z_3E+i(\mathfrak z_1q_1+\mathfrak z_2q_2)}|\le e^{-d_\circ(\mathfrak z)E}$; this gives the contractions $\mathcal T(\mathfrak z)$, holomorphic inside the tube. By $(\mathrm{Rec4})_V$ the forms $(F,F')\mapsto\sigma(\theta\bar F\cdot(h)\cdot F')$ are bounded, whence insertion operators $B_\eta(h)$ with $\|B_\eta(h)\|\le C_V\eta^{-p}\|h\|_{L^1}$, covariant under the translations, $B_\eta(\tau_yh')=\mathcal T(y+(\eta-\eta')e_3)B_{\eta'}(h')\mathcal T(-y+(\eta-\eta')e_3)$. Since translations act on them Lipschitz-continuously (on the cone each derivative of $e^{-(\eta/2+y_3)E+i\vec y\cdot q}$ is at most $4/(e\eta)$), the limits $\mathsf B(\eta,\eta;e)=\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}B_\eta(\delta_\epsilon e)$, $\delta_\epsilon=\epsilon^{-3}\chi(\cdot/\epsilon)$ with $\chi\ge0$ radial of integral $1$, exist in norm, and $\mathsf b(w|e|w')=\mathcal T(w-se_3)\mathsf B(s,s;e)\mathcal T(w'-se_3)$ are holomorphic point operators with $B_\eta(h)=\int\mathsf b(y+\eta e_3|h(y)|-y+\eta e_3)\,\mathrm{d}y$.

Ordered tuples are products of insertion operators and semigroup factors; this gives $\mathbf W_n$, $\Psi_n$ and the integral formulas. Any $n$ distinct points are ordered in some frame $\mathsf R\in\mathrm{SO}(3)$ whose cap $\{\mathsf Re_3\cdot\hat v>\frac12\}$ contains a given direction (the zones $\{|u\cdot(x_a-x_b)|<\gamma_N|x_a-x_b|\}$, $\gamma_N=1/(2N^2)$ with $N\ge n$, cover less than a quarter of the sphere); the pieces in two frames agree at the real points of the intersection of two convex tubes, hence on it, and they form one function $\mathbf S_n$. Totality: the map $y\mapsto\Phi(y)$, the limit of the classes of tuples of bumps at $y$, has the real-analytic Gram kernel $\mathsf s_{2n}(\theta y,y')$, so its matrix elements are real-analytic; for a vector orthogonal to the $\Psi_n$ they vanish on the ordered configurations, hence on the connected set of the non-coinciding ones.

The fields are defined by the forms $q_0$ with $\mathsf A_l(e)=\Gamma(l)^{-2}\int\!\!\int(ss')^{l-1}e^{-s-s'}\mathsf B(s,s';e)\,\mathrm{d}s\,\mathrm{d}s'$, $\mathsf B(s,s';e)=\mathsf b(se_3|e|s'e_3)$, convergent for $l>p$; then $\mathcal T(w)\phi(f)\mathcal T(w')=\int\mathsf b(w+\iota x|f(x)|w'-\iota x)\,\mathrm{d}x$ for $w,w'$ in the open tube, and $\|(1+H)^j\phi(f)\psi\|\le c_j(f)\|(1+H)^{2l+j}\psi\|$. \emph{Boundary values} (vi): with $c_k=\iota(\frac i2\epsilon\alpha_k)$, $\alpha_k$ in the open forward cone, the contractions $\mathcal T(2c_k)$ commute with $H$ and tend strongly to $1$ as $\epsilon\downarrow0$; inserted between the fields, they turn $\langle\Omega,\phi(f_1)\cdots\phi(f_n)\Omega\rangle$ into $\int\mathbf W_n(\iota(x_2-x_1+i\epsilon\alpha_1),\dots;f_1(x_1),\dots,f_n(x_n))\,\mathrm{d}x$, up to an error that the energy bounds, applied from the right to the left, send to $0$.

\emph{The density of $\mathcal D_0$} (v): let $\psi\perp\mathcal D_0$. For a word $\mathsf w$ in the operators $\phi(f)$ and $\mathcal T(w)$, $\psi\perp\mathsf w\Omega$, by induction on the number of the letters $\mathcal T$: the matrix element is continuous on the closed tube and holomorphic inside in the argument $w$ of the leftmost such letter; it vanishes at $w=\iota a$, $a\in\mathbb R^{1+2}$, because $\mathcal T(\iota a)=U(a)$ moves the rest of the word into a word with translated test functions and one such letter fewer; so it vanishes on the half planes in time by the reflection principle, and on the tube by the identity theorem in the space variables. As $\mathcal T(w)\phi(g_ke)\mathcal T(w')\to\mathsf b(w|e|w')$ in norm for $g_k\ge0$ of integral $1$ whose supports shrink to a point, $\psi\perp\Psi_n(z;e)$, and $\psi=0$ by (viii).

\emph{The representation $D$}: with the covering $\mathsf p:\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb C)\to\mathrm{SO}(3,\mathbb C)$, the differential of $\rho\circ\mathsf p$ on $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ continues complex-linearly to $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb C)$ and integrates to a holomorphic representation of the simply connected $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb C)$, trivial on $\pm1$, hence to a holomorphic representation $\rho_{\mathbb C}$ of $\mathrm{SO}(3,\mathbb C)$ that continues $\rho$; $\Lambda\mapsto\hat\Lambda$ is a homomorphism of $\mathcal L$ into $\mathrm{SO}(3,\mathbb C)$, so $D(\Lambda)=\rho_{\mathbb C}(\hat\Lambda)$ is a representation, and $D(\Lambda)e^*=(D(\Lambda)e)^*$. Every $\Lambda\in\mathcal L$ is $(1\oplus\mathsf R_1)B(s)(1\oplus\mathsf R_2)$ with rotations $\mathsf R_1,\mathsf R_2$ of the space plane and the boost $B(s)$ : a spatial rotation and a boost send the future unit vector $e_0$ to $\Lambda e_0$, and their inverse followed by $\Lambda$ fixes $e_0$ and acts as a rotation of its orthogonal spatial plane; $\widehat{1\oplus\mathsf R}=\mathsf R\oplus1$, and $\widehat{B(s)}$ is the rotation in the plane $(e_1,e_3)$ by the imaginary angle $is$.

\emph{Lorentz covariance}: $\mathbf W_n$ is invariant under the real rotations about $e_3$ and under those in the plane $(e_1,e_3)$, and this last invariance continues holomorphically in the angle to imaginary angles, the boosts, the labels being moved by $e^{is\,\mathrm{d}\rho(\omega_1)}$, $\omega_1=E_{13}-E_{31}$, $d\rho$ the differential of $\rho$; no bound on this factor is needed. So $\mathbf W_n(\hat\Lambda\mathfrak z;D(\Lambda)e)=\mathbf W_n(\mathfrak z;e)$, and the boundary values at the cone vectors $\Lambda^{-1}\alpha_k$ give $\langle\Omega,\phi(\Lambda f_1)\cdots\phi(\Lambda f_n)\Omega\rangle=\langle\Omega,\phi(f_1)\cdots\phi(f_n)\Omega\rangle$ with $(\Lambda f)(x)=D(\Lambda)f(\Lambda^{-1}x)$.

As $(\Lambda f)^*=\Lambda(f^*)$, the map $\phi(f_1)\cdots\phi(f_n)\Omega\mapsto\phi(\Lambda f_1)\cdots\phi(\Lambda f_n)\Omega$ is isometric on the dense $\mathcal D_0$ and extends to a unitary operator $U(\Lambda)$; these form a representation with $U(\Lambda)U(a)U(\Lambda)^{-1}=U(\Lambda a)$, whose strong continuity reads of $D$ only that it is locally bounded. With the spectrum of $U(\cdot,1)$, the image of $\mathcal P$, carried by the closed forward cone by $(\mathrm{Rec3})_V$, this gives (i)--(iii). \emph{Locality}: the componentwise argument is that of Prop.~\YMMref{110.2}{777}. Fix the labels and compactly supported scalar tests with two adjacent supports spacelike separated. The height deformation used there stays in tilted tubes with every consecutive margin at least $3\eta$. The Cauchy--Riemann equations and integration by parts move derivatives onto the tests, and Lem.~\YMMref{109.4}{774} gives a finite smeared bound $Q_e(g)$ uniform along the deformation. For $g$ the product test, the integrals for the two adjacent orders differ by at most $2\eta Q_e(D'g)$, where $D'=\frac12(\partial_{t_{k+1}}-\partial_{t_k})$ and $k,k+1$ are the exchanged entries. Their endpoint boundary values therefore agree as $\eta\to0$. Graph-norm continuity extends the equality to Schwartz tests, as in the cited proof.

These are the proofs for scalar data of Props.~\YMMref{108.3}{771}, \YMMref{109.1}{773}, \YMMref{110.1}{776}, \YMMref{110.2}{777} and Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AO}{778}} among the construction results, with a label at each entry and with $D$ in the place of the trivial representation; besides them they read the spectral theorem, the identity theorem, the reflection principle in one variable and the covering of $\mathrm{SO}(3,\mathbb C)$ by $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb C)$. They read the reality of $\sigma$ and its invariance under an orientation-reversing isometry at one place only, the adjoint $B_\eta(h)^*=B_\eta(\theta\bar h)$, where $\overline{\sigma(W)}=\sigma(\theta\bar W)$ is all that is used; this gives (i)--(vi) for the complex functionals of the last sentence of (a). (b) For a combination $Y$ of tuples put $\mathsf e(Y)=P_0[\tau_{se_3}Y]$, $P_0$ the projection onto $\ker H$ and $s$ so large that $\tau_{se_3}Y$ lies over $\mathbb E_+$: it does not depend on $s$, it is invariant under the translations, and these vectors are dense in $\ker H$.

In a frame $\mathsf R$, by the cone, $\sigma(A\cdot\tau_wY)\to\langle\mathsf e(\theta\bar A'),\mathsf e(Y')\rangle$, $A'=\mathsf R^{-1}A$, $Y'=\mathsf R^{-1}Y$, uniformly as $|w|\to\infty$ with $\mathsf Re_3\cdot w\ge\frac12|w|$; two frames whose caps meet give the same limit, and the caps cover the sphere; so the two-fold plateau exists, $m_2(A,Y)=\langle\mathsf e(\theta\bar A),\mathsf e(Y)\rangle$. \emph{The rotations are trivial at infinity}: for a unit vector $u$, $\beta_u(F,G)=m_2(\theta_u\bar F,G)$ is a positive Hermitian form; for $u'\perp u$ the involution $\theta_u\theta_{u'}$ acts on its space as a self-adjoint unitary operator $\ge0$, which is $1$; hence $m_2(\theta_uA,Y)$ does not depend on $u$, $m_2(\mathsf rA,Y)=m_2(A,Y)$ and $\mathsf e(\mathsf rY)=\mathsf e(Y)$ for the orientation-preserving isometries $\mathsf r$, and $J\mathsf e(Y)=\mathsf e(\theta Y)$ defines a unitary involution $J$ of $\ker H$ with $m_2(\bar A,Y)=\langle J\mathsf e(A),\mathsf e(Y)\rangle$.

\emph{The operators at infinity}: $M(X)$ is the bounded operator of $\ker H$ with $\langle\mathsf e(Z),M(X)\mathsf e(Y)\rangle=\lim_{|v|\to\infty}m_2(\theta\bar Z,X\cdot\tau_vY)$, the limit of $\sigma(\tau_w\theta\bar Z\cdot X\cdot\tau_vY)$ as $w$ and $v$ go to infinity on opposite sides of $X$; for $X$ ordered in a frame, $M(X)=P_0\mathsf b_X|_{\ker H}$, $\mathsf b_X$ the product of the insertion operators and semigroup factors of the ordered tuple, and a partition of unity reduces every tuple to such ones. Then $M(F)^*=M(\theta\bar F)$, $M(\mathsf rX)=M(X)$ for the orientation-preserving and $M(\mathsf rX)=JM(X)J$ for the other isometries, $M(X\cdot\tau_vY)\to M(X)M(Y)$ strongly as $|v|\to\infty$, and, $\sigma$ being symmetric, the $M(X)$ commute.

They generate a separable commutative $C^*$-algebra; its space of characters is $\mathsf X$, the vacuum gives $\lambda$, whose support is $\mathsf X$ because $\Omega$ is cyclic, hence separating, for the algebra; $\ker H$ is carried unitarily onto $L^2(\mathsf X,\lambda)$, $\sigma_\xi(X)$ is the Gelfand transform of $M(X)$, so that $\overline{\sigma_\xi(X)}=\sigma_\xi(\theta X)$, and the iterated plateaux of $\sigma$ are $\langle\Omega,\prod_iM(X^i)\Omega\rangle$. Uniqueness follows from the density of the polynomials in the $\sigma_\xi(X)$ and their conjugates. \emph{Reality}: $m_2(\bar F,F)=\langle J\mathsf e(F),\mathsf e(F)\rangle$, so $m_2(F,F)\ge0$ for the real combinations $F$ if and only if $J\ge0$, that is $J=1$, that is $M(X)^*=M(X)$ for every tuple, that is every $\sigma_\xi$ is real.

\emph{The components}: an inequality of $\sigma$ at the tuples $F\cdot\tau_{tu}Y$, the spectator $Y$ sent to infinity along $u$, becomes an inequality between elements of the algebra on a dense set of $\ker H$, and, the Gelfand transforms being continuous and $\operatorname{supp}\lambda=\mathsf X$, an inequality at every $\xi$ (test it with $\lambda(O)^{-1/2}\mathbf 1_O$ for small neighbourhoods $O$ of $\xi$); so every $\sigma_\xi$ is reflection positive at every mirror, has $(\mathrm{Rec4})_V$ with the numbers of $\sigma$, and the translations act on its space by contractions and unitary operators, which gives $(\mathrm{Rec2})_V$, one countable family of tuples making all these spaces separable.

The spectral measures disintegrate, $\mu_F=\int\mu^\xi_F\,\mathrm{d}\lambda(\xi)$ for $F$ over $\mathbb E_+$; so $\mu^\xi_F(\{E<|q|\})=0$ for $\lambda$-almost every $\xi$, and, this number being lower semicontinuous in $\xi$, for every $\xi$: $(\mathrm{Rec3})_V$. At $\{(0,0)\}$ the disintegration gives $\int\|P^\xi_0[F]_\xi\|^2\,\mathrm{d}\lambda=\|P_0[F]\|^2=\int|\sigma_\xi(F)|^2\,\mathrm{d}\lambda$, while $\|P^\xi_0[F]_\xi\|\ge|\sigma_\xi(F)|$, $P^\xi_0$ the projection onto $\ker H_\xi$: so $\ker H_\xi=\mathbb C\Omega_\xi$ for almost every $\xi$. \emph{The rate}: for data, and for Hermitian data, $|\sigma(X\cdot\tau_vY)-m_2(X,Y)|\le K(X,Y)|v|^{-1}$ for $|v|\ge r(X,Y)$, with $K$, $r$ formed from $C_V$, $p$, $c_0$ and the two tuples alone.

In each frame of a finite family whose caps cover the sphere and in which $X$ and $Y$ are ordered, the difference $f(v)$ is the integral of $e^{-(v'_3-c)E+i\vec v'\cdot q}$, $v'=\mathsf R^{-1}v$, against a complex measure off $(0,0)$ whose variation is at most the product of the numbers $C_V\eta^{-p}\|h\|_{L^1}$ of the entries of $X$ and $Y$. The image $\kappa_v$ of this measure, with the exponential, under $(E,q)\mapsto s=E^2-|q|^2$ has the moments $\Delta^kf(v)$, which are independent of the frame. Its damping gives $\int e^{a\sqrt s}\,d|\kappa_v|(s)<\infty$ for every $a>0$ below the positive time margin, since $0\le\sqrt s\le E$. This square-root exponential condition determines complex measures within this class by their moments. Indeed, the real and imaginary parts of the difference of two such measures have zero moments, including order zero. Their positive and negative parts have equal masses and moments and inherit the same integrability condition; after normalization when the common mass is nonzero, Hardy's criterion applies to them \cite[Thm.~1]{StoyanovLin2013}. Thus $\kappa_v$ is independent of the frame, and its masses $f_{\mathsf B}(v)=\kappa_v(\mathsf B)$ on windows $\mathsf B$ are functions outside a ball $\{|v|<r_2\}$, with $\Delta f_{\mathsf B}(v)=\int_{\mathsf B}s\,\kappa_v(ds)$.

For $\mathsf B=[m_1^2,m_2^2)$, $|(\Delta-m_1^2)\operatorname{Re}(e^{i\varphi}f_{\mathsf B})|\le(m_2^2-m_1^2)\mathsf V_{\mathsf B}$, $\mathsf V_{\mathsf B}$ the variation of the part, and the comparison principle for $\Delta-m_1^2$ outside the ball, with the radial solution $\frac{r_2}re^{-m_1(r-r_2)}$ of the dimension three, gives $|f_{\mathsf B}(v)|\le\mathsf V_{\mathsf B}(\frac{r_2}{|v|}+\frac{m_2^2-m_1^2}{m_1^2})$; the harmonic part at the mass $0$, which tends to $0$ at infinity, is at most $\mathsf V_{\{0\}}\frac{r_2}{|v|}$; the sum over the windows $[(1+\epsilon)^j,(1+\epsilon)^{j+1})$, $j\in\mathbb Z$, with $\epsilon\downarrow0$, gives the rate. One rate serves all the components, which are Hermitian data with the numbers of $\sigma$; with the continuity in $\xi$ and $\operatorname{supp}\lambda=\mathsf X$ the bound by $\sigma_\xi(X)\sigma_\xi(Y)$ holds at every $\xi$, so that $\langle[F]_\xi,e^{-tH_\xi}[F]_\xi\rangle\to|\sigma_\xi(F)|^2$ and $\ker H_\xi=\mathbb C\Omega_\xi$ for every $\xi$.

\emph{The subrepresentation}: the defining limits of the operators at infinity of $\sigma|_{V_0}$ and of $\sigma$ agree at the tuples with entries in $V_0$; when their classes are total, $\sigma|_{V_0}$ and $\sigma$ have one space and one $\ker H$, the operators of these tuples generate a $C^*$-subalgebra with the same unit, for which $\Omega$ is cyclic too, $\pi$ is the restriction of the characters, the only map with $\sigma_\xi|_{V_0}=\sigma_{0,\pi(\xi)}$ because $\zeta\mapsto\sigma_{0,\zeta}$ is injective, $\pi_*\lambda=\lambda_0$ by the vacuum state, $\pi$ is onto because its image is compact of full measure, and $g\mapsto g\circ\pi$ is unitary because both decompositions carry the one space $\ker H$ unitarily onto their $L^2$; $\pi$ is injective if and only if the subalgebra is the whole algebra, by the theorem of Stone and Weierstrass, that is if and only if every $g_X$ agrees almost everywhere with a continuous function; and if $\dim\ker H=N<\infty$, then $\mathsf X$ and $\mathsf X_0$ have $N$ points each.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The circular cone from five mirrors; for data]\label{C-355-26}
Let $\sigma$ be a real symmetric multilinear functional on labelled tuples, with $\sigma(\varnothing)=1$ and bounds independent of the position, invariant under the translations. For a unit vector $u$ at whose mirror $\{u\cdot x=0\}$ $\sigma$ is reflection positive, let $\mathcal H_u$, $H_u$, $\mathcal P_u$ be formed as in {\cite[Def.~2.2]{YMM2}}~(3) with $u$ in the place of $e_3$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] Let $u'$ be a unit vector orthogonal to $u$. If $\sigma$ is reflection positive at the mirrors with the normals $u$ and $(u+u')/\sqrt2$, then $H_u\ge|u'\cdot P_u|$.
\item[(b)] Let $(u,u',u'')$ be an orthonormal basis and $n_\beta=\cos\beta\,u+\sin\beta\,u'$. If $\sigma$ is reflection positive at the four planes through the axis $\mathbb Ru''$ with the normals $n_0,n_{\pi/4},n_{\pi/2},n_{3\pi/4}$ and at one plane with the normal $(n_{\beta_1}+u'')/\sqrt2$, $\beta_1\in\frac\pi4\mathbb Z$, then $\mathcal P_{n_\beta}(\{E<|q|\})=0$ for every $\beta\in\frac\pi4\mathbb Z$.
\item[(c)] \emph{(Eight measures in one plane; analysis alone.)} Let $R>0$, $\kappa>0$, $C<\infty$, $\mathsf V=\{(E,q)\in\mathbb R^2:E\ge|q|\}$, and for each of the eight angles $\beta\in\frac\pi4\{0,1,\dots,7\}$ let $m_\beta$ be a complex Borel measure on $\mathsf V$ with $|m_\beta|(\mathsf V)\le C$; for $\rho>0$ and complex $c$ put
