Then $a_K\le\rho/4M$; with the tent $\tau$ of height $1$ and radius $\frac13a_K$, the functions $f_a=\sum_pw_a(p)\tau(\cdot-x(p))$ are Lipschitz, $f_a\circ x=w_a$, $\operatorname{supp}f_a\subset\mathbb B(x_a,2r)$, and (a) applies at $k=\mathsf k(r)$ with $\bar{\mathsf d}=2r$. For $0\le i\le K$: (P1) $\sum_p|w_a(p)|\le81(\rho/a_K)^3|w_a|_\infty$; (P2) $\mathsf N_i(w_a)\le(2\hat\rho_i/M+3)^3\le108(1+t_i)$, $t_i=\frac{27}{8M^3}\hat\rho_i^3$; (P3) $\mathsf D^{12}_i\ge\hat r_i/\sqrt3-1$; and every corner of a plaquette of $\operatorname{supp}w_1\cup\operatorname{supp}w_2$ lies within the sup distance $R_w\le11\hat r_{i+1}$, in level-$(i+1)$ units, of a bare site next to $x_1$. For weights placed at $(\rho,r,\mathsf d)$, or forming two pairs at $(\rho,r,\mathsf d)$, with $\mathsf d\le e^{-2\sqrt3}$, the same holds, (P3) holds across the clusters with $\hat{\mathsf d}_i$ for $\hat r_i$, and (a) applies to the two clusters at $k=\mathsf k(\mathsf d)$, each lying in a ball of radius $10\mathsf d$; for two weights with $\Sigma(w_a)\subset\mathbb B(x_a,\rho)$ at a distance $\ge\mathsf d\ge\rho$, (a) applies at $k=\mathsf k(\mathsf d)$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(a) First consider a pair satisfying the four geometric hypotheses
in the statement. The first-passage construction gives
$x_0>\cdots>x_K>g^{-2}$ and the running comparison in
\eqref{eq:pair-frame-running}; see Prop.~\YMMref{74.1}{615}.
Since $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$, it also gives
$MR(x_K)\le L^m$. The lattice is therefore admissible over every
initial segment of the run. In particular $L^m\ge LM$ and
$\ell\ge N_{\mathsf H}$, by the proof of
Lem.~\YMMref{126.2}{845}.

{\cite[Prop.~B.21]{YMM2}}, applied with
$k=K-1$, supplies the actual setting \textup{(J)}, its weighted
progression and the identification \textup{(Pv)}. This is the same
canonical datum at every height, with the counterterms of this run.
The inequalities defining $x_{\rm J}$ apply at every $x_j$:
they give the regular-background radius, the half-ceiling and
$C_0^\flat\mathsf S_A\theta^{[K-1]}\le1$.
The cutoff bound $\varepsilon_j\le\varepsilon_\flat$ is part of the
actual history verification in that proposition.

The supports satisfy $\widehat d_k\ge M$ and $D_k\ge3M$ by
hypothesis. Their separation at earlier levels is
$D_j=L^{k-j}D_k$, so the decreasing function $\mathsf T$ obeys
$\mathsf T(D_j/M)\le\mathsf T(3)$ for $j<k$.
Equation~{\cite[eq.~228]{YMM2}} therefore gives
all the mixed derivative hypotheses at the lower cut. The threshold
inequalities in equation~\YMMref{(2326)}{845} give
\eqref{eq:pair-frame-lowering}. The factor $2$ in the corresponding
lowering-domain inequality makes its conclusion strict. They also
give $y_K\ge\max\{2\mathfrak p_0,1+\log L\}$ and
$x_K\ge4\bar B$.
Thus \textup{(Jt.1)--(Jt.3)} hold. Finally
$x_i>g^{-2}\ge x_{\rm jt}$ and the threshold computation in
Remark~\ref{C-352-9} give \textup{(Jt.6)}.

This verification uses only the four geometric properties in the
statement. It uses neither the filling nor the sign condition of a
test pair, nor the formula for the working level. For $n$ functions
in two clusters, apply it to the two sums over the clusters, with
real coefficients for which both sampled sums are nonzero.
Shrinking a support preserves the radius and separation conditions.

For a test pair at $k_0=\max\{K-s,2\}$, Lem.~\YMMref{126.1}{844}
gives $d\ge a_K$, $\widehat d_{k_0}\ge M$ and $D_{k_0}\ge3M$.
The preceding argument gives its frame. At all heights below $k_0$,
{\cite[eq.~228]{YMM2}} gives
$s^{[j]}\le s^\star/2$, including $j=0$, and the same separation
argument proves \textup{(Jt.4)}. Choose
\[
 n_T=\left\lceil\log_L
      (\widehat d_{k_0}y_{k_0}^{3\mathfrak p_0})\right\rceil,
 \qquad T=k_0+n_T.
\]
The room bound $\mathsf{Lm}_s\le L^{s-3}$ and the final assertion of
Lem.~\YMMref{126.1}{844} give $k_0<T\le K-2$.
This proves \textup{(Jt.5)} and the claimed full pair setting.

(b) The working level at $\varrho=\rho$ gives $a_K\le a_{K-\mathsf k(\rho)}\le\rho/4M$. Two distinct barycentres are at least $2^{-1/2}a_K$ apart, so the tents are disjoint and $f_a(x(p))=w_a(p)$.

A corner is at the distance $2^{-1/2}a_K$ from its barycentre: corners of the two supports are $\ge r-\sqrt2a_K$ apart, $\ge(r-\sqrt2a_K)/\sqrt3$ in the sup distance, that is $\ge\hat r_i/\sqrt3-1$ level-$i$ units. At $\varrho=r$ the working level gives $2\le\mathsf k(r)\le K-1$, $2\hat r_{\mathsf k(r)}\ge M$ and $\mathsf D^{12}_{\mathsf k(r)}\ge\frac4{\sqrt3}MY_r^{2\mathfrak p_0}-1\ge3M$, as $Y_r\ge2\sqrt3$. (P1): the barycentres of one orientation form a translate of $a_K\mathbb Z^3$, with at most $(2\rho/a_K+1)^3\le27(\rho/a_K)^3$ points in a ball of radius $\rho\ge a_K$, and there are three orientations. (P2): an interval of length $2\hat\rho_i+\eta_i$ meets at most $2\hat\rho_i/M+3$ intervals of length $M$, and $(2y+3)^3\le4(8y^3+27)$. $R_w$: all points of $\Sigma(w_1)\cup\Sigma(w_2)$ are within $9r$ of $x_1$.

The three-point and four-point cases are the same with $\mathsf d$ for $r$ across the clusters, and $9r+a_K\le10\mathsf d$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The calculus of the derivative families]\label{C-352-12}
Let $0<g\le\gamma$ with $g^{-2}\ge x_{\mathrm J}$, $(K,\beta)$ a first-passage datum at $g$ with $K\ge2$, $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$, and $w_1,\dots,w_p$ real weights, none identically $0$, $p\ge1$ arbitrary. For $\emptyset\ne\beta\subset[p]$, $m=|\beta|$, $0\le j\le K-1$, put
\[
\begin{multlined}
\mathsf m_{j,a}=12M^3\alpha_0^2L^{K-j}|w_a|_\infty,\quad\varkappa_j=\frac{M^{3/2}}{2\mathsf C_{\mathcal A}\mathfrak b_j},\quad\gamma_j=\theta^{[j]}\varkappa_j,\quad\mathsf U_{j;\beta} \\
=\varkappa_j^{m-1}(N^{[j]}_\star)^{1-m}\prod_{a\in\beta}2\mathsf m_{j,a},\quad\bar\nu_{j;\beta}=\gamma_j\mathsf U_{j;\beta},
\end{multlined}
\]
with the constant $\mathsf C_{\mathcal A}$ of the one-step theorem; the bare arrays of the weighted progression, $\mathfrak f_{\lambda,j}=((E^{(i)}_\lambda,e_i)_{i\le j},(\mathsf W_{L^{K-j}w_\lambda}))$ for $\lambda$ near $0$, where the counterterms $e_i$ of the regular progression of the run are real numbers that depend neither on $\lambda$ nor on the sources, and the weight member $\mathsf W_w$ is linear in $w$, so that $E^{(j+1)}_\lambda-E^{(j+1)}=\mathsf{St}^{[j]}(\mathfrak f_{\lambda,j})-\mathsf{St}^{[j]}(\mathfrak f_{0,j})$ (equation~{\cite[eq.~200]{YMM2}}); their value at $\lambda=0$, $\mathfrak f_{0,j}=((E^{(i)},e_i)_{i\le j},(0))$; and their derivatives $\mathfrak f_{\beta,j}=\partial_\beta\mathfrak f_{\lambda,j}|_{\lambda=0}=((E^{(i)}_\beta,0)_{i\le j},(H_\beta))$ with $H_{\{a\}}=\mathsf W_{L^{K-j}w_a}$ and $H_\beta=0$ for $m\ge2$; and $\bar{\mathsf h}_{j;\beta}=\mathfrak n[\mathfrak f_{\beta,j}]/\mathsf U_{j;\beta}$, $\bar\Psi_{j;\beta}=\|E^{(j+1)}_\beta\|_{j+1,\lambda_{\mathrm{out}}}/\bar\nu_{j;\beta}$. Then for $1\le j\le K-1$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] \emph{Chain rule.} $E^{(j+1)}_\beta=\sum_{\pi\in\mathrm{Part}(\beta)}\bigl(\prod_{\beta'\in\pi}\partial_{s_{\beta'}}\bigr)\mathsf{St}^{[j]}\bigl(\mathfrak f_{0,j}+\sum_{\beta'\in\pi}s_{\beta'}\mathfrak f_{\beta',j}\bigr)\big|_{s=0}$; $E^{(j)}_\beta$ is $m$-linear in $(w_a)_{a\in\beta}$, depends on no other source, and is the same in every progression that holds the sources of $\beta$.
\item[(b)] \emph{Derivatives of the step.} $N(\mathfrak f_{0,j})\le\frac12N^{[j]}_\star$, and for bare arrays $\mathfrak f,\mathfrak g_1,\dots,\mathfrak g_q$ with $N(\mathfrak f)\le\frac12N^{[j]}_\star$
\[
\bigl\|\partial_{s_1}\cdots\partial_{s_q}\mathsf{St}^{[j]}\bigl(\mathfrak f+\textstyle\sum_ls_l\mathfrak g_l\bigr)\big|_0\bigr\|_{j+1,\lambda_{\mathrm{out}}}\le(2(q-1))^{q-1}\,\theta^{[j]}\varkappa_j^q\,(N^{[j]}_\star)^{1-q}\prod_l\mathfrak n[\mathfrak g_l].
\]
\item[(c)] \emph{Lags.} If $\mathfrak g=((G^{(i)},0)_{i\le j},(H))$ and each $G^{(i)}(X,\cdot,z)$ vanishes unless $X$ meets a set $\mathsf{Cr}$ of bare sites, then $\mathfrak n[\mathfrak g]\le\|H\|_{j,\kappa}+\sum_{i\le j}\omega^{\mathrm{sp}}_{j-i}(i)\|G^{(i)}\|_{i,\kappa}$, where $\omega^{\mathrm{sp}}_0=1$, $\omega^{\mathrm{sp}}_l(i)=\varpi_l+L^{-4l}\min\{L^{3l},c_3\mathsf n^{\mathrm{cb}}_i(\mathsf{Cr})\}$, $0\le\varpi_l\le L^{8-5l}$, $\mathsf n^{\mathrm{cb}}_i(\mathsf{Cr})$ is the number of the cubes of $\pi_i$ that hold a site of $\mathsf{Cr}$, and $c_3$ is a constant.
\item[(d)] \emph{Support.} $E^{(i)}_\beta(X,\cdot,z)=0$ unless every $\operatorname{supp}w_a$, $a\in\beta$, has a plaquette with its corners in $X$; and then $d_i(X)\ge[\max_{a,b\in\beta}\mathsf D^{ab}_i/M-2]_+$.
\item[(e)] \emph{Start.} $\bar\Psi_{0;\beta}\le m^m(\mathsf c^\flat/2)^m$ with a constant $\mathsf c^\flat$; and if $\sum_p|w_a(p)|\le81(\rho/a_K)^3|w_a|_\infty$ for a width $\rho\ge a_K$, then $\|\mathsf W_{L^{K-j}w_a}\|_{j,\kappa}\le\varsigma_j\mathsf m_{j,a}$, $\varsigma_j=\min\{1,t_j\}$.
\item[(f)] \emph{Units.} $\gamma_j=c_\gamma x_j^{-1/2}$, $\bar\nu_{j;\beta}=\bar c_mx_j^{-m/2}\prod_{a\in\beta}(|w_a|_\infty/a_{K-j})$; for $i\le j$: $(\frac45)^{m/2}L^{(j-i)m/2}\bar\nu_{j;\beta}\le\bar\nu_{i;\beta}\le(\frac43)^{m/2}L^{(j-i)m/2}\bar\nu_{j;\beta}$, $\gamma_i\le(\frac43)^{1/2}L^{-(j-i)/2}\gamma_j$, $\sum_{i<j}\gamma_i\le0.45\gamma_j$; and $\varkappa_j\le\frac16L^{-3/2}$.
\item[(g)] \emph{Recursions.} $\bar\Psi_{j;\beta}\le\sum_{\pi\in\mathrm{Part}(\beta)}(2(|\pi|-1))^{|\pi|-1}\prod_{\beta'\in\pi}\bar{\mathsf h}_{j;\beta'}$; and for $m\ge2$ and every $a_*\in\beta$, with $\omega^{\mathrm{sp}}$ formed with $\mathsf n^{\mathrm{cb}}_i=\mathsf N_i(w_{a_*})$,
\[
\begin{multlined}
\bar{\mathsf h}_{j;\beta}\le\gamma_j(\tfrac43)^{m/2}\sum_{i\le j}\omega^{\mathrm{sp}}_{j-i}(i)\,\sigma_{i;\beta}\,L^{(j-i+1)m/2}\,\bar\Psi_{i-1;\beta},\qquad\sigma_{i;\beta}=e^{-c_\sigma[\max_{a,b\in\beta}\mathsf D^{ab}_i/M-2]_+}, \\
c_\sigma=\min\{\tfrac12,4\beta_{\mathrm s}\kappa\}.
\end{multlined}
\]
\end{enumerate}
No assumption of (a)--(g) depends on $p$; the order $m$ enters through the displayed numbers alone. There are numbers $\tau^\natural,\gamma^\natural>0$ formed from the constants such that $\theta^{[K-1]}\le\tau^\natural$ gives $\gamma_j\le\gamma^\natural$ for all $j<K$ and $2C_\omega\mathsf c^\flat\theta^{[0]}\le1$, $C_\omega$ the constant of Lem.~\ref{C-352-15}; and a number $r_1(\mathsf b)>0$, formed from the constants and $\mathsf b$ and not increasing in $\mathsf b$, such that every width $0<\rho\le r_1(\mathsf b)$ with $s(\rho)\le K$ has $\rho\ge4Ma_K$ and $E_\sigma(\hat\rho_1/2)\le\varkappa_0^4$, where $E_\sigma(u)=\exp(-c_\sigma[u/\sqrt3M-3]_+)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(a) The progression is $E^{(j+1)}_\lambda-E^{(j+1)}=\mathsf{St}^{[j]}(\mathfrak f_{\lambda,j})-\mathsf{St}^{[j]}(\mathfrak f_{0,j})$ (equation~{\cite[eq.~200]{YMM2}}), and the multilinear derivatives at $\lambda=0$ of a composition are sums over partitions; the dependence through $w_\lambda$ alone gives the multilinearity. (b) Within the holomorphic, gauge-invariant input class of Prop.~\ref{prop:source-entry}, the fourth family must vanish at the block field $0$ and have finite norm \eqref{eq:source-entry-norm} on the polydisc $|B(b)|<\mathsf C_{\mathcal A}\mathfrak b_j$. A family that vanishes at $B=0$ and is bounded on that polydisc is at most its supremum times $|B|/\mathsf C_{\mathcal A}\mathfrak b_j$ (Schwarz's lemma); so $\mathsf{St}^{[j]}(\mathfrak f)$ is formed for $\varkappa_j\mathfrak n[\mathfrak f]\le N^{[j]}_\star$, with
\[
|\mathsf{St}^{[j]}(\mathfrak f)-\mathsf{St}^{[j]}(\mathfrak f')|(X,P,z)\le\theta^{[j]}\varkappa_j\,\mathfrak n[\mathfrak f-\mathfrak f']\,e^{-\lambda_{\mathrm{out}}d_{j+1}(X)},
\]
and it is holomorphic in the parameters of $\mathfrak f+\sum s_l\mathfrak g_l$ on $\{\varkappa_j\mathfrak n[\cdot]<N^{[j]}_\star\}$. Dividing the Lipschitz bound by $|s|$ and letting $s\to0$ gives $\|\mathsf D\mathsf{St}^{[j]}(\mathfrak h)[\mathfrak g_1]\|_{j+1,\lambda_{\mathrm{out}}}\le\theta^{[j]}\varkappa_j\mathfrak n[\mathfrak g_1]$ wherever $\varkappa_j\mathfrak n[\mathfrak h]<N^{[j]}_\star$; this is (b) at $q=1$. For $q\ge2$, as $\varkappa_j\mathfrak n[\mathfrak f]\le N(\mathfrak f)\le\frac12N^{[j]}_\star$, the point $\mathfrak f+\sum_{l\ge2}s_l\mathfrak g_l$ stays in that set on the polydisc of the radii $N^{[j]}_\star/2(q-1)\varkappa_j\mathfrak n[\mathfrak g_l]$ in $s_2,\dots,s_q$; Cauchy's inequality in these $q-1$ variables, applied to the first derivative in the direction $\mathfrak g_1$, gives the factor $\prod_{l\ge2}2(q-1)\varkappa_j\mathfrak n[\mathfrak g_l]/N^{[j]}_\star$, that is (b), with $(2(q-1))^{q-1}=1,2,16,216$ for $q=1,\dots,4$.

This factor $1/\mathfrak b_j$ for every order in the sources is the whole of the loss $\mathfrak b_j^2$ that a bound through the size $N$ would cost. $N(\mathfrak f_{0,j})\le\frac12N^{[j]}_\star$ is the half-ball estimate in the proof of Prop.~\YMMref{122.2}{827}: the admitted bound $s_j=\theta^{[j]}/K_{\mathbf M}\le s_\omega^\star/2$ gives $N_j(f_{0,j})\le N_\star\le w_\star/(4K_\Lambda s_\omega^\star)\le w_\star/(8K_\Lambda s_j)=N_{\star,j}/2$. {\cite[Prop.~B.21]{YMM2}} verifies this ceiling at the actual run. (c) Use the wide-domain and octet decomposition in the proof of
Prop.~\YMMref{51.16}{412}, with zero counterterms and all relative
localization radii equal to $1$. Put $l=j-i\ge1$ and
$D_l=\max\{2L^{l-1}-2,0\}$. The wide domains have size at least $D_l$.
Their rooted sum gives the factor
$\varpi_l=L^{3l}e^{-D_l}$ of equation~\YMMref{(884)}{414}.
For $l=1$ this is $L^3$; for $l\ge2$,
\[
 D_l\ge2(l-1)(L-1)\ge8(l-1)\log L,
 \qquad\varpi_l\le L^{8-5l},
\]
where the second inequality uses $L\ge13$.
For a narrow domain, equation~\YMMref{(864)}{408} bounds the octet
term minus its constant by
\[
 C_{\rm oc}\|G^{(i)}\|_{i,\kappa}
      (d_i(X)+2)^2L^{4-4l}e^{-\kappa d_i(X)}.
\]
Sum first over domains meeting $\mathsf{Cr}$ and then over their
base points. The rooted count in {\cite[Lem.~B.10]{YMM2}}
applies with the marked sites of $\mathsf{Cr}$ in place of plaquette
corners: each relevant domain contains one of the
$\mathsf n_i^{\rm cb}(\mathsf{Cr})$ marked cubes, and
$\#(X\cap\mathbb T^{(i)})\le8M^3(d_i(X)+1)$.
The remaining sum is bounded by the same convergent series of a
polynomial in $d_i(X)$ times its exponential decay.
This replaces the $L^{3l}$ possible positions in the unrestricted
count by $c_3\mathsf n_i^{\rm cb}(\mathsf{Cr})$.
Taking the better of the two counts, with the normalization of
equation~\YMMref{(885)}{414}, gives the narrow contribution
$L^{-4l}\min\{L^{3l},c_3\mathsf n_i^{\rm cb}(\mathsf{Cr})\}$.
The fixed constants, including $L^4$, are those in the bracket
normalization and in $c_3$. There is no growing-radius factor here:
the relative radii are $1$. The level-$j$ family and $H$ have no lag
and retain their ordinary norm bounds. This proves (c). (d) is the locality of the progression with the linear size of a domain. (e) The one-step theorem applied at the height $0$, where the source stands in the fourth place itself, with Schwarz's lemma as in (b); the weight member: $|a_p|<\frac12\alpha_0^2\eta_j^4$ on the cores, and the count of plaquettes. (f) is arithmetic along the run (Lem.~\ref{C-352-10}). (g) follows from (a), (b), (e) in the units, and from (c) with $\mathsf{Cr}=\mathsf{Cr}_{a_*}$, (d) and (f).

The number $\gamma^\natural$, formed from the constants, is the smallness that Lem.~\ref{C-352-15} reads: $\gamma^\natural\le(3.6\,C_\omega)^{-1}$, so that $\epsilon^{(1)}_j=C_\omega(0.9\gamma_j+\mathsf c^\flat\theta^{[0]})\le\frac34$ in Lem.~\ref{C-352-15}(a) once $2C_\omega\mathsf c^\flat\theta^{[0]}\le1$; $\gamma^\natural$ is at most the number under which the feedback $\sum_{i'<j}\gamma_{i'}\le0.45\gamma_j$ is absorbed in the recursion of the proof of Lem.~\ref{C-352-15}(b); and $\gamma^\natural\le(5C_1L^{7/2}\hat C)^{-1}$, which the proof of Lem.~\ref{C-352-15}(e) reads, where $\hat C=\sup_{v>0}(1+v^3)\max\{1,v^{12}\}E_\sigma(v/2)$ is finite, $E_\sigma$ decaying exponentially, and $C_1$ is the constant of the bound $\omega^{\mathrm{sp}}_l(i)\le C_1L^{-4l}(1+t_i)$ in that proof.

Then $\tau^\natural=\min\{6L^{3/2}\gamma^\natural,(2C_\omega\mathsf c^\flat)^{-1}\}$: for $j<K$, $\delta_j\le\delta_{K-1}$ (Lem.~\ref{C-352-10}(a)) gives $\theta^{[j]}\le\theta^{[K-1]}$, in particular $\theta^{[0]}\le\theta^{[K-1]}$, and with $\varkappa_j\le\frac16L^{-3/2}$ of (f), $\theta^{[K-1]}\le\tau^\natural$ gives $\gamma_j=\theta^{[j]}\varkappa_j\le\gamma^\natural$ and $2C_\omega\mathsf c^\flat\theta^{[0]}\le1$. For $r_1$, let $C_7=\sup_{u\ge1}[4\mathfrak p_0\log(1+\log u)-c_\sigma u/4\sqrt3LM]$, finite, let $\Lambda_1(\mathsf b)\ge1$ be the least number such that for all $\Lambda\ge\Lambda_1(\mathsf b)$
\[
\frac{c_\sigma}{\sqrt3L}\Lambda^{2\mathfrak p_0}\ge3c_\sigma+C_7+4\log^+\bigl(2\mathsf C_{\mathcal A}A_1M^{-3/2}\bigr)+4\mathfrak p_0\bigl[\log(1+\log^+\mathsf b)+\log(1+\Lambda)\bigr],
\]
and $r_1(\mathsf b)=e^{-\Lambda_1(\mathsf b)}$. The left member grows like $\Lambda^{2\mathfrak p_0}$, $\mathfrak p_0\ge1$, the right one like $\log\Lambda$, so $\Lambda_1(\mathsf b)$ is finite; it is formed from the constants and $\mathsf b$, it holds no $K$, and since the right member increases with $\mathsf b$, $r_1$ does not increase in $\mathsf b$. Let $0<\rho\le r_1(\mathsf b)$ with $s(\rho)\le K$, $\Lambda=\log\frac1\rho\ge\Lambda_1(\mathsf b)\ge1$ and $u=\rho/a_K=\hat\rho_0$. The working level at $\varrho=\rho<1$ gives $u\ge\hat\rho_{\mathsf k(\rho)}\ge4MY_\rho^{2\mathfrak p_0}\ge4M\Lambda^{2\mathfrak p_0}\ge4M$, so $\rho\ge4Ma_K$. Next, $1/\varkappa_0=2\mathsf C_{\mathcal A}A_1M^{-3/2}y_0^{\mathfrak p_0}$, and $x_0=\beta=\mathsf b/a_K=\mathsf bu/\rho$ gives $y_0=\log\mathsf b+\log u+\Lambda$, whence $\log y_0\le\log(1+\log^+\mathsf b)+\log(1+\log u)+\log(1+\Lambda)$, as $x+y+z\le(1+x)(1+y)(1+z)$ for $x,y,z\ge0$. As $\hat\rho_1=u/L$, the bound $E_\sigma(\hat\rho_1/2)\le\varkappa_0^4$ follows from
\[
c_\sigma\Bigl(\frac u{2\sqrt3LM}-3\Bigr)\ge4\log^+\bigl(2\mathsf C_{\mathcal A}A_1M^{-3/2}\bigr)+4\mathfrak p_0\log y_0 .
\]
Halve the first term: by $u\ge4M\Lambda^{2\mathfrak p_0}$ one half is at least $\frac{c_\sigma}{\sqrt3L}\Lambda^{2\mathfrak p_0}$, and the other half is at least $4\mathfrak p_0\log(1+\log u)-C_7$; with the bound of $\log y_0$, what is left is the display that defines $\Lambda_1(\mathsf b)$, at $\Lambda=\log\frac1\rho$. The term $\log(1+\log u)$, through which $y_0$ grows with $K$, is beaten by the half of the exponent, so no number in the argument depends on $K$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The kernel family and the rest family]\label{C-352-13}
In the data of Lem.~\ref{C-352-12} with $p\ge2$, let $\dot{\mathfrak e}_{a,j}=((E^{(i)}_a,0)_{i\le j},(0))$ and $\mathfrak u_{a,j}=((0,0)_{i\le j},(\mathsf W_{L^{K-j}w_a}))$, so that $\mathfrak f_{\{a\},j}=\dot{\mathfrak e}_{a,j}+\mathfrak u_{a,j}$, and $\mathsf B_j(\mathfrak g_1,\mathfrak g_2)=\partial_{s_1}\partial_{s_2}\mathsf{St}^{[j]}(\mathfrak f_{0,j}+s_1\mathfrak g_1+s_2\mathfrak g_2)|_0$. With the kernel family $\mathsf K^{(j+1)}=\mathsf B_j(\mathfrak u_{1,j},\mathfrak u_{2,j})$, for $1\le j\le K-1$
\[
E^{(j+1)}_{12}=\mathsf K^{(j+1)}+\mathsf R^{(j+1)},\qquad\mathsf R^{(j+1)}=\mathsf B_j(\dot{\mathfrak e}_{1,j},\mathfrak u_{2,j})+\mathsf B_j(\mathfrak u_{1,j},\dot{\mathfrak e}_{2,j})+\mathsf B_j(\dot{\mathfrak e}_{1,j},\dot{\mathfrak e}_{2,j})+\mathsf D\mathsf{St}^{[j]}(\mathfrak f_{0,j})[\mathfrak f_{12,j}],
\]
and $\mathsf R^{(j+1)}$ is a pointed family of level $j+1$ that vanishes off $\mathsf{Cr}_1$ and off $\mathsf{Cr}_2$; $\mathsf K^{(j+1)}(X,\cdot,z)=0$ unless a plaquette of $\operatorname{supp}w_1$ and one of $\operatorname{supp}w_2$ have their corners in $X$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Lem.~\ref{C-352-12}(a) at $\beta=\{1,2\}$ has two partitions. $\mathsf B_j$ is additive in each entry: for bare arrays $\mathfrak a,\mathfrak b,\mathfrak g$ the value $h(t)=\mathsf{St}^{[j]}(\mathfrak f_{0,j}+t_1\mathfrak a+t_2\mathfrak b+t_3\mathfrak g)(X,P,z)$ is holomorphic on a polydisc about $0$, the size being subadditive, and $\partial_{s_1}\partial_{s_2}h(s_1,s_1,s_2)|_0=(\partial_{t_1}+\partial_{t_2})\partial_{t_3}h(0)$. The first and second derivatives of the step are pointed families with the locality of the step, and Lem.~\ref{C-352-12}(d) gives where they vanish.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[One level at a regular configuration]\label{C-352-14}
Let $g$ satisfy $(\Gamma1)$, $(K,\beta)$ be a first-passage datum at $g$ and $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] Let the frame at a level $k_0$ hold for a pair of real Lipschitz functions (Lem.~\ref{C-352-11}(a)), and let $k_0\le n<K$, $1\le i'\le n$, $A\in\mathsf{Cc}_n(r_n)$, $\mathsf{Cr}$ a set of bare sites, $D'\ge0$, and $\mathsf f$ a pointed family of level $i'$ that vanishes off $\mathsf{Cr}$ and on the domains $X$ with $d_{i'}(X)<D'$. Then
\[
|\Delta[\mathsf f]|\le C_\Delta\,\mathsf n^{\mathrm{cb}}_{i'}(\mathsf{Cr})\,\|\mathsf f\|_{i',\lambda_{\mathrm{out}}}\,r_n^2\,L^{-4(n-i')}e^{-D'/2}.
\]
\item[(b)] Let $G$ be a family of local terms of level $i$ that vanishes unless $\mathcal P(X)$, the set of the plaquettes with their corners in $X$, meets a set $\mathcal S$ of plaquettes and $d_i(X)\ge D_i$, and let $\mathsf N_i$ be the number of the cubes of $\pi_i$ that hold a corner of a plaquette of $\mathcal S$. At every configuration $U$ whose pairs of level $i$ lie in the cores, $\sum_{(X,z)}|G(X,U,z)|\le8M^3C_{\mathrm E,1}\mathsf N_ie^{-D_i}\|G\|_{i,\lambda_{\mathrm{out}}}$; if $U$ is besides regular of a level $t'\ge i$ at a radius $\varepsilon$ with $4M\varepsilon\le c_{\mathrm A}\alpha_0$, then $\sum_{(X,z)}|G(X,U,z)-G(X,\mathbf 1,z)|\le2C_{\mathrm f}L^{-4(t'-i)}\mathsf N_ie^{-D_i/2}\|G\|_{i,\lambda_{\mathrm{out}}}$.
\end{enumerate}
The numbers $C_\Delta,C_{\mathrm f},C_{\mathrm E,1},c_{\mathrm A}$ are formed from the constants. Of $(\Gamma1)$ the proof of (a) uses only, besides the frame at $k_0$, the two bounds $2r_n\le\varrho_{\mathrm{ch}}$ and $x_n^{-1}\le r_n^2$ at the heights concerned, and the proof of (b) only $g\le\gamma$ and $g^{-2}\ge x_{\mathrm J}$; both use besides the bound $L^m\ge LMy_K$ of the sides $\ell=2L^m\in\mathfrak L(g)$. So (a) holds whenever the frame at $k_0$ and these two bounds hold, and (b) holds whenever $g\le\gamma$ and $g^{-2}\ge x_{\mathrm J}$, with no frame.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(a) Let $k_0\le n<K$. Then $r_n>0$ and $2r_n\le\varrho_{\mathrm{ch}}$ (Lem.~\ref{C-352-10}(a), (b)); in the frame at $k_0$, Lem.~\ref{lem:weighted-chain-background}, at the radii $r_n<r'=2r_n\le\varrho_{\mathrm{ch}}$, gives that $\tilde U$ is regular of level $n$ at the radius $\varepsilon:=6r_n$ on $T_\ell$ and that the actions of the bare arrays over the absolute system of height $n$ are formed at it; this is where the frame is read. For one domain $X$ of size $d$ and $\mathsf E=\mathsf f(X,\cdot,z)$, the evaluation of a local term at a regular configuration gives either $|\mathsf E(\tilde U)-\mathsf E(\mathbf 1)|\le C_{\mathrm A}\|\mathsf f\|e^{-\lambda_{\mathrm{out}}d}(\varepsilon/\alpha_0)^2L^{-4(n-i')}M^2(1+d)^2$, or $d\ge[d_*]_+$ and $|\mathsf E(\tilde U)-\mathsf E(\mathbf 1)|\le2\|\mathsf f\|e^{-\lambda_{\mathrm{out}}d}$, with the depth $d_*=\min\{c_{\mathrm A}\alpha_0\tau/6M,(L^{m+K-i'}-4)/2M\}-1$, $\tau=L^{2(n-i')}/r_n$.

A contributing $X$ holds one of the $\mathsf n^{\mathrm{cb}}_{i'}$ cubes, has $d\ge D'$ and at most $8M^3(d+1)$ base points; the sum over domains through a cube is bounded by {\cite[eq.~320]{YMM2}}. In the tail, $e^{-[d_*]_+/2}\le e^{1/2}[e^{-c_{\mathrm A}\alpha_0\tau/12M}+e^{-(L^{m+K-i'}-4)/4M}]$; the first part is $\le C\tau^{-2}$; for the second, $L^m\ge LMy_K$ on the sides of $\mathfrak L(g)$, $x_n\le\frac53L^{K-n}x_K$ and $x_n^{-1}\le r_n^2$ give $e^{-(L^{m+K-i'}-4)/4M}\le\frac53e^{1/M}r_n^2L^{-4(n-i')}$. So the bound holds on every side $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$. (b) is the same count at a configuration whose pairs lie in the cores, and, for the difference, at a configuration regular of level $t'$, with $\vartheta=L^{-(t'-i)}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Sizes at three lengths]\label{C-352-15}
Let $g$ satisfy $(\Gamma1)$, $(K,\beta)$ be a first-passage datum at $g$ and $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$, and let real weights be placed at $(\rho,r)$, or at $(\rho,r,\mathsf d)$, or form two pairs at $(\rho,r,\mathsf d)$, with $0<\rho\le r\le\mathsf d\le e^{-2\sqrt3}$, $s(\rho)\le K$, $\rho\le r_1(\mathsf b)$. Put $q=\rho/r$, $u_i=\hat r_i$, $v_i=\hat{\mathsf d}_i$, $\Xi^r_j=q^6\min\{1,u_j\}^3$, $\mathsf z(\beta)=q^{3c(\beta)}(\rho/\mathsf d)^6$ for crossing $\beta$, $\mathsf D(u)=[u/\sqrt3M-3]_+$, $C_\sigma=\sup_u\max\{1,u^6\}E_\sigma(u)$ and $\bar\nu_j=\bar\nu_{j;12}$. There are numbers $C_\omega,\mathsf A_{\mathrm N},C_{\mathrm B},\mathsf A^\times_m,C^\Psi_m,C_\times$ formed from the constants such that for $1\le j\le K-1$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] $\mathfrak n[\mathfrak u_{a,j}]\le\varsigma_j\mathsf m_{j,a}$, $\mathfrak n[\dot{\mathfrak e}_{a,j}]\le\epsilon^{(1)}_j\varsigma_j\mathsf m_{j,a}$ with $\epsilon^{(1)}_j=C_\omega(0.9\gamma_j+\mathsf c^\flat\theta^{[0]})\le\frac34$, and $\bar{\mathsf h}_{j;a},\bar\Psi_{j;a}\le\varsigma_j$;
\item[(b)] for a pair, $\bar{\mathsf h}_{j;12}\le\mathsf A_{\mathrm N}\gamma_j\Xi^r_j$ and $\bar\Psi_{j;12}\le2\varsigma_j^2+\mathsf A_{\mathrm N}\gamma_j\Xi^r_j$;
\item[(c)] $\|\mathsf K^{(j+1)}\|_{j+1,\lambda_{\mathrm{out}}}\le\frac12\varsigma_j^2\bar\nu_j$ and $\|\mathsf R^{(j+1)}\|_{j+1,\lambda_{\mathrm{out}}}\le[\frac32\epsilon^{(1)}_j\varsigma_j^2+\mathsf A_{\mathrm N}\gamma_j\Xi^r_j]\bar\nu_j$;
\item[(d)] below the level of the distance: if $1\le n\le K-1$, $u_n\ge\sqrt3M$, and the pairs of all levels $\le n$ of $U$ lie in the cores, then $|\sum_{i\le n}\mathsf{Sum}[E^{(i)}_{12}](U)|\le C_{\mathrm B}q^6e^{-u_n/2\sqrt3M}\bar\nu_n$;
\item[(e)] for crossing $\beta$, $m=|\beta|\le4$, with $\Xi^3_j(\beta)=\mathsf z(\beta)\min\{1,v_j\}^{3/2}$: $\bar{\mathsf h}_{j;\beta}\le\mathsf A^\times_m\gamma_j\Xi^3_j(\beta)$, and $\mathsf N_iE_\sigma(v_i)\bar\Psi_{i-1;\beta}\le108\,C^\Psi_m\mathsf z(\beta)\min\{1,v_i\}^{3/2}E_\sigma(v_i/6)$ for $1\le i\le K$; and at $n=\mathsf k(\mathsf d)$, with $P=v_n$ and $A\in\mathsf{Cc}_n(r_n)$, $|G_{n;\beta}(A)|\le C_\times e^{-P/2\sqrt3M}\mathsf z(\beta)\bar\nu_{n;\beta}$;
\item[(f)] \emph{without the placing:} the bounds (a)--(d), and those of (e) but the last one, at the level $\mathsf k(\mathsf d)$, hold with the same numbers for real weights, none identically $0$, that form one pair, or a pair and a third source, or two pairs, with numbers $0<\rho\le r\le\mathsf d\le1$ such that for $0\le i\le K$: $a_K\le\rho$; (P1) and (P2); the corners of the plaquettes of the supports are at least $u_i/\sqrt3-1$ level-$i$ spacings apart in a cluster and at least $v_i/\sqrt3-1$ across; $\rho\ge\frac23Ma_K$; $E_\sigma(\hat\rho_1/2)\le\varkappa_0^4$; and $\gamma_{K-1}\le\gamma^\natural$. No bound on the distances of the centres and no bound $\mathsf d\le e^{-2\sqrt3}$ is asked in (f); these serve only the frame, the working level, the number $R_w$ and the rings.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
All of it is Lem.~\ref{C-352-12} with (P1)--(P3) of Lem.~\ref{C-352-11}, $\rho\ge\frac23Ma_K$ (so $\varsigma_0=1$), $E_\sigma(\hat\rho_1/2)\le\varkappa_0^4$, $\gamma_j\le\gamma^\natural$, and three inequalities of arithmetic, $\omega^{\mathrm{sp}}_l(i)L^{l+1}\varsigma_{i-1}\le C_\omega\varsigma_{i+l}$, $\omega^{\mathrm{sp}}_l(i)\le C_1L^{-4l}(1+t_i)$ and $(1+t_i)\varsigma_{i-1}^2\le2L^6t_i^2$, which use only $a_K\le\rho$ and (P2). (a) By induction on $j$, with (c) of Lem.~\ref{C-352-12} at $\mathsf{Cr}=\mathsf{Cr}_a$, (e) and the first of these inequalities; then (b) of Lem.~\ref{C-352-12} at $q=1$. (b) In the recursion (g) of Lem.~\ref{C-352-12} the support rule and (P3) give $\sigma_{i;12}\le E_\sigma(u_i)$; the kernel parts are $(1+t_i)2\varsigma_{i-1}^2\le4L^6q^6u_i^6$, and
\[
\sum_{i\le j}L^{-3(j-i)}\min\{u_i^6,C_\sigma\}\le2.002\,C_\sigma\min\{1,u_j\}^3
\]
($u_i=L^{j-i}u_j$: two geometric sums); the term $i=1$ uses $E_\sigma(u_1)\le E_\sigma(u_1/2)E_\sigma(\hat\rho_1/2)\le E_\sigma(u_1/2)\varkappa_0^4$; the feedback $\sum_{i'<j}\gamma_{i'}\le0.45\gamma_j$ is absorbed under $\gamma_j\le\gamma^\natural$. (c) $\mathsf K^{(j+1)}=\mathsf B_j(\mathfrak u_1,\mathfrak u_2)$ and (b) of Lem.~\ref{C-352-12} at $q=2$; for $\mathsf R^{(j+1)}$, Lem.~\ref{C-352-13} with (a), (b) and $\frac12(2+\epsilon)\epsilon\le\frac32\epsilon$. (d) By the support rule $E^{(i)}_{12}$ vanishes on the domains with $d_i(X)<\mathsf D(u_i)$; Lem.~\ref{C-352-14}(b) with (b), $\bar\nu_{i-1}\le\frac43L^{n-i+1}\bar\nu_n$, and $\sum_lL^{l+1}e^{-\frac58\mathsf D(L^lu_n)}\le Ce^{-u_n/2\sqrt3M}$. (e) Induction on $m$ and, for one $\beta$, on the level, through one inequality on the natural sizes $\mu_i(\beta')=\hat\rho_i^{3|\beta'|}u_i^{-3c(\beta')}v_i^{-6[\beta'\text{ crosses}]}$, which is $\hat\rho_i^3$ at a point, $q^6u_i^3$ at a whole pair and $\mathsf z(\beta')$ at a crossing set, at every level (there $3|\beta'|=3c(\beta')+6$): for crossing $\beta$ and a partition $\pi$ of it with $|\pi|\ge2$,
\[
\prod_{\beta'\in\pi}\mu_i(\beta')\le\max\{1,v_i^{12}\}\,\mathsf z(\beta);
\]
the quotient is $u_i^{3s}v_i^{6-6k_\times}$, $s$ the number of whole pairs of $\beta$ that $\pi$ cuts and $k_\times$ the number of its crossing blocks (with $k$ blocks that do not cross, $3k+6k_\times=6+3s$), and $u_i\le v_i$, $k_\times\le2$, and $k_\times=2$ forces $s=2$: at $k_\times=0$ the quotient is $\le v_i^{3s+6}$, at $k_\times=1$ (then $s=k\ge1$) it is $u_i^{3s}\le\max\{1,v_i^6\}$, at $k_\times=2$ it is $(u_i/v_i)^6\le1$. At $v_i<1$ the display gives the bound $\mathsf z(\beta)$ alone (at $k_\times=2$ the quotient is $1$ when $r=\mathsf d$); the factor $\min\{1,v_i\}^{3/2}$ comes, at $k_\times\ge1$, from the crossing blocks, whose factor of the induction is kept, and at $k_\times=0$ from the quotient.

\emph{The blocks.} At a level $i-1\ge1$: a point by (a), $\bar{\mathsf h}_{i-1;a}\le\varsigma_{i-1}\le t_{i-1}=L^3t_i\le L^3\mu_i(\{a\})$; a whole pair $c$ by (b), $\bar{\mathsf h}_{i-1;c}\le\mathsf A_{\mathrm N}\gamma^\natural q^6\min\{1,Lu_i\}^3\le\mathsf A_{\mathrm N}\gamma^\natural L^3\mu_i(c)$; a crossing proper subset $\beta'$ by the first bound of (e) at $|\beta'|<m$, $\bar{\mathsf h}_{i-1;\beta'}\le\mathsf A^\times_{|\beta'|}\gamma^\natural\mathsf z(\beta')\min\{1,Lv_i\}^{3/2}\le\mathsf A^\times_{|\beta'|}\gamma^\natural L^{3/2}\mu_i(\beta')\min\{1,v_i\}^{3/2}$. With $\mathsf a_{(2)}=\max\{1,\mathsf A_{\mathrm N}\gamma^\natural\}$ and $\mathsf a_{(m+1)}=\max\{\mathsf a_{(m)},\mathsf A^\times_m\gamma^\natural\}$, every partition $\pi$ of $\beta$ with $|\pi|\ge2$ has
\[
\prod_{\beta'\in\pi}\bar{\mathsf h}_{i-1;\beta'}\le(L^3\mathsf a_{(m)})^m\min\{1,v_i\}^{3/2}\max\{1,v_i^{12}\}\,\mathsf z(\beta):
\]
if $\pi$ has a crossing block, the factor $\min\{1,v_i\}^{3/2}$ of one of them is kept and the display bounds the rest; if it has none, $k_\times=0$ and the quotient is $\le v_i^{3s+6}\le\min\{1,v_i\}^{3/2}\max\{1,v_i^{12}\}$, as $s\le2$. The block $\pi=\{\beta\}$ is the first bound of (e) for $\beta$ itself at the level $i-1$: $\bar{\mathsf h}_{i-1;\beta}\le\mathsf A^\times_m\gamma^\natural L^{3/2}\mathsf z(\beta)\min\{1,v_i\}^{3/2}$. \emph{The second bound.} Put $T_i=(1+t_i)E_\sigma(v_i)\bar\Psi_{i-1;\beta}$ and $\hat C=\sup_v(1+v^3)\max\{1,v^{12}\}E_\sigma(v/2)$. As $t_i\le\hat\rho_i^3\le v_i^3$, $E_\sigma(v)\le E_\sigma(v/2)^2$ and $E_\sigma(v/2)\le E_\sigma(v/6)^3\le1$, we have $(1+t_i)\max\{1,v_i^{12}\}E_\sigma(v_i)\le\hat C\,E_\sigma(v_i/6)$; so the first recursion of (g) of Lem.~\ref{C-352-12} gives for $2\le i\le K$
\[
\begin{multlined}
T_i\le\hat C\bigl[L^{3/2}\mathsf A^\times_m\gamma^\natural+\mathsf b_m(L^3\mathsf a_{(m)})^m\bigr]\mathsf z(\beta)\min\{1,v_i\}^{3/2}E_\sigma(v_i/6),\qquad\mathsf b_m=\sum_{\pi\in\mathrm{Part}(\beta),\,|\pi|\ge2}(2(|\pi| \\
-1))^{|\pi|-1}=2,22,326 .
\end{multlined}
\]
At $i=1$, (e) of Lem.~\ref{C-352-12} gives $\bar\Psi_{0;\beta}\le\mathsf a^\flat_m:=m^m(\mathsf c^\flat/2)^m$; as $\rho\ge\frac23Ma_K$ and $M\ge L$, $v_1\ge u_1\ge\hat\rho_1\ge\frac23$, so that $\mathsf z(\beta)=\hat\rho_1^{3m}u_1^{-3c(\beta)}v_1^{-6}\ge(\hat\rho_1/v_1)^{3m}\ge(\frac23)^{12}\max\{1,v_1^{12}\}^{-1}$ and $\min\{1,v_1\}^{3/2}\ge(\frac23)^{3/2}$; hence $T_1\le\mathsf a^\flat_m(\frac32)^{27/2}\hat C\,\mathsf z(\beta)\min\{1,v_1\}^{3/2}E_\sigma(v_1/6)$. With $C^\Psi_m=2\hat C[\mathsf b_m(L^3\mathsf a_{(m)})^m+\mathsf a^\flat_m(\frac32)^{27/2}]$, $\mathsf A^\times_m=2.5\,C_1L^2C^\Psi_m$ and $\gamma^\natural\le(5C_1L^{7/2}\hat C)^{-1}$, a smallness of the same kind as the one that absorbs the feedback in (b) and part of the choice of $\gamma^\natural$, the feedback $\hat CL^{3/2}\mathsf A^\times_m\gamma^\natural$ is $\le\frac12C^\Psi_m$, and $T_i\le C^\Psi_m\mathsf z(\beta)\min\{1,v_i\}^{3/2}E_\sigma(v_i/6)$ for $1\le i\le K$; with $\mathsf N_i\le108(1+t_i)$ (P2) this is the second bound of (e). \emph{The first bound.} By the second recursion of (g), with $\sigma_{i;\beta}\le E_\sigma(v_i)$ (the corners across are $v_i/\sqrt3-1$ apart, and $[(v_i/\sqrt3-1)/M-2]_+\ge\mathsf D(v_i)$), $\omega^{\mathrm{sp}}_{j-i}(i)\le C_1L^{-4(j-i)}(1+t_i)$, $v_{j-l}=L^lv_j$ and $\min\{1,L^lv_j\}^{3/2}\le L^{3l/2}\min\{1,v_j\}^{3/2}$:
\[
\bar{\mathsf h}_{j;\beta}\le(\tfrac43)^{\frac m2}C_1L^{\frac m2}\gamma_j\sum_{l=0}^{j-1}L^{(-4+\frac m2)l}T_{j-l}\le(\tfrac43)^{\frac m2}C_1L^{\frac m2}C^\Psi_m\,\gamma_j\,\mathsf z(\beta)\min\{1,v_j\}^{3/2}\sum_{l\ge0}L^{(-4+\frac m2+\frac32)l};
\]
the exponent $-4+\frac m2+\frac32\le-\frac12$ ($m\le4$) gives $\sum_l\le1.39$, and $\bar{\mathsf h}_{j;\beta}\le\mathsf A^\times_m\gamma_j\Xi^3_j(\beta)$. The induction runs over $m=2,3,4$ and, for one $\beta$, over the level: $T_i$ reads the first bounds at the levels $\le i-1$ only. The bound of $G_{n;\beta}$ at the level of $\mathsf d$ is Lem.~\ref{C-352-14}(b) with the factors $e^{-\frac12\mathsf D(v_i)}$, summed over $i\le n$. (f): the proofs of (a)--(d) and of the first two bounds of (e) use of the weights only the properties listed in (f), the separation of the corners standing for (P3); the last bound of (e) uses besides the working level $\mathsf k(\mathsf d)$, which asks $\mathsf d\le e^{-2\sqrt3}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[One source of any width]\label{C-352-16}
Let $g$ satisfy $(\Gamma1)$, let the frame at $k_0$ hold for a pair that holds the source $w_a$, and let $w_a$ satisfy (P1), (P2) at a width $\rho$ with $\frac23Ma_K\le\rho$. Then for $k_0\le n\le K$ and $A\in\mathsf{Cc}_n(r_n)$, with $q_{n;a}(F)=\frac1{2a_K}\sum_pw_a(p)|F_p|^2$,
\[
\bigl|G_{n;a}(A)-G_{n;a}(0)-q_{n;a}(\mathsf{ang}^{[n]}(A))\bigr|\le C_{\mathrm S}\,\mathfrak b_n^2\delta_n\,\hat\rho_n^3\,\mathsf u_a .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
At $n=K$, $A=0$ and both members vanish; let $k_0\le n<K$. $G_{n;a}(A)=\mathcal O(w_a)(\tilde U)+\sum_{i\le n}\mathsf{Sum}[E^{(i)}_a](\tilde U)$ and $a_p(\mathbf 1)=0$. The weight member: the expansion of $a_p$ on the chain class and (P1) give $|\mathcal O(w_a)(\tilde U)-q_{n;a}(\mathsf{ang}^{[n]}(A))|\le C r_n^3\hat\rho_n^3x_n\mathsf u_a\le C\mathfrak b_n^2\delta_n\hat\rho_n^3\mathsf u_a$ (Lem.~\ref{C-352-10}). The families: Lem.~\ref{C-352-14}(a), in the frame at $k_0$, at $\mathsf{Cr}_a$, $D'=0$, with $\|E^{(i)}_a\|\le\varsigma_{i-1}\mathsf m_{i-1,a}\mathsf g_i$, $\mathsf g_i=2\gamma_{i-1}$ ($i\ge2$), $\mathsf g_1=\mathsf c^\flat\theta^{[0]}$ (Lem.~\ref{C-352-15}(a)), and $\mathsf N_i\varsigma_{i-1}\le216L^3t_i$; then every level gives the same natural size
\[
t_i\,\mathsf m_{i-1,a}L^{-4(n-i)}=\tfrac{81}2\alpha_0^2L\,\hat\rho_n^3|w_a|_\infty/a_{K-n}
\]
times $\mathsf g_i$, and $\sum_{i\le n}\mathsf g_i\le C\delta_n$, $|w_a|_\infty r_n^2/a_{K-n}\le C\mathfrak b_n^2\mathsf u_a$.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{The kernel families.}

\begin{lemma}[From a real segment to the second order]\label{C-352-17}
Let $R>0$, $0<\mathsf e\le\mathsf M$, and let $\psi$ be holomorphic on $\{|\zeta|<R\}$ with $|\psi|\le\mathsf M$ there, $|\psi(t)|\le\mathsf e$ for real $t\in(-R,R)$, and $\psi(0)=\psi'(0)=0$. With $\Lambda=\max\{1,\log(\mathsf M/\mathsf e)\}$, $|\psi(\zeta)|\le4e\,\mathsf e\,\Lambda^2|\zeta|^2/R^2$ for $|\zeta|\le R/2\Lambda$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
On the upper half disc $h(\zeta)=\frac2\pi\arg\frac{R+\zeta}{R-\zeta}$ is harmonic, $0$ on the diameter and $1$ on the arc; $\log|\psi|-\log\mathsf e-h\log(\mathsf M/\mathsf e)$ is subharmonic and bounded above, with nonpositive boundary values but at two points, so it is $\le0$ (the two-constants theorem); the same on the lower half disc. As $h(\zeta)\le2|\zeta|/R$, $|\psi|\le e\,\mathsf e$ on $|\zeta|\le R/2\Lambda$; $\psi(\zeta)/\zeta^2$ is holomorphic, and the maximum principle on that disc gives the claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[A local gauge]\label{C-352-18}
In units of a level, let the bare lattice have the spacing $\xi\le\frac1{13}$, let $x_0$ be a bare site, $N_s=\{x:|x-x_0|_\infty\le s\}$, $\rho\ge2$ with $4\rho+4$ at most the side of the torus, and let $v=(A,\mathbf J)$ be a real pair of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued $1$-forms on the bare bonds with $|A|\le\alpha\le\frac1{60}$, $|\nabla^\xi A|\le\gamma_\circ$, $|\mathbf J|\le\iota$. With $c_\mu=A_\mu(x_0)$, $X(x)=\sum_\mu(x-x_0)_\mu c_\mu$ and $u=e^{iX}$ on $N_{2\rho+1}$, there is a real pair $v'=(A',\mathbf J')$ which at the bonds with base point in $N_\rho$ is the gauge transform of $v$ under $u$, with $\|v'\|\le\max\{\rho(6\gamma_\circ+19\alpha^2),\iota\}$ in the norm of the chart, $|A'(b)|\le3s\gamma_\circ+(9s+8\xi)\alpha^2$ at the bonds with base point in $N_s$, $s\le\rho$, and $|\nabla^\xi A'|\le\frac{100}{99}(\gamma_\circ+3\alpha^2)$ on $N_\rho$. In the sharp first-difference bound, the whole difference stencil must lie in $N_\rho$; the chart-norm bound is global.

The same holds in a local form, with data on $N_{\rho+1}$ alone: let $U$ be a configuration, $\mathsf g\colon N_{\rho+1}\to SU(2)$ and $A$ a real $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued $1$-form on the bonds $b=\langle b_-,b_+\rangle$ with both end points in $N_{\rho+1}$ such that $\mathsf g(b_-)U(b)\mathsf g(b_+)^{-1}=e^{i\xi A(b)}$, $|A|\le\alpha\le\frac1{60}$ and $|\nabla^\xi A|\le\gamma_\circ$ there, the current $\mathbf J(U)$ of $U$ being at most $\iota$ there; with $c_\mu$ and $X$ as above and $h=e^{iX}\mathsf g$ on $N_{\rho+1}$, there is a real pair $v'$ on all the bare bonds which, at the bonds with base point in $N_\rho$, is the image of $U$ and of $\mathbf J(U)$ under the gauge transformation $h$, and which obeys the three bounds above; and if $\|v'\|$ is less than the radius $r_\alpha$ of the ball of the chart, every local term of the level whose domain lies in $N_{\rho-1}$, formed at $U$, has the same value at $P[v']$ restricted to that domain.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For hermitian $Y,a,c$ with $|a|+|c|\le\frac14$ let $\Psi(Y,a,c)=-i\log(e^{iY}e^{ia}e^{-i(Y+c)})$; matrix calculus gives $|\Psi|\le|a-c|+3|Y||c|+2(|a|+|c|)^2$ and a Lipschitz bound in $(Y,a)$. Put $A^u_\mu(x)=\xi^{-1}\Psi(X(x),\xi A_\mu(x),\xi c_\mu)$, so that $e^{i\xi A^u_\mu(x)}=u(x)e^{i\xi A_\mu(x)}u(x+\xi e_\mu)^{-1}$, a real form; $|X|\le3s\alpha$ and $|A_\mu-c_\mu|\le3s\gamma_\circ$ on $N_s$ along three segments. Cut off with $\chi(x)=\min\{1,\max\{0,2-|x-x_0|_\infty/\rho\}\}$: $A'=\chi A^u$, $\mathbf J'=\chi u\mathbf Ju^{-1}$. The point is that all first difference quotients of $A$ are bounded; lowered by $m$ levels, $|A|$ falls like $L^{-m}$ and $|\nabla A|$ like $L^{-2m}$, and only the constant part is too large, which a gauge linear in $x$ removes at the price $|c|^2$.

In the local form $A^u$ is formed by the same formula from the potential $A$ of the transform of $U$ under $\mathsf g$, so that $e^{i\xi A^u(b)}=h(b_-)U(b)h(b_+)^{-1}$ at the bonds with both end points in $N_{\rho+1}$, and the cut-off $\chi(x)=\min\{1,\max\{0,(\rho+1-2\xi-|x-x_0|_\infty)/(1-2\xi)\}\}$, of the width $1-2\xi$ and equal to $1$ on $N_\rho$, takes the place of the cut-off of the width $\rho$: $A'=\chi A^u$, $\mathbf J'=\chi h\mathbf J(U)h^{-1}$. Both vanish at the bonds whose base point lies at a distance $\ge\rho+1-2\xi$ from $x_0$, and the other bonds have both end points in $N_{\rho+1}$, where $A$, $h$ and the bound $\iota$ are given. As $\nabla^\xi_\nu(\chi A^u)(x)=\chi(x+\xi e_\nu)\nabla^\xi_\nu A^u(x)+A^u(x)(\chi(x+\xi e_\nu)-\chi(x))/\xi$, $|\chi(x+\xi e_\nu)-\chi(x)|\le\frac{13}{11}\xi$, and, on $N_{\rho+1}$, $|\nabla^\xi A^u|\le\frac{100}{99}(\gamma_\circ+3\alpha^2)$ and $|A^u|\le3(\rho+1)\gamma_\circ+(9\rho+9.62)\alpha^2$ (the third and the second bound, at $s=\rho+1$, by the Lipschitz bound of $\Psi$ and the three segments in $N_{\rho+1}$, with $8\xi\le0.62$), for $\rho\ge2$
\[
|\nabla^\xi A'|\le\tfrac{100}{99}(\gamma_\circ+3\alpha^2)+\tfrac{13}{11}\bigl[3(\rho+1)\gamma_\circ+(9\rho+9.62)\alpha^2\bigr]\le\rho(6\gamma_\circ+19\alpha^2),\qquad|A'|\le\rho(6\gamma_\circ+19\alpha^2),
\]
which with $|\mathbf J'|\le\iota$ gives the global chart bound; on stencils contained in $N_\rho$, the cutoff equals $1$ and the sharper local bounds are unchanged. The bonds that a local term with its domain in $N_{\rho-1}$ reads have their end points in $N_\rho$, where $P[v']$ is the image of $U$ under $h$, and a local term is a gauge invariant function of the pair on its domain.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The kernel families]\label{C-352-19}
Let $g$ satisfy $(\Gamma1)$, let the frame at $k_0$ hold for $(w_1,w_2)$, let the forms $q_n$ be formed over a base level $k_\flat\le k_0$, and let $k_0\le i<n\le K$, $m=n-i-1$, $A\in\mathsf{Cc}_n(r_n)$. As $k_\flat\le i$, $\mathcal S_{i+1}-\mathcal S_i=\upsilon_{i+1}\mathcal C_{(i+1)}$, so that $\mathcal Q_i=q_{i+1}-q_i$ is the slice $\mathcal Q_i(F)=a_K^{-1}\upsilon_{i+1}\sum_{p,q}w_1(p)\mathcal C_{(i+1)}(p,q)w_2(q)\langle F_p,F_q\rangle$. At $n=K$, $A=0$ and the member $\mathsf{LM}$ below is $0$; the numbers below are formed for $n<K$. Put $\mathsf w_a=a_K^{-1}\eta_i^4\sum_p|w_a(p)|$; let $R_w$ be such that every corner of a plaquette of $\operatorname{supp}w_1\cup\operatorname{supp}w_2$ lies within the sup distance $R_w$, in level-$(i+1)$ units, of one bare site; $\alpha=L^{-m}r_n$, $\gamma_\circ=L^{-2m}r_n$, $\mathsf c_i=C_{\mathrm{tp}}e^{-\delta_{\mathrm{tp}}[\mathsf D^{12}_i-1]_+}$, $\mathsf M^{\mathsf K}_i=8M^3C_{\mathrm E,1}\mathsf N_{i+1}(w_1)\|\mathsf K^{(i+1)}\|_{i+1,\lambda_{\mathrm{out}}}$, $\mathsf M_i=2\mathsf M^{\mathsf K}_i+4L^{-4}\mathsf c_ig_i^2\delta_i^2\mathsf w_1\mathsf w_2$, and, with $\varrho_\wedge=\min\{\varrho_{\mathrm{ch}},\varrho_{\mathrm{fl}}\}$, $\epsilon=\epsilon^{\mathrm{cu}}_i$ and $\mathsf c_{\mathbf C}$ of Lem.~\ref{C-352-20}(a), $\epsilon'=\epsilon+2\mathsf c_{\mathbf C}\delta_i/r_\alpha$, the number $C^{\mathrm{row}}_{\mathrm{tp}}$ of Prop.~\YMMref{120.6}{821} that bounds the row sums $\sum_b|\mathsf T^{\mathrm{cv}}_i(p,b)|\le C^{\mathrm{row}}_{\mathrm{tp}}\eta_i^2$ of the matrix $\mathsf T^{\mathrm{cv}}_i$ of step 3 (Prop.~\YMMref{120.6}{821}, equation~\YMMref{(2239)}{821}), $\bar X=(4L^{-2}\mathsf c_{\mathfrak h}+2\mathsf c_{\mathfrak h}^2)\delta_i^2$ and $\bar\rho=\mathsf M_{\mathrm{pl}}^2\delta_i^3/\varrho_\wedge^3$,
\[
\begin{multlined}
\mathsf E_i=12L^{-4}(C^{\mathrm{row}}_{\mathrm{tp}})^2g_i^2\delta_i^2\epsilon'+6\sqrt3L^{-2}(C^{\mathrm{row}}_{\mathrm{tp}})^3g_i^3\delta_i\epsilon(1+2\mathsf c_{\mathbf C}+2\epsilon)+\tfrac94(C^{\mathrm{row}}_{\mathrm{tp}})^4g_i^4\bigl[\epsilon+4\epsilon^2+4(\mathsf c_{\mathbf C} \\
+\epsilon)\epsilon^2+2\epsilon'(2\mathsf c_{\mathbf C}+\epsilon)\bigr]+4\bar X\bar\rho+2\bar\rho^2,
\end{multlined}
\]
and for $\delta_i\le\mathsf r\le\frac12\varrho_{\mathrm{ch}}$ let $\mathsf E_i(\mathsf r)$ be the same number with $g_i^2\mathsf r^2$, $g_i^3\mathsf r$ in the places of $g_i^2\delta_i^2$, $g_i^3\delta_i$, with $\epsilon+2\mathsf c_{\mathbf C}\mathsf r/r_\alpha$ in the place of $\epsilon'$, $4L^{-2}\mathsf c_{\mathfrak h}\mathsf r\delta_i+2\mathsf c_{\mathfrak h}^2\delta_i^2$ in that of $\bar X$ and $\mathsf M_{\mathrm{pl}}^2\max\{\mathsf r/\varrho_{\mathrm{ch}},\delta_i/\varrho_{\mathrm{fl}}\}^3$ in that of $\bar\rho$. All summands are $\ge0$ and the last one is $2\bar\rho^2$, so $2\mathsf M_{\mathrm{pl}}^4\varrho_\wedge^{-6}\delta_i^6\le\mathsf E_i$. As $g_i\le\delta_i$ (Lem.~\ref{C-352-10}(b)) and $\epsilon^{\mathrm{cu}}_i\le1$, $\mathsf E_i$ and, for $\mathsf r\le\delta_i+r_{i+1}$, $\mathsf E_i(\mathsf r)$ are at most $C_{\mathsf E}\delta_i^4(\delta_i+\epsilon^{\mathrm{cu}}_i)$, with a number $C_{\mathsf E}$ formed from the constants; and as $\epsilon^{\mathrm{cu}}_i\le C_{\mathrm{cu}}(\delta_i+\mathsf p_{\star,i})$ (Lem.~\ref{C-352-20}(a)) and $\mathsf p_{\star,i}\le\max\{1,(c_{\mathsf p}/A_1)e^{y_{\mathsf p}/2}\}\delta_i$ at every height (the quotient $\mathsf p_{\star,i}/\delta_i=(c_{\mathsf p}/A_1)y_i^{-\mathfrak p_0}\exp[\frac{y_i}2-(LM)^{-3}A_1^2y_i^{2\mathfrak p_0}]$ is $\le1$ for $y_i\ge y_{\mathsf p}$ by the proof of Lem.~\ref{C-352-10}(b), and $\le(c_{\mathsf p}/A_1)e^{y_{\mathsf p}/2}$ for $1\le y_i<y_{\mathsf p}$; $y_i>\log g^{-2}\ge\log\gamma^{-2}>1$ since $\gamma\le\frac12$), they are at most $C\delta_i^5$.

Let $\bar{\mathsf e}$ be any number $\ge2\mathsf w_1\mathsf w_2\mathsf E_i$; $\Lambda_i=\max\{1,\log(\mathsf M_i/\bar{\mathsf e})\}$, $\mathsf h_i=\max\{2,R_w+1+M(2+\Lambda_i+2\log^+(\delta_i/\gamma_\circ))\}$, $\mathsf s=\mathsf h_i\gamma_\circ(6+19r_n)$. Then $\mathsf{LM}=|\Delta[\mathsf K^{(i+1)}]-\mathcal Q_i(\mathsf{ang}^{[n]}(A))|$ satisfies:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] always $\mathsf{LM}\le2\mathsf w_1\mathsf w_2\mathsf E_i(\max\{\delta_i,\alpha\})$, where $\max\{\delta_i,\alpha\}\le\min\{\frac12\varrho_{\mathrm{ch}},\delta_i+r_{i+1}\}$ ($\alpha\le r_{i+1}$, as $r_j\ge L^{-1}r_{j+1}$; $2\delta_i\le\varrho_\wedge$ and $2r_{i+1}\le\varrho_{\mathrm{ch}}$ in the frame, and under $(\Gamma1)$ by Lem.~\ref{C-352-10}(b)), so that $\mathsf E_i(\max\{\delta_i,\alpha\})\le C\delta_i^5$;
\item[(ii)] if $\mathsf s\le\delta_i/2\Lambda_i$: $\mathsf{LM}\le8e\,\bar{\mathsf e}\Lambda_i^2\mathsf s^2/\delta_i^2+L^{-4}\mathsf c_ig_i^2\mathsf w_1\mathsf w_2[18(\alpha^2+\alpha'^2)(\gamma_\circ+\gamma')+48R_w\alpha\gamma_\circ^2]$, with $\alpha'=(R_w+1)(3\gamma_\circ+10\alpha^2)$, $\gamma'=\frac{100}{99}(\gamma_\circ+3\alpha^2)$.
\end{enumerate}
The weights enter only through $\mathsf w_a$, $R_w$, $\mathsf D^{12}_i$, $\mathsf N_{i+1}(w_1)$ and $\|\mathsf K^{(i+1)}\|$; no test pair, filling or sign is asked. For weights placed at $(\rho,r)$ as in (B.2), with $k_0=\mathsf k(r)$, this gives for $\mathsf k(r)\le i<n\le K$
\[
\mathsf{LM}\le\bigl\{C_{\mathrm K}\mathfrak b_i^4\delta_i\Lambda_\sharp^2\mathsf h_\sharp^2u_i^3+C'_{\mathrm K}\mathsf c_i(1+u_i)^2u_i^3\,\mathfrak b_n^2r_n\bigr\}(\rho/r)^6\hat r_n^3\mathsf u_1\mathsf u_2,\qquad\Lambda_\sharp\le CY_r,\quad\mathsf h_\sharp\le CY_r^{2\mathfrak p_0},
\]
and neither $\Lambda_\sharp$ nor $\mathsf h_\sharp$ depends on $\rho$. Of $(\Gamma1)$ the proofs of (i) and (ii) use only the frame at $k_0$ and, at the heights concerned, $2r_n\le\varrho_{\mathrm{ch}}$ (so $r_n\le\frac1{120}$, as $\varrho_{\mathrm{ch}}\le\frac1{60}$ by equation~\YMMref{(2285)}{833}), $\epsilon^{\mathrm{cu}}_i\le1$ and $x_n^{-1}\le r_n^2$, besides the bound $\ell\ge2LMy_K$ of the sides $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$; (i) and (ii), with the bounds of $\mathsf E_i$ and $\mathsf E_i(\cdot)$ stated above, hold whenever these hold. The narrow display holds under the data of (B.2), where step 6 reads besides Lem.~\ref{C-352-15}(c) and $\delta_i\le\delta_n$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
1. \emph{Lowering.} $L^{-m}A$, viewed at the level $i+1$, is a real point $v$ of the chart with $|A_m|\le\alpha$, $|\nabla A_m|\le\gamma_\circ$, current $\le\gamma_\circ$, and $\mathsf{ang}^{[i+1]}(A_m)=\mathsf{ang}^{[n]}(A)$; $\mathsf{Sum}[\mathsf K^{(i+1)}](\tilde U)=\mathcal K_i(v):=\mathsf{Sum}[\mathsf K^{(i+1)}](P[v])$, and $\mathcal Q_i(v)$ is the third term.

2. \emph{Holomorphy and no first order.} $\mathcal K_i$ is holomorphic on the ball of radius $r_\alpha$ of the chart, $|\mathcal K_i|\le\mathsf M^{\mathsf K}_i$, and it is invariant under constant gauge rotations; as $\sum_{k=1}^3\operatorname{Ad}(i\sigma_k)=-\mathrm{id}$, its first derivative at $0$ vanishes.

3. \emph{The real ball.} At the real points $\|v\|\le\delta_i$, $\mathcal K_i(v)$ is a covariance under the probability measure $\nu_{i,v}$ of one step of the plaquette terms at the lowered configuration; this rests on a sum rule at every point of the chart, which (a) and (b) give.

(a) \emph{The sum rule at every point.} Prop.~\YMMref{51.15}{410} proves the sum rule of one local term at the two admitted background points, in equation~\YMMref{(872)}{411}, and from it the sum rule of the totals at the chart points $v_A$ of the chain classes (Prop.~\YMMref{124.2}{834}, equation~\YMMref{(2289)}{834}). The finite-vertex argument in that proof uses only membership in the localization domain $\mathfrak D(T_\ell)$ until it identifies the two endpoint values with background values; so for a term $f$ on a domain $X$ whose radius exceeds $1$, as do those of the localisation of bare arrays, and every point $\mathfrak u=(P,\mathcal A)\in\mathfrak D(T_\ell)$, critical or not,
\[
\sum_{Y'\in\mathcal D_i:\,Y'\supset X^\uparrow}\mathbb V[f]\bigl(Y';\mathfrak u|_{Y'}\bigr)=f\bigl(\rho_XP\dotplus\mathfrak h_{T_\ell}(\mathbf 1;\mathfrak u)\bigr)-f(\rho_XP).
\]
Indeed, with the interpolating function $F(s)=\Phi_{T_\ell}[f](s,1;\mathfrak u)$ of equation~\YMMref{(869)}{410}, including its distinct rescaling factors for the potential and the current, the resummation of brackets (\eqref{eq:analytic-bracket-resummation}) writes $F(\mathbf 1)-F(0)$ as the sum of the brackets $F^*[\mathcal K|\mathsf N_0]$ over the sets $\mathcal K$ of fine cubes off the cubes $\mathsf N_0$ of $X^\uparrow$; a bracket for which $\mathcal K\cup\mathsf N_0$ has more than one wall-component vanishes, $F$ being local for the roots $\mathsf N_0$ (Prop.~\YMMref{51.15}{410} and Lem.~\ref{lem:analytic-rooted-bracket}); if it has one, its union is a region $Y'\supset X^\uparrow$ and the bracket is $\mathbb V[f](Y';\mathfrak u|_{Y'})$ by the zero-extension consistency in Prop.~\YMMref{51.15}{410}, and $\mathcal K\mapsto Y'$ is a bijection onto these regions; finally $F(\mathbf 1)=f(\rho_XP\dotplus\mathfrak h_{T_\ell}(\mathbf 1;\mathfrak u))$ by the definition of $F$, and $F(0)=f(\rho_XP)$ by the zero-value statement in Prop.~\YMMref{51.15}{410}. Identifying the endpoint values with the two background values gives equation~\YMMref{(872)}{411}; the finite-bracket identity itself requires only the stated domain membership.

(b) \emph{The totals at every point of the chart.} The weight member of a weight $w$ is, on a domain $X$ of level $i$, $\eta_i^{-1}\sum_{p:X(p)=X}w(p)a_p$, every bare plaquette $p$ having one domain $X(p)$; let $w=w^{[i]}_a=L^{K-i}w_a$, so that $\eta_i^{-1}L^{K-i}=L^K$, and let $\mathfrak f_i[\mathsf W_{w^{[i]}_a}]$ be the bare array whose only member is this weight member. Applied to its members at the point $\mathfrak u=(P[v],g_iB)$, with the pair identity in equation~\YMMref{(2286)}{833} for the configuration of the substituted pair, (a) gives at every point $v=(A,\mathbf J)$ of the chart of level $i+1$ with $\|v\|<\varrho_{\mathrm{ch}}$, real or not, in a chain class or not, and every $B\in\mathsf{Rg}_{x_i}$ (as $\delta_i<\varrho_{\mathrm{fl}}$)
\[
\mathbb V'\bigl[\mathfrak f_i[\mathsf W_{w^{[i]}_a}]\bigr]^{\mathrm{tot}}(P[v];B)=L^K\sum_pw_a(p)\Bigl[a_p\bigl(e^{i\eta_iA^{\mathrm{lw}}(v,g_iB)}\bigr)-a_p\bigl(e^{i\eta_{i+1}A}\bigr)\Bigr],
\]
This proves at every such chart point the algebraic identity whose real-background form is equation~\YMMref{(2290)}{834}.

(c) \emph{The covariance.} By Lem.~\ref{lem:weighted-step-integrals} and equation~\YMMref{(2298)}{837}, $\mathsf{Sum}[\mathsf K^{(i+1)}](P)$ is, at every triple $P$ of the core, the covariance under $\nu_i[P]$ of the two totals of (b); the terms $a_p(e^{i\eta_{i+1}A})$ are constants. So at every real $v$ with $\|v\|\le\delta_i$
\[
\mathcal K_i(v)=L^{2K}\sum_{p,q}w_1(p)w_2(q)\bigl\langle a_p(\tilde U^{\mathrm{lw}});a_q(\tilde U^{\mathrm{lw}})\bigr\rangle_{\nu_{i,v}},\qquad\tilde U^{\mathrm{lw}}(B)=e^{i\eta_iA^{\mathrm{lw}}(v,g_iB)},
\]
where $\nu_{i,v}$ is a probability measure on $\mathsf{Rg}_{x_i}$ and $|\langle F;F'\rangle_{\nu_{i,v}}|\le2\sup|F|\sup|F'|$ (Prop.~\YMMref{124.5}{836}).

(d) \emph{The plaquette terms.} $(v,g_iB)$ is a real point with $\|v\|\le\delta_i$ and $\sup|g_iB|<g_i\mathfrak b_i=\delta_i$. The linear part of the lowered angle in the fluctuation is $\mathsf{sg}_i\sum_b\mathsf T^{\mathrm{cv}}_i(p,b)\mathcal A(b)$, where $\mathsf T^{\mathrm{cv}}_i=(\mathsf T^{\mathrm{cv}}_i(p,b))$ is the real matrix, indexed by the bare plaquettes and the positively oriented fluctuation bonds, of the curvature response of one step composed with its elimination map (the definitions preceding Lem.~\YMMref{124.3}{835}), $\mathsf{sg}_i\in\{1,-1\}$ is the sign of Lem.~\YMMref{124.3}{835}, and $\sum_b|\mathsf T^{\mathrm{cv}}_i(p,b)|\le C^{\mathrm{row}}_{\mathrm{tp}}\eta_i^2$ (Prop.~\YMMref{120.6}{821}, equation~\YMMref{(2239)}{821}). Lem.~\YMMref{124.4}{835} at $r=a=\delta_i$, $\mathsf{rt}=\varrho_\wedge/\delta_i\ge2$, gives
\[
a_p(\tilde U^{\mathrm{lw}}(B))=\tfrac12|F_p|^2+\langle F_p,\xi_p\rangle+\tfrac12\langle\xi_p,\xi_p\rangle+\mathsf o_p(B),\qquad\xi_p=\mathsf{sg}_ig_i\sum_b\mathsf T^{\mathrm{cv}}_i(p,b)B(b),
\]
with $F_p=\mathsf{ang}^{[i+1]}_p(A)$, $|\mathsf o_p|\le\mathsf M_{\mathrm{pl}}^2\eta_i^4\mathsf{rt}^{-3}=\eta_i^4\bar\rho$, $|F_p|\le2L^{-2}\eta_i^2\delta_i$ and $|\xi_p|\le2\mathsf c_{\mathfrak h}\eta_i^2\delta_i$. So $\mathsf X_p=\langle F_p,\xi_p\rangle+\frac12\langle\xi_p,\xi_p\rangle$ has $\sup|\mathsf X_p|\le\eta_i^4\bar X$, and $\langle a_p;a_q\rangle_{\nu_{i,v}}$ differs from $\langle\mathsf X_p;\mathsf X_q\rangle_{\nu_{i,v}}$ by at most $\eta_i^8(4\bar X\bar\rho+2\bar\rho^2)$.

(e) \emph{The Gaussian part.} Under $\nu_{i,v}$ the joint cumulants of the orders $1$, $3$, $4$ of the components of $B$ are at most $\epsilon=\epsilon^{\mathrm{cu}}_i$, and those of the order $2$ lie within $\epsilon'=\epsilon+2\mathsf c_{\mathbf C}\delta_i/r_\alpha$ of $\mathbf C_0$, the covariance of the step at $v=0$ (Prop.~\YMMref{124.5}{836}, equations~\YMMref{(2296)}{836}--\YMMref{(2297)}{836}, at $\|v\|\le\delta_i$); and $\mathbf C_0=(\mathsf A^{\mathrm{cv}}_i)^{-1}\otimes1$ with $\mathsf T^{\mathrm{cv}}_i(\mathsf A^{\mathrm{cv}}_i)^{-1}(\mathsf T^{\mathrm{cv}}_i)^{\mathsf T}=\eta_i\mathcal C_{(i+1)}$, $\mathsf A^{\mathrm{cv}}_i$ the real symmetric matrix of one step at the trivial configuration on the fluctuation bonds (equation~\YMMref{(2297)}{836}).

A covariance of products is the sum, over the partitions that are no refinements of the two factors, of the products of the cumulants of the blocks. With $\mathbf C_0$ in the place of the second cumulants, the part of $\langle\langle F_p,\xi_p\rangle;\langle F_q,\xi_q\rangle\rangle$ is $g_i^2\eta_i\mathcal C_{(i+1)}(p,q)\langle F_p,F_q\rangle$, that of $\frac14\langle\langle\xi_p,\xi_p\rangle;\langle\xi_q,\xi_q\rangle\rangle$ is $\frac32g_i^4\eta_i^2\mathcal C_{(i+1)}(p,q)^2$ (three colours, two pairings), the mixed covariances $\langle\langle F_p,\xi_p\rangle;\frac12\langle\xi_q,\xi_q\rangle\rangle$ have none, and the rest is at most $\eta_i^8$ times the first three summands of $\mathsf E_i$, by the row sums.

Multiplied by $L^{2K}w_1(p)w_2(q)$ and summed ($L^{2K}\eta_i^8\sum_p|w_1(p)|\sum_q|w_2(q)|=\mathsf w_1\mathsf w_2$, $L^{2K}g_i^2\eta_i=a_K^{-1}\upsilon_{i+1}$), this gives, with $\mathsf k_i=\frac32g_i^4\eta_i^2L^{2K}\sum_{p,q}w_1(p)w_2(q)\mathcal C_{(i+1)}(p,q)^2$ and $\mathcal Q_i(v)=\mathcal Q_i(\mathsf{ang}^{[i+1]}(A))$,
\[
|\mathcal K_i(v)-\mathsf k_i-\mathcal Q_i(v)|\le\mathsf w_1\mathsf w_2\mathsf E_i .
\]

(f) \emph{Why a ball.} A ball of the chart is closed under $v\mapsto\zeta v$, under cut-offs and under small gauge transformations, which steps 4 and 5 use; a chain class is closed under none of the three, and this is why the totals are taken at every point of the chart. The radius $\delta_i$ enters only the expansion, the bound of $|F_p|$ and the ratio $\|v\|/r_\alpha$; read at a radius $\delta_i\le\mathsf r\le\frac12\varrho_{\mathrm{ch}}$ ($a=\delta_i$, $\mathsf{rt}=\min\{\varrho_{\mathrm{ch}}/\mathsf r,\varrho_{\mathrm{fl}}/\delta_i\}\ge2$), the same argument gives $|\mathcal K_i(v)-\mathsf k_i-\mathcal Q_i(v)|\le\mathsf w_1\mathsf w_2\mathsf E_i(\mathsf r)$ at the real points with $\|v\|\le\mathsf r$; at $\mathsf r=\max\{\delta_i,\alpha\}$, at the point $v$ of step 1 and at $0$, this is (i).

4. \emph{Two constants.} For real $v'$ with $\|v'\|\le\delta_i/2\Lambda_i$ put $\psi(\zeta)=\mathcal K_i(\zeta v')-\mathcal K_i(0)-\zeta^2\mathcal Q_i(v')$: holomorphic for $|\zeta|<\delta_i/\|v'\|$, $\psi(0)=\psi'(0)=0$, $|\psi|\le\mathsf M_i$, $|\psi|\le\bar{\mathsf e}$ on the real segment (step 3 at $tv'$ and at $0$); Lem.~\ref{C-352-17} gives $|\psi(1)|\le4e\bar{\mathsf e}\Lambda_i^2\|v'\|^2/\delta_i^2$ (if $\bar{\mathsf e}>\mathsf M_i$, then $|\psi|\le\mathsf M_i<\bar{\mathsf e}$ on the disc and Schwarz's lemma of the order two gives more). Of the complex ball only the bound $\mathsf M_i$ is used, through $\log\mathsf M_i$; the smallness comes from the real ball, where the step measure is a probability measure, and any $\bar{\mathsf e}\ge2\mathsf w_1\mathsf w_2\mathsf E_i$ serves.

5. \emph{The gauge.} Let first $4\mathsf h_i+4$ be at most the side $\ell L^{K-i-1}$ of the torus in level-$(i+1)$ units. Lem.~\ref{C-352-18} on the box $N_{\mathsf h_i}$ about the pair gives $v'$ with $\|v'\|\le\mathsf s$; the domains in the box take the same values at $v$ and at $v'$, those outside have $d_{i+1}(X)\ge(\mathsf h_i-1-R_w)/M-2$ and cost $2\mathsf M^{\mathsf K}_ie^{-[\cdot]_+}\le\bar{\mathsf e}\gamma_\circ^2/\delta_i^2$ by the choice of $\mathsf h_i$; replacing $\mathcal Q_i(v')$ by $\mathcal Q_i(v)$ costs the last term of (ii), since $|\mathcal C_{(i+1)}|\le\mathsf c_i\eta_i^3$ on the supports. If $4\mathsf h_i+4>\ell L^{K-i-1}$, then $L^m\le L^{K-i-1}<(4\mathsf h_i+4)/\ell\le\mathsf h_i$, as $\ell\ge8$ and $\mathsf h_i\ge2$; so $\|v\|\le\max\{\alpha,\gamma_\circ\}=\alpha=L^m\gamma_\circ\le\mathsf h_i\gamma_\circ\le\mathsf s$, and step 4 applies at $v'=v$ itself, with no gauge and no domains outside a box: (ii) holds without its last term.

6. \emph{The narrow pair.} Take $\bar{\mathsf e}=2\bar{\mathsf w}_1\bar{\mathsf w}_2\mathsf E_i$ with $\bar{\mathsf w}_a=81\hat\rho_i^3|w_a|_\infty/a_{K-i}\ge\mathsf w_a$. By Lem.~\ref{C-352-15}(c), $\|\mathsf K^{(i+1)}\|\le\frac12t_i^2\bar\nu_i=C x_i^{-1}\bar{\mathsf w}_1\bar{\mathsf w}_2$: the factor $\hat\rho_i^6$ cancels in $\mathsf M_i/\bar{\mathsf e}\le C(1+\mathsf N_{i+1})x_i^{-1}\delta_i^{-6}\le C(1+u_{\mathsf k(r)}^3)x_{\mathsf k(r)}^2$ (by the lower bound $2\mathsf M_{\mathrm{pl}}^4\varrho_\wedge^{-6}\delta_i^6\le\mathsf E_i$), so $\Lambda_i\le CY_r$ by the working level; $R_w\le11u_{i+1}$ and $\log^+(\delta_i/\gamma_\circ)\le2m\log L\le2Y_r$ give $\mathsf h_i\le CY_r^{2\mathfrak p_0}$. If $\mathsf s\le\delta_i/2\Lambda_i$, (ii) with $\bar{\mathsf w}_1\bar{\mathsf w}_2x_i^{-1}L^{-4m}r_n^2\le C\mathfrak b_n^2u_i^3(\rho/r)^6\hat r_n^3\mathsf u_1\mathsf u_2$; else $L^{3(n-i)}\le C\mathsf h_i^2\Lambda_i^2$, and (i) gives the first term.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{The induction over the levels; the jets.}

\begin{lemma}[One step: cumulants, quadratic polynomials, the Gaussian step]\label{C-352-20}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[beginpenalty=10000]
\item[(a)] In the data of one renormalisation step at a height $i$, for a real point $v$ of the chart of the level $i+1$ with $\|v\|<r_\alpha$, every $n\ge1$ and components $B^{\alpha_1}(b_1),\dots,B^{\alpha_n}(b_n)$ of the fluctuation field, repetitions allowed, the joint cumulants under the measure $\nu_{i,v}$ of the step are formed and satisfy $|\kappa(B^{\alpha_1}(b_1),\dots)|\le\epsilon^{\mathrm{cu},n}_i$ for $n\ne2$ and $|\kappa(B^{\alpha_1}(b_1),B^{\alpha_2}(b_2))-\mathbf C_v((b_1,\alpha_1),(b_2,\alpha_2))|\le\epsilon^{\mathrm{cu},2}_i$, where \[
 \epsilon^{\mathrm{cu},n}_i=C_{\mathrm E,0}(K_\Pi\mathsf n^{\mathbb V}_i+K^\Pi_P\mathsf p_{\star,i})(n\mathsf n_{\mathrm f}/w_\star)^n
\] with construction constants, $\mathsf n^{\mathbb V}_i\le c_{\mathbb V}\delta_i$; $\mathbf C_v$ is the covariance of the step, $|\mathbf C_v|\le\mathsf c_{\mathbf C}$ and $|\mathbf C_v-\mathbf C_0|\le2\mathsf c_{\mathbf C}\|v\|/r_\alpha$ entry by entry, $\mathbf C_0=(\mathsf A^{\mathrm{cv}}_i)^{-1}\otimes1$, and $\mathsf T^{\mathrm{cv}}_i(\mathsf A^{\mathrm{cv}}_i)^{-1}(\mathsf T^{\mathrm{cv}}_i)^{\mathsf T}=\eta_i\mathcal C_{(i+1)}$ (at $n\le4$ the bounds on the cumulants are those of the proof of Prop.~\YMMref{124.5}{836}, and the statements on $\mathbf C_v$ and $\mathbf C_0$ are in Prop.~\YMMref{124.5}{836}).

Here $\mathsf A^{\mathrm{cv}}_i$ is the real symmetric matrix of one step at the trivial configuration on the positively oriented fluctuation bonds $b\in\mathfrak X^+$, positive definite as $\mathbf C_0$ is (Prop.~\YMMref{124.5}{836} at $v=0$); $\mathsf T^{\mathrm{cv}}_i=(\mathsf T^{\mathrm{cv}}_i(p,b))$ is the real matrix, indexed by the bare plaquettes and the bonds of $\mathfrak X^+$, of the curvature response of one step composed with its elimination map (the definitions preceding Lem.~\YMMref{124.3}{835}); and there are a sign $\mathsf{sg}_i\in\{1,-1\}$ and the number $C^{\mathrm{row}}_{\mathrm{tp}}$ of Prop.~\YMMref{120.6}{821} such that the linear part of the lowered angle in a fluctuation $\mathcal A$ is $\mathsf{sg}_i\sum_b\mathsf T^{\mathrm{cv}}_i(p,b)\mathcal A(b)$ and $\sum_b|\mathsf T^{\mathrm{cv}}_i(p,b)|\le C^{\mathrm{row}}_{\mathrm{tp}}\eta_i^2$ (Lem.~\YMMref{124.3}{835} and Prop.~\YMMref{120.6}{821}, equation~\YMMref{(2239)}{821}, on a side $\ell$ at least the constant $N_{\mathsf H}$ fixed in Section~\YMMref{120.3}{820}, as in the frame).

At a real point $(v,g_iB)$, $v=(A,\mathbf J)$, $B\in\mathsf{Rg}_{x_i}$, with $r\ge\|v\|$ and $\mathsf{rt}=\min\{\varrho_{\mathrm{ch}}/r,\varrho_{\mathrm{fl}}/\delta_i\}\ge2$, Lem.~\YMMref{124.4}{835} (at $a=\delta_i$) splits the angle of the lowered configuration:
\[
\mathsf{ang}^{[i]}_p\bigl(A^{\mathrm{lw}}(v,g_iB)\bigr)=\mathsf{ang}^{[i+1]}_p(A)+\psi_p(B)+\zeta_p(B),\qquad\psi_p(B)=\mathsf{sg}_ig_i\sum_b\mathsf T^{\mathrm{cv}}_i(p,b)B(b),
\]
$|\psi_p|\le2\mathsf c_{\mathfrak h}\eta_i^2\delta_i$, $|\zeta_p|\le4\mathsf M_{\mathrm{gr}}\eta_i^2\mathsf{rt}^{-2}$, with the number $\mathsf M_{\mathrm{gr}}$ of equation~\YMMref{(2285)}{833}; under the centred Gaussian with covariance $\mathbf C_0$, $\psi$ has the covariance $g_i^2\eta_i\mathcal C_{(i+1)}=a_K\upsilon_{i+1}\mathcal C_{(i+1)}$, as $\mathsf{sg}_i^2=1$ and $g_i^2\eta_i=a_K\upsilon_{i+1}$. At $v=v_{A'}$, $A'\in\mathsf{Cc}_{i+1}(r_{i+1})$, one takes $r=r_{i+1}$; under $(\Gamma1)$ Lem.~\ref{C-352-10}(b) gives $\mathsf{rt}\ge2$ and $|\zeta_p|\le C\eta_i^2\delta_i^2$. We put $\epsilon^{\mathrm{cu}}_i=\epsilon^{\mathrm{cu},4}_i$; with $C_\star=C_{\mathrm E,0}\max\{K_\Pi c_{\mathbb V},K^\Pi_P\}$, so that $\epsilon^{\mathrm{cu},n}_i\le C_\star(\delta_i+\mathsf p_{\star,i})(n\mathsf n_{\mathrm f}/w_\star)^n$, we take $C_{\mathrm{cu}}=C_\star(4\mathsf n_{\mathrm f}/w_\star)^4$, $c^{(n)}_{\mathrm{cu}}=2C_\star(2n\mathsf n_{\mathrm f}/w_\star)^{2n}$ and $c_{\mathrm{cu}}=c^{(3)}_{\mathrm{cu}}$, so that $\epsilon^{\mathrm{cu}}_i\le C_{\mathrm{cu}}(\delta_i+\mathsf p_{\star,i})$ and $\epsilon^{\mathrm{cu},2n}_i\le c^{(n)}_{\mathrm{cu}}(\delta_i+\mathsf p_{\star,i})/2$; we put $\epsilon'^{(n)}_i=\epsilon^{\mathrm{cu},2n}_i+2\mathsf c_{\mathbf C}r_{i+1}/r_\alpha$ and $\epsilon'_i=\epsilon'^{(3)}_i$, and $c^{(n)}_\epsilon$ is the number $c_\epsilon$ of Lem.~\ref{C-352-10}(b) with $c^{(n)}_{\mathrm{cu}}$ in place of $c_{\mathrm{cu}}$.

We have $4\mathsf n_{\mathrm f}/w_\star>1$ ($\mathsf n_{\mathrm f}=\frac12M^{3/2}$ and $w_\star<1$: equation~\YMMref{(2294)}{836} and the proof of Prop.~\YMMref{124.5}{836}); so with $x=\mathsf n_{\mathrm f}/w_\star$, $(nx)^n\le(n'x)^n\le(n'x)^{n'}$ for $n\le n'$, $n'\ge4$, and $\epsilon^{\mathrm{cu},n}_i\le\epsilon^{\mathrm{cu},2m}_i$ for $n\le2m$, $m=2,3,4$: at $\|v\|\le r_{i+1}$ the joint cumulants of all the orders $\le2m$ lie within $\epsilon'^{(m)}_i$ of those of the centred Gaussian with covariance $\mathbf C_0$ (at the order two through $|\mathbf C_v-\mathbf C_0|\le2\mathsf c_{\mathbf C}r_{i+1}/r_\alpha$). Besides $\epsilon'^{(2)}_i\le\epsilon'_i\le\epsilon'^{(4)}_i$ and $c^{(2)}_\epsilon\le c_\epsilon\le c^{(4)}_\epsilon$; so $(\Gamma1)$ with $c^{(4)}_\epsilon$ in place of $c_\epsilon$ contains $(\Gamma1)$, and $(\Gamma^{(4)})$ contains $(\Gamma)$.
\item[(b)] Let $I$ be finite, $\nu$ a probability measure with bounded support on $\mathbb R^I$, $\mathbf C$ a real symmetric positive semidefinite matrix on $I$ with $|\mathbf C(\mathsf i,\mathsf j)|\le\mathsf c$, $\mathsf c\ge1$, $0\le\epsilon\le1$, and let the cumulants of $\nu$ of orders $n\le6$ be within $\epsilon$ of those of the centred Gaussian $\mathsf G$ with covariance $\mathbf C$. For quadratic polynomials $P_1,P_2,P_3$ in the coordinates, with $\|P\|_{\mathrm{pol}}$ the sum of the moduli of their coefficients of orders one and two, and $1\le m\le3$: $|\kappa_\nu(P_1,\dots,P_m)-\kappa_{\mathsf G}(P_1,\dots,P_m)|\le c_6\epsilon\prod_l\|P_l\|_{\mathrm{pol}}$, $c_6=1218(\mathsf c+1)^5$. If only the cumulants of the orders $n\le4$ are within $\epsilon$ of those of $\mathsf G$, the same holds for $m\le2$ with $c_4=60(\mathsf c+1)^3$; if those of the orders $n\le8$ are, it holds for $m\le4$ (four sources) with $c_8=33120(\mathsf c+1)^7$; and $c_4\le c_6\le c_8$.
\item[(c)] Let $k_\flat\le i<K$, $\mathsf s=\upsilon_{i+1}\mathcal C_{(i+1)}$, and let $\psi$ be a centred Gaussian vector of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued functions of the plaquettes with $\mathbb E\psi^\alpha_p\psi^{\alpha'}_q=a_K\delta_{\alpha\alpha'}\mathsf s(p,q)$. For every $F'$ and every nonempty set $\beta$ of sources,
\[
\sum_{\pi\in\mathrm{Part}(\beta)}\kappa\bigl(q_{i;\beta'}(F'+\psi):\beta'\in\pi\bigr)=(g_{i+1;\beta}-g_{i;\beta})+q_{i+1;\beta}(F').
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(a) The bound on the cumulants of one step (the proof of Prop.~\YMMref{124.5}{836}) is proved with $n$ insertions of one sort, and depends on the number $n$ only through the factor $(n\mathsf n_{\mathrm f}/w_\star)^n$; so it holds at every order. The remaining statements in (a) follow from the results cited there, and the comparison of the orders is the arithmetic stated in (a). (b) The cumulant of products $X_{S_1},\dots,X_{S_m}$ is the sum, over the partitions $\sigma$ of $S=\bigsqcup S_l$ with $\sigma\vee\{S_1,..,S_m\}=\{S\}$, of the products of the cumulants of the blocks (from the expansions of $\exp$ and $\log$ in $\mathbb C[z]/(z_l^2)$). Replacing the factors one by one costs $|\sigma|\epsilon(\mathsf c+1)^{|\sigma|-1}\le2m\epsilon(\mathsf c+1)^{2m-1}$, as $|S|\le2m$, and a set of $2m$ elements has $B_{2m}$ partitions, $B_4=15$, $B_6=203$, $B_8=4140$: so $c_{2m}=2m\,B_{2m}(\mathsf c+1)^{2m-1}$ serves, which is $c_6=6\cdot203(\mathsf c+1)^5$ for $m\le3$, $c_4$ for $m\le2$ and $c_8$ for $m\le4$. (c) Put $w_\lambda=\sum_a\lambda_aw_a$, $R^\lambda_i=w_\lambda(1-\mathcal S_iw_\lambda)^{-1}$, $g^\lambda_i=-\frac32\operatorname{Tr}\log(1-\mathcal S_iw_\lambda)$ and $q^\lambda_i(F)=\frac1{2a_K}\langle F,R^\lambda_iF\rangle$; their coefficients of $\lambda^\beta=\prod_{a\in\beta}\lambda_a$ are $R_{i;\beta}$, $g_{i;\beta}$ and $q_{i;\beta}$.

The Gaussian integral, with the factor $3$ from the dimension of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$, is
\[
\log\mathbb E\,e^{q^\lambda_i(F'+\psi)}=-\tfrac32\operatorname{Tr}\log(1-\mathsf sR^\lambda_i)+\tfrac1{2a_K}\langle F',R^\lambda_i(1-\mathsf sR^\lambda_i)^{-1}F'\rangle,
\]
and $1-\mathsf sR^\lambda_i=(1-\mathcal S_{i+1}w_\lambda)(1-\mathcal S_iw_\lambda)^{-1}$, $R^\lambda_i(1-\mathsf sR^\lambda_i)^{-1}=R^\lambda_{i+1}$, as $\mathcal S_{i+1}=\mathcal S_i+\mathsf s$. The coefficient of $\lambda^\beta$ of the left member is the sum over the partitions of the joint cumulants; that of the right member is $(g_{i+1;\beta}-g_{i;\beta})+q_{i+1;\beta}(F')$. This is Wick's rule for the photon fields of one step.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The tower identity at several sources]\label{C-352-20a}
Let $0<g\le\gamma_{\mathrm{jt}}$, $g^{-2}\ge x_{\mathrm J}$, $(K,\beta)$ a first-passage datum at $g$, $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$, $n\ge2$, and let $w_a=f_a\circ x\not\equiv0$, $a\in[n]$, with real Lipschitz functions $f_a$ on $T_\ell$ with pairwise disjoint supports (for instance the tents of Lem.~\ref{C-352-11}(b)) that fall into two nonempty clusters $[n]=I_1\sqcup I_2$ lying in the frame at a level $k$. Let $k\le i<K$, $A'\in\mathsf{Cc}_{i+1}(r_{i+1})$, $\tilde U=e^{i\eta_{i+1}A'}$, $v_{A'}=(A',J^{(i+1)}(\tilde U))$ the real point of the chart of level $i+1$ that $A'$ gives, with $\|v_{A'}\|\le r_{i+1}$, $\nu=\nu_{i,A'}:=\nu_{i,v_{A'}}$ the measure of the step, and $B\mapsto A^{\mathrm{lw}}(B)=A^{\mathrm{lw}}(v_{A'},g_iB)$ the lowering map (Prop.~\YMMref{124.2}{834}). Then for every nonempty $\beta\subset[n]$
\[
G_{i+1;\beta}(A')=\sum_{\pi\in\mathrm{Part}(\beta)}\kappa_\nu\bigl(G_{i;\beta'}\circ A^{\mathrm{lw}}:\beta'\in\pi\bigr).
\]
The same holds for real mixed sources $\mathfrak s_a\ne0$, $a\in[n]$, at $0<g\le\gamma_{\mathrm N}$ with $K\ge2$, the progression being formed with their weight members in the source slot (the lemma on bond sources, which follows Lem.~\ref{C-352-36}), when the two unions of the hulls of the clusters $I_1$, $I_2$ satisfy the conditions of the frame at $k$ of clause~(6) of that lemma. For mixed sources the frame is that of clause~(6), read with the hulls in the place of the supports, and the tower identity for a pair is the one stated in that clause.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For $\lambda$ near $0$ in $\mathbb C^n$ put $\Phi(\lambda)=\exp D^\lambda_{i+1}(\tilde U)-\int\exp D^\lambda_i(e^{i\eta_iA^{\mathrm{lw}}(B)})\,\mathrm{d}\nu(B)$, formed with the progression of $(w_1,\dots,w_n)$. Each relative exponent is a finite sum of functions that are holomorphic in $\lambda$, and the integrand is bounded uniformly in $B$ for $\lambda$ near $0$, as the progression with any number of sources lies in the setting of one step (Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8}); so $\Phi$ is holomorphic near $0$. Let $t\in\mathbb R^n$ be nonzero on $I_1$ and on $I_2$, and put $f^t=\sum_{a\in I_1}t_af_a$, $h^t=\sum_{a\in I_2}t_af_a$. These are real Lipschitz functions; $f^t\circ x$ and $h^t\circ x$ do not vanish identically, the supports of the $w_a$ being disjoint; and their supports lie in the two unions of supports.

So $(f^t,h^t)$ lies in the frame at $k$, and the tower identity among the construction results for a pair (equation~\eqref{eq:weighted-pair-tower}) gives $\exp D^\mu_{i+1}[f^t,h^t](\tilde U)=\int\exp D^\mu_i[f^t,h^t](e^{i\eta_iA^{\mathrm{lw}}})\,\mathrm{d}\nu$ for $\mu$ near $0$ in $\mathbb C^2$, with the same measure $\nu$ and the same lowering map, neither of which depends on the sources. The progression depends on the parameters and the sources only through $w_\lambda$; at $\lambda(\mu)=(\mu_1t|_{I_1},\mu_2t|_{I_2})$ one has $w_{\lambda(\mu)}=\mu_1f^t\circ x+\mu_2h^t\circ x$, so $D^{\lambda(\mu)}_\cdot=D^\mu_\cdot[f^t,h^t]$, and at $\mu=(s,s)$: $\Phi(st)=0$ for all small real $s$. With the expansion $\Phi=\sum_N\Phi_N$ in homogeneous polynomials, $\sum_Ns^N\Phi_N(t)=0$ for small $s$; so $\Phi_N(t)=0$ for every $N$ and every $t$ of a dense subset of $\mathbb R^n$, hence $\Phi_N=0$ and $\Phi=0$ near $0$.

As $D^0_{i+1}=0$ and $D^0_i=0$, the multilinear jets of the two members of $\exp D^\lambda_{i+1}(\tilde U)=\int\exp D^\lambda_i\,\mathrm{d}\nu$ agree in $\mathbb C[\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n]/(\lambda_a^2)$, and the logarithm of a moment series is the cumulant series; differentiation under the integral is allowed by Cauchy's formula in $\lambda$. The coefficient of $\lambda^\beta$ is the claim. At $n=2$ the lemma is the identity among the construction results. For mixed sources the argument is the same, with the weight member of $\mathfrak s_\lambda=\sum_a\lambda_a\mathfrak s_a$, which is linear in $\mathfrak s_\lambda$ (clause~(1) of the lemma on bond sources), in the source slot. The $t\in\mathbb R^n$ at which $\sum_{a\in I_1}t_a\mathfrak s_a$ or $\sum_{a\in I_2}t_a\mathfrak s_a$ is $0$ form two proper linear subspaces, every $\mathfrak s_a$ being nonzero; off them, a dense set, the two sums are nonzero mixed sources whose hulls lie in the two unions of the hulls of the clusters, so they are in the frame of clause~(6), and the identity for a pair stated there, with the same measure $\nu$ and the same lowering map, stands in the place of equation~\eqref{eq:weighted-pair-tower}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The induction over the levels]\label{C-352-21}
Let $n\in\{2,3,4\}$ and let $g$ satisfy $(\Gamma1)$, with $c^{(4)}_\epsilon$ in place of $c_\epsilon$ if $n=4$; let $(K,\beta)$ be a first-passage datum at $g$, $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$, and let real weights $w_1,\dots,w_n$ with the two clusters $\{1\},\{2\}$, or $\{1,2\},\{3\}$, or $\{1,2\},\{3,4\}$ lie in the frame at a level $k$; let $k\le k_1<K$, $0\le k_\flat\le k_1$, and form the free objects over the base level $k_\flat$. Let numbers $\mathsf v_\beta>0$, $c^\circ_\beta$ and $\epsilon_\circ\ge0$, $\emptyset\ne\beta\subset[n]$, satisfy
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(I1)] $|G_{k_1;\beta}(A)-c^\circ_\beta-q_{k_1;\beta}(\mathsf{ang}^{[k_1]}(A))|\le\epsilon_\circ\mathsf v_\beta$ for $A\in\mathsf{Cc}_{k_1}(r_{k_1})$;
\item[(I2)] $\varrho_{i;\beta}:=\eta_i^4\sum_{p,q}|R_{i;\beta}(p,q)|/(a_Kx_i)\le L^{-3(i-k_1)}\mathsf v_\beta$ for $k_1\le i<K$;
\item[(I3)] $\prod_{\beta'\in\pi}\mathsf v_{\beta'}\le\mathsf v_\beta$ for every partition $\pi$ of $\beta$.
\end{enumerate}
Put $Z=Z_0(1+\mathfrak b_{k_1})^2$ and $\varpi=\epsilon_\circ+\sum_{i=k_1}^{K-1}L^{-3(i-k_1)}(\delta_i+c_{2n}\epsilon'^{(n)}_i)$, with a number $Z_0$ formed from the constants and the numbers $c_{2n}$ of Lem.~\ref{C-352-20}(b), and let $(K-k_1)\varpi\le1$. Then $\varpi\le\epsilon_\circ+\frac65(1+c_{2n}c^{(n)}_\epsilon)\delta_{k_1}$, and for $k_1\le i\le K$, $A\in\mathsf{Cc}_i(r_i)$ and every $\beta$, $m=|\beta|$,
\[
\bigl|G_{i;\beta}(A)-c^\circ_\beta-(g_{i;\beta}-g_{k_1;\beta})-q_{i;\beta}(\mathsf{ang}^{[i]}(A))\bigr|\le\mathsf a_mZ^m\varpi\,\mathsf v_\beta,\qquad(\mathsf a_1,\mathsf a_2,\mathsf a_3)=(1,14,285),
\]
$\mathsf a_4$ a number; in particular $|\mathsf J_n-c^\circ_{[n]}-g_{K;[n]}+g_{k_1;[n]}|\le\mathsf a_nZ^n\varpi\mathsf v_{[n]}$. Of the base level only the relation $\mathcal S_{i+1}-\mathcal S_i=\upsilon_{i+1}\mathcal C_{(i+1)}$, $i\ge k_1$, is used.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Let $\mathsf e_{i;\beta}$ be the supremum over $\mathsf{Cc}_i(r_i)$ of the left member. 1. \emph{The tower.} For $A'\in\mathsf{Cc}_{i+1}(r_{i+1})$ and the measure $\nu=\nu_{i,A'}$ of the step, $G_{i+1;\beta}(A')=\sum_{\pi}\kappa_\nu(G_{i;\beta'}\circ A^{\mathrm{lw}}:\beta'\in\pi)$ (the lemma on the tower identity at several sources, which precedes this proposition, for the two clusters of the frame). 2. \emph{The lowered angle.} The point $v_{A'}$ of the chart is real, with $\|v_{A'}\|\le r_{i+1}<\varrho_{\mathrm{ch}}\le r_\alpha$ by the definition of the chain classes (equation~\eqref{eq:weighted-chain-class}); $\nu=\nu_{i,v_{A'}}$ is a probability measure carried by the real $B$ with $|B(b)|<\mathfrak b_i$ (Prop.~\YMMref{124.5}{836}), and $A^{\mathrm{lw}}(B)\in\mathsf{Cc}_i(r_i)$ (Prop.~\YMMref{124.2}{834} with the radius recurrence~\YMMref{(2291)}{834}).

By the splitting of Lem.~\ref{C-352-20}(a) at $r=r_{i+1}$, $\mathsf{ang}^{[i]}_p(A^{\mathrm{lw}}(B))=F'_p+\psi_p(B)+\zeta_p(B)$, with $F'=\mathsf{ang}^{[i+1]}(A')$, $\psi_p(B)=\mathsf{sg}_ig_i\sum_b\mathsf T^{\mathrm{cv}}_i(p,b)B(b)$ linear in the fluctuation field $B$, $|\psi_p|\le2\mathsf c_{\mathfrak h}\eta_i^2\delta_i$ and $|\zeta_p|\le C\eta_i^2\delta_i^2$ by the smallness of Lem.~\ref{C-352-10}(b); besides $|F'_p|\le2\eta_{i+1}^2r_{i+1}\le\mathsf c_{\mathfrak h}\eta_i^2\delta_i$. So $Y_\beta=G_{i;\beta}\circ A^{\mathrm{lw}}$ is within $\mathsf e_{i;\beta}+Z\delta_iL^{-3(i-k_1)}\mathsf v_\beta$ of the quadratic polynomial $P_\beta=c^\circ_\beta+g_{i;\beta}-g_{k_1;\beta}+q_{i;\beta}(F'+\psi)$ in the coordinates $B^\alpha(b)$: the term with $\zeta$ is at most $Ca_K^{-1}\eta_i^4\delta_i^3\sum_{p,q}|R_{i;\beta}(p,q)|=C\mathfrak b_i^2\delta_i\varrho_{i;\beta}$.

The linear part of $P_\beta$ has the coefficients $\mathsf{sg}_ig_ia_K^{-1}\sum_{p,q}R_{i;\beta}(p,q)\mathsf T^{\mathrm{cv}}_i(q,b)F'^\alpha_p$, its quadratic part the coefficients $\frac12g_i^2a_K^{-1}\sum_{p,q}R_{i;\beta}(p,q)\mathsf T^{\mathrm{cv}}_i(p,b)\mathsf T^{\mathrm{cv}}_i(q,b')$ of $B^\alpha(b)B^\alpha(b')$; with the row sums $\sum_b|\mathsf T^{\mathrm{cv}}_i(p,b)|\le C^{\mathrm{row}}_{\mathrm{tp}}\eta_i^2$, $x_ig_i\delta_i=\mathfrak b_i$ and $x_ig_i^2=1$,
\[
\|P_\beta\|_{\mathrm{pol}}\le\bigl[2\mathsf c_{\mathfrak h}C^{\mathrm{row}}_{\mathrm{tp}}\mathfrak b_i+\tfrac32(C^{\mathrm{row}}_{\mathrm{tp}})^2\bigr]\varrho_{i;\beta};
\]
so, by (I2), $\mathfrak b_i\le\mathfrak b_{k_1}$ and $|B(b)|<\mathfrak b_i$, $\|P_\beta\|_{\mathrm{pol}}$ and $\sup|P_\beta-\text{const}|$ are $\le ZL^{-3(i-k_1)}\mathsf v_\beta$, $Z_0$ being at least $2\mathsf c_{\mathfrak h}C^{\mathrm{row}}_{\mathrm{tp}}+\frac32(C^{\mathrm{row}}_{\mathrm{tp}})^2$ and the constant of the term with $\zeta$. 3. \emph{The Gaussian value.} Under the Gaussian with covariance $\mathbf C_0$, $\psi=\mathsf{sg}_ig_i\mathsf T^{\mathrm{cv}}_iB$ has the covariance $g_i^2\eta_i\mathcal C_{(i+1)}=a_K\upsilon_{i+1}\mathcal C_{(i+1)}$ (Lem.~\ref{C-352-20}(a): $\mathsf{sg}_i^2=1$, $\mathsf T^{\mathrm{cv}}_i(\mathsf A^{\mathrm{cv}}_i)^{-1}(\mathsf T^{\mathrm{cv}}_i)^{\mathsf T}=\eta_i\mathcal C_{(i+1)}$, $g_i^2\eta_i=a_K\upsilon_{i+1}$), and Lem.~\ref{C-352-20}(c) gives $\sum_\pi\kappa_{\mathsf G}(P_{\beta'})=c^\circ_\beta+g_{i+1;\beta}-g_{k_1;\beta}+q_{i+1;\beta}(F')$. 4.

\emph{From $\mathsf G$ to $\nu$} by Lem.~\ref{C-352-20}(a), (b), with $\mathsf c=\max\{1,\mathsf c_{\mathbf C}\}$: as $\|v_{A'}\|\le r_{i+1}$, all the cumulants of the orders $\le2n$ lie within $\epsilon=\epsilon'^{(n)}_i$ of those of $\mathsf G$, and $\epsilon'^{(n)}_i\le c^{(n)}_\epsilon\delta_i\le1$ (under $(\Gamma1)$, as $c^{(2)}_\epsilon\le c_\epsilon$, and with $c^{(4)}_\epsilon$ at $n=4$); the number is $c_{2n}$; \emph{from $P$ to $Y$} by $|\kappa(X,Y)|\le\|X\|^\sim\|Y\|^\sim$, $|\kappa(X,Y,W)|\le2\|X\|^\sim\|Y\|^\sim\|W\|^\sim$, $\|X\|^\sim=\inf_c\sup|X-c|$. 5. \emph{The recursion.} With (I3) every product of sizes over a partition is at most $Z^m\mathsf v_\beta$ times pure numbers, and $\varepsilon_{i;\beta}=\mathsf e_{i;\beta}/Z^m\mathsf v_\beta$ obeys $\varepsilon_{i+1;a}\le\varepsilon_{i;a}+\tau_i$, $\varepsilon_{i+1;ab}\le\varepsilon_{i;ab}+2\tau_i+4\varpi^2+4\theta_i\varpi$ and the like at three sources, $\tau_i=L^{-3(i-k_1)}(\delta_i+c_{2n}\epsilon'^{(n)}_i)$, $\theta_i=L^{-3(i-k_1)}$; summed over at most $K-k_1$ heights with $(K-k_1)\varpi\le1$ this gives $1$, $14$ and $285$.

At $i=K$, $\mathsf{Cc}_K=\{0\}$ and $q_{K;\beta}(0)=0$. The bound of $\varpi$: $\epsilon'^{(n)}_i\le c^{(n)}_\epsilon\delta_i$ (as $\epsilon'_i\le c_\epsilon\delta_i$ in Lem.~\ref{C-352-10}(b)), $\delta_i\le(\frac54)^{1/2}L^{(i-k_1)/2}\delta_{k_1}$, $(\frac54)^{1/2}\sum_kL^{-5k/2}\le\frac65$.
