For two sources Steps 1--5 use only \eqref{eq:weighted-pair-tower-derivatives} and the cumulants up to order four.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The slices]\label{C-352-22}
Let $(K,\beta)$ be a first-passage datum at $g\le\gamma$, $p\ne q$ plaquettes, $\mathsf r=|x(p)-x(q)|_\infty$, $c^{(N)}_L=\sup_\tau\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}(L^j\tau)^Ne^{-\delta_{\mathrm{tp}}L^j\tau}$ and $\mathsf m_K=\frac54C_{\mathrm{tp}}c^{(3)}_L$. (a) For every set $\mathcal J\subset\{1,\dots,K\}$: $|\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\upsilon_j\mathcal C_{(j)}(p,q)|\le\mathsf m_K\mathsf b^{-1}a_K^3\mathsf r^{-3}$. (b) If $t=\mathsf r/a_{K-k}$ satisfies $\delta_{\mathrm{tp}}L(L-1)t\ge3\log L+\log2$, then
\[
\Bigl|\sum_{k<j\le K}\upsilon_j\mathcal C_{(j)}(p,q)-\mathsf b^{-1}C^{\mathrm{free}}_K(p,q)\Bigr|\le\mathsf b^{-1}a_K^3\bigl[\tfrac54C_{\mathrm{tp}}c^{(2)}_L\bar B\,\mathsf r^{-2}\mathsf b^{-1}+C^{\mathrm{bg}}_{\mathrm{tp}}+2L^3C_{\mathrm{tp}}\mathsf r^{-3}t^3e^{-\delta_{\mathrm{tp}}Lt}\bigr],
\]
with $C^{\mathrm{bg}}_{\mathrm{tp}}$ from Prop.~\YMMref{120.5}{821}, evaluated at $s=0$ in equation~\YMMref{(2236)}{821}.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(a) $\upsilon_j=(a_{K-j+1}x_{j-1})^{-1}\le\frac{24}{23}\mathsf b^{-1}\le\frac54\mathsf b^{-1}$ at every $0<g\le\gamma$: the flow bound and $g^{-2}<\mathsf b$, which Lem.~\ref{C-352-10}(a) states for every first-passage datum at every $0<g\le\gamma$, give $|a_{K-j+1}x_{j-1}-\mathsf b|\le a_{K-j+1}\bar B\le\bar B/L$, and $\bar B\le\frac{13}{24}g^{-2}<\frac{13}{24}\mathsf b$ at $g\le\gamma$ ({\cite[Lem.~G.3]{YMM2}} gives this bound), so $a_{K-j+1}x_{j-1}\ge\frac{23}{24}\mathsf b$ as $L\ge13$; and the decay of the slices: $\sum_j(\mathsf r/a_{K-j+1})^3e^{-\delta_{\mathrm{tp}}\mathsf r/a_{K-j+1}}\le c^{(3)}_L$, a lacunary sum. (b) Equation~\YMMref{(2227)}{818} gives $\sum_{k<j\le K}\mathcal C_{(j)}=C^{\mathrm{free}}_K-C^{\mathrm{bg}}_{K,0}-\sum_{j\le k}\mathcal C_{(j)}$, and Prop.~\YMMref{120.5}{821} bounds $|C^{\mathrm{bg}}_{K,0}(p,q)|$ by $C^{\mathrm{bg}}_{\mathrm{tp}}a_K^3$; $|\upsilon_j-\mathsf b^{-1}|=|\mathsf b-a_{K-j+1}x_{j-1}|\upsilon_j\mathsf b^{-1}\le\frac54\bar Ba_{K-j+1}\mathsf b^{-2}$ by the same bounds of the run, which with the decay gives the first term; the slices of the levels $j\le k$ are at $t_j\ge Lt$ and give the last term.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The explicit sizes; the weights of the induction]\label{C-352-23}
Let weights be placed at $(\rho,r,\mathsf d)$, or form two pairs at $(\rho,r,\mathsf d)$, with $\mathsf d\le e^{-2\sqrt3}$, $s(\rho)\le K$; let $k_\flat=\mathsf k(r)$, $k_1=\mathsf k(\mathsf d)$, $u=\hat r_{k_1}$, $\hat\rho=\hat\rho_{k_1}=qu$, $P=\hat{\mathsf d}_{k_1}$, and $I_1,I_2$ the clusters. Put $\mathsf w(\emptyset)=1$, $\mathsf w(\{a\})=\hat\rho^3$, $\mathsf w(\text{a whole pair})=q^6u^3\max\{1,u^3\}$, $c_*=\max\{102,4\cdot81\cdot3^{3/2}(1+\mathsf m_K)\}$, and
\[
\mathsf v_\beta=c_*^{|\beta|}\,\mathsf w(\beta\cap I_1)\,\mathsf w(\beta\cap I_2)\,\mathsf u_\beta,\qquad\mathsf u_\beta=\prod_{a\in\beta}\mathsf u_a .
\]
Then (I2) and (I3) of Prop.~\ref{C-352-21} hold; $\mathsf v_{[3]}\le c_*^3P^9\mathrm{nat}_3$ and $\mathsf v_{[4]}\le c_*^4P^{12}\mathrm{nat}_4$; for crossing $\beta$, $\mathsf z(\beta)\mathsf u_\beta\le P^{-6}\mathsf v_\beta$, and if $\mathsf e_{\mathrm{far}}=8e^{-\delta_{\mathrm{tp}}LP/2\sqrt3}\le1$, then $\varrho_{k_1;\beta}\le\mathsf e_{\mathrm{far}}\mathsf v_\beta$ and $|g_{k_1;[n]}|\le\frac32(n-1)!(81\cdot3^{3/2}\mathsf m_K)^n\mathsf e_{\mathrm{far}}^2\mathrm{nat}_n$. The factor $\max\{1,u^3\}$ cannot be dropped: $u$ may be a power of $\log\frac1{\mathsf d}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
By Lem.~\ref{C-352-22}(a), $|\mathcal S_i(p,q)|\le\mathsf m_K\mathsf b^{-1}a_K^3\mathsf r^{-3}$ with $\mathsf r\ge r/\sqrt3$ in a cluster and $\ge\mathsf d/\sqrt3$ across. An ordering of $\beta$ is a path with $m-1$ edges, at most $c(\beta)$ of them inside a whole pair; with (P1),
\[
\varrho_{i;\beta}\le\tfrac54m!\,81^m(3^{3/2}\mathsf m_K)^{m-1}\rho^{3m}r^{-3c}\mathsf d^{-3(m-1-c)}a_{K-i}^{-3}\mathsf u_\beta,
\]
and with $a=a_{K-k_1}$ the powers of $a$ cancel: $\rho^{3m}r^{-3c}\mathsf d^{-3(m-1-c)}a^{-3}=\hat\rho^{3m}u^{-3c}P^{-3(m-1-c)}\le\mathsf w(\beta\cap I_1)\mathsf w(\beta\cap I_2)$, $a_{K-i}^{-3}=L^{-3(i-k_1)}a^{-3}$: (I2). (I3): either $\beta\cap I_\iota$ lies in one block, or it is a whole pair cut into two points, and $\hat\rho^6=q^6u^6\le q^6u^3\max\{1,u^3\}$. The top sets: $q^6u^3\hat\rho^3=P^6\rho^9r^{-3}\mathsf d^{-6}$. At the level $k_1$ the slices of the levels $\le k_1$ at distances $\ge\mathsf d/\sqrt3$ are exponentially small, $|\mathcal S_{k_1}(p,q)|\le\mathsf e_{\mathrm{far}}\mathsf m_K\mathsf b^{-1}a_K^3\mathsf r^{-3}$; a path through a crossing set has a far edge, a ring through all sources two.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The jets of narrow bumps]\label{C-352-24}
There are numbers $C(g)$ and $\mathsf d_4(g),\mathsf d^{(4)}_4(g)\in(0,\min\{e^{-2(15\mathfrak p_0+2)},r_1(\bar{\mathsf b})\}]$, formed from the constants and $g$, such that the following holds for $g$ under $(\Gamma1)$, every first-passage datum $(K,\beta)$ at $g$, every side $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$ with $64\mathsf d\le\ell$, and $s(\rho)\le K$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] For real weights placed at $(\rho,r,\mathsf d)$ with $0<\rho\le r\le\mathsf d\le\mathsf d_4(g)$: $|\mathsf J_3-3\operatorname{Tr}\prod_a(w_a\mathsf b^{-1}C^{\mathrm{free}}_K)|\le\epsilon^{\mathrm{nar}}(g,\mathsf d)\,\mathrm{nat}_3$.
\item[(b)] For real weights $w_1,w_2$ with $\Sigma(w_a)\subset\mathbb B(x_a,\rho)$, $\operatorname{dist}(\Sigma(w_1),\Sigma(w_2))\ge\mathsf d$, $|x_1-x_2|\le18\mathsf d$, $0<\rho\le\mathsf d\le\mathsf d_4(g)$: $|\mathsf J_2-\frac32\mathsf b^{-2}\sum_{p,q}w_1(p)w_2(q)C^{\mathrm{free}}_K(p,q)^2|\le\epsilon^{\mathrm{nar}}_2(g,\mathsf d)(\rho/\mathsf d)^6\mathsf u_1\mathsf u_2$.
\item[(c)] Under $(\Gamma1)$ with $c^{(4)}_\epsilon$ in place of $c_\epsilon$, for two pairs at $(\rho,r,\mathsf d)$ with $\mathsf d\le\mathsf d^{(4)}_4(g)$: $|\mathsf J_4-\frac32\sum_\varsigma\operatorname{Tr}\prod_l(w_{\varsigma(l)}\mathsf b^{-1}C^{\mathrm{free}}_K)|\le\epsilon^{\mathrm{nar}}_4(g,\mathsf d)\,\mathrm{nat}_4$.
\end{enumerate}
The normalized error factors and constants are uniform in $\rho/r$, $r/\mathsf d$, $K$, $\ell$, position and direction; in particular they hold for $w_a=f_a\circ x$ with bounded Borel $f_a$, and for plane weights.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
1. \emph{Levels and data.} $k_1=\mathsf k(\mathsf d)$, $k_\flat=\mathsf k(r)\le k_1$, $P=\hat{\mathsf d}_{k_1}$; by the working level $4MY_{\mathsf d}^{2\mathfrak p_0}\le P<CY_{\mathsf d}^{2\mathfrak p_0}$, $K-k_1\le Y_{\mathsf d}/\log L$, $\delta_{k_1}\le A_1Y_{\mathsf d}^{\mathfrak p_0}(\mathsf d/\mathsf b)^{1/2}$. Lem.~\ref{C-352-11}(b) puts the two clusters in the frame at $k_1$; the smallness holds at all heights (Lem.~\ref{C-352-10}); (I2), (I3) hold with the weights of Lem.~\ref{C-352-23}.

2. \emph{(I1).} At a single source, $c^\circ_a=G_{k_1;a}(0)$ and Lem.~\ref{C-352-16} give the tolerance $C\mathfrak b_{k_1}^2\delta_{k_1}\mathsf v_a$. At the whole pair, $c^\circ=G_{k_1;12}(0)$: by the multilinearity $G_{k_1;12}$ is the pair functional of the pair alone, and (B.2) at $n=k_1\ge\mathsf k(r)$ (its proof, given below, rests on Lems.~\ref{C-352-10}--\ref{C-352-19} alone) gives $[C_{\mathrm N}\mathfrak b_{k_1}^2\delta_{k_1}+\epsilon'_{\mathrm N}(r)]q^6u^3\mathsf u_{12}\le[\dots]\mathsf v_{12}$. At a crossing set, $c^\circ_\beta=0$: Lem.~\ref{C-352-15}(e) and Lem.~\ref{C-352-23} give $|G_{k_1;\beta}|\le Ce^{4Y_{\mathsf d}-\frac2{\sqrt3}Y_{\mathsf d}^{2\mathfrak p_0}}\mathsf v_\beta$, and $|q_{k_1;\beta}|\le C\mathfrak b_{k_1}^2\mathsf e_{\mathrm{far}}\mathsf v_\beta$. So
\[
\epsilon_\circ=C_\circ\bigl\{\mathfrak b_{k_1}^2\delta_{k_1}+\epsilon'_{\mathrm N}(r)+e^{4Y_{\mathsf d}-\frac2{\sqrt3}Y_{\mathsf d}^{2\mathfrak p_0}}+\mathfrak b_{k_1}^2\mathsf e_{\mathrm{far}}\bigr\}.
\]
Here $C_\circ$ is a number formed from the constants that dominates the constants of these four bounds (of Lem.~\ref{C-352-16}, of (B.2), of Lem.~\ref{C-352-15}(e) with Lem.~\ref{C-352-23}, and of the bound of $q_{k_1;\beta}$), and those of the two bounds of (I1) in step 6. The tolerance of (B.2) falls together with its yardstick; for this reason no relation between $r$ and $\mathsf d$ is needed, and the bounds hold at every ratio $r/\mathsf d\in(0,1]$.

3. \emph{The induction} (Prop.~\ref{C-352-21}) at $i=K$: $|\mathsf J_n-g_{K;[n]}+g_{k_1;[n]}|\le\mathsf a_nZ^n\varpi c_*^nP^{3n}\mathrm{nat}_n$.

4. \emph{The rings.} Lem.~\ref{C-352-22}(b) at $k=\mathsf k(r)$ for $p,q$ in different supports ($t\ge\hat r_{\mathsf k(r)}/\sqrt3$) gives $|\mathcal S_K-\mathsf b^{-1}C^{\mathrm{free}}_K|\le\mathrm{br}\,\mathsf b^{-1}a_K^3\mathsf r^{-3}$ with
\[
\mathrm{br}=25C_{\mathrm{tp}}c^{(2)}_L\bar B\,\mathsf d/\mathsf b+8000C^{\mathrm{bg}}_{\mathrm{tp}}\mathsf d^3+2L^3C_{\mathrm{tp}}\sup_{t\ge\frac4{\sqrt3}MY_r^{2\mathfrak p_0}}t^3e^{-\delta_{\mathrm{tp}}Lt};
\]
telescoping a product of $n$ kernels, $|g_{K;[n]}-\frac32\sum_\varsigma\operatorname{Tr}\prod_l(w_{\varsigma(l)}\mathsf b^{-1}C^{\mathrm{free}}_K)|\le C\,\mathrm{br}\,\mathrm{nat}_n$; at $n=3$ the subtrahend is $3\operatorname{Tr}\prod_a(w_a\mathsf b^{-1}C^{\mathrm{free}}_K)$, two cyclic orders with one trace. With Lem.~\ref{C-352-23} for $g_{k_1;[n]}$:
\[
\epsilon^{\mathrm{nar}}_{(n)}=\mathsf a_nZ^nc_*^nP^{3n}\varpi+C\,[\mathsf e_{\mathrm{far}}^2+\mathrm{br}].
\]

5. \emph{The threshold $\mathsf d_4(g)$.} It is fixed by six conditions: (i) $\mathsf d\le e^{-2(15\mathfrak p_0+2)}$, so that by Lem.~\ref{C-352-10}(c) $\epsilon'_{\mathrm N}(r)\le C(g)(\log\frac1{\mathsf d})^{15\mathfrak p_0+2}\mathsf d^{1/2}$ for all $r\le\mathsf d$; (ii) $\frac4{\sqrt3}M\delta_{\mathrm{tp}}L(L-1)(\log\frac1{\mathsf d})^2\ge3\log L+\log2$; (iii) $\log\frac1{\mathsf d}\ge\max\{5,\sqrt3/\delta_{\mathrm{tp}}LM\}$, so that $e^{4Y_{\mathsf d}-\frac2{\sqrt3}Y_{\mathsf d}^2}\le\mathsf d$, $\mathsf e_{\mathrm{far}}\le8\mathsf d^2$ and the last member of $\mathrm{br}$ is $\le C\mathsf d$; (iv) $8\mathsf d^2\le1$, $\overline{\mathrm{br}}\le1$; (v) $(Y_{\mathsf d}/\log L)[\bar\epsilon_\circ+\frac65(1+c_6c_\epsilon)A_1Y_{\mathsf d}^{\mathfrak p_0}g\mathsf d^{1/2}]\le1$; (vi) $\mathsf d\le r_1(\bar{\mathsf b})$, so that $\rho\le r_1(\mathsf b)$ holds of itself. In (iv) and (v) the numbers $\mathrm{br}$ and $\epsilon_\circ$, which read $r$ and the datum, stand replaced by majorants that read $g$ and $\mathsf d$ alone. As $r\le\mathsf d$, $s(r)\ge s(\mathsf d)$ and $Y_r\ge Y_{\mathsf d}$; with $\mathsf d/\mathsf b<g^2\mathsf d$,
\[
\mathrm{br}\le\overline{\mathrm{br}}=25C_{\mathrm{tp}}c^{(2)}_L\bar B\,g^2\mathsf d+8000C^{\mathrm{bg}}_{\mathrm{tp}}\mathsf d^3+2L^3C_{\mathrm{tp}}\sup_{t\ge\frac4{\sqrt3}MY_{\mathsf d}^{2\mathfrak p_0}}t^3e^{-\delta_{\mathrm{tp}}Lt}.
\]
In $\epsilon_\circ$, $\epsilon'_{\mathrm N}(r)$ is at most the bound of (i); $\mathfrak b_{k_1}\le A_1Y_{\mathsf d}^{\mathfrak p_0}$ and $\delta_{k_1}\le A_1Y_{\mathsf d}^{\mathfrak p_0}g\mathsf d^{1/2}$ (step 1, $\mathsf b>g^{-2}$); and $\mathsf e_{\mathrm{far}}\le8\mathsf d^2$ by (iii), as $P\ge4MY_{\mathsf d}^{2\mathfrak p_0}$. So
\[
\epsilon_\circ\le\bar\epsilon_\circ=C_\circ\bigl\{A_1^3Y_{\mathsf d}^{3\mathfrak p_0}g\mathsf d^{1/2}+C(g)(\log\tfrac1{\mathsf d})^{15\mathfrak p_0+2}\mathsf d^{1/2}+e^{4Y_{\mathsf d}-\frac2{\sqrt3}Y_{\mathsf d}^{2\mathfrak p_0}}+8A_1^2Y_{\mathsf d}^{2\mathfrak p_0}\mathsf d^2\bigr\}.
\]
$Y_{\mathsf d}$ is a function of $g$ and $\mathsf d$, with $\log\frac1{\mathsf d}\le Y_{\mathsf d}\le2\log\frac1{\mathsf d}+C(g)$ (Lem.~\ref{C-352-10}(c)). So (i)--(vi) are conditions on $(g,\mathsf d)$ alone, and they hold for all small $\mathsf d$, every majorised member tending to $0$ with $\mathsf d$. $\mathsf d_4(g)$ is half the supremum of the numbers $\mathsf d_*$ such that (i)--(vi) hold at every $0<\mathsf d\le\mathsf d_*$: a positive number formed from the constants and $g$, which reads no $K$, $\beta$, $\ell$, $\rho$, $r$; at every $\mathsf d\le\mathsf d_4(g)$, every $r\le\mathsf d$, every datum at $g$ and every label $\mathsf b\in(g^{-2},\bar{\mathsf b}]$ the conditions hold with $\mathrm{br}$ and $\epsilon_\circ$ themselves.

As $\varpi\le\epsilon_\circ+\frac65(1+c_6c_\epsilon)\delta_{k_1}$ at $n=3$ (Prop.~\ref{C-352-21}) and $K-k_1\le Y_{\mathsf d}/\log L$, (v) secures $(K-k_1)\varpi\le1$; at $n=2$ (step 6) the same (v) secures it, as $c_4c^{(2)}_\epsilon\le c_6c_\epsilon$ (Lem.~\ref{C-352-20}) and $C_\circ$ dominates the constants of step 6. $\mathsf d^{(4)}_4(g)$ is formed in the same way with $n=4$, that is with $c_8c^{(4)}_\epsilon$ in (v) and the tolerance $\epsilon_\circ$ of two pairs, under $(\Gamma1)$ with $c^{(4)}_\epsilon$. Then $Z^n\le CY_{\mathsf d}^{2n\mathfrak p_0}$, $P^{3n}\le CY_{\mathsf d}^{6n\mathfrak p_0}$, $\mathfrak b^2_{k_1}\delta_{k_1}\le CY_{\mathsf d}^{3\mathfrak p_0}g\mathsf d^{1/2}$, and the exponents are $8n\mathfrak p_0+15\mathfrak p_0+2$: $39\mathfrak p_0+2$ at $n=3$, $47\mathfrak p_0+2$ at $n=4$.

6. \emph{Two sources (b).} The same with the base level equal to the start level $k_1=\mathsf k(\mathsf d)$, $\mathsf v_a=c_*\hat\rho^3\mathsf u_a$, $\mathsf v_{12}=c_*^2\hat\rho^6\mathsf u_{12}$; at the pair $\mathcal S_{k_1}=0$, so $q_{k_1;12}=g_{k_1;12}=0$, and Lem.~\ref{C-352-15}(d) at $n=k_1$ gives $|G_{k_1;12}|\le Ce^{2Y_{\mathsf d}-\frac2{\sqrt3}Y_{\mathsf d}^{2\mathfrak p_0}}\mathsf v_{12}$; then $g_{K;12}=\frac32\sum w_1(p)w_2(q)\mathcal S_K(p,q)^2$ and Lem.~\ref{C-352-22}(b) at $k=k_1$; the logarithms count $4\mathfrak p_0+12\mathfrak p_0+3\mathfrak p_0=19\mathfrak p_0$.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{The connected functions on the least torus.}

\begin{lemma}[The mixture; the conditioning stopped at any level]\label{C-352-25}
Let $0<g\le\gamma$ with $g^{-2}\ge x_{\mathrm J}$, $(K,\beta)$ a first-passage datum at $g$ with $K\ge2$, $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$, and $w_1,\dots,w_p$ real weights, $p\ge1$ arbitrary. For $0\le k\le K$ let $\Omega_k=\mathcal V_k\sqcup\bigsqcup_{t=1}^k\mathcal V_{t-1}$ and $\mathbb P_k=Z_k^{-1}[\mathsf m_k\oplus\bigoplus_{t\le k}\mathsf g^{\mathrm w}_t\mathsf m_{t-1}]$, where $\mathcal V_t$ is the space of the block fields of the level $t$, $\mathsf m_t$ the measure of the never-large history up to the level $t$, and $\mathsf g^{\mathrm w}_t\ge0$ the weight of a first large field at the step $t$ in \eqref{eq:ward-first-creation}; $t'=k$ on the first part and $t'=t-1$ on the part $t$; $\alpha=a_{K-t'}$; $U_0(W)=W$, and for $t'\ge1$ let $U_{t'}(W)$ be the background configuration of $W$ in the small-field region $\mathcal V^\chi_{t'}$. Write $\Omega=\Omega_K$, $\mathbb P=\mathbb P_K$, and $\mathsf Y_\beta(\omega)=\partial_\beta[D^\lambda_{t'}(U_{t'}(W))-D^\lambda_K(\mathbf 1)]|_{\lambda=0}$ on $\Omega$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] $\mathbb P_k$ is a Borel probability measure formed with no source; its parts with $t\le k$ are parts of $\mathbb P$; the part $t$ of $\mathbb P$ has the mass $\mathsf w_t$, and $\int\alpha^{-b}d\mathbb P=\mathbb P(\mathcal V_K)+\sum_tL^{b(K-t+1)}\mathsf w_t$ for every real $b$.
\item[(b)] $\langle e^{\mathcal O(w_\lambda)}\rangle_{K,\ell,\beta}=\int\exp[D^\lambda_{t'}(U_{t'}(W))]\,\mathrm{d}\mathbb P_k$ for $\lambda$ near $0$; coefficientwise, $\langle\prod_{\iota\in\gamma}\mathcal O(w_\iota)\rangle_{K,\ell,\beta}=\int[\exp\mathbb W]_\gamma\,\mathrm{d}\mathbb P$ in $\mathbb C[\lambda_\iota]/(\lambda_\iota^2)$, with $\mathbb W$ the multilinear jet of $\lambda\mapsto D^\lambda_{t'}(U_{t'}(W))$; each $[\mathbb W]_\gamma$ is a bounded Borel function that depends on the sources of $\gamma$ alone.
\item[(c)] $S^T_n-\mathsf J_n=\sum_{\pi\in\mathrm{Part}([n])}\kappa_{\mathbb P}(\mathsf Y_{\beta'}:\beta'\in\pi)$; and with $G_\beta(\omega)=G_{t';\beta}(U_{t'}(W))$ on $\Omega_k$, $S^T_n=\sum_\pi\kappa_{\mathbb P_k}(G_{\beta'}:\beta'\in\pi)$.
\item[(d)] Where $t'\ge1$, $U_{t'}(W)$ has its pairs of all levels $\le t'$ in the cores and is regular of the level $t'$ at the radius $2B_3\varepsilon_{t'}$, with $8MB_3\varepsilon_{t'}\le c_{\mathrm A}\alpha_0$.
\item[(e)] On the least torus, under $(\Gamma2)$: $\int\alpha^{-b}d\mathbb P\le1+2L^b\mathsf C_{\mathrm{ag}}(b+1,\frac12)$ for every $b\ge0$, so $\mathsf M'=\int\alpha^{-24}d\mathbb P\le\bar{\mathsf M}^{(24)}$; and $\int\alpha^{-b}d\mathbb P_k\le a_{K-k}^{-b}+\mathsf M'$, $\int_{\{\alpha<\varrho\}}\alpha^{-b}d\mathbb P_k\le\varrho^{24-b}\mathsf M'$ for $0\le b\le24$, $\varrho\le a_{K-k}$. On a side $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$: $\int\alpha^{-b}d\mathbb P\le1+4L^bM^{-3}\ell^3e^{\mathsf B(X_g)\ell^3}\mathsf C_{\mathrm{ag}}(b+1,\eth)$, finite and growing with $\ell$, with the function $\mathsf B$ and the letter $\eth$ and $X_g=L(g^{-2}+B_\sharp)$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Equation~\eqref{eq:ward-first-creation} writes the torus expectation of a bounded gauge invariant function $F$ as $Z^{-1}$ times the integral against $\mathsf m_k$ of its quotient at the level $k$ plus the integrals against $\mathsf g^{\mathrm w}_t\mathsf m_{t-1}$ of its quotients at the levels $t-1$, $t\le k$, at every level $k\le K$. At $F=1$ this makes $\mathbb P_k$ a probability measure; at $F=e^{\mathcal O(w_\lambda)}$ the quotient at a level $t$ is, on $\mathcal V^\chi_t$, $\exp D^\lambda_t(U_t(W))$, by {\cite[Prop.~B.15]{YMM2}}, applied to the finite progression of {\cite[Prop.~B.8]{YMM2}}. Coefficients of the multilinear jets give (b); the logarithm of the moment series is the cumulant series, and constants drop out of the cumulants of orders $\ge2$, which gives (c), at every level $k$. (d) is {\cite[Lem.~B.17]{YMM2}}, in the setting verified by {\cite[Prop.~B.21]{YMM2}} at $x_K\ge x_{\mathrm J}$. (e) The mass $\mathsf w_t$ is at most the probability that the first large field arises at the step $t$; on the least torus Prop.~\ref{prop:ward-fixed-volume-rarity}, under $\log g^{-2}\ge\mathsf Y_{\mathrm{lt}}(\frac12)$, gives $\sum_tL^{b(K-t+1)}\mathsf w_t\le2L^b\mathsf C_{\mathrm{ag}}(b+1,\frac12)$ for every real $b\ge0$; on a larger torus the number of places costs $\ell^3e^{\mathsf B(X_g)\ell^3}$. The parts $t\le k$ of $\mathbb P_k$ are those of $\mathbb P$, and on the first part $\alpha=a_{K-k}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The remainder]\label{C-352-26}
Let $g$ satisfy $(\Gamma)$, $(K,\beta)$ be a first-passage datum at $g$, $\ell=\ell_g$, $n\in\{3,4\}$, and let real weights satisfy the conditions of weights placed at $(\rho,r,\mathsf d)$ (if $n=3$), or of two pairs at $(\rho,r,\mathsf d)$ (if $n=4$), but for the upper bounds on the distances of the centres, with $0<\rho\le r\le\mathsf d\le1$, $\rho\le\frac12$, $s(\rho)\le K$, $\rho\le r_1(\mathsf b)$, all supports in one ball of radius $\le\frac18\ell_g-1$. There are numbers $\Lambda_3\ge1$ and $C_{\mathrm J}$ formed from the constants such that at $\mathbb P$-almost every $\omega$, for every nonempty $\beta$,
\[
\begin{multlined}
|\mathsf Y_\beta(\omega)|\le\Lambda_3\,\alpha^{-6}\,\mathsf s(\beta)\prod_{a\in\beta}|w_a|_\infty,\qquad\mathsf s(\beta)=\rho^3\ \relax (\text{a point}),\quad\rho^6r^{-3}\ \relax (\text{a whole pair}), \\
(\rho/r)^{3c(\beta)}\rho^6\mathsf d^{-9/2}\ \relax (\beta\text{ crossing});
\end{multlined}
\]
hence $|S^T_n-\mathsf J_n|\le\mathsf k_n\Lambda_3^n\mathsf M'^n\mathsf b^n\mathsf d^{3/2}\mathrm{nat}_n$ with $\mathsf k_3=13$, $\mathsf k_4=77$, and $|\mathsf J_n|\le C_{\mathrm J}(\mathsf b/\mathsf d)^{n/2}\mathrm{nat}_n$, uniformly in $\rho\le r\le\mathsf d$ and in $K$. For two weights $w_1,w_2$ with $\Sigma(w_a)\subset\mathbb B(x_a,\rho)$ whose supports are at a distance $\ge\mathsf d$, with $0<\rho\le\mathsf d\le1$, $\rho\le\frac12$, $s(\rho)\le K$, $\rho\le r_1(\mathsf b)$ and both supports in one ball of radius $\le\frac18\ell_g-1$, at $\mathbb P$-almost every $\omega$
\[
\begin{multlined}
|\mathsf Y_a(\omega)|\le\Lambda_3\,\alpha^{-6}\rho^3|w_a|_\infty,\qquad|\mathsf Y_{12}(\omega)|\le\Lambda_3\,\alpha^{-6}\rho^6\mathsf d^{-3}|w_1|_\infty|w_2|_\infty \\
\le\Lambda_3\,\alpha^{-6}\rho^6\mathsf d^{-9/2}|w_1|_\infty|w_2|_\infty,
\end{multlined}
\]
and 
\[
|S^T_2-\mathsf J_2|\le3\Lambda_3^2\mathsf M'^2\rho^6\mathsf d^{-9/2}|w_1|_\infty|w_2|_\infty;
\]
 if besides the balls are $\ge\mathsf d$ apart, 
\[
|\mathsf J_2|\le C_{\mathrm J}(\mathsf b/\mathsf d)\rho^6\mathsf d^{-6}\mathsf b^{-2}|w_1|_\infty|w_2|_\infty.
\]

\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For $|\beta|\ge2$, $\mathsf Y_\beta=\sum_{i\le t'}(\mathsf{Sum}[E^{(i)}_\beta](U)-\mathsf{Sum}[E^{(i)}_\beta](\mathbf 1))-\sum_{t'<i\le K}\mathsf{Sum}[E^{(i)}_\beta](\mathbf 1)$, $U=U_{t'}(W)$; at a point $\mathcal O(w_a)(U)-\mathcal O(w_a)(\mathbf 1)$ comes besides, and for $t'\ge1$ it is $\le162B_3^2\varepsilon_{t'}^2\rho^3\alpha^{-4}|w_a|_\infty$ on the regular configuration of Lem.~\ref{C-352-25}(d). The first sum is bounded by Lem.~\ref{C-352-14}(b) at the regular background of Lem.~\ref{C-352-25}(d), the second at $\mathbf 1$, both with the sizes of Lem.~\ref{C-352-15}(f) at the width $\rho$, whose conditions hold: (P1), (P2) and the separation of the corners follow, as in the proof of Lem.~\ref{C-352-11}(b), from the balls that hold the supports and from the distances of the supports alone, and $\rho\ge\frac23Ma_K$, $E_\sigma(\hat\rho_1/2)\le\varkappa_0^4$ from $\rho\le r_1(\mathsf b)$, $s(\rho)\le K$ (Lem.~\ref{C-352-12}); the sums over the levels on both sides of $t'$ are geometric.

For $t'\ge1$, with $j=t'-1$, $a_{K-j}=\alpha/L$ and $x_j>1$: $\bar\nu_{j;\beta}\le\bar c_m(L/\alpha)^m\prod|w_a|_\infty$, $\Xi^r_j\le\rho^6r^{-3}L^3\alpha^{-3}$, and $\mathsf z(\beta)\min\{1,v_j\}^{3/2}\le\mathsf s(\beta)L^{3/2}\alpha^{-3/2}$; so $|\mathsf Y_\beta|\le C\alpha^{-6}\mathsf s(\beta)\prod|w_a|_\infty$ ($\alpha\le1$, $m\le4$). The part $t=1$ of $\Omega$ has $t'=0$, $\alpha=a_K$, and there $W\in\mathcal V_0$ is any configuration and $U_0(W)=W$: $D^\lambda_0=\mathcal O(w_\lambda)$, so the first sum is empty; at a point $0\le a_p\le2$ and (P1) give $|\mathcal O(w_a)(W)|\le2a_K^{-1}\sum_p|w_a(p)|\le162\rho^3a_K^{-4}|w_a|_\infty=162\rho^3\alpha^{-4}|w_a|_\infty$, and $\mathcal O(w_a)(\mathbf 1)=0$; the second sum runs over $1\le i\le K$ at $\mathbf 1$ and is led by $i=1$, with the sizes above at $j=0$: $\bar\nu_{0;\beta}\le\bar c_m\alpha^{-m}\prod|w_a|_\infty$ ($x_0>1$), $\Xi^r_0\le\rho^6r^{-3}\alpha^{-3}$, $\mathsf z(\beta)\min\{1,v_0\}^{3/2}\le\mathsf s(\beta)\alpha^{-3/2}$.

So the bound holds at every $\omega$ of this part, with $\Lambda_3\ge162$. The weights $\mathsf v_1=\mathsf v_2=\rho^3r^{-3/2}$, $\mathsf v_3=\rho^3\mathsf d^{-9/2}$ (and $\mathsf v_a=\rho^3r^{-3/2}\mathsf d^{-9/8}$ at $n=4$) have $\mathsf s(\beta)\le\mathsf v^\beta$ and $\mathsf v^{[n]}=\mathsf s([n])$, so every product over a partition is $\le\mathsf s([n])$; Lem.~\ref{C-352-25}(c), the bounds $|\kappa_2|\le2$, $|\kappa_3|\le6$ times the mean of the product of the bounds, and the moments of $\alpha^{-1}$ give $13=1+3\cdot2+6$ at $n=3$; finally $\mathsf s([3])\prod|w_a|_\infty=\mathsf b^3\mathsf d^{3/2}\mathrm{nat}_3$. The bound of $\mathsf J_n$ is Lem.~\ref{C-352-14}(b) at $\mathbf 1$ with the bounds of Lem.~\ref{C-352-15}(e) at all the levels, in the form (f).

At two sources whose supports are at a distance $\ge\mathsf d$ the two weights form one pair at the widths $(\rho,\mathsf d)$ in the sense of Lem.~\ref{C-352-15}(f): (P1), (P2) and the separation of the corners follow from the balls $\mathbb B(x_a,\rho)$ and from the distance $\ge\mathsf d$ of the supports, and $\rho\ge\frac23Ma_K$, $E_\sigma(\hat\rho_1/2)\le\varkappa_0^4$ from $\rho\le r_1(\mathsf b)$, $s(\rho)\le K$, as above. The proof of the bound above, run for the list of the two weights, gives at a point and at the whole pair, read at $r=\mathsf d$, the display at two sources, as $\rho^6\mathsf d^{-3}\le\rho^6\mathsf d^{-9/2}$ for $\mathsf d\le1$; with $S^T_2-\mathsf J_2=\int\mathsf Y_{12}d\mathbb P+\kappa_{\mathbb P}(\mathsf Y_1,\mathsf Y_2)$ (Lem.~\ref{C-352-25}(c)), $|\kappa_2|\le2$ and the moments of $\alpha^{-1}$ it gives $3=1+2$.

If besides the balls are $\ge\mathsf d$ apart, put a dummy bump $w_2'$, the indicator of the plaquettes with barycentres in $\mathbb B(x_1+3\rho e,\rho)$, $e$ the unit vector from $x_2$ to $x_1$; the three are at the lengths $(\rho,\rho,\mathsf d)$, and by multilinearity the objects of the pair are those of the list with the dummy: $S^T_2-\mathsf J_2=\int\mathsf Y_{12}d\mathbb P+\kappa_{\mathbb P}(\mathsf Y_1,\mathsf Y_2)$, with $|\mathsf Y_a|\le\Lambda_3\alpha^{-6}\rho^3|w_a|_\infty$ and $|\mathsf Y_{12}|\le\Lambda_3\alpha^{-6}\rho^6\mathsf d^{-9/2}|w_1|_\infty|w_2|_\infty$; and the bound of $\mathsf J_n$ above, at the crossing set that the two weights form in this list, is the bound of $\mathsf J_2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Lattice sums and continuum integrals]\label{C-352-27}
For every side $\ell$ and every cutoff $K$, that is on the torus $T_\ell$ with the lattice $a_K\mathbb Z^3$, and with the least lifts of the differences, the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] For $4a_K\le\rho\le r\le\mathsf d\le\mathsf d^+$, $4\mathsf d^+<\ell$, $\vartheta\in(0,1]$ and Lipschitz $f_1,f_2,f_3$ with $\operatorname{supp}f_a\subset\mathbb B(x_a,\rho)$, $\operatorname{Lip}f_a\le\|f_a\|_\infty/\vartheta\rho$, $\operatorname{dist}(\operatorname{supp}f_1,\operatorname{supp}f_2)\ge r$, $\operatorname{dist}(\operatorname{supp}f_a,\operatorname{supp}f_3)\ge\mathsf d$, all supports in one ball of radius $\frac12\mathsf d^+$:
\[
\Bigl|\operatorname{Tr}\prod_a\bigl((f_a\circ x)C^{\mathrm{free}}_K\bigr)-\int k_3\prod_af_a\Bigr|\le C^{(3)}\Bigl[\frac{a_K}{\vartheta\rho}+\Bigl(\frac{\mathsf d^+}\ell\Bigr)^3\Bigr]\rho^9r^{-3}\mathsf d^{-6}\prod_a\|f_a\|_\infty .
\]
\item[(b)] For two pairs with the same data ($8a_K\le\rho$, the balls $\ge r$ apart in a pair and $\ge\mathsf d$ apart across): $|\frac12\sum_\varsigma\operatorname{Tr}\prod_l((f_{\varsigma(l)}\circ x)C^{\mathrm{free}}_K)-\int k_4\prod f_a|\le C^{(4)}[\frac{a_K}{\vartheta\rho}+(\frac{\mathsf d^+}\ell)^3]\rho^{12}r^{-6}\mathsf d^{-6}\prod\|f_a\|_\infty$.
\item[(c)] For $8a_K\le\rho\le\mathsf d$, $64\mathsf d\le\ell$, Lipschitz $\varphi_a$ in $\mathbb B(x_a,\rho)$ with $\operatorname{Lip}\varphi_a\le\|\varphi_a\|_\infty/\vartheta\rho$, the balls $\ge\mathsf d$ apart and $|x_1-x_2|\le18\mathsf d$:
\[
\Bigl|\sum_{\lambda(p)=\lambda,\,\lambda(q)=\mu}\varphi_1(x(p))\varphi_2(x(q))C^{\mathrm{free}}_K(p,q)^2-\mathcal K_{\lambda\mu}(\varphi_1,\varphi_2)\Bigr|\le C_{\mathrm{Rs}}\Bigl[\frac{a_K}{\vartheta\rho}+\Bigl(\frac{\mathsf d}\ell\Bigr)^3\Bigr]\Bigl(\frac\rho{\mathsf d}\Bigr)^6\|\varphi_1\|_\infty\|\varphi_2\|_\infty .
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\emph{Step A.} In a ring, and in a square, every sign $\epsilon_p$ stands twice, so $C^{\mathrm{free}}_K(p_l,p_{l+1})$ may be replaced by $\epsilon\epsilon C^{\mathrm{free}}_K$ and then, by equations~\YMMref{(2245)--(2246)}{824}, by $a_K^3\mathbb K_3(u_l)_{\lambda(p_l)\lambda(p_{l+1})}$; both are $\le(1+3C_{\mathrm{lat}})a_K^3|u|^{-3}$, and telescoping costs $C_{\mathrm{lat}}a_K^3[a_K^2|u_l|^{-5}+\ell^{-3}]$ times the other factors, with at most $81(\rho/a_K)^3$ plaquettes for each source. \emph{Step B.} For each choice of the directions the remaining sum is a Riemann sum over the cubes of side $a_K$ about the barycentres, which for one orientation form a translate of $a_K\mathbb Z^3$; summed over the directions, $\sum\prod_l\mathbb K_3(\cdot)_{\lambda_l\lambda_{l+1}}=\operatorname{tr}\prod_l\mathbb K_3$. On the cubes that count the differences are at least $0.56$ times their least values, $\|\mathbb K_3(u)\|\le\frac1{2\pi}|u|^{-3}$, $\|\partial\mathbb K_3(u)\|\le\frac6{4\pi}|u|^{-4}$ (Lem.~\ref{C-352-29}(b)), and the Lipschitz bounds of the $f_a$ give the error $a_K/\vartheta\rho$ times the natural size; the numbers $C^{(3)},C^{(4)},C_{\mathrm{Rs}}$ are these counts.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Kernels of forms bounded on small bumps]\label{C-352-28}
Let $U_1,\dots,U_p$ be open subsets of $\mathbb R^3$ or of a torus, $\rho_0>0$, $\mathsf A\ge0$, and $T$ a $p$-linear form on $\prod_a\mathrm{Lip}_c(U_a)$ with $|T(f_1,\dots,f_p)|\le\mathsf A\rho^{3p}\prod_a\|f_a\|_\infty$ whenever $\rho\le\rho_0$ and each $f_a$ has its support in a ball of radius $\rho$ in $U_a$. Then: (a) $T(f)=\int k\prod_af_a$ with a Borel function $k$, $|k|\le(\frac3\pi)^p\mathsf A$ almost everywhere, and at every point where $T$ has a continuous kernel; (b) $T$ extends to bounded Borel functions with compact supports in the $U_a$, and for balls $\mathbb B(z_a,\rho)\subset U_a$, $\rho\le\rho_0$, the mean of $k$ over $\prod_a\mathbb B(z_a,\rho)$ is at most $(\frac3{4\pi})^p\mathsf A$ in modulus, at every choice of the centres; with the radial tents, $|\int k\prod_a\chi^\rho_{z_a}|\le(\frac3\pi)^p\mathsf A$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let $k_\rho(x_1,\dots,x_p)=T(\chi^\rho_{x_1},\dots,\chi^\rho_{x_p})$; $\|\chi^\rho\|_\infty=3/\pi\rho^3$ gives $|k_\rho|\le(\frac3\pi)^p\mathsf A$. On functions with supports in fixed compact sets $T$ is bounded in the sup norms (a Lipschitz partition of unity of width $\rho_0$), and the Riemann sums of $f_a*\chi^\rho$ converge uniformly, so $\int k_\rho\prod f_a=T(f_1*\chi^\rho,\dots)\to T(f)$; a weak-$*$ limit point of $k_\rho$ in $L^\infty$ is a kernel. (b) By dominated convergence $T$ extends with the same bound; at $f_a=\mathbf 1_{\mathbb B(z_a,\rho)}$, $|\int_{\prod\mathbb B(z_a,\rho)}k|\le\mathsf A\rho^{3p}$, which is the bound of the mean.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The free template]\label{C-352-29}
Let $X\ne0$, $\mathsf d=|X|$, $\mathsf b>0$, $n,n'$ unit vectors.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] $\mathbb K_3(X)^2=(16\pi^2\mathsf d^6)^{-1}(3\hat X\hat X^{\mathsf T}+1)$; $\frac32\mathsf b^{-2}\sum_\mu\{[\mathbb K_3(X)_{\lambda\mu}]^2-\frac13\sum_{\lambda'}[\mathbb K_3(X)_{\lambda'\mu}]^2\}=\mathsf t^\circ(e_\lambda,X)$; $\frac32\mathsf b^{-2}\sum_{\lambda,\mu}[\mathbb K_3(X)_{\lambda\mu}]^2=\frac9{16\pi^2}\mathsf b^{-2}\mathsf d^{-6}$; $\sum_\lambda n_\lambda^2\mathsf t^\circ(e_\lambda,X)+\sum_{\lambda<\lambda'}n_\lambda n_{\lambda'}3\mathsf b^{-2}[\mathbb K_3(X)^2]_{\lambda\lambda'}=\mathsf t^\circ(n,X)$; and $|\mathsf t^\circ(n,X)-\mathsf t^\circ(n',X)|\le0.057|n-n'|\mathsf b^{-2}\mathsf d^{-6}$.
\item[(b)] In the operator norm, $\|\mathbb K_3(y)\|=\frac2{4\pi}|y|^{-3}$, $\|(h\cdot\nabla)\mathbb K_3(y)\|\le\frac6{4\pi}|h||y|^{-4}$, $\|(h\cdot\nabla)^2\mathbb K_3(y)\|\le\frac{24}{4\pi}|h|^2|y|^{-5}$.
\item[(c)] For $0<r\le\frac12\mathsf d$ and $c-z=X$: $|\frac{2\pi}3\mathsf br^3\cdot3\mathsf b^{-3}k_3(c+\frac r2n,c-\frac r2n,z)-\mathsf t^\circ(n,X)|\le2.66\,(r/\mathsf d)^2\mathsf b^{-2}\mathsf d^{-6}$; and for $0<\rho<\frac14r$ the same function averaged against the radial tents $\chi^\rho$ about the three points differs from its value by at most $7900\,(\rho/r)\mathsf b^{-2}\mathsf d^{-6}$.
\item[(d)] For $0<\rho\le\frac18\mathsf d$: $|\mathcal K_{\lambda\mu}(\chi^\rho_c,\chi^\rho_z)-[\mathbb K_3(X)_{\lambda\mu}]^2|\le2.28\,(\rho/\mathsf d)\mathsf d^{-6}$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(a) With $E=\hat X\hat X^{\mathsf T}$, $E^2=E$: $(3E-1)^2=3E+1$; $\sum_\mu[\mathbb K_3(X)_{\lambda\mu}]^2=[\mathbb K_3(X)^2]_{\lambda\lambda}$ and $\operatorname{tr}\mathbb K_3(X)^2=6(16\pi^2\mathsf d^6)^{-1}$; the identity in $n$ is the expansion of $\langle n,\mathbb K_3(X)^2n\rangle$; the last bound is $\frac{18}{32\pi^2}\le0.057$ times $|n-n'|$. (b) $\mathbb K_3=(4\pi)^{-1}\nabla\nabla|y|^{-1}$; the third and fourth derivatives of $|y|^{-1}$ contracted with $h$, in a frame with $\hat y=e_1$, have eigenvalues bounded by $6$ and $24$ times $|h|^k|y|^{-3-k}$. (c) With $D(n)=3nn^{\mathsf T}-1$, $h=\frac r2n$ and $\phi(t)=\operatorname{tr}[D(n)\mathbb K_3(X-th)\mathbb K_3(X+th)]$: $\mathbb K_3(rn)=(4\pi r^3)^{-1}D(n)$, so the first member is $\frac12\mathsf b^{-2}\phi(1)$, while $\frac12\mathsf b^{-2}\phi(0)=\mathsf t^\circ(n,X)$ by (a). $\phi$ is even, since $\operatorname{tr}[DAB]=\operatorname{tr}[DBA]$ for symmetric matrices, so $|\phi(1)-\phi(0)|\le\frac12\sup|\phi''|$; with $|X\pm th|\ge\frac34\mathsf d$, the trace norm $4$ of $D(n)$ and (b),
\[
|\phi''|\le\frac4{(4\pi)^2}(24\cdot2+2\cdot6\cdot6+2\cdot24)\frac{r^2}4\Bigl(\frac43\Bigr)^8\mathsf d^{-8}=10.63\,(r/\mathsf d)^2\mathsf d^{-6},
\]
and $\frac14\cdot10.63\le2.66$. The tents: the mean value theorem with (b) for the three factors of $k_3$. (d) $|\nabla(\mathbb K_{3,\lambda\mu}^2)|\le\frac3{2\pi^2}|u|^{-7}$ on a segment in $\{|u|\ge\frac34\mathsf d\}$, and $\frac3{2\pi^2}(\frac43)^7\cdot2\le2.28$.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Every state.}

\begin{lemma}[The chessboard bound]\label{C-352-30}
Let $0<g\le\gamma$, $(K,\beta)$ a first-passage datum at $g$, $\ell'\in\mathfrak L(g)$, and consider the board of $\mathbb L_K$ into cubes of side $\frac12\ell'$, the cells, with any offset in $a_K\mathbb Z^3$; let $\mathsf Q_0=\exp[\frac18\ell'^3(2C_{\mathrm S}+C_g)]$ with the constants $C_{\mathrm S},C_g$ of the two-sided stability bound. For every $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$ with $\ell\ge\ell'$, every $\nu\in\mathcal G^{\mathrm{per}}_{K,\beta}$, every cell and every bounded complex Borel function $F$ of the variables of that cell,
\[
|\tilde\mu_{K,\ell,\beta}(F)|,\ |\nu(F)|\le\mathsf Q_0\|F\|_{\mathrm{ch}},\qquad\|F\|_{\mathrm{ch}}^8=\tilde\mu_{K,\ell',\beta}\Bigl(\prod_{\text{the eight cells of }T_{\ell'}}F^{[\cdot]}\Bigr)\ge0,
\]
$F^{[\cdot]}$ are the reflected copies of $F$, conjugated when an odd number of coordinate reflections is used.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The bound is a chain of four links. The cells are cubes of side $\mathsf l=\frac12\ell'$; the torus $T_\ell$ holds $\mathsf N_\ell=(2\ell/\ell')^3$ of them and $T_{\ell'}$ eight. For $F$ as in the statement let $F^{\mathrm{all}}_\ell$ be the product of the reflected copies of $F$, conjugated with the parity convention in the statement, over all the cells of $T_\ell$, and $Z_{K,\ell,\beta}[F^{\mathrm{all}}_\ell]$ the integral of the density of $T_\ell$ with this insertion. (1) \emph{Reflection positivity on $T_\ell$.} The torus measures are reflection positive in the planes of the board, and the chessboard estimate ({\cite[Cor.~B.1]{YMM2}}(b), (c)) gives $|\tilde\mu_{K,\ell,\beta}(F)|\le\|F\|_{\mathrm{ch},\ell}$, where $\|F\|_{\mathrm{ch},\ell}^{\mathsf N_\ell}=Z_{K,\ell,\beta}[F^{\mathrm{all}}_\ell]/Z_{K,\ell,\beta}\ge0$; on $T_{\ell'}$ this is the number of the statement, $\|F\|_{\mathrm{ch},\ell'}=\|F\|_{\mathrm{ch}}$. (2) \emph{Two sides, with the insertions.} As $\ell/\ell'$ is a power of $L$, the subadditivity in the volume of the integrals with the reflected copies inserted (Prop.~\YMMref{86.5}{682}, Cor.~\YMMref{86.6}{683}) gives $Z_{K,\ell,\beta}[F^{\mathrm{all}}_\ell]^{1/\mathsf N_\ell}\le Z_{K,\ell',\beta}[F^{\mathrm{all}}_{\ell'}]^{1/8}$; with $p_\ell=\ell^{-3}\log Z_{K,\ell,\beta}$, $Z_{K,\ell,\beta}^{1/\mathsf N_\ell}=e^{\mathsf l^3p_\ell}$ and $Z_{K,\ell',\beta}^{1/8}=e^{\mathsf l^3p_{\ell'}}$ this is clause~(e) of the same corollary:
\[
\|F\|_{\mathrm{ch},\ell}\le\|F\|_{\mathrm{ch},\ell'}\,e^{\mathsf l^3(p_{\ell'}-p_\ell)} .
\]
(3) \emph{Stability, with no insertion.} The two-sided stability bound among the construction results, which rests on Thms.~\YMMref{AJ}{673} and~\YMMref{AD}{607} ({\cite[Lem.~N.1]{YMM2}}), concerns the partition functions without insertions: $Z_{K,\ell,\beta}=e^{E_{K,\ell,\beta}}\widetilde Z_\ell$ with the vacuum constant $E_{K,\ell,\beta}$ and a number $e^{-C_g\ell^3}\le\widetilde Z_\ell\le e^{C_{\mathrm S}\ell^3}$, and $|E_{K,\ell,\beta}\ell^{-3}-E_{K,\ell',\beta}\ell'^{-3}|\le C_{\mathrm S}$ for two sides $\ell,\ell'\in\mathfrak L(g)$. So
\[
p_{\ell'}-p_\ell\le\bigl(E_{K,\ell',\beta}\ell'^{-3}+C_{\mathrm S}\bigr)-\bigl(E_{K,\ell,\beta}\ell^{-3}-C_g\bigr)\le2C_{\mathrm S}+C_g ,
\]
and (1)--(3), with $\mathsf l^3=\frac18\ell'^3$, give $|\tilde\mu_{K,\ell,\beta}(F)|\le\mathsf Q_0\|F\|_{\mathrm{ch}}$. (4) \emph{Periodic Gibbs states.} For $\nu\in\mathcal G^{\mathrm{per}}_{K,\beta}$ the domination theorem (Prop.~\YMMref{91.9}{705}, for every board of $\mathbb L_K$ and every offset) gives $|\nu(F)|\le\liminf_k\|F\|_{\mathrm{ch},\ell_k}$ along every sequence $\ell_k\to\infty$ in $\mathfrak L(g)$, and (2), (3) at $\ell=\ell_k$ bound the right member by $\mathsf Q_0\|F\|_{\mathrm{ch}}$. No link reads what $F$ is made of, and $\mathsf Q_0$ depends neither on $\ell\ge\ell'$ nor on $K$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The fold]\label{C-352-31}
Let $\mathfrak N_I=\mathbb C[\lambda_\iota:\iota\in I]/(\lambda_\iota^2)$, $[x]_\gamma$ the coefficient of $\lambda^\gamma$, $\mathfrak m=\{[x]_\emptyset=0\}$, and $\|x\|_u=\sum_\gamma|[x]_\gamma|/u^\gamma$ for numbers $u_\iota>0$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] $\|\cdot\|_u$ is submultiplicative; for $y\in\mathfrak m$, $\|e^y-1\|_u\le(1+\|y\|_u)^{|I|}-1$ and $\|\log(1+y)\|_u\le\|y\|_u(1+\|y\|_u)^{|I|-1}$; the logarithm of the moment series is the cumulant series.
\item[(b)] In the data of Lem.~\ref{C-352-30} let $f_1,\dots,f_n$ be bounded real functions that vanish off the interior of one cell, $w_\iota$, $\iota\in I=[n]\times\{\text{the eight cells}\}$, the eight mirror images of the $f_a\circ x$ on $T_{\ell'}$, and $(\Omega,\mathbb P)$ a probability space with a measurable $\mathbb W\colon\Omega\to\mathfrak m$ such that $\langle\prod_{\iota\in\gamma}\mathcal O(w_\iota)\rangle_{K,\ell',\beta}=\int[\exp\mathbb W]_\gamma d\mathbb P$ for all $\gamma\subset I$. Let $u_{(a,\cdot)}=u_a>0$, $\mathsf c=\sum\mathsf c^{(\cdot)}$ a sum of constants of $\mathfrak m$ each in the variables of one cell, of any size, and $\mathsf Z\ge0$ measurable with $\|\mathbb W-\mathsf c\|_u\le\mathsf Z$ almost everywhere. Put $\mathsf y=\int[(1+\mathsf Z)^n-1]d\mathbb P$, $\mathsf h=\mathsf y(1+\mathsf y)^{n-1}$, $\eta_0=[\int(1+\mathsf Z+8\mathsf h)^{8n}d\mathbb P]^{1/8}$, $\eta=(2^n-1)\mathsf Q_0\eta_0$. Then for every nonempty $\beta\subset[n]$, every $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$ with $\ell\ge\ell'$, and $\mathfrak s=\tilde\mu_{K,\ell,\beta}$ or $\mathfrak s\in\mathcal G^{\mathrm{per}}_{K,\beta}$:
\[
\bigl|S^T_{|\beta|}[\mathfrak s]((f_a)_{a\in\beta})-S^T_{|\beta|}[\tilde\mu_{K,\ell',\beta}]((f_a)_{a\in\beta})\bigr|\le\eta(1+\eta)^{n-1}u^\beta .
\]
\end{enumerate}
The bound holds at every size of $\mathsf Z$, of the constants $\mathsf c$ and of $\eta$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(a) is the algebra of $\exp$ and $\log$ in an algebra with $|I|$ nilpotent generators. (b) Let $\mathsf k=\log\sum_\beta\tilde\mu_{K,\ell',\beta}(\prod_{a\in\beta}\mathcal O(f_a))\lambda^\beta$ and $\Xi_\beta=[\exp(\sum_a\lambda_a\mathcal O(f_a)-\mathsf k)]_\beta$, a function of the variables of the cell. The mirror images of $\Xi_\beta$ are the same expressions in the mirrored sources, so by the representation $\|\Xi_\beta\|^8_{\mathrm{ch}}=\int[\exp(\mathbb W-\mathsf k^{\mathrm{all}})]_{\beta\times\{\text{cells}\}}d\mathbb P$, $\mathsf k^{\mathrm{all}}$ the sum of the eight copies of $\mathsf k$. Each copy has $e^{\mathsf k^{(\cdot)}}=\int\exp(\pi_{\text{cell}}\mathbb W)d\mathbb P$, so $\mathsf k^{(\cdot)}-\mathsf c^{(\cdot)}=\log(1+\mathsf y^{(\cdot)})$ with $\|\mathsf y^{(\cdot)}\|_u\le\mathsf y$ and $\|\mathsf k^{(\cdot)}-\mathsf c^{(\cdot)}\|_u\le\mathsf h$; the constants of any size cancel, $\|\mathbb W-\mathsf k^{\mathrm{all}}\|_u\le\mathsf Z+8\mathsf h$, and $|[\exp(\cdot)]_{\beta\times\{\text{cells}\}}|\le(1+\mathsf Z+8\mathsf h)^{8n}(u^\beta)^8$.

So $\|\Xi_\beta\|_{\mathrm{ch}}\le\eta_0u^\beta$, and Lem.~\ref{C-352-30} gives $|\mathfrak s(\Xi_\beta)|\le\mathsf Q_0\eta_0u^\beta$. With $\mathsf b'=\sum_\beta\mathfrak s(\Xi_\beta)\lambda^\beta=\mathsf M_{\mathfrak s}e^{-\mathsf k}$, $\mathsf M_{\mathfrak s}$ the moment series of $\mathfrak s$: $\|\mathsf b'-1\|_u\le\eta$ and $\|\log\mathsf M_{\mathfrak s}-\mathsf k\|_u=\|\log\mathsf b'\|_u\le\eta(1+\eta)^{n-1}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Mirror copies]\label{C-352-32}
Zero sources are omitted before forming the weighted jet norm; coefficients involving their directions vanish by multilinearity. Assume the remaining source weights are nonzero. Let $g$ satisfy $(\Gamma)$, $\ell'=\ell_g$, and let $f_1,\dots,f_n$, $n\in\{2,3,4\}$, be as in (A.4)(i) (for $n=4$, two pairs; for $n=2$, two bounded real Borel functions with $\operatorname{supp}f_a\subset\mathbb B(x_a,\rho)$, the two supports at a distance $\ge\mathsf d$, $0<\rho\le\mathsf d\le1$, $\rho\le\frac12$, $s(\rho)\le K$, $\rho\le r_1(\mathsf b)$, both supports in one ball of radius $\le\frac18\ell_g-1$), placed by the offset in the interior of one cell, so that two mirror copies are at least $\frac14\ell_g\ge6.5$ apart. Let $\mathbb W$ be the multilinear jet of $\lambda\mapsto D^\lambda_{t'}(U_{t'}(W))$ for the $8n$ sources $w_\iota$ on the space of Lem.~\ref{C-352-25}, $[\mathsf c]_\gamma=\partial^\gamma D^\lambda_K(\mathbf 1)|_0$ for $\gamma$ in one cell and $[\mathsf c]_\gamma=0$ for $\gamma$ that link two cells, and $u_a=\mathsf v_a|w_a|_\infty$ with $\mathsf v_1=\mathsf v_2=\rho^3r^{-3/2}$, $\mathsf v_3=\rho^3\mathsf d^{-9/2}$ ($n=3$), $\mathsf v_a=\rho^3r^{-3/2}\mathsf d^{-9/8}$ ($n=4$), $\mathsf v_a=\rho^3\mathsf d^{-9/4}$ ($n=2$).

Then $\|\mathbb W(\omega)-\mathsf c\|_u\le\mathsf Z_n\alpha(\omega)^{-6}$ almost everywhere, $\mathsf Z_n=8(2^n-1)\Lambda_3+2^{8n}\max_m\Lambda^{\mathrm L}_m$, where the numbers $\Lambda^{\mathrm L}_m$, formed from the constants, bound the linking jets: for $\gamma$ linking two copies, $|\sum_{i\le t}\mathsf{Sum}[E^{(i)}_\gamma](U)|\le\Lambda^{\mathrm L}_m\mathsf b^{-m/2}\prod_{\text{copies}}\mathsf s(\gamma\cap\text{copy})\prod_{\iota\in\gamma}|w_\iota|_\infty$ at every $U$ whose pairs of the levels $\le t$ lie in the cores.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Within one cell the coefficients of $\mathbb W-\mathsf c$ are the $\mathsf Y_\beta$ of the copy (by multilinearity the mixture names no source), bounded by Lem.~\ref{C-352-26} and $\mathsf s(\beta)\le\mathsf v^\beta$; there are $8(2^n-1)$ such sets. At $n=2$ the two bumps are taken as one pair at the widths $(\rho,\mathsf d)$ in the sense of Lem.~\ref{C-352-15}(f), since (P1), (P2) and the separation of the corners follow from the balls $\mathbb B(x_a,\rho)$ and from the distance $\ge\mathsf d$ of the supports, as in the proof of Lem.~\ref{C-352-26}; that proof, with the size $\rho^6\mathsf d^{-3}$ of a whole pair at the distance $\mathsf d$ in the place of $\rho^6r^{-3}$, gives at $\mathbb P$-almost every $\omega$
\[
|\mathsf Y_a|\le\Lambda_3\alpha^{-6}\rho^3|w_a|_\infty,\qquad|\mathsf Y_{12}|\le\Lambda_3\alpha^{-6}\rho^6\mathsf d^{-3}|w_1|_\infty|w_2|_\infty\le\Lambda_3\alpha^{-6}\rho^6\mathsf d^{-9/2}|w_1|_\infty|w_2|_\infty\quad(\mathsf d\le1),
\]
and $\rho^3\le\mathsf v_a$, $\rho^6\mathsf d^{-9/2}=\mathsf v_1\mathsf v_2$. For a set $\gamma$ that links two copies, the calculus of Lem.~\ref{C-352-12} at $8n$ sources, with the copies as cells and $\mathsf D^{\iota\iota'}_i\ge\hat{\mathsf D}^\times_i/\sqrt3-1$ across, where $\mathsf D^\times\ge\frac14\ell_g$ is the least distance on $T_{\ell_g}$ of the supports of two different mirror copies and $\hat{\mathsf D}^\times_i=\mathsf D^\times/a_{K-i}$, gives by the recursion (g), with $\sigma_{i;\gamma}\le E_\sigma(\hat{\mathsf D}^\times_i)$, bounds on $\bar{\mathsf h}_{j;\gamma}$ and $\bar\Psi_{j;\gamma}$ by products of the one-cell sizes; with Lem.~\ref{C-352-14}(b) and the geometric sums this is the bound of the linking jets. The products of natural sizes over a partition do not exceed that of the whole set. The numbers $\Lambda^{\mathrm L}_m$ are finite and formed from the constants, two copies being at least $\frac14\ell_g\ge6.5$ apart; no condition on $g$ beyond $(\Gamma)$ is needed.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Transfer to every state]\label{C-352-33}
Let $g$ satisfy $(\Gamma)$ and $(K,\beta)$ be a first-passage datum at $g$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] For $n\in\{3,4\}$ and the data of (A.4)(i) (for $n=4$ two pairs, all supports in one ball of radius $\le\frac18\ell_g-1$), every $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$ and every state $\mathfrak s$ at $(K,\beta)$: $|S^T_n[\mathfrak s](f)-S^T_{n;K,\ell_g,\beta}(f^{\langle\ell_g\rangle})|\le C^{\mathrm{tr}3}_n(g)\mathsf b^n\mathsf d^{3/2}\mathrm{nat}_n$, where $C^{\mathrm{tr}3}_n(g)=\eta(1+\eta)^{n-1}$, $\eta=(2^n-1)\mathsf Q_0(g)\eta_0$, $\eta_0=(1+\mathsf Z_n+8\mathsf h)^n(\bar{\mathsf M}^{(48n)})^{1/8}$, $\mathsf h=\mathsf y(1+\mathsf y)^{n-1}$, $\mathsf y=(1+\mathsf Z_n)^n\bar{\mathsf M}^{(6n)}$, $\bar{\mathsf M}^{(b)}=1+2L^b\mathsf C_{\mathrm{ag}}(b+1,\frac12)$ and $\mathsf Q_0(g)=\exp[\frac18\ell_g^3(2C_{\mathrm S}+C_g)]$.
\item[(b)] For two bumps: let $0<\rho\le\mathsf d\le1$, $\rho\le\frac12$, $s(\rho)\le K$, $\rho\le r_1(\mathsf b)$, $f_1,f_2$ bounded real Borel functions on $\mathbb R^3$ with $\operatorname{supp}f_a\subset\mathbb B(x_a,\rho)$, the two supports at a distance $\ge\mathsf d$, both in one ball of radius $\le\frac18\ell_g-1$, $t_a\colon\{1,2,3\}\to[-1,1]$, $w_a(p)=t_a(\lambda(p))f_a(x(p))$, and $\bar w_a$ the same with $f^{\langle\ell_g\rangle}_a$ on $T_{\ell_g}$. Then for every state $\mathfrak s$ at $(K,\beta)$, $|\langle\mathcal O(w_1);\mathcal O(w_2)\rangle_{\mathfrak s}-\langle\mathcal O(\bar w_1);\mathcal O(\bar w_2)\rangle_{K,\ell_g,\beta}|\le C^{\mathrm{tr}}_2(g)(\rho/\mathsf d)^6\mathsf d^{3/2}\|f_1\|_\infty\|f_2\|_\infty$, where $C^{\mathrm{tr}}_2(g)=\eta(1+\eta)$ is the number of (a) formed at $n=2$, with $\mathsf Z_2$ of Lem.~\ref{C-352-32}.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Every periodic Gibbs state is invariant under lattice translations by Prop.~\YMMref{103.4}{758}; choose the offset of the board so that the tuple lies in the interior of one cell. Lem.~\ref{C-352-31} with $\ell'=\ell_g$, the representation of Lem.~\ref{C-352-25}(b) at the $8n$ mirrored sources, $\mathsf Z=\mathsf Z_n\alpha^{-6}$ by Lem.~\ref{C-352-32}, and the moments of Lem.~\ref{C-352-25}(e): $\mathsf y\le(1+\mathsf Z_n)^n\bar{\mathsf M}^{(6n)}$ and $\eta_0\le(1+\mathsf Z_n+8\mathsf h)^n(\bar{\mathsf M}^{(48n)})^{1/8}$, so $\eta$ is formed from the constants and $g$. With the weights of Lem.~\ref{C-352-32}, $u^{[n]}=\mathsf s([n])\prod|w_a|_\infty=\mathsf b^n\mathsf d^{3/2}\mathrm{nat}_n$. For (b) the same argument runs at $n=2$, with Lem.~\ref{C-352-32} at $n=2$, whose bounds read only the balls of radius $\rho$ and the distance $\ge\mathsf d$ of the supports; a mirror map carries $a_p$ to $a_{\mathsf rp}$ with $x(\mathsf rp)=\mathsf rx(p)$ and $\lambda(\mathsf rp)=\lambda(p)$, so plane weights go to plane weights, and $u_1u_2=(\rho/\mathsf d)^6\mathsf d^{3/2}|w_1|_\infty|w_2|_\infty$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Limits and components]\label{C-352-34}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[beginpenalty=10000]
\item[(a)] Every Gibbs sequence at $g$ that converges has subsequences on which the labels converge (they lie in $(g^{-2},\bar{\mathsf b}]$); along every such subsequence the members are states at their data, the limit $\sigma$ is a law on $\mathbb R^3$ with $S^T_n[\nu_j]\to S^\sigma_n$ on separated tuples, and for every component $\sigma_\xi$ of a canonical decomposition of $\sigma$ its approximants $\rho_j$ are periodic Gibbs states at the same data with $S^T_n[\rho_j]\to S^{\sigma_\xi}_n$.
\item[(b)] For a law with continuous moment kernels through order
three, the connected kernel is
$\mathsf s_3=\mathsf s^{\mathrm m}_3-\mathsf s_2\otimes\mathsf s_1
-\dots+2\mathsf s_1\otimes\mathsf s_1\otimes\mathsf s_1$,
and $\mathsf s^T_2=\mathsf s_2-\mathsf s_1\otimes\mathsf s_1$.
These kernels are continuous. For the periodic-Gibbs limits and
components in (a), they are also real analytic and Euclidean
invariant, by Prop.~\YMMref{108.3}{771}.
\item[(c)] Let $\eta(t)=1$ $(t\le0)$, $1-3t^2+2t^3$ $(0\le t\le1)$, $0$ $(t\ge1)$, $\psi_\rho(v)=\eta(5|v|/\rho-4)$ and $f^\rho_a=\psi_\rho(\cdot-z_a)/\int\psi_\rho$. These are $C^1$ probability densities supported in $\mathbb B(z_a,\rho)$ with $\rho^9\prod_{a\le3}\|f^\rho_a\|_\infty\le0.102$; if $\mathsf s_3$ is continuous at $(z_1,z_2,z_3)$ and
$|\int(\mathsf s_3-3\mathsf b^{-3}k_3)\prod f^\rho_a|\le\mathsf A$
for all small $\rho$, then $|\mathsf s_3-3\mathsf b^{-3}k_3|(z_1,z_2,z_3)\le\mathsf A$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(a) follows from the component approximation in Thm.~\YMMref{AP}{780} and the canonical decomposition of Thm.~\YMMref{AL}{746}; a joint cumulant of order $\ge2$ does not change if constants are added to its entries, so the centring of the approximants does not enter. (b) Apply the finite moment--cumulant formula to the assumed
continuous moment kernels. For the laws in (a), their analytic
and invariance properties follow from Thm.~\YMMref{AP}{780}
and Prop.~\YMMref{108.3}{771}. For a self-centred limit,
$S^\sigma_1=0$. (c) $\psi_\rho$ is constant on $|v|\le\frac45\rho$, and $\mathsf s_3-3\mathsf b^{-3}k_3$ is continuous at the point.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[One subsequence for all pairs of bumps]\label{C-352-35}
Let $\Omega$ be an open subset of $\{(x,y):0<|x-y|<\mathsf d_\Omega\}$ in $T_\ell^2$ or in $(\mathbb R^3)^2$, and let bilinear forms $\mathsf t^{(j)}_{\lambda\mu}$, $\lambda,\mu\in\{1,2,3\}$, $j\in\mathbb N$, on bounded real Borel functions be such that for every $(x_0,y_0)\in\Omega$, with closed balls $\bar U,\bar V$ about $x_0,y_0$ of a radius $\varrho(x_0,y_0)>0$ for which $\bar U\times\bar V\subset\Omega$, there is $\mathsf B<\infty$ with $|\mathsf t^{(j)}_{\lambda\mu}(f,h)|\le\mathsf B\|f\|_\infty\|h\|_\infty$ for all large $j$ and all $f,h$ supported in $\bar U,\bar V$. Then there is a subsequence along which $\mathsf t^{(j)}_{\lambda\mu}(\varphi_1,\varphi_2)$ converges for all $\lambda,\mu$ and all real Lipschitz $\varphi_1,\varphi_2$ with compact supports, $\operatorname{supp}\varphi_1\times\operatorname{supp}\varphi_2\subset\Omega$; the limits are bilinear. If on every such product of balls the limit forms satisfy the assumption of Lem.~\ref{C-352-28}, they have Borel kernels on $\Omega$, unique almost everywhere.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
$\mathrm{Lip}_c(U)$ is a subset of the separable space $C_0(U)$, so it has a countable dense subset in the sup norm. Take a countable dense set of centres in $\Omega$ and a diagonal subsequence along which the countably many bounded sequences $\mathsf t^{(j)}_{\lambda\mu}(f,h)$, $f,h$ in these dense sets, converge; by the uniform bound and bilinearity the sequences converge at all Lipschitz $f,h$ in the balls. A pair $\varphi_1,\varphi_2$ as in the claim is decomposed by a Lipschitz partition of unity into cubes of a side small against the distances of $\operatorname{supp}\varphi_1\times\operatorname{supp}\varphi_2$ to the diagonal and to the boundary of $\Omega$: finitely many pairs, each in one product of balls. Two kernels that represent one form on an open product agree almost everywhere (mollification), and a numbering of the countable cover glues the local kernels into one Borel function.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{The bond forms.}

\begin{lemma}[Dilation to two couplings below the ceiling]\label{C-352-36}
Let $0<g\le\gamma$, let $z=z(g)\ge1$ be the least integer with $L^{z-1}(g^{-2}+\bar B)-\bar B\ge x_{\mathrm N}=\gamma_{\mathrm N}^{-2}$ (Def.~\ref{C-352-2}(1)), and define $g'_1,g'_2$ by $g_1'^{-2}=L^z(g^{-2}+\bar B)-\bar B$, $g_2'^{-2}=L^{-1}(g_1'^{-2}+2B_\sharp)-B_\sharp$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] $0<g'_1<g'_2\le\gamma_{\mathrm N}$, and both depend on $g$ and the constants alone.
\item[(b)] For a first-passage datum $(K,\beta)$ at $g$ with $K\ge z+1$ there is $\iota\in\{1,2\}$ such that $(K-z,\beta)$ is a first-passage datum at $g'_\iota$; its run is $(x_0,\dots,x_{K-z})$, and its label is $L^z\mathsf b$.
\item[(c)] $L^z\ell\in\mathfrak L(g'_\iota)$ for $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$; if $s(t)\ge z$, then $s'_\iota(L^zt)\le s(t)-z$ for the witness depth $s'_\iota$ at $g'_\iota$, and if $s(t)<z$, then $L^zt>1$.
\item[(d)] $U\mapsto U^{(z)}$, $U^{(z)}(L^zb)=U(b)$, carries $\mu_{K,\ell,\beta}$ to $\mu_{K-z,L^z\ell,\beta}$, with $a_{L^zp}(U^{(z)})=a_p(U)$ and $q_{L^zb}(U^{(z)})=q_b(U)$. So $\mathcal O^T(\mathfrak s)(U)=L^z\mathcal O'^T(\mathfrak s^{(z)})(U^{(z)})$ and $\langle\mathcal O^T(\mathfrak s_1);\mathcal O^T(\mathfrak s_2)\rangle_{K,\ell,\beta}=L^{2z}\langle\mathcal O'^T(\mathfrak s^{(z)}_1);\mathcal O'^T(\mathfrak s^{(z)}_2)\rangle_{K-z,L^z\ell,\beta}$, primes marking the objects of the torus $T_{L^z\ell}$ at the cutoff $K-z$ and $\mathfrak s^{(z)}(L^z\cdot)=\mathfrak s(\cdot)$; and the numbers $\|\varphi\|_\infty$, $r\operatorname{Lip}\varphi$, $a_K/r$, $\mathsf d'/\ell$, $r/\mathsf d'$ and the integrals $\iint\varphi_1\varphi_2\mathbb K_3(x-y)_{\lambda\gamma}\mathbb K_3(x-y)_{\lambda'\gamma'}$ are the same for $(\varphi_a;r,\mathsf d',\ell,K)$ and for $(\varphi^{(z)}_a;L^zr,L^z\mathsf d',L^z\ell,K-z)$.

Hence each display of (D.1) at $(K,\ell,\beta)$ is the same display at $(K-z,L^z\ell,\beta)$, with the same tolerance, both members being multiplied by $L^{-2z}$. The identity $\mathcal O^T(\mathfrak s)(U)=L^z\mathcal O'^T(\mathfrak s^{(z)})(U^{(z)})$ holds at every configuration $U$ of $\mathbb L_K$ as well, the primes now marking the fields of $\mathbb L_{K-z}$; in particular $\mathcal O(f)(U)=L^z\mathcal O'(f^{(z)})(U^{(z)})$ with $f^{(z)}=f(L^{-z}\cdot)$. So for every law $\nu$ on the configurations of $\mathbb L_K$ and its image $\nu^{(z)}$ under the dilation, $S^T_n[\nu](f_1,\dots,f_n)=L^{nz}S^T_n[\nu^{(z)}](f^{(z)}_1,\dots,f^{(z)}_n)$ for bounded real functions $f_a$ with compact supports, and the joint cumulants of the fields $\mathcal O^T(\mathfrak s_a)$ of mixed sources scale in the same way; and $\nu\mapsto\nu^{(z)}$ is a bijection of $\mathcal G^{\mathrm{per}}_{K,\beta}$ onto $\mathcal G^{\mathrm{per}}_{K-z,\beta}$.

These statements of (d) hold with every integer $0\le z'<K$ in the place of $z$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(a), (b) are arithmetic of the inverse couplings. Put $G=g^{-2}+\bar B$ and $X_{g'}=L(g'^{-2}+B_\sharp)$ for a coupling $g'$. One step of the run is $x_{j-1}=L(x_j+b_j)$ with $|b_j|\le B_\sharp$ (the flow bound in {\cite[\S{}G.2]{YMM2}}); as $\bar B=B_\sharp L/(L-1)$ sums the geometric series, $z$ steps give $L^z(x_K-\bar B)+\bar B\le x_{K-z}\le L^z(x_K+\bar B)-\bar B$, and with $g^{-2}<x_K\le X_g$ and $X_g+\bar B=LG$:
\[
L^z(g^{-2}-\bar B)+\bar B<x_{K-z}\le L^{z+1}G-\bar B .
\]
(a) $g_2'^{-2}=L^{z-1}G-\bar B+2B_\sharp/L\ge L^{z-1}G-\bar B\ge x_{\mathrm N}$ by the choice of $z$, and $g_1'^{-2}-g_2'^{-2}=(L-1)L^{z-1}G-2B_\sharp/L>0$; both read $g$ and the constants alone. (b) $X_{g'_1}=L^{z+1}G-\bar B$ is the upper end above, and $X_{g'_2}=g_1'^{-2}+2B_\sharp$; so the half-open intervals $I_\iota=(g_\iota'^{-2}+2B_\sharp,X_{g'_\iota}]$, $\iota=1,2$, abut, are disjoint, and $I_2\cup I_1=(g_2'^{-2}+2B_\sharp,X_{g'_1}]$. For the lower end, $g_2'^{-2}+2B_\sharp\le L^{z-1}G+2\bar B$ and
\[
\bigl[L^z(g^{-2}-\bar B)+\bar B\bigr]-\bigl[L^{z-1}G+2\bar B\bigr]=L^{z-1}\bigl[(L-1)g^{-2}-(L+1)\bar B\bigr]-\bar B\ge(L^{z-1}-1)\bar B\ge0,
\]
since $\bar B\le\frac{13}{24}g^{-2}$ at $g\le\gamma$ ({\cite[Lem.~G.3]{YMM2}} gives this bound) gives $(L-1)g^{-2}\ge\frac{24}{13}(L-1)\bar B\ge(L+2)\bar B$, as $11L\ge50$. So $x_{K-z}$ lies in exactly one $I_\iota$. There $x_{K-z}\le X_{g'_\iota}$ and $x_{K-z-1}=L(x_{K-z}+b_{K-z})\ge L(x_{K-z}-B_\sharp)>L(g_\iota'^{-2}+B_\sharp)=X_{g'_\iota}$, and the run decreases: $K-z$ is the first index at which the run that starts at $\beta$ is at most $X_{g'_\iota}$, which is the first passage at the coupling $g'_\iota\le\gamma_{\mathrm N}\le\gamma$. The run of $(K-z,\beta)$ is the same sequence cut at $K-z$, and its label is $a_{K-z}\beta=L^z\mathsf b$.

The margin $2B_\sharp$ in the lower ends of the $I_\iota$ is what gives $x_{K-z-1}>X_{g'_\iota}$, the second half of the first passage. (c) Put $G=g^{-2}+\bar B$. Then $g_1'^{-2}+\bar B=L^zG$ and $g_2'^{-2}+\bar B\le L^zG$. The radius-scaling inequality~\YMMref{(1534)}{616}, applied to $X=LG$ and $X'=L(g_\iota'^{-2}+\bar B)$, gives $R(X')\le L^zR(X)$. The admissibility formula~\YMMref{(1528)}{615} therefore holds with $m+z$ at $g'_\iota$ whenever it holds with $m$ at $g$; its fixed $C_{\mathrm s}$ threshold is also preserved. Moreover $C_W^{g'_\iota}(s-z)\le C_W^g(s)$ for $s\ge z$, directly from the displayed definition of $C_W$. Thus a witness at depth $s(t)$ transfers to depth $s(t)-z$. If $s(t)<z$, then $L^{s(t)}t\ge C_W^g(s(t))\ge1$, whence $L^zt>1$. (d) is the dilation; $\mathsf b'=L^z\mathsf b$, so $\mathsf b^{-2}=L^{2z}\mathsf b'^{-2}$, and $\mathbb K_3(L^zu)=L^{-3z}\mathbb K_3(u)$ makes the integrals invariant. The identity of the fields reads of the configuration only $a_{L^zp}(U^{(z)})=a_p(U)$ and $q_{L^zb}(U^{(z)})=q_b(U)$, and of the lattice only $x(L^zp)=L^zx(p)$, $x_{L^zb}=L^zx_b$ and $a_{K-z}=L^za_K$; so it holds at every configuration of $\mathbb L_K$, and the joint cumulants under a law are multilinear in the fields.

The dilation maps the bonds, the plaquettes and the finite sets of bonds of $\mathbb L_K$ onto those of $\mathbb L_{K-z}$. The Gibbs kernel of a finite set of bonds has the exponent $-\beta\sum_pa_p$ over the plaquettes that contain a bond of the set, which reads $\beta$ and the incidences of the bonds and the plaquettes alone; so the image of a Gibbs state at $(a_K,\beta)$ satisfies the equations of the kernels at $(a_{K-z},\beta)$, and invariance under a subgroup of finite index of $a_K\mathbb Z^3$ becomes invariance under its image under $x\mapsto L^zx$, a subgroup of finite index of $a_{K-z}\mathbb Z^3$. The inverse dilation carries the periodic Gibbs states at $(K-z,\beta)$ back in the same way, so $\nu\mapsto\nu^{(z)}$ is a bijection of $\mathcal G^{\mathrm{per}}_{K,\beta}$ onto $\mathcal G^{\mathrm{per}}_{K-z,\beta}$ (equation~\YMMref{(1819)}{698} and the definition of periodic states following it).

The same arguments hold at every integer $0\le z'<K$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Bond sources]\label{C-352-36b}
Let $0<g\le\gamma_{\mathrm N}$, $(K,\beta)$ a first-passage datum at $g$ with $K\ge2$, $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$, and let $\mathfrak s=(w,\mathsf w)$ be a real mixed source whose barycentres $x(p)$, $w(p)\ne0$, and midpoints $x_b$, $\mathsf w(b)\ne0$, lie in a ball of a radius $\rho\ge a_K$. Put $\mathsf m_j=12M^3\alpha_0^2L^{K-j}|\mathfrak s|_\infty$ and $\mathsf u=\mathsf b^{-1}|\mathfrak s|_\infty$, let $\varsigma_j$ be as in Lem.~\ref{C-352-12}(e) at the width $\rho$, and let
\[
\mathsf W_{\mathfrak s}(p,q)=w(p)\delta_{pq}-\sum_b\mathsf w(b)\bigl[u_{b,\lambda_b}(p)u_{b,\lambda'_b}(q)+u_{b,\lambda'_b}(p)u_{b,\lambda_b}(q)\bigr],
\]
a symmetric matrix that joins two plaquettes only through a bond of the support, with the coefficients $u_{b,\lambda}(p)$ of the paragraph on the fields. There are numbers $C$ formed from the constants such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)] the weight member of the source $L^{K-j}\mathfrak s$ at the level $j$ is linear in $\mathfrak s$, vanishes on the domains that hold no corner of a plaquette $p$ with $w(p)\ne0$ and no site of a bond $b$ with $\mathsf w(b)\ne0$, and its norm in $\|\cdot\|_{j,\kappa}$ is at most $C\varsigma_j\mathsf m_j$;
\item[(2)] at the first level, $\|E^{(1)}_{\mathfrak s}\|_{1,\lambda_{\mathrm{out}}}\le C\theta^{[0]}\mathsf m_0$;
\item[(3)] for $1\le n\le K$, $A\in\mathsf{Cc}_n(r_n)$, $\tilde U=e^{i\eta_nA}$ and $F=\mathsf{ang}^{[n]}(A)$: 
\[
\bigl|\mathcal O^T(\mathfrak s)(\tilde U)-\frac1{2a_K}\sum_{p,q}\mathsf W_{\mathfrak s}(p,q)\langle F_p,F_q\rangle\bigr|\le C\mathfrak b_n^2\delta_n\hat\rho_n^3\mathsf u,
\]
and $\eta_n^4\sum_{p,q}|\mathsf W_{\mathfrak s}(p,q)|/(a_Kx_n)\le C\hat\rho_n^3\mathsf u$;
\item[(4)] Lem.~\ref{C-352-20}(c) and Prop.~\ref{C-352-21} hold with the matrices $\mathsf W_{\mathfrak s_a}$ in the place of the diagonal matrices $w_a$ in $R_{i;\beta}$, $q_{i;\beta}$ and $g_{i;\beta}$, for two mixed sources in the frame of (6), the tower identity of (6) standing in Step~1 of the proof of Prop.~\ref{C-352-21};
\item[(5)] the weighted progression and the representation of the torus expectations through the never-large histories, which name no source, are formed for mixed sources at $g\le\gamma_{\mathrm N}$ on every side $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$, with the weight member of (1) in the source slot of the bare arrays; the lemma on the tower identity at several sources (it precedes Prop.~\ref{C-352-21}), for clusters in the frame of (6), the representation of Lem.~\ref{C-352-25} and the almost everywhere bound of Lem.~\ref{C-352-26} on the remainders hold for mixed sources, the moments of $\alpha^{-1}$ being those of Lem.~\ref{C-352-25}(e) on that side;
\item[(6)] \emph{the frame and the tower identity.} The hull of a mixed source $\mathfrak s=(w,\mathsf w)$ is the set of the plaquettes $p$ with $w(p)\ne0$ and of the four plaquettes through each bond $b$ with $\mathsf w(b)\ne0$. For $2\le k<K$, two mixed sources, neither $0$, are in the frame at $k$, that is they satisfy the four conditions \textup{(Jt.1)}--\textup{(Jt.3)} and \textup{(Jt.6)} of the frame at $k$ of Lem.~\ref{C-352-11}(a), read with the hulls in the place of the supports and with the members of (1) in the slot, if each hull has its barycentres in a closed ball of a radius $\bar{\mathsf d}\ge a_K$ with $\bar{\mathsf d}/a_{K-k}\ge M$ and the corners of the plaquettes of the two hulls are at least $3M$ level-$k$ spacings apart in the sup distance; this holds at $k=\mathsf k(\mathsf d)$ for hulls in balls of radius $\le\mathsf d$ at a distance $\ge\mathsf d$, $0<\mathsf d\le e^{-2\sqrt3}$, $s(\mathsf d)\le K$, as in Lem.~\ref{C-352-11}(b). In the frame, for $k\le i<K$, $A'\in\mathsf{Cc}_{i+1}(r_{i+1})$, $\tilde U=e^{i\eta_{i+1}A'}$ and $\lambda$ near $0$,
\[
\exp D^\lambda_{i+1}(\tilde U)=\int\exp D^\lambda_i\bigl(e^{i\eta_iA^{\mathrm{lw}}(B)}\bigr)\,\mathrm{d}\nu_{i,A'}(B),
\]
with the measure $\nu_{i,A'}$ of the step and the lowering map; and the one-source Lem.~\ref{C-352-16} holds for each source $\mathfrak s$ of such a pair, with $\frac1{2a_K}\sum_{p,q}\mathsf W_{\mathfrak s}(p,q)\langle F_p,F_q\rangle$ in the place of $q_{n;a}(F)$, its frame read with the hulls and its count (P1) replaced by the second bound of (3).
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(1) $\mathcal O^T(\mathfrak s)=a_K^{-1}\sum_pw(p)a_p-a_K^{-1}\sum_b\mathsf w(b)q_b$, and $q_b$ is a gauge invariant function of the variables of the four plaquettes through $b$; so the source is a local term of the bare level, linear in $\mathfrak s$, which lives at the sites of its support. On the cores the plaquette variables are within $C\alpha_0\eta_j^2$ of $\mathbf 1$, so that $|q_b|\le|u_{b,\lambda_b}||u_{b,\lambda'_b}|\le C\alpha_0^2\eta_j^4$ there, as $|a_p|<\frac12\alpha_0^2\eta_j^4$; at most $81(\rho/a_K)^3$ bonds have their midpoints in a ball of the radius $\rho\ge a_K$; with $|\mathfrak s|_\infty=|w|_\infty+8|\mathsf w|_\infty$ the count of Lem.~\ref{C-352-12}(e) gives the bound. (2) The one-step theorem at the height $0$, with this member in the fourth place, and Schwarz's lemma, as in Lem.~\ref{C-352-12}(e). (3) On the chain class the angle of a plaquette variable of $\tilde U$ is $\pm F_p$ up to $C\eta_n^2r_n^2$, and $\mathrm w(e^{i\theta})=\theta+O(|\theta|^3)$; so $u_{b,\lambda}=\sum_pu_{b,\lambda}(p)F_p$ up to $C\eta_n^2r_n^2$, and, as $|F_p|\le2\eta_n^2r_n$, $|q_b-\langle\sum_pu_{b,\lambda_b}(p)F_p,\sum_qu_{b,\lambda'_b}(q)F_q\rangle|\le C\eta_n^4r_n^3$, the bound that the expansion of $a_p$ on the chain class has.

Summed against $\mathsf w$, this gives the bond part of $\frac1{2a_K}\langle F,\mathsf W_{\mathfrak s}F\rangle$ with the error $Ca_K^{-1}(\rho/a_K)^3|\mathsf w|_\infty\eta_n^4r_n^3$; with the plaquette part as in the proof of Lem.~\ref{C-352-16}, $a_{K-n}x_n\ge\frac45\mathsf b$ and $x_nr_n^2\le C\mathfrak b_n^2$, this is the first bound. Each $u_{b,\lambda}$ has two coefficients of modulus $\frac12$, so $\sum_{p,q}|\mathsf W_{\mathfrak s}(p,q)|\le\sum_p|w(p)|+2\sum_b|\mathsf w(b)|\le81(\rho/a_K)^3|\mathfrak s|_\infty$, and $\eta_n^4a_K^{-4}=a_{K-n}^{-4}$ gives the second. (4) In the proof of Lem.~\ref{C-352-20}(c) the sources enter only through $R^\lambda_i=\mathsf W_\lambda(1-\mathcal S_i\mathsf W_\lambda)^{-1}$, $\mathsf W_\lambda=\sum_a\lambda_a\mathsf W_{\mathfrak s_a}$, which is symmetric as $\mathsf W_\lambda$ and $\mathcal S_i$ are, and through the Gaussian integral of a quadratic form with a symmetric matrix; the identity $1-\mathsf sR^\lambda_i=(1-\mathcal S_{i+1}\mathsf W_\lambda)(1-\mathcal S_i\mathsf W_\lambda)^{-1}$ does not use that $\mathsf W_\lambda$ is diagonal.

The proof of Prop.~\ref{C-352-21} uses the sources only through the tower identity of its Step~1, which (6) gives for two mixed sources in the frame, through (I1)--(I3), through the sums $\sum_{p,q}|R_{i;\beta}(p,q)|$, which the second bound of (3) controls as (P1) does for plaquette weights, and through the lowered angles at the plaquettes of the hulls. (5) Props.~{\cite[Prop.~B.8]{YMM2}} and~{\cite[Prop.~B.15]{YMM2}}, together with \eqref{eq:ward-first-creation}, give the weighted progression and the history representation for sources on the bare plaquettes, on every side of $\mathfrak L(g)$ with $g^{-2}\ge x_{\mathrm J}$ (Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8}). For mixed sources the same construction is made with the weight member of (1) in the source slot of the bare arrays; the other data of the progression name no source.

The proofs among the construction results read a source only through that member, and of the member they read these properties: the entry of the objects into the settings of one step, for any number of sources, $K\ge2$ and every side, reads that it is a local term of the bare level with the bound of (1); the never-large histories and the measures of the mixture are formed with no source; the representation reads that $\mathcal O^T(\mathfrak s)$ is a bounded gauge invariant function, linear in $\mathfrak s$ and $0$ at $\mathbf 1$, whose member is that of (1), so that the quotient at a level $t$ of $e^{\mathcal O^T(\mathfrak s_\lambda)}$ is $\exp D^\lambda_t$; and the tower identity reads the member in the slot of the step map, which takes any member there with the bound of (1).

By (1) a mixed source has these properties. The proofs of the lemma on the tower identity at several sources, which precedes Prop.~\ref{C-352-21}, and of Lem.~\ref{C-352-25} use the sources only through the progression and the tower identity for a pair, which (6) gives for mixed sources; the almost everywhere bound of Lem.~\ref{C-352-26} uses them only through (1), (2), the support rule of Lem.~\ref{C-352-12}(d) and the sizes of Lem.~\ref{C-352-15}(f), which hold for mixed sources by (1)--(3) with the hulls in the place of the supports; on a side $\ell$ the moments of $\alpha^{-1}$ are bounded by Lem.~\ref{C-352-25}(e). (6) The frame at $k$ is formed by the four conditions \textup{(Jt.1)}--\textup{(Jt.3)} and \textup{(Jt.6)} of the setting of the pair functional among the construction results, read with the hulls in the place of the supports: the proof of Lem.~\ref{C-352-11}(a), using Def.~\ref{def:pair-functional-frame}, reads of the two sources only the four geometric properties listed there, now of the hulls, which hold all the plaquettes that the members of the sources read, and the members in the slot.

The tower identity for a pair is that among the construction results, read with the member of (1) in the slot: its proof forms the measure $\nu_{i,A'}$ and the lowering map with no source and reads the sources only through the relative exponents. Hulls at a distance $\ge\mathsf d$ have corners at least $(\mathsf d-\sqrt2a_K)/\sqrt3$ apart in the sup distance, which is at least $3M$ level-$\mathsf k(\mathsf d)$ spacings by the working level, as in the proof of Lem.~\ref{C-352-11}(b); a ball of radius $\mathsf d$ has $\mathsf d/a_{K-\mathsf k(\mathsf d)}\ge4M$. In Lem.~\ref{C-352-16} the member of $\mathfrak s$ is expanded on the chain class by the first bound of (3), and the families by the count of its proof with the second bound of (3).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Lattice sums at two balls on every torus]\label{C-352-36a}
On every torus $T_\ell$ with the lattice $a_K\mathbb Z^3$, with the least lifts of the differences, let $4a_K\le r$, $16r\le\mathsf d'$, $8\mathsf d'\le\ell$, $x_1,x_2\in T_\ell$ with $|x_1-x_2|=\mathsf d'$, $\vartheta\in(0,1]$, and let $\varphi_1,\varphi_2$ be real Lipschitz functions with $\operatorname{supp}\varphi_a\subset\mathbb B(x_a,r)$ and $\operatorname{Lip}\varphi_a\le\|\varphi_a\|_\infty/\vartheta r$. Put $\mathsf e_{\mathrm{PS}}=[a_K/\vartheta r+(\mathsf d'/\ell)^3](r/\mathsf d')^6\|\varphi_1\|_\infty\|\varphi_2\|_\infty$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] For all $\lambda,\mu$: $\bigl|\sum_{\lambda(p)=\lambda,\,\lambda(q)=\mu}\varphi_1(x(p))\varphi_2(x(q))\,C^{\mathrm{free}}_K(p,q)^2-\mathcal K_{\lambda\mu}(\varphi_1,\varphi_2)\bigr|\le C_{\mathrm{PS}}\,\mathsf e_{\mathrm{PS}}$.
\item[(b)] Let $\{\lambda,\lambda',\mu\}=\{1,2,3\}$, $\gamma$ a direction, $\mathsf w(b)=\varphi_1(x_b)\mathbf 1_{\{\mu_b=\mu\}}$, $w_2(q)=\varphi_2(x(q))\mathbf 1_{\{\lambda(q)=\gamma\}}$, and $C_\alpha(b,q)=\sum_pu_{b,\alpha}(p)C^{\mathrm{free}}_K(p,q)$ for a direction $\alpha\ne\mu$. Then
\[
\Bigl|-\sum_{b,q}\mathsf w(b)w_2(q)\,C_\lambda(b,q)C_{\lambda'}(b,q)-\iint\varphi_1(x)\varphi_2(y)\,\mathbb K_3(x-y)_{\lambda\gamma}\mathbb K_3(x-y)_{\lambda'\gamma}\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y\Bigr|\le C^{\mathrm{od}}_{\mathrm{PS}}\,\mathsf e_{\mathrm{PS}} .
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Points of the two balls are at least $\mathsf d'-2r\ge\frac78\mathsf d'$ and at most $\mathsf d'+2r\le\frac98\mathsf d'<\frac14\ell$ apart, so all the least lifts are taken in one ball of radius $\frac14\ell$. (a) Steps A and B of the proof of Lem.~\ref{C-352-27} at these distances. In a square every sign $\epsilon_p$ stands twice, so equations~\YMMref{(2245)--(2246)}{824} replace $C^{\mathrm{free}}_K(p,q)^2$ by $a_K^6[\mathbb K_3(u)_{\lambda\mu}]^2$ at the cost $C_{\mathrm{lat}}(2+3C_{\mathrm{lat}})a_K^6|u|^{-3}[a_K^2|u|^{-5}+\ell^{-3}]$ for each pair, and a ball of radius $r\ge a_K$ holds at most $27(r/a_K)^3$ barycentres of one orientation; with $|u|\ge\frac78\mathsf d'$ and $a_Kr\le\frac14r^2\le\frac1{1024}\mathsf d'^2$ this costs at most $729(\frac87)^3C_{\mathrm{lat}}(2+3C_{\mathrm{lat}})\,\mathsf e_{\mathrm{PS}}\le1089\,C_{\mathrm{lat}}(2+3C_{\mathrm{lat}})\,\mathsf e_{\mathrm{PS}}$.

The Riemann sums over the cubes of side $a_K$ about the barycentres, which for one orientation form a translate of $a_K\mathbb Z^3$, with $\|\mathbb K_3(u)\|\le\frac1{2\pi}|u|^{-3}$, $\|\partial\mathbb K_3(u)\|\le\frac6{4\pi}|u|^{-4}$ (Lem.~\ref{C-352-29}(b)) and the Lipschitz bounds of the $\varphi_a$, give the rest of $C_{\mathrm{PS}}\mathsf e_{\mathrm{PS}}$. (b) $u_{b,\alpha}(p)\ne0$ only at the two plaquettes $p_\pm$ with the barycentres $x_b\pm\frac12a_Ke_\alpha$, which lie in the plane of $\mu$ and $\alpha$, and there $u_{b,\alpha}(p_\pm)=\frac12\epsilon_{\alpha\mu\alpha'}\epsilon_{p_\pm}$, $\{\alpha,\mu,\alpha'\}=\{1,2,3\}$. By equation~\YMMref{(2245)}{824}, $C_\lambda(b,q)$ is $\epsilon_{\lambda\mu\lambda'}\epsilon_qa_K^3$ times the mean of $\mathbb K_3(\cdot)_{\lambda'\gamma}$ at the two differences $x(p_\pm)-x(q)$, and $C_{\lambda'}(b,q)$ is $\epsilon_{\lambda'\mu\lambda}\epsilon_qa_K^3$ times the like mean of $\mathbb K_3(\cdot)_{\lambda\gamma}$, up to the terms of the comparison.

As $\epsilon_{\lambda\mu\lambda'}\epsilon_{\lambda'\mu\lambda}=-1$ and $\epsilon_q^2=1$, $-C_\lambda(b,q)C_{\lambda'}(b,q)$ is $a_K^6\,\mathbb K_3(x_b-x(q))_{\lambda\gamma}\mathbb K_3(x_b-x(q))_{\lambda'\gamma}$ up to these terms and to the shifts by $\pm\frac12a_Ke_\lambda$, $\pm\frac12a_Ke_{\lambda'}$, which cost $a_K\|\partial\mathbb K_3\|$. The midpoints of the bonds of one direction form a translate of $a_K\mathbb Z^3$, as the barycentres of the plaquettes of one orientation do, and steps A and B as in (a) give $C^{\mathrm{od}}_{\mathrm{PS}}\mathsf e_{\mathrm{PS}}$. The numbers $C_{\mathrm{PS}}$ and $C^{\mathrm{od}}_{\mathrm{PS}}$ of Def.~\ref{C-352-2}(3) are these counts.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Two mixed sources on every side]\label{C-352-37}
For $0<g\le\gamma_{\mathrm N}$ let $t_{\mathrm N}(g)\in(0,\frac12e^{-2\sqrt3}]$ be the threshold, formed from the constants and $g$, below which the conditions of the induction at two sources with the base level equal to the start level hold at $g$ and at every label in $(g^{-2},\bar{\mathsf b}]$ (the conditions of step~5 of the proof of Prop.~\ref{C-352-24} that its step~6 reads, with the members that $g\le\gamma_{\mathrm N}$ gives), and put $r_g=\frac12\min\{r_1(\bar{\mathsf b}),t_{\mathrm N}(g)\}$. For $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$ there is a finite function $\epsilon^{\mathrm{ev}}_\sharp(g,\ell,\cdot)$ on $(0,\frac18\ell]$, formed from the constants, $g$ and $\ell$ (it is written out at the end of the proof), with $\epsilon^{\mathrm{ev}}_\sharp(g,\ell,\mathsf d')\le C(g,\ell)(\log\frac1{\mathsf d'})^{19\mathfrak p_0}\mathsf d'^{1/2}$ for $\mathsf d'\le\frac76t_{\mathrm N}(g)$, such that the following holds. Let $(K,\beta)$ be a first-passage datum at $g$, $\mathsf b=a_K\beta$, $x_1,x_2\in T_\ell$ with $|x_1-x_2|=\mathsf d'$, $0<16r\le\mathsf d'\le\frac18\ell$, $s(\min\{r,r_g\})\le K$. For real mixed sources $\mathfrak s_a=(w_a,\mathsf w_a)$ with $\{x(p):w_a(p)\ne0\}\cup\{x_b:\mathsf w_a(b)\ne0\}\subset\mathbb B(x_a,r)$,
\[
\Bigl|\langle\mathcal O^T(\mathfrak s_1);\mathcal O^T(\mathfrak s_2)\rangle_{K,\ell,\beta}-\tfrac32\mathsf b^{-2}\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(\mathsf W_{\mathfrak s_1}C^{\mathrm{free}}_K\mathsf W_{\mathfrak s_2}C^{\mathrm{free}}_K\bigr)\Bigr|\le\epsilon^{\mathrm{ev}}_\sharp(g,\ell,\mathsf d')\Bigl(\frac r{\mathsf d'}\Bigr)^6\mathsf b^{-2}|\mathfrak s_1|_\infty|\mathfrak s_2|_\infty,
\]
where $\mathsf W_{\mathfrak s}(p,q)=w(p)\delta_{pq}-\sum_b\mathsf w(b)[u_{b,\lambda_b}(p)u_{b,\lambda'_b}(q)+u_{b,\lambda'_b}(p)u_{b,\lambda_b}(q)]$ and $u_{b,\alpha}(p)$ are the coefficients of the plaquette angles in the linear part of $u_{b,\alpha}$, given in the paragraph on the fields (it is the matrix of the lemma on bond sources, which follows Lem.~\ref{C-352-36}). Consequently both displays of (D.1) hold at $g\le\gamma_{\mathrm N}$, with $\epsilon^{\mathrm{ev}}_\sharp$ in place of $\epsilon^{\mathrm{cl}}$, for every $K$ with $s(\min\{r,r_g\})\le K$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
A bond weight enters the progression through its weight member, a local term on the plaquettes of the two planes that contain the bond. Put $\rho=\min\{r,r_g\}$; the working level at $\rho$ ($\rho\le\frac14e^{-2\sqrt3}$, $s(\rho)\le K$) gives $a_K\le\rho/4M\le\frac1{52}\rho$. The hull of $\mathfrak s_a$ (clause (6) of the lemma on bond sources, which follows Lem.~\ref{C-352-36}) has its barycentres in $\mathbb B(x_a,r+\frac12a_K)$, so that for $p,q$ in the two hulls
\[
\tfrac67\mathsf d'\le|x(p)-x(q)|\le\tfrac87\mathsf d'=:\mathsf d^+,
\]
all these points lying in a ball of radius $<\frac14\ell$, where the least lifts are taken. Put $\mathsf d=\min\{\frac67\mathsf d',t_{\mathrm N}(g)\}$, the floor of the distances that is read.

\emph{The case $r<r_g$.} The width $r_T=r+\frac12a_K\le\frac{105}{104}r$ has $r_T\le\mathsf d$, $s(r_T)\le K$, and $r_T\le\frac12\cdot1.01\,r_1(\bar{\mathsf b})\le r_1(\mathsf b)$, as $r_1$ does not increase and $\mathsf b\le\bar{\mathsf b}$; so the two sources are in the frame at $\mathsf k(\mathsf d)$ (clause (6) of the lemma on bond sources). By the lemma on bond sources the calculus of Lem.~\ref{C-352-12}, the sizes of Lem.~\ref{C-352-15}(f), the one-source Lem.~\ref{C-352-16} and the induction at two sources (Prop.~\ref{C-352-21}, base level equal to start level $\mathsf k(\mathsf d)$, as in step~6 of the proof of Prop.~\ref{C-352-24}) apply to the mixed sources, with the explicit form $\frac1{2a_K}\langle F,\mathsf W_{\mathfrak s}F\rangle$ of a source, the orientation signs entering through $u_{b,\lambda}(p)$. Of $(\Gamma1)$ these use only the members that $g\le\gamma_{\mathrm N}$ gives: the member $\delta(g^{-2})\le1/2C_{\mathrm{cu}}$ is used only for the kernel families (Prop.~\ref{C-352-19}), which do not occur at two sources whose distance fixes the base level. The difference of the two members of the display is at most the sum of three members.

(i) \emph{The remainder.} $S^T_2-\mathsf J_2=\int\mathsf Y_{12}\,\mathrm{d}\mathbb P+\kappa_{\mathbb P}(\mathsf Y_1,\mathsf Y_2)$ (Lem.~\ref{C-352-25}(c) for mixed sources, by clause (5) of the lemma on bond sources). The two sources form one pair at the widths $(r_T,\mathsf d)$ in the sense of Lem.~\ref{C-352-15}(f), so the proof of Lem.~\ref{C-352-26}, with the sizes of clauses (1)--(3) of the lemma on bond sources, gives at $\mathbb P$-almost every $\omega$ the bounds $|\mathsf Y_a|\le\Lambda_T\alpha^{-6}r_T^3|\mathfrak s_a|_\infty$ and $|\mathsf Y_{12}|\le\Lambda_T\alpha^{-6}r_T^6\mathsf d^{-9/2}|\mathfrak s_1|_\infty|\mathfrak s_2|_\infty$, with a number $\Lambda_T\ge1$ formed from the constants. With the moments of $\alpha^{-1}$ on the side $\ell$, $\int\alpha^{-24}d\mathbb P\le\bar{\mathsf M}_\ell:=1+4L^{24}M^{-3}\ell^3e^{\mathsf B(X_g)\ell^3}\mathsf C_{\mathrm{ag}}(25,\eth)$ (Lem.~\ref{C-352-25}(e)), which grows with $\ell$, this member is at most $3\Lambda_T^2\bar{\mathsf M}_\ell^2\bar{\mathsf b}^2\mathsf d^{3/2}\,(r_T/\mathsf d)^6\mathsf b^{-2}|\mathfrak s_1|_\infty|\mathfrak s_2|_\infty$.

(ii) \emph{The induction.} The Gaussian step of Lem.~\ref{C-352-20}(c) with $\mathsf W_{\mathfrak s}$ in place of $w$ gives at the top the value $g_{K;12}=\frac32\operatorname{Tr}(\mathsf W_{\mathfrak s_1}\mathcal S_K\mathsf W_{\mathfrak s_2}\mathcal S_K)$, $\mathcal S_K=\sum_{\mathsf k(\mathsf d)<j\le K}\upsilon_j\mathcal C_{(j)}$, Wick's rule for two quadratic forms of the photon field. Prop.~\ref{C-352-21} and Lem.~\ref{C-352-15}(d), as in step~6 of the proof of Prop.~\ref{C-352-24}, bound $|\mathsf J_2-g_{K;12}|$ by $\mathsf E_{\mathrm J}(g,\mathsf d)(r_T/\mathsf d)^6\mathsf b^{-2}|\mathfrak s_1|_\infty|\mathfrak s_2|_\infty$, with a function $\mathsf E_{\mathrm J}$ of $(g,\mathsf d)$ alone that is at most $C(g)(\log\frac1{\mathsf d})^{19\mathfrak p_0}\mathsf d^{1/2}$ for $\mathsf d\le t_{\mathrm N}(g)$.

(iii) \emph{The free kernel.} For $p,q$ in the two hulls, $\mathsf r=|x(p)-x(q)|_\infty\in[\mathsf d/\sqrt3,\mathsf d^+]$ and $t=\mathsf r/a_{K-\mathsf k(\mathsf d)}\ge\hat{\mathsf d}_{\mathsf k(\mathsf d)}/\sqrt3$, the floor of the working level, at which the condition of Lem.~\ref{C-352-22}(b) holds by the conditions that fix $t_{\mathrm N}(g)$ (as condition (ii) of step~5 of the proof of Prop.~\ref{C-352-24}). So Lem.~\ref{C-352-22}(b) at $k=\mathsf k(\mathsf d)$, multiplied by $\mathsf r^3$, gives $|\mathcal S_K-\mathsf b^{-1}C^{\mathrm{free}}_K|(p,q)\le\mathsf b^{-1}a_K^3\mathsf r^{-3}\,\mathsf e_{\mathrm{fr}}(g;\mathsf d,\mathsf d^+)$, with $\mathsf b^{-1}<g^2$ and
\[
\mathsf e_{\mathrm{fr}}(g;\mathsf d,\mathsf d^+)=\tfrac54C_{\mathrm{tp}}c^{(2)}_L\bar Bg^2\,\mathsf d^++C^{\mathrm{bg}}_{\mathrm{tp}}(\mathsf d^+)^3+2L^3C_{\mathrm{tp}}\sup_{t\ge\hat{\mathsf d}_{\mathsf k(\mathsf d)}/\sqrt3}t^3e^{-\delta_{\mathrm{tp}}Lt}.
\]
