Telescoping the two kernels in $\operatorname{Tr}(\mathsf W_{\mathfrak s_1}\cdot\,\mathsf W_{\mathfrak s_2}\cdot\,)$, with Lem.~\ref{C-352-22}(a), $|C^{\mathrm{free}}_K(p,q)|\le(1+3C_{\mathrm{lat}})a_K^3|u|^{-3}$, $\mathsf r^{-3}\le3^{3/2}\mathsf d^{-3}$ and the second bound of clause (3) of the lemma on bond sources for $\sum_{p,q}|\mathsf W_{\mathfrak s_a}(p,q)|$, this member is at most $C\,\mathsf e_{\mathrm{fr}}(g;\mathsf d,\mathsf d^+)(r_T/\mathsf d)^6\mathsf b^{-2}|\mathfrak s_1|_\infty|\mathfrak s_2|_\infty$: a member polynomial in $\mathsf d^+$, besides the far term at the floor.

The members (i) and (ii), which carry the renormalisation group, read of the distances the floor $\mathsf d$ alone; the largest distance $\mathsf d^+$ enters the one explicit member (iii), the comparison of the sum of the slices with the free kernel, through a bound polynomial in $\mathsf d^+$.

\emph{The case $r\ge r_g$.} Then $\rho=r_g$ and $s(r_g)\le K$. Tile the lift by the half-open cubes $Q$ of side $r_g$ and cut $\mathfrak s_a=\sum_Q\mathfrak s^Q_a$, $\mathfrak s^Q_a$ the restriction of $\mathfrak s_a$ to the plaquettes and the bonds whose barycentres or midpoints lie in $Q$; $|\mathfrak s^Q_a|_\infty\le|\mathfrak s_a|_\infty$, and at most $(2r/r_g+2)^3\le64(r/r_g)^3$ pieces of each source are not $0$. The hull of a piece is a part of the hull of $\mathfrak s_a$ and has its barycentres within $\frac{\sqrt3}2r_g+\frac12a_K\le r_g$ of the centre of its cube; so every pair of pieces, neither $0$, is in the data of the first case at the widths $(r_g,\mathsf d)$, with $r_g\le\mathsf d$, $s(r_g)\le K$, $r_g\le r_1(\mathsf b)$, the centres of the cubes in the place of $x_1,x_2$, and the same bounds $\frac67\mathsf d'\le|x(p)-x(q)|\le\mathsf d^+$ on the hulls. Both members of the display are bilinear in $(\mathfrak s_1,\mathfrak s_2)$, as $\mathcal O^T$ and $\mathsf W_{\mathfrak s}$ are linear in $\mathfrak s$, and the sum over the pairs of pieces costs $64^2(r/r_g)^6(r_g/\mathsf d)^6=4096(r/\mathsf d)^6$.

\emph{Together.} $(\mathsf d'/\mathsf d)^6=(\frac76)^6\max\{1,6\mathsf d'/7t_{\mathrm N}(g)\}^6$ and $4096(\frac76)^6(\frac{105}{104})^6\le11060$ give the display with
\[
\begin{multlined}
\epsilon^{\mathrm{ev}}_\sharp(g,\ell,\mathsf d')=11060\max\Bigl\{1,\frac{6\mathsf d'}{7t_{\mathrm N}(g)}\Bigr\}^6\Bigl[\mathsf E_{\mathrm J}(g,\mathsf d)+C\,\mathsf e_{\mathrm{fr}}\bigl(g;\mathsf d,\tfrac87\mathsf d'\bigr)+3\Lambda_T^2\bar{\mathsf M}_\ell^2\bar{\mathsf b}^2\mathsf d^{3/2}\Bigr],\qquad\mathsf d \\
=\min\{\tfrac67\mathsf d',t_{\mathrm N}(g)\},
\end{multlined}
\]
a finite function on $(0,\frac18\ell]$ formed from the constants, $g$ and $\ell$. For $\mathsf d'\le\frac76t_{\mathrm N}(g)$ one has $\mathsf d=\frac67\mathsf d'$ and $\mathsf d^+=\frac43\mathsf d$, and each of the three members is at most $C(g,\ell)(\log\frac1{\mathsf d'})^{19\mathfrak p_0}\mathsf d'^{1/2}$: the first by step~6 of the proof of Prop.~\ref{C-352-24}, the second as the member $\mathrm{br}$ of its step~4 under the conditions of its step~5, the third as $\mathsf d^{3/2}\le\mathsf d^{1/2}$.

\emph{The plane and the bond forms.} For Lipschitz bumps the lattice form is turned into the integrals of (D.1) by Lem.~\ref{C-352-36a}, whose data hold: $4a_K\le r$, $16r\le\mathsf d'$, $8\mathsf d'\le\ell$. For the plane fields take $\mathfrak s_a=(\mathbf 1_{\{\lambda(\cdot)=\lambda_a\}}\varphi_a\circ x,0)$, $\lambda_1=\lambda$, $\lambda_2=\mu$, so that $|\mathfrak s_a|_\infty\le\|\varphi_a\|_\infty$ and the main term is $\frac32\mathsf b^{-2}\sum_{p,q}w_1(p)w_2(q)C^{\mathrm{free}}_K(p,q)^2$; Lem.~\ref{C-352-36a}(a) times $\frac32\mathsf b^{-2}$ gives the second display of (D.1). For the bond form take $\mathfrak s_1=(0,\mathsf w)$, $\mathsf w(b)=\varphi_1(x_b)\mathbf 1_{\{\mu_b=\mu\}}$, so that $Y[\mathsf w]=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{od}}_{\lambda\lambda'}(\varphi_1)$ and $|\mathfrak s_1|_\infty\le8\|\varphi_1\|_\infty$, and $\mathfrak s_2=(\mathbf 1_{\{\lambda(\cdot)=\gamma\}}\varphi_2\circ x,0)$.

For the symmetric matrix $C=C^{\mathrm{free}}_K$, $\operatorname{Tr}(\mathsf W_{\mathfrak s_1}C\mathsf W_{\mathfrak s_2}C)=-2\sum_{b,q}\mathsf w(b)w_2(q)C_\lambda(b,q)C_{\lambda'}(b,q)$ with $C_\alpha(b,q)=\sum_pu_{b,\alpha}(p)C(p,q)$, so the main term is $-3\mathsf b^{-2}\sum_{b,q}\mathsf w(b)w_2(q)C_\lambda(b,q)C_{\lambda'}(b,q)$, and Lem.~\ref{C-352-36a}(b) times $3\mathsf b^{-2}$ gives the first display, with $8\epsilon^{\mathrm{ev}}_\sharp$ in the place of $8\epsilon^{\mathrm{cl}}$.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Pair minus tensor field.}

\begin{lemma}[A regular gauge on a cube; the curvature is H\"older continuous]\label{C-352-37a}
Fix $\beta_{\mathrm H}\in(0,1)$. There are numbers $\epsilon_{\mathrm G}\in(0,1]$ and $C^\sharp_{\mathrm G},C_{\mathrm H}\ge1$, formed from the constants and $\beta_{\mathrm H}$, such that the following holds for $1\le n\le K$; lengths are in level-$n$ units, $\xi=\eta_n$, and $Q_s(x_0)$ is the set of the bare sites at the sup distance at most $s$ from a bare site $x_0$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] Let $12a_{K-n}\le\ell$ and let $A$ be a real $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued $1$-form on the bonds of $Q_2(x_0)$ such that $|A|$, $|\nabla^\xi A|$ and the current of $e^{i\xi A}$ are at most $\mathsf r_\circ\le\frac1{120}$ there. Then the linear angles $F_p=\xi(\mathrm{d}A)(p)$ satisfy $|F_p|\le2\xi^2\mathsf r_\circ$ and $|F_{p_{\mu\nu}(x)}-F_{p_{\mu\nu}(x')}|\le C_{\mathrm H}\,\xi^2\mathsf r_\circ|x-x'|^{\beta_{\mathrm H}}$ for the plaquettes $p_{\mu\nu}(x)$, $p_{\mu\nu}(x')$ of one orientation with $x,x'\in Q_{1/2}(x_0)$.
\item[(b)] Let $W\in\mathcal V^\chi_n$, $U=U_n(W)$, and let $\varrho\ge1$ with $(8\varrho+2)a_{K-n}<\ell$ and $(4\varrho)^2(1+4\varrho)\,4B_3\varepsilon_n\le\epsilon_{\mathrm G}$. Then there are $\mathsf g\colon Q_{4\varrho}(x_0)\to SU(2)$ and a real $1$-form $A$ on the bonds of $Q_{2\varrho}(x_0)$ with $\mathsf g(b_-)U(b)\mathsf g(b_+)^{-1}=e^{i\xi A(b)}$ there and, on $Q_\varrho(x_0)$, $|A|\le80C^\sharp_{\mathrm G}B_3\varrho^2\varepsilon_n$ and $|\nabla^\xi A|\le80C^\sharp_{\mathrm G}B_3\varrho\,\varepsilon_n$; the plaquette variables and the current of $e^{i\xi A}$ are those of $U$ conjugated by $\mathsf g$, and the current has a modulus $<2B_3\varepsilon_n$.
\end{enumerate}
None of these numbers depends on $n$, $K$, $\ell$, the spacing, $x_0$ or the configuration.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(a) The $2$-form $f_{\mu\nu}=\xi^{-2}F_{p_{\mu\nu}}=\nabla^\xi_\mu A_\nu-\nabla^\xi_\nu A_\mu$ is antisymmetric and closed, $\mathrm{d}f=0$, and its lattice codifferential differs from the current of $e^{i\xi A}$ by at most $40|A||\nabla^\xi A|+32|A|^3$ in the sup bounds, by the expansion of the lattice current; so $|f|\le2\mathsf r_\circ$ and $|\mathrm{d}^*f|\le2\mathsf r_\circ$. For an antisymmetric lattice $2$-form $f$ on a cube $Q_R(x_0)$, $R\ge8\xi$, with $|f|\le m_0$ and $|\mathrm{d}f|,|\mathrm{d}^*f|\le m_1$, the lattice Hodge identity $\Delta(\chi f)=\mathrm{d}^*\mathrm{d}(\chi f)+\mathrm{d}\mathrm{d}^*(\chi f)$, for a cut-off $\chi$ equal to $1$ on $Q_{R/2}(x_0)$ and written as $\chi f=G_\xi*\Delta(\chi f)$ with the lattice Green function $G_\xi$ of $\xi\mathbb Z^3$, and the bounds $|\nabla G_\xi(z)|\le C(|z|+\xi)^{-2}$, $|\nabla^2G_\xi(z)|\le C(|z|+\xi)^{-3}$, which are uniform in $\xi$, give $|f(x)-f(x')|\le C(\beta_{\mathrm H})(m_0+Rm_1)(|x-x'|/R)^{\beta_{\mathrm H}}$ for $x,x'\in Q_{R/2}(x_0)$. At $R=1$, $m_0=m_1=2\mathsf r_\circ$ this is (a).
(b) Put $\alpha=4B_3\varepsilon_n$ and lift the sites of $Q_{4\varrho}(x_0)$ to the box $\Omega=x_0+\xi\{-M,\dots,M\}^3$, $M=\lfloor4\varrho/\xi\rfloor$, of side $s=(2M+1)\xi\le9\varrho$. The room hypothesis makes the lift injective. By Lem.~\ref{C-352-25}(d), $U$ is regular of level $n$ at radius $\alpha_0=2B_3\varepsilon_n$. The current-to-matrix-divergence calculation in Lem.~\YMMref{9.4}{40} gives $|D_U^{\mathsf T}\partial U|\le\xi^{-1}(\alpha_0\xi^2)^2+\xi^2\alpha_0<\alpha\xi^2$ at every full box bond; its plaquette bound is also $<\alpha\xi^2$. Choose $\epsilon_{\mathrm G}\le\min\{1,c_\square\}$ and $C^\sharp_{\mathrm G}\ge\max\{1,B_\square\}$, where $c_\square,B_\square$ are the box-gauge constants in the proof of Thm.~\YMMref{F}{199}. The stated smallness implies $s\alpha\le c_\square$.

That box estimate gives a real gauge and potential on $\Omega$ with $|A|<B_\square s\alpha\le36B_\square B_3\varrho\varepsilon_n$, and the same bound for first differences at base sites of depth at least $3/2$. Every positive bond with an endpoint in $Q_\varrho$ has base depth at least $3\varrho-2\xi>3/2$. Restricting the potential to $Q_{2\varrho}$ gives both displayed bounds, since $\varrho\ge1$. Plaquette and current moduli are preserved by the real gauge.
\end{proof}

In Lems.~\ref{C-352-38}--\ref{C-352-41} the data are those of Thm.~\ref{C-352-7}; one progression holds the sources $w_1,w_2,w_T,w_3$, so that by multilinearity the objects of the two lists $(w_1,w_2,w_3)$ and $(w_T,w_3)$ are obtained from it. We write $\Delta_n=\mathsf cG_{n;12}-G_{n;T}$ and $\Gamma_n=\mathsf cG_{n;123}-G_{n;T3}$, functions of the configurations of the level $n$ whose pairs lie in the cores, and $\mathrm{nat}^{\mathcal W}_n=\varepsilon_n^2a_{K-n}^{-4}$.

\begin{lemma}[Pair minus tensor field on all small-field backgrounds]\label{C-352-38}
Let $r\le r_\alpha(g,\mathsf b)$; let $n_1$ and $n_0$ be the least levels with $a_{K-n_1}\ge(\frac r2)^{3/4}$ and $a_{K-n_0}\ge r^{1/2}$, $N_0=n_0+m_1$, where $m_1\ge1$ is the least integer with $L^{m_1/2}\ge C_7A_0/(0.85\,\mathsf c_{\mathfrak h}A_1)$, $C_7=2B_3+69\cdot1280\,C^\sharp_{\mathrm G}B_3$, an integer formed from the constants and $\beta_{\mathrm H}$ (through $C^\sharp_{\mathrm G}$ of the lemma on a regular gauge on a cube, which precedes this lemma), $\epsilon=r^{\beta_{\mathrm H}/36}+(a_K/r)^{1/9}$, and let $x_\sharp\ge e^{2\mathfrak p_0}$ be the least number such that every $x\ge x_\sharp$ has $17408B_3\varepsilon(x)\le\epsilon_{\mathrm G}$ and $1280C^\sharp_{\mathrm G}B_3\varepsilon(x)\le\frac1{100}$, with the numbers $\epsilon_{\mathrm G}$, $C^\sharp_{\mathrm G}$ of the lemma on a regular gauge on a cube.

Let $L^{N_0-n_1}\ge2M$, and let $\epsilon^{\mathrm e}_i=C_\omega[1.45\gamma_{i-1}+\frac12\mathsf c^\flat\theta^{[0]}]\le1$ for $\mathsf k(\frac r2)\le i<n_1$; this number bounds the single-source arrays of the near pair at the level $i$, $\mathfrak n[\dot{\mathfrak e}_{a,i}]\le2\epsilon^{\mathrm e}_i\varsigma_i\mathsf m_{i,a}$ ($a=1,2$, $\varsigma_i$ formed at the width $\frac r8$), as in Lem.~\ref{C-352-15}(a). For $N_0\le n^\sharp<K$ with $x_{n^\sharp}\ge x_\sharp$ there are real numbers $\mathsf c_n$, $N_0\le n\le n^\sharp$, such that for $\mathsf m_n$-almost every $W\in\mathcal V^\chi_n$
\[
|\Delta_n(U_n(W))-\mathsf c_n|\le\varepsilon^{\mathcal W}\,\mathrm{nat}^{\mathcal W}_n,\qquad|\mathsf c_n-\mathsf c_{n'}|\le2.01\,\tilde\varepsilon\,\mathrm{nat}^{\mathcal W}_n\quad(n\le n'\le n^\sharp),
\]
with $\varepsilon^{\mathcal W}\le\tilde\varepsilon\le C(g,\mathsf b)\,\epsilon$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(i) We use the regular-field estimate of {\cite[Lem.~B.22]{YMM2}} and the insertion identity of Lem.~\ref{lem:weighted-step-integrals} on the small-field backgrounds. The first is the evaluation of a local term at a configuration that is regular of a level, with the factor $\varepsilon_n^2$: for $1\le i\le n\le K$, $W\in\mathcal V^\chi_n$ and a pointed family $\mathsf f$ of level $i$ that vanishes unless one of $\mathsf N$ given cubes of $\pi_i$ is a cube of the domain, and on the domains with $d_i(X)<D$,
\[
\sum_{(X,z)}\bigl|\mathsf f(X,U_n(W),z)-\mathsf f(X,\mathbf 1,z)\bigr|\le C\,\mathsf N\,\|\mathsf f\|_{i,\lambda_{\mathrm{out}}}\,\varepsilon_n^2\,L^{-4(n-i)}e^{-D/2} .
\]
It is {\cite[eq.~230]{YMM2}} at the radius $\varepsilon=2B_3\varepsilon_n$ at which $U_n(W)$ is regular of the level $n$ (Lem.~\ref{C-352-25}(d), $4M\varepsilon\le c_{\mathrm A}\alpha_0$), which gives for one domain of size $d$ the factor $(\varepsilon/\alpha_0)^2L^{-4(n-i)}M^2(1+d)^2$, together with the tails of the proof of Lem.~\ref{C-352-14}(a): the domains beyond the depth $d_*=\min\{c_{\mathrm A}\alpha_0L^{2(n-i)}/M\varepsilon,(L^{m+K-i}-4)/2M\}-1$ have $e^{-[d_*]_+/2}\le C\varepsilon_n^2L^{-4(n-i)}$, by $e^{-s/2}\le8s^{-2}$, by $L^{m+K-n}\ge13My_n$ on the sides $\ell=2L^m$ of $\mathfrak L(g)$ (from $L^m\ge LMy_K$ and Lem.~\ref{C-352-10}(a)) and by $x_n^{-1}\le\varepsilon_n^2/A_0^2$; no ceiling beyond those of the data is read. (Lem.~\ref{C-352-14}(b) is the same count without the factor $\varepsilon_n^2$.) The second is the averaging identity of one step: the quotient $\mathsf{Qt}_{j+1}$ of one step, a positive normalised mean that takes bounded Borel functions of the block fields of the level $j$ to functions of those of the level $j+1$, takes the action $S[\mathfrak g](U_j(\cdot))$ of a bare array $\mathfrak g$ of the level $j$ to $(S[\mathfrak g]+\mathsf{Sum}[\mathsf D\mathsf{St}^{[j]}(\mathfrak f_{0,j})[\mathfrak g]])(U_{j+1}(\cdot))$, $\mathsf m_{j+1}$-almost everywhere; so the seminorm $\inf_c\operatorname{ess\,sup}_{\mathsf m_n}|\Phi(U_n(W))-c|$ of such actions does not grow from one level to the next. (ii) \emph{The split.} For $n_0\le j<K$ let $\mathfrak x_j$ be the bare array whose families are $\mathsf c$ times the kernel families $\mathsf K^{(i)}$ of the near pair at the levels $\mathsf k(\frac r2)<i\le n_1$ and whose slot holds minus the weight member of $w_T$; its action $X^{\mathrm{fz}}=S[\mathfrak x_j]$, the frozen part, does not depend on $j$.

Let $\mathfrak r_j$ hold all the other families of $\Delta$ of the levels $\le n_0$. Then $\Delta_n=\Delta_n(\mathbf 1)+X_n+S_n$, where $X_n$ adds to $X^{\mathrm{fz}}$ the families that the first derivatives of the steps above $n_0$ make from $\mathfrak x$ alone, and $S_n$ is the action of $\mathfrak r_n$ together with the families $\mathsf s^{(i)}$, $n_0<i\le n$, that the first derivatives of the steps make from $\mathfrak r$ and from the $\mathsf s^{(i')}$ of the lower levels, and with the second derivatives $\mathsf c\,\mathsf B_{i-1}(\mathfrak f_{\{1\},i-1},\mathfrak f_{\{2\},i-1})$ of the steps (Lem.~\ref{C-352-13}). The evaluation of (i), the lags of Lem.~\ref{C-352-12}(c) and the sizes of Lem.~\ref{C-352-15} give $|S_n|\le C\varepsilon_S\,\mathrm{nat}^{\mathcal W}_n$ at every small-field background of the level $n$, with $\varepsilon_S=2\varepsilon_{\mathfrak r}+C(r/a_{K-n_0})^3$ and the number $\varepsilon_{\mathfrak r}$ of step (i) of the proof of the lemma on the chain classes, which follows this lemma; that step uses the same split on the chain classes. (iii) The explicit parts cancel.

With $D(n)=3n\otimes n-1$, the pair, multiplied by $\mathsf c$, carries the explicit form with the kernel $\mathsf b^{-1}C^{\mathrm{free}}_K\approx\mathsf b^{-1}a_K^3\mathbb K_3(re_\lambda)=\mathsf b^{-1}a_K^3(4\pi r^3)^{-1}D(e_\lambda)$, while the tensor source carries $\frac1{2a_K}\sum_pw_T(p)|F_p|^2$ with $\delta_{\lambda(p)\lambda}-\frac13=\frac13D(e_\lambda)_{\lambda(p)\lambda(p)}$; the moment condition $\sum_k\mathsf a_kD(n_k)=\mathsf a_TD(e_\lambda)$, here with one pair of direction $e_\lambda$ and $\mathsf a_1=\mathsf a_T=1$, makes them equal. (iv) \emph{The frozen part on the backgrounds.} Let $N_0\le n\le n^\sharp$, $W\in\mathcal V^\chi_n$, $U=U_n(W)$, $x_0$ a bare site with $|x_0-c|_\infty\le a_K$, and let lengths be in level-$n$ units, $\xi=\eta_n$.

\emph{The gauge.} As $x_n\ge x_\sharp$ and $34a_{K-n}<\ell$, clause (b) of the lemma on a regular gauge on a cube, which precedes this lemma, applies at $\varrho=4$ and gives $\mathsf g$ on $Q_{16}(x_0)$ and a potential $A$ on the bonds of $Q_8(x_0)$ with $\mathsf g(b_-)U(b)\mathsf g(b_+)^{-1}=e^{i\xi A(b)}$, and on $Q_4(x_0)$ the bounds $|A|,|\nabla^\xi A|\le C_6\varepsilon_n\le\frac1{100}$, $C_6=1280C^\sharp_{\mathrm G}B_3$, and a current of modulus $<2B_3\varepsilon_n$. \emph{The cut-off.} Let $h=\prod_\mu\chi(|x_\mu-x_{0,\mu}|)$ with $\chi=1$ on $[0,3]$, $\chi=0$ on $[\frac{15}4,\infty)$, $|\chi'|\le2$ and $\operatorname{Lip}\chi'\le11$; put $\hat A=hA$ on the bonds of $Q_4(x_0)$, $\hat A=0$ on all other bonds of $T_\ell$, and $\hat U=e^{i\xi\hat A}$.

Then $\hat U$ is the transform of $U$ by $\mathsf g$ on every bond with an end in $Q_3(x_0)$, and the product rules for $hA$ with the expansion of the lattice current give
\[
\max\bigl\{\sup|\hat A|,\ \sup|\nabla^\xi\hat A|,\ \sup|J(\hat U)|\bigr\}\le(2B_3+69\,C_6)\,\varepsilon_n=C_7\varepsilon_n\qquad\text{on all of }T_\ell .
\]
\emph{The shift of the level.} Seen from the level $n^\flat=n-m_1\ge n_0$, the same configuration has the potential $\hat A^\flat=L^{-m_1}\hat A$, with $|\hat A^\flat|\le L^{-m_1}C_7\varepsilon_n$, differences $\le L^{-2m_1}C_7\varepsilon_n$ and current $\le L^{-3m_1}C_7\varepsilon_n$ in level-$n^\flat$ units; with $\varepsilon_n=(A_0/A_1)\delta_n$, $\delta_n\le(\frac54)^{1/2}L^{m_1/2}\delta_{n^\flat}$ (Lem.~\ref{C-352-10}(a)) and the choice of $m_1$,
\[
L^{-m_1}C_7\varepsilon_n\le(\tfrac54)^{1/2}\cdot0.85\,\mathsf c_{\mathfrak h}\delta_{n^\flat}<\tfrac{11}{10}\mathsf c_{\mathfrak h}\delta_{n^\flat}\le r_{n^\flat} .
\]
This is the norm clause of the chain class of radius $r_{n^\flat}$, and it is all that the steps below read of the field. \emph{The pair.} Step (ii) of the proof of the lemma on the chain classes is read at the level $n^\flat$ with $U$ in the place of $\tilde U$, with two changes. (1) The gauge $u=e^{iX}$ of Lem.~\ref{C-352-18} at the pair is formed for $\hat A^\flat$ on the bonds within two level-$n^\flat$ units of $x_0$, where $\hat U$ is the transform of $U$; it gives the angles $F'$, H\"older continuous as in that step, through the estimate of the proof of clause (a) of the lemma on a regular gauge on a cube on $Q_1(x_0)$ at $m_0=2.08\,r_{n^\flat}$ and $m_1=3.7\,r_{n^\flat}$, and the plaquette term of the weight member of $w_T$ in this gauge, as $a_p(U)=a_p(\hat U)$ at the plaquettes of $\operatorname{supp}w_T$, which lie in $Q_{1/2}(x_0)$. (2) For the kernel families of the levels $\mathsf k(\frac r2)\le i<n_1$, $m=n^\flat-i-1$: Lem.~\ref{C-352-18} for the real pair of the level $i+1$ that $\hat A^\flat$ and its current give on all of $T_\ell$ (the potential multiplied by $L^{-m}$, the current by $L^{-3m}$), on the box $N_{\rho'}$ about $x_0$, $\rho'=\min\{\mathsf h_i,3L^{n-i-1}-1\}$, with the same $u$, gives a real point $v'$ of the chart with $\|v'\|\le\mathsf h_iL^{-2m}r_{n^\flat}(6+19r_{n^\flat})\le\delta_i/2\Lambda_i$, by \textup{($\alpha$2)} at $n^\flat\ge n_0$, the pair having $|L^{-m}\hat A^\flat|\le L^{-m}r_{n^\flat}$ and differences and current $\le L^{-2m}r_{n^\flat}$.

A domain $X$ of the level $i+1$ with all its sites within $\rho'-1$ of $x_0$ lies in $Q_3(x_0)$, where $\hat U$ is the transform of $U$, so that $\mathsf K^{(i+1)}(X,U,z)=\mathsf K^{(i+1)}(X,P[v']|_X,z)$ by the gauge invariance and the locality of a local term; the other domains have $d_{i+1}(X)\ge2L^{n-i-1}/M-2$, or the depth of step~5 of the proof of Prop.~\ref{C-352-19} if $\rho'=\mathsf h_i$, and are paid by the norm (Lem.~\ref{C-352-14}(b) at $U$ and at $P[v']$). Steps 2--4 of the proof of Prop.~\ref{C-352-19} (holomorphy, the real ball, two constants), which read of the field only the real point $v'$ and its norm, give at $v'$ the kernel step with the angles $F'$. As $L^{n-i-1}\ge L^{N_0-n_1}\ge2M$ and $\epsilon^{\mathrm e}_i\le1$, the domains that leave the box cost at most $C\mathsf b\,r\,\mathrm{nat}^{\mathcal W}_n$ together.

With $r_{n^\flat}^2a_{K-n^\flat}^{-4}\le C\,\mathrm{nat}^{\mathcal W}_n$ (Lem.~\ref{C-352-10}(a), $a_{K-n^\flat}=L^{-m_1}a_{K-n}$) this bounds the frozen part: $|X^{\mathrm{fz}}(U)|\le\varepsilon^{\mathcal W}_X\mathrm{nat}^{\mathcal W}_n$, with $\varepsilon^{\mathcal W}_X\le C[\varepsilon_X+\mathsf b\,r]$ and the number $\varepsilon_X$ of step (ii) of the proof of the lemma on the chain classes. (v) Carried upward with (i) and the lags of Lem.~\ref{C-352-12}(c), $\|X_n\|\le[\varepsilon^{\mathcal W}_X+C\gamma_{N_0-1}+C\gamma_n^{8/9}(\varepsilon^{\mathcal W}_X)^{1/9}]\mathrm{nat}^{\mathcal W}_n$; the exponents $\frac89,\frac19$, and $\frac12$ below, come from interpolations between the oscillation bound and the bound of the sizes, and the choice of the levels, $\mathsf k(\frac r2)<n_1<n_0$ with $a_{K-n_1}\ge(\frac r2)^{3/4}$, costs the exponent $\frac14$.

Together $\varepsilon^{\mathcal W}\le\tilde\varepsilon\le C(g,\mathsf b)[r^{\beta_{\mathrm H}/36}+(a_K/r)^{1/9}]$ for $r\le r_\alpha(g,\mathsf b)$, the levels being ordered by \textup{($\alpha$1)}--\textup{($\alpha$5)} of Def.~\ref{C-352-2}(5); the constants $\mathsf c_n$ of two levels differ by at most these oscillations plus the part of the steps between that the sizes of the sources at those levels bound, which is of the same order.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Pair minus tensor field on the chain classes]\label{C-352-38a}
Let $r\le r_\alpha(g,\mathsf b)$, let $n_1$ and $n_0$ be the levels of Lem.~\ref{C-352-38}, and $\epsilon=r^{\beta_{\mathrm H}/36}+(a_K/r)^{1/9}$. There are numbers $\mathsf c'_n$, $n_0\le n\le K$, and a number $\varepsilon_\alpha\le C(g,\mathsf b)\,\epsilon$ such that
\[
\sup_{A\in\mathsf{Cc}_n(r_n)}\bigl|\Delta_n(e^{i\eta_nA})-\mathsf c'_n\bigr|\le\varepsilon_\alpha\,r_n^2a_{K-n}^{-4}\qquad(n_0\le n\le K).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(i) \emph{The split} is that of step (ii) of the proof of Lem.~\ref{C-352-38}. For $n_0\le j<K$, $\mathfrak x_j$ is the array whose families are $\mathsf c$ times the kernel families $\mathsf K^{(i)}$ of the near pair at the levels $\mathsf k(\frac r2)<i\le n_1$ and whose slot holds minus the weight member of $w_T$; its action $X^{\mathrm{fz}}$, the frozen part, does not depend on $j$. $\mathfrak r_j$ holds all the other families of $\Delta$ of the levels $\le n_0$. Lem.~\ref{C-352-12} and the sizes of Lem.~\ref{C-352-15} give $\mathfrak n[\mathfrak x_j]\le Ca_{K-j}^{-4}$ and $\mathfrak n[\mathfrak r_j]\le\varepsilon_{\mathfrak r}a_{K-j}^{-4}$, where $\varepsilon_{\mathfrak r}$ is a constant times $\gamma_{n_0}+s(\frac r2)\theta^{[0]}+(r/a_{K-n_1})^3$ and terms exponentially small in $\hat r_{\mathsf k(r/2)}$ and in $r/a_{K-1}$, so that $\varepsilon_{\mathfrak r}\le C(g,\mathsf b)[r^{1/4}+(a_K/r)^{1/4}]$.

On the chain classes $\Delta_n=\Delta_n(\mathbf 1)+X_n+S_n$, where $X_n$ adds to $X^{\mathrm{fz}}$ the families that the first derivatives of the steps above $n_0$ make from $\mathfrak x$ alone, and $S_n$ collects the rest: the action of $\mathfrak r_n$, the families that the first derivatives make from $\mathfrak r$ and from them, and the second derivatives of the steps; Lem.~\ref{C-352-14}(a), in the frame at $\mathsf k(\frac r2)$ in which Lem.~\ref{C-352-11}(a) puts the near pair, a test pair of the scale $\frac r2$, under the conditions $3\le s(\frac r2)\le K$ and $\mathsf{Lm}_{s(r/2)}\le L^{s(r/2)-3}$ of the data (and $\mathsf k(\frac r2)<n_1<n_0\le n<K$ by \textup{($\alpha$1)}), and the lags of Lem.~\ref{C-352-12}(c) give $|S_n|\le C\varepsilon_Sr_n^2a_{K-n}^{-4}$ with $\varepsilon_S=2\varepsilon_{\mathfrak r}+C(r/a_{K-n_0})^3$.
(ii) \emph{The frozen part.} Let $n_0\le n\le K$, $A\in\mathsf{Cc}_n(r_n)$, $x_0$ a bare site with $|x_0-c|_\infty\le a_K$, let $u=e^{iX}$, $X$ linear, be the gauge of Lem.~\ref{C-352-18} at the pair, about $x_0$, $A'$ the potential of $\tilde U=e^{i\eta_nA}$ in this gauge and $F'=\eta_n\mathrm{d}A'$ its angles. Near the pair $|A'|$, $|\nabla A'|$ and the current are at most a constant times $r_n$ (Lem.~\ref{C-352-18}, at $\alpha=\gamma_\circ=r_n$, in the units of the level $n$): on $N_2$, $|A'|\le6r_n+18.7r_n^2\le6.2\,r_n$ and $|\nabla^{\eta_n}A'|\le\frac{100}{99}(r_n+3r_n^2)\le1.04\,r_n$, and the current, conjugated by the gauge, is at most $r_n$. So the $2$-form $f=\eta_n^{-2}F'$ is closed, $|f|\le2.08\,r_n$, and, as its codifferential differs from the current by at most $40|A'||\nabla^{\eta_n}A'|+32|A'|^3$, $|\mathrm{d}^*f|\le3.7\,r_n$ on $Q_1(x_0)$, since $2r_n\le\varrho_{\mathrm{ch}}$ (Lem.~\ref{C-352-10}(b)) and $\varrho_{\mathrm{ch}}\le\frac1{60}$ by equation~\YMMref{(2285)}{833}.

The lemma on a regular gauge on a cube, which precedes Lem.~\ref{C-352-38}, is read through the estimate of the proof of its clause (a) on $Q_1(x_0)$, at $m_0=2.08\,r_n$ and $m_1=3.7\,r_n$: it makes $F'$ H\"older continuous with the exponent $\beta_{\mathrm H}$ on $Q_{1/2}(x_0)$, on the scale of the pair. Prop.~\ref{C-352-19}, in the frame of step (i), at the levels $\mathsf k(\frac r2)\le i<n_1$, where \textup{($\alpha$2)} of Def.~\ref{C-352-2}(5) gives its condition in (ii), taken before the last replacement of step 5 of its proof, so that $\mathcal Q_i$ stands at $F'$ and the last term of (ii) does not occur, replaces $\mathsf c\sum_i(\mathsf{Sum}[\mathsf K^{(i+1)}](\tilde U)-\mathsf{Sum}[\mathsf K^{(i+1)}](\mathbf 1))$ by $\mathsf c\,q_{n_1}(F')$ with an error at most $C\sum_i\hat r_i^3\mathfrak b_i^2(\delta_i+\epsilon^{\mathrm{cu}}_i)\Lambda_i^2\mathsf h_i^2\,r_n^2a_{K-n}^{-4}\le C(g,\mathsf b)\,r^{1/4}r_n^2a_{K-n}^{-4}$; the weight member of $w_T$ is expanded in the gauge $u$ at the pair.

With $\xi=\eta_n$, the plaquette angles of $\tilde U$ in this gauge are $F'_p+\Psi_p$ with the commutator part $|\Psi_p|\le24\xi^2|A'|^2$; Lem.~\ref{C-352-18} at $\alpha=\gamma_\circ=r_n$ gives $|A'(b)|\le3sr_n+(9s+8\xi)r_n^2\le4sr_n+8\xi r_n^2$ at the bonds with base point within $s$ of $x_0$, and $|F'_p|\le2.08\,\xi^2r_n$; as $a_p=\frac12|\theta|^2+O(|\theta|^4)$ in the plaquette angle $\theta$,
\[
\bigl|a_p(\tilde U)-\tfrac12|F'_p|^2\bigr|\le|F'_p||\Psi_p|+\tfrac12|\Psi_p|^2+C|F'_p+\Psi_p|^4\le C\xi^4r_n^3(s+\xi)^2
\]
at the plaquettes within $s\le\frac12$ of $x_0$. The plaquettes of $\operatorname{supp}w_T$ lie within $s\le r/a_{K-n}$ of $x_0$, so $s+\xi\le2r/a_{K-n_0}$; summed against $w_T$, with $\sum_p|w_T(p)|\le Ca_K^{-3}$, this replaces the tensor source by $\frac1{2a_K}\sum_pw_T(p)|F'_p|^2$ up to $C(r/a_{K-n_0})^2r_n^2a_{K-n}^{-4}\le C\,r\,r_n^2a_{K-n}^{-4}$, as $a_{K-n_0}\ge r^{1/2}$: in the gauge at the pair the angles are small at the scale $s+\xi$ of the tensor source. By the H\"older continuity and the comparison of $\mathcal S_{n_1}$ with $\mathsf b^{-1}C^{\mathrm{free}}_K$ and of $C^{\mathrm{free}}_K$ with $a_K^3\mathbb K_3$ (Lem.~\ref{C-352-22}(b), with \textup{($\alpha$5)}), both main terms equal $\frac1{6a_K^4}\sum_{\mu,\nu}D(e_\lambda)_{\mu\nu}\langle F^\circ_\mu,F^\circ_\nu\rangle$, $F^\circ_\mu$ the angle of the orientation $\mu$ at the centre, up to $C[(r/a_{K-n_1})^{\beta_{\mathrm H}}+a_K/r]\,r_n^2a_{K-n}^{-4}$ and terms of the same order; the moment condition of step (iii) of the proof of Lem.~\ref{C-352-38} cancels the main terms. So $\sup_{\mathsf{Cc}_n(r_n)}|X^{\mathrm{fz}}|\le\varepsilon_Xr_n^2a_{K-n}^{-4}$ with $\varepsilon_X\le C(g,\mathsf b)[r^{\beta_{\mathrm H}/4}+a_K/r]$.
(iii) \emph{Carrying upward.} On the chain classes the averaging identity of one step holds at every point: for $n_0\le m<K$, $A'\in\mathsf{Cc}_{m+1}(r_{m+1})$, the measure $\nu=\nu_{m,A'}$ of the step and every bare array $\mathfrak g$ of the level $m$ of size below $N^{[m]}_\star$,
\[
\int S[\mathfrak g]\bigl(e^{i\eta_mA^{\mathrm{lw}}(B)}\bigr)\,\mathrm{d}\nu(B)=\bigl(S[\mathfrak g]+\mathsf{Sum}[\mathsf D\mathsf{St}^{[m]}(\mathfrak f_{0,m})[\mathfrak g]]\bigr)\bigl(e^{i\eta_{m+1}A'}\bigr)+c_{\mathfrak g},
\]
with a number $c_{\mathfrak g}$ that does not depend on $A'$. It is the first derivative, in the direction of $\mathfrak g$, of the exact step integral in Lem.~\ref{lem:weighted-step-integrals} at the real chart point $A'$, which writes the action of the level $m+1$ through the mean under $\nu_{m,A'}$ of the exponential of the action of the level $m$ at the lowered configurations; the measure $\nu_{m,A'}$ and the lowering map name no array, and the step takes any bare array of that size in its fourth place (Lem.~\ref{C-352-12}(b)). As $A^{\mathrm{lw}}(B)\in\mathsf{Cc}_m(r_m)$ and $\nu$ is a probability measure, the oscillation of the right member over $\mathsf{Cc}_{m+1}(r_{m+1})$ is at most the oscillation of $S[\mathfrak g]$ over $\mathsf{Cc}_m(r_m)$.

A family that the steps above $n_0$ make from $\mathfrak x$, first created at the level $m+1$, is bounded in two ways: by the norm of the calculus, with the factor $\gamma_m$ (Lem.~\ref{C-352-12}(b), (c)), and, through this identity at $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak x_m$, by the oscillation of $X^{\mathrm{fz}}$ at the levels $m$ and $m+1$, at most $2\varepsilon_XL^{4(n-m)}r_n^2a_{K-n}^{-4}$. The smaller of the two, summed over $m$ with $\sum_{l\ge0}\min\{aL^{-l/2},bL^{4l}\}\le2.4a^{8/9}b^{1/9}$ ($L\ge13$), bounds the oscillation of $X_n$ by $[\varepsilon_X+C\gamma_{K-1}^{8/9}\varepsilon_X^{1/9}]r_n^2a_{K-n}^{-4}$. Together the oscillation of $\Delta_n$ on $\mathsf{Cc}_n(r_n)$ is at most $\varepsilon_\alpha r_n^2a_{K-n}^{-4}$ with $\varepsilon_\alpha=\varepsilon_X+C\gamma_{K-1}^{8/9}\varepsilon_X^{1/9}+C\varepsilon_S\le C(g,\mathsf b)\,\epsilon$, as $\gamma_{K-1}\le1$; $\mathsf c'_n$ is the centre of this oscillation.

At $n=K$ the chain class is $\{0\}$ and $r_K=0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Pair minus tensor field up to the last level]\label{C-352-38b}
Let $g$ satisfy besides $(\Gamma3)$ of Def.~\ref{C-352-2}(6), let $r\le r^{\mathcal W}_\alpha(g,\mathsf b)$, let $n_0$ be the level of Lem.~\ref{C-352-38}, and $\varepsilon^{\mathcal W}=C(g,\mathsf b)[r^{\beta_{\mathrm H}/72}+(a_K/r)^{1/18}]$ with a suitable number $C(g,\mathsf b)\ge1$. There are numbers $\mathsf c_n$, $n_0\le n\le K$, such that for $\mathsf m_n$-almost every $W\in\mathcal V^\chi_n$
\[
|\Delta_n(U_n(W))-\mathsf c_n|\le\varepsilon^{\mathcal W}\,\mathrm{nat}^{\mathcal W}_n,\qquad|\mathsf c_n-\mathsf c_K|\le\varepsilon^{\mathcal W}\,\mathrm{nat}^{\mathcal W}_n,
\]
and, for $w_3\not\equiv0$ and $\mathsf d'=|c-z|$, $|\Gamma_n(U_n(W))|+|\Gamma_K(\mathbf 1)|\le C(\mathsf b)\,\mathsf d'^{-5/2}\varepsilon^{\mathcal W}\mathsf b^{-2}\mathsf d'^{-6}\mu_3$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The proof of Lem.~\ref{C-352-38} is made at every level $n_0\le n\le K$, with the radius $C_{\mathcal W}\varepsilon_n$ of the backgrounds in the place of the radius of a chain class and without the shift of the level. (i) By the first two members of $(\Gamma3)$ the domains that leave the cores at the radius $2B_3\varepsilon_n$ have a depth that makes the tails of Lem.~\ref{C-352-14}(b) at most $C\varepsilon_n^2L^{-4(n-i)}$; so a pointed family of level $i$ that vanishes off a set of sites changes on the backgrounds of the level $n$ by at most a constant times its norm, the number of the cubes that hold a site of the set, $L^{-4(n-i)}$ and $\mathrm{nat}^{\mathcal W}_n$. (ii) Lem.~\ref{C-352-37a}(b) at $\varrho=3$, which applies as $7488B_3\varepsilon_n\le\epsilon_{\mathrm G}$ by $(\Gamma3)$ and $26a_{K-n}<\ell_g$ (as $\ell_g\ge2LMy_K\ge338$), gives about a bare site $x_0$ next to $c$ a gauge $\mathsf g$ on $Q_{12}(x_0)$ and a potential $A$ on the bonds of $Q_6(x_0)$ with $\mathsf g(b_-)U(b)\mathsf g(b_+)^{-1}=e^{i\eta_nA(b)}$ there, $U=U_n(W)$; on $Q_3(x_0)$ the potential, its differences and the current are at most $\mathsf r_\circ:=C_{\mathcal W}\varepsilon_n\le\frac1{120}$.

Lem.~\ref{C-352-18} is used in a local form, with data on $N_{\rho+1}$: \emph{in the units of a level, with the bare spacing $\xi\le\frac1{13}$, let $\rho\ge2$ with $4\rho+4$ at most the side of the torus, and let $\mathsf g\colon N_{\rho+1}\to SU(2)$ and a real $1$-form $A$ on the bonds with both end points in $N_{\rho+1}$ satisfy $\mathsf g(b_-)U(b)\mathsf g(b_+)^{-1}=e^{i\xi A(b)}$, $|A|\le\alpha\le\frac1{60}$ and $|\nabla^\xi A|\le\gamma_\circ$ there, the current of $U$ being at most $\iota$ there; with $c_\mu=A_\mu(x_0)$, $X(x)=\sum_\mu(x-x_0)_\mu c_\mu$ and $h=e^{iX}\mathsf g$ on $N_{\rho+1}$ there is a real pair $v'$ on all the bare bonds which, at the bonds with base point in $N_\rho$, is the image of $U$ and of its current under the gauge transformation $h$, and which obeys the three bounds of Lem.~\ref{C-352-18}; if $\|v'\|$ is less than the radius of the ball of the chart, every local term of the level on a domain $X\subset N_{\rho-1}$ that is formed at $U$ has the same value at $P[v']|_X$.} Its proof is that of Lem.~\ref{C-352-18}, with the transformed potential formed on $N_{\rho+1}$ and the cut-off $\chi(x)=\min\{1,\max\{0,(\rho+1-2\xi-|x-x_0|_\infty)/(1-2\xi)\}\}$, of the width $1-2\xi$ and equal to $1$ on $N_\rho$, in the place of the cut-off of the width $\rho$: as $|\chi(x+\xi e_\nu)-\chi(x)|\le\frac{13}{11}\xi$, $|\nabla^\xi A'|\le\frac{100}{99}(\gamma_\circ+3\alpha^2)+\frac{13}{11}[3(\rho+1)\gamma_\circ+(9\rho+9.62)\alpha^2]\le\rho(6\gamma_\circ+19\alpha^2)$ for $\rho\ge2$; and the bonds that a local term on $X\subset N_{\rho-1}$ reads have their end points in $N_\rho$, where $P[v']$ is the image of $U$ under $h$, while a local term is a gauge invariant function of the pair on its domain.

Viewed from the level $i+1$, $\mathsf k(\frac r2)\le i<n_1$, $m=n-i-1$, the data on $Q_3(x_0)$ have $|A|\le\alpha=L^{-m}\mathsf r_\circ$, $|\nabla A|\le\gamma_\circ=L^{-2m}\mathsf r_\circ$ and a current at most $L^{-3m}\mathsf r_\circ\le\gamma_\circ$, and the cube $N_{\mathsf h_i+1}$ of the level $i+1$ lies in $Q_3(x_0)$, as $(\mathsf h_i+1)L^{-m}\le3$ (Def.~\ref{C-352-2}(6)). The local form at $\rho=\mathsf h_i$, where $(4\mathsf h_i+4)a_{K-i-1}\le\ell_g$, gives a real point $v'$ of the chart with $\|v'\|\le\mathsf h_i\gamma_\circ(6+19\mathsf r_\circ)\le7\mathsf h_iL^{-2m}C_{\mathcal W}\varepsilon_n\le\delta_i/2\Lambda_i$ (Def.~\ref{C-352-2}(6)), inside the ball of the chart; the linear gauge $X$ is the same function at all the levels $i$, so that one $h$ serves them all.

Steps 2--4 of the proof of Prop.~\ref{C-352-19} at the real point $v'$, the domains in $N_{\mathsf h_i-1}$ taking the same values at $U$ and at $P[v']$, and the others, of a linear size at least $D_*=(\mathsf h_i-1-R_w)/M-2$, costing $2\mathsf M^{\mathsf K}_ie^{-[D_*]_+}\le\bar{\mathsf e}\gamma_\circ^2/\delta_i^2$ by the choice of $\mathsf h_i$, replace $\mathsf c\sum_i(\mathsf{Sum}[\mathsf K^{(i+1)}](U)-\mathsf{Sum}[\mathsf K^{(i+1)}](\mathbf 1))$ by $\mathsf c\,q_{n_1}(F')$, $F'$ the linear angles in the gauge $h$, up to $C\sum_i\hat r_i^3\mathfrak b_i^2(\delta_i+\epsilon^{\mathrm{cu}}_i)\Lambda_i^2\mathsf h_i^2\,C_{\mathcal W}^2\mathrm{nat}^{\mathcal W}_n$. In the gauge $h$, in the units of the level $n$, $|A'|\le4s\mathsf r_\circ+8\eta_n\mathsf r_\circ^2$ at the bonds with base point within $s\le2$ of $x_0$, $|\nabla A'|\le1.04\,\mathsf r_\circ$ and $|F'_p|\le2.08\,\eta_n^2\mathsf r_\circ$ there, and $|a_p(U)-\frac12|F'_p|^2|\le C\eta_n^4\mathsf r_\circ^3(s+\eta_n)^2$ at the plaquettes within $s\le\frac12$ of $x_0$; this replaces the tensor source by $\frac1{2a_K}\sum_pw_T(p)|F'_p|^2$ up to $C(r/a_{K-n_0})^2C_{\mathcal W}^2\mathrm{nat}^{\mathcal W}_n$.

Lem.~\ref{C-352-37a}(a) is read through the estimate of its proof on $Q_1(x_0)$, at $m_0=2.08\,\mathsf r_\circ$ and $m_1=3.7\,\mathsf r_\circ$ (on $N_2$, $|A'|\le6.2\,\mathsf r_\circ$, and the codifferential of $\eta_n^{-2}F'$ differs from the current by at most $40|A'||\nabla A'|+32|A'|^3$): it makes $F'$ H\"older continuous with the exponent $\beta_{\mathrm H}$ on the scale of the pair. The comparison of $\mathcal S_{n_1}$ with $\mathsf b^{-1}C^{\mathrm{free}}_K$ and of $C^{\mathrm{free}}_K$ with $a_K^3\mathbb K_3$ (Lem.~\ref{C-352-22}(b), with \textup{($\alpha$5)}) brings both main terms to $\frac1{6a_K^4}\sum_{\mu\nu}D(e_\lambda)_{\mu\nu}\langle F^\circ_\mu,F^\circ_\nu\rangle$, $F^\circ$ the angles at the centre, up to $C[(r/a_{K-n_1})^{\beta_{\mathrm H}}+a_K/r]C_{\mathcal W}^2\mathrm{nat}^{\mathcal W}_n$; the moment condition cancels them, and the frozen part on the backgrounds is at most $\varepsilon^{\mathcal W}_X\mathrm{nat}^{\mathcal W}_n$. (iii) From one level to the next the averaging identity of one step, written for arbitrary bare arrays, gives $\mathsf m_{n+1}$-almost everywhere $\Delta_{n+1}=\mathsf{Qt}_{n+1}[\Delta_n]+\mathsf b_n$, where $\mathsf{Qt}_{n+1}$ is the quotient of the step, a positive normalised mean, and $\mathsf b_n$ is $\mathsf c$ times the covariance, under the step, of the quotients of the two single sources of the near pair.

The one-source bound $|G_{n;a}-G_{n;a}(\mathbf 1)|\le Cr^3|w_a|_\infty\mathrm{nat}^{\mathcal W}_n$ on the backgrounds gives $|\mathsf b_n|\le CA_0^2y_{n_0}^{2\mathfrak p_0}(r/a_{K-n_0})^3\mathrm{nat}^{\mathcal W}_n\le C(\mathsf b)\,r\,\mathrm{nat}^{\mathcal W}_n$. A quotient does not increase the oscillation, so the centres $\mathsf c_n$ of the oscillations of two consecutive levels differ by at most twice the oscillation bound plus $C(\mathsf b)\,r\,\mathrm{nat}^{\mathcal W}_n$; as $\mathrm{nat}^{\mathcal W}$ falls by the factor $\frac54L^{-3}$ from one level to the next, the sum over the levels gives the second bound. (iv) For $\Gamma_n$ the averaging identity of one step, in its form for two and for three arrays, gives $\mathsf m_{i+1}$-almost everywhere, for $n_0\le i<K$, $\Gamma_{i+1}=\mathsf{Qt}_{i+1}[\Gamma_i]+\mathsf{Qt}_{i+1}[\Delta_i;G_{i;3}]+\mathsf c\,\mathsf{Sum}[\mathsf C^{(i+1)}]$; here $\mathsf{Qt}_{i+1}[\,\cdot\,;\cdot\,]$ is the covariance of the quotients of the step, and the family $\mathsf C^{(i+1)}$ is made of the mixed second derivatives of the step in the arrays of the sets $\{1,3\}$ and $\{2\}$ and in those of $\{2,3\}$ and $\{1\}$, and of its third derivative in the arrays of the three single sources.

A quotient does not raise the essential supremum, so the bound of $\Gamma_n$ is that of $\Gamma_{n_0}$ plus the sum over $n_0\le i<n$ of the bounds of the two other terms. The covariance is at most the smaller of the bound by the oscillations of $\Delta_i$ and of the far source on the backgrounds and the bound by the norms, $\mathsf C^{(i+1)}$ is bounded by the norms, and $\Gamma_{n_0}$ by the first display of Lem.~\ref{C-352-39} at $U_{n_0}(W)$, whose pairs of all levels $\le n_0$ lie in the cores (Lem.~\ref{C-352-25}(d)); the sum over the levels is that of the proof of Lem.~\ref{C-352-40}, with the bound of the oscillation of $\Delta$ on the backgrounds in the place of $\varepsilon_\alpha$.

All the numbers so formed are at most $C(g,\mathsf b)[r^{\beta_{\mathrm H}/36}+(a_K/r)^{1/9}]$ for $r\le r^{\mathcal W}_\alpha$; with $(\frac{\mathsf b}{\mathsf d'})^{3/2}(\frac r{\mathsf d'})^3\le\mathsf b^{3/2}\mathsf d'^{-2}r^{1/2}$ and $(\frac{\mathsf b}{\rho_0})^{3/2}e^{-\mathsf d'/8M\rho_0}\le C\mathsf b^{3/2}\mathsf d'^{-5/2}r^{1/2}$, $\rho_0=a_{K-n_0}$, the claims follow.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Crossing functionals at levels below the distance]\label{C-352-39}
For $\beta\in\{13,23,123\}$ of the list $(w_1,w_2,w_3)$ and $\beta=T3$ of the list $(w_T,w_3)$, $m=|\beta|$, $1\le i\le K$, and every configuration $U$ whose pairs of the level $i$ lie in the cores,
\[
\sum_{(X,z)}|E^{(i)}_\beta(X,U,z)|\le C_\times\bigl(\tfrac{8r}{3\mathsf d}\bigr)^6\bar\nu_{i-1;\beta}\,e^{-D^\sharp_i/2},\qquad D^\sharp_i=[\mathsf d/2Ma_{K-i}-2]_+ .
\]
So if $8Ma_{K-n}\le\mathsf d$, then for every such $U$ of the level $n$: 
\[
|G_{n;\beta}(U)|\le C'_\times\mathsf b^{-m/2}a_{K-n}^{-m/2}e^{-\mathsf d/4Ma_{K-n}}(\frac{8r}{3\mathsf d})^6\prod_{a\in\beta}|w_a|_\infty.
\]

\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
By the support rule (Lem.~\ref{C-352-12}(d)) a crossing family lives on domains that reach from the pair to the piece, of linear size at least $D^\sharp_i$; the near supports lie in $\mathbb B(c,\frac58r)$, the piece in $\mathbb B(z,\frac14r)$, so the corners of the two kinds are at least $\frac12\mathsf d$ apart in the sup distance; its norm is bounded by the sizes of Lem.~\ref{C-352-15}(e), in the form (f), at the width $r$ and a crossing distance $\mathsf d_\times\ge\frac38\mathsf d$, with $(r/\mathsf d_\times)^6\le(\frac{8r}{3\mathsf d})^6$; Lem.~\ref{C-352-14}(b) at $U$ gives the sum with the factor $e^{-D^\sharp_i/2}$, and $\bar\nu_{i-1;\beta}\le\bar c_m(5L/4\mathsf b)^{m/2}a_{K-i}^{-m/2}\prod|w_a|_\infty$; the sum over $i\le n$ is led by $i=n$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The difference of the jets]\label{C-352-40}
Let $w_3\not\equiv0$. Then the centre $z$ of its cube has $(1-\frac1{64})\mathsf d\le|c-z|\le6\mathsf d$, and
\[
\bigl|\mathsf c\,\mathsf J_3(w_1,w_2,w_3)-\mathsf J_2(w_T,w_3)\bigr|\le C(g,\mathsf b)\,\mathsf d^{-12}\bigl[r^{\beta_{\mathrm H}/72}+(a_K/r)^{1/18}\bigr]\mathsf b^{-2}\mathsf d^{-6}\mu_3 .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
A barycentre in the cube lies in $\operatorname{supp}\varphi_2$, at a distance $\ge\mathsf d$ from $c$ and $\le\frac{\sqrt3}8r\le\frac1{64}\mathsf d$ from $z$, as $r\le(\mathsf d/5LM)^2$. Put $\mathsf d'=|c-z|$ and $\rho_0=a_{K-n_0}$; the data give $16r\le\mathsf d'\le\min\{1,\mathsf b\}$, $4M\rho_0\le\mathsf d'$ and $64\mathsf d'\le\ell_g$ ($\mathsf d'\le6\mathsf d$, $r\le(\mathsf d/5LM)^2$, $\rho_0<Lr^{1/2}$, $\ell_g\ge2LMy_K\ge338$). The corners of the plaquettes of the near supports and of the piece are at least $\frac12\mathsf d'$ apart in the sup distance, so Lem.~\ref{C-352-39} holds with $\mathsf d'$ in the place of $\mathsf d$. Lem.~\ref{C-352-15} is used in its form (f), which bounds the crossing distance by $1$ in the place of the bound $e^{-2\sqrt3}$ of the placing: at the width $r$ and the crossing distance $\mathsf d_\times=\frac38\mathsf d'\in[6r,1]$, with the corners of the two kinds at least $\frac12\mathsf d'\ge\mathsf d_\times/\sqrt3$ apart, its conditions hold as in the proof of Lem.~\ref{C-352-39}. By the support rule (Lem.~\ref{C-352-12}(d)) a domain of the level $i+1$ that holds corners of both kinds has a linear size at least $D_{i+1}=[\mathsf d'/2Ma_{K-i-1}-2]_+$.

\emph{The tower.} Let $n_0\le i<K$, $A'\in\mathsf{Cc}_{i+1}(r_{i+1})$ and $\nu=\nu_{i,A'}$. The tower identity at several sources (step 1 of the proof of Prop.~\ref{C-352-21}; the two clusters, the near sources and the piece, lie in the frame at the level $n_0-1$, as $4M\rho_0\le\mathsf d'$), at the five partitions of $\{1,2,3\}$ and the two of $\{T,3\}$, with every $G_{i;\beta}$ taken at $A^{\mathrm{lw}}(B)$, gives
\[
\Gamma_{i+1}(A')=\int\Gamma_i\,\mathrm{d}\nu+\kappa_\nu(\Delta_i,G_{i;3})+\mathsf c\bigl[\kappa_\nu(G_{i;13},G_{i;2})+\kappa_\nu(G_{i;23},G_{i;1})+\kappa_\nu(G_{i;1},G_{i;2},G_{i;3})\bigr].
\]
As $A^{\mathrm{lw}}(B)\in\mathsf{Cc}_i(r_i)$ and $\nu$ is a probability measure, the mean is at most $\sup_{\mathsf{Cc}_i(r_i)}|\Gamma_i|$; as $\mathsf{Cc}_K(r_K)=\{0\}$, $|\Gamma_K(\mathbf 1)|=|\mathsf c\mathsf J_3-\mathsf J_2|$ is at most $\sup_{\mathsf{Cc}_{n_0}(r_{n_0})}|\Gamma_{n_0}|$ plus the sum over $n_0\le i<K$ of the suprema of the four cumulants.

\emph{The covariance of $\Delta$ and of the far source.} By the oscillations: the explicit parts of $\Delta_i$ cancel by the moment condition of step (iii) of the proof of Lem.~\ref{C-352-38}, and Lem.~\ref{C-352-38a} bounds the oscillation of $\Delta_i$ on $\mathsf{Cc}_i(r_i)$ by $2\varepsilon_\alpha r_i^2a_{K-i}^{-4}$; Lem.~\ref{C-352-16} and $|\mathsf{ang}^{[i]}_p|\le2\eta_i^2r_i$ bound that of $G_{i;3}$ by $C\mu_3r_i^2a_{K-i}^{-4}$; with $x_ir_i^2\le C\mathfrak b_i^2$ and $a_{K-i}x_i\ge\frac45\mathsf b$, $|\kappa_\nu(\Delta_i,G_{i;3})|\le C\varepsilon_\alpha\mathfrak b_i^4\mathsf b^{-2}a_{K-i}^{-6}\mu_3$. By the norms: $\kappa_\nu(\Delta_i,G_{i;3})$ is the value of $\mathsf{Sum}$ of the mixed second derivative of the step in the array of $\Delta_i$, of the size at most $Ca_{K-i}^{-4}$ (Lem.~\ref{C-352-12}, and Lem.~\ref{C-352-15} in the form (f)), and in the array of the far source; this family vanishes on the domains with $d_{i+1}(X)<D_{i+1}$, and Lem.~\ref{C-352-12}(b), the sizes of Lem.~\ref{C-352-15}(a), in the form (f), and Lem.~\ref{C-352-14}(b) give $|\kappa_\nu(\Delta_i,G_{i;3})|\le C\mathsf b^{-1}a_{K-i}^{-7}e^{-D_{i+1}}\mu_3$.

The smaller of the two bounds is at most their geometric mean, $C\varepsilon_\alpha^{1/2}\mathfrak b_i^2\mathsf b^{-3/2}a_{K-i}^{-13/2}e^{-D_{i+1}/2}\mu_3$; with $\mathfrak b_i=A_1y_i^{\mathfrak p_0}$ and $y_i\le\log(4\mathsf b/3a_{K-i})$ the sum over $i$ is led by the levels with $a_{K-i}$ about $\mathsf d'$ and gives the first term below.

\emph{The crossing terms.} $\kappa_\nu(G_{i;1},G_{i;2},G_{i;3})$ is the value of $\mathsf{Sum}$ of the third derivative of the step in the arrays of the three single sources, and $\kappa_\nu(G_{i;13},G_{i;2})$, $\kappa_\nu(G_{i;23},G_{i;1})$ are the values of $\mathsf{Sum}$ of its mixed second derivatives in the arrays of a crossing set and of a single source; these families vanish on the domains with $d_{i+1}(X)<D_{i+1}$. Lem.~\ref{C-352-12}(b) at $q=3$, the sizes of Lem.~\ref{C-352-15}(a), in the form (f), and Lem.~\ref{C-352-14}(b) give $\mathsf c|\kappa_\nu(G_{i;1},G_{i;2},G_{i;3})|\le C\mathsf c\,\bar\nu_{i;123}\varsigma_i^3e^{-D_{i+1}}\le C\mathsf b^{-1/2}r^3a_{K-i}^{-21/2}e^{-D_{i+1}}\mu_3$, the widths of the three sources being of the order of $r$; the two others are smaller, by a factor $\gamma_i$ (Lem.~\ref{C-352-15}(e), in the form (f)). The sum over $i$, led by the levels with $a_{K-i}$ about $\mathsf d'$, gives the second term below.

\emph{The start.} At the configurations of $\mathsf{Cc}_{n_0}(r_{n_0})$, whose pairs lie in the cores, 
\[
\Gamma_{n_0}=\sum_{i\le n_0}\mathsf{Sum}[\mathsf cE^{(i)}_{123}-E^{(i)}_{T3}];
\]
 the first display of Lem.~\ref{C-352-39}, with 
\[
\bar\nu_{i-1;\beta}\le\bar c_m(5L/4\mathsf b)^{m/2}a_{K-i}^{-m/2}\prod_{a\in\beta}|w_a|_\infty
\]
 and 
\[
e^{-D^\sharp_i/2}\le e\cdot e^{-\mathsf d'/4Ma_{K-i}},
\]
 summed over $i\le n_0$, where the quotient of two consecutive terms is at most $L^{3/2}e^{-(L-1)}<1$ as $4M\rho_0\le\mathsf d'$, gives 
\[
|\Gamma_{n_0}|\le C(\mathsf b/\rho_0)^{3/2}e^{-\mathsf d'/4M\rho_0}\mathsf b^{-2}\mathsf d'^{-6}\mu_3,
\]
 at most the third term below.

The result is
\[
\begin{multlined}
|\Gamma_K(\mathbf 1)|\le C\Bigl[\Bigl(\frac{\mathsf b}{\mathsf d'}\Bigr)^{1/2}\mathsf L_{\mathsf d'}\varepsilon_\alpha^{1/2}+\Bigl(\frac{\mathsf b}{\mathsf d'}\Bigr)^{3/2}\Bigl(\frac r{\mathsf d'}\Bigr)^3+\Bigl(\frac{\mathsf b}{\rho_0}\Bigr)^{3/2}e^{-\mathsf d'/8M\rho_0}\Bigr]\mathsf b^{-2}\mathsf d'^{-6}\mu_3,\qquad\mathsf L_{\mathsf d'}=\Bigl(1 \\
+\log^+\frac{\mathsf b}{\mathsf d'}\Bigr)^{2\mathfrak p_0},
\end{multlined}
\]
where $\varepsilon_\alpha\le C(g,\mathsf b)\epsilon$ is the number of Lem.~\ref{C-352-38a}. Then $\varepsilon_\alpha^{1/2}\le C(g,\mathsf b)[r^{\beta_{\mathrm H}/72}+(a_K/r)^{1/18}]$, $(r/\mathsf d')^3\le\mathsf d'^{-3}r^{\beta_{\mathrm H}/72}$, $e^{-s}\le2s^{-2}$ at $s=\mathsf d'/8M\rho_0$ with $\rho_0<Lr^{1/2}$, and $(1-\frac1{64})\mathsf d\le\mathsf d'\le6\mathsf d\le1$ give the claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Uniformity in the label]\label{C-352-41}
Let $0<g\le\gamma_{\mathrm R}$ and let $\mathcal K\subset(g^{-2},\bar{\mathsf b}]$ be compact. Then $C_{\mathrm A}(g,\mathsf b)$, $\mathsf C_{\mathrm R}(g,\mathsf b;\mathsf d)$ and $\mathsf C(\mathsf d)$ of Thm.~\ref{C-352-7} are bounded, and $r_\alpha(g,\mathsf b)$, $r_{\mathcal W}(g,\mathsf b,\mathsf d)$, $r_\sharp$, $r_0(\mathsf b)$, $r_1(\mathsf b)$ are bounded away from $0$, uniformly in $\mathsf b\in\mathcal K$; here $r_\sharp$ and $\mathsf C(\mathsf d)$ are the numbers that steps 2 and 3 of the proof of (E.3) form at a first-passage datum at $g$ with the label $\mathsf b$, for every $\mathsf b\in(g^{-2},\bar{\mathsf b}]$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\emph{The thresholds.} $r_1$ does not increase in $\mathsf b$, so $r_1(\mathsf b)\ge r_1(\bar{\mathsf b})>0$, and the infimum of $r_0$ over the labels at $g$ is positive by (B.1). The threshold $r_\alpha(g,\mathsf b)$ is the largest number below which the inequalities \textup{($\alpha$1)}--\textup{($\alpha$5)} of Def.~\ref{C-352-2}(5) hold, and the bound $r\le r_\alpha(g,\mathsf b)$ enters Lem.~\ref{C-352-38} and the lemma on the chain classes through these inequalities; by the bounds given there each of them holds as soon as $r$ is below a number formed from the constants and $g$, or, for \textup{($\alpha$3)}, below $2\min\{\inf_{\mathsf b'}r_0(\mathsf b'),r_1(\bar{\mathsf b})\}$; so $r_\alpha(g,\mathsf b)\ge r^-_\alpha(g)>0$ for every label at $g$. $r_{\mathcal W}(g,\mathsf b,\mathsf d)$ adds to $r_\alpha$ the inequalities of step 0 of the proof of (E.2), which depend on $\mathsf b$ only through $a_\sharp=4\mathsf b/5x_\sharp\ge4g^{-2}/5x_\sharp$; and $r_\sharp$ is the least of these thresholds and of those of the data. So all the thresholds are bounded below by positive numbers formed from the constants, $\beta_{\mathrm H}$, $g$ and $\mathsf d$, for all labels in $(g^{-2},\bar{\mathsf b}]$.

\emph{The constants.} The label enters the proofs of Lems.~\ref{C-352-38}--\ref{C-352-40} and of Thm.~\ref{C-352-7} through five kinds of quantities. (1) The run: by Lem.~\ref{C-352-10}(a), $\frac45\mathsf b\le a_{K-j}x_j\le\frac43\mathsf b$, so that $x_j$, $y_j$, $\delta_j$, $\varepsilon_j$, $\mathfrak b_j$, $\gamma_j=c_\gamma x_j^{-1/2}$, $\theta^{[j]}$ and $r_j$ lie between two functions of $\mathsf b/a_{K-j}$, each continuous in $\mathsf b$, and $\frac3{4\mathsf b}\le\upsilon_j\le\frac5{4\mathsf b}$. (2) The prefactor $\mathsf c=\frac{2\pi}3\mathsf br^3$ and the units $\mathsf u_a=\mathsf b^{-1}|w_a|_\infty$. (3) The slices, through $\mathsf b^{-1}$ and $\bar B/\mathsf b$ (Lem.~\ref{C-352-22}). (4) The number $a_\sharp=4\mathsf b/5x_\sharp$, through $a_*^{-1}\le L\max\{8M,5x_\sharp/4\mathsf b\}\ell_\epsilon/\mathsf d$. (5) The thresholds, bounded below as above.

Member by member: $\gamma_{n_0}\le c_\gamma(5Lr^{1/2}/4\mathsf b)^{1/2}$; $s(\frac r2)\theta^{[0]}$, with $x_0=\mathsf b/a_K$; $\sum_i\hat r_i^3\mathfrak b_i^2(\delta_i+\epsilon^{\mathrm{cu}}_i)\Lambda_i^2\mathsf h_i^2$, with $x_i\ge\frac45\mathsf b/a_{K-i}$, while $\Lambda_i\le C(1+Y_{r/2})$ and $\mathsf h_i\le C(1+Y_{r/2})^{2\mathfrak p_0}$ are formed with $g$ and $r$; the cost, at most $C\mathsf b\,r\,\mathrm{nat}^{\mathcal W}_n$, of the domains that leave the cube of the gauge, and the part of the steps between two levels, of the same order (proof of Lem.~\ref{C-352-38}); $y_{n_0}\le\log(4\mathsf b/3\rho_0)$; the bracket of the proof of Lem.~\ref{C-352-40}, through $(\mathsf b/\mathsf d')^{1/2}$, $(\mathsf b/\mathsf d')^{3/2}$, $(\mathsf b/\rho_0)^{3/2}$ and $\mathsf L_{\mathsf d'}$; the size $b_\Delta=(C\mathsf b+C)\Lambda_3$ of $\mathsf Y_\Delta$, the terms $T_1$--$T_4$ and the moments $\mathsf M_b$ of the proof of (E.2); the number $\epsilon_0(g,\mathsf b)$, the reciprocal of the constant in $\sum_i\epsilon^{\mathrm e}_i\le C(g,\mathsf b)\,\epsilon$; the quotients that form $\mathsf C_{\mathrm R}$; and the constant $C(\mathsf b,\mathsf d)$ of step 3 of the proof of (E.3).

Each majorant so formed is a sum of products of a factor that does not contain $\mathsf b$ and of a function of $\mathsf b$ made by finitely many products, powers, logarithms and maxima from $\mathsf b$, $\mathsf b^{-1}$, the constants, $\beta_{\mathrm H}$, $g$, $\mathsf d$ and the lower bounds of the thresholds; such a function is continuous on the compact interval $[g^{-2},\bar{\mathsf b}]$, where $g^{-2}\ge e^{2\mathfrak p_0}>1$, and so bounded there. Hence $C_{\mathrm A}(g,\mathsf b)$, $\mathsf C_{\mathrm R}(g,\mathsf b;\mathsf d)$ and $\mathsf C(\mathsf d)$ are bounded on all of $(g^{-2},\bar{\mathsf b}]$ by numbers formed from the constants, $\beta_{\mathrm H}$, $g$, $\mathsf d$ and $\mathsf d\operatorname{Lip}\varphi_1/\|\varphi_1\|_\infty$, in particular on $\mathcal K$.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Proofs of the theorems.}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Thm.~\ref{C-352-3}]
\emph{(B.2).} 1. \emph{The data.} By Lem.~\ref{C-352-11}(b) the tents put the pair in the frame at $k_0=\mathsf k(r)$; $(\Gamma1)$ gives $g\le\gamma_{\mathrm{jt}}$ and $g^{-2}\ge x_{\mathrm J}$, so Lem.~\ref{C-352-12} applies, with (P1)--(P3), and $\rho\le r_1(\mathsf b)$ gives $\rho\ge4Ma_K$ and $E_\sigma(\hat\rho_1/2)\le\varkappa_0^4$; the smallness holds at all heights (Lem.~\ref{C-352-10}(b)). At $n=K$, $A=0$ and both members vanish; let $\mathsf k(r)\le n<K$.

2. \emph{The decomposition.} Differentiate the defining formula for $D_n^\lambda$ twice: the source term is linear in $\lambda$, so $\mathsf F_n=\sum_{i\le n}\mathsf{Sum}[E^{(i)}_{12}]$; with Lem.~\ref{C-352-13} and $q_n=\sum_{i=\mathsf k(r)}^{n-1}\mathcal Q_i$, $q_{\mathsf k(r)}=0$,
\[
\mathsf F_n(\tilde U)-\mathsf F_n(\mathbf 1)-q_n(\mathsf{ang}^{[n]}(A))=\underbrace{\sum_{i=1}^{\mathsf k(r)}\Delta[E^{(i)}_{12}]}_{\mathrm I}+\underbrace{\sum_{j=\mathsf k(r)}^{n-1}\Delta[\mathsf R^{(j+1)}]}_{\mathrm{II}}+\underbrace{\sum_{i=\mathsf k(r)}^{n-1}\bigl(\Delta[\mathsf K^{(i+1)}]-\mathcal Q_i(\mathsf{ang}^{[n]}(A))\bigr)}_{\mathrm{III}} .
\]

3. \emph{The passage to the yardstick} $\mathsf Y_n=(\rho/r)^6\hat r_n^3\mathsf u_1\mathsf u_2$. For a pointed family $\mathsf f$ of level $j+1$ that vanishes off $\mathsf{Cr}_1$ and on the domains with $d_{j+1}(X)<D'$, with $\|\mathsf f\|\le\Phi\bar\nu_j$, Lem.~\ref{C-352-14}(a) in the frame at $k_0=\mathsf k(r)$ of step 1, $\bar\nu_j\le\frac{25}{16}\bar c_2x_j\mathsf u_1\mathsf u_2$, $x_j\le\frac53L^{n-j}x_n$ and $x_nr_n^2\le C\mathfrak b_n^2$ give
\[
|\Delta[\mathsf f]|\le C_{\mathrm U}\,\mathfrak b_n^2\,\mathsf N_{j+1}(w_1)\,\Phi\,u_j^{-3}e^{-D'/2}\,u_n^3\mathsf u_1\mathsf u_2 .
\]

4. \emph{I, the levels at and below the working level, are cut by the distance.} By the support rule $D'=\mathsf D(u_i)$; Lem.~\ref{C-352-15}(b) and (P2) give $\mathsf N_i\bar\Psi_{i-1;12}\le Cq^6(1+u_i^6)$; with $u_i=L^lu_{\mathsf k(r)}$ and $u_{\mathsf k(r)}/\sqrt3M\ge\frac4{\sqrt3}Y_r^{2\mathfrak p_0}$ the sum is led by $i=\mathsf k(r)$: $|\mathrm I|\le C\mathfrak b_n^2e^{-Y_r^{2\mathfrak p_0}/\sqrt3}\mathsf Y_n$.

5. \emph{II, the rest families.} Step 3 with $D'=0$ and Lem.~\ref{C-352-15}(c); $\mathsf N_{j+1}\varsigma_j^2u_j^{-3}\le216L^3q^6u_{j+1}^3$, $\mathsf N_{j+1}\Xi^r_ju_j^{-3}\le216q^6$, $\sum_{j<n}\gamma_j\le0.45\gamma_n\le C\delta_n/\mathfrak b_n$, and $u_{\mathsf k(r)}^3[\gamma_{\mathsf k(r)}+\theta^{[0]}]\le CY_r^{6\mathfrak p_0}\delta_{\mathsf k(r)}$, $\delta_{\mathsf k(r)}\le A_1Y_r^{\mathfrak p_0}(r/\mathsf b)^{1/2}$ (Lem.~\ref{C-352-10}(c)):
\[
|\mathrm{II}|\le\bigl\{C\mathfrak b_n\delta_n+C\mathfrak b_n^2Y_r^{7\mathfrak p_0}(r/\mathsf b)^{1/2}\bigr\}\mathsf Y_n .
\]

6. \emph{III, the kernel families.} Prop.~\ref{C-352-19}, narrow form; $\mathsf c_i\le Ce^{-\delta_{\mathrm{tp}}u_i/\sqrt3}$, so $\sum_i\mathsf c_i(1+u_i)^2u_i^3\le C$, and $\sum_{i\ge\mathsf k(r)}\mathfrak b_i^4\delta_iu_i^3\le1.12\,\mathfrak b_{\mathsf k(r)}^4u_{\mathsf k(r)}^3\delta_{\mathsf k(r)}$:
\[
|\mathrm{III}|\le\bigl\{CY_r^{15\mathfrak p_0+2}(r/\mathsf b)^{1/2}+C\mathfrak b_n^2r_n\bigr\}\mathsf Y_n .
\]

7. \emph{The sum.} $\mathfrak b_n\le\mathfrak b_{\mathsf k(r)}\le A_1Y_r^{\mathfrak p_0}$, $r_n\le\frac85\mathsf c_{\mathfrak h}\delta_n$ and $(r/\mathsf b)^{1/2}\le g\,r^{1/2}$ give the bound. The factor $(\rho/r)^6$ costs nothing: $\mathsf F_n$ is bilinear in $(w_1,w_2)$, every estimate depends on the weights only through $\sum_p|w_a(p)|$ or through a norm that (P1) bounds, and the one place where a sup norm could enter, $\Lambda_i$, sees a quotient (Prop.~\ref{C-352-19}, step 6). By Lem.~\ref{C-352-10}(c), $\log\frac1r\le Y_r\le2\log\frac1r+C(g)$, whence $\epsilon'_{\mathrm N}(r)(\log\frac1r)^N\to0$.

\emph{(B.1).} 1. Lem.~\ref{C-352-11}(a) and its proof put the test pair in all six conditions of Def.~\ref{def:pair-functional-frame} at $k_0=\max\{K-s,2\}$, under $3\le s\le K$ and $\mathsf{Lm}_s\le L^{s-3}$, as required in (B.1); there the number $\theta^{[j]}/K_{\mathbf M}$ of every step is at most half of the largest value that the one-step theorem admits, $\hat r_{k_0}\ge M$, so $\varsigma_i=1$ for $i\le k_0$, and $\mathsf D^{12}_i\ge\hat r_i/\sqrt3-1$. 2. Below $k_0$, Prop.~\YMMref{122.2}{827} gives $\|E^{(j)}_{12}\|\le C\nu_{j-1}$, with $\nu_j$ defined in {\cite[eq.~199]{YMM2}}; its running, half-ceiling and separation hypotheses are those verified in the pair frame of Lem.~\ref{C-352-11}(a); from $k_0$ on, Lem.~\ref{C-352-12}(b), (c) and the start at $k_0$ give the rest families with $\|\mathsf R^{(j+1)}\|_{j+1,\lambda_{\mathrm{out}}}\le\epsilon^{(2)}_j\varsigma_j\bar\nu_j$,
\[
\epsilon^{(2)}_j\le C\bigl[x_j^{-1/2}(1+\mathsf e_\downarrow)+\theta^{[k_0]}\bigr],\qquad\mathsf e_\downarrow=\sum_{i\le k_0}e^{-4\beta_{\mathrm s}\kappa[\mathsf D^{12}_i/M-2]_+}\varkappa_{i-1}^{-2}:
\]
no number in it grows with $\log\frac1r$ or with $n-k_0$, as the derivatives of the step gain the factor $1/\mathfrak b_j$ per order in the sources (Lem.~\ref{C-352-12}(b)) and the lags of Lem.~\ref{C-352-12}(c) fall like $L^{-4l}$ and sum geometrically over the levels. 3. The decomposition of step 2 above, over the base level $k_0$, with Lem.~\ref{C-352-14}(a), in the frame at $k_0$, for I and II and Prop.~\ref{C-352-19} at the test pair for III, both in the form stated after them, whose conditions are the frame, the smallness at the heights concerned ($2r_n\le\varrho_{\mathrm{ch}}$, so that $r_n\le\frac1{120}$ as $\varrho_{\mathrm{ch}}\le\frac1{60}$; $\epsilon^{\mathrm{cu}}_i\le1$; $x_n^{-1}\le r_n^2$) and the side bound $\ell\ge2LMy_K$: for a test pair at $k_0=\max\{K-s,2\}$ these hold for $g\le\min\{\gamma_{\mathrm{jt}},\gamma_{\mathrm O}\}$ and $r\le r_0(\mathsf b)$, the frame by Lem.~\ref{C-352-11}(a), the side bound as $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$, and the smallness at the heights $\ge k_0$ being among the conditions that fix $\gamma_{\mathrm O}$ and $r_0(\mathsf b)$.

The shape $\vartheta$ does not enter, since any $\bar{\mathsf e}\ge2\mathsf w_1\mathsf w_2\mathsf E_i$ is admissible. 4. In the yardstick $\hat r_n^3\mathsf u_1\mathsf u_2$ the main part of II is $\le C\mathfrak b_n^2[\gamma_n(1+\mathsf e_\downarrow)+(n-k_0)\theta^{[k_0]}]$, III is $\le C\hat r_{k_0}^3\mathfrak b_{k_0}^4(\delta_{k_0}+\epsilon^{\mathrm{cu}}_{k_0})\Lambda^2\mathsf h^2+C\mathfrak b_n^2r_n$, by the bound $\mathsf E_i\le C_{\mathsf E}\delta_i^4(\delta_i+\epsilon^{\mathrm{cu}}_i)$ of Prop.~\ref{C-352-19}, and I is $\le C\mathfrak b_n^2e^{-c'Y_s^{2\mathfrak p_0}}$. With $\theta^{[k_0]}\le C(r/\mathsf b)^{1/2}y_{k_0}^{\mathfrak p_0}$, $K-k_0\le s\le Cy_{k_0}$ and $\mathsf e_\downarrow\le Cy_{k_0}^{2\mathfrak p_0}e^{-c'Y_s^{2\mathfrak p_0}}$, and the smallness that the recursions need holding for $g\le\gamma_{\mathrm O}$ and $r\le r_0(\mathsf b)$, this is the bound of (B.1); its last term $C\mathfrak b_n^2r_n\le C\mathfrak b_n^2\delta_n$ is the price of writing the form with the linear angles of one chart. 5.

The conditions that fix $r_0(\mathsf b)$ depend on $\mathsf b$ through $(r/\mathsf b)^{1/2}$, through $y_{k_0}\le\log\frac{\mathsf b}r+C\log\log\frac{\mathsf b}r$ and through $x_{k_0}\le\frac{24}{23}\mathsf b\hat r_{k_0}/r$; on $(g^{-2},\bar{\mathsf b}]$ these are bounded by their values at the two ends, so $r_0$ has a positive infimum over the labels at $g$.

\emph{(B.3).} $|\mathsf{ang}^{[n]}_p(A)|\le2\eta_n^2r_n$, Lem.~\ref{C-352-22}(a) with $\mathsf r\ge r/\sqrt3$, and (P1):
\[
|q_n(\mathsf{ang}^{[n]}(A))|\le C\,r_n^2\,\mathsf b\,a_{K-n}^{-4}\rho^6r^{-3}\mathsf u_1\mathsf u_2=C\,r_n^2\,\mathsf b\,a_{K-n}^{-1}(\rho/r)^6\hat r_n^3\mathsf u_1\mathsf u_2\le C\mathfrak b_n^2(\rho/r)^6\hat r_n^3\mathsf u_1\mathsf u_2,
\]
as $\mathsf b\,a_{K-n}^{-1}\le\frac54x_n$ and $x_nr_n^2\le C\mathfrak b_n^2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Thm.~\ref{C-352-4}]
1. \emph{(A.1).} Prop.~\ref{C-352-24}(a) bounds $\mathsf J_3$ against the lattice ring ($64\mathsf d\le\ell_g$ as $\ell_g\ge26$ and $\mathsf d\le e^{-34}$; $\rho\le r_1(\mathsf b)$ by $\mathsf d\le\mathsf d_4(g)\le r_1(\bar{\mathsf b})\le r_1(\mathsf b)$), and Lem.~\ref{C-352-26} bounds $S^T_3-\mathsf J_3$ by $13\Lambda_3^3\mathsf M'^3\mathsf b^3\mathsf d^{3/2}\mathrm{nat}_3$ (all supports lie within $20\mathsf d\le\frac18\ell_g-1$ of $x_1$).

2. \emph{The geometry of (A.2).} For a triple $(z_1,z_2,z_3)=(x,y,z)$ of $\mathcal D$ put $r=\frac12r_*$, $\mathsf d=\frac12\mathsf d_*$; bumps $f_a$ with supports in balls of radius $\rho<\min\{\frac14r_*,r_1(\bar{\mathsf b})\}$ inside the open balls of radius $\frac14r_*$ about the $z_a$ are placed at $(\rho,r,\mathsf d)$: their supports are $\ge r_*-\frac12r_*=r$ apart in the pair and $\ge\mathsf d_*-\frac12r_*\ge\mathsf d$ across, with $|x_1-x_2|\le3r$, $|x_a-x_3|\le5\mathsf d$, all in $\mathbb B(z_1,\frac94\mathsf d_*)$; this holds for every ratio $r_*/\mathsf d_*\in(0,1]$, and $\mathsf d_*\le\mathsf d_5(g)$ gives $\mathsf d\le\mathsf d_4(g)$.

3. \emph{Lattice to continuum.} Lem.~\ref{C-352-27}(a) with $\mathsf d^+=5\mathsf d_*$ and a Lipschitz number $\vartheta$ of the $f_a$:
\[
|3\operatorname{Tr}\prod_a((f_a\circ x)\mathsf b^{-1}C^{\mathrm{free}}_K)-3\mathsf b^{-3}\!\int k_3\prod f_a|\le3C^{(3)}\bigl[a_K/\vartheta\rho+(5\mathsf d_*/\ell_g)^3\bigr]\mathrm{nat}_3 .
\]

4. \emph{The limit.} Along first-passage data with $K_j\to\infty$ and labels $\to\mathsf b$, $S^T_3(f)\to S^{(\ell_g,\mathsf b)}_3(f)$ (Thm.~\YMMref{A}{5}), $a_{K_j}/\vartheta\rho\to0$, and the brackets are bounded with $\bar{\mathsf b}$ and $\bar{\mathsf M}^{(24)}$ (Lem.~\ref{C-352-25}(e)); with $r^{-3}\mathsf d^{-6}=512\,r_*^{-3}\mathsf d_*^{-6}$ this is the bound of the form in (A.2).

5. \emph{Kernels.} Lem.~\ref{C-352-28}(a) on $\prod_aU_a$, with $(\frac3\pi)^3\le1$: a Borel kernel, bounded at its Lebesgue points by the bound of the form at the centre; the cover of $\mathcal D$ by such products and the glueing of Lem.~\ref{C-352-35} give one kernel on $\mathcal D$; the closest pair of a triple is $(x,y)$ after a relabelling. \emph{(A.3)} is Lem.~\ref{C-352-28}(b).

6. \emph{(A.4).} (i) is Prop.~\ref{C-352-33}(a) at $n=3$. (ii) For a triple with $\mathsf d_*\le\mathsf d_5(g)$, the bumps of Lem.~\ref{C-352-34}(c) about it are in the data of (i) at every large $j$ (the cube of side $\frac92\mathsf d_*\le\frac12\ell_g$ about $x$ holds them, so the projection keeps all distances and the integrals of $k_3$); (i), step 4 at the label $\mathsf b$, and $S^T_3[\nu_j]\to S^{\sigma'}_3$ give $|\int(\mathsf s_3-3\mathsf b^{-3}k_3)\prod f^\rho_a|\le[\epsilon_{\mathrm A}+512C^{\mathrm{tr}3}_3\mathsf b^3\mathsf d_*^{3/2}]\mathsf b^{-3}r_*^{-3}\mathsf d_*^{-6}\cdot0.102\le\mathsf E_3(g,\mathsf d_*)\mathsf b^{-3}r_*^{-3}\mathsf d_*^{-6}$, and Lem.~\ref{C-352-34}(c) gives the bound at the point. (iii) is Lem.~\ref{C-352-34}(a).

7. \emph{(A.5).} Let $(K_j,\beta_j,\nu_j)$ be a Gibbs sequence at $g_0$; its members are periodic Gibbs states, $\nu_j\in\mathcal G^{\mathrm{per}}_{K_j,\beta_j}$. For large $j$, $\beta_j$ exceeds $L(g^{-2}+B_\sharp)$; let $K'_j$ be the first-passage index of $\beta_j$ at $g$ and $z_j=K_j-K'_j$; as $g\le g_0$, $0\le z_j\le z_+$ with $z_+$ formed from $g_0$, $g$ and the constants. (1) \emph{The states.} For $0\le z<K$ the dilation $U\mapsto U^{(z)}$, $U^{(z)}(L^zb)=U(b)$, maps the bonds, the plaquettes and the finite sets of bonds of $\mathbb L_K$ onto those of $\mathbb L_{K-z}$, with $a_{L^zp}(U^{(z)})=a_p(U)$. The Gibbs kernel of a finite set of bonds has the exponent $-\beta\sum_pa_p$ over the plaquettes that contain a bond of the set, which reads $\beta$ and the lattice and not its spacing; so the image $\nu^{(z)}$ of a Gibbs state at $(a_K,\beta)$ satisfies the equations of the kernels at $(a_{K-z},\beta)$, and invariance under a subgroup $\Gamma'$ of finite index of $a_K\mathbb Z^3$ becomes invariance under $L^z\Gamma'$, of finite index in $a_{K-z}\mathbb Z^3$.

So the dilation carries $\mathcal G^{\mathrm{per}}_{K,\beta}$ onto $\mathcal G^{\mathrm{per}}_{K-z,\beta}$ (equation~\YMMref{(1819)}{698} and the definition of periodic states following it), and $\nu^{(z_j)}_j$ is a periodic Gibbs state at the first-passage datum $(K'_j,\beta_j)$ at $g$, with the label $L^{z_j}a_{K_j}\beta_j$. (2) \emph{The fields.} At every configuration $U$ of $\mathbb L_K$, $x(L^zp)=L^zx(p)$ and $a_{K-z}=L^za_K$ give $\mathcal O(f)(U)=L^z\mathcal O'(f^{(z)})(U^{(z)})$, $f^{(z)}=f(L^{-z}\cdot)$, the prime marking the field at the cutoff $K-z$, as in Lem.~\ref{C-352-36}(d), which is the dilation; so in every law $\nu$ on $\mathbb L_K$, $S^T_3[\nu](f)=L^{3z}S^T_3[\nu^{(z)}](f^{(z)})$. (3) \emph{The approximants} of a component of a canonical decomposition of the limit are periodic Gibbs states at the same data, by the definition of the components and their approximants in Lem.~\ref{C-352-34}(a); (1) and (2) apply to them. (4) \emph{The limit.} On a subsequence $z_j=z$ is constant and the labels converge, to $\mathsf b_0$ say; along it $S^T_3[\nu^{(z)}_j](f)=L^{-3z}S^T_3[\nu_j](f(L^z\cdot))\to L^{-3z}S^\sigma_3(f(L^z\cdot))$ on separated triples, $\sigma$ the limit, and this functional has the continuous kernel $\mathsf s^{(z)}_3=L^{-12z}\mathsf s_3(L^{-z}\cdot)$; likewise for a component and its approximants.

The proof of (A.4)(ii) uses of the law $\sigma'$ the convergence $S^T_3[\nu_j]\to S^{\sigma'}_3$ on separated triples and the continuity of the kernel of $S^{\sigma'}_3$ at the triple (Lem.~\ref{C-352-34}(c)); so (A.4)(ii) at $g$ applies to the dilated sequence, whose labels tend to $L^z\mathsf b_0$, at the triples with $L^z\mathsf d_*\le\mathsf d_5(g)$. In kernels $\mathsf s_3(x)=L^{12z}\mathsf s^{(z)}_3(L^zx)$, and the natural size is invariant: $L^{12z}(L^z\mathsf b_0)^{-3}(L^zr_*)^{-3}(L^z\mathsf d_*)^{-6}=\mathsf b_0^{-3}r_*^{-3}\mathsf d_*^{-6}$, $k_3(L^z\cdot)=L^{-9z}k_3$. The approximants of a component are periodic Gibbs states at the same couplings and are dilated alike.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Thm.~\ref{C-352-5}]
1. \emph{(C.1).} At $x,y=c\pm\frac r2n$: $r_*=r$; the two distances $|c-z\pm\frac r2n|$ lie in $[\mathsf d-\frac r2,\mathsf d+\frac r2]$ and the sum of their squares is $2\mathsf d^2+\frac12r^2$, so $\mathsf d_*\in[\frac34\mathsf d,\frac{17}{16}\mathsf d]$, $r\le\mathsf d_*\le\mathsf d_5(g)$. (A.2) multiplied by $\frac{2\pi}3\mathsf br^3$ gives $\frac{2\pi}3(\frac43)^6\le12$ times $\bar\epsilon_{\mathrm A}\mathsf b^{-2}\mathsf d^{-6}$, and Lem.~\ref{C-352-29}(c) gives $2.66\le2.7$; ``almost everywhere'' is in $(c,h,z)$, a linear change of the variables $(x,y,z)$. (ii) (A.3) at every triple; $k_3$ is continuous off the diagonals, so its means tend to its values; with tents, (A.3) in the tent form and the second part of Lem.~\ref{C-352-29}(c). (iii) (A.4)(ii) at every triple and Lem.~\ref{C-352-29}(c).

2. \emph{(C.2)(i).} Prop.~\ref{C-352-24}(b) bounds $\mathsf J_2$; Lem.~\ref{C-352-26} at two sources gives \[
 |S^T_2-\mathsf J_2|\le3\Lambda_3^2\mathsf M'^2\mathsf b^2\mathsf d^{3/2}(\rho/\mathsf d)^6\mathsf b^{-2}|w_1|_\infty|w_2|_\infty
\]; at the plane weights $w_1=\mathbf 1_{\{\lambda(p)=\lambda\}}\varphi_1\circ x$, $w_2=\mathbf 1_{\{\lambda(p)=\mu\}}\varphi_2\circ x$, Lem.~\ref{C-352-27}(c) turns the lattice square into $\mathcal K_{\lambda\mu}$ ($8a_K\le\rho$ by $s(\rho)\le K$; the assumption $|x_1-x_2|\le18\mathsf d$ is the one that this step and the rings need).

3. \emph{(C.2)(ii).} For $(x_0,y_0)\in\Omega_{\mathrm P}$ and bounded Borel $f,h$ supported in the closed balls of radius $\frac18\mathsf d_0$ about $x_0,y_0$, the jets, the remainder, $|C^{\mathrm{free}}_K(p,q)|\le(1+3C_{\mathrm{lat}})a_K^3|u|^{-3}$ and the count of plaquettes give
\[
|\langle\mathcal O_\lambda(f);\mathcal O_\mu(h)\rangle_{K_j,\ell_g,\beta_j}|\le\mathsf B(g,\mathsf d_0)\|f\|_\infty\|h\|_\infty,\qquad\mathsf B=4^{-6}g^4\bigl[\tfrac32\cdot729(1+3C_{\mathrm{lat}})^2+\mathsf E_2(g,\tfrac12\mathsf d_0)\bigr],
\]
with no Lipschitz number (the Riemann sums of step 2 involve $a_K/\vartheta\rho$ and give no bound in the sup norms). Lem.~\ref{C-352-35} gives one subsequence for all pairs of balls; along it step 2, with $a_{K_j}/\vartheta\rho\to0$, gives the bump form at every centre: the balls of radius $\frac18\mathsf d_0$ are $\ge\frac12\mathsf d_0=:\mathsf d$ apart, $|x_1-x_2|\le\frac52\mathsf d$, and $(\rho/\mathsf d)^6=64(\rho/\mathsf d_0)^6$. Lem.~\ref{C-352-28} at $p=2$ gives the kernels and the almost everywhere bound, and Lem.~\ref{C-352-29}(a) gives $t_\lambda-\mathsf t^\circ(e_\lambda,\cdot)=\sum_\mu(\delta_{\lambda\mu}-\frac13\sum_{\lambda'}\delta_{\lambda'\mu})$ with $\delta_{\lambda\mu}=\tau_{\lambda\mu}-\frac32\mathsf b^{-2}[\mathbb K_{3,\lambda\mu}]^2$: three terms and a third of nine, so the factor $6$.

4. \emph{(C.3).} Along the subsequence of the limit point $S^T_3\to S^{(\ell_g,\mathsf b)}_3$, since that limit is taken along all data with labels $\to\mathsf b$. By (A.3) and by Lem.~\ref{C-352-28}(b) applied to the bump form of (C.2)(ii) at the centre $(c,z)$, the means over balls of radius $\rho$ of $\mathsf s_3-3\mathsf b^{-3}k_3$ and of $\tau_{\lambda\mu}-\frac32\mathsf b^{-2}[\mathbb K_{3,\lambda\mu}]^2$ are bounded at every centre, with the factors $(\frac3{4\pi})^3,(\frac3{4\pi})^2\le1$; $k_3$ and $[\mathbb K_3]^2$ are continuous off the diagonals; adding with Lem.~\ref{C-352-29}(a), (c) gives the display, and the tents likewise. The cone form: (C.1)(i) at $n$, (C.2)(ii) at $(c,z)$ almost everywhere (a null set of $(c,z)$ is a null set of $(c,h,z)$), and $|\mathsf t^\circ(n,X)-\mathsf t^\circ(e_\lambda,X)|\le0.057|n-e_\lambda|\mathsf b^{-2}|X|^{-6}$.

5. \emph{(C.4).} (d) is Prop.~\ref{C-352-33}(b) with step 2 on the least torus (the projection is injective and keeps distances on $\mathbb B(x_0,\frac32\mathsf d_0)$, so the integrals and the norms are those of the periodised functions); it gives the bound $\mathsf B(g,\mathsf d_0)$ of step 3 along $\nu_j$ for $j$ large. (a) Lem.~\ref{C-352-35} on $\Omega_\sigma$. (b) The bump form at every centre of $\Omega_\sigma$ with $64\mathsf E_2(g,\frac12\mathsf d_0)\mathsf b^{-2}\mathsf d_0^{-6}\rho^6$; Lem.~\ref{C-352-28}; the bound at a point by centres $\zeta_m\to(x,y)$ of distances $\mathsf d_{\zeta_m}<|x-y|$, whence the supremum in $\epsilon_\sigma$. Every $\nu_j$ is invariant under the translations of $\mathbb L_{K_j}$ by Prop.~\YMMref{103.4}{758}, so the limit forms are invariant under all translations, and by Fubini's theorem $\tau^\sigma_{\lambda\mu}(x,y)$ is a function of $x-y$ almost everywhere. $\sum_{\lambda,\mu}\langle\mathcal O_\lambda;\mathcal O_\mu\rangle=S^T_2$, which converges along the whole sequence to $S^{\sigma'}_2$ with the continuous kernel $\mathsf s^T_2$; with Lem.~\ref{C-352-29}(a) this gives the bound of $\mathsf s^T_2$ almost everywhere, and at every point by continuity, $\epsilon_\sigma(g,\cdot)$ being nondecreasing. (c) Let $\mathcal N$ be the union of the null sets of (b); it is fixed before $r$ is named.

Off $\mathcal N$, (b) and Lem.~\ref{C-352-29}(a) give $|t^\sigma_\lambda-\mathsf t^\circ(e_\lambda,\cdot)|\le6(\frac3\pi)^2\epsilon_\sigma\mathsf b^{-2}\mathsf d^{-6}\le6\epsilon_\sigma\mathsf b^{-2}\mathsf d^{-6}$, and (C.1)(iii) at $n=e_\lambda$ holds at every point, since $\mathsf s_3$ is continuous; $12\sup\mathsf E_3+6\epsilon_\sigma=\epsilon'_\sigma$. With tents of radius $\rho<\frac18\mathsf d$ at $(c,z)$: the bump form of (b) at the centre $(c,z)$, and Lem.~\ref{C-352-29}(d) times $\frac32$, six times, give $21\rho/\mathsf d$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Thm.~\ref{C-352-6}]
1. \emph{(D.1) below $\gamma_{\mathrm N}$} is Prop.~\ref{C-352-37}. 2. \emph{(D.1) at every $g\le\gamma$.} Let $z,g'_1,g'_2$ be as in Lem.~\ref{C-352-36} and $K_\circ(g)=z+\max_\iota s'_\iota(r_{g'_\iota})$. For $K\ge K_\circ(g)$, $(K-z,\beta)$ is a first-passage datum at some $g'_\iota\le\gamma_{\mathrm N}$, on the side $L^z\ell\in\mathfrak L(g'_\iota)$, and the conditions of Prop.~\ref{C-352-37} hold at $(L^zr,L^z\mathsf d')$; by Lem.~\ref{C-352-36}(d) each display at $(K,\ell,\beta)$ is that display at $(K-z,L^z\ell,\beta)$. So (D.1) holds with
\[
\epsilon^{\mathrm{cl}}(g,\ell,\mathsf d')=\max_{\iota=1,2}\epsilon^{\mathrm{ev}}_\sharp(g'_\iota,L^z\ell,L^z\mathsf d'),\qquad\mathsf d_{\mathrm{cl}}(g)=\tfrac76L^{-z}\min_\iota t_{\mathrm N}(g'_\iota),
\]
a finite function of $(g,\ell,\mathsf d')$, with the rate for $\mathsf d'\le\mathsf d_{\mathrm{cl}}(g)$. On the dilated torus, at the distance $L^z\mathsf d'$, the members of $\epsilon^{\mathrm{ev}}_\sharp$ that carry the renormalisation group, the remainder and the induction, read the distances through the floor $\min\{\frac67L^z\mathsf d',t_{\mathrm N}(g'_\iota)\}$ alone; the largest distance $\frac87L^z\mathsf d'$ enters the one explicit member, the comparison of the sum of the slices with the free kernel (Lem.~\ref{C-352-22}(b)), which is polynomial in that distance; and the passage from the floor to $L^z\mathsf d'$ costs the factor $\max\{1,6L^z\mathsf d'/7t_{\mathrm N}(g'_\iota)\}^6$ of $\epsilon^{\mathrm{ev}}_\sharp$ (proof of Prop.~\ref{C-352-37}). 3.

\emph{(D.2).} The forms are bounded in the sup norms at every pair of small balls in $\Omega^\circ$, as in step 3 of the proof of Thm.~\ref{C-352-5}; Lem.~\ref{C-352-35} gives one subsequence for the plane and the bond forms; (D.1) with $a_{K_j}/\vartheta r\to0$ gives the bump forms at every centre; Lem.~\ref{C-352-28}, with centres in the window $[\frac79t,\frac97t]$ and $(\frac3\pi)^2(\frac97)^6\le4.2$, gives the kernels. For $T_n$: the kernel of $\langle T_\lambda;\mathcal O\rangle$ is within $3(4.2+4.2)\bar\epsilon^{\mathrm{cl}}=25.2\,\bar\epsilon^{\mathrm{cl}}$ of $\mathsf t^\circ(e_\lambda,\cdot)$, that of $\langle\mathcal O^{\mathrm{od}}_{\lambda\lambda'};\mathcal O\rangle=\sum_\gamma\langle\mathcal O^{\mathrm{od}}_{\lambda\lambda'};\mathcal O_\gamma\rangle$ within $12.6\,\bar\epsilon^{\mathrm{cl}}$ of $3\mathsf b^{-2}[\mathbb K_3^2]_{\lambda\lambda'}$; with $\sum_\lambda n_\lambda^2=1$, $\sum_{\lambda<\lambda'}|n_\lambda n_{\lambda'}|\le1$ and Lem.~\ref{C-352-29}(a), $25.2+12.6\le38$.

The kernel $t_n$ is a quadratic polynomial in $n$ whose coefficients are the nine kernels, so one null set serves all $n$. 4. \emph{(D.3)} is (C.1) and (D.2) by the triangle inequality: almost everywhere in $(c,h,z)$ by Fubini's theorem; for the means and the tents, the bump forms of (D.1) at the centre $(c,z)$ itself, extended to indicators of balls by Lem.~\ref{C-352-28}(b), bound the means of the kernels with factors below those of the almost everywhere bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Thm.~\ref{C-352-7}]
\emph{(E.2).} 0. \emph{The stopping level.} Let $\epsilon=r^{\beta_{\mathrm H}/36}+(a_K/r)^{1/9}$, $\ell_\epsilon=\max\{1,\log\frac1\epsilon\}$, $a^\flat=\min\{\mathsf d/8M\ell_\epsilon,a_\sharp\}$ with $a_\sharp=4\mathsf b/5x_\sharp$, so that $a_{K-n}\le a_\sharp$ gives $x_n\ge x_\sharp$ (Lem.~\ref{C-352-10}(a)), $n_*$ the largest level with $a_{K-n_*}\le a^\flat$, and $a_*=a_{K-n_*}\in(a^\flat/L,a^\flat]$. The conditions that define $r_{\mathcal W}(g,\mathsf b,\mathsf d)$, namely $r\le\min\{r_\alpha,(\mathsf d/5LM)^2,e^{-1}\}$, $8ML^{m_1+2}r^{1/2}(1+\log\frac1r)\le\mathsf d$, $L^{m_1+2}r^{1/2}\le a_\sharp$ and $r^{-1/4}\ge2M$, secure $N_0<n_*$, $x_{n_*}\ge x_\sharp$ and $L^{N_0-n_1}\ge2M$, as $L^{N_0-n_1}=L^{m_1}a_{K-n_0}/a_{K-n_1}\ge r^{-1/4}$ (so Lem.~\ref{C-352-38} holds with $n^\sharp=n_*$ when $\epsilon^{\mathrm e}_i\le1$), $8Ma_*\le\mathsf d$, $e^{-\mathsf d/4Ma_*}\le\epsilon^2$ and $a_*^{-1}\le C\ell_\epsilon/\mathsf d$.

1. \emph{The identity.} Lem.~\ref{C-352-25}(c) at $k=n_*$, $\mathbb P_*=\mathbb P_{n_*}$, for the two lists, $G_3$ being the same function in both:
\[
\begin{multlined}
\mathsf cS^T_3(w_1,w_2,w_3)-S^T_2(w_T,w_3)=\int\Gamma\,\mathrm{d}\mathbb P_*+\kappa_{\mathbb P_*}(\Delta,G_3)+\mathsf c[\kappa_{\mathbb P_*}(G_{13},G_2)+\kappa_{\mathbb P_*}(G_{23},G_1)] \\
+\mathsf c\,\kappa_{\mathbb P_*}(G_1,G_2,G_3)=:T_1+T_2+T_3+T_4,
\end{multlined}
\]
with $\Delta$, $\Gamma$, $G_\beta$ taken at $U_{t'}(W)$.

2. \emph{Sizes.} $r^3|w_{1,2}|_\infty\le489$, $|w_T|_\infty\le\frac23|w_1|_\infty$, $\mathsf c|w_1|_\infty|w_2|_\infty r^3\le C\mathsf b$, $|w_3|_\infty\le\mu_3r^{-3}$; the bounds of Lem.~\ref{C-352-26} hold at every point of the small-field region, as their proof uses of $W$ only that the background is regular.

3. \emph{$T_1$, $T_3$: the crossings.} At $t'\le n_*$, $8Ma_{K-t'}\le\mathsf d$, and Lem.~\ref{C-352-39} with $e^{-\mathsf d/4Ma_*}\le\epsilon^2$ gives $|T_1|\le C(\mathsf b)a_*^{-3/2}\mathsf d^{-6}\epsilon^2\mu_3$ and $|T_3|\le Ca_*^{-1}r^3\mathsf d^{-6}\epsilon^2\mu_3\mathsf M_6$, $\mathsf M_b=\int\alpha^{-b}d\mathbb P_*$: no negative power of $r$ is left.

4. \emph{$T_4$.} $|T_4|\le C\mathsf br^3\Lambda_3^3\mathsf M_{18}\mu_3$.

5. \emph{$T_2$: pair minus tensor field.} $T_2=\int(\Delta-\mathsf c_{n_*})(G_3-\int G_3)d\mathbb P_*$, and $|G_3-\int G_3|\le\Lambda_3\mu_3(\alpha^{-6}+\mathsf M_6)$ by step 2. On the parts with $t'\ge N_0$ each measure is absolutely continuous with respect to $\mathsf m_{t'}$, and Lem.~\ref{C-352-38} gives $|\Delta-\mathsf c_{n_*}|\le3.01\,\tilde\varepsilon\,\alpha^{-4}$ almost everywhere. The number $\mathsf c_{n_*}$: the first part of $\mathbb P_*$, on which $t'=n_*$ and $\alpha=a_*$, has positive mass, as the density of $\mathsf m_{n_*}$ on $\mathcal V_{n_*}^\chi$
is a positive exponential by {\cite[eq.~224]{YMM2}} and
{\cite[eq.~225]{YMM2}}. This region is open, its defining
tests are strict, and they hold at the trivial field, where all
curvature and fluctuation defects vanish. It therefore has positive
Haar measure; at almost every point of it $|\Delta-\mathsf c_{n_*}|\le\varepsilon^{\mathcal W}a_*^{-4}$ (Lem.~\ref{C-352-38}) and $|\mathsf Y_\Delta|=|\Delta-\Delta_K(\mathbf 1)|\le b_\Delta a_*^{-6}$, $b_\Delta=(C\mathsf b+C)\Lambda_3$ (Lem.~\ref{C-352-26} at every point, step 2), so that $|\mathsf c_{n_*}-\Delta_K(\mathbf 1)|\le(\varepsilon^{\mathcal W}+b_\Delta)a_*^{-6}$.

On the parts with $t'<N_0$, $\alpha<a_{K-N_0}=L^{m_1}a_{K-n_0}<L^{m_1+1}r^{1/2}<a_*$, so that there $|\Delta-\mathsf c_{n_*}|\le|\mathsf Y_\Delta|+|\Delta_K(\mathbf 1)-\mathsf c_{n_*}|\le(2b_\Delta+\varepsilon^{\mathcal W})\alpha^{-6}$ and $\mathsf M_6\le(1+\mathsf M')\alpha^{-6}$; and $\int_{\{\alpha<\varrho\}}\alpha^{-12}d\mathbb P_*\le\varrho^{12}\mathsf M'$ (Lem.~\ref{C-352-25}(e)) at $\varrho=a_{K-N_0}$ gives a factor $Cr^6$.

6. \emph{Together.} $\mathsf M_b\le a_*^{-b}+\mathsf M'\le C(g,\mathsf b)\ell_\epsilon^b\mathsf d^{-b}$, $\epsilon^{1/2}\ell_\epsilon^{10}\le C$ and $r^{3-\beta_{\mathrm H}/72}(1+\log\frac1r)^{18}\le C$ give $|\mathsf cS^T_3-S^T_2|\le C_{\mathrm A}(g,\mathsf b)\mathsf d^{-18}[r^{\beta_{\mathrm H}/72}+(a_K/r)^{1/18}]\mu_3$. If the smallness $\epsilon^{\mathrm e}_i\le1$ of the single-source arrays of the near pair, which Lem.~\ref{C-352-38} asks at the levels $\mathsf k(\frac r2)\le i<n_1$, fails, then, as $\sum_{\mathsf k(r/2)\le i<n_0}\epsilon^{\mathrm e}_i\le C_\omega[2.2\gamma_{n_0}+\frac12s(\frac r2)\mathsf c^\flat\theta^{[0]}]\le C(g,\mathsf b)\,\epsilon$ (with $\gamma_{n_0}\le C(\mathsf b)r^{1/4}$ and $s(\frac r2)\theta^{[0]}\le C(\mathsf b)(a_K/r)^{1/4}$), the number $\epsilon$ exceeds a number $\epsilon_0(g,\mathsf b)>0$, the bracket is $\ge(\frac12\epsilon_0)^{1/2}$, and the bounds of Lem.~\ref{C-352-26} give the claim with a larger $C_{\mathrm A}$.

\emph{(E.1).} By Lem.~\ref{C-352-25}(c) for the two lists,
\[
\begin{multlined}
[\mathsf cS^T_3-S^T_2]-[\mathsf c\mathsf J_3-\mathsf J_2]=\int\mathsf Y_{\Delta3}d\mathbb P+\kappa_{\mathbb P}(\mathsf Y_\Delta,\mathsf Y_3)+\mathsf E,\qquad\mathsf E=\mathsf c[\kappa_{\mathbb P}(\mathsf Y_{13},\mathsf Y_2)+\kappa_{\mathbb P}(\mathsf Y_{23},\mathsf Y_1) \\
+\kappa_{\mathbb P}(\mathsf Y_1,\mathsf Y_2,\mathsf Y_3)],
\end{multlined}
\]
and Lem.~\ref{C-352-26} gives $|\mathsf E|\le C\Lambda_3^3\mathsf M'\mathsf b^3\mathsf d^{3/2}r^3\cdot\mathsf b^{-2}\mathsf d^{-6}\mu_3$.
