On the real configurations one factor of a monomial is at most $a_p+a_{p'}$, $p,p'$ plaquettes of its lassos: a factor $\langle w,w'\rangle$ or $\det(w,w',w'')$, since $|w|^2\le2a_p$ and $|w|\le1$, or a plaquette term itself; every other factor is at most $1$, or $2$ if it is a plaquette term; so $|\mathrm{Fm}^c(k)|\le\mathcal O(2\|c\||k|_\infty\mathbf 1_{{\rm Pl}(k)})$, ${\rm Pl}(k)$ the plaquettes of the blocks of the sites with $k\ne0$, and the set $\{k\ne0\}$ carries all the representations: $\mathrm{Fm}^c(k)$ is a dominated local source with the comparison weight $\varpi\mathbf 1_{{\rm Pl}(k)}$ for every $\varpi\ge76\|c\||k|_\infty$.

If all the orders are $\ge3$, the factor $(5.04\,\alpha_0\eta_j^2)^{m_i-2}\le\max\{1,5.04\,\alpha_0\}^{{\rm Ord}(c)-2}L^{-2j}$, ${\rm Ord}(c)$ the largest order, gives the fall $L^{-2j}$ of the sizes; on the backgrounds of the level $t$ the plaquette terms are below $\bar a=2B_3^2\varepsilon_t^2L^{-4t}$, $\varepsilon_t$ the radius of regularity of the level $t$, a factor of the order $q\in\{2,3\}$ is at most $(2\bar a)^{q/2}$, and the values fall like $L^{-2t}$. With the comparison weight $\Gamma^\circ_c\|c\||k|_\infty\mathbf 1_{{\rm Pl}(k)}$ of the statement, $\Gamma^\circ_c=\max\{76,\,34\max\{1,5.04\,\alpha_0\}^{{\rm Ord}(c)-2},\,2\max\{1,2B_3\}^{{\rm Ord}(c)-2}\}$, this is the hypothesis of (c), with $L^{-2j}$ and $L^{-2t}$. (e) The density of a source at the never-large history of the level $t$ is its first derivative in (a); its oscillation is bounded by the size of the source at that level, which is $y_2$ up to a constant, and the mixed part is the second mixed derivative, which carries the factor of the distance from (a), with $\mathsf D_t\ge L^{s'}\mathsf d'\ge3M$.

The second mixed derivatives are summed over the levels finer than $t$ as in (b) at $p=2$, $\frac43L\,\mathsf T^\circ_2$ being the series $\mathsf T_2$, and the condition $\mathsf h_2(s')\le1$ closes that induction up to the level $t$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Rough entries]\label{C-360-6}
A petal at a site $x$ is a pair $\pi=(\alpha,\alpha')$ of signed directions with $|\alpha|\ne|\alpha'|$, $W_x(\pi)$ the holonomy from $x$ of the plaquette that it spans, and $q_x(\pi,\pi')=\langle\mathbf w(W_x(\pi)),\mathbf w(W_x(\pi'))\rangle$. For real $k=(k_{\pi\pi'}(x))$ put ${\rm Pf}(k)=a^{-1}\sum_x\sum_{\pi,\pi'}k_{\pi\pi'}(x)q_x(\pi,\pi')$ and $|k|_1=\sup_x\sum_{\pi,\pi'}|k_{\pi\pi'}(x)|$. A \emph{rough entry} is $F={\rm Pf}(k)+\mathcal O(v)$ with a real weight $v$; its norm is $\|F\|=13|k|_1+|v|_\infty$, and it is carried by the barycentres of the plaquettes of ${\rm supp}\,v$ and of those with a corner at which $k\ne0$. Let $0<g\le\gamma^{\rm ref}_W$, $\ell'\in\mathfrak L(g)$, $r\ge2$ and $0<\mathsf d<1$. There are $K'_0(r,\mathsf d)$ and $k'(r,\mathsf d)\le C_{r,p}\mathsf d^{-pr}$ $(p>7)$ such that
\[
|\langle F_1;\dots;F_r\rangle_{K,\ell',\beta}|\le k'(r,\mathsf d)\prod_a\|F_a\|
\]
for all $(K,\beta)\in\mathfrak D(g)$ with $K\ge K'_0(r,\mathsf d)$ and all rough entries whose carriers are pairwise $\ge\mathsf d$ apart. Moreover $\Theta_\beta[\eta]=\mathsf b\,{\rm Pf}(k^\eta)$ with $|k^\eta|_1\le12\max_\rho{\rm Lip}_\infty\eta^\rho$, so $\|{\rm Pf}(k^\eta)\|\le156\max_\rho{\rm Lip}_\infty\eta^\rho$; $-\beta\sum_ph_{\omega,\chi}(p)=\mathsf b\,{\rm Pf}(k^h)$ with $|k^h|_1\le12|\omega|\,{\rm Lip}(\chi)R_1(\chi)\le36\ell|\omega|\,{\rm Lip}_\infty\chi$; $\mathfrak B_{\omega,\chi}=\mathsf b\,{\rm Pf}(k^h)+\mathcal O(v^{\mathfrak B})$ with $|v^{\mathfrak B}|_\infty\le(2\mathsf b+3a)|\omega|\,{\rm Lip}(\chi)R'_1(\chi)$, where $R'_1(\chi)\le\frac32\ell$ is the number of Thm.~\ref{C-360-3}(a), the largest $|x(p)|_1$, taken in the chart $(-\frac\ell2,\frac\ell2)^3$, at the plaquettes where $\nabla^s_\omega\chi$ or $v_\chi$ does not vanish (at their barycentres $x(p)$, $\chi$ is not constant on the points $x(p)\pm ae_\rho$, $x(p)\pm\frac a2e_\rho$, $\rho=1,2,3$); the entries $\mathsf b\,{\rm Pf}(k^\eta)$, $\mathsf b\,{\rm Pf}(k^h)$ and $\mathfrak B_{\omega,\chi}$ are carried within $2a$ of ${\rm supp}\,\eta$, resp.\ ${\rm Var}(\chi)$; and $T_{lr}(\varphi)=\mathsf b\,({\rm Pf}(k^{lr})+\mathcal O(v^{lr}))$ with $13|k^{lr}|_1+|v^{lr}|_\infty\le C_T\sup|\varphi|$, $C_T$ an absolute constant.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
A rough entry is a dominated local source in the sense of Lem.~\ref{C-360-24}: a gauge invariant polynomial with a local representation at every height, with $|F|\le\mathcal O(w)$ for a weight $w$ of size $\|F\|$ on its carrier. Put $\sum_a\lambda_aF_a$ into the weighted progression (Lem.~\ref{C-360-24}(a)). Its families are holomorphic in $\lambda$ near $0$ with sizes that depend on the $\sup|w_a|$ alone, and they are local: $\partial_BE^{(i)}_\lambda(X)=0$ unless $X$ meets every carrier in $B$, so that $d_i(X)\ge D_i/M-2$, $D_i$ being the least sup distance of these carriers in level-$i$ units, and a factor $e^{-\kappa^+[D_i/M-2]_+}$ appears. We split the mean over the level $t$ of the first creation of a large field. Up to that level the history is the never-large one, and
\[
\begin{multlined}
\tau_{h_t}\bigl[\rho_0e^{\sum_a\lambda_aF_a}\bigr]=e^{D^\lambda_t(U_t(\cdot))}\,\mathsf m_t,\qquad\Phi\Bigl[\prod_{a\in B}(F_a-c_a)\Bigr]=\sum_\pi\prod_{\beta\in\pi}\kappa_\beta,\quad\kappa_\beta=\partial_\beta D^\lambda_t|_{\lambda=0}\ \relax (\#\beta \\
\ge2),\quad\kappa_{\{a\}}=\partial_aD^\lambda_t|_{\lambda=0}-c_a,
\end{multlined}
\]
with the signs of Lem.~\ref{C-360-24}(a); each $\kappa_\beta$ with $\#\beta\ge2$ is bounded by the mixed derivatives above. Behind the level $t$ only a positive weight enters, of the mass $\mathsf w_t\le2M^{-3}\ell'^3e^{B(X_g)\ell'^3}L^{3(K-t)}e^{-c'p_0(g_t)^2}$, which is smaller than every power of $L^{-(K-t)}$, while the centred insertions carried to the level $t-1$ are at most powers of $L^{K-t}$. The mixed derivatives of the orders $\le r$ converge at the depth $s(\mathsf d'')$, $\mathsf d''=\min\{\frac45\mathsf d,L^{-\bar s(r)}\}$, where $\bar s(r)$ is the least integer $s\ge3$ with $2\mathsf T_r(3)\theta(L^{s-2}g^{-2})\le1$, with the series $\mathsf T_r$ and the size $\theta$ of Lem.~\ref{C-360-24}(b); at every $s\ge\bar s(r)$ the condition holds, since $\theta$ does not increase.

Apply {\cite[Prop.~2.10]{YMM2}}(a$'$), (b) to the dominated local sources just constructed. Its summability condition is the one defining $\bar s(r)$ above, and it permits the fixed side $\ell'$: the local cumulant constant may be chosen with $k_r(g,s;\ell')\le C_r(g,\ell')Y_s^{8r\mathfrak p_0}$. Cutting every weight into at most $(2\ell'/\mathsf d'')^3$ pieces and using $\mathsf b^{-r}\le g^{2r}$ therefore gives $k'(r,\mathsf d)\le C_r(g,\ell')g^{2r}(2\ell'/\mathsf d'')^{3r}Y_{s(\mathsf d'')}^{8r\mathfrak p_0}$. The same proposition bounds $Y_{s(\mathsf d'')}\le2\log(1/\mathsf d'')+C(g)$; since $\mathsf d''=\min\{4\mathsf d/5,L^{-\bar s(r)}\}$, this proves the asserted $C_{r,p}\mathsf d^{-pr}$ bound for every $p>7$. The same decomposition, at the least depth $s$ with $L^s\mathsf d\ge3M$ at which the mixed derivatives of the order $q$ are summable, gives the second bound of Thm.~\ref{C-360-2}(a): $L^s\le\max\{1,LM\mathsf u_q/\mathsf d\}$ with $\mathsf u_q=O(q\log q)$, the sums over partitions are at most $C^q(q!)^{3/2+\mathfrak p_0}$, and the rarity of a first creation, at which all the $q$ insertions are bounded by their suprema, costs $\exp[c_L(4q+4)^2]$. The formulas for $k^\eta$, $k^h$ and $k^{lr}$ are the definitions written in petals: for $b=\langle x,x+ae_\mu\rangle$ and $p=p(b,\alpha'')$, $\mathfrak d_{b,p,\rho}=-\frac12[q_x((\mu,\rho),(\mu,\alpha''))-q_x((\mu,-\rho),(\mu,\alpha''))]$, and the shell lies in $|x|_1\le\frac12+\frac32\ell$.

For the whole flux insertion, $\mathfrak B_{\omega,\chi}-\mathsf b\,{\rm Pf}(k^h)=\mathcal O(v^{\mathfrak B})$ with $v^{\mathfrak B}(p)=\mathsf b\,\nabla^s_\omega\chi(x(p))-\frac32a\,v_\chi(p)$; as $\sum_\rho|(\omega y)_\rho|\le2|\omega||y|_1$ and the difference quotients of $\chi$ in $\nabla^s_\omega\chi$ and in $v_\chi$ are at most ${\rm Lip}(\chi)$, $|v^{\mathfrak B}(p)|\le(2\mathsf b+3a)|\omega|\,{\rm Lip}(\chi)|x(p)|_1$, and $v^{\mathfrak B}(p)\ne0$ only at the plaquettes where $\nabla^s_\omega\chi$ or $v_\chi$ does not vanish, at whose barycentres $\chi$ is not constant on the points $x(p)\pm ae_\rho$, $x(p)\pm\frac a2e_\rho$: this gives the factor $R'_1(\chi)$ of Thm.~\ref{C-360-3}(a).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Chessboard bound]\label{C-360-7}
Let $0<g\le\gamma$, $\ell'\in\mathfrak L(g)$, $(K,\beta)\in\mathfrak D(g)$, and let a board of cubic cells of side $\mathsf l'$ dividing $\frac{\ell'}2$ be placed on $T_{\ell'}$, on every $T_\ell$ with $\ell\ge\ell'$ in $\mathfrak L(g)$ and on $a_K\mathbb Z^3$; $N'=(\ell'/\mathsf l')^3$. For a bounded Borel function $F$ of the bonds inside one cell put $\|F\|_{\rm ch}=|\langle\prod_\kappa F^{[\kappa]}\rangle_{K,\ell',\beta}|^{1/N'}$, the product running over the mirror copies of $F$, conjugated on odd reflection parity, in the $N'$ cells of $T_{\ell'}$. Then
\[
|s(F_1\cdots F_q)|\le\prod_ie^{G_g\mathsf l'^3}\|F_i\|_{\rm ch}
\]
for functions $F_1,\dots,F_q$ of distinct cells, $s$ being a periodic Gibbs state at $(K,\beta)$ or the measure of $T_\ell$, $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$, $\ell\ge\ell'$. In particular, for real $F_1,F_2$ of two distinct cells and real $c_1,c_2$: $|s(F_1)-c_1|\le e^{G_g\mathsf l'^3}\|F_1-c_1\|_{\rm ch}$ and $|s(A^s[F_1]A^s[F_2])|\le2e^{2G_g\mathsf l'^3}\|F_1-c_1\|_{\rm ch}\|F_2-c_2\|_{\rm ch}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
On $T_\ell$, $\ell\ge\ell'$, reflection positivity at the walls gives the chessboard estimate $|\langle F_1\cdots F_q\rangle_{K,\ell,\beta}|\le\prod_i\langle\prod_\kappa F_i^{[\kappa]}\rangle_{K,\ell,\beta}^{1/N_\ell}$, $N_\ell=(\ell/\mathsf l')^3$. The product of the mirror copies over all the cells of $T_\ell$ is a periodisation of the product over the cells of $T_{\ell'}$, and the chessboard seminorms on the two sides compare by the inequality $\langle\prod_\kappa F^{[\kappa]}\rangle_{K,\ell,\beta}^{1/N_\ell}\le\langle\prod_\kappa F^{[\kappa]}\rangle_{K,\ell',\beta}^{1/N'}\,e^{\mathsf l'^3(p_{\ell'}-p_\ell)}$ ({\cite[Cor.~B.1]{YMM2}}(e)). It is reflection positivity at the walls applied once more, to the periodised product: the pattern of the copies has the period $2\mathsf l'$, which divides $\ell'$, so that a slab of that length is a half slab and its mirror image, the transfer operator across it is positive, and ${\rm Tr}\,T^n\le({\rm Tr}\,T)^n$ in each of the three directions; this bounds the unnormalised $N_\ell$-th root by the unnormalised $N'$-th root, and the ratio $Z_{K,\ell',\beta}^{1/N'}/Z_{K,\ell,\beta}^{1/N_\ell}$ of the plain partition functions per cell is $e^{\mathsf l'^3(p_{\ell'}-p_\ell)}\le e^{G_g\mathsf l'^3}$, the pressures $p_\ell=\ell^{-3}\log Z_{K,\ell,\beta}$ being formed with the plain partition functions (Section~\YMMref{86}{680}).

A periodic Gibbs state is dominated by the torus measures through its conditional laws (Prop.~\YMMref{91.9}{705}), and this domination carries the bound to every periodic Gibbs state. The last two bounds are the cases $q=1$ and $q=2$, with $s(A^s[F_1]A^s[F_2])=s((F_1-c_1)(F_2-c_2))-(s(F_1)-c_1)(s(F_2)-c_2)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Exact identities]\label{C-360-8}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[beginpenalty=10000]
\item[(a)] Let $\mathbf X$ be a polynomial field of directions that vanishes off a finite set $\Lambda$ of bonds: at each positively oriented bond $b$ a $\mathfrak g$-valued polynomial $\mathbf X(b)$ in the plaquette variables, $0$ for $b\notin\Lambda$; let $v_{\mathbf X}F=\sum_b\sum_{\mathsf a}\langle\sigma_{\mathsf a},\mathbf X(b)\rangle\partial^{\mathsf a}_bF$ and ${\rm div}\,v_{\mathbf X}=\sum_b\sum_{\mathsf a}\partial^{\mathsf a}_b\langle\sigma_{\mathsf a},\mathbf X(b)\rangle$, $\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3$ the Pauli matrices and $\partial^{\mathsf a}_b$ the derivative along $e^{i\epsilon\sigma_{\mathsf a}}U(b)$ at $\epsilon=0$. Then $\nu((\beta v_{\mathbf X}A-{\rm div}\,v_{\mathbf X})Y)=0$ for every Gibbs state or torus measure $\nu$ at $(a_K,\beta)$ and every bounded Borel $Y$ that does not depend on the bonds of $\Lambda$; so every joint cumulant under $\nu$ with the entry $\beta v_{\mathbf X}A-{\rm div}\,v_{\mathbf X}$ and further entries not depending on $\Lambda$ vanishes. $N_\beta[\eta]=\Theta_\beta[\eta]+\mathfrak K^{\rm v}[\beta\eta]-\mathsf b\,\mathcal O({\rm div}^s\eta)+\frac32a\,\mathcal O(e^\eta)$ is such a null term.

With the contact terms, for all weights $f_i$ and every vector field $\eta$, $\langle N_\beta[\eta];\mathcal O(f_\cdot)\rangle+\sum_i\langle{\rm Ct}[f_i;\eta];(\mathcal O(f_l))_{l\ne i}\rangle=0$, where ${\rm Ct}[f;\eta]=\mathcal O({\rm div}^s(f\eta))-a^{-1}\Theta_f[\eta]-a^{-1}\mathfrak K^{\rm v}[f\eta]$.
\item[(b)] Identically in $U$, $\mathfrak K^{\rm v}[\eta]=-\sum_p\sum_\rho(\nabla^+_\rho\eta^\rho)(x(p))\Psi_\rho(p)+\mathfrak K^\sharp[\eta]$; for $\rho\in P(p)$, $\mathfrak r^\sharp_\rho(p)=0$ and $-(a_p+a_{p+ae_\rho})\le\Psi_\rho(p)\le0$; $\mathfrak r^\sharp$ transforms as a vector under the coordinate mirrors of the lattice: $\mathfrak r^\sharp_\rho$ is odd under the mirror normal to $\rho$ and even under the two mirrors that contain $e_\rho$, so that it is odd, for every $\rho$, under the inversion $y\mapsto2z-y$ through a site $z$, the product of the three mirrors through $z$. Hence $\langle\mathfrak K^\sharp[\eta]\rangle_{K,\ell,\beta}=0$, and by translation invariance also $\langle\mathfrak K^{\rm v}[\eta]\rangle_{K,\ell,\beta}=0$; and if a field $\zeta$ has $\zeta^\rho(y+se_\rho)=\zeta^\rho(y)$ for all $y$, $s$ and $\rho$, then $\langle\mathfrak K^\sharp[\zeta];\mathcal O(f)\rangle_{K,\ell,\beta}=0$ for every weight $f$.

A \emph{block form} is a combination $c=\sum_i\kappa_im_i$ of monomials in the lassos of the block ${\rm Bk}(x)=x+a\{-1,0,1\}^3$ of $27$ sites centred at a site $x$: a lasso is a path of at most three steps from $x$ inside the block to a corner $y$ of a plaquette of the block, the holonomy of that plaquette from $y$, and the path back; with $w=\mathbf w(W)$ and $a_{\rm lz}=1-\frac12{\rm tr}\,W$ the vector part and the plaquette term of the holonomy $W$ of a lasso, a monomial is a product of $n_2$ factors $\langle w,w'\rangle$, $n_3$ factors $\det(w,w',w'')$ and $n_a$ factors $a_{\rm lz}$, and $2n_2+3n_3+2n_a$ is its order in the field strength. The same lassos are taken at every site, $c_x$ is the form at the block of $x$, the order of $c$ is the least order of its monomials, and its norm is the number $\|c\|=\sum_i|\kappa_i|2^{n_a(m_i)}$ of Lem.~\ref{C-360-24}(d).

For a real function $k$ of the sites, $\mathrm{Fm}^c(k)=a^{-1}\sum_xk(x)c_x(U)$ is a dominated local source of size $\le76\|c\||k|_\infty$, carried by $\{k\ne0\}$, with $|\mathrm{Fm}^c(k)|\le\mathcal O(2\|c\||k|_\infty\mathbf 1_{{\rm Pl}(k)})$, ${\rm Pl}(k)$ the plaquettes of the blocks of the sites with $k\ne0$; and if all the monomials of $c$ have order $\ge3$, as for the commutator terms, the defects of the linear Bianchi identity, $a_p^2$ and $a_pa_{p_+}$, its sizes fall like $L^{-2j}$ with the level $j$ and its values on the backgrounds like $L^{-2t}$ with the level $t$, with the comparison weight $\Gamma^\circ_c\|c\||k|_\infty\mathbf 1_{{\rm Pl}(k)}$ of Lem.~\ref{C-360-24}(d). $\Psi_{\lambda(p)}(p)$ is a block form of order $2$ and norm $1$, and $\mathfrak r^\sharp_\rho(p)$, $\rho=\lambda(p)$, a block form of order $2$ and norm $\le8$, both at the block of the lowest corner of $p$; so for a real weight $k$ the sums $a^{-1}\sum_pk(p)\Psi_{\lambda(p)}(p)$ and $a^{-1}\sum_pk(p)\mathfrak r^\sharp_{\lambda(p)}(p)$ over the plaquettes of one normal are sources $\mathrm{Fm}^c(\tilde k)$, $\tilde k(x)$ the value of $k$ at the plaquette of that normal with the lowest corner $x$, and they are dominated local sources of the sizes $\le76|k|_\infty$ and $\le608|k|_\infty$; as a function $|\mathfrak r^\sharp_\rho(p)|\le C\bar a^{3/2}$, $\bar a$ the largest $a_q$ near $p$, and $\beta\mathfrak K^\sharp$ is treated by parity (Lems.~\ref{C-360-9}, \ref{C-360-10}).
\item[(c)] For a vector field $\mathsf k$, $\beta\sum_{p,\rho}\mathsf k^\rho(x(p))\Psi_\rho(p)=-\frac14\mathfrak N[\mathsf k]+\sum_{v=1}^5\mathfrak J_v[\mathsf k]-\frac14c_{\mathsf k}$, where $\mathfrak N[\mathsf k]=\beta v_{\mathbf X^{\mathsf k}}A-{\rm div}\,v_{\mathbf X^{\mathsf k}}$ is the null term of (a) for the field of directions $\mathbf X^{\mathsf k}(b)=\sum_{\rho\ne\mu_b}\mathsf k^\rho(x_b)G_\rho(b)$, $c_{\mathsf k}=6\sum_b\sum_{\rho\ne\mu_b}\mathsf k^\rho(x_b)$ is a number, and $\mathfrak J_1,\dots,\mathfrak J_5$ are sums of local densities of the orders $2,2,2,3,4$ with weights at most $3|\mathsf k|_\infty+\frac32\mathsf b{\rm Lip}_\infty\mathsf k$, $\frac18\mathsf b{\rm Lip}_\infty\mathsf k$, $\frac12\mathsf b{\rm Lip}_\infty\mathsf k$, $\frac14\beta|\mathsf k|_\infty$ and $\beta|\mathsf k|_\infty$, vanishing beyond the sup distance $a$ of ${\rm supp}\,\mathsf k$. Consequently, with $\mathsf k^\rho_\eta=\nabla^+_\rho\eta^\rho$, $\mathrm{St}_K[\eta]=N_\beta[\eta]-\frac14\mathfrak N[\mathsf k_\eta]-\mathrm{Rm}_K[\eta]-\frac14c_{\mathsf k_\eta}$, where $\mathrm{Rm}_K[\eta]=\beta\mathfrak K^\sharp[\eta]-\sum_v\mathfrak J_v[\mathsf k_\eta]+\frac32a\,\mathcal O(e^\eta)$ is the remainder of the stress insertion.
\item[(d)] $\Delta_K[\eta]=F^0+F^1$, rough entries carried within $2a$ of ${\rm supp}\,\eta$, with $\|F^0\|\le286\mathsf b\sup|\nabla\eta|$ and $\|F^1\|\le780\mathsf b\,a\sup|\nabla^2\eta|$; $F^0$ is null: its classical density, a quadratic form in the field strength with coefficients linear in $\nabla\eta$, vanishes identically.
\item[(e)] For a positively oriented bond $b$ and directions $\lambda,\rho$: $\sum_{p\ni b}a^{-1}(x_b-x(p))_\lambda\mathfrak d_{b,p,\rho}=\langle\mathbf u_{b,\lambda},\mathbf u_{b,\rho}\rangle$, so that $\sum_p\mathfrak s_{\lambda\rho}(p)=\sum_b\langle\mathbf u_{b,\lambda},\mathbf u_{b,\rho}\rangle$ is a symmetric positive semidefinite matrix; for $\lambda\ne\mu_b$ and $p_\pm=p(b,\pm\lambda)$, $|\mathbf u_{b,\lambda}|^2=(a_{p_+}+a_{p_-})-\frac14(a_{p_+}^2+a_{p_-}^2)+\Psi_\lambda(p_-)$ and $\Psi_\lambda(p_-)=-\frac14|G_\lambda(b)|^2-\frac14(a_{p_+}^2+a_{p_-}^2)$; for $\nu\in P(p)$, $\mathfrak s_{\nu\nu}(p)=\frac32a_p+\frac14(a_{p+ae_\nu}+a_{p-ae_\nu})-\frac12a_p^2+\frac12(\Psi_\nu(p)+\Psi_\nu(p-ae_\nu))$, and $\mathfrak s_{\lambda\rho}(p)=0$ if $\lambda=\lambda(p)$. Consequently, identically in $U$,
\[
T_{mm}(\varphi)-\mathsf b\check D_m(\varphi)=\beta\sum_{p:\,m\in P(p)}\varphi(x(p))\Bigl[\tfrac12\bigl(\Psi_m(p)+\Psi_m(p-ae_m)\bigr)-\tfrac12a_p^2\Bigr]+\mathsf b\,\mathcal O(\tilde\varphi_m),
\]
$\tilde\varphi_m(p)=\frac14[\varphi(x(p)+ae_m)-2\varphi(x(p))+\varphi(x(p)-ae_m)]\mathbf 1\{m\in P(p)\}$, so $|\tilde\varphi_m|\le\frac12a\,{\rm Lip}\,\varphi$; and $\sum_mT_{mm}(\varphi)-\mathsf b\,\mathcal O(\varphi)=\sum_m(T_{mm}(\varphi)-\mathsf b\check D_m(\varphi))$.
\item[(f)] \emph{The null term against sources that meet its carrier.} For a complex vector field $\mathsf k$ and a complex function $f$ on $T_\ell$ put $\mathsf e^{\mathsf k}(p)=\sum_{\rho\in P(p)}[\mathsf k^\rho(x(p)+\frac a2e_\rho)+\mathsf k^\rho(x(p)-\frac a2e_\rho)]$ and
\[
\begin{multlined}
\mathfrak C'[\mathsf k;f]=\sum_p\sum_{b\subset\partial p}\sum_{\rho\ne\mu_b}a^{-1}\bigl(f(x(p))-f(x_b)\bigr)\mathsf k^\rho(x_b)\,\langle G_\rho(b),\mathbf w(W_{b,p})\rangle,\qquad\mathfrak R[\mathsf k;f] \\
=\mathsf b^{-1}{\rm div}\,v_{\mathbf X^{f\mathsf k}}+\mathfrak C'[\mathsf k;f],
\end{multlined}
\]
with $\mathbf X^{\mathsf k}$ and $\mathfrak N[\mathsf k]$ as in (c). Then: (N1) $v_{\mathbf X^{\mathsf k}}\mathcal O(f)=\mathsf b^{-1}\mathfrak N[f\mathsf k]+\mathfrak R[\mathsf k;f]$, identically in $U$; (N2) $\int\mathfrak N[\mathsf k]\,e^{\mathcal O(w)}e^{-\beta A}\,\mathrm{d}U=\int\bigl(v_{\mathbf X^{\mathsf k}}\mathcal O(w)\bigr)e^{\mathcal O(w)}e^{-\beta A}\,\mathrm{d}U$ for every complex function $w$ on $T_\ell$; (N3) for a finite set $\mathsf A$ and complex functions $f_l$, $l\in\mathsf A$,
\[
\bigl\langle\mathfrak N[\mathsf k];(\mathcal O(f_l))_{l\in\mathsf A}\bigr\rangle_{K,\ell,\beta}=\sum_{j=1}^{\#\mathsf A}\ \sum_{(q_1,\dots,q_j)}\mathsf b^{-(j-1)}\Bigl\langle\mathfrak R\bigl[f_{q_1}\cdots f_{q_{j-1}}\mathsf k;f_{q_j}\bigr];(\mathcal O(f_l))_{l\in\mathsf A\setminus\{q_1,\dots,q_j\}}\Bigr\rangle_{K,\ell,\beta},
\]
the inner sum over the sequences of $j$ distinct elements of $\mathsf A$ (for $\mathsf A=\emptyset$ the left member is the mean, and it is $0$); (N4) $\mathfrak R[\mathsf k;f]=\mathsf b^{-1}c_{f\mathsf k}-3\mathsf b^{-1}\sum_pa_p\,\mathsf e^{f\mathsf k}(p)+\mathfrak C'[\mathsf k;f]$ is a number, the density $a_p$ with weights $\le12\,\mathsf b^{-1}\sup|f|\sup|\mathsf k|$ and the densities $\langle G_\rho(b),\mathbf w(W_{b,p})\rangle$ of the order $2$ with weights $\le\frac12{\rm Lip}_\infty f\,\sup|\mathsf k|$: no factor $\beta$ enters. Its weight at a plaquette $p$ vanishes unless a bond $b$ of $p$ has $\mathsf k(x_b)\ne0$ and $f\ne0$ at $x_b$ or at $x(p)$, so that its densities are carried within the sup distance $2a$ of ${\rm supp}\,\mathsf k$ and of ${\rm supp}\,f$, and the number vanishes unless $\mathsf k(x_b)f(x_b)\ne0$ at some bond.

Consequently, if the spread $D$ of ${\rm supp}\,\mathsf k$ and the ${\rm supp}\,f_l$, $l\in\mathsf A$, is $>4a$, the terms of (N3) with $j=\#\mathsf A$ vanish, the numbers drop from the other terms, and in each of them the entry is carried by a set whose spread with the supports of the remaining $f_l$ is $\ge D-2a$. This rests on the merging of sets: if $S_0,\dots,S_n$ have the spread $D$, $Q\subset\{1,\dots,n\}$, $2r<D$, and $T$ lies within the sup distance $r$ of $S_0$ and of every $S_q$, $q\in Q$, then $T=\emptyset$ if $Q=\{1,\dots,n\}$, and otherwise the spread of $T$ and the $S_l$, $l\notin Q$, is $\ge D-r$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(a) The Haar measure is invariant; with $\partial^{\mathsf a}_b\langle\sigma_{\mathsf a},\mathbf w(W_{b,p})\rangle=1-a_p$, an integration by parts in each bond variable against $e^{-\beta A}$ gives $\nu((\beta v_{\mathbf X}A-{\rm div}\,v_{\mathbf X})Y)=0$ in finite volume, and in a Gibbs state through its conditional laws. With sources the same integration by parts against $e^{-A(\beta-a^{-1}w_z,\cdot)}$, $w_z=\sum_iz_if_i$, followed by the mixed derivative in $z$ at $0$, gives the contact terms, since $v_\eta A(v,\cdot)$ is linear in the weight $v$. (b) For $q_\pm=p(b,\pm\rho)$ in one plane, $\langle\mathbf w(W_{b,q_-}),\mathbf w(W_{b,q_+})\rangle=-2\Psi_\rho(q_-)-a_{q_-}-a_{q_+}$; so $\mathfrak r_\rho(p)=\Psi_\rho(p)-\Psi_\rho(p_-)$ in the plane, and the split is a summation by parts.

Under the mirror $\mathsf r$ normal to $\rho$, $\mathfrak d_{\mathsf rb,\mathsf rp,\rho}(\mathsf rU)=-\mathfrak d_{b,p,\rho}(U)$ and $\Psi_\rho(\mathsf rp)(\mathsf rU)=\Psi_\rho(p_-)(U)$, and the measure of a torus is invariant under $\mathsf r$. Under a coordinate mirror that contains $e_\rho$ these quantities are carried to the same quantities at the image bond and plaquette: the holonomy $W_{b,p}$ is taken from the initial point of $b$ along $b$, and where the mirror reverses the orientation of $b$ both factors of $\mathfrak d_{b,p,\rho}$ change their sign together; so $\mathfrak r^\sharp_\rho$ is even under it, and the three coordinate mirrors through a site compose to the inversion through it.

For $\zeta$: $\langle\mathfrak K^\sharp[\zeta];\mathcal O(f)\rangle=a^{-1}\sum_{p'}f(p')\langle\mathfrak K^\sharp[\zeta];a_{p'}\rangle$, and for each $p'$ and $\rho$ the mirror normal to $\rho$ through $x(p')$ keeps $a_{p'}$, the measure and $\zeta^\rho$, carries the plaquettes normal to $\rho$ among themselves, and changes the sign of $\mathfrak r^\sharp_\rho$ on them. A block form has local representations at every height of size $76\|c\||k|_\infty$ (the proof of Lem.~\ref{C-360-24}(d), with the lassos from the centre of the block, which reach its $27$ sites in at most three steps); the field strength is $O(L^{-2j})$ in level-$j$ units on the backgrounds, which gives the fall for monomials of order $\ge3$, with the comparison weight $\Gamma^\circ_c\|c\||k|_\infty\mathbf 1_{{\rm Pl}(k)}$ of Lem.~\ref{C-360-24}(d). (c) Take in (a) $\mathbf X(b)=\sum_\rho\mathsf k^\rho(x_b)[\mathbf w(W_{b,p(b,\rho)})+\mathbf w(W_{b,p(b,-\rho)})]$; then $v_{\mathbf X}a_p=\sum_{b\subset\partial p}\langle\mathbf X(b),\mathbf w(W_{b,p})\rangle$, ${\rm div}\,v_{\mathbf X}$ is the number $c_{\mathsf k}$ minus $3\sum_pa_p$ times a weight formed from $\mathsf k$, and the in-plane remainder is $-2a_p^2$, of order $4$. (d) At a constant field strength, with $G=\nabla\eta$ and $T_{lr}={\rm tr}B_lB_r$, the classical density of $\Delta_K[\eta]$ is $\mathsf b[{\rm tr}G\,{\rm tr}T-{\rm Tr}\,GT]-\frac{\mathsf b}2{\rm tr}G\,{\rm tr}T-\frac{\mathsf b}2{\rm Tr}(H^{\rm cons}T)=0$, since ${\rm Tr}(H^{\rm cons}T)={\rm tr}G\,{\rm tr}T-2{\rm Tr}\,GT$; the Taylor remainder of $\eta$ gives $F^1$. (e) $\sum_{p\ni b}a^{-1}(x_b-x(p))_\lambda\mathbf w(W_{b,p})=\mathbf u_{b,\lambda}$ and the form is bilinear; with $w_\pm=\mathbf w(W_{b,p_\pm})$, $|w_\pm|^2=a_{p_\pm}(2-a_{p_\pm})$ and $\Psi_\lambda(p_-)=-\frac14|w_++w_-|^2-\frac14(a_{p_-}^2+a_{p_+}^2)$, and the parallelogram law $4|\mathbf u_{b,\lambda}|^2=|w_+-w_-|^2=2|w_+|^2+2|w_-|^2-|w_++w_-|^2$ gives the first identity; the formula for $\mathfrak s_{\nu\nu}$ is the same computation at the two bonds of $p$ of the direction other than $\nu$, and no vector $x_b-x(p)$ has a component normal to $p$.

Inserting these in $T_{mm}(\varphi)=\beta\sum_p\varphi(x(p))[\mathfrak s_{mm}(p)-a_p]$ and $\mathsf b\check D_m(\varphi)=\beta\sum_p\varphi(x(p))a_p(1-2\cdot\mathbf 1\{\lambda(p)=m\})$, the plaquettes normal to $m$ cancel, and moving the shifts $a_{p\pm ae_m}$ onto $\varphi$ gives $\tilde\varphi_m$. Finally $\sum_m\check D_m=3\mathcal O-2\mathcal O=\mathcal O$. (f) $\mathcal O(f)=a^{-1}\sum_pf(x(p))a_p$ and $v_{\mathbf X}a_p=\sum_{b\subset\partial p}\langle\mathbf X(b),\mathbf w(W_{b,p})\rangle$; with $f(x(p))=f(x_b)+(f(x(p))-f(x_b))$ and $f(x_b)\mathbf X^{\mathsf k}(b)=\mathbf X^{f\mathsf k}(b)$, the first part is $a^{-1}v_{\mathbf X^{f\mathsf k}}A=\mathsf b^{-1}\beta v_{\mathbf X^{f\mathsf k}}A=\mathsf b^{-1}(\mathfrak N[f\mathsf k]+{\rm div}\,v_{\mathbf X^{f\mathsf k}})$ and the second is $\mathfrak C'[\mathsf k;f]$: this is (N1). (N2) is the integration by parts of (a) along $\mathbf X^{\mathsf k}$ against $e^{\mathcal O(w)}e^{-\beta A}$.

At the source $w_z=\sum_{l\in\mathsf A}z_lf_l$, (N2) says that the mean of $\mathfrak N[\mathsf k]-\sum_qz_q\,v_{\mathbf X^{\mathsf k}}\mathcal O(f_q)$ under the measure with the source vanishes, and this function is affine in $z$; the mixed derivative in $z$ at $0$ gives $\langle\mathfrak N[\mathsf k];(\mathcal O(f_l))_{l\in\mathsf A}\rangle=\sum_{q\in\mathsf A}\langle v_{\mathbf X^{\mathsf k}}\mathcal O(f_q);(\mathcal O(f_l))_{l\ne q}\rangle$, and inserting (N1), whose first part is a null term of the same kind with $f_q\mathsf k$ for $\mathsf k$, an induction on $\#\mathsf A$ gives (N3). (N4): ${\rm div}\,v_{\mathbf X^{\mathsf k}}=c_{\mathsf k}-3\sum_pa_p\,\mathsf e^{\mathsf k}(p)$, by $\partial^{\mathsf a}_b\langle\sigma_{\mathsf a},\mathbf w(W_{b,p})\rangle=1-a_p$; $|\mathsf e^{f\mathsf k}|\le4\sup|f\mathsf k|$, $|x(p)-x_b|_\infty=\frac a2$, and the boxes of the densities lie within the sup distance $\frac32a$ of $x(p)$.

The merging: if $Q=\{1,\dots,n\}$, points of $S_0,\dots,S_n$ within $r$ of one point of $T$ are pairwise at most $2r<D$ apart, which the spread forbids; otherwise, for $t\in T$, $y_l\in S_l$ $(l\notin Q)$ and points $y_0\in S_0$, $y_q\in S_q$ within $r$ of $t$, some pair of the family $y_0,(y_q),(y_l)$ is at least $D$ apart, it is no pair among $y_0,(y_q)$, and so two of the $y_l$, or one $y_l$ and $t$, are at least $D-r$ apart.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The chain with an entry; the cubic insertion]\label{C-360-9}
Let $\gamma^{-2}\le\mathsf b_-\le\mathsf b_+$, $MR(\mathsf b_+)\le L^m$, $\ell=2L^m$, $0<\tau\le\frac14$, $0<\phi<\frac1{42}$, $u=\lceil\phi K\rceil$, $t=K-u$ and $c'_0=\min\{\frac1{14}-\frac\tau7,\frac1{14}-3\phi\}$. Let $K_\phi$ be the least integer $K\ge2$ with $(1-\phi)K\ge2$, $L^{\phi K}\gamma^{-2}\ge\mathsf t_\natural$ and $\phi K>16\mathfrak p_0^2c_{\log}/(\log L)^2$, $\mathsf t_\natural$ being the calibration of \S\ref{sec:cutoff-calibration} and $c_{\log}=\log L/\log\gamma^{-2}$; it depends on the constants and on $\phi$ alone. For $K\ge K_\phi$ and $\mathsf b'\in[\mathsf b_-,\mathsf b_+]$ let $\rho_0dU$ be the measure of $T_\ell$ at $\beta=L^K\mathsf b'$; the data $(K,\mathsf b',m)$ with the top level $t$ form the setting (Th) (\S\ref{sec:cutoff-calibration}), and the small-field chain is formed along the couplings $x_j=L^{K-j}\mathsf b'$ up to the level $t$. Let $\mathcal M^k$ be the block map to the level $k$, ${\rm Cut}_k$ the field cut and ${\rm In}_k\subset{\rm Cut}_k$ the inner ball of the level $k$ (the definitions preceding Lem.~\YMMref{113.10}{796}), $\mathfrak G_k[x_k]\ge0$ the gauge-fixing factor and $\chi^{\rm sf}_{x_k}\in\{0,1\}$ the fluctuation test of the step from the level $k$ ({\cite[\S{}B.2]{YMM2}}), and
\[
\mathsf p_k(U)=\mathbf 1_{{\rm Cut}_k}(\mathcal M^kU)\prod_{j<k}\bigl[\mathbf 1_{{\rm Cut}_j}\,\mathfrak G_j[x_j]\,\chi^{\rm sf}_{x_j}\bigr](\mathcal M^jU),
\]
the weight of the small-field chain up to the level $k$: a bounded Borel function with values in $[0,\infty)$, with $\mathsf p_0=\mathbf 1_{{\rm Cut}_0}$ and $\mathsf p_{k+1}=(\mathbf 1_{{\rm Cut}_{k+1}}\circ\mathcal M^{k+1})\,\bigl((\mathfrak G_k[x_k]\chi^{\rm sf}_{x_k})\circ\mathcal M^k\bigr)\,\mathsf p_k$; and $(\mathbf 1_{{\rm In}_t}\circ\mathcal M^t)\,\mathsf p_t$ is the weight $\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}_t$ of the small-field chain of the definitions preceding Prop.~\YMMref{115.2}{806}. Let $\nu_k=(\mathcal M^k)_*(\mathsf p_k\rho_0dU)$, the measure of the level $k$ of the chain among the construction results at the source $0$ (Prop.~\YMMref{114.2}{801} and the proof of Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{115.2}{806}}), a finite positive measure with $\nu_{k+1}=\mathbf 1_{{\rm Cut}_{k+1}}\mathbf T(\mathfrak G_k[x_k]\chi^{\rm sf}_{x_k}\nu_k)$, $\mathbf T$ the image under the block averaging; let $Q_kh$ be the density of $\mathbf 1_{{\rm Cut}_{k+1}}\mathbf T(\mathfrak G_k[x_k]\chi^{\rm sf}_{x_k}h\,\nu_k)$ with respect to $\nu_{k+1}$, the mean of $h$ over the range ${\rm Rg}_{x_k}$ of the chart of the fibre of the step ({\cite[Lem.~B.3]{YMM2}}), and $Q_{t\leftarrow0}=Q_{t-1}\cdots Q_0$, so that $(\mathcal M^t)_*(\mathsf p_tY\rho_0dU)=(Q_{t\leftarrow0}Y)\,\nu_t$ for bounded Borel $Y$: $(Q_{t\leftarrow0}Y)\circ\mathcal M^t$ is the conditional mean of $Y$ given $\mathcal M^tU$ under $\mathsf p_t\rho_0dU$.

An \emph{entry of the type} $(m_J,c,\hat c,N)$ is a finite family $J=(\mathsf Q_\iota,j_\iota,\varkappa_\iota)_\iota$ of boxes $\mathsf Q_\iota=\{x+a\sum_\mu n_\mu e_\mu:0\le n_\mu\le r_\mu\}$, $(r_1,r_2,r_3)\in\{0,1,2\}^3$ with at least two $r_\mu\ge1$, $x$ the lowest site of the box, of densities $j_\iota$ on them and of complex weights $\varkappa_\iota$, at most $N$ indices having one lowest site. A density on a box is a polynomial in the entries of the complex configurations $\mathbf U(b)\in{\rm SL}(2,\mathbb C)$ at its bonds, $\mathbf U(\bar b)=\mathbf U(b)^{-1}$, invariant under the gauge transformations of the box; it has the height $\hat c$ if $|j|\le\hat c$ wherever $|\mathbf U(b)|\le2$ at all the bonds, and the order $m_J$ with the constant $c$ if $|j|\le c\,\epsilon^{m_J}$ wherever, besides, $|\partial\mathbf U(q)-\mathbf 1|\le\epsilon$ at all the plaquettes $q$ of the box, $0<\epsilon\le1$.

Zero insertions and zero scalar sources are omitted before inverse norms and source radii are formed; the multilinear estimates are immediate when an insertion vanishes. We write $J(U)=\sum_\iota\varkappa_\iota j_\iota(U|_{\mathsf Q_\iota})$ and $|\varkappa|_\infty=\max_\iota|\varkappa_\iota|$; the carrier of $J$ is the set of the sites of the boxes with $\varkappa_\iota\ne0$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] For $K\ge K_\phi$, an entry of the type $(m_J,c,\hat c,N)$ with $m_J\ge2$, $|s|<r_J$ with $r_J^{-1}\le C|\varkappa|_\infty$, and $1\le k\le t$:
\[
(\mathcal M^k)_*\bigl(\mathsf p_ke^{sJ}\rho_0dU\bigr)=\exp\Bigl[\sum_{i\le k}c_i(s)\Bigr]\mathbf 1_{{\rm Cut}_k}e^{\Phi^s_k}\,\mathrm{d}V,
\]
the numbers $c_i(s)$ and the action $\Phi^s_k$ being holomorphic in $s$ and sums of local families, each of which depends on $\varkappa$ in its domain only. $Q_{t\leftarrow0}J$ is a number plus $\partial_s\Phi^s_t|_{s=0}$ $\nu_t$-almost everywhere on ${\rm Cut}_t$, and its oscillation is at most $CK^{2\mathfrak p_0}L^{4u-K}|\varkappa|_\infty$ for $m_J=2$ and $CK^{3\mathfrak p_0}L^{4u-\frac32K}|\varkappa|_\infty$ for $m_J\ge3$. Here $C$ depends on the constants, $\ell$, $\mathsf b_+$, $\phi$ and the type of the entry.
\item[(b)] There are $K_2\ge K_\phi$, $C_2$, $p_2$, depending on these data alone, such that for $K\ge K_2$ and every $\mathsf b'\in[\mathsf b_-,\mathsf b_+]$ the following holds. For every field $\Xi$ there is a number $\mathsf a$ with $|Q_{t\leftarrow0}(\beta\mathfrak K^\sharp[\Xi])-\mathsf a|\le C_2\mathsf H(\Xi)K^{p_2}L^{-c'_0K}$ $\nu_t$-almost everywhere on ${\rm Cut}_t$. The same holds at real sources: let $n\ge1$, $f_1,\dots,f_n$ real Lipschitz functions, $\mathsf M_t\le CK^{2\mathfrak p_0}\ell^3L^{3u}$ the inverse radius of the sources of the chain at the level $t$, and $x$ real in the polydisc $\mathbb D_t$ of the radii $r_i=(8n\mathsf M_t\|f_i\|_\sharp)^{-1}$; then $w_x=\sum_ix_if_i$ lies in the class of sources of the setting (Th), and with the measure $\rho_0e^{\mathcal O(w_x)}dU$ in the place of $\rho_0dU$, its chain measure $\nu^{w_x}_t$ and its conditional mean $Q^{w_x}_{t\leftarrow0}$, and the entry with the moved weight $\mathfrak K^\sharp[(\beta-a^{-1}w_x)\Xi]$ in the place of $\beta\mathfrak K^\sharp[\Xi]$, the same bound holds with a number $\mathsf a(x)$, the numbers $C_2,p_2,K_2$ being free of $x$ and of $\mathsf b'$.

The number $\mathsf a(x)$ is the sum, over the levels $j\le t$, of the values at the configuration $\mathbf 1$ of local families of the level $j$ whose member at a polymer $X$ reads $w_x$ and $\Xi$ on the plaquettes of $X$ alone and vanishes if $\Xi$ vanishes at the barycentres of these plaquettes. For free photons the cubic piece vanishes identically.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(a) The entry is typed anew at each level. At a height $j\ge1$ the sum of the $\varkappa_\iota j_\iota$ over the boxes whose cubes of the level $j$ form a given polymer is a pointed family of the level $j$: at most $8N(ML^j)^3$ boxes have one polymer, and on the cores each density is at most $c\,\alpha_0^{m_J}L^{-2m_Jj}$ by its order, so that the family has the size $8NM^3c\,\alpha_0^{m_J}|\varkappa|_\infty L^{-(2m_J-3)j}$; this is the power counting, of order $|\varkappa|_\infty L^{(3-2m_J)j}$ in level-$j$ units. At the height $0$ the family in the fourth place $\sum_\iota\varkappa_\iota[j_\iota(e^{iB'}\mathbf U)-j_\iota(\mathbf U)]$, $B'$ the fluctuation field with its values at the pivot bonds, sums to $J(e^{iB'}\mathbf U)-J(\mathbf U)$ and has the size of a number times $N\hat c\,\delta(x_0)|\varkappa|_\infty$, by the height and Schwarz's lemma in the fluctuation field.

So for $|s|<r_J$, $r_J^{-1}\le C|\varkappa|_\infty$ with $C$ reading $N$, $c$ and $\hat c$, the entry enters each step as one more local term, inside the radii of the one-step theorem with sources (Prop.~\ref{prop:source-entry}); the members of the families are holomorphic in $s$ and read $s$ only on the polymers that the entry meets. The identity of the measures follows by induction on $k$ from the recursion of $\mathsf p_k$: the images $\nu^s_k=(\mathcal M^k)_*(\mathsf p_ke^{sJ}\rho_0dU)$ obey $\nu^s_{k+1}=\mathbf 1_{{\rm Cut}_{k+1}}\mathbf T(\mathfrak G_k[x_k]\chi^{\rm sf}_{x_k}\nu^s_k)$, the small-field pushforward in {\cite[Lem.~B.3]{YMM2}}, a chart integral over ${\rm Rg}_{x_k}$ that the one-step theorem evaluates; one function $e^{\Phi^s_k}$ is both the density reached at the level $k$ and the integrand of the step from the level $k$.

The derivative of the exponent in $s$ at $0$ is the conditional mean up to the number $\dot c_t=\sum_i\partial_sc_i(0)$. On ${\rm Cut}_t$ the plaquette variables of the background are within $\mathsf e^{\rm c}_tL^{-2t}$ of $\mathbf 1$, $\mathsf e^{\rm c}_t$ the radius of the field cut, so that the entry at the background is at most $N(\ell L^K)^3c\,(\mathsf e^{\rm c}_t)^{m_J}L^{-2m_Jt}|\varkappa|_\infty$; with what the families of the earlier levels carry, $|\Phi^s_t-\Phi^{s'}_t|\le|s-s'|\,\mathsf o_t$ with $\mathsf o_t$ of the order of the stated oscillation, which is at most $2\mathsf o_t$. The threshold $K\ge K_\phi$ makes $t$ a top level of the setting (Th): $(1-\phi)K\ge2$ gives $1\le t\le K-1$, $L^{\phi K}\gamma^{-2}\ge\mathsf t_\natural$ gives $x_t=L^u\mathsf b'\ge\mathsf t_\natural$, and the third condition keeps the size of a source at the coupling $x_k$, $k\le t$, below the bound of the step; this size $\theta_k$ obeys $L\theta_k\le\Theta_KL^{-(K-k)/2}$, $\Theta_K$ a power of $K$. (b) Let $S=\beta\mathfrak K^\sharp[\Xi]=\sum_p\varkappa(p)\mathfrak r^\sharp_{\lambda(p)}(p)$, $\varkappa(p)=L^{2K}\mathsf b'\,\Xi^{\lambda(p)}(x(p))$, so that $\max|\varkappa|\le L^{2K}\mathsf b_+\mathsf H(\Xi)$; the density vanishes to the third order at $\mathbf 1$ (Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(b)).

At a real source the weight is moved, $\varkappa(p)=L^{2K}(\mathsf b'-w_x(x(p)))\Xi^{\lambda(p)}(x(p))$, and the chain carries the source; we write the source $0$, the other case being the same with the index $w_x$. Let $s_0=S$ and $s_j=S\circ U_j$ on ${\rm Cut}_j$, the entry read at the background of the level $j$. For a pointed family $\mathsf f$ of a level $\le n$ let $\Sigma_n[\mathsf f](V)$, $V\in{\rm Cut}_n$, be the sum over the polymers of the members of $\mathsf f$ at the background $U_n(V)$, and ${\rm Sum}[\mathsf f](\mathbf 1)$ the same sum at the configuration $\mathbf 1$, a number. Let $S_n\mathsf f$ be the first-order response of the step from the level $n$ to a family $\mathsf f$ of a level $i\le n$, a family of the level $n+1$ with $\|S_n\mathsf f\|_{n+1}\le\theta_nL^{-(n-i)}\|\mathsf f\|_i$, so that $Q_n\Sigma_n[\mathsf f]=\Sigma_{n+1}[\mathsf f+S_n\mathsf f]$ on ${\rm Cut}_{n+1}$; and let $D^{(j)}=D^{(j)}[w;\varkappa]$ be the family born at the level $j$ from the entry at the source $w$ and the weight $\varkappa$: $Q_{j-1}s_{j-1}-s_j=\Sigma_j[D^{(j)}]$ on ${\rm Cut}_j$.

With $T_t={\rm id}$ and $T_n\mathsf g=T_{n+1}(\mathsf g+S_n\mathsf g)$, the carriage of a family from the level $n$ to the level $t$ with all that it feeds, $Q_{t-1}\cdots Q_n\Sigma_n[\mathsf g]=\Sigma_t[T_n\mathsf g]$; so, with $n_0=K-\lceil\frac K7\rceil$ and $Q_{t\leftarrow n_0}=Q_{t-1}\cdots Q_{n_0}$,
\[
Q_{t\leftarrow0}S=Q_{t\leftarrow n_0}s_{n_0}+\sum_{j\le n_0}\Sigma_t[T_jD^{(j)}]\qquad\text{on }{\rm Cut}_t .
\]
The births are small by the parity in the fluctuation field: the part of the variation of the density that is odd in the fluctuation field has the size $g_{j-1}=x_{j-1}^{-1/2}$ and the Gaussian mean $0$, so that it meets only the odd part of the interaction, of the size $g_{j-1}(\log x_{j-1})^{\mathfrak p_0}$, while the even part has the size $g_{j-1}^2$; so $\|D^{(j)}\|\le C(\log x_{j-1})^{\mathfrak p_0}g_{j-1}^2L^{-3(j-1)}\max|\varkappa|$ once $K-j$ exceeds a fixed construction threshold, and $L^j\|D^{(j)}\|\le CK^{\mathfrak p_0}L^{K-j}\mathsf H(\Xi)$. $T_jD^{(j)}$ is $D^{(j)}$ plus the sum of the chains $S_{k_m}\cdots S_{k_1}D^{(j)}$, $j\le k_1<\dots<k_m<t$, of the families that it feeds; each chain is stopped at a level $n$ of its own, chosen with the free fraction $\tau$, at which the variation ${\rm Sum}[\mathsf f](U_n(V))-{\rm Sum}[\mathsf f](\mathbf 1)$ of a family $\mathsf f$ of the level $i$ is at most $\beta_nL^i\|\mathsf f\|_i$, $\beta_n=CK^pL^{3(K-n)-K}$, the square of the radius of regularity of the level $n$ entering. $Q_{t\leftarrow n}$ does not enlarge an oscillation, and each feeding costs $L\theta_k\le\Theta_KL^{-(K-k)/2}$, so that what is fed is forgotten.

The variation of ${\rm Sum}[D^{(j)}]$ over ${\rm Cut}_{n_0}$, $j<n_0$, is where the parity of the cubic density enters. The step is covariant under the isometries of the lattice of its level, and $\mathfrak r^\sharp$ transforms as a vector (Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(b)); so under the inversion $r_z:y\mapsto2z-y$ through a site $z$ of the lattice of the level $j$, ${\rm Sum}[D^{(j)}[w;\varkappa]](r_zU)=-{\rm Sum}[D^{(j)}[r_z^*w;r_z^*\varkappa]](U)$, $(r_z^*v)(p)=v(r_zp)$. With a partition of unity $\psi_z\ge0$ over these sites, $\psi_z\circ r_z=\psi_z$, $\psi_z(p)=0$ unless $|x(p)-z|_\infty\le\frac12L^{j-K}$, and $\Sigma_z[w;\varkappa]={\rm Sum}[D^{(j)}[w;\psi_z\varkappa]]$, this gives the exact split
\[
\begin{multlined}
\Sigma_z[w;\varkappa](U)=\tfrac12\bigl(\Sigma_z[w;\varkappa](U)-\Sigma_z[w;\varkappa](r_zU)\bigr)+\tfrac12\Sigma_z[w;\varkappa-r_z^*\varkappa](U)+\tfrac12\bigl(\Sigma_z[w;r_z^*\varkappa](U) \\
-\Sigma_z[r_z^*w;r_z^*\varkappa](U)\bigr).
\end{multlined}
\]
(I) The first part compares the background with its image under $r_z$. In the H\"older gauge (Thm.~\textup{{\cite[Thm.~BT]{YMM2}}} for real backgrounds) the curvature, a $2$-form, is even under the inversion, so that the linear part of the potential is kept and the potential and its image differ by the odd part of the H\"older remainder, at most $R^2\vartheta^{2+b}e_3$ on a cube of the radius $R$ about $z$, $\vartheta=L^{-(n_0-j)}$, $b=\frac34$, $e_3$ of the order of the radius of regularity of the level $n_0$: a gain $\vartheta^b$. (II) The second part carries the asymmetry of the weight, $|\varkappa-r_z^*\varkappa|\le L^{2K}{\rm Lip}(\Xi)L^{j-K}$ where $\psi_z\ne0$. (III) The third part is the asymmetry of the source in the step: it vanishes at the source $0$, and at a real source it is of the second order at the trivial triple, of the size ${\rm Lip}(w_x)\,\delta(x_{j-1})$, $\delta(x_{j-1})$ of the order of $L^{-(K-j)/2}$ being the threshold of the level.

Summed over $j<n_0$, the parts (I), (II) and (III) are $O(L^{-3K/14})$, $O(L^{-4K/7})$ and $O(L^{-K/14})$; the stopped entry contributes $O(L^{-5K/14})$ and the family born at $n_0$ $O(L^{-3K/7})$; forgetting leaves $O(L^{-(\frac1{14}-\frac\tau7)K})$ of what is fed, and against the factor $L^{3u}$ of the levels above $t$ it leaves $O(L^{-(\frac1{14}-3\phi)K})$; all this up to powers of $K$. The least of these exponents is $c'_0$; at the source $0$ the last two meet at $\frac1{14}$ as $\tau,\phi\to0$, and at a real source the part (III) meets them there. The number $\mathsf a$, the sum of the values at the configuration $\mathbf 1$ of the families born and fed up to their levels of stopping, depends on no $V$, and each of these families reads the source and the weight on its polymer alone and vanishes where the weight vanishes.

The numbers are uniform on $[\mathsf b_-,\mathsf b_+]$ because the frame of {\cite[Def.~B.14]{YMM2}} holds for the chain along $x_j=L^{K-j}\mathsf b'$ at every label of the interval and $\mathsf b'$ enters only through $x_i\in[\gamma^{-2}L^{K-i},\mathsf b_+L^{K-i}]$ and $\max|\varkappa|$, each time in a monotone way; on the polydisc $\mathbb D_t$ the source stays in the class of the setting (Th) and the mass of the small-field chain stays away from $0$, and at real $x$ the measures of the chain are positive.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The cubic remainder]\label{C-360-10}
In the setting of Lem.~\ref{C-360-9}, let $n\ge1$, $\mathsf d>0$ and $c<\frac1{14}$. There are $C,p$, free of $K$ and of $\mathsf b'$, such that for all $K\ge2$, $\mathsf b'\in[\mathsf b_-,\mathsf b_+]$, $\beta=L^K\mathsf b'$, all real Lipschitz $f_i$ and all fields $\eta$, the spread of $\{\eta\ne0\},{\rm supp}\,f_1,\dots,{\rm supp}\,f_n$ being $\ge\mathsf d$,
\[
|\mathfrak U^\sharp[\eta](f)|\le CK^pL^{-cK}\mathsf H(\eta)\prod_i\|f_i\|_\sharp .
\]
The spread condition holds if two of the sets are at sup distance $\ge\mathsf d$, and if $\eta=0$ within the sup distance $\mathsf d$ of one support. By $x\mapsto L^zx$ the same holds at every label and on every side.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Moving the weight of the entry with the sources produces the contact terms:
\[
\mathfrak U^\sharp[\eta](f)=-\partial_s\partial_{z_1}\cdots\partial_{z_n}\log\Bigl\langle\exp\Bigl(s\,\mathfrak K^\sharp\bigl[(\beta-a^{-1}\textstyle\sum_iz_if_i)\eta\bigr]+\sum_iz_i\mathcal O(f_i)\Bigr)\Bigr\rangle\Big|_{s=z=0}.
\]
After discarding the histories with large fields, Lem.~\ref{C-360-9}(b), applied to the chain with the real sources $x$ in its polydisc $\mathbb D_t$ and to the field $\eta$, makes the conditional mean of the entry with the moved weight equal, up to $\varepsilon=K^pL^{-c'_0K}$, to its number $\mathsf a(x)$; and $\mathsf a(x)$ is a sum $\sum_ic_i(x)$ of functions each of which does not depend on $x_i$, up to a remainder below every power of $L^{-K}$. Indeed, let $c_i(x)$ collect the members of the families of $\mathsf a(x)$ at the polymers on whose plaquettes $f_i$ is the first of the sources that vanishes at all the barycentres; such a member reads the sources on its polymer alone, so it does not read $x_i$; the members at the other polymers, which meet $\{\eta\ne0\}$ and all the ${\rm supp}\,f_i$, are left over; under the spread such a polymer of the level $j$ has the linear size $\ge\mathsf dL^{K-j}/M-3$, so that these members cost $e^{-\mathsf dL^{K-j}/M}$ against the sizes.

Such sums have no mixed derivative. At complex sources the mean is crudely at most $B=C\ell^3L^{3K}\max|\varkappa|$, $\varkappa$ the weight of the entry. Interpolating between the two bounds, the mixed derivative is at most $2^n\varepsilon^{1-\sigma}B^\sigma(\frac{4n}{\pi\sigma})^n\prod_ir_i^{-1}$ with $r_i^{-1}\le CK^{2\mathfrak p_0}\ell^3L^{3u}\|f_i\|_\sharp$, and $\sigma,\phi,\tau$ small give every $c<\frac1{14}$. The finitely many $K<K_2$ are paid by the crude bound of the cumulant by the suprema of its entries, which goes into $C$. For $n\ge2$ the bound holds also where $\{\eta\ne0\}$ covers the supports, as in the uses below, since the spread of the $n+1$ sets is at least that of the supports among themselves.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Chessboard bound in one cell]\label{C-360-11}
Let $0<g\le\gamma$, $\ell'=2\mathsf l\in\mathfrak L(g)$, $0<\phi\le\frac1{84}$, $u=\lceil\phi K\rceil$, $t=K-u$, $0<\delta\le\frac18\mathsf l$ and $m\ge1$. There are $C,p,K_3$, depending on $g,\ell',\phi,m,\delta$, such that for $(K,\beta)\in\mathfrak D(g)$ with $K\ge K_3$, every board of side $\mathsf l$ with offset in $a_{K-t}\mathbb Z^3=L^{-u}\mathbb Z^3$, every cell, every $\mathsf d$ with $\mathsf dL^u\ge K^2$, and $m$ slots $X_1,\dots,X_m$ supported in the cell at sup distance $\ge\delta$ from its walls and pairwise $\ge\mathsf d$ apart,
\[
\Bigl\|\prod_a\bigl(X_a-\langle X_a\rangle_{K,\ell',\beta}\bigr)\Bigr\|_{\rm ch}\le C\prod_a\varpi(X_a)\,\mathsf n(X_a),
\]
where a slot is $\mathcal T_K(H)$, with $\varpi=K^pL^{4u}$ and $\mathsf n=|H|_\infty$, or one of 
\[
\mathcal T_K(H^{\rm cons}[\eta]),\mathrm{St}_K[\eta],\Delta_K[\eta],\mathrm{Rm}_K[\eta],\mathfrak K^{\rm v}[\beta\eta]
,\]
with $\varpi=K^pL^{3u-K/28}$ and $\mathsf n=\|\eta\|_{C^2}$. For $m=1$ and $\phi=\frac1{400}$ we have $\|\mathrm{St}_K[\eta]-\langle\cdot\rangle\|_{\rm ch}\le CK^pL^{-K/28}\|\eta\|_{C^2}$ and 
\[
\|\Delta_K[\eta]-\langle\cdot\rangle\|_{\rm ch}+\|\mathcal T_K(H^{\rm cons}[\eta])-\langle\cdot\rangle\|_{\rm ch}\le CK^pL^{-K/36}\|\eta\|_{C^2}
;\]
for a plain tensor entry $\|\mathcal T_K(H')-\langle\cdot\rangle\|_{\rm ch}\le CK^{2\mathfrak p_0}L^{K/100}|H'|_\infty$. At $m=1$ and $\phi=\frac1{400}$, moreover, $\|\mathrm{Rm}_K[\eta]-\langle\cdot\rangle\|_{\rm ch}=\|\mathrm{St}_K[\eta]-\langle\cdot\rangle\|_{\rm ch}$, and the bound $CK^pL^{-K/28}\|\eta\|_{C^2}$ holds also for $\|F_\eta\|_{\rm ch}$, where
\[
F_\eta=\mathfrak K^{\rm v}[\beta\eta]-\tfrac14\mathfrak N[\mathsf k_\eta]=\beta\mathfrak K^\sharp[\eta]-\sum_{v=1}^5\mathfrak J_v[\mathsf k_\eta]+\tfrac14c_{\mathsf k_\eta},\qquad\langle F_\eta\rangle_{K,\ell',\beta}=0,
\]
with $\mathsf k^\rho_\eta=\nabla^+_\rho\eta^\rho$ and the objects of Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(c); for every state $s$ of Lem.~\ref{C-360-7}, $s(\mathfrak K^{\rm v}[\beta\eta])=s(F_\eta)$, so that $|s(\mathfrak K^{\rm v}[\beta\eta])|\le e^{G_g\mathsf l^3}\|F_\eta\|_{\rm ch}$ by Lem.~\ref{C-360-7} at $q=1$, $c_1=0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
By Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(c), $\mathrm{St}_K[\eta]=N_\beta[\eta]-\frac14\mathfrak N[\mathsf k_\eta]-\mathrm{Rm}_K[\eta]-\frac14c_{\mathsf k_\eta}$, so that the slots $\mathrm{St}_K[\eta]$ and $-\mathrm{Rm}_K[\eta]$ differ by null terms and a number; inside the mean of the $8m$ mirror copies on $T_{\ell'}$ the null terms drop, since no other copy depends on their bonds. A product of centred slots in one cell expands into joint cumulants over the partitions into blocks of at least two members. Apply {\cite[Prop.~3.15]{YMM2}}(a), with its common insertion radius $r_1$, size $\bar{\mathsf d}$ and polymer sum $\mathsf t_\times$. It bounds the higher mixed jets of the exponent as well as the separate conditional means and gives
\[
|\langle J_0;\dots;J_r\rangle|\le{\rm op}_{r+1}\prod_a\omega_t(J_a)+9\cdot2^{r+1}(r+2)\bar{\mathsf d}\,\mathsf t_\times r_1^{-r}+4\,{\rm op}'_{r+1}\mathsf R_t\prod_a\sup|J_a|,\qquad{\rm op}_n=\sum_{\pi}(|\pi|-1)!,
\]
$\pi$ over the partitions of $n$ points, with ${\rm op}'_n$ as in {\cite[Prop.~3.15]{YMM2}}; $\omega_t$ is the oscillation of the conditional mean (Lem.~\ref{C-360-9}) and $\mathsf R_t$ the weight of the histories with large fields. After allowing the carrier collars, take $\mathsf d_\times\ge c\min\{\mathsf d,\delta\}$. The hypothesis $\mathsf dL^u\ge K^2$ gives $\mathsf d_\times L^u\ge cK^2$ for all sufficiently large $K$, uniformly in $\mathsf d$. The prefactor estimates in the proof of {\cite[Prop.~3.24]{YMM2}} bound the second term by a polynomial in $K$ times $L^{AK}e^{-cK^2}$; thus the condition of {\cite[Prop.~3.15]{YMM2}}(a) holds and this term is below any prescribed $L^{-BK}$. The large-field term is controlled there separately. Six of the seven pieces of $\mathrm{Rm}_K$ are small by power counting, the seventh is the cubic one, of oscillation $K^pL^{-c'_0K}$. The principal part of $\Delta_K$ is null (Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(d)): on the backgrounds of the level $K-\lceil\frac K{14}\rceil$ its value is at most $CK^{2\mathfrak p_0}L^{\frac72\lceil K/14\rceil-\frac K2}\mathsf b\sup|\nabla\eta|$, what is born below that level is born at a small coupling and is forgotten, and a conditional mean is never larger than a supremum.

Each crude tensor entry costs $L^{4u}$. At $m=1$: by (a)--(c) of Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}, $\mathfrak K^{\rm v}[\beta\eta]=\frac14\mathfrak N[\mathsf k_\eta]+\beta\mathfrak K^\sharp[\eta]-\sum_v\mathfrak J_v[\mathsf k_\eta]+\frac14c_{\mathsf k_\eta}$, so that $F_\eta$ consists of six of the seven pieces of $\mathrm{Rm}_K[\eta]$ and a number. The cubic piece has the oscillation $K^pL^{-K/28}\|\eta\|_{C^2}$ by Lem.~\ref{C-360-9}(b) at $\tau=\frac14$, where $c'_0=\frac1{28}$ for $\phi\le\frac1{84}$; the five pieces $\mathfrak J_v$, of the orders $2,2,2$ with weights of the order of $\|\eta\|_{C^2}$ and of the orders $3,4$ with weights at most $\beta\|\eta\|_{C^2}$, have oscillations at most $K^{3\mathfrak p_0}L^{4u-K/2}\|\eta\|_{C^2}$ by Lem.~\ref{C-360-9}(a); so no factor $L^{3u}$ enters the bound of $F_\eta$; in the bounds of the slots of the kind of $\eta$ it enters through $\Delta_K$ alone.

The means of $\mathfrak K^{\rm v}[\beta\eta]$ and of $\mathfrak N[\mathsf k_\eta]$ on $T_{\ell'}$ are $0$ (Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(a), (b)), so is that of $F_\eta$, and $s(\mathfrak N[\mathsf k_\eta])=0$ in every state $s$ by Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(a).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[From sup norms to an integrable density]\label{C-360-12}
Let $H\ge0$ be self-adjoint, $T_t=e^{-tH}$, and for every $\eta>0$ let $\rho\mapsto S_\eta[\rho]$ be linear from $C_c((-\eta,\eta))$ to the bounded operators, with $\|S_\eta[\rho]\|\le A_J\sup|\rho|$ for ${\rm supp}\,\rho$ in a compact $J\subset(-\eta,\eta)$, and $S_\eta[\rho(\cdot-c)]=T_{\delta+c}S_{\eta-\delta}[\rho]T_{\delta-c}$ for $|c|\le\delta<\eta$. Then there is a unique family of bounded operators $B(s,s')$, $s,s'>0$, with $T_tB(s,s')T_{t'}=B(s+t,s'+t')$ and $S_\eta[\rho]=\int\rho(c)B(\eta+c,\eta-c)\,\mathrm{d}c$; for $0<\gamma'<\eta$ and ${\rm supp}\,\rho\subset[-(\eta-\gamma'),\eta-\gamma']$, $\|S_\eta[\rho]\|\le\|S_{\gamma'/2}[{\rm tent}_{\gamma'/8}]\|\,\|\rho\|_{L^1}$; and $B(s,s')^*=B(s',s)$ if $S_\eta[\rho]^*=S_\eta[\bar\rho(-\cdot)]$. The same holds in the space directions for commuting momenta $P$ with $H\ge|P_k|$ in the direction $k$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
For $G$ holomorphic and bounded on the strip $\{|{\rm Re}\,z|<h'\}$, $h'>2h$, integrating $\Gamma(z)\sin^{-2}(\pi z/2h)$, $\Gamma'=G$, over the boundary of the strip gives
\[
G(0)=\int\mu_2(\,\mathrm{d}s)\int{\rm tent}_{2h}(c)\,G(c+is)\,\mathrm{d}c,\qquad\mu_2=\mu_1*\mu_1,\quad\mu_1(\,\mathrm{d}s)=\tfrac\pi{4h}{\rm sech}^2\bigl(\tfrac{\pi s}{2h}\bigr)\,\mathrm{d}s .
\]
Thus an average in real time inverts a tent smearing in Euclidean time. Apply it to $z\mapsto\langle T_{\delta+\bar z}\psi_2,S[\rho]T_{\delta-z}\psi_1\rangle$ for vectors $\psi_1,\psi_2$, holomorphic by the covariance, and use $\rho_0*\rho_1=\rho_1*\rho_0$: the $\mu_2$-average of $e^{-isH}S_{\gamma'/2}[{\rm tent}]e^{isH}$ is the operator $\mathbb B$ of the density, $S_\eta[\rho]=\int\rho(c)T_{\eta-\gamma'/2+c}\mathbb BT_{\eta-\gamma'/2-c}\,\mathrm{d}c$. In space, $G(0)=\int h_{d'}(x)\frac12[G(x+id')+G(x-id')]\,\mathrm{d}x$ with $h_{d'}=(2d')^{-1}{\rm sech}(\pi x/2d')$, with the imaginary translations that $H\ge|P|$ allows.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Functions of the block field]\label{C-360-17}
For a history $h$ let $\mathfrak w_h\ge0$ be its weight in the law of the field and of the history and $\mathsf t(h)=\int\mathfrak w_h\rho_0\,\mathrm{d}U$ its mass, so that $\sum_h\mathsf t(h)=Z$ (equations~\YMMref{(646)--(648)}{342} and Prop.~\YMMref{44.1}{342}).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] In the setting of Lem.~\ref{C-360-9}, let $1\le t\le K-1$ be a level up to which the chain is formed (a top level of the chain at the label $\mathsf b'$), $h_t$ the history without large-field regions of the level $t$, ${\rm In}_t=\{V:\varpi(V)<2\varepsilon(x_t)\}\subset{\rm Cut}_t$ the inner ball of the level $t$ (the definitions preceding Lem.~\YMMref{113.10}{796}; $\varpi(V)$ is the largest $|\partial V(p')-\mathbf 1|$ over the plaquettes $p'$ of the level $t$), and $\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}_t$ the weight of the level $t$ of the small-field chain with its number $\mathsf R_t$ (the definitions preceding Prop.~\YMMref{115.2}{806}, the definition preceding Prop.~\YMMref{115.2}{806}, \YMMref{(2187)}{806}): $\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}_t(U)=\mathbf 1_{{\rm In}_t}(\mathcal M^tU)\prod_{i<t}[\mathbf 1_{{\rm Cut}_i}\mathfrak G_i[x_i]\chi^{\rm sf}_{x_i}](\mathcal M^iU)$, with the gauge-fixing factors $\mathfrak G_i[x_i]$ and the fluctuation tests $\chi^{\rm sf}_{x_i}$ among the construction results, so that $\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}_t=(\mathbf 1_{{\rm In}_t}\circ\mathcal M^t)\,\mathsf p_t$ with $\mathsf p_t(U):=\mathbf 1_{{\rm Cut}_t}(\mathcal M^tU)\prod_{i<t}[\mathbf 1_{{\rm Cut}_i}\mathfrak G_i[x_i]\chi^{\rm sf}_{x_i}](\mathcal M^iU)$.

The measure $\nu_t$ of the level $t$ of the chain is $(\mathcal M^t)_*(\mathsf p_t\rho_0\,\mathrm{d}U)$ (Prop.~\YMMref{114.2}{801}, the measure recursion in Prop.~\YMMref{114.2}{801}), and $Q_{t\leftarrow0}$ is the conditional mean given $\mathcal M^tU$ under $\mathsf p_t\rho_0\,\mathrm{d}U$; the tower of Lem.~\ref{C-360-9} is read with this $\mathsf p_t$. By Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{115.2}{806}}, $\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}_t$ is a bounded Borel function with values in $[0,\infty)$, $(\mathcal M^t)_*(\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}_t\rho_0\,\mathrm{d}U)=\mathbf 1_{{\rm In}_t}\nu_t$ \YMMref{(2188)}{806}, $0\le\mathfrak w_{h_t}\le\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}_t$ at every point \YMMref{(2189)}{806}, and $0\le Z-\int\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}_t\rho_0\,\mathrm{d}U\le Z-\mathsf t(h_t)\le\mathsf R_tZ$ \YMMref{(2190)}{806}: $\mathsf R_t$ bounds the weight of the histories with a large field up to the level $t$.

For every bounded real Borel gauge invariant $Y$, real $a_0$ and $\epsilon\ge0$ with $|Q_{t\leftarrow0}Y-a_0|\le\epsilon$ $\nu_t$-almost everywhere on ${\rm In}_t$, and every bounded Borel function $\psi$ of the block fields of the level $t$, $|\langle Y;\psi\circ\mathcal M^t\rangle|\le2[\epsilon+2(\sup|Y|+|a_0|)\mathsf R_t]\sup|\psi|$; if besides $\mathsf R_t\le\frac12$, then $|a_0|\le\sup|Y|+\epsilon$.
\item[(ii)] In the setting of Lem.~\ref{C-360-24} at $0<g\le\gamma$ with $g^{-2}\ge x_{\rm J}$ (a first-passage datum $(K,\beta)\in\mathfrak D(g)$, a side $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$, a depth $s$ and the working level $k$), let $2\le T\le k$ be a level, $h_T$ the history without large-field regions of the level $T$, $\mathsf m_T=\tau_{h_T}[\rho_0]$ (Lem.~\ref{C-360-24}(a)), and $W_T<1$ the weight of a first creation of a large field at a level $\le T$, so that $Z-\mathsf t(h_T)=W_TZ$. A dominated local source $F_2$ acts on a dominated local source $F_1$ at the sup distance $\mathsf d'$, with $L^{K-T}\mathsf d'\ge3M$ and $\mathsf h_2(K-T)\le1$ (the conditions of Lem.~\ref{C-360-24}(e) at $t=T$), through a bounded function of the block field of the level $T$: let $r_2$ be the real part of the bounded density $D_{T,2}$ of $\tau_{h_T}[F_2\rho_0]$ with respect to $\mathsf m_T$, $c$ real, $E$ the essential supremum of $|r_2-c|$ for $\mathsf m_T$, and $\psi=(r_2-c)\mathbf 1\{|r_2-c|\le E\}$, a bounded real Borel function with $\sup|\psi|\le E$ and $\psi=r_2-c$ $\mathsf m_T$-almost everywhere; then
\[
|\langle F_1;F_2\rangle-\langle F_1;\psi\circ\mathcal M^T\rangle|\le C_2e^{3-\mathsf D_T/M}y_1y_2+2\sup|F_1|\bigl(\sup|F_2|+\sup|\psi|+|c|\bigr)W_T,
\]
with $y_a\le4\ell^3L^{4(K-T)}$ times the sizes of the sources and $\mathsf D_T\ge L^{K-T}\mathsf d'$ the least sup distance of the carriers in level-$T$ units; at $c={\rm Re}\,c_2$, $c_2$ the constant of $F_2$ at the level $T$, $E\le C_1y_2$ and $|c|\le\sup|F_2|+C_1y_2$. The display is additive in $F_1$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The law of the field and of the history, Prop.~\YMMref{44.1}{342} with the measures in equation~\YMMref{(647)}{342}, gives \[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbf T^k(\Psi\rho_0\,\mathrm{d}U)&=\sum_h\tau_h[\Psi\rho_0],\\
 \int F\,\mathrm{d}\tau_h[\Psi\rho_0]
 &=\int F(\mathcal M^kU)\,\mathfrak w_h(U)\Psi(U)\rho_0(U)\,\mathrm{d}U
\end{aligned}
\] for every bounded gauge invariant $\Psi$, when $\varepsilon_j\le\varepsilon_\flat=c_2^{\rm SO}$ for $j<k$; hence $Z\langle\Psi\cdot\psi\circ\mathcal M^k\rangle=\sum_{h}\int\psi\,\mathrm{d}\tau_h[\Psi\rho_0]$, and, as $\mathfrak w_h\ge0$ and $\sum_h\mathsf t(h)=Z$, \[
 \left|Z\langle\Psi\cdot\psi\circ\mathcal M^k\rangle-
 \int\psi\,\mathrm{d}\tau_{h_k}[\Psi\rho_0]\right|
 \le\sup|\Psi|\sup|\psi|\,(Z-\mathsf t(h_k)).
\] (i) At the level $t$ replace $\mathfrak w_{h_t}$ by $\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}_t$: the difference $\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}_t-\mathfrak w_{h_t}$ is $\ge0$ at every point, of the mass $\int\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}_t\rho_0\,\mathrm{d}U-\mathsf t(h_t)\le Z-\mathsf t(h_t)\le\mathsf R_tZ$; with the histories other than $h_t$ this gives $|Z\langle\Psi\cdot\psi\circ\mathcal M^t\rangle-\int\Psi\,\psi(\mathcal M^tU)\,\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}_t\rho_0\,\mathrm{d}U|\le2\sup|\Psi|\sup|\psi|\mathsf R_tZ$, the factor $2$ counting the two parts.

By the tower property, $\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}_t=(\mathbf 1_{{\rm In}_t}\circ\mathcal M^t)\mathsf p_t$ and ${\rm In}_t\subset{\rm Cut}_t$, $\int\psi(\mathcal M^tU)\,(Y-a_0)\,\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}_t\rho_0\,\mathrm{d}U=\int_{{\rm In}_t}\psi\,(Q_{t\leftarrow0}Y-a_0)\,\mathrm{d}\nu_t$, of a modulus at most $\epsilon\int_{{\rm In}_t}|\psi|\,\mathrm{d}\nu_t\le\epsilon\sup|\psi|\,Z$, since $\nu_t\ge0$ and $\nu_t({\rm In}_t)=\int\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}_t\rho_0\,\mathrm{d}U\le Z$. Applied at $\Psi=Y-a_0$, for $\psi$ and for $1$, with $\langle Y;\psi\circ\mathcal M^t\rangle=\langle(Y-a_0)\,\psi\circ\mathcal M^t\rangle-\langle Y-a_0\rangle\langle\psi\circ\mathcal M^t\rangle$, this is the bound of (i). If $\mathsf R_t\le\frac12$: $|Q_{t\leftarrow0}Y|\le\sup|Y|$ $\nu_t$-almost everywhere and $\nu_t({\rm In}_t)\ge(1-\mathsf R_t)Z>0$, so ${\rm In}_t$ holds points at which $|a_0|\le|Q_{t\leftarrow0}Y|+\epsilon\le\sup|Y|+\epsilon$. (ii) By the first display at the level $T$, where $Z-\mathsf t(h_T)=W_TZ$, the means $\langle F_1F_2\rangle$, $\langle F_1\,\psi\circ\mathcal M^T\rangle$, $\langle F_1\rangle$, $\langle F_2\rangle$ and $\langle\psi\circ\mathcal M^T\rangle$ are the integrals against $Z^{-1}\mathsf m_T$ of the bounded densities of these functions at $h_T$, up to the weight $W_T$ times their suprema, and $Z^{-1}\mathsf m_T(1)=1-W_T$.

The densities of $F_1$, $F_2$ and $F_1F_2$ are $D_{T,1}$, $D_{T,2}$ and $D_{T,1}D_{T,2}+D_{T,12}$; the real part $r_2$ of $D_{T,2}$ is again a density of the real source $F_2$, two bounded densities of one function agree $\mathsf m_T$-almost everywhere, and $r_2=\psi+c$ there; so the density of $F_1F_2$ is $D_{T,12}+D_{T,1}(\psi+c)$ almost everywhere, and subtracting, $\langle F_1;F_2\rangle-\langle F_1;\psi\circ\mathcal M^T\rangle$ is $Z^{-1}\int D_{T,12}\,\mathrm{d}\mathsf m_T$, at most $C_2e^{3-\mathsf D_T/M}y_1y_2$ by Lem.~\ref{C-360-24}(e), plus two brackets of errors that together are at most $2\sup|F_1|(\sup|F_2|+\sup|\psi|+|c|)W_T$. At $c={\rm Re}\,c_2$: $|r_2-c|\le|D_{T,2}-c_2|\le C_1y_2$ on the small block fields of the level $T$, which carry $\mathsf m_T$ (Lem.~\ref{C-360-24}(e)), and $|r_2|\le\sup|F_2|$ there.

Every member but $D_{T,12}$ is formed with $F_1$ linearly, and $D_{T,12}$ is additive in $F_1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[One entry against separated sources]\label{C-360-18}
Let $0<g\le\gamma$, $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$, $n\ge1$, $\mathsf d>0$, $0<c_*<\frac12$, and let $J=\sum_\iota\varkappa_\iota j_\iota$ be an entry of the order $m\ge2$ (Lem.~\ref{C-360-9}) of the type $(m,c,\hat c,N)$: at complex configurations with $|\mathbf U(b)|\le2$ at all the bonds of its box, $|j_\iota|\le c\,r^m$ where the plaquette variables of the box are within $r\le1$ of $\mathbf 1$, and $|j_\iota|\le\hat c$ everywhere; and at most $N$ indices have boxes with one lowest site. There are $C,K_1$, depending on $g$, $\ell$, $n$, $\mathsf d$, $c_*$ and the type, such that for $K\ge K_1$, every label $\mathsf b'\in[\gamma^{-2},X_g+\bar B]$ (so at every first-passage datum $(K,\beta)\in\mathfrak D(g)$, and at $\beta=L^K\mathsf b'$ for every $\mathsf b'\in I(g)$) and all real Lipschitz $f_q$, if the spread of the $n+1$ sets formed by the carrier of $J$ and the ${\rm supp}\,f_q$ is $\ge\mathsf d$, as it is when two of them are at sup distance $\ge\mathsf d$,
\[
\begin{multlined}
|\langle J;\mathcal O(f_1);\dots;\mathcal O(f_n)\rangle_{K,\ell,L^K\mathsf b'}|\le C|\varkappa|_\infty L^{-\mathsf g_mK}K^{(2n+1)\mathfrak p_0}L^{(\frac12-c_*)K}\prod_q\|f_q\|_\sharp,\qquad\mathsf g_2=1,\ \relax \mathsf g_m \\
=\tfrac32\ \relax (m\ge3).
\end{multlined}
\]
On all the sides at once: let besides $R>0$ and $\ell'\in\mathfrak L(g)$ with $\ell'\ge2R+2\mathsf d$, and let the weights $\varkappa_\iota$ be real and the densities real on the $G$-valued configurations. There are $C',K'_1$, depending on $g$, $\ell'$, $n$, $\mathsf d$, $R$, $c_*$ and the type, and on no side, such that for all $(K,\beta)\in\mathfrak D(g)$ with $K\ge K'_1$, every side $\ell\ge\ell'$ in $\mathfrak L(g)$, every entry of the type whose boxes lie in one sup ball of radius $R$, and all real Lipschitz $f_q$ on $\mathbb R^3$ that vanish outside that ball, read on $T_\ell$, with the carrier of the entry at sup distance $\ge\mathsf d$ from every ${\rm supp}\,f_q$ (the sources lie anywhere among themselves),
\[
|\langle J;\mathcal O(f_1);\dots;\mathcal O(f_n)\rangle_{K,\ell,\beta}|\le C'|\varkappa|_\infty L^{-\mathsf g_mK}K^{1+\mathfrak p_0}L^{(\frac12-c_*)K}\prod_q\|f_q\|_\sharp ;
\]
the same holds under every periodic Gibbs state at $(K,\beta)$ and under every weak limit point of the torus laws as $\ell\to\infty$ in $\mathfrak L(g)$, and, with the further factor $2^{n+1}$, for complex weights and complex Lipschitz $f_q$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Put $\phi=(\frac12-c_*)/(3n+4)$, $u=\lceil\phi K\rceil$, $t=K-u$. Since $M\,R(X_g+\bar B)\le L^m$ and $R$ increases, the frame of {\cite[Def.~B.14]{YMM2}} holds for the chain along $x_j=L^{K-j}\mathsf b'$ at every label of $[\gamma^{-2},X_g+\bar B]$, and from a $K_1$ on $t$ is a top level of it with $\mathsf R_t\le\frac12$ and $8a\le\mathsf d$.

\emph{The cut.} Let $D\ge\mathsf d$ be the spread. For every site $y_0$ of the carrier there is a source $q$ with ${\rm dist}_\infty(y_0,{\rm supp}\,f_q)\ge\frac12D$: otherwise there are points $y_q\in{\rm supp}\,f_q$ with $|y_0-y_q|_\infty<\frac12D$, and $y_0,y_1,\dots,y_n$ are pairwise closer than $D$, against the definition of the spread. Give each index $\iota$ of $J$ the least such $q$ for the lowest site of its box; this cuts $J$ into at most $n$ entries $J_q$ of the same type, the carrier of $J_q$ being at sup distance $\ge\frac12D-2a\ge\frac14\mathsf d$ from ${\rm supp}\,f_q$, while the other sources lie anywhere. The cumulant is linear in its first entry and symmetric in the others; in the cumulant of $J_q$ the far source is $f_q$.

\emph{The chain with the entry and a complex source.} The chain of Lem.~\ref{C-360-9}(a) is formed with the entry $sJ_q$ and with the source $w=\sum_q\zeta_qf_q$ at once, for $|s|<r_J$ and \[
\|w\|_\flat=\max\{\sup|w|,\frac{40}{\sqrt3}M{\rm Lip}_\infty w\}<2\varrho
\] (the polydisc of the sources of Thms.~\YMMref{AJ}{673} and~\YMMref{AD}{607}): its families $E^{(i)}[w,s]$ are pointed families of the levels $i$, holomorphic in $(w,s)$ and local, the member at a domain $X$ reading $w$ on the plaquettes of $X$ alone, and $s$ only if a box of the entry lies in $X$; with them $(\mathcal M^t)_*(\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}_te^{sJ_q}\rho^w_0\,\mathrm{d}U)=\exp[\sum_{i\le t}c_i(w,s)]\mathbf 1_{{\rm In}_t}e^{\Phi^{w,s}_t}dV$, $\rho^w_0=\rho_0e^{\mathcal O(w)}$, and on ${\rm Cut}_t$
\[
|\Phi^{w,s}_t-\Phi^{w,s'}_t|\le|s-s'|\,\mathsf o_t,\qquad|\Phi^{w,0}_t-\Phi^{0,0}_t|\le N_t\mathsf C_t\|w\|_\flat ,
\]
wherever the sources lie, with $N_t=\ell^3L^{3u}$ the number of the sites of the level $t$ and $\mathsf C_t\le CK^{2\mathfrak p_0}$. The entry enters each step as one more local term, as in Lem.~\ref{C-360-9}(a); bounding the radius $\mathsf e^{\rm c}_t\le1$ of the field cut, raised to the order of the entry, by $\mathsf e^{\rm c}_t$ itself, the size of the entry at the level $t$ and what the steps made of it give $\mathsf o_t\le CK^{\mathfrak p_0}L^{4u-\mathsf g_mK}|\varkappa|_\infty$.

\emph{The bound.} Let $T(s,\zeta)=\int e^{sJ_q+\sum_{q'}\zeta_{q'}\mathcal O(f_{q'})}\,\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}_t\rho_0\,\mathrm{d}U$. The cumulant under the positive measure $\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}_t\rho_0\,\mathrm{d}U$ is $\partial_s\partial_{\zeta_1}\cdots\partial_{\zeta_n}\log T(0,0)$, and it differs from the cumulant under the measure of the torus by at most $4\,{\rm op}_{n+1}\mathsf R_t\sup|J_q|\prod_{q'}6\ell^3L^{4K}\sup|f_{q'}|$ (Prop.~\YMMref{115.2}{806}, its cumulant bound), which is smaller than every power of $L^{-K}$. By the identity of measures, $\partial_s\log T(0,\zeta)=\partial_s\mathsf C(0,\zeta)+\langle\partial_s\mathsf D\rangle_\zeta$, where $\mathsf C(s,\zeta)=\sum_{i\le t}(c_i(w,s)-c_i(w,0))$ collects the values of the families at the trivial triple, $\mathsf D=\Phi^{w,s}_t-\Phi^{w,0}_t$, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_\zeta$ is the mean under $e^{\Phi^{w,0}_t-\Phi^{0,0}_t}$ times the image of $\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}_t\rho_0\,\mathrm{d}U$, normalised.

On the polydisc $|\zeta_{q'}|<(2nN_t\mathsf C_t\|f_{q'}\|_\sharp)^{-1}$ the exponent $\Phi^{w,0}_t-\Phi^{0,0}_t$ is at most $\frac12$, so $|\langle G\rangle_\zeta|\le3.1\sup|G|$, and the second member is at most $3.1\,\mathsf o_t$. In the first, a member at a domain that does not hold both a box of $J_q$ and a plaquette of the far source $f_q$ does not depend on $\zeta_q$ (locality), and has no mixed derivative; the members at the domains $X$ of the levels $i$ that hold both have $d_i(X)\ge(\frac14\mathsf d-a)L^{K-i}/M-2$, and with the count of the domains their sum is at most a power of $L^K$ times $e^{-\mathsf dL^u/8M}$. Cauchy's estimates in the $n$ sources on this polydisc cost $\prod_{q'}(nCK^{2\mathfrak p_0}L^{3u}\|f_{q'}\|_\sharp)$.

Together, $K^{(2n+1)\mathfrak p_0}L^{(3n+4)u-\mathsf g_mK}$, and $(3n+4)u\le(\frac12-c_*)K+3n+4$.

\emph{On all the sides.} Let $\mathsf l=L^{-i}$ be the largest power of $L$ with $\mathsf l\le\frac12\mathsf d$; then $\ell'\ge2R+4\mathsf l$. On $T_{\ell'}$ and on every $T_\ell$, $\ell\ge\ell'$, a board of side $\mathsf l$ puts the boxes of the entry and the supports of the sources, which lie in one sup ball of radius $R$ inside one period box of side $\ell'$, in different cells. The cumulant on $T_\ell$ is a mixed derivative at $0$ of a quotient whose coefficients are means on $T_\ell$ of products of functions of different cells of that period box; the chessboard bound (Lem.~\ref{C-360-7}) bounds each by a product of chessboard seminorms on $T_{\ell'}$, at the price $e^{\mathsf l^3(p_{\ell'}-p_\ell)}\le e^{G_g\mathsf l^3}$ for a cell; this ratio $Z_{K,\ell',\beta}^{1/N'}/Z_{K,\ell,\beta}^{1/N_\ell}$ of the plain partition functions per cell, $N'$ and $N_\ell$ being the numbers of the cells of $T_{\ell'}$ and of $T_\ell$, is the one number that depends on $\ell$, and its bound is free of $\ell$.

After a subtraction of Wick type in the functions of the cells, which removes the cumulants of the families inside one cell, the chessboard seminorm of the function of the cell of the entry, the mean on $T_{\ell'}$ of the product of its mirror copies, is by the moment--cumulant formula a sum over the partitions of the copies all of whose blocks join different cells; each such cumulant is small by the bound on one torus, read at a free depth $u$ with $C_{\rm u}K^{1/(2\mathfrak p_0)}\le u\le\frac12K$, $C_{\rm u}\ge1$ a number formed with the data and the type: a factor $|\varkappa|_\infty K^{1+\mathfrak p_0}L^{4u-\mathsf g_mK}$ for each copy of the entry and a factor of Cauchy's estimate for each copy of a source.

The number of the cells that the ball of radius $R$ meets, at most $(2R/\mathsf l+3)^3$, enters $C'$, and at $u=\lceil\frac14(\frac12-c_*)K\rceil$ the bound follows. Every periodic Gibbs state is dominated by the torus measures through its conditional laws (Prop.~\YMMref{91.9}{705}), and the weak limit points of the torus laws inherit the bound; for complex data the real and imaginary parts are taken apart.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The cubic remainder uniformly in the side]\label{C-360-19}
Let $0<g\le\gamma$, $\ell'\in\mathfrak L(g)$, $n\ge2$, $\mathsf d>0$, $c<\frac1{14}$, and let $Q$ be a cube of side $\frac14\ell'$. There are $C,p,K_0$, depending on $g,\ell',n,\mathsf d,c$ and independent of the larger side $\ell$, such that for all $\ell\ge\ell'$ in $\mathfrak L(g)$, all $(K,\beta)\in\mathfrak D(g)$ with $K\ge K_0$, all Lipschitz fields $\eta$ and real Lipschitz $f_q$ carried by $Q$ with the supports of the $f_q$ pairwise $\ge\mathsf d$ apart,
\[
|\mathfrak U^\sharp[\eta](f)_{T_\ell}|+|\mathfrak U^\sharp[\eta](f)_{T_\ell}-\mathfrak U^\sharp[\eta](f)_{T_{\ell'}}|\le CK^pL^{-cK}\mathsf H(\eta)\prod_q\|f_q\|_\sharp ;
\]
the finitely many sides of $\mathfrak L(g)$ below $\ell'$ are covered by Lem.~\ref{C-360-10}.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Every label of $\mathfrak D(g)$ lies in $[\gamma^{-2},X_g+\bar B]$, and $MR(X_g+\bar B)\le L^m$ on every side of $\mathfrak L(g)$; so the frame of {\cite[Def.~B.14]{YMM2}} holds for the chain along $x_j=L^{K-j}\mathsf b$ at the label of every first-passage datum, and Lem.~\ref{C-360-9}(b) holds with one triple of numbers for all of them, also with real sources $\sum_ix_if_i$ in its polydisc. The chain is formed with several entries and complex sources as well, as in the proof of Lem.~\ref{C-360-18} (Lem.~\ref{C-360-9}(a), polarisation and locality in each entry).

\emph{The reduction.} With $\mathcal S[\Xi]=a^{-2}\sum_p\Xi^{\lambda(p)}(x(p))\,\mathfrak r^\sharp_{\lambda(p)}(p)$ for a field $\Xi$ we have $\beta\mathfrak K^\sharp[\eta]=\mathcal S[\mathsf b\eta]$ and $a^{-1}\mathfrak K^\sharp[f_i\eta]=\mathcal S[f_i\eta]$, so $\mathfrak U^\sharp[\eta](f)=-\langle\mathcal S[\mathsf b\eta];\mathcal O(f_1);\dots;\mathcal O(f_n)\rangle+\sum_i\langle\mathcal S[f_i\eta];(\mathcal O(f_l))_{l\ne i}\rangle$, with $\mathsf H(\mathsf b\eta)\le(X_g+\bar B)\mathsf H(\eta)$ and $\mathsf H(f_i\eta)\le2\|f_i\|_\sharp\mathsf H(\eta)$. It suffices therefore to compare $G_\ell=\langle\mathcal S[\Xi];\mathcal O(h_1);\dots;\mathcal O(h_{n'})\rangle_{K,\ell,\beta}$ with $G_{\ell'}$, $n'\in\{n-1,n\}$, $n'\ge1$, for Lipschitz fields $\Xi$ and real Lipschitz $h_q$ carried by $Q$ whose supports are pairwise $\ge\mathsf d$ apart, nothing being asked of $\Xi$ relative to them.

\emph{The fold with one factor for each copy.} Place $Q$ in the middle of one cell of the board of side $\mathsf l=\frac12\ell'$; it lies at sup distance $\ge\frac18\ell'\ge1$ from the walls. On every $T_\ell$, $\ell\ge\ell'$, $\mathcal S[\Xi]$ and the $\mathcal O(h_q)$ are the realisations of one model function each, and their mirror copies in the eight cells of $T_{\ell'}$ are again a cubic entry $\mathcal S[\Xi^\kappa]$, $\mathsf H(\Xi^\kappa)\le\mathsf H(\Xi)$, and sources $\mathcal O(h_{(q,\kappa)})$ with $\|h_{(q,\kappa)}\|_\sharp=\|h_q\|_\sharp$; copies in different cells are $\ge1$ apart. The chessboard bound (Lem.~\ref{C-360-7}) carries the cumulant on $T_\ell$ to the mean on $T_{\ell'}$ of the product of the eight mirror copies, at the price $e^{G_g\mathsf l^3}$ for each function, and by the moment--cumulant formula of the copies (an identity of formal power series, as in the proof of Thm.~\ref{C-360-2}(g)(ii)) the difference $G_\ell-G_{\ell'}$ reads the joint cumulants on $T_{\ell'}$ of the families $B$ of copies that join different cells alone, the families inside one cell entering nowhere. If each of these is at most $\Gamma\prod_{(i,\kappa)\in B}\omega_i$, where $\Gamma\ge1$, with one factor $\omega_0$ for each copy of the entry and one factor $\omega_q$ for each copy of the source $h_q$, then
\[
|G_\ell-G_{\ell'}|\le\mathsf c_{n'}\,e^{(n'+1)G_g\mathsf l^3}\,\Gamma^{(n'+1)/2}\prod_{i=0}^{n'}\omega_i ,
\] To see the exponent, use the within-cell normalization and logarithm identities of Lem.~\ref{C-352-31}. In a fold of $q$ entries, every remaining block joins cells and has at least two members; a partition of the $8q$ copies has at most $4q$ such blocks. Its bound is at most $\Gamma^{4q}\prod_i\omega_i^8$, and the eighth root gives $\Gamma^{q/2}\prod_i\omega_i$. The subsequent logarithm partitions preserve this exponent, since their subset sizes sum to $q=n'+1$. This proves the display, including the stated pressure factor.
Here $\mathsf c_{n'}$ is a pure number. With $u=\lceil\phi K\rceil$, $t=K-u$, the factors $\omega_0=K^pL^{-c_1K}\mathsf H(\Xi)$ and $\omega_q=K^{2\mathfrak p_0}L^{3u}\|h_q\|_\sharp$ serve, in three cases. (i) No copy of the entry: the family holds two copies of sources in different cells, $\ge1$ apart, and the bound \eqref{eq:torus-cumulant-bound} on $T_{\ell'}$ at separated supports applies. (ii) One copy $\mathcal S[\Xi^\kappa]$: moving the weight of the entry with the sources writes the cumulant as $-\mathfrak U^\sharp[\Xi^\kappa/\mathsf b](h)$ plus, when two or more sources are present, the cubic remainders $-\mathfrak U^\sharp[h_\alpha\Xi^\kappa/\mathsf b^2]((h_{\alpha'})_{\alpha'\ne\alpha})$ (the supports of the $h$'s being disjoint), and with one source the contact member is a mean of $\mathfrak K^\sharp$, which vanishes; a source of another cell is $\ge1$ from the entry, and $h_\alpha\Xi^\kappa$ is carried by ${\rm supp}\,h_\alpha$, at sup distance $\ge\min\{\mathsf d,1\}$ from the other supports: the spread condition holds, and Lem.~\ref{C-360-10} on $T_{\ell'}$ at the rate $c_1$ applies. (iii) Two to eight copies of the entry, in different cells, the sources anywhere: the cumulant is a mixed derivative of the logarithm of the generating function of the chain with these entries and the complex source $w_\zeta=\sum\zeta_\alpha h_\alpha$, at the level $t$.
For case (iii), retain the higher mixed jets as in the proof of {\cite[Prop.~3.15]{YMM2}}(b). {\cite[Prop.~3.13]{YMM2}}(v) permits the fixed complex source $w$ and the several insertion parameters $\mathbf s$ together. Write their small-field generating function as $T_w(\mathbf s)=T_w(0)e^{\mathsf C_w(\mathbf s)}\langle e^{\mathsf D_{w,\mathbf s}}\rangle_w$, with the normalized block-field functional $\langle\cdot\rangle_w$. For $q$ copies of the entry and $I$ with $|I|\ge2$, locality and the Cauchy estimate in that proof give $\max\{|\partial_I\mathsf C_w(0)|,\sup|\partial_I\mathsf D_{w,\mathbf s}|_{\mathbf s=0}\}\le2E_0\mathsf t'_\times\prod_{a\in I}(q/r_a)$, where $r_a$ are the insertion radii and $\mathsf t'_\times$ is the polymer sum of that proposition. Copies of the entry lie in distinct cells with a fixed positive margin. Their inverse radii are at most $CL^{2K}\mathsf H(\Xi^a)$, whereas $\mathsf t'_\times\le CK^pL^{AK}e^{-cL^u}$. Hence the mixed-jet bound is below $\prod_{a\in I}\epsilon_a$ for large $K$, uniformly on a fixed fraction of the displayed, $K$-dependent source polydisc. Zero entries are omitted. At real sources the block-field functional is positive; at complex sources it has norm at most $3.1$ on the smaller polydisc, by the exponent bound in the proof of Lem.~\ref{C-360-18}. The moment and logarithm partition formulas in {\cite[Prop.~3.15]{YMM2}}(b) therefore apply in both cases, with finite constants adjusted in the complex case.
At a real source $x$ in the polydisc of the radii $(CK^{2\mathfrak p_0}L^{3u}\|h_\alpha\|_\sharp)^{-1}$, Lem.~\ref{C-360-9}(b), applied to the field $\Xi^\kappa/(\mathsf b-w_x)$, makes the conditional mean of each copy given the block field of the level $t$ a number up to $\epsilon_a=C\mathsf H(\Xi)K^{p_2}L^{-c'_0K}$. Subtracting these constants from the first jets, and using the higher mixed-jet bound above, the same partition formulas bound the cumulant by a constant times $\prod_a\epsilon_a$. At a complex source, the norm bound for the normalized functional and the mixed-jet estimate instead give a constant times the product of the crude bounds $\hat{\mathsf o}_a=C\mathsf H(\Xi)K^{\mathfrak p_0}L^{4u+\frac12K}$ of the oscillations of the cubic entries, of the order $3$ and of the weight $a^{-2}$. The estimate with two constants for a function holomorphic on a polydisc of the radii $r_\alpha$, bounded by $B$ there and by $\epsilon$ at its real points, $|\partial_{\zeta_1}\cdots\partial_{\zeta_{n''}}(0)|\le\epsilon^{1-\sigma}B^\sigma(\frac{4n''}{\pi\sigma})^{n''}\prod_\alpha r_\alpha^{-1}$, gives one factor $\epsilon_a^{1-\sigma}\hat{\mathsf o}_a^\sigma\le C\mathsf H(\Xi)K^pL^{-c_1K}$ for each copy of the entry, $c_1=(1-\sigma)c'_0-\sigma(\frac12+4\phi)$.

In all three cases the histories with a large field up to the level $t$ cost on $T_{\ell'}$ less than every power of $L^{-K}$.
