The remainder of the two-point function beyond the Gaussian value is bounded by placing a dummy bump at the distance $\rho$ from the first bump, applying the bound on the remainder of three sources of (iii) at the lengths $(\rho,\rho,\mathsf d)$, and setting the parameter of the dummy bump to $0$ in the mixture over the histories; it is $\le C\mathsf b^2\mathsf d^{3/2}(\rho/\mathsf d)^6$; the chessboard bound, read at two lengths (the fold at two lengths), carries it to every state with a further error $\le C(g)(\rho/\mathsf d)^6\mathsf d^{3/2}$; the comparison of $\sum_{\lambda(p)=\lambda,\lambda(q)=\mu}\varphi_1\varphi_2(C^{\rm free}_K)^2$ with $\mathcal K_{\lambda\mu}$ costs $C[\frac{a_K}{\vartheta\rho}+(\frac{\mathsf d}{\ell_g})^3](\rho/\mathsf d)^6$.

The change of units $x\mapsto L^zx$ multiplies the label, the side and the distances by $L^z$, and for $z$ large it carries a first-passage datum at $g\le\gamma$ to one at a coupling below $\gamma_\sigma$; this gives the narrow form at every $0<g\le\gamma$. (ii) For bumps of radius $\rho$ the bounds of (i) are $A\rho^{6}\prod\|\phi_a\|_\infty$, uniform in $j$; a bilinear form with such bounds at all small radii has a Borel kernel with $|k|\le(\frac3\pi)^2A$; the subsequence is taken at all pairs through partitions of unity; every periodic Gibbs state at $\mathfrak D(g)$ is invariant under the lattice translations, and the tori too, so the kernels depend on $x-y$; $\sum_\lambda\mathcal O_\lambda=\mathcal O$ gives $\sum\tau_{\lambda\mu}=\mathsf s^T_2$. (iii) With three sources at two scales, an induction over the levels shows: let $k_1=\max\{K-s(\mathsf d),2\}$ be the level of the distance $\mathsf d$, $\mathsf b_{k_1}=A_1(\log x_{k_1})^{\mathfrak p_0}$ its threshold and $\delta_{k_1}=\delta(x_{k_1})=A_1x_{k_1}^{-1/2}(\log x_{k_1})^{\mathfrak p_0}\le A_1Y_{s(\mathsf d)}^{\mathfrak p_0}(\mathsf d/\mathsf b)^{1/2}$ (equation~\YMMref{(634)}{339}), and $Z=Z_0(1+\mathsf b_{k_1})^2$ with a number $Z_0$ formed with the constants among the construction results, so that $Z^m\le C\,Y_{s(\mathsf d)}^{2m\mathfrak p_0}$; if at the level $k_1$ each jet of the sources is a constant plus an explicit quadratic form of the curvature, up to $\epsilon_\circ\mathsf v_\beta$ with weights $\mathsf v_\beta$ whose products over partitions do not exceed $\mathsf v_\beta$, then at every later level, up to the last level $K$, it is the Gaussian value, up to $\mathsf a_mZ^m\varpi\mathsf v_\beta$ with $(\mathsf a_m)=(1,14,285)$ and $\varpi\le\epsilon_\circ+C\delta_{k_1}$, provided $(K-k_1)\varpi\le1$, which holds for $\mathsf d$ below a threshold depending on $g$.

As $Y_{s(\mathsf d)}\le2\log\frac1{\mathsf d}+C(g)$, the factors $Z^m$ and $\mathsf b_{k_1}^2\delta_{k_1}$ give the powers of $\log\frac1{\mathsf d}$ below. The explicit Gaussian part is the ring $3\mathsf b^{-3}\mathcal K^{(3)}_K$, with the error $C(g)(\log\frac1{\mathsf d})^{39\mathfrak p_0+2}\mathsf d^{1/2}$ times the natural size $\rho^9r^{-3}\mathsf d^{-6}\mathsf b^{-3}\prod\|f_a\|_\infty$; the remainder $S^T_3-\mathsf J_3$ is at most $C\mathsf b^3\mathsf d^{3/2}$ times the natural size, with no power of $r$; the passage over the least torus costs $(\mathsf d/\ell_g)^3$, and the comparison of the lattice and continuum rings at two scales is explicit. As in (i), the fold at two lengths carries the three-point law at narrow bumps from the least torus to every state, with the further error $C^{\rm tr3}_3(g)\,\mathsf d^{3/2}\rho^9r^{-3}\mathsf d^{-6}\prod_a\|f_a\|_\infty$, $C^{\rm tr3}_3(g)$ a number formed with $g$ and the constants among the construction results; $E_3$ contains this term, the labels at $g$ lying in a compact interval and $\mathsf d^{3/2}\le\mathsf d^{1/2}$, and the law of (h)(iii) along the states $s_j$ rests on it. (iv) follows from (ii), (iii) and the free identity
\[
\bigl|\tfrac{2\pi}3\mathsf br^3\cdot3\mathsf b^{-3}k_3\bigl(c+\tfrac r2n,c-\tfrac r2n,z\bigr)-\mathsf t^\circ(n,c-z)\bigr|\le2.66\,(r/\mathsf d)^2\mathsf b^{-2}\mathsf d^{-6},
\]
with $|t_\lambda(c,z)-\mathsf t^\circ(e_\lambda,c-z)|\le6\epsilon_\sigma(g,|c-z|)\mathsf b^{-2}|c-z|^{-6}$ almost everywhere by (ii) and the identity for $\mathsf t^\circ$ of the setting; the null set lies in $(c,z)$ alone because $\mathsf s^T_3$ is continuous. (v) The limit in $K$ exists at disjoint supports by (d): its clause on one plane field among action densities gives the limit of $\langle\mathcal O_\lambda(\phi_1);\mathcal O(\phi_2)\rangle$ at the fixed label, and $\langle\mathcal O(\phi_1);\mathcal O(\phi_2)\rangle$ converges by the convergence of $S^T_2$ at a fixed label. For the identification, the narrow bumps are the $f^c_\pm$ of the statement, the radial tents of radius $\rho=\frac r8$, of mass $1$ and of height $3/(\pi\rho^3)=1536/(\pi r^3)$ about $c\pm\frac r2e_\lambda$; the threshold on $K$ is $128a_K\le r$, that is $16a_K\le\rho$, and $s(\rho)\le K$, which gives $s(\frac r2)\le K$, the depth function being non-increasing.

The number $r_*$ is taken so that for $0<r\le r_*$ the depth $s=s(\frac r2)$ obeys $s\ge3$ and $L^2C_W(s)Y_s^{3\mathfrak p_0}\le L^{s-3}$, the condition under which the family near the pair is formed, and $\frac r2\le\min\{r_0(\mathsf b),r_1(\mathsf b)\}$, the radii up to which the induction of (iii) and the frame of the pair are formed, which read $g$ and $\mathsf b$; all three hold for small $r$, since $s(\frac r2)\to\infty$ as $r\to0$ and the second holds at all large $s$; and $r_*\le\frac16\mathsf d$. Write $S^T_3=\mathsf J_3+(S^T_3-\mathsf J_3)$, $\mathsf J_3$ the explicit Gaussian part, cut $\phi_2$ into pieces carried by cubes of side $\frac14r$, of the natural size $\mathsf b^{-2}\mathsf d^{-6}r^3\|\phi_2\|_\infty$, and compare, at each $c\in{\rm supp}\,\phi_1$ and for each piece, the pair of narrow bumps at $c\pm\frac r2e_\lambda$, weighted by $\frac{2\pi}3\mathsf br^3$, with the plane field $\mathcal O_\lambda-\frac13\mathcal O$ at $c$.

For the remainder: for almost every block field, at every level $n$ with $a_{K-n}\ge r^{1/2}$, the difference jet at the background, the jet of the weighted pair minus that of the plane field, is a constant up to $C[r^{\beta_H/72}+(a_K/r)^{1/18}]\varepsilon_n^2a_{K-n}^{-4}$, $\varepsilon_n$ the radius of regularity of the level $n$ and $\beta_H$ the H\"older exponent; this comes from the H\"older regularity, with the exponent $\beta_H$, of the backgrounds at the scale of the pair, carried over the levels by the induction of (iii). Integrating over the mixture of the histories on the least torus, whose moments of the scale of regularity are bounded uniformly in $K$, gives for the remainder the difference estimate $C(g,\mathsf b)\mathsf d^{-5/2}[r^{\beta_H/72}+(a_K/r)^{1/18}]$ times the natural size.

The explicit Gaussian parts are compared on the lattice of $T_{\ell_g}$, with $C(g,\mathsf b,\vartheta_0)\mathsf d^{-9/2}$ and the same bracket. In the ring of the left member the near leg, between the two tents, whose plaquettes are between $\frac34r$ and $\frac54r$ apart, is $a_K^3\mathbb K_3(re_\lambda)$ up to the cost $(a_K/r)^2+(r/\ell_g)^3$, by the comparison \YMMref{(2245)}{824} of the lattice kernel with $\mathbb K_3$ in the setting. The two far legs $\mathsf a$, $\mathsf a'$, from the two tents to the support of $\phi_2$, enter through $\mathsf a\mathsf a'=\frac12(\mathsf a^2+\mathsf a'^2)-\frac12(\mathsf a-\mathsf a')^2$: the term $(\mathsf a-\mathsf a')^2$ costs $(r/\mathsf d)^2$ by the bound on the differences of $C^{\rm free}_K$ along one plane of the setting, its two plaquettes being parallel, equally oriented and at most $\frac54r\le\frac14(\mathsf d-\frac58r)$ apart; and in each square the far leg reads one tent alone.

There the lattice sums over the tents are Riemann sums, at the cost $a_K/\rho=8a_K/r$; the entries of $\mathbb K_3$ are harmonic off $0$, so its mean over the two radial tents, over the one through the sum over its plaquettes and over the other through the integral over $c$, is its value at $re_\lambda$; and the integral over $c$ moves the argument of $\phi_1$ by at most $r$, at the cost $r\,{\rm Lip}\,\phi_1\le r\|\phi_1\|_\infty/(\vartheta_0\mathsf d)$. Finally $\frac{2\pi}3r^3\cdot3\mathbb K_3(re_\lambda)=\frac32(E_{\lambda\lambda}-\frac13\mathbf 1)$, so the weighted pair becomes the plane field $\mathcal O_\lambda-\frac13\mathcal O$ at $c$ in the explicit part of the two-point function of the right member, whose legs are lattice kernels as well.

Each of these costs is a number formed with $g,\mathsf b,\vartheta_0,\mathsf d$ times the bracket, as $a_K/r\le\frac1{128}$ and $r\le1$. Summing over the at most $9^3(\mathsf d/r)^3$ pieces and integrating over $c$, against the mass $\le\frac{4\pi}3\mathsf d^3\|\phi_1\|_\infty$, gives the display of (h)(v), uniformly in $K$. Letting $K\to\infty$ at a fixed $r$, which is allowed since $128a_K\le r$ and $s(\rho)\le K$ from some $K$ on, and then $r\to0$ gives the identification at the fixed $\mathsf d$.

\emph{Step 5: Thm.~\ref{C-360-3}(a), (b).} By Lem.~\ref{C-360-6}, $-\beta\sum_ph_{\omega,\chi}=\mathsf b\,{\rm Pf}(k^h)$, with \[
 \|{\rm Pf}(k^h)\|\le156|\omega|\,{\rm Lip}(\chi)R_1(\chi)\le468\ell'|\omega|\,{\rm Lip}_\infty(\chi)
\], and (i) is Lem.~\ref{C-360-6} at $r=n+1$, with $C^\flat_n(\rho)=468\ell'k^\flat_n(\rho)$, $k^\flat_n(\rho)=\max\{k'(n+1,\frac\rho2),\text{the crude bound below }K'_0\}$. Both clauses follow the one rule of the statement for a rough entry $F$: its norm $\|F\|$ times a number, and, free of the side and of the state, times the counts $N_F$ and $N_i$ of the cubes of the mesh that meet its carrier and the supports. For (ii) we put the rough entry alone in its cell of a board and the Lipschitz fields in other cells, in any mutual position.

For groups $G_j$ of entries, $R_G=\partial_G[e^{\sum_{e\in G}z_eX_e}/\nu(e^{\sum_{e\in G}z_eX_e})]_{z=0}$ has $\nu(\prod_jR_{G_j})=\sum_\pi\prod_{I\in\pi}\kappa(I)$ over the partitions all of whose blocks meet two groups; and, for integers $n\ge0$, $p\ge1$ and numbers $s_1,\dots,s_n>0$, $\rho_*>0$, $Q\ge1$, $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_p\ge0$: if $A_1,\dots,A_p,B$ are holomorphic on the domain $\mathsf D=\{z\in\mathbb C^n:\sum_r|z_r|s_r<\rho_*\}$, with $B(0)=1$, $|A_j(z)|\le\alpha_jQ^{\#z}$ and $|B(z)|\le Q^{\#z}$ on $\mathsf D$, $\#z$ being the number of the non-zero coordinates of $z$, then $A_1\cdots A_pB^{-p}$ is holomorphic near $0$ and $|\partial_{[n]}(A_1\cdots A_pB^{-p})(0)|\le\binom{n+p-1}nn!\prod_j\alpha_j\prod_r(2eQs_r/\rho_*)$.

The chessboard bound of Lem.~\ref{C-360-7} and the bounds of Thms.~\YMMref{AJ}{673} and~\YMMref{AD}{607} on tori for the scalar fields, through their cumulant polynomial, with $e^{nc_V\ell'^3}$, conclude. On the larger sides the chessboard seminorm of a centred rough entry is at most $e^{G_g\mathsf l^3}k_{N_0}(\mathsf d)\|F\|$, $k_N(\mathsf d)=[\sum_\pi\prod_{I\in\pi}k'(\#I,\mathsf d)]^{1/N}$ over the partitions of $N$ points into blocks of at least two, by its $N_0$ mirror copies on the reference side; a partition of unity by tents of the mesh $h(n,\rho)$ cuts the shell and the fields, which gives the counts $N_\chi,N_i$; the domination of the periodic Gibbs states (Lem.~\ref{C-360-7}) gives the states, and the change of units $x\mapsto L^zx$ gives every label and side.

The whole flux insertion is the rough entry $\mathsf b\,{\rm Pf}(k^h)+\mathcal O(v^{\mathfrak B})$, of the norm $13\mathsf b|k^h|_1+|v^{\mathfrak B}|_\infty\le(158\mathsf b+3a)|\omega|\,{\rm Lip}(\chi)R'(\chi)$, $R'(\chi)=\max\{R_1(\chi),R'_1(\chi)\}$ (Lem.~\ref{C-360-6}), and the same rule bounds it. For $\Theta_\beta[\eta]$ we use $\Theta_\beta[\eta]=\mathsf b\,{\rm Pf}(k^\eta)$; for $\mathfrak K^{\rm v}[\beta\eta]$, Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(a) gives $\mathfrak K^{\rm v}[\beta\eta]=N_\beta[\eta]-\Theta_\beta[\eta]+\mathsf b\,\mathcal O({\rm div}^s\eta)-\frac32a\,\mathcal O(e^\eta)$, and the null term drops beside fields that do not depend on the bonds near ${\rm supp}\,\eta$. (b) The spin densities written in petals give $T_{lr}(\varphi)=\mathsf b({\rm Pf}(k^{lr})+\mathcal O(v^{lr}))$; for two entries the two-source mixed derivatives of Lem.~\ref{C-360-24}(a), (e) give the bound first at $0<g\le\gamma$ with $g^{-2}\ge x_{\rm J}$, the setting of that lemma, with the factor $(2\ell/\mathsf d'')^6k_2(g,s(\mathsf d''))g^4$.

Every $0<g\le\gamma$ is then reached by the change of units $x\mapsto L^zx$, which carries $\mu_{K,\ell,\beta}$ to $\mu_{K-z,L^z\ell,\beta}$ and multiplies the label by $L^z$: take $z$ with $L^z\gamma^{-2}\ge2\max\{\gamma^{-2},x_{\rm J}\}$. The labels of $\mathfrak D(g)$ lie in the compact interval $[\gamma^{-2},X_g+\bar B]$, whose image under the multiplication by $L^z$ lies in $[2\max\{\gamma^{-2},x_{\rm J}\},\infty)$; every $\mathsf b'$ there lies inside $I(g')$ at $g'=(\mathsf b'/2)^{-1/2}\le\gamma$, where $g'^{-2}=\frac12\mathsf b'\ge x_{\rm J}$, so finitely many intervals $I(g'_i)$ cover the image, and at the cutoffs $K>z$ the bound at the couplings $g'_i$ applies; the cutoffs $K\le z$ are bounded crudely, by the suprema of the entries.

The limits are formed as in Step~1. For the symmetry in $(l,r)$ of the limits: for Lipschitz $\varphi$, by Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(e), $(T_{lr}-T_{rl})(\varphi)=\beta\sum_b\sum_{p\ni b}(\varphi(x(p))-\varphi(x_b))a^{-1}[(x_b-x(p))_l\mathfrak d_{b,p,r}-(x_b-x(p))_r\mathfrak d_{b,p,l}]$, which is $\mathsf b$ times a rough entry of norm $\le15a\,{\rm Lip}\,\varphi$; so, by the two-entry bounds just proved, at every first-passage datum and every $0<g\le\gamma$, both $\langle(T_{lr}-T_{rl})(\varphi);\mathcal O(f)\rangle$ and $\langle(T_{lr}-T_{rl})(\varphi);T_{l'r'}(\varphi')\rangle$ are $O(a)$ at separated supports. The limits are continuous in the sup norms of the entries, by the same bounds, and the Lipschitz functions are dense in the continuous ones in the sup norm; so every limit point is symmetric in $(l,r)$.

\emph{Step 6: Thm.~\ref{C-360-3}(c), (d).} (c) By Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(a) the null term drops, and $a\,\mathcal O(e^\eta)$ contributes $O(a)$ by Thm.~\ref{C-360-2}(a). By Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(b), $\mathfrak K^{\rm v}[\beta\eta]=-\mathsf b\sum_\rho P_\rho(\nabla^+_\rho\eta^\rho)+\beta\mathfrak K^\sharp[\eta]$, $P_\rho(\mathsf k)=a^{-1}\sum_p\mathsf k(x(p))\Psi_\rho(p)$: a bilinear half and a cubic half. In the bilinear half an exact identity in $U$, direction by direction and with one integration by parts, is used. For a real weight $W$ of the plaquettes and a direction $\rho$, let $(\mu,\nu,\rho)$ be the cyclic permutation of $(1,2,3)$ that ends with $\rho$; for a bare site $y$ let $p(y;\alpha,\alpha')$ be the plaquette with the corners $y$, $y+ae_\alpha$, $y+ae_\alpha+ae_{\alpha'}$, $y+ae_{\alpha'}$, and $w_0(y)=W(p(y;\mu,\nu))$, the weight of the plaquette normal to $\rho$ at $y$; let $g_\mu(y)=G_\rho(\langle y,y+ae_\mu\rangle)$ and $g_\nu(y)=G_\rho(\langle y,y+ae_\nu\rangle)$, the transported differences of the field strengths of the setting, and $E_\mu(y)=\sum_{p\ni b}\mathbf w(W_{b,p})$, the sum over the four plaquettes that hold the bond $b=\langle y,y+ae_\mu\rangle$, the lattice equation of motion at $b$, and $E_\nu(y)$ in the same way. Then
\[
-4\sum_pW(p)\Psi_\rho(p)=\sum_yw_0(y)\bigl[\langle g_\mu,E_\mu\rangle+\langle g_\nu,E_\nu\rangle\bigr]+{\rm Bil}+{\rm Cub}+{\rm Q4},
\]
where ${\rm Bil}$ comes from the differences of the weight $W$, ${\rm Cub}$ from the defect of the linear Bianchi identity and from commutators (factors ${\rm Ad}(W_{b,p})-\mathbf 1$ of plaquette holonomies), and ${\rm Q4}$ from $a_p^2+a_{p_+}^2$. For each plaquette $p=p(y;\mu,\alpha')$ through the bond $b=\langle y,y+ae_\mu\rangle$, the one-bond term $\beta\langle\mathbf w(W_{b,p}),E_\mu(y)\rangle-3(1-a_p)$ has vanishing cumulants with every entry that does not depend on $U(b)$ (an integration by parts in $U(b)$, as in Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(a)), and $g_\mu(y)$ is the sum of the $\mathbf w(W_{b,p})$ over the two plaquettes through $b$ in the directions $\pm\rho$; so $\beta$ times the first sum is, up to a number, $-3a\,\mathcal O(v)$ inside cumulants whose other entries avoid the bonds concerned, with the weight $v=w_0(y)+w_0(y+ae_\rho)$ on the plaquettes $p(y;\rho,\mu)$ and $p(y;\rho,\nu)$ and $v=0$ on the plaquettes normal to $\rho$; $|v|\le2\sup|W|$ gives the factor $\frac32$ below; $\beta\,{\rm Bil}$ is $a\mathsf b\,{\rm Lip}_\infty\mathsf k$ times a bounded petal form; ${\rm Cub}$ and ${\rm Q4}$ are block forms all of whose monomials have an order $\ge3$, whose sizes fall like $L^{-2j}$ with the level $j$ and give $L^{-(K-s-1)/4}$ at the working depth $s$ (Lem.~\ref{C-360-24}(c), (d)).

So, for $r\ge1$ spectators $F_q$ of the sizes $\omega_q$ (block forms with weights, or $\mathcal O(v_q)$) whose carriers are at Euclidean distances $\ge\mathsf d$ from one another and from $\{\mathsf k\ne0\}$, at all first-passage data with $36a\le\mathsf d$, $K\ge s(\mathsf d_1'')$ and $K\ge s(\mathsf d_1''')$, $\mathsf d_1=\frac34\mathsf d$,
\[
|\mathsf b\langle P_\rho(\mathsf k\circ x);F_1;\dots;F_r\rangle|\le\Bigl\{a\bigl[\tfrac32\sup|\mathsf k|+190\,\mathsf b\,{\rm Lip}_\infty\mathsf k\bigr]e_2+50\,\mathsf b\,\Gamma L^{-(K-s-1)/4}e_3\sup|\mathsf k|\Bigr\}\prod_q\omega_q,
\]
where $e_2=e_2(r+1,\mathsf d_1)$ and $e_3=e_3(r+1,\mathsf d_1)$, the cumulant having $r+1$ entries; for a number $r'\ge2$ of entries and a distance $\mathsf d_1$, $e_2(r',\mathsf d_1)=(3\ell'/\mathsf d_1'')^{3r'}k^{\rm loc}_{r'}(g,s(\mathsf d_1'');\ell')g^{2r'}$, $\mathsf d_1''=\min\{\frac45\mathsf d_1,L^{-\bar s(r')}\}$, with the depth $\bar s(r')$ of the proof of Lem.~\ref{C-360-6}, the least integer $s\ge3$ with the condition $2\mathsf T_{r'}(3)\theta(L^{s-2}g^{-2})\le1$ of Lem.~\ref{C-360-24}(b), read with the series $\mathsf T_{r'}$ of the mixed derivatives of the order $r'$ and the size $\theta$ stated there, and the number $k^{\rm loc}_{r'}$ of Lem.~\ref{C-360-24}(b); $e_3(r',\mathsf d_1)=(3\ell'/\mathsf d_1''')^{3r'}\tilde k_{r'}(g,s(\mathsf d_1''');\ell')g^{2r'}$ is the like number at the second depth $\mathsf d_1'''=\min\{\frac34\mathsf d_1,L^{-\tilde s(r')}\}$, $\tilde s(r')$ the least integer $s\ge3$ with the condition of Lem.~\ref{C-360-24}(c) at $p=r'$, and $\tilde k_{r'}$ the number of the bound of Lem.~\ref{C-360-24}(c); $\Gamma=\max\{\Gamma^\circ_{\rm Cub},\Gamma^\circ_{\rm Q4}\}$, the larger of the comparison weights $\Gamma^\circ_c$ of Lem.~\ref{C-360-24}(d) of the two block forms ${\rm Cub}$ and ${\rm Q4}$; and $s=s(\mathsf d_1''')$ at $r'=r+1$.

In (c) this is used with $r=n$ spectators $\mathcal O(f_i)$ and $\frac12\mathsf d$ in the place of $\mathsf d$, so that the numbers are formed at $(n+1,\frac38\mathsf d)$. These numbers depend on $g,\ell',r,\mathsf d$ and on no $K$ or $\beta$. The cubic half is Lem.~\ref{C-360-10}, the spread being $\ge\mathsf d$; the norm $\|\cdot\|_\sharp$ and the rate $c<\frac1{14}$ come from it alone. (d) For the cubic half in sup norms we couple on one probability space the chain of the first-passage datum and the chain along $x_j=L^{K-j}\mathsf b$ of Lem.~\ref{C-360-9}, which share only the block map, the Haar measure and the bare density, and use the law of total covariance given the block field of the level $t=K-\lceil\phi K\rceil$:
\[
\langle X;F\rangle=\int(r_{XF}-r_Xr_F)\,\mathrm{d}\mathsf m_t+\int(r_X-\mathsf a)(r_F-f_0)\,\mathrm{d}\mathsf m_t+(\text{large fields}),
\]
$r_X,r_F,r_{XF}$ the densities at the never-large history. The first term is a mixed derivative of two separated sources, $\le C_2e^{3-L^u\mathsf d'/M}y_Xy_F$, $\mathsf d'=\frac12\mathsf d$, $y_X=4\ell'^3L^{4u}\cdot608\,\mathsf bL^K\sup|\eta|$, by Lem.~\ref{C-360-24}(e) at the level $t$, whose conditions $L^u\mathsf d'\ge3M$ and $\mathsf h_2(u)\le1$ hold for large $K$; the second is the oscillation of Lem.~\ref{C-360-9}(b) times $3C_1y_F$, $y_F=4\ell'^3L^{4u}\sup|w|$, and $4\phi<c'_0$; the rest is at most $\mathsf V_{\ell'}(\mathsf b)L^{-11K}$. In words (Lem.~\ref{C-360-17}): a spectator acts on the cubic insertion only through a bounded function of the block field, and the cubic insertion is uncorrelated with every function of the block field up to its oscillation, at the price $L^{4\phi K}$, which a small $\phi$ pays.

For $n$ spectators the mixed derivatives of every order of the never-large term are bounded by Cauchy's estimates, locality and a count, $e^{-L^u\mathsf d/2M}$ paying every power of $L^K$. In the bilinear half in sup norms, $\mathsf b\,a^{-1}\sum_pw(p)\Psi_{\lambda(p)}(p)$, summed over the plaquettes of one normal, is a dominated local source of the weight $76\mathsf b\sup|w|$ (Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(b)), and a source cut at a level, with the H\"older bound~\textup{{\cite[Thm.~BT]{YMM2}}}, gives $L^{-K/200}$. For two cubic insertions the same argument is used twice, and the factor $L^{4u}$ does not enter; two orbital insertions and two stress insertions follow with the bilinear half and the null identity.

The numbers of Lem.~\ref{C-360-9}(b) are uniform on $[\gamma^{-2},X_g+\bar B]$, which holds every label of $\mathfrak D(g)$. The several-source statements used above hold clause by clause in their own ranges: Lem.~\ref{C-360-24}(a), (e), which the clauses on the cubic insertion alone read, at $0<g\le\gamma$ with $g^{-2}\ge x_{\rm J}$; Lem.~\ref{C-360-24}(b), (c), which the bilinear half reads, at $0<g\le\gamma^{\rm ref}_W$, and so does Thm.~\ref{C-360-2}(a), which bounds the term $a\,\mathcal O(e^\eta)$. So at every first-passage datum at $g$ on every side of $\mathfrak L(g)$, with numbers that depend on $g$ and on no label, the clauses on the cubic insertion alone hold for $0<g\le\gamma$ with $g^{-2}\ge x_{\rm J}$, and the other clauses for $0<g\le\gamma^{\rm ref}_W$, where $g^{-2}\ge x_{\rm J}$ holds of itself; and $x\mapsto L^zx$ gives every fixed label and side.

\emph{Step 7: Thm.~\ref{C-360-3}(e)--(g).} In the mean of the mirror copies $\mathrm{St}_K[\eta]$ may be replaced by $-\mathrm{Rm}_K[\eta]$ (Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(a) and the proof of Lem.~\ref{C-360-11}). A partition of unity cuts $\eta,\eta',H'$ into at most $C(R/\mathsf d)^3$ pieces of sup diameter $\le\frac18\mathsf d$, at the cost $C\mathsf d^{-2}$ in the $C^2$ norms. For two sets of sup diameter $\le\frac18\delta_0$ that are $\delta_0$ apart along one direction there is an offset in $h\mathbb Z^3$, $h\le\frac1{64}\delta_0$, of a board of side $\frac12\ell_g$ for which they lie in different cells at sup distance $\ge\frac1{16}\delta_0$ from the walls; Lems.~\ref{C-360-7} and~\ref{C-360-11} give $|\nu(A^\nu[F_1]A^\nu[F_2])|\le2e^{2G_g\mathsf l^3}\|F_1-c_1\|_{\rm ch}\|F_2-c_2\|_{\rm ch}$.

Two stress insertions give $L^{-K/28}$ each, hence $L^{-K/14}$; for two conserved tensors $L^{-K/36}$ each gives $L^{-K/18}\le L^{-K/20}$; against a plain tensor entry, which costs $L^{4u}=L^{K/100}$, the factor $L^{-K/36}$ leaves $L^{-K/60}$; and $\mathsf b\,\mathcal T_K(H^{\rm cons}[\eta])=\mathrm{St}_K[\eta]-\Delta_K[\eta]$. For the mean of the orbital insertion, cut into the pieces of the partition of unity, $\nu(\mathfrak K^{\rm v}[\beta\eta])=\nu(F_\eta)$ with $F_\eta=\mathfrak K^{\rm v}[\beta\eta]-\frac14\mathfrak N[\mathsf k_\eta]$, $\mathsf k^\rho_\eta=\nabla^+_\rho\eta^\rho$, since $\nu(\mathfrak N[\mathsf k_\eta])=0$ by Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(a); Lem.~\ref{C-360-11} at $m=1$, $\phi=\frac1{400}$ gives $\|F_\eta\|_{\rm ch}\le CK^pL^{-K/28}\|\eta\|_{C^2}$, $F_\eta$ having the mean $0$ on $T_{\ell'}$, and Lem.~\ref{C-360-7} at $q=1$, $c_1=0$ gives $|\nu(\mathfrak K^{\rm v}[\beta\eta])|\le e^{G_g\mathsf l^3}CK^pL^{-K/28}\|\eta\|_{C^2}$. (f) $n$ sets of sup diameter $\le\frac{\mathsf l}{4n}$ lie at sup distance $>\frac{\mathsf l}{8n}$ from all the walls of some board with offset on a grid of mesh $<\frac{\mathsf l}{2n}$ (a pigeonhole); several slots may share a cell (Lem.~\ref{C-360-11}); Lem.~\ref{C-360-7} holds with any number of cells; recentring from the torus mean to $\nu$ costs $2^n$ terms; and $4\phi(n-1)<\min\{c'_0,\frac1{28}-3\phi\}$ pays the factors $L^{4u}$.

At $n_1=1$, $c=\frac1{56}$, a fixed $\mathsf d>0$ satisfies $\mathsf dL^u\ge K^2$ for $K\ge K_0(\mathsf d)$. (g) $\sigma(H^{\rm cons}[\eta],H_2,\dots,H_n)$ is the limit of the left member of (f) at $n_1=1$, which tends to $0$ at every fixed $\mathsf d>0$, and disjoint compact supports have a positive sup distance. By reflection positivity of $\sigma$ at the mirror $\theta$, $\sigma(H^{\rm cons}[\theta\eta],H^{\rm cons}[\eta])$ is the square of the norm of the vector of $\mathcal T(H^{\rm cons}[\eta])$ in the reconstruction, which therefore vanishes. The equivalence along the sequence is Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(a) with the bound on $\Delta_K$ in (e), the labels lying in $[\gamma^{-2},X_g+\bar B]$.

For $0<g\le\gamma^{\rm sd}_W$ the cited bound on centred products of tensor entries and a diagonal argument give the convergent subsequences; the covariance and the reflection positivity pass to the limits from the periodic Gibbs states, and $\mathcal T_K(f\mathbf 1)=\mathcal O(f)$ gives the trace part.

\emph{Step 8: Thm.~\ref{C-360-4}(a), (b).} (a) We write $\mathfrak U_{\omega,\chi}=(\mathfrak U_{\omega,\chi}-\mathfrak U^\sharp[\chi\,\omega y])+\mathfrak U^\sharp[\chi\,\omega y]$, where $\chi\,\omega y$ is a field with $\mathsf H(\chi\,\omega y)\le(2+3\ell)|\omega|\|\chi\|_{C^{1,1}}$; since $\chi$ covers the $f_i$, $f_i\chi=f_i$, and the cubic member of the bulk term is $\mathfrak U^\sharp[\chi\,\omega y](f)$. The first part has $2(n+1)$ members, a spin member and a bilinear orbital member for each $\varphi\in\{\chi,f_1,\dots,f_n\}$. The spin members are $-\beta\langle\mathfrak S_\omega[\chi];\mathcal O(f_\cdot)\rangle$, with $\beta\,\mathfrak S_\omega[\chi]=\mathsf b\,a^{-1}\mathfrak S_\omega[\chi]$, and $\langle a^{-1}\mathfrak S_\omega[f_i];(\mathcal O(f_l))_{l\ne i}\rangle$. By Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(e), $\sum_{p\ni b}a^{-1}(x_b-x(p))_\lambda\mathfrak d_{b,p,\rho}$ is symmetric in $(\lambda,\rho)$ and $\omega$ is antisymmetric, so that
\[
a^{-1}\mathfrak S_\omega[\varphi]=\sum_b\sum_{p\ni b}\sum_\rho k^\varphi_{b,p,\rho}\,\mathfrak d_{b,p,\rho},\qquad k^\varphi_{b,p,\rho}=a^{-1}\bigl(\varphi(x(p))-\varphi(x_b)\bigr)\sum_\lambda\omega_{\rho\lambda}\,a^{-1}(x_b-x(p))_\lambda :
\]
an entry of the order $2$ with real weights $|k^\varphi|\le\frac14|\omega|{\rm Lip}\,\varphi$, which vanish unless $\varphi(x(p))\ne\varphi(x_b)$; $\beta\,\mathfrak S_\omega[\chi]$ is $\mathsf b$ times such an entry. By Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(b), and since $\nabla^+_\rho(\varphi\,(\omega y)_\rho)=(\omega y)_\rho\nabla^+_\rho\varphi$, $(\omega y)_\rho$ being free of $y_\rho$, the bilinear members are $\langle\mathfrak J^{\rm bl}[\mathsf k^\chi];\mathcal O(f_\cdot)\rangle$ and $-\mathsf b^{-1}\langle\mathfrak J^{\rm bl}[\mathsf k^{f_i}];(\mathcal O(f_l))_{l\ne i}\rangle$, where $\mathfrak J^{\rm bl}[\mathsf k]=\beta\sum_{p,\rho}\mathsf k^\rho(x(p))\Psi_\rho(p)$ and $\mathsf k^{\varphi,\rho}(y)=(\omega y)_\rho\nabla^+_\rho\varphi(y)$; these vector fields are Lipschitz, with norm $\le5|\omega|(1+\ell)\|\varphi\|_{C^{1,1}}$, which is where the norms $\|f_i\|_{C^{1,1}}$ enter, and supported in the $a$-neighbourhood of ${\rm supp}\,\varphi$.

By Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(c), $\mathfrak J^{\rm bl}[\mathsf k]=-\frac14\mathfrak N[\mathsf k]+\sum_{v=1}^5\mathfrak J_v[\mathsf k]-\frac14c_{\mathsf k}$: a null term, entries of the orders $2,2,2,3,4$ with weights of the order of the norm of $\mathsf k$ and, for the orders $3,4$, of $\beta$ times it, and a number, which drops from the cumulants. In (i) let $D\ge\mathsf d$ be the spread of the supports. Two rules on spreads are used. A family of sets has a spread at least that of each of its subfamilies of two or more sets. And if $2r'<D$ and a set $T$ lies within the sup distance $r'$ of one of the sets and of each set of an index set $Q$, then $T$ is empty when these are all the sets, and otherwise $T$ and the remaining sets have a spread $\ge D-r'$: points of $T$ and of the remaining sets that were closer would give points of all the sets that are pairwise closer than $D$.

With $\chi$ in the first entry, the carrier of the entry and the supports have a spread $\ge D$. With $f_i$ in the first entry, the carrier lies within $\frac32a$ of ${\rm supp}\,f_i$ and the cumulant is taken with the $\mathcal O(f_l)$, $l\ne i$: the spread is $\ge D-\frac32a$. The null terms meet the sources: the covering fixes $\chi$ at the barycentres and at the bond midpoints of the plaquettes of the supports, while $\mathsf k^\chi$ reads $\chi$ at the points $y+ae_\rho$ as well, so that ${\rm supp}\,\mathsf k^\chi$ may meet a support; and ${\rm supp}\,\mathsf k^{f_i}$ may meet ${\rm supp}\,f_l$. They are taken apart by the contact formula of Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(f): by (N3) the cumulant of $\mathfrak N[\mathsf k]$ with the sources of a set $\mathsf A$ is a sum of cumulants of the entries $\mathfrak R[f_{q_1}\cdots f_{q_{j-1}}\mathsf k;f_{q_j}]$ with the remaining sources, and by (N4) each such entry is a number, the density $a_p$ and densities of the order $2$, with no factor $\beta$, carried within the sup distance $2a$ of ${\rm supp}\,\mathsf k$ and of the supports that it absorbs.

The spread of ${\rm supp}\,\mathsf k^\chi$ and the supports is $\ge D$, and that of ${\rm supp}\,\mathsf k^{f_i}$ and the ${\rm supp}\,f_l$, $l\ne i$, is $\ge D-a$; once these exceed $4a$, the terms that absorb all the sources vanish, the numbers drop from the others, and by the merging of sets of Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(f) every remaining entry has with the remaining supports a spread $\ge D-2a$, resp.\ $\ge D-3a$. So in every term that is left the spread is $\ge\mathsf d-3a$, which is $\ge\frac12\mathsf d$ once $6a\le\mathsf d$, and Lem.~\ref{C-360-18} gives $L^{-K+(\frac12-c_*)K}\le L^{-c_*K}$ for the orders $2$ and $L^K\cdot L^{-\frac32K+(\frac12-c_*)K}=L^{-c_*K}$ for the orders $3,4$. The cubic part is Lem.~\ref{C-360-10}, whose spread condition holds because the support of the field $\chi\,\omega y$ is added to the supports, whose spread is $D$.

In (ii), $n=1$: the members with $f_1$ in the first entry are means, of the spin insertion and of the bilinear density $\mathfrak K^{\rm v}-\mathfrak K^\sharp$, and vanish by the mirror symmetries of the measure (Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(b)); in the members with $\chi$ the weights vanish unless $\chi$ varies across the plaquette or the bond, so, $\chi$ being $1$ on the $\mathsf d$-neighbourhood of ${\rm supp}\,f_1$, their carriers are at sup distance $\ge\mathsf d-2a$ from ${\rm supp}\,f_1$, the null term meets no source, and Lem.~\ref{C-360-18} applies to the pair. The cubic member is $\mathfrak U^\sharp[\chi\,\omega y](f_1)=-\beta\langle\mathfrak K^\sharp[\chi\,\omega y];\mathcal O(f_1)\rangle$, the contact member $a^{-1}\langle\mathfrak K^\sharp[f_1\chi\,\omega y]\rangle$ being a mean of $\mathfrak K^\sharp$, which vanishes (Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(b)).

Here ${\rm supp}\,f_1$ lies in the set where the field does not vanish, and a periodic field is subtracted: let $\mathsf s$ be the $\ell$-periodic continuous function with $\mathsf s(\tau)=\tau$ for $|\tau|\le\frac\ell2-\delta_0$ that is affine on $[\frac\ell2-\delta_0,\frac\ell2+\delta_0]$, and $\zeta^\rho(y)=\sum_\lambda\omega_{\rho\lambda}\mathsf s(y_\lambda)$. Then $\zeta=\omega y$ on the closure of the cube of the margin, $\zeta^\rho$ does not depend on $y_\rho$, $\sup|\zeta^\rho|\le|\omega|\ell$ and ${\rm Lip}_\infty\zeta^\rho\le|\omega|\ell/\delta_0$. As $\zeta^\rho(y+se_\rho)=\zeta^\rho(y)$ for all $y$, $s$ and $\rho$, the clause of Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(b) on such fields gives $\langle\mathfrak K^\sharp[\zeta];\mathcal O(f_1)\rangle=0$: for each direction $\rho$ and each plaquette $q$, the mirror normal to $\rho$ through the barycentre of $q$ keeps the measure, $a_q$ and $\zeta^\rho$, and changes the sign of $\mathfrak K^\sharp[\zeta^\rho e_\rho]$.

The field $\eta'=\chi\,\omega y-\zeta$ vanishes on the $\mathsf d$-neighbourhood of ${\rm supp}\,f_1$, where $\chi=1$ and $\zeta=\omega y$; so $f_1\eta'=0$, $\mathfrak U^\sharp[\chi\,\omega y](f_1)=\mathfrak U^\sharp[\eta'](f_1)$, and Lem.~\ref{C-360-10} applies, $\eta'$ vanishing within $\mathsf d$ of the support, with $\mathsf H(\eta')\le|\omega|[(\ell+2)\sup|\chi|+\ell\,{\rm Lip}_\infty\chi+\ell+\ell/\delta_0]$: here the margin $\delta_0$ enters $C$. In (iii), $\chi-\chi'$ vanishes within $\mathsf d$ of all the supports, so the exact identity gives $\langle\mathfrak B_{\omega,\chi}-\mathfrak B_{\omega,\chi'};\mathcal O(f_\cdot)\rangle=\beta\langle\mathfrak S_\omega[\chi-\chi']+\mathfrak K^{\rm v}[(\chi-\chi')\omega y];\mathcal O(f_\cdot)\rangle$, an insertion that vanishes near the sources, and no condition on the supports is needed.

The limit of the flux follows from the exact identity, $\nabla^s_\omega f=(\omega y)\cdot\nabla f+D_f$ with $\|D_f\|_\sharp\le C_0M|\omega|(1+\ell)a\|f\|_{C^3}$ by Taylor's formula, the bound \eqref{eq:torus-cumulant-bound} on connected functions at separated supports, and the convergence of $S^T_n$ at a fixed label with the rate $K^pL^{-K/10}$ (Cor.~\YMMref{117.1}{812}). For the quarter turn: $e^{\frac\pi2\omega_{13}}$ is a signed permutation of the axes, an exact symmetry of the lattice measure on $T_\ell$, so $S^T_n(f^{\pi/2})=S^T_n(f)$; since $\frac d{dt}f^t=-(\omega y)\cdot\nabla f^t$, $\int_0^{\pi/2}\sum_iS^T_n(\dots,(\omega y)\cdot\nabla f^t_i,\dots)dt=0$ at every $K$; with the exact identity and $\nabla^s_\omega f^t-(\omega y)\cdot\nabla f^t=O(a)$ this is the first display, and in the limit the second. (b) In $\mathfrak U-\mathfrak U^\sharp$ the entries sit where $\chi_R$ varies, in $\{\frac43R\le|y|\le\frac53R\}$ up to $2a$, or near one of the supports, which lie in $\{|y|<\frac R2\}$ at mutual distances $\ge\mathsf d_0$; all the boxes and supports lie in the sup ball of radius $2R$ about $0$, and in each cumulant the carrier of the entry is at a sup distance $\ge\min\{\frac{5R}{6\sqrt3},\frac{\mathsf d_0}{\sqrt3}\}-2a\ge\mathsf d_{\rm b}:=\frac12\min\{\frac{5R}{6\sqrt3},\frac{\mathsf d_0}{\sqrt3}\}$ from every source of that cumulant, for $K$ large, the cumulants with $f_i$ in the first entry being taken with the other sources.

So Lem.~\ref{C-360-18} in its form on all the sides, at the radius $2R$, the distance $\mathsf d_{\rm b}$ and on the sides $\ell\ge\ell'$ with $\ell'\ge4R+2\mathsf d_{\rm b}$, gives the bracket with a number free of the side, the finitely many smaller sides being covered by the form on one torus; the spin part comes with $L^{-(\frac12+c_*)K}$. The cubic member $\mathfrak U^\sharp[\chi_R\,\omega y](f)$ has its entry on top of the sources, so no wall parts them; it is Lem.~\ref{C-360-19}, with Lem.~\ref{C-360-10} for the finitely many smaller sides. Weak limit points of the torus laws inherit the bounds. Along a sequence with converging connected functions, the exact identity gives $\mathfrak U^{(j)}+\langle\mathfrak B;\mathcal O(f_\cdot)\rangle^{(j)}=\sum_qS^T_n(f_1,\dots,\nabla^s_\omega f_q,\dots)\to-\frac d{dt}S_n(f(e^{-t\omega}\cdot))|_{t=0}$, and $\mathfrak U^{(j)}\to0$.

For the volume-first limits Thm.~\YMMref{AP}{780} gives invariance under ${\rm O}(3)$, so the flux tends to $0$. With the limits one after the other: at a label $\mathsf b'\in I(g)$, on each torus $T_\ell$, $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$, (a) gives the limit in $K$ of the flux, $\sum_iS^{(\ell,\mathsf b')}_n(f_1,\dots,(\omega y)\cdot\nabla f_i,\dots,f_n)$, through every enclosing shell. Along the sides $\ell_k\to\infty$ the convergence $S^{(\ell_k,\mathsf b')}_n\to S^\circ_n$ is the hypothesis of the clause; the functions $(\omega y)\cdot\nabla f_i$ are Lipschitz, with the supports of the $f_i$, so the limit in $k$ is $\sum_iS^\circ_n(f_1,\dots,(\omega y)\cdot\nabla f_i,\dots,f_n)$; and this is $-\frac d{dt}S^\circ_n(f(e^{-t\omega}\cdot))|_{t=0}$, as $S^\circ_n$ is multilinear and bounded per ball in the norms $\|\cdot\|_\sharp$, the per-ball bound of Prop.~\YMMref{91.13}{709} passing to the limit once $\ell\ge16n(R+1)$ and the fixed supports lie in the central cube, and $t\mapsto f_i(e^{-t\omega}\cdot)$ is differentiable in these norms with the derivative $-(\omega y)\cdot\nabla f_i$ at $t=0$.

The integers $K^*_k\ge k$ are chosen so that for $K\ge K^*_k$ and $n\le k$ the connected functions on $T_{\ell_k}$ at the label $\mathsf b'$ lie within $\frac1k$ of $S^{(\ell_k,\mathsf b')}_n$ at all tuples of norms $\|\cdot\|_\sharp\le1$ with supports in the ball of radius $R_k=\min\{k,\frac18\ell_k\}$ about $0$ at mutual distances $\ge\frac1k$, by the rate $K^pL^{-K/10}$ of Cor.~\YMMref{117.1}{812}; every tuple of the clause lies, up to a factor, in these classes from some $k$ on, so along every sequence $K_k\ge K^*_k$ the connected functions converge to $S^\circ_n$. For given $f_i$ and $\chi_k$, raising $K^*_k$ makes the bulk term on $T_{\ell_k}$ at most $\frac1k$ as well, by (a), and the flux converges along such sequences to the limit of the display.

For slowly growing tori, the threshold in the cutoff comparison must
also be uniform in the side. Fix $n\ge2$ and a positive separation
$\mathsf d$. Take the label interval
\[
 J=[\mathsf b_-,\mathsf b_+],\qquad
 \mathsf b_-=g^{-2}+B_\sharp-L^{-1}\bar B\ge g^{-2},\qquad
 \mathsf b_+=L(g^{-2}+\bar B).
\]
It contains all first-passage labels by Cor.~\YMMref{74.2}{616}.
For large sides $\ell=2L^m$, $MR(\mathsf b_+)\le L^m$, so
the interval is admitted by Thm.~\YMMref{AR}{810}.
Its cutoff comparison uses
\[
 \phi_1=\frac1{180(3n+4)},\qquad
 u=\lceil\phi_1K\rceil,\qquad s=\lceil K/9\rceil.
\]
All its smallness conditions are products of powers of $\ell$ and
quantities decaying exponentially or faster in $K$, except for the
volume factor in the discarded mass. The proof of that theorem
writes the latter majorant as
\[
 \bar{\mathsf R}=2M^{-3}\ell^3L^{3u}
 \exp\!\left[-c'A_0^2(\log(L^u\mathsf b_-))^{2\mathfrak p_0}
                     +C_3\ell^3\right],\qquad
 C_3=\mathsf C^\Sigma_{\rm maj}+2+C_{\rm low}(\mathsf b_+).
\]
Put
\[
 c_\ell(n,g)=
 \left[\frac{c'A_0^2(\phi_1\log L)^{2\mathfrak p_0}}{2C_3}\right]^{1/3}.
\]
If $\ell\le c_\ell(n,g)K^{2\mathfrak p_0/3}$, the positive
volume exponent uses at most half of the negative exponent, since
$\mathsf b_-\ge\gamma^{-2}\ge1$ and
$\log(L^u\mathsf b_-)\ge\phi_1K\log L$.
As $2\mathfrak p_0>1$, the remaining bound decays faster than every
exponential in $K$, uniformly over these sides. The other comparison
conditions then hold beyond a threshold independent of the side;
they continue to hold at every $K'\ge K$ with the side fixed.
Thm.~\YMMref{AR}{810} and Cor.~\YMMref{117.1}{812} give
\[
 \sum_{K'\ge K}
 |S^T_{n;K'+1,\ell}-S^T_{n;K',\ell}|
 \le C\ell^{3(n+1)}K^{\mathsf p_n}L^{-K/10}
                         \prod_i\|f_i\|_\sharp,
 \qquad \mathsf p_n=2\mathfrak p_0(n+1)+\tfrac12.
\]
Under the stated side bound this is at most
$C'K^{2\mathfrak p_0(n+1)+\mathsf p_n}L^{-K/10}
\prod_i\|f_i\|_\sharp$, which tends to zero.
Thus the finite-cutoff connected functions and their spacing limits
on those tori have the same limit, and increasing the cutoffs changes
the values by at most the same tail.

For completeness, the label bounds follow directly from the canonical
flow, as in Prop.~\YMMref{74.1}{615} and
Cor.~\YMMref{74.2}{616}. Put
$\mathcal W_K(g)=\{\beta:(K,\beta)\in\mathfrak D(g)\}$ and
$X_g=L(g^{-2}+B_\sharp)$. The flow has increments of modulus at most
$B_\sharp$ and satisfies
\[
 |x_j(\beta)-L^{-j}\beta|
 \le\bar B(1-L^{-j}).
\]
At its first passage, $x_K(\beta)\le X_g<x_{K-1}(\beta)$.
Thus, for $\mathsf b=L^{-K}\beta$,
\[
 L\mathsf b>X_g-\bar B,
 \qquad
 \mathsf b\le X_g+\bar B-\bar B L^{-K}
                    \le X_g+\bar B.
\]
These imply the outer inclusion because
$L^{-1}(X_g-\bar B)=g^{-2}+B_\sharp-L^{-1}\bar B$ and
$X_g+\bar B=L(g^{-2}+\bar B)$.
To prove the inner inclusion, take
$\mathsf b\in I(g)=(L^{-1}(X_g+\bar B),X_g-\bar B]$
and put $\beta=L^K\mathsf b$. The first passage exists at some
$K'\ge1$, since $\beta>X_g$. Its label
$\mathsf b'=L^{K-K'}\mathsf b$ obeys the preceding two inequalities.
If $K'\ge K+1$, then
$L\mathsf b'\le\mathsf b\le X_g-\bar B$, a contradiction.
If $K'\le K-1$, then
$\mathsf b'\ge L\mathsf b>X_g+\bar B$, also a contradiction.
Hence $K'=K$. Existence and uniqueness of the first passage also
show that the sets $\mathcal W_K(g)$ are disjoint and have union
$(X_g,\infty)$.

\emph{Step 9: Thm.~\ref{C-360-4}(c)--(e).} (c) By Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(e), $T_{mm}(\varphi)-\mathsf b\check D_m(\varphi)$ is $\beta$ times orbital potentials in the plane, which are $-\frac14|G_m(b)|^2$ up to densities of the order $4$, plus $\beta$ times densities of the order $4$ with weights $\le\sup|\varphi|$, plus $\mathsf b\,\mathcal O(\tilde\varphi_m)$ with $|\tilde\varphi_m|\le\frac12a\,{\rm Lip}\,\varphi$. Lem.~\ref{C-360-20}(c) bounds the first by $CK^pL^{-c_nK}\sup|\varphi|\prod_i\|f_i\|_\sharp$, Lem.~\ref{C-360-20}(a) the second by $CK^pL^{-\lambda_LK/4}$, and Lem.~\ref{C-360-20}(b) the third by $C_\epsilon a^{1-\epsilon}{\rm Lip}\,\varphi$. The sum over $m$ gives the trace. By Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(e), $\sum_{p\ni b}a^{-1}(x_b-x(p))_\lambda\mathfrak d_{b,p,\rho}$ is symmetric in $(\lambda,\rho)$, so $(T_{lr}-T_{rl})(\varphi)=\beta\sum_b\sum_{p\ni b}(\varphi(x(p))-\varphi(x_b))a^{-1}[(x_b-x(p))_l\mathfrak d_{b,p,r}-(x_b-x(p))_r\mathfrak d_{b,p,l}]$, an insertion of the order $2$ with weights $\le\beta a\,{\rm Lip}\,\varphi$, and Lem.~\ref{C-360-20}(b) at $\sigma=0$ gives $O(a^{1-\epsilon}){\rm Lip}\,\varphi$; at $\sigma=1$ it gives $C_\epsilon a^{-\epsilon}\sup|\varphi|$ for $T_{lr}$ itself.

By Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(b), $\mathfrak K^{\rm v}[\beta\eta]-\beta\mathfrak K^\sharp[\eta]=-\mathsf b\sum_\rho P_\rho(\nabla^+_\rho\eta^\rho)$, whose in-plane potentials are $-\frac14|G|^2$ up to the order $4$ and whose normal potentials are $\Psi_{\lambda(p)}(p)$: Lem.~\ref{C-360-20}(a), (c). The limit at a fixed label follows from the clause of Thm.~\ref{C-360-2}(d) on one plane field among action densities, with the convergence of the connected functions of $\mathcal O$ at a fixed label, since $\check D_m=\mathcal O-2\mathcal O_m$. (d) One lattice step along $e_r$ is $U(b)\mapsto W(\pm r,\mu_b)U(b)$ up to a gauge, and for every gauge invariant $\Phi$
\[
a\,v_{e_r}\Phi=\tfrac12({\rm Sh}^+_r-{\rm Sh}^-_r)\Phi+\mathcal P_r\Phi-{\rm Sh}^-_r\mathcal P_r\Phi+\mathcal R_r\Phi,\qquad|\mathcal P_r\Phi|\le C\bar a,\quad|\mathcal R_r\Phi|\le C\bar a^{3/2},
\]
${\rm Sh}^\pm_r$ the shifts by $\pm ae_r$ and $\bar a$ the largest plaquette term near the support of $\Phi$. With the null identity of Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(a), its contact form and (c), every member of the Ward identity for the field $\chi\xi$ but $\mathfrak U^\sharp[\chi\xi](f)$ is its stated limit up to $O(K^pL^{-c_nK})$, and $\mathfrak U^\sharp[\chi\xi](f)$ is bounded by Lem.~\ref{C-360-10}, the spread being positive (the field $\chi\xi$ vanishes near the supports of the $f_i$ with $i\notin I$, and near the boundary of the chart for $\xi=\omega y,y$). For $\xi=y$, $\partial_ly^r=\delta_{lr}$, so the contraction with $T_{lr}$ contains the trace, which by (c) is $\mathsf b\,\mathcal O$; this gives the terms $|I|S_n-\mathsf bS_{n+1}(\chi,f)$. For $\xi=e_r$ and $\chi$ a function of $y_3$ alone, $\sum_lT_{lr}(\xi^r\partial_l\chi)=T_{3r}(\chi')$. (e) The equality is the exact identity for the constant field $e_\rho$ (Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(a) with the contact terms; the stress functional of a constant field vanishes). Put $(\tau_\pm f)(y)=f(y\pm ae_\rho)$, $g_i=\nabla^s_\rho f_i$, $f^e_i=\frac12(\tau_+f_i+\tau_-f_i)$ and $h_i=(f^e_i-f_i)/a^2$. The measure is invariant under the lattice translations, so $S^T_n(\tau_+f)=S^T_n(\tau_-f)$; with $\tau_\pm f_i=f^e_i\pm ag_i$ this gives $0=2\sum_{|J|\ {\rm odd}}a^{|J|}S^T_n(g_J,f^e_{J^c})$, and with $f^e=f+a^2h$,
\[
\sum_iS^T_n(g_i,(f_l)_{l\ne i})=-\sum_{|J|\ge3\ {\rm odd}}a^{|J|-1}S^T_n(g_J,f^e_{J^c})-\sum_i\sum_{J'\ne\emptyset}a^{2|J'|}S^T_n(g_i,h_{J'},f_{\rm rest}),
\]
at most $2^n+n2^n$ terms, each with a factor $a^k$, $k\ge2$. The functions $g_i$ and $h_i$ are averages of translates of $\partial_\rho f_i$ and of $\frac12\partial^2_\rho f_i$, so their norms $\|\cdot\|_\sharp$ are bounded by those of these derivatives, and their supports lie in the $a$-neighbourhoods of the ${\rm supp}\,f_i$; the bound \eqref{eq:torus-cumulant-bound} on connected functions at separated supports bounds each term. At $n=2$, $\langle\mathcal O(\tau_\pm f_1);\mathcal O(f_2)\rangle=\langle\mathcal O(f_1);\mathcal O(\tau_\mp f_2)\rangle$ by the invariance, and the two members cancel exactly: the statement has content for $n\ge3$ and expresses the invariance under lattice translations and the failure of the Leibniz rule for $\nabla^s_\rho$. For the second display, the contact form of Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(a) at the field $\chi e_\rho$, where $\Theta_{f_i}[\chi e_\rho]=0$ because $\chi(x_b)=\chi(x(p))$ at every plaquette $p$ at which $f_i$ does not vanish and at its four bonds $b$, and the vector weight $f_i\chi e_\rho$ is $f_ie_\rho$ for $i\in I$ and $0$ otherwise, gives the left member as $-\sum_{i\in I}S^T_n(\dots,\nabla^s_\rho f_i,\dots)$; and $\nabla^s_\rho f-\partial_\rho f$ is an average of translates of $\partial^3_\rho f$ with the total weight $\frac{a^2}6$.

\emph{Step 10: Remark~\ref{C-360-16}.} For a trilinear form that is invariant under the lattice translations along $e_\rho$, write the functions through their Fourier coefficients at $k_1+k_2+k_3=0$ and put $z_i=e^{iak_i}$; then $\nabla^s_\rho$ and $\nabla^+_\rho$ act by $(z-z^{-1})/2a$ and $(z-1)/a$, and since $z_1z_2z_3=1$,
\[
\prod_{i=1}^3(z_i-1)=\sum_iz_i-\sum_{i<j}z_iz_j=\sum_i(z_i-z_i^{-1}),
\]
which is the displayed identity. Prop.~\ref{C-360-21}(c) gives
$a^3S^T_3(g_1,g_2,g_3)\to6\mathsf b'^{-3}\int g_1g_2g_3$
for Lipschitz functions, without a separation assumption. Thus the
two sides can have order $a^{-1}$ when the supports meet. In the
rotational identity the flux through a shell separated from the
supports stays bounded, by Thm.~\ref{C-360-3}(a), whereas
the difference between the symmetric and continuous generators
contains three derivatives.

We first give the free-photon calculation. Its local part requires
a difference estimate for the curvature kernel. For equally
oriented parallel plaquettes $p,p'$, put $u=x(p)-x(q)$, using a
least lift. If $|x(p)-x(p')|\le|u|/4$ and $|u|\ge8a$, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:free-curvature-difference}
 |C^{\rm free}_K(p,q)-C^{\rm free}_K(p',q)|
 \le C_\nabla a^3|x(p)-x(p')|\,|u|^{-4},
 \qquad C_\nabla=256\sqrt3 C_{\rm h}(1+3C_{\rm lat}).
\end{equation}
Here $C_{\rm h}$ is an absolute constant in the interior
gradient estimate for a scalar discrete harmonic function;
Thm.~6.3.8(a) of \cite{LawlerLimic} gives this estimate,
with the finitely many small radii absorbed into the constant.
Indeed, $dd^*+d^*d$ acts on each plane component as the scalar
lattice Laplacian and commutes with the projection onto exact
$2$-forms. Applied to the column $C^{\rm free}_K(\cdot,q)$,
it gives $dd^*\delta_q$, which vanishes beyond the plaquettes
sharing a bond with $q$. The column is therefore harmonic at
distance at least $2a$ from $x(q)$. Join $x(p)$ to $x(p')$
by a lattice path of length at most $\sqrt3|x(p)-x(p')|$.
This path stays at distance at least $|u|/2$ from $x(q)$.
On balls of radius $|u|/4$ about its points,
equation~\YMMref{(2246)}{824} bounds the column by
$4^3(1+3C_{\rm lat})a^3|u|^{-3}$.
The gradient estimate bounds each lattice step by
$4^4C_{\rm h}(1+3C_{\rm lat})a^4|u|^{-4}$.
Summing along the path proves \eqref{eq:free-curvature-difference}.

Let the real functions $f_i$ have compact supports inside the
margin and bounded derivatives through order five, and let
$\chi=1$ on a neighbourhood of these supports. Write $\theta_p$
for the three-colour Gaussian curvature of covariance
$\beta^{-1}C^{\rm free}_K$. In this model
\[
 a_p=\tfrac12|\theta_p|^2,\qquad
 \mathbf w(W_{b,p})=\pm\theta_p,\qquad
 \Psi_\rho(p)=-\tfrac14|\theta_{p_+}-\theta_p|^2.
\]
The sign records the plaquette orientation. The spin densities
and the other insertions are quadratic. The linear Bianchi
identity gives $\mathfrak r^\sharp=0$, hence
$\mathfrak U^\sharp=0$, and Wick's formula gives the connected
functions as rings. The exact Ward identity remains valid after
removing the terms $\frac32a\,\mathcal O(\cdot)$ coming from
the curvature of $SU(2)$; against separated sources these terms
are $O(a)$. The expression with the continuous generator is
therefore, up to $O(a)$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:free-continuous-ward-remainder}
 \mathfrak U_{\omega,\chi}(f)
 -\sum_iS^T_n\bigl(\ldots,
       \nabla^s_\omega f_i-(\omega y)\cdot\nabla f_i,\ldots\bigr).
\end{equation}

The terms with $\chi$ in the first slot have their quadratic
insertion separated from the supports. The ring formula makes
them $O(a)$. The terms with $f_i$ in that slot are local.
For the bilinear part their kernel is
\[
 M_\rho(p,q)
   =[C^{\rm free}_K(p_+,q)-C^{\rm free}_K(p,q)]^2.
\]
Equation~\eqref{eq:free-curvature-difference} bounds it by
$Ca^8|u|^{-8}$ for $|u|\ge8a$; at the remaining distances
use the kernel bound and the projection bound on the diagonal.
The spin part has one additional factor $a$ and kernels
$C^{\rm free}_K(q,q')C^{\rm free}_K(q',p)$, where the
plaquettes $q$ meet a bond of $p$.

Expand the test functions about the midpoint of $x(p),x(p_+)$
in the first case and about $x_b$ in the second. In lattice units
these kernels have uniformly bounded moments through orders
four and two, respectively; the third-order tail in the second
case is even and has degree $-6$. Together with
\[
 \nabla^s_\omega f-(\omega y)\cdot\nabla f
   =\frac{a^2}{6}\sum_\rho(\omega y)_\rho\partial_\rho^3f
        +O(a^4),
\]
the expansion writes \eqref{eq:free-continuous-ward-remainder}
as local forms with factors $a^{-3},a^{-2},a^{-1},a^0$, plus
an $O(a)$ remainder for $n=2$ and an
$O(a\log(1/a))$ remainder for $n=3$.
The infinite-lattice coefficients are independent of $a$ by
scaling. The torus correction changes each term by $O(a)$.
At order three, configurations with two nearby entries and a
third at distance $|u|$ use the fourth moment of a kernel of
degree $-7$. Their contribution is bounded by $a$ times
the sum of $a^3|u|^{-3}$ over $a\le|u|\le1$, which gives
the logarithm. Five derivatives suffice for these Taylor
remainders and for the $O(a^4)$ error in replacing the lattice
sum of $(\omega y)\cdot\nabla\prod_i f_i$ by its integral.
The constants use the suprema of derivatives through order five.

All four local terms vanish. Inversion through the centre of
the chart preserves the Gaussian measure and the expression,
and removes the odd orders in this local expansion,
namely the coefficients of $a^{-2}$ and $a^0$.
The coefficient of $a^{-3}$ is a multiple of
\[
 \int(\omega y)\cdot\nabla\prod_i f_i=0,
\]
since $\operatorname{div}(\omega y)=0$.
For the coefficient of $a^{-1}$, use the other expression
for the same quantity: the variation of $S^T_n$ under
continuous rotations minus the bounded shell flux.
The potentially divergent terms are rotation derivatives of
cubic-invariant local forms with at most two derivatives.
A cubic-invariant symmetric tensor of rank two is a scalar
multiple of the identity, so these forms are rotation invariant.
At $n=2$ the terms can also be written as combinations of
\[
 \int(\omega y)_\rho
        \partial_\rho(\partial_\rho f_1\partial_\rho f_2)=0,
 \qquad
 \int\bigl[(\omega y\cdot\nabla f_1)\Delta f_2
            +(\omega y\cdot\nabla f_2)\Delta f_1\bigr]=0.
\]
The first identity uses that $(\omega y)_\rho$ is independent
of $y_\rho$. The first cubic-invariant local form that need
not be rotation invariant has four derivatives. Thus only the
stated remainders remain. Finally,
$a^3S^T_3\to6\mathsf b^{-3}\int$ in the Gaussian model and
\[
 \sum_i\int(\omega y)_\rho\partial_\rho^3f_i
                        \prod_{l\ne i}f_l
   =3\int(\omega y)_\rho\prod_i\partial_\rho f_i.
\]
Multiplying the difference of the generators by $a$ gives
the asserted limit of $a\mathfrak U_{\omega,\chi}$.

At order one the neighbourhood condition has a concrete role.
Take
\[
 S=[-1,1]\times[-2,2]\times[-1,1],\qquad
 \kappa(y)=3-y_1y_2,\qquad
 f_1=\kappa\,\operatorname{dist}(\cdot,\partial S)
           \ \hbox{on }S,
 \qquad f_1=0\ \hbox{off }S.
\]
The faces of $S$ are lattice planes at every cutoff, and
$f_1$ is Lipschitz with a kink at its boundary. Let
$\chi=\varsigma(\operatorname{dist}(\cdot,S))$, where
$\varsigma\in C^{1,1}$ equals $1-\mu s^2/2$ for
$0\le s\le s_0$, with $\mu>0$, and decreases to zero
inside the margin. Then $\chi=1$ on $S$ but on no
neighbourhood of it. It covers $f_1$: the barycentre and
bond midpoints of every contributing plaquette lie in $S$.
Choose $\omega_{21}=-\omega_{12}=1$, with the other entries zero.
The contact terms are means of the spin and vector insertions
and vanish by reflection, as in Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(b). Hence
\[
 \mathfrak U_{\omega,\chi}(f_1)
 =-\beta\langle\mathfrak S_\omega[\chi]
       +\mathfrak K^{\rm v}[\chi\omega y];\mathcal O(f_1)\rangle.
\]
Its bilinear part is
\[
 -\tfrac34\mathsf b^{-1}
   \sum_{p,q,\rho}(\omega x(p))_\rho
      \nabla^+_\rho\chi(x(p))f_1(x(q))M_\rho(p,q),
 \qquad M_\rho\ge0.
\]
Away from the edges of a face with normal $n_F=\pm e_\nu$,
only $\rho=\nu$ contributes. The factor
$-(n_F)_\nu\nabla^+_\nu\chi$ is $\mu a$ times a nonnegative
function of the exterior lattice distance; $f_1$ is $\kappa a$
times the interior lattice distance. Summing the kernel over
pairs across the plane and then over the $a^{-2}$ plaquettes
per unit area gives
\[
 \tfrac34\mathsf b^{-1}\mu c_{\rm lat}
       \int_{\partial S}(\omega y)\cdot n_F\,\kappa\,\mathrm{d}S.
\]
The positive constant $c_{\rm lat}$ is the pair sum per unit
lattice face. Cubic symmetry makes it the same for every face;
its convergence is bounded by
$\int_0^\infty\int_0^\infty st(s+t+1)^{-6}\,\mathrm{d}s\,\mathrm{d}t$.
Pairs a fixed distance apart contribute $O(a^2)$.
The contribution near the edges vanishes with the width of
the edge neighbourhood; the spin part is $O(a\log(1/a))$
by its $a^6|u|^{-6}$ kernel, and the torus correction is $O(a)$.
The divergence theorem gives
\[
 \int_{\partial S}(\omega y)\cdot n_F\,\kappa\,\mathrm{d}S
   =\int_S(\omega y)\cdot\nabla\kappa
   =\int_S(y_2^2-y_1^2)=16.
\]
Consequently
$\mathfrak U_{\omega,\chi}(f_1)\to
12\mathsf b^{-1}\mu c_{\rm lat}>0$.

For the $SU(2)$ example, choose an even smooth function
$\psi:\mathbb R\to[0,1]$, equal to one on $[-1,1]$ and
zero off $[-2,2]$, and put $\mathsf c=100$ and
\[
 \varPi_{(r_1,r_2,r_3)}(y)=
 \psi((y_1-\mathsf c)/r_1)\psi(y_2/r_2)\psi(y_3/r_3).
\]
Set $g_3=\varPi_{(1,1,1)}$, $g_2=\varPi_{(3,3,3)}$,
$g_1=\varPi_{(7,7,7)}$, and
\[
 G_i(y)=\int_{-\infty}^{y_2}g_i(y_1,t,y_3)\,\mathrm{d}t,
 \qquad f_i=G_i(\cdot+30e_2)+G_i-2G_i(\cdot-30e_2)
       \quad(i\le3).
\]
For $3<j\le n$ take $f_j=\varPi_{(15,45,15)}$ and take
$\chi=\varPi_{(31,91,31)}$, with the same $\omega$ as above
and $\delta_0=\mathsf d=1$. These fixed smooth data have
compact supports with a common point. The cutoff is one on
their closed unit neighbourhood and vanishes outside
$\{|y|_\infty\le182\}$, inside the margin of every admitted
side, since its exponent $m$ is at least seven.

Reflection in $y_1=\mathsf c$ removes the rotation about
the axis through $\mathsf c e_1$; the remaining vector field
is $\mathsf c e_2$. Translation invariance therefore writes
the left side of the exact identity as
\[
 \frac{\mathsf c}{2a}\sum_{|J|\ge3}(|J|-2)a^{|J|}
 S^T_n\bigl((\nabla^+_2f_i)_{i\in J},(f_j)_{j\notin J}\bigr).
\]
The bulk term is this expression minus the flux. The latter
has a quadratic insertion, weights $O(\beta)$ and distance
at least $1/2$ from the supports. Lem.~\ref{C-360-18}, at
$c_*=1/4$, bounds it by
$CK^{(2n+1)\mathfrak p_0}L^{K/4}$.
If $J$ contains an index above three, its derivative entry
vanishes near the support of $f_3$, so the same bound applies.
For $J=\{1,2,3\}$ the three derivatives are translates of
$g_i^K=a^{-1}\int_0^ag_i(\cdot+te_2)\,\mathrm{d}t$ with coefficients
$(1,1,-2)$. Replace the spectators by one, discard triples
with different translates, and replace $g_1^K,g_2^K$ by one.
Each error has an entry separated by at least $1/2$ and is
again covered by that lemma. The equal translates sum to
$1+1-8=-6$. With
$I_K=(a^3/3)\sum_pg_3^K(x(p))$, translation invariance gives
\[
 S^T_n(g_3^K,1,\ldots,1)
    =3a^{-n-3}I_K(-1)^{n-1}E^{(n-1)}(\beta).
\]
Thus, up to $CK^{(2n+1)\mathfrak p_0}L^{-3K/4}$,
\[
 a_K\mathfrak U_{\omega,\chi}(f)
   =900 I_K(-1)^n\mathsf b'^{-n}\beta^nE^{(n-1)}(\beta).
\]
The inner and outer boxes of $g_3^K$ give $1\le I_K\le125$,
and its Lipschitz approximation gives $I_K\to\int g_3$.
Prop.~\ref{C-360-21}(b) gives
$(-1)^n\beta^nE^{(n-1)}(\beta)=-(n-1)!+
O(K^{2n+3}L^{-K/20})$, uniformly in $\mathsf b'\in I(g)$.
Finally $900/2=450$ and $900\cdot125\cdot2\le2.3\cdot10^5$
give the asserted two-sided bounds.

\emph{Step 11: Thm.~\ref{C-360-5}.} Let a board of side $a_i\le\frac{\ell'}2$ be placed, $\{x_3=c\}$ one of its wall planes, $\theta_c$ the mirror at it, $\tau_{a_ie_3}$ the translation by $a_ie_3$, and let $\tilde w$ be a real weight carried by the cell between $\{x_3=c\}$ and its translate by $a_i$ that vanishes within $\frac12\mathsf d$ of the walls. The centred entry $D=\mathcal O_K(\tilde w)-c_0$, $c_0$ its mean on $T_{\ell'}$, has the chessboard seminorm $\|D\|_{\rm ch}\le\mathsf q_i(\mathsf d)\sup|\tilde w|$ for $K\ge K^\#(i,\mathsf d)$, with $\mathsf q_i=e^{G_ga_i^3}{\rm Bl}_{N'_i}(k(\cdot,\mathsf d))^{1/N'_i}$, $N'_i=(\ell'L^i)^3$ and ${\rm Bl}_N(k)=\sum_\pi\prod_{I\in\pi}k(\#I,\mathsf d)$ over the partitions of $N$ points into blocks of at least two: the mean on $T_{\ell'}$ of the product of its $N'_i$ mirror copies is, by the moment--cumulant formula, the sum over these partitions of products of cumulants of copies that are $\ge\mathsf d$ apart, each bounded by Lem.~\ref{C-360-6} at the orders $\le N'_i$ (Thm.~\ref{C-360-2}(a)), and the passage between the sides costs $e^{G_ga_i^3}$ (Lem.~\ref{C-360-7}). A law $\nu$ of the lattice that is invariant under its symmetries, reflection positive at the wall planes of the boards, and dominated by the torus measures through its conditional laws obeys the reflection inequality
\[
|\nu(\overline{\theta_cF'}\,D\,\tau_{a_ie_3}F)|\le\|D\|_{\rm ch}\,\|F'\|\,\|F\|,\qquad\|F\|=\nu(\overline{\theta_cF}F)^{1/2},
\]
for bounded local functions $F,F'$ of the bonds in the half space $\{x_3>c\}$: the form $(F,G)\mapsto\nu(\overline{\theta_cF}G)$ is positive, and the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality for it, repeated at the walls of the board on the dominating tori (the chessboard estimate, Prop.~\YMMref{86.3}{681}, with the Cauchy--Schwarz inequalities of Prop.~\YMMref{91.4}{700}), bounds the left member by the chessboard seminorm of $D$ read along these tori. Every periodic Gibbs state has the three properties: it is invariant under the lattice symmetries, it is reflection positive at all the families of mirrors (Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{103.4}{758}}), and it is dominated by the torus measures (Prop.~\YMMref{91.9}{705}). Recentring from $c_0$ to $\nu(\mathcal O_K(\tilde w))$ costs $\mathsf q_i(\mathsf d)\sup|\tilde w|\,\|F'\|\,\|F\|$ more, by Lem.~\ref{C-360-7} at $q=1$ and $|\nu(\overline{\theta_cF'}\,\tau_{a_ie_3}F)|\le\|F'\|\,\|F\|$; whence the factor $2$:
\[
|\nu(\overline{\theta_cF'}\,[\mathcal O_K(\tilde w)-\nu(\cdot)]\,\tau_{a_ie_3}F)|\le2\mathsf q_i(\mathsf d)\sup|\tilde w|\,\|F'\|\,\|F\|\qquad(K\ge K^\#(i,\mathsf d));
\]
eight shifted boards cover all positions. Along subsequences the limits exist (Thm.~\ref{C-360-2}(c)), and in the reconstruction the bound is what Lem.~\ref{C-360-12} asks, and that lemma gives $B^{(m)}$, the density and the $L^1$ bound. The reconstruction of the limits of Gibbs sequences at $0<g\le\gamma$ has $H\ge0$ (Thm.~\YMMref{AP}{780}), the hypothesis of Lem.~\ref{C-360-12} in the direction $x_3$; and it has $H\ge|P_k|$, $k=1,2$, for the commuting momenta $P_k$ that generate the translations $U(\vec x)$ in the directions orthogonal to $e_3$, the hypothesis of the last sentence of that lemma in the directions $x_1,x_2$: every periodic Gibbs state obeys the five-point inequality \textup{({\cite[eq.~241]{YMM2}})} of Lem.~\ref{lem:spectral-steps} at the mirror normal to $e_3$ and the direction $e_k$, which passes to the limit and puts the spectral measure of every class on $\{\cosh(tE)+\cos(tq_k)\ge2\}$ for a dense set of $t>0$, hence on $\{E\ge|q_k|\}$, as $\cosh(tE)+\cos(tq_k)=2+\frac12t^2(E^2-q_k^2)+O(t^4)$.

The same holds for the reconstruction of a tensor limit. So Lem.~\ref{C-360-12} applies in the three directions, which gives the density in all three coordinates and the $L^1$ bound in them. For the bound on $\|B^{(m)}\|$: for $g\le\gamma^{\rm sd}_W$ the chessboard seminorm of a centred tensor entry in a cell of side $a_i$ is at most $2\mathsf C_TY_i^{\mathsf q_T}a_i^{-11/2}\mathsf b^{-1}|H|_\infty$, uniformly in the cutoff, the datum, the board, the side and the state ({\cite[\S{}2]{YMM2}}, {\cite[eq.~4]{YMM2}} of {\cite[Thm.~B]{YMM2}}(a)); with Lem.~\ref{C-360-12} every tensor limit has the insertion bound with every $p>\frac{17}2$, and $B^{(m)}$ is the compression to the scalar subspace of the point operator at $e=\mathbf 1-2E_{mm}$, $|e|=\sqrt3$; that every limit with converging labels arises from a tensor limit along a further subsequence is the extraction of Thm.~\ref{C-360-3}(g).

For the behaviour under turns: by {\cite[\S{}5]{YMM2}}, every tensor limit at $0<g\le\gamma^{\rm sd}_W$ obeys $\sigma(RX)=\sigma(X)$, $R\in{\rm O}(3)$, at tuples with one non-scalar entry among scalar ones ({\cite[Thm.~U]{YMM2}}, which gives {\cite[Thm.~R]{YMM2}}(c) at these tuples); $R(\mathbf 1-2E_{33})R^{\rm T}=\mathbf 1-2nn^{\rm T}$ with $n=Re_3$, and the sum over $\pm\alpha$ cancels the off-diagonal part of $nn^{\rm T}$, leaving $2\cos^2\alpha(\mathbf 1-2E_{33})+2\sin^2\alpha(\mathbf 1-2E_{ii})$; the entries of $nn^{\rm T}$ are combinations of $1$, $\cos2\alpha$ and $\sin2\alpha$, which gives the form $c_0+c_1\cos2\alpha+c_2\sin2\alpha$ and the second derivative.

\emph{Step 12: Thm.~\ref{C-360-13}.} (a) Put $\lambda=L^{-(k-j)}$, $d=d_j(Z)$ and $S=\sup|E|$; the left member is at most $2S$, and the numbers $a_3$, $C^Q_2$, $\bar C_2=\max\{C^Q_2,1\}$, $c^Q_3$, $c_s=c^Q_s$ and $\lambda_Q$ are those of the extended list. The trivial cases come first: if $\lambda>\lambda_Q$, then $2S\le2\lambda_Q^{-4}\lambda^4S$; if $(d+4)\lambda>c_s$, then $2S\le2((d+4)\lambda/c_s)^4S\le32c_s^{-4}(d+2)^4\lambda^4S$, as $d+4\le2(d+2)$. Let now $\lambda\le\lambda_Q$ and $(d+4)\lambda\le c_s$. Then $\lambda\le1/(4a_3)$, and on a cube that holds the box of $Z$, whose sites lie within the $\ell^1$-distance $l=3(d+4)M$ (level-$j$ units) of its least site, the definition of the cores gives a gauge in which the real part of the potential obeys $|A|\le\lambda$ and $|\nabla A|\le\lambda^2$ in level-$j$ units; with the clause on the complex part this gives a complex potential $A^0$ of the sizes $\lambda$ and $\lambda^2$, up to the complex gauge transformations $g_t=e^{itm}$, $0\le t\le1$, with $|m|\le l\lambda a_3\le3Ma_3c_s\le\frac14$, as $c_s\le1/(12Ma_3)$, so of the size $e^{1/4}$.

The constant part, of the first order, is removed by $g_1$: a term is invariant under real gauge transformations and holomorphic, so it is invariant under every complex gauge transformation that is reached by a path inside its domain, and the path $t\mapsto g_t$ stays there, its triples lying in the cores and below the third radius. What is left, $\tilde A$, vanishes at the least site of the cube and has the gradient $|\nabla\tilde A|\le C^Q_2\lambda^2\le\bar C_2\lambda^2$, so that $|\tilde A|\le l\bar C_2\lambda^2=3(d+4)M\bar C_2\lambda^2$ on the cube; the disc $\zeta\mapsto(\mathbf 1,\zeta\tilde A,\zeta\tilde J)$ of the radius $R=c^Q_3/(l\bar C_2\lambda^2)=c^Q_3/(3(d+4)M\bar C_2\lambda^2)$, of the order $((d+2)\lambda^2)^{-1}$, stays in the domain, because the H\"older number depends only on the curl of the potential, up to squares, and scales with the power $\frac52>2$ under $\rho^{k\to j}_Z$; at the trivial field the first derivative of a gauge invariant term vanishes, since the adjoint representation of ${\rm SU}(2)$ has no invariant vector; and the Schwarz lemma gives $|E((\mathbf 1,\tilde A,\tilde J))-E(\mathbf 1)|\le2SR^{-2}=2l^2\bar C_2^2(c^Q_3)^{-2}\lambda^4S\le72M^2\bar C_2^2(c^Q_3)^{-2}(d+2)^2\lambda^4S$, since $l\le6(d+2)M$ (if $R\le1$ the bound $2S\le2SR^{-2}$ holds already).

This is the clause with $(d+2)^2$, and with the trivial cases it gives 
\[
C_Q=\max\{2\lambda_Q^{-4},32c_s^{-4},72M^2\bar C_2^2(c^Q_3)^{-2}\}
\]
 and the power $(d+2)^4$. For ${\rm U}(1)^3$ the field strength scales like $\lambda^2$ and the linear term survives. The power $4$ is attained by a term of the second order in the field strength at one plaquette, against a triple with a constant field strength of the largest admitted size. (b) A block of the level $k$ holds $L^{3(k-j)}$ regions of the level $j$, each constant up to $L^{-4(k-j)}$ by (a); the count of regions among the construction results with the rate $\kappa_{\rm lf}\ge4\log18432$ of (b) gives the bound, uniformly in $k$. (c) The complex centre of each Gaussian integral is kept as a free argument, one $1$-form for every earlier level, in a polydisc.

The first order of a plane weight gives $\sup|w|L^{-5/2}{\rm hol}$, hence the third radius, which is small at the true points and stable under the shift system among the construction results; the weight and the trees enter as potentials, so that the action of the step carries no explicit weight; a tree of the level $j$ weighs $L^{k-j+1}$ seen from the level $k$, there are $L^{3(k-j)}$ of them and each is smaller by $L^{-5(k-j)}$; the non-classical terms stay at their levels and are lifted afresh at every step by (b), at the rate $r_1$, which (b) admits since $r_1>\mathsf C_{\rm cs}>4\log18432$. Each step is then the identity of the statement, classical times ideal times the exponential of a tiny term, with $c_k(W)\Xi_0[V_{\mathsf m}](Q)=\Phi_{k+1}[\omega](W)$; at $k=0$ the step is written with bond labels.

On the plain cores the H\"older number is at most $\alpha_0$ times a factor that grows like $L^{n/2}$ with the level, while $\alpha_2/\alpha_0\ge4.99\cdot10^6e^{L/4}$; so the condition of the third radius follows from the plain core at the levels $n\le(\frac L2+29.39)/\log L$. At $k=0$ the weight enters linearly through the bond labels, and the centre, the solution of the linear system of the step with a source of the size $\sigma$, is at most $K_Z\sigma$. The extended list, stated before Thm.~\ref{C-360-13}, places each new constant after the constants on which it depends and before $\gamma$; its four new lower bounds are laid on the chosen constants $\mathsf C_{\rm ex}$, $\kappa$, $\bar\kappa$ and $M$, which are free upward, each by a function of earlier constants, its new conditions on $\gamma$ are ceilings whose left members tend to $0$, and it lays no condition on $L$ itself; so it keeps the admissible shape, its choices exist, and they restrict to choices of the lists of Thms.~\YMMref{D}{8}, \YMMref{AJ}{673} and~\YMMref{AD}{607}.

At every choice $L>4\cdot10^{19}$: the retained floor $L\ge L_\Pi=2\mathsf C_{\rm ex}(1+4\beta_{\rm s})/(1-2\delta_{\rm w})\ge2\mathsf C_{\rm ex}$ (equation~\YMMref{(904)}{418}, with $\beta_{\rm s}>0$ and $0<\delta_{\rm w}<\frac12$), the new lower bound $\mathsf C_{\rm ex}\ge2\mathsf C_{\rm cs}$, and $\mathsf C_{\rm cs}\ge24C_{\mathrm E}^2e^{24}$ by the choice preceding equation~\YMMref{(1332)}{552}, $C_{\mathrm E}=4096$, give $L\ge4\mathsf C_{\rm cs}\ge96C_{\mathrm E}^2e^{24}>4\cdot10^{19}$. The further conditions named in the statement are of three kinds. The tower hypotheses of \S\ref{sec:analytic-core-complements} and the inequality $\alpha_0+\alpha_1\le a^\sharp$, even $2(\alpha_0+\alpha_1)\le a^\sharp$, are closed inequalities between constants that hold at every choice of the list of Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8}, and so at every choice of the extended list, which restricts to such a choice.

The standing conditions of the frame of {\cite[Def.~B.14]{YMM2}} follow, condition by condition, from members of the lists of Thms.~\YMMref{D}{8}, \YMMref{AJ}{673} and~\YMMref{AD}{607}, to which the choices of the extended list restrict. The locality for all pairs of regions and the gauge covariance at all decoupling parameters are properties of the Gaussian structure among the construction results as it is formed, at all admitted constants: its structures form a local system, and they are covariant under real gauge transformations at all decoupling parameters $s$ of the closed polydisc (Thm.~\YMMref{U}{378}(2) and the covariance of the operators in \YMMref{(765)}{378}: restrictions commute with the unitary gauge actions, as do inversion and the functional calculus used to form the covariance and coupling).

\emph{Step 13: Thm.~\ref{C-360-14}.}
(a) Prop.~\ref{prop:weighted-critical-response} proves the
uniform critical-background and Hessian assertions. We give the
remaining comparisons and check the actual step data.

At $U_0=1$ with all regions the whole torus, the quadratic form
for plane weights is
\[
 \langle B,Z_\epsilon B\rangle
 =\min_{Qd=B}
 \{(\partial d,\mathsf a\,\partial d)+\|RD^{\mathsf T}d\|^2\},
 \qquad 1-\epsilon\le\mathsf a\le1+\epsilon.
\]
Each form before minimization lies between $1-\epsilon$ and
$1+\epsilon$ times the unweighted form, including its
nonnegative slice term. Taking the infimum gives the claimed
comparison of block Hessians. For the single mixed tensor term,
$2|\langle f_{\mu\nu},f_{\mu\lambda}\rangle|
\le|f_{\mu\nu}|^2+|f_{\mu\lambda}|^2$ gives the same form
comparison in the stated normalization. Adding the square of the
linearized block averages preserves it. Thus the linearization
of the constrained system is invertible at zero. On each fixed
finite lattice the analytic implicit-function theorem gives
the stated family near zero.

The reason a uniform H\"older estimate needs the H\"older norm
of the weight can be seen in this same quadratic problem.
Fix $B\in Y_0$, $B\ne0$, and write
$h_\epsilon=d_bA\cdot B$ at $b=0$.
Take the torus side $N=2L^{m+K-k}$ in level units, as in the
construction; it has the even number $N/\eta_k=2L^{m+K}$
of bare sites in each direction.
Choose a plane $(\mu\nu)$ in which
$F^0=\partial h_0$ has largest component norm, and put
$v_{\mu\nu}(x)=\epsilon(-1)^{x_\mu/\eta_k}$,
with all other plane weights zero. Then
\[
 Qh_\epsilon=B,\quad RD^{\mathsf T}h_\epsilon=0,\quad
 \partial^{\mathsf T}\mathsf a\,\partial h_\epsilon
                              =Q^{\mathsf T}Z_\epsilon B.
\]
The supremum of the source on the right is at most
$(1+\epsilon)C_{\rm tr}c_Z\|B\|$, with
$c_Z\ge\|Z_0\|$ and the row-to-supremum norm $C_{\rm tr}$ of
$Q^{\mathsf T}$ depending only on $L$.
Since $\delta=h_\epsilon-h_0$ has $Q\delta=0$, subtracting
the two variational equations and testing by $\delta$ gives
\[
 \|\partial\delta\|^2+\|RD^{\mathsf T}\delta\|^2
 =-\epsilon\bigl((-1)^{x_\mu/\eta_k}
       (\partial h_\epsilon)_{\mu\nu},
                         (\partial\delta)_{\mu\nu}\bigr).
\]
It follows that
\[
 \|(\partial h_\epsilon)_{\mu\nu}\|
 \ge(1+\epsilon)^{-1}\|F^0_{\mu\nu}\|
 \ge(1+\epsilon)^{-1}(\gamma^{\rm pc}/3)^{1/2}\|B\|.
\]
On the torus of side $N$ in level units, its supremum
$f_\epsilon$ is therefore at least
$(1+\epsilon)^{-1}(\gamma^{\rm pc}/(3N^3))^{1/2}\|B\|$.
At two neighbouring sites in direction $\mu$, use the bond
equation at the site carrying the factor $1+\epsilon$.
It expresses $2\epsilon(\partial h_\epsilon)_{\mu\nu}$
as $\eta_k$ times the source minus two first differences of
curvature components, with coefficients at most $1+\epsilon$
and $1$. Consequently
\[
 2\epsilon f_\epsilon\le
 (2+\epsilon)\operatorname{osc}(\partial h_\epsilon)
       +\eta_k(1+\epsilon)C_{\rm tr}c_Z\|B\|.
\]
Here $\operatorname{osc}$ is the largest modulus of the change
of one curvature component between neighbouring bare sites.
For $\eta_k\le c_\eta\epsilon N^{-3/2}$ this gives
\[
 [\partial h_\epsilon]_{\beta_H}
 \ge\frac16\Bigl(\frac{\gamma^{\rm pc}}{3N^3}\Bigr)^{1/2}
                       \epsilon\eta_k^{-\beta_H}\|B\|.
\]
Here the seminorm includes neighbouring sites. At fixed $N$
this diverges as $k\to\infty$, although the weight has supremum
$\epsilon$. Since the background vanishes at zero block datum,
the example concerns its derivative there. Cauchy's estimate
would bound that derivative if the backgrounds had a uniform
H\"older bound on a common block-datum ball.

The constant-weight assertion follows from the exact identity
\[
 F+T_{(h,v+c)}=(1+c)(F+T_{(h,v)/(1+c)}).
\]
Multiplying the critical equation multiplies its multiplier by
$1+c$ and leaves its constraint and gauge unchanged.
Uniqueness in Prop.~\ref{prop:weighted-critical-response}
then gives the asserted identity of critical fields.

For the history application use the collared sequence before the
step and its completion by the next large-field region.
The background of the run is its real unweighted critical
configuration at the prescribed averages. The block field $A_k$
is read about its finer average in the axial gauge, and its row
datum is $b=JA_k$, extended by zero to the remaining rows.
The regular-background and chart estimates for these actual
step fields, Lem.~\YMMref{37.5}{287},
Prop.~\YMMref{53.12}{457}, and the fibre-chart bounds in
{\cite[\S{}B.2]{YMM2}}, give
\[
 \alpha\le2C_{\mathfrak P}\mathfrak M B_3\varepsilon(x_t),
 \qquad
 \sup|b|\le2C_\chi\mathsf c_{\rm fl}\delta(x_k),
 \quad C_{\mathfrak P}=504L^2B^{\rm p}_1 .
\]
For the natural-class assertion, apply Lem.~\YMMref{37.5}{287}
with the separated witness $m=\mathfrak M$, increasing the
common block floor if necessary. The layerwise regularity
radius of the real background is at most $2B_3\varepsilon(x_t)$,
so that lemma gives the displayed natural-class radius on the
completed sequence. The chart converts the fluctuation field
to the row datum with the displayed factor $2C_\chi$.
Choose
\[
 a_N\le\min\{a_*,a^{\rm pc},\gamma^{\rm pc}/(4e_0)\},
 \quad \rho_N^+\le\frac{\gamma^{\rm pc}\rho_*}{4\kappa_0},
 \quad z_N^+\le\frac{\gamma^{\rm pc}z_*}{4\kappa_0},
\]
also keeping $\rho_N^+<\rho_*$ and $z_N^+<z_*$.
Impose the ceilings, for all $x\ge\gamma^{-2}$,
\[
 2C_{\mathfrak P}\mathfrak M B_3\varepsilon(x)\le a_N,
 \qquad 2C_\chi\mathsf c_{\rm fl}\delta(x)\le\rho_N^+ .
\]
Their left sides tend to zero with $\gamma$.
Thus $e_0\alpha\le\gamma^{\rm pc}/4$ and
$\kappa_0s\le\gamma^{\rm pc}/4$ at every step $t\ge2$,
which gives the asserted half-floor.

At the first step $k=0$, the lattice spacing is one, the block
averages are the identity and the slice projection vanishes.
There is no minimization at this step. At the real regular
reference the fluctuation floor differs from the action Hessian
by the second derivative of the block constraint paired with
the current. Its loss is at most $8c_{\rm pc}\alpha$, where
$c_{\rm pc}=\sqrt2C_Kn_{\rm pc}$ and $n_{\rm pc}=36L^3$.
For a complex block field $A^{(0)}$ with
$r_A=\sup|A^{(0)}|$, differentiating the four link factors in
each plaquette and summing their incident bonds gives the

Therefore
\begin{align*}
 \operatorname{Re}(F+T_{\mathbf h})''(JA^{(0)})[J\bar B,JB]
 \ge\bigl(&\gamma^{\rm pc}-8c_{\rm pc}\alpha
       -128r_Ae^{4r_A}\\
       &-512e^{8r_A}\|h\|_\infty
       -32e^{4r_A}\sup|v|\bigr)\|B\|^2 .
\end{align*}
This uses the real natural pair on the two-region sequence
$(\Omega_0,\Omega_1)$ and $\mathfrak M\ge M^{\rm pc}$,
exactly as in the unweighted positivity argument above.
Take
\[
 a_N^1\le\min\{a^{\rm pc},\varpi_\chi,
                       \gamma^{\rm pc}/(64c_{\rm pc})\},
 \quad r_N^1=\min\{1/4,\gamma^{\rm pc}/(1024e)\},
 \quad z_N^1=\gamma^{\rm pc}/(2048e^2).
\]
The ceilings
\[
 2C_{\mathfrak P}\mathfrak M B_3\varepsilon(x)\le a_N^1,
 \qquad
 2C_\chi\mathsf c_{\rm fl}\delta(x)
                         \le\min\{r_N^1,r_\chi\},
 \qquad x\ge\gamma^{-2},
\]
put the first-step data in these ranges.
The losses through $\alpha$, through $r_A$, and through the
weights are at most $\gamma^{\rm pc}/8$,
$\gamma^{\rm pc}/8$, and $\gamma^{\rm pc}/4$ respectively.
This leaves $\gamma^{\rm pc}/2$ for the stated complex data.

(b) Lem.~\ref{lem:weighted-local-hessian} identifies the perturbation as $D^{(1)\mathsf T}vD^{(1)}+Z_{1,v}$. The complete mean-square argument is Prop.~\ref{prop:weighted-system-L2}: its proof first controls the divergence-input system with the actual averaging rows, inserts $vD^{(1)}A$ as a source, and then localizes with a divergence-form cutoff. It proves both inverse existence and the termwise walk bounds without taking a difference of $v$.

The grouping by visited pieces after Prop.~\ref{prop:weighted-system-L2} gives the connected-set factor in (b). (c) The label supplies its background regular at the radius $C_m\varepsilon_k$ with the envelope $e(x)=C_m\varepsilon_{j(x)}$. Two of the three ceilings of the statement are the label's: $\sup_{x\ge\gamma^{-2}}C_m\varepsilon(x)\le\alpha_\star$ bounds the radius of regularity and the envelope at every level by the number $\alpha_\star$ of $L$, and $\sup_{x\ge\gamma^{-2}}\max\{w_{\rm G},w_{\rm lin}\}(\log x)^{-r}\le1$ gives $MR(\gamma^{-2})\ge\max\{w_{\rm G},w_{\rm lin}\}$, $w_{\rm G}=4c_U^{-1}(7\log L+\log2)$; under these, and with $t({\rm an})<t_0\le t_{\rm lin}(L)\le\frac14$, Lem.~\ref{C-360-22} and the locality below are applied; the third, the membership ceiling, is read below.

Use Lems.~\ref{C-360-22} and~\ref{hyp:complex-scalar-transfer}. The pair $(A,\omega)$ is the fixed point of the critical-point contraction built on \eqref{eq:uniform-linear-response-bound} and the local H\"older bounds. To localize it, write $G'=(\Delta_D+Q'^*\mathsf a'Q')^{-1}$ in the scalar notation and retain $Q'Q'^*=1$. Since $\ker R=\operatorname{ran}(G'Q'^*)$, the slice condition is equivalently the local equation $(1-Q'^*Q')\Delta_DD^*A=0$. Cut the far field off with a slow cutoff ${\rm ch}$ of width $w(L)$ and bounded scaled first and second differences. In the augmented scalar system the cutoff error is supported where ${\rm ch}$ varies. Its inverse is the actual compression $\mathbb K^{[2]}$ described in Lem.~\ref{hyp:complex-scalar-transfer}; the two nonlinear remainders are precisely $N$ and $q$ there. Estimate \eqref{eq:complex-scalar-transfer} therefore makes the scalar correction a contraction in the exponentially weighted norm. Applying its contraction gives the stated locality estimate with $c_U$ and $K_U=7K_{\rm lin}^2(1+2L^3)^2e^{c_Uw_*}$, after the permitted enlargement of $K_{\rm lin}$, where $w_*=w+21L$.

Continuity: a uniform limit of iterates, with the error $\frac23\,4^{-n}$. Uniqueness is in the normalized class: the gauge functions preserve the block averages and induce the identity at the tops. If $v_j[A']$ denotes the accumulated averaging gauge, this means
\[
 u(y)=v_j[A'^u](y)v_j[A'](y)^{-1}
 \quad\text{at every top }y\text{ of level }j.
\]
The scalar transfer carries a sufficiently small critical point into the slice.
