       =e_1\{D^{(1)\mathsf T}vD^{(1)}A+Z_{1,v}A\}
       =\iota^+ V_v\Psi.
\]
To read the last expression in the system's source space, put the
antisymmetric components of $vD^{(1)}A$ whose indices belong to that
space into $X_1$. Put $Z_{1,v}A$ and the omitted boundary contributions
into $f_1$; the other entries are zero. Indeed, the ambient plaquette
form retains plaquettes meeting the boundary, whereas the system's
$\nabla$ omits a translated bond outside its inner-bond index set.
Their difference is supported on bonds a bounded number of bare steps
from the boundary. Every such cell is in the bare layer, where
$\xi_y=\xi$. Each difference has bounded row and column multiplicity
and size at most $C|v|_\infty\xi^{-2}|A|$ on neighboring bonds.
The weighted Schur estimate therefore gives it source weight $-3$
from the potential weight $-1$. This is the same boundary treatment
used above for $D^{\mathsf T}A$. In the interior the identification
with the transpose of
$D^{(1)}A=\nabla_\mu A_\nu-\nabla_\nu A_\mu$ is exact.
The curvature bound of the natural pair and the local plaquette
support consequently give
\begin{equation}\label{eq:weighted-vertex-L2}
 \|V_v\Psi\|_y\le C|v|_\infty
                       \max_{d(y,z)\le\rho_0}\|\Psi\|_z.
\end{equation}
No derivative of $v$ occurs. For a small-field local inverse,
$\|V_v\mathbb E\iota^+\|\le1/4$ follows by decreasing $r_2$.
Consequently
\[
 \mathbb E_v\iota^+
 =\mathbb E\iota^+[I+V_v\mathbb E\iota^+]^{-1}
\]
converges at the same fixed local rate. It is a right inverse on all
sources: $\iota^+$ is surjective, since the plain source components
alone span the equations. Finite dimensionality therefore gives
invertibility. The scalar compressions do not contain the changed
first equation. This proves the local weighted conclusion for all
four systems.

\emph{Localization.}
Use the pieces, $\widetilde h_\kappa$, $\theta_\kappa$ and local
sequences of Lem.~\YMMref{27.5}{207}. Lem.~\YMMref{27.6}{209}
identifies the global and local physical averaging germs, including
$C^{(2)}$, on $\kappa^{[5/6]}$. The pair on a regular piece has a
real gauge in which its size is at most
$8L^2(\alpha_0+\alpha_1+\gamma_0+\gamma')$.
Choose $a_2$ to place this below the small-field threshold above.
A boundary piece has only the bare layer; its mean-square norms are
finite-component Euclidean norms, uniformly equivalent to the local
supremum norms. The boundary-piece inverse in the proof of
Thm.~\YMMref{G}{204}, followed by the same bounded insertion,
gives its local estimate. Thus every local weighted inverse has a
uniform mean-square bound at a rate $2\delta_2$.

The source cutoff must respect divergence form. Define
$h\star g^+$ by multiplying all components by $h$ and subtracting
$[\nabla^{\mathsf T},h]X_1$ from the first component and
$[D^{\mathsf T},h]X_5$ from the fifth. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:weighted-source-cutoff}
 \iota^+(h\star g^+)=h\,\iota^+g^+.
\end{equation}
The additional commutators have coefficients bounded by the first
scaled difference of $h$, so are bounded in mean square. For the
system commutator write
\[
 [\mathbb K_v,h]=\iota^+ C_{v,h}^+.
\]
The unweighted terms have the same three kernel types checked in
\eqref{eq:weighted-small-defect-L2}, with $\epsilon$ replaced by the
scaled first or second difference of $h$. For example,
$[Q,h](c,b)=Q(c,b)(h(b)-h(c))$; the quadratic-row term is treated by
its symmetric Schur bounds. The weighted principal term is exactly
\[
 [D^{(1)\mathsf T}vD^{(1)},h]A
  =D^{(1)\mathsf T}\{v[D^{(1)},h]A\}
                +[D^{(1)\mathsf T},h]vD^{(1)}A.
\]
Keep the admitted indices of its first term as a divergence source.
Its omitted boundary indices are placed in the ordinary first slot,
by the same bare-layer calculation as for $V_v$. Commuting their local
kernel with $h$ introduces the difference of $h$ across at most a
fixed number of bare steps. Thus both the interior and boundary terms
cost a first scaled difference of $h$ and $|v|_\infty$; no difference
of $v$ is taken. The local remainder $[Z_{1,v},h]$ has the same bound
by its plaquette support. The piece cutoffs consequently give
\[
 \|C_{v,\widetilde h_\kappa}^+\Psi\|_y
      \le C\mathfrak M^{-1}
                    \max_{d(y,z)\le2\rho_0}\|\Psi\|_z.
\]
The commutator is supported where the cutoff is nonconstant, at
distance at least $D_0$ from the input cutoff. All these norms coincide
under the local/global identification: the values, differences and
one-step shifts that occur here lie in $\kappa^{[5/6]}$. This is the
same margin used in Lem.~\YMMref{27.6}{209}; raising $M_2$ to ensure
$\mathfrak M\ge32L^4$ also includes the two shifts in the differentiated
norms.

Define maps on divergence-form sources by
\[
 T_\kappa^+=\widetilde h_\kappa\mathbb E_{v,\kappa}\iota^+
                                      (\theta_\kappa\star\cdot),
 \qquad
 R_\kappa^+=-C_{v,\widetilde h_\kappa}^+
                   \mathbb E_{v,\kappa}\iota^+
                                      (\theta_\kappa\star\cdot).
\]
The identity $\sum_\kappa\theta_\kappa=1$ gives
\[
 \mathbb K_v\sum_\kappa T_\kappa^+
       =\iota^+\left(I-\sum_\kappa R_\kappa^+\right).
\]
Use half the local exponential decay for the input-to-commutator
distance. The remaining half yields $\|T_\kappa^+\|\le C$ and
$\|R_\kappa^+\|\le q_2$ with the supports in the statement.
The local geometry bounds the number of possible next pieces by a
number $N=N(L)$; at a fixed output top at most $N$ first pieces
contribute. Increase $M_2$ until $Nq_2\le1/2$. Then
\[
 \mathbb E_v\iota^+
 =\sum_{m\ge0}\ \sum_{\kappa_0,\ldots,\kappa_m}
       T_{\kappa_0}^+R_{\kappa_1}^+\cdots R_{\kappa_m}^+.
\]
Composition gives \eqref{eq:weighted-L2-walk}; summing the geometric
series $\sum_m N^{m+1}q_2^m$ gives
\eqref{eq:weighted-system-L2-decay}. The local construction also proves
the stated dependence on the visited regions. This completes the proof.
\end{proof}

A convenient precise meaning of a connected walk term is now available.
Make a graph whose vertices are the pieces and whose edges join pieces
with meeting $[5/6]$ enlargements. For a finite vertex set $S$, sum the
walks whose set of visited pieces is exactly $S$. There is no such walk
when $S$ is disconnected. If $|S|=s$, every contributing walk has at
least $s-1$ transitions. Given $0<\epsilon_*<1$, increase $M_2$ until
$Nq_2\le\min\{1/2,\epsilon_*\}$. At each fixed output top its sum is
then bounded, in \eqref{eq:weighted-system-L2-decay}, by
\[
 C\sum_{m\ge s-1}(Nq_2)^m\le2C\epsilon_*^{s-1}.
\]
Locality follows from the union of the corresponding local regions.
The same grouping applies to a difference of two local inverses:
$E_v-E_0=-E_0(\mathbb K_v-\mathbb K_0)E_v$ and the displayed local
vertex identify its support. This is the connected-set factor used
for the weighted fluctuation form; its cubes are these pieces, with
the indicated enlargements, rather than an arbitrary partition.

The proposition also permits an envelope $h$ with
$h(z)/h(y)\le C_h e^{\delta_2d(y,z)/2}$. Dividing
\eqref{eq:weighted-system-L2-decay} by $h(y)$ gives the corresponding
weighted mean-square estimate, with constant $B_2C_h$ and at least
half the decay rate. This quantitative ratio is what is meant here
when an envelope varies slowly.

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:weighted-energy-L2}
Under the hypotheses of Prop.~\ref{prop:weighted-system-L2}, let
the only forcing be the first-slot divergence $D^{(1)\mathsf T}Y$,
with homogeneous row data. The potential component of the solution
satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:weighted-global-energy-L2}
 \xi^3\sum_b\xi_{y(b)}^{-2}|A(b)|^2
     +\xi^3\sum_{b,\mu}|\nabla_\mu A(b)|^2
       \le C\xi^3\sum_p|Y(p)|^2.
\end{equation}
Ambient boundary plaquettes are included on the right. The constant
depends only on $L$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Decompose the divergence source by its cell positions and apply the
local estimate to one cell at a time. The antisymmetric embedding
and its bare-layer boundary correction have uniformly bounded
multiplicities, as in the proof of
\eqref{eq:weighted-vertex-L2}. Thus the block norm of the map from
$Y$ to $(A,\nabla A)$ is at most $Ce^{-\delta_2d(y,z)}$, with weights
$-2$ on $Y$ and $\nabla A$ and $-1$ on $A$.
The squares of these normalized cell norms acquire the common factor
$\xi_y^{-1}$ when expressed in the energy norm of
\eqref{eq:weighted-global-energy-L2}. On the resulting ordinary
sequence $\ell^2$ spaces the block bound is therefore
\[
 Ce^{-\delta_2d(y,z)}(\xi_z/\xi_y)^{1/2}
       \le C'L^{1/2}e^{-\delta_2d(y,z)/2},
\]
after the same increase of the layer separation used in the flat
estimate. The row and column sums of this nonnegative matrix are
bounded by the cell-summation estimate of
Lem.~\YMMref{21.2}{141}. Cauchy--Schwarz, first with its row sum and
then with its column sum, proves its boundedness on $\ell^2$.
This is \eqref{eq:weighted-global-energy-L2}.
\end{proof}


\section{The two-term short-distance law}\label{supp:C-350-1}
The leading action-density covariance is the free kernel of
degree $-6$. Its first correction has degree $-5$. A test pair
of scale $d$ and shape $\vartheta\in(0,1)$ consists of nonzero
Lipschitz functions $f,h\ge0$, carried by two closed balls of
radius $d$ whose distance lies in $[d,6d]$, with
\[
 \int f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x\ge\vartheta|f|_\infty d^3,\qquad
 \operatorname{Lip}f\le |f|_\infty/(\vartheta d),
\]
and the same bounds for $h$. On a torus require $20d\le\ell$.
Write this class as $\mathfrak T(d;\vartheta)$ and put
\[
 \mathcal K_q(f,h)=\iint f(x)h(y)|x-y|^{-q}
                         \,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y,
 \qquad
 L_b^+=c_2b^{-2}(\mathcal K_6+c_1b^{-1}\mathcal K_5),
\]
where
\[
 c_2=\frac9{16\pi^2},\qquad c_1=\frac8{3\pi}.
\]
On the least admissible torus the distance is read in the small
Euclidean lift containing the test pair.

\begin{sketch}[The first correction]
\label{supp:C-350-3}
At sufficiently small reference coupling, fixed label
$b\in I(g)$ and sufficiently small $d$, the connected
two-point function satisfies
\[
 |S_{2;K}-L_b^+|(f,h)
 \le\left[\bar\varepsilon(d)b^{-3}d
             +C_{\rm lat}b^{-2}\frac{a_K}{d}\right]
                  |f|_\infty|h|_\infty,
 \qquad\bar\varepsilon(d)\longrightarrow0.
\]
The working depth of $d$ must lie below $K$. After removal of
the cutoff, the first error can be bounded by
$Cb^{-3}d^{3/2}|f|_\infty|h|_\infty$. The law transfers, in
the separately stated ranges, to other admitted tori, periodic
states, volume-first limits and their components.
\end{sketch}

\paragraph{Sketch of the argument.}
There are two jobs: identify the coefficient and control the
interacting remainder. A finite-box perturbative calculation
does only the first. To connect it with the full correlation,
introduce two source parameters and differentiate the local
normalizing energies twice. Sum these mixed derivatives over
the renormalisation levels. An auxiliary complex field scale
$\lambda$, multiplying every fluctuation field, makes this
source-energy sum an even holomorphic function. The free
contribution is explicit; the coefficient of $\lambda^6$
contains the first correction. Parity removes the half-integer
orders in the equivalent Laplace expansion.

The coefficient is compared through a sequence of finite
objects. First truncate the levels at a working scale, with a
bound for the omitted tail. At zero field scale, the fluctuation
laws are Gaussian laws restricted to their small-field boxes.
Their precision matrices have a uniform positive lower bound. Gaussian
tails therefore control the error made by removing the boxes.
The coefficient is now a finite Gaussian expression with the
coarsest background fixed at the identity. Compare these
expressions in different boxes, then exhaust the lattice and
compare the resulting lattice kernel with its
homogeneous continuum part. Each comparison has its own
geometry and error; the auxiliary box and cutoff are chosen
so those errors are all small relative to $b^{-3}d$.

The last comparison is where the numerical value enters. The
six two-loop graph classes are reduced to a finite residue
functional. Their sum gives
\[
 \kappa^{\rm lat}=\frac3{2\pi^3}=c_2c_1.
\]
The finite-box coefficient is independent of the intermediate
gauge parameter. Its infinite-lattice limit is obtained by
taking the large-inverse-coupling expansion first at fixed box,
then exhausting the lattice. This order does not establish a
uniform remainder for growing boxes. The renormalisation
comparisons above are needed precisely to return from that
coefficient to the interacting measure.

Initially the expansion is proved in a cutoff window
$L^K\le d^{-P}$. At fixed label, consecutive-cutoff comparison
allows one to stop at a sufficiently fine $K_\sharp(d)$ inside
that window and estimate every larger cutoff by it. Thus the
window disappears from the fixed-label conclusion. The two
errors in the result remain conceptually different:
$a_K/d$ is a lattice approximation error, whereas
$\bar\varepsilon(d)b^{-3}d$ controls the correction beyond the
two retained continuum kernels.

This is a two-term short-distance statement. It neither gives
the arbitrary-order free law left open in the preceding sketch
nor permits the cutoff and short-distance limits to be exchanged
without their displayed scale restrictions.




\subsection{The two-term short-distance law on the torus}\label{C-350-1}

For the action density, the first correction to the free two-point law is
of relative order $d/b$. More precisely, the two-term approximation is
\[
c_2b^{-2}\bigl[\mathcal K_6+c_1b^{-1}\mathcal K_5\bigr](f,h),\qquad c_2=\frac9{16\pi^2},\quad c_1=\frac8{3\pi},
\]
The error is
$[\bar\varepsilon(d)b^{-3}d+C_{\rm lat}b^{-2}a_K/d]\|f\|_\infty\|h\|_\infty$.
Thm.~\ref{C-350-3} states the cutoff and label ranges, the improvement
to a remainder of order $d^{3/2}$, and the averaged logarithmic correction.
Cor.~\ref{C-350-28} passes the law to every periodic state and to the
continuum limits and their components.

The proof first expresses the covariance as an average of source-energy
jets over translated pairs. A complex field scale separates the free
term, of order four, from the correction, of order six. A composed
block-field chart identifies the latter with a constrained lattice
Laplace coefficient. Comparison of two bare tori and removal of the flat
block constraint then connect it to the infinite-lattice coefficient.
The lattice calculation is proved in \S\ref{IV-73-0}.

That calculation first takes the weak-coupling limit in a fixed box and
then exhausts the lattice. Its box-dependent remainder is not a bound in
the simultaneous continuum and large-volume limit. The renormalisation
and finite-torus comparisons below provide the separate passage needed
here.

\subsubsection{Parameters and test pairs}

We use the Wilson $G=\mathrm{SU}(2)$ model in three dimensions.
Its Lie algebra consists of the hermitian traceless $2\times2$ matrices
with $\langle X,Y\rangle=\frac12\operatorname{tr}XY$, extended
complex bilinearly. The trace is the ordinary matrix trace, and $|X|$
is the operator norm on $\mathbb C^2$. Near the identity we use
$\log X=-\sum_{n\ge1}(I-X)^n/n$, for $|X-I|<1$.
For $U\in\mathrm{SU}(2)\setminus\{-I\}$ the intrinsic branch is
$\log U=iY$, where $Y$ is Hermitian and traceless and $|Y|<\pi$;
these branches agree on their common domain.
Fix a mollifier, a source radius $2\varrho>0$, and one common choice
of the constants in Prop.~\YMMref{69.1}{595} and
Section~\YMMref{82}{665}. In particular $L\ge13$ is odd and $a_j=L^{-j}$.
We retain all the real-step conditions when imposing the sourced-step
conditions: restricting to the real construction leaves every retained
constant unchanged. The two radius conditions are
\[
 2\varrho\le\sigma^{\rm S}(x-\bar B),\qquad
 2\varrho x^{-1/2}(\log x)^{\mathfrak p_0}
       \le\sigma^{\rm S}_{\rm L}\qquad(x\ge\gamma^{-2}).
\]
They are imposed by Prop.~\YMMref{82.2}{668}, after the
radius-independent choices of Section~\YMMref{82}{665}. Thus all
uses of the real flow, the sourced progression and the sourced chain
below refer to the same numerical assignment and the same canonical
data.

The running couplings and the data at a reference coupling, the sides, the torus measures and the states, the weighted progression, the sourced chain on the least torus and its histories are therefore formed with this one choice, and every statement of this section is made at it; where Thms.~\YMMref{AJ}{673} and~\YMMref{AD}{607} enter, they are read at the radius $\varrho$ and at the choice of the longer list. Among the constants are $B_\sharp>0$, with $\bar B=B_\sharp L/(L-1)$, the powers $M$, $C_L$ of $L$ in the geometric setting of Section~\YMMref{52.7}{432}, $A_0,A_1>0$ and $p_0\in\mathbb N$. The real and source hypotheses are those imposed jointly in Section~\YMMref{82}{665}. A number is \emph{determined by the constants} if it depends on them alone.

For $\ell\in\mathfrak L=\{2L^m:m\in\mathbb N\}$ the torus $T_\ell=\mathbb R^3/\ell\mathbb Z^3$ carries the lattice of spacing $a_K$. The \emph{lattice} $(\ell,K)$, a side with a cutoff, carries the lattices $\mathbb T^{(j)}=a_{K-j}\mathbb Z^3/\ell\mathbb Z^3$ of the levels $0\le j\le K$, of spacing $D_j=a_{K-j}$; the level $0$ is the bare lattice, which in bare units is $\Lambda_N=\mathbb Z^3/N\mathbb Z^3$, $N=\ell L^K$. The \emph{height} $i$ is the averaging step from the level $i$ to the level $i+1$. Blocks, the bonds of the coarser lattices and the non-pivot bonds are those of Section~\YMMref{4}{16} and the pivot definition preceding Lem.~\YMMref{40.1}{297}, contours those of Section~\YMMref{4}{16} (coordinate-order contours), and $\mathcal M$ is the block-averaging map (equations~\YMMref{(37)--(39)}{20}).

For a plaquette $p$, $a_p(U)=1-\frac12\operatorname{tr}\partial U(p)$ and $x(p)$ is its barycentre; $A=\sum_pa_p$, $\mu_{K,\ell,\beta}(dU)=Z^{-1}e^{-\beta A(U)}dU$, $\mathcal O(f)=a_K^{-1}\sum_pf(x(p))a_p$, for a complex function $w$ on the bare plaquettes, a \emph{source}, $\mathcal O(w)=a_K^{-1}\sum_pw(p)a_p$, so that $\mathcal O(f)=\mathcal O(f\circ x)$, and $S^T_{2;K,\ell,\beta}(f,h)$ is the covariance of $\mathcal O(f)$ and $\mathcal O(h)$ under $\mu_{K,\ell,\beta}$. The lattice isometries preserve $\mu_{K,\ell,\beta}$ and carry $\mathcal O(f)$ to $\mathcal O$ of the carried function ({\cite[Lem.~G.1]{YMM2}}: plaquette holonomies are conjugated or inverted, and the positive-bond variables are permuted or inverted under product Haar measure); so $S^T_{2;K,\ell,\beta}(\tau_vf,\tau_vh)=S^T_{2;K,\ell,\beta}(f,h)$ for every $v\in a_K\mathbb Z^3$ and all real Lipschitz $f,h$, whatever their supports, $\tau_v$ being the translation by $v$.

For a reference coupling $0<g\le\gamma$ ($\gamma$ the last constant) put $X_g=L(g^{-2}+B_\sharp)$, $b_+=L(g^{-2}+\bar B)$ and $I(g)=(g^{-2}+\bar B,X_g-\bar B]$. The sides at $g$ form $\mathfrak L(g)=\{2L^m:m\ge m_{\mathfrak L}(g)\}$ (equation~\YMMref{(1528)}{615}), with least member $\ell_g$; so $\ell_gL^s\in\mathfrak L(g)$ for every integer $s\ge0$. A \emph{datum} at $g$ is a first-passage datum $(K,\beta)$ at $g$ (Cor.~\YMMref{74.2}{616}): its running couplings $x_0=\beta>x_1>\dots>x_K$ obey $x_{j+1}=L^{-1}x_j-e_{j+1}$ with $|e_{j+1}|\le B_\sharp$, and $K$ is the least index with $x_K\le X_g$; its label is $b=a_K\beta$. The running couplings depend on $(K,\beta)$ alone.

Every label at $g$ lies in $[g^{-2},b_+]$ \YMMref{(1531)}{615}, and for $b\in I(g)$ the pair $(K,L^Kb)$ is a datum at $g$ for every $K\in\mathbb N$ (Cor.~\YMMref{74.2}{616}). The \emph{witness depth} is $s(d)=\min\{s\ge0:L^sd\ge C_W(s)\}$, $C_W(s)=C_{W,0}A_0^2(\log[L^{s+1}(g^{-2}+\bar B)])^{2p_0}$, $C_{W,0}=\max\{1,4L^2M/A_0^2\}$, as in equation~\YMMref{(2321)}{843} and Thm.~\YMMref{AV}{851}; it depends on $g$, $d$ and the constants, and on no cutoff, label or side. As $C_W(s)\ge4L^2M$, for $d\le L^{-1}$ and $K>s(d)$ one has $L^{s(d)}\ge4L^3M$, $s(d)\ge2$, $K\ge3$ and $a_K\le L^{-1-s(d)}<d/13$; moreover $L^{s(d)}\ge1/d$, so $C_W(s(d))\ge(\log\frac1d)^2$ and $d/a_K\ge LC_W(s(d))\ge L(\log\frac1d)^2$.

Finally $\gamma^{\rm sd}_W\le\gamma^{\rm ref}_W\le\gamma$ are the coupling thresholds of the choices in equations~\YMMref{(2326)--(2327)}{845}; $(\gamma^{\rm sd}_W)^{-2}\ge4\bar B$.

For $\vartheta\in(0,1)$, $d>0$, and $\mathbb E=\mathbb R^3$ or $\mathbb E=T_\ell$ with $20d\le\ell$, $\mathfrak T_{\mathbb E}(d;\vartheta)$ is the following class of test pairs: Lipschitz functions $f,h\ge0$ on $\mathbb E$, neither $0$, with supports in closed balls of radius $d$ at a distance in $[d,6d]$, $\int f\ge\vartheta\|f\|_\infty d^3$, $\operatorname{Lip}f\le\|f\|_\infty/(\vartheta d)$, and the same for $h$. Then both supports lie in one ball of radius $5d$, and $d\le|x-y|\le10d$ for $x\in\operatorname{supp}f$, $y\in\operatorname{supp}h$. The conditions involve distances alone. So the class is invariant under translations; and for $36d<\ell$ the periodisation of a pair of $\mathfrak T_{\mathbb R^3}(d;\vartheta)$ is a pair of $\mathfrak T_{T_\ell}(d;\vartheta)$ with the same sup norms and the same kernels $\mathcal K_q$ below, every pair of $\mathfrak T_{T_\ell}(d;\vartheta)$ being the periodisation of one such pair, its \emph{lift}, since all the distances that occur are at most $10d<\ell/2$.

For two sides $\ell\le\breve\ell$, the \emph{pair with the same lift} as a pair $(f,h)$ on $T_\ell$ is the periodisation on $T_{\breve\ell}$ of the lift of $(f,h)$.

We put $\eta=\|f\|_\infty\|h\|_\infty$, $\mathcal K_q(f,h)=\iint f(x)h(y)|x-y|^{-q}\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y$, $\varkappa=c_1c_2=\frac3{2\pi^3}$ and $L_b^+=c_2b^{-2}[\mathcal K_6+c_1b^{-1}\mathcal K_5]$. On $\mathbb Z^3$, $\mathsf B_1^{\rm lat}(p,q)$ is the coefficient of $\beta^{-3}$ in the covariance of $a_p$ and $a_q$ (Def.~\textup{\ref{IV-73-22}}), and $\mathsf P_1^{\rm lat}(f,h;a)=a\sum_{p,q}f(ax(p))h(ax(q))\mathsf B^{\rm lat}_1(p,q)$. There are a pure number $C_{\rm T}$ and a constant $\kappa^{\rm lat}$ with
\[
|\mathsf P_1^{\rm lat}(f,h;a)-\kappa^{\rm lat}\mathcal K_5(f,h)|\le C_{\rm T}\vartheta^{-1}a\lg(d/a)\,\eta\qquad\bigl((f,h)\in\mathfrak T_{\mathbb R^3}(d;\vartheta),\ 0<a\le d\bigr),
\]
$\lg t=1+|\log t|$ (Cor.~\textup{\ref{IV-73-73}}), and $\kappa^{\rm lat}=\frac3{2\pi^3}=c_1c_2$ (Thms.~\textup{\ref{IV-73-98}}, \textup{\ref{IV-73-100}}). For real Lipschitz $f,h$ on $T_\ell$, $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$, with disjoint supports and $b\in\overline{I(g)}$, $S_2^{(\ell,b)}(f,h)=\lim_{K\to\infty}S^T_{2;K,\ell,L^Kb}(f,h)$ is the limit of Thm.~\YMMref{A}{5}. That theorem gives existence for every $b>0$, continuity in $b$ on $(0,\infty)$, and bilinearity on real Lipschitz functions supported in two fixed disjoint closed sets. A function on $\mathbb R^3$ with support in a ball of radius $<\ell/4$ is read on $T_\ell$ by periodisation, and $f_\rho:=f(\cdot/\rho)$.

\begin{lemma}[Kernel bounds for test pairs]\label{lem:test-pair-kernels}
For $(f,h)\in\mathfrak T_{\mathbb E}(d;\vartheta)$ and $q>0$,
\[
 10^{-q}\vartheta^2d^{6-q}\|f\|_\infty\|h\|_\infty
 \le\mathcal K_q(f,h)
 \le(4\pi/3)^2d^{6-q}\|f\|_\infty\|h\|_\infty.
\]
Moreover $d\le\mathcal K_5(f,h)/\mathcal K_6(f,h)\le10d$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
All cross-distances of the two supports lie between $d$ and
$10d$. Positivity gives
\[
 (10d)^{-q}\int f\int h
 \le\mathcal K_q(f,h)\le d^{-q}\int f\int h.
\]
The defining mass bounds give the lower estimate, and the
volumes of the two radius-$d$ balls give the upper estimate.
On a torus the balls have the same volumes because $20d\le\ell$.
Finally $|x-y|^{-5}=|x-y|\,|x-y|^{-6}$ on the product of the
supports; integration gives the ratio bound. Its denominator
is positive by the lower estimate.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}\label{C-350-2}
Let $N_3$ be the threefold convolution of $\mathbf 1_{[-1/2,1/2)}$, $\Phi(x)=\prod_{\mu=1}^3N_3(x_\mu)$, $\zeta=1$ on $[0,7]$, $\zeta(t)=1-3(t-7)^2+2(t-7)^3$ on $[7,8]$, $\zeta=0$ on $[8,\infty)$, $P(y)=|y|^2-\frac34$ and $\Xi(y)=P(y)\zeta(|y|)$. For odd $q\ge1$ let $J_q=\{-\frac{q-1}2,\dots,\frac{q-1}2\}$, $c^q_j=\prod_{\mu}q^{-2}\#\{\iota\in J_q^3:\iota_1+\iota_2+\iota_3=j_\mu\}$ for $j\in\mathbb Z^3$, and
\[
\Upsilon^{(q)}(y)=q^{-1}\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z^3}c^q_j\,\Xi\bigl((y+j)/q\bigr)-\Xi(y).
\]
With $e(u)=\int\Phi(x)\Xi(x+u)\,\mathrm{d}x$ let $\mathsf k_6=\int_0^\infty\bigl(4\pi-t^{-2}\int_{S^2}e(t\omega)\,\mathrm{d}\omega\bigr)t^{-2}\,\mathrm{d}t$.
\end{definition}

\subsubsection{The scale of the remainder}

The two terms in the covariance have different homogeneities. For
a test pair of scale $d$, the kernel $|x-y|^{-6}$ integrates to a
quantity of order one, while $|x-y|^{-5}$ integrates to a quantity
of order $d$. Thus the leading contribution is of size $b^{-2}$
and its first correction is of size $b^{-3}d$. To identify that
correction, an error merely tending to zero relative to the leading
term is inadequate. The error must be $o(b^{-3}d)$ after the mesh
error has been separated.

The nonnegativity and mass bounds in the test-pair definition give
\begin{equation}\label{supp-exp:two-term-kernel-floors}
 10^{-q}\vartheta^2d^{6-q}|f|_\infty|h|_\infty
 \le\mathcal K_q(f,h)
 \le(4\pi/3)^2d^{6-q}|f|_\infty|h|_\infty.
\end{equation}
These floors do more than normalize the functions. They show that
the second term is detected by every pair in the class, and they
permit division by $\mathcal K_5$ when recovering its coefficient.
The lattice comparison retains the Lipschitz bound, which measures
the error from replacing an integral by samples at plaquette
barycentres. These sampling errors and the interacting remainder
are kept as separate terms in \cref{C-350-3}.

The coefficient calculation later in the section is finite
dimensional. Its remainder depends on the box. The present
renormalization argument supplies the estimates needed to use that
coefficient in an interacting continuum limit. This distinction
determines the order of the comparison: begin with the actual
covariance, express it through the sourced progression, and only
then compare the coefficient of that progression with a lattice
Laplace coefficient.

\subsubsection{The even expansion and its two retained orders}

Let $\mathsf n_j$ be the mixed derivative in the two sources of
the local normalizing energy at level $j$, summed over its domains.
Its sum is $\mathsf J_2$. A packing of translated pairs gives
\[
 \left|S_2^T(f,h)
       -\frac1{\#\mathsf{Pk}}\sum_{v\in\mathsf{Pk}}
                          \mathsf J_2(\tau_vf,\tau_vh)\right|
 \le C(g)\vartheta^{-1}d^2b^{-2}|f|_\infty|h|_\infty.
\]
The covariance is unchanged by the lattice translations. The
packing therefore allows the contributions left by the
conditioning procedure to be averaged while keeping the original
quantity. In the units $b^{-3}d|f|_\infty|h|_\infty$, its cost
is $C(g)\vartheta^{-1}bd$, which tends to zero at fixed admitted
labels.

Multiply every fluctuation field by one complex parameter
$\lambda$ and move the quadratic coefficients of the action by
\[
 \xi_j(\lambda)=L^{-j}\beta
                      +\lambda^2(x_j-L^{-j}\beta).
\]
Write $\mathsf J_2(\lambda)$ for the deformed sum, so that
$\mathsf J_2=\mathsf J_2(1)$, and put
$\mathsf h_r=[\lambda^r]\mathsf J_2(\lambda)$ for $r=4,6$.
This deformation preserves the identities relating the steps.
The simultaneous analyticity domains in \cref{C-350-7} justify
using the same parameter at every height. The jets are even
holomorphic functions of $\lambda$, and their constant and
quadratic coefficients vanish. At the quadratic order the possible
term is a covariance of linear colour forms at the identity;
invariance under constant gauge rotations makes those linear forms
zero. Cauchy's estimate then gives
\begin{equation}\label{supp-exp:two-term-even-remainder}
 |\mathsf J_2-\mathsf h_4-\mathsf h_6|
 \le Cb^{-4}d^2\bigl(\max\{1,\log(2b/d)\}\bigr)^{8p_0}
                         |f|_\infty|h|_\infty.
\end{equation}
The orders four and six are the leading covariance and its first
correction. The power $d^2$ in the remaining orders makes
\eqref{supp-exp:two-term-even-remainder} small on the scale required
for identifying the second term.

The order-four tower is compared with the free curvature template.
Its covariance is a sum of nested curvature projections, so the
telescoping slice identity identifies the free kernel. The supplied
estimate retains the error from the truncated Gaussian boxes, the
coarsest background and the lattice-to-integral comparison. In
particular the order-four error is bounded by
$C(g)b^{-3}d^{3/2}+C_{\rm lat}b^{-2}a_K/d$, multiplied by the two
suprema. The slowest part of the eventual continuum error comes
from this comparison.

For the sixth order, let $\mathsf h_6^{(n)}$ be the sum of the
sixth-order coefficients through level $n$, and stop at a level with
spacing $D_n\ge d$. The tail estimate is
\[
 |\mathsf h_6-\mathsf h_6^{(n)}|
  \le Cb^{-3}d\bigl(\max\{1,\log(2b/d)\}\bigr)^{6p_0}
            (d/D_n)^{3/2}|f|_\infty|h|_\infty.
\]
This is the freedom used to compare finite objects while keeping
the discarded coarse levels below the second-term scale.

\subsubsection{The comparison of the sixth-order coefficient}

The composed block-field chart puts all earlier fluctuation fields
on the fibre where the coarsest block field is the identity. At
real field scale its exact density contains the Wilson action,
the gauge-fixing terms and the chart Jacobian. The run equation
gives the identity
\begin{equation}\label{supp-exp:two-term-counterterm-cancellation}
 \lambda^{-2}\xi_j(\lambda)L^j+\sum_{i\le j}L^ie_i
                            =\lambda^{-2}\beta.
\end{equation}
Thus the intermediate counterterms disappear from the total phase.
The field changes between matched charts are triangular colour
rotations. They preserve Lebesgue measure and the Euclidean balls
used for the fluctuation cutoffs. Consequently the sixth-order
coefficient agrees exactly with the second Laplace coefficient in
that chart, apart from the separately bounded removal of the
Gaussian boxes. Coordinate cubes in the colour components would
not be preserved by this change; the shape of the boxes enters the
argument here.

Set $\mathsf H^{(n)}=\beta^3a_K^2\mathsf h_6^{(n)}$ and let
$\mathsf T[N,n]$ be the coefficient on a bare torus of $N$ sites
per direction, with the $n$-fold block constraint. The same
$\mathsf T[N,n]$ can be reached from different running couplings,
because \eqref{supp-exp:two-term-counterterm-cancellation} leaves
no dependence on that run. Let $D$ be the original datum on a bare
torus of side $N_0$, and let $D^{\prime}$ be the comparison datum
on an enlarged bare torus of side $N^{\prime}$. The truncation
depths $n_0,n_1$ are chosen with the geometric and error inequalities
of the detailed comparison below. In the case requiring the enlarged
torus, the comparison is:
\begin{align}
 \mathsf H^{(K)}[D]&\longrightarrow\mathsf H^{(n_0)}[D]
  \longrightarrow\mathsf T[N_0,n_0]
  \longrightarrow\mathsf T[N',n_0]
  \longrightarrow\mathsf H^{(n_0)}[D']\notag\\
 &\longrightarrow\mathsf H^{(n_1)}[D']
  \longrightarrow\mathsf T[N',n_1]
  \longrightarrow\mathsf T^{\rm lat}
  \longrightarrow a_K^{-1}\kappa^{\rm lat}\mathcal K_5.
 \label{supp-exp:two-term-comparison-chain}
\end{align}
Each kind of comparison addresses a different obstruction. The
first and fifth arrows discard coarse tails using the preceding
estimate. Passing between $\mathsf H$ and $\mathsf T$ removes
Gaussian boxes; their precisions have a uniform positive lower
bound, so the error is an exponential in minus the squared
cutoff radius, times the stated polynomial in the finite size.
The change of bare torus uses locality of the chart and connected
Wick pairings. A pairing reaching the remote part must contain a
long line, whose exponential bound pays for the polynomial count.
The lattice anchor removes the remaining block constraint, and
the last arrow replaces the infinite-lattice kernel by its
homogeneous part of degree $-5$. The numerical value of $c_1$
enters only at this last arrow.

The choices of $K',n_0,n_1$ in the proof make all these costs small
in the common units $r|f|_\infty|h|_\infty$, where $r=d/a_K$.
Their dependence is displayed because it is what permits the
box-removal exponential to beat its finite-size polynomial. An
unqualified passage from finite-box perturbation theory to the
continuum covariance would omit this comparison.

\subsubsection{Removing the cutoff window and accumulating scales}

The initial expansion holds in a window $L^K\le d^{-P}$. For a
fixed label, \cref{C-350-16} supplies a cutoff $K_\sharp(d)$
inside that window and a bound for every finer cutoff by the
quantity at $K_\sharp(d)$. Its error is $O(d^{178})$ with the
stated shape factor. Apply the expansion at that one cutoff,
then compare all larger cutoffs with it. The full-sequence limit
follows from the already supplied cutoff comparison. This
procedure removes the window without exchanging a short-distance
limit with an uncontrolled finite-box expansion. The separate
same-datum comparisons pass the result to other sides and states,
and the conditioned-state limits pass it to the canonical
components with their common label.

There is also a reason to retain the improved error, beyond
identification of $c_1$. The spline identity in \cref{C-350-29}
writes the logarithmic observable as a sum of differences at
scales $\varrho_k=L^{-k}r_0$. After subtracting the two explicit
kernels, the $k$th term is bounded by a constant times
$\varrho_k^{1/2}b^{-3}$. These bounds are summable. They give the
uniform limit of $\Delta_n$ and its geometric tail. A tolerance
only tending to zero, without a summable rate, would not justify
that accumulation over all scales.

\subsubsection{The quantitative two-term law}

\begin{theorem}\label{C-350-3}
There is $\gamma_{\rm e}\in(0,\frac12]$, determined by the constants, with the following property. Let $0<g\le\gamma_{\rm e}$, $\vartheta\in(0,1)$, $\ell=\ell_g$, $P\ge P_\sharp:=3601$, and put $C_{\rm lat}=\frac32C_{\rm tm}\vartheta^{-1}$ and $C^\flat_{\rm lat}=\frac92C_{\rm tm}\vartheta^{-1}+1$, where $C_{\rm tm}$, determined by the constants, is the constant of the template sums of test pairs (Prop.~\YMMref{121.2}{824} and Lem.~\ref{lem:ward-fluctuation-template}). There are $d_{\rm e}>0$, $c_{1/2}<\infty$, $c_{\rm r}<\infty$ and a non-decreasing $\bar\varepsilon:(0,d_{\rm e}]\to[0,\infty)$ with $\bar\varepsilon(d)\to0$ as $d\to0$, depending on $g$, $\vartheta$, $P$ and the constants, and on no cutoff, label, pair or position, such that for $0<d\le d_{\rm e}$ and $(f,h)\in\mathfrak T_{T_\ell}(d;\vartheta)$ the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] At every datum $(K,\beta)$ at $g$ with $s(d)<K$ and $L^K\le d^{-P}$, with $b=a_K\beta$,
\begin{equation}\label{C-350-4}
|S^T_{2;K,\ell,\beta}-L_b^+|(f,h)\le\bigl[\bar\varepsilon(d)\,b^{-3}d+C_{\rm lat}\,b^{-2}a_K/d\bigr]\eta .
\end{equation}
\item[(b)] For every $b\in I(g)$, \eqref{C-350-4} holds at $(K,L^Kb)$ for every $K>s(d)$, and $|S_2^{(\ell,b)}-L_b^+|(f,h)\le\min\{\bar\varepsilon(d),c_{1/2}d^{1/2}\}\,b^{-3}d\,\eta$.
\item[(c)] If moreover $g\le L^{-1/4}\min\{\gamma_{\rm e},\gamma^{\rm sd}_W\}$, there are $d'_{\rm e}>0$ and $\bar\varepsilon'$ with $\bar\varepsilon'(d)\to0$, depending on $g$, $\vartheta$, $P$, the radius $\varrho$ and the choice of the longer list of which the constants are the restriction, and on no cutoff, label, pair or position, such that \eqref{C-350-4}, with $\bar\varepsilon'$ in the place of $\bar\varepsilon$, holds for $0<d\le d'_{\rm e}$, $(f,h)\in\mathfrak T_{T_\ell}(d;\vartheta)$ and every datum $(K,\beta)$ at $g$ with $K>s(d)$.
\item[(d)] Let $k_0\in\mathbb Z$ with $44L^{-k_0}<\ell_g$, $r_0=L^{-k_0}$, and for $n\ge1$ let $r_1=L^{-n}r_0$ and
\[
\Delta_n(b)=r_1^{-1}S_2^{(\ell,b)}\bigl(\Phi_{r_1},\Upsilon^{(L^n)}_{r_1}\bigr)-c_2b^{-2}\mathsf k_6\,(r_1^{-1}-r_0^{-1})-\frac6{\pi^2}\,b^{-3}\log\frac{r_0}{r_1}
\]
(the pair has disjoint supports, so that the limit is defined at it). Then $\Delta_n$ converges uniformly on $I(g)$ to a bounded continuous function $\Delta_\infty$, and there are $C_{\rm co}<\infty$ and $n_{\rm co}\in\mathbb N$, depending on $g$, $k_0$ and the constants, with $\sup_{I(g)}|\Delta_n|\le C_{\rm co}$ for all $n\ge1$ and $\sup_{I(g)}|\Delta_n-\Delta_\infty|\le C_{\rm co}L^{-n/2}$ for $n\ge n_{\rm co}$.
\item[(e)] For every $b\in I(g)$ and every $K>s(d)$,
\begin{equation}\label{C-350-30}
|S^T_{2;K,\ell,L^Kb}-L_b^+|(f,h)\le\bigl[c_{\rm r}\,b^{-3}d^{3/2}+C^\flat_{\rm lat}\,b^{-2}a_K/d\bigr]\eta ;
\end{equation}
and \eqref{C-350-30}, with $\beta$ for $L^Kb$, holds at every datum $(K,\beta)$ at $g$ with $s(d)<K\le K_\sharp(d)$ and $b=a_K\beta$, where $K_\sharp(d)$ is the cutoff of Prop.~\ref{C-350-16} at the side $\ell_g$.
\item[(f)] Under the assumptions of (c) there are $d''_{\rm e}>0$ and $c'_{\rm r}<\infty$, depending on $g$, $\vartheta$, the radius $\varrho$ and the choice of the longer list of which the constants are the restriction, and on no $P$, which enters them as $P_\sharp$, and no cutoff, label, pair or position, such that \eqref{C-350-30}, with $c'_{\rm r}$ for $c_{\rm r}$ and $\beta$ for $L^Kb$, holds for $0<d\le d''_{\rm e}$, $(f,h)\in\mathfrak T_{T_\ell}(d;\vartheta)$ and every datum $(K,\beta)$ at $g$ with $K>s(d)$, $b=a_K\beta$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

As $|x-y|\le10d$ on the supports, $\mathcal K_5(f,h)\ge(10d)^{-5}\int f\int h\ge10^{-5}\vartheta^2d\,\eta$ by the nonnegativity and integral floors in {\cite[Lem.~I.1]{YMM2}}. So clause (b) determines the number:
\[
\Bigl|\frac{(S_2^{(\ell,b)}-c_2b^{-2}\mathcal K_6)(f,h)}{c_2b^{-3}\mathcal K_5(f,h)}-\frac8{3\pi}\Bigr|\le10^5c_2^{-1}\vartheta^{-2}\min\{\bar\varepsilon(d),c_{1/2}d^{1/2}\}.
\]
The continuum limit on $T_{\ell_g}$ at a label of $I(g)$ determines first the label, since 
\[
S_2^{(\ell,b)}(f,h)/(c_2\mathcal K_6(f,h))\to b^{-2}
\]
 along pairs of the class with $d\to0$, and then the number $\frac8{3\pi}$. The number enters the proof at one place, the last link of the chain of Step~3 below, through $\kappa^{\rm lat}=c_1c_2$; it depends on no $L$, $g$, side or label.

\begin{corollary}[Every state; every side; the limits on $\mathbb R^3$]\label{C-350-28}
Let $g$, $\vartheta$ and $P$ be as in clause (c) of Thm.~\ref{C-350-3}, with $d'_{\rm e},\bar\varepsilon'$ of (c) and $d''_{\rm e},c'_{\rm r}$ of (f); let $C^{\rm T}_2(g)$ and $\mathsf d_\star(g,\vartheta)$ be the numbers of Prop.~\ref{C-350-21}, and put
\[
d_\infty=\min\bigl\{d'_{\rm e},d''_{\rm e},\tfrac1{180},\mathsf d_\star(g,\vartheta),L^{-1}\bigr\},\qquad\bar\varepsilon_\infty(d)=\min\{\bar\varepsilon'(d),c'_{\rm r}d^{1/2}\}+C^{\rm T}_2(g)\vartheta^{-1}b_+d .
\]
The numbers $d_\infty$ and $\bar\varepsilon_\infty(d)$ depend on $g$, $\vartheta$, $P$, the radius $\varrho$ and the choice of the longer list of which the constants are the restriction, and on no cutoff, label, side, state, sequence, component, pair or position. Let $0<d\le d_\infty$ and $(\tilde f,\tilde h)\in\mathfrak T_{\mathbb R^3}(d;\vartheta)$, with $\eta=\|\tilde f\|_\infty\|\tilde h\|_\infty$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] For every state $\mathfrak s$ at $g$ at a datum $(K,\beta)$ at $g$ with $K>s(d)$ (Prop.~\ref{C-350-21}), $b=a_K\beta$:
\[
|S^T_2[\mathfrak s]-L_b^+|(\tilde f,\tilde h)\le\bigl[(\bar\varepsilon'(d)+C^{\rm T}_2(g)\vartheta^{-1}b_+d)\,b^{-3}d+C_{\rm lat}b^{-2}a_K/d\bigr]\eta,
\]
and the same with $c'_{\rm r}d^{1/2}$ in the place of $\bar\varepsilon'(d)$ and $C^\flat_{\rm lat}$ in the place of $C_{\rm lat}$. In particular this holds for the torus measure of every side of $\mathfrak L(g)$ at the periodisations of the pair, and for every periodic Gibbs state at $(a_K,\beta)$.
\item[(ii)] For every side $\ell'\in\mathfrak L(g)$, every $b\in I(g)$ and every $(f,h)\in\mathfrak T_{T_{\ell'}}(d;\vartheta)$: $|S_2^{(\ell',b)}-L_b^+|(f,h)\le\bar\varepsilon_\infty(d)\,b^{-3}d\,\eta$.
\item[(iii)] Let $\mathfrak s_j$ be states at $g$ at data $(K_j,\beta_j)$ at $g$ with $K_j\to\infty$ and labels $b_j=a_{K_j}\beta_j\to b$; the torus measures of sides $\ell_j\in\mathfrak L(g)$ that grow with $j$ are among them. Then $b\in[g^{-2},b_+]$, and every limit point $S$ of the sequence $S^T_2[\mathfrak s_j](\tilde f,\tilde h)$ satisfies $|S-L_b^+(\tilde f,\tilde h)|\le\bar\varepsilon_\infty(d)\,b^{-3}d\,\eta$. The labels are determined by the two-point functions: if $\mathfrak s_j$ are states at $g$ at data $(K_j,\beta_j)$ at $g$ with $K_j\to\infty$, and $S^T_2[\mathfrak s_j](F)$ converges at every pair $F$ of a set that holds, for arbitrarily small $d\in(0,d_\infty]$, a pair of $\mathfrak T_{\mathbb R^3}(d;\vartheta)$, then the labels $a_{K_j}\beta_j$ converge, to a number $b\in[g^{-2},b_+]$.

Consequently the labels of every convergent Gibbs sequence at $g$ (a sequence $(K_j,\beta_j,\nu_j)$ of data at $g$ with $K_j\to\infty$ and periodic Gibbs states $\nu_j$ at $(a_{K_j},\beta_j)$) converge, to a number $b$; and the connected two-point function $S^\sigma_2$ of the action density of its limit $\sigma$, and that of every component of a canonical decomposition of $\sigma$, satisfy $|S_2^\sigma-L_b^+|(\tilde f,\tilde h)\le\bar\varepsilon_\infty(d)\,b^{-3}d\,\eta$ whenever $\tilde f$ and $\tilde h$ are of class $C^1$. Such a pair is a separated tuple, at which these functionals are defined, and $\mathfrak T_{\mathbb R^3}(d;\vartheta)$ holds pairs of class $C^1$ for every $d>0$ and $\vartheta\in(0,1)$.

Every volume-first limit at $g$ has one label $b$, the same along all its defining sequences, and the same inequality holds for it and for its ergodic components ({\cite[\S{}K.1]{YMM2}} and Def.~\ref{C-365-5}(2)) at the pairs of $\mathfrak T_{\mathbb R^3}(d;\vartheta)$ of class $C^1$. Every $b\in I(g)$ is the label of such limits.
\item[(iv)] In the cases (ii) and (iii), with $S$ the two-point function in question at a pair at which (ii) or (iii) states the inequality, $|(S-c_2b^{-2}\mathcal K_6)/(c_2b^{-3}\mathcal K_5)-\frac8{3\pi}|\le10^5c_2^{-1}\vartheta^{-2}\bar\varepsilon_\infty(d)$: one number $\frac8{3\pi}$ holds for all the limits on the tori of the sides at $g$, the limits of states at $g$ and their components, and each of these limits determines its label and the number. In the case (i), at a state at a finite cutoff, the same quotient differs from $\frac8{3\pi}$ by at most $10^5c_2^{-1}\vartheta^{-2}\bigl[\bar\varepsilon'(d)+C^{\rm T}_2(g)\vartheta^{-1}b_+d+C_{\rm lat}\,b\,a_K/d^2\bigr]$, and by at most the same with $c'_{\rm r}d^{1/2}$ in the place of $\bar\varepsilon'(d)$ and $C^\flat_{\rm lat}$ in the place of $C_{\rm lat}$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}

\subsubsection{Renormalisation and coefficient inputs}

Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8} stands behind all the statements on the renormalisation group that we use, and Thms.~\YMMref{AJ}{673} and~\YMMref{AD}{607} behind the existence of the limit on a torus, the rate of the cutoffs and the agreement of states, into which it enters through the bounds on the partition functions of the tori at the source $0$. We use the following construction results: the flow of the coupling and its data (Section~\YMMref{74}{614}, \YMMref{74}{614}, \S\ref{sec:complex-field-scale}, Prop.~\ref{prop:source-entry}, equation~\YMMref{(1528)}{615}, \YMMref{74.2}{616}, Section~\YMMref{82}{665}, Prop.~\YMMref{74.1}{615}, Cor.~\YMMref{74.2}{616}, the ordered real choice in Prop.~\YMMref{69.1}{595} and the common source choice of Section~\YMMref{82}{665}, the coupling-sequence quantities in equation~\YMMref{(634)}{339} and the function $R$ of equation~\YMMref{(634)}{339}); \subsubsection{Source-energy jets and the field-scale expansion}

\emph{Notation.} Throughout, $D=(K,\beta)$ is a datum at $g$ with label $b$, $\ell=2L^m\in\mathfrak L(g)$, and $f,h$ are real bounded functions on $T_\ell$; $w_1=f\circ x$ and $w_2=h\circ x$ are the lattice sources on the bare plaquettes. We write $N=\ell L^K$, $\mathsf N=N+\beta$, $r=d/a_K$, $l=\max\{1,\log(2b/d)\}$, $\mathfrak b(x)=A_1(\log x)^{p_0}$, $\delta(x)=\mathfrak b(x)x^{-1/2}$ and $\langle z\rangle=\max\{1,|z|\}$. With $E^{(j)}_\mu$ the local terms of the level $j$ of the weighted progression ({\cite[eq.~200]{YMM2}}) at the datum, with the weight $\mu_1w_1+\mu_2w_2$ of the plaquettes, and $\mathcal D_j$ its domains of the level $j$, the second jet of the level $j$ is
\[
\mathsf n_j=\sum_{X\in\mathcal D_j}\ \sum_{z\in X\cap\mathbb T^{(j)}}\partial_{\mu_1}\partial_{\mu_2}E^{(j)}_\mu(X,\mathbf 1,z)\big|_{\mu=0},\qquad\mathsf J_2=\sum_{j=1}^K\mathsf n_j .
\]
The same construction at a complex field scale $\lambda$ (every fluctuation field multiplied by $\lambda$, the coefficient of the action at the height $j$ moved to $\xi_j(\lambda)=L^{-j}x_0+\lambda^2(x_j-L^{-j}x_0)$) gives the local terms $E^{(j),\lambda}_\mu$ of the level $j$ at the field scale $\lambda$, with $E^{(j),1}_\mu=E^{(j)}_\mu$, and their second jets $\mathsf n^\lambda_j=\sum_{X\in\mathcal D_j}\sum_{z\in X\cap\mathbb T^{(j)}}\partial_{\mu_1}\partial_{\mu_2}E^{(j),\lambda}_\mu(X,\mathbf 1,z)|_{\mu=0}=\sum_{m\ge0}\mathsf n_{j,[2m]}\lambda^{2m}$ (Prop.~\ref{C-350-7}); $\mathsf h^{(n)}_{2m}=\sum_{j\le n}\mathsf n_{j,[2m]}$, $\mathsf h_{2m}=\mathsf h^{(K)}_{2m}$, and $\mathsf H^{(n)}[D]=\beta^3a_K^2\mathsf h^{(n)}_6$. As $\beta^{-3}a_K^{-2}=b^{-3}a_K$ and $a_Kr=d$, a size $r\eta$ of $\mathsf H$ is a size $b^{-3}d\eta$ of $\mathsf h_6$. Where the side matters we write $\mathsf J_2[\ell]$, $\mathsf h_6[\ell]$, $\mathsf H^{(n)}[D,\ell]$.

\emph{The free template} (Section~\YMMref{120}{817}) is the free abelian model of the curvature: cochains, plaquette averages and nested projections. At the height $0\le i<K$, $\mathsf A^{\rm cv}_i=\mathsf B^{\rm cv}_i+\hat{\mathsf G}$ is its one-step quadratic form, a sum of two real symmetric matrices $\ge0$ on the non-pivot bonds of $\mathbb T^{(i)}$, and $\mathsf A^{\rm cv}_i\ge\gamma^{\rm tr}$ with a lower bound $\gamma^{\rm tr}>0$ (Prop.~\YMMref{120.3}{819}); $\mathsf T_i$ is its curvature map onto the bare plaquettes (Prop.~\YMMref{120.3}{819}). $\Pi^{\rm tp}_0$ is the orthogonal projection onto the exact bare curvatures and $\Pi^{\rm tp}_n$, $n\ge1$, the projection onto those that the plaquette averages of the level $n$ determine, so that $\Pi^{\rm tp}_0-\Pi^{\rm tp}_n$ is the orthogonal projection onto the curvatures whose plaquette averages of the level $n$ vanish; $\mathcal C_{(j)}=\Pi^{\rm tp}_{j-1}-\Pi^{\rm tp}_j$ are the curvature slices, and $C^{\rm fl}_{K,K-n}=\Pi^{\rm tp}_0-\Pi^{\rm tp}_n=\sum_{1\le j\le n}\mathcal C_{(j)}$ is the fluctuation kernel, the conditional covariance of the free lattice curvature given its plaquette averages of the level $n$; on a lattice with $t$ levels we write $\Pi^{\rm fl}_t=\Pi^{\rm tp}_0-\Pi^{\rm tp}_t$.

The numbers $\delta_{\rm tp}\in(0,\frac1{12}]$ and $C_{\rm tp}\ge1$ of the decay of the slices (Props.~\YMMref{120.5}{821} and~\YMMref{120.6}{821}), and the number $C^{\rm row}_{\rm tp}$ of the row sums of the curvature maps,
\[
\sum_b|\mathsf T_i(p,b)|\le C^{\rm row}_{\rm tp}L^{-2i}\qquad\text{for every bare plaquette }p,
\]
uniformly in the volume, at the height $i=0$ and at every height at which the side $\ell L^{K-i}$ of the level $i$, in its units, is at least $N_{\mathsf H}$, so at every height if $\ell\ge N_{\mathsf H}$ (Prop.~\YMMref{120.6}{821}), depend on $L$ and on the least admissible side $N_{\mathsf H}$ fixed with $C_{\mathsf H}$ and $\delta_{\mathsf H}$ in Section~\YMMref{52.6}{426} and the beginning of Section~\YMMref{120.3}{820}; they, $\gamma^{\rm tr}$ and $N_{\mathsf H}$ are determined by the constants.

\emph{The Gaussian measures of the heights.} Put $\tau_i=L^{-i}x_0/x_i$ and $\mathsf M_i=\tau_i\mathsf B^{\rm cv}_i+\hat{\mathsf G}$. $\nu^\circ_i$ is the centred Gaussian measure with the precision $\mathsf M_i\otimes1$ on the real $\mathfrak g$-valued $1$-forms $B_i$ on the non-pivot bonds of $\mathbb T^{(i)}$, and $\nu^{\rm r}_i$ is $\nu^\circ_i$ conditioned on the box $\{|B_i(b)|<\mathfrak b(x_i)\ \forall b\}$, $|\cdot|$ being the Euclidean norm of $\mathfrak g\cong\mathbb R^3$: the boxes are products of Euclidean balls. As $\tau_i\in[\frac34,\frac43]$ (Prop.~\ref{C-350-6}) and both matrices are $\ge0$, $\mathsf M_i\ge\min\{\tau_i,1\}\mathsf A^{\rm cv}_i\ge\frac34\gamma^{\rm tr}$, so every variance in $\nu^\circ_i$ is at most $\frac4{3\gamma^{\rm tr}}$.

The measures $\nu^\circ_i$ are tied to the steps by Lem.~\ref{C-350-23}(iii): at $\lambda=0$, at the trivial configuration, the density of the step of the height $i$ is proportional to $\exp[-\frac12(B_i,(\mathsf M_i\otimes1)B_i)]$ on the box of the height, the height $0$ included, where $\tau_0=1$ and $\mathsf M_0=\mathsf A^{\rm cv}_0$. For polynomials $X_{a,m}$ ($a=1,2$, $m=0,1,2$), $W_1$, $W_2$ in these fields and a probability measure $\nu$, with the joint cumulants $\langle\cdot;\dots;\cdot\rangle$ taken in $\nu$,
\begin{align}
\gamma_2[\nu]={}&\langle X_{1,2};X_{2,0}\rangle+\langle X_{1,0};X_{2,2}\rangle+\langle X_{1,1};X_{2,1}\rangle-\langle X_{1,1};X_{2,0};W_1\rangle\nonumber\\
&-\langle X_{1,0};X_{2,1};W_1\rangle-\langle X_{1,0};X_{2,0};W_2\rangle+\tfrac12\langle X_{1,0};X_{2,0};W_1^2\rangle ;\label{C-350-5}
\end{align}
$\gamma^{\rm r}_2=\gamma_2[\bigotimes_{0\le i<n}\nu^{\rm r}_i]$ and $\gamma^\circ_2=\gamma_2[\bigotimes_{0\le i<n}\nu^\circ_i]$, with the polynomials of Prop.~\ref{C-350-11}. If $\nu$ is invariant under $B\mapsto-B$, the $X_{a,0}$ are even and $W_1$ is odd, then $\frac12\langle X_{1,0};X_{2,0};W_1^2\rangle=\frac12\langle X_{1,0};X_{2,0};W_1;W_1\rangle$: a cumulant with a product entry is $\langle X;Y;W^2\rangle=\langle X;Y;W;W\rangle+2\langle X;W\rangle\langle Y;W\rangle+2\langle W\rangle\langle X;Y;W\rangle$, and the last two terms vanish by parity.

\emph{Laplace's method} (Lem.~\textup{\ref{IV-73-26}}). Let $\phi,\psi,X,Y$ be real and smooth near $0\in\mathbb R^m$, $\phi(0)=0$, $\nabla\phi(0)=0$, with a positive definite Hessian $H$ at $0$, and let $X$, $Y$ vanish at $0$ with their gradients. Let $\phi_j,\psi_j,X'_j,Y'_j$ be their homogeneous Taylor polynomials of order $j$ at $0$, and $W_j=\phi_{j+2}+\psi_j$, $X_{1,j}=X'_{j+2}$, $X_{2,j}=Y'_{j+2}$. Then the covariance of $X$ and $Y$ under the density proportional to $e^{-\beta\phi-\psi}$ on a small window about $0$ is
\begin{equation}\label{C-350-31}
\beta^{-2}\gamma^{\rm L}_0+\beta^{-3}\gamma^{\rm L}_2+O(\beta^{-4})\qquad(\beta\to\infty),
\end{equation}
where $\gamma^{\rm L}_0=\langle X_{1,0};X_{2,0}\rangle$ and $\gamma^{\rm L}_2$ is \eqref{C-350-5}, both in the centred Gaussian measure of covariance $H^{-1}$. In the variable $\beta^{1/2}x$ the density is the Gaussian one times $e^{-\beta^{-1/2}W_1-\beta^{-1}W_2-\dots}$ and the observables are $\beta^{-1}(X_{a,0}+\beta^{-1/2}X_{a,1}+\beta^{-1}X_{a,2}+\dots)$; the coefficient of $\beta^{-3}$ of the covariance, expanded in joint cumulants, is \eqref{C-350-5}, written with the parity just noted, and the half-integer orders vanish by parity. We write $\gamma^{\rm L}_{m'}[\phi,\psi,X,Y]$, $m'=0,2$. The numbers $\mathsf g_{m'}[N,t](p,q)$ of a flat top are set in Prop.~\ref{C-350-12}; for functions $w_1,w_2$ on the plaquettes of $\Lambda_N$, $\mathsf T[N,t](w)=\sum_{p,q}w_1(p)w_2(q)\mathsf g_2[N,t](p,q)$, and for functions $\tilde w_1,\tilde w_2$ of finite support on the plaquettes of $\mathbb Z^3$, $\mathsf T^{\rm lat}(\tilde w)=\sum\tilde w_1(\tilde p)\tilde w_2(\tilde q)\mathsf B_1^{\rm lat}(\tilde p,\tilde q)$.

If $\tilde w_1(\tilde p)=\tilde f(a_Kx(\tilde p))$, $\tilde w_2(\tilde p)=\tilde h(a_Kx(\tilde p))$, then $a_K\mathsf T^{\rm lat}(\tilde w)=\mathsf P_1^{\rm lat}(\tilde f,\tilde h;a_K)$.

\begin{proposition}[The setting of the expansion]\label{C-350-6}
There is $\gamma_{\rm s}\in(0,\min\{\gamma^{\rm ref}_W,\frac12\}]$, determined by the constants, such that for $0<g\le\gamma_{\rm s}$, every datum $(K,\beta)$ at $g$ with $K\ge3$, every $\ell=2L^m\in\mathfrak L(g)$, and real bounded $f,h$ with supports in balls of radius $d$ at a distance $\ge d$, $8a_K\le d$, at every position of $(f,h)$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $2L^{m+K-j+1}\ge C_LM$ for $1\le j\le K$, in particular $\ell L\ge C_LM$; and $\ell\ge N_{\mathsf H}$;
\item[(ii)] $x_0>x_1>\dots>x_K>g^{-2}$, $x_{K-1}>Lg^{-2}\ge4L$, and for $0\le j<K$: $\frac34b/D_j\le x_j\le2b/D_j$ and $\frac34\le\tau_j\le\frac43$;
\item[(iii)] at every level $j<K$ the constants, the lattice of the step $j\to j+1$ and $x_j$ are data under (Im) of {\cite[Def.~B.2]{YMM2}};
\item[(iv)] the data of the weighted progression ({\cite[Def.~B.7]{YMM2}}) are given with $k=K-1$, the sources $w_1,w_2$ and the running couplings as thresholds; the setting (J) of {\cite[Def.~B.16]{YMM2}} holds at $k=K-1$; $\log x_{K-1}\ge\max\{2p_0,1+\log L\}$; and $\delta(x_{K-1})$ lies below the threshold of the chain classes (equations~\YMMref{(2285)}{833} and~\eqref{eq:weighted-tower-smallness}) and below the smallness that Prop.~\ref{C-350-7} asks of its discs.
\end{enumerate}
No condition is put on the witness depth, on the signs or on the Lipschitz constants of $f$ and $h$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(i) For a side at $g$ the lattice of a datum is large at every level, by the flow of the coupling (Section~\YMMref{74}{614}, \YMMref{74}{614}) and Lem.~\YMMref{126.2}{845}; at $j=K$ this is $\ell L\ge C_LM$. The condition on $N_{\mathsf H}$ and its two companion numbers is a member of the collective condition, which holds at the fixed constants and under which the geometric hypotheses of Section~\YMMref{52.7}{432} hold; it is a condition on these three numbers, and no side occurs in it. The bound $\ell\ge N_{\mathsf H}$ is a property of the sides at $g$: for $\ell=2L^m\in\mathfrak L(g)$ the flow of the coupling gives $LM\,R(x_K)\le L^m$ (Prop.~\YMMref{74.1}{615}; $R$ is the function of equation~\YMMref{(634)}{339}), so $M\,R(x_K)\le L^m$, and with this Lem.~\YMMref{126.2}{845} gives $\ell\ge N_{\mathsf H}$, together with the frames of the datum on $T_\ell$; the setting (J) at $k=K-1$ follows in (iv).

(ii) The run equation gives $|x_j-L^{-j}x_0|\le B_\sharp\sum_{i\ge0}L^{-i}=\bar B$, and $L^{-j}x_0=b/D_j$. As $K$ is the first passage, $x_j\ge x_{K-1}>X_g\ge Lg^{-2}$ for $j<K$, and $x_K=L^{-1}x_{K-1}-e_K>g^{-2}$; $\gamma_{\rm s}$ is so small that $X_g\ge12\bar B$. Hence $|\tau_j-1|\le\bar B/x_j\le\frac1{12}$, and $\frac{12}{13}b/D_j\le x_j\le b/D_j+\bar B\le2b/D_j$. (iii), (iv) $\gamma_{\rm s}\le\gamma^{\rm ref}_W$ is the least of two thresholds determined by the constants. For $g\le\gamma_{\rm s}$, {\cite[Cor.~B.9]{YMM2}}, {\cite[Prop.~B.21]{YMM2}} and Lem.~\YMMref{126.2}{845} give the data of the progression and the setting (J) at $k=K-1$; in that setting, at every level, the constants, the lattice of the step and $x_j$ are data under (Im), so that in particular the ratio $A_0/A_1$ lies above the number that (Im) asks.

As $x_{K-1}>L\gamma_{\rm s}^{-2}$ and $\delta$ decreases for large arguments, $\delta(x_{K-1})\le\delta(L\gamma_{\rm s}^{-2})$, which lies below both thresholds for $\gamma_{\rm s}$ small, and $\log x_{K-1}\ge\log(L\gamma_{\rm s}^{-2})\ge\max\{2p_0,1+\log L\}$. The sources enter through their supports alone.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[One field scale]\label{C-350-7}
Under the assumptions of Prop.~\ref{C-350-6} the progression is formed at one complex field scale for all its steps. There are $R_j>1$ ($0\le j<K$) with $R_j^{-2}\le c_0(\log x_j)^{2p_0}D_j/b$, and $\rho\in(0,\frac12]$ with $(\rho R_j)^2\ge2$, such that, with $c_0,\rho,C_{\mathsf n},C_{\rm E},C_{{\rm E},m},C_{\rm R},C_{\rm J}$ determined by the constants (they depend on no cutoff, side, run, scale, position or pair), the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $\lambda\mapsto\mathsf n^\lambda_{j+1}$ is holomorphic and even on $|\lambda|<R_j$, $\mathsf n^1_{j+1}=\mathsf n_{j+1}$, its Taylor coefficients $\mathsf n_{j+1,[0]}$, $\mathsf n_{j+1,[2]}$ of the orders $0$ and $2$ vanish, and for $|\lambda|\le\rho R_j$
\[
\begin{multlined}
|\mathsf n^\lambda_{j+1}|\le C_{\mathsf n}|\lambda|^2R_j^{-2}D_j^{-2}\min\{1,(d/D_j)^{5/2}\}\,\Pi_{j+1}\,\eta,\qquad\Pi_{j+1}=\max\{1, \\
(d/D_{j+1})^3\}e^{-[d/(4MD_{j+1})-2]_+}.
\end{multlined}
\]
\item[(ii)] $|\mathsf J_2-\mathsf h_4-\mathsf h_6|\le C_{\rm E}b^{-4}d^2l^{8p_0}\eta$ and $|\mathsf h_{2m}|\le C_{{\rm E},m}b^{-m}d^{m-2}l^{2mp_0}\eta$ for $m=2,3$.
\item[(iii)] For $0\le n\le K-1$ with $D_n\ge d$ and $m=2,3$: 
\[
\sum_{j=n}^{K-1}|\mathsf n_{j+1,[2m]}|\le C_{\rm R}b^{-m}l^{2mp_0}d^{m-2}(d/D_n)^{\frac52-(m-2)}\eta
.\]
In particular, for $n\le n'\le K$ with $L^n\ge r$: $|\mathsf H^{(n')}[D]-\mathsf H^{(n)}[D]|\le C_{\rm R}l^{6p_0}(r/L^n)^{3/2}r\,\eta$.
\item[(iv)] Let $\dot E^{(i+1),\lambda}_a=\partial_{\mu_a}E^{(i+1),\lambda}_\mu|_{\mu=0}$ ($a=1,2$) and $\ddot E^{(i+1),\lambda}=\partial_{\mu_1}\partial_{\mu_2}E^{(i+1),\lambda}_\mu|_{\mu=0}$ be the first and the second jets of the level $i+1$ at the field scale $\lambda$, pointed families of the level $i+1$, and let $\psi_i=\min\{1,(d/D_i)^3\}$, $\chi_i=\min\{1,(d/D_i)^{5/2}\}$. At every $\lambda$ at which they are formed, the member of $\dot E^{(i+1),\lambda}_a$ on a domain $X$ vanishes unless $X$ holds a plaquette of the support of $w_a$, and the member of $\ddot E^{(i+1),\lambda}$ on $X$ vanishes unless $X$ holds a plaquette of each of the two supports. For $0\le i\le j<K$ and $|\lambda|\le\rho R_j$, their sizes \YMMref{(759)}{375} at the rate $\kappa^+=(1+4\beta_{\rm s})\kappa$, at which the parts of the local terms that depend on the sources decay in the linear size of the domain (Prop.~\YMMref{122.1}{826}), obey
\[
\|\dot E^{(i+1),\lambda}_a\|_{i+1,\kappa^+}\le C_{\rm J}|\lambda|^2R_i^{-2}D_i^{-1}\psi_i\|w_a\|_\infty,\qquad\|\ddot E^{(i+1),\lambda}\|_{i+1,\kappa^+}\le C_{\rm J}|\lambda|^2R_i^{-2}D_i^{-2}\chi_i\,\eta .
\]
\end{enumerate}
If $w_a$ vanishes identically, all the jets in the direction $w_a$ vanish; so (i)--(iii) hold trivially if $w_1$ or $w_2$ vanishes, and so do the bounds of (iv) that involve a vanishing source.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
One step at a complex field scale is Prop.~\ref{IV-71-37}, applied with a parameter set (Def.~\ref{IV-71-26}) that holds the field scales of the earlier steps; the scale is put on the diagonal afterwards. A lower calibration $\mathsf t_\flat$, fixed with the constants, gives room for the size of the deformed bare array, the bound of the step being uniform in the parameter. The counterterms $e_i$ are kept, and the coefficient of the action is moved along $\xi_j(\lambda)$, which stays in the admitted disc about $x_j$ for $|\lambda|<R_j:=\delta(\mathsf t_\flat)/(2\delta(x_j))$, because $|\xi_j(\lambda)-x_j|=|\lambda^2-1|\,|x_j-L^{-j}x_0|<2R_j^2\bar B$. To make the last bound smaller than $\sigma_*x_j$, decrease $\gamma_{\rm s}$, if necessary, so that
\[
 \bar B\delta(\mathsf t_\flat)^2
       <2\sigma_*A_1^2(\log x_j)^{2p_0}
\]
for every coupling of the run. This is possible by the lower bound on $x_j$ in Prop.~\ref{C-350-6}; substitution of the formula for $R_j$ gives $2R_j^2\bar B<\sigma_*x_j$. Thus the simultaneous substitution in the field scale and the quadratic coefficient stays within the product domain of Prop.~\ref{IV-71-37}.

By Prop.~\ref{C-350-6}(ii), $R_j^{-2}=4\delta(x_j)^2/\delta(\mathsf t_\flat)^2\le\frac{16}3A_1^2\delta(\mathsf t_\flat)^{-2}(\log x_j)^{2p_0}D_j/b$. Induction over the heights gives the holomorphy, the evenness, $\mathsf n^1_{j+1}=\mathsf n_{j+1}$ and the locality in the weight of (iv): the member of the level $i+1$ on a domain $X$ is formed from the members of the lower levels on the domains in $X$ and from the weight on the plaquettes of $X$, at every field scale as at the field scale $1$ (Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{122.1}{826}}(c)). The derivatives in the weights obey two linear recursions over the levels, by the chain rule and Cauchy's estimate in the direction of the bare array: one step at the field scale $\lambda$ multiplies the size of the derivative in the direction of a bare array by at most $c\,|\lambda|^2R_i^{-2}$ (clauses (cx3), (cx8) of Prop.~\ref{IV-71-37}, uniformly in the parameter), and the weight member of the level $i$ in the direction $w_a$ has the size at most $36M^3\alpha_0^2D_i^{-1}\psi_i\|w_a\|_\infty$, its source meeting at most $35(d/a_K)^3$ plaquettes; so the first derivatives follow the profile $\psi_i=\min\{1,(d/D_i)^3\}$, the second the profile $\chi_i=\min\{1,(d/D_i)^{5/2}\}$.

They close on these profiles for $|\lambda|\le\rho R_j$ by the locality in the weight, the bare array of a source with support of diameter $\le2d$ meeting at most $77\max\{1,(d/D_i)^3\}$ cubes of the level $i$, the cubes of side $MD_i$ of the partition $\pi_i$ of the torus whose wall-connected unions are the domains of the level $i$ (the level-$i$ localization partition of Section~\YMMref{45}{351}); $\rho$ is fixed by the two inequalities that close the induction, and the closed recursions are the two bounds of (iv). A domain that meets both supports holds two points at a distance at least $d/4$, so that its linear size in the units of its level is at least $[d/(4MD_{j+1})-2]_+$; with the count of such domains this gives the display of (i).

At the order $2$ the earlier members are taken at the field scale $0$, where they do not depend on the sources, and the coefficient is a covariance of two linear forms $\ell_Y$ of the field at the trivial configuration. A constant gauge rotation $u$ fixes the trivial configuration, so $\ell_Y(\operatorname{Ad}(u)B)=\ell_Y(B)$, and $\int_G\operatorname{Ad}(u)Y\,\mathrm{d}u=0$ for $Y\in\mathfrak g$ gives $\ell_Y=0$.

(ii), (iii): an even holomorphic $H$ with $|H|\le\mathsf B$ on $|\lambda|<R$ has $|H_{[2m]}|\le\mathsf BR^{-2m}$ and $|H(1)-\sum_{m\le p}H_{[2m]}|\le\mathsf BR^{-2p-2}/(1-R^{-2})$. Applied on $|\lambda|<\rho R_j$, where $(\rho R_j)^2\ge2$, with the bound of (i), each level gives at most $c\,b^{-m}(\log x_j)^{2mp_0}D_j^{m-2}\chi_j\Pi_{j+1}\eta$ at the order $2m$, and $m=4$ for the remainder. The levels with $D_j\ge d$ have $\Pi_{j+1}=1$, $\log x_j\le l$ and $D_j^{m-2}\chi_j=d^{m-2}(d/D_j)^{\frac52-(m-2)}$: a geometric series over the levels. The other levels are summed against $\Pi_{j+1}$, which is summable against every power of the logarithm. For (iii) at $m=3$: $\mathsf h^{(n')}_6-\mathsf h^{(n)}_6=\sum_{n\le j<n'}\mathsf n_{j+1,[6]}$, $D_n\ge d$ if and only if $L^n\ge r$, $d/D_n=r/L^n$ and $\beta^3a_K^2b^{-3}d=r$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The front on the least torus]\label{C-350-8}
There are $\gamma_{\rm C}>0$, determined by the constants, and for $0<g\le\gamma_{\rm C}$ numbers $d_{\rm A}(g)>0$ and $C_{\rm A}(g)<\infty$, depending on $g$ and the constants and on no $K$, $\beta$, $b$, $\vartheta$, $d$, pair or position, such that for every datum $(K,\beta)$ at $g$, $\ell=\ell_g$, $0<d\le d_{\rm A}(g)$ with $s(d)\le K$, $\vartheta\in(0,1)$ and $(f,h)\in\mathfrak T_{T_\ell}(d;\vartheta)$: $K\ge3$ and $a_K\le d$; the set
\[
\mathsf{Pk}=\bigl\{v\in\delta\mathbb Z^3:\ |v_\mu|\le0.575-9d\ (\mu=1,2,3)\bigr\},\qquad\delta=a_K\lceil18d/a_K\rceil,
\]
which lies in $a_K\mathbb Z^3$ and depends on $a_K$ and $d$ alone, consists of vectors of length $<1$, has $\#\mathsf{Pk}\ge(30d)^{-3}$, and $(\tau_vf,\tau_vh)\in\mathfrak T_{T_\ell}(d;\vartheta)$ for $v\in\mathsf{Pk}$; and
\[
\Bigl|S^T_{2;K,\ell,\beta}(f,h)-\frac1{\#\mathsf{Pk}}\sum_{v\in\mathsf{Pk}}\mathsf J_2(\tau_vf,\tau_vh)\Bigr|\le C_{\rm A}(g)\vartheta^{-1}d^2b^{-2}\eta .
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Decrease $\gamma_{\rm C}\le\gamma_{\rm s}$ to satisfy the
source and radius conditions of \S\ref{sec:levelwise-first-creation}.
These are conditions on the fixed constants and on the lower
coupling threshold. Choose $d_{\rm A}(g)$ small enough for
the packing and amplitude bounds below.

If $f\circ x=0$, every lattice translate of this bare
weight is zero. Both the covariance and its source-energy
mixed derivative therefore vanish; the assertion follows.
The same applies to $h\circ x$. Henceforth neither is zero.
Choose $x_1$ with $\operatorname{supp}f\subset\mathbb B(x_1,d)$.
Both supports lie in $\mathbb B(x_1,9d)$. The balls
$\mathbb B(x_1+v,9d)$, $v\in\mathsf{Pk}$, have disjoint
interiors, since $\delta\ge18d$, and lie in
$\mathbb B(x_1,1)$. Indeed,
$|v|\le\sqrt3(0.575-9d)$ and
$\sqrt3(0.575-9d)+9d<1$.
The condition $s(d)\le K$ gives
$L^Kd\ge C_W(s(d))\ge4L^2M$, so $a_K\le d$;
for $d$ small it also gives $K\ge3$.
Now $\delta\le18d+a_K\le19d$. Thus, for $d$ small,
\[
 \#\mathsf{Pk}=
  \left(2\left\lfloor\frac{0.575-9d}{\delta}\right\rfloor+1\right)^3
  \ge(30d)^{-3}.
\]
The translates preserve the support separation, amplitude
and Lipschitz conditions defining the test class.

Use the norm \eqref{eq:levelwise-source-norm} and the
holomorphic total source energy $\mathcal E$ of
Prop.~\ref{prop:levelwise-source-density}.
Lem.~\ref{lem:packed-levelwise-source} bounds a disjoint
sum $w=(\sum_\iota\zeta_\iota u_\iota)\circ x$ by
\[
 \|w\|_{\rm lw}\le
   \max_\iota|\zeta_\iota|\mathsf A_\iota/\mathsf A_\star(d),
 \qquad
 \mathsf A_\star(d)=\min\left\{\sigma_{\rm src}b^\vee,
   \frac{\mu_\star}{K_{\rm L}^\vee}
   \frac{b^\vee}{(b^\wedge)^{1/2}}
       \left(\frac{\vartheta d}{4\sqrt3M}\right)^{1/2}\right\},
\]
where $\|u_\iota\|_\infty\le\mathsf A_\iota$,
$\operatorname{Lip}u_\iota\le\mathsf A_\iota/(\vartheta d)$,
$b^\vee=g^{-2}-\bar B$ and $b^\wedge=b_+$.
The total-energy identity in
Prop.~\ref{prop:levelwise-source-density} shows that
$\mathsf J_2$ is the mixed derivative of $\mathcal E$ at
zero. Therefore $S^T_2-\mathsf J_2$ is the mixed derivative
of $\log(Z[\cdot]/Z[0])-\mathcal E$.

For signs $\epsilon\in\{\pm1\}^{\mathsf{Pk}}$ put
\[
 F^\epsilon=\sum_v\epsilon_v\tau_vf,\qquad
 H^\epsilon=\sum_v\epsilon_v\tau_vh,\qquad
 w_z=(z_1F^\epsilon+z_2H^\epsilon)\circ x,
 \qquad
 \Omega_\epsilon(z)=Z[w_z]e^{-\mathcal E(w_z)}/Z[0].
\]
The nonzero sets of the individual bumps are pairwise
disjoint. With $u_1=\|f\|_\infty/\mathsf A_\star(d)$ and
$u_2=\|h\|_\infty/\mathsf A_\star(d)$, the amplitude bound
gives $\|w_z\|_{\rm lw}\le\max_a|z_a|u_a$.
Thus $\Omega_\epsilon$ is holomorphic on
$\mathbb P=\{|z_1|u_1<1,\ |z_2|u_2<1\}$ and
$\Omega_\epsilon(0)=1$.

Split the sourced partition by its first large-field
creation, using \eqref{eq:first-creation-split}:
\[
 \Omega_\epsilon=\Omega_\epsilon^\emptyset
                  +\sum_{t=1}^K\Omega_\epsilon^t,\qquad
 \Omega_\epsilon^\emptyset=
        e^{-\mathcal E(w_z)}m_K^{w_z}(\mathcal V_K)/Z[0],
 \qquad
 \Omega_\epsilon^t=
        e^{-\mathcal E(w_z)}\mathsf{Cr}_t(w_z)/Z[0].
\]
Every source here is supported in the one ball
$\mathbb B(x_1,1)$. Prop.~\ref{prop:first-creation-envelopes}
therefore gives
\[
 |\Omega_\epsilon^\emptyset|\le e^{\mathsf G_K}
       \quad\hbox{on }\mathbb P,\qquad
 |\Omega_\epsilon^t|\le
 e^{\|w_z\|_{\rm lw}(\mathsf G_{t-1}+\mathsf H_{t-1})}\mathsf w_t.
\]
Choose $\mathsf C_{\rm cnt}=C_{\rm cnt}(g)\ge1$ in
\eqref{eq:first-creation-count}, and set
$\mathsf{Cnt}_t=\mathsf C_{\rm cnt}L^{4(K-t+1)}$.
On $\mathbb P_t=\{|z_a|u_a\mathsf{Cnt}_t<1, a=1,2\}$
the second bound is at most $e\mathsf w_t$.
For $\emptyset\ne B\subset\{1,2\}$ write
$[z^B]\Omega=(\prod_{a\in B}\partial_{z_a})\Omega(0)$ and
$u^B=\prod_{a\in B}u_a$. Cauchy's formula on these polydiscs
gives
\[
 |[z^B]\Omega_\epsilon^\emptyset|\le e^{\mathsf G_K}u^B,
 \qquad
 |[z^B]\Omega_\epsilon^t|
    \le e\mathsf w_t\mathsf{Cnt}_t^{|B|}u^B
    \le e(\mathsf C_{\rm cnt}L^4)^2
                         L^{8(K-t)}\mathsf w_tu^B.
\]
By \eqref{eq:first-creation-rarity}, the latter coefficients
sum to at most $e(\mathsf C_{\rm cnt}L^4)^2C_8(g)u^B$.
Choose $\mathsf Q(g)\ge1$ above this coefficient bound plus
$e^{\sup\mathsf G_K}$. It is finite and independent of
the datum, the positions and the signs. Thus
\[
 |[z^B]\Omega_\epsilon|\le\mathsf Q(g)u^B,
 \qquad
 |\partial_{12}\log\Omega_\epsilon(0)|
 \le(\mathsf Q+\mathsf Q^2)u_1u_2
 \le2\mathsf Q^2\mathsf A_\star(d)^{-2}\eta.
\]
The logarithm is needed only near zero, where
$\Omega_\epsilon(0)=1$ ensures its existence.

By bilinearity the last mixed derivative is
\[
 \sum_{v,v'}\epsilon_v\epsilon_{v'}
       (S^T_2-\mathsf J_2)(\tau_vf,\tau_{v'}h).
\]
Average over the independent signs. The terms $v\ne v'$
vanish and the diagonal terms remain. Translation
invariance of $S^T_2$ and the packing count then give
\[
 \left|S^T_2(f,h)-\frac1{\#\mathsf{Pk}}
                   \sum_v\mathsf J_2(\tau_vf,\tau_vh)\right|
 \le(30d)^3\,2\mathsf Q^2\mathsf A_\star(d)^{-2}\eta.
\]
For $d\le4\sqrt3Mg^{-2}(K_{\rm L}^\vee/K_{\rm Q}^\vee)^2$
the second entry in the minimum defining $\mathsf A_\star$
is the smaller one. Substitution bounds the last expression
by $C(g)\vartheta^{-1}d^2\eta$. Since the label satisfies
$b\le b_+$, enlarging this fixed-$g$ constant by $b_+^2$
gives the asserted $C_{\rm A}(g)\vartheta^{-1}d^2b^{-2}\eta$.
The finitely many ceilings on $d$ determine $d_{\rm A}(g)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The order four]\label{C-350-9}
Let $0<g\le\gamma_{\rm s}$, $(K,\beta)$ a datum at $g$, $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$, $0<d\le L^{-1}$, $s(d)<K$, $20d\le\ell$, $\vartheta\in(0,1)$ and $(f,h)\in\mathfrak T_{T_\ell}(d;\vartheta)$, at any position. Then $K\ge3$, $8a_K\le d$, $d/a_K\ge L(\log\frac1d)^2$, and
\[
|\mathsf h_4-c_2b^{-2}\mathcal K_6|(f,h)\le\bigl[\bar\varepsilon_4(g,d)\,b^{-3}d+C_{\rm lat}\,b^{-2}a_K/d\bigr]\eta,
\]
where, with $l'=\max\{1,\log\frac{2b'}d\}$,
\[
\bar\varepsilon_4(g,d)=\sup_{g^{-2}<b'\le b_+}\frac{b'}d\Bigl\{3C_{\rm tm}d^3+C_{\rm Bx}\bigl[d^{3/2}+e^{-\mathsf c_\chi(\log\frac{3b'}{4d^{1/2}})^2}\bigr]+C_{\rm Bt}\,l'^{\,4p_0}e^{-\mathsf c_\flat L(\log\frac1d)^2}\Bigr\},
\]
$C_{\rm Bx},C_{\rm Bt},\mathsf c_\chi>0$ being determined by the constants and $\mathsf c_\flat=\min\{\frac1{8ML},\frac{\delta_{\rm tp}}{2\sqrt3}\}$. The function $\bar\varepsilon_4(g,\cdot)$ depends on $g$ and the constants alone and is the same for all sides and data at $g$; and $\bar\varepsilon_4(g,d)\le C_4(g)d^{1/2}$, with $C_4(g)$ depending on $g$ and the constants.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The first three assertions are those of the setting on the witness depth. Let $2\le n\le K$ with $D_n\ge d$.

(1)

\emph{The tower at a real field scale.} Let $0<\lambda\le1$, $g_i=x_i^{-1/2}$, and let $c_{\mathfrak h}$ be the constant of the shift systems of the steps. The chain of the levels at the field scale $\lambda$ is formed downwards from the flat top of the level $n$: $A^\lambda_n:=0$ and, for $i=n-1,\dots,1$,
\[
A^\lambda_i:=A^{\rm lw}\bigl(v^{[i+1]}_{A^\lambda_{i+1}},\lambda g_iB_i\bigr),\qquad\tilde U^\lambda_i:=e^{iL^{-i}A^\lambda_i},
\]
with the lowered $1$-form $A^{\rm lw}$ of equation~\YMMref{(2286)}{833} and the chart point $v^{[i+1]}_A$ of a chain class (equation~\eqref{eq:weighted-chain-class}). A \emph{chart point} of a level $k$ is a pair $v=(A,\mathbf J)$ of $1$-forms on the bare bonds; $P[v]=(\mathbf 1,A,\mathbf J)$ is its triple in the chart at the trivial pair (Section~\YMMref{124}{832}), and $P[0]$ is the trivial triple; its norm $\|v\|$ is the largest of the numbers $|A(b)|$, $|\mathbf J(b)|$ over the bare bonds $b$ and of the moduli of the difference quotients of $A$ at the spacing $L^{-k}$; and $\mathsf{Cc}_k(r)$ is the chain class of the level $k$ and the radius $r$. The $A^\lambda_i$ are real $1$-forms on the bare bonds, and $\tilde U^\lambda_i$, a configuration on the bare bonds, is the \emph{background of the level $i$}, as in the proof of Prop.~\ref{C-350-11}(i): up to a gauge transformation it is a background of the level $i$ in the sense of the actual-background condition in \eqref{eq:weighted-chain-class}; $\mathcal O(w_a)$ and the $a_p$ are taken at it.

By Prop.~\YMMref{124.2}{834}, equation~\YMMref{(2288)}{834}, read at the field $\lambda B_i$, which lies in the box, as the box is a product of Euclidean balls, and by the bounds of equation~\YMMref{(2287)}{834} and its domain verification at $\sup|\lambda g_iB_i|\le\lambda\delta(x_i)$, $A^\lambda_i\in\mathsf{Cc}_i(\lambda r_i)$, with $r_n:=0$ and $r_i:=L^{-1}r_{i+1}+\frac{11}{10}c_{\mathfrak h}\delta(x_i)\le\frac85c_{\mathfrak h}\delta(x_i)$; the conditions of that Proposition hold at every height, and $r_1\le\frac12r_\alpha$, $r_\alpha$ being the usable radius of the fixed radii (equations~\YMMref{(933)}{427} and~\YMMref{(2285)}{833}), as $\delta(x_{K-1})$ lies below the threshold of the chain classes (Prop.~\ref{C-350-6}(iv)).

The same Proposition gives $v^{[i]}_{A^\lambda_i}=v^{\rm lw}(v^{[i+1]}_{A^\lambda_{i+1}},\lambda g_iB_i)$, the lowered point of equation~\YMMref{(2286)}{833}; the lowered points are holomorphic (the holomorphy following equation~\YMMref{(2286)}{833}) and obey the bounds of equation~\YMMref{(2287)}{834} and its domain verification at complex points as well, so the same recursion, with the lowered points, continues the chain to the complex field scales $|\lambda|\le1$, where the $A^\lambda_i$ take complex values and the $\tilde U^\lambda_i$ lie in $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb C)$; one name, $\tilde U^\lambda_i$, serves for both. For $\mu\in\mathbb C^2$ near $0$ put $w_\mu=\mu_1w_1+\mu_2w_2$ and
\[
D^{\lambda,\mu}_i=\mathcal O(w_\mu)+\sum_{i'\le i}\mathsf{Sum}\bigl[E^{(i'),\lambda}_\mu-E^{(i'),\lambda}_0\bigr],
\]
$\mathsf{Sum}[\cdot]$ being the sum of a pointed family at a configuration or at a triple (the definitions preceding equation~\YMMref{(2276)}{831}). Each step at a height $1\le i<n$ obeys an identity of its own at the field scale $\lambda$, whose case $\lambda=1$ uses the quotient argument of Prop.~\ref{prop:weighted-pair-tower}: for $r\le r_{i+1}$, $A\in\mathsf{Cc}_{i+1}(r)$, $v=v^{[i+1]}_A$, $\tilde U=e^{iL^{-i-1}A}$ and $\tilde U^{\rm lw}(B)=e^{iL^{-i}A^{\rm lw}(v,\lambda g_iB)}$,
\[
\exp D^{\lambda,\mu}_{i+1}(\tilde U)=\int\exp D^{\lambda,\mu}_i\bigl(\tilde U^{\rm lw}(B)\bigr)\,\mathrm{d}\nu^\lambda_i[v](B).
\]
Here $\nu^\lambda_i[v]$ is the complex measure of mass $1$ on the box of the height $i$ whose density is the integrand of the integral form of the step at the field scale $\lambda$, at the source $0$ and at the triple $P[v]$ (clause (cx10) of Prop.~\ref{IV-71-37}), divided by its integral, which is not $0$: the Gaussian density of the covariance $\tau_i(\lambda)^{-1}\mathbf C_\ast(P[v])$, with $\tau_i(\lambda)=\xi_i(\lambda)/x_i$, positive for real $|\lambda|\le1$, and the whole covariance $\mathbf C_\ast$ of the step, times $\exp[-\frac{1-\tau_i(\lambda)}2\sum_\square(B,\hat{\mathsf G}_\square(P[v]|_\square)B)]$, with the gauge-fixing operators $\hat{\mathsf G}_\square$ of the fine cubes (equation~\YMMref{(823)}{394}), times the exponential of the potentials of the step at the field scale $\lambda$. At complex $\lambda$ this is the holomorphic continuation supplied by the same one-step theorem, with its nonvanishing normalizer; no positivity is asserted there.

The identity is proved as follows. The integral form of the step at the triple $P[v]$, at the source $\mu$ and at the source $0$ (Prop.~\ref{IV-71-37}(cx10), at the data of Prop.~\ref{C-350-7}), and the quotient of the two give
\[
\exp\mathsf{Sum}\bigl[E^{(i+1),\lambda}_\mu-E^{(i+1),\lambda}_0\bigr](P[v])=\int\exp\bigl[\mathbb V'[\mathfrak g]^{\rm tot}(P[v];\lambda B)\bigr]\,\mathrm{d}\nu^\lambda_i[v](B),
\]
because $\mu$ stands in the rule of the step alone and the rule is linear in the bare array, $\mathfrak g$ being the difference of the bare arrays of the height $i$ at $\mu$ and at $0$, whose members are the $E^{(i'),\lambda}_\mu-E^{(i'),\lambda}_0$, $i'\le i$, and the weight member of $w_\mu$. Prop.~\YMMref{124.2}{834}, equation~\YMMref{(2289)}{834}, which holds for every bare array and every field of the box, read at $\lambda B$, in the plaquette form of equation~\YMMref{(2290)}{834} and by linearity, gives $\mathbb V'[\mathfrak g]^{\rm tot}(P[v];\lambda B)=D^{\lambda,\mu}_i(\tilde U^{\rm lw}(B))-D^{\lambda,\mu}_i(\tilde U)$; and the proof of Prop.~\YMMref{124.2}{834} gives $\mathsf{Sum}[\cdot](P[v])=\mathsf{Sum}[\cdot](\tilde U)$ for the family of the level $i+1$. Multiplying by $\exp D^{\lambda,\mu}_i(\tilde U)$ gives the identity. Iterating it from the height $n-1$, where $A=0$ and $\tilde U=\mathbf 1$, down to the height $1$ along the chain, and taking the mixed derivative in $\mu$ at $0$ of the logarithms, gives
\[
\sum_{j=2}^n\mathsf n^\lambda_j=\bigl\langle\mathcal F^\lambda_1(\tilde U^\lambda_1);\mathcal F^\lambda_2(\tilde U^\lambda_1)\bigr\rangle_{\mathbb Q^\lambda_n}+\int\bigl[\mathsf F^\lambda_1(\tilde U^\lambda_1)-\mathsf F^\lambda_1(\mathbf 1)\bigr]d\mathbb Q^\lambda_n,
\]
where $\mathbb Q^\lambda_n(dB)=\prod_{1\le i<n}\nu^\lambda_i\bigl[v^{[i+1]}_{A^\lambda_{i+1}}\bigr](dB_i)$ is a complex measure of mass $1$ on the product of the boxes, with a bounded continuous density, each factor being formed at the chart point that the chain gives above its height; $\mathcal F^\lambda_a=\mathcal O(w_a)+\mathsf{Sum}[\dot E^{(1),\lambda}_a]$ is $\mathcal O(w_a)$ plus the first jet of the level $1$ in the direction $w_a$, and $\mathsf F^\lambda_1=\mathsf{Sum}[\ddot E^{(1),\lambda}]$ is the second jet of the level $1$, with $\mathsf F^\lambda_1(\mathbf 1)=\mathsf n^\lambda_1$ (the jets of Prop.~\ref{C-350-7}(iv)).

(2)

\emph{The limit $\lambda\to0$.} The lattice being fixed, let $\lambda\downarrow0$ in the identity of (1) divided by $\lambda^4$. Its left side tends to $\sum_{j=2}^n\mathsf n_{j,[4]}$, by Prop.~\ref{C-350-7}(i).

\emph{The measures.} The chart points of the chain have $\sup_B\|v^{[i+1]}_{A^\lambda_{i+1}}\|\le\lambda r_{i+1}\to0$, and $\tau_i(\lambda)\to\tau_i(0)=\tau_i$. Two facts tie the step at the trivial configuration to the free template: the whole covariance of the step at the trivial triple is $(\mathsf A^{\rm cv}_i)^{-1}\otimes1$ (equation~\YMMref{(2297)}{836}; Prop.~\YMMref{120.3}{819}); and the gauge-fixing operators of the fine cubes at the trivial triple add up to the gauge-fixing operator at the block field $\mathbf 1$, which is $\hat{\mathsf G}\otimes1$, as the fine cubes partition the sites of the level $i+1$ and the operator of a cube is the gauge-fixing form restricted to the blocks of that cube (equation~\YMMref{(823)}{394}; Prop.~\YMMref{120.3}{819}).

The covariance and the gauge-fixing operators at the triple $P[v]$ tend to these, entry by entry, as $v\to0$ (equation~\YMMref{(2296)}{836}; the kernels of the $\hat{\mathsf G}_\square$ are holomorphic in the chart point), and the potentials at the field scale $\lambda$ are at most $c\lambda$ times a function bounded on the box (\eqref{eq:complex-input-bounds} of Def.~\ref{IV-71-26}). So the density of $\mathbb Q^\lambda_n$ tends, uniformly on the product of the boxes, to the product over the heights of the densities proportional to
\[
e^{-\frac12(B_i,(\tau_i\mathsf A^{\rm cv}_i+(1-\tau_i)\hat{\mathsf G})B_i)}=e^{-\frac12(B_i,\mathsf M_iB_i)} ;
\]
as the boxes have finite volume and the limits of the normalisations are positive, $\mathbb Q^\lambda_n\to\mathbb Q^0_n:=\bigotimes_{1\le i<n}\nu^{\rm r}_i$ in total variation.
