\emph{The plaquette terms.} At every height the linear part of one step of the chain in the field $B_i$, read in the plaquette angle, is $\mathsf{sg}_i(\mathsf T_i\otimes1)$ with a sign $\mathsf{sg}_i\in\{1,-1\}$ (Lem.~\YMMref{124.3}{835}, which reads $\ell\ge N_{\mathsf H}$ of Prop.~\ref{C-350-6}(i); its map $\mathsf T^{\rm cv}_i$ is $\mathsf T_i$, the definitions preceding Lem.~\YMMref{124.3}{835}). With the expansion of the plaquette terms and of the plaquette angles to the second order at one step (Lem.~\YMMref{124.4}{835}), summed along the chain, this gives, uniformly on the boxes and for every bare plaquette $p$,
\[
\bigl|a_p(\tilde U^\lambda_1)-\tfrac12\lambda^2|\Theta_p(B)|^2\bigr|\le c_\Theta\lambda^3,\qquad\Theta_p(B):=\sum_{1\le i<n}\mathsf{sg}_i\,x_i^{-1/2}(\mathsf T_iB_i)(p),
\]
with $c_\Theta$ determined by the constants. Hence $\lambda^{-2}\mathcal O(w_a)(\tilde U^\lambda_1)\to q_a(B):=\frac12a_K^{-1}\sum_pw_a(p)|\Theta_p(B)|^2$ uniformly on the boxes.

\emph{The level $1$.} The local terms of the level $1$ at $\tilde U^\lambda_1$ take the values of their members at the restrictions of the triple $P[v]$, $v=v^{[1]}_{A^\lambda_1}$, as in the proof of Prop.~\YMMref{124.2}{834}. For a pointed family $\mathsf f$ of the level $1$, a domain $X$ of the level $1$, a site $z$ of $X$ and $\kappa'>0$, $d_1(X)$ being the linear size of $X$ in the units of the level $1$,
\[
\bigl|\mathsf f\bigl(X,P[v]|_X,z\bigr)-\mathsf f(X,\mathbf 1,z)\bigr|\le2\|\mathsf f\|_{1,\kappa'}e^{-\kappa'd_1(X)}\lambda^2(r_1/r_\alpha)^2 :
\]
the function $\zeta\mapsto\mathsf f(X,P[\zeta v]|_X,z)$ is holomorphic on $|\zeta|<r_\alpha/\|v\|$, where $r_\alpha/\|v\|\ge r_\alpha/(\lambda r_1)\ge2$, and bounded there by $\|\mathsf f\|_{1,\kappa'}e^{-\kappa'd_1(X)}$; its derivative at $0$ vanishes, because a constant gauge rotation $u$ fixes the trivial configuration and acts on the chart point by $\operatorname{Ad}(u)$, the local terms are invariant, and $\int_G\operatorname{Ad}(u)Y\,\mathrm{d}u=0$ for $Y\in\mathfrak g$; Cauchy's estimate bounds the rest of the series. At $\mathsf f=\dot E^{(1),\lambda}_a$, whose size at the rate $\kappa^+$ is at most $C_{\rm J}\lambda^2R_0^{-2}a_K^{-1}\|w_a\|_\infty$ (Prop.~\ref{C-350-7}(iv) at $i=0$, where $\psi_0=1$), this shows that the first jet of the level $1$ changes along the chain by $O(\lambda^4)$, uniformly on the boxes; as a covariance does not change when constants are added, $\lambda^{-4}\langle\mathcal F^\lambda_1(\tilde U^\lambda_1);\mathcal F^\lambda_2(\tilde U^\lambda_1)\rangle_{\mathbb Q^\lambda_n}\to\langle q_1;q_2\rangle_{\mathbb Q^0_n}$.

At $\mathsf f=\ddot E^{(1),\lambda}$, whose size is at most $C_{\rm J}\lambda^2R_0^{-2}a_K^{-2}\eta$ and whose members vanish on the domains that do not meet both supports (Prop.~\ref{C-350-7}(iv) at $i=0$), the count of the domains of the level $1$ that meet both supports, weighted with $e^{-\kappa^+d_1(X)}$ ({\cite[Lem.~B.10]{YMM2}}), brings the factor $\Pi_1$, as in the proof of Prop.~\ref{C-350-7}(i), and gives
\[
\bigl|\mathsf F^\lambda_1(\tilde U^\lambda_1)-\mathsf F^\lambda_1(\mathbf 1)\bigr|\le\lambda^4\,\mathrm{Er}_\flat,\qquad\mathrm{Er}_\flat=c\,R_0^{-2}a_K^{-2}(r_1/r_\alpha)^2\,\Pi_1\,\eta .
\]
So the limit $\mathsf e_\flat$ of $\lambda^{-4}\int[\mathsf F^\lambda_1(\tilde U^\lambda_1)-\mathsf F^\lambda_1(\mathbf 1)]\,\mathrm{d}\mathbb Q^\lambda_n$ exists, $|\mathsf e_\flat|\le\mathrm{Er}_\flat$, the total variation of $\mathbb Q^\lambda_n$ tending to $1$, and
\[
\sum_{j=2}^n\mathsf n_{j,[4]}=\langle q_1;q_2\rangle_{\mathbb Q^0_n}+\mathsf e_\flat .
\]
The covariance $\langle q_1;q_2\rangle_{\mathbb Q^0_n}$ does not depend on the signs $\mathsf{sg}_i$: every $\nu^{\rm r}_i$ is invariant under $B_i\mapsto-B_i$, its box being symmetric, so that the law of $(\mathsf{sg}_iB_i)_i$ under $\mathbb Q^0_n$ is $\mathbb Q^0_n$. By Prop.~\ref{C-350-7}(i) at $j=0$ and Cauchy's estimate on $|\lambda|=\rho R_0$, $|\mathsf n_{1,[4]}|\le C_{\mathsf n}\rho^{-2}R_0^{-4}a_K^{-2}\Pi_1\eta$. As $x_0=\beta=b/a_K$, $R_0^{-2}\le c_0(\log x_0)^{2p_0}a_K/b$, $r_1\le\frac85c_{\mathfrak h}\delta(x_1)$ and $\delta(x_1)^2\le\frac43A_1^2(\log x_0)^{2p_0}La_K/b$ (Prop.~\ref{C-350-6}(ii)), both $|\mathsf e_\flat|$ and $|\mathsf n_{1,[4]}|$ are at most $c\,b^{-2}(\log\frac b{a_K})^{4p_0}\Pi_1\eta$.

With $u_0=d/a_K\ge8$, $\log\frac b{a_K}\le l\,(1+\log u_0)$ and $\Pi_1\le\max\{1,u_0^3\}e^{2-u_0/(4ML)}$; as $(1+\log u)^{4p_0}\max\{1,u^3\}e^{2-u/(8ML)}$ is bounded on $u\ge8$ and $\mathsf c_\flat\le\frac1{8ML}$, this is below $C\,b^{-2}l^{4p_0}e^{-\mathsf c_\flat d/a_K}\eta$.

(3)

\emph{The boxes out at the order four.} The cumulants of the orders $2$ and $4$ of the components $B^\alpha_i(b)$ in $\nu^{\rm r}_i$ and in $\nu^\circ_i$ differ by at most $C_\chi e^{-\mathsf c_\chi(\log x_i)^{2p_0}}$, uniformly in the volume, with $C_\chi$, $\mathsf c_\chi$ determined by the constants (Lem.~\ref{lem:ward-box-cumulants}, read with the one quadratic system of the height and the threshold $\mathfrak b(x_i)$); the odd cumulants vanish in both measures by the symmetry $B\mapsto-B$, and the Gaussian ones are $\delta_{\alpha\beta}\mathsf M_i^{-1}(b,b')$ at the order $2$ and $0$ at the order $4$.

(4)

\emph{Wick's rule and the slices.} The $B_i$ are independent in $\mathbb Q^0_n$ and each $\nu^{\rm r}_i$ is even. With $F^\alpha_i(p)=\mathsf{sg}_i\,x_i^{-1/2}\sum_b\mathsf T_i(p,b)B^\alpha_i(b)$, so that $|\Theta_p|^2=\sum_\alpha\bigl(\sum_iF^\alpha_i(p)\bigr)^2$ in an orthonormal basis $(t_\alpha)$ of $\mathfrak g$, $c^{\alpha\beta}_i(p,q)=\langle F^\alpha_i(p)F^\beta_i(q)\rangle_{\nu^{\rm r}_i}$ and $\kappa^{\alpha\beta}_i(p,q)$ the joint fourth cumulant of $F^\alpha_i(p),F^\alpha_i(p),F^\beta_i(q),F^\beta_i(q)$,
\[
\langle q_1;q_2\rangle_{\mathbb Q^0_n}=\tfrac14a_K^{-2}\sum_{p,q}w_1(p)w_2(q)\sum_{\alpha,\beta}\Bigl[2\Bigl(\sum_ic^{\alpha\beta}_i(p,q)\Bigr)^2+\sum_i\kappa^{\alpha\beta}_i(p,q)\Bigr].
\]
By the slice identity $\mathsf T_i\mathsf M_i^{-1}\mathsf T_i^{\mathsf T}=L^{-i}\tau_i^{-1}\mathcal C_{(i+1)}$ (Prop.~\YMMref{120.3}{819}, valid at every $\tau_i\ne0$) and
\[
x_i^{-1}L^{-i}\tau_i^{-1}=x_0^{-1},
\]
the running couplings drop out: in the Gaussian measures $c^{\alpha\beta}_i=\delta_{\alpha\beta}x_0^{-1}\mathcal C_{(i+1)}$. As $a_Kx_0=b$, the Gaussian value of $\langle q_1;q_2\rangle$ is $\frac32b^{-2}\sum_{p,q}w_1(p)w_2(q)\Sigma(p,q)^2$ with
\[
\Sigma=\sum_{1\le i<n}\mathcal C_{(i+1)}=C^{\rm fl}_{K,K-n}-\mathcal C_{(1)} .
\]
The differences of (3) are carried to the $F^\alpha_i$ through the row sums of $\mathsf T_i$, which are at most $C^{\rm row}_{\rm tp}L^{-2i}$ at every height, uniformly in the volume, as $\ell\ge N_{\mathsf H}$ (Prop.~\YMMref{120.6}{821}; Prop.~\ref{C-350-6}(i)). By multilinearity, with $\epsilon_i=C_\chi e^{-\mathsf c_\chi(\log x_i)^{2p_0}}$, $\mathsf{sg}_i^2=1$ and $x_i^{-1}L^{-4i}=\tau_ix_0^{-1}L^{-3i}\le\frac43x_0^{-1}L^{-3i}$,
\[
\bigl|c^{\alpha\beta}_i(p,q)-\delta_{\alpha\beta}x_0^{-1}\mathcal C_{(i+1)}(p,q)\bigr|\le\bar e_i:=\tfrac43(C^{\rm row}_{\rm tp})^2x_0^{-1}L^{-3i}\epsilon_i,\qquad|\kappa^{\alpha\beta}_i(p,q)|\le\tfrac{16}9(C^{\rm row}_{\rm tp})^4x_0^{-2}L^{-6i}\epsilon_i .
\]
There are at most $35^2(d/a_K)^6$ pairs $(p,q)$ with $w_1(p)w_2(q)\ne0$, and for them $|x(p)-x(q)|_\infty\ge d/\sqrt3$; with $u_i=d/D_i$ one has $L^{-3i}(d/a_K)^3=u_i^3$, and Prop.~\YMMref{120.6}{821} gives $(d/a_K)^3(|\Sigma|+|\mathcal C_{(1)}|)(p,q)\le C_{\rm tp}S_\Sigma$, $S_\Sigma=\sup_{u>0}\sum_{s\in\mathbb Z}(uL^s)^3e^{-\delta_{\rm tp}uL^s/\sqrt3}$. Expanding the square, with $\mathsf E_k=\sum_{1\le i<n}u_i^k\epsilon_i$ for $k=3,6$,
\[
\begin{multlined}
\Bigl|\langle q_1;q_2\rangle_{\mathbb Q^0_n}-\tfrac32b^{-2}\sum_{p,q}w_1(p)w_2(q)\Sigma(p,q)^2\Bigr|\le\tfrac{35^2}4\,b^{-2}\bigl[16C_{\rm tp}S_\Sigma(C^{\rm row}_{\rm tp})^2\mathsf E_3+32(C^{\rm row}_{\rm tp})^4\mathsf E_3^2 \\
+16(C^{\rm row}_{\rm tp})^4\mathsf E_6\bigr]\eta .
\end{multlined}
\]
The numbers $\mathsf E_k$ are bounded in three ranges of levels. As $\log x_i\ge\log\frac{3b}{4D_i}\ge0$ (Prop.~\ref{C-350-6}(ii), and $\frac34b\ge1\ge D_i$), $\log x_i\ge1$ and $2p_0\ge2$, one has $\epsilon_i\le C_\chi e^{-\mathsf c_\chi(\log\frac{3b}{4D_i})^2}$. At the levels with $D_i<d$, $\log\frac{3b}{4D_i}=\Lambda_b+t_i$ with $\Lambda_b=\log\frac{3b}{4d}\ge\log\frac{3b}{4d^{1/2}}$ and $t_i=\log u_i>0$, the $t_i$ being spaced by $\log L$, and $(\Lambda_b+t)^2\ge\Lambda_b^2+t^2$, so that $u_i^k\epsilon_i\le C_\chi e^{-\mathsf c_\chi\Lambda_b^2}e^{6t_i-\mathsf c_\chi t_i^2}$ for $k\le6$; so these levels give at most $C_\chi S_\chi e^{-\mathsf c_\chi\Lambda_b^2}$, with $S_\chi=\sup_{t_0\ge0}\sum_{s\ge0}e^{6(t_0+s\log L)-\mathsf c_\chi(t_0+s\log L)^2}$. At the levels with $d\le D_i\le d^{1/2}$, $\sum u_i^3\le2$ and $\epsilon_i\le C_\chi e^{-\mathsf c_\chi(\log\frac{3b}{4d^{1/2}})^2}$. At the levels with $D_i>d^{1/2}$, $\sum u_i^3\le2d^{3/2}$ and $\epsilon_i\le C_\chi$. So
\[
\mathsf E_3,\ \mathsf E_6\le C_\chi(S_\chi+2)\bigl[d^{3/2}+e^{-\mathsf c_\chi(\log\frac{3b}{4d^{1/2}})^2}\bigr]\le2C_\chi(S_\chi+2),
\]
and the bracket above gives the member $C_{\rm Bx}b^{-2}[d^{3/2}+e^{-\mathsf c_\chi(\log(3b/(4d^{1/2})))^2}]\eta$, with $C_{\rm Bx}$ formed with $C_{\rm tp}$, $S_\Sigma$, $C^{\rm row}_{\rm tp}$, $C_\chi$ and $S_\chi$, and so determined by the constants. The missing first slice is small: by Prop.~\YMMref{120.6}{821}, $(d/a_K)^3|\mathcal C_{(1)}(p,q)|\le C_{\rm tp}u_0^3e^{-\delta_{\rm tp}u_0/\sqrt3}$, $u_0=d/a_K$, at $|x(p)-x(q)|\ge d/\sqrt3$; with the terms of the level $1$ of (2) it gives the member $C_{\rm Bt}l^{4p_0}e^{-\mathsf c_\flat d/a_K}b^{-2}\eta$.

(5)

\emph{The free value.} Lem.~\ref{lem:ward-fluctuation-template} (the template sums) gives $|\sum_{p,q}w_1w_2(C^{\rm fl}_{K,K-n})^2-\frac3{8\pi^2}\mathcal K_6|\le C_{\rm tm}[\frac{a_K}{\vartheta d}+(\frac d\ell)^3+(\frac d{D_n})^3]\eta$, and $\frac32\cdot\frac3{8\pi^2}=c_2$. Take $n=K$, $D_K=1$: $(d/\ell)^3+d^3\le2d^3$, the member $\frac32C_{\rm tm}\vartheta^{-1}b^{-2}a_K/d$ is $C_{\rm lat}b^{-2}a_K/d$, and $b^{-2}=\frac bd\,b^{-3}d$; the supremum over the labels at $g$ and $d/a_K\ge L(\log\frac1d)^2$ give $\bar\varepsilon_4$. Finally $\log\frac{3b'}{4d^{1/2}}\ge\frac12\log\frac1d$, as $\frac34b'\ge1$; so $\frac{b'}de^{-\mathsf c_\chi(\cdot)^2}\le b_+e^{\log\frac1d-\frac14\mathsf c_\chi(\log\frac1d)^2}$, $\frac{b'}dC_{\rm Bx}d^{3/2}\le C_{\rm Bx}b_+d^{1/2}$, and the other members are smaller: $\bar\varepsilon_4(g,d)\le C_4(g)d^{1/2}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{C-350-32}
With Prop.~\ref{C-350-7}(ii) at $m=3$, Prop.~\ref{C-350-9} gives, on every side $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$ and at every position,
\[
|\mathsf J_2-c_2b^{-2}\mathcal K_6|(f,h)\le\bigl[(C_{{\rm E},3}l^{6p_0}+C_{\rm E}b^{-1}d\,l^{8p_0}+\bar\varepsilon_4(g,d))\,b^{-3}d+C_{\rm lat}b^{-2}a_K/d\bigr]\eta ,
\]
and on $T_{\ell_g}$, under the assumptions of Prop.~\ref{C-350-8} besides ($g\le\gamma_{\rm C}$, $d\le d_{\rm A}(g)$), by that Proposition, the same for $S^T_{2;K,\ell_g,\beta}(f,h)$ with $C_{\rm A}(g)\vartheta^{-1}bd$ added to the coefficient of $b^{-3}d$. The member $\bar\varepsilon_4(g,d)\,b^{-3}d\,\eta$ holds the two finite-size terms of the free value, $\frac32C_{\rm tm}b^{-2}[(d/\ell)^3+(d/D_K)^3]\eta$, of the torus and of the constraint at the top level $D_K=1$, which the proof of Prop.~\ref{C-350-9} bounds by $3C_{\rm tm}b^{-2}d^3\eta=3C_{\rm tm}bd^2\cdot b^{-3}d\,\eta$: they are at most $3C_{\rm tm}\,b^{-3}d\,\eta$ for $d^2\le1/b$, and of the order $bd^2$ relative to the first correction beyond.

The other members of $\bar\varepsilon_4(g,d)\,b^{-3}d\,\eta$ are at most $C_4(g)\,d^{1/2}\,b^{-3}d\,\eta$ (Prop.~\ref{C-350-9}), and $C_{\rm E}b^{-1}d\,l^{8p_0}\le C_{\rm E}c_{\mathfrak p}\,l^{6p_0}$ with $c_{\mathfrak p}=\sup_{0<t\le1}t\max\{1,\log\frac2t\}^{2p_0}$. So, beside the lattice term $C_{\rm lat}b^{-2}a_K/d$ and the two finite-size terms, the deviation from the free law is at most $C\,l^{6p_0}\,b^{-3}d\,\eta$, with a $C$ formed with $g$ and the constants (and with $\vartheta$ on $T_{\ell_g}$): of the order of the first correction, up to the factor $l^{6p_0}$; for $d^2\le1/b$ the two finite-size terms are of that order too. The coefficient of the first correction is fixed by the order six.
\end{remark}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian measures conditioned on a convex set]\label{C-350-10}
Let $\nu$ be a centred Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^I$, $I$ finite, with variances $\le\sigma_i^2$, and $Q\supset\prod_i(-c_i,c_i)$ open, bounded, convex and symmetric; put $t_i=c_i/\sigma_i$ and $\epsilon=\sum_ie^{-t_i^2/2}$. Let $F_1,\dots,F_r$ ($r=2,3$) be complex polynomials of orders $\le k_j$ with $|F_j|\le S_j$ on $Q$, and $k=\sum_jk_j$. If $t_i^2\ge\max\{4,2k\}$ for all $i$ and $2^k\epsilon\le1$, the joint cumulants of $F_1,\dots,F_r$ in $\nu(\cdot\,|\,Q)$ and in $\nu$ differ by at most $q_r(1+2^k)\epsilon\prod_jS_j$, with $q_2=5$, $q_3=37$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
For $z\notin Q$ let $s=\max_i|z_i|/c_i\ge1$. The segment from $-z/s$ to $z/s$ lies in $\bar Q$, so $\tau\mapsto F_j(\tau z/s)$ is a polynomial of order $\le k_j$ bounded by $S_j$ on $[-1,1]$, and the extremal property of Chebyshev's polynomials gives $|F_j(z)|\le S_j(2s)^{k_j}$. On $Q^{\rm c}$, $s^k\le\sum_i(|z_i|/c_i)^k\mathbf 1\{|z_i|\ge c_i\}$, and for a centred Gaussian variable of variance $\le\sigma_i^2$, $\mathbb E[(|z_i|/c_i)^k;|z_i|\ge c_i]\le e^{-t_i^2/2}$ once $t_i^2\ge\max\{4,2k\}$; so
\[
\nu(Q^{\rm c})\le\epsilon,\qquad\int_{Q^{\rm c}}\prod_j|F_j|\,\mathrm{d}\nu\le2^k\epsilon\prod_jS_j .
\]
Let $F$ be a product of some of the $F_j$, $S$ the product of their $S_j$, and $m$, $m^{\rm r}$ its moments in $\nu$ and in $\nu(\cdot\,|\,Q)$. Then $m^{\rm r}-m=m^{\rm r}\nu(Q^{\rm c})-\int_{Q^{\rm c}}F\,\mathrm{d}\nu$ and $|m^{\rm r}|\le S$, so $|m^{\rm r}-m|\le(1+2^k)\epsilon S$; and $|m|\le S+2^k\epsilon S\le2S$. A joint cumulant of order $r$ is a sum, over the partitions into $p$ blocks, of $(-1)^{p-1}(p-1)!$ times products of $p$ moments; telescoping each product, with the factors bounded by $S$ and by $2S$, bounds its change by $p\,2^{p-1}(1+2^k)\epsilon\prod_jS_j$. So $q_r=\sum_p\mathrm S(r,p)\,p!\,2^{p-1}$, $\mathrm S$ the Stirling numbers of the second kind: $q_2=1+4$, $q_3=1+12+24$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The coefficients of a logarithm]\label{C-350-22}
Let $G$ be holomorphic on $|\lambda|<1$ with $G(0)=0$ and $\operatorname{Re}G\le\mathsf E$. Then every Taylor coefficient $G_{[m]}$, $m\ge1$, has $|G_{[m]}|\le2\mathsf E$. Consequently, if $F$ is holomorphic on $|\lambda|<1$, $F(0)=1$, $F\ne0$, $|F|\le e^{\mathsf E}$, and $F=1+\lambda\mathsf R_1+\lambda^2\mathsf R_2+O(\lambda^3)$, then $W_1=-\mathsf R_1$ and $W_2=\frac12\mathsf R_1^2-\mathsf R_2$ have $|W_1|,|W_2|\le2\mathsf E$. The condition $F\ne0$ cannot be dropped.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
For $0<\rho<1$ and $m\ge1$, $G_{[m]}\rho^m=-\pi^{-1}\int_0^{2\pi}(\mathsf E-\operatorname{Re}G(\rho e^{i\phi}))e^{-im\phi}\,\mathrm{d}\phi$; the factor $\mathsf E-\operatorname{Re}G$ is $\ge0$ and has the mean $\mathsf E$ over the circle, as $\operatorname{Re}G(0)=0$; let $\rho\to1$. For $F$, the function $G=\log F$ is defined on the disc, as $F$ has no zero there; $\operatorname{Re}G=\log|F|\le\mathsf E$ and $G=-\lambda W_1-\lambda^2W_2+O(\lambda^3)$. For $F=1+\mathsf c\lambda$ with $\mathsf c\ge3$, which has a zero in the disc, $|\mathsf R_1|=\mathsf c>2\log(1+\mathsf c)=2\mathsf E$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The order six at one level]\label{C-350-11}
Under the assumptions of Prop.~\ref{C-350-6}, let $2\le n\le K$ and $\mathsf{Bx}=\prod_{0\le i<n}\{B_i:|B_i(b)|<\mathfrak b(x_i)\ \forall b\}$, a product of Euclidean balls in $\mathfrak g$, one for each non-pivot bond of the heights $0\le i<n$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] There are functions $\mathsf O^\lambda_1$, $\mathsf O^\lambda_2$, $\mathsf D^\lambda$ on $\mathsf{Bx}$, continuous and bounded on $\{|\lambda|\le1\}\times\mathsf{Bx}$ and holomorphic in $|\lambda|<1$, with $\mathsf O^\lambda_a(B)=\mathsf o_a(\lambda B)$ for a function $\mathsf o_a$ holomorphic near $0$, $\mathsf O^{-\lambda}_a(-B)=\mathsf O^\lambda_a(B)$, $\mathsf D^{-\lambda}(-B)=\mathsf D^\lambda(B)$, $\int_{\mathsf{Bx}}\mathsf D^\lambda dB=1$, $\mathsf D^0dB=\bigotimes_{0\le i<n}\nu^{\rm r}_i$, and
\[
\sum_{j\le n}\mathsf n^\lambda_j=\bigl\langle\mathsf O^\lambda_1;\mathsf O^\lambda_2\bigr\rangle_{\mathsf D^\lambda dB}\qquad(|\lambda|<1).
\]
Here $\mathsf D^\lambda$ is the product over the heights $0\le i<n$ of the normalised densities of the steps along the chain of the backgrounds, which reads $(\lambda,B)$ through $\lambda B$; for $0\le i<n$, the height $0$ included, the density of the step of the height $i$ at $\lambda=0$, at the trivial configuration, is proportional to $\exp[-\frac12(B_i,(\mathsf M_i\otimes1)B_i)]$ on the box of the height, with the real symmetric $\mathsf M_i\ge\frac34\gamma^{\rm tr}$ of the measures $\nu^\circ_i$ (Lem.~\ref{C-350-23}(iii)); and for real $0<\lambda\le1$, $\log(\mathsf D^\lambda/\mathsf D^0)$ is the sum of a term that does not depend on $B$, of terms $\lambda^{-2}F(\lambda,\lambda B)$ and of terms $F(\lambda,\lambda B)$, with functions $F(\lambda,\zeta)$ holomorphic near $(0,0)$, those of the first kind with $F=O(|\zeta|^2)$.

Uniformly on $\mathsf{Bx}$, $\mathsf O^\lambda_a=\lambda^2(X_{a,0}+\lambda X_{a,1}+\lambda^2X_{a,2})+O(\lambda^5)$ and $\mathsf D^\lambda=\mathsf D^0\exp[-\lambda W_1-\lambda^2W_2+O(\lambda^3)]$, where $X_{a,m}$ is homogeneous of order $m+2$, $X_{a,0}=q_a+q^{(0)}_a$ with the $q_a$ of the proof of Prop.~\ref{C-350-9}, formed with the signs $\mathsf{sg}_i$ of Lem.~\YMMref{124.3}{835} there, and a quadratic form $q^{(0)}_a$ that vanishes where $B_0=0$, $W_1$ is odd of order $\le3$, and $W_2$ is, up to the constant that the term without $B$ gives, even of order $\le4$. These are polynomials on the whole space, with Taylor coefficients at the trivial configuration formed with $L$ and the running couplings, so that the cumulants of \eqref{C-350-5} are formed in $\bigotimes_{0\le i<n}\nu^\circ_i$ as well.

Hence $\mathsf h^{(n)}_4=\langle X_{1,0};X_{2,0}\rangle$ and $\mathsf h^{(n)}_6=\gamma^{\rm r}_2$, the cumulants being taken in $\bigotimes_{0\le i<n}\nu^{\rm r}_i$.
\item[(ii)] If $\gamma^{\rm tr}\mathfrak b(x_{n-1})^2\ge80$ and $10240N^3e^{-\gamma^{\rm tr}\mathfrak b(x_{n-1})^2/8}\le1$, then
\[
\beta^3a_K^2|\gamma^{\rm r}_2-\gamma^\circ_2|\le\mathcal U(x_{n-1},\mathsf N)\|w_1\|_\infty\|w_2\|_\infty,\qquad\mathcal U(x,\mathsf N)=C_{\rm X}\mathsf N^{36}\exp\bigl[-\tfrac18\gamma^{\rm tr}A_1^2(\log x)^{2p_0}\bigr],
\]
with $C_{\rm X}$ determined by the constants.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(i)

\emph{The chain of the backgrounds.} For $|\lambda|\le1$ and $B\in\mathsf{Bx}$ put $v^\lambda_n:=0$ and, downwards for $i=n-1,\dots,1$, let $v^\lambda_i$ be the lowered point (equation~\YMMref{(2286)}{833}) that the step $i+1$ forms of the point $v^\lambda_{i+1}$ of the level $i+1$ and of the fluctuation $\lambda x_i^{-1/2}B_i$. Its first member $A^\lambda_i$ is a $1$-form on the bare bonds, and $\tilde U^\lambda_i:=\exp(iL^{-i}A^\lambda_i)$, a configuration on the bare bonds, is the \emph{background of the level $i$}. The maps of the step are holomorphic on their domain, at real and at complex points (the holomorphy following equation~\YMMref{(2286)}{833}); by their bounds (equation~\YMMref{(2287)}{834} and its domain verification), as $\sup|\lambda x_i^{-1/2}B_i|\le|\lambda|\delta(x_i)$ on the box, $\|v^\lambda_i\|\le|\lambda|r_i$ at every height, with the radii $r_n=0$, $r_i=L^{-1}r_{i+1}+\frac{11}{10}c_{\mathfrak h}\delta(x_i)\le\frac85c_{\mathfrak h}\delta(x_i)$ of equation~\YMMref{(2291)}{834}, which keep the chain in the domain of the maps, as $\delta(x_{K-1})$ lies below the threshold of the chain classes (Prop.~\ref{C-350-6}(iv)).

So the chain is formed for $|\lambda|\le1$, it reads $(\lambda,B)$ through $\lambda B$, and for real $\lambda\in[0,1]$ it stays in the chain classes (Prop.~\YMMref{124.2}{834}, equation~\YMMref{(2288)}{834}). At complex $\lambda$ the background has values in $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb C)$, and $a_p$ is read there as $1-\frac12\operatorname{tr}$ of the product of the variables around $p$; on $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ this is $a_p$. The observable is $\mathsf O^\lambda_a(B):=a_K^{-1}\sum_pw_a(p)\,a_p(\tilde U^\lambda_1)+\mathsf w^\lambda_a(B_0)$: its first member is $\mathcal O(w_a)$ at the background of the level $1$, which carries the fields of the heights $1\le i<n$, and its second, the source term of the height $0$, is the sum over the domains of the level $0$ of the action term of the source $w_a$ at the point $v^\lambda_1$ and the field $\lambda x_0^{-1/2}B_0$; the field of the height $0$ enters $\mathsf O^\lambda_a$ through this term alone.

The density is $\mathsf D^\lambda(B):=\prod_{0\le i<n}\rho^\lambda_i/Z^\lambda_i$, with $\rho^\lambda_i$ the density of the step of the height $i$ at the field scale $\lambda$ at the point $v^\lambda_{i+1}$, the exponential of the quadratic forms of the step in $B_i$ and of its potentials, and $Z^\lambda_i$ its integral over the box of the height.

\emph{The identity.} At real $0<\lambda\le1$ each step at a height $1\le i<n$ obeys the identity of one step at the field scale $\lambda$ of step (1) of the proof of Prop.~\ref{C-350-9}, whose case $\lambda=1$ uses the quotient argument of Prop.~\ref{prop:weighted-pair-tower}, and at the height $0$ the source enters linearly, through the action term of the sources. Iterating from the height $n-1$ down,
\[
\exp D^{\lambda,\mu}_n=\int_{\mathsf{Bx}}\exp\bigl[\mu_1\mathsf O^\lambda_1+\mu_2\mathsf O^\lambda_2\bigr]\mathsf D^\lambda\,\mathrm{d}B,
\]
$D^{\lambda,\mu}_n$ the exponent of the progression at the trivial configuration with the sources $\mu_1w_1+\mu_2w_2$. Both sides are holomorphic in $\mu$ near $0$, and holomorphic in $|\lambda|<1$, as the maps of the chain are holomorphic at complex points and the normalisations $Z^\lambda_i$ have no zero (Lem.~\ref{C-350-23}(ii)); they agree on $(0,1]$. The mixed derivative in $\mu$ at $0$ of the logarithms is the covariance.

\emph{At $\lambda=0$.} The chain is trivial and the potentials vanish. At the heights $1\le i<n$ the density of the step is $\exp[-\frac12(B_i,((\tau_i\mathsf A^{\rm cv}_i+(1-\tau_i)\hat{\mathsf G})\otimes1)B_i)]=\exp[-\frac12(B_i,(\mathsf M_i\otimes1)B_i)]$, and at the height $0$, where $\tau_0=1$, it is $\exp[-\frac12(B_0,(\mathsf A^{\rm cv}_0\otimes1)B_0)]$, $\mathsf M_0=\mathsf A^{\rm cv}_0$; the sources of these two identities are given with Lem.~\ref{C-350-23}(iii). So $\mathsf D^0dB=\bigotimes_{0\le i<n}\nu^{\rm r}_i$.

\emph{The orders.} The orders $0$ and $1$ of $\mathsf O^\lambda_a$ vanish, the order $1$ by the constant gauge rotations, as in Prop.~\ref{C-350-7}. As $\mathsf O^\lambda_a=\mathsf o_a(\lambda B)$ with $\mathsf o_a$ holomorphic near $0$, the coefficient of $\lambda^{m+2}$ is a homogeneous polynomial of order $m+2$. For real $0<\lambda\le1$ the integral identity of the step at a complex field scale (Prop.~\ref{IV-71-37}), read at the points of the chain, writes each $Z^\lambda_i$ as $\det^{1/2}$ of the covariance of the step times the exponential of a sum of local terms of the step; in the product of the quotients the families of the progression drop out, by the sum rule of the chain classes (Prop.~\YMMref{124.2}{834}, equation~\YMMref{(2289)}{834}), which telescopes over the heights, and $\mathsf D^\lambda(B)$ is a number $c_n(\lambda)$, which does not depend on $B$, times the exponential of a sum of terms $\lambda^{-2}F(\lambda,\lambda B)$ with $F=O(|\zeta|^2)$, namely the quadratic forms of the steps, $\lambda^{-2}$ times forms in $\lambda B_i$ whose coefficients read $\lambda B$ through the chain, and the potentials of the marks of the gauge fixing and of the action, $x_i\lambda^{-2}$ times functions of $\lambda x_i^{-1/2}B_i$, and of terms $F(\lambda,\lambda B)$, namely the other potentials, the logarithms of the determinants of the covariances along the chain, the localised Gaussian families of the steps and the counterterms at the backgrounds; in all of them $F(\lambda,\zeta)$ is holomorphic near $(0,0)$.

This is the form of $\log(\mathsf D^\lambda/\mathsf D^0)$ stated in (i), the term without $B$ being $\log(c_n(\lambda)/c_n(0))$. With $F=\sum_{k,\alpha}f_{k\alpha}\lambda^k\zeta^\alpha$ the coefficient of $\lambda^m$ of $\lambda^{-2}F(\lambda,\lambda B)$ is $\sum_{k+|\alpha|=m+2}f_{k\alpha}B^\alpha$, a polynomial of order $\le m+2$, and that of $F(\lambda,\lambda B)$ one of order $\le m$; this gives the orders of $W_1$ and $W_2$, and the identity between holomorphic functions of $\lambda$ passes from $(0,1]$ to a disc about $0$. Odd functions have the mean $0$ in $\mathsf D^0dB$, the mass $1$ removes the mean of the order $2$ of $\mathsf D^\lambda/\mathsf D^0$, and the coefficient of $\lambda^2$ in $\lambda^{-4}\langle\mathsf O^\lambda_1;\mathsf O^\lambda_2\rangle$ is \eqref{C-350-5}; at $\lambda^0$ it is $\langle X_{1,0};X_{2,0}\rangle$.

By Prop.~\ref{C-350-7}(i), $\lambda^{-4}\sum_{j\le n}\mathsf n^\lambda_j=\mathsf h^{(n)}_4+\lambda^2\mathsf h^{(n)}_6+O(\lambda^4)$.

(ii) By Lem.~\ref{C-350-23}, on $\mathsf{Bx}$ the $X_{a,m}$ are at most $C_{\rm S}\mathsf N^8\|w_a\|_\infty$ and $W_1$, $W_2$ at most $2C_{\rm S}\mathsf N^7$; a cumulant of order $\ge2$ does not see the constant in $W_2$. By (iii) of that Lemma the variances of $\nu^\circ_i$ are at most $\frac4{3\gamma^{\rm tr}}$; $\mathsf{Bx}$ holds the cube of the half-sides $\mathfrak b(x_{n-1})/\sqrt3$ in the components, as $x_i\ge x_{n-1}$ for $i<n$; so $t_i^2\ge\frac14\gamma^{\rm tr}\mathfrak b(x_{n-1})^2\ge20$ and $\epsilon\le10N^3e^{-\gamma^{\rm tr}\mathfrak b(x_{n-1})^2/8}$. Lem.~\ref{C-350-10} at the seven cumulants, whose entries have the total order $k\le10$, and $\beta^3a_K^2\le\mathsf N^3$ give (ii).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The suprema on the boxes]\label{C-350-23}
In the setting of Prop.~\ref{C-350-11}(i) there is $C_{\rm S}\ge1$, determined by the constants, such that for $|\lambda|<1$ and $B\in\mathsf{Bx}$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $|\mathsf O^\lambda_a(B)|\le C_{\rm S}\mathsf N^8\|w_a\|_\infty$ for $a=1,2$;
\item[(ii)] $\mathsf D^\lambda(B)\ne0$ and $|\mathsf D^\lambda(B)|\le e^{C_{\rm S}\mathsf N^7}|\mathsf D^0(B)|$;
\item[(iii)] for $0\le i<n$, the height $0$ included, the density of the step of the height $i$ at $\lambda=0$, at the trivial configuration, is proportional to $\exp[-\frac12(B_i,(\mathsf M_i\otimes1)B_i)]$ on the box of the height: its Gaussian part is $\nu^\circ_i$, the centred Gaussian measure with the real symmetric precision $\mathsf M_i\otimes1\ge\frac34\gamma^{\rm tr}$, and its normalised restriction to the box is $\nu^{\rm r}_i$, a probability measure; at the height $0$, $\tau_0=1$ and $\mathsf M_0=\mathsf A^{\rm cv}_0$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, on $\mathsf{Bx}$, $|X_{a,m}|\le C_{\rm S}\mathsf N^8\|w_a\|_\infty$ for $m=0,1,2$, and $|W_1|,|W_2|\le2C_{\rm S}\mathsf N^7$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(i) The first member of $\mathsf O^\lambda_a$ is $a_K^{-1}\sum_pw_a(p)a_p(\tilde U^\lambda_1)$, at the background $\tilde U^\lambda_1$ of the level $1$ of the chain of the proof of Prop.~\ref{C-350-11}(i), a configuration on the bare bonds whose values stay near $\mathbf 1$ in $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb C)$ by the radii of the chain, with at most $3N^3$ plaquettes and $a_K^{-1}\le N$; the second, the source term of the height $0$, is a sum over at most $8N^3$ domains of members of the family of the source, each bounded on the box by the size bounds of the step at a complex field scale (Prop.~\ref{IV-71-37}) and by $\mathfrak b(\beta)^2\le C\beta$.

(ii) $\mathsf D^\lambda=\prod_{0\le i<n}\rho^\lambda_i/Z^\lambda_i$ along the chain at the complex field scale $\lambda$, a product over the at most $K\le N$ heights. Each $\rho^\lambda_i$ is the exponential of a finite sum, so $\rho^\lambda_i\ne0$; its exponent is a sum over at most $8N^3$ places of quadratic forms in the field, whose coefficients are holomorphic along the chain, and of potentials, and on the box each of them is bounded by the size bounds of the step at a complex field scale (Prop.~\ref{IV-71-37}) and by $\mathfrak b(x_i)^2\le C\beta$, the radii of the chain keeping the points of all the heights in the discs where these bounds hold.

By the integral identity of the step at a complex field scale, $Z^\lambda_i$ is $\det^{1/2}$ of the covariance of the step times the exponential of a sum of local terms of the step, each bounded by the size bounds of the step; so $Z^\lambda_i\ne0$, and $|Z^\lambda_i|$ is bounded below by a determinant bound for its Gaussian part. Hence $\mathsf D^\lambda\ne0$, and, with at most $CN^3$ terms a height, each at most a number determined by the constants times $\mathfrak b(\beta)^2\le C\beta\le C\mathsf N$, this gives the bound with $\mathsf N^7$. (iii) For a height $1\le i<n$, at $\lambda=0$ the chain is trivial and the potentials vanish, and the density of the step at the trivial triple is $\exp[-\frac{\tau_i}2(B,\mathbf C_\ast^{-1}B)-\frac{1-\tau_i}2\sum_\square(B,\hat{\mathsf G}_\square B)]$.

Here the whole covariance of the step at the trivial triple is $\mathbf C_\ast=(\mathsf A^{\rm cv}_i)^{-1}\otimes1$ (equation~\YMMref{(2297)}{836}, from Prop.~\YMMref{120.3}{819} at the place of the height $i$), and the sum over the cubes of the local gauge-fixing forms is $\hat{\mathsf G}\otimes1$ (equation~\YMMref{(828)}{395} at the trivial block field, with Prop.~\YMMref{120.3}{819}); so the density is $\exp[-\frac12(B,((\tau_i\mathsf A^{\rm cv}_i+(1-\tau_i)\hat{\mathsf G})\otimes1)B)]=\exp[-\frac12(B,(\mathsf M_i\otimes1)B)]$, as $\mathsf A^{\rm cv}_i=\mathsf B^{\rm cv}_i+\hat{\mathsf G}$. At the height $0$, $\tau_0=1$, because $\xi_0\equiv x_0$, and the gauge-fixing term drops out.

The provision of the step $1$ is the canonical provision of the step at $(x_0;\mathfrak a^{\rm abs}_0)$, the quadruple $(0,x_0,\mathfrak a^{\rm abs}_0,\mathfrak w)$ being a place by the setting (J) of {\cite[Def.~B.16]{YMM2}} at $k=K-1$ (Prop.~\ref{C-350-6}(iv)); by Prop.~\YMMref{120.3}{819} and Prop.~\YMMref{120.6}{821} at $k=0$, its whole covariance at the trivial triple is the scalar operator with the real matrix $(\mathsf A^{\rm cv}_0)^{-1}$. So the density of the height $0$ is $\exp[-\frac12(B_0,(\mathsf A^{\rm cv}_0\otimes1)B_0)]$, and $\mathsf M_0=\mathsf A^{\rm cv}_0$. At every height $\mathsf B^{\rm cv}_i$ and $\hat{\mathsf G}$ are real symmetric matrices $\ge0$ (equation~\YMMref{(2231)}{819}), $\mathsf A^{\rm cv}_i\ge\gamma^{\rm tr}$ (Prop.~\YMMref{120.3}{819}) and $\frac34\le\tau_i\le\frac43$ (Prop.~\ref{C-350-6}(ii)); so $\mathsf M_i$ is real and symmetric, $\mathsf M_i\ge\min\{\tau_i,1\}\mathsf A^{\rm cv}_i\ge\frac34\gamma^{\rm tr}$, the Gaussian part of the density is $\nu^\circ_i$, and $\nu^{\rm r}_i$ is a probability measure.

The consequences: Cauchy's estimate on $|\lambda|<1$ for $\lambda\mapsto\mathsf o_a(\lambda B)$, whose coefficient of $\lambda^{m+2}$ is $X_{a,m}(B)$, and Lem.~\ref{C-350-22} for $\lambda\mapsto\mathsf D^\lambda(B)/\mathsf D^0(B)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The composed chart; the lattice number of a flat top]\label{C-350-12}
Let $N=\ell L^K$, $\ell=2L^m$, and $1\le t\le K$ with $2L^{m+K-t+1}\ge C_LM$; the levels are those of the lattice $(\ell,K)$, $\mathcal V_j$ is the space of the configurations of the level $j$, and $\mathsf Y$ the space of the $y=(\mathcal A_j)_{j<t}$, $\mathcal A_j$ a real $\mathfrak g$-valued $1$-form on the non-pivot bonds of the level $j$ (Section~\YMMref{4}{16} and the pivot definition preceding Lem.~\YMMref{40.1}{297}).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] There are an open neighbourhood $\mathsf O_t$ of $\mathbf 1$ in $\mathcal V_t$, $\rho_2\in(0,1]$ and $C_{\rm H}>0$ such that, with $\mathsf Y_{\rho_2}=\{y\in\mathsf Y:|\mathcal A_j|<\rho_2,\ j<t\}$: the chain $W_t=W$, $W_j=V_{W_{j+1}}[\mathcal A_j]$ of the charts of {\cite[\S{}B.2]{YMM2}} is defined on $\mathsf O_t\times\mathsf Y_{\rho_2}$, with $\mathcal M(W_j)=W_{j+1}$; $\Psi(W,y)=W_0$ is a real analytic diffeomorphism of $\mathsf O_t\times\mathsf Y_{\rho_2}$ onto an open set $\mathsf U\ni\mathbf 1$; and there is a real continuous $\theta$, real analytic near $(\mathbf 1,0)$, with $\int H\,\mathrm{d}U=C_{\rm H}\int_{\mathsf O_t}\,\mathrm{d}W\int_{\mathsf Y_{\rho_2}}\,\mathrm{d}y\,e^{-\theta}H\circ\Psi$ for every bounded Borel $H$ that vanishes off $\mathsf U$.
\item[(ii)] For $\kappa\in(0,\infty)^t$ let $F_\kappa=A+\sum_{j<t}\kappa_jG_j(\mathcal M^j\cdot)$, $G_j$ the gauge-fixing function \YMMref{(54)}{27} at the level $j$, and $\phi_\kappa=F_\kappa\circ\Psi(\mathbf 1,\cdot)$. Then $\phi_\kappa\ge0$, $\phi_\kappa(0)=0$, $\nabla\phi_\kappa(0)=0$, and the Hessian of $\phi_\kappa$ at $0$ is block diagonal for the decomposition of $\mathsf Y$ by the levels and positive definite.
\item[(iii)] The numbers $\mathsf g_{m'}[N,t](p,q)=\gamma^{\rm L}_{m'}[\phi_\kappa,\theta(\mathbf 1,\cdot),a_p\circ\Psi(\mathbf 1,\cdot),a_q\circ\Psi(\mathbf 1,\cdot)]$, $m'=0,2$, do not depend on $\kappa$, and they are the same in every adapted chart. An \emph{adapted chart} of $(\mathcal V_0,dU,\operatorname{Lg}\mathcal M^t)$, $\operatorname{Lg}$ being the Lie algebra logarithm of the intrinsic logarithm on $G\setminus\{-1\}$, is $(\mathsf E',\Psi',\theta',C',\varrho')$ with: $\mathsf E'$ an open neighbourhood of $(0,0)$ in $\mathsf W_t\times\mathbb R^{\dim\mathsf Y}$, $\mathsf W_t$ the space of the $\mathfrak g$-valued $1$-forms $w$ on the bonds of the level $t$; $\Psi'$ a $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism of $\mathsf E'$ onto an open subset of the domain of $\operatorname{Lg}\mathcal M^t$, with $\Psi'(0,0)=\mathbf 1$ and $\operatorname{Lg}\mathcal M^t\Psi'(w,y)=w$; $\theta'$ a real continuous function on $\mathsf E'$, with $\theta'(0,\cdot)$ of class $C^\infty$; $C'>0$; $\varrho'>0$ a continuous function of $w$ alone; and $\int H\,\mathrm{d}U=C'\int_{\mathsf E'}\varrho'(w)\,e^{-\theta'(w,y)}H(\Psi'(w,y))\,\mathrm{d}w\,\mathrm{d}y$ for every bounded Borel $H$ that vanishes off $\Psi'(\mathsf E')$.

In it the numbers are $\gamma^{\rm L}_{m'}[F_\kappa\circ\Psi'(0,\cdot),\theta'(0,\cdot),a_p\circ\Psi'(0,\cdot),a_q\circ\Psi'(0,\cdot)]$. They depend on $N$, $t$, $L$, $p$, $q$ alone.
\item[(iv)] One may take $\mathsf O_t=\{e^{iw}:|w|<\rho_2\}$ for every $\rho_2\in(0,\rho_\star]$, with a $\rho_\star\in(0,1]$. Then $W_j$, $V^{\rm bf}_j(W_{j+1})$, $G_j(W_j)$, $\theta$ and $a_p\circ\Psi$ are real analytic in $(w,y)$ on $\mathsf O_t\times\mathsf Y_{\rho_2}$, $W_j(\mathbf 1,0)=\mathbf 1$, $0<e^{-\theta}\le\prod_{j<t}(27L^9)^{\#\Gamma_j}$, and $C_{\rm H}=\prod_{j<t}(2\pi^2)^{-\#\mathfrak X^+_j}L^{-3\#\Gamma_j}$, where $\mathfrak X^+_j$ are the positively oriented non-pivot bonds of the level $j$ and $\Gamma_j$ the positively oriented bonds of the level $j+1$. One may also take $\mathsf O_t=\{W\in\mathcal V_t:\max_p|\partial W(p)-\mathbf 1|<\varepsilon_*\}$, $p$ running over the plaquettes of the level $t$, and $\rho_2=\rho_*$, with numbers $\varepsilon_*,\rho_*\in(0,1]$ determined by $L$ and the constants and independent of $t$, $K$ and $m$; (i)--(iii) hold for this choice as well.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(i), (iv) One real number $\mathsf t_*>1$ serves at all levels: with it the constants, the lattice of each step and $\mathsf t_*$ are data under (Im) of {\cite[Def.~B.2]{YMM2}}. For such data {\cite[Lem.~B.3]{YMM2}} gives, on an open set of block fields $W$ and for $|\mathcal A|$ below the bound that belongs to $\mathsf t_*$: the averaged configuration $V^{\rm bf}_j(W)$ is defined and $\mathcal M(V^{\rm bf}_j(W))=W$; $\mathcal M(V_W[\mathcal A])=W$; and $\operatorname{Lg}(V_W[\mathcal A](b)V^{\rm bf}_j(W)(b)^{-1})=\mathcal A(b)$ on the non-pivot bonds. {\cite[Lem.~B.3]{YMM2}} gives the one-step integral formula, with the constant $(2\pi^2)^{-\#\mathfrak X^+_j}L^{-3\#\Gamma_j}$, a Jacobian factor in $(0,(27/8)^{\#\Gamma_j}]$ and a normalisation in $(0,(8L^9)^{\#\Gamma_j}]$.

Neighbourhoods of $\mathbf 1$ chosen downwards, by continuity in $(W,\mathcal A)$, keep the chain where these statements apply; by induction over the levels the integral formula holds for every Borel subset of the natural domain of the chain, with $C_{\rm H}$ the product of the constants. The map
\[
U\mapsto\Bigl(\mathcal M^tU,\ \bigl(\operatorname{Lg}(\mathcal M^jU(b)\,V^{\rm bf}_j(\mathcal M^{j+1}U)(b)^{-1})\bigr)_{j<t}\Bigr)
\]
is a real analytic left inverse of $\Psi$ with injective differential, and $\dim\mathcal V_t+\dim\mathsf Y=\dim\mathcal V_0$; the inverse function theorem gives (i) after shrinking, and (iv) with $W=e^{iw}$, $dW=\varrho_{\rm H}(w)\,\mathrm{d}w$, $\varrho_{\rm H}>0$ the continuous density of the Haar measure of $\mathcal V_t$ in the variable $w$, on one set that carries (i)--(iii). For the second choice in (iv) one follows, level by level, a regularity number $\mathfrak r_j(W_j)$, which measures the plaquette variables of the averaged configuration of the level $j$ and is comparable with $\max_p|\partial W_j(p)-\mathbf 1|$: one step gives $\mathfrak r_j(W_j)\le L^{-2}\mathfrak r_{j+1}(W_{j+1})+C_{\mathfrak r}|\mathcal A_j|$, with $C_{\mathfrak r}$ determined by $L$ and the constants.

So a threshold $\mathfrak r_\flat$ for $\mathfrak r$, with $\varepsilon_*$ a fixed fraction of it and $\rho_*\le(1-L^{-2})\mathfrak r_\flat/C_{\mathfrak r}$, keeps every level in the sets where the statements of one step apply; nothing in this sees $t$, $K$ or $m$. (ii) $a_p\ge0$ and $G_j\ge0$; at $\mathbf 1$, $a_p(e^{iA})=\frac12|\mathrm{d}A(p)|^2+O(|A|^3)$, $G_j$ is half the sum of the squares of the linearised contour variables up to $O(|A|^3)$, and a fibre variable whose linearised curvature and contour variables vanish is $0$. At the linear order the composed chart is the chart of the free template: the bare curvature of the field of the level $j$ is $\mathsf T_j$ applied to it, with values in the slice $\mathcal C_{(j+1)}$ (Prop.~\YMMref{120.3}{819}), the slices are mutually orthogonal, and the linearised contour variables of the level $j$ are those of $\mathcal A_j$ alone; this makes the Hessian block diagonal.

(iii) By (i) and (iv), near $(0,0)$ the composed chart $(w,y)\mapsto\Psi(e^{iw},y)$, with $C_{\rm H}$, $\varrho_{\rm H}$ and $\theta(e^{iw},y)$, is an adapted chart: it is a real analytic diffeomorphism onto an open set, $\Psi(\mathbf 1,0)=\mathbf 1$ ($W_j(\mathbf 1,0)=\mathbf 1$), $\operatorname{Lg}\mathcal M^t\Psi(e^{iw},y)=w$, and $\theta$ is real analytic. Let $(\mathsf E',\Psi',\theta',C',\varrho')$ be an adapted chart, and $\mathsf E_1$ an open neighbourhood of $(0,0)$ that the composed chart maps into $\Psi'(\mathsf E')$. Then $\sigma:=\Psi'^{-1}\circ\Psi$ is a $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism of $\mathsf E_1$ onto an open set of the form $\sigma(w,y)=(w,s(w,y))$, both charts carrying $\operatorname{Lg}\mathcal M^t$ to the first variable, and $\sigma(0,0)=(0,0)$, as $\Psi(\mathbf 1,0)=\mathbf 1=\Psi'(0,0)$.

The two formulas for $dU$ give
\[
C_{\rm H}\,\varrho_{\rm H}(w)\,e^{-\theta(e^{iw},y)}=C'\varrho'(w)\,e^{-\theta'(\sigma(w,y))}\,|\det D_ys(w,y)|
\]
almost everywhere on $\mathsf E_1$, and, both sides being continuous, at every point of $\mathsf E_1$; in particular on the fibre $w=0$, a null set, where the numbers are read. So $y\mapsto s(0,y)$, a diffeomorphism near $0$ that fixes $0$, carries the phase $F_\kappa\circ\Psi(\mathbf 1,\cdot)$, the observables and the density $e^{-\theta(\mathbf 1,y)}dy$ into $F_\kappa\circ\Psi'(0,\cdot)$, the observables and $e^{-\theta'(0,y')}dy'$, up to the constant factor $C'\varrho'(0)/(C_{\rm H}\varrho_{\rm H}(0))$; the Taylor polynomials are taken at the minimum $0$ in both charts. The two coefficients of Laplace's method in either chart are those of the expansion of one quantity, the covariance of $a_p$ and $a_q$ under $e^{-\beta F_\kappa}$ on the fibre $\mathcal M^tU=\mathbf 1$ near $\mathbf 1$, and so they are the same in both.

The gauge transformations equal to $\mathbf 1$ on the top lattice preserve the fibre, $A$ and the $a_p$, and the normalised gauge-fixing factor (Def.~\YMMref{6.1}{27} and equations~\YMMref{(51)--(52)}{27}) integrates to one over their orbits at every strength (Lem.~\YMMref{5.3}{26} and equation~\YMMref{(55)}{28}); integrating over the orbits, the finest sites first, the covariance does not depend on $\kappa$ up to errors $e^{-c\beta}$, and neither do its coefficients. Near $(0,0)$ the composed chart is itself an adapted chart.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The identification of the order six]\label{C-350-13}
Under the assumptions of Prop.~\ref{C-350-11}, $\beta^3a_K^2\gamma^\circ_2=\mathsf T[N,n](w)$, the plaquettes being read in bare units on $\Lambda_N$; $\mathsf T[N,n](w)$ depends on $N$, $n$, $L$ and the lattice sources alone. The identity has no error term and holds at every size of the boxes.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
By Prop.~\ref{C-350-6}(i), Prop.~\ref{C-350-12} applies at $t=n$ on the lattice of the datum. For real $0<\lambda\le1$ the exact formula of the steps (Prop.~\YMMref{123.1}{829}), read at the fields $\lambda B$, and the sum rules of the chain classes (Prop.~\YMMref{124.2}{834}, equation~\YMMref{(2289)}{834}) add the exponents of the steps of Prop.~\ref{C-350-11}(i) up to
\[
\mathsf D^\lambda(B)=c_n(\lambda)\exp\Bigl[-\lambda^{-2}\Bigl(x_0A(W_0)+\sum_{j<n}x_jG_j(W_j)\Bigr)-\theta\Bigr],
\]
where $c_n(\lambda)$ does not depend on $B$ and $(W_j)$ is the composed chart over the flat top $\mathbf 1$ of the level $n$ at the fields $\mathcal A_i=\lambda x_i^{-1/2}\check B_i$, $\check B_i=\operatorname{Ad}(u_{i+1})B_i$, with $u_{i+1}\in G$ a function of the fields of the heights $>i$ alone: the chain of Prop.~\ref{C-350-11} runs through configurations in another gauge than the composed chart. The observables become $a_K^{-1}\sum_pw_a(p)a_p(W_0)$ at the same fields. No $\tau_i$ and no counterterm $e_i$ is left, because
\[
\lambda^{-2}\xi_j(\lambda)L^j+\sum_{i\le j}L^ie_i=\lambda^{-2}x_0
\]
by the run equation; this is what $\xi_j$ is chosen for. So the density is the Wilson weight at $\beta\lambda^{-2}$ with the gauge-fixing strengths $\kappa_j=x_j/\beta$ on the fibre $\mathcal M^nU=\mathbf 1$. The triangular change $B\mapsto\check B$ preserves the volume and the boxes, which are Euclidean balls $|B_i(b)|<\mathfrak b(x_i)$ and are preserved by the rotations $\operatorname{Ad}(u)$; its linear part at $0$ is a constant rotation of the colours, so it preserves the Gaussian part $\bigotimes_{i<n}\nu^\circ_i$; and the two numbers of Laplace's method are kept by a diffeomorphism that carries phase, observables and density into each other.

So $\gamma^\circ_2$ is the second coefficient of Laplace's method \eqref{C-350-31} at the parameter $\beta\lambda^{-2}$, and $\beta^3a_K^2\gamma^\circ_2=\sum_{p,q}w_1(p)w_2(q)\gamma^{\rm L}_2$ in the chart of Prop.~\ref{C-350-12}, which does not depend on $\kappa$. The dilation $x\mapsto L^{K-n}x$ carries the lattice $(\ell,K)$ with its flat top at the level $n$ to the lattice $(\ell L^{K-n},n)$, with the same bare torus, plaquettes to plaquettes with their barycentres; so the number is $\mathsf g_2[N,n](p,q)$. The argument uses that the boxes are Euclidean balls; it would not apply to boxes that are cubes in the components.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[An implicit function, Stokes's formula in a box, Wick's rule]\label{C-350-24}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[beginpenalty=10000]
\item[(i)] Let $\mathsf V$ be a finite-dimensional complex normed space, $0<\varsigma\le\frac1{120}$, and $F$ holomorphic from $\{\|y\|<\varsigma\}\times\{\lambda\in\mathfrak g^{\mathbb C}:|\lambda|<\varsigma\}$ to $\mathfrak g^{\mathbb C}$ with $|F|\le\frac1{40}$, $F(0,0)=0$ and $D_\lambda F(0,0)=1$. Then for $\|y\|<\varsigma^3$ there is exactly one $h(y)$ with $|h(y)|\le\varsigma^2$ and $F(y,h(y))=0$; $h$ is holomorphic, $|h(y)|\le\|y\|/(15\varsigma)$, and $h$ is $\mathfrak g$-valued at the real points if $F$ is.
\item[(ii)] Let $\mathsf B$ be the injective image in a bare torus of a box of $\mathbb Z^3$. For every closed bare path $\gamma$ in $\mathsf B$ there is an integer function $\mathsf k_\gamma$ on the plaquettes with all corners in $\mathsf B$, $|\mathsf k_\gamma|\le|\gamma|$ (the number of bonds of $\gamma$), with $a(\gamma)=\sum_p\mathsf k_\gamma(p)\,(\mathrm{d}a)(p)$ for every $1$-cochain $a$.
\item[(iii)] Let $(\zeta_\iota)$ be a centred Gaussian family with covariance $C$, and $P_1,\dots,P_r$ homogeneous polynomials in it of orders $n_1,\dots,n_r$, $n=\sum n_a$, $\|P\|_1$ the sum of the moduli of the coefficients. For monomials the joint cumulant $\langle P_1;\dots;P_r\rangle$ is the sum, over the pairings of the factors that are connected (the graph on $\{1,\dots,r\}$ with an edge for every pair that joins two of the $P_a$ is connected), of the products of the covariances, and by multilinearity this extends to polynomials; the cumulant vanishes if $n$ is odd. With $\mathsf c\ge\sup|C|$ on the supports, $|\langle P_1;\dots;P_r\rangle|\le(n-1)!!\prod_a\|P_a\|_1\mathsf c^{n/2}$; if every connected pairing has a pair with $|C|\le\varepsilon$, the bound holds with $\mathsf c^{n/2-1}\varepsilon$ for $\mathsf c^{n/2}$; and for two covariances $C$, $C'$ bounded by $\mathsf c$ the two cumulants differ by at most $(n-1)!!\frac n2\prod_a\|P_a\|_1\mathsf c^{n/2-1}\sup|C-C'|$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(i) Put $g(y,\lambda)=\lambda-F(y,\lambda)$, so $|g|\le\frac1{40}+\varsigma\le\frac1{30}$, $g(0,0)=0$, $D_\lambda g(0,0)=0$. Cauchy's estimate and Schwarz's lemma give $|D_\lambda g(y,\lambda)|\le\frac2{15}\varsigma^{-2}\max\{\|y\|,|\lambda|\}$ for $\max\{\|y\|,|\lambda|\}\le\frac12\varsigma$, and $|g(y,0)|\le\|y\|/(30\varsigma)$. So for $\|y\|<\varsigma^3$ the map $\lambda\mapsto g(y,\lambda)$ sends $\{|\lambda|\le\varsigma^2\}$ into itself and contracts by $\frac2{15}$; its fixed point is $h(y)$, the uniform limit of holomorphic iterates, and $|h|\le|g(y,0)|+\frac2{15}|h|$. (ii) With the paths $P_z$ from a corner $o$ of the box to $z$ that run first in the direction $1$, then $2$, then $3$, the quantity $a(P_z)+a(e)-a(P_{z+e_\mu})$ of a bond $e=\langle z,z+e_\mu\rangle$ is the sum of $\pm(\mathrm{d}a)$ over a strip of plaquettes of the box; along a closed path the terms $a(P_\cdot)$ telescope.

(iii) By Wick's theorem the moments are sums over all pairings; a pairing determines the partition of the factors into the components of its graph and is connected on each block, which identifies the sums over connected pairings with the joint cumulants. The bounds count the $(n-1)!!$ pairings and use $|\prod_{i\le m}c_i-\prod_{i\le m}c'_i|\le m\,\mathsf c^{m-1}\max|c_i-c'_i|$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Two bare tori under one flat top]\label{C-350-14}
Let $N=2L^{\mathsf m}$, $N'=L^sN$ ($s\ge1$), $1\le t<\mathsf m$, $\pi:\Lambda_{N'}\to\Lambda_N$ the reduction, and
\[
\nu=N/L^t\ge\nu_{\rm W}=\max\Bigl\{192,\ \frac{48(3\log L+\log2)}{\delta_{\rm tp}L(L-1)},\ \frac{C_LM}L\Bigr\}.
\]
For plaquettes $p',q'$ of $\Lambda_{N'}$ whose base points lie within $N/8$ of each other (the base point of the plaquette $p_{\mu\nu}(x)$ being $x$, the distance being the sup distance of the bare torus, in bare units) and $m'=0,2$,
\[
|\mathsf g_{m'}[N,t](\pi p',\pi q')-\mathsf g_{m'}[N',t](p',q')|\le C'_{\rm W}N'^{237}e^{-\delta_{\rm tp}L\nu/48},
\]
with $C'_{\rm W}$ determined by $L$ and $C_{\rm tp}$. Hence, for real $w_1,w_2$ on the plaquettes of $\Lambda_N$ with supports in balls of radius $r\ge8$, all base points within $N/8$ of each other, and $\breve w_a$ equal to $w_a\circ\pi$ on one lift of a ball of radius $N/4$ that holds the supports and $0$ elsewhere,
\[
|\mathsf T[N,t](w)-\mathsf T[N',t](\breve w)|\le900r^6C'_{\rm W}N'^{237}e^{-\delta_{\rm tp}L\nu/48}\|w_1\|_\infty\|w_2\|_\infty .
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
\emph{Signs.} Let $S\in\{N,N'\}$, and read the objects of the lattice $(S/L^t,t)$ in bare units on $\Lambda_S$; distances are those of the bare torus, $|\cdot|_\infty$ its sup distance, and $x(p)$ is the barycentre of a plaquette $p$, its base point being $x$ if $p=p_{\mu\nu}(x)$. For a bond $c$ of the top lattice $\mathbb T^{(t)}$, $B^t(c_\pm)$ are the blocks of order $t$ of its end points, its double block is their union, and its corridor ${\rm cor}(c)$ is the set of the bare bonds $b$ with $b_-\in B^t(c_-)$, $b_+\in B^t(c_+)$; $\mathsf 1_c$ is the bare $1$-cochain that is $1$ on ${\rm cor}(c)$, $-1$ on the reversed bonds and $0$ elsewhere. As $\nu\ge8$, every bare bond lies in one top block or in exactly one corridor, and no bond of the corridor of $c'$ has both end points in the double block of $c$ unless $c'\in\{c,\bar c\}$; the bonds of the double block of $c$ are those with both end points in it.

For a bare site $x\notin\mathbb T^{(t)}$, $j(x)=\max\{j:x\in\mathbb T^{(j)}\}<t$, its parent $\hat x\in\mathbb T^{(j(x)+1)}$ is the centre of the block of order $1$ that holds $x$, and ${\rm anc}(z)=\{z,\hat z,\hat{\hat z},\dots\}\setminus\mathbb T^{(t)}$; the sums over $x$ below run over the bare sites off $\mathbb T^{(t)}$. $\mathsf Q_k$ is the linear part of the $k$-fold block average, and $\xi_A(x)=(\mathsf Q_{j(x)}A)(\hat x,x)$ is the linearised contour variable of the site $x$. A $\mathfrak g$-valued $1$-form $y$ has the coordinates $y(\iota)$, $\iota=(b,\alpha)$, $b>0$ a bare bond and $\alpha$ a colour; $\iota+\gamma$ is the translate of $\iota$ by $\gamma$, and ${\rm dist}(\iota,\iota')=|b_--b'_-|_\infty$.

By Prop.~\ref{C-350-12}(iii) the numbers do not depend on $\kappa$; we take $\kappa\equiv1$.

\emph{A chart made for locality.} $\mathsf Q_k$ is a mean over bare paths: for every bond $c$ of $\mathbb T^{(k)}$ there is a probability measure on the bare paths from $c_-$ to $c_+$ in the double block of $c$, with at most $(4L)^k$ bonds, whose mean of $A(\gamma)$ is $(\mathsf Q_kA)(c)$; and $\mathsf Q_t\mathsf 1_c$ is $1$ at $c$ and $0$ at the other top bonds. $\mathcal M^t(U)(c)$ depends on $U$ on the double block of the top bond $c$ alone. So, for $y$ in $Y_S:=\ker\mathsf Q_t$ near $0$, the constraint $\mathcal M^t(e^{i\hat y})=\mathbf 1$ for $\hat y:=y+\sum_{c>0}h_c(y)\mathsf 1_c$ is solved one top bond at a time, with one element $h_c(y)\in\mathfrak g$ (three unknowns) for each: Lem.~\ref{C-350-24}(i) at $\varsigma=\varsigma_t:=(75L)^{-t}/(60L)$, applied to $(y,\lambda)\mapsto\operatorname{Lg}\mathcal M^t(e^{i(y+\lambda\mathsf 1_c)})(c)$, which is holomorphic and bounded by $\frac1{40}$ on the polydisc of the Lemma, vanishes at $(0,0)$ and has the derivative $1$ in $\lambda$ there, gives exactly one holomorphic $h_c$ with $|h_c(y)|\le\|y\|_\infty/(15\varsigma_t)$ for $\|y\|_\infty<\varsigma_t^3$, $\mathfrak g$-valued at real $y$; it reads $y$ on the double block of $c$ alone, $\hat y=y$ on the top blocks, and $\hat y=y+O(y^2)$ on $Y_S$.

The map $A\mapsto(\operatorname{Lg}\mathcal M^t(e^{iA}),\,A-\sum_{c>0}(\mathsf Q_tA)(c)\mathsf 1_c)$ is a real analytic diffeomorphism near $0$, as its differential at $0$ has the inverse $(w,y)\mapsto y+\sum_cw(c)\mathsf 1_c$; its inverse, followed by $A\mapsto e^{iA}$, is an adapted chart $\Psi'$ in the sense of Prop.~\ref{C-350-12}(iii), with $\varrho'=1$, a real analytic $\theta'$ and $\Psi'(0,y)=e^{i\hat y}$ for $y\in Y_S$; so both numbers may be computed in it. In it the action, the gauge terms, the Haar density (the exponential-coordinate Haar formula following equation~\YMMref{(911)}{420}) and the Jacobian, the product over the top bonds $c$ of the determinants of the derivatives of $\operatorname{Lg}\mathcal M^t(e^{i\cdot})(c)$ in the direction $\mathsf 1_c$, are sums of terms, each holomorphic and bounded by $1$ on the polydisc $\|y\|_\infty<\varsigma_t^3$ and depending on $y$ on at most $12L^{3t}$ bonds with end points in a set of diameter $\le2L^t$; for a plaquette $p$ these are the top blocks that hold a corner of $p$, within $L^t$ of its base point.

The reduction $\pi$ carries the lattices, blocks, contours, corridors and the block average of $\Lambda_{N'}$ to those of $\Lambda_N$ on every set of diameter $\le N/2$, so these are the same functions on both tori after the renaming of the variables by $\pi$.

\emph{The lines.} The gauge terms and the Haar terms of the chart read $y$ on the bonds, and not its curvature alone; so the lines of Wick's rule in this chart are the entries of the covariance $C_S$ of the chart variable $y\in Y_S$ under the centred Gaussian measure with the density proportional to $e^{-\frac12\mathsf H_S(y,y)}$, $\frac12\mathsf H_S(y,y)$ being the second Taylor polynomial at $0$ of the action with the gauge terms,
\[
\mathsf H_S(A,A')=(\mathrm{d}A,\mathrm{d}A')+\sum_x\langle\xi_A(x),\xi_{A'}(x)\rangle .
\]
Let $\mathcal X_S$ be the space of the $\mathfrak g$-valued functions on the bare sites that vanish on $\mathbb T^{(t)}$. Then $\mathrm{d}\mathcal X_S\subset Y_S$, as $\mathsf Q_t\mathrm{d}\chi=\mathrm{d}(\chi|_{\mathbb T^{(t)}})$, and $\chi\mapsto\xi_{\mathrm{d}\chi}=(\chi(x)-\chi(\hat x))_x$ is a bijection of $\mathcal X_S$ onto the functions on the sites off $\mathbb T^{(t)}$, with the inverse $\chi(x)=\sum_{x''\in{\rm anc}(x)}\xi(x'')$. So $Y_S$ is the direct sum of its axial part $Y^{\rm ax}_S=\{A\in Y_S:\xi_A=0\}$ and of $\mathrm{d}\mathcal X_S$, $y=y^{\rm ax}+\mathrm{d}\chi_y$, and
\[
\mathsf H_S(y,y)=\|\mathrm{d}y^{\rm ax}\|^2+\sum_x|\xi_y(x)|^2 ;
\]
$\mathrm{d}$ maps $Y^{\rm ax}_S$ one to one onto the curvatures whose plaquette averages of the order $t$ vanish, and $\mathsf H_S$ is positive definite on $Y_S$. In the Gaussian measure $y^{\rm ax}$ and the $\xi(x)$ are independent: the $\xi(x)$, one for each site off the top lattice, are independent with the variance $1$ in each colour, $(\mathrm{d}\chi)(b)=\sum_x\sigma(b,x)\xi(x)$ with $\sigma(b,x)=\mathbf 1[x\in{\rm anc}(b_+)]-\mathbf 1[x\in{\rm anc}(b_-)]$, and $\mathrm{d}y^{\rm ax}$ has the covariance $\Pi^{\rm fl}_t=\Pi^{\rm tp}_0-\Pi^{\rm tp}_t$ in each colour. On $Y^{\rm ax}_S$ the means of $y$ over two families of bare paths vanish: over the paths from the centre of the top block of a site $x$ to $x$, inside that block and with at most $(4L)^t$ bonds, whose mean of $y(\gamma)$ is $\sum_{x''\in{\rm anc}(x)}\xi_y(x'')=0$ (the contour averages of the levels composed from the top down), and over the paths of $\mathsf Q_t$ along a top bond, as $y\in\ker\mathsf Q_t$.

So $y(b)$ is the mean of the values of $y$ on closed bare paths of at most $4(4L)^t$ bonds in the box of $b$, the top block that holds $b$, or the double block of $c$ if $b\in{\rm cor}(c)$, and by Lem.~\ref{C-350-24}(ii), the box being the injective image of a box of $\mathbb Z^3$, $y(b)=\sum_p\tau(b,p)\,(\mathrm{d}y)(p)$ with real Stokes coefficients, $|\tau(b,p)|\le4(4L)^t$, $\tau(b,p)=0$ unless all the corners of $p$ lie in the box of $b$. Hence $C_S((b,\alpha),(b',\alpha'))=\delta_{\alpha\alpha'}[C^{\rm ax}_S+C^{\rm g}_S](b,b')$,
\[
C^{\rm ax}_S(b,b')=\sum_{p,p'}\tau(b,p)\tau(b',p')\,\Pi^{\rm fl}_t(p,p'),\qquad C^{\rm g}_S(b,b')=\sum_x\sigma(b,x)\sigma(b',x),
\]
and $C^{\rm g}_S(b,b')=0$ unless an end point of $b$ and one of $b'$ lie in one top block. A box holds at most $6L^{3t}$ plaquettes, $|\Pi^{\rm fl}_t|\le1$ (the orthogonal projections in~\YMMref{(2226)}{818}), and $\sigma(b,\cdot)\ne0$ at no more than $2t$ sites; so $\sup|C_S|\le\mathsf c_\tau^2+2t$, $\mathsf c_\tau=24L^{3t}(4L)^t$. By Prop.~\YMMref{120.6}{821} on the lattice $(S/L^t,t)$ at $s=0$, uniformly in the volume,
\[
|\Pi^{\rm fl}_t(p,q)|\le2L^3C_{\rm tp}L^{-3t}e^{-\delta_{\rm tp}L|x(p)-x(q)|_\infty/L^t}\qquad\text{if }\delta_{\rm tp}L(L-1)|x(p)-x(q)|_\infty\ge(3\log L+\log2)L^t ,
\]
the barycentres being taken in bare units. The barycentre of a plaquette in the box of $b$ lies within $2L^t$ of $b_-$; so if ${\rm dist}(\iota,\iota')\ge R\ge8L^t$ and $\delta_{\rm tp}L(L-1)(R-4L^t)\ge(3\log L+\log2)L^t$, then $C^{\rm g}_S(b,b')=0$ and
\[
|C_S(\iota,\iota')|\le\mathsf c_\tau^2\,2L^{3-3t}C_{\rm tp}\exp\bigl[-\delta_{\rm tp}L(R-4L^t)/L^t\bigr].
\]
At $R=N/24$ these conditions hold, and the exponent is at least $\delta_{\rm tp}L\nu/48$: $R=\frac\nu{24}L^t\ge8L^t$ and $R-4L^t\ge\frac\nu{48}L^t$ as $\nu\ge192$, and $\delta_{\rm tp}L(L-1)\frac\nu{48}\ge3\log L+\log2$ by the second member of $\nu_{\rm W}$. Finally the covariance on $\Lambda_N$ is the periodisation of that on $\Lambda_{N'}$, exactly: with $\Gamma=N\mathbb Z^3/N'\mathbb Z^3$, $|\Gamma|=(N'/N)^3$,
\[
C_N(\pi\iota,\pi\iota')=\sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma}C_{N'}(\iota,\iota'+\gamma).
\]
For $\pi^*$ commutes with $\mathrm{d}$, the $\mathsf Q_k$ and $\xi$, and $\pi$ is $|\Gamma|$ to one on the plaquettes and on the sites, so that $\mathsf H_{N'}(\pi^*A,\pi^*A')=|\Gamma|\,\mathsf H_N(A,A')$ and $\pi^*Y_N=Y_{N'}\cap\pi^*\mathcal E_N$, $\mathcal E_N$ the $1$-forms on $\Lambda_N$; $u=\sum_\gamma C_{N'}(\cdot,\iota'+\gamma)$ is the one solution in $Y_{N'}$ of $\mathsf H_{N'}(u,v)=\sum_\gamma v(\iota'+\gamma)$ for all $v\in Y_{N'}$, a problem invariant under $\Gamma$, so $u=\pi^*u_0$ with $u_0\in Y_N$, and the test functions $v=\pi^*v_0$ give $\mathsf H_N(u_0,v_0)=v_0(\pi\iota')$ for all $v_0\in Y_N$, that is $u_0=C_N(\cdot,\pi\iota')$.

\emph{Near and far.} By Laplace's method in the chart, each of the seven cumulants of $\mathsf g_{m'}$ is, by multilinearity, a sum over at most $64N'^6$ tuples of places of cumulants of homogeneous Taylor polynomials of the terms, of total order $\le10$, in the Gaussian family with the covariance $C_S$; Lem.~\ref{C-350-24}(iii) writes each as a sum over connected pairings of products of lines. A place is near if the set on which its term reads $y$ lies within $N/4$ of the base point of $p'$, and far otherwise; $\pi$ maps the near places of $\Lambda_{N'}$ one to one onto those of $\Lambda_N$, and $p'$, $q'$ are near, as $L^t\le N/192$. A tuple of near places gives the same polynomials on both tori, renamed by $\pi$, so that its cumulant on $\Lambda_N$ is that of the polynomials of $\Lambda_{N'}$ in the covariance $C_N(\pi\iota,\pi\iota')$; its indices lie within $N/2$ of each other, so that by the periodisation the two covariances differ by $\sum_{\gamma\ne0}C_{N'}(\iota,\iota'+\gamma)$, a sum of fewer than $|\Gamma|$ lines of length $\ge N/2$.

If a tuple has a far place, every connected pairing of it contains a line of length $\ge N/24$, on either torus: a path without repetitions in the graph of the pairing leads from the place $p'$ to the far place in at most three edges, the polynomials of one place depend on $y$ on a set of diameter $\le2L^t\le\frac2{192}N$, and so the lengths of the at most three lines of the path add up to more than $\frac N4-7L^t>\frac N8$. By the bound of the lines at $R=N/24$, such a line is at most $\varepsilon_C=2L^{3-3t}C_{\rm tp}\mathsf c_\tau^2e^{-\delta_{\rm tp}L\nu/48}$, and $\sup|C_S|\le2\mathsf c_\tau^2$; the bounds of Lem.~\ref{C-350-24}(iii) then bound the far tuples on each torus by a multiple of $\varepsilon_C$ and the difference at a near tuple by a multiple of $|\Gamma|\varepsilon_C$, with Cauchy's estimate on the polydisc for the coefficients of the polynomials, at most $(108L^{3t}\varsigma_t^{-3})^k$ in the sum of their moduli at the order $k$.

The powers of $L^t\le N'$, the factor $|\Gamma|\le N'^3$ and the number of the tuples are collected in $N'^{237}$, with $C'_{\rm W}$ determined by $L$ and $C_{\rm tp}$. A ball of radius $r\ge8$ holds at most $30r^3$ barycentres of plaquettes, which gives the second display.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The anchor]\label{C-350-15}
Let $\ell=2L^m\ge N_{\mathsf H}$ with $\ell L\ge C_LM$, and $K\ge1$. For all plaquettes $p,q$ of $\Lambda_{\ell L^K}$ and all plaquettes $\tilde p,\tilde q$ of $\mathbb Z^3$ over them whose base points are at sup-distance $\le\frac18\ell L^K$,
\[
|\mathsf g_2[\ell L^K,K](p,q)-\mathsf B^{\rm lat}_1(\tilde p,\tilde q)|\le C_\star\bigl[\ell^{29/2}KL^{-K/2}+\ell^{18}L^{-2K}+\ell^{19}K^2L^{-5K}\bigr]\le3C_\star\ell^{19}KL^{-K/2},
\]
with $C_\star$ determined by the constants and independent of the side; if $\ell^3\le L^K$, the left member is at most $3C_\star\ell^{29/2}KL^{-K/2}$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Write $\mathsf N=\ell L^K$. Distances are those of the bare torus $\Lambda_{\mathsf N}$, in bare units, $|\cdot|$ its Euclidean distance and $|\cdot|_\infty$ its sup distance, $\langle z\rangle=\max\{1,|z|\}$; $x_p$ is the base point of the plaquette $p$, $\langle b-b'\rangle:=\langle b_--b'_-\rangle$, $\langle x_p-b\rangle:=\langle x_p-b_-\rangle$; and $o$ is a fixed site of the top lattice $\mathbb T^{(K)}$.

\emph{The covariant gauge below the flat top.} By Prop.~\ref{C-350-12}(iii) and its proof, $\mathsf g_2[\mathsf N,K](p,q)$ is the coefficient of $\beta^{-3}$ of one gauge-invariant quantity, the covariance of $a_p$ and $a_q$ under $e^{-\beta A}$ on the fibre $\mathcal M^KU=\mathbf 1$ near $\mathbf 1$; so every normalised gauge-fixing factor may be used to compute it. We take the covariant one with the gauge parameter $1$ of Def.~\textup{\ref{IV-73-15}}, with its Faddeev--Popov determinant as in Lem.~\textup{\ref{IV-73-12}}, for the whole bare gauge group modulo the constant transformations, and widen the flat top to its orbit under the gauge transformations of the top lattice: the top field runs over the pure gauges $w(\mu')(c)=\operatorname{Lg}(e^{i\mu'(c_-)}e^{-i\mu'(c_+)})$, $\mu'$ a $\mathfrak g$-valued function on $\mathbb T^{(K)}$ with $\mu'(o)=0$.

The constraint $\operatorname{Lg}\mathcal M^K(e^{i\mathsf a})=w(\mu')$ is linearised in straight frames: the linear part of $\operatorname{Lg}\mathcal M^K(e^{i\cdot})$ is $\mathbf Q^s_K-\mathrm{d}\vartheta_K$, where the straight averages $\mathbf Q^s_K$ of the free template (Section~\YMMref{120}{817}) map the bare $1$-forms to the $1$-forms of the top lattice, with $\mathrm{d}\mathbf Q^s_K=Q^{\rm pl}_K\mathrm{d}$ (Lem.~\YMMref{120.1}{818}), $Q^{\rm pl}_K$ the plaquette averages of the level $K$, and the exact difference $\mathrm{d}\vartheta_K$ on the top lattice goes into $\mu'$. So the linearised constraint is $\mathbf Q^s_K\mathsf a+\mathrm{d}\mu'=0$.

Laplace's method under the constraint, with the harmonic right inverse $\omega\mapsto(\mathsf a_\omega,\mu'_\omega)$ of the linearised constraint, which parametrises the constraint set up to the order three as a graph over the kernel
\[
\hat E=\{(\mathsf a,\mu'):\ \mathbf Q^s_K\mathsf a+\mathrm{d}\mu'=0,\ \mu'(o)=0\},
\]
gives the exact splitting $\mathsf g_2[\mathsf N,K]=\mathsf B^{\hat E}_1+\sum_{i\le11}\mathsf t_i$. Here $\mathsf B^{\hat E}_1$ collects the terms without the inverse: it is the formula \textup{(\ref{IV-73-24})} of $\mathsf B_1^{\rm lat}$ at the gauge parameter $1$, with the same vertices and measure terms, its kernels $\mathsf C,\mathsf E,\Pi$ being those of the centred Gaussian field $(\mathsf a,\mu')$ on $\hat E\otimes\mathfrak g$ with the form $\frac12\|\mathrm{d}\mathsf a\|^2+\frac12\|\mathrm{d}^*\mathsf a\|^2$, diagonal in the colours, and its kernels $\mathsf g,\mathsf D$ being formed with the Green's function $\mathsf G^{\rm tor}$ of $\mathrm{d}^*\mathrm{d}$ on the torus off the constants.

The $\mathsf t_i$ hold the inverse: $\mathsf t_1,\dots,\mathsf t_5$ come from the observables, $\mathsf t_6$, $\mathsf t_7$ from the cubic vertex, $\mathsf t_8$ from the quadratic form at the correction, $\mathsf t_9$, $\mathsf t_{10}$ from the traces of the Jacobian of the constraint, and $\mathsf t_{11}$ from the measure of $\mu'$; each is a cumulant of polynomials in the Gaussian field, in which the quadratic and cubic terms of the block average enter through the response $\omega\mapsto\mathsf a_\omega$ of the field to a source $\omega$ on the top lattice.

\emph{The lines.} Let $\mathsf C^{\rm tor}$ be the inverse of $\mathrm{d}^*\mathrm{d}+\mathrm{d}\mathrm{d}^*$ off the constant $1$-forms and $0$ on them, and $\mathsf S_0:=\mathsf C^{\rm tor}\mathrm{d}^*$ on the exact curvatures: $\mathsf S_0F$ is the primitive of $F$ in the range of $\mathrm{d}^*$, and $\mathrm{d}\mathsf S_0=1$. The $\mathsf a$-members of $\hat E$ are the $\mathsf a=\mathsf S_0F+\mathrm{d}\lambda$ with $F$ a curvature whose plaquette averages of the level $K$ vanish; in the Gaussian measure $F$ and $\lambda$ are independent, with the covariances $\Pi^{\rm tp}_0-\Pi^{\rm tp}_K$ and $(\mathsf G^{\rm tor})^2$. So the covariance of $\mathsf a$ is $C_{\hat E}=\mathsf C^{\rm tor}-\mathsf S_0\Pi^{\rm tp}_K\mathsf S_0^{\mathsf T}$, with $\mathrm{d}C_{\hat E}\,\mathrm{d}^*=\Pi:=\Pi^{\rm tp}_0-\Pi^{\rm tp}_K$; and the response is $\mathsf a_\omega=\mathsf S_0\mathsf H^{\rm cv}_K\omega$ plus a constant $1$-form, with $\mathrm{d}\mathsf a_\omega=\mathsf H^{\rm cv}_K\omega$, the curvature response of the level $K$, and $\mathrm{d}^*\mathsf a_\omega=0$.

The kernels $\mathsf C^{\rm tor}$, $\mathrm{d}\mathsf C^{\rm tor}$ and $\Pi^{\rm tp}_0=\mathrm{d}\mathsf C^{\rm tor}\mathrm{d}^*$ are Fourier sums $\mathsf N^{-3}\sum_{k\ne0}e^{ik\cdot z}\sigma(k)$ over the non-zero modes of the torus, $z$ the difference of the base points, with the symbols $\sigma$ of the lines of $\mathbb Z^3$ (Lem.~\textup{\ref{IV-73-51}}) at the gauge parameter $1$, of the classes $\mathcal S^{-2}$, $\mathcal S^{-1}$, $\mathcal S^0$; by Lem.~\textup{\ref{IV-73-75}}(a) they are at most $c_{\rm T}\langle z\rangle^{-1}$, $c_{\rm T}\langle z\rangle^{-2}$, $c_{\rm T}\langle z\rangle^{-3}$, with one number $c_{\rm T}$ for all sides. With $|\Pi^{\rm tp}_K(p,q)|\le CL^{-3K}=C\ell^3\mathsf N^{-3}$ uniformly in the volume (Prop.~\YMMref{120.5}{821}) and $\sum_z\langle z\rangle^{-2}\le14\mathsf N$ over the torus, the corrections $\mathsf S_0\Pi^{\rm tp}_K\mathsf S_0^{\mathsf T}$, $\Pi^{\rm tp}_K\mathsf S_0^{\mathsf T}$ and $\Pi^{\rm tp}_K$ are at most $c\,\ell^3\mathsf N^{-1}$, $c\,\ell^3\mathsf N^{-2}$ and $c\,\ell^3\mathsf N^{-3}$, every distance of the torus is below $\mathsf N$, and $|\Pi|\le1$, $\Pi$ being the kernel of an orthogonal projection (the orthogonal projections in~\YMMref{(2226)}{818}).

So, with $\mathsf c_0=c\,\ell^3$, the lines obey
\[
|C_{\hat E}(b,b')|\le\mathsf c_0\langle b-b'\rangle^{-1},\qquad|\mathrm{d}C_{\hat E}(p,b)|\le\mathsf c_0\langle x_p-b\rangle^{-2},\qquad|\Pi(p,q)|\le\min\{1,\mathsf c_0\langle x_p-x_q\rangle^{-3}\},
\]
and the kernels $\mathsf g,\mathsf D$ formed with $\mathsf G^{\rm tor}$ obey the majorants of \textup{(\ref{IV-73-56})} in the same way. The response has $|\mathsf a_\omega|\le C\ell L^{-K}$ and $|\mathrm{d}\mathsf a_\omega|\le CL^{-2K}$ in the sup norm of $\omega$: the latter from the row sums $\le CL^{-2K}$ of the response kernel at every admissible side (equation~\YMMref{(2234)}{820}, whose row sum follows by summing its exponential kernel bound), the former from these and the row sums $\le c\,\mathsf N$ of $\mathsf S_0$.

\emph{The Gaussian member against $\mathbb Z^3$.} Let $\mathcal L_{\mathsf N}$ be a Fourier sum over the non-zero modes of the torus of side $\mathsf N$ with a symbol of the class $\mathcal S^s$, $s>-3$, and $\mathcal L_\infty$ the kernel of $\mathbb Z^3$ with the same symbol. Then $\sum_{v\in\{0,1\}^3}\mathcal L_{2\mathsf N}(z+\mathsf Nv)=\mathcal L_{\mathsf N}(z)$ exactly, as $\sum_ve^{ik\cdot\mathsf Nv}$ is $8$ on the modes of the smaller torus and $0$ on the others; for $|z|_\infty\le\frac34\mathsf N$ the seven images with $v\ne0$ are at most $C\mathsf N^{-3-s}$ each, by Lem.~\textup{\ref{IV-73-75}}(a), and telescoping over the sides $2^i\mathsf N$, with Lem.~\textup{\ref{IV-73-75}}(b), gives $|\mathcal L_{\mathsf N}(z)-\mathcal L_\infty(z)|\le C\mathsf N^{-3-s}$.

With the three corrections from $\Pi^{\rm tp}_K$, the difference at $|z|_\infty\le\frac34\mathsf N$ between a line of $\mathsf B^{\hat E}_1$ and the line of $\mathbb Z^3$ at the same base points is at most $C\mathsf N^{-1/2}$ times the majorant $\mathsf c_0\langle z\rangle^{-n}$ of the line with its exponent $n$ lowered by $\frac12$. The two-loop sums of \textup{(\ref{IV-73-24})}, written out over monomials, connected pairings and places by Lems.~\textup{\ref{IV-73-21}} and~\textup{\ref{IV-73-53}}, converge absolutely with these majorants, uniformly in the side, also with one line weakened by $\frac12$, as in Lem.~\textup{\ref{IV-73-55}}(ii), the sums over a torus being bounded by those over $\mathbb Z^3$ at the nearest images of the arguments: the sum is at most $C\mathsf c_0^5$.

The terms all of whose places lie within $\frac14\mathsf N$ of $x_p$ in the sup distance correspond one to one on the torus and on $\mathbb Z^3$, with the same monomials, pairings and coefficients, and together they differ by at most $C\mathsf N^{-1/2}\mathsf c_0^5$. Every other term has a place that is the end of a line whose other end is $p$ or $q$, of length $\ge\frac1{16}\mathsf N$, as $|x_p-x_q|_\infty\le\frac18\mathsf N$; so the sum of the other terms is at most $(16/\mathsf N)^{1/2}C\mathsf c_0^5$ on each side. Hence $|\mathsf B^{\hat E}_1-\mathsf B^{\rm lat}_1|\le C\ell^{15}(\ell L^K)^{-1/2}$, $\mathsf B^{\rm lat}_1$ being taken at the gauge parameter $1$, as in \textup{(\ref{IV-73-25})}.

\emph{The other terms.} Each $\mathsf t_i$ is at most $C\ell^{q_i}$ times one of the rates $KL^{-K}$, $K^2L^{-2K}$, $L^{-3K/2}$, $KL^{-K/2}$, $L^{-K/2}$, $L^{-5K/2}$, $KL^{-3K}$, $L^{-2K}$, $K^2L^{-5K}$, none worse than $KL^{-K/2}$, and $\sum_i|\mathsf t_i|\le C[\ell^{13}KL^{-K/2}+\ell^{18}L^{-2K}+\ell^{19}K^2L^{-5K}]$. The side enters only through $\mathsf c_0$, through paths of at most $\frac32\ell$ bonds on the top lattice, through one sum of $\langle\cdot\rangle^{-2}$ over the torus, through the number of plaquettes and through the dimension $9\ell^3$ of the top fields; no inverse on the top lattice is bounded by a norm, and so $C_\star$ does not depend on the side. For $\ell^3\le L^K$ the last two members are below the first.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[One lattice is enough]\label{C-350-16}
Let $0<g\le\gamma$ and $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$. There are integers $K_0,K_\flat$ and numbers $C_\diamond<\infty$, $d_{\rm K}>0$, depending on $g$, $\ell$ and the constants, such that, with $K_\sharp(d)=\max\{K_0,K_\flat,\lceil3600\log_L(\sqrt3M/d)\rceil\}$: for $0<d\le1$, $20d\le\ell$, $\vartheta\in(0,1)$, $(f,h)\in\mathfrak T_{T_\ell}(d;\vartheta)$, $b\in[\gamma^{-2},L^2(g^{-2}+\bar B)]$ and $K'\ge K\ge K_\sharp(d)$,
\[
|S^T_{2;K',\ell,L^{K'}b}-S^T_{2;K,\ell,L^Kb}|(f,h)\le C_\diamond\vartheta^{-2}d^{178}\eta,
\]
also with $S_2^{(\ell,b)}$ for the first member; and for $0<d\le d_{\rm K}$, $s(d)<K_\sharp(d)$ and $(\sqrt3M/d)^{3600}\le L^{K_\sharp(d)}\le d^{-3601}$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Cor.~\YMMref{117.1}{812}, equation~\YMMref{(2207)}{812} gives, for $K'\ge K\ge K_1(\mathsf d_\infty)$ and the labels of the interval $[\gamma^{-2},L^2(g^{-2}+\bar B)]$,
\[
\begin{multlined}
|S^T_{2;K'}-S^T_{2;K}|(f,h)\le\mathsf C'\ell^9K^{\mathsf p_2}L^{-K/10}\|f\|_\sharp\|h\|_\sharp,\qquad\|f\|_\sharp=\max\{\|f\|_\infty,40M\operatorname{Lip}f\} \\
\le40M\|f\|_\infty/(\vartheta d),
\end{multlined}
\]
with $\mathsf C'$ and $\mathsf p_2=6p_0+\frac12$ the constants of that statement; the limit $K'\to\infty$ exists along the full sequence. Here $\mathsf d_\infty\ge d/\sqrt3$ is the sup distance of the supports, and $K_1(\mathsf d_\infty)$ (the constants and thresholds in Thm.~\YMMref{AR}{810}) is the least integer $\ge K_0$ from which on, with $u=\lceil K/1800\rceil$, the two threshold inequalities at the end of the proof of Thm.~\YMMref{AR}{810} hold: $\mathsf d_\infty L^u\ge6M$, and $c_9\ell^3L^{3u}e^{-\mathsf d_\infty L^u/M}\le\frac12\mathsf C\ell^9K^{\mathsf p_2}L^{-K/10}$, with the numbers $c_9$, $\mathsf C$ of the two threshold inequalities at the end of the proof of Thm.~\YMMref{AR}{810} at $n=2$: $\mathsf C$ is the constant \YMMref{(2206)}{811}, and $c_9\ell^3L^{3u}$ is the factor of $e^{-\mathsf d_\infty L^u/M}$ in the left member of the second condition.

Let $K\ge K_\sharp(d)$ and $y=K/1800$. The second condition follows, in logarithms, from $\mathsf d_\infty L^u/M\ge c_{10}+(3u+\frac K{10})\log L$, $c_{10}=\max\{0,\log(2c_9/\mathsf C)\}$, and this from the two inequalities $L^{y/2}\ge c_{10}+3\log L+200y\log L$, which defines $K_\flat=\lceil1800y_0\rceil$ through the least $y_0$ from which on it holds, and $L^{y/2}\ge\sqrt3M/d$, which is $K\ge3600\log_L(\sqrt3M/d)$; the first condition follows from the same product. So $K_1(\mathsf d_\infty)\le K_\sharp(d)$, and $K^{\mathsf p_2}L^{-K/10}\le cL^{-K/20}\le c(d/\sqrt3M)^{180}$, which gives the factor $C_\diamond\vartheta^{-2}d^{178}$. By the minimality of $s(d)$, $L^{s(d)}d<LC_{W,0}A_0^2(\log L^{s(d)}+\log b_+)^{2p_0}$, so that $L^{s(d)}\le d^{-2}$ for small $d$; and $(\sqrt3M/d)^{3600}\le L^{K_\sharp(d)}<L(\sqrt3M/d)^{3600}\le d^{-3601}$ for small $d$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The agreement of states]\label{C-350-21}
Let $0<g\le\gamma^{\rm sd}_W$, $(K,\beta)$ a datum at $g$ with $K\ge3$ and label $b$, $\vartheta\in(0,1)$, and $0<d\le\frac1{180}$ with $a_K\le9d$. A \emph{state at $g$ at $(K,\beta)$} is the periodically extended torus measure $\tilde\mu_{K,\ell',\beta}$ of a side $\ell'\in\mathfrak L(g)$, or a periodic Gibbs state at $(a_K,\beta)$; $S^T_2[\tilde\mu_{K,\ell',\beta}](\tilde f,\tilde h)$ is $S^T_{2;K,\ell',\beta}$ at the periodisations of $\tilde f,\tilde h$ on $T_{\ell'}$. Put $\mathsf d_\star(g,\vartheta)=4\sqrt3M\vartheta^{-1}(K^\vee_{\rm L}/K^\vee_{\rm Q})^2g^{-2}$, with the pair $K^\vee_{\rm L},K^\vee_{\rm Q}$ of equation~\YMMref{(2166)}{800}. There are $\mathsf Q^{\rm T}_2(g)\ge1$ and $C^{\rm T}_2(g)<\infty$, depending on $g$, on the fixed radius $\varrho$ and the common sourced choice of Section~\YMMref{82}{665} specified at the beginning of this section, and on no $K$, $\beta$, side, state, $d$, $\vartheta$, pair or position, with the following property.

Let $(\tilde f,\tilde h)$ be real Lipschitz functions on $\mathbb R^3$, neither $0$, each vanishing off a closed ball of radius $d$, with disjoint sets $\{\tilde f\ne0\}$, $\{\tilde h\ne0\}$, both vanishing off one ball of radius $9d$, and with $\operatorname{Lip}\tilde f\le\|\tilde f\|_\infty/(\vartheta d)$, $\operatorname{Lip}\tilde h\le\|\tilde h\|_\infty/(\vartheta d)$; no sign and no lower bound of the integrals is asked. Then for every state $\mathfrak s$ at $g$ at $(K,\beta)$
\[
|S^T_2[\mathfrak s]-S^T_2[\tilde\mu_{K,\ell_g,\beta}]|(\tilde f,\tilde h)\le(30d)^3\cdot2\,\mathsf Q^{\rm T}_2(g)^2\,\mathsf A_\star(d)^{-2}\eta,
\]
with a number $\mathsf A_\star(d)$ of the order $(b\vartheta d)^{1/2}$ formed with the datum; and for $d\le\mathsf d_\star(g,\vartheta)$, in particular for the pairs of $\mathfrak T_{\mathbb R^3}(d;\vartheta)$,
\begin{equation}\label{C-350-17}
\bigl|S^T_2[\mathfrak s]-S^T_2[\tilde\mu_{K,\ell_g,\beta}]\bigr|(\tilde f,\tilde h)\le C^{\rm T}_2(g)\vartheta^{-1}d^2b^{-2}\eta .
\end{equation}
Any two states at $g$ at $(K,\beta)$ differ at such pairs by at most twice this.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Let $\ell'=\ell_g=2L^m$, $\mu'=\tilde\mu_{K,\ell',\beta}$ and $\mathsf l=\ell'/2=L^m$. Let $x_1$ be the centre of the ball of radius $9d$ off which $\tilde f$ and $\tilde h$ vanish, and let $o\in a_K\mathbb Z^3$ be a site with $|o_\mu-(x_1)_\mu|\le\frac12a_K$ for $\mu=1,2,3$. Consider the board of the least torus: the eight cells $\square_{\mathbf k}=o+\mathsf l\mathbf k+[-\frac{\mathsf l}2,\frac{\mathsf l}2]^3$, $\mathbf k\in\{0,1\}^3$, with the reflections $x_\mu\mapsto2o_\mu+\mathsf l-x_\mu$ in the planes $x_\mu=o_\mu\pm\frac{\mathsf l}2$, which carry one cell into another. As $o\in a_K\mathbb Z^3$ and $\mathsf l$ is a multiple of $a_K$, these reflections are maps of the lattice, and they carry plaquettes to plaquettes.

The source families used below are those of
Prop.~\ref{prop:levelwise-source-density}, at the common
sourced choice fixed in this section. Its numerical source
conditions are the ones retained in
\S\ref{sec:levelwise-first-creation}.
The radius condition for Prop.~\ref{prop:first-creation-envelopes}
holds at the present coupling: $g\le\gamma_W^{\rm sd}\le
\gamma_W^{\rm ref}$ and equation~\YMMref{(2326)}{845} give
$\varepsilon(x_t)\le c_A\alpha_0/(8MB_3)$ at every level.
Also $\mathsf l\ge L^2M$ by the least-side definition,
so both entries in the minimum defining $d_*(t)+1$ in
\eqref{eq:first-creation-radius} are at least $4$.
The calibrated rarity hypotheses are those of the same real
history, as in Prop.~\ref{prop:ward-fixed-volume-rarity}.
Thus Cor.~\ref{cor:packed-source-coefficients} applies
without a further restriction on this datum.

As $1+\frac12a_K<\frac12\mathsf l$, the ball $\mathbb B(x_1,1)$ lies in the interior of $\square_0$; the signed sums of (3) below vanish off it. Its images under the reflections are eight balls of radius $1$, one in each cell, with the centres $o_\mu+\mathsf lk_\mu+(-1)^{k_\mu}(x_1-o)_\mu$ ($\mu=1,2,3$); any two of these centres differ, in a coordinate $\mu$ in which their cells differ, by $\pm(\mathsf l-2(x_1-o)_\mu)$ modulo $2\mathsf l$, so that they lie at a sup distance at least $\mathsf l-2|(x_1-o)_\mu|\ge\mathsf l-a_K$ on $T_{\ell'}$.

(1)

\emph{One cell against the least torus.} For a bounded
complex Borel function $F$ of the inner bonds of one cell,
the reflected copies, conjugated on odd reflection parity,
satisfy
\[
 \|F\|_{\rm ch}^8=
       \mu'\Bigl(\prod_{\mathbf k\in\{0,1\}^3}F^{[\mathbf k]}\Bigr)
       \ge0.
\]
For $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$,
{\cite[Cor.~B.1]{YMM2}} gives
\[
 |\tilde\mu_{K,\ell,\beta}(F)|
 \le\|F\|_{{\rm ch},\ell}
 \le\|F\|_{\rm ch}\exp[\mathsf l^3(p_{\ell'}-p_\ell)].
\]
{\cite[Lem.~N.1]{YMM2}} bounds
$p_{\ell'}-p_\ell$ by
$C_{\rm gap}+C_{\rm S}+C_g\le2C_{\rm S}+C_g$.
Thus one may take
$\mathsf Q_0=\exp[\mathsf l^3(2C_{\rm S}+C_g)]\ge1$.
For a periodic Gibbs state, Prop.~\YMMref{91.9}{705}
gives
\[
 |\mathfrak s(F)|\le
 \liminf_{r\to\infty}\|F\|_{{\rm ch},\ell_gL^r}
 \le\mathsf Q_0\|F\|_{\rm ch}.
\]
The constants are those of {\cite[Lem.~N.1]{YMM2}},
with $C_{\rm S}\ge C_{\rm gap}$ chosen there. In particular
$\mathsf Q_0$ is independent of the cutoff and the larger side.

This is the one place where Thms.~\YMMref{AJ}{673} and~\YMMref{AD}{607} enter, and the place through which $\mathsf Q^{\rm T}_2(g)$ and $C^{\rm T}_2(g)$ depend on the radius and on the choice of the longer list.

(2)

\emph{Only linking cumulants are left.} With $X_a=\mathcal O(F_a)$, $\mathcal P_a=X_a-\mu'(X_a)$ and $\mathcal P_{12}=\mathcal P_1\mathcal P_2-S^T_2[\mu'](F_1,F_2)$ one has $S^T_2[\mathfrak s](F_1,F_2)-S^T_2[\mu'](F_1,F_2)=\mathfrak s(\mathcal P_{12})-\mathfrak s(\mathcal P_1)\mathfrak s(\mathcal P_2)$. Expanding $\mu'(\prod_{\mathbf k}\mathcal P_{12}^{[\mathbf k]})$ in joint cumulants of the sixteen copies $X_{a,\mathbf k}$, the blocks that stay in one cell cancel exactly, because $\mathcal P_{12}$ is centred by the covariance of $\mu'$ itself; what is left is a sum, over the at most $\mathsf{Bl}_{16}$ partitions into linking blocks (blocks that meet two cells), of products of linking cumulants, $\mathsf{Bl}_n$ being the Bell numbers.

So if every linking cumulant of the copies is at most $C_{\rm LK}\prod u_a$, then $|S^T_2[\mathfrak s]-S^T_2[\mu']|(F_1,F_2)\le[\mathsf Q_0\mathsf{Bl}_{16}^{1/8}+\mathsf Q_0^2\mathsf{Bl}_8^{1/4}]C_{\rm LK}u_1u_2\le2\mathsf Q_1^2u_1u_2$, $\mathsf Q_1=\mathsf Q_0\mathsf{Bl}_{16}^{1/8}C_{\rm LK}$.

(3)
