In the third line the four numbers in the bracket come from the monomials $A^2$, $A'^2$, $-2PA$, $-2PA'$ of $(A+A'-P)^2$, the others having the value $0$; thus $\mathsf L_5\bigl((A+A'-P)^2\bigr)=\frac13+1-2-2=-\frac83$, the value used in the last line. Consequently
\[
\mathcal R[F_5]=-2\bigl(-\tfrac73\bigr)+3\cdot0-6\cdot\tfrac1{12}+3\bigl(-\tfrac23\bigr)=\tfrac{14}3-\tfrac52=\tfrac{13}6 .
\]

\emph{Step 9: values for the denominator $AA'BB'C$.} For a monomial $\mathsf m=P^nA^iA'^{i'}B^jB'^{j'}C^m$ of degree $3$ we put $\mathsf L(\mathsf m):=\mathcal R[\mathsf m/AA'BB'C]$. Now $(a_1,\dots,a_5)=(1-i,1-i',1-j,1-j',1-m)$ and $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3)=(2-i-i',\,2-j-j',\,1-m)$, and again $\mathsf L(\mathsf m)\ne0$ requires $m=0$. Let $X\in\{A,A'\}$ and $Y\in\{B,B'\}$. The values are as follows.
\begin{itemize}
\item $n=1$: $\mathsf L(PXY)=1$.
\item $n=0$, $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3)=(0,1,1)$ (then $i+i'=2$, $j+j'=1$, value $\mathsf q(1-i')+\frac23(1-i')(1-j')$): $\mathsf L(A^2B)=\frac13+\frac23=1$, $\mathsf L(A^2B')=\frac13$, $\mathsf L(A'^2B)=1-\frac23=\frac13$, $\mathsf L(A'^2B')=1$, $\mathsf L(AA'Y)=0$.
\item $n=0$, $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3)=(1,0,1)$ (then $i+i'=1$, $j+j'=2$, value $\mathsf q(1-j')+\frac23(1-i')(1-j')$): $\mathsf L(AB^2)=1$, $\mathsf L(A'B^2)=\frac13$, $\mathsf L(AB'^2)=\frac13$, $\mathsf L(A'B'^2)=1$, $\mathsf L(XBB')=0$.
\end{itemize}
All other monomials of degree $3$ have the value $0$: those containing $C$ or $P^2$, and those of the forms $PX_1X_2$, $PY_1Y_2$, $X_1X_2X_3$, $Y_1Y_2Y_3$ with $X_i\in\{A,A'\}$, $Y_i\in\{B,B'\}$. These values are invariant under the exchange of primes and under $(A,A')\leftrightarrow(B,B')$.

\emph{Step 10: $\Gamma=1$, reduction.} As in Step~4, $T_{\mu\nu}=V_2(k,\mathsf p-k)_{\mu\nu}=a\,\delta_{\mu\nu}-k_\nu k'_\mu$, and $k_\mu T_{\mu\nu}=0=T_{\mu\nu}k'_\nu$. Similarly,
\[
S_{\rho\sigma}:=V_2(-l,l-\mathsf p)_{\rho\sigma}=V_2(-l,l')_{\rho\sigma}=b\,\delta_{\rho\sigma}-l_\sigma l'_\rho,\qquad l_\rho S_{\rho\sigma}=0=S_{\rho\sigma}l'_\sigma .
\]
The tensor $V_3(-k,l,q)_{\mu\rho\alpha}=\delta_{\mu\alpha}(l-2k)_\rho+\delta_{\mu\rho}(k+l)_\alpha+\delta_{\rho\alpha}(k-2l)_\mu$ is contracted with $T_{\mu\nu}S_{\rho\sigma}$, which annihilates the terms with $l_\rho$ and with $k_\mu$; in this contraction it may therefore be replaced by
\[
\mathsf W_{\mu\rho\alpha}:=-2k_\rho\,\delta_{\mu\alpha}+(k+l)_\alpha\,\delta_{\mu\rho}-2l_\mu\,\delta_{\rho\alpha}.
\]
Likewise, $V_3(k-\mathsf p,\mathsf p-l,l-k)_{\nu\sigma\alpha}=V_3(k',-l',l'-k')_{\nu\sigma\alpha}=\delta_{\nu\alpha}(2k'-l')_\sigma-\delta_{\nu\sigma}(k'+l')_\alpha+\delta_{\sigma\alpha}(2l'-k')_\nu$, contracted with $T_{\mu\nu}S_{\rho\sigma}$, may be replaced by $-\mathsf W'_{\nu\sigma\alpha}$, where $\mathsf W'$ denotes $\mathsf W$ with $(k',l')$ in place of $(k,l)$. Hence
\[
F_1=+\tfrac12\,N'/AA'BB'C,\qquad N':=T_{\mu\nu}S_{\rho\sigma}\,\mathsf W_{\mu\rho\alpha}\mathsf W'_{\nu\sigma\alpha}.
\]
We use the bilinear forms
\[
T(X,Y):=X_\mu T_{\mu\nu}Y_\nu=a\,X\cdot Y-(k'\cdot X)(k\cdot Y),\qquad S(X,Y):=X_\rho S_{\rho\sigma}Y_\sigma=b\,X\cdot Y-(l'\cdot X)(l\cdot Y),
\]
the vectors $\mathsf s_\sigma:=k_\rho S_{\rho\sigma}=(bk-fl)_\sigma$ and $\mathsf t_\rho:=S_{\rho\sigma}k'_\sigma=(bk'-f'l')_\rho$, and the identities $T_{\mu\mu}=2a$, $S_{\rho\rho}=2b$, $T_{\mu\nu}S_{\mu\nu}=3ab-ab-ab+ee'=ab+ee'$. Let $N'_{ij}$ be the contribution to $N'$ of the $i$-th term of $\mathsf W$ and the $j$-th term of $\mathsf W'$. Then
\[
\begin{gathered}
N'_{11}=4T_{\mu\mu}S(k,k')=8a(ab-ff'),\qquad\\
 N'_{33}=4T(l,l')S_{\rho\rho}=8b(ab-ff'),\qquad\\
 N'_{22}=(k+l)\cdot(k'+l')\,(ab+ee'),\\
N'_{13}=4T(\mathsf s,l'),\quad\\
 N'_{31}=4T(l,\mathsf t),\quad\\
 N'_{12}=-2T(k'+l',\mathsf s),\quad\\
 N'_{21}=-2T(\mathsf t,k+l),\\
N'_{23}=-2\,T_{\mu\nu}l'_\nu\,S_{\mu\sigma}(k+l)_\sigma,\qquad\\
 N'_{32}=-2\,l_\mu T_{\mu\nu}\,(k'+l')_\rho S_{\rho\nu}.
\end{gathered}
\]
Under the exchange of primes, $T_{\mu\nu}$ goes over into $T_{\nu\mu}$, so that $T(X,Y)$ becomes the value of $T$ at the images of $Y$ and $X$, in this order, and $\mathsf s$ goes over into $\mathsf t$; hence $N'_{13}$ goes over into $N'_{31}$, and $N'_{12}$ into $N'_{21}$. Under the exchange $(k,k')\leftrightarrow(l,l')$, the tensors $T_{\mu\nu}$ and $S_{\mu\nu}$ are interchanged; hence $N'_{12}=-2(k'+l')_\mu T_{\mu\nu}k_\rho S_{\rho\nu}$ goes over into $N'_{32}$, $N'_{21}=-2S_{\mu\sigma}k'_\sigma T_{\mu\nu}(k+l)_\nu$ into $N'_{23}$, and $N'_{11}$ into $N'_{33}$. By the invariance of the values in Step~9,
\[
\mathsf L(N'_{33})=\mathsf L(N'_{11}),\qquad\mathsf L(N'_{31})=\mathsf L(N'_{13}),\qquad\mathsf L(N'_{21})=\mathsf L(N'_{32})=\mathsf L(N'_{23})=\mathsf L(N'_{12}).
\]

\emph{Step 11: $\Gamma=1$, values.} By Step~9 we may set $C=0$. Then
\[
4(ab-ff')=(A+A'-P)(B+B'-P)-(A'+B-P)(A+B'-P)=AB'+A'B-AA'-BB'=:\mathsf D .
\]
\begin{itemize}
\item $N'_{11}=(A+A'-P)\,\mathsf D$. Of its monomials only $A^2B'$, $A'^2B$, $-PAB'$ and $-PA'B$ have non-zero values, and $\mathsf L(N'_{11})=\frac13+\frac13-1-1=-\frac43$.
\item $N'_{13}$: since $\mathsf s\cdot l'=bf-fb=0$ and $k'\cdot\mathsf s=ab-ff'$, we have $N'_{13}=-4f(ab-ff')=-\frac12(A'+B-P)\,\mathsf D$. In $(A'+B-P)\,\mathsf D$ the monomials with non-zero values are $A'^2B$, $A'B^2$, $-PAB'$ and $-PA'B$; they give $\frac13+\frac13-2=-\frac43$, and therefore $\mathsf L(N'_{13})=\frac23$.
\item $N'_{22}$: here $(k+l)\cdot(k'+l')=a+f+f'+b=A+A'+B+B'-2P$, and
\[
\begin{multlined}
4(ab+ee')=(A+A'-P)(B+B'-P)+(A+B)(A'+B')=\mathsf E+AA'+BB'-P(A \\
+A'+B+B')+P^2,\qquad\mathsf E:=AB+2AB'+2A'B+A'B' .
\end{multlined}
\]
We have $\mathsf L\bigl[(A+A'+B+B')\,\mathsf E\bigr]=(1+\frac23)+(\frac23+1)+(1+\frac23)+(\frac23+1)=\frac{20}3$, the four contributions coming from $A(AB+2AB')$, $A'(2A'B+A'B')$, $B(AB+2A'B)$ and $B'(2AB'+A'B')$. Further, $\mathsf L\bigl[(A+A'+B+B')(AA'+BB')\bigr]=0$, $\mathsf L\bigl[-P(A+A'+B+B')^2\bigr]=-2\cdot4=-8$ and $\mathsf L[-2P\,\mathsf E]=-2\cdot6=-12$, while the remaining monomials, which contain $P^2$ or have one of the forms $PX_1X_2$, $PY_1Y_2$, have the value $0$. Hence $\mathsf L(N'_{22})=\frac14\bigl(\frac{20}3-20\bigr)=-\frac{10}3$.
\item $N'_{12}=-2\bigl[a\,(k'+l')\cdot\mathsf s-\bigl(k'\cdot(k'+l')\bigr)(k\cdot\mathsf s)\bigr]$. Since $(k'+l')\cdot\mathsf s=ab-ff'$, the first term is $a(ab-ff')=\frac18(A+A'-P)\,\mathsf D$, with the value $\frac18\cdot(-\frac43)=-\frac16$. Next, $k'\cdot(k'+l')=A'+e'=\frac12(3A'+B')$ and
\[
k\cdot\mathsf s=bA-fe=\tfrac14\bigl[2A(B+B'-P)-(A'+B-P)(A+B)\bigr]=\tfrac14\bigl[AB+2AB'-AA'-A'B-B^2-PA+PB\bigr].
\]
In $(3A'+B')\bigl[AB+2AB'-AA'-A'B-B^2-PA+PB\bigr]$ the monomials with non-zero values are $-3A'^2B$, $-3A'B^2$, $+3PA'B$, $+2AB'^2$ and $-PAB'$; they give $-1-1+3+\frac23-1=\frac23$. The second term, $\frac18(3A'+B')\bigl[\cdots\bigr]$, therefore has the value $\frac18\cdot\frac23=\frac1{12}$, and $\mathsf L(N'_{12})=-2\bigl(-\frac16-\frac1{12}\bigr)=\frac12$.
\item Summing, with the identities at the end of Step~10,
\[
\mathsf L(N')=2\bigl(-\tfrac43\bigr)+2\cdot\tfrac23-\tfrac{10}3+4\cdot\tfrac12=-\tfrac83,\qquad\text{hence}\qquad\mathcal R[F_1]=\tfrac12\bigl(-\tfrac83\bigr)=-\tfrac43 .
\]
\end{itemize}

\emph{Step 12: the sum.} Adding the six values obtained in Steps~2, 3, 5, 6, 8 and~11, we find
\[
\sum_{\Gamma=1}^6\mathcal R[F_\Gamma]=-\tfrac43-\tfrac{13}{12}-\tfrac1{12}+0+\tfrac{13}6-\tfrac13=\frac{-16-13-1+26-4}{12}=-\tfrac23 ,
\]
which completes the proof of \eqref{IV-73-97}.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{The value: $\kappa^{\mathrm{lat}}$ and $c_1$}

Adding the six contributions of Prop.~\ref{IV-73-94} and Prop.~\ref{IV-73-96}, we now obtain the value of the constant $\kappa^{\mathrm{lat}}$ of Thm.~\ref{IV-73-71}, and with it the number $c_1$.

\begin{theorem}[The value of $\kappa^{\mathrm{lat}}$]\label{IV-73-98}
The number $\kappa^{\mathrm{lat}}$ of Thm.~\ref{IV-73-71} is
\[
\kappa^{\mathrm{lat}}=\frac3{2\pi^3}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
In \eqref{IV-73-72}, $\kappa^{\mathrm{lat}}$ is the sum of the numbers $\kappa_\Gamma^{\mathrm{lat}}$ of Lem.~\ref{IV-73-70}. Expressing each of them by \eqref{IV-73-95} and inserting the sum from \eqref{IV-73-97}, we obtain
\[
\kappa^{\mathrm{lat}}=\sum_{\Gamma=1}^6\kappa_\Gamma^{\mathrm{lat}}=-\frac3{32\pi^3}\cdot24\cdot\sum_{\Gamma=1}^6\mathcal R[F_\Gamma]=-\frac3{32\pi^3}\cdot24\cdot\Bigl(-\frac23\Bigr)=\frac{48}{32\pi^3}=\frac3{2\pi^3},
\]
as asserted.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[The number $c_1$]\label{IV-73-99}
We put
\[
c_1:=\frac{\kappa^{\mathrm{lat}}}{\mathsf c_2},
\]
where $\kappa^{\mathrm{lat}}$ is the number of Thm.~\ref{IV-73-71} and $\mathsf c_2=\frac{3\dim\mathfrak g}{16\pi^2}=\frac9{16\pi^2}$ is the leading constant fixed in \S\ref{C-350-1}; here $\dim\mathfrak g=3=\mathsf n$.

This fixes the coefficient used in \S\ref{C-350-1}; it does not by itself give a cutoff-uniform remainder for the interacting measure.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The number $c_1$]\label{IV-73-100}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[beginpenalty=10000]
\item[\textup{(a)}] $c_1=\dfrac8{3\pi}$, and $\mathsf c_2c_1=\dfrac3{2\pi^3}$.
\item[\textup{(b)}] There is a pure constant $C$ with the following property. Let $\mathsf d>0$, $\vartheta\in(0,1)$, $(f,h)\in\mathfrak T_{\mathbb R^3}(\mathsf d;\vartheta)$ and $0<a\le\mathsf d$, the class of test pairs and the functional $\mathcal K_5$ being those of Cor.~\ref{IV-73-73}. Then
\begin{equation}\label{IV-73-101}
\Bigl|\frac{\mathsf P_1^{\mathrm{lat}}(f,h;a)}{\mathsf c_2\,\mathcal K_5(f,h)}-c_1\Bigr|\le C\,\vartheta^{-3}\,\frac a{\mathsf d}\,\lg\frac{\mathsf d}a .
\end{equation}
Consequently, $\lim_{a\to0}\mathsf P_1^{\mathrm{lat}}(f,h;a)/\mathsf c_2\mathcal K_5(f,h)=c_1$ for every such pair.
\item[\textup{(c)}] For all plaquettes $p,q$ of $\mathbb Z^3$, with $n$ ranging over the integers for which $p+o_n,q+o_n\in\mathsf{Pl}_n$,
\[
\mathsf B_1^{\mathrm{lat}}(p,q)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\ \lim_{\beta\to\infty}\ \beta^3\Bigl[\langle a_{p+o_n};a_{q+o_n}\rangle_{n,\beta}-\beta^{-2}\,\mathsf B_0^{[n]}(p+o_n,q+o_n)\Bigr].
\]
The right side is gauge independent: no gauge fixing enters it.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
(a) By Thm.~\ref{IV-73-98},
\[
c_1=\frac3{2\pi^3}\cdot\frac{16\pi^2}9=\frac{48}{18\pi}=\frac8{3\pi},
\]
and $\mathsf c_2c_1=\kappa^{\mathrm{lat}}=\frac3{2\pi^3}$.

(b) Lem.~\ref{lem:test-pair-kernels} on $\mathbb E=\mathbb R^3$, with $q=5$, gives
\[
\mathcal K_5(f,h)\ge10^{-5}\,\vartheta^2\,\mathsf d\,\|f\|_\infty\|h\|_\infty ,
\]
and the right side is positive, since neither $f$ nor $h$ vanishes identically. We divide \eqref{IV-73-74} by $\mathsf c_2\mathcal K_5(f,h)$ and use $\kappa^{\mathrm{lat}}=\mathsf c_2c_1$. The left side of \eqref{IV-73-101} is then at most
\[
C\,\vartheta^{-1}\,a\,\lg(\mathsf d/a)\cdot10^5\,\mathsf c_2^{-1}\,\vartheta^{-2}\,\mathsf d^{-1},
\]
which is the asserted bound, with a pure constant. Since $\frac a{\mathsf d}\lg\frac{\mathsf d}a\to0$ as $a\to0$, the limit follows.

(c) We apply \eqref{IV-73-28} at $\tau_{\mathrm{gf}}=1$ to the plaquettes $p+o_n,q+o_n\in\mathsf{Pl}_n$: for $\beta\ge1$ the expression $\beta^3[\,\cdots]$ differs from $\mathsf B_1^{[n]}(p+o_n,q+o_n;1)$ by at most $C\beta^{-1}$, with a constant $C$ depending on $n$, $p$ and $q$. This gives the inner limit. By \eqref{IV-73-77} with $j=1$ and $\tau_{\mathrm{gf}}=1$, the outer limit equals $\mathsf B_1^{\mathrm{lat}}(p,q;1)$, which is $\mathsf B_1^{\mathrm{lat}}(p,q)$ by \eqref{IV-73-25}. The mean $\langle\cdot\rangle_{n,\beta}$ is taken in the Wilson measure of the box, and $\mathsf B_0^{[n]}=\frac{\mathsf n}2(\Pi^{\Lambda_n})^2$ by \eqref{IV-73-23}, where $\Pi^{\Lambda_n}$ does not depend on $\tau_{\mathrm{gf}}$ (Def.~\ref{IV-73-15}(2)); thus no gauge fixing enters the right side.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{What one shell adds; scope}

We close the section with two items. The first, Lem.~\ref{IV-73-102}, concerns a kernel $\mathsf U(u)=\mathsf c\,|u|^{-5}\varphi(u)$ with $\varphi(Lu)=\varphi(u)$ for a real number $L>1$, for instance $\kappa^{\mathrm{lat}}|u|^{-5}$, the case $\mathsf c=\kappa^{\mathrm{lat}}$, $\varphi\equiv1$; it computes the part of the quadratic form $\frac12\iint w(x)\,w(y)\,\mathsf U(x-y)\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y$ that comes from the shell $r\le|x-y|<Lr$, which covers the scales from $r$ to $Lr$. The second, Remark~\ref{IV-73-105}, delimits the results of the section.

\begin{lemma}[What one shell adds]\label{IV-73-102}
Let $L>1$ and $\mathsf c\ge0$ be real numbers, and let $\varphi\colon\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}\to\mathbb R$ be bounded, Borel and even, with $\varphi(Lu)=\varphi(u)$. Put $\mathsf U(u):=\mathsf c\,|u|^{-5}\varphi(u)$ and, for $r>0$,
\[
\mathsf{Ann}_r:=\{u\in\mathbb R^3:r\le|u|<Lr\}.
\]
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textup{(a)}] For every $r>0$,
\begin{equation}\label{IV-73-103}
\int_{\mathsf{Ann}_r}\mathsf U(u)\,|u|^2\,\mathrm{d}u=\mathsf c\int_{S^2}\int_1^L\varphi(t\omega)\,\frac{dt}t\,\mathrm{d}\omega ;
\end{equation}
for $\varphi\equiv1$ this equals $4\pi\,\mathsf c\log L$.
\item[\textup{(b)}] Assume moreover that $\int_{\mathsf{Ann}_r}\mathsf U(u)\,u_iu_j\,\mathrm{d}u$ is a multiple of $\delta_{ij}$; this is the case if $\varphi$ is invariant under the signed permutations of the coordinates. Then for every real $w\in C_c^2(\mathbb R^3)$
\begin{equation}\label{IV-73-104}
\begin{gathered}
\tfrac12\iint_{x-y\in\mathsf{Ann}_r}w(x)\,w(y)\,\mathsf U(x-y)\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y=\\
\tfrac12\Bigl(\int_{\mathsf{Ann}_r}\mathsf U\Bigr)\int w^2\\
-\tfrac1{12}\Bigl(\int_{\mathsf{Ann}_r}\mathsf U(u)\,|u|^2\,\mathrm{d}u\Bigr)\int|\nabla w|^2+\mathrm{Rem},\\
|\mathrm{Rem}|\le\tfrac\pi{24}\,\mathsf c\,\|\varphi\|_\infty\,(Lr)^2\,\|\Delta w\|_2^2 .
\end{gathered}
\end{equation}
\item[\textup{(c)}] If $\mathsf c=\mathsf c_2c_1\mathsf b^{-3}$ with $\mathsf b>0$, and $\varphi\equiv1$, then the middle term on the right of \eqref{IV-73-104} equals
\[
-\frac1{2\pi^2}\,\mathsf b^{-1}\log L\int\bigl|\nabla(w/\mathsf b)\bigr|^2 .
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(a) In polar coordinates the left side of \eqref{IV-73-103} equals
\[
\mathsf c\int_{S^2}\int_r^{Lr}t^{-5}\varphi(t\omega)\,t^2\,t^2\,\mathrm{d}t\,\mathrm{d}\omega=\mathsf c\int_{S^2}\int_r^{Lr}\varphi(t\omega)\,\frac{dt}t\,\mathrm{d}\omega .
\]
For fixed $\omega$ the function $\tau\mapsto\varphi(e^\tau\omega)$ is bounded, Borel and periodic with period $\log L$; its integral over an interval of length $\log L$ is therefore the same for all such intervals, and
\[
\int_r^{Lr}\varphi(t\omega)\,\frac{dt}t=\int_{\log r}^{\log r+\log L}\varphi(e^\tau\omega)\,\mathrm{d}\tau=\int_1^L\varphi(t\omega)\,\frac{dt}t .
\]
For $\varphi\equiv1$ the right side of \eqref{IV-73-103} is $\mathsf c\cdot4\pi\cdot\log L$.

(b) If $\varphi$ is invariant under the signed permutations of the coordinates, then so are $\mathsf{Ann}_r$ and $\mathsf U$. Changing the sign of $u_i$ shows that the off-diagonal entries of the matrix $\bigl(\int_{\mathsf{Ann}_r}\mathsf U\,u_iu_j\bigr)_{ij}$ vanish, and permuting the coordinates shows that its diagonal entries are equal.

We turn to the expansion. The substitution $x=y+u$ (Fubini's theorem and translation invariance) turns the left side of \eqref{IV-73-104} into
\[
\tfrac12\int_{\mathsf{Ann}_r}\mathsf U(u)\,\mathsf a(u)\,\mathrm{d}u,\qquad\mathsf a(u):=\int w(y+u)\,w(y)\,\mathrm{d}y .
\]
Since $w(\cdot+u)$ has the transform $e^{ip\cdot u}\hat w(p)$, Plancherel's theorem gives
\[
\mathsf a(u)=\int|\hat w(p)|^2\,e^{ip\cdot u}\,d^\circ p=\int|\hat w(p)|^2\cos(p\cdot u)\,d^\circ p ,
\]
the second equality because $\mathsf a$ is real. For real $\vartheta'$, Taylor's formula with integral remainder and $|\cos^{(4)}|\le1$ give $|\cos\vartheta'-1+\frac12\vartheta'^2|\le\frac1{24}\vartheta'^4$. The functions $w$, $\partial_iw$ and $\Delta w$ belong to $L^2$, with the transforms $\hat w$, $ip_i\hat w$ and $-|p|^2\hat w$, by the rule for the transform of a derivative, applied to $w$ and to $\partial_iw\in C_c^1(\mathbb R^3)$. Plancherel's theorem therefore yields
\[
\int|\hat w|^2\,d^\circ p=\int w^2,\qquad\int|\hat w|^2\,p_ip_j\,d^\circ p=\int\partial_iw\,\partial_jw,\qquad\int|\hat w|^2\,|p|^4\,d^\circ p=\|\Delta w\|_2^2 ,
\]
and, with $\vartheta'=p\cdot u$ and $|p\cdot u|\le|p||u|$,
\[
\Bigl|\mathsf a(u)-\int w^2+\tfrac12\sum_{i,j}u_iu_j\int\partial_iw\,\partial_jw\Bigr|\le\tfrac1{24}\,|u|^4\,\|\Delta w\|_2^2 .
\]
By the hypothesis of (b), taking the trace, $\int_{\mathsf{Ann}_r}\mathsf U\,u_iu_j=\frac13\delta_{ij}\int_{\mathsf{Ann}_r}\mathsf U\,|u|^2$. Inserting the expansion of $\mathsf a$, we obtain the right side of \eqref{IV-73-104}: its first term is $\frac12(\int_{\mathsf{Ann}_r}\mathsf U)\int w^2$, its second term has the coefficient $\frac12\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac13=\frac1{12}$, and the remainder satisfies
\[
|\mathrm{Rem}|\le\tfrac12\cdot\tfrac1{24}\,\|\Delta w\|_2^2\int_{\mathsf{Ann}_r}|\mathsf U|\,|u|^4\,\mathrm{d}u\le\tfrac1{48}\,\|\Delta w\|_2^2\,\mathsf c\,\|\varphi\|_\infty\,4\pi\int_r^{Lr}t\,\mathrm{d}t\le\tfrac1{48}\,\|\Delta w\|_2^2\,\mathsf c\,\|\varphi\|_\infty\,4\pi\,\frac{(Lr)^2}2 ,
\]
which is the bound in \eqref{IV-73-104}.

(c) By (a) and Thm.~\ref{IV-73-100}(a), the middle term equals
\[
-\tfrac1{12}\cdot4\pi\cdot\frac3{2\pi^3}\,\mathsf b^{-3}\log L\int|\nabla w|^2=-\frac1{2\pi^2}\,\mathsf b^{-3}\log L\int|\nabla w|^2 ,
\]
and $\mathsf b^{-3}\int|\nabla w|^2=\mathsf b^{-1}\int|\nabla(w/\mathsf b)|^2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Scope of the results]\label{IV-73-105}
The results of this section are delimited as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] We make no statement about the cumulants of the smeared plaquette observables $\mathcal O_a(f)$ in Wilson measures on tori. In particular, it is not asserted that $\mathsf B_1^{\mathrm{lat}}$ is an expansion coefficient of these cumulants when $\beta=\mathsf b/a$ and the side of the torus, measured in lattice spacings, grow jointly as $a\to0$.
\item[(ii)] The constant $C$ of \eqref{IV-73-28} is not controlled as a function of $n$. Accordingly, the limits in Thm.~\ref{IV-73-100}(c) are iterated limits, to be taken in the order written there: first $\beta\to\infty$, then $n\to\infty$.
\item[(iii)] Cor.~\ref{IV-73-73} concerns test pairs, whose supports are at distance at least $\mathsf d$ from each other; it gives no information on the terms with $p=q$ of the double sum \eqref{IV-73-25}, on constant functions $f,h$, or on functions $f,h$ with intersecting supports.
\item[(iv)] The group is $SU(2)$ throughout; nothing is asserted for $N>2$.
\item[(v)] Of the term of degree $-6$ in the large-distance behaviour of $\mathsf B_1^{\mathrm{lat}}$, we prove only the bound \eqref{IV-73-72}.
\end{enumerate}
\end{remark}


\section{Natural scaling and failure of dilation covariance}\label{supp:C-351-1}
The physical label $b$ has the dimension of a length. The natural
small parameter in the preceding law is consequently $d/b$.
Writing the error in this variable makes the range of the law
independent of the reference coupling used to describe a fixed
physical sequence.

For a test pair $\Psi=(f,h)$ put $|\Psi|=|f|_\infty|h|_\infty$ and write
$\Psi_r=(f(\cdot/r),h(\cdot/r))$. The normalization of these
weights is unchanged: they are not multiplied by $r^{-3}$.
Hence
\[
 \mathcal K_q(\Psi_r)=r^{6-q}\mathcal K_q(\Psi).
\]
In particular the leading $\mathcal K_6$ term is constant in
$r$, while the next term is linear.

\begin{sketch}[The natural-scale law]
\label{supp:C-351-3}
For every volume-first limit in the stated short-distance
coupling range and every canonical component, the two-point
function $\mathsf S$ satisfies
\[
 |\mathsf S(\Psi)-L_b^+(\Psi)|
 \le\varepsilon^{\rm nat}(d/b)b^{-3}d|\Psi|,
 \qquad
 \varepsilon^{\rm nat}(\delta)\le C\delta^{1/2},
\]
for the fixed-shape pairs at $0<d\le\delta_c b$.
The constants depend on the admitted construction and the
shape, not on the component. On a fixed torus there is the
corresponding law at every positive label, in its stated range.
None of these two-point functions is dilation covariant.
\end{sketch}

\paragraph{Sketch of the argument.}
The transfer to natural scales uses the exact dilation of the
lattices and Wilson measures. Dilating a sequence moves its
label and its observation scale by the same factor. One may
therefore move to an admitted reference window where the
short-distance estimate is available, apply it there, and carry
the result back. The ratio $d/b$ is unchanged. The comparison
with the least admissible torus then transfers the law to the
periodic-state limit and its components. The error constants
must be uniform in the component for this last assertion.

For a fixed nonzero positive test pair at scale $d_1$, put
\[
 A=c_2b^{-2}\mathcal K_6(\Psi),\qquad
 B=\frac3{2\pi^3}b^{-3}\mathcal K_5(\Psi)>0.
\]
The law gives
\[
 \mathsf S(\Psi_r)=A+Br+O(r^{3/2}).
\]
This exhibits two distinct homogeneities with nonzero
coefficients. Dilation covariance, in the sense
$\mathsf S(\Phi_r)=r^\varpi\mathsf S(\Phi)$ for all
separated pairs and all $r>0$, is incompatible with them.
The nonzero constant limit fixes the possible exponent, and
the nonzero linear term excludes that exponent.

A three-scale combination isolates the correction without
subtracting $A$ separately. For $t>1$, define
\[
 \mathcal N_t(\Psi;r)
 =\mathsf S(\Psi_{t^2r})
       -(1+t^6)\mathsf S(\Psi_{tr})
       +t^6\mathsf S(\Psi_r).
\]
Its weights annul constants and terms proportional to $r^6$.
For the linear correction they give
$-t(t-1)(t^5-1)Br$. At $t=2$ this reads
\[
 \mathsf S(\Psi_{4r})-65\mathsf S(\Psi_{2r})
                         +64\mathsf S(\Psi_r)
       =-62Br+O(r^{3/2}).
\]
It is negative at all sufficiently small $r$. The estimate
retains a quantitative tolerance, so this is a conclusion
about the correlation function, not merely a formal
comparison of degrees. The same test works in every canonical
component because the coefficient and the tolerance survive
the component transfer.

Failure of dilation covariance does not by itself establish
interaction. A quadratic observable of a Gaussian field can
have the same two-term law; the construction gives such an
example. Its three-point behaviour distinguishes it from the
torus limits under discussion. A claim of non-Gaussianity
must therefore use that additional information, rather than
the second two-point coefficient alone.




\subsection{Natural scaling and failure of dilation covariance}\label{C-351-1}

We now express the two-term law in the natural parameter $d/b$.
The resulting tolerance is uniform over the admitted reference couplings.
The law holds at every positive label on a fixed torus and, on
$\mathbb R^3$, in every volume-first limit at the stated coupling ceiling
and in each of its canonical components. The nonzero second term excludes
dilation covariance of the two-point function.

We give two passages to this conclusion: a direct transfer of the law
between labels and an alternative using blocking factors with
incommensurable logarithms. We also retain the leading law for signed
test functions, with its sharp linear rate. These conclusions do not by
themselves establish interaction. Prop.~\ref{C-351-24} constructs a
quadratic Gaussian model with the same two-term law; its three-point
behavior distinguishes it from the torus limits considered here.

\subsubsection{Parameters and test pairs}

We retain the construction setting of \S\ref{C-350-1}, and
write $b$ and $d$ for the label $\mathsf b$ and scale $\mathsf d$.
A \emph{choice} $\mathfrak c$ consists of a mollifier, a radius
$\varrho>0$, the common real and sourced numerical assignment of
Prop.~\YMMref{69.1}{595} and Section~\YMMref{82}{665} at source
radius $2\varrho$, and the canonical auxiliary data for these
constructions. Every constant in the real restriction keeps its value.
The choice fixes an odd $L\ge13$, $B_\sharp\ge0$,
$\bar B=B_\sharp L/(L-1)$, $M$, and $0<\gamma\le1/2$.
The short-distance ceilings $\gamma_W$ of
Thm.~\YMMref{AV}{851} and $\gamma_W^{\rm sd}$ of
the choices in equations~\YMMref{(2326)--(2327)}{845} are both at most $\gamma$.
The ceiling $\gamma_{\rm e}\in(0,\gamma]$, depending only on the
constants, is fixed at the beginning of the subsection on the least
torus, and $\Gamma:=\min\{\gamma_{\rm e},\gamma_W^{\rm sd}\}$.

We write $a_K=L^{-K}$, $X_g=L(g^{-2}+B_\sharp)$, $I(g)=(g^{-2}+\bar B,X_g-\bar B]$ for the interval of labels at $g$ (Section~\YMMref{74}{614}) and $I^\circ(g)$ for its interior, $\mathfrak L(g)=\{2L^m:m\ge m_{\mathfrak L}(g)\}$ for the set of the sides at $g$ (equation~\YMMref{(1528)}{615}) and $\ell_g$ for its least member, and $T_\ell=\mathbb R^3/\ell\mathbb Z^3$. A triple $(g,b,\ell)$ is \emph{admissible} if $0<g\le\gamma_W^{\rm sd}$, $b\in I^\circ(g)$ and $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$. Since $LB_\sharp=(L-1)\bar B$, we have $I^\circ(g)=(g^{-2}+\bar B,\,Lg^{-2}+(L-2)\bar B)$, an interval of length $(L-1)g^{-2}+(L-3)\bar B>0$.

We use the lattices, first-passage data, labels and torus cumulants of
\S\ref{C-350-1}, with the same fixed choice of construction data.
The continuum torus cumulants $S_n^{(\ell,b)}$ exist for every $b>0$ on
Lipschitz tuples with no common point, by Thm.~\YMMref{A}{5}.
A volume-first limit $S$ at $g$ is defined by a sequence $(K_j,\beta_j,\nu_j)$ as in {\cite[\S{}K.1]{YMM2}}; for $g\le\gamma_W$ it has one label $\mathsf b(S)=\lim_ja_{K_j}\beta_j$. $(\mathsf X,\lambda,(\sigma_\xi))$ denotes a canonical decomposition of its functional $\sigma_S$, with the probability measure $\lambda$ on $\mathsf X$; $S_2$ and $S_2^\xi$ are the two-point functions of $\sigma_S$ and $\sigma_\xi$, and $\mathsf N\subset\mathsf X$ is the set of the $\xi$ for which $S_2^\xi$ is not dilation covariant.

The class $\mathfrak T_{\mathbb E}(d;\vartheta)$ is the test-pair class
of \S\ref{C-350-1}. $\mathfrak T^1(d;\vartheta)$ is the set of its pairs on $\mathbb R^3$ of class $C^1$. Over $\mathbb R^3$ the pairs of real $C^1$ functions with compact disjoint supports are called \emph{separated}; the pairs of $\mathfrak T^1(d;\vartheta)$ are separated. On a torus we admit real Lipschitz entries with disjoint supports. Every $\mathfrak T^1(d;\vartheta)$, $d>0$, $\vartheta\in(0,1)$, contains a pair ({\cite[Lem.~I.1]{YMM2}}(c)); for $\vartheta\le3\sqrt3/8$ one may take $f(u)=(1-|u-x|^2/d^2)_+^2$, $h(u)=(1-|u-y|^2/d^2)_+^2$ with $3d\le|x-y|\le8d$. For a pair we write $|\Psi|=\|f\|_\infty\|h\|_\infty$, $\Psi_r=(f(\cdot/r),h(\cdot/r))$ for $r>0$, $\Psi^{\langle\ell\rangle}$ for the periodisation, and
\[
\mathcal K_q(\Psi)=\iint f(x)h(y)\,|x-y|^{-q}\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y ,
\]
on $T_\ell$ with the Euclidean distance of $T_\ell$; further $T^{(\ell,b)}(\Psi)=S_2^{(\ell,b)}(\Psi^{\langle\ell\rangle})$, $c_2=\frac9{16\pi^2}$, $c_1=\frac8{3\pi}$, $\varkappa=c_1c_2=\frac3{2\pi^3}$ and $L_b^+=c_2b^{-2}[\mathcal K_6+c_1b^{-1}\mathcal K_5]$. By {\cite[Lem.~I.1]{YMM2}} and equation~\YMMref{(2247)}{824} and~{\cite[Lem.~I.1]{YMM2}}(b): $\Psi_r\in\mathfrak T^1(rd;\vartheta)$ for $\Psi\in\mathfrak T^1(d;\vartheta)$, with the same $\vartheta$, $|\Psi_r|=|\Psi|$ and $\mathcal K_q(\Psi_r)=r^{6-q}\mathcal K_q(\Psi)$; translations keep the classes, the suprema and the $\mathcal K_q$; for $d<\ell/20$ the periodisation maps $\mathfrak T_{\mathbb R^3}(d;\vartheta)$ into $\mathfrak T_{T_\ell}(d;\vartheta)$, keeps the suprema, and $\mathcal K_q(\Psi^{\langle\ell\rangle})=\mathcal K_q(\Psi)$ for every real $q>0$. As $d\le|x-y|\le10d$ on the supports of a pair of the class, $(10d)^{-q}\int f\int h\le\mathcal K_q(\Psi)\le d^{-q}|\Psi|(\frac{4\pi}3d^3)^2$, that is,
\begin{equation}\label{C-351-2}
10^{-5}\vartheta^2d\,|\Psi|\le\mathcal K_5(\Psi)\le\bigl(\tfrac{4\pi}3\bigr)^2d\,|\Psi|,\qquad10^{-6}\vartheta^2|\Psi|\le\mathcal K_6(\Psi)\le\bigl(\tfrac{4\pi}3\bigr)^2|\Psi|,\qquad\varkappa\bigl(\tfrac{4\pi}3\bigr)^2=\tfrac8{3\pi};
\end{equation}
note $10^{-5}\varkappa=4.837\ldots\cdot10^{-7}$.

A functional $\sigma$ on separated tuples over $\mathbb R^3$ \emph{obeys the law} (L) \emph{with} $(b,c,\varepsilon,d_7,\vartheta)$, where $\varepsilon$ is non-decreasing on $(0,d_7]$ and $\varepsilon(d)\to0$ as $d\to0$, if
\[
|S_2^\sigma(\Psi)-c_2b^{-2}[\mathcal K_6+cb^{-1}\mathcal K_5](\Psi)|\le\varepsilon(d)\,b^{-3}d\,|\Psi|\qquad(0<d\le d_7,\ \Psi\in\mathfrak T^1(d;\vartheta)).
\]
$S_2^\sigma$ is \emph{dilation covariant} if there is a real $\varpi$ with $S_2^\sigma(\Phi_r)=r^\varpi S_2^\sigma(\Phi)$ for all $r>0$ and all separated pairs $\Phi$. For a function $\mathsf S$ on pairs, $t>1$ and $r>0$ we call
\[
\mathcal N^{\mathsf S}_t(\Psi;r)=\mathsf S(\Psi_{t^2r})-(1+t^6)\,\mathsf S(\Psi_{tr})+t^6\,\mathsf S(\Psi_r)
\]
the $t$-scale number; at $t=2$ it is the \emph{three-scale number} $\mathsf S(\Psi_{4r})-65\,\mathsf S(\Psi_{2r})+64\,\mathsf S(\Psi_r)$. The weights annul constants and multiples of $r^6$, and give the function $r\mapsto r$ the factor $t^2-(1+t^6)t+t^6=-t(t-1)(t^5-1)$, which is $-62$ at $t=2$. For a triple $\tau=(g,b,\ell)$ and a pair $\Psi$ we put $E_\tau=2C_2^{\rm T}(g)\vartheta^{-1}b^2$, with the number $C_2^{\rm T}$ of Prop.~\ref{C-351-7}, and $Y_\tau(\delta)=b^2\,T^{(\ell,b)}(\Psi_{\delta b})$.

\subsubsection{Changing units and keeping the label}

The natural short-distance variable is $d/b$. The label $b$ has
the dimension of length, and under a lattice dilation the mesh,
side and label change together. At powers of the blocking factor,
the exact identity is
\begin{equation}\label{supp-exp:natural-exact-dilation}
 T^{(\ell,b)}(\Psi)
       =L^{2s}T^{(L^s\ell,L^sb)}(\Psi_{L^s}),
 \qquad \Psi_r=(f(\cdot/r),h(\cdot/r)).
\end{equation}
It follows at finite cutoff by transporting the same Wilson
measure to the dilated lattice, keeping the bare inverse coupling
fixed, and using the factor $L^s$ in each smeared observable.
The full-sequence cutoff limits then give
\eqref{supp-exp:natural-exact-dilation}. This identity compares
theories at different labels. Dilation covariance of one
two-point function would instead keep its label fixed and
require one power of $r$ for every separated pair.

The two explicit kernels transform compatibly with
\eqref{supp-exp:natural-exact-dilation}:
$\mathcal K_6(\Psi_r)=\mathcal K_6(\Psi)$ and
$\mathcal K_5(\Psi_r)=r\mathcal K_5(\Psi)$.
Their common natural parameter is consequently $d/b$. The
purpose of \cref{C-351-3} is to make the tolerance uniform in
that parameter across the admitted labels and canonical
components. A bound $C(g)d^{1/2}$ on the least torus does
not yet have this uniformity.

The supplied proof obtains it by putting labels into one
multiplicative period. Choose $\Lambda$ once from the fixed
construction constants. Every $b>0$ has a unique dilate
$b'=L^zb$ in $[\Lambda,L\Lambda)$. Two fixed reference
couplings have admissible label intervals covering that
period. The least-torus law is therefore needed at only
these two couplings. The state comparison of
\cref{C-351-15} bounds the difference between a continuum
component and the corresponding torus function by a
constant times $(d/b)^2$ after multiplication by $b^2$.
At the dilated label this comparison constant is bounded
throughout the fixed period.

The torus tolerance contributes a constant times
$(d/b)^{1/2}$ in the normalized remainder, and the state
comparison contributes a constant times $d/b$. Taking
their nondecreasing majorant gives
$\varepsilon^{\rm nat}(d/b)\le C(d/b)^{1/2}$.
For components, the comparison is justified by their
conditioned periodic-Gibbs approximants. Centring affects
only the first cumulant; the covariance is the limit of
those approximants. Thus the same transfer applies to
each component with the same recovered label. No averaging
over components is used to obtain a pointwise assertion
about an individual component.

\subsubsection{The nonzero linear term}

Fix a test pair $\Psi$ of scale $d_1$ in the positive class.
The natural-scale law gives
\begin{equation}\label{supp-exp:natural-linear-expansion}
 \mathsf S(\Psi_r)=A+Br+O(r^{3/2}),\qquad
 A=c_2b^{-2}\mathcal K_6(\Psi)>0,\qquad
 B=\kappa^{\rm lat}b^{-3}\mathcal K_5(\Psi)>0,
\end{equation}
for the volume-first two-point function and for each
canonical component. Positivity of $A$ and $B$ follows
from the mass floors of the test class, not merely from
the signs of their displayed numerical coefficients.
The error is uniform in the small-radius range specified
by the natural variable.

If $\mathsf S$ were dilation covariant with exponent
$\varpi$, its value at $\Psi_r$ would be
$r^\varpi\mathsf S(\Psi)$. The positive finite limit $A$
as $r\to0$ forces $\varpi=0$. Covariance would then make
the value constant in $r$, whereas dividing
\eqref{supp-exp:natural-linear-expansion} minus $A$ by
$r$ gives the positive limit $B$. This is the direct
contradiction in \cref{C-351-16}.

The scale difference used in the source gives a quantitative
version. For $t>1$, the combination
\[
 \mathcal N_t^{\mathsf S}(\Psi;r)
   =\mathsf S(\Psi_{t^2r})-(1+t^6)\mathsf S(\Psi_{tr})
                                      +t^6\mathsf S(\Psi_r)
\]
annuls constants and terms proportional to $r^6$. Its
value on the linear term is
$-t(t-1)(t^5-1)Br$. At $t=2$ this is $-62Br$, and the
sum of the three remainder bounds has coefficient $198$.
Hence the three-scale number is negative for sufficiently
small $r$, with an explicit threshold given by the
normalized tolerance. The test records a property of the
two-point function at fixed label, rather than the exact
change-of-units identity between labels.

The alternative proof in \cref{C-351-19,C-351-20} transfers
this obstruction from a single admitted triple. Choose
a second blocking factor whose logarithm is
incommensurable with the first. Sequences of powers of
the two factors approximate any positive ratio of scales.
On each pair of corresponding lattices, transport the
same bare periodic Gibbs state. Its two rescaled
covariances agree exactly after multiplication by the
squares of their labels. Comparing each with its torus
limit leaves an error $O((d/b)^2)$. Thus a hypothetical
quadratic-order agreement with the free law in one limit
would transfer to the triple where the nonzero linear
correction is already known. It cannot absorb that
correction. This second route retains the original
comparison estimates and continuity in the varying
label and test pair; density of scale ratios alone would
not justify passage to the limit.

\subsubsection{Signed pairs and what the two-term law detects}

The positivity conditions on the test class are used
to identify the coefficient and its sign. A leading
short-distance estimate for arbitrary signed separated
Lipschitz functions follows by a finite decomposition
into signed nonnegative pieces. A common test shape
serves the finitely many pairs of pieces. Apply the
two-term estimate to each pair and use bilinearity.
This gives the $O(r)$ error in \cref{C-351-22} uniformly
in position and on compact label intervals. A nonzero
positive reflected pair has $\mathcal K_5>0$, so its
linear correction shows that this rate is attained.
The label derivative identity is retained separately:
inserting the constant function differentiates the
coupling, and integration over a compact interval of
labels gives the stated bound involving $S_3(1,f_r,h_r)$.

The failure of dilation covariance is not by itself a
test of interaction. \Cref{C-351-24} supplies a concrete
comparison model. On $T_\ell$, take three independent
Gaussian fields with covariance symbol
\[
 \widehat G_b(k)=(b|k|^2+\alpha|k|+\upsilon)^{-1},
 \qquad \upsilon=\upsilon_0/\ell>0.
\]
Its positive spectral representation is
\[
 (bu^2+\alpha u+\upsilon)^{-1}
  =\int_0^\infty\frac{\rho_{\rm sp}(m)}{u^2+m^2}
                            \,\mathrm{d}m,\qquad
 \rho_{\rm sp}(m)=\frac{2\alpha}{\pi}
     \frac{m^2}{(\upsilon-bm^2)^2+\alpha^2m^2}.
\]
Reflection positivity follows by integrating the
reflection-positive massive covariances against this
positive density. The model's observable is a quadratic
functional of mollified fields, combining
$-\tfrac12{:}|\nabla\varphi|^2{:}$ with
$-{:}\varphi\Delta\varphi{:}$ as specified there.
Its separated cumulants have limits independent of the
mollifier, although its variance at a nonzero single
test function diverges. Consequently it is important
to retain the separated-cumulant formulation and not
claim an $L^2$ limiting observable.

Let $\mathcal C$ be its covariance kernel and
$\mathcal H=\Delta\mathcal C$ off the origin.
Wick's rule gives the two-point kernel
\[
 \frac32\left[
   \operatorname{tr}(\nabla\nabla^{\mathsf T}\mathcal C)^2
   +4\nabla\mathcal C\cdot\nabla\mathcal H
   +2\mathcal H^2+2\mathcal C\Delta\mathcal H\right].
\]
The supplied expansion of $\mathcal C$ makes its first
two singular terms
\[
 c_2b^{-2}\left[|x|^{-6}
       +\frac{4\alpha}{3\pi}b^{-1}|x|^{-5}\right].
\]
At $\alpha=2$ the relative coefficient is exactly
$8/(3\pi)$. After smearing, the remaining error is
$O(d^2(1+\log(\ell/d)))$, which is smaller than the
linear correction. This model therefore reproduces the
same two-term law.

The source distinguishes it using a three-point property
of the torus limits. Their cutoff estimates imply
convergence to zero for tuples with uniformly bounded supremum
norms and Lipschitz constants, fixed positive spread, and a product
of supremum norms tending to zero. Here the spread of supports
$S_1,\ldots,S_n$ is
$\inf_{x_a\in S_a}\max_{a,a^{\prime}}|x_a-x_{a^{\prime}}|_\infty$. For
$f_{\mathbf q}=|\mathbf q|^{-1}\psi\cos(\mathbf q\cdot x)$
with $\psi$ separated from a nonzero $h\ge0$, these
conditions hold. The first two supports may coincide; the third
stays separated from them. The quadratic Gaussian model instead
has the limit
\[
 \mathcal S_3(f_{\mathbf q},f_{\mathbf q},h)
 \longrightarrow-\frac3{2b}
   \iint\psi(x)^2h(y)
       \bigl[|\nabla\mathcal C|^2
                    +2\mathcal C\Delta\mathcal C\bigr](x-y)
                             \,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y<0.
\]
The spectral representation makes the bracket positive
off the origin. This is the supplied test that excludes
that comparison model. It also explains why the
two-point coefficient, despite detecting a scale, cannot
alone identify the full field theory.

\subsubsection{The law at natural scales}

\begin{theorem}[The components]\label{C-351-3}
Let $\mathfrak c$ be a choice and $\vartheta\in(0,1)$. There are $\delta_{\rm c}>0$ and a non-decreasing function $\varepsilon^{\rm nat}$ on $(0,\delta_{\rm c}]$ with $\varepsilon^{\rm nat}(\delta)\le C\delta^{1/2}$, where $\delta_{\rm c}$, $\varepsilon^{\rm nat}$ and $C$ depend only on $\mathfrak c$ and $\vartheta$, such that for every $0<g\le\gamma_W$, every volume-first limit $S$ at $g$ with $b=\mathsf b(S)$, every canonical decomposition $(\mathsf X,\lambda,(\sigma_\xi))$ of $\sigma_S$, and for $\mathsf S=S_2$ and $\mathsf S=S_2^\xi$, $\xi\in\mathsf X$, the following holds.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)] $|\mathsf S(\Psi)-L_b^+(\Psi)|\le\varepsilon^{\rm nat}(d/b)\,b^{-3}d\,|\Psi|$ for $0<d\le\delta_{\rm c}b$ and $\Psi\in\mathfrak T^1(d;\vartheta)$. So $\sigma_S$ and every $\sigma_\xi$ obey (L) with $(b,\frac8{3\pi},\varepsilon^S,d^S,\vartheta)$, where $\varepsilon^S(d)=\varepsilon^{\rm nat}(g^2d)$ and $d^S=\delta_{\rm c}g^{-2}$ depend only on $\mathfrak c$, $g$ and $\vartheta$. They obey (L) also with a tolerance formed at any dilated label: if $z$ is an integer with $L^zb\ge2\Gamma^{-2}$ and $g'=(2/(L^zb))^{1/2}$, then (L) holds with $(b,\frac8{3\pi},\varepsilon',d',\vartheta)$, where $\varepsilon'(d)=\varepsilon^L_{g',\vartheta}(L^zd)+2C_2^{\rm T}(g')\vartheta^{-1}L^{2z}b\,d$ and $d'=L^{-z}\min\{d^L,d_\flat\}(g',\vartheta)$, with the objects of Thm.~\ref{C-351-4}~(a) and Prop.~\ref{C-351-7}.
\item[(2)] Let $d_1>0$, $\Psi\in\mathfrak T^1(d_1;\vartheta)$ and $B_S=\varkappa b^{-3}\mathcal K_5(\Psi)$, so that $B_S\ge10^{-5}\varkappa\vartheta^2b^{-3}d_1|\Psi|>0$; let $t>1$. Then
\begin{align}
&|\mathsf S(\Psi_r)-c_2b^{-2}\mathcal K_6(\Psi)-B_Sr|\le\varepsilon^{\rm nat}(rd_1/b)\,b^{-3}d_1|\Psi|\,r&&(rd_1\le\delta_{\rm c}b),\notag\\
&|\mathcal N^{\mathsf S}_t(\Psi;r)+t(t-1)(t^5-1)B_Sr|\le(t^2+t+t^6+t^7)\,\varepsilon^{\rm nat}(t^2rd_1/b)\,b^{-3}d_1|\Psi|\,r&&(t^2rd_1\le\delta_{\rm c}b).\notag
\end{align}
So $\mathsf S(\Psi_r)=c_2b^{-2}\mathcal K_6(\Psi)+B_Sr+O(r^{3/2})$; $|r^{-1}[\mathsf S(\Psi_{tr})-\mathsf S(\Psi_r)]-(t-1)B_S|\le(t+1)\,\varepsilon^{\rm nat}(trd_1/b)\,b^{-3}d_1|\Psi|$, so that $r^{-1}[\mathsf S(\Psi_{tr})-\mathsf S(\Psi_r)]\to(t-1)B_S$; $r^{-1}\mathcal N^{\mathsf S}_t(\Psi;r)\to-t(t-1)(t^5-1)B_S$, and so do the means $n^{-1}\sum_{j<n}(t^{-j}r_0)^{-1}\mathcal N^{\mathsf S}_t(\Psi;t^{-j}r_0)$ as $n\to\infty$, for every $r_0$ with $t^2r_0d_1\le\delta_{\rm c}b$; and $\mathcal N^{\mathsf S}_t(\Psi;r)<0$ as soon as $(t^2+t+t^6+t^7)\,\varepsilon^{\rm nat}(t^2rd_1/b)<t(t-1)(t^5-1)\cdot10^{-5}\varkappa\vartheta^2$. At $t=2$: the three-scale number is $-62B_Sr+O(r^{3/2})$, within $198\,\varepsilon^{\rm nat}(4rd_1/b)\,b^{-3}d_1|\Psi|\,r$ of $-62B_Sr$, and negative as soon as $198\,\varepsilon^{\rm nat}(4rd_1/b)<62\cdot10^{-5}\varkappa\vartheta^2$, that is, for all small $r$.
\item[(3)] Neither $S_2$ nor any $S_2^\xi$ is dilation covariant: $\mathsf N=\mathsf X$ and $\lambda(\mathsf N)=1$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The tori]\label{C-351-4}
Let $\mathfrak c$ be a choice and $\vartheta\in(0,1)$; let $d_{\rm e}$, $\bar\varepsilon=\bar\varepsilon_{g,\vartheta}$, $\bar\varepsilon_\infty=\bar\varepsilon_{\infty;g,\vartheta}$ and $C_{\rm cut}$ be the objects of Prop.~\ref{C-351-14} and the depth $s(d)$ that of the subsection on the least torus, and $d_\flat$, $C_2^{\rm T}$ those of Prop.~\ref{C-351-7}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)]

\emph{The least torus.} For $0<g\le\gamma_{\rm e}$ there are $d^L(g,\vartheta)>0$ and a non-decreasing function $\varepsilon^L_{g,\vartheta}$ on $(0,d^L(g,\vartheta)]$ with $\varepsilon^L_{g,\vartheta}(d)\le C(g,\vartheta)d^{1/2}$, all depending only on $\mathfrak c$, $g$ and $\vartheta$, such that
\[
|T^{(\ell_g,b)}(\Psi)-L_b^+(\Psi)|\le\varepsilon^L_{g,\vartheta}(d)\,b^{-3}d\,|\Psi|\qquad\bigl(b\in I(g),\ 0<d\le d^L(g,\vartheta),\ \Psi\in\mathfrak T_{\mathbb R^3}(d;\vartheta)\bigr).
\]
\item[(b)]

\emph{Every torus of the family; every state at a finite cutoff.} Let $0<g\le\Gamma$, $b\in I(g)$, $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$, $0<d\le\min\{d_{\rm e},\ell_g/20,d_\flat\}(g,\vartheta)$ and $\Psi\in\mathfrak T_{\mathbb R^3}(d;\vartheta)$. Then
\[
|T^{(\ell,b)}(\Psi)-L_b^+(\Psi)|\le\bigl[\bar\varepsilon_\infty(d)+2C_2^{\rm T}(g)\vartheta^{-1}bd\bigr]\,b^{-3}d\,|\Psi|,
\]
and the bracket is at most $C(g,\vartheta)(1+b)d^{1/2}$. Moreover, for every cutoff $K>s(d)$ and every state $\mathfrak s$ at the datum $(K,L^Kb)$ in the sense of Prop.~\ref{C-351-7},
\[
|S^T_2[\mathfrak s](\Psi)-L_b^+(\Psi)|\le\Bigl[\bigl(\bar\varepsilon(d)+C_2^{\rm T}(g)\vartheta^{-1}bd\bigr)\,b^{-3}d+C_{\rm cut}\,b^{-2}\frac{a_K}d\Bigr]|\Psi| ,
\]
and the same holds with $C_{\rm r}d^{1/2}$ in the place of $\bar\varepsilon(d)$ and $C'_{\rm cut}$ in the place of $C_{\rm cut}$, with the numbers of Prop.~\ref{C-351-14}~(c).
\item[(c)]

\emph{Every side, every label.} Let $\ell=2L^m$, $m\ge1$, $b>0$, $s\ge0$ an integer and $0<g''\le\Gamma$ a coupling for which $(g'',L^sb,L^s\ell)$ is admissible; this holds for all large $s$ with $g''=(2/(L^sb))^{1/2}$. Then for $0<d\le L^{-s}\min\{d_{\rm e},\ell_{g''}/20,d_\flat\}(g'',\vartheta)$ and $\Psi\in\mathfrak T^1(d;\vartheta)$
\[
|T^{(\ell,b)}(\Psi)-L_b^+(\Psi)|\le\bigl[\bar\varepsilon_\infty(L^sd)+2C_2^{\rm T}(g'')\vartheta^{-1}L^{2s}bd\bigr]\,b^{-3}d\,|\Psi|,
\]
with $\bar\varepsilon_\infty$ formed at $(g'',\vartheta)$; the bracket is at most $Cd^{1/2}$, with $C$ depending on $\mathfrak c$, $g''$, $s$, $b$ and $\vartheta$.
\item[(d)]

\emph{Exact dilation by powers of $L$.} $T^{(\ell,b)}(\Psi)=L^{2s}\,T^{(L^s\ell,L^sb)}(\Psi_{L^s})$ for $\ell=2L^m$, $b>0$, integers $s\ge0$ and pairs $\Psi$ of real Lipschitz functions with compact supports whose periodisations to $T_\ell$ have disjoint supports. In particular, for $0<g\le\gamma_{\rm e}$, $b\in I(g)$ and every integer $z\ge0$, the law of~(a) holds on the side $L^z\ell_g$ at the label $L^zb$ with no comparison of states:
\[
|T^{(L^z\ell_g,L^zb)}(\Psi)-L^+_{L^zb}(\Psi)|\le\varepsilon^L_{g,\vartheta}(L^{-z}d)\,(L^zb)^{-3}d\,|\Psi|\qquad\bigl(0<d\le L^zd^L(g,\vartheta),\ \Psi\in\mathfrak T_{\mathbb R^3}(d;\vartheta)\bigr).
\]
\item[(e)]

\emph{One coefficient.} If at one side $2L^m$ and one label the inequality of~(c) holds with a number $c$ and with a number $c'$ in the place of $\frac8{3\pi}$, each with a tolerance that tends to $0$, then $c=c'$.
\item[(f)]

\emph{Compact sets of labels.} At a fixed side, one tolerance, one range of $d$ and one constant $C$ serve in~(c) for all the labels of a compact subset of $(0,\infty)$.
\end{enumerate}
Let now $0<g\le\gamma_{\rm e}$, $b\in I(g)$, $T=T^{(\ell_g,b)}$, $\varepsilon^L=\varepsilon^L_{g,\vartheta}$, $d^L=d^L(g,\vartheta)$, $d_1>0$, $\Psi\in\mathfrak T^1(d_1;\vartheta)$, $\mathsf A=c_2b^{-2}\mathcal K_6(\Psi)$, $\mathsf B=\varkappa b^{-3}\mathcal K_5(\Psi)$ and $\mathsf u=b^{-3}d_1|\Psi|$. Then $10^{-5}\varkappa\vartheta^2\mathsf u\le\mathsf B\le\frac8{3\pi}\mathsf u$, and for $0<rd_1\le d^L$
\begin{equation}\label{C-351-5}
|T(\Psi_r)-\mathsf A-\mathsf Br|\le\varepsilon^L(rd_1)\,\mathsf u\,r\le C(g,\vartheta)\,d_1^{1/2}\,\mathsf u\,r^{3/2}.
\end{equation}
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] For $t>1$ and $0<trd_1\le d^L$: $|r^{-1}[T(\Psi_{tr})-T(\Psi_r)]-(t-1)\mathsf B|\le(t+1)\,\varepsilon^L(trd_1)\,\mathsf u\to0$; for $0<t^2rd_1\le d^L$: $|r^{-1}\mathcal N^T_t(\Psi;r)+t(t-1)(t^5-1)\mathsf B|\le(t^2+t+t^6+t^7)\,\varepsilon^L(t^2rd_1)\,\mathsf u\to0$. At $t=2$: $|r^{-1}[T(\Psi_{2r})-T(\Psi_r)]-\mathsf B|\le3\varepsilon^L(2rd_1)\mathsf u$.
\item[(ii)] $r^{-2}|T(\Psi_r)-\mathsf A|\ge r^{-1}\mathsf u\,[10^{-5}\varkappa\vartheta^2-\varepsilon^L(rd_1)]\to\infty$ as $r\to0$.
\item[(iii)] For all $d_n\to0$ and all $\Psi_n\in\mathfrak T^1(d_n;\vartheta)$: $|T(\Psi_n)-c_2b^{-2}\mathcal K_6(\Psi_n)|/(d_n^2|\Psi_n|)\ge b^{-3}[10^{-5}\varkappa\vartheta^2-\varepsilon^L(d_n)]/d_n\to\infty$.
\item[(iv)] Let $g\le\Gamma$ and $b\in I^\circ(g)$. For every $0<C<\infty$, every $d\le d^L$ with $\varepsilon^L(d)\le\frac12\cdot10^{-5}\varkappa\vartheta^2$ and $d/b<\frac12\cdot10^{-5}\varkappa\vartheta^3/C$, and every $\Psi\in\mathfrak T^1(d;\vartheta)$: $b^2|T(\Psi)-c_2b^{-2}\mathcal K_6(\Psi)|>C\vartheta^{-1}(d/b)^2|\Psi|$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}[The leading term with the rate $r$, for signed functions]\label{C-351-22}
Let $\mathfrak c$ be a choice, $\ell=2L^m$ with $m\ge1$, $b>0$, $p\in T_\ell$ with a lift $\tilde p$, let $f_0,h_0$ be real Lipschitz functions on $\mathbb R^3$ with compact disjoint supports, and put $f_r=(f_0((\cdot-\tilde p)/r))^{\langle\ell\rangle}$ and $h_r=(h_0((\cdot-\tilde p)/r))^{\langle\ell\rangle}$ for $r>0$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] There are $C,r_*>0$, independent of $p$ and the same for all the labels of a compact subset of $(0,\infty)$, with
\[
|S_2^{(\ell,b)}(f_r,h_r)-c_2b^{-2}\mathcal K_6(f_0,h_0)|\le Cr\qquad(0<r\le r_*).
\]
In particular, for $\theta_\mu x=x-2x_\mu e_\mu$ and every real Lipschitz function $\psi_0$ with compact support in $\{x_\mu>0\}$, the pair $(f_0,h_0)=(\psi_0\circ\theta_\mu,\psi_0)$ gives $S_2^{(\ell,b)}(f_r,h_r)=c_2b^{-2}\mathcal K_6(\psi_0\circ\theta_\mu,\psi_0)+O(r)$.
\item[(b)] The rate $r$ is attained: if $\psi_0\ge0$ is of class $C^1$, not $0$, with support in the ball $\mathbb B(e_\mu,\frac12)$, then
\[
S_2^{(\ell,b)}(f_r,h_r)-c_2b^{-2}\mathcal K_6(\psi_0\circ\theta_\mu,\psi_0)=\varkappa\,b^{-3}\mathcal K_5(\psi_0\circ\theta_\mu,\psi_0)\,r+O(r^{3/2}),\qquad\mathcal K_5(\psi_0\circ\theta_\mu,\psi_0)>0 ;
\]
so no bound $o(r)$ holds in~(a).
\item[(c)] For $0<b_1<b_2$, with the constant $C$ of~(a) for the labels of $[b_1,b_2]$ and $0<r\le r_*$,
\[
\Bigl|\int_{b_1}^{b_2}\bigl[b^2S_3^{(\ell,b)}(1,f_r,h_r)-2b\,S_2^{(\ell,b)}(f_r,h_r)\bigr]\,\mathrm{d}b\Bigr|\le(b_1^2+b_2^2)\,C\,r ,
\]
where $1$ is the constant function on $T_\ell$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}

\subsubsection{Construction inputs}

The proof rests on Thms.~\YMMref{D}{8}, \YMMref{AJ}{673} and~\YMMref{AD}{607} among the construction results, with its conditions on the constants, through the statements cited below. Among them are Section~\YMMref{74}{614}, {\cite[result~G.2]{YMM2}}, \YMMref{(1528)}{615} and~\YMMref{82}{665}, the real-sequence conditions and smallness floor~\YMMref{(972)}{438} preceding Thm.~\YMMref{Y}{438}, the bounds~\YMMref{(1531)}{615} on labels, Cor.~\YMMref{74.2}{616} and {\cite[Lem.~G.4]{YMM2}} on couplings and labels, which we use in the form of Lem.~\ref{C-351-25} below, the exact dilation by powers of $L$~\YMMref{(2215)}{814}, Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AS}{813}} on the limits at a fixed label (their existence, the rate of removal of the cutoff, the bounds~\YMMref{(2214)}{814} uniform in the cutoff and in the labels of a compact set, the continuity in the label and the convergence along converging labels), Prop.~\YMMref{118.3}{814} on the derivatives in the label, the uniform cutoff estimate of Thm.~\YMMref{AR}{810} on the removal of the cutoff, the weighted progression and its source energies ({\cite[Def.~B.7]{YMM2}} and {\cite[Cor.~B.9]{YMM2}}), its setting (J) for the canonical objects ({\cite[Def.~B.16]{YMM2}} and equation~{\cite[eq.~228]{YMM2}} and {\cite[Prop.~B.21]{YMM2}}), the places with a lower place of a step at a complex field scale (Def.~\ref{IV-71-12} and Prop.~\ref{IV-71-50}), the sourced renormalisation-group chain and its source energies ({\cite[Prop.~B.12]{YMM2}} and equations~{\cite[eq.~212]{YMM2}}--{\cite[eq.~214]{YMM2}}), the histories, the sum over the level of the first creation of a large-field region and the rarity of large fields (Section~\YMMref{123}{828}, equation~\eqref{eq:ward-first-creation} and Prop.~\ref{prop:ward-fixed-volume-rarity}), the reflection positivity of the limits on the tori (proved in Prop.~\ref{C-351-24}(c) from Thm.~\YMMref{A}{5} and finite-cutoff positivity, for every side $2L^m$, every $b>0$ and $C^1$ entries at every coordinate mirror) and that of the Wilson measures on the tori at the site and bond mirrors (Prop.~\YMMref{91.4}{700}), which, with the existence of the limits along the full sequence of the cutoffs, gives it for real Lipschitz entries at the mirrors $\{x_\mu=c\}$, $c\in\bigcup_{K\in\mathbb N}\frac12L^{-K}\mathbb Z$, of the lattices of the cutoffs, the block averages ({\cite[Lem.~B.3]{YMM2}}), the template sum of the free lattice curvature (Prop.~\YMMref{121.2}{824} and Lem.~\ref{lem:ward-fluctuation-template}), Laplace's method (Lem.~\textup{\ref{IV-73-26}}) and the coefficients of lattice perturbation theory (Def.~\textup{\ref{IV-73-22}}, Cor.~\textup{\ref{IV-73-73}}, Thms.~\textup{\ref{IV-73-98}} and~\textup{\ref{IV-73-100}}), the chessboard estimate ({\cite[Cor.~B.1]{YMM2}}), the representation of the components by conditioned periodic Gibbs states (Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AP}{780}}), and, for $g\le\gamma_W$, the leading law of Thm.~\YMMref{AW}{852} for $\sigma_S$ and, using the conditioned approximants in Thm.~\YMMref{AP}{780}, for its components: for $0<d\le\mathsf d_0(g,\vartheta)$ and the $C^1$ pairs of $\mathfrak T_{\mathbb R^3}(d;\vartheta)$, $\mathsf S(\Psi)=c_2b^{-2}\mathcal K_6(\Psi)(1+\eta)$ with $|\eta|\le\eta_{g,\vartheta}(d)\le\frac13$ and $\eta_{g,\vartheta}(d)\to0$ as $d\to0$.

Two further statements are proved below from these: the agreement of all states at one datum at two points, which uses no decay of correlations (Prop.~\ref{C-351-7}), and the next-order law on the least torus (Prop.~\ref{C-351-14}).

\begin{lemma}[Couplings and labels]\label{C-351-25}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[beginpenalty=10000]
\item[(a)] $\gamma^{-2}>\bar B$. For every real $b'>2\bar B$, in particular for every $b'\ge2\gamma^{-2}$, the coupling $g'=(2/b')^{1/2}$ satisfies $b'\in I^\circ(g')$; if $b'\ge2\gamma^{-2}$, then $g'\le\gamma$.
\item[(b)] Let $0<g'\le\gamma$, and let $(K_j,\beta_j)$ be pairs of integers $K_j\ge1$ and reals $\beta_j>0$ with $a_{K_j}\beta_j\to b'\in I^\circ(g')$. Then $(K_j,\beta_j)$ is a first-passage datum at $g'$ for all large $j$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(a) Cor.~\YMMref{74.2}{616} and {\cite[Lem.~G.4]{YMM2}} at the label $2\gamma^{-2}$, where the coupling is $\gamma$, puts $2\gamma^{-2}$ in $I(\gamma)=(\gamma^{-2}+\bar B,X_\gamma-\bar B]$; so $\gamma^{-2}>\bar B$. With $g'^{-2}=b'/2$ the formula for $I^\circ$ in the setting gives $I^\circ(g')=(\frac12b'+\bar B,\,\frac12Lb'+(L-2)\bar B)$. Its upper end exceeds $b'$, as $L\ge3$, and its lower end is less than $b'$ if and only if $b'>2\bar B$, which holds for $b'\ge2\gamma^{-2}$; and then $g'\le(2/(2\gamma^{-2}))^{1/2}=\gamma$. (b) As $I^\circ(g')$ is open, $a_{K_j}\beta_j\in I(g')$ for all large $j$, and Cor.~\YMMref{74.2}{616} at the label $a_{K_j}\beta_j$ says that $(K_j,L^{K_j}a_{K_j}\beta_j)=(K_j,\beta_j)$ is a first-passage datum at $g'$.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Agreement of states at two points}

\begin{proposition}[Agreement of two states at two points]\label{C-351-7}
Let $\mathfrak c$ be a choice, $0<g'\le\gamma_W^{\rm sd}$, $(K,\beta)$ a first-passage datum at $g'$ with $K\ge3$ and label $b=a_K\beta$, $\vartheta\in(0,1)$, $0<d\le d_\flat(g',\vartheta)$ and $a_K\le9d$. A \emph{periodic Gibbs state} of the Wilson action at $\beta$ on $a_K\mathbb Z^3$ is a Gibbs state at $(a_K,\beta)$ that is invariant under the translations of a subgroup of finite index of $a_K\mathbb Z^3$ (Section~\YMMref{91}{697}); these states form the set $\mathcal G^{\rm per}_{K,\beta}$. For every $K$ and every $\beta>0$ this set is the set $\mathcal G^{\rm inv}_{K,\beta}$ of the periodic Gibbs states that are invariant under all the translations of $a_K\mathbb Z^3$ (Prop.~\YMMref{103.4}{758}; {\cite[\S{}K.1]{YMM2}}), and it contains the states of the tori, the weak limit points of the periodic extensions of the Wilson measures on the tori $T_{2L^m}$, $m\to\infty$ (Prop.~\YMMref{91.2}{699}; {\cite[\S{}K.1]{YMM2}}).

A \emph{state at the datum} is the periodic extension to $a_K\mathbb Z^3$ of the Wilson measure on $T_\ell$ at $(K,\beta)$, for some $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g')$, or a periodic Gibbs state of the Wilson action at $\beta$ on $a_K\mathbb Z^3$: a state at $g'$ at $(K,\beta)$ in the sense of {\cite[\S{}K.1]{YMM2}}. Every state at the datum is invariant under the translations of $a_K\mathbb Z^3$, and so are its cumulants: $S^T_n[\mathfrak s](\tau_vf_1,\dots,\tau_vf_n)=S^T_n[\mathfrak s](f_1,\dots,f_n)$ for all $v\in a_K\mathbb Z^3$ ({\cite[\S{}K.1]{YMM2}}). Let $\mu'$ be the periodic extension of the Wilson measure on the least torus $T_{\ell_{g'}}$ at $(K,\beta)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] Every state $\mathfrak s$ at the datum satisfies $|S^T_2[\mathfrak s](\Psi)-S^T_2[\mu'](\Psi)|\le C_2^{\rm T}(g')\vartheta^{-1}d^2b^{-2}|\Psi|$ for all $\Psi\in\mathfrak T_{\mathbb R^3}(d;\vartheta)$; hence any two states $\mathfrak s,\mathfrak s'$ at the datum have
\[
|S^T_2[\mathfrak s](\Psi)-S^T_2[\mathfrak s'](\Psi)|\le2C_2^{\rm T}(g')\,\vartheta^{-1}d^2(a_K\beta)^{-2}|\Psi| .
\]
\item[(b)] Here $d_\flat(g',\vartheta)=\min\{\frac1{180},d_\star(g',\vartheta)\}$ with $d_\star(g',\vartheta)=c_{\rm a}\vartheta^{-1}g'^{-2}$, and
\[
C_2^{\rm T}(g')=C_{\rm a}\bigl[Q_0(g')\,Q_1(g')\bigr]^2\,\frac{(X_{g'}+\bar B)^3}{(g'^{-2}-\bar B)^2},\qquad Q_0(g')=\exp\bigl[\tfrac18\ell_{g'}^3(2C_{\rm S}+C_{g'})\bigr],
\]
where $C_{\rm S}$ and $C_{g'}$ are the numbers of the bounds of Thms.~\YMMref{AJ}{673} and~\YMMref{AD}{607} on the partition functions of the tori, $Q_1(g')\ge1$ is the bound on the linking cumulants of step~(4) of the proof, and $c_{\rm a},C_{\rm a}>0$ depend only on the constants. So $d_\star>0$ and $C_2^{\rm T}(g')<\infty$ depend only on the radius, the constants and $g'$ (and on $\vartheta$, for $d_\star$), and on no $K$, $\beta$, side, state, pair or position.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Let $\ell'=\ell_{g'}$, let $x_1$ be a centre of a ball of radius $d$ that holds ${\rm supp}f$, and consider on $a_K\mathbb Z^3$ the board of cubic cells of side $\ell'/2$ one of which, $\square_0$, is centred within $\frac12a_K$ of $x_1$; on $T_{\ell'}$ there are eight cells, the mirror images of $\square_0$ under lattice reflections.

(1)

\emph{One cell against the least torus.} For a bounded function $F$ of the configuration that depends only on the bonds in the interior of $\square_0$ put $\|F\|_{\rm ch}^8=\mu'(\prod_{\mathbf k\in\{0,1\}^3}F^{[\mathbf k]})\ge0$, the $F^{[\mathbf k]}$ being the mirror copies of $F$ in the eight cells, conjugated when the number of reflections is odd. This is the chessboard seminorm $\|F\|_{{\rm ch},\ell'}$ of the side $\ell'$. Then $|\mathfrak s(F)|\le Q_0\|F\|_{\rm ch}$ for every state at the datum. For the torus of a side $\ell\ge\ell'$ of $\mathfrak L(g')$ the chessboard estimate at the mirrors of the cells gives $|\mathfrak s(F)|\le\|F\|_{{\rm ch},\ell}$ (clause~(c) of {\cite[Cor.~B.1]{YMM2}}), and the comparison of two sides gives $\|F\|_{{\rm ch},\ell}\le\|F\|_{{\rm ch},\ell'}\,e^{(\ell'/2)^3(p_{\ell'}-p_\ell)}$ with the pressures $p_\ell=\ell^{-3}\log Z_{K,\ell,\beta}$ (clause~(e) there); Thms.~\YMMref{AJ}{673} and~\YMMref{AD}{607} at the source $0$ bound $p_{\ell'}-p_\ell$ by $2C_{\rm S}+C_{g'}$, so that $e^{(\ell'/2)^3(p_{\ell'}-p_\ell)}\le Q_0$.

A periodic Gibbs state $\mathfrak s$ is dominated through tori of growing sides: by the domination of the means of a periodic Gibbs state by the chessboard seminorms of the tori (Prop.~\YMMref{91.9}{705}, for the board above, the one cell $\square_0$ and a sequence of sides $\ell_k\in\mathfrak L(g')$ with $\ell_k\to\infty$), $|\mathfrak s(F)|\le\liminf_k\|F\|_{{\rm ch},\ell_k}$, and every $\|F\|_{{\rm ch},\ell_k}$ is at most $Q_0\|F\|_{\rm ch}$ by the comparison of two sides.

(2)

\emph{Normalised moments; only linking cumulants remain.} For bounded real $F_1,F_2$ localised in $\square_0$ let $X_a=\mathcal O_K(F_a)$, $M'(z)=\mu'(e^{z_1X_1+z_2X_2})$, $M_{\mathfrak s}(z)=\mathfrak s(e^{z_1X_1+z_2X_2})$, and $c_I=\partial_I(1/M')(0)$, $I\subset\{1,2\}$, which are real. For $\emptyset\ne B\subset\{1,2\}$ the function $P_B=\sum_{I\subset B}c_{B\setminus I}\prod_{a\in I}X_a$ has $\mathfrak s(P_B)=\partial_B(M_{\mathfrak s}/M')(0)$. Its mirror copies are the same polynomials in the mirror images $X_{a,\mathbf k}=\mathcal O_K(F_a\circ\hat{\mathsf r}^{-1}_{\mathbf k})$, and as $\mu'$ is invariant under the lattice isometries,
\[
\|P_B\|_{\rm ch}^8=\mu'\Bigl(\prod_{\mathbf k}P_B^{[\mathbf k]}\Bigr)=\sum_\pi\prod_{\gamma\in\pi}\bigl\langle X_{a,\mathbf k};\,(\mathbf k,a)\in\gamma\bigr\rangle_{\mu'},
\]
the sum running over the partitions $\pi$ of $\{0,1\}^3\times B$ into \emph{linking} blocks, blocks that hold images in two different cells: all cumulants within one cell cancel. So if every linking cumulant is at most $Q_1\prod_{(\mathbf k,a)\in\gamma}u_a$, then $|\partial_B(M_{\mathfrak s}/M')(0)|\le Q_0\mathsf{Bl}_{16}^{1/8}Q_1^{|B|/2}\prod_{a\in B}u_a$, $\mathsf{Bl}_N$ the number of partitions of a set of $N$ elements, and the two cumulants $\partial_1\partial_2\log M_{\mathfrak s}(0)$, $\partial_1\partial_2\log M'(0)$ differ by $|\partial_1\partial_2\log(M_{\mathfrak s}/M')(0)|\le2(Q_0\mathsf{Bl}_{16}^{1/8}Q_1)^2u_1u_2$.

(3)

\emph{Packing and signs.} Let $\iota=a_K\lceil18d/a_K\rceil$ and $\mathsf{Pk}=\{v\in\iota\mathbb Z^3:|v_\mu|\le0.575-9d\}$. The balls $\mathbb B(x_1+v,9d)$, $v\in\mathsf{Pk}$, are disjoint and lie in $\mathbb B(x_1,1)\subset\square_0$, both supports of $\Psi$ lie in $\mathbb B(x_1,9d)$, and $\#\mathsf{Pk}\ge(0.3/9d)^3=(30d)^{-3}$. For signs $\epsilon=(\epsilon_v)$ apply~(2) to $F_1=\sum_v\epsilon_v\tau_vf$, $F_2=\sum_v\epsilon_v\tau_vh$. The difference $\mathsf D=S^T_2[\mathfrak s]-S^T_2[\mu']$ is bilinear, its mean over the signs at $(F_1,F_2)$ is $\sum_v\mathsf D(\tau_vf,\tau_vh)$, and both cumulants are invariant under the translations of $a_K\mathbb Z^3$ ({\cite[\S{}K.1]{YMM2}}); so $|\mathsf D(f,h)|\le(30d)^3\sup_\epsilon|\mathsf D(F_1,F_2)|$.

(4)

\emph{The linking cumulants on the least torus.} For a complex source $w$ on the plaquettes of $T_{\ell'}$ let $Z[w]=\int\rho_0\,e^{\mathcal O(w)}\,\mathrm{d}U$ be the partition function of $T_{\ell'}$ with the source $w$, $\rho_0$ the Wilson density at $(K,\beta)$ and $\mathcal O(w)(U)=L^K\sum_pw(p)\,a_p(U)$, and $Z=Z[0]$. The generating function of the sixteen mirrored, packed and signed observables is $Z[W_z]/Z$, with the source $W_z=\sum_{\mathbf k,a}z_{\mathbf k,a}(F_a\circ\hat{\mathsf r}_{\mathbf k}^{-1})^{\langle\ell'\rangle}\circ x$; it vanishes off the plaquettes whose barycentres lie in the eight mirror images of $\mathbb B(x_1,1)$, closed balls of radius $1$ whose centres are at pairwise sup distances $\ge\frac12\ell'-a_K$. Write
\[
\log\frac{Z[W]}Z=\log\frac{Z[W]e^{-\mathcal E(W)}}Z+\Bigl[\mathcal E(W)-\sum_{\mathbf k}\mathcal E(w^{(\mathbf k)})\Bigr]+\sum_{\mathbf k}\mathcal E(w^{(\mathbf k)}),
\]
$\mathcal E$ the source energy of $T_{\ell'}$, the sum over the levels and localisation domains of the source energies {\cite[eq.~212]{YMM2}} of the sourced renormalisation-group chain {\cite[eq.~205]{YMM2}}, and $w^{(\mathbf k)}$ the part of $W$ in the cell $\mathbf k$.

(4a) \emph{The setting on $T_{\ell'}$.} Let $\ell'=2L^m$, $m=m_{\mathfrak L}(g')$. By~\YMMref{(1528)}{615}, $L^m=LM\max\{R(L(g'^{-2}+\bar B)),L^{\lceil\log_LC_{\rm s}\rceil}\}$, and the values of the cube-size function $R$ are powers $L^{\mathsf u}$ with $\mathsf u\ge1$; so the cells have the side $\mathsf l:=\frac12\ell'\ge L^2M$. As $g'\le\gamma_W^{\rm sd}$, the least side is small over the run: $MR(x_K)\le L^m$ (Lem.~\YMMref{126.3}{846}). As $K\ge3$, Lem.~\YMMref{126.2}{845}, whose head asks $K\ge3$, gives $x_j\ge x_{\rm J}$ for $0\le j\le K$ and makes the cuts of the run, on the lattice $(\ell',K)$, frames of the construction; so the setting (J) holds with the last height $K-1$ ({\cite[Prop.~B.21]{YMM2}}), and the canonical sourced chain of $T_{\ell'}$ is formed, its conditions holding by {\cite[Cor.~B.13]{YMM2}}, at the sources of a class of small sources, an open neighbourhood of $0$.

By the running estimate~\YMMref{(1530)}{615} at the index $K$ and the endpoint bounds~\YMMref{(1529)}{615}, $b_-\le a_{K-j}x_j\le b_+$ for $0\le j\le K$, with $b_\pm=x_K\pm\bar B$; and $g'^{-2}-\bar B<b_-$, $b_+\le X_{g'}+\bar B$. The places, the classes of the sum rule, the image sets and the chart integrals of the steps, the backgrounds and the minimal orbits that the setting (J) names ({\cite[Lem.~B.17]{YMM2}} and {\cite[Prop.~B.18]{YMM2}}) are the objects that the sourced chain names ({\cite[Prop.~B.15]{YMM2}} and its one-step proof): both use the same definitions (among them {\cite[Def.~B.2]{YMM2}} and equation~{\cite[eq.~191]{YMM2}} of the chart integral and {\cite[Def.~B.2]{YMM2}} of the image set), at the same lattice $(\ell',K)$, the same height $j$ and the same coupling $\mathsf t=x_j$.

(4b)

\emph{The level-wise norm; the families and the energies.} For a source $w$ let $v^w_j=-L^{K-j}w/x_j$ be its weight at the level $j$. The \emph{level-wise norm} $\|w\|_{\rm lw}$ is the largest, over $0\le j<K$, of $|v^w_j|_\infty/\sigma_{\rm a}$ and of $\operatorname{sw}_j(v^w_j)/(\mu_{\rm a}x_j^{-1/2})$, where $\operatorname{sw}_j(v)$ is the largest difference of the values of $v$ at two plaquettes whose barycentres are at a sup distance $\le Ma_{K-j}$, and $\sigma_{\rm a}=\sigma_{\rm src}$, $\mu_{\rm a}x_j^{-1/2}=o_{\rm src}(x_j)$ are the radii of the class of the weights of \eqref{eq:source-weight-room}, $\sigma_{\rm a}$ and $\mu_{\rm a}$ depending only on the constants.

It is a norm; its open unit ball $\mathsf{Src}^{\rm lw}$ is convex, consists of the sources whose weights lie at every level in the class of the weights at which Prop.~\ref{prop:source-entry} is stated, and contains the class of small sources of~(4a); and $|w|_\infty\le\sigma_{\rm a}b_+\|w\|_{\rm lw}$, as $|v^w_j|_\infty=|w|_\infty/(a_{K-j}x_j)$. {\cite[Prop.~B.12]{YMM2}} runs the induction on $\mathsf{Src}^{\rm lw}$; consequently the sourced families of all levels are formed there, holomorphic in the source, bounded by $E_0$, a constant of the canonical list, in the norm of the localised terms at the rate $\kappa+1$, and the family on a domain reads the source on the plaquettes of that domain alone.

So the source energies $e_j(X;w)$ of the domains $X$ of the level $j$ are holomorphic on $\mathsf{Src}^{\rm lw}$, vanish at $w=0$ and read $w$ on the plaquettes of $X$ alone (equation~{\cite[eq.~212]{YMM2}} and its proof), and, by~{\cite[eq.~213]{YMM2}} at the bound $2E_0$ of the differences of the families and by Schwarz's lemma for $\zeta\mapsto e_j(X;\zeta w/\|w\|_{\rm lw})$ on the unit disc,
\[
|e_j(X;w)|\le16M^3E_0\,\|w\|_{\rm lw}\,e^{-\kappa d_j(X)},
\]
$d_j(X)$ the linear size of $X$ in the units of the level $j$. Put $\mathcal E_t(w)=\sum_{j\le t}\sum_{X\in\mathcal D_j}e_j(X;w)$, $\mathcal D_j$ the localisation domains of the level $j$; so $\mathcal E=\mathcal E_K$, and these functions are holomorphic on $\mathsf{Src}^{\rm lw}$ and vanish at $0$.

(4c)

\emph{The term without large fields, with a source.} For $0\le t\le K$ let $h_t$ be the history without large-field regions up to the level $t$ and $\tau_{h_t}[\cdot]$ its term (Section~\YMMref{123}{828}), a complex Borel measure on the configurations $\mathcal V_t$ of the level $t$, and $\mathsf m_t=\tau_{h_t}[\rho_0]$: a positive measure of mass at most $Z$ (equation~\eqref{eq:ward-first-creation}), equal to $\rho_0\,\mathrm{d}U$ at $t=0$ and carried, for $t\ge1$, by the open set $\mathcal V^\chi_t$ of the configurations that pass the density tests of the level (Prop.~\YMMref{123.1}{829}). For $w\in\mathsf{Src}^{\rm lw}$ and $0\le t\le K$,
\[
\tau_{h_t}\bigl[\rho_0e^{\mathcal O(w)}\bigr]=e^{\mathcal E_t(w)}\,e^{\mathsf R_t(w,\cdot)}\,\mathsf m_t ,
\]
an identity of complex Borel measures on $\mathcal V_t$, with $\mathsf R_0(w,\cdot)=\mathcal O(w)$ and, for $t\ge1$ and $W\in\mathcal V^\chi_t$,
\[
\mathsf R_t(w,W)=\mathcal O(w)(U)+S[\mathfrak f_t[w]](U)-S[\mathfrak f_t[0]](U),
\]
$U$ an element of the minimal orbit over $W$ and $S[\mathfrak f_t[w]]$ the action of the sourced bare array of the level $t$; this value does not depend on the element of the orbit, the domain of definition of the action being a condition on the configuration alone, and $\mathsf R_t(w,\cdot)$ is a bounded Borel function on $\mathcal V^\chi_t$. For the small sources of~(4a) and $1\le t\le K$, the density of $\tau_{h_t}[\rho_0e^{\mathcal O(w)}]$ is
\[
\exp\Bigl[\mathsf C_t(w)-A^{\eta_t}\bigl(x^w_t,U_t(W)\bigr)+S[\mathfrak f_t[w]]\bigl(U_t(W)\bigr)\Bigr]\quad\text{on }\mathcal V^\chi_t,\ \text{and $0$ off it},\qquad\mathsf C_t(w)=\sum_{1\le j\le t}\mathsf c_j+\mathcal E_t(w),
\]
with numbers $\mathsf c_j$ formed with the source $0$ alone, the weight $x^w_t=x_t-L^{K-t}w$ of the weighted action $A^{\eta_t}$, $\eta_t=L^{-t}$, and the background $U_t(W)$ over $W$. This follows by induction over $t$. At $t=0$ the term is $\rho_0e^{\mathcal O(w)}dU$, and $\rho_0e^{\mathcal O(w)}=e^{-A^{\eta_0}(x^w_0,\cdot)}$ (equation~{\cite[eq.~216]{YMM2}}). From $t$ to $t+1$: the term of the history is carried by one step, $\tau_{h_{t+1}}[\cdot]=\mathbf T(\mathsf g_{t+1}\tau_{h_t}[\cdot])$ with the factor $\mathsf g_{t+1}\ge0$ of the step, and a measure whose density on $\mathcal V^\chi_t$ is $e^{\mathsf e}$ times a bounded Borel function $F$ is carried to the density $e^{\mathsf e}\,\mathsf I[F]$ on $\mathcal V^\chi_{t+1}$, and $0$ off it, $\mathsf I[F]$ being the chart integral of the step ({\cite[Prop.~B.18]{YMM2}}); here, for $t\ge1$, $\mathsf e=\mathsf C_t(w)$ and $F$ is the function $F^w_t$ in the proof of {\cite[Prop.~B.15]{YMM2}} at $k=t$, which on $\mathcal V^\chi_t$ is $\exp[-A^{\eta_t}(x^w_t,U_t(V))+S[\mathfrak f_t[w]](U_t(V))]$ (the definition preceding {\cite[eq.~218]{YMM2}}), and for $t=0$, $\mathsf e=0$ and $F=\rho_0e^{\mathcal O(w)}$, whose chart integral is that of $F^w_0$ on the class of the sum rule (the height-zero case in that proof); $\mathcal V^\chi_{t+1}$ lies in the class of the sum rule of the step and in the set on which the chart integral is formed ({\cite[Lem.~B.17]{YMM2}}); and there the one-step identity of the sourced chain {\cite[eq.~218]{YMM2}} gives
\[
\mathsf I[F^w_t](W)=\exp\Bigl[\mathsf c_{t+1}+\sum_{X\in\mathcal D_{t+1}}e_{t+1}(X;w)-A^{\eta_{t+1}}\bigl(x^w_{t+1},U_{t+1}(W)\bigr)+S[\mathfrak f_{t+1}[w]]\bigl(U_{t+1}(W)\bigr)\Bigr].
\]
The weighted action is linear in the weight, $A^{\eta_t}(x^w_t,U)=A^{\eta_t}(x_t,U)-\mathcal O(w)(U)$; so the quotient of the density by the same density at $w=0$, which is the density of $\mathsf m_t$, is $e^{\mathcal E_t(w)+\mathsf R_t(w,\cdot)}$ on $\mathcal V^\chi_t$: the identity holds for the small sources. For $w\in\mathsf{Src}^{\rm lw}$, $w\ne0$, and a bounded Borel function $\psi$ on $\mathcal V_t$, the function $\zeta\mapsto\int\psi\,\mathrm{d}\tau_{h_t}[\rho_0e^{\zeta\mathcal O(w)}]$ is entire, and $\zeta\mapsto e^{\mathcal E_t(\zeta w)}\int\psi\,e^{\mathsf R_t(\zeta w,\cdot)}\,\mathrm{d}\mathsf m_t$ is holomorphic on $\{|\zeta|\,\|w\|_{\rm lw}<1\}$, by~(4b); they agree for small $\zeta$, hence at $\zeta=1$.

(4d)

\emph{The remainders.} Let $w\in\mathsf{Src}^{\rm lw}$ vanish off the plaquettes whose barycentres lie in $N_{\rm b}$ closed balls of radius $1$. Then
\[
\begin{multlined}
|\mathsf R_K(w,\cdot)|\le\|w\|_{\rm lw}N_{\rm b}\,\mathsf g_\emptyset\ \relax \ \relax \text{on }\mathcal V^\chi_K,\qquad|\mathsf R_{n-1}(w,\cdot)|+|\mathcal E(w)-\mathcal E_{n-1}(w)| \\
\le\|w\|_{\rm lw}N_{\rm b}\,C_{\rm cnt}\,L^{4(K-n+1)}\ \relax \ \relax \text{on }\mathcal V^\chi_{n-1}\quad(1\le n\le K),
\end{multlined}
\]
on all of $\mathcal V_0$ for $n=1$, with numbers $\mathsf g_\emptyset$ and $C_{\rm cnt}\ge1$ that depend only on $g'$ and the constants. Indeed, let $W\in\mathcal V^\chi_s$. The background over $W$ has $0\le a_p(U_s(W))<2B_3^2\varepsilon_s^2L^{-4s}$ at every bare plaquette~{\cite[eq.~221]{YMM2}}, $\varepsilon_s=\varepsilon(x_s)\le\varepsilon(g'^{-2})$ being the threshold of the small fields at the coupling $x_s$ and $B_3$ a constant of the canonical list; at most $81N_{\rm b}L^{3K}$ plaquettes have their barycentres in the balls; and $|w|_\infty\le\sigma_{\rm a}b_+\|w\|_{\rm lw}$. So $|\mathcal O(w)(U_s(W))|\le162N_{\rm b}B_3^2\varepsilon_s^2\sigma_{\rm a}b_+L^{4(K-s)}\|w\|_{\rm lw}$, and at $s=0$, where $0\le a_p\le2$, $|\mathcal O(w)|\le162N_{\rm b}\sigma_{\rm a}b_+L^{4K}\|w\|_{\rm lw}$.

The difference of the two actions is the sum, over the levels $j\le s$, the domains $X$ of the level $j$ that meet the support of $w$ and their points $z$, of the differences between the values at $U$ and at $\mathbf 1$ of the local terms $(E^{(j)}[w]-E^{(j)}[0])(X,\cdot,z)$, each of a norm at most $2E_0\|w\|_{\rm lw}e^{-(\kappa+1)d_j(X)}$ by~(4b). Every element of the minimal orbit over $W$ is regular of the level $s$ at the radius $2B_3\varepsilon_s$ ({\cite[Lem.~B.17]{YMM2}}); at such a configuration a local term of the level $j$ moves from its value at $\mathbf 1$ by at most its norm times $C(\varepsilon_s/\alpha_0)^2L^{-4(s-j)}(1+d_j(X))^2$ on the domains that are small against the radius, and by at most twice its norm on the other ones, whose linear sizes are large (equation~\YMMref{(2263)}{828} and its proof), $\alpha_0$ being the fixed radius of the localised terms; the bound in {\cite[Lem.~B.10]{YMM2}}, with at most $27N_{\rm b}L^{3(K-s)}$ cubes of the level $s$ holding a corner of a plaquette of the support, sums these differences to at most $CN_{\rm b}L^{3(K-s)}\|w\|_{\rm lw}$.

The energies of the levels $>s$ are bounded in the same way, by~(4b) and~(q3), by $CN_{\rm b}L^{3(K-s)}\|w\|_{\rm lw}$. With $b_+\le X_{g'}+\bar B$ this gives the two bounds.

(4e) \emph{The coefficients of $Z[w]e^{-\mathcal E(w)}/Z$.} By \eqref{eq:ward-first-creation} at level $K$, applied to the bounded gauge invariant function $e^{\mathcal O(w)}$, with the canonical history measures of Section~\YMMref{123}{828},
\[
Z[w]=Z_\emptyset[w]+\sum_{n=1}^KZ_n[w],\qquad Z_\emptyset[w]=\tau_{h_K}\bigl[\rho_0e^{\mathcal O(w)}\bigr](\mathcal V_K),\qquad Z_n[w]=\int\mathsf g^{\rm w}_n\,\mathrm{d}\tau_{h_{n-1}}\bigl[\rho_0e^{\mathcal O(w)}\bigr],
\]
where $\mathsf g^{\rm w}_n\ge0$ is the factor of the step $n$ at which a large-field region is first created, and $\mathsf w_n=Z^{-1}\int\mathsf g^{\rm w}_n\,\mathrm{d}\mathsf m_{n-1}$ is the weight of that event; each term is an entire function of $w$. By~(4c),
\[
Z_\emptyset[w]e^{-\mathcal E(w)}=\int e^{\mathsf R_K(w,\cdot)}\,\mathrm{d}\mathsf m_K,\qquad Z_n[w]e^{-\mathcal E(w)}=e^{-(\mathcal E-\mathcal E_{n-1})(w)}\int\mathsf g^{\rm w}_n\,e^{\mathsf R_{n-1}(w,\cdot)}\,\mathrm{d}\mathsf m_{n-1},
\]
so that, by~(4d) and as $\mathsf m_K$ has a mass at most $Z$,
\[
\bigl|Z_\emptyset[w]e^{-\mathcal E(w)}\bigr|\le e^{\|w\|_{\rm lw}N_{\rm b}\mathsf g_\emptyset}\,Z,\qquad\bigl|Z_n[w]e^{-\mathcal E(w)}\bigr|\le\exp\bigl[\|w\|_{\rm lw}N_{\rm b}C_{\rm cnt}L^{4(K-n+1)}\bigr]\,\mathsf w_n\,Z .
\]
At $w=W_z$ take $N_{\rm b}=8$ and the polydisc $\mathbb P=\{|z_{\mathbf k,a}|<r_a\}$, $r_a=A_\star(d)/\|f_a\|_\infty$, on which $\|W_z\|_{\rm lw}\le\max_{\mathbf k,a}|z_{\mathbf k,a}|/r_a<1$ by~(4g). The function $\Phi_{\rm D}(z)=Z[W_z]e^{-\mathcal E(W_z)}/Z$ is holomorphic on $\mathbb P$, $Z[w]$ being entire, and $\Phi_{\rm D}(0)=1$; its term without large fields is at most $e^{8\mathsf g_\emptyset}$ on the whole of $\mathbb P$, and its term of the level $n$ at most $e\,\mathsf w_n$ on the polydisc smaller by the factor $8C_{\rm cnt}L^{4(K-n+1)}$. Cauchy's estimate on each polydisc gives, for every set $J$ of at most sixteen of the variables,
\[
|\partial_J\Phi_{\rm D}(0)|\le\Bigl[e^{8\mathsf g_\emptyset}+e\,(8C_{\rm cnt}L^4)^{16}\sum_{n=1}^KL^{64(K-n)}\mathsf w_n\Bigr]\prod_{i\in J}r_i^{-1}.
\]
By \eqref{eq:ward-first-creation}, $\mathsf w_n\le\widetilde\nu_K\{Z_n\ne\emptyset\}$. Equation~\eqref{eq:ward-weighted-tail}, at $q=64$ and $t=K$, therefore bounds $\sum_nL^{64(K-n)}\mathsf w_n$ by
\[
 4M^{-3}(\ell')^3e^{\mathsf B(X_{g'})(\ell')^3}
          \mathsf C_{\rm ag}(65)e^{-c'p_0(g_K)^2/2}.
\]
The assumptions hold by the canonical choice of the fixed history thresholds in Prop.~\ref{prop:ward-fixed-volume-rarity}; the ceiling $g'\le\gamma_W^{\rm sd}$ preserves them. Since $\ell'$ depends only on $g'$ and the constants, the square bracket is bounded by a number $Q_{\rm D}(g')\ge1$ with the same dependence.

(4f)

\emph{The linking cumulants.} The last sum of the decomposition is a sum of functions each of which reads the variables of one cell; it is annulled by every linking derivative. In the bracket only the domains $X$ that meet the supports of two parts $w^{(\mathbf k)}$ contribute, the source energies being local and vanishing at $0$. Such a domain of the level $j$ holds corners of plaquettes whose barycentres lie in two different balls, and two such corners are at a sup distance $\ge\mathsf l-3$, while two points of a domain of the level $j$ are at a sup distance at most $M(d_j(X)+2)a_{K-j}$; so $d_j(X)\ge(\mathsf l-3)L^{K-j}/M-2\ge166L^{K-j}$, as $\mathsf l\ge L^2M$ and $L\ge13$. The bound of~(4b) at the nine sources $W$, $w^{(\mathbf k)}$ and the bound in {\cite[Lem.~B.10]{YMM2}} give
\[
\Bigl|\mathcal E(W)-\sum_{\mathbf k}\mathcal E(w^{(\mathbf k)})\Bigr|\le C_\Delta\max_{\mathbf k}\bigl\{\|W\|_{\rm lw},\|w^{(\mathbf k)}\|_{\rm lw}\bigr\},
\]
this exponential decay of the source energies in the size of their domains summing over the levels to a number $C_\Delta$ depending only on the constants. On $\mathbb P$ the bracket is holomorphic and at most $C_\Delta$, so that Cauchy's estimate bounds its squarefree coefficients by $C_\Delta\prod_ir_i^{-1}$. A derivative $\partial_J$ at $0$ of the logarithm of a function equal to $1$ at $0$ is the sum, over the partitions $\pi$ of $J$, of $(-1)^{|\pi|-1}(|\pi|-1)!$ times the product over the blocks of its derivatives; so the squarefree coefficients of $\log\Phi_{\rm D}$ are at most $\mathsf{cu}_{|J|}Q_{\rm D}^{|J|}\prod_{i\in J}r_i^{-1}$, with $\mathsf{cu}_N=\sum_\pi(|\pi|-1)!$ over the partitions of $N$ elements.

(4g)

\emph{The packed bumps.} For a source made of bumps with pairwise disjoint sets of non-vanishing, of height at most $A$ and Lipschitz constant at most $A/(\vartheta d)$, the supremum of the weight of the level $j$ is at most $A/b_-$, and its oscillation at most $(A/b_-)\min\{2,2\sqrt3Ma_{K-j}/(\vartheta d)\}$; as $a^{-1/2}\min\{2,ca\}\le(2c)^{1/2}$ for all $a>0$, its level-wise norm is at most $A/A_\star(d)$ at every level, with
\[
A_\star(d)=\min\Bigl\{\sigma_{\rm a}b_-,\ \mu_{\rm a}\frac{b_-}{b_+^{1/2}}\Bigl(\frac{\vartheta d}{4\sqrt3M}\Bigr)^{1/2}\Bigr\}\ge c\,(g'^{-2}-\bar B)(X_{g'}+\bar B)^{-3/2}(\vartheta d)^{1/2}\,b\qquad(d\le d_\star(g',\vartheta)),
\]
$d_\star$ being the scale below which the second member of the minimum is the smaller one. The bumps of $W_z$ are the mirror images of the $z_{\mathbf k,a}\epsilon_v\tau_vf_a$; their sets of non-vanishing are pairwise disjoint, their heights are at most $A=\max_{\mathbf k,a}|z_{\mathbf k,a}|\,\|f_a\|_\infty$ and their Lipschitz constants at most $A/(\vartheta d)$, as ${\rm Lip}f_a\le\|f_a\|_\infty/(\vartheta d)$; so $\|W_z\|_{\rm lw}\le\max_{\mathbf k,a}|z_{\mathbf k,a}|/r_a$.
So, by~(4f), every linking cumulant is at most $(\mathsf{cu}_{16}Q_{\rm D}^{16}+C_\Delta)\prod_{(\mathbf k,a)\in\gamma}r_a^{-1}$: the linking cumulants obey the bound of~(2) with $u_a=\|f_a\|_\infty/A_\star(d)$ and $Q_1=\mathsf{cu}_{16}Q_{\rm D}^{16}+C_\Delta$.

(5)

\emph{Conclusion.} By (1)--(4), 
\[
|S^T_2[\mathfrak s](\Psi)-S^T_2[\mu'](\Psi)|\le(30d)^3\,2(Q_0\mathsf{Bl}_{16}^{1/8}Q_1)^2A_\star(d)^{-2}|\Psi|\le C_2^{\rm T}(g')\vartheta^{-1}d^2b^{-2}|\Psi|
\]
 for $d\le d_\flat$, which is~(a) with the constants of~(b); two states differ by at most twice this.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
The proof uses only the following properties of the pair: real Lipschitz functions, neither $0$, each vanishing off a ball of radius $d$, whose sets of non-vanishing are disjoint and lie in one ball of radius $9d$, with ${\rm Lip}f_a\le\|f_a\|_\infty/(\vartheta d)$. So Prop.~\ref{C-351-7} holds also for such pairs of either sign. With $n$ entries in the place of two, every pair of which lies in $\mathfrak T_{\mathbb R^3}(d;\vartheta)$, the same argument gives a difference of at most $2C_n^{\rm T}(g')\vartheta^{-n/2}d^{3-n/2}b^{-n}\prod_a\|f_a\|_\infty$, which is small against the natural size $b^{-n}\prod_a\|f_a\|_\infty$ for $n\le5$; we use only $n=2$.
\end{remark}

\subsubsection{The coefficient on the least torus}

Here the constants are an admissible assignment of the canonical list.
