The statements used in Lems.~\ref{C-351-8}--\ref{C-351-12} are made for the data (Wp1)--(Wp6) of a weighted progression ({\cite[Def.~B.7]{YMM2}}), in its setting (J) ({\cite[Def.~B.16]{YMM2}}) and, where a step is continued to a complex field scale, at a place with a lower place (Def.~\ref{IV-71-12}); we call this the setting of the weighted progression (the statements used in Lem.~\ref{C-351-13}, the constants and thresholds in Thm.~\YMMref{AR}{810}, Thm.~\YMMref{AR}{810}, equation~\YMMref{(2203)}{810}, Cor.~\YMMref{117.1}{812}, Lem.~\ref{lem:cutoff-admissible-labels} and Cor.~\YMMref{118.4}{815}, are made in the setting (Th1), (Th2), whose datum is the choice of the constants).

For the canonical objects at every admissible assignment of the canonical list it holds: the data are given by {\cite[Cor.~B.9]{YMM2}}; the setting (J) holds by {\cite[Prop.~B.21]{YMM2}} as soon as the couplings are at least the threshold $x_{\rm J}$ of the definitions preceding {\cite[eq.~228]{YMM2}}, a number depending only on the constants, and at a first-passage datum at $g$ this is the case whenever $g^{-2}\ge x_{\rm J}$, all the couplings of the run exceeding $g^{-2}$ (Lem.~\ref{C-351-8}); and the places with a lower place are those of Prop.~\ref{IV-71-50}. Besides the constants the setting involves two auxiliary real numbers: the lower place $\mathsf t_\flat\ge\gamma^{-2}$, and a room $\mathsf q>0$, such that a bound on the sizes of the bare arrays formed with the constants alone, increased by $2\mathsf q$, does not exceed the size ceiling at the lower place.

For the canonical objects $\mathsf q=1$, and $\mathsf t_\flat$ is a number depending only on the constants. No further condition on the constants enters. $\gamma_{\rm e}\in(0,\gamma]$ is the largest number under which the setting holds and all the conditions on $g$ of these statements hold (each has the form $g\le\gamma'$ or $\log g^{-2}\ge Y$ with numbers $\gamma'$, $Y$ depending only on the constants), together with $g^{-2}\ge4\bar B$; for $0<g\le\gamma_{\rm e}$, $d_{\rm e}(g,\vartheta)\in(0,L^{-13}]$ is the largest number below which their conditions on $d$ and those of the proof of Prop.~\ref{C-351-14} hold (the arithmetic of the levels there uses $d\le L^{-13}$, and the removal of the cutoff there uses $d\le d_{\rm K}$, the number of Lem.~\ref{C-351-13} at $\ell=\ell_g$).

The depth of the scale $d$ at $g$ is the witness depth $s(d)=\min\{s\ge0:L^sd\ge C_W(s)\}$, $C_W(s)=\mathsf c_W(\log[L^{s+1}(g^{-2}+\bar B)])^{2p_0}$, with a number $\mathsf c_W\ge1$ depending only on the constants (equation~\YMMref{(2321)}{843}); so $C_W(s(d))\le L^{s(d)}d<LC_W(s(d))$, $C_W(s(d))\ge(\log\frac1d)^2$, $s(d)\to\infty$ as $d\to0$, and $K>s(d)$ entails $d/a_K\ge L(\log\frac1d)^2$, hence $K\ge3$ and $8a_K\le d$. We write $D_j=a_{K-j}$ (the spacing of the level $j$), $\mathsf l=\max\{1,\log(2b/d)\}$, $\mathfrak b(x)=A_1(\log x)^{p_0}$ for the field cut-off, $A_1$ and the integer $p_0\ge1$ being constants of the canonical list, $\|u\|_\sharp=\max\{\|u\|_\infty,40M\,{\rm Lip}\,u\}$ and $\mathbb Z^3_N=\mathbb Z^3/N\mathbb Z^3$; $C$ denotes numbers that depend only on the constants, and on $g$ and $\vartheta$ where this is shown.

\begin{lemma}[The run]\label{C-351-8}
Let $0<g\le\gamma_{\rm e}$ and $(K,\beta)$ a first-passage datum at $g$ with $K\ge3$ and label $b$. Then $|x_j-L^{-(j-i)}x_i|\le\bar B$ for $0\le i\le j\le K$, $g^{-2}<x_K\le X_g$, and $\frac34b/D_j\le x_j\le2b/D_j$ for $0\le j\le K$. On every $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$ the setting of the weighted progression holds with the sources $f\circ x$, $h\circ x$ for all real bounded $f,h$ on $T_\ell$ supported in closed balls of radius $d$ at a distance $\ge d$, with $8a_K\le d$, neither $f\circ x$ nor $h\circ x$ vanishing identically; no other condition on $d$ enters. If $f\circ x$ or $h\circ x$ vanishes identically, then so does $(\tau_vf)\circ x$, respectively $(\tau_vh)\circ x$, for every $v\in a_K\mathbb Z^3$, and $S^T_{2;K,\ell,\beta}(f,h)$, the jets $\mathsf n_j(f,h)$ and $\mathsf n^{\mathsf z}_j(f,h)$ of Lem.~\ref{C-351-10} and every sum $\sum_{p,q}(f\circ x)(p)\,(h\circ x)(q)\,\mathsf k(p,q)$ against a kernel $\mathsf k$ on the plaquettes vanish.

So, for $b_*\in I(g)$, $K'\ge3$ and real functions $w_1,w_2$ on the plaquettes of $\mathbb Z^3_{\ell L^{K'}}$, neither identically $0$, supported in balls of radius $r\ge8$ at a distance $\ge r$, $w_a=f'_a\circ x$ for such a pair $(f'_1,f'_2)$ at the scale $ra_{K'}$ and the first-passage datum $(K',L^{K'}b_*)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The first two assertions are the running and endpoint estimates~\YMMref{(1529)--(1530)}{615}. As $L^{-j}x_0=b/D_j$ and $x_j\ge x_K>g^{-2}\ge4\bar B$: $b/D_j\le x_j+\bar B\le\frac43x_j$, and $x_j\le b/D_j+\bar B\le2b/D_j$ because $b/D_j\ge b>g^{-2}\ge\bar B$. The data of the weighted progression are those of the canonical objects ({\cite[Cor.~B.9]{YMM2}}) at the calibrations $x_0,\dots,x_{K-1}$ of the run, with the lower place $\mathsf t_\flat$ and the room $\mathsf q=1$; the lattice $(\ell,K)$, with the run, is admissible over every cut of the run, for every $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$ (Prop.~\YMMref{74.1}{615}); and the setting (J) holds, as $x_j\ge x_K>g^{-2}\ge x_{\rm J}$ ({\cite[Prop.~B.21]{YMM2}}).

The other conditions of the setting are lower bounds on $x_{K-1}$ and on $\log x_K$ by numbers formed with the constants and with $\mathsf t_\flat$; they hold as $x_{K-1}>X_g\ge Lg^{-2}$ and $x_K>g^{-2}$ once $g$ is small, and they enter $\gamma_{\rm e}$. Of the sources the setting reads only that they are real and bounded, supported in balls of radius $d$ at a distance $\ge d$, with $8a_K\le d$, and not identically $0$; a translation by $v\in a_K\mathbb Z^3$ permutes the barycentres of the plaquettes. If $f\circ x\equiv0$, then $\mathcal O_K(f)=0$, the source $\mu_1f\circ x+\mu_2h\circ x$ does not read $\mu_1$, so that the source energies of the weighted progression do not read it at any field scale, and a sum of the values $(f\circ x)(p)$ against anything vanishes.

For the last sentence let $f'_a$ take the values of $w_a$ at the barycentres of the plaquettes of spacing $a_{K'}$ and vanish elsewhere: they are real and bounded, supported in balls of radius $ra_{K'}$ at a distance $\ge ra_{K'}$, with $8a_{K'}\le ra_{K'}$, and no condition on the depth of the scale $ra_{K'}$ enters; $(K',L^{K'}b_*)$ is a first-passage datum since $b_*\in I(g)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The chart of the iterated block averages]\label{C-351-9}
Let $\ell=2L^m$, $1\le n\le K$ and $2L^{m+K-n+1}\ge C_LM$, $C_L$ a constant of the canonical list. For a block field $W$ of the level $n$ and fluctuation fields $y=(\mathcal A_j)_{j<n}$, $\mathcal A_j$ an $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued $1$-form on the non-pivot bonds of the level $j$, let $W_n=W$, $W_j=V_{W_{j+1}}[\mathcal A_j]$ ({\cite[\S{}B.2]{YMM2}}), $\Upsilon(W,y)=W_0$, and $\theta_{\rm ch}=-\sum_{j<n}[\mathsf J_{V_j}[\mathcal A_j]+\log z^{(j)}_{V_j}]$, with the Jacobian term $\mathsf J$ and the normalisation $z^{(j)}$ of {\cite[Lem.~B.3]{YMM2}}, $V_j=V^{\rm bf}_j(W_{j+1})$ being the averaged background over the block field $W_{j+1}$ ({\cite[\S{}B.2]{YMM2}}).

There are an open neighbourhood $\mathsf O_n$ of $\mathbf 1$ among the block fields of the level $n$ and a number $\rho_2\in(0,1]$, both defined by bounds that depend only on the constants and not on $n$, $K$ or $m$ (they are written out in the proof), such that, with $\Omega=\{|\mathcal A_j|<\rho_2,\ j<n\}$ and
\[
C_{\rm H}=\prod_{j<n}(2\pi^2)^{-\#\mathfrak X^+_j}L^{-3\#\mathfrak B^+_{j+1}},
\]
$\mathfrak X^+_j$ the positively oriented non-pivot bonds of the level $j$ and $\mathfrak B^+_{j+1}$ the positively oriented bonds of the level $j+1$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] on $\mathsf O_n\times\Omega$ the chain and $\theta_{\rm ch}$ are formed, $W_{j+1}$ is the block average of $W_j$, and $\theta_{\rm ch}$ is real analytic;
\item[(ii)] $\Upsilon$ is a real analytic diffeomorphism of $\mathsf O_n\times\Omega$ onto an open set $\mathcal U\ni\mathbf 1$;
\item[(iii)] $\int H\,\mathrm{d}U=C_{\rm H}\int_{\mathsf O_n}\,\mathrm{d}W\int_\Omega \,\mathrm{d}y\,e^{-\theta_{\rm ch}}H(\Upsilon(W,y))$ for every bounded Borel function $H$ that vanishes off $\mathcal U$, and the same holds with every open subset of $\mathsf O_n\times\Omega$ and its image.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
\emph{The numbers and the good sets.} For a configuration $V$ of a level let $\varpi(V)=\max_p|\partial V(p)-\mathbf 1|$, the maximum over the plaquettes of that level, and $\varpi_c(V)$ the same maximum over the plaquettes of the double block of a bond $c$ of the next level; $\mathcal M$ is the block average and $\operatorname{Lg}$ the $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued logarithm. With the numbers $\varpi_\chi$, $\varpi_1=2\varpi_\chi$, $r_\chi$, $C_\chi$ of the chart of the fibre ({\cite[\S{}B.2]{YMM2}}), which depend only on $L$, the small-curvature radius $c^{\rm SO}_2$ of Prop.~\YMMref{14.1}{61} and the response constant $K_{\rm B}$ of {\cite[Lem.~P.5]{YMM2}}, and the constants $B_3$, $\bar\varepsilon$, $\varepsilon_{\rm v}$, $r_{\rm B}$ of the canonical list, put
\[
\begin{multlined}
\mu_\flat=\min\Bigl\{c^{\rm SO}_2,\ \relax \tfrac12\bar\varepsilon,\ \relax \tfrac14L^2\varpi_\chi,\ \relax \tfrac18\varepsilon_{\rm v}\Bigr\},\qquad\rho_2=\min\Bigl\{\frac{r_\chi}{C_\chi},\ \relax \frac{r_{\rm B}}{4C_\chi},\ \relax \frac{(1-L^{-2})\,\mu_\flat}{4K_{\rm B}C_\chi},\ \relax \frac{\varepsilon_{\rm v}}{64C_\chi}\Bigr\},\qquad\mathsf O_n \\
=\Bigl\{W:\ \relax \varpi(W)<\frac{\mu_\flat}{B_3}\Bigr\};
\end{multlined}
\]
they read neither $n$ nor $K$ nor $m$, and $\rho_2\le r_\chi/C_\chi\le1$. For $1\le i\le n$ let $\mathsf{Gd}_i$ be the set of the block fields $W$ of the level $i$ over which the background exists and has a regularity number $\mu_i(W)<\mu_\flat$ ({\cite[Def.~B.2]{YMM2}}; the number is the same at all the elements of the minimal orbit, by unitary gauge invariance), and $\mathsf{Gd}_0=\{V:\varpi(V)<\frac14\varepsilon_{\rm v}\}$.

(1)

\emph{The averaged background over a good block field.} $\mathsf{Gd}_i$ is open and $\{\varpi<\mu_\flat/B_3\}\subset\mathsf{Gd}_i\subset\{\varpi<2\mu_\flat\}$ for $1\le i\le n$: over a block field with $\varpi<\mu_\flat/B_3$ the background exists and has a regularity number $<\mu_\flat$ (Thm.~\YMMref{E}{10} in the setting of Section~\YMMref{52.7}{432}), a regularity number $<\mu_\flat$ gives $\varpi<2\mu_\flat\le\bar\varepsilon$ (Lem.~\ref{lem:background-iterated-average}), and the representative of the background is a real analytic function of the block field (Thm.~\YMMref{E}{10} and {\cite[Lem.~P.5]{YMM2}}); so $\mathbf 1\in\mathsf O_n\subset\mathsf{Gd}_n$. Let $0\le j<n$ and $W\in\mathsf{Gd}_{j+1}$. Then $V_j(W)=V^{\rm bf}_j(W)$ is defined and $\mathcal MV_j(W)=W$: it is the average $\mathcal M^jU$ of an element $U$ of the minimal orbit over $W$, carried to the axial gauge by a gauge transformation (the definition of $p(W)$ in {\cite[Def.~B.2]{YMM2}}), which conjugates the plaquette variables; so Lem.~\ref{lem:background-iterated-average} gives $\varpi(V_j(W))\le2L^{-2}\mu_{j+1}(W)<\frac12\varpi_\chi$.

The map $W\mapsto V_j(W)$ is real analytic on $\mathsf{Gd}_{j+1}$: $\mathcal M^jU^\circ(W)$, with the representative $U^\circ(W)$ of the background, is real analytic by Thm.~\YMMref{E}{10} and Lem.~\ref{lem:background-iterated-average}, on the good-set and actual-average domains just established, and the gauge transformation to the axial gauge is $v(x)=(\mathcal M^jU^\circ(W))(y,x)$, $x$ in the block of $y$, an averaged contour variable, a real analytic function of the configuration where it is formed. And $V_j(\mathbf 1)=\mathbf 1$: $\mathbf 1$ is flat, lies in the minimal orbit over $\mathbf 1$, and every path product and its average are $\mathbf 1$; uniqueness of the minimal orbit in Thm.~\YMMref{E}{10} identifies its axial representative with $\mathbf 1$.

(2)

\emph{One step.} Let $\mathsf O$ be an open subset of $\mathsf{Gd}_{j+1}$, $0<\rho\le r_\chi/C_\chi$, $G(\rho)=\{u\in SU(2):|\operatorname{Lg}u|<\rho\}$, and
\[
\mathcal N=\bigl\{V:\ \mathcal MV\in\mathsf O,\ \ V(\mathsf e)\,V_j(\mathcal MV)(\mathsf e)^{-1}\in G(\rho)\ \text{at every non-pivot bond }\mathsf e\bigr\}.
\]
At $W'\in\mathsf O$ the configuration $V_j(W')$, with $\varpi_c(V_j(W'))\le\varpi_\chi$, is a reference configuration of the chart of the fibre, and Prop.~\YMMref{53.2}{441}, with empty exterior, gives for $|\mathcal A|<\rho$: $V_j(W')$ is real and admissible, with invertible pivot coefficients; the chart is formed at $\mathcal A$, $V_{W'}[\mathcal A]=e^{iB'}V_j(W')$ with a real $B'$, $\sup|B'|\le2C_\chi|\mathcal A|$; $\mathcal MV_{W'}[\mathcal A]=W'$; $\operatorname{Lg}(V_{W'}[\mathcal A](\mathsf e)V_j(W')(\mathsf e)^{-1})=\mathcal A(\mathsf e)$ at the non-pivot bonds; $\varpi_c(V_{W'}[\mathcal A])<\varpi_1$; and $\mathsf J_{V_j}[\mathcal A]$, $z^{(j)}_{V_j}$ are formed, real and continuous (the continuity statement and the local bounds in its proof).

By the converse in that proposition, $\Phi_j(W',\mathcal A)=V_{W'}[\mathcal A]$ is a bijection of $\mathsf O\times\{|\mathcal A|<\rho\}$ onto the open set $\mathcal N$, with the inverse $\Xi_j(V)=(\mathcal MV,(\operatorname{Lg}(V(\mathsf e)V_j(\mathcal MV)(\mathsf e)^{-1}))_{\mathsf e})$. The map $\Xi_j$ is real analytic on $\mathcal N$: $\mathcal M$ is real analytic at configurations whose plaquettes in the double blocks are small, $V_j$ is by~(1), and $\operatorname{Lg}$ is the logarithmic series where $|u-\mathbf 1|<1$. Its differential is injective: if the derivatives of $\mathcal MV$ and of the second member of $\Xi_j(V)$ vanish along a tangent vector $\dot a$, then $\dot a=0$ at the non-pivot bonds, and then the derivative of $(\mathcal MV)(c)$ at a bond $c$ of the level $j+1$ is $\mathsf n_c\,\dot a(b_0(c))$, with the invertible kernel $\mathsf n_c$ at the pivot bond $b_0(c)$ (the pivot differential preceding equation~\YMMref{(911)}{420}), so that $\dot a=0$.

The dimensions agree, the positively oriented bonds of the level $j$ being the non-pivot ones and one pivot bond for each positively oriented bond of the level $j+1$. By the inverse function theorem $\Xi_j$ is a local real analytic diffeomorphism; being injective, it has the real analytic inverse $\Phi_j$, a real analytic diffeomorphism of $\mathsf O\times\{|\mathcal A|<\rho\}$ onto $\mathcal N$. The integral identity of the chart of the fibre (equation~\YMMref{(986)}{442}, with $e^{\mathsf z_c(V)}=L^{-3}z^{(j)}_V(c)$ because $\mathsf n_c=L\mathsf m_c$ acts on a three-dimensional pivot space) gives, for every Borel function $H\ge0$ on the configurations of the level $j$,
\[
\begin{multlined}
\int_{\mathcal N}H\,\mathrm{d}V=c_j\int_{\mathsf O}dW'\,z^{(j)}_{V_j}\int_{|\mathcal A|<\rho}e^{\mathsf J_{V_j}[\mathcal A]}\,H\bigl(V_{W'}[\mathcal A]\bigr)\,\mathrm{d}\mathcal A,\qquad V_j=V_j(W'),\quad c_j \\
=(2\pi^2)^{-\#\mathfrak X^+_j}L^{-3\#\mathfrak B^+_{j+1}},
\end{multlined}
\]
and the exponent has the closed form
\[
\mathsf J_{V_j}[\mathcal A]+\log z^{(j)}_{V_j}=\sum_{\mathsf e\in\mathfrak X^+_j}\log\sigma_1\bigl(|\mathcal A(\mathsf e)|^2\bigr)+\sum_c\mathsf z_c\bigl(V_{W'}[\mathcal A]\bigr)+3\,\#\mathfrak B^+_{j+1}\log L,\qquad\sigma_1(s^2)=\Bigl(\frac{\sin s}s\Bigr)^2,
\]
where $\mathsf z_c=-\log\det\mathsf n_c$ is a real analytic function of the configuration on $\{\varpi_c<\varpi_1\}$.

(3)

\emph{The step keeps the good sets, with constants alone.} Let $W'\in\mathsf{Gd}_{j+1}$, $|\mathcal A|<\rho_2$ and $W''=V_{W'}[\mathcal A]$. For $j\ge1$: $V_j(W')=\mathcal M^jU_+$ with an element $U_+$ of the minimal orbit over $W'$, which lies in the minimal orbit over $V_j(W')$ ({\cite[Lem.~B.4]{YMM2}}(2)), so that $\mu_j(V_j(W'))=L^{-2}\mu_{j+1}(W')$ (the level scaling in {\cite[Def.~B.2]{YMM2}}); and $W''=e^{iB'}V_j(W')$ with $\sup|B'|\le2C_\chi|\mathcal A|<\frac12r_{\rm B}$ moves the representative of the background so that its regularity number moves by at most $2K_{\rm B}\sup|B'|$ ({\cite[Lem.~P.5]{YMM2}}): the background over $W''$ exists and
\[
\mu_j(W'')\le L^{-2}\mu_{j+1}(W')+4K_{\rm B}C_\chi|\mathcal A|<L^{-2}\mu_\flat+(1-L^{-2})\mu_\flat=\mu_\flat .
\]
For $j=0$: every bond moves by $|e^{iB'(\mathsf e)}-\mathbf 1|\le|B'(\mathsf e)|$, and a plaquette variable by at most the sum over its four bonds, so that $\varpi(W'')\le\varpi(V_0(W'))+8C_\chi|\mathcal A|\le2L^{-2}\mu_1(W')+8C_\chi|\mathcal A|<\frac14\varepsilon_{\rm v}$. So the step maps $\mathsf{Gd}_{j+1}\times\{|\mathcal A|<\rho_2\}$ into $\mathsf{Gd}_j$.

(4)

\emph{Composition.} Put $\mathcal U_n=\mathsf O_n$ and, downwards, $\mathcal U_j=\Phi_j(\mathcal U_{j+1}\times\{|\mathcal A_j|<\rho_2\})$. By~(2) at $\mathsf O=\mathcal U_{j+1}$, which lies in $\mathsf{Gd}_{j+1}$ by~(3), every $\mathcal U_j$ is open and lies in $\mathsf{Gd}_j$, and $\Phi_j\times{\rm id}$ is a real analytic diffeomorphism. $\Upsilon$ is their composite: a real analytic diffeomorphism of $\mathsf O_n\times\Omega$ onto the open set $\mathcal U=\mathcal U_0$, injective on all of $\mathsf O_n\times\Omega$, with the inverse $U\mapsto(\mathcal M^nU,(\operatorname{Lg}(\mathcal M^jU(\mathsf e)\,V_j(\mathcal M^{j+1}U)(\mathsf e)^{-1}))_{\mathsf e,j})$, and $\Upsilon(\mathbf 1,0)=\mathbf 1$ by~(1). Along the chain the backgrounds exist (at level $0$ the background is $U_0(W_0)=W_0$, and $|J(W_0)|\le4\varpi(W_0)<\varepsilon_{\rm v}$, as in the height-zero part of the proof of Prop.~\YMMref{52.3}{433}), $\mathcal MW_j=W_{j+1}$ and $\theta_{\rm ch}$ is formed; this is~(i) and~(ii), and by the closed form of~(2)
\[
\theta_{\rm ch}=-\sum_{j<n}\Bigl[\sum_{\mathsf e\in\mathfrak X^+_j}\log\sigma_1\bigl(|\mathcal A_j(\mathsf e)|^2\bigr)+\sum_c\mathsf z_c(W_j)\Bigr]-3\log L\sum_{j<n}\#\mathfrak B^+_{j+1},
\]
a real analytic function on $\mathsf O_n\times\Omega$. The identities of the steps, applied downwards with Tonelli's theorem, give~(iii) for Borel $H\ge0$ that vanish off $\mathcal U$, with $C_{\rm H}=\prod_jc_j$, and for bounded complex Borel $H$ by linearity. As $\Upsilon$ is injective on all of $\mathsf O_n\times\Omega$, a function that vanishes off the image of an open subset $E$ gives an integrand that vanishes off $E$: this is~(iii) for $E$. The density is fixed by~(iii): if a continuous $\theta'$ satisfied~(iii) as well, the function $H$ equal to the sign of $e^{-\theta'}-e^{-\theta_{\rm ch}}$, carried to $\mathcal U$ by $\Upsilon$, would give $\int|e^{-\theta'}-e^{-\theta_{\rm ch}}|\,\mathrm{d}W\,\mathrm{d}y=0$, and a continuous function with this property vanishes.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The jets of the weighted progression]\label{C-351-10}
Let $0<g\le\gamma_{\rm e}$, $(K,\beta)$ and $b$ as in Lem.~\ref{C-351-8}, $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$, and $f,h$ as there, with $d<1$; $\Psi=(f,h)$. $\mathsf n_j(f,h)$ is the mixed second derivative at $0$ in $(\mu_1,\mu_2)$ of the source energy of the level $j$ of the weighted progression with the source $\mu_1f\circ x+\mu_2h\circ x$, summed over the localisation domains and points of the level $j$; $\mathsf J_2=\sum_{j\le K}\mathsf n_j$. When all fluctuation fields are multiplied by a complex field scale $\mathsf z$ and each $x_i$ is replaced by $L^{-i}\beta+\mathsf z^2(x_i-L^{-i}\beta)$, $\mathsf n_{j+1}$ becomes an even function $\mathsf n^{\mathsf z}_{j+1}=\sum_m\mathsf n_{j+1,[2m]}\mathsf z^{2m}$, holomorphic for $|\mathsf z|<R_j$ with $R_j^{-2}\le C(\log x_j)^{2p_0}D_j/b$, and $\mathsf n^1_{j+1}=\mathsf n_{j+1}$; put $\mathsf h^{(n)}_{2m}=\sum_{j<n}\mathsf n_{j+1,[2m]}$ and $\mathsf h_{2m}=\mathsf h^{(K)}_{2m}$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $\mathsf n_{j,[0]}=\mathsf n_{j,[2]}=0$, and $|\mathsf J_2-\mathsf h_4-\mathsf h_6|\le Cb^{-4}d^2\mathsf l^{8p_0}|\Psi|$;
\item[(ii)] for $0\le n\le K-1$ with $D_n\ge d$: $|\mathsf h_6-\mathsf h_6^{(n)}|\le Cb^{-3}\mathsf l^{6p_0}d\,(d/D_n)^{3/2}|\Psi|$;
\item[(iii)] for $(f,h)\in\mathfrak T_{T_\ell}(d;\vartheta)$, $20d\le\ell$, $d\le L^{-1}$ and $K>s(d)$: $|\mathsf h_4-c_2b^{-2}\mathcal K_6(f,h)|\le[\bar\varepsilon_4(g,d)\,b^{-3}d+\frac32C_{\rm tm}\vartheta^{-1}b^{-2}a_K/d]|\Psi|$, with $\bar\varepsilon_4(g,d)\le C(g)d^{1/2}$ and the constant $C_{\rm tm}$ of Prop.~\YMMref{121.2}{824} and Lem.~\ref{lem:ward-fluctuation-template};
\item[(iv)] for $\ell=\ell_g$, $(f,h)\in\mathfrak T_{T_\ell}(d;\vartheta)$, $d\le d_{\rm e}(g,\vartheta)$ and $s(d)\le K$: there is a set $\mathsf{Pk}=\mathsf{Pk}(a_K,d)\subset a_K\mathbb Z^3$, depending on $a_K$ and $d$ alone, with $|v|<1$ on it and $\#\mathsf{Pk}\ge(30d)^{-3}$, such that
\[
\Bigl|S^T_{2;K,\ell,\beta}(f,h)-\frac1{\#\mathsf{Pk}}\sum_{v\in\mathsf{Pk}}\mathsf J_2(\tau_vf,\tau_vh)\Bigr|\le C_{\rm A}(g)\,\vartheta^{-1}d^2b^{-2}|\Psi|,
\]
$\tau_v$ the translation by $v$ and $C_{\rm A}(g)$ a number depending only on $g$ and the constants.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(i), (ii). By Lem.~\ref{C-351-8}, if $f\circ x$ or $h\circ x$ vanishes identically, all the jets vanish; let neither vanish.

\emph{The steps at one field scale.} When the fluctuation fields of all the steps are multiplied by one complex field scale $\mathsf z$ and the coefficients of the action are moved as in the statement, the step of the level $j+1$ is a step at the place $x_j$ with the lower place $\mathsf t_\flat$ (Def.~\ref{IV-71-12}; Prop.~\ref{IV-71-50} for the canonical objects), the deformed activities of all the earlier levels standing in its bare array: the room $\mathsf q$ bounds their size uniformly in $\mathsf z$, so that one induction over the levels forms all the steps at once. So the activities of the level $j+1$ are pointed families, holomorphic and even in $\mathsf z$ on $|\mathsf z|<R_j$, $R_j=\delta(\mathsf t_\flat)/(2\delta(x_j))$ with $\delta(\mathsf t)=\mathsf t^{-1/2}\mathfrak b(\mathsf t)$, equal at $\mathsf z=1$ to the activities of the weighted progression, and local in the weights; and $R_j^{-2}=4\delta(x_j)^2/\delta(\mathsf t_\flat)^2\le C(\log x_j)^{2p_0}D_j/b$, as $x_j\ge\frac34b/D_j$ (Lem.~\ref{C-351-8}).

One step at the field scale $\mathsf z$, as a map of its bare array (the activities of the earlier levels and the weight of the level), has first and second derivatives at most $C\,q(|\mathsf z|/R_j)$ times the sizes of the increments, $q(t)=t^2/(1-t^2)$, by Cauchy's estimate, its order $0$ in $\mathsf z$ reading no bare array (Prop.~\ref{IV-71-37} with Prop.~\ref{IV-71-46}); the chain rule gives the derivatives in the two parameters $\mu_1,\mu_2$ of the activities of the level $j+1$ from those of the earlier levels and from the weight.

\emph{The derivatives in the sources.} The weight of the source $a$ at the level $i$ is $L^{K-i}w_a$, $w_1=f\circ x$, $w_2=h\circ x$, of size $\|f_a\|_\infty/D_i$ at a plaquette, $f_1=f$, $f_2=h$. The weight member of the bare array of the level $i$ is $L^i$ times its sum against the $a_p$ over the plaquettes of a domain, $a_p$ being at most of the order $L^{-4i}$ on the analyticity core; a domain of one cube holds at most of the order $L^{3i}$ plaquettes, and at most $35(d/a_K)^3$ plaquettes carry $w_a$; as $L^{-3i}(d/a_K)^3=(d/D_i)^3$, the size of this member is at most $C(\|f_a\|_\infty/D_i)\psi_i$, $\psi_i=\min\{1,(d/D_i)^3\}$. An activity of an earlier level $i-n$ that vanishes off the domains meeting a set of sites enters the bare array of the level $i$ with a size at most $C[\varpi_n+(n+2)L^{-4n}\min\{L^{3n},N_{\rm cb}\}]$ times its norm, $\varpi_n=L^{3n}e^{-\max\{2L^{n-1}-2,0\}}$ and $N_{\rm cb}$ the number of the cubes of the level $i-n$ that hold such a site; for the supports of the sources $N_{\rm cb}\le77\max\{1,(d/D_{i-n})^3\}$.

Along the run $\delta(x_{i-n})\le C(1+n)^{p_0}L^{-n/2}\delta(x_i)$, so $R_{i-n}^{-2}\le C(1+n)^{2p_0}L^{-n}R_i^{-2}$. By induction over $i\le j$ one obtains, for $|\mathsf z|\le\eta_0R_j$, $\eta_0\in(0,\frac12]$ a number depending only on the constants: the first derivative in $\mu_a$ of the activity of the level $i+1$ has a norm at most $C|\mathsf z|^2R_i^{-2}(\|f_a\|_\infty/D_i)\psi_i$, and the mixed second derivative a norm at most $C|\mathsf z|^2R_i^{-2}(\|f\|_\infty/D_i)(\|h\|_\infty/D_i)\chi_i$, $\chi_i=\min\{1,(d/D_i)^{5/2}\}$; here $\psi_i^2\le\chi_i$ bounds the product of two first derivatives, and the second derivatives of the earlier levels, carried up with the sizes above, sum to at most $C\chi_i$, the levels below the scale $d$ through the decay of the activities across the distance of the two supports, those above it through the factor $L^{-n/2}$ that is left when the factor $L^{-4n}$ of the size is set against the growth $L^{n}$ of the radii and weights and $L^{5n/2}$ of the profile.

\emph{The jet.} $\mathsf n^{\mathsf z}_{j+1}$ is the sum, over the domains of the level $j+1$ and their points, of the mixed second derivative at the trivial configuration. Only the domains that meet both supports contribute, the activities being local in the weights; the cubes of the level $j+1$ that hold a corner of a plaquette of a support number at most $77\max\{1,(d/D_{j+1})^3\}$; two corners of plaquettes of the two supports are at a sup distance $\ge d/4$, so that such a domain has a linear size $\ge[d/(4MD_{j+1})-2]_+$ in the units of the level $j+1$, and the decay of the localised terms in the size of their domains, summed by the bound in {\cite[Lem.~B.10]{YMM2}}, gives the factor $e^{-[d/(4MD_{j+1})-2]_+}$. Hence, on $|\mathsf z|\le\eta_0R_j$,
\[
\begin{multlined}
|\mathsf n^{\mathsf z}_{j+1}|\le C|\mathsf z|^2R_j^{-2}D_j^{-2}\chi_j\,\Xi_{j+1}|\Psi|,\qquad\chi_j=\min\{1,(d/D_j)^{5/2}\},\qquad\Xi_{j+1}=\max\{1, \\
(d/D_{j+1})^3\}\,e^{-[d/(4MD_{j+1})-2]_+};
\end{multlined}
\]
$\chi_j$ records that a source of width $d$ is seen at the spacing $D_j$ through its mean, and $\Xi_{j+1}$ counts the cubes of the level $j+1$ that meet the supports and the decay of the activities across the distance of the two supports; the bound is local, and it reads no $K$, side, position or pair.

\emph{The orders.} At $\mathsf z=0$ the steps add nothing that reads the sources, so the order $0$ in $\mathsf z$ vanishes. The order $\mathsf z^2$ comes from the step of the level $j+1$ alone, the earlier levels being taken at the field scale $0$, where they read no source; it is the covariance, in the measure of the step, of the parts linear in the fluctuation field of the two source potentials at the trivial configuration. These linear forms are invariant under the adjoint action of the constant gauge transformations, which leave the trivial configuration and the gauge invariant terms unchanged, and the mean of ${\rm Ad}(u)$ over $u\in SU(2)$ is $0$ on $\mathfrak{su}(2)$; so they vanish, and the order $2$ vanishes. Cauchy's estimate on $|\mathsf z|=\eta_0R_j$ gives
\[
|\mathsf n_{j+1,[2m]}|\le C\eta_0^{-2m}R_j^{-2m}\,D_j^{-2}\chi_j\,\Xi_{j+1}|\Psi|\le Cb^{-m}(\log x_j)^{2mp_0}D_j^{m-2}\chi_j\,\Xi_{j+1}|\Psi| ,
\]
and the same with $m=4$ for the sum of the orders $\ge8$ at $\mathsf z=1$, as $\eta_0^2R_j^2\ge2$ for $g\le\gamma_{\rm e}$ (geometric summation of the even coefficient bounds in Prop.~\ref{IV-71-37}(cx8)).

\emph{The sums over the levels.} For $D_j\ge d$: $\Xi_{j+1}=1$, $D_j^{m-2}\chi_j=d^{m-2}(d/D_j)^{9/2-m}$ is geometric in $j$ with the ratio $L^{-(9/2-m)}\le L^{-1/2}$ for $m\le4$, and $\log x_j\le\log(2b/D_j)\le\mathsf l$. For $D_j<d$: $D_j^{m-2}\chi_j\le d^{m-2}$, $\log x_j\le\mathsf l\,(1+(r+1)\log L)$ at the $r$-th such level counted from above, and $\Xi_{j+1}\le\sup_{u\in[L^{r-1},L^r]}\max\{1,u^3\}e^{-[u/4M-2]_+}$, which is summable against every power of $r$. Summing over all the levels gives (i), with $|\mathsf h_{2m}|\le Cb^{-m}d^{m-2}\mathsf l^{2mp_0}|\Psi|$ for $m=2,3$; summing over the levels $j\ge n$ alone, where $D_j\ge D_n\ge d$, gives $\sum_{j\ge n}|\mathsf n_{j+1,[6]}|\le Cb^{-3}\mathsf l^{6p_0}d\,(d/D_n)^{3/2}|\Psi|$, which is (ii).

(iii). If $f\circ x$ or $h\circ x$ vanishes identically, $\mathsf h_4=0$ and the template sum below vanishes, so that its bound alone gives the assertion; let neither vanish.

\emph{At a real field scale.} The coefficients $\xi_i(\mathsf z)=L^{-i}\beta+\mathsf z^2(x_i-L^{-i}\beta)$ of the action are chosen so that, the counterterms $e_{i'}$ of the progression being kept, $\mathsf z^{-2}\xi_i(\mathsf z)L^i+\sum_{1\le i'\le i}L^{i'}e_{i'}=\mathsf z^{-2}\beta$, by the run equation $L^ix_i+\sum_{1\le i'\le i}L^{i'}e_{i'}=\beta$; and the sum rules of the steps are stated for every field of the box. So at a real field scale $0<\mathsf z\le1$ the chain of the weighted progression is the chain of the chart integrals of the Wilson weight at $\beta/\mathsf z^2$, read at the fields $\mathsf z\zeta$, $\zeta=(\zeta_i)_i$ the fluctuation fields of the levels in their boxes $|\zeta_i|<\mathfrak b(x_i)$, and $\sum_{2\le j\le K}\mathsf n^{\mathsf z}_j$ is, up to a term of the first level, the covariance of the first source derivatives of the exponent of the level $1$, taken at the background that the chain builds at the level $1$ from these fields, in a complex measure of mass $1$ on the product of the boxes, the product over the levels $1\le i<K$ of normalised measures on the box of the level $i$, each of which depends on the fields of the higher levels.

As $\mathsf z\to0$ at a fixed lattice, the backgrounds tend to the trivial configuration uniformly on the boxes, all the potentials vanish, and the coefficient of the action of the level $i$ tends to $L^{-i}x_0$, so that this measure tends in total variation to the product $\mathbb Q$ of the measures $\nu^{\rm r}_i$ below; dividing by $\mathsf z^4$,
\[
\sum_{2\le j\le K}\mathsf n_{j,[4]}=\langle q_1;q_2\rangle_{\mathbb Q}+\mathsf e_1,\qquad q_a=\tfrac12a_K^{-1}\sum_pw_a(p)\,|\Theta_p|^2,
\]
$\Theta_p$ the linear curvature of the plaquette $p$ in the fields $\zeta_i$, $\mathbb Q=\bigotimes_{1\le i<K}\nu^{\rm r}_i$, $\nu^{\rm r}_i$ the centred Gaussian measure of the quadratic part of the step of the level $i$ at the coefficient $L^{-i}x_0$ of the action, restricted to the box of the level $i$ and normalised, and $\mathsf e_1$ a term of the first level. With $\mathsf n_{1,[4]}$ and the slice of the level $1$ below, $\mathsf e_1$ costs at most $C\,b^{-2}\mathsf l^{4p_0}e^{-c_\flat d/a_K}|\Psi|$, $c_\flat=\min\{1/(8ML),\delta_{\rm tp}/(2\sqrt3)\}$, $\delta_{\rm tp}$ the rate of Props.~\YMMref{120.5}{821} and~\YMMref{120.6}{821}, as the supports are $d/a_K$ bare spacings apart.

\emph{The Gaussian values; the running couplings drop out.} Under the Gaussian measure of the level $i$ at the coefficient $L^{-i}x_0$ the curvature of the fluctuation field of the level $i$ has the covariance $x_0^{-1}\mathcal C_{(i+1)}$, $\mathcal C_{(i+1)}$ the slice of the level $i+1$ of the free lattice curvature (Prop.~\YMMref{120.3}{819}): the coupling $x_i$ enters the scaled field and the coefficient of the action in inverse proportions and drops out. The slices $\mathcal C_{(i+1)}$, $1\le i<K$, add up to $C^{\rm fl}_{K,0}-\mathcal C_{(1)}$, where $C^{\rm fl}_{K,0}=\sum_{1\le j\le K}\mathcal C_{(j)}$ is the fluctuation kernel of depth $0$ of Section~\YMMref{120}{817} (Props.~\YMMref{120.5}{821} and~\YMMref{120.6}{821}), the kernel of the orthogonal projection of the plaquette $2$-cochains, in each colour, onto the curvatures of the fields whose $K$-fold linear block average vanishes, that is, onto $\mathsf{Fl}_K=\mathrm{d}(\ker\mathbf Q^s_K)$, $\mathbf Q^s_K$ the straight average of Section~\YMMref{120}{817}; it has no dimension and $|C^{\rm fl}_{K,0}|\le1$; the slice $\mathcal C_{(1)}$ of the level $1$ goes into $\mathsf e_1$.

The variables of different levels are independent and every $\nu^{\rm r}_i$ is even; by Wick's rule, with three colours, the Gaussian value of $\langle q_1;q_2\rangle$ is, up to that slice,
\[
\tfrac14a_K^{-2}\cdot2\cdot3\,x_0^{-2}\sum_{p,q}w_1(p)\,w_2(q)\,C^{\rm fl}_{K,0}(p,q)^2=\tfrac32\,b^{-2}\,\mathcal K[C^{\rm fl}_{K,0}](f,h),\qquad b=a_Kx_0,
\]
with the template sum $\mathcal K[\mathsf k](f,h)=\sum_{p,q}f(x(p))\,h(x(q))\,\mathsf k(p,q)^2$; no further power of $a_K$ enters.

\emph{The boxes.} Every joint cumulant of order $2$ or $4$ of the components of the field of the level $i$ under $\nu^{\rm r}_i$ differs from the Gaussian one by at most $C_{\rm bx}e^{-\frac12\gamma_2\mathfrak b(x_i)^2}$, uniformly in the volume and in the cutoff (Lem.~\ref{lem:ward-box-cumulants}, the components entering as insertions), with numbers $C_{\rm bx}$, $\gamma_2$ depending only on the constants; the odd cumulants vanish. The map from the fields of the level $i$ to the curvature has row sums at most $CL^{-2i}$, and at most $35^2(d/a_K)^6$ pairs of plaquettes have $w_1(p)w_2(q)\ne0$; with $L^{-3i}(d/a_K)^3=(d/D_i)^3$ the boxes change $\langle q_1;q_2\rangle$ by at most $Cb^{-2}[\mathsf E^{(3)}+(\mathsf E^{(3)})^2+\mathsf E^{(6)}]|\Psi|$, $\mathsf E^{(q)}=\sum_{1\le i<K}u_i^q\epsilon_i$, $u_i=d/D_i$, $\epsilon_i=e^{-\frac12\gamma_2\mathfrak b(x_i)^2}\le\phi_{\rm bx}(\frac34b/D_i)$, where $\phi_{\rm bx}(s)=e^{-c_{\rm bx}(\log s)^2}$, $c_{\rm bx}=\frac12\gamma_2A_1^2$, since $\mathfrak b(x_i)^2\ge A_1^2(\log x_i)^2$ and $x_i\ge\frac34b/D_i$ (Lem.~\ref{C-351-8}).

For $s,s'\ge1$, $\phi_{\rm bx}$ decreases, $\phi_{\rm bx}(ss')\le\phi_{\rm bx}(s)\phi_{\rm bx}(s')$ and $s^q\phi_{\rm bx}(s)\le e^{q^2/(4c_{\rm bx})}$. Cut the levels at $D_i\approx d^{1/2}$: the levels with $D_i<d$ give at most $C\phi_{\rm bx}(\frac34b)\phi_{\rm bx}(d^{-1/2})$, their $u_i$ being spaced by the factor $L$; those with $d\le D_i\le d^{1/2}$ have $u_i\le1$, $\sum u_i^3\le2$ and $\epsilon_i\le\phi_{\rm bx}(\frac34b)\phi_{\rm bx}(d^{-1/2})$; those with $D_i>d^{1/2}$ have $\sum u_i^3\le2d^{3/2}$ and $\epsilon_i\le\phi_{\rm bx}(\frac34b)$. As $\phi_{\rm bx}(d^{-1/2})\le Cd^{3/2}$ and $\phi_{\rm bx}(\frac34b)\le C/b$, $\mathsf E^{(3)},\mathsf E^{(6)}\le Cb^{-1}d^{3/2}$, and also $\le C$; so the boxes cost at most $Cb^{-3}d^{3/2}|\Psi|$, with $C$ depending only on the constants.

The bound is uniform in $K$ and in the side through the locality of the cumulant bounds; no count of the restrictions enters.

\emph{The template sum.} Lem.~\ref{lem:ward-fluctuation-template} at the depth $0$, where $a_0=1\ge d$:
\[
\Bigl|\mathcal K[C^{\rm fl}_{K,0}](f,h)-\frac3{8\pi^2}\mathcal K_6(f,h)\Bigr|\le C_{\rm tm}\Bigl[\frac{a_K}{\vartheta d}+\Bigl(\frac d\ell\Bigr)^3+d^3\Bigr]|\Psi|,
\]
and $\frac32\cdot\frac3{8\pi^2}=c_2$. Collecting,
\[
|\mathsf h_4-c_2b^{-2}\mathcal K_6(f,h)|\le b^{-2}\Bigl\{\tfrac32C_{\rm tm}\Bigl[\frac{a_K}{\vartheta d}+\Bigl(\frac d\ell\Bigr)^3+d^3\Bigr]+C\,\frac db\,d^{1/2}+C\,\mathsf l^{4p_0}e^{-c_\flat d/a_K}\Bigr\}|\Psi| .
\]
As $\ell\ge1$, $d/a_K\ge L(\log\frac1d)^2$ for $K>s(d)$, and $g^{-2}<b\le L(g^{-2}+\bar B)$, the members other than $\frac32C_{\rm tm}b^{-2}a_K/(\vartheta d)$ are at most $\bar\varepsilon_4(g,d)\,b^{-3}d\,|\Psi|$ with
\[
\bar\varepsilon_4(g,d)=\sup_{g^{-2}<b\le L(g^{-2}+\bar B)}\Bigl\{3C_{\rm tm}\,b\,d^2+C\,d^{1/2}+C\,\frac bd\,\mathsf l^{4p_0}e^{-c_\flat L(\log\frac1d)^2}\Bigr\}\le C(g)\,d^{1/2},
\]
$e^{-c(\log\frac1d)^2}$ being below every power of $d$.

(iv). Let $Z[w]$ be the generating function of $T_\ell$, the partition function with the source $w$, and $\mathcal E(w)$ its source energy, the sum over the levels and localisation domains of the source energies {\cite[eq.~212]{YMM2}} of the sourced chain on $T_\ell$ {\cite[eq.~205]{YMM2}}. On the least torus the setting and the identity of~(4a)--(4c) in the proof of Prop.~\ref{C-351-7} hold, the conditions on $g$ of the statements read there entering $\gamma_{\rm e}$: the term without large-field regions in the sum over the level of the first creation of a large-field region (equation~\eqref{eq:ward-first-creation}, with the histories of Section~\YMMref{123}{828}) is $e^{\mathcal E(w)}\int e^{\mathsf R_K(w,\cdot)}\,\mathrm{d}\mathsf m_K$ for the sources of level-wise norm $<1$, with $|\mathsf R_K(w,\cdot)|\le\|w\|_{\rm lw}\mathsf g_\emptyset$ for a source carried by one ball of radius $1$, and with a measure $\mathsf m_K$ of mass at most $Z[0]$ (steps~(4c), (4d) there).

The weighted progression ({\cite[Def.~B.7]{YMM2}}) and the sourced chain are made level by level by the same renormalisation step, with the same couplings, the same auxiliary data and the same lattice, and the source enters both only through the weights $x_j-L^{K-j}w$ of the plaquettes. At the trivial configuration every localised term is taken at the trivial pair, and $a_p(\mathbf 1)=0$, so that there the relative exponent of the weighted progression after the level $K$ is the sum over the levels and localisation domains of its source energies; following the two constructions level by level, this sum is $\mathcal E(w)$ for all sources near $0$, with no condition on the depth.

So the mixed second derivative of $\mathcal E$ at $(\tau_vf,\tau_vh)$ is $\mathsf J_2(\tau_vf,\tau_vh)$, and $\log(Z[w]/Z[0])-\mathcal E(w)$ is holomorphic near $0$ with the mixed second derivative $\mathsf R=S^T_2-\mathsf J_2$. Take $\iota=a_K\lceil18d/a_K\rceil$ and $\mathsf{Pk}=\{v\in\iota\mathbb Z^3:|v_\mu|\le0.575-9d\}$; the balls of radius $9d$ about the $x_1+v$, $x_1$ a centre of a ball of radius $d$ that holds ${\rm supp}f$, are disjoint and lie in $\mathbb B(x_1,1)$. For signs $\epsilon_v$ the source $z_1\sum_v\epsilon_v\tau_vf+z_2\sum_v\epsilon_v\tau_vh$ has level-wise norm $<1$ for $|z_1|\|f\|_\infty,|z_2|\|h\|_\infty<A_\star$, with $A_\star\ge c(g)(\vartheta d)^{1/2}b$, and on this polydisc the squarefree coefficients of $Z[w]e^{-\mathcal E(w)}/Z[0]$ in $(z_1,z_2)$ are at most $Q_{\rm D}(g)\prod_a\|f_a\|_\infty/A_\star$, with the number $Q_{\rm D}(g)$ of~(4e) in the proof of Prop.~\ref{C-351-7} formed with one ball and two variables: split at the level of the first creation of a large field, bound the part in which no field is large, and apply Cauchy's estimate on a polydisc for each level, as in~(4e) there.

So $|\mathsf R(\sum_v\epsilon_v\tau_vf,\sum_v\epsilon_v\tau_vh)|\le2Q_{\rm D}^2A_\star^{-2}|\Psi|$; its mean over the signs is $\sum_v\mathsf R(\tau_vf,\tau_vh)$; $S^T_2$ is invariant under the translations of $a_K\mathbb Z^3$; divide by $\#\mathsf{Pk}\ge(30d)^{-3}$.
\end{proof}

For $N=2L^{\mathsf M}$, $1\le n<\mathsf M$ with $2L^{\mathsf M-n+1}\ge C_LM$, and plaquettes $p,q$ of $\mathbb Z^3_N$, let $\mathsf g_2[N,n](p,q)$ be the coefficient of $\beta^{-3}$ in the expansion by Laplace's method (Lem.~\textup{\ref{IV-73-26}}), as $\beta\to\infty$, of the covariance of $a_p$ and $a_q$ on the fibre $\{\mathcal M^nU=\mathbf 1\}$ of $\mathbb Z^3_N$ under $\exp[-\beta(A+\sum_{j<n}\mathsf k_jG_j\circ\mathcal M^j)]$, written in the chart $\Upsilon(\mathbf 1,\cdot)$ of Lem.~\ref{C-351-9}; here $A=\sum_pa_p$ is the Wilson action, $G_j$ the gauge-fixing function~\YMMref{(54)}{27} of the level $j$, and $\mathsf k\in(0,\infty)^n$ are strengths. This is the number $\mathsf g_2[N,n]$ of
Prop.~\ref{C-350-12}(iii): both definitions take the coefficient of
the covariance on the same fibre, and that proposition proves independence
from the adapted chart and from the gauge-fixing strengths. In particular,
it depends only on the bare torus, the number of blocking levels, $L$ and
the plaquettes, with no running coupling or cutoff remaining. $\mathsf B_1^{\rm lat}$ and $\mathsf P_1^{\rm lat}(f,h;a)=a\sum_{\tilde p,\tilde q}f(ax(\tilde p))h(ax(\tilde q))\mathsf B_1^{\rm lat}(\tilde p,\tilde q)$, sums over the plaquettes of $\mathbb Z^3$, are the coefficients of Def.~\textup{\ref{IV-73-22}}; Cor.~\textup{\ref{IV-73-73}} and Thms.~\textup{\ref{IV-73-98}}, \textup{\ref{IV-73-100}}~(a) give, for $(f,h)\in\mathfrak T_{\mathbb R^3}(d;\vartheta)$, $0<a\le d$ and $\lg(\cdot)=1+|\log(\cdot)|$,
\begin{equation}\label{C-351-11}
|\mathsf P_1^{\rm lat}(f,h;a)-\varkappa\,\mathcal K_5(f,h)|\le C_\varkappa\vartheta^{-1}a\lg(d/a)\,\|f\|_\infty\|h\|_\infty,\qquad\varkappa=\tfrac3{2\pi^3}=c_1c_2,
\end{equation}
with an absolute number $C_\varkappa$.

\begin{lemma}[Lattice perturbation theory]\label{C-351-12}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[beginpenalty=10000]
\item[(i)] In the setting of Lem.~\ref{C-351-10} let $N=\ell L^K$, $w_1=f\circ x$ and $w_2=h\circ x$ on $\mathbb Z^3_N$, $2\le n\le K$, 
\[
\mathsf H^{(n)}=\beta^3a_K^2\mathsf h_6^{(n)}
\]
 and 
\[
\mathsf T[N,n](w)=\sum_{p,q}w_1(p)w_2(q)\mathsf g_2[N,n](p,q).
\]
 If $\gamma^{\rm tr}\mathfrak b(x_{n-1})^2\ge80$ and 
\[
10240\,N^3e^{-\gamma^{\rm tr}\mathfrak b(x_{n-1})^2/8}\le1,
\]
 $\gamma^{\rm tr}>0$ a number depending only on the constants, then
\[
|\mathsf H^{(n)}-\mathsf T[N,n](w)|\le C(N+\beta)^{36}e^{-\gamma^{\rm tr}\mathfrak b(x_{n-1})^2/8}\,\|w_1\|_\infty\|w_2\|_\infty .
\]
\item[(ii)] Let $N=2L^{\mathsf M}$, $N'=L^sN$ with $s\ge1$, $1\le n<\mathsf M$ with $N/L^n\ge\max\{192,\,48(3\log L+\log2)/(\delta_{\rm tp}L(L-1)),\,C_LM/L\}$, $\delta_{\rm tp}>0$ the rate of Props.~\YMMref{120.5}{821} and~\YMMref{120.6}{821}, and $\pi$ the reduction $\mathbb Z^3_{N'}\to\mathbb Z^3_N$. For plaquettes $p',q'$ of $\mathbb Z^3_{N'}$ whose base points have a distance $\le N/8$: $|\mathsf g_2[N,n](\pi p',\pi q')-\mathsf g_2[N',n](p',q')|\le CN'^{237}e^{-\delta_{\rm tp}N/(48L^{n-1})}$.
\item[(iii)] Let $\ell'=2L^{m'}\ge N_{\mathsf H}$, the side threshold fixed in Section~\YMMref{52.6}{426} and retained for the kernel bounds in Section~\YMMref{120.3}{820}, $\ell'L\ge C_LM$ and $K\ge1$. For plaquettes $p,q$ of $\mathbb Z^3_{\ell'L^K}$ and plaquettes $\tilde p,\tilde q$ of $\mathbb Z^3$ over them with $|x_{\tilde p}-x_{\tilde q}|_\infty\le\ell'L^K/8$: $|\mathsf g_2[\ell'L^K,K](p,q)-\mathsf B_1^{\rm lat}(\tilde p,\tilde q)|\le3C_\star\ell'^{19}KL^{-K/2}$, with a number $C_\star$ independent of the side.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(i) In the chart of Lem.~\ref{C-351-9} at the trivial block field of the level $n$, an exact identity, made one level at a time along matched chains of fields, shows that at a real field scale $\mathsf z$ the sum of the jets of the levels $\le n$ is the covariance of two observables in the probability measure $\propto\exp[-\mathsf z^{-2}\mathcal Q(\mathsf zg\zeta)-\mathcal Q'(\mathsf zg\zeta)]d\zeta$ on the product of the boxes, $g\zeta=(x_i^{-1/2}\zeta_i)_i$. Here $\mathcal Q\ge0$ has a positive definite Hessian, block diagonal over the levels; $\mathcal Q$, $\mathcal Q'$ and the observables are real analytic near $0$ and contain no $\mathsf z$, no counterterm and no box; and, up to colour rotations at each level, which keep the boxes and the Lebesgue measure, they are $\beta$ times the action with the gauge fixing of the strengths $\mathsf k_j=x_j/\beta$, the function $\theta_{\rm ch}$, and $\mathcal O(w_a)\circ\Upsilon$.

The chart is read there on the product of the boxes $|\mathcal A_i|<x_i^{-1/2}\mathfrak b(x_i)$ of the fields $\mathcal A_i=x_i^{-1/2}\zeta_i$, and these boxes lie in $\Omega$ once $\delta(x_i)=x_i^{-1/2}\mathfrak b(x_i)<\rho_2$; as $\rho_2$ depends only on the constants (it is written out in the proof of Lem.~\ref{C-351-9}), and as $\delta$ decreases on $[e^{2p_0},\infty)$ while all the couplings of the run exceed the inverse square of the coupling $g$ of the datum (Lem.~\ref{C-351-8}), this is a condition on the coupling $g$ alone, and it enters $\gamma_{\rm e}$. So $\mathsf h^{(n)}_6$ is the second Laplace coefficient computed with the Gaussian measures restricted to the boxes.

Without the boxes, $\beta^3a_K^2$ times this coefficient is $\mathsf T[N,n](w)$, by the intrinsic fibre-coefficient identity of Prop.~\ref{C-350-12}(iii) and because the second Laplace coefficient of $c\,\mathcal Q$ scales like $c^{-3}$. For these matched chains, Prop.~\ref{C-350-11}(ii) bounds the change on restricting the Gaussian cumulants to the boxes: the total polynomial order is at most $10$, there are at most $N^3$ places, and its Gaussian precision and normalisation bounds give the stated $(N+\beta)^{36}$ times exponential error.
(ii) Apply Prop.~\ref{C-350-14} with $t=n$ and
$m'=2$. Its lower bound on $N/L^n$ is the one in this statement, and
$\delta_{\rm tp}L(N/L^n)/48=\delta_{\rm tp}N/(48L^{n-1})$.
The coefficients are the same intrinsic fibre coefficients by
Prop.~\ref{C-350-12}(iii), so its estimate gives the assertion.

(iii) This is the coarser bound already stated in
Prop.~\ref{C-350-15}, at the side $\ell'$. The side threshold, room
condition and separation of the lifted plaquettes are exactly those of
that proposition. Its detailed proof keeps both the torus-to-lattice
kernel comparison and the correction from the flat top.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Removal of the cutoff at a fixed label]\label{C-351-13}
Let $0<g\le\gamma_{\rm e}$, $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$ and $\vartheta\in(0,1)$. Let $\mathsf J_g=[\gamma^{-2},L(X_g+\bar B)]$, let $\mathsf C'=\mathsf C'_2(\mathsf J_g)$ be the number of the definition in Cor.~\YMMref{117.1}{812} at $n=2$ on the side $\ell$, $\mathsf p_2=6p_0+\frac12$ the exponent~the exponent defined before Thm.~\YMMref{AR}{810} at $n=2$, $c_\diamond=\sup_{k\ge1}k^{\mathsf p_2}L^{-k/20}<\infty$, and
\[
\epsilon_\diamond(d)=(X_g+\bar B)^3\,\mathsf C'\,\ell^9\,c_\diamond\Bigl(\frac{40M}\vartheta\Bigr)^2d^{87}.
\]
There are $d_{\rm K}\in(0,\frac1{200}]$ and integers $K_\sharp(d)>s(d)$ with $d^{-1800}<L^{K_\sharp(d)}\le d^{-1801}$ for $0<d\le d_{\rm K}$, such that the following holds at every label $b\in I(g)$, at which every pair $(K,L^Kb)$, $K\in\mathbb N$, is a first-passage datum at $g$, for $0<d\le d_{\rm K}$ and $(f,h)\in\mathfrak T_{T_\ell}(d;\vartheta)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] For every $K\ge K_\sharp(d)$
\[
|S^T_{2;K,\ell,L^Kb}(f,h)-S^T_{2;K_\sharp(d),\ell,L^{K_\sharp(d)}b}(f,h)|\le\epsilon_\diamond(d)\,b^{-3}d\,\|f\|_\infty\|h\|_\infty ,
\]
and the same with $S_2^{(\ell,b)}(f,h)$ in the place of the first term.
\item[(b)] If, for numbers $\epsilon_{\rm h},C_{\rm h}\ge0$, the cutoff $K_\sharp(d)$ has $|S^T_{2;K_\sharp(d),\ell,L^{K_\sharp(d)}b}-L_b^+|(f,h)\le[\epsilon_{\rm h}\,b^{-3}d+C_{\rm h}\,b^{-2}a_{K_\sharp(d)}/d]\,\|f\|_\infty\|h\|_\infty$, then for every $K\ge K_\sharp(d)$
\[
|S^T_{2;K,\ell,L^Kb}-L_b^+|(f,h)\le\bigl[\epsilon_{\rm h}+\epsilon_\diamond(d)+C_{\rm h}(X_g+\bar B)\,d^{1798}\bigr]\,b^{-3}d\,\|f\|_\infty\|h\|_\infty ,
\]
with no term in $a_K$, and the same with $S_2^{(\ell,b)}$ in the place of $S^T_{2;K,\ell,L^Kb}$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
\emph{The rate.} the constants and thresholds in Thm.~\YMMref{AR}{810} and Thm.~\YMMref{AR}{810}, equation~\YMMref{(2203)}{810} are made in the setting (Th1), (Th2), whose datum is the choice of the constants and whose numbers are formed from it. The interval $\mathsf J_g$ contains $I(g)$, and it is an interval of labels under (Tor) on the side $\ell$ (Lem.~\ref{lem:cutoff-admissible-labels}). Let $\mathsf C=\mathsf C_2(\mathsf J_g)$, $K_0=K_0(\ell,2,\mathsf J_g)$ and $K_1(\cdot)=K_1(\ell,2,\mathsf J_g,\cdot)$ be the other numbers of the constants and thresholds in Thm.~\YMMref{AR}{810} at $n=2$; so $\mathsf C'=\mathsf C\sum_{j\ge0}(1+j)^{\mathsf p_2}L^{-j/10}$. For real Lipschitz functions $f,h$ on $T_\ell$, neither of them $0$, whose supports have the spread $\mathsf d_\infty(f,h)\ge d'>0$ in the sup distance, the uniform cutoff estimate of Thm.~\YMMref{AR}{810} gives, at every label $b\in\mathsf J_g$ and every integer $K\ge K_1(d')$, the inequality~\YMMref{(2203)}{810} at $n=2$,
\[
|S^T_{2;K+1,\ell,L^{K+1}b}(f,h)-S^T_{2;K,\ell,L^Kb}(f,h)|\le\mathsf C\,\ell^9K^{\mathsf p_2}L^{-K/10}\,\|f\|_\sharp\|h\|_\sharp ,
\]
and its sum over the cutoffs, with $(K+j)^{\mathsf p_2}\le K^{\mathsf p_2}(1+j)^{\mathsf p_2}$, is the inequality~\YMMref{(2207)}{812} of Cor.~\YMMref{117.1}{812}:
\[
|S^T_{2;K',\ell,L^{K'}b}(f,h)-S^T_{2;K,\ell,L^Kb}(f,h)|\le\mathsf C'\,\ell^9K^{\mathsf p_2}L^{-K/10}\,\|f\|_\sharp\|h\|_\sharp\qquad(K'\ge K\ge K_1(d')).
\]
The supports of a pair $(f,h)\in\mathfrak T_{T_\ell}(d;\vartheta)$ are at the Euclidean distance $\ge d$, so at the sup distance $\ge d/\sqrt3$, both distances of $T_\ell$ being minima over the lifts and $|v|_\infty\ge|v|/\sqrt3$ on $\mathbb R^3$; so $\mathsf d_\infty(f,h)\ge d/\sqrt3$ (the definition preceding Lem.~\YMMref{114.6}{805}), and $d'=d/\sqrt3$ serves; put $K_\diamond(d)=K_1(d/\sqrt3)$. Moreover $\|f\|_\sharp\le40M\|f\|_\infty/(\vartheta d)$, as ${\rm Lip}\,f\le\|f\|_\infty/(\vartheta d)$ and $40M\ge\vartheta d$, and the same for $h$.

\emph{The threshold.} By~the two threshold inequalities at the end of the proof of Thm.~\YMMref{AR}{810} at $n=2$, $K_1(d')$ is the least integer $k\ge K_0$ such that every integer $K\ge k$ has
\[
d'L^u\ge6M\qquad\text{and}\qquad A_\diamond\,N_{[u]}\,e^{-d'L^u/M}\le\tfrac12\mathsf C\,\ell^9K^{\mathsf p_2}L^{-K/10},
\]
with the depth $u=\lceil K/1800\rceil$ of~the depth choice preceding Thm.~\YMMref{AR}{810} at $n=2$, $N_{[u]}=\ell^3L^{3u}$, and $A_\diamond=8e^3E_0C_{\rm E,0}\varrho^{-2}$ the factor in front of $N_{[u]}$ in~the two threshold inequalities at the end of the proof of Thm.~\YMMref{AR}{810}, $\varrho$ being the radius of the class of sources~in \S\ref{sec:cutoff-calibration} that stands in the formulas of the constants and thresholds in Thm.~\YMMref{AR}{810}, not the radius of the choice. The first condition at $K=K_\diamond(d)$, with $u<K/1800+1$, gives $L^{K_\diamond(d)}>(6\sqrt3M/(Ld))^{1800}$; as $6\sqrt3M>L$ (the cube size is $M=L^{m'}$ with $m'\ge5$), $a_{K_\diamond(d)}<d^{1800}$. Conversely let $\Lambda_\diamond(d)=4000+366\log(\sqrt3M/d)$, and let $K$ be an integer whose number $v=L^u$ has $v\ge(\sqrt3M/d)\Lambda_\diamond(d)$.

The first condition holds at $d'=d/\sqrt3$, as $\Lambda_\diamond(d)\ge6$. As $K\le1800u$, $L^{-K/10}\ge v^{-180}$; with $K^{\mathsf p_2}\ge1$ and $\ell\ge1$ the second condition follows from $A_\diamond v^{183}e^{-d'v/M}\le\frac12\mathsf C$, that is, from $\varphi_\diamond(v)=d'v/M-183\log v\ge\log(2A_\diamond/\mathsf C)$, and $2A_\diamond<\mathsf C$: at $n=2$, as $\log(L\cdot L(X_g+\bar B))\ge1$ and $\bar{\mathsf C}_{\mathsf M}\ge\varrho^{-1}$ in~the majorant definitions in the proof of Thm.~\YMMref{AR}{810}, the number $\mathsf C$ of~\YMMref{(2206)}{811} is at least $4\,(16\varrho^{-1})^2\,2^3(640/\pi)^2(1+8E_0C_{\rm E,0})>2A_\diamond$. So $\varphi_\diamond(v)\ge0$ suffices. The function $\varphi_\diamond$ increases for $v\ge183M/d'$, and at $v=(M/d')\Lambda_\diamond(d)=(\sqrt3M/d)\Lambda_\diamond(d)$, since $183\log\lambda<\frac12\lambda$ for $\lambda\ge4000$, $\varphi_\diamond>\frac12\Lambda_\diamond(d)-183\log(\sqrt3M/d)=2000$; so $\varphi_\diamond(v)>0$ for all these $v$.

Every $K\ge1800\log_L(\sqrt3M\Lambda_\diamond(d)/d)$ has such a $v$, and $L^{\lceil x\rceil}<L\cdot L^x$. So
\[
\Bigl(\frac{6\sqrt3M}{Ld}\Bigr)^{1800}<L^{K_\diamond(d)}\le\max\Bigl\{L^{K_0},\ L\Bigl(\frac{\sqrt3M\,\Lambda_\diamond(d)}d\Bigr)^{1800}\Bigr\}.
\]

\emph{(a).} For $K\ge K_\diamond(d)$: $K^{\mathsf p_2}L^{-K/10}\le c_\diamond L^{-K/20}\le c_\diamond\,a_{K_\diamond(d)}^{1/20}<c_\diamond d^{90}$. So for $b\in I(g)\subset\mathsf J_g$, $K'\ge K\ge K_\diamond(d)$ and $(f,h)\in\mathfrak T_{T_\ell}(d;\vartheta)$
\[
|S^T_{2;K',\ell,L^{K'}b}(f,h)-S^T_{2;K,\ell,L^Kb}(f,h)|\le\mathsf C'\ell^9c_\diamond\Bigl(\frac{40M}\vartheta\Bigr)^2d^{88}\,\|f\|_\infty\|h\|_\infty\le\epsilon_\diamond(d)\,b^{-3}d\,\|f\|_\infty\|h\|_\infty ,
\]
as $d^{88}=b^{-3}d\cdot b^3d^{87}$ and $b\le X_g+\bar B$ on $I(g)$. Put $K_\sharp(d)=\max\{K_\diamond(d),s(d)+1\}$; then $L^{K_\sharp(d)}\ge L^{K_\diamond(d)}>d^{-1800}$. From $L^{s(d)}d<LC_W(s(d))=L\mathsf c_W(\log L^{s(d)}+\log(X_g+\bar B))^{2p_0}$ one gets $L^{s(d)}\le d^{-2}$, so $L^{s(d)+1}\le d^{-3}$, for small $d$; and, $K_0$ being fixed with $g$ and $\ell$, $L^{K_0}\le L(\sqrt3M\Lambda_\diamond(d)/d)^{1800}\le d^{-1801}$ for small $d$. Let $d_{\rm K}\in(0,\frac1{200}]$ be a number below which these hold; then $L^{K_\sharp(d)}\le d^{-1801}$ for $0<d\le d_{\rm K}$. The last display, with $K\ge K_\sharp(d)$ in the place of $K'$ and $K_\sharp(d)$ in the place of $K$, is~(a) at the finite cutoffs. At the labels of $I(g)$ the limit $S_2^{(\ell,b)}(f,h)$ exists along the full sequence of the cutoffs (Cor.~\YMMref{118.4}{815}), and a bound that holds at all large $K$ with one right member holds for the limit.

\emph{(b).} For $b\in I(g)$ the pairs $(K,L^Kb)$, $K\in\mathbb N$, are the first-passage data at $g$ with the label $b$ (Cor.~\YMMref{118.4}{815}). The main term $L_b^+(f,h)$ reads the label and the pair, not the cutoff. By the triangle inequality, (a) and the inequality assumed at $K_\sharp(d)$, the left member at $K\ge K_\sharp(d)$, and at the limit, is at most $[\epsilon_{\rm h}b^{-3}d+\epsilon_\diamond(d)b^{-3}d+C_{\rm h}b^{-2}a_{K_\sharp(d)}/d]\|f\|_\infty\|h\|_\infty$, and $b^{-2}a_{K_\sharp(d)}/d=b^{-3}d\cdot b\,a_{K_\sharp(d)}d^{-2}<b^{-3}d\cdot(X_g+\bar B)\,d^{1798}$, as $a_{K_\sharp(d)}\le a_{K_\diamond(d)}<d^{1800}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The law on the least torus]\label{C-351-14}
Let $0<g\le\gamma_{\rm e}$, $\vartheta\in(0,1)$, $\ell=\ell_g$ and $C_{\rm cut}=\frac32C_{\rm tm}\vartheta^{-1}$. There is a non-decreasing function $\bar\varepsilon=\bar\varepsilon_{g,\vartheta}$ on $(0,d_{\rm e}(g,\vartheta)]$, $\bar\varepsilon(d)\to0$, depending on $g$, $\vartheta$ and the constants and on no $K$, $\beta$, label, pair or position, such that for $0<d\le d_{\rm e}(g,\vartheta)$ and $\Psi=(f,h)\in\mathfrak T_{T_\ell}(d;\vartheta)$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] at every first-passage datum $(K,\beta)$ at $g$ with $s(d)<K$ and $L^K\le d^{-1801}$, whatever its label $b=a_K\beta$,
\[
|S^T_{2;K,\ell,\beta}-L_b^+|(f,h)\le\bigl[\bar\varepsilon(d)\,b^{-3}d+C_{\rm cut}\,b^{-2}a_K/d\bigr]|\Psi| ;
\]
\item[(b)] for $b\in I(g)$ the same holds at $(K,L^Kb)$ for every $K>s(d)$, and $|S_2^{(\ell,b)}-L_b^+|(f,h)\le\bar\varepsilon_\infty(d)\,b^{-3}d\,|\Psi|$ with a non-decreasing $\bar\varepsilon_\infty=\bar\varepsilon_{\infty;g,\vartheta}\le\bar\varepsilon$ and $\bar\varepsilon_\infty(d)\le C(g,\vartheta)d^{1/2}$;
\item[(c)] with $C'_{\rm cut}=\frac92C_{\rm tm}\vartheta^{-1}+1$ in the place of $C_{\rm cut}$, the tolerance has the rate $d^{1/2}$ at every cutoff: there is $C_{\rm r}(g,\vartheta)<\infty$ with $|S^T_{2;K,\ell,L^Kb}-L_b^+|(f,h)\le[C_{\rm r}\,b^{-3}d^{3/2}+C'_{\rm cut}\,b^{-2}a_K/d]|\Psi|$ for all $b\in I(g)$ and $K>s(d)$, and $|S_2^{(\ell,b)}-L_b^+|(f,h)\le C_{\rm r}\,b^{-3}d^{3/2}|\Psi|$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
\emph{Before the chain.} If $f\circ x$ or $h\circ x$ vanishes identically, then $S^T_{2;K,\ell,\beta}(f,h)$, all the jets and every lattice sum of the sources vanish (Lem.~\ref{C-351-8}), and Lem.~\ref{C-351-10}~(iii) holds by the template sum alone; in the chain below every arrow but the last then reads $0=0$, and the last is~\eqref{C-351-11} as it stands, with $\mathsf P_1^{\rm lat}=0$. Let $\mathsf r=d/a_K$, so that $\mathsf r\ge L(\log\frac1d)^2$. Translations keep the class and the $\mathcal K_q$, so Lem.~\ref{C-351-10}~(iv), (i), (iii) at the pairs $(\tau_vf,\tau_vh)$ give
\[
\begin{multlined}
|S^T_{2;K,\ell,\beta}-L_b^+|(f,h)\le\Bigl[C(g,\vartheta)\bigl(d^{1/2}+d(\log\tfrac1d)^{8p_0}\bigr)b^{-3}d+C_{\rm cut}\,b^{-2}\frac{a_K}d\Bigr]|\Psi|+\max_{v\in\mathsf{Pk}}|\mathsf h_6 \\
-\varkappa b^{-3}\mathcal K_5|(\tau_vf,\tau_vh),
\end{multlined}
\]
the packing mean costing $C_{\rm A}(g)\vartheta^{-1}bd$ and the orders $\ge8$ costing $Cb^{-1}d\,\mathsf l^{8p_0}$ in the unit $b^{-3}d|\Psi|$. As $\mathsf h_6=b^{-3}a_K\mathsf H^{(K)}$ and $b^{-3}a_K\mathsf r=b^{-3}d$, it remains to show $|\mathsf H^{(K)}-\varkappa\mathcal K_5/a_K|\le\eta(d)\,\mathsf r\,|\Psi|$ with $\eta(d)\to0$ uniformly; all the costs below are in the unit $\mathsf r|\Psi|$.

\emph{The levels.} Let $K'=\max\{K,\lceil24\log_L\mathsf r\rceil\}$, so that $L^{K'}\ge\mathsf r^{24}$ and $K'\le C\log\frac1d$; let $n_1=K'-\lceil K'/78\rceil$, $N_0=\ell L^K$ and $N'=\ell L^{K'}$. If $K'>K$, let $n_0$ be the level with $D_{n_0}\in[d^{1/2},Ld^{1/2})$, $b_*\in I(g)$ fixed, $D'=(K',L^{K'}b_*)$, a first-passage datum at $g$, and $\breve w_a$ the sources lifted to one copy in $\mathbb Z^3_{N'}$ of a ball of radius $N_0/4$ that holds the supports; by Lem.~\ref{C-351-8} the lifted sources are a pair at the datum $D'$, with no condition on its depth. The chain is
\[
\mathsf H^{(K)}\to\mathsf H^{(n_0)}\to\mathsf T[N_0,n_0]\to\mathsf T[N',n_0]\to\mathsf H^{(n_0)}[D']\to\mathsf H^{(n_1)}[D']\to\mathsf T[N',n_1]\to\mathsf T^{\rm lat}\to\varkappa\mathcal K_5/a_K ,
\]
with $\mathsf T^{\rm lat}=\sum\tilde w_1(\tilde p)\tilde w_2(\tilde q)\mathsf B_1^{\rm lat}(\tilde p,\tilde q)$ for the sources of the lifts $\tilde f,\tilde h$ to $\mathbb R^3$. By Lem.~\ref{C-351-10}~(ii) at $n=n_0$, the first arrow costs at most $C\mathsf l^{6p_0}(d/D_{n_0})^{3/2}\le C\mathsf l^{6p_0}d^{3/4}$. By Lem.~\ref{C-351-12}~(i), with $x_{n_0-1}\ge\frac34b/D_{n_0-1}\ge\frac34d^{-1/2}$ (Lem.~\ref{C-351-8}) and $N_0+\beta\le(\ell+X_g+\bar B)d^{-1801}$, as $b\le L(g^{-2}+\bar B)=X_g+\bar B$, the second costs at most $e^{-c(\log\frac1d)^{2p_0}}$ times a power of $1/d$. By Lem.~\ref{C-351-12}~(ii), applied pair by pair to the at most $900\mathsf r^6$ pairs of plaquettes of the supports, with $N_0/L^{n_0}=\ell/D_{n_0}\ge\ell d^{-1/2}/L$, the third costs at most $900\mathsf r^5CN'^{237}e^{-\delta_{\rm tp}\ell d^{-1/2}/48}$.

By Lem.~\ref{C-351-12}~(i) at $(D',n_0)$, the number $\mathsf T[N',n_0]$ being free of $\beta$, and with $x'_{n_0-1}\ge\frac34\mathsf r^{11}$, the fourth costs less than every power of $d$. By Lem.~\ref{C-351-10}~(ii) at $D'$ the fifth costs at most $C\mathsf l'^{6p_0}d^{3/4}$, $\mathsf l'\le\log(2X_g+2\bar B)+K'\log L$. By Lem.~\ref{C-351-12}~(i) at $(D',n_1)$, with $x'_{n_1-1}\ge L^{K'/78}$, the sixth costs less than every power of $d$. By Lem.~\ref{C-351-12}~(iii) on the torus of the side $N'/L^{n_1}=\ell L^{\lceil K'/78\rceil}$ with $n_1$ levels, over at most $900\mathsf r^6$ pairs, the seventh costs at most $C\ell^{19}K'\mathsf r^5L^{-K'/4}\le CK'/\mathsf r$, since $\mathsf r^{24}\le L^{K'}$.

By~\eqref{C-351-11} at $a=a_K$, as $a_K\mathsf T^{\rm lat}=\mathsf P_1^{\rm lat}(\tilde f,\tilde h;a_K)$, the eighth costs at most $C_\varkappa\vartheta^{-1}\lg(\mathsf r)/\mathsf r$. If $K'=K$, that is $\mathsf r^{24}\le L^K$, there is no second datum and no second torus: the chain is $\mathsf H^{(K)}\to\mathsf H^{(n_1)}\to\mathsf T[N_0,n_1]\to\mathsf T^{\rm lat}\to\varkappa\mathcal K_5/a_K$, its first arrow by Lem.~\ref{C-351-10}~(ii) at $n=n_1$, with the cost $C\mathsf l^{6p_0}(\mathsf r/L^{n_1})^{3/2}$, $\mathsf r/L^{n_1}\le L^{1-0.94K}$ and $\mathsf l\le\log(2X_g+2\bar B)+K\log L$, and the other three as the last three above with $D'=D$ and $N'=N_0$.

\emph{The conditions and the limits.} At the three places where Lem.~\ref{C-351-12}~(i) is used its two conditions hold for $d\le d_{\rm e}$, because $\frac18\gamma^{\rm tr}\mathfrak b(X)^2=\frac18\gamma^{\rm tr}A_1^2(\log X)^{2p_0}$ with $2p_0\ge2$ outgrows $10+\log(10240N^3)$, the logarithm of $N$ being at most a constant plus a fixed multiple of $\log X$ at the lower bounds $X$ of the three places. Every cost tends to $0$ with $d$, uniformly ($\mathsf r\to\infty$, $K'\le C\log\frac1d$), and depends only on $g$, $\vartheta$ and the constants; $\bar\varepsilon(d)$ is the supremum over $d''\le d$ of their sum. This is~(a).

\emph{Removal of the cutoff.} For $b\in I(g)$ the pairs $(K,L^Kb)$ are first-passage data at $g$, and for $s(d)<K\le K_\sharp(d)$, (a) applies, as $L^K\le d^{-1801}$. At $K_\sharp(d)$ the inequality of (a) is the one that Lem.~\ref{C-351-13}~(b) asks there, with $\epsilon_{\rm h}=\bar\varepsilon(d)$ and $C_{\rm h}=C_{\rm cut}$; so for $K\ge K_\sharp(d)$ and for the limit the inequality holds with the tolerance $\bar\varepsilon(d)+\epsilon_\diamond(d)+C_{\rm cut}(X_g+\bar B)d^{1798}$ and without the second member, and $\bar\varepsilon+\sup_{d''\le d}[\epsilon_\diamond(d'')+C_{\rm cut}(X_g+\bar B)d''^{1798}]$ serves in (a) and (b). At $K_\sharp$ one has $\mathsf r\ge d^{-3}$, so the second, third, fourth and sixth costs are below every power of $d$, $K'/\mathsf r$ and $\lg(\mathsf r)/\mathsf r$ are at most $Cd^2$, the packing mean and the orders $\ge8$ give $Cd(\log\frac1d)^{8p_0}$, the order six $C\mathsf l^{6p_0}d^{3/4}$, and the slowest member is the order four, $\bar\varepsilon_4(g,d)\le C(g)d^{1/2}$: this is the rate of $\bar\varepsilon_\infty$.

\emph{The rate at every cutoff.} Run the same chain with the cut at $D_{n_0}\in[d^{1/5},Ld^{1/5})$; the arithmetic of the levels goes through as before for $d\le L^{-13}$. The first and fifth arrows now cost at most $C\mathsf l^{6p_0}d^{6/5}$ and $C\mathsf l'^{6p_0}d^{6/5}$, the third $e^{-c\ell d^{-1/5}}$ times a power of $1/d$, and the second, fourth and sixth stay below every power of $d$. The seventh and eighth members, which near the smallest $\mathsf r$ decay only like a power of $\log\frac1d$, contribute at most $C(K'+\lg\mathsf r)\mathsf r^{-1}\,b^{-3}d|\Psi|=C(K'+\lg\mathsf r)(d/b)\,b^{-2}(a_K/d)|\Psi|\le\eta(d)\,b^{-2}(a_K/d)|\Psi|$, with $\eta(d)=Cg^2d\log\frac1d\le1$ for $d\le d_{\rm e}$; they go into the second member, whose constant becomes at most $C_{\rm cut}+1\le C'_{\rm cut}$.

All the remaining members are $O(d\,(\log\frac1d)^{8p_0})$ but the order four, which is at most $C(g)d^{1/2}$. Beyond $K_\sharp(d)$, Lem.~\ref{C-351-13}~(b), with $C_{\rm h}=C'_{\rm cut}$, removes the second member at the price $\epsilon_\diamond(d)+C'_{\rm cut}(X_g+\bar B)d^{1798}$, at most a constant times $d^{1/2}$. This is~(c).
\end{proof}

The coefficient $\frac8{3\pi}$ comes from $\varkappa=c_1c_2$ in~\eqref{C-351-11} alone; in particular it does not depend on $L$, $g$ or the label.

\subsubsection{Transfer to continuum components}

\begin{lemma}[From a limit at a fixed label to the components]\label{C-351-15}
Let $\mathfrak c$ be a choice, $0<g\le\gamma_W$, $S$ a volume-first limit at $g$, $b=\mathsf b(S)$, $\mathsf S$ the function $S_2$ or a function $S_2^\xi$ of a canonical decomposition of $\sigma_S$, $\vartheta\in(0,1)$, $z\in\mathbb Z$, and $\tau'=(g',b',\ell')$ an admissible triple with $b'=L^zb$. For $L^zd\le d_\flat(g',\vartheta)$ and $\Psi\in\mathfrak T^1(d;\vartheta)$,
\[
|b^2\mathsf S(\Psi)-b'^2T^{(\ell',b')}(\Psi_{L^z})|\le E_{\tau'}\,(d/b)^2|\Psi| .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Let $(K_j,\beta_j,\nu_j)$ define $S$; then $a_{K_j}\beta_j\to b$. $\mathsf S$ is the limit of $S_2^T[\rho_j]$ for periodic Gibbs states $\rho_j$ at $(K_j,\beta_j)$, the class of Prop.~\ref{C-351-7}, which is $\mathcal G^{\rm per}_{K_j,\beta_j}=\mathcal G^{\rm inv}_{K_j,\beta_j}$ and holds the states of the tori: $\rho_j=\nu_j$ for $S_2$ ({\cite[\S{}K.1]{YMM2}}), and for $S_2^\xi$ the conditioned states of Thms.~\YMMref{AL}{746} and~\YMMref{AP}{780}. By Lem.~\ref{C-351-17}~(a) with $s=L^z$ the dilates $\rho_j^{(z)}$ are such states at $(K_j-z,\beta_j)$, and $S_2^T[\rho_j](\Phi)=L^{2z}S_2^T[\rho_j^{(z)}](\Phi_{L^z})$. As $a_{K_j-z}\beta_j=L^za_{K_j}\beta_j\to b'\in I^\circ(g')$, the pairs $(K_j-z,\beta_j)$ are first-passage data at $g'$ for large $j$ (Lem.~\ref{C-351-25}~(b)). Prop.~\ref{C-351-7} there, the $\rho_j^{(z)}$ being states at the datum, at the scale $L^zd\le\frac1{180}<\ell'/20$ and with $a_{K_j-z}\le9L^zd$ for large $j$, gives
\[
|S_2^T[\rho_j^{(z)}](\Psi_{L^z})-S^T_{2;K_j-z,\ell',\beta_j}((\Psi_{L^z})^{\langle\ell'\rangle})|\le2C_2^{\rm T}(g')\vartheta^{-1}(L^zd)^2(a_{K_j-z}\beta_j)^{-2}|\Psi| .
\]
Let $j\to\infty$, using the convergence along converging labels (Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AS}{813}}), and multiply by $b'^2=L^{2z}b^2$; then $2C_2^{\rm T}(g')\vartheta^{-1}L^{2z}d^2=E_{\tau'}(d/b)^2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[A second term excludes covariance]\label{C-351-16}
Let a functional $\sigma$ on separated tuples over $\mathbb R^3$ obey (L) with $(b,c,\varepsilon,d_7,\vartheta)$, $c\ne0$; let $d_1>0$, $\Psi\in\mathfrak T^1(d_1;\vartheta)$, $\mathsf B=c\,c_2b^{-3}\mathcal K_5(\Psi)$, $\mathsf u=b^{-3}d_1|\Psi|$ and $t>1$. Then
\[
\begin{multlined}
|S^\sigma_2(\Psi_r)-c_2b^{-2}\mathcal K_6(\Psi)-\mathsf Br|\le\varepsilon(rd_1)\,\mathsf u\,r\quad(rd_1\le d_7),\qquad|\mathcal N^{S_2^\sigma}_t(\Psi;r)+t(t-1)(t^5-1)\mathsf Br| \\
\le(t^2+t+t^6+t^7)\,\varepsilon(t^2rd_1)\,\mathsf u\,r\quad(t^2rd_1\le d_7);
\end{multlined}
\]
$\mathcal N^{S_2^\sigma}_t(\Psi;r)\ne0$, with the sign of $-c$, as soon as $(t^2+t+t^6+t^7)\varepsilon(t^2rd_1)<t(t-1)(t^5-1)\cdot10^{-5}|c|c_2\vartheta^2$; and $S_2^\sigma$ is not dilation covariant.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(L) at $\Psi_r\in\mathfrak T^1(rd_1;\vartheta)$, with $|\Psi_r|=|\Psi|$, $\mathcal K_6(\Psi_r)=\mathcal K_6(\Psi)$ and $\mathcal K_5(\Psi_r)=r\mathcal K_5(\Psi)$, gives the first bound. In $\mathcal N_t$ the weights $1,-(1+t^6),t^6$ at $t^2r,tr,r$ annul the constant $c_2b^{-2}\mathcal K_6(\Psi)$, give $\mathsf Br$ the factor $t^2-(1+t^6)t+t^6=-t(t-1)(t^5-1)$, and give the remainders a sum at most $(t^2+t+t^6+t^7)\varepsilon(t^2rd_1)\mathsf ur$, $\varepsilon$ being non-decreasing; at $t=2$ these are $-62$ and $198$. By~\eqref{C-351-2}, $|\mathsf B|\ge10^{-5}|c|c_2\vartheta^2\mathsf u$, which gives the sign. If $S_2^\sigma(\Phi_r)=r^\varpi S_2^\sigma(\Phi)$ for all $r>0$ and all separated $\Phi$, take $\Phi=\Psi$: by the first bound the left side tends to $c_2b^{-2}\mathcal K_6(\Psi)\in(0,\infty)$ as $r\to0$, so $S_2^\sigma(\Psi)\ne0$ and $r^\varpi$ has a finite non-zero limit, whence $\varpi=0$; then $S_2^\sigma(\Psi_r)=S_2^\sigma(\Psi)=c_2b^{-2}\mathcal K_6(\Psi)$ for all $r$, and the first bound gives $|\mathsf B|\le\varepsilon(rd_1)\mathsf u\to0$, against $|\mathsf B|\ge10^{-5}|c|c_2\vartheta^2\mathsf u>0$.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{An alternative transfer using two blocking factors}

\begin{lemma}[Three facts on the lattices]\label{C-351-17}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[beginpenalty=10000]
\item[(a)] For $a,s,\beta>0$ the map $x\mapsto sx$ carries the Gibbs states of the Wilson action at $\beta$ on $a\mathbb Z^3$, and the periodic ones, onto those on $sa\mathbb Z^3$. For the image $D_s\nu$ of $\nu$, $S^T_n[\nu](f_1,\dots,f_n)=s^nS^T_n[D_s\nu](f_1(\cdot/s),\dots,f_n(\cdot/s))$; so $(sa\beta)^2S^T_2[D_s\nu](\Psi_{sr})=(a\beta)^2S^T_2[\nu](\Psi_r)$.
\item[(b)] For $\ell=2L^m$, a compact set $J'\subset(0,\infty)$ and $d_*>0$ there is $C$ with $|S^T_{2;K,\ell,L^Kb}(u,w)|\le C\|u\|_\sharp\|w\|_\sharp$ for all $K$, all $b\in J'$ and all real Lipschitz $u,w$ on $T_\ell$ at a sup-distance $\ge d_*$. Hence, if $K_j\to\infty$, $a_{K_j}\beta_j\to b>0$ and $r_j\to r>0$, then $S^T_{2;K_j,\ell,\beta_j}((\Psi_{r_j})^{\langle\ell\rangle})\to T^{(\ell,b)}(\Psi_r)$ for every separated pair $\Psi$ whose dilate $\Psi_r$ has both supports in one ball of radius $<\ell/16$; for $\Psi\in\mathfrak T^1(d_1;\vartheta)$ it suffices that $80rd_1<\ell$.
\item[(c)] If $\log L_1/\log L_2\notin\mathbb Q$ and $\sigma_0>0$, there are integers $K_j,K'_j\to\infty$ with $L_1^{K_j}L_2^{-K'_j}\to\sigma_0$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(a) The action and the Haar measure depend on the lattice as a graph, and $a^{-1}\sum_pf(x(p))a_p=s\,(sa)^{-1}\sum_pf(sx(p)/s)\,a_p$, the plaquette $p$ of $a\mathbb Z^3$ going to the plaquette $sp$ of $sa\mathbb Z^3$; cumulants are multilinear. (b) The bound is Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AS}{813}} and its uniform bound~\YMMref{(2214)}{814}. For $C^1$ entries with compact supports $\|f(\cdot/r_j)-f(\cdot/r)\|_\sharp\to0$, and the dilated supports stay at a distance bounded below; so, by bilinearity, the pair may be fixed at $\Psi_r$, and the convergence along converging labels, Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AS}{813}}, applies. A pair of $\mathfrak T^1(d_1;\vartheta)$ dilated by $r$ lies in two balls of radius $rd_1$ whose centres are at most $8rd_1$ apart, so in one ball of radius $5rd_1$. (c) The multiples $K\log L_1$ are dense modulo $\log L_2$ (Kronecker's theorem).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[A second choice]\label{C-351-18}
Let $\varrho>0$, values of the constants of $\mathcal T^{\rm S}[2\varrho]$ with the blocking factor $L$, and an odd integer $Q\ge1$ be given. There is $j_0$ such that for every $j\ge j_0$ there is an admissible assignment of $\mathcal T^{\rm S}[2\varrho]$ in which the constants before $L$ keep their values and the blocking factor is $\tilde L=(LQ)^j+2$. $\tilde L$ is odd and prime to $L$ and to $Q$; $\log L/\log\tilde L\notin\mathbb Q$, and $\log Q/\log\tilde L\notin\mathbb Q$ if $Q>1$. With the radius and the mollifier of a choice $\mathfrak c$ it is a \emph{second choice} $\tilde{\mathfrak c}$ of $\mathfrak c$; at $Q=L$, $\tilde L=L^{2j}+2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
By the ordered choices in the proofs of Prop.~\YMMref{69.1}{595} and Lem.~\YMMref{82.1}{665}, for an admissible assignment $\sigma_0$ of the constants before $L$ there is an odd integer $L_\uparrow(\sigma_0)$ such that $(\sigma_0,L')$ is admissible for every odd $L'\ge L_\uparrow(\sigma_0)$: the conditions attached to the blocking factor are oddness and floors formed with the earlier constants; and every admissible assignment up to a place of the order of the constants is the truncation of a full admissible assignment. For large $j$, $\tilde L\ge L_\uparrow$. $\tilde L$ is odd; a prime that divides $\tilde L$ and $L$ (or $Q$) divides $2$, which is impossible. If $\log L/\log\tilde L=p/q$ with integers $p,q\ge1$, then $L^q=\tilde L^p$ with coprime $L,\tilde L>1$, which is impossible; the same for $Q>1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Two blocking factors]\label{C-351-19}
Let $\mathfrak c_1,\mathfrak c_2$ be choices with $\log L_1/\log L_2\notin\mathbb Q$, $\tau_i=(g_i,b_i,\ell_i)$ an admissible triple of $\mathfrak c_i$ (for $i=1$, $b_1\in I(g_1)$ suffices), $\vartheta\in(0,1)$, $d_1>0$, $\Psi\in\mathfrak T^1(d_1;\vartheta)$, and $\delta>0$ with $\delta b_1d_1\le d^{(1)}_\flat(g_1,\vartheta)$ and $\delta b_2d_1<d^{(2)}_\flat(g_2,\vartheta)$, the thresholds of Prop.~\ref{C-351-7} at $\mathfrak c_1$ and $\mathfrak c_2$. With $T$, $E$ and $Y$ formed at the respective choice,
\[
|Y_{\tau_1}(\delta)-Y_{\tau_2}(\delta)|\le(E_{\tau_1}+E_{\tau_2})\,d_1^2|\Psi|\,\delta^2 .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Lem.~\ref{C-351-17}~(c) gives $K_j,K'_j\to\infty$ with $s_j=L_2^{K'_j}L_1^{-K_j}\to b_1/b_2$. Put $\beta_j=L_1^{K_j}b_1$: $(K_j,\beta_j)$ is a first-passage datum of $\mathfrak c_1$ at $g_1$ with the label $b_1$, and $b_{2,j}=L_2^{-K'_j}\beta_j=b_1/s_j\to b_2\in I^\circ(g_2)$, so that $(K'_j,\beta_j)$ is a first-passage datum of $\mathfrak c_2$ at $g_2$ for large $j$ (Lem.~\ref{C-351-25}~(b) at $\mathfrak c_2$). Both data have the bare coupling $\beta_j$ on the lattice $\mathbb Z^3$ in lattice units. Let $\rho_j$ be a periodic Gibbs state at $\beta_j$ there, and $\rho_j^{(1)}$, $\rho_j^{(2)}$ its images on $L_1^{-K_j}\mathbb Z^3$ and $L_2^{-K'_j}\mathbb Z^3$; then $\rho_j^{(1)}=D_{s_j}\rho_j^{(2)}$, and by Lem.~\ref{C-351-17}~(a)
\[
b_1^2S^T_2[\rho^{(1)}_j](\Psi_{\delta b_1})=b_{2,j}^2S^T_2[\rho^{(2)}_j](\Psi_{\delta b_{2,j}}) .
\]
Prop.~\ref{C-351-7} at $\mathfrak c_1$ and at $\mathfrak c_2$ compares $\rho_j^{(1)}$ and $\rho_j^{(2)}$ with the Wilson measures on $T_{\ell_1}$ and $T_{\ell_2}$; after multiplication by $b_1^2$ and $b_{2,j}^2$ the errors are $E_{\tau_1}d_1^2|\Psi|\delta^2$ and, in the limit, $E_{\tau_2}d_1^2|\Psi|\delta^2$. As $j\to\infty$ the torus terms tend to $Y_{\tau_1}(\delta)$, by the limit at a fixed label along the full sequence, and to $Y_{\tau_2}(\delta)$, by Lem.~\ref{C-351-17}~(b), since $80\,\delta b_2d_1<1<\ell_2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Two labels; all real dilations]\label{C-351-23}
Let $\mathfrak c$ be a choice, $\tilde{\mathfrak c}$ a second choice of $\mathfrak c$ (Lem.~\ref{C-351-18} with $Q=L$) with an admissible triple $\tau_2=(g_2,b_2,\ell_2)$ and the threshold $\tilde d_\flat$, and $\vartheta\in(0,1)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] For admissible triples $\tau=(g,b,\ell)$ and $\tau'=(g',b',\ell')$ of $\mathfrak c$, $d_1>0$, $\Psi\in\mathfrak T^1(d_1;\vartheta)$ and $\delta>0$ with $\delta bd_1\le d_\flat(g,\vartheta)$, $\delta b'd_1\le d_\flat(g',\vartheta)$ and $\delta b_2d_1<\tilde d_\flat(g_2,\vartheta)$,
\[
|Y_\tau(\delta)-Y_{\tau'}(\delta)|\le(E_\tau+E_{\tau'}+2E_{\tau_2})\,d_1^2|\Psi|\,\delta^2 .
\]
Equivalently, with $s=b'/b$, for $\Phi\in\mathfrak T^1(d;\vartheta)$ with $d\le d_\flat(g,\vartheta)$, $sd\le d_\flat(g',\vartheta)$ and $(b_2/b)d<\tilde d_\flat(g_2,\vartheta)$: $|b'^2T^{(\ell',b')}(\Phi_s)-b^2T^{(\ell,b)}(\Phi)|\le(E_\tau+E_{\tau'}+2E_{\tau_2})(d/b)^2|\Phi|$. So, up to errors $O((d/b)^2)$, the limits on the tori at the labels $b$ and $b'$ are carried into each other by the real dilation by $b'/b$; for $b'/b$ a power of $L$ and $\ell'/\ell=b'/b$ this holds exactly, by Thm.~\ref{C-351-4}~(d).
\item[(ii)] If at one admissible triple $\tau_*=(g_*,b_*,\ell_*)$ of $\mathfrak c$ a function $T_*=T^{(\ell_*,b_*)}$ satisfies $|T_*(\Phi)-c_2b_*^{-2}[\mathcal K_6+cb_*^{-1}\mathcal K_5](\Phi)|\le\varepsilon(d)b_*^{-3}d|\Phi|$ for $0<d\le d_7$ and $\Phi\in\mathfrak T^1(d;\vartheta)$, with a real $c$ and a non-decreasing $\varepsilon\to0$, then at every admissible triple $\tau=(g,b,\ell)$ of $\mathfrak c$ the same inequality holds with the same $c$, with $b$ in the place of $b_*$ and with the tolerance $\varepsilon(b_*d/b)+(E_\tau+E_{\tau_*}+2E_{\tau_2})b^{-1}d$, for $d$ below the least of $(b/b_*)d_7$, $(b/b_*)d_\flat(g_*,\vartheta)$, $d_\flat(g,\vartheta)$ and $\frac12(b/b_2)\tilde d_\flat(g_2,\vartheta)$.

In particular the law of Thm.~\ref{C-351-4}~(a) at one admissible triple $(g^\circ,b^\circ,\ell_{g^\circ})$ with $g^\circ\le\Gamma$ gives the law with the same $\frac8{3\pi}$ at every admissible triple of $\mathfrak c$, on every side of $\mathfrak L(g)$, with the tolerance $\varepsilon^L_{g^\circ,\vartheta}(b^\circ d/b)+Cb^{-1}d$.
\item[(iii)] Let $S$ and $S'$ be volume-first limits at couplings $g$ and $g'$ with $0<g,g'\le\gamma_W$, with the labels $b=\mathsf b(S)$ and $b'=\mathsf b(S')$; let $\mathsf S$ be $S_2$ or a function $S_2^\xi$ of a canonical decomposition of $\sigma_S$, and $\mathsf S'$ be $S'_2$ or a function $S'^{\,\eta}_2$ of a canonical decomposition of $\sigma_{S'}$; let $z,z'\in\mathbb Z$, and let $\tau=(g_\tau,L^zb,\ell_\tau)$ and $\tau'=(g_{\tau'},L^{z'}b',\ell_{\tau'})$ be admissible triples of $\mathfrak c$. For $d_1>0$, $\Psi\in\mathfrak T^1(d_1;\vartheta)$ and $\delta>0$ with $\delta L^zbd_1\le d_\flat(g_\tau,\vartheta)$, $\delta L^{z'}b'd_1\le d_\flat(g_{\tau'},\vartheta)$ and $\delta b_2d_1<\tilde d_\flat(g_2,\vartheta)$,
\[
|b^2\mathsf S(\Psi_{\delta b})-b'^2\mathsf S'(\Psi_{\delta b'})|\le(2E_\tau+2E_{\tau'}+2E_{\tau_2})\,d_1^2|\Psi|\,\delta^2 .
\]
Equivalently, with $s=b'/b$, for $\Phi\in\mathfrak T^1(d;\vartheta)$ with $L^zd\le d_\flat(g_\tau,\vartheta)$, $L^{z'}sd\le d_\flat(g_{\tau'},\vartheta)$ and $(b_2/b)d<\tilde d_\flat(g_2,\vartheta)$: $|b'^2\mathsf S'(\Phi_s)-b^2\mathsf S(\Phi)|\le(2E_\tau+2E_{\tau'}+2E_{\tau_2})(d/b)^2|\Phi|$. So, up to errors $O((d/b)^2)$, the two-point functions of the volume-first limits and of all their components at the couplings $g\le\gamma_W$ are carried into each other by the real dilation by the quotient of their labels. The law of Thm.~\ref{C-351-3}~(1) at the two labels gives the same comparison with the error $2\varepsilon^{\rm nat}(d/b)(d/b)|\Phi|$, which is only $O((d/b)^{3/2})|\Phi|$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(i) Lem.~\ref{C-351-19} for the pair $(\mathfrak c,\tilde{\mathfrak c})$, whose blocking factors have incommensurable logarithms, at $(\tau,\tau_2)$ and at $(\tau',\tau_2)$, and the triangle inequality. For the second form put $\Phi=\Psi_{\delta b}$ and $d=\delta bd_1$; then $\Psi_{\delta b'}=\Phi_{b'/b}$ and $d_1^2\delta^2=(d/b)^2$. (ii) Let $\Phi\in\mathfrak T^1(d;\vartheta)$ and $\Phi_*=\Phi_{b_*/b}\in\mathfrak T^1(b_*d/b;\vartheta)$. By~(i), $b^2T^{(\ell,b)}(\Phi)$ is within $(E_\tau+E_{\tau_*}+2E_{\tau_2})(d/b)^2|\Phi|$ of $b_*^2T_*(\Phi_*)$, and by the assumption of~(ii) $b_*^2T_*(\Phi_*)$ is within $\varepsilon(b_*d/b)(d/b)|\Phi|$ of $c_2[\mathcal K_6(\Phi_*)+cb_*^{-1}\mathcal K_5(\Phi_*)]=c_2[\mathcal K_6(\Phi)+cb^{-1}\mathcal K_5(\Phi)]$; divide by $b^2$.

(iii) Lem.~\ref{C-351-15}, for $S$ with $z$ and $\tau$ at the pair $\Psi_{\delta b}\in\mathfrak T^1(\delta bd_1;\vartheta)$, and for $S'$ with $z'$ and $\tau'$ at the pair $\Psi_{\delta b'}$, gives $|b^2\mathsf S(\Psi_{\delta b})-Y_\tau(\delta)|\le E_\tau d_1^2|\Psi|\delta^2$ and $|b'^2\mathsf S'(\Psi_{\delta b'})-Y_{\tau'}(\delta)|\le E_{\tau'}d_1^2|\Psi|\delta^2$, as $(\Psi_{\delta b})_{L^z}=\Psi_{\delta L^zb}$ and $(d/b)^2=d_1^2\delta^2$ at $d=\delta bd_1$; (i) at $(\tau,\tau')$ and the triangle inequality give the bound, and the second form follows as in~(i). By Thm.~\ref{C-351-3}~(1) at $\Phi$ and at $\Phi_s\in\mathfrak T^1(sd;\vartheta)$, $b^2\mathsf S(\Phi)$ and $b'^2\mathsf S'(\Phi_s)$ lie within $\varepsilon^{\rm nat}(d/b)(d/b)|\Phi|$ of the one number $c_2[\mathcal K_6(\Phi)+\frac8{3\pi}b^{-1}\mathcal K_5(\Phi)]$, as $sd/b'=d/b$ and $b'^{-1}\mathcal K_5(\Phi_s)=b^{-1}\mathcal K_5(\Phi)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Non-covariance from the law at one triple]\label{C-351-20}
Let $\mathfrak c_*$ and $\mathfrak c^\circ$ be choices, equal or not, $\vartheta\in(0,1)$, and $\tau^\circ=(g^\circ,b^\circ,\ell^\circ)$ an admissible triple of $\mathfrak c^\circ$ such that, with $T^\circ=T^{(\ell^\circ,b^\circ)}$ formed at $\mathfrak c^\circ$, there are $d_n\to0$ and $\Psi_n\in\mathfrak T^1(d_n;\vartheta)$ with $|T^\circ(\Psi_n)-c_2b^{\circ-2}\mathcal K_6(\Psi_n)|/(d_n^2|\Psi_n|)\to\infty$. Then for every $0<g\le\gamma_W$ of $\mathfrak c_*$, every volume-first limit $S$ at $g$ and every canonical decomposition $(\mathsf X,\lambda,(\sigma_\xi))$ of $\sigma_S$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] neither $S_2$ nor any $S_2^\xi$ is dilation covariant: $\mathsf N=\mathsf X$ and $\lambda(\mathsf N)=1$;
\item[(ii)] there is no $d_*>0$ such that the three-scale number $S_2(\Psi_{4r})-65S_2(\Psi_{2r})+64S_2(\Psi_r)$ vanishes for all $d,r$ with $4rd\le d_*$ and all $\Psi\in\mathfrak T^1(d;\vartheta)$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Let $b=\mathsf b(S)$ and $\mathsf S=S_2$ or $S_2^\xi$. Both assertions follow once a bound
\begin{equation}\label{C-351-21}
|\mathsf S(\Phi)-c_2b^{-2}\mathcal K_6(\Phi)|\le C\,d^2|\Phi|\qquad(0<d\le d_0,\ \Phi\in\mathfrak T^1(d;\vartheta))
\end{equation}
is excluded for every $C$ and $d_0>0$. If $\mathsf S$ is dilation covariant with the exponent $\varpi$, the leading laws~\YMMref{(2353)}{852} and~\YMMref{(2356)}{854} gives $\mathsf S(\Phi_r)\to c_2b^{-2}\mathcal K_6(\Phi)\in(0,\infty)$ as $r\to0$, so $\varpi=0$ and $\mathsf S=c_2b^{-2}\mathcal K_6$ on the pairs of all the classes $\mathfrak T^1(d;\vartheta)$: \eqref{C-351-21} with $C=0$. If the three-scale number vanishes as in~(ii), we may take $d_*\le4\mathsf d_0(g,\vartheta)$; for $\Phi\in\mathfrak T^1(d';\vartheta)$ with $d_*/8<d'\le d_*/4$ the numbers $u_k=S_2(\Phi_{2^{-k}})$ satisfy $u_k-65u_{k+1}+64u_{k+2}=0$, so $u_k=\alpha+\alpha'64^{-k}$; by the leading law $\alpha=\lim_ku_k=c_2b^{-2}\mathcal K_6(\Phi)$ and $|\alpha'|=|u_0-\alpha|\le\frac13c_2b^{-2}\mathcal K_6(\Phi)\le C|\Phi|$.

Every pair of $\mathfrak T^1(d;\vartheta)$ with $d\le d_*/4$ is $\Phi_{2^{-k}}$ for such a $\Phi$ and some $k\ge0$, so $|S_2(\Phi_{2^{-k}})-c_2b^{-2}\mathcal K_6(\Phi_{2^{-k}})|\le C|\Phi|\,2^{-6k}\le C(8/d_*)^6d^6|\Phi|$: \eqref{C-351-21} with $d^6$ in the place of $d^2$.

Suppose now~\eqref{C-351-21}.
