For the squares $Q_i$ of side $a_i$ with corners in $\Lambda_i$ there are $i_2$ and $n_Q$ with $\mathcal W_K(Q_i)\ge\frac18$ for all $\mathsf b\in\mathsf J$, $i\ge i_2$ and $K>i+n_Q$. On sides with $\mathsf V_\ell>1$ these small rectangles must be so small that $\mathsf V_\ell L^{-i}$ is small. If $s\times T$ and $s\times2T$ are rectangles with $\kappa<\frac12$, then $\liminf_K\mathcal W_K(s\times nT)\ge\mathcal W(s\times2T)[\mathcal W(s\times2T)/\mathcal W(s\times T)]^{n-2}$ for every $n\ge2$ with $nT<\ell/2$.
\item[(5)] \emph{Block fields; a static source.} Let $\kappa<\frac12$ and $H$ be a bounded Borel gauge invariant function on $\mathcal V_{s_1}$. For $K>d'\ge\max\{s_0,s_1\}$,
\[\Bigl|a_K^{-\kappa}\langle W_{\mathsf C}H(\mathcal M^{K-s_1}U)\rangle_K-a_K^{-\kappa}\Xi_{K-d'}\frac1Z\int W^{(K-d')}_{\mathsf C}\,(H\circ\mathcal M^{d'-s_1})\,\mathrm{d}m_{K-d'}\Bigr|\le\sup|H|\,\mathsf E'_{d'};\]
so $\lim_Ka_K^{-\kappa}\langle W_{\mathsf C}H(\mathcal M^{K-s_1}U)\rangle_K$ exists along the full sequence and equals $\lim_d\mathsf l_d\int F^{[d]}_{\mathsf C}\,(H\circ\mathcal M^{d-s_1})\,\mathrm{d}\mu_d$. For a rectangle $C$ the quotients $\langle W_CH(\mathcal M^{K-s_1}U)\rangle_K/\langle W_C\rangle_K$ converge; their limit $\omega(H)$ is a linear functional on the bounded gauge invariant Borel functions of all block fields, real on the real ones, normalised, $\omega(1)=1$, consistent between the depths, $\omega(H\circ\mathcal M)=\omega(H)$, and bounded at each depth: $|\omega(H)|\le\sup|H|\,(c_\Xi L^{\kappa d'}+\mathsf E'_{d'})/\mathcal W(C)$ with $d'=\max\{s_0,s_1\}$, $\mathcal W(C)>0$ by (4); $c^{-1}a_d^\kappa\le\int Y_{d,C}\,\mathrm{d}\mu\le c\,a_d^\kappa$ for large $d$, and $\int H(V_{s_1})Y_{d,C}\,\mathrm{d}\mu/\int Y_{d,C}\,\mathrm{d}\mu$ tends to $\omega(H)$ as $d\to\infty$. For $H$ bounded Borel but not gauge invariant all of this holds with the gauge average $\bar H(V)=\int H(V^v)\,\mathrm{d}v$ (Haar measure on the gauge transformations of $\Lambda_{s_1}$) in the place of $H$, the Wilson measure, $\mu$ and $Y_{d,C}$ being gauge invariant.
\item[(6)] \emph{Mixed functions.} Let a coordinate mirror $\theta$ part $\mathsf C$, at distance $\ge\delta_1>0$ from its planes, from the supports of real Lipschitz $f_1,\dots,f_n$, at distance $\ge\delta>0$ from the planes, and let $2\kappa<\frac12$. Then $Q_K(z)=a_K^{-\kappa}\langle W_{\mathsf C}e^{\mathcal O(w_z)}\rangle_K/\langle e^{\mathcal O(w_z)}\rangle_K$, $w_z=\sum_qz_qf_q$, obeys $|Q_K(z)|\le\sqrt6\,e^{\Delta(\delta)/2}\mathcal W_K(\mathsf C,\theta\mathsf C)^{1/2}$ for $K>s_0$ on a polydisc free of $K$, and converges locally uniformly there to a holomorphic $Q$; the supports need not be disjoint. If they are pairwise disjoint, then $\lim_K\mathcal W_K(\mathsf C;f_1,\dots,f_n)$ exists along the full sequence and equals $\sum_{A\subset\{1,\dots,n\}}\partial_AQ(0)\sum_\pi\prod_{\beta\in\pi}S_{|\beta|}(f_\beta)$, $\pi$ running over the partitions of the complement of $A$ into blocks of at least two elements, $f_\beta=(f_q)_{q\in\beta}$.

The same holds for two orthogonal coordinate mirrors $\theta_1$, $\theta_2$ if $4\kappa<\frac12$, $\mathsf C$ lies on one side of both at distance $\ge\delta_1$ from their planes, and the $f_q$ fall into two groups, the first with supports on the other side of $\theta_1$, the second with supports on the side of $\mathsf C$ of $\theta_1$ and on the other side of $\theta_2$, the two groups at sup-distance $\ge2\delta$ and all supports at distance $\ge\delta$ from the planes. For $n=1$ it holds, if $2\kappa<\frac12$ and $\mathsf C$ has extent $<\frac\ell2$ in each coordinate direction, for every real Lipschitz $f$ whose support misses the least closed coordinate box that holds $\mathsf C$. Where no such mirror parts them, but $N$ equal coordinate boxes between equally spaced walls in $\frac12a_i\mathbb Z$, for an index $i$, hold each polygon in one box, the number of the boxes being even in every direction that the walls cut, so that both fixed planes $c$ and $c+\frac\ell2$ of every wall mirror are walls (on $\ell=2L^m$, $2L^j$ or $4L^j$ slabs in each cut direction), each $f_q$ is supported in one box, the supports lie off the walls and no box meets both a polygon and a support, one has $\langle W_{\mathsf C^{\rm f}_\iota}\rangle_K\ge0$ and $|Q_K(z)|\le M_S\prod_\iota\mathcal W_K(\mathsf C^{\rm f}_\iota)^{1/N}$ for $\sum_q|z_q|\|f_q\|_\sharp<\rho_D/N$, a polydisc free of $K$, with $\|f\|_\sharp$, $\rho_D$ and $M_S$ of Prop.~\ref{C-372-14}, $\mathsf C^{\rm f}_\iota$ being the family of the images under the wall reflections of the polygons $\mathsf C_\iota$ of the box $\iota$, which has exactly one image in every box, with $\kappa(\mathsf C^{\rm f}_\iota)=N\kappa(\mathsf C_\iota)$; so, if $N\kappa(\mathsf C_\iota)<\frac12$ for every box $\iota$, $\sup_K|\partial_AQ_K(0)|<\infty$ for every $A\subset\{1,\dots,n\}$, and this holds whatever the supports off the walls, a function whose support misses the walls being the sum of pieces each supported in one box; and $\sup_K|\mathcal W_K(\mathsf C;f_1,\dots,f_n)|<\infty$ when the supports are pairwise disjoint, the truncated functions of the action density being bounded in $K$ there \YMMref{(2212)}{813}; for $n=1$, $\mathcal W_K(\mathsf C;f_1)=\partial_1Q_K(0)$, with no further condition.

The limits obey the law of dilations $\mathcal W^{(L^z\ell,L^z\mathsf b)}(L^z\mathsf C;f^{(z)})=L^{-z\kappa-zn}\mathcal W^{(\ell,\mathsf b)}(\mathsf C;f)$, $f^{(z)}_q=f_q(L^{-z}\cdot)$, and the positive form of Prop.~\ref{C-372-13}(b) with mixed entries: let $\theta'$ be the coordinate mirror $\theta'x=x-2(x_\mu-\hat c)e_\mu$ with a place $\hat c\in\frac12a_{i_0}\mathbb Z$, let families $G_1,\dots,G_s$ lie in $\{\hat c<x_\mu<\hat c+\frac\ell4\}$ and tuples $f_1,\dots,f_s$ of real Lipschitz functions, each tuple with pairwise disjoint supports, have their supports in $\{\hat c+\frac\ell4<x_\mu<\hat c+\frac\ell2\}$, all at positive distance from the planes $x_\mu\in\hat c+\frac\ell4\mathbb Z$, and let $2[\kappa(G_i)+\kappa(G_j)]<\frac12$ for all $i$, $j$; then each entry $\mathcal W(\theta'G_i,G_j;\theta'f_i,f_j)$ is a limit of the kind above, the coordinate mirror with the place $\hat c+\frac\ell4$, which lies in $\frac12a_{i_0}\mathbb Z$ as $\frac\ell4=\frac12L^m$, parting the family $(\theta'G_i,G_j)$ from the supports of $\theta'f_i$ and $f_j$, and $\sum_{i,j}\bar c_ic_j\mathcal W(\theta'G_i,G_j;\theta'f_i,f_j)\ge0$ for all complex $c_1,\dots,c_s$.
\item[(7)] \emph{The action density beside a loop.} Let $C$ be a polygon with $\psi=\langle W_C\rangle_K>0$ (every coordinate rectangle has it), $f$ bounded and real, and $\theta$ a site mirror with $C$ in one open half torus and every plaquette $p$ with $f(x(p))\ne0$ with its bonds in the other closed half $S$. Write $\langle X;Y\rangle_K=\langle XY\rangle_K-\langle X\rangle_K\langle Y\rangle_K$. At every cutoff, for every bounded real Borel function $H_0$ of the bonds of $S$ and $H=\mathcal O(f)-H_0$: $\langle W_C;W_{\theta C}\rangle_K\ge0$, $\langle\theta H;H\rangle_K\ge0$, and
\[\Bigl|\frac{\langle W_C;\mathcal O(f)\rangle_K}\psi-\frac{\langle W_C;H_0\rangle_K}\psi\Bigr|\le\Bigl[\frac{\langle W_CW_{\theta C}\rangle_K}{\psi^2}-1\Bigr]^{1/2}\langle\theta H;H\rangle_K^{1/2};\]
at $H_0=0$ the left side is $|\langle W_C\mathcal O(f)\rangle_K/\psi-\langle\mathcal O(f)\rangle_K|$. Let moreover, in the frame, $g\le\gamma_W$, the ceiling of equation~\YMMref{(2346)}{850}; let $\vartheta_{\rm sh}\in(0,1)$ be a shape parameter, $\mathsf d\in(0,\mathsf d_0]$ with the threshold $\mathsf d_0=\mathsf d_0(g,\vartheta_{\rm sh})\in(0,\frac1{200}]$ of equation~\YMMref{(2350)}{851}, and $K-s(\mathsf d)\ge1$, $s(\mathsf d)$ the witness depth at $g$ of equation~\YMMref{(2321)}{843}; and let $(\theta f,f)$ be a test pair of the class $\mathfrak T_{T_\ell}(\mathsf d;\vartheta_{\rm sh})$ of {\cite[Lem.~I.1]{YMM2}}, on a torus with $20\mathsf d\le\ell$: $f$ is non-negative, Lipschitz and not $\equiv0$, the supports of $\theta f$ and $f$ lie in closed balls of radius $\mathsf d$ and are at a distance in $[\mathsf d,6\mathsf d]$, $\int f\ge\vartheta_{\rm sh}\|f\|_\infty\mathsf d^3$ and ${\rm Lip}\,f\le\|f\|_\infty/\vartheta_{\rm sh}\mathsf d$.

As $(K,L^K\mathsf b)$ is a first-passage datum at $g$ with the label $\mathsf b\in\mathsf I(g)$ (Cor.~\YMMref{74.2}{616}), on the side $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$ of the frame, the law of the truncated two-point function of the action density, Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AV}{851}}, gives $\langle\theta\mathcal O(f);\mathcal O(f)\rangle_K=\mathsf c_2\mathsf b^{-2}\int\!\!\int f(\theta x)f(y)|x-y|^{-6}\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y\,(1+\epsilon')$, with $\mathsf c_2=\frac9{16\pi^2}$ the constant of \YMMref{C}{7}, the double integral the free kernel \YMMref{(2240)}{822} of the test pair, and $|\epsilon'|\le\epsilon_{\rm tp}:=\bar\varepsilon_{g,\vartheta_{\rm sh}}(\mathsf d)$, the tolerance of equation~\YMMref{(2349)}{851}, which is at most $\frac13$ in that theorem; with the bound above and $\mathsf c_2^{1/2}=\frac3{4\pi}$ this gives
\[\Bigl|\frac{\langle W_C\mathcal O(f)\rangle_K}\psi-\langle\mathcal O(f)\rangle_K\Bigr|\le\frac3{4\pi\mathsf b}\Bigl[(1+\epsilon_{\rm tp})\int\!\!\int\frac{|f(\theta x)f(y)|}{|x-y|^6}\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y\Bigr]^{1/2}\Bigl[\frac{\langle W_CW_{\theta C}\rangle_K}{\psi^2}-1\Bigr]^{1/2};\]
and, as the free kernel of a test pair is at most $(\frac{4\pi}3)^2\|f\|_\infty^2$ (equation~\YMMref{(2247)}{824}; two balls of radius $\mathsf d$ at a distance $\ge\mathsf d$), the same two-point estimate gives on this whole class $\langle\theta\mathcal O(f);\mathcal O(f)\rangle_K\le\frac43(\frac{4\pi}3)^2\mathsf c_2\mathsf b^{-2}\|f\|_\infty^2=\frac43\mathsf b^{-2}\|f\|_\infty^2$, so that, with no condition beyond this class,
\[\Bigl|\frac{\langle W_C\mathcal O(f)\rangle_K}\psi-\langle\mathcal O(f)\rangle_K\Bigr|\le\frac2{\sqrt3}\,\mathsf b^{-1}\|f\|_\infty\Bigl[\frac{\langle W_CW_{\theta C}\rangle_K}{\psi^2}-1\Bigr]^{1/2}.\]
Besides, at every cutoff,
\[
\begin{multlined}
\frac{\langle W_C\mathcal O(f)\rangle_K}\psi-\langle\mathcal O(f)\rangle_K=-\frac1{a_K}\sum_pf(x(p))\langle W_{\partial p}\rangle_K\Bigl[\frac{\langle W_CW_{\partial p}\rangle_K}{\psi\langle W_{\partial p}\rangle_K}-1\Bigr], \\
\frac d{d\mathsf b}\log\langle W_C\rangle_K=-\Bigl[\frac{\langle W_C\mathcal O(1)\rangle_K}\psi-\langle\mathcal O(1)\rangle_K\Bigr].
\end{multlined}
\]
For a rectangle with $2\kappa<\frac12$ at positive distance from the planes of $\theta$ and Lipschitz $f$ with support at positive distance from them, $\langle W_C;\mathcal O(f)\rangle_K/\psi=\mathcal W_K(C;f)/\mathcal W_K(C)$, $\langle W_CW_{\theta C}\rangle_K/\psi^2=\mathcal W_K(C,\theta C)/\mathcal W_K(C)^2$ and $\langle\theta\mathcal O(f);\mathcal O(f)\rangle_K=S^{\sf T}_{2,K}(\theta f,f)$ converge as $K\to\infty$.
\item[(8)] \emph{Short distances.} Let $0<\vartheta<\frac12$ and $p\ge1$. (a) For rectangles $C_i=n_1a_i\times n_2a_i$ with corners in $\Lambda_i$, $n_1$, $n_2$ fixed, $\varrho_i=\max\{n_1,n_2\}a_i$, $\mathsf n=\max\{L,n_1,n_2\}$, all large $i$ and all $K>i$ with $\Delta_i\le\frac12$,
\[\Bigl|\log\mathcal W_K(C_i)+\frac3{2\mathsf b}\bigl[c_{\rm lat}|C_i|+\mathcal J_\ell(C_i)+E_{a_K}(C_i)\bigr]\Bigr|\le\kappa\log L+c\frac{|C_i|}{\mathsf b}+2\Delta_i,\]
\[\Delta_i=4B_3^2A_0^2\mathsf n^3\frac{\varrho_i}{\mathsf b}\Bigl(1+\log\frac{\mathsf n\mathsf b}{\varrho_i}\Bigr)^{2\mathfrak p_0}+C_1\frac{|C_i|}{\mathsf b}\Bigl(\frac{\varrho_i}{\mathsf b}\Bigr)^{\vartheta/2}+C_3\mathsf V_\ell C_{\rm r}(p)\varrho_i^{p-1/2},\]
$E_a$ the remainder of Prop.~\ref{C-372-11}(a) and $c$, $C_1$, $C_3$ depending on the constants, $\vartheta$, $n_1$, $n_2$ and $\mathsf J$: an error of the order of the main term, which gives the two-sided bound of (4) at these rectangles. (b) For rectangles $C$ with sides in $[c_0\varrho,10\varrho]$ and corners in $\Lambda_i$, $i$ the integer with $a_i\le\frac12c_0\varrho<La_i$, put $a_*=\varrho(\mathsf b/\varrho)^{\vartheta/(3+\vartheta)}$, a length coarser than the loop. At every level $t$ with $a_{K-t}\le a_*$ the mean over the block field of the defect of one step, $\bar{\mathsf D}_{t+1}$ of Prop.~\ref{C-372-12}(b) for $C$, has modulus at most $C_*\frac\varrho{\mathsf b}(\frac{a_{K-t}}{\mathsf b})^\vartheta$, $C_*$ depending on the constants, $c_0$, $\vartheta$ and $\mathsf J$ alone: at the levels finer than the corners, $K-t>s_0=\max\{i,s'_0\}$, by Prop.~\ref{C-372-10}(b), and at the levels with $a_i\le a_{K-t}\le a_*$, about $\frac\vartheta{3+\vartheta}\log_L\frac{\mathsf b}\varrho$ of them, where the loop passes a number of the cubes of the level that is bounded in terms of $L$ and $c_0$, by the argument of one step with this bounded number of segments. Hence, as $\varrho\to0$, with a constant depending on the constants, $c_0$, $\vartheta$, $\mathsf J$ and $\ell$,
\[\log\mathcal W(C)=-\frac3{2\mathsf b}\bigl[\mathcal J(C)+c_{\rm lat}|C|\bigr]+O\Bigl(\Bigl(\frac\varrho{\mathsf b}\Bigr)^{1+\frac{3\vartheta}{3+\vartheta}}\Bigl(1+\log\frac{\mathsf b}\varrho\Bigr)^{2\mathfrak p_0}+\frac{\varrho^4}{\mathsf b\,\ell^3}\Bigr);\]
the exponent $1+\frac{3\vartheta}{3+\vartheta}$ reaches $\frac{10}7$ as $\vartheta\to\frac12$, the length $a_*$ balancing the step errors, $\frac\varrho{\mathsf b}(\frac{a_*}{\mathsf b})^\vartheta$, against the last level, $\frac{\varrho^4}{\mathsf ba_*^3}$, and the remainder, which holds $\log(\mathsf b/\varrho)$ and not $\log\varrho$, is invariant under dilations.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Without the renormalisation group]\label{C-372-6}
Let $C$ be a coordinate rectangle on a torus of side $\ell$, $\mathsf b>0$, $a$ the spacing, $\beta=\mathsf b/a\ge e^3$, $\Lambda=\max\{1,|C|/\mathsf b\}$, $\rho=\lfloor(\frac{\beta}{\Lambda\log^3\beta})^{1/4}\rfloor\ge2$, the sides of $C$ at least $(4\rho+1)a$, and the points within $(\rho+1)a$ of $C$ in a cube of side $\le\frac\ell2$. Then
\[|\langle W_C\rangle|\le6e^{3.1\mathsf b/\ell}\,1.58^{|C|/\mathsf b}\Bigl[\Lambda\frac a{\mathsf b}\log^3\frac{\mathsf b}a\Bigr]^{k|C|/4\mathsf b}.\]
With a dyadic $\rho=2^S$ instead, sides at least $(4\rho+1)a$ and $k|C|/\mathsf b<3$, the ceiling of the tube with the profiles of the scales $2,4,\dots,2^S$ reads
\[|\langle W_C\rangle|\le e^{\delta_0+2.2144k|C|/\mathsf b}\rho^{-k|C|/\mathsf b}\Bigl[1+\frac{72\,\bar a\,\rho^3\log^2\rho}{2^{3-k|C|/\mathsf b}-1}\Bigr]+35\,\bar a,\qquad\delta_0=\frac{16k\rho\log\rho+k^2(|C|/\mathsf b)\log^2\rho}\beta,\]
with the plaquette mean $\bar a=\langle a_p\rangle\le\beta^{-1}\log\mathfrak M_\nu$ (Lem.~\ref{C-372-17}(f)), the condition $k|C|/\mathsf b<3$ keeping the denominator positive; at $\rho\in(\frac12\beta^{1/3},\beta^{1/3}]$, where $\bar a\rho^3\log^2\rho$ is at most a multiple of $\log^3\beta$, and $\beta\ge\beta_2$, a threshold depending on $k|C|/\mathsf b$ alone (the term $192\frac{\mathsf b}\ell$ of $\log\mathfrak M_\nu$ is at most $384\mathsf b/|C|$, as $|C|<2\ell$): $|\langle W_C\rangle|\le C(\frac{k|C|}{\mathsf b})(\frac a{\mathsf b})^{|C|/4\pi\mathsf b}\log^3\frac{\mathsf b}a$, as $\rho^{-k|C|/\mathsf b}\le2^{k|C|/\mathsf b}(\frac a{\mathsf b})^{k|C|/3\mathsf b}$ and $\frac k3=\frac1{4\pi}$. The first bound holds in the same form, with a constant depending also on the number of pieces, for polygons whose pieces have at least $4\rho+1$ steps and whose pieces without a common corner are at sup-distance at least $(2\rho+1)a$, for families of such polygons in which also any two pieces of different polygons are at sup-distance at least $(2\rho+1)a$, also with a further factor $G$, $|G|\le1$, a Borel function of the bonds farther than $\rho a$ from the polygons; and for the characters $\chi_j$ of spin $j$, with $\kappa_j=\frac43j(j+1)\le20\log\beta$ and $A=6e^{3.1\mathsf b/\ell}$:
\[|\langle\chi_j(U(C))\rangle|\le(2j+1)\bigl(A\,1.58^{|C|/\mathsf b}\bigr)^{\kappa_j}e^{\kappa_j^2/100}\Bigl[\Lambda\frac a{\mathsf b}\log^3\frac{\mathsf b}a\Bigr]^{\kappa_jk|C|/4\mathsf b}.\]
These bounds hold with $3$ in the place of $6e^{3.1\mathsf b/\ell}$ for every periodic Gibbs state of the Wilson action at $\beta$ on $\mathbb Z^3$ that is invariant under the isometries of $\mathbb Z^3$ and reflection positive in the lattice planes. So, as $a\to0$ with $\mathsf b$ in a compact set, uniformly in $\ell\ge\ell_0$, for polygons: $\langle h(W_C)\rangle\to\sigma(h)=\frac2\pi\int_{-1}^1h(w)\sqrt{1-w^2}\,\mathrm{d}w$ for continuous $h$, $\langle W_C^2\rangle\to\frac14$, and for polygons $C_i$ at pairwise positive distances, continuous $h_i$ and Borel $G$, $|G|\le1$, depending only on the bonds at distance $\ge\delta>0$ from them, $\langle\prod_ih_i(W_{C_i})\,G\rangle-\prod_i\sigma(h_i)\langle G\rangle\to0$.

For a coordinate rectangle, whose mean $\langle W_C\rangle$ is positive (Prop.~\ref{C-372-13}(c)), the normalised sharp loop has the variance $\mathrm{Var}(W_C/\langle W_C\rangle)=(1+\langle\chi_1(U(C))\rangle)/(4\langle W_C\rangle^2)-1$, which tends to infinity as $a\to0$, at least like a positive constant times $[\Lambda\frac a{\mathsf b}\log^3\frac{\mathsf b}a]^{-k|C|/2\mathsf b}$; and no multiple $c_aW_C$ of the sharp loop has both a limit law and a mean $c_a\langle W_C\rangle$ that stays away from $0$. In the other direction, $\langle W_C\rangle\ge\langle W_{\partial p}\rangle^{A_C/a^2}\ge\exp[-\frac32\frac{A_C}{a\mathsf b}(192\frac{\mathsf b}\ell+56.6+12\log\beta)]$ for a rectangle of area $A_C$ and sides $<\ell/2$, the second inequality when $192\frac{\mathsf b}\ell+56.6+12\log\beta\le\frac\beta2$; for the Gibbs states above and rectangles with even numbers of steps, $\langle W_C\rangle\ge\exp[-\frac{A_C}{a\mathsf b}(43+9\log\frac{\mathsf b}a)]$ when $28.3+6\log\beta\le\frac\beta2$.

Without the renormalisation group the floor falls like the exponential of the area in units of $a\mathsf b$.
\end{theorem}

the bound on the history without large-field regions (Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{115.2}{806}}, \YMMref{(2187)}{806}); the rarity of large-field regions (Prop.~\ref{prop:ward-fixed-volume-rarity}); the bound at one place at the fixed and at the lowered constants (Lem.~\ref{lem:rarity-chessboard}, Def.~\ref{def:rarity-choices}); the covariance of the block averages and of the backgrounds under the lattice isometries ({\cite[\S{}G.1]{YMM2}}, {\cite[Lem.~G.1]{YMM2}}); for one step, the triples, the analyticity cores, the chart at the trivial pair and the ball about the trivial triple in the core (\S\ref{sec:analytic-core-complements}, Def.~\YMMref{49.1}{374}, and equation~\YMMref{(933)}{427}), the background triple and its regularity (the triple defined before equation~\YMMref{(827)}{395} and \S\ref{sec:normalized-step-measure}), the kernel of one step (\eqref{eq:normalized-step-measure} and Prop.~\ref{prop:normalized-step-kernel}), the provision of the step on the whole core (Def.~\YMMref{52.1}{415}, Thm.~\YMMref{W}{423}), the shift of Prop.~\YMMref{51.5}{396} with their brackets (equations~\YMMref{(806)}{392}--\YMMref{(809)}{392} and Lem.~\ref{lem:analytic-rooted-bracket}), the chart and the pivot values at $t=0$ (equation~\YMMref{(804)}{391} and the bounds and covariance proved with it), the potential on a cube of any side (Thm.~\YMMref{F}{199}), the cluster expansion of the step with up to four potential
families (Thm.~\YMMref{R}{361}, Cor.~\YMMref{47.3}{364}
and Prop.~\YMMref{47.4}{365}, with the following covariance
argument), applied to the actual Gaussian structure and the two
potentials of Prop.~\ref{prop:normalized-step-kernel}, the constrained variational equation for critical curves at
the trivial field (the proof of Lem.~\YMMref{124.1}{832}, through
its gauge normalization), and its curvature identification
(equation~\YMMref{(2230)}{819}), the curvature response (the curvature-response construction preceding Lem.~\YMMref{120.2}{819}, the curvature-response calculation preceding Lem.~\YMMref{120.2}{819}), the slice of the free Coulomb energy at the trivial triple (Prop.~\YMMref{120.3}{819}, Prop.~\YMMref{120.3}{819}) and the linearised shift system (Lem.~\YMMref{124.3}{835}, whose proof, with the two changes named in the proof of Prop.~\ref{C-372-10}(a), runs for the objects of the frame on every side of $\mathfrak L(g)$); and the limits of the truncated functions of the action density \YMMref{(2212)}{813}.

Thms.~\YMMref{AJ}{673} and~\YMMref{AD}{607}, the bound for a history with a source on a polydisc uniformly in $K$, is used in this section only in Prop.~\ref{C-372-14}, hence in Thm.~\ref{C-372-4}(6) and in the convergence of the three quantities of Thm.~\ref{C-372-4}(7); the explicit ceiling of Thm.~\ref{C-372-4}(7) uses besides the law of the truncated two-point function of the action density, Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AV}{851}}, with its test pairs ({\cite[Lem.~I.1]{YMM2}}), the free kernel \YMMref{(2240)}{822} and its bound on a test pair (equation~\YMMref{(2247)}{824}), the constant $\mathsf c_2$ \YMMref{C}{7}, its ceiling $\gamma_W$ equation~\YMMref{(2346)}{850}, its threshold $\mathsf d_0$ equation~\YMMref{(2350)}{851}, its witness depth $s(\mathsf d)$ in equation~\YMMref{(2321)}{843} and its tolerance equation~\YMMref{(2349)}{851}, and the first-passage data (Cor.~\YMMref{74.2}{616}).

The facts on the constants (Prop.~\YMMref{69.1}{595}, the calibration in \S\ref{sec:cutoff-calibration}, and {\cite[Cor.~B.13]{YMM2}}) make fixed constants satisfy the conditions of the setting. Besides these we use standard facts: reflection positivity of the Wilson measure on the torus at site and bond mirrors, the chessboard estimate, Kolmogorov's extension theorem, Vitali's theorem, Schwarz's lemma and Cauchy's estimates. In Thm.~\ref{C-372-3}(1)--(5) and in Props.~\ref{C-372-8} and~\ref{C-372-9}(a)--(d) one torus and one label are fixed, and the limit is $K\to\infty$, with the limit $n\to\infty$ of the tower inside it; in the frame the numbers of the rate of Prop.~\ref{C-372-9}(d) serve all the labels of $\mathsf J$.

Thm.~\ref{C-372-4} takes besides the limit $d\to\infty$ of means after $K\to\infty$ ((2), (5)), lets the label move in a compact set $\mathsf J$ and along labels $\mathsf b_K\to\mathsf b$ ((2)), lets rectangles shrink, $i\to\infty$ and $\varrho\to0$ ((4), (8)), and moves the torus and the label together by dilations ((3), as Thm.~\ref{C-372-3}(6) does). Thm.~\ref{C-372-6} takes $a\to0$ uniformly in $\ell\ge\ell_0$ with $\mathsf b$ in a compact set, and holds also for periodic Gibbs states on $\mathbb Z^3$. In Thms.~\ref{C-372-3} and~\ref{C-372-4} the side $\ell$ of the torus is fixed, or moves together with the label, by dilations.

\subsubsection{Auxiliary estimates}

\begin{lemma}\label{C-372-7}
Let $L\ge2$, $m'\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$, $r,m\in\mathbb N$, $M=L^{m'}$, $\mathsf b$ real with $\log\mathsf b>1$, and $Q(\mathsf b)=\min\{L^j:j\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0},\ L^j\ge(\log\mathsf b)^r\}$. Then $M\,Q(\mathsf b)\le L^m$ if and only if $L^m\ge M(\log\mathsf b)^r$. The hypothesis $\log\mathsf b>1$ is needed: at $L=3$, $m'=2$, $m=1$, $r=2$, $\mathsf b=1.2$ the second condition holds and the first fails. In the setting it holds since $\gamma\le\frac12$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof]
$Q\ge(\log\mathsf b)^r$ gives $M(\log\mathsf b)^r\le MQ\le L^m$. Conversely $L^{m-m'}\ge(\log\mathsf b)^r>1$, so $j=m-m'$ is a positive integer, $L^j$ lies in the set whose least element is $Q$, and $Q\le L^{m-m'}$. In the example $(\log1.2)^2=0.033\ldots$, so $Q=1$ and $MQ=9>3=L^m\ge9\cdot0.033$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Laws on the threads; small plaquettes]\label{C-372-8}
In the one-torus setting:
(a) there is exactly one Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathcal X$ whose image under $V_\bullet\mapsto(V_0,\dots,V_D)$ is, for every $D$, the image of $\mu_D$ under $V\mapsto(\mathcal M^DV,\dots,\mathcal MV,V)$; $\mu(\mathsf{Thr})=1$, the image of $\mu$ under $\pi_d$ is $\mu_d$, $\mu$ is $\theta_v$-invariant, and the law of $(\mathcal M^KU,\dots,\mathcal M^{K-D}U)$ under $\langle\cdot\rangle_K$ tends in total variation to the image of $\mu$ under $(\pi_0,\dots,\pi_D)$;
(b) each $I_d$ is open and gauge invariant; for $d\ge d_\natural$ and $K>d$, $\mu^K_d(\mathcal V_d\setminus I_d)\le R_d$ and $\mu_d(\mathcal V_d\setminus I_d)\le R_d$; for $D\ge d_\natural$, $\mu(\tau_0>D)\le\sum_{d\ge D}R_d$, which is at most $\frac L{L-1}R_D$ if $c'A_0^2\log x_{[D]}\ge2$; and $R_d$ tends to $0$ faster than every $L^{-pd}$;
(c) for $d\ge s_\natural$, $K>d$ and every set $S$ of sites of $\Lambda_d$, the $\mu^K_d$- and the $\mu_d$-probability that some plaquette with a corner in $S$ has $|\partial V(p)-\mathbf 1|\ge2\varepsilon_{[d]}$ are at most $\#S\,e^{-c^\natural A_0^2(\log x_{[d]})^{2\mathfrak p_0}}$;
(d) with the constants $C_5,\mathsf C_{\rm maj}\ge0$ of Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8}, $s_d=\frac14\min\{\bar\varepsilon,B_3^{-1}\varepsilon_{[d]}\}$,
\[
\begin{multlined}
\mathsf p^{[d]}=\exp\bigl[-(c_{\rm low}+\tfrac92\log x_{[d]}+\mathsf C_{\rm maj}+2)(\ell L^d)^3\bigr],\qquad\mathsf q^{[d]}=\exp\Bigl[-\Bigl(C_5+\mathsf C_{\rm maj}+2+3\log\frac7{s_d^3} \\
+24B_3^2s_d^2x_{[d]}\Bigr)(\ell L^d)^3\Bigr],
\end{multlined}
\]
one has at every admitted depth $d$ and for $K\ge\max\{2,d+1\}$: $\mu^K_d(J_d)\ge\mu^K_d(I_d)\ge\mathsf q^{[d]}>0$, and $\mu^K_d(I_d)\ge\max\{1-R_d,\mathsf p^{[d]},\mathsf q^{[d]}\}$ if $d\ge1$; the same holds for $\mu_d$. The floors hold no $K$ and fall like $e^{-c(\ell L^d)^3}$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof]
(a) By one block map, $\mu_{d+1}\circ\mathcal M^{-1}=\mu_d$ (Cor.~\textup{\ref{IV-62-66}}(c)), so the images of the $\mu_D$ form a projective family of Borel probabilities on the finite products of the compact metric spaces $\mathcal V_d$, which has exactly one extension to $\mathcal X$ (Kolmogorov's theorem). Each marginal is carried by the Borel set $\{V_d=\mathcal MV_{d+1},\ d<D\}$, whence $\mu(\mathsf{Thr})=1$; gauge invariance of the $\mu_d$ and covariance of $\mathcal M$ give the invariance; the joint law at the cutoff $K$ is the image of the single law $\mu^K_D$ under $V\mapsto(\mathcal M^DV,\dots,V)$, and $\mu^K_D\to\mu_D$ in total variation. (b) $\varpi$ is continuous and $\varpi(V^v)=\varpi(V)$.

Here Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8} is applied along the line of couplings $x_{[d']}=L^{d'}\mathsf b$, $0\le d'\le K$ (the run with all $u_t=0$, at the label $\mathsf b$), with the inner ball $I_{d'}=\{\varpi<2\varepsilon_{[d']}\}$ at the depth $d'$: the partition function is a sum over the histories of large-field regions, and the small-field chain of this line (Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{115.2}{806}}), which at the depths $d'>d$ cuts the fields at the radii $c_\rho\varepsilon_{[d']}$, measured on their backgrounds (the definitions preceding Lem.~\YMMref{113.10}{796}), is a bounded Borel weight $\mathfrak w\ge0$ on the bare fields with three properties: the image of $\mathfrak w\,e^{-\beta\sum_pa_p}dU$ under $\mathcal M^{K-d}$ is carried by $I_d$ (clause (a) there); $\int F(1-\mathfrak w)e^{-\beta\sum_pa_p}\,\mathrm{d}U\ge0$ for every gauge invariant bounded Borel $F\ge0$ (clause (b), which places $\mathfrak w$ between the history without large-field regions and the full density); and $\int(1-\mathfrak w)e^{-\beta\sum_pa_p}\,\mathrm{d}U\le R_dZ$, $R_d$ being \YMMref{(2187)}{806} at the depth $d$ and the label $\mathsf b$ (clause (c)).

As $I_d$ is gauge invariant, $\mu^K_d(\mathcal V_d\setminus I_d)=Z^{-1}\int\mathbf 1_{\mathcal V_d\setminus I_d}(\mathcal M^{K-d}U)(1-\mathfrak w)e^{-\beta\sum_pa_p}\,\mathrm{d}U\le R_d$, uniformly in $K$. This chain of the line is another object than the measures $m_t$ of the frame, which follow the run, with $|x_{K-d}-x_{[d]}|\le\bar B$ and the thresholds $2\varepsilon(x_t)$: the tame set $\mathsf O_{K-d}$ that carries $m_{K-d}$ is placed by Prop.~\ref{C-372-9}(e) in the larger ball $J'_d$. The bound for $\mu^K_d$ passes to $\mu_d$ in total variation. For $D\ge d_\natural$, $\{\tau_0>D\}=\bigcup_{d\ge D}\pi_d^{-1}(\mathcal V_d\setminus I_d)$, and the image of $\mu$ under $\pi_d$ is $\mu_d$ by (a); countable subadditivity gives $\mu(\tau_0>D)\le\sum_{d\ge D}R_d$.

As $(y+\log L)^{2\mathfrak p_0}-y^{2\mathfrak p_0}\ge2y\log L$ for $y\ge1$, and $\log x_{[d]}\ge\log\mathsf b>1$, $R_{d+1}/R_d\le L^{3-2c'A_0^2\log x_{[d]}}$, which is at most $L^{-1}$ for all $d\ge D$ if $c'A_0^2\log x_{[D]}\ge2$; then $\sum_{d\ge D}R_d\le\frac L{L-1}R_D$. $R_d$ falls faster than every $L^{-pd}$ because $(\log x_{[d]})^{2\mathfrak p_0}\ge(d\log L)^2$. (c) One witness function of a large plaquette at one place has a mean at most $e^{-c^\natural A_0^2(\log x_{[d]})^{2\mathfrak p_0}}$, free of the volume: Lem.~\ref{lem:rarity-chessboard}, which applies Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8} at the fixed constants and at the lowered choice and frees the bound of the volume by the chessboard estimate for the reflection positive Wilson measure.

Sum over the corners in $S$; the bound passes to $\mu_d$ in total variation. (d) For $\mathsf p^{[d]}$: Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8}, along the line of couplings of (b), bounds, at the level of $\Lambda_d$, the mass of the history without large-field regions below by $e^{E}e^{-(c_{\rm low}+\frac92\log x_{[d]})(\ell L^d)^3}$ and the partition function above by $e^{E}e^{(\mathsf C_{\rm maj}+2)(\ell L^d)^3}$, with one number $E$, and that history is carried by fields whose block field of the depth $d$ lies in the inner ball $I_d$ of the line. For $\mathsf q^{[d]}$: Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8} along the line bounds the density of the block field of the depth $d$ below, as a measure, by $e^{E-C_5(\ell L^d)^3}$ times the small-field indicator times the Boltzmann factor of the background over $V$; on the ball of the fields with $|V(b)-\mathbf 1|<s_d$ at every bond, whose plaquettes are $<4s_d\le\varepsilon_{[d]}$ so that it lies in $I_d$, the integral of this density is at least $\exp[-(3\log\frac7{s_d^3}+24B_3^2s_d^2x_{[d]})(\ell L^d)^3]$; with the upper bound on the partition function this gives $\mathsf q^{[d]}$.

The floors hold no $K$; let $K\to\infty$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Two consecutive cutoffs over one block field; the Lipschitz bound of the tower]\label{C-372-31}
In the one-torus setting put $\varepsilon_{\rm r}(s)=2c_\rho\varepsilon_{[s]}$; for two fields $V$, $V'$ on one lattice put ${\rm dist}(V,V')=\max_b\theta(V(b)V'(b)^{-1})$, $\theta(X)\in[0,\pi]$ the angle of $X\in G$, $\cos\theta(X)=\frac12\operatorname{tr}X$; for a real $1$-form $B$ on the bonds of a lattice (its values $B(b)$ hermitian and traceless, $B(\bar b)=-B(b)$) put $\sup|B|=\max_b|B(b)|$ and $(e^{iB}X')(b)=e^{iB(b)}X'(b)$ at the positively oriented bonds $b$. With the chart constant $C_{\rm db}=8L^3$ and the constant $\gamma_{\rm r}\in(0,1]$ of the lower bound on the excess of a competitor (the global hypotheses preceding equation~\YMMref{(2132)}{790}, Prop.~\YMMref{113.5}{792}), the constant $\mathsf K_u$ of the comparison of the background actions at two consecutive cutoffs (equation~\YMMref{(2155)}{795}, \YMMref{(2154)}{795}), the numbers $\varepsilon_{\rm cp}$, $\varrho_{\rm no}=\min\{r_{\rm B},\varrho^0_{\rm R}\}$ and $\mathsf S_{\rm e}$ of the definitions preceding and in equation~\YMMref{(2133)}{790}, the radius $c_4\in(0,1]$ and the positive curvature ceiling $c'_2=c^{\rm g}_2$ of Lem.~\ref{C-368-7}(v), decreasing $c_4$ to $1$ if necessary, and the constant $B^{\rm e}_5\ge8$ of the response of the background to a change of its datum (\S\ref{sec:background-step-complements}), we put
\[
\begin{multlined}
\mathsf c_{\rm A}=16\,C_{\rm db}\,c_\rho\,(\mathsf K_u/\gamma_{\rm r})^{1/2},\qquad a_s(K)=\mathsf c_{\rm A}\,\varepsilon_{[s]}\,(\ell L^s)^{3/2}L^{-(K-s+1)/2},\qquad r_s(K) \\
=\sum_{K'\ge K}a_s(K')=\frac{a_s(K)}{1-L^{-1/2}}=r_s(s)L^{-(K-s)/2},
\end{multlined}
\]
\[\varepsilon_{\rm L}=\min\{\varepsilon_{\rm cp},\,c'_2/B_3\},\qquad\beta_{\rm L}=\min\Bigl\{1,\ \tfrac12\varrho_{\rm no},\ \frac{c_4}{2B^{\rm e}_5\mathsf S_{\rm e}}\Bigr\},\qquad\mathsf c_9=\frac{2L}{L^{1/2}-1}\,B^{\rm e}_5\mathsf S_{\rm e};\]
$\mathsf c_{\rm A}$, $\varepsilon_{\rm L}$, $\beta_{\rm L}$ and $\mathsf c_9$ depend on the constants alone, $a_s(\cdot)$ decreases, and $\varepsilon_{\rm r}(s)\le\varepsilon_{\rm L}$ at every admitted depth $s$, by the conditions of the comparison of two consecutive cutoffs that define $\Theta_\star$.
(a) \emph{One depth.} Let $s$ be admitted, $K\ge\max\{2,s+1\}$ and $X\in\mathcal V_s$ with $\varpi(X)<\varepsilon_{\rm r}(s)$. Then $H^K_s(X)$ and $H^{K+1}_s(X)$ are defined; each is in the axial gauge on $\Lambda_s$, has the average $X$ and has plaquettes at most $2B_3L^{-2}\varpi(X)$; and
\[{\rm dist}\bigl(H^{K+1}_s(X),H^K_s(X)\bigr)\le a_s(K).\]
Hence $H^\infty_s(X)=\lim_KH^K_s(X)$ exists, ${\rm dist}(H^\infty_s(X),H^K_s(X))\le r_s(K)$ uniformly on $\{\varpi<\varepsilon_{\rm r}(s)\}$, $H^\infty_s$ is continuous there, $\mathcal MH^\infty_s(X)=X$, $\varpi(H^\infty_s(X))\le2B_3L^{-2}\varpi(X)$, and $H^\infty_s(X^u)=H^\infty_s(X)^{u\circ\pi}$ for every gauge transformation $u$ of $\Lambda_s$, $\pi$ mapping each site of $\Lambda_{s+1}$ to the site of $\Lambda_s$ whose block holds it.
(b) \emph{Along the tower.} Let $d$ be admitted, $K\ge\max\{2,d+1\}$, $W\in J_d$, and $Y_j=H^{K+1}_{d,j}(W)$, $0\le j\le K+1-d$, the tower over $W$ at the cutoff $K+1$. Then for $0\le j<K-d$
\[{\rm dist}\bigl(Y_{j+1},H^K_{d+j}(Y_j)\bigr)\le L^{-j/2}a_d(K),\]
whereas (a) at the depth $d+j$ gives the number $a_{d+j}(K)=(\varepsilon_{[d+j]}/\varepsilon_{[d]})L^{2j}a_d(K)$, up to $L^{2j}a_d(K)$.
(c) \emph{The Lipschitz bound in the block field.} Let $K\ge2$, $d'<K$, $X'\in\mathcal V_{d'}$ with $\varpi(X')<\varepsilon_{\rm L}$, $B$ a real $1$-form on the bonds of $\Lambda_{d'}$ with $\sup|B|\le\beta_{\rm L}$, and $X=e^{iB}X'$. Then $\mathcal C_K(X')$ and $\mathcal C_K(X)$ are non-empty, each one orbit of $\mathcal G^{d'}_K$, and for $U'\in\mathcal C_K(X')$, $U\in\mathcal C_K(X)$, every depth $d''$ with $d'\le d''\le K$ and every closed path $\Gamma$ of $\Lambda_{d''}$ with $N$ bonds
\[\Bigl|\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(\mathcal M^{K-d''}U)(\Gamma)-\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(\mathcal M^{K-d''}U')(\Gamma)\Bigr|\le2B^{\rm e}_5\mathsf S_{\rm e}\,N\,L^{-(d''-d')}\sup|B|;\]
the constant holds neither $K$, nor $d'$, nor the number $d''-d'$ of the depths between.
(d) \emph{Two consecutive cutoffs: the loops at the depth $d+n$.} Let $d$ be admitted, $n\ge1$, $K\ge\max\{2,d+n+1\}$ with $a_d(K)\le\beta_{\rm L}$, $W\in J_d$, $\Gamma$ a closed path of $\Lambda_{d+n}$ with $N$ bonds and $W_\Gamma(V)=\frac12\operatorname{tr}V(\Gamma)$. Then
\[
\begin{multlined}
\bigl|W_\Gamma(H^{K+1}_{d,n}W)-W_\Gamma(H^K_{d,n}W)\bigr|\le\mathsf c_9\,N\,L^{-n/2}a_d(K),\qquad\bigl|W_\Gamma(H^\infty_{d,n}W)-W_\Gamma(H^K_{d,n}W)\bigr| \\
\le\mathsf c_9\,N\,L^{-n/2}r_d(K),
\end{multlined}
\]
$H^\infty_{d,n}W$ being the limit of the towers $H^K_{d,n}W$ (Prop.~\ref{C-372-9}(a)).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof]
(a) Let $t=K-s$ and $\tilde U$ a background over $X$ at the cutoff $K+1$ (it exists by Thm.~\YMMref{E}{10} in the setting of Section~\YMMref{52.7}{432}, as $\varepsilon_{\rm r}(s)\le\bar\varepsilon$). Its average $U'=\mathcal M\tilde U$, a field of the bare lattice of the cutoff $K$ with $\mathcal M^tU'=X$, is a competitor there (Lem.~\YMMref{113.8}{794}): its action, in the units of the level $t$, exceeds the action of the backgrounds over $X$ at the cutoff $K$ by at most $2\mathsf K_u\varepsilon_{\rm r}(s)^2L^{-t}(\ell L^s)^3$, the comparison of the background actions at the cutoffs $K$ and $K+1$ (equation~\YMMref{(2155)}{795}) and the energy of the background (equation~\YMMref{(2149)}{794}) bounding the two parts of this excess.

The excess is at least $\frac18\gamma_{\rm r}\sum_{k<t}L^{t-k}\|\mathcal A_k\|^2$ (Prop.~\YMMref{113.5}{792}), where $\|\cdot\|$ is the $\ell^2$ norm over the bonds and $\mathcal A_k$ the real $1$-form by which the average $\mathcal M^kU'$, in the gauge of its averaged contour variables, differs from the averaged background over $\mathcal M^{k+1}U'$; the term $k=t-1$ alone gives $\|\mathcal A_{t-1}\|\le4(\mathsf K_u/\gamma_{\rm r})^{1/2}\varepsilon_{\rm r}(s)(\ell L^s)^{3/2}L^{-(t+1)/2}$. In that gauge $\mathcal M^{t-1}U'$ is the averaged background over $X$ at the cutoff $K+1$, that is $H^{K+1}_s(X)$ (the axial-normalization argument in the proof of Prop.~\YMMref{52.3}{433}), and the chart of the fibre over $X$ writes it as $e^{iB'}H^K_s(X)$ with $\sup|B'|\le2C_{\rm db}\sup|\mathcal A_{t-1}|$ (equation~\YMMref{(2138)}{791}); with $\varepsilon_{\rm r}(s)=2c_\rho\varepsilon_{[s]}$ this is $a_s(K)$.

The axial gauge, the average and the plaquettes are equation~\YMMref{(953)}{433}. Summed over the cutoffs, a geometric series of ratio $L^{-1/2}$, the bound makes $(H^K_s(X))_K$ a Cauchy sequence in a compact space, uniformly in $X$; each $H^K_s$ is continuous (Prop.~\YMMref{52.3}{433}) and covariant, a bare gauge transformation equal to $u\circ\pi$ on $\Lambda_{s+1}$ carrying the elements of the minimal orbit over $X$ whose averages are in the axial gauge to those over $X^u$; $\mathcal M$ is continuous on the fields with plaquettes $<1/200L^2$, which holds the fields $H^K_s(X)$; and the limit inherits all this. (b) The same argument with $\tilde U=Y_{t+1}$, $t=K-d$, the bare field at the end of the tower of the cutoff $K+1$: it is a background over $W$ and over every $Y_j$, with $\mathcal M^{t+1-j}\tilde U=Y_j$ (the minimal orbit over $H^{K+1}_{d+j}(Y_j)$ lies in the one over $Y_j$, {\cite[Lem.~B.4]{YMM2}}(2)).

The competitor $U'=\mathcal M\tilde U=Y_t$ has the averages $\mathcal M^kU'=Y_{t-k}$, and its excess is bounded once, at the depth $d$, by $2\mathsf K_u\varepsilon_{\rm r}(d)^2L^{-t}(\ell L^d)^3$. At $k=t-1-j$ the term of the lower bound has the weight $L^{t-k}=L^{j+1}$, so $\|\mathcal A_k\|\le4(\mathsf K_u/\gamma_{\rm r})^{1/2}\varepsilon_{\rm r}(d)(\ell L^d)^{3/2}L^{-(t+1)/2}L^{-j/2}$; at the point $Y_j$ the chart of the fibre and the axial-normalization argument in the proof of Prop.~\YMMref{52.3}{433} give $Y_{j+1}=e^{iB'}H^K_{d+j}(Y_j)$ with $\sup|B'|\le2C_{\rm db}\sup|\mathcal A_k|\le L^{-j/2}a_d(K)$. The single bound on the excess at the depth $d$ pays for all the depths of the tower together. (c) The response of the background to a change of its datum (Thm.~\YMMref{E}{10} and Lem.~\YMMref{51.6}{398}, with the thresholds of \S\ref{sec:background-step-complements}, for the $n=K-d'$ averaging steps on the whole torus, the datum $X'$ and the radius $\varepsilon_{\rm L}$): $\mathcal C_K(X')$ and $\mathcal C_K(e^{iB}X')$ are single orbits of $\mathcal G^{d'}_K$, and a background over $X$ is, up to a bare gauge transformation, $e^{iL^{-n}\mathcal H(B)}U^\circ$ with $U^\circ\in\mathcal C_K(X')$ and $|\mathcal H(B)(b)|\le\sigma:=B^{\rm e}_5\mathsf S_{\rm e}\sup|B|$ at every bare bond $b$, the exponentially decaying weights of the response summing to at most $\mathsf S_{\rm e}$.

The averages of every order $i\le n$ of a field so moved are, up to gauge, $e^{ia_i}\mathcal M^iU^\circ$ with $|a_i|\le2L^{-(n-i)}\sigma$ (Lem.~\ref{C-368-7}(v)). Along a closed path a gauge transformation conjugates the holonomy; the product bound $|\prod_iA_i-\prod_iA'_i|\le\sum_i|A_iA_i'^{-1}-\mathbf 1|$ on $G$, $|e^{iY}-\mathbf 1|\le|Y|$ and $|\operatorname{tr}Y|\le2|Y|$ give the bound at $i=K-d''$. (d) A telescope over the depths $d+j$, $0\le j<n$, along the tower $Y_j=H^{K+1}_{d,j}(W)$ of the finer cutoff. For a field $Y$ of a depth between $d$ and $d+n$ and $K'\in\{K,K+1\}$ let $\mathsf u^{K'}(Y)$ be the loop along $\Gamma$ of the average down to $\Lambda_{d+n}$ of a background over $Y$ at the cutoff $K'$: one number on the orbit, with $\mathsf u^{K'}(Y)=\mathsf u^{K'}(H^{K'}_s(Y))$ at the depth $s$ of $Y$ ({\cite[Lem.~B.4]{YMM2}}(2)) and $\mathsf u^{K'}(Y)=W_\Gamma(Y)$ at the depth $d+n$.

With $\Delta_j=\mathsf u^{K+1}(Y_j)-\mathsf u^K(Y_j)$ one has $\Delta_n=0$, $\Delta_0$ the left side of the first bound, and $\Delta_j-\Delta_{j+1}=\mathsf u^K(Y_{j+1})-\mathsf u^K(H^K_{d+j}(Y_j))$. By (b), $H^K_{d+j}(Y_j)=e^{iB}Y_{j+1}$ with $\sup|B|\le L^{-j/2}a_d(K)\le\beta_{\rm L}<\pi$, and $\varpi(Y_{j+1})\le2B_3\varpi(W)L^{-2(j+1)}<\varepsilon_{\rm r}(d+j+1)\le\varepsilon_{\rm L}$; so (c) at $d'=d+j+1$ and $d''=d+n$, $n-j-1$ depths apart, gives $|\Delta_j-\Delta_{j+1}|\le2B^{\rm e}_5\mathsf S_{\rm e}NL^{-(n-j-1)}L^{-j/2}a_d(K)$. The roles of the two fields are so chosen because (c) asks a bound on the plaquettes of $X'$ alone, which the tower of the finer cutoff has. The sum over $j$ is a geometric series of the ratio $L^{1/2}$, $\sum_{j<n}L^{j/2}\le L^{n/2}/(L^{1/2}-1)$, which gives $\mathsf c_9NL^{-n/2}a_d(K)$.

The conditions persist for $K'\ge K$, as $a_d$ decreases, and the sum over $K'\ge K$ with $\sum_{K'\ge K}a_d(K')=r_d(K)$ gives the second bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Smoothed loops over a fixed field]\label{C-372-9}
In the one-torus setting let $d$ be admitted, $W\in J_d$ and $C$ a lattice loop of $\Lambda_{d'}$, $d'\ge d$. Put $\varepsilon_{\rm r}=2c_\rho\varepsilon_{[d]}$; let $\mathsf c_{\rm A}>0$ be the constant with which the comparison of two consecutive cutoffs (Prop.~\YMMref{113.9}{795}) bounds the distance of the averaged backgrounds of two consecutive cutoffs over one block field (Lem.~\ref{C-372-31}(a)), and $\mathsf c_9,\beta_{\rm L}>0$ the constant and the radius of the Lipschitz bound of the tower in the block field (Lem.~\ref{C-372-31}(c), (d)), the numbers formed in Lem.~\ref{C-372-31}; all three depend on the constants alone. Put $a_s(K)=\mathsf c_{\rm A}\varepsilon_{[s]}(\ell L^s)^{3/2}L^{-(K-s+1)/2}$ and $r_d(K)=\sum_{K'\ge K}a_d(K')=r_d(d)L^{-(K-d)/2}$; let $K_2$ be the least $K\ge2$ with $\lfloor\frac{K-d}3\rfloor\ge\max\{1,d'-d\}$ and $a_d(K)\le\beta_{\rm L}$; and put $\mathsf c_{\rm f}=\frac{28L\varepsilon_{\rm r}}{1-L^{-1}}+\mathsf c_9r_d(d)$ and $\mathsf c_{\rm g}=\frac{1544L^2\varepsilon_{\rm r}}{1-L^{-1}}+6\mathsf c_9r_d(d)$, numbers that depend on $d$, $\ell$, $\mathsf b$ and the constants ($K_2$ also on $d'-d$).
(a) $V_n=H^\infty_{d,n}(W)$ satisfies $\mathcal MV_{n+1}=V_n$, $\varpi(V_n)\le2B_3\varpi(W)L^{-2n}$ and, for $n\ge d'-d$, $|W_C(V_n)-W_C(V_{n+1})|\le28B_3|C|L^d\varpi(W)L^{-n}$. So $W^{[d]}_C$ exists uniformly on $J_d$, with $|W^{[d]}_C-W_C(V_n)|\le\frac{14}{1-L^{-1}}|C|L^d\varepsilon_{\rm r}L^{-n}$ there; it is continuous and gauge invariant on $J_d$ with values in $[-1,1]$; $F^{[d]}_C$ is Borel; and $0\le1-W^{[d]}_C(W)\le\frac12(2B_3\varpi(W)L^{2d}s_1s_2)^2$ for a coordinate rectangle with sides $s_1$, $s_2$.
(b) For $K\ge\max\{2,d+1,d'\}$, $\mathcal C_K(W)$ is one non-empty orbit of $\mathcal G^d_K$; $w^K_C$ is continuous and gauge invariant on $J_d$; $\sup_{J_d}|w^K_C-W^{[d]}_C|\to0$, and this supremum is at most $|C|L^d\mathsf c_{\rm f}L^{-(K-d)/3}$ for $K\ge K_2$.
(c) For curves and any shadows, $|W_{\Gamma^{(d+n)}}(V_n)-W_{\Gamma^{(d+n+1)}}(V_{n+1})|\le772(|\gamma|L^{d+n+1}+2)L^{-2n}\varepsilon_{\rm r}$; so $W^{[d]}_\gamma$ exists uniformly on $J_d$, does not depend on the shadows, equals $W^{[d]}_C$ along a lattice loop $C$, and is continuous and gauge invariant, and $F_\gamma$ is Borel. $w^K_\gamma(W)$ is one number on $\mathcal C_K(W)$; two shadows on the bare lattice change it by at most $1496(|\gamma|L^K+2)L^{-2(K-d)}\varepsilon_{\rm r}$; and $\sup_{J_d}|w^K_\gamma-W^{[d]}_\gamma|\le(|\gamma|L^d+2)\mathsf c_{\rm g}L^{-(K-d)/3}$ for $K\ge K_2$, taken at $d'=d$.
(d) For $K\ge K_{\rm bf}$ with $\lceil K/1260\rceil\ge d$,
\[
\begin{multlined}
\Bigl|\langle F^{[d]}_C(\mathcal M^{K-d}U)\rangle_K-\int F^{[d]}_C\,\mathrm{d}\mu_d\Bigr|\le\mathfrak r_K:=\mathsf C_{\rm bf}S_L\ell^3K^{2\mathfrak p_0+1/2}L^{-K/10},\qquad S_L=\sum_{j\ge0}(1 \\
+j)^{2\mathfrak p_0+1/2}L^{-j/10},
\end{multlined}
\]
a bound free of $C$ and $d$, where $\mathsf C_{\rm bf}$ and $K_{\rm bf}$ are the numbers of Def.~\textup{\ref{IV-62-62}}(5), formed at an interval of labels under the condition (Tor) on the side $\ell$ (\S\ref{sec:cutoff-calibration}) that holds $\mathsf b$, and depend on the label only through that interval (Cor.~\textup{\ref{IV-62-66}}(a)); in the frame $[\mathsf b_-,\mathsf b_+]$ is such an interval, and it gives one pair of numbers for all $\mathsf b\in\mathsf J$, with the range $K\ge K_{\rm bf}$, $\lceil K/1260\rceil\ge d$; for $K\ge K_2$ besides, $|\langle(\mathbf 1_{J_d}w^K_C)(\mathcal M^{K-d}U)\rangle_K-\int F^{[d]}_C\,\mathrm{d}\mu_d|\le|C|L^d\mathsf c_{\rm f}L^{-(K-d)/3}+\mathfrak r_K$. The same holds for curves, with $F_\gamma$, $w^K_\gamma$ and $(|\gamma|L^d+2)\mathsf c_{\rm g}$.
(e) In the frame put $\mathsf b'=\mathsf b-\bar B$ and $J'_d=\{\varpi<c_\rho\varepsilon(L^d\mathsf b')/B_3\}$, and let $d\ge d_0$, the least integer $d_0\ge1$ with $L^{d_0}\gamma^{-2}\ge\Theta_\star$ and $\log(L^{d_0}\gamma^{-2})>2\mathfrak p_0$. Then the one-torus setting holds at the labels $\mathsf b$ and $\mathsf b'$ and $d$ is admitted at both; $I_d\subset J_d\subset J'_d$ and $\mathsf O_{K-d}\subset J'_d$ for every $K>d$, so that $m_{K-d}$ gives no mass to $\mathcal V_d\setminus J'_d$, and $\mu^K_d(\mathcal V_d\setminus J'_d)\le R_d$; over every $V\in J'_d$ and every $K>d$ the backgrounds form one non-empty orbit, $w^K_C$ is Borel, and (a), (b) hold on $J'_d$, also for families: $\sup_{J'_d}|w^K_{\mathsf C}-\prod_iW^{[d]}_{C_i}|\to0$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof]
(a) Over $W$ the backgrounds of the finer cutoffs are built one block step at a time, $H^K_{d,n}(W)$, and all of them are, up to gauge, block averages $\mathcal M^{K-d-n}U$ of one bare background $U$, whose plaquettes are $<B_3\varpi(W)(a_K/a_d)^2$ (Thm.~\YMMref{E}{10} in the setting of Section~\YMMref{52.7}{432}); so the factor $2B_3$ is paid once, not at every step: $\varpi(\mathcal M^{K-d-n}U)\le2B_3\varpi(W)L^{-2n}<\varepsilon_{\rm r}L^{-2n}\le L^{-3n/2}\,2c_\rho\varepsilon_{[d+n]}$. Induction on $n$, uniform continuity on the compact set $\{\varpi\le L^{-3n/2}2c_\rho\varepsilon_{[d+n]}\}$ and Lem.~\ref{C-372-31}(a) give $H^K_{d,n}\to H^\infty_{d,n}$ uniformly on $J_d$; the bound passes to $V_n$, which lies in $\{\varpi<2c_\rho\varepsilon_{[d+n]}\}$, so that $H^\infty_{d+n}(V_n)$ is defined.

The ball $\{\varpi<2c_\rho\varepsilon_{[d]}\}$, larger than $J_d$ by the factor $2B_3\ge2$, is the domain of the single step $H^\infty_d$; the whole tower needs room for the factor $2B_3$ that the backgrounds pay, which is why the proposition asks $W\in J_d$, and why the smaller ball $I_d\subset J_d$, and not the larger one, enters the starting depth. One refinement costs $|W_\Gamma(\mathcal MV)-W_\Gamma(V)|\le14L^2N\varpi(V)$ for a loop of $N$ bonds if $\varpi(V)<1/200L^2$ (in a gauge fixed along the blocks the average of a nearly flat field moves each bond by $O(L^2\varpi(V))$), which holds as $2c_\rho\varepsilon_{[d]}<1/200L^2$; with $N=|C|L^{d+n}$ the number of bonds grows like $L^n$ while the plaquettes fall like $L^{-2n}$: a geometric series, whose tail with $\varpi(W)<\varepsilon_{\rm r}/2B_3$ is the stated bound.

For a rectangle, $a_p=\frac12|\partial U(p)-\mathbf 1|^2$ and the holonomy of $\partial R$ is an ordered product of conjugated plaquette variables, so $1-W_{\partial R}\le(\sum_{p\subset R}\sqrt{a_p})^2$ (Prop.~\ref{C-372-13}(c)), and the bare plaquettes of the background are $<2B_3\varpi(W)(a_K/a_d)^2$.
(b) The tower ends in the non-empty set $\mathcal C_K(W)$, one orbit by Thm.~\YMMref{E}{10} in the setting of Section~\YMMref{52.7}{432} and \S\ref{sec:analytic-core-complements}. The comparison of two consecutive cutoffs (Prop.~\YMMref{113.9}{795}) gives ${\rm dist}(H^{K+1}_s(X),H^K_s(X))\le a_s(K)$ for $\varpi(X)<2c_\rho\varepsilon_{[s]}$ (Lem.~\ref{C-372-31}(a)). At a depth $d+n$ we split into three terms. $|w^K_C(W)-W_C(\mathcal M^{K-d-n}U)|$ and $|W^{[d]}_C(W)-W_C(V_n)|$ are at most $\frac{14}{1-L^{-1}}|C|L^d\varepsilon_{\rm r}L^{-n}$, uniformly in $K$, by the series of (a); and $|W_C(H^K_{d,n}W)-W_C(V_n)|\le|C|L^{d+n}\sup{\rm dist}(H^K_{d,n},H^\infty_{d,n})\to0$ at fixed $n$. Choose $n$, then $K$. For the rate we use the Lipschitz bound of the tower in the block field (Lem.~\ref{C-372-31}(d)): for $n\ge1$, $K\ge\max\{2,d+n+1\}$ with $a_d(K)\le\beta_{\rm L}$, $W\in J_d$ and every closed path $\Gamma$ of $\Lambda_{d+n}$ with $N$ bonds, $|W_\Gamma(H^{K+1}_{d,n}W)-W_\Gamma(H^K_{d,n}W)|\le\mathsf c_9NL^{-n/2}a_d(K)$.

It is a telescope over the depths $d+j$, $0\le j<n$, along the tower $Y_j=H^{K+1}_{d,j}(W)$ of the finer cutoff: at the depth $d+j$ the one-depth smoothings $H^{K+1}_{d+j}$ and $H^K_{d+j}$ of the two cutoffs, applied to $Y_j$, give fields of the depth $d+j+1$ at distance at most $L^{-j/2}a_d(K)$ (Lem.~\ref{C-372-31}(b): the excess of the action of the averaged background of the finer cutoff is bounded once, at the depth $d$, and the term of the depth $d+j$ in the lower bound on the excess carries the weight $L^{j+1}$; the bound $a_{d+j}(K)$ of one depth, applied at $Y_j$, is up to $L^{2j}$ times larger), and the loop along $\Gamma$ of the average down to $\Lambda_{d+n}$ of the background over such a field, $n-j-1$ depths below it, moves by at most $2B^{\rm e}_5\mathsf S_{\rm e}NL^{-(n-j-1)}$ times that distance, a constant free of the cutoff and of the number of the depths between (Lem.~\ref{C-372-31}(c)); the sum over $j$ is a geometric series of the ratio $L^{1/2}$, which gives $\mathsf c_9$.

Summed over $K'\ge K$, with $\sum_{K'\ge K}a_d(K')=r_d(K)$, at $\Gamma=C^{\langle d+n\rangle}$ it bounds the middle term by $\mathsf c_9|C|L^dL^{n/2}r_d(K)$; at $n=\lfloor\frac{K-d}3\rfloor$ both $L^{-n}$ and $L^{n/2}L^{-(K-d)/2}$ are at most $L\cdot L^{-(K-d)/3}$, which gives $\mathsf c_{\rm f}$. Continuity and gauge invariance of $w^K_C$ on $J_d$ come with the tower.
(c) Two shadows of consecutive lattices, evaluated at $V_{n+1}$, differ by a band of $O(|\gamma|L^{d+n+1}+2)$ plaquettes of size $O(L^{-2n}\varepsilon_{\rm r})$; two shadows on the bare lattice, evaluated at a background over $W$, differ by a band of $O(|\gamma|L^K+2)$ bare plaquettes of size $O(L^{-2(K-d)}\varepsilon_{\rm r})$; then argue as in (a), (b).
(d) By Cor.~\textup{\ref{IV-62-66}} and \textup{(\ref{IV-62-68})}, two consecutive cutoffs differ on a gauge invariant bounded Borel function $F$ of the block field of a depth at most $\lceil K/1260\rceil$ ($1260=180(3N+4)$ at $N=1$ in \S\ref{sec:cutoff-calibration}) by at most $\mathsf C_{\rm bf}\ell^3K^{2\mathfrak p_0+1/2}L^{-K/10}\sup|F|$; the comparison there is made through the small-field chains of the two cutoffs at that depth, and its numbers, formed at an interval of labels under (Tor), serve every label of the interval (Cor.~\textup{\ref{IV-62-66}}(a)). In the frame $[\mathsf b_-,\mathsf b_+]$ is such an interval on the side $\ell$: $\mathsf b_->g^{-2}\ge\gamma^{-2}$, and $M\,Q(\mathsf b_+)\le L^m$, with $Q$ of Lem.~\ref{C-372-7}, holds on the sides of $\mathfrak L(g)$ at every label of $\mathsf I(g)$, as in (e). Sum over $K'\ge K$ with $F=F^{[d]}_C$; the second mean adds the rate of (b).
(e) $\gamma^{-2}\le g^{-2}<\mathsf b'<\mathsf b<L(g^{-2}+\bar B)$, so the sides at $g$ satisfy the condition on the side at both labels, and $L^d\mathsf b'\ge L^d\gamma^{-2}\ge\Theta_\star$; the constraint sets, the action and the regularity radius hold no label, so (a), (b) apply at the label $\mathsf b'$ on its ball $J'_d$. $x_{K-d}\ge L^d\mathsf b-\bar B\ge L^d\mathsf b'$, $\varepsilon$ decreases for $\log t>2\mathfrak p_0$ and $c_\rho\ge2B_3$; so $2\varepsilon(x_{K-d})\le2\varepsilon(L^d\mathsf b')\le c_\rho\varepsilon(L^d\mathsf b')/B_3$, that is $\mathsf O_{K-d}\subset J'_d$, and $J_d\subset J'_d$ likewise. $\mu^K_d(\mathcal V_d\setminus J'_d)\le\mu^K_d(\mathcal V_d\setminus I_d)\le R_d$ by Prop.~\ref{C-372-8}(b). For families $|\prod_ix_i-\prod_iy_i|\le\sum_i|x_i-y_i|$ on $[-1,1]$.
\end{proof}

The new estimate is one renormalisation step with lines inserted. Its soft part rests on three facts about ordered products of matrices under a measure.

\begin{lemma}[Ordered products under a measure]\label{C-372-16}
(a) Let $\mathfrak A$ be a unital normed algebra, $I$ a finite totally ordered set, and for $j\in I$ let $\mathsf{At}_j$ be a finite set of atoms $\alpha$, each with an element $\tau_\alpha\in\mathfrak A$, $|\tau_\alpha|\le1$. A block is a non-empty set of atoms of pairwise different indices, a packing $\pi$ a set of blocks with pairwise disjoint sets of indices, and $\tau^\to(\pi)$ the product of the $\tau_\alpha$, $\alpha$ in the blocks of $\pi$, in the order of $I$. For complex weights $w$ on the blocks put $Z[w]=\sum_\pi\prod_{\beta\in\pi}w(\beta)\,\tau^\to(\pi)$ and $|w|_1=\sum_\beta|w(\beta)|$. Then $|Z[w]|\le e^{|w|_1}$ and $|Z[w_1+w_2]-Z[w_1]|\le|w_2|_1e^{|w_1|_1+|w_2|_1}$. If bounded functions $f_\alpha$ on a space with a complex measure $\nu$ of mass $1$ and finite total variation have $\int e^{\sum_\alpha z_\alpha f_\alpha}\,\mathrm{d}\nu=e^{F(z)}$ with $F$ holomorphic near $0$ and $F(0)=0$, then
\[\int\prod^{\to}_{j\in I}\Bigl(\mathbf 1+\sum_{\alpha\in\mathsf{At}_j}f_\alpha\tau_\alpha\Bigr)\,\mathrm{d}\nu=Z[\kappa],\qquad\kappa(\beta)=\Bigl(\prod_{\alpha\in\beta}\partial_{z_\alpha}\Bigr)F(0),\]
the joint cumulants of the $f_\alpha$, $\alpha\in\beta$.
\emph{Generators.} Here and below $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ is the real space of the Hermitian traceless $2\times2$ matrices, as the chart $e^{ig_tB(b)}V_W(0)(b)$ of the frame asks, with the scalar product $\langle X,Y\rangle=\frac12\operatorname{tr}XY$, and $t_1,t_2,t_3$ is an orthonormal basis of it: $t_at_b+t_bt_a=2\delta_{ab}\mathbf 1$, $t_a^2=\mathbf 1$, $|t_a|=1$ in the operator norm and $\sum_at_a^2=3\cdot\mathbf 1$ (the Pauli matrices up to a rotation). The components of $X\in\mathfrak{su}(2)$ are $X^a=\langle t_a,X\rangle$, so that $X=\sum_aX^at_a$ and $|X|=(\sum_a(X^a)^2)^{1/2}$; this is used for the variables $y_j$, the fluctuation field $B$, the test forms $\varphi$ and the rotations $\Upsilon$ below, and $(\varphi,B)=\sum_b\sum_a\varphi^a(b)B^a(b)$. A complex $2\times2$ matrix is written $x=x^0\mathbf 1+\sum_ax^a\,it_a$, with $x^0=\frac12\operatorname{tr}x$, $x^a=-\frac i2\operatorname{tr}(xt_a)$ and $|x^0|,|x^a|\le|x|$; as $(\sum_ax^at_a)^2=\sum_a(x^a)^2\mathbf 1$, $\det x=(x^0)^2+\sum_a(x^a)^2$. For $h\in\mathrm{SU}(2)$, ${\rm R}(h)\in SO(3)$ is the rotation with $ht_bh^{-1}=\sum_a{\rm R}(h)_{ab}t_a$, ${\rm R}(h)_{ab}=\langle t_a,ht_bh^{-1}\rangle$.
(b) Let $\mathfrak A=M_2(\mathbb C)^{\otimes r}$ with the operator norm and $I=I_1<\dots<I_r$ a union of intervals; let $c_j$ ($j\in I$) and $p_e$ ($e=\{j<j'\}$ in a set of pairs, each inside one $I_i$) be complex numbers, and $w_{\rm g}$ the weight that is $c_j$ at one block $\{\alpha^0_j\}$ with $\tau=\mathbf 1$, $p_e$ at the three blocks $\{\alpha^a_j,\alpha^a_{j'}\}$, $a=1,2,3$, with $\tau=it_a$ in the $i$-th factor, and $0$ elsewhere. Two pairs cross if their end points interlace. With $\mathfrak T=\sum_j|c_j|+3\sum_e|p_e|$, $\mathfrak X=\sum9|p_e||p_{e'}|$ over the crossing pairs of pairs, and $\mathfrak O=\sum|\hat w(\beta)||\hat w(\beta')|$ over the ordered pairs (equal ones included) of overlapping sets $\beta,\beta'$ among the $\{j\}$ and the $e$, $\hat w=c_j$ resp.\ $-3p_e$:
\[\Bigl|Z[w_{\rm g}]-\exp\Bigl(\sum_jc_j-3\sum_ep_e\Bigr)\mathbf 1\Bigr|\le(2\mathfrak X+\tfrac12\mathfrak O)\,e^{\mathfrak T}.\]
(c) Let $J=J_1\sqcup\dots\sqcup J_r$ be finite cyclically ordered sets (the lines), $g_j\in\mathrm{SU}(2)$, and $w(y)=\prod_i\frac12\operatorname{tr}\prod_{j\in J_i}(e^{i\sum_ay^a_jt_a}g_j)$ for $y=(y_j)\in(\mathbb R^3)^J$; every derivative of $w$ of every order has modulus at most $1$. Let $\varrho$ be a complex Borel measure of mass $1$ on $\{|y_j|\le\bar y\ \forall j\}$ whose logarithmic Laplace transform $\ell(z)=\log\int e^{(z,y)}d\varrho$ is holomorphic on a polydisc of radius $r_1>1$, with the cumulants $\kappa_\gamma=\partial^\gamma\ell(0)$, and let $s_{jj'}=s_{j'j}$ be real numbers, for the pairs $\{j,j'\}$ of one line and for $j=j'$, with $S=\sum_js_{jj}+2\sum_{\{j,j'\}}s_{jj'}\ge0$. For a pair of one line let $j\to j'$ be the arc from $j$ forward to $j'$, $G_{j\to j'}=g_jg_{j+1}\cdots g_{j'-1}$, ${\rm R}(h)\in SO(3)$ the rotation with $ht_bh^{-1}=\sum_a{\rm R}(h)_{ab}t_a$, $\kappa^{(2)}_{jj'}=(\kappa_{e_{ja}+e_{j'b}})_{a,b}$, $d_{jj'}=\kappa^{(2)}_{jj'}-s_{jj'}{\rm R}(G_{j\to j'})$, $d_{jj}=\kappa^{(2)}_{jj}-s_{jj}\mathbf 1$, and $|m|_1=\sum_{a,b}|m^{ab}|$. Then
\[
\begin{multlined}
\Bigl|\int w\,\mathrm{d}\varrho-e^{-\frac32S}w(0)\Bigr|\le|\varrho|\,(E_1+E_2+E_3),\qquad E_1=\sum_\alpha|\kappa_{e_\alpha}|,\quad E_2=\sup_{|y_j|\le\bar y}\mathsf e(y),\quad E_3 \\
=\sum_{|\gamma|\ge3}\frac{|\gamma|}{\gamma!}|\kappa_\gamma|,
\end{multlined}
\]
$|\varrho|$ the total variation, with
\[
\begin{multlined}
\mathsf e(y)=\sum_{\{j,j'\}}\Bigl[|d_{jj'}|_1+6|s_{jj'}|\sum_{i\in(j\to j')}|y_i|+|\kappa^{(2)}_{jj'}|_1(|y_j|+|y_{j'}|+|y_j||y_{j'}|)\Bigr]+\sum_j\bigl[\tfrac12|d_{jj}|_1 \\
+|\kappa^{(2)}_{jj}|_1|y_j|\bigr]+\sum_{\rm two\ \relax lines}|\kappa^{(2)}_{jj'}|_1,
\end{multlined}
\]
the first sum over the pairs of one line, $i$ over the indices strictly between $j$ and $j'$ on the arc. If $\ell=\sum_X\ell_X$, $|\ell_X|\le A_X$ on the polydisc, $\ell_X$ depending on at most $N_X$ of the variables, and $r_1\ge2$, then $E_3\le3\sum_XA_X(N_X/r_1)^3e^{2(N_X+3)/r_1}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof]
(a) $|\tau^\to(\pi)|\le1$, and a packing with $n$ blocks arises from $n!$ of the $n$-tuples of blocks, so $\sum_\pi\prod|w(\beta)|\le e^{|w|_1}$; expanding $\prod(w_1+w_2)(\beta)$ and isolating one block of $w_2$ gives the second bound. For the identity, multiply out: the left side is $\sum_{S\subset I}\sum_{(\alpha_j)_{j\in S}}\int\prod_{j\in S}f_{\alpha_j}\,\mathrm{d}\nu\prod^\to\tau_{\alpha_j}$; the moment is $\prod\partial_{z_{\alpha_j}}e^F$ at $0$, and by induction from $\partial e^F=(\partial F)e^F$ the derivatives of $e^F$ in pairwise different variables are, at $0$, sums over the partitions of the variables of products of derivatives of $F$; a choice of $S$, of the atoms and of a partition is a packing. (b) A packing in the support of $w_{\rm g}$ is a set of singletons, a set $\mathsf m$ of disjoint pairs and a colouring of $\mathsf m$.

If no two pairs of $\mathsf m$ cross, the sum over the colours is $(-3)^{\#\mathsf m}\mathbf 1$: take a shortest pair; between its two factors $\tau_a$ stand only factors $\mathbf 1$, and $\sum_a\tau_a\tau_a=-\sum_at_a^2=-3$; induct. The packings with a crossing contribute at most $2\mathfrak Xe^{\mathfrak T}$; and $\exp\sum\hat w-Z_{\rm nc}$, $Z_{\rm nc}$ the sum over the packings with the values $(-3)^{\#\mathsf m}$, is a sum over tuples of sets with an overlap, at most $\frac12\mathfrak Oe^{\mathfrak T}$. (c) Let $f(\tau)=\int w(\tau y)\,\mathrm{d}\varrho$. The cumulant formula $\int y_\alpha G\,\mathrm{d}\varrho=\sum_\beta\frac1{\beta!}\kappa_{\beta+e_\alpha}\int\partial^\beta G\,\mathrm{d}\varrho$, for entire $G$ with bounded derivatives at $0$ (from $\partial_\alpha Z=Z\,\partial_\alpha\ell$ for $Z=e^\ell$, coefficient by coefficient, then by Taylor polynomials and dominated convergence), gives $f'(\tau)=\sum_{\alpha,\beta}\frac{\tau^{|\beta|}}{\beta!}\kappa_{\beta+e_\alpha}\int(\partial^\beta\partial_\alpha w)(\tau y)\,\mathrm{d}\varrho$.

The terms $|\beta|=0$ are at most $|\varrho|E_1$, those with $|\beta|\ge2$ at most $|\varrho|E_3$. For $|\beta|=1$ the matrix identity $\sum c^{ab}_{jj'}\partial_{y^a_j}\partial_{y^b_{j'}}w=-3Sw+\mathcal R$, $|\mathcal R|\le2\mathsf e(y)$, at $c=\kappa^{(2)}$ holds: by cyclicity the trace of the line of a pair is $\frac12\operatorname{tr}(u_jHu_{j'}H')$ with $u_j=e^{i\sum_ay^a_jt_a}$; moving $e^{iy\cdot t}$ across $t_a$ costs $|y|$; $\sum_{a,b}{\rm R}(G)_{ab}t_aHt_b=\sum_b(Gt_bG^{-1})Ht_b=3H+\rho$ with $|\rho|\le6|H-G|\le6\sum_{i\in(j\to j')}|y_i|$ (a telescoping product of unitaries; $\sum_bt_b^2=3$); on the diagonal $\partial_a\partial_bu=-\delta_{ab}u$ up to $2|y|$. So $f'=-3\tau Sf+\mathcal E$ with $|\mathcal E|\le|\varrho|(E_1+2\tau E_2+E_3)$, and $f(1)=e^{-\frac32S}f(0)+\int_0^1e^{-\frac32S(1-\tau^2)}\mathcal E\,\mathrm{d}\tau$, $S\ge0$.

The bound on $E_3$: Cauchy's estimates for each $\ell_X$ and $\sum_mm\binom{m+N-1}mx^m=Nx(1-x)^{-N-1}$, $x=1/r_1\le\frac12$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[One step with lines inserted]\label{C-372-10}
In the frame let $\mathsf C$ be a family with corners in $\Lambda_{i_0}$.
(a) There are $C_\eta<\infty$ and an integer $s_0\ge i_0$, depending on the constants, $g$, $\mathsf J$ and on $\mathsf C$ only through $\#\mathsf C$, $|\mathsf C|$, $s_{\mathsf C}$, $\rho_{\mathsf C}$ and $i_0$, not on $K$, $\mathsf b\in\mathsf J$, $\ell$, $t$, $W$, such that for $\mathsf b\in\mathsf J$, $K>s_0$, $0\le t<K-s_0$ and every $W\in\mathsf O_{t+1}$
\[\Bigl|\int W^{(t)}_{\mathsf C}(V_W(B))\,\nu_W(\,\mathrm{d}B)-\lambda_{t+1}W^{(t+1)}_{\mathsf C}(W)\Bigr|\le C_\eta L^{-(K-t)/4};\]
more precisely, with $s=K-t$ (in (a) and its proof), $\Lambda_{\mathsf C}=\frac{3|\mathsf C|}{2M\mathsf b_-}$, $\mathsf g_s=(\frac3{2\mathsf b_-})^{1/2}L^{-s/2}$ and $\mathsf y_s=\log(2\mathsf b_+)+s\log L$, the left side is at most
\[C'(1+\#\mathsf C+\Lambda_{\mathsf C})e^{C''\Lambda_{\mathsf C}}\bigl[\mathsf y_s^{2\mathfrak p_0}(\mathsf g_s+L^{-s/2})+e^{-\rho_{\mathsf C}L^s/LM}\bigr]+\tfrac32\,\mathsf c\,C_X\mathsf b_-^{-2}|\mathsf C|L^{-s},\qquad\mathsf c=\tfrac54\bar B,\]
with $C'$, $C''$, $C_X$ depending on the constants alone; so for every $\vartheta<\frac12$ the same holds with $L^{-\vartheta(K-t)}$ and another $C_\eta$. For one polygon the same bound holds for the holonomy matrix, $|\int{\rm Hol}_C(e^{i\eta_t\mathbf A(B)}U_+)\,\nu_W(\,\mathrm{d}B)-\lambda_{t+1}{\rm Hol}_C(U_+)|\le C_\eta L^{-(K-t)/4}$ in the operator norm, from a fixed base point, $e^{i\eta_t\mathbf A(B)}U_+$ being the configuration of the shift formula of step~1 of the proof (at $t=0$, where $\eta_0=1$, the chart $e^{iB'}U_+$ itself). No positivity of $\nu_W$ is used.
(b) If $\nu_W\ge0$, which is the case for $m_{t+1}$-almost every $W$, and $K-t>s_0$, the left side is at most
\[C_\sharp\frac{|\mathsf C|}{\mathsf b}\Bigl[(1+\mathfrak b_t)^2(\varepsilon_{t+1}+\delta_t+L^{-(K-t)})+e^{-\mathsf D_t}+\frac{\bar B}{\mathsf b}L^{-(K-t)}\Bigr],\qquad\mathsf D_t=\frac{\delta'_{\mathsf C}L^{K-t}}{LM}-2,\]
where $C_\sharp$ depends only on the constants, $n_{\mathsf C}$ and $c_{\mathsf C}$, and $s_0$ is the least integer $\ge i_0$ such that every $x\ge\frac23\mathsf b_-L^{s_0-1}$ satisfies explicit smallness conditions formed from the constants and $n_{\mathsf C}$, so that $s_0=\max\{i_0,s'_0\}$ with $s'_0$ formed from the constants, $\mathsf b_-$ and $n_{\mathsf C}$ alone; with the Euclidean distance in the place of the sup-distance in $\delta'_{\mathsf C}$, $\mathsf D_t$ would carry a further factor $1/\sqrt3$. At every $W\in\mathsf O_{t+1}$ a bound of the same form holds with the total variation of $\nu_W$ as a further factor. The right side is at most $C_\eta L^{-\vartheta(K-t)}$ for every $\vartheta<\frac12$, with $C_\eta$ depending on the constants, $\vartheta$, $\mathsf J$, $|\mathsf C|$, $n_{\mathsf C}$, $c_{\mathsf C}$, $\delta'_{\mathsf C}$, and on $g$ through $\mathsf J$ alone. For the squares $Q_i$ of side $a_i$ with corners in $\Lambda_i$ one has $s_0=\max\{i,s'_0\}=i+O(1)$, so $s_0=i$ for $i\ge s'_0$, and the bound $C(\mathsf J)\frac{a_i}{\mathsf b}L^{-\vartheta(K-t)}\le C(\mathsf J)L^{-\vartheta(K-t-i)}$, which depends on the scale of the step only through $a_{K-t}/a_i$.
(c) (The drift along a small square.) Let $C$ be a square of side $a_s$ in a coordinate plane with corners in $\Lambda_s$, let $\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_N$ be its $N=4L^{K-t-s}$ bonds of $\Lambda_{K-t}$, and let $\Upsilon_i(B)=\frac1i\log[{\rm hol}_{\sigma_i}(e^{i\eta_t\mathbf A(B)}U_+)\,{\rm hol}_{\sigma_i}(U_+)^{-1}]\in\mathfrak{su}(2)$ be the rotation of $\sigma_i$ in the shift formula of step~1 of the proof of (a) (at $t=0$ the $\sigma_i$ are bare bonds, $\Upsilon_i=B'(\sigma_i)$ at a positively oriented $\sigma_i$ and $\Upsilon_i=-\operatorname{Ad}(U_+(\sigma_i))B'(\bar\sigma_i)$ at a reversed one). For every $\alpha<\frac12$ there are $c_1(\alpha)$ and $s_A$, depending on the constants, $\mathsf J$, $\alpha$ and a lower bound of $\ell$, not on $g$, $K$, $t$, $s$, $\mathsf b$, $W$, such that for $s\ge s_A$, $K>s$, $0\le t<K-s$ and every $W\in\mathsf O_{t+1}$
\[\sum_{i,a}\Bigl|\int\Upsilon^a_i\,\mathrm{d}\nu_W\Bigr|\le c_1(\alpha)L^{-s}L^{-\alpha(K-t)}.\]
These are the rotations of the shift formula; the loop, being a trace, does not see the difference to the rotations of the background over $V_W(B)$ in any other gauge.
(d) (The mean of the fluctuation field.) For every $W\in\mathsf O_{t+1}$ and every real $1$-form $\varphi$ on the fluctuation bonds, $|\int(\varphi,B)\,\nu_W(\,\mathrm{d}B)|\le C_4\delta_t(\varepsilon_{t+1}+a_{K-t}/\ell)\sum_b\max_a|\varphi^a(b)|$, $C_4$ depending on the constants: the mean of the fluctuation field is of the order of the coupling with its logarithm, $\delta_t$, times the bound $\varepsilon_{t+1}$ of the curvature of a tame $W$, the term $a_{K-t}/\ell$ coming from the domains that do not fit into the torus; on tame $W$ it is so of the order of the coupling squared, up to logarithms. The order $g_t^2$ times the curvature, up to a logarithm, is that of the mean of one rotation $\Upsilon_i$ of (c), which holds the further factor $g_t$ of $g_tB$.
(e) (Levels at least as coarse as the corners.) Let $0<\vartheta<\frac12$, $c_0>0$ and $\varrho>0$, let $C$ be a rectangle with sides in $[c_0\varrho,10\varrho]$ and corners in $\Lambda_i$, $i$ the integer with $a_i\le\frac12c_0\varrho<La_i$, and put $a_*=\varrho(\mathsf b/\varrho)^{\vartheta/(3+\vartheta)}$, a length coarser than the loop for small $\varrho/\mathsf b$. There is $C_*$, depending on the constants, $c_0$, $\vartheta$ and $\mathsf J$ alone, such that at every cutoff $K\ge i$, at every level $0\le t<K$ with $a_i\le a_{K-t}\le a_*$ and at every $W\in\mathsf O_{t+1}$ with $\nu_W\ge0$, hence for $m_{t+1}$-almost every $W$,
\[\Bigl|\int W^{(t)}_C(V_W(B))\,\nu_W(\,\mathrm{d}B)-\lambda_{t+1}W^{(t+1)}_C(W)\Bigr|\le C_*\frac\varrho{\mathsf b}\Bigl(\frac{a_{K-t}}{\mathsf b}\Bigr)^\vartheta;\]
so the mean of the defect over the block field, $\bar{\mathsf D}_{t+1}$ of Prop.~\ref{C-372-12}(b) for $C$, has modulus at most $C_*\frac\varrho{\mathsf b}(\frac{a_{K-t}}{\mathsf b})^\vartheta$, as $Z^{-1}m_{t+1}$ has mass at most $1$ (Prop.~\ref{C-372-12}(c)). At the levels finer than the corners, $K-t>s_0=\max\{i,s'_0\}$, (b) gives the same bound with another $C_*$ of the same kind: there $|C|\le40\varrho$, $n_C=4$, the chord-arc constant of $C$ is bounded below in terms of $c_0$, and the bracket of (b), whose distance term vanishes for one polygon ($\delta'_C=\infty$), is at most a multiple of $(a_{K-t}/\mathsf b)^\vartheta$ formed from the constants, $\vartheta$ and $\mathsf J$. The levels $i<K-t\le s'_0$ occur only when $i<s'_0$, and then $\varrho>2a_{s'_0}/c_0$ and $a_{K-t}\ge a_{s'_0}$, so that there the bound $2$ of the defect at $\nu_W\ge0$ is at most $C_*\frac\varrho{\mathsf b}(\frac{a_{K-t}}{\mathsf b})^\vartheta$ for $C_*$ of the same kind. So the bound of one step holds at every level with $a_{K-t}\le a_*$; this is the bound of one step in Thm.~\ref{C-372-4}(8)(b).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof]
(a) \emph{0. The objects of the step.} A \emph{triple} on a domain $X$ is $P=(U,A',\mathbf J)$, $U$ an $\mathrm{SU}(2)$-valued configuration and $A'$, $\mathbf J$ complex $1$-forms on the bare bonds of $X$; it enters through its pair $\mathbf p(P)=(e^{i\eta_{t+1}A'}U,\mathbf J)$, and a gauge transformation $u$ acts by $P^u=(U^u,\operatorname{Ad}(u)A',\operatorname{Ad}(u)\mathbf J)$ (\S\ref{sec:analytic-core-complements}). The \emph{background triple} of $W\in\mathsf O_{t+1}$ is $P_W=(U_+,0,J^{(t+1)}(U_+))$, $U_+$ a background over $W$ whose average $\mathcal M^tU_+$ is in the axial gauge and $J^{(t+1)}(U_+)$ its current (the background triple defined before equation~\YMMref{(827)}{395}, \S\ref{sec:normalized-step-measure}); by Thm.~\YMMref{E}{10} in the setting of Section~\YMMref{52.7}{432} at the radius $2\varepsilon_{t+1}$, $|\partial U_+(p)-\mathbf 1|$ and $|(D^{\sf T}_{U_+}\partial U_+)(b)|$ are below $\alpha\eta_{t+1}^2$ at all bare plaquettes and bonds, $\alpha:=2B_3\varepsilon_{t+1}$, and $|J^{(t+1)}(U_+)|<\alpha$ (\S\ref{sec:normalized-step-measure} at the level $t+1$).

The \emph{trivial triple} is $(\mathbf 1,0,0)$; the constant gauge transformations fix it. For a pair $v=(A,\mathbf J)$ of $1$-forms on $X$, $P[v]=(\mathbf 1,A,\mathbf J)$, and $\|v\|_X$ is the largest of $|A|$, $|\nabla A|$, $|\mathbf J|$ on the bonds of $X$ (\S\ref{sec:analytic-core-complements}). The \emph{analyticity core} $\mathcal U^\circ(X)$ is a set of complex triples on $X$ given by bounds whose radii are formed from the constants alone (Def.~\YMMref{49.1}{374}); it is carried onto itself by $P\mapsto P^u$, kept by restriction to smaller domains, holds $P_W|_X$ for tame $W$ (Prop.~\ref{prop:normalized-step-kernel}), and holds the ball of the $P[v]$, $\|v\|_X<r_\alpha$, about the trivial triple, $r_\alpha$ formed from the constants (equation~\YMMref{(933)}{427}).

Three cited facts enter. (i) \emph{The kernel.} On $\{|B|<\mathfrak b_t\}$, $\nu_W=\Xi_W^{-1}e^{\mathsf E_W}\mu_{C_W}$: the Gaussian measure $\mu_{C_W}$ of the covariance $C_W$ of the step at $P_W$, times the exponential of two local potentials, the interaction and the part of the bare array of couplings, each with a norm with quadratic growth at most $c\,\delta_t$ and below the admitted norm $w_\star$ of the cluster expansion, normalised to the mass $1$ (\eqref{eq:normalized-step-measure} and Prop.~\ref{prop:normalized-step-kernel}). (ii) \emph{The provision on the core.} At every triple $P$ of $\mathcal U^\circ(X)$, complex ones included, the Gaussian structure and both potentials of the step are given, holomorphic in $(A',\mathbf J)$ at a fixed $U$, functions of the pair, gauge covariant, local (their restrictions to a smaller domain are the objects formed there) and with the same bounds as at $P_W$ (Def.~\YMMref{52.1}{415} and Thm.~\YMMref{W}{423}); so the cluster expansion for data with up to four potentials (Thm.~\YMMref{R}{361} for the logarithm and bound; Cor.~\YMMref{47.3}{364} for an added potential and the comparison with the Gaussian part; Prop.~\YMMref{47.4}{365} for holomorphy and locality, and the covariance argument following it) bounds every cluster term on the whole core, and not only at $P_W$. (iii) \emph{A potential on a cube.} If $|\partial U-\mathbf 1|$ and $|D^{\sf T}_U\partial U|$ are below $\alpha\eta^2$ near a cube $Q$ of integer side $\mathsf l$ in level units, with $\mathsf l\alpha\le c_*$ and $\mathsf l+4$ less than half the side of the torus, then $U^{u^{-1}}=e^{i\eta A}$ on $Q$ for a gauge transformation $u$ and a real $1$-form $A$ with $|A|,|\nabla A|<B_*\mathsf l\alpha$, $B_*$ and $c_*$ formed from the constants and free of $\mathsf l$ (Thm.~\YMMref{F}{199}).
\emph{1. The exact formula.} For $t\ge1$ the shift of Prop.~\YMMref{51.5}{396}, taken at the background triple and the $1$-form $g_tB$, gives a $1$-form $\mathbf A(B)$ on the bare bonds such that $e^{i\eta_t\mathbf A(B)}U_+$ is a gauge transform of a background over $V_W(B)$ (equation~\YMMref{(827)}{395}); the loop being gauge invariant, $W^{(t)}_{\mathsf C}(V_W(B))=W_{\mathsf C}(e^{i\eta_t\mathbf A(B)}U_+)$ exactly, $\eta_t=a_K/a_{K-t}$. $\mathbf A$ is holomorphic in $B$ and in the triple, at most $\mathsf c_{\mathfrak h}\sup|g_tB|$, local through the decoupling parameters, gauge covariant and real at real data (the shift properties proved in Prop.~\YMMref{51.5}{396}). At $t=0$ there is no shift system and no decoupling parameter: $\eta_0=1$, $W^{(0)}_{\mathsf C}=W_{\mathsf C}$, and the chart itself gives $V_W(B)=e^{iB'}U_+$, $U_+=V_W(0)$, with $B'=g_0B$ on the fluctuation bonds and, at the pivot bond $b_0(c)$ of each block bond $c$, $B'(b_0(c))=\beta_c(P_W,g_0B)$, a pivot value that reads the double block of $c$ alone, vanishes at $B=0$, is at most $2C_P\sup|g_0B|$, is holomorphic in the triple and in $B$, covariant at its first end point and $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued at real data (equation~\YMMref{(804)}{391} and the bounds and covariance proved with it); we put $\mathbf A(B):=B'$.

In both cases $U':=e^{i\eta_t\mathbf A(B)}U_+$ is the configuration of the shift formula. \emph{2. Segments.} The trace does not see where a closed path begins: each $C_i$ is cut at one site, its base point, and run from there. For $s\ge i_0+m'+1$, which $s_0$ ensures, the corners are centres of cubes of side $M$ of the level $t$, and the cubes that $\mathsf C$ passes are all different; we cut $\mathsf C$ into $N=|\mathsf C|/(Ma_{K-t})$ segments, one for each such cube, the segment $j$ being the steps of the path that start in the $j$-th cube. The segments of $C_i$ form an interval $I_i$ of indices, in the order of the path from the base point, and $I=I_1<\dots<I_r$. In the frames $R_x$ carried along the loop by $U_+$, $R_x$ the product of the $U_+(b')$ over the steps of $C_i$ from the base point to $x$, the holonomy of $U'$ from the base point is $\prod^\to_{j\in I_i}(\mathbf 1+k_j)\cdot{\rm Hol}_{C_i}(U_+)$, where $\mathbf 1+k_j$ is the ordered product over the steps $b$ of the segment $j$ of $R_be^{i\eta_t\sigma_b\mathbf A(b^+)}R_b^{-1}$, $b^+$ the positively oriented bond of the step $b$, $\sigma_b=\pm1$ its orientation and $R_b$ the frame at the first end point of $b^+$ (a step against the orientation gives $U'(b)=U_+(b)e^{-i\eta_t\mathbf A(b^+)}$); $\det(\mathbf 1+k_j)=1$.

For $t\ge1$ the brackets in the decoupling parameters of the shift system (equations~\YMMref{(806)}{392}--\YMMref{(809)}{392} and Lem.~\ref{lem:analytic-rooted-bracket}) make each $k_j$ a sum of local terms over the domains of the level $t$ that hold the cube of $j$, each with a factor $e^{-c\,d}$ in its size $d$, $c>1$ formed from the constants; at $t=0$, $k_j$ is one local term, on the cube of the segment with its six neighbours. The linear part of $k_j$ in $B$, which has no component along $\mathbf 1$ (its exponents have trace $0$), and its remainder have, in the norm with quadratic growth of the cluster expansion, the sizes $\mathsf n_\ell\le c\,g_t$ and $\mathsf n_{\rm r}\le c\,g_t^2$, $c$ formed from the constants, and not $c\,\delta_t$, which is what keeps every sum below of the order $|\mathsf C|/\mathsf b$; a sum of them over any set of segments has the same norms up to the factors $3$ and $4$.

In components, $k_j=\sum_a\ell^a_j\,it_a+\sum_{\mu=0}^3r^\mu_j\tau_\mu$, $\tau_0=\mathbf 1$, $\tau_a=it_a$, with the linear parts $\ell^a_j$ and the remainders $r^\mu_j$; so the atoms of $j$ are three linear ones, with $\tau=it_a$, and four remainder ones, with $\tau=\mathbf 1$ and $\tau=it_a$, and $k^0_j=r^0_j$, $k^a_j=\ell^a_j+r^a_j$. \emph{3. Cumulants.} The linear parts and the remainders are entered as two further potentials into the cluster expansion of the step (Thm.~\YMMref{R}{361}, with four potential families,
and Prop.~\YMMref{47.4}{365} for holomorphy and locality;
the two families already in $\nu_W$ are those of
Prop.~\ref{prop:normalized-step-kernel}), the linear parts as potentials given at every real $B$, the remainders as potentials given below the threshold $\mathfrak b_t$: $\log\int\exp(\sum_\alpha z_\alpha f_\alpha)\,\mathrm{d}\nu_W=\sum_XF_X(z)$, the sum over the domains $X$ of the level $t+1$, with $F_X$ holomorphic, $F_X(0)=0$, $|F_X|\le c\,e^{-\lambda d(X)}$, $c$ and $\lambda>2$ constants of the cluster expansion ($\lambda-1$ exceeding the growth constant of the number of domains) and $d(X)$ the linear size of $X$, and $F_X$ depending on the variables of the segments in $X$ alone.

The polydisc is the one on which the inserted potentials stay below the admitted norm: its radii are $\rho_\ell=w_\star/(3\mathsf n_\ell)$, of the order $1/g_t$, in the variables of the linear atoms and $\rho_{\rm r}=w_\star/(4\mathsf n_{\rm r})$, of the order $1/g_t^2$, in those of the remainder atoms, the inverses of the sizes of step~2; they do not depend on $N$. Cauchy's estimates give all joint cumulants $\kappa(\beta)=\partial_\beta\sum_XF_X(0)$, with tree decay: a block $\beta$ with $n_\ell$ linear and $n_{\rm r}$ remainder atoms has $|\kappa(\beta)|\le\sum_Xc\,\rho_\ell^{-n_\ell}\rho_{\rm r}^{-n_{\rm r}}e^{-\lambda d(X)}$, of the order $g_t^{n_\ell+2n_{\rm r}}$, the sum over the $X$ that hold the segments of $\beta$.

We write $E(X)$ for the $X$-term of this expansion with one or two insertions, that is a first or a second derivative of $F_X$ at $z=0$, regarded as a function of the triple at which the step is formed. \emph{4. The ordered product.} By Lem.~\ref{C-372-16}(a), with $\mathfrak A=M_2(\mathbb C)^{\otimes r}$, one tensor factor for each polygon, the integral of the ordered product $\bigotimes_i\prod^\to_{j\in I_i}(\mathbf 1+k_j)$ is $Z[\kappa]$; the functional $T\mapsto2^{-r}\operatorname{tr}(T\cdot\bigotimes_i{\rm Hol}_{C_i}(U_+))$ has norm at most $1$, sends $\mathbf 1$ to $W^{(t+1)}_{\mathsf C}(W)$ and the integral of the ordered product to $\int W^{(t)}_{\mathsf C}(V_W(B))\,\nu_W(\,\mathrm{d}B)$, so that the left side of (a) is at most $|Z[\kappa]-\lambda_{t+1}\mathbf 1|$.

For all $j\le j'$ in $I$ let $\delta_{cc'}p_{jj'}$ be the second cumulant of the linear parts $\ell^c_j$, $\ell^{c'}_{j'}$ formed at the trivial triple with the frames $\mathbf 1$, under the measure of the step there; it is a multiple of $\delta_{cc'}$ by step~5, it depends neither on $W$ nor on the colour, and $p_{j'j}:=p_{jj'}$. Let $c_j:=\kappa(\{(j;{\rm r},0)\})=\int k^0_j\,\mathrm{d}\nu_W$, the first cumulant of the central remainder atom. A pair $j<j'$ of one polygon is \emph{near} if $j'-j\le N_\sharp:=\lfloor s_{\mathsf C}/(2Ma_{K-t})\rfloor$; the arc from the segment $j$ to the end of the segment $j'$ then has length at most $\frac12s_{\mathsf C}+Ma_{K-t}\le s_{\mathsf C}$ ($s_0$ ensures $N_\sharp\ge1$), so that it holds at most one corner, and it does not pass the base point.

It is \emph{straddling} if it is not near and $N_i-(j'-j)\le N_\sharp$, $N_i=\#I_i$ (near across the base point), and \emph{far} otherwise; pairs on two polygons are far. A far pair is at sup-distance at least $\rho_{\mathsf C}/a_{K-t}$ in level units, so that the domains that hold it have $d(X)\ge\rho_{\mathsf C}/(LMa_{K-t})-2$. We write $\kappa=w_{\rm g}+w_{\rm b}$, $w_{\rm g}$ the weight of Lem.~\ref{C-372-16}(b) with these $c_j$ and with $p_e=p_{jj'}$ at the near pairs $e=\{j<j'\}$, and $w_{\rm b}=\kappa-w_{\rm g}$; $w_{\rm b}$ holds the coloured singletons, the colour defects $\kappa(\{(j;\ell,a),(j';\ell,a')\})-\delta_{aa'}p_{jj'}$ of the near pairs, the other blocks with a remainder atom (all but the central singletons), the blocks of three or more atoms, and the far and the straddling pairs.

With $\mathsf g_s\ge g_t$, $N\mathsf g_s^2=\Lambda_{\mathsf C}$, and the bounds of steps~3 and~5, $|w_{\rm b}|_1\le c(1+\Lambda_{\mathsf C})\mathsf y_s^{2\mathfrak p_0}(\mathsf g_s+L^{-s/2})+c\Lambda_{\mathsf C}e^{2-\rho_{\mathsf C}L^s/LM}+c\,\#\mathsf C\,\mathsf g_s^2$, the far pairs giving the term with $\rho_{\mathsf C}$ and the straddling ones, of the order $g_t^2$ for each polygon, the term with $\#\mathsf C$. Further $\mathfrak T\le c\Lambda_{\mathsf C}$, and $\mathfrak X,\mathfrak O\le c\Lambda_{\mathsf C}\mathsf g_s^2$: a near pair that crosses a near pair $\{j_1<j_2\}$ has an end point among the $j_2-j_1$ indices between them, and $\sum_{j'}|p_{jj'}|$ and $\sum_{j'}|j'-j||p_{jj'}|$, the latter over the near pairs, are at most $c\,g_t^2$.

Lem.~\ref{C-372-16}(a), (b) give $Z[\kappa]=\exp(\sum_jc_j-3\sum_ep_e)\mathbf 1$ up to these errors. \emph{5.
