Symmetry.} What is not small by size, the first cumulants of the colour components and the colour defects of the near pairs and of the second cumulants $\langle\ell^a_j;\ell^{a'}_j\rangle$ of one segment, is small by symmetry. By fact (ii) each cluster term $E(X)$ is defined at every triple of $\mathcal U^\circ(X)$, holomorphic there in the sense of the slices, and bounded there as at $P_W$. Let $X$ be small, $d(X)\le\frac12s\log L$, and let $Q_X$ be the cube of side $\mathsf l_X=2M(d(X)+2)+1$ (level-$(t+1)$ units) about a cube of $X$; it holds $X$ and the arc of every near pair whose segments lie in $X$.

For $s\ge s_0$ the conditions of fact (iii) hold on $Q_X$ for every small $X$ ($\mathsf l_X\alpha\le c\,Ms\log L\,\varepsilon_{t+1}$ is small and $\mathsf l_X+4$ is far below the side of the torus), and fact (iii) at the $\alpha$ of step~0 gives $u$ and a real $A$ with $U_+^u=e^{i\eta_{t+1}A}$ on $Q_X$ and $|A|,|\nabla A|<B_*\mathsf l_X\alpha$; with $v_X:=(A,\operatorname{Ad}(u)J^{(t+1)}(U_+))$ on the bonds of $X$, $\|v_X\|_X<B'_*\mathsf l_X\alpha$, $B'_*=\max\{B_*,1\}$, and $(P_W|_X)^u$ and $P[v_X]$ have one pair. So the triple lies, up to the gauge transformation $u$, on the disc $\zeta\mapsto P[\zeta v_X]$, $|\zeta|<\rho_X$, about the trivial triple, inside the core by equation~\YMMref{(933)}{427}; its radius $\rho_X=\min\{r_\flat,1/(3\mathsf l_X)\}/(B'_*\mathsf l_X\alpha)$, $r_\flat$ formed from the constants, has $1/\rho_X\le cM^2\varepsilon_{t+1}(d(X)+2)^2$, $c$ formed from the constants, keeps the frames along the arcs in $Q_X$ within a factor $e$ of $\mathbf 1$, and is at least $2$ for large $s$.

The locality, the covariance and the dependence on the pair alone of the cluster terms (Prop.~\YMMref{47.4}{365} and the covariance argument following it, applied with fact (ii)) turn $E(X)$ at $P_W$, formed on the torus, into $E(X)$ at $P[v_X]$, formed on $X$, the frames being changed by one constant rotation, so that the colours are turned by one $O_X\in SO(3)$. At $\zeta=0$ the constant gauge rotations fix the trivial triple: a colour vector that they turn, the first derivative of a term in one coloured atom, vanishes there, and a bilinear form in the colours that commutes with all of them is a multiple of $\delta_{ab}$, $\mathbb C^3$ being irreducible under $SO(3)$. Schwarz' lemma for $\zeta\mapsto E(X)[P[\zeta v_X]]-E(X)[P[0]]$ on the disc gives the factor $1/\rho_X\le cM^2\varepsilon_{t+1}(d(X)+2)^2$, paid by the decay $e^{-\lambda d(X)}$; the domains with $d(X)>\frac12s\log L$ cost $e^{-\frac12s\log L}=L^{-s/2}$.

The size that this factor multiplies is the size of step~3, except for the first cumulant of a linear part, whose size is smaller: the Gaussian part of a cluster term, the same term formed with the linear insertions alone under the Gaussian measure of the step without threshold, is even under $B\mapsto-B$ (apply the covariance argument following Prop.~\YMMref{47.4}{365} to the reflection $B\mapsto-B$), so that its derivative in one linear atom vanishes at $z=0$; the first cumulant of a linear part is therefore the derivative of the difference of the term and its Gaussian part, which is at most $c\,\delta_t\,e^{-\lambda d(X)}$ (Cor.~\YMMref{47.3}{364}, equation~\YMMref{(724)}{364}): it has the amplitude $c\,\delta_t\mathsf n_\ell$, that of the non-Gaussian potentials.

With $\alpha\le c\,\mathsf g_s\mathsf y_s^{\mathfrak p_0}$, $\delta_t\le A_1\mathsf g_s\mathsf y_s^{\mathfrak p_0}$ and the sums over the $N$ segments, these are the bounds of step~4. \emph{6. Singletons.} $\det(\mathbf 1+k_j)=1$ and $\det x=(x^0)^2+\sum_a(x^a)^2$ give $(1+k^0_j)^2+\sum_a(k^a_j)^2=1$, that is $k^0_j=-\frac12\sum_a(k^a_j)^2-\frac12(k^0_j)^2$; integrated with $\int f^2\,\mathrm{d}\nu_W=\langle f;f\rangle+(\int f\,\mathrm{d}\nu_W)^2$, $\langle f;f\rangle$ the second cumulant, and with $\langle\ell^a_j;\ell^a_j\rangle=p_{jj}$ plus a diagonal defect, this gives $c_j=-\frac32p_{jj}$ up to errors of the size of step~4 (the diagonal defects, the mixed second cumulants with a remainder, the squares of first cumulants, $c_j^2$).

As $\sum_{j,j'\in I_i}p_{jj'}=\sum_{j\in I_i}p_{jj}+2\sum_{j<j'}p_{jj'}$,
\[\sum_jc_j-3\sum_ep_e=-\frac32\sum_i\sum_{j,j'\in I_i}p_{jj'}+\sum_j\bigl(c_j+\tfrac32p_{jj}\bigr)+3\!\!\sum_{j<j'\text{ in one }I_i,\text{ not near}}\!\!p_{jj'},\]
and the last two sums are of the size of the errors of step~4. \emph{7. The flat value.} At the trivial triple with the frames $\mathbf 1$ the linear part of a segment is linear in $B$, and the sum over the segments of $C_i$ of its colour component $a$ is $g_t(j_{C_i},\eta_t(\dot{\mathbf A}B)^a)=g_t(X_{C_i},\eta_t\,{\rm d}(\dot{\mathbf A}B)^a)$, $\dot{\mathbf A}$ the derivative at $0$ of $\mathcal A\mapsto\mathbf A$ formed at the trivial triple (at $t=0$ the derivative $\mathsf C_{\mathbf 1}=\mathsf C_{\mathbf 1,\mathbb R}\otimes1$ of the chart), $j_C$ the current of $C$ and ${\rm d}^{\sf T}X_C=j_C$. The linear part of the shift system at the trivial triple produces, up to one sign, the curvature response of the step: on every side of $\mathfrak L(g)$ and for $1\le t<K$ there is $\mathsf{sg}_t\in\{1,-1\}$ with $\eta_t\,{\rm d}(\dot{\mathbf A}\mathcal A)=\mathsf{sg}_t(\mathsf T^{\rm cv}_t\otimes1)\mathcal A$ for every $1$-form $\mathcal A$ on the fluctuation bonds, $\mathsf T^{\rm cv}_t=\mathsf H^{\rm cv}_t\mathsf C_{\mathbf 1,\mathbb R}$, $\mathsf H^{\rm cv}_t$ the curvature response of the level $t$ (the curvature-response construction preceding Lem.~\YMMref{120.2}{819}).

The proof follows that of Lem.~\YMMref{124.3}{835}, which is stated for data with two real sources and on large sides only; two changes make it run for the objects of the frame on every side of $\mathfrak L(g)$. First, the block field $\mathbf 1$ lies in $\mathsf O_{t+1}$, so that it has the properties that the kernel lemma of fact (i) (Prop.~\ref{prop:normalized-step-kernel}) gives to every tame block field and on which the hypotheses of (F7) rest; the configuration $\mathbf 1$ is a background over it, its average $\mathcal M^t\mathbf 1=\mathbf 1$ is in the axial gauge and its current vanishes, so that its background triple is the trivial triple; and the value of the shift on the curve below is taken from (F7) at the block field $\mathbf 1$.

Second, we use only the constrained variational equation in
the proof of Lem.~\YMMref{124.1}{832} and the curvature identity
\YMMref{(2230)}{819}. These calculations hold on every side;
the large-side identification with the full Landau inverse is
not needed. Constant gauge rotations fix the trivial triple,
so covariance makes the shift derivative commute with every
$\operatorname{Ad}(g_0)$, $g_0\in\mathrm{SU}(2)$.
It is therefore one real kernel times the identity on colours.
For real $\mathcal A$, (F7) makes
$U_\tau=e^{i\eta_t\mathbf A(\tau\mathcal A)}$ a curve of
configurations critical over their own averages. Write
$\dot A=\dot{\mathbf A}\mathcal A$ and
$\mathcal M^tU_\tau=\mathbf1+i\tau\dot V+o(\tau)$.
The cited variational calculation gives a real fine-site function
$\theta$ and a multiplier $\omega$ such that
\[
 h=\dot A+\nabla\theta,\qquad
 D_{\mathbf1}^{\mathsf T}D_{\mathbf1}h=Q^{\mathsf T}\omega,
 \qquad Qh=\dot V.
\]
Indeed, differentiation of the action on the moving constraint
kernel makes its flat Hessian pairing with $\dot A$ vanish on
the kernel of the linearized average. Factoring through that average gives the
multiplier; its value on gradients is zero, and the gauge
normalization restores the straight average $Qh=\dot V$.
Equation~\YMMref{(2230)}{819} now gives
\[
 \eta_t\,{\rm d}\dot A
 =\eta_t^2D_{\mathbf1}h
 =(\mathsf H_t^{\rm cv}\otimes1)\dot V.
\]
The chart over $\mathbf1$ identifies $\dot V$, up to a constant
rotation $\operatorname{Ad}(g_*)$, with
$\mathsf C_{\mathbf1}\mathcal A$ minus a gradient.
The curvature response annihilates this gradient. On a single
colour the remaining rotation gives a sign; linearity in
$\mathcal A$ makes it the same sign for all $\mathcal A$,
as in the last paragraph of the proof of
Lem.~\YMMref{124.3}{835}.

At $t=0$, $\mathsf H^{\rm cv}_0={\rm d}$ (the curvature-response calculation preceding Lem.~\YMMref{120.2}{819}) and the sign is $+$. At the trivial triple the covariance of the step is $\mathbf C_\ast(P_{\mathbf 1})=(\mathsf A^{\rm cv}_t)^{-1}\otimes1$, and $\mathsf T^{\rm cv}_t(\mathsf A^{\rm cv}_t)^{-1}(\mathsf T^{\rm cv}_t)^{\sf T}=\eta_t\,\mathcal C_{(t+1)}$ (Prop.~\YMMref{120.3}{819}, Prop.~\YMMref{120.3}{819}); so the Gaussian variance of the sum of the linear parts along $C_i$ is $g_t^2\eta_t(X_{C_i},\mathcal C_{(t+1)}X_{C_i})$ in each colour, the slice $(X_{C_i},\mathcal C_{(t+1)}X_{C_i})$ of the free Coulomb energy, and the sign drops out. The true pair sum differs from the Gaussian one, as in step~5, by the difference of the terms and their Gaussian parts: $\sum_{j,j'\in I_i}p_{jj'}=g_t^2\eta_t(X_{C_i},\mathcal C_{(t+1)}X_{C_i})$ up to $cN_i\delta_tg_t^2$, $N_i$ the number of segments of $C_i$.

With step~6, $\sum_jc_j-3\sum_ep_e=-\frac32S$ up to the errors of step~4, where 
\[
S:=g_t^2\eta_t\sum_i(X_{C_i},\mathcal C_{(t+1)}X_{C_i})\ge0,
\]
 $\mathcal C_{(t+1)}$ being an orthogonal projection: three colours and $\frac12\operatorname{tr}$ give $\frac32$. Between different polygons all pairs are far, and 
\[
|a_K(X_{C_i},\mathcal C_{(t+1)}X_{C_{i'}})|\le C_X|\mathsf C|e^{2-\rho_{\mathsf C}/LMa_{K-t}}
\]
 for $i\ne i'$; and $0\le a_K(X_C,\mathcal C_{(t+1)}X_C)\le C_X|C|$, $C_X$ formed from the constants. \emph{8. The label.} $g_t^2\eta_t=a_K/(a_{K-t}x_t)$ and $|1/(a_{K-t}x_t)-1/\mathsf b|\le\mathsf c\,\mathsf b^{-2}L^{-(K-t)}$, $\mathsf c=\frac54\bar B$, turn $e^{-\frac32S}$ into $\lambda_{t+1}$ up to $\frac32\mathsf cC_X\mathsf b_-^{-2}|\mathsf C|L^{-s}$, both exponents being $\le0$.

Steps~4 to~8 together give the bound, with $C'$, $C''$ formed from the constants; $\sup_s\mathsf y_s^{2\mathfrak p_0}L^{-s/4}<\infty$ and $\sup_sL^{s/4}e^{-\rho_{\mathsf C}L^s/LM}<\infty$ give $C_\eta$. The matrix form is step~4 without the trace, for one polygon from its base point.

(b) The variables are now the rotations $\Upsilon_\sigma(B)=\frac1i\log[(e^{i\eta_t\mathbf A(B)}U_+)(\sigma)U_+(\sigma)^{-1}]$ of the $|\mathsf C|/a_{K-t}$ bonds $\sigma$ of $\Lambda_{K-t}$ along $\mathsf C$, oriented as $\mathsf C$ runs (at $t=0$ the bare bonds of $\mathsf C$, with $\Upsilon_\sigma=B'(\sigma)$ at a positively oriented $\sigma$ and $-\operatorname{Ad}(U_+(\sigma))B'(\bar\sigma)$ at a reversed one), $|\Upsilon_\sigma|\le c\delta_t$, so that $W^{(t)}_{\mathsf C}(V_W(B))=w(\Upsilon(B))$, $W^{(t+1)}_{\mathsf C}(W)=w(0)$, with $w$ as in Lem.~\ref{C-372-16}(c), $g_\sigma=U_+(\sigma)$. By the brackets each $\Upsilon_\sigma$ is a sum of local terms, gauge covariant at $\sigma_-$ ($\Upsilon_\sigma\mapsto\operatorname{Ad}(u(\sigma_-))\Upsilon_\sigma$); their linear parts and remainders enter the cluster expansion as in (a), with $\log\nu_W(e^{(z,\Upsilon)})=\sum_X\ell_X(z)$ on a polydisc of radius $r_1\ge c/(n_{\mathsf C}g_t)$, one variable $z_\sigma\in\mathbb C^3$ for the whole of $\Upsilon_\sigma$.

Lem.~\ref{C-372-16}(c), with $\varrho$ the image of $\nu_W\ge0$ under $B\mapsto\Upsilon(B)$, and with $s_{\sigma\sigma'}\delta_{aa'}$ the covariance of the linear parts of $\Upsilon^a_\sigma$, $\Upsilon^{a'}_{\sigma'}$ formed at the trivial triple under the Gaussian measure of the step there (real, symmetric, free of $W$; a multiple of $\delta_{aa'}$ by the constant rotations), gives the bound with $E_1\le C_1\mathsf lg_t^2(\mathfrak b_t+\mathfrak b_t^2)\epsilon^\circ_t$, $E_2\le C_2\mathsf lg_t^2[\epsilon^\circ_t+(1+\mathfrak b_t)^2\delta_t+e^{-\mathsf D_t}]$ and $E_3\le C_3\mathsf lg_t^3$, $\mathsf l=|\mathsf C|/a_{K-t}$, where $\epsilon^\circ_t\le c(\varepsilon_{t+1}+L^{-(K-t)})$ is the price of the symmetry argument: the first cumulants and the defects of the second cumulants from $s_{\sigma\sigma'}{\rm R}(U_+(\sigma_-\to\sigma'_-))$ are small by the symmetry of (a), step 5, the transport running along the shorter arc, whose length the chord-arc constant bounds; the pairs on two polygons have $d(X)\ge\mathsf D_t$. $\sum_{\sigma,\sigma'\in C_i}s_{\sigma\sigma'}=g_t^2\eta_t(X_{C_i},\mathcal C_{(t+1)}X_{C_i})\ge0$ as in (a), step 7, and $\mathsf lg_t^2\le\frac32|\mathsf C|/\mathsf b$; the label costs $\frac94C_2\bar B|\mathsf C|\mathsf b^{-2}L^{-(K-t)}$.

For a complex $\nu_W$ of mass $1$ Lem.~\ref{C-372-16}(c) holds with the total variation as a factor. Positivity: by the disintegration with $m_t$, $m_{t+1}$, $\mathsf h_{t+1}\ge0$, $\int H(W)[\int G(V_W(B))\nu_W(\,\mathrm{d}B)]m_{t+1}(\,\mathrm{d}W)\ge0$ for all bounded Borel $H,G\ge0$; testing a countable set of continuous $G\ge0$ dense among them, the image of $\nu_W$ under $B\mapsto V_W(B)$ is a positive measure of mass $1$ for $m_{t+1}$-almost every $W$; as $V_W(B)(b)=e^{ig_tB(b)}V_W(0)(b)$ at the fluctuation bonds and $|g_tB(b)|<\delta_t<\log2$, the chart is injective with a Borel inverse on $\{|B|<\mathfrak b_t\}$, so $\nu_W$ itself is $\ge0$ for almost every $W$. The exponent $\frac12$ is the order of the error: five of its members are of the order $\frac{|\mathsf C|}{\mathsf b}x_t^{-1/2}$ up to logarithms, two of them of first order in the curvature of $W$.

For $Q_i$: $n_{Q_i}=4$ and $c_{Q_i}=\frac12$ are free of $i$, there is no distance term, and $|Q_i|/\mathsf b=4a_i/\mathsf b$.

(c), (d) A covariant insertion based at a site $x_0$ is a family of local terms of the step that turns under gauge transformations as a vector at $x_0$. For such an insertion each term $D(X;P)$ of the first cumulant, formed at the triple $P$ on a domain $X$ (the derivative at $0$ of the cluster term of $X$ with the insertion multiplied by $z$), is holomorphic in $P$ on the analyticity core and bounded there by $\mathsf A(\mathbb W)e^{-\lambda d(X)}$ (fact (ii) in step~0 of the proof of (a)), is a function of the pair, turns as a vector under constant rotations, and so vanishes at the trivial triple; a tame background on $X$ is gauge equivalent to a potential of norm $\le c\,M(d(X)+2)\varepsilon_{t+1}$, $c$ formed from the constants (fact (iii) on the cube of side $2M(d(X)+2)+1$ about $X$), as long as this cube fits into the torus and $c\,M(d(X)+2)\varepsilon_{t+1}$ stays below a number formed from the constants, the other domains costing $a_{K-t}/\ell$, resp.\ $\varepsilon_{t+1}$, with the factor $d(X)+2$; Schwarz' lemma gives $\sum_a|\int\mathbb W^{\rm tot}_a\,\mathrm{d}\nu_W|\le c\,\mathsf A(\mathbb W)\varsigma_t$, $\varsigma_t=c\varepsilon_{t+1}+6LMa_{K-t}/\ell$, where $\mathbb W^{\rm tot}_a$ is the sum of the local terms of the insertion and $\mathsf A(\mathbb W)$ its amplitude in the cluster expansion.

For the fluctuation field, an odd insertion linear in $B$, the amplitude is that of the non-Gaussian potentials, $\lesssim\delta_t$, because the Gaussian part is even: this is (d). For the rotations $\Upsilon_i$ the linear part is an odd insertion of norm $\le cg_t$ and the remainder an insertion of norm $\le cg_t^2$, so each bond costs $cg_t^2(\log x_t)^{\mathfrak p_0}\varsigma_t$; and $Ng_t^2\le c\,a_s/\mathsf b$ for the $N=4L^{K-t-s}$ bonds, which gives (c). At $t=0$ the rotations are those of the chart, step~1 of the proof of (a), and the same argument runs.

(e) As $a_{K-t}\ge a_i>c_0\varrho/2L$ and $|C|\le40\varrho$, $|C|/a_{K-t}<80L/c_0$, and $C$ lies in a cube of side less than $20L/c_0$ in the units of the level. If $\varrho/\mathsf b$ is at least a number $\eta_0>0$ formed from the constants, $c_0$, $\vartheta$ and $\mathsf J$, the bound $2$ of the defect at $\nu_W\ge0$ is at most $C_*\frac\varrho{\mathsf b}(\frac{c_0\varrho}{2L\mathsf b})^\vartheta\le C_*\frac\varrho{\mathsf b}(\frac{a_{K-t}}{\mathsf b})^\vartheta$ for $C_*\ge2(2L/c_0)^\vartheta\eta_0^{-1-\vartheta}$; so let $\varrho/\mathsf b<\eta_0$, and with it $a_{K-t}/\mathsf b\le a_*/\mathsf b=(\varrho/\mathsf b)^{3/(3+\vartheta)}$, $g_t$, $\delta_t$ and $\varepsilon_{t+1}$ be small, and $K-t$ large.

The proof of (b) runs with the pieces of $C$ in the cubes of the level in the place of the bonds of the level. \emph{The exact formula.} Step~1 of the proof of (a) holds for every bare loop, the corners entering nowhere: $W^{(t)}_C(V_W(B))=W_C(U')$, $U'=e^{i\eta_t\mathbf A(B)}U_+$, at every level. \emph{Pieces.} From a base point, $C$ is cut into the maximal runs $C_1,\dots,C_n$ of consecutive steps that start in one of the half-open cubes of side $a_{K-t}$ about the sites of $\Lambda_{K-t}$, the cubes of the level that $C$ passes; each of the four sides of $C$ gives at most its length over $a_{K-t}$ plus $2$ of them, so that $n<80L/c_0+8$, a number formed from $L$ and $c_0$. With $g_j=U_+(C_j)$, the holonomy of $U_+$ along the piece, and $\Upsilon_j(B)=\frac1i\log[U'(C_j)\,U_+(C_j)^{-1}]\in\mathfrak{su}(2)$, one has $|\Upsilon_j|\le c\,\delta_t|C_j|/a_{K-t}$, $c$ formed from the constants (the shift is at most $\mathsf c_{\mathfrak h}\sup|g_tB|$, at $t=0$ at most $2C_P\sup|g_0B|$, at each of the $|C_j|/a_K$ bare steps, and $\eta_t|C_j|/a_K=|C_j|/a_{K-t}$), and $W^{(t)}_C(V_W(B))=w(\Upsilon(B))$, $W^{(t+1)}_C(W)=w(0)$, with $w$ as in Lem.~\ref{C-372-16}(c) for one line.

\emph{Insertions.} By the brackets each $\Upsilon_j$ is a sum of local terms of the level, gauge covariant at the first end point of $C_j$, with a linear part in $B$ of norm at most $c\,g_t|C_j|/a_{K-t}$ and a remainder of norm at most $c\,g_t^2\frac{|C_j|}{a_{K-t}}(1+\frac{|C_j|}{a_{K-t}})$ in the norm of the cluster expansion; each piece is one insertion, of norm of the order $g_t$ times its length over $a_{K-t}$. Entered into the cluster expansion of the step as in step~3 of the proof of (a), they give $\log\nu_W(e^{(z,\Upsilon)})=\sum_X\ell_X(z)$, one variable $z_j\in\mathbb C^3$ for the whole of $\Upsilon_j$, on a polydisc of radius $r_1\ge c\,a_{K-t}/(g_t|C|)\ge c\,c_0/(Lg_t)\ge2$, and Cauchy's estimates give a cumulant of order $m$ the factor $(c\,g_t|C|/a_{K-t})^m$ and the decay of its domains.

\emph{Symmetry.} Let $s_{jj'}\delta_{aa'}$ be the covariance of the linear parts of $\Upsilon^a_j$, $\Upsilon^{a'}_{j'}$ formed at the trivial triple under the Gaussian measure of the step there (real, symmetric, free of $W$; a multiple of $\delta_{aa'}$ by the constant rotations). At the trivial triple the first cumulants, colour vectors, vanish, and the pair cumulants are multiples of $\delta_{aa'}$, which differ from $s_{jj'}\delta_{aa'}$ by parts of the relative size $c\,\delta_t$, from the non-Gaussian potentials, and $c\,g_t$, from the remainders (step~5 of the proof of (a)). For a domain $X$ that holds pieces of $C$, with $d(X)\le\frac12(K-t)\log L$, fact (iii) of step~0 of the proof of (a), on a cube of side at most $2M(d(X)+2)+1+40L/c_0$ that holds $X$ and $C$, where its conditions hold for $\varrho/\mathsf b<\eta_0$, puts the background triple, up to a gauge transformation, on a disc about the trivial triple whose radius $\rho_X$ has $1/\rho_X\le c\,\varepsilon_{t+1}(d(X)+2)^2$, $c$ formed from the constants, $L$ and $c_0$, the frames along $C$ staying within a factor $e$ of $\mathbf 1$; Schwarz' lemma on this disc bounds the terms of $X$ of the first cumulants, and of the pair cumulants less their values at the trivial triple turned by the frames, by $1/\rho_X$ times their size, paid by the decay $e^{-\lambda d(X)}$, and the domains with $d(X)>\frac12(K-t)\log L$ cost $L^{-(K-t)/2}$.

So the first cumulants and the defects $d_{jj'}$ of the pair cumulants from $s_{jj'}{\rm R}(G_{j\to j'})$ carry, relative to their size, the factor $c\,(\varepsilon_{t+1}+L^{-(K-t)/2}+\delta_t+g_t)$, and the first cumulant of a linear part carries besides the amplitude $c\,\delta_t$ of the non-Gaussian potentials, its Gaussian part being even. \emph{The pair term.} The argument of step~7 of the proof of (a) holds for every bare loop: at the trivial triple with the frames $\mathbf 1$ the sum of the linear parts of the $\Upsilon_j$ is $g_t\eta_t(j_C,\dot{\mathbf A}B)$, so that $S:=\sum_{j,j'}s_{jj'}=g_t^2\eta_t(X_C,\mathcal C_{(t+1)}X_C)\ge0$, the slice of the free Coulomb energy at the step, at the depths coarser than the corners as at the finer ones.

By Prop.~\ref{C-372-11}(c), (d), which hold at every depth, $0\le a_K(X_C,\mathcal C_{(t+1)}X_C)=v_{K,K-t}(C)-v_{K,K-t-1}(C)\le C^{\rm bg}A_C^2/a_{K-t}^3\le c\,|C|$, with the area $A_C\le100\varrho^2$ of $C$, $|C|\ge4c_0\varrho$ and $c$ formed from $L$ and $c_0$; so step~8 of the proof of (a) turns $e^{-\frac32S}$ into $\lambda_{t+1}$ up to $c\,|C|\mathsf b^{-2}a_{K-t}$. \emph{The bound.} Lem.~\ref{C-372-16}(c), its measure being the image of $\nu_W\ge0$ under $B\mapsto\Upsilon(B)$, a probability measure on $\{|y_j|\le c\,\delta_t|C|/a_{K-t}\}$, bounds the defect by $E_1+E_2+E_3$ and this term of the label, the sum over two lines being empty. With $g_t^2\le\frac32a_{K-t}/\mathsf b$, $\delta_t=g_t\mathfrak b_t$, $\varepsilon_{t+1}$ and $L^{-(K-t)/2}$ of the order $(a_{K-t}/\mathsf b)^{1/2}$ up to logarithms, and the sizes above, each of $E_1$, $E_2$, $E_3$ is at most $\frac{|C|}{\mathsf b}(\frac{a_{K-t}}{\mathsf b})^{1/2}y_t^{\mathfrak p}$, $y_t=\log x_t$, $\mathfrak p$ formed from $\mathfrak p_0$, times a polynomial in $|C|/a_{K-t}$ with coefficients formed from the constants and $\mathsf J$, and the term of the label is at most $c\frac{|C|}{\mathsf b}\frac{a_{K-t}}{\mathsf b}$.

As $|C|/a_{K-t}<80L/c_0$, $|C|\le40\varrho$ and $(\frac{a_{K-t}}{\mathsf b})^{1/2}y_t^{\mathfrak p}\le c\,(\frac{a_{K-t}}{\mathsf b})^\vartheta$ for $\vartheta<\frac12$, $c$ formed from the constants, $\vartheta$ and $\mathsf J$, the defect is at most $C_*\frac\varrho{\mathsf b}(\frac{a_{K-t}}{\mathsf b})^\vartheta$. The mean over the block field follows, $|\bar{\mathsf D}_{t+1}|$ being at most the bound of the defect at $m_{t+1}$-almost every $W$ times $Z^{-1}m_{t+1}(\mathcal V_{K-t-1})\le1$. The levels finer than the corners are treated in the statement of (e) itself.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Numbers of the free field]\label{C-372-11}
Let $L\ge3$ be odd, $\ell=2L^m$, and $C$ a polygon with corners in $\Lambda_i$; no measure and no $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ enter.
(a) For $K\ge i$ and $a=a_K$: $\mathcal I_a(C,C)=\frac{|C|}{2\pi}\log\frac1a+c_{\rm lat}|C|+\mathcal J_\ell(C)+E_a(C)$ with $|E_a(C)|\le c[n_Ca(1+\log\frac{|C|}a)+a^2|C|^2{\rm Lg}(\ell/a)(\delta_C^{-3}+\ell^{-3})]$, $c$ absolute; pieces in perpendicular directions do not interact in the sum; $|\mathcal J_\ell(C)-\mathcal J(C)|\le c|C|^2{\rm diam}(C)^2\ell^{-3}$; for a rectangle $s\times t$,
\[\mathcal J(C)=\frac1\pi\Bigl[s\log s+t\log t-s\operatorname{asinh}\frac st-t\operatorname{asinh}\frac ts+2\sqrt{s^2+t^2}-2(s+t)\Bigr].\]
For polygons $C$, $D$ at distance $\delta>0$: $|\mathcal I_a(C,D)-\mathcal I_\ell(C,D)|\le ca^2|C||D|\,{\rm Lg}(\ell/a)(\delta^{-3}+\ell^{-3})$.
(b) For $0\le d\le K$ and every closed path $C'$ of $\Lambda_K$, $v_{K,d}(C')$ is the largest value of $2\mathcal I_{a_K}(j_{C'},Q^{\sf T}\iota)-\mathcal I_{a_K}(Q^{\sf T}\iota,Q^{\sf T}\iota)$ over the closed currents $\iota$ of $\Lambda_d$ without zero mode, $Q$ the linearisation of $\mathcal M^{K-d}$ at the trivial field (the mean over a block of the straight bare paths): the energy of the best smeared current. For the polygon $C$ and $i\le d\le K$,
\[v_{K,d}(C)=\frac{|C|}{2\pi}\log\frac1{a_d}+(c_{\rm lat}+c_{r,K-d})|C|+\mathcal J_\ell(C)+{\rm Rem}_{K,d}(C),\]
$|{\rm Rem}_{K,d}(C)|\le|E_{a_d}(C)|+c[n_C^2a_d+n_Ca_d(1+\log\frac{|C|}{a_d})+a_d|C|^2/\delta_C^2]$, a bound free of $K$. Here the numbers $c_{r,j}$, $j\ge0$ an integer, are formed as $c_r$ in the setting, with $S_{(j)}(z)=\frac{\sin(z/2)}{L^j\sin(z/2L^j)}$ in the place of $S(z)$, $E_{(j)}(p_\nu)=4L^{2j}\sin^2\frac{p_\nu}{2L^j}$ in the place of $p_\nu^2$ in the denominators, and the sums over the $n\in\mathbb Z^2$ with $|n_2|,|n_3|\le\frac{L^j-1}2$ in the places of the sums over $\mathbb Z^2$, in $\mathsf N$ and in $\mathsf D$; at $j=K-d$, $L^j=a_d/a_K$ is the ratio of the two spacings. The number $c_{r,j}$ depends on $L^j$ alone, $c_{r,0}=0$ (then $S_{(0)}=1$ and only $n=0$ enters), $|c_{r,j}|\le c_3$, and $c_{r,j}\to c_r$ as $j\to\infty$. The limit $v_d=\lim_Kv_{K,d}$ exists and obeys the same remainder bound:
\[\Bigl|v_d-\frac{|C|}{2\pi}\log\frac1{a_d}-c_Q|C|-\mathcal J_\ell(C)\Bigr|\le |E_{a_d}(C)|+c\Bigl[n_C^2a_d+n_Ca_d\Bigl(1+\log\frac{|C|}{a_d}\Bigr)+\frac{a_d|C|^2}{\delta_C^2}\Bigr].\]
For a fixed polygon the right side is $O_{C,\ell}(a_d(1+\log^+(1/a_d)))$ as $d\to\infty$. The constants $c$ and $c_3$ are free of the side; $c_Q$ is a number of the plane, free of $L$, $\ell$ and $C$.
(c) $\prod_{n\le K-d}\lambda_n=\exp[-\frac3{2\mathsf b}(\mathcal I_{a_K}(C,C)-v_{K,d}(C))]$ for all $0\le d\le K$. Hence for $i\le d\le K$
\[a_K^{-\kappa}\prod_{n\le K-d}\lambda_n=L^{\kappa d}\exp\Bigl[\frac3{2\mathsf b}\bigl(c_{r,K-d}|C|+{\rm Rem}_{K,d}(C)-E_{a_K}(C)\bigr)\Bigr],\]
and one step, $n=K-d$ with $d\ge i$, gives $\lambda_n=L^{-\kappa}\exp[-\frac3{2\mathsf b}((c_{r,n-1}-c_{r,n})|C|+{\rm Rem}_{K,d+1}-{\rm Rem}_{K,d})]$: each step takes away $\kappa\log L$ and a multiple of the length; the steps sum to $\sum_{n\ge1}(c_{r,n-1}-c_{r,n})=-c_r=c_{\rm lat}-c_Q$, every term depending on $L$ and the sum not. For families, $c_\Xi^{-1}L^{\kappa d}\le a_K^{-\kappa}\Xi_{K-d}\le c_\Xi L^{\kappa d}$ for $i_0\le d\le K$, with $c_\Xi$ free of $d$ and $K$ and uniform for $\mathsf b$ in a compact set, and $\mathsf l_d=\lim_Ka_K^{-\kappa}\Xi_{K-d}=a_d^{-\kappa}\exp[-\frac3{2\mathsf b}((c_{\rm lat}-c_Q)|\mathsf C|+O_{\mathsf C,\ell}(a_d(1+\log^+(1/a_d))))]$, so $a_d^\kappa\mathsf l_d\to e^{-0.047235\ldots|\mathsf C|/\mathsf b}$.
(d) For a rectangle $C$ of area $A$ with corners in $\Lambda_K$, in any position, and $0\le d\le K$: $0\le v_{K,d}(C)\le C^{\rm bg}A^2/a_d^3$, $C^{\rm bg}$ absolute.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof]
(a) Fourier analysis of $g_N$: a component of the current couples only to the same component, so perpendicular pieces do not meet; the sum of $g_N$ along an axis gives the logarithm and the constant $c_{\rm lat}$, a computation with the lattice Green function on a line; the torus gives $\mathcal J_\ell$; distant pieces are compared with the continuum with an error $O(a^2)$, the corners with an error $O(a)$ each. The formula for the rectangle is the double integral of $\frac1{4\pi|x-y|}$ over its four sides, the parallel pieces interacting with the sign $-1$ and the perpendicular ones not at all. (b) The range of $\Pi_{K-d}$ is spanned by the curvatures of the bare fields $\Delta^{-1}Q^{\sf T}\iota$, $\iota$ a closed current of $\Lambda_d$ (the Lagrange multiplier of the linearised background problem); as $(X,\Pi X)$ is the largest value of $2(X,Y)-(Y,Y)$ over the range and $(X_{C'},{\rm d}A)=(j_{C'},A)$, $v_{K,d}$ is the stated maximum, at every depth and for every closed bare path.

Since the corners of the polygon lie in $\Lambda_d$ for $d\ge i$, the Fourier transform of the sharp loop at the momenta $(q+2\pi n)/a_d$ is the transform $\hat\jmath(q)$ of its chain on $\Lambda_d$ times the form factor of one bond; the quadratic form is diagonal in $q$ and in the direction of the current, and the maximum is solved mode by mode. Without the constraint that $\iota$ be closed one gets $a_dN^{-3}\sum_{q\ne0}\sum_\mu|\hat\jmath_\mu(q)|^2\mathsf m^{(K-d)}_\mu(q)$, $N=\ell/a_d$, where $\mathsf m^{(j)}_\mu=(\mathsf N^{(j)}_\mu)^2/\mathsf D^{(j)}_\mu$ is the propagator that the block averages see: with $p=q+2\pi n$, $s_{(j)}(p)=\prod_\nu S_{(j)}(p_\nu)$ and $\Delta_{(j)}(p)=\sum_\nu E_{(j)}(p_\nu)$, $\mathsf N^{(j)}_\mu$ sums, over the aliases ($n$ in the $L^{3j}$ classes $|n_\nu|\le\frac{L^j-1}2$ at a finite cutoff, $j=K-d$, and in $\mathbb Z^3$ at $K=\infty$, where $S_{(\infty)}=S$ and $E_{(\infty)}(z)=z^2$), the bare propagator $1/\Delta_{(j)}(p)$ times the form factors $S_{(j)}(p_\mu)$ of the sharp bond and $S_{(j)}(p_\mu)s_{(j)}(p)$ of the smeared bond, and $\mathsf D^{(j)}_\mu$ the same with the smeared bond twice; at $q_\mu=0$ only $n_\mu=0$ survives, and they reduce to the sums $\mathsf N$, $\mathsf D$ of $c_{r,j}$ (of $c_r$ at $K=\infty$).

The constraint costs a non-negative term at most $cn_C^2a_d$: with $\partial_\mu(q)=e^{iq_\mu}-1$ and $\langle z,z'\rangle=\sum_\mu\bar z_\mu z'_\mu$, $\langle\partial(q),\hat\jmath(q)\rangle=0$ for a closed $C$ (the sum over the steps telescopes), $|\bar\partial_\mu\hat\jmath_\mu|$ is at most twice the number of pieces in the direction $\mu$, $\mathsf N^{(j)}_\mu/\mathsf D^{(j)}_\mu$ differs from $1/s_{(j)}(q)$, the inverse form factor of the block, which does not depend on $\mu$, by $O(|q|^2)$, and $\sum_\mu|\partial_\mu|^2/\mathsf D^{(j)}_\mu\ge c|q|^4$. With $\Delta_1(q)=\sum_\nu4\sin^2\frac{q_\nu}2$, the symbol $\mathsf m^{(j)}_\mu-1/\Delta_1$ is bounded with derivatives at most $c|q|^{-|\alpha|}$, $c$ free of $j$; its kernel falls like $|x|^{-2}$; along one straight piece of $n$ bonds its sum gives $c_{r,j}$ per unit length (the sum along an axis is the integral over the plane $q_\mu=0$, whence the two-dimensional formula) up to $O(a_d(1+\log n))$, and parallel pieces at distance $\ge\delta_C$ interact through it by $O(a_d|C|^2/\delta_C^2)$.

With (a) at the spacing $a_d$ this gives the law at every finite cutoff, with a remainder free of $K$; $c_{r,j}\to c_r$ by dominated convergence, and $|c_{r,j}|\le c_3$ by the bound on the symbol. (c) $\sum_{n\le K-d}\mathcal C_{(n)}=\Pi_0-\Pi_{K-d}$ at every $d$, and $a_K(X_C,\Pi_0X_C)=\mathcal I_{a_K}(C,C)$; insert (a) and (b): $\frac3{2\mathsf b}\frac{|C|}{2\pi}\log\frac{a_d}{a_K}=\kappa\log\frac{a_d}{a_K}$; one step is $a_K(X_C,\mathcal C_{(K-d)}X_C)=v_{K,d+1}-v_{K,d}$.

For families the factors multiply, and one may take $c_\Xi=\prod_i\exp[\frac3{2\mathsf b}(c_3|C_i|+2\mathsf r_i)]$, $\mathsf r_i$ the supremum over $d\ge i_0$ of the bound on $|{\rm Rem}_{K,d}(C_i)|$ in (b), which also bounds $|E_{a_K}(C_i)|$ for $K\ge d$. (d) $v_{K,d}\ge0$, $\Pi_{K-d}$ being an orthogonal projection. It vanishes on the $2$-cochains $Y$ with ${\rm d}^{\sf T}Y=0$, as its range consists of exact cochains; so $v_{K,d}(C)=a_K(X,\Pi_{K-d}X)$ for every $2$-cochain $X$ with ${\rm d}^{\sf T}X=j_C$, in particular for $X$ the indicator of the bare plaquettes of the rectangle, with $\|X\|_1=\sum_p|X(p)|=A/a_K^2$. The maximum of (b) holds at every depth $0\le d\le K$ for this bare current, wherever the corners lie (corners in $\Lambda_d$ are needed only to factor $\hat\jmath$ in the proof of (b)).

Drop the constraint that $\iota$ be closed: the maximum can only grow. With $\mathfrak q=a_d/a_K=L^{K-d}$, the bare momenta $\varkappa=(q+2\pi n)/\mathfrak q$, $q\in(2\pi/N)\mathbb Z^3$, $|n_\nu|\le\frac{\mathfrak q-1}2$, and $p=\mathfrak q\varkappa$, the transform of $Q^{\sf T}\iota$ at $\varkappa$ is $\hat\iota_\mu(q)\varphi_\mu(\varkappa)$, $|\varphi_\mu(\varkappa)|=\mathfrak q|S_{(K-d)}(p_\mu)s_{(K-d)}(p)|$ the form factor of the smeared bond, and $\Delta_1(\varkappa)=\mathfrak q^{-2}\Delta_{(K-d)}(p)$; the maximum over all $\iota$, taken mode by mode, gives
\[v_{K,d}(C)\le a_K(N\mathfrak q)^{-3}\sum_{q\ne0}\sum_\mu\frac{|\mathcal B_\mu(q)|^2}{\mathfrak q^4\mathsf D^{(K-d)}_\mu(q)},\qquad\mathcal B_\mu(q)=\sum_n\frac{\hat\jmath_\mu(\varkappa)\,\overline{\varphi_\mu(\varkappa)}}{\Delta_1(\varkappa)},\]
$\hat\jmath$ the transform of the bare current $j_C$. Three bounds hold uniformly in $\mathfrak q$: $|\hat\jmath_\mu(\varkappa)|\le\Delta_1(\varkappa)^{1/2}\|X\|_1$, as $j_C={\rm d}^{\sf T}X$ and $\sum_\nu|e^{i\varkappa_\nu}-1|^2=\Delta_1(\varkappa)$; $\sum_n|S_{(K-d)}(p_\mu)s_{(K-d)}(p)|\Delta_{(K-d)}(p)^{-1/2}\le c/|q|$, the term $n=0$ being at most $(0.3|q|)^{-1}$ and, for $n\ne0$, each one-dimensional factor at most $51/\max\{1,|n_\nu|\}$ and $\Delta_{(K-d)}(p)\ge0.2|n|^2$, so that the terms $n\ne0$ add up to at most $c\sum_n\prod_\nu\max\{1,|n_\nu|\}^{-4/3}$; and $\mathsf D^{(K-d)}_\mu(q)\ge0.3^8|q|^{-2}$ ($S_{(j)}\ge0.3$ on $[-\frac32\pi,\frac32\pi]$ and $E_{(j)}(z)\le z^2$). So $|\mathcal B_\mu(q)|\le c\,\mathfrak q^2\|X\|_1/|q|$, each of the $N^3$ modes contributes at most $c\|X\|_1^2$, and $v_{K,d}(C)\le c\,a_K\mathfrak q^{-3}\|X\|_1^2=c\,A^2/a_d^3$, as $a_K\mathfrak q=a_d$: $C^{\rm bg}$ is absolute, for every odd $L\ge3$, every $0\le d\le K$ and every position. Equivalently, the kernel of $\Pi_{K-d}$ on the bare plaquettes is at most $c\,(a_K/a_d)^3$ in modulus: at one plaquette this is the bound on the diagonal, and Schwarz' inequality gives the rest.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The tower]\label{C-372-12}
In the frame let $F=W_{\mathsf C}$ and let $0\le\bar t\le K$ be the last level of the tower.
(a) Suppose $|\int W^{(t)}_{\mathsf C}(V_W(B))\,\nu_W(\,\mathrm{d}B)-\lambda_{t+1}W^{(t+1)}_{\mathsf C}(W)|\le\eta_{t+1}$ for $m_{t+1}$-almost every $W$ and $0\le t<\bar t$, and put $\mathsf e_t=\sum_{s\le t}\Xi_{s-1}\eta_s$. Then $|\Phi^{(t)}[F]-\Xi_tW^{(t)}_{\mathsf C}|\le\mathsf e_t$ $m_t$-almost everywhere for $t\le\bar t$, and
\[\Bigl|\langle F\rangle_K-\Xi_{\bar t}\frac1Z\int W^{(\bar t)}_{\mathsf C}\,\mathrm{d}m_{\bar t}\Bigr|\le\mathsf e_{\bar t}+\sum_{t\le\bar t}(\Xi_{t-1}+\mathsf e_{t-1})\mathsf w_t;\]
the same holds with a further factor $H(\mathcal M^{K-s_1}U)$ in $\langle F\rangle_K$ and $H\circ\mathcal M^{K-\bar t-s_1}$ in the integral, for $H$ bounded Borel gauge invariant on $\mathcal V_{s_1}$ and $K-\bar t\ge s_1$, with $\sup|H|$ multiplying the right side. No positivity of $\nu_W$ is used.
(b) Without any hypothesis, let $\mathsf A_t=Z^{-1}\int W^{(t)}_{\mathsf C}\,\mathrm{d}m_t$ and $\bar{\mathsf D}_t=Z^{-1}\int[\int W^{(t-1)}_{\mathsf C}(V_W(B))\,\nu_W(\,\mathrm{d}B)-\lambda_tW^{(t)}_{\mathsf C}(W)]\,m_t(\,\mathrm{d}W)$, the mean of the defect of the step over the block field. Then $\mathsf A_{t-1}=\lambda_t\mathsf A_t+\bar{\mathsf D}_t+\omega_t$ with $|\omega_t|\le\mathsf w_t$, and so
\[\langle W_{\mathsf C}\rangle_K=\Xi_{\bar t}\mathsf A_{\bar t}+\sum_{t\le\bar t}\Xi_{t-1}(\bar{\mathsf D}_t+\omega_t):\]
as an identity between numbers, only the means of the defects over the block field enter.
(c) On gauge invariant Borel sets $\mu^K_{K-\bar t}-Z^{-1}m_{\bar t}$ is a positive measure of mass $\sum_{t\le\bar t}\mathsf w_t$, and $1-2\mathsf V_\ell C_{\rm r}(1)L^{-(K-\bar t)}\le Z^{-1}m_{\bar t}(\mathcal V_{K-\bar t})\le1$.
(d) For a coordinate rectangle $C$ with sides $s_1$, $s_2$: $1-\frac12\theta_d^2\le W^{(K-d)}_C\le1$ on $\mathsf O_{K-d}$, with $\theta_d=2B_3\varepsilon_{K-d}L^{2d}s_1s_2$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof]
(a) For $m_{t+1}$-almost every $W$,
\[
\begin{multlined}
\Phi^{(t+1)}[F](W)-\Xi_{t+1}W^{(t+1)}_{\mathsf C}(W)=\int[\Phi^{(t)}[F]-\Xi_tW^{(t)}_{\mathsf C}](V_W(B))\,\nu_W(\,\mathrm{d}B) \\
+\Xi_t\Bigl[\int W^{(t)}_{\mathsf C}(V_W(B))\,\nu_W(\,\mathrm{d}B)-\lambda_{t+1}W^{(t+1)}_{\mathsf C}(W)\Bigr].
\end{multlined}
\]
The second member is at most $\Xi_t\eta_{t+1}$ almost everywhere by hypothesis. The first, $\tilde\Psi(W):=\int\Psi_t(V_W(B))\,\nu_W(\,\mathrm{d}B)$ with $\Psi_t:=\Phi^{(t)}[F]-\Xi_tW^{(t)}_{\mathsf C}$, is at most $\mathsf e_t$ in modulus for $m_{t+1}$-almost every $W$ whenever $|\Psi_t|\le\mathsf e_t$ $m_t$-almost everywhere; this duality step reads only $m_t,m_{t+1},\mathsf h_{t+1}\ge0$. The disintegration at $G=\Psi_t$, a bounded Borel function, and the transport identity $\int G'\,\mathrm{d}m_{t+1}=\int(G'\circ\mathcal M)\,\mathsf h_{t+1}\,\mathrm{d}m_t$ at $G'=|H|$ give, for every bounded Borel $H$,
\[\Bigl|\int H\tilde\Psi\,\mathrm{d}m_{t+1}\Bigr|=\Bigl|\int(H\circ\mathcal M)\,\Psi_t\,\mathsf h_{t+1}\,\mathrm{d}m_t\Bigr|\le\mathsf e_t\int|H\circ\mathcal M|\,\mathsf h_{t+1}\,\mathrm{d}m_t=\mathsf e_t\int|H|\,\mathrm{d}m_{t+1};\]
at $H=\overline{{\rm sgn}\,\tilde\Psi}\,\mathbf 1\{|\tilde\Psi|>\mathsf e_t+\epsilon\}$ this says $(\mathsf e_t+\epsilon)\,m_{t+1}(|\tilde\Psi|>\mathsf e_t+\epsilon)\le\mathsf e_t\,m_{t+1}(|\tilde\Psi|>\mathsf e_t+\epsilon)$, so the set has measure $0$, for every $\epsilon>0$. No law of $V_W(B)$, no null set of $m_t$ under $\nu_W$ and no positivity of $\nu_W$ enter. Induction on $t$, with $\mathsf e_{t+1}=\mathsf e_t+\Xi_t\eta_{t+1}$; then \eqref{C-372-2} with $|W^{(t)}_{\mathsf C}|\le1$ and $|\Phi^{(t-1)}[F]|\le\Xi_{t-1}+\mathsf e_{t-1}$. With $H$: $\Phi^{(t)}[W_{\mathsf C}\,H\circ\mathcal M^{K-s_1}]=\Phi^{(t)}[W_{\mathsf C}]\,H\circ\mathcal M^{K-t-s_1}$ for $K-t\ge s_1$. (b) For gauge invariant bounded Borel $G$ on $\mathcal V_{K-t+1}$, \eqref{C-372-2} at $F=G\circ\mathcal M^{t-1}$ for $\bar t=t-1$ and $\bar t=t$, with $\Phi^{(t-1)}[G\circ\mathcal M^{t-1}]=G$ (functions pull out and $\Phi^{(t-1)}[1]=1$), gives $\int G\,\mathrm{d}m_{t-1}=\int G\,(\mathsf h_t+\mathsf h^{\rm w}_t)\,\mathrm{d}m_{t-1}$.

At $G=W^{(t-1)}_{\mathsf C}$ the disintegration with $H=1$ turns $Z^{-1}\int W^{(t-1)}_{\mathsf C}\mathsf h_t\,\mathrm{d}m_{t-1}$ into $\lambda_t\mathsf A_t+\bar{\mathsf D}_t$, and $\omega_t=Z^{-1}\int W^{(t-1)}_{\mathsf C}\mathsf h^{\rm w}_t\,\mathrm{d}m_{t-1}$; $\mathsf A_0=\langle W_{\mathsf C}\rangle_K$. (c) \eqref{C-372-2} at $F=\mathbf 1_E\circ\mathcal M^{\bar t}$, $E$ gauge invariant: $Z\mu^K_{K-\bar t}(E)-m_{\bar t}(E)=\sum_{t\le\bar t}\int(\mathbf 1_E\circ\mathcal M^{\bar t-t+1})\mathsf h^{\rm w}_t\,\mathrm{d}m_{t-1}\ge0$, of total mass $Z\sum_{t\le\bar t}\mathsf w_t$; the rarity bound at $p=0$ in its summed form. (d) Over a tame field the background has bare plaquettes $<2B_3\varepsilon_{K-d}(a_K/a_d)^2$ (Thm.~\YMMref{E}{10} in the setting of Section~\YMMref{52.7}{432}), and $1-W_{\partial R}\le(\sum_{p\subset R}\sqrt{a_p})^2$ over the $s_1s_2/a_K^2$ plaquettes of the rectangle (Prop.~\ref{C-372-13}(c)).
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Identities and inequalities at every cutoff]\label{C-372-13}
For every $\beta>0$, every torus and every cutoff:
(a) $\mathcal W^{(L^z\ell,L^z\mathsf b)}_{K-z}(L^z\mathsf C;f^{(z)})=L^{-z\kappa-zn}\mathcal W^{(\ell,\mathsf b)}_K(\mathsf C;f_1,\dots,f_n)$, $f^{(z)}_q=f_q(L^{-z}\cdot)$;
(b) if families $G_1,\dots,G_s$ lie in the interior of $S^+_\theta$ for a coordinate mirror $\theta$ and the supports of the tuples $f_i$ lie in $S^+_\theta$ (and do not meet the fixed planes if $\theta$ is a bond mirror), then $\sum_{i,j}\bar c_ic_j\mathcal W_K(\theta G_i,G_j;\theta f_i,f_j)\ge0$ for all complex $c_i$; so $\mathcal W_K(G_1,\theta G_2)^2\le\mathcal W_K(G_1,\theta G_1)\,\mathcal W_K(G_2,\theta G_2)$ for real entries; if $\theta$ cuts a loop $C_{12}$ into two halves and $C_{11}$, $C_{22}$ are the loops made of each half and its mirror image, then $\mathcal W_K(C_{12})^2\le\mathcal W_K(C_{11})\,\mathcal W_K(C_{22})$;
(c) the plaquette mean $\langle W_{\partial p}\rangle_K$ is $>0$; for bare rectangles $p\times q$ with $p,q<\ell/2a_K$, $w(p,q)=\langle W_{p\times q}\rangle_K\ge w(1,1)^{pq}>0$, and $\log w$ is convex in $p$ and in $q$; and $0\le1-W_{\partial R}\le(\sum_{p\subset R}\sqrt{a_p})^2$ for every field and every rectangle $R$.
For the rectangles $s\times T$ of one coordinate plane, $s$ and $T$ lengths in $\bigcup_ia_i\mathbb Z$, put $\mathcal W(s\times T):=\lim_K\mathcal W_K(s\times T)=\lim_Ka_K^{-\kappa}\langle W_{s\times T}\rangle_K$, $\kappa=\kappa(s\times T)$, wherever the limit exists. A \emph{range} of the limits is a set of such rectangles on which they exist and are finite, closed downwards (with $s\times T$ it holds every $s'\times T'$ with $s'\le s$, $T'\le T$) and open upwards (with $s\times T$ it holds a rectangle with both sides larger); in the frame, and by dilation on every torus and at every label, the polygons $s\times T$ with $\kappa<\frac12$ form one (Thm.~\ref{C-372-4}(1)--(3)). Every limit inherits (a), (b), $\mathcal W\ge0$ and the midpoint inequality $\mathcal W(s\times\frac{T'+T''}2)^2\le\mathcal W(s\times T')\,\mathcal W(s\times T'')$, and the same in $s$, whenever the three rectangles lie in a range, the powers of $a_K$ matching because $2|s\times\frac{T'+T''}2|=|s\times T'|+|s\times T''|$; a limit that is $>0$ at one rectangle of a range is $>0$ at all rectangles of that range. Strict positivity of a limit is not inherited; it comes from the floor of Thm.~\ref{C-372-4}(4).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof]
(a) The Wilson measure at $(K,\ell,\mathsf b)$ is the one at $(K-z,L^z\ell,L^z\mathsf b)$ relabelled, as $\beta=L^K\mathsf b=L^{K-z}(L^z\mathsf b)$: lengths are multiplied by $L^z$, $\kappa$ is unchanged, $a_K^{-\kappa}$ gains $L^{-z\kappa}$ and each $\mathcal O(f)$ the factor $L^{-z}$. (b) Reflection positivity of the Wilson measure at site and bond mirrors, for functions of the bonds of one closed (resp.\ open) half torus, and Schwarz' inequality: each $a_K^{-\kappa(G_i)}W_{G_i}\prod_q(\mathcal O(f_{iq})-\langle\mathcal O(f_{iq})\rangle_K)$ lives on one side of $\theta$, and the powers of $a_K$ split because lengths add. For the cut loop, $W_{C_{12}}=\frac12\operatorname{tr}(U(\gamma_1)U(\gamma_2))$ with the two halves $\gamma_1$, $\gamma_2$, and reflection positivity for matrix-valued functions with Schwarz' inequality gives the bound; $|C_{11}|+|C_{22}|=2|C_{12}|$. (c) $s\mapsto\log\int e^{s\sum_p\frac12\operatorname{tr}\partial U(p)}\,\mathrm{d}U$ has the derivative $0$ at $s=0$ (the Haar mean of a non-trivial character vanishes) and is strictly convex, so its derivative at $s=\beta$, the number of plaquettes times the plaquette mean, is $>0$.

Reflection positivity in the two directions of the plane of the rectangle gives $w(p,q)^2\le w(p,q-1)\,w(p,q+1)$ and the same in $p$; with $w(p,0)=1$ the ratios $w(p,q)/w(p,q-1)$ increase, so $w(p,q)\ge w(p,1)^q\ge w(1,1)^{pq}$. For $g\in\mathrm{SU}(2)$, $1-\frac12\operatorname{tr}g=\frac12|g-\mathbf 1|^2$; the holonomy of $\partial R$ is an ordered product of conjugated plaquette variables, and $|\prod_ig_i-\mathbf 1|\le\sum_i|g_i-\mathbf 1|$. Limits keep $\ge0$, the positive forms and the inequalities; the midpoint inequality of $\mathcal W_K$ is the convexity of $\log w$ in each side, multiplied by $a_K^{-2\kappa(s\times\frac{T'+T''}2)}=a_K^{-\kappa(s\times T')-\kappa(s\times T'')}$, at every cutoff at which the three rectangles have their corners in $\Lambda_K$.

Spreading in a range $\mathsf R$, the limits being finite there (Thm.~\ref{C-372-4}(1)): if $\mathcal W(s\times T_0)>0$ and $s\times(T_0\pm\epsilon)\in\mathsf R$, the product $\mathcal W(s\times(T_0-\epsilon))\,\mathcal W(s\times(T_0+\epsilon))\ge\mathcal W(s\times T_0)^2>0$ of two finite numbers $\ge0$ makes both positive; going down from the lowest positive point with an upper point of $\mathsf R$ fixed, the distance to it doubles at each step, so that every $T$ below $T_0$ is reached, and upwards in the same way with a lower point; then the same in $s$; and two rectangles of $\mathsf R$ are joined through the one with the smaller sides, which lies in $\mathsf R$. The values of $\epsilon$ are taken in $\bigcup_ia_i\mathbb Z$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[A source off the loop]\label{C-372-14}
In the frame let $f_1,\dots,f_n$ be real Lipschitz, $\|f\|_\sharp=\max\{\sup|f|,40M\,{\rm Lip}f\}$, and $z$ in the polydisc $\sum_q|z_q|\|f_q\|_\sharp<\rho_D$, where $\rho_D=2\varrho_S/(2e^{(C_S+C_g)\ell^3}+2)$ is formed from the radius $\varrho_S$ and the constants $C_S$, $C_g$ of Thms.~\YMMref{AJ}{673} and~\YMMref{AD}{607}; $\rho_D$ depends on neither $K$ nor $\mathsf b\in\mathsf I(g)$. Write $w_z=\sum_qz_qf_q$. The radius estimates below are stated for a family with $\max_q\|f_q\|_\sharp>0$. If every $f_q$ vanishes, the source is zero, its derivatives of positive order vanish, and the assertions reduce directly to the zero-source statements.
(a) $\langle e^{\mathcal O(w_z)}\rangle_K=e^{\mathcal E(w_z)}h_K(z)$ with $\frac12\le|h_K(z)|\le\frac32$, whatever the supports, $\mathcal E(w)$ a sum of local energies of the source; the energies of sources $v_i=\sum_qz^{(i)}_qf^{(i)}_q$, $i=1,\dots,s$, $f^{(i)}_q$ real Lipschitz, with $\sum_i\sum_q|z^{(i)}_q|\|f^{(i)}_q\|_\sharp<\rho_D$ and supports at pairwise sup-distance $\ge2\delta$, add up to an error: $|\mathcal E(\sum_iv_i)-\sum_i\mathcal E(v_i)|\le\Delta_s(\delta)=c(s+1)(\ell/2\delta)^3$, $c$ formed from the constants of Thms.~\YMMref{AJ}{673} and~\YMMref{AD}{607}, free of $K$; so, with $\mathsf e(v)=|\langle e^{\mathcal O(v)}\rangle_K|$, $\frac12(\frac23)^se^{-\Delta_s(\delta)}\prod_i\mathsf e(v_i)\le\mathsf e(\sum_iv_i)\le\frac32\,2^se^{\Delta_s(\delta)}\prod_i\mathsf e(v_i)$; we write $\Delta(\delta)=\Delta_2(\delta)$. In particular $\langle e^{\mathcal O(w_z)}\rangle_K\ne0$ on the polydisc, for all $K$.
(b) The objects of the frame exist with the weight $e^{\mathcal O(w)}$. For complex bounded $w$ and bounded Borel $F$ on $\mathcal V_K$ let $m^w_t[F]=\Phi^{(t)}[Fe^{\mathcal O(w)}]\,m_t$, a complex measure on $\mathcal V_{K-t}$, and $m^w_t=m^w_t[1]$. Then $\int G\,\mathrm{d}m^w_t[F]=\int(G\circ\mathcal M)\,\mathsf h_t\,\mathrm{d}m^w_{t-1}[F]$ for bounded Borel $G$, and, for gauge invariant $F$ and $G$ and $0\le\bar t\le K$, the sum over the level of the first creation of a large field
\[
\begin{aligned}
Z\bigl\langle F\,G(\mathcal M^{\bar t}U)\,e^{\mathcal O(w)}\bigr\rangle_K
&=\int G\,\mathrm{d}m^w_{\bar t}[F]\\
&\quad+\sum_{t\le\bar t}\int(G\circ\mathcal M^{\bar t-t+1})\,\mathsf h^{\rm w}_t\,\mathrm{d}m^w_{t-1}[F].
\end{aligned}
\]
At real $w$ only, $\Phi^{(t)}[e^{\mathcal O(w)}]>0$ $m_t$-almost everywhere, and the quotients 
\[
\Phi^{(t),w}[F]=\Phi^{(t)}[Fe^{\mathcal O(w)}]/\Phi^{(t)}[e^{\mathcal O(w)}],
\]
 with $|\Phi^{(t),w}[F]|\le\sup|F|$, and the kernel 
\[
\nu^w_W(dB)=\Phi^{(t)}[e^{\mathcal O(w)}](V_W(B))\,\nu_W(dB)/\Phi^{(t+1)}[e^{\mathcal O(w)}](W),
\]
a probability measure for $m_{t+1}$-almost every $W$, obey \eqref{C-372-2} and the disintegration for $(m^w,\nu^w)$, with $Z\langle e^{\mathcal O(w)}\rangle_K$ in the place of $Z$; $m^w_t$ is then a positive measure with the null sets of $m_t$, and on gauge invariant sets $\mu^{K,w}_{K-\bar t}-m^w_{\bar t}/(Z\langle e^{\mathcal O(w)}\rangle_K)$ is a positive measure of mass $\sum_{t\le\bar t}\mathsf w^w_t$, $\mathsf w^w_t=(Z\langle e^{\mathcal O(w)}\rangle_K)^{-1}\int\mathsf h^{\rm w}_t\,\mathrm{d}m^w_{t-1}$, $\mu^{K,w}_d$ being the law of $\mathcal M^{K-d}U$ under $e^{\mathcal O(w)}\langle\cdot\rangle_K/\langle e^{\mathcal O(w)}\rangle_K$.

The rarity bound holds with a source, at complex $z$ for the integral of $\mathsf h^{\rm w}_t$: 
\[
|Z\langle e^{\mathcal O(w)}\rangle_K|^{-1}|\int\mathsf h^{\rm w}_t\,\mathrm{d}m^w_{t-1}|\le\mathsf V_SC^S_{\rm r}(p)L^{-p(K-t)},
\]
with $\mathsf V_S$, $C^S_{\rm r}(p)$ formed from the constants of Thms.~\YMMref{D}{8}, \YMMref{AJ}{673} and~\YMMref{AD}{607}, $p$ and $\ell$; at real $z$ this bounds $\mathsf w^w_t$, and $\sum_{t\le\bar t}L^{\kappa(K-t)}\mathsf w^w_t\le2\mathsf V_SC^S_{\rm r}(\kappa+1)L^{-(K-\bar t)}$.
(c) For bounded Borel gauge invariant $F$ on $\mathcal V_d$, 
\[
\mu^{K,w_z}_d(F)=\langle F(\mathcal M^{K-d}U)e^{\mathcal O(w_z)}\rangle_K/\langle e^{\mathcal O(w_z)}\rangle_K
\]
 obeys $|\mu^{K,w_z}_d(F)|\le B_d\sup|F|$, with $B_d$ formed from the constants of Thms.~\YMMref{D}{8}, \YMMref{AJ}{673} and~\YMMref{AD}{607}, $d$, $\mathsf b$ and $\ell$, and free of $K$. The limit $\mu^{w_z}_d(F)=\lim_K\mu^{K,w_z}_d(F)$ exists for $z$ in the polydisc $|z_q|<\rho_*:=\rho_D/(n\max_q\|f_q\|_\sharp)$, which lies in the polydisc of the head and is free of $K$, uniformly on its half $|z_q|\le\frac12\rho_*$ and in $\sup|F|\le1$; it is holomorphic in $z$, a probability measure at real $z$, and $\mu^w_{d+1}(\mathcal M^{-1}E)=\mu^w_d(E)$. No condition on the supports is asked; so the derivatives at $z=0$, the mixed functions of $F(\mathcal M^{K-d}U)$ and of the $\mathcal O(f_q)$, converge too.
(d) If a coordinate mirror $\theta$ parts $\mathsf C$, at distance $\ge\delta_1$ from its planes, from the supports, at distance $\ge\delta$, and $z$ lies in half the polydisc, then for every bounded function $X$ of the bonds on the side of $\mathsf C$
\[|\langle Xe^{\mathcal O(w_z)}\rangle_K|\le M_0\|X\|_\theta\,|\langle e^{\mathcal O(w_z)}\rangle_K|,\qquad\|X\|_\theta^2=\langle X\,\overline{\theta X}\rangle_K\ge0,\qquad M_0=\sqrt6\,e^{\Delta(\delta)/2};\]
so $|Q_K(z)|\le M_0\,\mathcal W_K(\mathsf C,\theta\mathsf C)^{1/2}$. For two orthogonal mirrors, the sources in two groups as in Thm.~\ref{C-372-4}(6), and $z$ in a quarter of the polydisc, $\sum_q|z_q|\|f_q\|_\sharp<\rho_D/4$ (for one mirror, half the polydisc is $\sum_q|z_q|\|f_q\|_\sharp<\rho_D/2$), 
\[
|\langle Xe^{\mathcal O(w_z)}\rangle_K|^4\le M_0'^4\langle X\,\overline{\theta_1X}\,\overline{\theta_2X}\,\theta_1\theta_2X\rangle_K\,|\langle e^{\mathcal O(w_z)}\rangle_K|^4
\]
 for $X$ on the side of $\mathsf C$ of both mirrors, $M_0'^4=24\cdot36\cdot(\frac92)^4e^{\Delta_4(\delta)+6\Delta_2(\delta)}$, the mean on the right holding no source and being $\ge0$. Where equally spaced coordinate walls part the polygons from the supports as in Thm.~\ref{C-372-4}(6), with an even number of boxes in each direction that the walls cut, so that both fixed planes $c$ and $c+\frac\ell2$ of every wall mirror are walls ($N$ boxes in all; on $\ell=2L^m$, with walls in $\frac12a_i\mathbb Z$, the number of slabs in a cut direction divides $4L^{m+i}$, and it is taken even, $2L^j$ or $4L^j$), and with each $f_q$ supported in one box: $\langle W_{\mathsf C^{\rm f}_\iota}\rangle_K\ge0$, $\kappa(\mathsf C^{\rm f}_\iota)=N\kappa(\mathsf C_\iota)$, and
\[
\begin{multlined}
|Q_K(z)|\le M_S\prod_\iota\mathcal W_K(\mathsf C^{\rm f}_\iota)^{1/N}\quad\text{for }\sum_q|z_q|\|f_q\|_\sharp<\rho_D/N,\qquad M_S \\
=2(\tfrac32)^{n_{\rm b}}e^{\Delta_{n_{\rm b}}(\delta)}\bigl[\tfrac32\,2^Ne^{\Delta_N(\delta)}\bigr]^{n_{\rm b}/N},
\end{multlined}
\]
$n_{\rm b}$ the number of boxes that meet the supports and $\delta$ the distance of the supports to the walls; a function whose support misses the walls is the sum of such pieces, one for each box.
(e) $\mathcal W_K(\mathsf C;f_1,\dots,f_n)=\sum_{A}\partial_AQ_K(0)\,\partial_{A^c}E_K(0)$, $E_K(z)=\langle\exp\sum_qz_q(\mathcal O(f_q)-\langle\mathcal O(f_q)\rangle_K)\rangle_K$, and $\partial_{A^c}E_K(0)=\sum_\pi\prod_{\beta\in\pi}S^{\sf T}_{|\beta|,K}(f_\beta)$, $\pi$ over the partitions of $A^c$ into blocks of at least two elements: only the derivatives of $Q_K$ in pairwise different variables enter.
(f) Let $0<\vartheta'\le1$, $\bar t(K)=K-\lceil\vartheta'K\rceil$, $\eta=(24\ell^3\sum_q\sup|f_q|)^{-1}$, and let $q_{K,\bar t}(z)=a_K^{-\kappa}\int\Phi^{(\bar t)}[W_{\mathsf C}e^{\mathcal O(w_z)}]\,\mathrm{d}m_{\bar t}\big/\int\Phi^{(\bar t)}[e^{\mathcal O(w_z)}]\,\mathrm{d}m_{\bar t}$ be the same quotient formed with the measure $m_{\bar t}$ without large fields. For every multi-index $\alpha$, with $p=(4|\alpha|+\kappa+1)/\vartheta'$, and all $K$ with $2\mathsf V_\ell C_{\rm r}(p)L^{-p\vartheta'K}\le0.16$: $|\partial^\alpha Q_K(0)-\partial^\alpha q_{K,\bar t(K)}(0)|\le14\,\alpha!\,\eta^{-|\alpha|}\mathsf V_\ell C_{\rm r}(p)L^{-K}$: the Taylor coefficients of $Q_K$ at $0$ are those of the chain without large fields.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof]
(a) Thms.~\YMMref{AJ}{673} and~\YMMref{AD}{607} for the Wilson measure with the source $w_z$ writes $\langle e^{\mathcal O(w_z)}\rangle_K$ as $e^{\mathcal E(w_z)}h$, $\mathcal E(w)=\sum_{j\le K}\sum_Xe_j(X;w)$ a sum of local terms $e_j(X;w)$ over the levels $j$ and the domains $X$ of the level $j$, which read $w$ near $X$ alone and vanish at $w=0$, with $|e_j(X;w)|\le C_Se^{-\kappa_Sd_j(X)}$, $\kappa_S$ the decay number of Thms.~\YMMref{AJ}{673} and~\YMMref{AD}{607} and $d_j(X)$ the size of $X$ in cubes of side $M$ of the level $j$; and $h$ holomorphic with $h(0)=1$ and $|h|\le e^{(C_S+C_g)\ell^3}$. With $\|z\|=\sum_q|z_q|\|f_q\|_\sharp$, Schwarz' lemma for $\zeta\mapsto h(w_{\zeta z})-1$ on $|\zeta|<2\varrho_S/\|z\|$ gives $|h-1|\le\frac12$ on the polydisc.

In $\mathcal E(\sum_iv_i)-\sum_i\mathcal E(v_i)$ a local term that sees one support alone cancels; one that sees two supports at sup-distance $\ge2\delta$ belongs to a domain $X$ with $d_j(X)\ge2\delta L^{K-j}/M-4$ and is at most $(s+1)C_Se^{-\kappa_Sd_j(X)}$; the sum over such domains and levels is at most $c(s+1)(\ell/2\delta)^3$. The bounds on $\mathsf e(\sum_iv_i)$ follow, as $\frac12e^{{\rm Re}\,\mathcal E(v)}\le\mathsf e(v)\le\frac32e^{{\rm Re}\,\mathcal E(v)}$ for every source $v$ of the polydisc. (b) A history is linear in the bare density, so $\Phi^{(t)}[Fe^{\mathcal O(w)}]$ is the density of the history without large fields with the source, at complex $w$ as well. The transport identity is that of the frame at $Fe^{\mathcal O(w)}$, and the sum over the first creation is \eqref{C-372-2} at the gauge invariant function $F\,(G\circ\mathcal M^{\bar t})\,e^{\mathcal O(w)}$, the factor $G\circ\mathcal M^{\bar t}$ pulling out of $\Phi^{(\bar t)}$ and of $\Phi^{(t-1)}$ as $G$ and as $G\circ\mathcal M^{\bar t-t+1}$.

The quotients and the kernel are formed at real $w$: there $e^{\mathcal O(w)}\ge e^{-\sup|\mathcal O(w)|}>0$ gives, at every level $t$, $\Phi^{(t)}[e^{\mathcal O(w)}]\ge e^{-\sup|\mathcal O(w)|}$ off one $m_t$-null set $\mathcal N_t$, so $m^w_t$ has the null sets of $m_t$. The kernel $\nu^w_W$ is $\nu_W$ times the density $B\mapsto\Phi^{(t)}[e^{\mathcal O(w)}](V_W(B))/\Phi^{(t+1)}[e^{\mathcal O(w)}](W)$, and it is a probability measure for $m_{t+1}$-almost every $W$: $\nu_W\ge0$ for $m_{t+1}$-almost every $W$ (Prop.~\ref{C-372-10}(b)); the denominator is $\ge e^{-\sup|\mathcal O(w)|}$ for $W\notin\mathcal N_{t+1}$; the numerator is $\ge e^{-\sup|\mathcal O(w)|}$ off $V_W^{-1}\mathcal N_t$, and $\nu_W(V_W^{-1}\mathcal N_t)=0$ for $m_{t+1}$-almost every $W$, the one set $\mathcal N_t$ being fixed first and the exceptional set of $W$ depending on it: the disintegration at $G=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal N_t}$ gives $\int H(W)\,\nu_W(V_W^{-1}\mathcal N_t)\,m_{t+1}(\,\mathrm{d}W)=\int(H\circ\mathcal M)\,\mathbf 1_{\mathcal N_t}\,\mathsf h_{t+1}\,\mathrm{d}m_t=0$ for every bounded Borel $H$; and the mass is $1$ by the disintegration at $F=e^{\mathcal O(w)}$, $\Phi^{(t+1)}[e^{\mathcal O(w)}](W)=\int\Phi^{(t)}[e^{\mathcal O(w)}](V_W(B))\,\nu_W(\,\mathrm{d}B)$ for $m_{t+1}$-almost every $W$.

The disintegration for $(m^w,\nu^w)$ is that of the frame at $G\,\Phi^{(t)}[e^{\mathcal O(w)}]$. The wild mass is a sum over the histories of the level $K$ in which a large field is created at the step $t$; Thms.~\YMMref{AJ}{673} and~\YMMref{AD}{607} bounds every history with a source as Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8} bounds it without one, with the constants of Thms.~\YMMref{AJ}{673} and~\YMMref{AD}{607}, and (a) bounds the denominator below; the rarity bound then follows as in the square-completion estimate \eqref{eq:ward-age-square} and the geometric-series calculation in the proof of Prop.~\ref{prop:ward-fixed-volume-rarity}, with the constants of Thms.~\YMMref{AJ}{673} and~\YMMref{AD}{607}. (c) Thms.~\YMMref{AJ}{673} and~\YMMref{AD}{607} at one depth bounds $|\langle F(\mathcal M^{K-d}U)e^{\mathcal O(w_z)}\rangle_K|$ by $\sup|F|$ times a number free of $K$ times $|\langle e^{\mathcal O(w_z)}\rangle_K|$: this is $B_d$.

For the limit let $\sup|F|\le1$ and $G_K(z)=\mu^{K,w_z}_d(F)$, holomorphic and bounded by $B_d$ on the polydisc $|z_q|<\rho_*$. We use an interpolation inequality: if $G$ is holomorphic on the polydisc of radius $\rho$ in $n$ variables, $|G|\le B$ there and $|G|\le\sigma$ on the real cube $[-r,r]^n$, $0<r\le\rho/2$, then its Taylor coefficients at $0$ obey $|c_\alpha(G)|\le C_{n,j}r^{-|\alpha|}(\sigma+2B(r/\rho)^{j+1})$ for $|\alpha|\le j$ (the Taylor polynomial of order $j$ is within $2B(r/\rho)^{j+1}$ of $G$ on the cube, by Cauchy's estimates on the complex lines through $0$, and on the polynomials of order at most $j$ in $n$ variables the largest coefficient and the supremum on a cube are two norms).

It suffices that every coefficient $c_\alpha(G_K)$ converges, uniformly in $F$: Cauchy's estimate $|c_\alpha(G_K)|\le B_d\rho_*^{-|\alpha|}$ makes the tails of the Taylor series small on $|z_q|\le\frac12\rho_*$, uniformly in $K$ and $F$. For $\alpha=0$ this is Cor.~\textup{\ref{IV-62-66}}. Fix $j=|\alpha|\ge1$. The proof of the limit laws of the block fields compares two consecutive cutoffs through the small-field chains at the depth $u=\lceil\phi_1K\rceil$, $\phi_1=1/(180(3N'+4))$, $N'$ the number of the test functions (\S\ref{sec:cutoff-calibration}); we prolong the tuple $f$ by copies of $f_1$ to $N'=\max\{n,j^2\}$ functions, the new variables being $0$, so that $u\ge d$ for large $K$. Let $G^{\rm sf}_K$ be the quotient of $F$ formed with the weight of the history without large-field regions down to the depth $u$, and $D_K=G_K-G^{\rm sf}_K$; then $c_\alpha(G_{K+1})-c_\alpha(G_K)=c_\alpha(D_{K+1})-c_\alpha(D_K)+c_\alpha(G^{\rm sf}_{K+1}-G^{\rm sf}_K)$, and the interpolation inequality is used twice, on two polydiscs. (i) On the polydisc of radius $\rho'=(24n\ell^3L^{4(K+1)}\max_q\sup|f_q|)^{-1}$, on which $|\mathcal O(w_z)|\le\frac14$ at the cutoffs $K$ and $K+1$ (there are $3(\ell/a_K)^3$ plaquettes and $0\le a_p\le2$), $|G_K|,|G^{\rm sf}_K|<1.8$ and $|D_K|\le3.6$; at its real points the measure without large-field regions is below the full one with a mass defect of the order of the rarity at the depth $u$, so that $|D_K|\le C\exp[3K\log L-cK^2]$, below every power of $L^K$; with $r=L^{-(4j+1)K}\rho'$ the coefficients of $D_K$ are at most $C(L^{(4j^2+5j+3)K}e^{-cK^2}+L^{-K})$, summable in $K$. (ii) On the polydisc on which the proof of the limit laws bounds the small-field chains, of radii $\rho''$ with $1/\rho''\le cK^{2\mathfrak p_0}L^{3u}$, so that $\rho''^{-j}\le(cK^{2\mathfrak p_0})^jL^{3j+K/(180j)}$ by $3\phi_1j\le1/(180j)$, which is where $N'\ge j^2$ enters, $|G^{\rm sf}_K|\le1.8$; at its real points that proof goes through with the source, the contact terms of the source standing in a factor that drops out of the quotient, and gives $|G^{\rm sf}_{K+1}-G^{\rm sf}_K|\le cK^{2\mathfrak p_0+1/2}L^{-K/10}$; with $r=L^{-K/(90j)}\rho''$ the coefficients are at most a power of $K$ times $L^{K(-\frac1{10}+\frac1{90}+\frac1{180j})}+L^{K(-\frac1{90j}+\frac1{180j})}$, summable in $K$, both exponents being negative.

So every $c_\alpha(G_K)$ converges with a summable rate, uniformly in $\sup|F|\le1$, and $G_K$ converges uniformly on $|z_q|\le\frac12\rho_*$; the limit is holomorphic, a complex measure of mass $1$ in $F$ (a limit, uniform in $\sup|F|\le1$, of such measures), a probability measure at real $z$, where the $\mu^{K,w}_d$ are, and $\mathcal M$-compatible, as $\mu^{K,w}_{d+1}(\mathcal M^{-1}E)=\mu^{K,w}_d(E)$ at every $K$. (d) Reflection positivity at $\theta$ and Schwarz' inequality give $|\langle XH\rangle_K|^2\le\|X\|_\theta^2\langle\overline{\theta H}H\rangle_K$ for $H$ on the other side; at $H=e^{\mathcal O(w)}$, $\overline{\theta H}H=e^{\mathcal O(w+w^\theta)}$ with $w^\theta=\overline{\theta w}=\sum\bar z_q\theta f_q$.

The mean, not the energy, is invariant: $\langle e^{\mathcal O(w^\theta)}\rangle_K=\overline{\langle e^{\mathcal O(w)}\rangle_K}$, as $\theta$ is a symmetry of the Wilson measure and the $a_p$ are real. By (a) for $w$, $w^\theta$ and $w+w^\theta$, which lie in the polydisc of the head as $z$ lies in its half and whose supports lie $2\delta$ apart, $\langle e^{\mathcal O(w+w^\theta)}\rangle_K\le\frac32e^{\Delta}e^{{\rm Re}\,\mathcal E(w)+{\rm Re}\,\mathcal E(w^\theta)}$, and $e^{{\rm Re}\,\mathcal E(v)}\le2|\langle e^{\mathcal O(v)}\rangle_K|$ at $v=w$ and $v=w^\theta$; so $\langle e^{\mathcal O(w+w^\theta)}\rangle_K\le6e^{\Delta}|\langle e^{\mathcal O(w)}\rangle_K|^2$. At $X=W_{\mathsf C}$, $\|W_{\mathsf C}\|_\theta^2=\langle W_{\mathsf C}W_{\theta\mathsf C}\rangle_K=a_K^{2\kappa}\mathcal W_K(\mathsf C,\theta\mathsf C)$.

Two mirrors: Schwarz at $\theta_1$ with $Xe^{\mathcal O(w_2)}$ on the side of $\mathsf C$, then at $\theta_2$; the sources that arise hold four images of the second group and two of the first, pairwise $2\delta$ apart, and together they stay in the polydisc of (a), $\sum_q|z_q|\|f_q\|_\sharp<\rho_D$ with each $z_q$ counted as often as its images, as soon as $z$ lies in a quarter of it; then (a) bounds the source factors. Walls: in a cut direction with an even number $n$ of slabs the reflections in the walls map walls to walls, both fixed planes of each being walls, and generate the $n/2$ translations by even multiples of the width and $n/2$ reflections, a group of $n$ elements that acts simply transitively on the slabs; so each box has exactly one image in every box, an image has a parity (the number of reflections modulo $2$), and the folds below are defined. (With an odd number of slabs the translation by one width lies in the group, and so does the reflection of a box in its own mid-plane, which is no wall; the evenness excludes this.) The chessboard estimate $|\langle\prod_\iota F_\iota\rangle_K|\le\prod_\iota\langle{\rm Fold}\,F_\iota\rangle_K^{1/N}$ for functions $F_\iota$ of the bonds of the boxes, ${\rm Fold}\,F_\iota$ the product of the $N$ images of $F_\iota$ under the group (conjugated at the odd ones), each $\langle{\rm Fold}\,F_\iota\rangle_K$ being $\ge0$, is applied with $F_\iota=W_{\mathsf C_\iota}$ for a box with polygons, $F_\iota=e^{\mathcal O(w_\iota)}$ for a box with a support, $w_\iota$ the part of $w$ in it, and $F_\iota=1$ otherwise. ${\rm Fold}\,W_{\mathsf C_\iota}=W_{\mathsf C^{\rm f}_\iota}$, with $\kappa(\mathsf C^{\rm f}_\iota)=N\kappa(\mathsf C_\iota)$, so that the powers of $a_K$ split. ${\rm Fold}\,e^{\mathcal O(w_\iota)}=e^{\mathcal O(\sum_gw^g_\iota)}$, the $N$ images $w^g_\iota$ lying in different boxes, pairwise $2\delta$ apart, each with $\mathsf e(w^g_\iota)=\mathsf e(w_\iota)$ and together in the polydisc of (a) for $\sum_q|z_q|\|f_q\|_\sharp<\rho_D/N$; by (a) at $s=N$, $\langle{\rm Fold}\,e^{\mathcal O(w_\iota)}\rangle_K^{1/N}\le[\frac32\,2^Ne^{\Delta_N(\delta)}]^{1/N}\mathsf e(w_\iota)$.

In the denominator, (a) at $s=n_{\rm b}$ gives $|\langle e^{\mathcal O(w)}\rangle_K|\ge\frac12(\frac23)^{n_{\rm b}}e^{-\Delta_{n_{\rm b}}(\delta)}\prod_\iota\mathsf e(w_\iota)$; the factors $\mathsf e(w_\iota)$ cancel and $M_S$ remains. (e) Leibniz' rule for $\partial_{\{1,\dots,n\}}[Q_K(z)E_K(z)]$ at $0$; the derivatives of $E_K$ at $0$ in pairwise different variables are sums over the partitions of products of joint cumulants, the blocks of one element vanishing because the $\mathcal O(f_q)$ are centred. (f) \eqref{C-372-2} at $F=W_{\mathsf C}e^{\mathcal O(w_z)}$ and at $F=e^{\mathcal O(w_z)}$, on the polydisc $|z_q|\le\eta a_K^4$, where $|\mathcal O(w_z)|\le\frac14$ (there are $3(\ell/a_K)^3$ plaquettes and $0\le a_p\le2$), together with the rarity bound at $p$, bounds the difference of the two quotients by $c\mathsf V_\ell C_{\rm r}(p)a_K^{-\kappa}L^{-p(K-\bar t)}$; Cauchy's estimate on this polydisc costs $\alpha!(\eta a_K^4)^{-|\alpha|}$, and $p(K-\bar t)\ge(4|\alpha|+\kappa+1)K$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Three free photon fields]\label{C-372-15}
(a) Uniformly in $K$, $\mathbb P(\max_p|F^{(d)}(p)|\ge2\varepsilon_{[d]})\le18\ell^3L^{3d}e^{-\frac23A_0^2(\log x_{[d]})^{2\mathfrak p_0}}$, and the probability that some plaquette with a corner in a set $S$ of sites of $\Lambda_d$ has $|F^{(d)}(p)|\ge2\varepsilon_{[d]}$ is at most $72\,\#S\,e^{-\frac23A_0^2(\log x_{[d]})^{2\mathfrak p_0}}$. These are bounds at one depth, uniform in $K$: the first has the form of $R^\natural_d$, with $18$ and $\frac23$ in the place of $1$ and $c^\natural$, the second the local form of Prop.~\ref{C-372-8}(c), with $72$ and $\frac23$ in the place of $1$ and $c^\natural$; summed over the depths $d\ge D$ (a union bound) they bound the probability that some depth $d\ge D$ has a plaquette with $|F^{(d)}(p)|\ge2\varepsilon_{[d]}$. There the smoothing is linear and needs no ball.
(b) For a family $\mathsf C=(C_1,\dots,C_r)$, at every length,
\[a_K^{-\kappa}\,\mathbb E\prod_iW^{\rm fr}_{C_i}\to\prod_ie^{-\frac3{2\mathsf b}[c_{\rm lat}|C_i|+\mathcal J_\ell(C_i)]}\Bigl[2^{-r}\sum_{\epsilon\in\{\pm1\}^r}e^{-\frac1{\mathsf b}\sum_{i<j}\epsilon_i\epsilon_j\mathcal I_\ell(C_i,C_j)}\Bigr]^3>0;\]
at $r=2$ the bracket is $\cosh(\mathcal I_\ell(C_1,C_2)/\mathsf b)$.
(c) For one loop the step is exact: the conditional mean of $W^{{\rm fr},(t)}_C$, the loop of the conditional mean of the field given the block field of the level $t$, given the block field of the level $t+1$ is $\lambda_{t+1}W^{{\rm fr},(t+1)}_C$; for a family the defect is at most $(e^{3x}-1)\lambda_{t+1}$, $x=\frac1{\mathsf b}\sum_{i<j}|a_K(X_{C_i},\mathcal C_{(t+1)}X_{C_j})|$, which for polygons at fixed distances falls faster than every power of $a_{K-t}$; so for families the factor without cross terms is the right one. The exponent $\kappa$, the perimeter constant $c_{\rm lat}|C|+\mathcal J_\ell(C)$ and the factor $\lambda_{t+1}$ of one step are those of three free photon fields.
(d) At every cutoff $K$, for every polygon $C$ with corners in $\Lambda_K$ and every bounded real $f$,
\[\frac{\mathbb E[W^{\rm fr}_C\mathcal O^{\rm fr}(f)]}{\mathbb E\,W^{\rm fr}_C}-\mathbb E\,\mathcal O^{\rm fr}(f)=-\frac3{2\mathsf b^2}\,a_K^{-1}\sum_pf(x(p))\,\mathcal I_{a_K}(C,\partial p)^2.\]
If $C$ has its corners in a fixed $\Lambda_i$ and $f$ is Lipschitz with support at positive distance from $C$, then as $K\to\infty$
\[
\begin{multlined}
-\frac3{2\mathsf b^2}\,a_K^{-1}\sum_pf(x(p))\,\mathcal I_{a_K}(C,\partial p)^2\ \relax \longrightarrow\ \relax -\frac3{2\mathsf b^2}\int_{T_\ell}f(x)\,|B_{C,\ell}(x)|^2\,\mathrm{d}x,\qquad B_{C,\ell}(x) \\
={\rm curl}_x\oint_CG_\ell(x-y)\,\mathrm{d}y,
\end{multlined}
\]
the field of $C$ on the torus; in the ball of radius $<\ell/4$ that holds the polygon, $|B_{C,\ell}(x)-B_C(x)|\le c\,|C|\,{\rm diam}(C)\,\ell^{-3}$, $c$ absolute, with $B_C(x)=\oint_C\frac{dy\times(x-y)}{4\pi|x-y|^3}$ the Biot--Savart field of $C$ in $\mathbb R^3$. For a bounded $f$ that is not Lipschitz the sums over the plaquette centres need not tend to the integral: an $f$ that vanishes at the plaquette centres of all cutoffs, a countable set, gives $0$ at every cutoff.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof]
(a) $F^{(d)}$ is a linear image of $F$; each component at a plaquette of $\Lambda_d$ is a centred Gaussian variable of variance at most $1/x_{[d]}$ (the smeared self-energy of the boundary of one plaquette of $\Lambda_d$, divided by $\beta$). $|F^{(d)}(p)|\ge2\varepsilon$ forces a component $\ge2\varepsilon/\sqrt3$, of probability at most $2e^{-\frac23\varepsilon^2x_{[d]}}$, and $\frac23\varepsilon_{[d]}^2x_{[d]}=\frac23A_0^2(\log x_{[d]})^{2\mathfrak p_0}$; a union bound over the $3(\ell L^d)^3$ plaquettes and the three components gives $18$, over the $12$ plaquettes at a site $72$. (b) $\mathbb E\prod_i\cos\phi^a_{C_i}=2^{-r}\sum_\epsilon\mathbb E\,e^{i\sum_i\epsilon_i\phi^a_{C_i}}=2^{-r}\sum_\epsilon\exp[-\frac1{2\mathsf b}\sum_{i,j}\epsilon_i\epsilon_j\mathcal I_{a_K}(C_i,C_j)]$; three independent colours; Prop.~\ref{C-372-11}(a) for the diagonal terms and for the distant pairs. (c) Given the block field of the level $t+1$, the curvature is its conditional mean, the curvature $\Pi_{t+1}F$ of the linear background, plus an independent Gaussian fluctuation; between the levels $t$ and $t+1$ the fluctuation of the flux through $C$ has the variance $\frac{a_K}{\mathsf b}(X_C,\mathcal C_{(t+1)}X_C)$ per colour, and $\mathbb E[\cos(\phi+\xi)\mid\phi]=e^{-\frac12{\rm Var}\,\xi}\cos\phi$; three colours give $\lambda_{t+1}$.

For a family the cross covariances $\frac{a_K}{\mathsf b}(X_{C_i},\mathcal C_{(t+1)}X_{C_j})$ enter as factors $e^{\mp\frac{a_K}{\mathsf b}(X_{C_i},\mathcal C_{(t+1)}X_{C_j})}$, at most $e^{x}$ for each colour. (d) For jointly Gaussian $\phi$, $F$: $\mathbb E[\cos\phi\,F^2]/\mathbb E\cos\phi-\mathbb E F^2=-{\rm Cov}(\phi,F)^2$; ${\rm Cov}(\phi^a_C,F^a(p))=\beta^{-1}(X_C,X_{\partial p})=\mathcal I_{a_K}(C,\partial p)/\mathsf b$; $\frac12$ and three colours give $\frac32$. The identity holds for every bounded $f$, as nothing in it is a limit. For the limit let the corners of $C$ lie in a fixed $\Lambda_i$: away from $C$, uniformly on the support of $f$, $\mathcal I_{a_K}(C,\partial p)=a_K^2(B_{C,\ell}(x(p))\cdot n_p+O(a_K{\rm Lg}(\ell/a_K)))$, the mutual energy of $C$ with a small loop being the flux through it of the field of $C$ formed with the Green function of the torus: Prop.~\ref{C-372-11}(a) for the two polygons $C$ and $\partial p$ at positive distance compares the lattice energy with $\mathcal I_\ell(C,\partial p)=\oint_{\partial p}\oint_CG_\ell(x-y)\,\mathrm{d}y\cdot dx$ up to $O(a_K^3{\rm Lg}(\ell/a_K))$, and Stokes' formula makes $\mathcal I_\ell(C,\partial p)$ the flux of $B_{C,\ell}$ through $p$; summing $a_K^3f(x(p))(B_{C,\ell}(x(p))\cdot n_p)^2$ over the three orientations of the plaquettes gives a Riemann sum of $f|B_{C,\ell}|^2$, which converges for Lipschitz $f$.

Finally $G_\ell(x)=\frac1{4\pi|x|}+H_\ell(x)$ with $H_\ell(x)=\ell^{-1}H_1(x/\ell)$ smooth on $|x|<\ell$; as $\oint_Cdy=0$, 
\[
{\rm curl}\oint_CH_\ell(x-y)\,\mathrm{d}y=\oint_C[\nabla H_\ell(x-y)-\nabla H_\ell(x-y_0)]\times dy,
\]
of modulus at most 
\[
|C|\,{\rm diam}(C)\sup_{|u|\le\ell/2}|\nabla^2H_\ell(u)|=|C|\,{\rm diam}(C)\,\ell^{-3}\sup_{|u|\le1/2}|\nabla^2H_1(u)|.
\]

\end{proof}

The proof of Thm.~\ref{C-372-6} uses the following tools; we state them in lattice units, with spacing $1$ and $\beta=\mathsf b/a$.

\begin{lemma}[Tools of the tube]\label{C-372-17}
Let $\nu$ be the Wilson measure at $\beta$ on a torus $(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z)^3$, $N$ even, or a periodic Gibbs state as in Thm.~\ref{C-372-6}. For a step $c=\langle x_-,x_+\rangle$ of a closed path let $c(y)$, $y\in\mathbb Z^2$, be its translates in the lattice plane through $x_-$ orthogonal to $c$; for an integer $\rho\ge2$ let $T_\rho(c)=\{c(y):|y|<\rho\}$ be the slab and $K_\rho(c)=\{x_-+y+se:|y|_\infty\le\rho,\ 0\le s\le1\}$ the box of $c$, $e$ its direction; let $\phi_\rho(y)=\min\{1,\log^+(\rho/|y|)/\log\rho\}$, $\phi_\rho(0)=1$, so that $\phi_\rho=0$ at $|y|\ge\rho$, $E_\rho=(2\pi\log\rho+7.63)/\log^2\rho$, and $c_j=j(j+1)$.
(a) (Admissible steps.) A set $I$ of steps of closed paths $C_1,\dots,C_r$ is admissible at $\rho$ if no other step of the family runs through a bond of $T_\rho(c_i)$, $i\in I$, and no bond of $T_\rho(c_{i'})$, $i'\ne i$, lies in $K_\rho(c_i)$. For closed paths without self-intersection with $s$ straight pieces in all, each of at least $4\rho+1$ steps, whose pieces without a common corner are at sup-distance at least $2\rho+1$, the steps $2\rho\le j\le l'-1-2\rho$ of each piece of $l'$ steps form an admissible set of $n-4\rho s$ steps, $n$ the number of steps; for a rectangle, $n-16\rho$.
(b) (The profile.) $\sum_{\langle x,y\rangle}(\phi_\rho(x)-\phi_\rho(y))^2\le E_\rho$, the sum over the bonds of $\mathbb Z^2$, and $(\log\rho-1.2144)/2\pi\le1/E_\rho\le\log\rho/2\pi$.
(c) (An information inequality, three colours at once.) Let $\varrho>0$ be a $C^2$ density on $\mathrm{SU}(2)^Y$ with $0\in Y$, $\phi:Y\to[0,\infty)$ with $\phi_0=1$, frames $P_y\in\mathrm{SU}(2)$ with $P_0=\mathbf 1$, and for a unit vector $\mathbf n=(\mathbf n_1,\mathbf n_2,\mathbf n_3)\in\mathbb R^3$ the moves $v_y\mapsto\exp[is\phi_yP_y^{-1}(\frac12\sum_a\mathbf n_a\sigma_a)P_y]v_y$, $\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3$ the Pauli matrices, with the derivative $D_{\mathbf n}$ at $s=0$; let $\bar I=\sup_{|\mathbf n|=1}\mathbb E[-D_{\mathbf n}^2\log\varrho]$. Then $\|\mathbb E\,D^j(v_0)\|^2\le\bar I/(\bar I+c_j)$ in the operator norm for every spin $j>0$, where $D^j$ is the representation of spin $j$. The spin-zero representation has norm $1$.
(d) (The second variation.) For these moves on the bonds $c(y)$ of a slab, with any frames, a bond $e'=\langle x,y\rangle$ of the plane, $p(e')$ the plaquette spanned by $e'$ and $c$, and $H_{e'}=P_yU(e')^{-1}P_x^{-1}$: $D_{\mathbf n}^2a_{p(e')}\le\frac14(\phi_x-\phi_y)^2+\phi_x\phi_y(3a(H_{e'})+a_{p(e')})$, $a(g)=1-\frac12\operatorname{tr}g$.
(e) (Ceilings multiply over cells.) Let $B=\bigsqcup_lB_l$ be a set of bonds made of cells $B_l$, no plaquette having bonds in two cells, and $C=\gamma_1\delta_1\cdots\gamma_s\delta_s$ a closed path with $\gamma_l$ through no bond of $B\setminus B_l$ and $\delta_l$ through no bond of $B$. If $Q_l$ is the conditional mean under $\nu$ of $D^j(U(\gamma_l))$ given the bonds off $B_l$, then $\nu(\chi_j(U(C))\,G)=\nu(\operatorname{tr}[\prod_lQ_lD^j(U(\delta_l))]\,G)$ for every bounded Borel $G$ of the bonds off $B$, and $|\nu(\chi_j(U(C))\,G)|\le(2j+1)\sup|G|\,\nu(\prod_l\|Q_l\|)$.
(f) (One plaquette.) With $\mathfrak M_\nu=\sup_p\nu(e^{\beta a_p})$: $\nu(a_p)\le\beta^{-1}\log\mathfrak M_\nu$ and $\nu(a_p\ge s)\le\mathfrak M_\nu e^{-\beta s}$; for $\beta\ge1$, $\log\mathfrak M_\nu\le192\frac{\mathsf b}\ell+4(14.15+3\log\beta)$ on the torus of side $\ell$, and $\log\mathfrak M_\nu\le28.3+6\log\beta$ for the Gibbs states.
(g) (The ceiling of a tube.) Let $\beta>0$, $\rho\ge2$, $C_l$ closed paths with spins $j_l$, $I$ admissible at $\rho$, $c_i=c_{j_l}$ for a step of $C_l$, $G$ a bounded Borel function of the bonds off $B=\bigcup_{i\in I}T_\rho(c_i)$, $\mathcal G=\sum_{i\in I}\frac{2c_i}{\beta E_\rho}(1-\frac{2c_i}{\beta E_\rho})$ and $\omega_\rho=40\rho^4\sum_{i\in I}c_i/(\beta E_\rho)^2$. If $\omega_\rho\le1$, then $|\nu(G\prod_l\chi_{j_l}(U(C_l)))|\le\sup|G|\prod_l(2j_l+1)\,e^{-\mathcal G}\mathfrak M_\nu^{\omega_\rho}$; and $2c_j/E_\rho\ge\frac43c_jk(\log\rho-1.2144)$: the number per scale is $k$.
(h) (The ceiling with dyadic profiles.) Let $\rho=2^S\ge2$ and $C$ a coordinate rectangle of $n$ steps with sides of at least $4\rho+1$ steps and, on the torus, with the points within $\rho+1$ of $C$ in a cube of side at most $\frac N2$; let $W_C=\frac12\operatorname{tr}U(C)$, $p=kn/\beta<3$, $\delta_0=(16k\rho\log\rho+pk\log^2\rho)/\beta$ and $\bar a=\nu(a_p)$, the plaquette mean. Then, with the profiles $\phi_r$ of the scales $r=2,4,\dots,2^S$,
\[|\nu(W_C)|\le e^{\delta_0+2.2144p}\rho^{-p}\Bigl[1+\frac{72\,\bar a\rho^3\log^2\rho}{2^{3-p}-1}\Bigr]+35\,\bar a;\]
the plaquette mean enters linearly, and $p<3$ keeps the denominator positive.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof]
(a) A step at distance $\ge2\rho$ from the ends of its piece has a slab that meets no other step, and the slabs of two steps of pieces without a common corner at sup-distance $\ge2\rho+1$ do not reach each other's boxes. (b) The sum is a lattice form of $\int|\nabla\phi_\rho|^2=2\pi\int_1^\rho(r\log\rho)^{-2}r\,\mathrm{d}r=2\pi/\log\rho$, with explicit corrections at the centre and at the rim. (c) The moves are one-parameter groups of maps of $\mathrm{SU}(2)^Y$ that keep the Haar measure; under the move of $v_0$, $D^j(v_0)$ is multiplied by $e^{isJ_{\mathbf n}}$, $J_{\mathbf n}$ the generator of spin $j$, the image of $\frac12\sum_a\mathbf n_a\sigma_a$, and $\sum_{\mathbf n}J_{\mathbf n}^2=c_j$ over an orthonormal basis of directions.

With $M=\mathbb E\,D^j(v_0)$ and a unit vector $u$, integration by parts gives $iJ_{\mathbf n}Mu=-\mathbb E[(D^j(v_0)-M)u\,D_{\mathbf n}\log\varrho]$. Put $s_a=D_{e_a}\log\varrho$ and $s=(s_1,s_2,s_3)$. Since the supremum defining $\bar I$ runs over every unit direction, integration by parts gives $\mathbb E(ss^{\sf T})\le\bar I\mathbf 1$. The vector form of Schwarz's inequality therefore gives $\sum_a|\mathbb E[Xs_a]|^2\le\bar I\mathbb E|X|^2$ for $X=(D^j(v_0)-M)u$. Using $\sum_a|J_{e_a}Mu|^2=c_j|Mu|^2$ and $\mathbb E|X|^2=1-|Mu|^2$ yields $c_j|Mu|^2\le\bar I(1-|Mu|^2)$. (d) Expansion of $a_{p(e')}$ in $s$: the abelian part gives $\frac14(\phi_x-\phi_y)^2$, and the commutator terms are bounded by the defect $a(H_{e'})$ of the frames and by $a_{p(e')}$. (e) The cells interact with the rest only through plaquettes with bonds in one cell and off $B$, so conditioning cell by cell replaces $D^j(U(\gamma_l))$ by $Q_l$, the $\delta_l$ and $G$ being functions of the bonds off $B$; $|\operatorname{tr}\prod A_i|\le(2j+1)\prod\|A_i\|$. (f) Jensen's and Chebyshev's inequalities; the chessboard estimate bounds $\nu(e^{\beta a_p})$ by a power of a ratio of partition functions, and $\int\exp[-\beta\sum_{p\in Q}a_p]\,\mathrm{d}U\ge(\mathsf K\beta^3)^{-|Q|}$, $\mathsf K=1.39\cdot10^6$, for a box $Q$ of sites ($\log\mathsf K<14.15$); the torus adds $192\mathsf b/\ell$. (g) In each slab of $I$ we use comb frames: in the plane through $x_-$ orthogonal to $c_i$ a coordinate axis through $x_-$ is the base, the lines of the plane orthogonal to it are the teeth, and $P_y$ is the transport from $x_-$ along the base and then along the tooth to $x_-+y$, a product over bonds of the plane, which lie off $B$.

Then $H_{e'}=\mathbf 1$ on the base and on the teeth, and at a rung $e'$, a bond parallel to the base at the height $t_{e'}\ne0$, $H_{e'}$ is conjugate to the holonomy of the boundary of the strip $S_{e'}$ of the $|t_{e'}|$ plaquettes between the rung and the base, so that $a(H_{e'})\le|t_{e'}|\sum_{q\in S_{e'}}a_q$ (Prop.~\ref{C-372-13}(c) and Schwarz' inequality). Write $\nu_B(F)$ for the conditional mean of $F$ under $\nu$ given the bonds off $B$. As no plaquette has bonds in two cells, given the bonds off $B$ the cells are independent, and the conditional law of the bonds of the slab of $c_i$ given the bonds off it is their conditional law given the bonds off $B$. The bonds of the slab enter the action only through the plaquettes $p(e')$, $e'$ a bond of the plane, so that $-D_{\mathbf n}^2$ of the logarithm of this conditional density is $\beta\sum_{e'}D_{\mathbf n}^2a_{p(e')}$, with $\phi$ taken as $0$ off the slab, whose bonds alone move; by (b), (d) its conditional mean is $\bar I\le\frac\beta4(E_\rho+X_i)$, with
\[X_i=4\sum_{e'}\phi_x\phi_y\bigl[3a(H_{e'})+\nu_B(a_{p(e')})\bigr],\]
a function of the bonds off $B$. It is at most $\sum_qw^{(i)}_q\,\nu_B(a_q)$, a sum over plaquettes with weights $w^{(i)}_q\ge0$: $4\phi_x\phi_y$ at the plaquette $p(e')$ of every bond $e'$ of the disc, and $12|t_{e'}|\phi_x\phi_y$ at each plaquette of the strip of every rung $e'$, where $\nu_B(a_q)=a_q$, the bonds of the strip lying in the box $K_\rho(c_i)$ and so off $B$. The total weight $\sum_qw^{(i)}_q$ is at most $20\rho^4$: the strips give about $12\int_{|y|<\rho}y_2^2\,\mathrm{d}y=3\pi\rho^4$, the plaquettes $p(e')$ a multiple of $\rho^2$. (c) gives $\|Q_i\|^2\le(1+4c_i/(\beta(E_\rho+X_i)))^{-1}$, so, by $-\frac12\log(1+z)\le-\frac z2+\frac{z^2}4$ and $\frac1{E+X}\ge\frac1E-\frac X{E^2}$, $\log\|Q_i\|\le-\frac{2c_i}{\beta E_\rho}(1-\frac{2c_i}{\beta E_\rho})+\frac{2c_iX_i}{\beta E_\rho^2}$; (e) multiplies these over the disjoint cells.

Put $w_q=\sum_i2c_iw^{(i)}_q/(\beta E_\rho^2)$. Jensen's inequality for the conditional mean $\nu_B$ gives $\exp\sum_i\frac{2c_iX_i}{\beta E_\rho^2}\le\nu_B\bigl(\prod_qe^{w_qa_q}\bigr)$; as $\sum_qw_q/\beta\le40\rho^4\sum_ic_i/(\beta E_\rho)^2=\omega_\rho\le1$, H\"older's inequality with the exponents $\beta/w_q$ and (f), with $\mathfrak M_\nu\ge1$, give $\nu(\prod_qe^{w_qa_q})\le\prod_q\nu(e^{\beta a_q})^{w_q/\beta}\le\mathfrak M_\nu^{\omega_\rho}$. The last inequality is (b) with $\frac43k=\frac1\pi$. (h) Keep the cells $T_\rho(c_i)$ of the $n-16\rho$ steps of the admissible set of (a) (spin $\frac12$, $c_{1/2}=\frac34$).
