On each cell and for every dyadic $2\le r\le\rho$ the moves with the profile $\phi_r$, which vanishes at $|y|\ge r$, rotate bonds of the cell alone, and (b)--(e), as in the proof of (g), give at every field $\prod_i\|Q_i\|\le\min_re^{-\mathcal G_r+Y_r}$, with $\mathcal G_r$ the number $\mathcal G$ of (g) formed with $E_r$, $Y_r=\sum_i2c_{1/2}X^{(r)}_i/(\beta E_r^2)$ and $X^{(r)}_i$ the $X_i$ of the proof of (g) formed with $\phi_r$; by (b), $e^{-\mathcal G_r}\le e^{\delta_0+1.2144p}r^{-p}$, $\delta_0$ paying for the $16\rho$ omitted steps and for the second-order term of $\mathcal G_r$, so that $e^{-\mathcal G_r+Y_r}\le e^{\delta_0+2.2144p}r^{-p}$ where $Y_r\le p$.

The sharper estimate of the non-abelian member of the second variation bounds the mean of $Y_r$ in the place of an exponential moment: in comb frames $a(H_{e'})$ at a rung $e'$ of height $t_{e'}$ is $1-W$ of the boundary of the strip $S_{e'}$ of $1\times|t_{e'}|$ plaquettes, whose mean is $1-w(1,|t_{e'}|)\le1-w(1,1)^{|t_{e'}|}\le|t_{e'}|\,\bar a$ by Prop.~\ref{C-372-13}(c) (for the Gibbs states the strips of even height by the reflections in the planes of sites, those of odd height by $\sqrt{a(gh)}\le\sqrt{a(g)}+\sqrt{a(h)}$), so that $\nu(X^{(r)}_i)\le c\,r^3\bar a$ and $\nu(Y_r)\le c\,p\,r^3\log^2r\,\bar a$: the plaquette mean enters linearly, and this bound of a mean takes the place of the condition $\omega_\rho\le1$ and of the weight $40\rho^4$ of (g).

Let $r_*$ be the largest dyadic $r\le\rho$ with $Y_r\le p$; for $r<\rho$ the event $\{r_*=r\}$ lies in $\{Y_{2r}>p\}$, of probability at most $\nu(Y_{2r})/p$ by Markov's inequality, and on the event that $Y_r>p$ at every $r$ the bound $1$ serves. The sum over the dyadic $r<\rho$ of $r^{-p}(2r)^3\log^2(2r)$ is geometric and led by its last term exactly when $p<3$, which gives the display.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Proof of Thm.~\ref{C-372-3}}

\emph{Step 1: (1).} For $D\ge d_\Theta\ge d_\natural$ (as $\Theta_\star\ge t_\natural$), $\{\tau\le D\}=\{\tau_0\le D\}=\bigcap_{d\ge D}\pi_d^{-1}(I_d)$: if $\tau_0\le D$, then $V_d\in I_d$ for all $d\ge\tau_0$, so for all $d\ge D$; if $V_d\in I_d$ for all $d\ge D$, then $D$ is one of the integers of which $\tau_0$ is the least. Each member is open ($I_d$ is open, $\pi_d$ continuous), $\{\tau\le D\}=\emptyset$ for $D<d_\Theta$, and $\{\tau=\infty\}=\{\tau_0=\infty\}$; a function into a countable set whose sublevel sets are Borel is Borel. As $\pi_d(\mu)=\mu_d$, Prop.~\ref{C-372-8}(b) and countable subadditivity give the tail by the sum, and the same clause of Prop.~\ref{C-372-8}(b) the bound $\frac L{L-1}R_D$ when $c'A_0^2\log x_{[D]}\ge2$, as then $R_{d+1}\le L^{-1}R_d$ for all $d\ge D$; $\sum_dR_d<\infty$ and $\mu(\mathsf{Thr})=1$ give $\mu(\Omega)=1$, and for this the bound $\mu_d(\mathcal V_d\setminus I_d)\le R_d$ with $R_d\to0$ faster than every power of $L^{-d}$ suffices.

If $c'A_0^2(\log x_{[D]})^{2\mathfrak p_0}\le26\ell^3$, the exponent in $R_D$ is at least $(\mathsf C^\Sigma_{\rm maj}+2+c_{\rm low}-26)\ell^3\ge0$ by $c_{\rm low}\ge24$, and $2\ell^3L^{3D}M^{-3}\ge16$ as $\ell\ge2M$; so $R_D>1$, and the two bounds, $\sum_{d\ge D}R_d$ and $\frac L{L-1}R_D$, both at least $R_D$, exceed $1$. Next, $\{\tau>D\}=\bigcup_{d\ge D}\pi_d^{-1}(\mathcal V_d\setminus I_d)$, and $\mathcal V_d\setminus I_d$ is the event of Prop.~\ref{C-372-8}(c) for the set of all $\ell^3L^{3d}$ sites, which gives the bound by $\sum_{d\ge D}R^\natural_d$. As $(y+\log L)^{2\mathfrak p_0}-y^{2\mathfrak p_0}\ge2y\log L$ for $y\ge1$, $R^\natural_{d+1}/R^\natural_d\le L^{3-2c^\natural A_0^2\log x_{[d]}}$, which is at most $L^{-1}$ for $d\ge D$ if $c^\natural A_0^2\log x_{[D]}\ge2$.

With $y=D\log L\le\log x_{[D]}$, $\log R^\natural_D\le3\log\ell+3y-c^\natural A_0^2y^2$; the first member of the condition gives $3y\le\frac12c^\natural A_0^2y^2$ and $c^\natural A_0^2\log x_{[D]}\ge6$, the second $\frac12c^\natural A_0^2y^2\ge3\log\ell+\log\frac1\eta$; so $R^\natural_D\le\eta$.

\emph{Step 2: (2).} Thm.~\YMMref{E}{10} in the setting of Section~\YMMref{52.7}{432} and \S\ref{sec:analytic-core-complements} give the orbit for $\varpi(W)<\bar\varepsilon$; the inclusion $\{\varpi<2c_\rho\varepsilon_{[d]}\}\subset\{\varpi<\bar\varepsilon\}$ for $x_{[d]}\ge t_\natural$ is the condition (cut1) at $t=x_{[d]}$, which gives $2c_\rho\varepsilon(t)\le\varepsilon_{\mathcal W}\alpha_0$, with $\varepsilon_{\mathcal W}\alpha_0\le\bar\varepsilon$ (equation~\YMMref{(2134)}{790}). For $d\ge\tau_0\ge d_\natural$, $x_{[d]}\ge t_\natural$ and $V_d\in I_d\subset\{\varpi<2c_\rho\varepsilon_{[d]}\}$. If $d\ge\tau(V_\bullet)$, then $d\ge d_\Theta$ is admitted and $d\ge\tau_0$, so $V_d\in I_d\subset J_d$. Each clause of Prop.~\ref{C-372-9} asks of $W$ only that it lie in $J_d$ at an admitted depth, not that it be a block average or a member of a thread; we substitute $W:=V_d$, and Prop.~\ref{C-372-9}(a)--(c) give the limits, the rate, the curves, the continuity, the gauge invariance and the bound for rectangles. The thread property enters no step, and $\Omega$ is defined without $d$, $C$, $\gamma$, $K$.

\emph{Step 3: (3).} $J_d$ is open and $W^{[d]}_C$ is continuous and gauge invariant on it; the inverse image of a Borel set under $F^{[d]}_C$ is a Borel subset of $J_d$, joined with the closed set $\mathcal V_d\setminus J_d$ if it contains $0$; $\pi_d$ is continuous; so $Y_{d,C}$ is Borel and $\sigma(\pi_d)$-measurable, $\sigma(\pi_d)\subset\mathcal F_d$, and its restriction to the Borel set $\mathsf{Thr}$ is a Borel function on the threads. $\sup_{\mathcal X}|Y^K_{d,C}-Y_{d,C}|\le\sup_{J_d}|w^K_C-W^{[d]}_C|\to0$ by Prop.~\ref{C-372-9}(b). $\theta_v$ is a bijection, with inverse $\theta_{v^{-1}}$, that maps every $\pi_j^{-1}(I_j)$ onto itself, and $Y_{d,C}(\theta_vV_\bullet)=F^{[d]}_C(V_d^{\,v|\Lambda_d})=Y_{d,C}(V_\bullet)$. $(C^{\langle d\rangle})^{\langle j\rangle}=C^{\langle j\rangle}$, so $W_{C^{\langle d\rangle}}=W_C$ on $\mathcal V_j$, and every $d\ge d_\Theta$ is admitted. For curves Prop.~\ref{C-372-9}(c) replaces (a), (b); the shadows are fixed lattice by lattice because $w^K_\gamma$ depends on the shadow on the bare lattice, and a curve has no refinement.

\emph{Step 4: (4).} $\pi_d(\mu)=\mu_d$ gives the first equality, Prop.~\ref{C-372-9}(b), (d) the others and the rates. $|Y_{d,C}|\le1$ and Step~1 give $|\int Y_{d,C}\,\mathrm{d}\mu-\int\mathbf 1\{\tau\le d\}Y_{d,C}\,\mathrm{d}\mu|\le\mu(\tau>d)\le\sum_{d'\ge d}R_{d'}$, at most $\frac L{L-1}R_d$ if $c'A_0^2\log x_{[d]}\ge2$ (Step~1). $G_d-F^{[d]}_C$ vanishes on $J_d$ and has modulus at most $1$ off it, and $\mu_d(\mathcal V_d\setminus J_d)\le\mu_d(\mathcal V_d\setminus I_d)\le R_d$; for $d\ge\tau$, $V_d\in J_d$ and so $G_d(V_d)=Y_{d,C}$. For the joint means, with $D=\max_id_i$: the law of $(V_0,\dots,V_D)$ is the image of $\mu_D$ under $V\mapsto(\mathcal M^DV,\dots,V)$, $\prod_iF^{[d_i]}_{C_i}\circ\mathcal M^{D-d_i}$ is one bounded Borel function on $\mathcal V_D$, $\mathcal M^{K-d_i}=\mathcal M^{D-d_i}\mathcal M^{K-D}$, and $\mu^K_D\to\mu_D$ in total variation; no measure on an infinite product is needed here. The means depend on the single laws $\mu_d$; what $\mu$ adds to them are the events that involve infinitely many depths, $\{\tau\le D\}$ and $\Omega$.

\emph{Step 5: (5).} We use the localisation of backgrounds (Prop.~\YMMref{53.5}{447}) at $n=K-d$, for the constant sequence $\Omega_0=\dots=\Omega_{K-d}=T_\ell$, whose datum is $V$ on the bonds of $\Lambda_d$ and whose minimal orbit is the set of the backgrounds over $V$; for the region $\Omega'$, a region for the partition into the $M_1$-cubes of the depth $d$, with the one part $\mathsf Y_1=T_\ell\setminus\Omega'$ of its complement and the index $l_1=K-d$; at $\varepsilon_{\rm r}=2\varepsilon_{K-d}\le\epsilon_{\rm lc}$; and at $V\in\mathsf O_{K-d}$. We verify its hypotheses for this region of $M_1$-cubes, using the joined sequence defined in equation~\YMMref{(999)}{446}: the joined sequence is the $\mathfrak r_2$-tower of $\Omega'$, whose minimal orbit over the datum induced by $V$ defines the localised background $U'$ (equation~\YMMref{(77)}{42}); it is separated; its tower bonds are the bonds of its members of index $<K-d$, with both end points in the collar $\mathsf Y_1^{\sim2}\setminus\mathsf Y_1$, which lies in the wide collar $\mathsf Y_1^{\sim3}\setminus\mathsf Y_1$ (Section~\YMMref{53.4}{445}), the points of $\Omega'$ within three layers of $M_1$-cubes of the depth $d$ of $T_\ell\setminus\Omega'$; the core $\Omega'^{\sim-2}$ lies in its last member, so that $j(b)=K-d$ at the bonds of the core; and both data are regular at the radius $2\varepsilon_{K-d}$, as $V\in\mathsf O_{K-d}$ (Prop.~\YMMref{44.2}{345}).

So, after gauge transformations, the background over $V$ and $U'$ differ by factors $e^{i\mathsf a(b)}$ at the bare bonds $b$ with no end point in the wide collar, with $|\mathsf a(b)|\le\mathsf C_{\rm lc}\,2\varepsilon_{K-d}L^{d-K}e^{-\delta_{\rm lc}D(b)/2}$, $D(b)$ the distance of $b$ from the tower bonds in the weighted distance of the tower (Section~\YMMref{53.4}{445}). The bare bonds of $C$ are such bonds of the core, as ${\rm dist}(C,T_\ell\setminus\Omega')\ge\frac{\delta_1}2\ge4M_1a_d$. The tower-bond endpoints lie within the two-layer collar: a row below the last level has both endpoints outside the next tower member, which contains the core $\Omega'^{\sim-2}$. Moreover every local spacing in the joined sequence is at most $a_d$. For any connected path $\Gamma$ joining two points, the layer pieces cover $\Gamma$, so its weighted length is at least $a_d^{-1}\operatorname{length}(\Gamma)$, and hence at least $a_d^{-1}$ times the periodic sup-distance between those points. Taking the infimum over paths proves the same bound for weighted distance; the sup-distance to the complement of a slab, or of the intersection of two slabs, is the distance; so on $C$, $D(b)\ge{\rm dist}(C,T_\ell\setminus\Omega')/a_d-2M_1\ge\frac{\delta_1}2L^d-2M_1\ge\frac{\delta_1}4L^d$, as $M_1a_d\le\frac{\delta_1}8$.

The loop is gauge invariant, $W_C=\frac12\operatorname{tr}$, and $|\operatorname{tr}\prod_iA_i-\operatorname{tr}\prod_iB_i|\le2\sum_i|A_i-B_i|$ for unitary matrices; summing $|e^{i\mathsf a(b)}-\mathbf 1|\le|\mathsf a(b)|$ over the $|C|/a_K$ bare bonds of $C$ gives $|w^K_C(V)-Y_{K,d}(V)|\le\frac{|C|}{a_K}\,2\mathsf C_{\rm lc}\varepsilon_{K-d}L^{d-K}e^{-\delta_{\rm lc}\delta_1L^d/8}=2\mathsf C_{\rm lc}\varepsilon_{K-d}|C|L^de^{-\delta_{\rm lc}\delta_1L^d/8}$, and $\varepsilon_{K-d}\le\hat\varepsilon_d$ because $\frac23x_{[d]}\le x_{K-d}\le x_{[d]}+\bar B$. Two fields that agree on the bonds of $\Omega'$ have the same $Y_{K,d}$; let $K\to\infty$ with Prop.~\ref{C-372-9}(b), (e).

\emph{Step 6: (6).} The Wilson measure at $(K,\ell,\mathsf b)$ is the one at $(K-s,L^s\ell,L^s\mathsf b)$ carried by $x\mapsto L^sx$, since $\beta=L^K\mathsf b=L^{K-s}(L^s\mathsf b)$, and $\Lambda_d$ goes to $\Lambda_{d-s}$; so the limit laws, the measure on the threads from the depth $s$ on and Prop.~\ref{C-372-8} hold at every $\mathsf b>0$ with $R_{d-s}[L^s\ell,L^s\mathsf b]$. At $(L^s\ell,L^s\mathsf b)$ the one-torus setting holds (Lem.~\ref{C-372-7}), and (1)--(4) hold there at the depth $d-s$, with the depths $d_\natural$, $d_\Theta$, $s_\natural$ of $(L^s\ell,L^s\mathsf b)$; increased by $s$, these depths take the places of $d_\natural$, $d_\Theta$, $s_\natural$ in (1)--(4) at $(\ell,\mathsf b)$, the depth $d-s$ of $(L^s\ell,L^s\mathsf b)$ being the depth $d$ of $(\ell,\mathsf b)$.

The dilation maps $\Lambda_j$ of $T_\ell$ onto $\Lambda_{j-s}$ of $T_{L^s\ell}$, one graph with the same $\ell L^j=2L^{m+j}$ sites in each direction, bond onto bond, block onto block and plaquette onto plaquette, and the cutoff $K$ onto the cutoff $K-s$, with the same number $K-d$ of block steps above the depth $d$; it leaves $\beta$, $x_{[d]}=L^d\mathsf b=L^{d-s}(L^s\mathsf b)$, $\varepsilon_{[d]}$, the balls $I_d$, $J_d$ and the length in units of the lattice, $|C|L^d$, unchanged. Every object in the definition of the smoothed loop is formed from these graphs, from $K-d$ and from the constants, in the units of the lattices, and holds neither the side, nor the label, nor the spacing. Item by item: the block averaging map with its averaging radius $1/200L^2$ (equations~\YMMref{(37)--(39)}{20}); the constraint sets $\{\mathcal M^{K-d}U=W\}$, the action $\sum_pa_p$, criticality for it on them and the regularity at the radius $\varepsilon_{\rm v}$, a constant, all measured in the units of the level, with the bare spacing $L^{-(K-d)}$ (Defs.~\YMMref{9.3}{40} and~\YMMref{9.5}{41}); the residual gauge groups $\mathcal G^d_K$ and the minimal orbit (\S\ref{sec:analytic-core-complements}); the axial gauge of the averaged backgrounds in the definition of $H^K_s$ ({\cite[\S{}B.2]{YMM2}}); the radius $\bar\varepsilon$ and the lattices of Thm.~\YMMref{E}{10} in the setting of Section~\YMMref{52.7}{432}, whose lattice hypotheses are imposed through the number of the sites in each direction at the levels used, so that the backgrounds over a field with $\varpi<\bar\varepsilon$ form one non-empty orbit at $(\ell,\mathsf b)$ and at $(L^s\ell,L^s\mathsf b)$ alike; and the plaquette size $\varpi$, a maximum over the plaquettes of one graph .

So the transported backgrounds over $V_d$ are the backgrounds over $V_d$ on the lattices of side $\ell$, the transported $\mathcal C_K(W)$, $H^K_d$, $H^\infty_{d,n}$, $w^K_C$, smoothed loops, balls and variables are those of $(\ell,\mathsf b)$ at the depth $d$, and (1)--(4) at $(L^s\ell,L^s\mathsf b)$ and the depth $d-s$ are (1)--(4) at $(\ell,\mathsf b)$ and the depth $d$.

\subsubsection{Proof of Thm.~\ref{C-372-4}}

\emph{Step 1: the ceiling.} Fix $\vartheta\in(\kappa,\frac12)$. Prop.~\ref{C-372-10}(a) gives the hypothesis of Prop.~\ref{C-372-12}(a) with $\eta_s=C_\eta L^{-\vartheta(K-s+1)}$ up to the last level $\bar t=K-d$, $d\ge s_0$. By Prop.~\ref{C-372-11}(c), $a_K^{-\kappa}\Xi_{s-1}\le c_\Xi L^{\kappa(K-s+1)}$, the depth $K-s+1\ge d$ being at least $i_0$; so
\[a_K^{-\kappa}\mathsf e_t\le c_\Xi C_\eta\sum_{j\ge K-t+1}L^{-(\vartheta-\kappa)j}=\epsilon_1L^{-(\vartheta-\kappa)(K-t+1)}:\]
the additive errors of the steps, weighed by $\Xi_t\approx L^{-\kappa t}$, sum after division by $a_K^\kappa$ exactly when $\vartheta>\kappa$; what ends at $\kappa=\vartheta$ is the additive error, not the tower. The rarity bound at $p=\kappa+1$ gives $\sum_{t\le\bar t}L^{\kappa(K-t)}\mathsf w_t\le2\mathsf V_\ell C_{\rm r}(\kappa+1)L^{-d}$, and $a_K^{-\kappa}(\Xi_{t-1}+\mathsf e_{t-1})\le(c_\Xi L^\kappa+\epsilon_1)L^{\kappa(K-t)}$; Prop.~\ref{C-372-12}(a) gives \eqref{C-372-5}. At $d=s_0$, $|W^{(\bar t)}_{\mathsf C}|\le1$ and $Z^{-1}m_{\bar t}(\mathcal V_{K-\bar t})\le1$ give the supremum, and $|\Phi^{(t)}[W_{\mathsf C}]|\le\Xi_t+\mathsf e_t\le(c_\Xi+\epsilon_1)L^{-\kappa t}$. A rectangle in a ball of radius $<\ell/4$ has $|C|<\sqrt2\,\ell$, which is $<\frac{2\pi}3\mathsf b$ if $\ell\le1.48\,\mathsf b$. If $\kappa\ge\frac12>\vartheta$, the same tower with $\Xi_{s-1}\le c\,L^{-\kappa(s-1)}$ gives $\mathsf e_{\bar t}\le c\,a_K^\vartheta$ and $\Xi_{\bar t}\le c\,a_K^\kappa$, and the rarity terms are smaller.

\emph{Step 2: the limit.} Let $d\ge\max\{s_0,d_0\}$. By Prop.~\ref{C-372-9}(e), $m_{K-d}$ is carried by $\mathsf O_{K-d}\subset J'_d$, where $W^{(K-d)}_{\mathsf C}=w^K_{\mathsf C}\to F':=\prod_iW^{[d]}_{C_i}$ uniformly. By Prop.~\ref{C-372-12}(c), $Z^{-1}m_{K-d}$ and $\mu^K_d$ differ on gauge invariant sets by a positive measure of mass $\sum_{t\le K-d}\mathsf w_t\le2\mathsf V_\ell C_{\rm r}(\kappa+1)L^{-(\kappa+1)d}$; $\mu^K_d\to\mu_d$ in total variation; $a_K^{-\kappa}\Xi_{K-d}\to\mathsf l_d\le c_\Xi L^{\kappa d}$; and $\mathbf 1_{J'_d}F'$ differs from $F^{[d]}_{\mathsf C}$ only off $J_d$, a set of $\mu_d$-measure at most $R_d$, which is also the difference of the two means. With \eqref{C-372-5}, $\limsup_K\mathcal W_K-\liminf_K\mathcal W_K\le2\mathsf E_d\to0$, so the limit exists, and $|\mathcal W(\mathsf C)-\mathsf l_d\int F^{[d]}_{\mathsf C}\,\mathrm{d}\mu_d|\le\mathsf E_d$.

The value of $\mathsf l_d$ (Prop.~\ref{C-372-11}(c)) gives the asymptotics of $a_d^{-\kappa}\int F^{[d]}_{\mathsf C}\,\mathrm{d}\mu_d$, its remainder giving $c\,a_d(1+\log^+(1/a_d))/\mathsf b$ for a fixed polygon, which tends to zero. Uniformity on $\mathsf J$: the numbers of Prop.~\ref{C-372-10} depend on $\mathsf J$ alone; $c_\Xi$ is uniform on $\mathsf J$; $a_K^{-\kappa}\prod_n\lambda_n\to\mathsf l_d$ locally uniformly in $\mathsf b$; the interval $[\mathsf b_-,\mathsf b_+]$ is an interval of labels under (Tor) on the side $\ell$ (\S\ref{sec:cutoff-calibration}: $\mathsf b_-\ge\gamma^{-2}$, and $M\,Q(\mathsf b_+)\le L^m$, with $Q$ of Lem.~\ref{C-372-7}, which is the function $R$ of that definition, holds on the sides of $\mathfrak L(g)$ at every label of $\mathsf I(g)$, as in the proof of Prop.~\ref{C-372-9}(e)), so the numbers $\mathsf C_{\rm bf}$, $K_{\rm bf}$ of Def.~\textup{\ref{IV-62-62}}(5) formed at this interval depend on the label only through it, and Cor.~\textup{\ref{IV-62-66}}(a) bounds the difference of the laws of the block field of the depth $d$ at two consecutive cutoffs $K'$, $K'+1$, on the gauge invariant sets, by $\mathsf C_{\rm bf}\ell^3K'^{2\mathfrak p_0+1/2}L^{-K'/10}$ at every $\mathsf b\in\mathsf J$ and every $K'\ge K_{\rm bf}$ with $\lceil K'/1260\rceil\ge d$; summed over $K'\ge K$, with Cor.~\textup{\ref{IV-62-66}}(b), (c) for the limit and for all Borel sets, $\sup_E|\mu^K_d(E)-\mu_d(E)|\le\sum_{K'\ge K}\mathsf C_{\rm bf}\ell^3K'^{2\mathfrak p_0+1/2}L^{-K'/10}$ for all $\mathsf b\in\mathsf J$ and all $K\ge K_{\rm bf}$ with $\lceil K/1260\rceil\ge d$; $R_d$ and the rate of Prop.~\ref{C-372-9}(b) are explicit and continuous in $\mathsf b$; the balls $J'_d$ may move with $\mathsf b$.

So Steps~1 and~2 hold uniformly on $\mathsf J$, $\mathcal W_K\to\mathcal W$ uniformly, each $\mathcal W_K$ is continuous in $\mathsf b$, and the same bounds hold at labels $\mathsf b_K\in\mathsf J$.

\emph{Step 3: every torus and label.} Given $m\in\mathbb Z$ and $\mathsf b>0$, for large $s$ the number $g_s=(L^s\mathsf b-\bar B-1)^{-1/2}$ is a reference coupling below the thresholds of the frame, $L^s\mathsf b\in\mathsf I(g_s)$, and $2L^{m+s}\in\mathfrak L(g_s)$; the exponent of Prop.~\ref{C-372-10} is the same for all $g$, $\kappa$ is invariant under dilations, and Prop.~\ref{C-372-13}(a) gives $\mathcal W^{(\ell,\mathsf b)}_K(\mathsf C)=L^{s\kappa}\mathcal W^{(L^s\ell,L^s\mathsf b)}_{K-s}(L^s\mathsf C)$; so the limit exists and obeys the law of dilations.

\emph{Step 4: the floor.} For $C_i=n_1a_i\times n_2a_i$, Prop.~\ref{C-372-10}(b) applies with $n_{C_i}=4$ and $c_{C_i}$ fixed, both invariant under dilations, with $s_0(i)=\max\{i,s'_0\}=i+O(1)$ and no distance term; its bound is at most $C(\mathsf J)\frac{a_i}{\mathsf b}L^{-\vartheta(K-t)}\le C(\mathsf J)L^{-\vartheta(K-t-i)}$, an error that depends on the scale of the step only through $a_{K-t}/a_i$; it holds for $m_{t+1}$-almost every $W$, which is all that Prop.~\ref{C-372-12}(a) asks, so Step~1 runs with $C_\eta(i)=C(\mathsf J)L^{\vartheta i}$ and $s_0(i)$ in the place of the numbers of Prop.~\ref{C-372-10}(a). Let $i$ be so large that $(n_1^2+n_2^2)a_i^2<\ell^2/4$, so that $C_i$ lies in a ball of radius $<\ell/4$ and is a polygon, that $\kappa(C_i)\le k|C_i|/\mathsf b_-<\vartheta$ for all $\mathsf b\in\mathsf J$, that $s_0(i)\le d_i$, which holds for large $i$ as $d_i\ge\frac76i$, and that $\theta_{d_i}\le1$, which holds for large $i$ as $\theta_{d_i}\to0$ (below).

We run Prop.~\ref{C-372-12} down to the depth $d_i=\lceil(\frac43-\frac u2)i\rceil$. There 
\[
\theta_{d_i}=2B_3\sup_{K>d_i,\mathsf J}\varepsilon_{K-d_i}L^{2d_i}n_1n_2a_i^2\le c\,L^{\frac32d_i-2i}(1+d_i)^{\mathfrak p_0}\to0,
\]
as $\frac32d_i\le(2-\frac34u)i+\frac32$ and $\varepsilon_{K-d}\le A_0(2a_d/\mathsf b_-)^{1/2}(\log(\mathsf b_-/2a_d))^{\mathfrak p_0}$ for large $d$. The numbers of the free field of $C_i$ tend to $0$: $\eta_i\to0$ by Prop.~\ref{C-372-11}(a), so $e^{-\frac3{2\mathsf b_-}\eta_i}\le a_K^{-\kappa}\Xi_{K-d_i}$ (as $v_{K,d}\ge0$), $c_\Xi\to1$ and $L^{\kappa(d_i+1)}\to1$ ($\kappa d_i\le c\,a_ii$); and $\mathsf E'_{d_i}\to0$, as $\epsilon_1\le2C(\mathsf J)L^{\vartheta i}/(1-L^{-\vartheta/2})$ and $d_i\ge(\frac43-\frac u2)i$.

Prop.~\ref{C-372-12}(a), (c), (d) give the display of (4): by (d) and $\theta_{d_i}\le1$, $W^{(K-d_i)}_{C_i}\ge1-\frac12\theta_{d_i}^2\ge\frac12$ on $\mathsf O_{K-d_i}$, which carries $m_{K-d_i}$, so 
\[
Z^{-1}\int W^{(K-d_i)}_{C_i}\,\mathrm{d}m_{K-d_i}\ge(1-\frac12\theta_{d_i}^2)Z^{-1}m_{K-d_i}(\mathcal V_{d_i})\ge(1-\frac12\theta_{d_i}^2)(1-2\mathsf V_\ell C_{\rm r}(1)L^{-d_i})
\]
 by (c), whatever the sign of the last factor, and this integral, being $\ge0$, is multiplied by $a_K^{-\kappa}\Xi_{K-d_i}\ge e^{-\frac3{2\mathsf b_-}\eta_i}$; both ends are $1+o(1)$ uniformly in $K>d_i$ and $\mathsf b\in\mathsf J$. For the squares $Q_i$ we use the mean form, Prop.~\ref{C-372-12}(b), at one $i$: by Prop.~\ref{C-372-10}(b) the mean defects are at most $C(\mathsf J)L^{-\vartheta(K-t-i)}$.

With $d=i+n_Q$, choose $n_Q$ and then $i$ so large that $\kappa(Q_i)\le\frac\vartheta2$, the free factor $a_K^{-\kappa}\Xi_{K-d}$ lies within a factor $\sqrt2$ of $L^{\kappa d}$, $L^{\kappa(d+1)}\le\sqrt2$, the summed step errors $2C(\mathsf J)L^{-\vartheta(n_Q+1)}/(1-L^{-\vartheta/2})$ are at most $\frac1{32}$, $2B_3L^{2n_Q}\sup_{K>d}\varepsilon_{K-d}\le1$ (so that the loop at the last level is at least $\frac12$ on tame fields), the mass of the measure without large fields is at least $\frac78$, and the rarity terms are at most $\frac1{32}$; then $\mathcal W_K(Q_i)\ge\frac1{\sqrt2}\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac78-\frac1{16}>\frac18$. For other rectangles we spread with Prop.~\ref{C-372-13}(b): $\rho_K(s,T)=\mathcal W_K(s\times T)$ has $\rho_K(s,\frac{T'+T''}2)^2\le\rho_K(s,T')\rho_K(s,T'')$, the powers of $a_K$ matching because lengths add; so $T\mapsto\log\rho_K(s,T)$ is convex, $\rho_K(s,nT)\ge\rho_K(s,2T)[\rho_K(s,2T)/\rho_K(s,T)]^{n-2}$, and a finite $\limsup$ (Step~1) on a set of rectangles closed downwards together with a positive $\liminf$ at one of them gives a positive $\liminf$ at all rectangles of the range, going down by $\log\rho(T)\ge2\log\rho(T')-\log\rho(2T'-T)$ and up by convexity, in each side.

\emph{Step 5: block fields; the static source.} $H\circ\mathcal M^{K-s_1}$ pulls out of the quotients, $\Phi^{(t)}[W_{\mathsf C}\,H\circ\mathcal M^{K-s_1}]=\Phi^{(t)}[W_{\mathsf C}]\,H\circ\mathcal M^{K-t-s_1}$ for $K-t\ge s_1$; so Steps~1 and~2 run with the factor $H$, $\sup|H|$ multiplying the errors (Prop.~\ref{C-372-12}(a)), and $Y_{d,C}$-means are those of $F^{[d]}_C$. For a rectangle we divide by $\mathcal W(C)>0$ (Step~4): the limit quotients $\omega(H)=\lim_K\langle W_CH(\mathcal M^{K-s_1}U)\rangle_K/\langle W_C\rangle_K$ form a real linear functional with $\omega(1)=1$ on the bounded gauge invariant Borel functions of all block fields, consistent between depths, $\omega(H\circ\mathcal M)=\omega(H)$, because $H\circ\mathcal M^{d'-s_1}$ is the same function seen at a finer depth; at the depth $s_1$ it is bounded, $|\omega(H)|\le\sup|H|\,(c_\Xi L^{\kappa d'}+\mathsf E'_{d'})/\mathcal W(C)$ with $d'=\max\{s_0,s_1\}$, by the display of (5) with $|W^{(K-d')}_C|\le1$, $Z^{-1}m_{K-d'}(\mathcal V_{d'})\le1$ and $a_K^{-\kappa}\Xi_{K-d'}\le c_\Xi L^{\kappa d'}$.

On the threads $H(V_{s_1})=H(\mathcal M^{d-s_1}V_d)$ $\mu$-almost surely, so $\int H(V_{s_1})Y_{d,C}\,\mathrm{d}\mu=\int F^{[d]}_C\,(H\circ\mathcal M^{d-s_1})\,\mathrm{d}\mu_d$, and Step~2, with $\mathsf l_d\asymp a_d^{-\kappa}$, gives the limits in $d$ and the two-sided bound for $\int Y_{d,C}\,\mathrm{d}\mu$. For $H$ not gauge invariant: for a gauge transformation $v$ of $\Lambda_K$, $\mathcal M^{K-s_1}(U^v)=(\mathcal M^{K-s_1}U)^{v|\Lambda_{s_1}}$; averaging $v$ over the Haar measure and using the invariance of the Wilson measure, of $W_{\mathsf C}$, of $\mu$ and of $Y_{d,C}$ replaces $H$ by $\bar H$.

\emph{Step 6: mixed functions.} By Prop.~\ref{C-372-14}(d) at $X=W_{\mathsf C}$, $|Q_K(z)|\le M_0\mathcal W_K(\mathsf C,\theta\mathsf C)^{1/2}$ on half the polydisc; $(\mathsf C,\theta\mathsf C)$ is a family (its polygons lie $2\delta_1$ apart) with $\kappa(\mathsf C,\theta\mathsf C)=2\kappa<\frac12$, so Step~1 bounds the right side uniformly in $K>s_0$. For the limit at real $z$ we take the source off the loop by Prop.~\ref{C-372-14}(d) applied to the difference of the loop and a function of the block field on the side of $\mathsf C$; no step with a source is used. Let $\bar t=K-d$. As $c\in\frac12a_{i_0}\mathbb Z$, $\theta$ is a lattice isometry of $\mathsf{Iso}_{i_0}$ ({\cite[\S{}G.1]{YMM2}}); let $d_1:=i_0+\log_LM_1$, so that from the depth $d_1$ on $\theta$ maps $\Lambda_d$ and the partition into the $M_1$-cubes of the depth $d$, cubes of side $M_1a_d$, onto themselves ({\cite[Lem.~G.1]{YMM2}}).

Let $d$ be at least $\max\{s_0(\mathsf C),s_0(\mathsf C,\theta\mathsf C),d_0,d_1\}$, $s_0(\cdot)$ the number of Prop.~\ref{C-372-10}(a) at the family named, and so large that $M_1a_d\le\frac{\delta_1}8$ and $2\hat\varepsilon_d\le\epsilon_{\rm lc}$, so that $2\varepsilon_{K-d}\le\epsilon_{\rm lc}$ for every $K>d$ and Thm.~\ref{C-372-3}(5) applies at $d$; let $K>d$. Then $\theta$ commutes with the block averages, $\mathcal M^j(\theta U)=\theta\,\mathcal M^jU$ for $j\le\bar t$, and carries the constraint sets, criticality, regularity and the backgrounds over $V$ to those over $\theta V$ ({\cite[Lem.~G.1]{YMM2}}); $\varpi$ is $\theta$-invariant, so $\mathsf O_{\bar t}$ is; and the lattice Green function is $\theta$-invariant and the linearised block averages are $\theta$-covariant ({\cite[Lem.~G.1]{YMM2}}), so the projections $\Pi_n$ commute with $\theta$ and the lattice Coulomb energies are $\theta$-invariant.

Hence $W^{(\bar t)}_{\mathsf C}(\theta^{-1}V)=W^{(\bar t)}_{\theta\mathsf C}(V)$ on $\mathsf O_{\bar t}$ and $\Xi_{\bar t}(\theta\mathsf C)=\Xi_{\bar t}(\mathsf C)$. Let $\mathcal Y_{K,d}(V)$ be the loop of $\mathsf C$ at the background localised to a slab $\Omega'$ on the side of $\mathsf C$ as in Thm.~\ref{C-372-3}(5); then $Y=\Xi_{\bar t}(\mathsf C)\mathcal Y_{K,d}(\mathcal M^{\bar t}U)$ is a function of the bonds on the side of $\mathsf C$, and $\sup_{\mathsf O_{\bar t}}|W^{(\bar t)}_{\mathsf C}-\mathcal Y_{K,d}|\le\epsilon^{\rm loc}_d$, the bound of Thm.~\ref{C-372-3}(5). Now $\|W_{\mathsf C}-Y\|_\theta^2=\langle W_{\mathsf C}W_{\theta\mathsf C}\rangle_K-2\langle W_{\mathsf C}\,\theta Y\rangle_K+\langle Y\,\theta Y\rangle_K$, and three towers without source evaluate the three means: Prop.~\ref{C-372-12}(a) for the family $(\mathsf C,\theta\mathsf C)$, whose loop at the background is $W^{(\bar t)}_{\mathsf C}W^{(\bar t)}_{\theta\mathsf C}$ and whose factor is $\Xi_{\bar t}^2$; Prop.~\ref{C-372-12}(a) for $\mathsf C$ with the gauge invariant factor $\theta\mathcal Y_{K,d}$ of the block field; and Prop.~\ref{C-372-12}(c) for the function $\mathcal Y_{K,d}\,\theta\mathcal Y_{K,d}$ of the block field.

The main terms add up to $\Xi_{\bar t}^2Z^{-1}\int[W^{(\bar t)}_{\mathsf C}(W^{(\bar t)}_{\theta\mathsf C}-\theta\mathcal Y_{K,d})-(W^{(\bar t)}_{\mathsf C}-\mathcal Y_{K,d})\,\theta\mathcal Y_{K,d}]\,\mathrm{d}m_{\bar t}$, of modulus at most $2\Xi_{\bar t}^2\epsilon^{\rm loc}_d$. With $a_K^{-\kappa}\Xi_{\bar t}\le c_\Xi L^{\kappa d}$ and the rarity bound at $p=2\kappa+1$,
\[a_K^{-2\kappa}\|W_{\mathsf C}-Y\|_\theta^2\le\sigma_d:=c_\Xi^2L^{2\kappa d}\bigl[2\epsilon^{\rm loc}_d+2\mathsf V_\ell C_{\rm r}(2\kappa+1)L^{-(2\kappa+1)d}\bigr]+\mathsf E'_d(\mathsf C,\theta\mathsf C)+2c_\Xi L^{\kappa d}\mathsf E'_d(\mathsf C),\]
free of $K$, and $\sigma_d\to0$ because $2\kappa<\vartheta<\frac12$ and $\epsilon^{\rm loc}_d$ falls faster than every power of $a_d$. At real $z$, Prop.~\ref{C-372-14}(d) at $X=W_{\mathsf C}-Y$ gives $|Q_K(z)-a_K^{-\kappa}\Xi_{\bar t}\,\mu^{K,w_z}_d(\mathcal Y_{K,d})|\le M_0\sigma_d^{1/2}$. By Prop.~\ref{C-372-14}(b) the probability $\mu^{K,w}_d$ gives at most $\sum_{t\le\bar t}\mathsf w^w_t\le2\mathsf V_SC^S_{\rm r}(\kappa+1)L^{-(\kappa+1)d}$ to the complement of $\mathsf O_{\bar t}\cap J'_d$, since the sourced measure without large fields has the null sets of $m_{\bar t}$ and is carried by $\mathsf O_{\bar t}\subset J'_d$; on $\mathsf O_{\bar t}\cap J'_d$, $|\mathcal Y_{K,d}-F'_d|\le\epsilon^{\rm loc}_d+\sup_{J'_d}|w^K_{\mathsf C}-F'_d|$ with $F'_d=\mathbf 1_{J'_d}\prod_iW^{[d]}_{C_i}$ (Prop.~\ref{C-372-9}(e)). With $a_K^{-\kappa}\Xi_{\bar t}\to\mathsf l_d$ and $\mu^{K,w}_d\to\mu^w_d$ (Prop.~\ref{C-372-14}(c)),
\[\limsup_K\bigl|Q_K(z)-\mathsf l_d\,\mu^{w_z}_d(F'_d)\bigr|\le M_0\sigma_d^{1/2}+c_\Xi L^{\kappa d}\epsilon^{\rm loc}_d+4c_\Xi\mathsf V_SC^S_{\rm r}(\kappa+1)L^{-d}\to0,\]
so $\lim_KQ_K(z)=\lim_d\mathsf l_d\,\mu^{w_z}_d(F'_d)$ exists at every real $z$ of half the polydisc. A bounded family of holomorphic functions that converges on a real cube converges locally uniformly to a holomorphic limit (Vitali's theorem); so $Q_K\to Q$, the derivatives converge, and Prop.~\ref{C-372-14}(e) with the limits $S_m$ of \YMMref{(2212)}{813}, for pairwise disjoint supports, gives the limit of $\mathcal W_K(\mathsf C;f)$. For two orthogonal mirrors the same argument runs with the four images of $\mathsf C$ and Prop.~\ref{C-372-14}(d) twice, on the quarter $\sum_q|z_q|\|f_q\|_\sharp<\rho_D/4$ of the polydisc, the towers at the subfamilies of $(\mathsf C,\theta_1\mathsf C,\theta_2\mathsf C,\theta_1\theta_2\mathsf C)$, of $\kappa$-value up to $4\kappa<\frac12$, and a region $\Omega'$ that is the intersection of two slabs; the limit then exists at the real $z$ with $|z_q|<\rho_D/(4n\max_q\|f_q\|_\sharp)$, a real cube in that quarter, and Vitali's theorem applies there.

For $n=1$, $\mathcal W_K(\mathsf C;f)$ is linear in $f$; as each coordinate extent of $\mathsf C$ is $<\frac\ell2$, every point outside the least closed coordinate box that holds $\mathsf C$ lies, with a neighbourhood, beyond a coordinate mirror that misses the box, with $c\in\frac12a_i\mathbb Z$ for some $i$; a Lipschitz partition of unity subordinate to finitely many such mirrors cuts $f$ into pieces, each of which the case of one mirror covers. With walls, the number of boxes is even in every direction that the walls cut and the walls lie in $\frac12a_i\mathbb Z$, so that both fixed planes $c$ and $c+\frac\ell2$ of every wall mirror are walls and each box has exactly one image in every box; and each $f_q$ is supported in one box, a function whose support misses the walls being the sum of its pieces in the boxes, with the derivatives in its variable the sums of those in the variables of its pieces.

Then Prop.~\ref{C-372-14}(d) on the polydisc $\sum_q|z_q|\|f_q\|_\sharp<\rho_D/N$, Step~1 for each family $\mathsf C^{\rm f}_\iota$, of $\kappa$-value $N\kappa(\mathsf C_\iota)<\frac12$, and Cauchy's estimates bound the derivatives $\partial_AQ_K(0)$ uniformly in $K$, for all supports off the walls; by Prop.~\ref{C-372-14}(e) this bounds $\mathcal W_K(\mathsf C;f_1,\dots,f_n)$ uniformly in $K$ for $n=1$, where $\mathcal W_K(\mathsf C;f_1)=\partial_1Q_K(0)$, and for pairwise disjoint supports, where the cumulants $S^{\sf T}_{|\beta|,K}(f_\beta)$ of the blocks of at least two elements converge \YMMref{(2212)}{813} and so are bounded in $K$. The law of dilations and the positive form with mixed entries hold at every cutoff (Prop.~\ref{C-372-13}(a), (b)) and pass to the limits; for the latter the plane $x_\mu=\hat c+\frac\ell4$, $\hat c\in\frac12a_{i_0}\mathbb Z$ the place of the mirror $\theta'$ of (6), a fixed plane of the coordinate mirror with the place $\hat c+\frac\ell4$, which lies in $\frac12a_{i_0}\mathbb Z$ as $\frac\ell4=\frac12L^m$, parts polygons and supports, so that every entry converges.

\emph{Step 7: beside the loop.} Let $X=W_C-\psi$, a function of the bonds on the side of $C$, and $Y=H-\langle H\rangle_K$, a real function of the bonds of $S$. Reflection positivity at the site mirror and Schwarz' inequality (as in Prop.~\ref{C-372-13}(b)) give $|\langle XY\rangle_K|^2\le\langle X\,\theta X\rangle_K\langle\theta Y\,Y\rangle_K$, with $\langle X\,\theta X\rangle_K=\langle W_CW_{\theta C}\rangle_K-\psi^2\ge0$ by the $\theta$-invariance of the measure, $\langle\theta Y\,Y\rangle_K=\langle\theta H;H\rangle_K\ge0$, and $\langle XY\rangle_K=\langle W_C;\mathcal O(f)\rangle_K-\langle W_C;H_0\rangle_K$; divide by $\psi$. The explicit ceiling uses the law of the truncated two-point function of the action density, Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AV}{851}}.

Let, as in (7), $g\le\gamma_W$ in the frame, $\gamma_W$ the ceiling of equation~\YMMref{(2346)}{850}; let $\vartheta_{\rm sh}\in(0,1)$ be a shape parameter, and $\mathsf d\in(0,\mathsf d_0(g,\vartheta_{\rm sh})]$ with $K-s(\mathsf d)\ge1$, $\mathsf d_0(g,\vartheta_{\rm sh})$ the threshold of equation~\YMMref{(2350)}{851} and $s(\mathsf d)$ the witness depth of equation~\YMMref{(2321)}{843} at $g$. As $\mathsf b\in\mathsf I(g)$, in the frame $(K,L^K\mathsf b)$ is a first-passage datum at $g$ with the label $\mathsf b$ (Cor.~\YMMref{74.2}{616}), and the side $\ell$ of the frame lies in $\mathfrak L(g)$. Then for every test pair $(h_1,h_2)\in\mathfrak T_{T_\ell}(\mathsf d;\vartheta_{\rm sh})$ on a torus $T_\ell$ with $20\mathsf d\le\ell$ ({\cite[Lem.~I.1]{YMM2}}: non-negative Lipschitz functions, neither $0$, with supports in closed balls of radius $\mathsf d$ at a distance between $\mathsf d$ and $6\mathsf d$, $\int h_j\ge\vartheta_{\rm sh}\|h_j\|_\infty\mathsf d^3$ and ${\rm Lip}\,h_j\le\|h_j\|_\infty/(\vartheta_{\rm sh}\mathsf d)$)
\[
\begin{multlined}
S^{\sf T}_{2,K}(h_1,h_2)=a_K^{-2}\sum_{p,q}h_1(x(p))h_2(x(q))\langle W_{\partial p};W_{\partial q}\rangle_K=\frac9{16\pi^2}\mathsf b^{-2}\int\!\!\int h_1(x)h_2(y)|x \\
-y|^{-6}\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y\,(1+\epsilon'),\qquad|\epsilon'|\le\epsilon_{\rm tp},
\end{multlined}
\]
with $\frac9{16\pi^2}$ the constant $\mathsf c_2$ of \YMMref{C}{7}, the double integral the free kernel \YMMref{(2240)}{822}, and $\epsilon_{\rm tp}:=\bar\varepsilon_{g,\vartheta_{\rm sh}}(\mathsf d)$, the tolerance equation~\YMMref{(2349)}{851}, one function for all these data, non-decreasing, tending to $0$ with $\mathsf d$ and at most $\frac13$ on $(0,\mathsf d_0(g,\vartheta_{\rm sh})]$ (Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AV}{851}}); so $|\epsilon'|\le\frac13$ and the bound $(\frac{4\pi}3)^2\|h_1\|_\infty\|h_2\|_\infty$ of the free kernel of a test pair, two balls of radius $\mathsf d$ at a distance $\ge\mathsf d$ (equation~\YMMref{(2247)}{824}), give $S^{\sf T}_{2,K}(h_1,h_2)\le\frac43\,(\frac{4\pi}3)^2\,\frac9{16\pi^2}\,\mathsf b^{-2}\|h_1\|_\infty\|h_2\|_\infty$, the bound of Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AV}{851}}.

As $\mathcal O(f)=a_K^{-1}\sum_pf(x(p))(1-W_{\partial p})$, $\langle\theta\mathcal O(f);\mathcal O(f)\rangle_K=a_K^{-2}\sum_{p,q}f(\theta x(p))f(x(q))\langle W_{\partial p};W_{\partial q}\rangle_K=S^{\sf T}_{2,K}(\theta f,f)$, and $\sqrt{9/16\pi^2}=\frac3{4\pi}$: for a test pair $(\theta f,f)$ the inequality at $H_0=0$ gives the bound of (7) with the factor $1+\epsilon_{\rm tp}$. On the whole class of the law, $\frac43\,(\frac{4\pi}3)^2\,\frac9{16\pi^2}=\frac43$ gives $\langle\theta\mathcal O(f);\mathcal O(f)\rangle_K\le\frac43\mathsf b^{-2}\|f\|_\infty^2$, and the inequality at $H_0=0$ gives the ceiling $\frac2{\sqrt3}\mathsf b^{-1}\|f\|_\infty[\langle W_CW_{\theta C}\rangle_K/\psi^2-1]^{1/2}$ with no further condition.

The identity follows from the same expression of $\mathcal O(f)$: 
\[
\langle W_C\mathcal O(f)\rangle_K/\psi-\langle\mathcal O(f)\rangle_K=a_K^{-1}\sum_pf(x(p))[\langle W_{\partial p}\rangle_K-\langle W_CW_{\partial p}\rangle_K/\psi],
\]
and $\langle W_{\partial p}\rangle_K>0$ (Prop.~\ref{C-372-13}(c)). The derivative is $\frac d{d\mathsf b}=L^K\frac d{d\beta}$ applied to $\log\langle W_C\rangle_K$. For a rectangle with $2\kappa<\frac12$ the three quantities converge by (6) at $n=1$ with (4), by (2) at the family $(C,\theta C)$, and by \YMMref{(2212)}{813}, the supports of $\theta f$ and $f$ being disjoint.

\emph{Step 8: short distances.} (a) We run the tower in its mean form, Prop.~\ref{C-372-12}(b), down to the depth $i$ of the corners, that is to the level $t_i=K-i$; when $\max\{n_1,n_2\}<L$ this is the level $t_\varrho$ with $a_{K-t_\varrho}\le\varrho_i<La_{K-t_\varrho}$. The number $s_0$ of Prop.~\ref{C-372-10}(b) for $C_i$ is $\max\{i,s'_0\}$, $s'_0$ formed from the constants, $\mathsf b_-$ and $n_{C_i}=4$; so $s_0=i$ for all large $i$, and every step that the tower uses, at a level $t<t_i$, has $K-t>i=s_0$. There Prop.~\ref{C-372-10}(b) bounds the steps with a constant free of the size of the loop; weighed by the free factors, whose ratios between the levels are bounded by Prop.~\ref{C-372-11}(c), they contribute $C_1\frac{|C_i|}{\mathsf b}(\frac{\varrho_i}{\mathsf b})^{\vartheta/2}$, and the rarity terms contribute $C_3\mathsf V_\ell C_{\rm r}(p)\varrho_i^{p-1/2}$.

At the depth $i$ a tame background has $1-W^{(t_i)}_{C_i}\le\frac12\theta^2=2B_3^2n_1^2n_2^2\varepsilon_{K-i}^2\le4B_3^2A_0^2\mathsf n^3\frac{\varrho_i}{\mathsf b}(1+\log\frac{\mathsf n\mathsf b}{\varrho_i})^{2\mathfrak p_0}$ (Prop.~\ref{C-372-12}(d), with $x_{K-i}\ge\frac23\mathsf b/a_i$, $n_1^2n_2^2a_i\le\mathsf n^3\varrho_i$ and $\mathsf b/a_i\le\mathsf n\mathsf b/\varrho_i$). The free factor down to that level is $a_K^{-\kappa}\Xi_{t_i}=\exp[-\frac3{2\mathsf b}(c_{\rm lat}|C_i|+\mathcal J_\ell(C_i)+E_{a_K}(C_i)-v_{K,i}(C_i))]$ (Prop.~\ref{C-372-11}(a), (c)), and $0\le\frac3{2\mathsf b}v_{K,i}(C_i)\le\kappa\log^+\frac{\varrho_i}{a_i}+c\frac{|C_i|}{\mathsf b}\le\kappa\log L+c\frac{|C_i|}{\mathsf b}$, $c$ depending on $n_1$, $n_2$: at the depth of the corners the logarithm of $v$ (Prop.~\ref{C-372-11}(b)) and that of $\mathcal J_\ell$ cancel up to $\frac{|C_i|}{2\pi}\log\max\{n_1,n_2\}$ and a multiple of $|C_i|$, and $\kappa\log\max\{n_1,n_2\}\le\kappa\log L+k\frac{|C_i|}{\mathsf b}\log\frac{\mathsf n}L$; $|\log(1-z)|\le2|z|$ for $|z|\le\frac12$. (b) Let $a_*:=\varrho(\mathsf b/\varrho)^{\vartheta/(3+\vartheta)}$ and let $d_*$ be the least depth with $a_{d_*}\le a_*$, so that $a_*/L<a_{d_*}\le a_*$; for small $\varrho$, $a_{d_*}>a_i$, and the depth $d_*$ is coarser than the corners.

At all the levels with $a_{K-t}\le a_*$ the defect of one step is at most $C_*\frac\varrho{\mathsf b}(\frac{a_{K-t}}{\mathsf b})^\vartheta$ at $m_{t+1}$-almost every $W$, hence in the mean, $|\bar{\mathsf D}_{t+1}|\le C_*\frac\varrho{\mathsf b}(\frac{a_{K-t}}{\mathsf b})^\vartheta$ with $\bar{\mathsf D}_{t+1}$ of Prop.~\ref{C-372-12}(b), $C_*$ depending on the constants, $c_0$, $\vartheta$ and $\mathsf J$ alone: this is the bound of one step of (8)(b), shown at the end of this step. We stop the tower, in its mean form, Prop.~\ref{C-372-12}(b), at the depth $d_*$. Prop.~\ref{C-372-11}(c), valid at every depth, and (d) give the factor $e^{-\frac3{2\mathsf b}(\mathcal I_{a_K}(C,C)-v_{K,d_*})}$ with $0\le v_{K,d_*}(C)\le C^{\rm bg}A_C^2/a_{d_*}^3$, $A_C$ the area of $C$; on tame fields $0\le1-W^{(K-d_*)}_C\le4B_3^2A_0^2\frac{A_C^2}{\mathsf ba_{d_*}^3}(1+\log\frac{\mathsf b}{a_{d_*}})^{2\mathfrak p_0}$ (Prop.~\ref{C-372-12}(d)).

As $A_C\le100\varrho^2$ and $a_*/L<a_{d_*}\le a_*$, these are $O(\varrho^4/a_*^3)$ and $O(\frac{\varrho^4}{\mathsf ba_*^3}(1+\log\frac{\mathsf b}{a_*})^{2\mathfrak p_0})$, with constants that hold $10^4L^3$ (and $\log L$ in the logarithm); the step errors add up to $O(\frac\varrho{\mathsf b}(\frac{a_*}{\mathsf b})^\vartheta)$; the terms of the large fields, $\sum_{t\le K-d_*}\Xi_{t-1}\omega_t$ with $|\omega_t|\le\mathsf w_t$, are by the rarity bound at $p=2$ at most $c\,\mathsf V_\ell C_{\rm r}(2)\,a_{d_*}^2\le c\,\mathsf V_\ell C_{\rm r}(2)\,a_*^2$ times the free factor, and $a_*^2=\mathsf b^2(\frac\varrho{\mathsf b})^{2-2\alpha}$ with $\alpha=\frac\vartheta{3+\vartheta}<\frac17$, below the remainder as $2-2\alpha>1+3\alpha$; and $\frac\varrho{\mathsf b}(\frac{a_*}{\mathsf b})^\vartheta=\frac{\varrho^4}{a_*^3\mathsf b}=(\frac\varrho{\mathsf b})^{1+\frac{3\vartheta}{3+\vartheta}}$: the choice of $a_*$ balances the two.

Prop.~\ref{C-372-11}(a) and $|\mathcal J_\ell-\mathcal J|\le c\varrho^4\ell^{-3}$ finish; $\log(\mathsf b/\varrho)$, and not $\log\varrho$, is the logarithm that dilations leave invariant. The bound of one step at the levels with $a_{K-t}\le a_*$. At the levels finer than the lattice of the corners, $K-t>s_0=\max\{i,s'_0\}$, which is $i$ for small $\varrho$, it is Prop.~\ref{C-372-10}(b): its constant depends on the constants, $n_C=4$ and the chord-arc constant of $C$, which is bounded below in terms of $c_0$, its factor $|C|/\mathsf b$ is at most $40\varrho/\mathsf b$, and its bracket, without a distance term for one polygon, is at most $c\,(a_{K-t}/\mathsf b)^\vartheta$ with $c$ depending on the constants, $\vartheta$ and $\mathsf J$.

At the remaining levels, $a_i\le a_{K-t}\le a_*$, at least as coarse as the lattice of the corners, $a_{K-t}\ge a_i>c_0\varrho/2L$ and $|C|\le40\varrho$, so that the loop passes a number of cubes of the level that is bounded in terms of $L$ and $c_0$, and $|C|/a_{K-t}<80L/c_0$. There the proof of Prop.~\ref{C-372-10}(b) runs with the segments $C_j$ of $C$, one for each cube of the level that the loop passes, in the place of the bonds of the level, down to one segment where the cells are larger than the loop. The shift of Prop.~\YMMref{51.5}{396} gives $W^{(t)}_C(V_W(B))=W_C(e^{i\eta_t\mathbf A(B)}U_+)$ exactly for every bare loop (step~1 of the proof of Prop.~\ref{C-372-10}(a)); so $W^{(t)}_C(V_W(B))=w(\Upsilon(B))$ and $W^{(t+1)}_C(W)=w(0)$, with $w$ as in Lem.~\ref{C-372-16}(c), $g_j=U_+(C_j)$ the holonomy of $U_+$ along the segment, and the rotations $\Upsilon_j(B)=\frac1i\log[(e^{i\eta_t\mathbf A(B)}U_+)(C_j)\,U_+(C_j)^{-1}]$ of the segments.

Each segment is one insertion into the four-family Gaussian
cluster expansion of Thm.~\YMMref{R}{361}, applied to the
two potentials in $\nu_W$ as in Step~3 of the proof of
Prop.~\ref{C-372-10}(a), with a linear part of norm of the order $g_t|C_j|/a_{K-t}$ and a remainder of the order $(g_t|C_j|/a_{K-t})^2$, so that $\log\nu_W(e^{(z,\Upsilon)})$ is a sum of local terms on a polydisc of radius of the order $a_{K-t}/(g_t|C|)$. The first cumulants, and the defects of the pair cumulants from their values $s_{jj'}{\rm R}(G_{j\to j'})$ at the trivial triple, are colour vectors and colour defects that vanish at the flat background, and Schwarz' lemma in the background gives them the factor $\varepsilon_{t+1}$, as in step~5 of the proof of Prop.~\ref{C-372-10}(a); the pair values at the trivial triple sum to the slice $g_t^2\eta_t(X_C,\mathcal C_{(t+1)}X_C)$ of the free Coulomb energy, as in its step~7, at depths coarser than the corners as well (Prop.~\ref{C-372-11}(c) holds at every depth); and $\nu_W\ge0$ for $m_{t+1}$-almost every $W$.

Lem.~\ref{C-372-16}(c) then bounds the defect of the step by $E_1+E_2+E_3$ and the term of the label, at most $c\,|C|\mathsf b^{-2}a_{K-t}$; each of $E_1$, $E_2$, $E_3$ is at most $\frac{|C|}{\mathsf b}(\frac{a_{K-t}}{\mathsf b})^{1/2}y_t^{\mathfrak p}$, $y_t=\log x_t$, $\mathfrak p$ formed from $\mathfrak p_0$, times a polynomial in $|C|/a_{K-t}$ with coefficients formed from the constants, since a cumulant of order $m$ carries the factor $(g_t|C|/a_{K-t})^m$, the first cumulants besides the amplitude $\delta_t=g_t\mathfrak b_t$ of the non-Gaussian potentials, the Gaussian part being even, the variables are at most $c\,\delta_t|C|/a_{K-t}$, $g_t^2$ is of the order $a_{K-t}/\mathsf b$, and the first cumulants and the defects of the pair cumulants carry the factor $\varepsilon_{t+1}$, of the order $(a_{K-t}/\mathsf b)^{1/2}y_t^{\mathfrak p_0}$.

As $|C|/a_{K-t}<80L/c_0$, $|C|\le40\varrho$ and $(\frac a{\mathsf b})^{1/2}y^{\mathfrak p}\le c\,(\frac a{\mathsf b})^\vartheta$ for $\vartheta<\frac12$, the bound is at most $C_*\frac\varrho{\mathsf b}(\frac{a_{K-t}}{\mathsf b})^\vartheta$. No level coarser than $a_*$ is used; at the levels with $a_{K-t}^3\ge\varrho^2\mathsf b$, coarser than $a_*$, the step bound holds by itself, since there $1-\lambda_{t+1}$ and $1-W^{(t)}_C$ on tame fields are at most of the order $\varrho^4/(\mathsf ba_{K-t}^3)$ up to logarithms, below $C_*\frac\varrho{\mathsf b}(\frac{a_{K-t}}{\mathsf b})^\vartheta$.

\subsubsection{Proof of Thm.~\ref{C-372-6}}

We work in lattice units, $\beta=\mathsf b/a$, $n=|C|/a$ steps. By Lem.~\ref{C-372-17}(a) the steps of $C$ at distance $\ge2\rho$ from the corners form an admissible set $I$ of $n-16\rho$ steps (of $n-4\rho s$ steps for polygons with $s$ pieces), whose slabs lie in disjoint cells. Lem.~\ref{C-372-17}(g) at spin $\frac12$, $c_i=\frac34$, gives $|\langle W_C\rangle|\le e^{-\mathcal G}\mathfrak M_\nu^{\omega_\rho}$: across each admissible step the bonds of the slab that cross the disc of radius $\rho$ about it are rotated together with the profile $\phi_\rho$, whose Dirichlet energy is about $2\pi/\log\rho$, at an action cost $\approx2\pi\beta/\log\rho$; the information inequality in three colours gives the factor $e^{-k\log\rho/\beta}$ per slab, up to the second-order term of $\mathcal G$ and the constant $1.2144$, and the bounds multiply exactly over the disjoint cells; with $n$ slabs, $e^{-kn\log\rho/\beta}=\rho^{-k|C|/\mathsf b}$.

The second variation (Lem.~\ref{C-372-17}(d)) limits $\rho$: its second member, summed over the disc, asks $\omega_\rho=40\rho^4\sum_ic_i/(\beta E_\rho)^2\le1$, $E_\rho\sim2\pi/\log\rho$; with $\rho=\lfloor(\frac{\beta}{\Lambda\log^3\beta})^{1/4}\rfloor$ one has $\omega_\rho\le c/\log\beta$, so that $\mathfrak M_\nu^{\omega_\rho}$, with Lem.~\ref{C-372-17}(f), the corrections of $\mathcal G$ and the $16\rho$ omitted steps give the prefactor $6e^{3.1\mathsf b/\ell}1.58^{|C|/\mathsf b}$, and $\rho^{-1}\le2(\Lambda\log^3\beta/\beta)^{1/4}$ gives the power $[\Lambda\frac a{\mathsf b}\log^3\frac{\mathsf b}a]^{k|C|/4\mathsf b}$, the factor $2^{k|C|/\mathsf b}$ going into the prefactor. For the second bound let $\rho=2^S\in(\frac12\beta^{1/3},\beta^{1/3}]$ and $p=k|C|/\mathsf b=kn/\beta<3$, and keep the cells $T_\rho(c_i)$ of the $n-16\rho$ admissible steps.

On each cell, for every dyadic $2\le r\le\rho$, the moves with the profile $\phi_r$, taken as $0$ at $|y|\ge r$, rotate bonds of the cell alone, and Lem.~\ref{C-372-17}(b)--(e), as in the proof of (g), give at every field $\prod_i\|Q_i\|\le\min_re^{-\mathcal G_r+Y_r}$, with $\mathcal G_r=\sum_i\frac{2c_i}{\beta E_r}(1-\frac{2c_i}{\beta E_r})$, $Y_r=\sum_i2c_iX^{(r)}_i/(\beta E_r^2)$ and $X^{(r)}_i$ the $X_i$ of that proof formed with $\phi_r$; by (b), $e^{-\mathcal G_r}\le e^{\delta_0+1.2144p}r^{-p}$, where $\delta_0=(16k\rho\log\rho+pk\log^2\rho)/\beta$ pays for the $16\rho$ omitted steps and the second-order term of $\mathcal G_r$. The sharper estimate bounds the mean of $Y_r$ instead of an exponential moment: in comb frames $a(H_{e'})$ at a rung $e'$ of height $t_{e'}$ is $1-W$ of the boundary of the strip $S_{e'}$ of $1\times|t_{e'}|$ plaquettes, whose mean is $1-w(1,|t_{e'}|)\le1-w(1,1)^{|t_{e'}|}\le|t_{e'}|\,\nu(a_p)$ by Prop.~\ref{C-372-13}(c), in the place of the bound $|t_{e'}|\sum_{q\in S_{e'}}a_q$ at every field; so $\nu(X^{(r)}_i)\le c\,r^3\nu(a_p)$, $r^3$ in the place of $r^4$, and $\nu(Y_r)\le c\,p\,r^3\log^2r\,\bar a$ with $\bar a=\nu(a_p)\le\beta^{-1}\log\mathfrak M_\nu$ (Lem.~\ref{C-372-17}(f)): the plaquette mean enters linearly, and this bound of a mean takes the place of the condition $\omega_\rho\le1$ and of the weight $40\rho^4$.

Let $r_*$ be the largest dyadic $r\le\rho$ with $Y_r\le p$; on $\{r_*=r\}$, $r<\rho$, $Y_{2r}>p$, an event of probability at most $\nu(Y_{2r})/p$ by Markov's inequality, and on the event that $Y_r>p$ at every $r$ the bound $1$ serves. So, as Lem.~\ref{C-372-17}(h) states,
\[|\langle W_C\rangle|\le e^{\delta_0+2.2144p}\rho^{-p}\Bigl[1+\frac{72\,\bar a\rho^3\log^2\rho}{2^{3-p}-1}\Bigr]+35\,\bar a,\]
the sum over the dyadic $r<\rho$ of $r^{-p}(2r)^3\log^2(2r)$ being geometric and led by its last term exactly when $p<3$. With $\rho^3\le\beta$, so that $\bar a\rho^3\le\log\mathfrak M_\nu$, with $\rho^{-p}\le2^p\beta^{-p/3}$, $\bar a\le\beta^{-p/3}\log\mathfrak M_\nu$ and $\log\mathfrak M_\nu\le192\frac{\mathsf b}\ell+4(14.15+3\log\beta)$, where $192\frac{\mathsf b}\ell\le\frac{384k}p$ as $|C|<2\ell$, this is at most $C(\frac{k|C|}{\mathsf b})(\frac a{\mathsf b})^{|C|/4\pi\mathsf b}\log^3\frac{\mathsf b}a$ for $\beta\ge\beta_2$, the threshold, depending on $p$ alone, from which on $n\ge16\rho+4$ and $\delta_0\le1$: $\frac p3=\frac{|C|}{4\pi\mathsf b}$, and the third logarithm is $\log^2\rho$ times $\log\mathfrak M_\nu$.

For the Gibbs states the strips of even height are treated by the reflections in the planes of sites, those of odd height by $\sqrt{a(gh)}\le\sqrt{a(g)}+\sqrt{a(h)}$. For the spin $j$, $c_j=j(j+1)$ replaces $\frac34$, that is $k\mapsto\frac43c_jk=\frac{j(j+1)}\pi$, and $\kappa_j\le20\log\beta$ keeps $\omega_\rho$ admissible. For a family of such polygons whose pieces, those of different polygons included, are at sup-distance at least $(2\rho+1)a$ when they have no common corner, Lem.~\ref{C-372-17}(a) applies to the whole family and gives one admissible set of $n-4\rho s$ steps, $n$ and $s$ the numbers of all the steps and of all the pieces, and Lem.~\ref{C-372-17}(e), (g) bound $\langle\prod_iW_{C_i}\,G\rangle$ in the same way, a factor $G$ of the bonds farther than $\rho a$ from the polygons being a function of the bonds off $B$; a fixed family at positive distances has this property as soon as $(2\rho+1)a$ is below these distances, that is for all small $a$, which is what the limits as $a\to0$ use.

The proof uses of $\nu$ only the conditional laws of finite sets of bonds, reflection positivity and invariance (through Lem.~\ref{C-372-17}(f), and for the second bound through Prop.~\ref{C-372-13}(c) for the strips); for the Gibbs states the bound of (f) gives $3$ in the place of $6e^{3.1\mathsf b/\ell}$. So all characters of the holonomy of non-zero spin have means tending to $0$: its class tends to the Haar law of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, whose image under $\frac12\operatorname{tr}$ has the density $\frac2\pi\sqrt{1-w^2}$ (the $\chi_j$ are the Chebyshev polynomials of the second kind in $W_C$, orthogonal for $\sigma$, and polynomials are dense among the continuous $h$); and $\langle W_C^2\rangle=\frac14(1+\langle\chi_1(U(C))\rangle)\to\frac14$, from $W_C^2=\frac14\chi_{1/2}(U(C))^2=\frac14(1+\chi_1(U(C)))$.

For a rectangle $\langle W_C\rangle>0$ (Prop.~\ref{C-372-13}(c)), so $\mathrm{Var}(W_C/\langle W_C\rangle)=\langle W_C^2\rangle/\langle W_C\rangle^2-1=(1+\langle\chi_1(U(C))\rangle)/(4\langle W_C\rangle^2)-1$; as $\langle\chi_1(U(C))\rangle\to0$ and the first bound gives \[
 \langle W_C\rangle^{-2}\ge(6e^{3.1\mathsf b/\ell}1.58^{|C|/\mathsf b})^{-2}[\Lambda\frac a{\mathsf b}\log^3\frac{\mathsf b}a]^{-k|C|/2\mathsf b}
\], the variance tends to infinity at least at this rate. If $c_aW_C$ had a limit law while $|c_a\langle W_C\rangle|\ge c>0$, then $|c_a|\ge c/|\langle W_C\rangle|\to\infty$; as the law of $W_C$ tends to the semicircle law, which gives no mass to $0$, $\langle\mathbf 1\{|c_aW_C|>R\}\rangle\to1$ for every $R$, and the laws of $c_aW_C$ are not tight: a contradiction.

The rotations touch only bonds within $\rho a\to0$ of the polygons, act on several polygons at once and leave $G$ unchanged, so $\langle\prod_i\chi_{j_i}(U(C_i))\,G\rangle\to0$ unless all $j_i=0$, which is the asymptotic independence. The floor: $\langle W_C\rangle\ge\langle W_{\partial p}\rangle^{A_C/a^2}$ by Prop.~\ref{C-372-13}(c), and $\langle W_{\partial p}\rangle=1-\langle a_p\rangle\ge1-\beta^{-1}\log\mathfrak M_\nu\ge e^{-\frac32\beta^{-1}\log\mathfrak M_\nu}$ when $\beta^{-1}\log\mathfrak M_\nu\le\frac12$ (Lem.~\ref{C-372-17}(f)), with $\frac{A_C}{a^2}\beta^{-1}=\frac{A_C}{a\mathsf b}$; for the Gibbs states the same argument, with reflections in planes of sites and even numbers of steps, and $\frac32(28.3+6\log\beta)\le43+9\log\beta$.

\subsubsection{Scope of the conclusions}

At a fixed depth the variable $Y_{d,C}$ of Thm.~\ref{C-372-3} is the smoothed loop on $\{V_d\in J_d\}$ and $0$ off it, and Prop.~\ref{C-372-8}(d) bounds the probability of $\{V_d\in J_d\}$ below; the starting depth is random and by its form no stopping time, since $\{\tau\le D\}$ involves all the coordinates of index $\ge D$; the loop of the depth $d$ uses $H^\infty_{d,n}(V_d)$ and not the finer members of the thread, so that $W^{[d]}_C(V_d)$ and $W^{[d+1]}_C(V_{d+1})$ are two different functions on the threads, and the limit in the depth is a limit of means and of quotients of means (Thm.~\ref{C-372-4}(2), (5)); for the sharp loop itself no multiple has both a limit law and a mean that stays away from $0$, by the non-tightness consequence of the semicircle law (Thm.~\ref{C-372-6}).

The bounds of the convergence in $n$ and in $K$ hold the factor $L^d\varepsilon_{[d]}=A_0\mathsf b^{-1/2}L^{d/2}(\log x_{[d]})^{\mathfrak p_0}$, which grows with $d$. On the side $\ell$ depend the tails of $\tau$, which hold $\ell^3$ or $e^{C\ell^3}$; the floors $\mathsf p^{[d]}$, $\mathsf q^{[d]}$; the speed of $K\to\infty$, as $a_s(K)$ holds $(\ell L^s)^{3/2}$, $\mathfrak r_K$ holds $\ell^3$ and $K_{\rm bf}$ depends on $\ell$; and $\mathsf V_\ell$; the event $\{V_d\in J_d\}$ asks all the $3(\ell L^d)^3$ plaquettes. Free of $\ell$ are the bounds in $n$ on the tower, on curves and on small rectangles (Prop.~\ref{C-372-9}(a), the first bound of (c)), the locality bound of Thm.~\ref{C-372-3}(5), the numbers $c_{\rm lat}$, $c_Q$, $c$ and $c_3$ (Prop.~\ref{C-372-11}), and, for $\ell\ge\ell_0$, all the ceilings of Thm.~\ref{C-372-6}.

Thm.~\ref{C-372-4} concerns $|\mathsf C|<\frac{2\pi}3\mathsf b$ and is a perimeter law, two-sided for rectangles. Three free photon fields at the label $\mathsf b$ have the same features: their block curvatures obey at each depth, uniformly in $K$, bounds of the same form as those of Prop.~\ref{C-372-8}(c) and of $R^\natural_d$ (Prop.~\ref{C-372-15}(a)), and their sharp loops have the same exponent $\kappa$, the same perimeter constant $c_{\rm lat}|C|+\mathcal J_\ell(C)$ and the same factor $\lambda_{t+1}$ of one step as the loops of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ in Thm.~\ref{C-372-4} and Prop.~\ref{C-372-10} (Prop.~\ref{C-372-15}(b), (c)). Thm.~\ref{C-372-4}(7) is an upper bound: for three free photon fields the response of the action density is $-\frac3{2\mathsf b^2}\int f|B_{C,\ell}|^2\,\mathrm{d}x$, with the field $B_{C,\ell}$ of $C$ on the torus, within $c|C|\,{\rm diam}(C)\ell^{-3}$ of its Biot--Savart field $B_C$ in the ball that holds the polygon (Prop.~\ref{C-372-15}(d)).

The quotients of Thm.~\ref{C-372-4}(5) formed for three free photon fields, $\lim_K\mathbb E[W^{\rm fr}_C\,H]/\mathbb E\,W^{\rm fr}_C$ for $H$ a bounded function of a block field, take negative values at functions $H\ge0$: by Prop.~\ref{C-372-15}(c) the conditional mean of $W^{\rm fr}_C$ given the block field of the level $t$ is $\Xi_tW^{{\rm fr},(t)}_C$, and $W^{{\rm fr},(t)}_C$ is a product of three cosines of independent centred Gaussian variables of the variance $v_{K,K-t}(C)/\mathsf b$, which grows like $\frac{|C|}{2\pi\mathsf b}\log\frac1{a_{K-t}}$ (Prop.~\ref{C-372-11}(b)); so $W^{{\rm fr},(t)}_C$ is negative with positive probability, and the quotient at the indicator of $\{W^{{\rm fr},(t)}_C<0\}$ is negative.

Alternatively, the levels $\varrho<a_{K-t}\le a_*$ of the proof of Thm.~\ref{C-372-4}(8)(b), whose cells are larger than the loop, can be traded for a law of one point at the depth of the size of the loop: $1-W^{(t)}_C$ is, on tame fields, a quadratic form in the curvature, and the law follows from a bound on $|Z^{-1}\int(1-W^{(t)}_C)\,\mathrm{d}m_t-\frac3{2\mathsf b}v_{K,K-t}(C)|$ at that level, the mean of one bounded function of the block field against its free value.


\section{Centre flux}\label{supp:C-366-1}

For $SU(2)$, reverse the plaquette trace on a column winding around
a periodic box. A twist class has three signs, one for each
coordinate two-torus. On choosing a time direction, write the class
as $(k,m)$, where $k\in\mathbb Z_2^2$ is electric and
$m\in\mathbb Z_2$ is magnetic. Let $T_m$ be the transfer operator
on a spatial section with magnetic twist $m$, and let $C^k$ be
the product of its two centre-flip operators.

\begin{sketch}[Positive electric-flux sectors]\label{supp:C-366-3}
The twisted partition functions have the decomposition
\[
 Z[(k,m)]=\operatorname{Tr}(T_m^NC^k),\qquad
 Z_{e,m}=\frac14\sum_k(-1)^{e\cdot k}Z[(k,m)]
        =\operatorname{Tr}(P_eT_m^N)\ge0,
\]
where $N$ is the number of time layers and
$P_e=\frac14\sum_k(-1)^{e\cdot k}C^k$.
Changing the time direction relates these sectors by a finite
Fourier transform. Reflection-positive mixtures are obtained when
their electric Fourier weights are nonnegative in each time
direction.
\end{sketch}

\paragraph{Sketch of the argument.}
Split the plaquette action into its spatial and crossing parts.
The crossing kernel is positive, and multiplication by the square
root of the spatial Boltzmann weight gives $T_m\ge0$. The centre
flips are commuting unitary involutions preserving this operator.
Their four character projections are the $P_e$. Closing the
time direction with the chosen electric twist inserts $C^k$ in
the trace, and Fourier inversion gives the displayed formulas.

The same box can be traced in a second coordinate direction.
Comparing the two formulas exchanges one electric index with
the magnetic index while retaining the common-plane flux.
This crossing relation supplies inequalities between the
sector traces. The strictly positive transfer kernel has a
simple largest eigenvalue in the zero-electric-flux sector.
Ratios of eigenvalues then give the electric and magnetic
free energies over the chosen spatial section.

For a mixture with weights $w(k,m)$, define its electric-sector
coefficients by
\[
 \widehat w(e,m)=\sum_k(-1)^{e\cdot k}w(k,m).
\]
Nonnegativity of these coefficients makes the reflected trace
positive in that time direction. Requiring it for each direction
gives the stated class of mixtures. A single twisted class does
not automatically satisfy all these positivity conditions.

The continuum sector ratios require a further comparison of
the twisted and untwisted small-field integrations. The source
leaves full-Hessian control on doubled domains and a quantitative
twisted-window estimate as additional work for its strongest
uniform asymptotics. These are steps to establish, not consequences
of the scalar Gaussian quadratic estimate. A gap found over one
fixed section also does not establish the infinite-volume mass gap.

Finally, the direction of the confinement asymptotic matters.
In the finite-size area-law regime the twisted quotient $Z^-/Z$
approaches one. Its defect $1-Z^-/Z$, or the associated odd-flux
weight, is the small quantity. The trace decomposition makes this
distinction explicit before any limiting argument is attempted.




\subsection{Centre flux and twisted partition functions}\label{C-366-1}

Centre twists admit a transfer-operator description in terms of electric-flux sectors. We establish the crossing and Fourier relations, the positivity properties of admissible mixtures and the continuum limits that follow from the construction estimates.

A single twisted class need not be reflection positive in every direction. The flux asymptotics remain sketches at the Hessian, window and transport steps specified below. We also distinguish a gap over a fixed small section from a gap of the infinite-volume continuum theory. In the conditional area-law regime the quotient $Z^-/Z$ tends to $1$; the small quantity is its defect.

The continuum centre-flux argument requires two estimates: \textbf{(Hess)} for the full fluctuation Hamiltonian on a doubled domain, and \textbf{(Flux-window)} for the probability of a twisted window. They are described below but are not consequences of the Gaussian quadratic estimate alone.

\subsubsection{Notation and hypotheses}

\emph{The lattice.} Throughout, $G=\mathrm{SU}(2)$, the directions are $\mu\in\{1,2,3\}$, and $\mathrm{tr}$ is the trace of $2\times2$ matrices, not halved. A box is a triple $N=(N_1,N_2,N_3)$ of integers $\ge3$ with its periodic lattice; $|N|=N_1N_2N_3$, a cube has equal sides, and $N^{\times3}=(N,N,N)$. $\partial U(p)$ is the plaquette variable of a plaquette $p$, $t_p=\mathrm{tr}\,\partial U(p)$, and $dU$ is the product of the Haar probability measures on the bonds. A sign field $\gamma$ on the bonds acts by $(\gamma U)(b)=\gamma(b)U(b)$, and $d\gamma(p)$ is the product of $\gamma$ over the four bonds of $p$. For a sign field $\eta$ on the plaquettes, $\beta\ge0$ and a bounded Borel function $F$ of the field,
\begin{equation}\label{C-366-2}
A_\eta(U)=\sum_p\bigl(1-\tfrac12\eta(p)\,\mathrm{tr}\,\partial U(p)\bigr),\qquad Z_\beta[\eta;F]=\int F\,e^{-\beta A_\eta(U)}\,\mathrm{d}U,
\end{equation}
and $A=A_\eta$ at $\eta\equiv1$.

\emph{Classes.} A class is $n=(n_{12},n_{13},n_{23})\in\mathbb Z_2^3$; a plane $\mu\nu$ with $n_{\mu\nu}=1$ is a twisted plane of $n$, and $n_{\mu\nu}$ also names the class whose one twisted plane is $\mu\nu$. A column of the plane $\mu\nu$ is the set of the plaquettes of that plane over one point of it; $\eta^n$ is $-1$ exactly on one column of each twisted plane; $Z[n;F]=Z_\beta[\eta^n;F]$, $Z[n]=Z[n;1]$, $r[n]=Z[n]/Z[0]$, $F^n=-\log r[n]$, $\mu_n=Z[n;\cdot\,]/Z[n]$ and $\langle\cdot\rangle=\mu_0$. On a cube, $r_i$ is $r[n]$ for a class with $i$ twisted planes; it depends on $i$ alone. A function of the field is centre-blind if it is invariant under $U\mapsto\gamma U$ for every sign field $\gamma$ on the bonds. A sign field $s$ on the plaquettes is closed if its product over the faces of each unit cube is $1$; its product over a lattice plane parallel to $\mu\nu$ is then $(-1)^{n_{\mu\nu}}$ for one class $n(s)$, and $[n]\ni\eta^n$ is the set of the closed $s$ with $n(s)=n$. A bounded function $G(U,s)$ of a field and a closed sign field, Borel in $U$, is covariant if $G(\gamma U,s\,\mathrm{d}\gamma)=G(U,s)$ for all sign fields $\gamma$ on the bonds; for it $Z_\beta[s;G(\cdot,s)]$ is the same number $\mathsf M_n[G]$ for all $s\in[n]$, and $\mu_n(G)=\mathsf M_n[G]/Z[n]$.

\emph{Transfer operators.} With $\mu$ as the time and $\nu<\rho$ the other two directions we write $n=(k,m)_\mu$, with the electric part $k=(n_{\mu\nu},n_{\mu\rho})$ and the magnetic part $m=n_{\nu\rho}$. The section is the periodic lattice $N_\nu\times N_\rho$, and a layer is the field on one section. On $L^2$ of the fields of the section, $T_m=D_m\mathsf KD_m$, where $\mathsf K$ is the crossing operator defined in Section~\YMMref{85}{677} by integrating the time-like bonds between two layers and $D_m^2=e^{-\beta A^m_\Sigma}$ is the Boltzmann weight of the section $\Sigma$, with the plaquette whose corner is a fixed site $\xi_*$ of the section reversed if $m=1$; a section with $m=1$ is called twisted. For a site $\xi$ of the section and $j\in\{\nu,\rho\}$, $(\xi,j)$ is the bond from $\xi$ to $\xi+e_j$, and the plaquette with the corner $\xi$ has the bonds $(\xi,\nu)$, $(\xi+e_\nu,\rho)$, $(\xi+e_\rho,\nu)$, $(\xi,\rho)$. The flip $C_j$ reverses the bonds $(\xi,j)$ with $\xi_j=(\xi_*)_j$, the bonds of direction $j$ that leave the line of the section through $\xi_*$ normal to $j$; $C^k=C_\nu^{k_1}C_\rho^{k_2}$ is composition with a map $c^k$ of the fields; $P_e=\frac14\sum_k(-1)^{e\cdot k}C^k$ for $e\in\mathbb Z_2^2$; and $Z_{e,m}=\mathrm{Tr}(P_eT_m^{N_\mu})$, written $Z^{[\mu]}_{e,m}$ where the time is to be named.

\emph{Numbers of a box.} $F_0=\log Z[0]$, $P=P(\beta)=\inf F_0/|N|$ over all boxes, the excess $\delta=F_0-|N|P$, and $\delta^n=\log Z[n]-|N|P=\log r[n]+\delta$. Over a section and with the height $M$, $\mathsf G(M)=\log(\mathrm{Tr}\,T_0^M/\|T_0\|^M)$ and $\mathsf d(M)=2F_0(M)-F_0(2M)$, the section being fixed. For integers $l\ge3$, $D_q(l)=q^3F_0(l^{\times3})-F_0((ql)^{\times3})$, $D_2(l)=8F_0(l,l,l)-F_0(2l,2l,2l)$ and $\mathsf e(l)=2F_0(l,2l,2l)-F_0(2l,2l,2l)$; over a section $(l_1,l_2)$, $\varepsilon_{\rm v}(l_1,l_2)=\log(\|T_0\|/\|T_1\|)$, and $\varepsilon_{\rm v}(l)=\varepsilon_{\rm v}(l,l)$. For a loop $C$, $W_C=\frac12\mathrm{tr}\,U(C)$; $W_{R\times T}$ is $W_C$ for the boundary of a rectangle $R\times T$ of a coordinate plane.

\emph{Gibbs states.} For a box $N$, $\mu_N$ is the measure $\langle\cdot\rangle=\mu_0$ of the periodic box $N$ (the index of $\mu_N$ is a box, that of $\mu_n$ a class); where it stands beside a measure on the fields of the infinite lattice, it is extended periodically. A Gibbs state at $\beta$ on the infinite lattice $a\mathbb Z^3$, $a>0$, is, as in Section~\YMMref{91}{697}, a Borel probability measure $\nu$ on its fields with $\nu(\gamma_BF)=\nu(F)$ for every finite set $B$ of bonds and every continuous function $F$ of finitely many bonds, $\gamma_B$ the Gibbs kernel of $B$ with the weight $\exp[-\beta\sum_p(1-\frac12\mathrm{tr}\,\partial U(p))]$, the sum over the plaquettes $p$ that hold a bond of $B$ (equation~\YMMref{(1818)}{698}); it is periodic if it is invariant under the translations of a subgroup of finite index of $a\mathbb Z^3$ (Section~\YMMref{91}{697}), and every periodic Gibbs state is invariant under all isometries of the lattice (Prop.~\YMMref{103.4}{758}). In Thm.~\ref{C-366-3}(10), (11) the lattice is $\mathbb Z^3$.

\emph{Mixtures and boards.} A weight $w\colon\mathbb Z_2^3\to[0,\infty)$, $w\ne0$, is admissible if 
\[
\hat w(e,m)=\sum_k(-1)^{e\cdot k}w((k,m)_\mu)\ge0
\]
 for all $\mu,e,m$; then $Z_w=\sum_nw(n)Z[n;\cdot\,]$, $|Z_w|=Z_w[1]$ and $\mu_w=Z_w/|Z_w|$. A board is a box with $N_\mu=\mathsf c\,\mathsf n_\mu$, $\mathsf c\ge3$ odd and $\mathsf n_\mu\ge2$ even, cut into $\mathsf N=\prod_\mu\mathsf n_\mu$ cells by mirrors through bonds, the columns placed where mirrors cross. For a bounded complex Borel function $F$ of one cell, $\mathrm{Fold}\,F$ is the product over the cells of the mirror copies of $F$, the copy in a cell being complex conjugated if the cell is odd relative to the given one, that is, reached from it by an odd number of reflections in the mirrors (equation~\YMMref{(1749)}{680}, \YMMref{(1749)}{680}, \YMMref{(1749)}{680}); for real $F$ the copies are the mirror images, and for complex $F$ the conjugation makes $Z[0;\mathrm{Fold}\,F]\ge0$ (with the plain mirror images the constant $e^{i\pi/8}$ on a board of $8$ cells would have the fold $-1$). 
\[
\|F\|_{\rm ch}^{\mathsf N}=Z[0;\mathrm{Fold}\,F]/Z[0]
\]
 is the periodic chessboard seminorm (Prop.~\YMMref{86.3}{681}), and $\|F\|_w^{\mathsf N}=Z_w[\mathrm{Fold}\,F]/|Z_w|$.

\emph{Cutoffs.} $L$, an odd integer with $L\ge13$, and $a_K=L^{-K}$ are the blocking factor and the spacings; the label is $b>0$ and $\beta=L^Kb$. A box $s$ of the cutoff $K$ has sides $s_\mu\in a_K\mathbb N$, $s_\mu\ge3a_K$; an index $K$ on a number above denotes that number at $N_\mu=s_\mu/a_K$ and $\beta=L^Kb$, as in $Z^z_K(s;b)=Z_K[z](s;b)$, $r_K[z](s;b)$ and $\delta^0_K$; with $p_\infty(K,b)=a_K^{-3}P(L^Kb)$ we put $\delta^n_K(s;b)=\log Z_K[n](s;b)-|s|\,p_\infty(K,b)$. A length is $L$-adic if it lies in $\mathbb D=\bigcup_Ka_K\mathbb N$. For $K,m\in\mathbb N$ the cube $\ell=2L^m$ is the lattice $\Lambda_{K,\ell}$ of the torus $T_\ell$ (Section~\YMMref{3}{13}); for other $m$ it is reached by the dilation $Z_K[n](s;b)=Z_{K-j}[n](L^js;L^jb)$. $Z_{K,\ell}$ is its periodic partition function, $\Delta_K[\ell,b]=\log Z_{K+1,\ell}-\log Z_{K,\ell}$, and on cubes $t=\ell/b$.

A box $s$ is mixed for the class $z$ if all $s_\mu\in L^{\mathbb Z}\cup2L^{\mathbb Z}$ and each twisted plane of $z$ has a side in $L^{\mathbb Z}$. We write $\rho^z(N,\beta)$ for $r[z]$ on the box $N$ at $\beta$, and, for a fixed class $z$, $\phi_j(t)=\rho^z((2L^j)^{\times3},2L^j/t)$. The constants $\gamma$, $M=L^{m'}$, $r_\star$ and $\mathfrak p_0$ are those of Prop.~\YMMref{69.1}{595}, with $r_\star=r$ and $2\mathfrak p_0>3r_\star+2$. Put $R(b)=\min\{L^a:a\in\mathbb N_0,\ L^a\ge(\log b)^{r_\star}\}$, $\ell_\flat(b)=2MR(b)$ and $\ell_\sharp(b)=L\ell_\flat(b)$, and set
\[
 m_0(b)=1+m'+\max\{\log_LR(b+\bar B),\lceil\log_LC_{\rm s}\rceil\},
 \qquad b\ge\gamma^{-2}.
\]
Here $C_{\rm s}$ is the torus-floor constant, chosen at least $C_L$ as in the paragraph following Prop.~\YMMref{74.5}{617}. With $\sigma$ and $\mathfrak b$ of Thm.~\ref{C-366-3}(3) at $\beta=L^Kb$, $\sigma_K(l)=a_K^{-2}\sigma(l/a_K)$ and $\mathfrak b_K(t,\lambda;l)$ is $\mathfrak b$ on the box $(t,\lambda,l)/a_K$.

\emph{Levels and block fields.} Over a section $l=(l_1,l_2)$ and with a time $\mu$, the levels are $E^{K,m,e}_i=a_K^{-1}\log(\|T_0\|/\lambda_i)$, $\lambda_1\ge\lambda_2\ge\dots>0$ the eigenvalues of $P_eT_m$, each repeated according to its multiplicity, and $E^{K,m,e}_i=\infty$ beyond them. $\mathcal M$ is the averaging map; on the cube $\ell$ at the cutoff $K$ the block field of depth $d\le K$ is $\mathcal M^{K-d}U$, a field on the block lattice of spacing $a_d$, and $\mu^K_d$ is its law under the periodic measure. A block line is a line of a block lattice.

\subsubsection{Positivity belongs to the electric sectors}

Fix a time direction. A magnetic twist $m$ determines a transfer
space and a positive transfer operator $T_m$. The two independent
centre flips commute with $T_m$ and generate a representation
$k\mapsto C^k$ of $\mathbb Z_2^2$. A temporal twist inserts
$C^k$ in the transfer trace. Thus the twisted partition function
has the exact finite-cutoff expression
\[
 Z[(k,m)]=\operatorname{Tr}(T_m^NC^k).
\]
The integer $N$ is the number of time steps. Although $T_m$ is
positive, the insertion $C^k$ may have both signs. This formula
does not imply that a fixed twisted class has all the reflection
positivity properties of the untwisted measure.

The character projections isolate the positive quantities. For
$e\in\mathbb Z_2^2$, put
\[
 P_e=\frac14\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z_2^2}(-1)^{e\cdot k}C^k.
\]
Character orthogonality makes the $P_e$ orthogonal projections
summing to the identity. They commute with $T_m$, so
\[
 Z_{e,m}=\operatorname{Tr}(P_eT_m^N)
       =\frac14\sum_k(-1)^{e\cdot k}Z[(k,m)]\ge0.
\]
The source's electric-flux decomposition is therefore a
decomposition of one positive transfer operator into invariant
subspaces. The positivity is visible before any limit is taken.
Changing which coordinate is time gives a second transfer-trace
description and the crossing identities between the finite
Fourier transforms. Those identities are retained below with
their finite-box parity and covering conventions.

The same distinction governs mixtures of classes. In a chosen
time direction, nonnegative electric Fourier weights ensure
reflection positivity. To obtain reflection positivity in every
coordinate direction by this argument, impose the same condition
in each description. Positivity in one description alone does
not establish the other conditions.

The continuum flux sketch asks for more than these algebraic
identities. Its window comparison concerns the actual
interacting integral in boxes with different twists. The
Hamiltonian differentiated there includes the interaction,
the chart Jacobian and the boundary regularization. A lower
bound for the Gaussian quadratic form at its reference field
does not control that full Hessian. Likewise, a change of sign
in two plane means specifies a candidate window but does not
estimate its probability or its transfer between cutoffs.
The sketch below specifies these probability and transfer estimates.
The finite-cutoff Fourier and transfer arguments do not depend on
their completion.

There are also two different large-distance spectral questions.
At a fixed small transverse section, the largest transfer
eigenvalue and the remaining thermal weights define sector
free energies and a transfer gap. An infinite-volume mass
gap requires control as the transverse section grows. The
finite-size confinement criterion in
\S\ref{supp:C-361-1} supplies a separate route to that
uniform control; the existence of one fixed-section gap
does not supply it.

Finally, the twist ratio in an area-law regime approaches one.
The decaying quantity is its defect. Keeping
$1-Z^-/Z$ visible in the finite Fourier formulas prevents the
electric-flux suppression from being misread as decay of
$Z^-/Z$ itself. The quantitative tube estimates later in the
confinement argument concern this small flux weight.

\subsubsection{Principal results}

The untwisted partition function supplies the reference for the
centre-flux ratios. We record the stability estimate at a fixed
physical label, including the room needed to compare two tori.

\begin{lemma}[Stability at a fixed label]\label{lem:pure-scaling-stability}
Use the common construction constants, with $C_{\rm s}\ge C_L$
as in the torus-floor choice following Prop.~\YMMref{74.5}{617},
and let $b\ge\gamma^{-2}$, $K\ge1$ and $m_i\ge m_0(b)$ for
$i=1,2$. Put $\ell_i=2L^{m_i}$ and $\theta_j=L^{K-j}b$.
The vacuum constants $E_i=E_{(K)}[((\ell_i,K),\theta_\bullet)]$
of the real progression are real, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:pure-scaling-stability}
 \begin{gathered}
 e^{-[c_{\rm low}+\frac92\log b]\ell_i^3}
 \le e^{-E_i}Z_{K,\ell_i,L^Kb}
 \le e^{(C_{\rm maj}+2)\ell_i^3},\\
 \left|E_1\ell_1^{-3}-E_2\ell_2^{-3}\right|
 \le2C_{\rm tt}C'_{\rm tt}E_0
       e^{-\kappa\min\{\ell_1,\ell_2\}/(5M)}.
 \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
Here $C_{\rm tt}=4096\sum_{q\ge0}e^{-q}$ and $C'_{\rm tt}=2$;
the rate and size constants are those of Prop.~\YMMref{74.5}{617}.
In particular, the first logarithmic error is bounded by
$(C_{\rm lab}+\frac92\log b)\ell_i^3$, where
$C_{\rm lab}=\max\{c_{\rm low},C_{\rm maj}+2\}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The increments of the sequence are
$L^{-1}\theta_{j-1}-\theta_j=0$, and
$\theta_j\ge b\ge\gamma^{-2}$. Thus it is an admissible
prescribed sequence in equation~\YMMref{(1524)}{614}, with last
radius $R(b)$. The definition of $m_0$ gives
\[
 L^{m_i}\ge LM R(b+\bar B)\ge LM R(b),\qquad
 \ell_i=2L^{m_i}\ge2LM C_{\rm s}\ge C_LM.
\]
Both tori are therefore admitted, including the stronger room
required for their comparison. Apply Prop.~\YMMref{74.4}{617}
at $k=K$, with $u_0=L^Kb$ and $u_K=b$, and
Prop.~\YMMref{74.5}{617} to this same sequence on the two
tori. These give the two bounds and the reality of the vacuum
constants. The vacuum terms are those of the canonical progression
of the prescribed sequence; its bare counterterms are its zero
increments. Finally $b\ge\gamma^{-2}\ge4$ implies $\log b>0$,
so the definition of $C_{\rm lab}$ gives the symmetric logarithmic
bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[One lattice]\label{C-366-3}
Let $N$ be a box, $\beta\ge0$, and $\mu$ a direction, taken as the time, $\nu<\rho$ the other two.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Transfer operator; order; momentum; crossing.)} $T_m\ge0$ is Hilbert--Schmidt with a continuous symmetric kernel $>0$; $C_\nu,C_\rho$ are commuting unitary involutions that commute with $T_m$. For every class $Z[(k,m)_\mu]=\mathrm{Tr}(T_m^{N_\mu}C^k)$, and $Z_{e,m}=\frac14\sum_k(-1)^{e\cdot k}Z[(k,m)_\mu]=\sum_i\lambda_i(P_eT_m)^{N_\mu}\ge0$ with eigenvalues $\lambda_i(P_eT_m)$ that do not depend on $N_\mu$; $Z_{e,m}<Z_{00,m}$ for $e\ne0$, and $Z_{e,m}>0$ if $\beta>0$. $\|T_m\|$ is a simple eigenvalue with an eigenfunction $>0$ in the range of $P_{00}$, and $\|T_1\|\le\|T_0\|$. Moreover
\[ e^{-2\beta(n_{23}N_1+n_{13}N_2+n_{12}N_3)}Z[0]\le Z[n]\le Z[(0,m)_\mu]\le Z[0], \]
the last two inequalities strict if $\beta>0$ and the classes differ; so $r[n]\le r[n']$ for every one-plane class $n'$ whose plane is twisted in $n$. Over a twisted section, with the reversed plaquette at the corner $\xi_*$ and the lines of $C_\nu$, $C_\rho$ through $\xi_*$, as in the setting, let $\mathcal T_\nu$ be the composition with the map $V\mapsto\mathsf S_\nu(\gamma_\nu V)$ of the fields, where $(\mathsf S_\nu V)_{(\xi,j)}=V_{(\xi+e_\nu,j)}$ is the step by one site in the direction $\nu$ and $\gamma_\nu$ reverses the one bond $(\xi_*+e_\nu,\rho)$, which the reversed plaquette shares with its neighbour in the direction $\nu$; and let $\mathcal T_\rho$ be formed likewise, with $\nu$ and $\rho$ exchanged and the bond $(\xi_*+e_\rho,\nu)$.

On all of $L^2$, $\mathcal T_\nu$ and $\mathcal T_\rho$ are unitaries that commute with $T_1$ and map the gauge invariant functions onto themselves, and $\mathcal T_\nu^{N_\nu}=C_\rho$, $\mathcal T_\rho^{N_\rho}=C_\nu$; so $\mathcal T_\nu$ commutes with $C_\rho$, and $\mathcal T_\rho$ with $C_\nu$. The products $\mathcal T_\nu\mathcal T_\rho$ and $\mathcal T_\rho\mathcal T_\nu$ differ by the reversal of the four bonds at the site $\xi_*+e_\nu+e_\rho$, and $\mathcal T_\nu C_\nu$ and $C_\nu\mathcal T_\nu$, as $\mathcal T_\rho C_\rho$ and $C_\rho\mathcal T_\rho$, by the gauge transformation that is $-1$ at the sites of one line of the section and $1$ elsewhere: gauge transformations with the values $\pm1$, which act as the identity on the gauge invariant functions.

On the gauge invariant functions, off which $T_1$ vanishes ($T_1=\Pi T_1\Pi$, $\Pi$ the gauge average) and which for $\beta>0$ form the closure of the range of $T_1$, the five operators $T_1$, $\mathcal T_\nu$, $\mathcal T_\rho$, $C_\nu$, $C_\rho$ commute pairwise. So the range of $P_e$, $e=(e_\nu,e_\rho)$, in the gauge invariant functions, on which $C_\nu=(-1)^{e_\nu}$ and $C_\rho=(-1)^{e_\rho}$, has an orthonormal basis of joint eigenvectors of $T_1$, $\mathcal T_\nu$ and $\mathcal T_\rho$, and the joint eigenvalues $(e^{i\theta_\nu},e^{i\theta_\rho})$ of $(\mathcal T_\nu,\mathcal T_\rho)$ there have $\theta_\nu\in\frac{2\pi}{N_\nu}(\mathbb Z+\frac{e_\rho}2)$ and $\theta_\rho\in\frac{2\pi}{N_\rho}(\mathbb Z+\frac{e_\nu}2)$; and $Z[(k,1)_\mu]=\mathrm{Tr}(T_1^{N_\mu}\mathcal T_\nu^{k_2N_\nu}\mathcal T_\rho^{k_1N_\rho})$.

For the times $1$ and $2$, with $e=(e_1,e_2)$ dual to $(n_{12},n_{13})$ and $m=n_{23}$ for the time $1$, and $(e_1,e_2')$ dual to $(n_{12},n_{23})$ and $m'=n_{13}$ for the time $2$, the crossing relation
\[ Z^{[1]}_{e_1e_2,m}=\tfrac12\sum_{m',e_2'\in\{0,1\}}(-1)^{e_2m'+e_2'm}\,Z^{[2]}_{e_1e_2',m'} \]
holds, and likewise for every pair of times: the flux of the common plane is kept, and the pairs $(e_2,m)$ and $(m',e_2')$ are exchanged by the Fourier transform of $\mathbb Z_2^2$. Hence, for every time, $Z_{e_1e_2,m}\le\min\{Z_{e_10,0},Z_{0e_2,0}\}$, $\|T_mP_{e_1e_2}\|\le\min\{\|T_0P_{e_10}\|,\|T_0P_{0e_2}\|\}$ and $\|\frac12(1-C_\nu)T_0\|=\|T_0P_{10}\|$: the least level of odd electric flux along $\nu$ has no flux along $\rho$. For $\beta>0$ and a fixed section, $\varepsilon_{\rm mag}=\log(\|T_0\|/\|T_1\|)=-\lim_{N_\mu\to\infty}N_\mu^{-1}\log r[n_{\nu\rho}]\in[0,\infty)$ and $\varepsilon_{\rm el}=\log(\|T_0\|/\|T_0P_{10}\|)=-\lim_{N_\mu\to\infty}N_\mu^{-1}\log\frac{Z[0]-Z[n_{\mu\nu}]}{Z[0]+Z[n_{\mu\nu}]}\in(0,\infty)$.
\item \emph{(Two lengths; the excess.)} Each of $\frac12(Z[0]\pm Z[n_{12}])$ is a sum of $N_1$-th powers of numbers $\ge0$ that do not depend on $N_1$, and a sum of $N_2$-th powers of numbers $\ge0$ that do not depend on $N_2$. $F_0/|N|$ does not increase in any side and tends to $P\ge-6\beta$ as all sides tend to infinity. Over every section and for every time, $0\le\mathsf G\le\delta$, $\mathsf G$ does not increase in the height, and $\mathsf G(M)\le\mathsf d(M)=2\delta(M)-\delta(2M)=2\mathsf G(M)-\mathsf G(2M)\le2\mathsf G(M)$.
