On $\mathfrak S$ the sign field $s(U)$ is locally constant and closed, $\mathsf w_{\rm mix}=e^{-\beta A_{s(U)}}\Xi(z)$ with $\Xi(z)=\sum_\Gamma\prod_{p\in\Gamma}z_p$ over the closed sets $\Gamma$, and the expansion of $\log\Xi$ in connected sets at $|z_p|\le\frac1{200}$ gives the $E(X)$, which vanish unless $X$ is connected and a union of vortices, connected for the relation of A(9): two plaquettes are neighbours if they are faces of one unit cube, that is, dual bonds with a common dual site. For this relation the faces of one cube are pairwise neighbours, so each cube meets one connected component of a closed set only, the components of a closed set are closed, the closed sets are the unions of vortices pairwise apart, and $\Xi$ is a gas of vortices; for a vortex $X$ that holds no smaller one the only clusters with the support $X$ are the repetitions of $X$, whose terms add up to $\log(1+\prod_{p\in X}z_p)$.

The last bound is the smallness, on $\mathfrak S_n$, of the weights $\sum_{s\in[n']}e^{-\beta A_s}/\mathsf w_{\rm mix}$ of the other classes, whose sets $\Gamma$ wind about the torus and so have at least $\min_\mu N_\mu$ plaquettes.

\emph{Step 5: one inequality; loops (A(10), A(11)).} Under the hypothesis $D_2(l_0)\le\frac1{20}$ of A(10), one inequality between the partition functions of the periodic cubes $l_0$ and $2l_0$, Lem.~\ref{C-366-9} gives $18D_2(2^il_0)\le(18D_2(l_0))^{2^i}$, hence $\delta(s,u,w)\le0.14108\,(suw/l^3)D_2(l)$ for $s,u,w\ge l\in\{2^il_0\}$ and $\mathsf r_h(l,l)\le\frac1{18}e^{-m_*h}$. Lem.~\ref{C-366-10} then gives, for $\bar\varepsilon\ge\varepsilon_{\rm v}(l)$ and an integer $h\ge2l$ with $e^{-m_*h}\le(h\bar\varepsilon)^4$, $h\bar\varepsilon\le\frac1{10}$ and $2(h/l)D_2(l)\le\frac14$,
\[ 2l\,\varepsilon_{\rm v}(2l)\le4.84\,(h/l)^3(l\bar\varepsilon)^4, \]
whose iteration from $l_1$ gives $l\varepsilon_{\rm v}(l)\le e^{-\sigma_*l^2}$; the bound $\sigma_*\ge\min\{\frac16m_*^2,m_*/l_0\}$ is the definition of $l_1$. With $2\zeta\le h\varepsilon_{\rm v}+\mathsf r_h$ and the doubling of the short sides (Lem.~\ref{C-366-10}) this is the bound on the boxes $(t,\lambda,h)$ and on the cubes; the bound on $\Lambda_-(N)$ is the same chain for the norm of $T_0$ on the odd functions, which is $\|T_0P_{10}\|$ by A(1). The loop bounds are Lem.~\ref{C-366-10} on the even cubes $N$, the factor $8^{T/N}$ tending to $1$ as $N\to\infty$; loops made of rows go the same way, row by row, with the norms of the transfer operators with static charges, the excess entering through $e^{1.13D_2(N/2)}$.

Uniqueness and convergence are Lem.~\ref{C-366-16}. Under the hypothesis $\mathsf e(l)\le0.069$, Lem.~\ref{C-366-9} gives $\theta\le0.8901$, $\mathsf e(4l)\le\theta^4/12.9$ and $D_2(8l)\le20\,\mathsf e(4l)^2\le20\theta^8/166.41\le0.047355$; for a cube $N\ge2l$ and the largest $M\in\{2^jl\}$, $j\ge1$, with $M\le N$, $\delta(N^{\times3})\le(N/M)^3\delta(M^{\times3})\le8\cdot0.01717\,\theta^{M/l}\le0.13736\,\theta^{N/2l}$; and $1-r[n]\le3(1-e^{-\mathsf G})\le3\delta$ (Lem.~\ref{C-366-9}), with $3\cdot0.13736\le0.4121$. A(11): $\nu$ is reflection positive at site mirrors and at bond mirrors, the exact statements on periodic Gibbs states and translation invariance comparing it with the periodic tori, where A(7) holds at $k=0$.

For a rectangle of height $T$, the paths from a point of the mirror that run $k$ bonds up, $R$ across and $k$ down, with $k=h+1,h$ at a site mirror for $T=2h+1$ and $k=h,h-1$ at a bond mirror for $T=2h$, form half loops whose Gram matrix has the entries $2\mathsf m(R,T+1)$, $2\mathsf m(R,T)$, $2\mathsf m(R,T-1)$; its positivity is the log-convexity. So $\mathsf m(R,T)/\mathsf m(R,T-1)$ does not decrease in $T$, $\mathsf m(R,T)\ge\mathsf m(R,1)^T\ge\mathsf w^{RT}$ by the symmetry, $V$ exists, is concave in $R$ by the log-convexity in $R$, and $V(R)/R$ does not increase; the bounds on $\mathsf w$, on $\mathsf m$ for $R,T\ge2$ and on $V(1)$, $V(R)$ come from integrating the bonds of the loop in their plaquettes.

\emph{Step 6: purity; small cubes; constructions (A(12)--(14)).} A(12): $\mathsf P=\mathsf Y^*\mathsf Y\ge0$ commutes with $C^k$; with $B_\pm=\frac12(1\pm C^k)\mathsf P\ge0$ and $d=\mathrm{Tr}(C^k\mathsf P)/\mathrm{Tr}\,\mathsf P\in[0,1]$,
\[ \mathrm{Tr}\,\mathsf P^i=\sum_\pm\mathrm{Tr}\,B_\pm^i\le\sum_\pm(\mathrm{Tr}\,B_\pm)^i=(\mathrm{Tr}\,\mathsf P)^i\sum_\pm\bigl(\tfrac{1\pm d}2\bigr)^i; \]
convexity in $d$ gives $d\ge(\mathfrak q_i-2^{1-i})/(1-2^{1-i})$, at $i=2$ the display gives $d^2\ge2\mathfrak q_2-1$, and as $i\to\infty$ it gives $\|\mathsf P\|\le\frac12(1+d)\,\mathrm{Tr}\,\mathsf P$; and $r[n]\ge Z[n;F\otimes\theta F]/Z[0]=d\,w_F$. For block fields, the averaging map commutes with the flip in a wall of the blocks of all orders, $L$ being odd. A(13): with the time $\mu$, $Z_{e,0}/Z[0]=\frac14\sum_k(-1)^{e\cdot k}r[(k,0)_\mu]$, and the three classes with $k\ne0$ have the quotients $r_1,r_1,r_2$: the first bound; $e^{-\mathsf G}=\|T_0\|^N/Z[0]\le Z_{00,0}/Z[0]$; $D_q(N)$ is a sum of defects of $q$-fold enlargement, the first $q^2[qF_0(N^{\times3})-F_0(qN,N,N)]\ge q^2(q-1)\mathsf G(N)$; the bound on $Z[0](N^{\times3})^2/Z[0](2N,N,N)$ is A(5)(a); if $r_1\le\frac13$, each sector trace at the height $N$ is at most $\frac12Z[0]$, and with $\mathrm{Tr}(P_eT_0^N)\le(\mathrm{Tr}\,P_eT_0^{N/2})^2$ this gives $(\mathrm{Tr}\,T_0^{N/2})^2\ge2\,\mathrm{Tr}\,T_0^N$, that is $\mathsf e(N/2)\ge\log2$; and $\Phi\ge F_0-N\log\|T_0\|=\mathsf G(N)$ on the cube gives the bound on $\mathfrak b$.

A(14)(a): there are two Haar-preserving, gauge covariant bijections $\Phi_\pm$ of the fields, moving only the bonds of the directions $\mu,\nu$ inside a tube of radius $h'$ about the reversed column, which spread the flux of the column over the cross-section of the tube; pointwise, $\frac12[A_\eta(\Phi_+U)+A_\eta(\Phi_-U)]-A(U)$ is at most a sum over the layers of the squares of the spread curvature, of order $(h'-\frac12)^{-2}$ in total, and of the actions of ladders of plaquettes of length of order $h'$ weighted by the angles of rotation. As $\Phi_\pm$ keep $dU$, $Z[\eta]=\int e^{-\beta A_\eta(\Phi_\pm U)}\,\mathrm{d}U$ for both signs; the arithmetic mean of the two integrands is at least their geometric mean, and Jensen's inequality in the periodic measure gives $\log r\ge-\beta\langle\frac12[A_\eta(\Phi_+U)+A_\eta(\Phi_-U)]-A(U)\rangle$.

For $\beta\ge1$ the mean actions $\bar a_{12},\bar a_{13},\bar a_{23}$ of the plaquettes of the three orientations in the periodic measure have $\bar a_{12}+\bar a_{13}+\bar a_{23}\le\lambda(\beta)/\beta$, by $\log Z[0]\ge-|N|[\frac92\log\beta+30]$ and the convexity of $\log Z[0]$ in $\beta$; and the mean action of a ladder of $1\times k$ plaquettes of one orientation is $k$ times the mean of that orientation. The second form is the choice of $h'$ of the order of $(\beta/\lambda(\beta))^{1/3}$, and for several twisted planes the tubes are disjoint. (b): $\log Z[0]\ge-|N|[\frac92\log\beta+30]$ by an elementary estimate; the chessboard estimate for $e^{\frac\beta2(1-\frac12t_p)}$ in one cell bounds its periodic mean by $\beta^{121.5}e^{810}$, so up to a factor $2$ in the partition function of the cube all plaquettes lie within $(130\pi^2\log\beta/\beta)^{1/2}$ of $\mathbf 1$ once $\log\beta\ge147.6$; cut the cube into eight free blocks, fix the gauge on a comb in each, and bound the action from below by a Gaussian whose determinant is the product over the inner Neumann momenta, the blocks having a side of the order $\beta^{1/6}$.

\emph{Step 7: the window (B(1)).} The first sentence of B(1) is A(1) and A(2) at $N_\mu=s_\mu/a_K$, $\beta=L^Kb$, with $|s|p_\infty=|N|P$; $\delta^0_K\ge0$ is the definition of $P$. On the cubes $2L^m$, $m\ge m_0(b)$, $b\ge\gamma^{-2}$, Lem.~\ref{lem:pure-scaling-stability} places $\log Z_K[0]$ within $C_*(b)\ell^3$ of a vacuum energy whose density varies boundedly from cube to cube, no constant depending on $K$ or $m$; the monotone density squeezes a box with sides $\ge2L^{m_0(b)}$ between two cubes, so $|\log Z_K[0](s)-\epsilon_K|s||\le C_*(b)|s|$ and $p_\infty\ge\epsilon_K-C_*(b)$, whence $\delta^0_K\le2C_*(b)|s|$ and, on the cubes, the explicit bound. For a compact set $\mathsf J\subset[b_-,b_+]$ of labels and $s_{\min}>0$, all labels of $\mathsf J$ and all sides $\ge s_{\min}$ are brought into this range at once by
\[ Z_K[n](s;b)=Z_{K-j}[n](L^js;L^jb), \]
with the least $j$ for which 
\[
L^jb_-\ge\gamma^{-2}
\]
 and 
\[
L^js_{\min}\ge2L^{m_0(L^jb_+)},
\]
which exists because 
\[
L^{-j}2L^{m_0(L^jb_+)}\to0
\]
: for $b\in\mathsf J$, $L^jb\ge\gamma^{-2}$ and, $m_0$ not decreasing, $L^js_{\min}\ge2L^{m_0(L^jb)}$; and, $C_*$ not decreasing, $C_*(L^jb)\le C_*(L^jb_+)$, so that $C=L^{3j}C_*(L^jb_+)$ serves for all $b\in\mathsf J$ and $K>j$. The bound on 
\[
\mathrm{Tr}\,T_m^{t/a_K}/\|T_0\|^{t/a_K}
\]
 follows from $\mathrm{Tr}\,T_1^M\le\mathrm{Tr}\,T_0^M$ and $\mathsf G\le\delta$. A lattice with $N_\mu/\beta$ in a compact set and $\beta$ large is a box of a cutoff $K$ at a label in $[1,L)$ with sides in a compact set, where these bounds hold uniformly, by the above at $\mathsf J=[1,L]$; for bounded $\beta$, $\delta^0\le6\beta|N|$. On a box with $L$-adic sides the remaining cutoffs are finitely many, each with a finite $\delta^0_K$ and $r_K[n]>0$, and $\delta^n_K-\log r_K[n]=\delta^0_K$ is bounded.

\emph{Step 8: floor and two cutoffs on mixed boxes (B(2)(a), B(4)).} After a dilation, $s$ is a centre sector of some $T_\ell$ (Lem.~\ref{C-366-7}), and the chain of $T_\ell$ restricted to the fixed fields is a chain for $Z^z_K(s;b)$. At the level $i$ the fluctuation integral over the fixed fields is, by Prop.~\ref{C-366-8} in the coordinates (requiring \textbf{(Hess)} for the full fluctuation Hamiltonian, and with least displacement $s_{\min}L^{K-i}$ in the units of that level), the $n$-th root of that of the cover up to $\epsilon_i\le C|s|L^{3(K-i)}e^{-cs_{\min}L^{K-i}}$. With $E(d)=\sum_{i\le K-d}\epsilon_i$, bounded independently of $K$, $\Sigma$ the small-field mass of the cover at the depth $d$ and $C_0$ formed from the constants,
\[ \log Z^z_K(s;b)\ge\frac{\log\Sigma}n-E(d)-|s|L^{3d}\bigl[C_0+\tfrac92\log(L^db)\bigr],\qquad\Sigma\ge\tfrac12Z_{K,\ell},\qquad\frac{|s|}{\ell^3}\log Z_{K,\ell}\ge|s|\,p_\infty(K,b), \]
the second when the large-field part of the cover is at most $\frac12$, the third by A(2); finitely many $K$ remain, at which the integrand is positive. Against the small periodic cube $\ell_\flat(b)$, box and cube being two sectors of one torus, the same chain gives the bound with $C_G$: the cover drops out. For two cutoffs, the small-field masses at $K$ and $K+1$ are compared pointwise at fixed fields as on $T_\ell$, the sector taking $|s|/\ell^3$ times the error of the cover; large fields are rare in the box, since an event of a slab passes by the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality at mirrors, with the power $\frac18$, to the small periodic cube $\ell_\flat(b)$, where Prop.~\ref{prop:ward-fixed-volume-rarity} controls it; box and cube are two sectors of one torus, whose partition function cancels.

The rate $L^{-K/10}$ and the uniformity in the label are those of the cover, with the arithmetic of the constants, which makes the condition on $K$ void for $|s|\le(\log b)^{2\mathfrak p_0-1}/C_V$. For two classes the terms $\frac{|s|}{\ell^3}\Delta_K$ cancel in the difference of the two laws, and the increments are summable. So, for a compact set $\mathsf J$ of labels, B(4) at $\mathsf J$ for $z$ and for the class $0$, for which $s$ is mixed too, gives $|\log r_{K+1}[z]-\log r_K[z]|\le2CL^{-K/10}$ for $K\ge K_0(\mathsf J)$; the first sentence of B(1) bounds $r_K[z]$ from below, uniformly on $\mathsf J$, at the finitely many $K<K_0$ at which $s$ is a box of the cutoff $K$; and as $\delta^0_K\ge0$, $\log Z^z_K(s;b)-|s|\,p_\infty(K,b)=\log r_K[z]+\delta^0_K\ge\log r_K[z]$: the floor of B(2)(a) holds with $C(s,b)$ bounded on $\mathsf J$, and $\inf_Kr_K[z]>0$ uniformly on $\mathsf J$.

On the boxes with sides in $2L^{\mathbb Z}$ the left member is the increment of $\log r_K[z]$, which tends to $0$ by B(2)(c) and B(3), plus the left member of the periodic class, for which every such box is mixed.

\emph{Step 9: compactness, no zero, the full sequence (B(2)(b), B(3)).} By B(1) at a compact set $\mathsf J$ of labels that holds the $b_j$, $i\,e^{-t_0E^K_i}\le e^{2Ct_0l_1l_2}$: Lem.~\ref{C-366-6}(b) applies, so every sequence $(K_j,b_j)$, $b_j\to b$, has a subsequence along which all levels converge, the sector traces divided by $\|T_0\|^{t/a_K}$ tend to $\mathcal W(e;m)(t;l)=\sum_ie^{-tE^{m,e}_i}$, holomorphic in $\mathrm{Re}\,t>0$, and $v_{(k,m)_\mu}=\sum_e(-1)^{e\cdot k}\mathcal W(e;m)/\mathcal D$, $\mathcal D=\sum_e\mathcal W(e;0)\ge1$, in each of the three expressions. The order of A(1) and A(5)(a) pass to the limit, and so does the crossing relation, for the sector weights $w^{[\mu]}_{e,m}=\frac14\sum_k(-1)^{e\cdot k}v_{(k,m)_\mu}=\mathcal W(e;m)/\mathcal D$, each the sector trace divided by the periodic trace of its own time and section: on each lattice the relation of A(1) divided by $Z[0]$ is the same relation between the numbers $Z^{[\mu]}_{e,m}/Z[0]=\frac14\sum_k(-1)^{e\cdot k}r[(k,m)_\mu]$, which converge to the $w^{[\mu]}_{e,m}$. A weight $w=\mathcal W(e;m)/\mathcal D$ vanishes at one height if and only if at all; it is real-analytic in a side $x$ of the section, and if it vanishes at $x_0$ then, for $q=L^p$ and $\mathsf c_q\ge\mathcal D(t/q;l_x)$ from B(1),
\[ w_t(x)\le\mathcal W(t;l_x)\le\mathcal W(t/q;l_x)^q\le\bigl[\mathsf c_q\,w_{t/q}(x)\bigr]^q=O(|x-x_0|^q), \]
so $w\equiv0$ in that side, and, side after side, on all boxes: this is the alternative of B(3), which passes to the limits of Step~10, and for a class with one twisted plane, whose quotient is the sum of its four sector weights with the time normal to its plane, it holds for $v_z$. With the floor on the box $(1,1,1)$, which is mixed for every class, this shows that the space of $H_{l,1}$ is not $\{0\}$ and, with the floor along the normal of A(5)(c) and compactness, B(2)(b); with B(5), which makes each electric weight on a small cube at least $\frac14(1-2C_\square t)$, each electric sector is not $\{0\}$, so $v_z<1$. On boxes with sides in $L^{\mathbb Z}$, B(4) makes the increments of $\log r_K[z]$ and of $L\log Z_K[0](s)-\log Z_K[0](s^{\mu+})$, $s^{\mu+}$ the box with $s_\mu$ multiplied by $L$, summable uniformly on compacts of labels, the terms $\Delta_K$ cancelling in the second: this is (R1) of Prop.~\ref{C-366-20} on the ray of the boxes with sides in $L^{\mathbb Z}$, and Prop.~\ref{C-366-20} gives the convergence of all levels along the full sequence, of $r_K[z]$ on every $L$-adic box, of $\delta^0_K$ and of the differences of the norms.

The same holds along every sequence $(K_j,b_j)$ of cutoffs and labels with $K_j\to\infty$ and $b_j\to b\in(0,\infty)$, in the place of the full sequence at the fixed label $b$; these sequences form a class that is closed under subsequences. (R1) holds along each of them: each $r_K[z](s;\cdot)$ and each difference $L\log Z_K[0](s)-\log Z_K[0](s^{\mu+})$ is continuous in the label at a fixed $K$, and their increments in $K$ are summable uniformly for the labels in a compact set, so that they converge uniformly on compacts of labels to limits that are continuous in the label, and so converge along $(K_j,b_j)$. The proof of Prop.~\ref{C-366-20} then runs along such a sequence as it stands: its only input, the window, is uniform for the labels in a compact set (B(1): the supremum of $\delta^0$ over the lattices with $N_\mu/\beta$ in a compact set is finite), and Lem.~\ref{C-366-6}(a), (b) and the turning of the box do not read the label.

So all levels, $r_K[z]$ on every $L$-adic box, $\delta^0_K$ and the differences of the norms converge along every such sequence. Two such sequences with one limit label $b$ interlace into a third one, along which the limits exist: the limits depend on $b$ alone. They are continuous in $b$: for $b_i\to b$ a choice of $K_i\to\infty$ with the values at $(K_i,b_i)$ within $1/i$ of the limits at $b_i$ gives a sequence of the class. And the convergence is uniform for the labels in a compact set, since otherwise a compact set of labels would hold a sequence $(K_j,b_j)$ with $b_j\to b$ whose values stay at a fixed distance from the limits at the labels $b_j$, which tend to those at $b$, against the convergence along it. $E_{\rm mag}$ and $E_{\rm el}$ are Lem.~\ref{C-366-6} for the limit lists, the space of $H_{l,1}$ not being $\{0\}$.

On the cubes, $L^3\log Z_{K,\ell}-\log Z_{K,L\ell}$ is a difference of periodic numbers of two cubes in which the terms $\Delta_K$ of B(4) cancel, so $D(t)$ exists; it depends on $t$ alone by the argument of Step~10; $\delta^0_K(\ell^{\times3})$, telescoped over the cubes $L^r\ell$, gives $\delta(t)=\sum_rL^{-3(r+1)}D(L^rt)$; and the behaviour of $D$ as $t\to0$ is the asymptotics of Prop.~\ref{C-366-13}(b), (e) for the periodic cubes, the bulk cancelling, carried to every cutoff by B(4) as in Step~11. By Thms.~\YMMref{AJ}{673} and~\YMMref{AD}{607}, through Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AD}{607}}, the periodic quotients are normal families in the label, and B(6) gives the analyticity.

\emph{Step 10: every lattice; two blocking factors (B(2)(c), B(3)).} By Lem.~\ref{C-366-11} and B(1) the quotients are equicontinuous in the sides for $N_\mu/\beta$ in a compact set; with Step~9, in its form for the sequences $(K_j,b_j)$ with a moving label $b_j=L^{-K_j}\beta_j\to b$, this gives a continuous $V^L_z(s;b)$, the limit along every sequence with $L^{-K_j}N_j\to s$, $L^{-K_j}\beta_j\to b$, with the Lipschitz bound of B(3); in each side, at real values of the others, it is $\sum_e(-1)^{e\cdot k}\mathcal W(e;m)/\mathcal D$, a quotient of Laplace transforms, and real-analytic. The constants may be chosen with the blocking factors $L_1=L$ and $L_2=L+2$, and $\log L_1/\log L_2\notin\mathbb Q$; so for $b_1,b_2>0$ there are $K_j,M_j\to\infty$ with $K_j\log L_1-M_j\log L_2\to\log(b_2/b_1)$, and $\beta_j=L_1^{K_j}b_1$, $N_j\approx\tau\beta_j$ is a sequence of both scales, of the label $b_1$ at the scale $L_1$ and of the moving label $L_2^{-M_j}\beta_j\to b_2$ at the scale $L_2$, to which Step~9 applies in its form for sequences:
\[ V^{L_1}_z(\tau b_1;b_1)=V^{L_2}_z(\tau b_2;b_2), \]
so $V_z(s;b)=v_z(s/b)$, every sequence with $\beta_j\to\infty$, $N_j/\beta_j\to\tau$ converges ($\beta_j=L^{K_j}b_j$, $b_j\in[1,L)$), and the limits do not depend on the choice of the constants. For $s\in(2L^{\mathbb Z})^3$, $V_z(s;b)=V_z(\frac12s;\frac12b)>0$, the box $\frac12s$ being mixed for every class; positivity of the limit and of each $r_K$ is the floor, uniform for the labels in a compact set, since the convergence is uniform there (Step~9), the limits are continuous and positive, and the first sentence of B(1) bounds the finitely many remaining cutoffs; and an infimum $0$ over the cubes with $N/\beta\in I$, or over the lattices with $N/\beta$ in a compact subset of $\{v_z>0\}$, would give, along $\beta_j\to\infty$, a point of that set with $v_z=0$. The same for the levels gives their extension to real sections and their homogeneity. The weights of the mixture converge with the $r_K[n]$, and $1\le\sum_nv_n\le8$ with $v_0=1\ge v_n$, so that their limits lie in $[v_n/8,\frac12]$ for $n\ne0$.

\emph{Step 11: small cubes (B(5)).} (a), the ceiling. By A(1), $r_2,r_3\le r_1$, and by the symmetry of the axes it is enough to bound $r[n]$ for $n=n_{13}=((1,0),0)_3$, whose twisted plane holds the time $3$, on the cubes $\ell=2L^m$. A dilation by a power of $L$ keeps $t$ and the lattices and brings $(\ell,b)$ into the range $b\ge b_0$, $MR(b)\le L^m$, $\ell\le2ML^2(\log b)^{r_\star}$ of Lem.~\ref{C-366-12}(b), where small $t$ is large $b$. In a block layer normal to $3$ of the block field of depth one, with $\bar h_1(y)$, $\bar h_2(y)$ the products of the block field along the straight closed block lines from $y$ in the directions $1$ and $2$ (as in \S\ref{C-366-15}), let $\bar s_1$ and $\bar s_+$ be the means over the sites $y$ of the layer of $\frac12\mathrm{tr}\,\bar h_1(y)$ and of $\frac12\mathrm{tr}[\bar h_1(y)\bar h_2(y)]$. The flip of $n$ changes the signs of both; on a flat field with the holonomies $e^{i\varphi_\mu\mathsf a\cdot\sigma}$ they are $\cos\varphi_1$ and $\cos(\varphi_1+\varphi_2)$, which vanish together exactly at the fixed points $\varphi_1=\pm\frac\pi2$, $\varphi_2\in\{0,\pi\}$ of the flip $\varphi_1\mapsto\varphi_1+\pi$, taken up to $\varphi\mapsto-\varphi$. Let
\[ F=\mathbf 1\bigl\{\max(|\bar s_1|,|\bar s_+|)<m_0t^{1/2}\bigr\}, \]
with an absolute $m_0$, be read at the block layer next to a block mirror normal to $3$ at the cutoffs $K\ge K_\sharp$ of Lem.~\ref{C-366-12}(b), and at the bare layer next to a mirror between two layers below $K_\sharp$; $F$ is gauge invariant, Borel with values in $[0,1]$ and flip-blind, and its mirror image $\theta F$ is $F$ read at the layer on the other side of the mirror. Establishing \textbf{(Flux-window)} would give, with absolute $C_2$ and $\epsilon_F$, at every cutoff and with the columns of $n$ away from the layers of $F$ and $\theta F$: \textbf{(F1)} $\mu(F)\le C_2t$, and \textbf{(F2)} $Z[n;1-F]\le\epsilon_F\,t\,Z[0]$.

Both estimates remain to be established in \textbf{(Flux-window)}. In particular, (F1) is a bound for a shrinking event of the block means, and does not follow from the uninserted periodic Laplace estimate of Prop.~\ref{C-366-13}. The sign reversal of the plane means under the twist likewise does not by itself establish (F2).

Now
\[ r[n]=\frac{Z[n;\theta F\,F]}{Z[0]}+\frac{Z[n;1-\theta F\,F]}{Z[0]} . \]
The first term is bounded through the overlap representation of the class with flux, in the form that A(6) takes for a function of a slab and its mirror image, the trace formula of Step~4 with $\alpha,\alpha'$ as there: $Z[n;\theta F\,F]=\sum_e(-1)^{e\cdot k}\|T_0^{\alpha/2}\hat F\,T_0^{\alpha'/2}P_e\|_2^2\le Z[0;\theta F\,F]\le Z[0;F]=\mu(F)\,Z[0]$. In the second, $1-\theta F\,F\le(1-F)+(1-\theta F)$, and $Z[n;1-\theta F]=Z[n;1-F]$ by the reflection, the columns being moved away from the layers of $F$ (Step~1). So $r_1\le(C_2+2\epsilon_F)\,t$ at every cutoff, with the absolute $C_\square=C_2+2\epsilon_F$; $t_0$ and both bounds are as specified in (Flux-window). (b) and (c): on the odd cube $s=\frac12\ell_\sharp(b)=LMR(b)$, $b\ge b_\sharp$, $S=s$, B(4) holds uniformly in the label from $K_0=\lceil c_2\log_LS\rceil$ on, $c_2=20\varpi$: its second condition is void on this cube, since $|s|\le L^6M^3(\log b)^{3r_\star}\le(\log b)^{2\mathfrak p_0-1}/C_V$ for large $b$, as $2\mathfrak p_0>3r_\star+1$, so that the low cutoff of B(4) is $K_0$.

At $K_0$ the lattice has $N_0=SL^{K_0}\in[S^{1+c_2},LS^{1+c_2}]$ sites a side, so $N_0\le C(\log b)^{r_\star(1+c_2)}$, at $\beta_0=bL^{K_0}\ge b$; this lattice and those of the cutoffs $K<K_0$, which are smaller at $\beta\ge b$, lie in the range of Prop.~\ref{C-366-13} for $c<1/(r_\star(1+c_2))$ and large $b$. From $K_0$ on, B(4), uniformly in the label, carries the lattice value to every cutoff with a relative error $o(1)$ as $b\to\infty$, the sum of $c_1S^\varpi L^{-K/10}$ over $K\ge K_0$ being at most a multiple of $S^{\varpi-c_2/10}=S^{-\varpi}$; this is (c), the values $t=LMR(b)/b$ filling $(0,t_0]$; $v_z$ depends on $t$ alone (B(3)), which gives $C^{-1}t\le v_z\le Ct$ and, with Prop.~\ref{C-366-13}(e), $v_z(t,t,t)/t\to\mathscr G_z$.

The ratios are Prop.~\ref{C-366-13}(c), (e) for two classes, the periodic denominators cancelling. (d): with the ceiling, $r_1\le\frac15$ on the cubes $2L^m$ with $t\le t_1=\min\{t_0,1/5C_\square\}$ at every cutoff, and A(13) applies; $\delta^0_K\ge\mathsf G\ge\log(4/(1+3r_1))\ge\log(4/(1+3C_\square t))$.

\emph{Step 12: the label (B(6)).} A source is a complex function $\mathsf h$ on $T_\ell$ in the ball of the norm of Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AD}{607}} (the source $w$ there); for a class $n$, with $x(p)$ the barycentre of the plaquette $p$, put
\[ Z_K[n;\mathsf h]=\int\exp\Bigl[-\sum_pL^K\bigl(b_0-\mathsf h(x(p))\bigr)\bigl(1-\tfrac12\eta^n(p)\,\mathrm{tr}\,\partial U(p)\bigr)\Bigr]\,\mathrm{d}U ; \]
at $n=0$ this is the left member of the identity of Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AD}{607}} at $\beta=L^Kb_0$, and at a constant source $\mathsf h\equiv c$ it is $Z_K[n]$ at the label $b_0-c$. Let $n$ have one or two twisted planes, $\mu$ a direction that lies in each of them, and $\theta$ the reflection $x_\mu\mapsto-x_\mu$, with the mirror planes $x_\mu\in\{0,\frac\ell2\}$, or $x_\mu\mapsto\frac\ell2-x_\mu$, with the mirror planes $x_\mu\in\{\frac\ell4,\frac{3\ell}4\}$; the two mirror planes cut $T_\ell$ into the closed halves $H_-$ and $H_+=\theta H_-$. Let $\mathsf h$ be symmetric under $\theta$ and real within $\frac\ell{16}$ of the two mirror planes, and let its conjugated fold $\mathsf h^\flat$ be $\mathsf h$ on $H_-$ and $\bar{\mathsf h}$ on $H_+$.

With $\mu$ as the time and the mirror layers $x_\mu\in\{0,\frac\ell2\}$, $Z_K[n;\mathsf h]=\iint\Psi_-(V,V')\,\Psi_+(V,c^kV')\,\mathrm{d}V\,\mathrm{d}V'$, where $V,V'$ are the fields of the two mirror layers, on whose plaquettes the weights $L^K(b_0-\mathsf h(x(p)))$ are real and positive and give the square roots of their factors to each half, $\Psi_\mp$ are the integrals over the bonds inside $H_\mp$, and $c^k$ is the flip of the electric part of $n$, whose magnetic part vanishes because $\mu$ lies in every twisted plane. The reflection $\theta$ keeps the Haar measure and the traces of the plaquettes, so the symmetry of $\mathsf h$ gives $\Psi_+=\Psi_-$, while $\overline{\Psi_-}$ is the integral over $H_-$ at the source $\bar{\mathsf h}$, that is, by $\theta$, over $H_+$ at $\bar{\mathsf h}$; the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality in the fields of the mirror layers, $c^k$ keeping their Haar measure, gives
\[ |Z_K[n;\mathsf h]|\le\|\Psi_-\|_2^2=Z_K[0;\mathsf h^\flat] . \]
At mirrors midway between two layers the same holds, the crossing kernel at the mirror being positive semidefinite at real positive weights (Step~1).
For three twisted planes the same with the time $3$, which lies in the planes $13$ and $23$ and whose section is twisted, gives $|Z_K[n;\mathsf h]|\le Z_K[n_{12};\mathsf h^\flat]$, the right member being $\ge0$, and a second fold with the time $1$, which lies in the plane $12$, at mirrors normal to the direction $1$ at which the source is symmetric and real as well, gives $Z_K[n_{12};\mathsf h^\flat]\le Z_K[0;\mathsf h^{\flat\flat}]$, $\mathsf h^{\flat\flat}$ being $\mathsf h$ or $\bar{\mathsf h}$ according to the product of the signs of the two halves. The identity of Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AD}{607}} writes $Z_K[0;\mathsf h^\flat]/|Z_K[0;\mathsf h]|$ as the exponential of the sum of the differences of the real parts of the local energies $e_j(X;\cdot)$ at $\mathsf h^\flat$ and at $\mathsf h$, times the quotient of the moduli of the two remainders $\widetilde Z$.

An energy at $\bar{\mathsf h}$ is the conjugate of the energy at $\mathsf h$, and it reads the source near its domain; so the real parts agree on every localization domain that does not meet both $H_-\cap\{\mathrm{Im}\,\mathsf h\ne0\}$ and $H_+\cap\{\mathrm{Im}\,\mathsf h\ne0\}$, two sets at a distance $\ge\frac\ell8$. A domain of the level $j$ that meets both has an extent of at least $\ell L^{K-j}/8M-4$ ({\cite[eq.~321]{YMM2}}); the number of the localization domains ({\cite[Lem.~O.1]{YMM2}}) and the decay of the energies in the extent bound their sum by a number that does not depend on $K$, and with the bounds on $\widetilde Z$, which also give $Z_K[0;\mathsf h]\ne0$ for small sources,
\[ |Z_K[n;\mathsf h]|\le Z_K[0;\mathsf h^\flat]\le\mathsf M_{\rm S}|Z_K[0;\mathsf h]|,\qquad Z_K[0;\mathsf h]\ne0 , \]
and the same with $\mathsf h^{\flat\flat}$ for three twisted planes. For the constant source $b_0\mapsto b_0-c$, written as $c\chi_1+c\chi_2$ with a partition of unity $\chi_1+\chi_2=1$ in $x_\mu$, $\chi_1$ vanishing within $\frac\ell{16}$ of the planes $x_\mu\in\{0,\frac\ell2\}$ and $\chi_2$ within $\frac\ell{16}$ of the planes $x_\mu\in\{\frac\ell4,\frac{3\ell}4\}$, the quotient $r_K=Z_K[n;\cdot\,]/Z_K[0;\cdot\,]$ at the source $\zeta_1\chi_1+\zeta_2\chi_2$, in which one of the two parts may be complex while the other is real, is bounded by $\mathsf M_{\rm S}$ on the two crosses of a bidisc in $(\zeta_1,\zeta_2)$, and the following lemma bounds it on a smaller bidisc. If $F$ is holomorphic near $\bar D_R^2$ and $|F|\le\mathsf M$ wherever one variable lies in $\bar D_R$ and the other in $[-R,R]$, then $|F|\le27\,\mathsf M$ on $\bar D_{R/8}^2$; if $F$ is holomorphic near $\bar D_R^4$ and $|F|\le\mathsf M$ wherever one variable lies in $\bar D_R$ and the three others in $[-R,R]$, then $|F|\le12600\,\mathsf M$ on $\bar D_{R/15}^4$ (this form serves for three twisted planes).

For the proof put $\rho_\circ=2+\sqrt3$ and $\mathsf j(u)=\frac R4(u+u^{-1})$, which maps the annulus $\rho_\circ^{-1}\le|u|\le\rho_\circ$ into $\bar D_R$ and the unit circle onto $[-\frac R2,\frac R2]$. Moving the circle of one variable of the Cauchy integral to $|u|=\rho_\circ^{\pm1}$, the other variables staying on the unit circle, where $\mathsf j$ is real, bounds the Laurent coefficients of $F\circ\mathsf j$ by $\mathsf M\rho_\circ^{-\max_i|k_i|}$; summing them on the annuli $1.3^{-1}\le|u_i|\le1.3$, whose images hold $\bar D_{R/8}$, gives at most $26.2\,\mathsf M$, and on $1.15^{-1}\le|u_i|\le1.15$, whose images hold $\bar D_{R/15}$, at most $12563\,\mathsf M$ in four variables. This bounds $r_K$ on a disc whose radius does not depend on $K$, and Cauchy's estimate gives the derivatives.

In $t$ this is the normal family of the $\phi_j$, and Vitali's theorem gives the analyticity of the limit. With $m_0=\inf_Kr_K(b_0)>0$, Cauchy's estimate keeps $r_K$ away from $0$ on a smaller disc, which, $Z[0]$ having no zero there, gives the zero-free discs and $\Omega$; the first two derivatives of $\log r_K$ in the label are differences of means and of variances of the total action, bounded by Cauchy's estimate.

\emph{Step 13: block pairs (B(7)).} A block mirror lies midway between two layers, $L$ being odd; for $G$ bounded Borel in the block pairs on one side, $(U,s)\mapsto G(\mathcal M^{K-d}_sU,s^{(d)})$ depends on the bonds and signs on that side, and the reflection commutes with $\mathcal M_s$: the clause on pairs in A(8) gives the positivity, which weak limits keep; at each cutoff $\mathcal M^{K-d}_s=\mathcal M_s\circ\mathcal M^{K-d-1}_s$ makes the tower consistent. Under the conditions of B(7), the small-field chain among the construction results on the periodic torus, with the rarity of its large-field regions (Prop.~\ref{prop:ward-fixed-volume-rarity}), bounds the periodic probability of a rough block plaquette of some depth $d'\in[d,K]$ by $\mathsf R(d)$, uniformly in $K$; the dilation carries this to the other pairs $(\ell,b)$, the depth $d$ becoming $d-j$.

With $\gamma$ a chart of $s$ near a block plaquette $P$, the sign of $P$ in the block sign field times $\partial(\mathcal M^k_sU)(P)$ is $\partial(\mathcal M^k(\gamma U))(P)$: the event of a rough plaquette is covariant and local, and off it the signs of the block traces are the block sign field. In $\mathbb Z/2\lambda$, $\lambda$ odd, every arc of at most $\frac12(\lambda+1)$ points lies in one of four arcs of $\lambda$ points, so each local event lies in one of sixteen quarters of the torus cut by mirrors in two directions; the quarter bound of A(8) carries the union of the events of one quarter into the class with the root $\frac14$, which gives $16\mathsf R(d)^{1/4}$, and the bound for the mixtures.

In a weak limit the class is then, up to null sets, the class of the block sign fields of the tower. For the other statements on limit points pass to a subsequence along which the laws of the towers converge in every class. The quarter bound of A(8) at each cutoff, $r_K[n]\mu_n(B)\le\mu^K_d(B_1)^{1/4}$, and the convergence in total variation of $\mu^K_d$ to $\mu_d$ (through Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8}) give $r_n\mathbb P^n(B)\le\mu_d(B_1)^{1/4}$ for open $B$ by the portmanteau theorem, and for Borel $B$ by outer regularity, the group of the sign changes being finite; the half bound of A(8) gives the exponent $\frac12$. For the consistency of the limit towers the identity at each cutoff is joined to Lusin's theorem, $\mathcal M_s$ being a Borel map and not continuous.

The relation between the block sign fields is a closed condition and passes to the limit. For the fields fix a class with $r_n>0$, a depth $d\ge1$, a block bond $c$ of depth $d$ and $\epsilon>0$; $\mathcal M(\cdot)(c)$ is a Borel function of the block field of depth $d+1$ near $c$, and by Lusin's theorem it is continuous on a compact set $\mathcal K$ of these local fields of $\mu_{d+1}$-measure at least $1-\epsilon$. The towers with $V_d(c)=(\mathcal M_{s_{d+1}}V_{d+1})(c)$ whose local field near $c$, read in a chart of $s_{d+1}$, lies in $\mathcal K$ form a closed set; at each cutoff it holds the tower off a covariant local event whose probability under $\mu_n$ is at most $r_K[n]^{-1}\mu^K_{d+1}(\mathcal K^c)^{1/4}$ by the quarter bound.

By the portmanteau theorem and the convergence of $\mu^K_{d+1}$ in total variation, $\mathbb P^n$ gives this closed set a probability at least $1-\epsilon^{1/4}/r_n$, and $\epsilon\to0$ gives the consistency at $c$, almost surely; there are finitely many $c$ and countably many $d$.

\emph{Step 14: tension of a slab (B(8)).} On one lattice, A(4)(a) at the heights and lengths $N/L$ and $N$, $N=\ell/a_K$, with $\mathsf G,\Phi\le\delta$ and the last inequality of A(2), $\delta(N/L,N,N)\le L^2\delta((N/L)^{\times3})$ and $\delta(N/L,N/L,N)\le L\delta((N/L)^{\times3})$, gives the two inequalities in lattice units, the three terms of the bound on $\sigma$ adding up to $(L/(L-1))^2L^3\delta((N/L)^{\times3})$ exactly; in physical units a product of two lattice lengths carries $L^{2K}$. The right members are bounded in $K$: $\delta^0_K$ by B(1), and $\kappa_K\to\log(2/(1-v_1(t,t,t)))<\infty$ by B(3), since $v_1<1$ on the cubes with $L$-adic sides. In the limit the least level of the sector $e=10$ is $\varepsilon_{\rm el}$ (A(1)) in physical units. The lower bound on $\sigma_K$ is A(3) in physical units, and the bound on $-\log\mathfrak b_K$ is the last bound of A(3) with $R_K(\lambda_0)\le\mathsf G_K(\lambda_0;l,2\lambda_0)/\lambda_0\le\delta^0_K(\lambda_0,l,2\lambda_0)/\lambda_0\le(2\lambda_0l/s'^3)\bar\delta(s')$ by A(4)(b) and A(2), and $\Phi_K(t_0,\lambda_0)\le(t_0\lambda_0l/s'^3)\bar\delta(s')$; the equivalence follows by choosing first $\lambda$, then $t$, large.

\emph{Step 15: the small twisted section (B(9)).} The levels are read in the normalisation of B(9): they are the numbers $a_K^{-1}\log(\lambda_0/\lambda_i)$, $\lambda_0=\|T_1\|$, the four sectors together, so that the least of them, the vacuum, is $E_0=0$; they are the levels of the setting diminished by $a_K^{-1}\log(\|T_0\|/\|T_1\|)$, and their limits are the eigenvalues of $H_{(l,l),1}$ diminished by $E_{\rm mag}(l,l)$. Over the twisted section $(N,N)$, $N=l/a_K$, at the time $1$, $\mathrm{Tr}\,T_1^h=Z[n_{23}](h,N,N)$; with $x(h)=\sum_{i\ge1}(\lambda_i/\lambda_0)^h$, in
\[ L\log\mathrm{Tr}\,T_1^h-\log\mathrm{Tr}\,T_1^{Lh}=L\log(1+x(h))-\log(1+x(Lh)) \]
the bulk and all that is proportional to the time cancel. The chain that bounds it has these links. (i) A dilation by a power of $L$ keeps $t$ and the lattices and takes $(l,b)$ to $(l',b')$ with $l'=\frac12\ell_\sharp(b')=LMR(b')\ge\ell_\flat(b')$, the values $LMR(b')/b'$ filling $(0,t_0]$ (Step~11); small $t$ is large $b'$. (ii) The odd boxes $(l',l',l')$, $(Ll',l',l')$, $(L^2l',l',l')$ and, for each fixed $j\ge1$, $(L^jl',l',l')$ have their sides in $L^{\mathbb N}$ and are mixed for $n_{23}$; on them B(4) holds uniformly in the label from its low cutoff $\lceil c_2\log_LS\rceil$ on, its second condition being void for large $b'$, since $|s|\le L^{j+6}M^3(\log b')^{3r_\star}\le(\log b')^{2\mathfrak p_0-1}/C_V$ as $2\mathfrak p_0>3r_\star+1$.

In the left member of the display at $h=N$, which in the dilated units is $L\log Z[n_{23}](l'^{\times3})-\log Z[n_{23}](Ll',l',l')$, and at $h=LN$, the terms $\frac{|s|}{\ell^3}\Delta_K$ of B(4) cancel, so that B(4) carries its value at the low cutoff to every cutoff with an error summable in $K$. (iii) At and below the low cutoff the lattices lie in the range of the twisted clause of Prop.~\ref{C-366-13}(a), whose volume terms cancel in the display and whose Gaussian term gives the free value: with $\theta^a$ the phases of the three colours $a$ of $n_{23}$ and the momenta $p\in((2\pi\mathbb Z+\theta^a_2)/N)\times((2\pi\mathbb Z+\theta^a_3)/N)$ mod $2\pi$, none of them $0$, $\prod_{j<h}(2\cosh\omega-2\cos\frac{2\pi j}h)=2\cosh h\omega-2$ gives $\log\mathscr D^{n_{23}}(h,N,N)=-hE_{\rm free}+\log(1+x_{\rm free}(h))$, $E_{\rm free}=\frac12\sum_{a,p}\omega(p)$, with
\[ 1+x_{\rm free}(h)=\prod_{a,p}\bigl(1-e^{-h\omega(p)}\bigr)^{-1},\qquad2\cosh\omega(p)-2=\hat p^2 , \]
and the free value of the display is that of $x_{\rm free}$. (iv) With $L\ge13$ of the setting, the free value at $h=N$ is at most $0.26(L-1)$: at $N=L=13$ it is $3.0917$ against $0.26(L-1)=3.12$, the margin $0.028$; at $h=LN$ it is about $4Le^{-\pi L}$. (v) $c_0$, formed from the constants, is chosen so that for $t\le c_0$ the errors of Laplace's method and of B(4) stay below that margin at $h=N$, and are small enough against the free value at $h=LN$ that $x(LN)\ge0.29693\,e^{-\pi L}$ follows. Then at every cutoff the display at $h=N$ is at most $0.26(L-1)$; as $x$ does not increase in $h$, $(L-1)\log(1+x(N))\le0.26(L-1)$, so $x(N)\le e^{0.26}-1=0.29693$ and $N\log(\lambda_0/\lambda_1)\ge\log(1/0.29693)\ge1.2142$; at $h=LN$, with this bound on $x(N)$ and $x(LN)\le(\lambda_1/\lambda_0)^{(L-1)N}x(N)$, $N\log(\lambda_0/\lambda_1)\le\pi L/(L-1)$.

The sharper bounds use the same comparison at smaller $t$ with the free values over the twisted section, whose least excitation is $\omega_N/N$ with $3.1264\le\omega_N<\pi$ for $N\ge13$. Likewise B(4) on the odd boxes $(L^jl',l',l')$, $j\ge1$, carries the quotients $Z[(k,1)_1]/Z[(0,1)_1]$ to their free values; the sector traces $\frac14\sum_k(-1)^{e\cdot k}Z[(k,1)_1]$ at the heights $L^jl$, which are $L^jl'$ in the dilated units, fix the levels (Lem.~\ref{C-366-6}); in the normalisation of B(9) the least free level of the sector $e\ne00$ is $\pi|e|/l$, its momenta lying in $\frac{2\pi}l(\mathbb Z+\frac{e_\rho}2)\times\frac{2\pi}l(\mathbb Z+\frac{e_\nu}2)$ by A(1), while in the sector $00$, whose least level is the vacuum $E_0=0$, the least positive free level, the second level of $00$ minus the vacuum, is $2\pi/l$.

For (c), the state of the cylinder has $\omega_K(\overline{\theta_KF}\,\tau_{n'}G)=\langle\psi(G),(T_1/\lambda_0)^{n'}\psi(F)\rangle$ for plaquette functions of finitely many layers, with vectors $\psi(F)$ formed from the slab operators and the top eigenvector of $T_1$. Lem.~\ref{C-366-21}(b) with cells of side $l/L$, that is $\lambda'=L^{J-1}$ sites and $k=L$ cells a side of the section, and with $\mathsf q=2$, compares the cylinder with the periodic cube $Q$ of side $2l/L$, at the cost of one factor $\Xi$ for each slab of cells in time that carries a function; at $k_0=L$, $\Xi\le\exp[\Phi'/(L-2)]$, and $\Phi'=\frac{L^3}8\delta^0_K(Q)-\delta^{n_{23}}_K(l^{\times3})$, the bulk cancelling, is bounded uniformly in $K$ by the window of B(1) on the cube $2l/L$ and the floor of B(2) on the odd cube $l$.

A partition of unity of each $f_q$ into pieces supported inside cells of translates of the board cuts a tuple into finitely many tuples placed in cells, at a cost formed from $n'$, $R$ and $l$; for a placed tuple the product of the centred observables of one cell is a polynomial in the numbers $1-\frac12\mathrm{tr}\,\partial U(p)$ of its plaquettes, and its seminorm on $Q$ is a centred moment of the observables of the eight mirror copies in the periodic measure of $Q$, the means $e_K$ being those of $Q$; the bounds on the joint cumulants of the action density on that periodic cube ({\cite[Lem.~N.2]{YMM2}}) then give $C_{n'}(d,R)$. Compactness (Lem.~\ref{C-366-6}(b) for the levels, a diagonal choice for the $S_{n'}$) gives the limit points; reflection positivity is A(7) at the mirrors normal to the time, which lies in no twisted plane of $n_{23}$.

In every limit, $S(\theta F,\tau_sG)=\sum_ie^{-sE_i}c_i(F,G)$ with a positive semidefinite matrix of coefficients, which defines an isometry of $\mathcal H$ into the $\ell^2$ space of the limit levels carrying $e^{-sH}$ to multiplication by $e^{-sE_i}$; $E_0=0$ is simple and belongs to $\Omega$, and the gap gives the spectral bound and the clustering. The action density is invariant under the flips $C^k$, so its vectors lie in the sector $00$, whose least positive level exceeds $6.1/l$ at small $t$ when the law of (4) is used on the boxes $(L^3l,l,l)$. Finally the lower bound on $S_2(\theta f^\circ,f^\circ)-S_1(f^\circ)^2$. Let $j(t)$ be the least integer for which $g=(L^{j(t)}/2t)^{-1/2}$ is at most the ceiling $\gamma_W$ of the reference couplings of Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AV}{851}} and $2L^{j(t)-1}$ is a side at $g$ (equation~\YMMref{(1528)}{615}); it is formed from $t$ and the constants.

Put $\hat L=L^{j(t)-m}$ and read everything in the units dilated by $\hat L$, which name the same lattice and the same $\beta$: the section has the side $\hat l=\hat Ll=L^{j(t)}$, the label is $\hat b=\hat Lb=L^{j(t)}/t=2g^{-2}$, the cutoff is $\hat K=K-j(t)+m$, the bump has the radius $d_*=\hat Ld^\circ$, and the partner of the cylinder is the periodic cube of side $2\hat l/L$, which is the cube $Q$ of side $2l/L$ above; by Cor.~\YMMref{74.2}{616} and {\cite[Lem.~G.4]{YMM2}} every $(\hat K,L^{\hat K}\hat b)$, $\hat K\ge1$, is a first-passage datum at $g$ with the label $\hat b$. (1) The state of the cylinder defines a law $\tilde\omega$ on the configurations of $a_{\hat K}\mathbb Z^3$, carried by the fields that are periodic up to the twist in the two directions of the section, with $\tilde\omega(G)=\omega_K(G^{\rm per})$ for the continuous plaquette functions $G$ of finitely many plaquettes, $G^{\rm per}$ reading each plaquette at its class modulo the section; on these functions $\tilde\omega$ is invariant under the translations of $a_{\hat K}\mathbb Z^3$. (2) Let $F_1,F_2$ be Lipschitz functions supported in one ball of radius $2$ whose centre lies at the distance $\ge3$ from the walls of a board of side $L$, and $\mathsf u=\zeta_1F_1+\zeta_2F_2$, $\zeta\in\mathbb C^2$.

Lem.~\ref{C-366-21}(b), with cells of side $L$, that is of $L^{\hat K+1}$ sites a side, one slab of cells in time that carries a function, and the same partner $Q$, gives $|\tilde\omega(e^{\mathcal O_{\hat K}(\mathsf u)})|\le\hat\Xi\,\|e^{\mathcal O_{\hat K}(\mathsf u)}\|_{{\rm ch};Q}$, where $\hat\Xi=\Xi^{L^{2-j(t)}}\le\Xi$, because at a fixed partner $\log\Xi$ is linear in the number of sites of a side of a cell; so $\hat\Xi$ is bounded uniformly in $K$ by a number $\Xi_*$ formed from $t$ and the constants. (3) By the normalisers among the construction results at the first-passage data (Prop.~\YMMref{91.12}{708}\,(1)) there is a function $\mathcal E$, holomorphic in $\zeta$ on the domain $\mathbb D_\varrho(F_1,F_2)$ among the construction results and with $\mathcal E(0)=0$, with $\|e^{\mathcal O_{\hat K}(\mathsf u)}\|_{{\rm ch};\ell''}\le|e^{\mathcal E(\zeta)}|\,\mathsf Q_1(L)$ for all sides $\ell''$ at $g$, the side $2\hat l/L$ among them; so $|e^{-\mathcal E(\zeta)}\mathfrak s(e^{\mathcal O_{\hat K}(\mathsf u)})|\le Q'=\Xi_*\mathsf Q_1(L)$ for $\mathfrak s=\tilde\omega$ and, by the transfer principle (Prop.~\YMMref{91.11}{707}), for the periodic state $\tilde\mu$ of $Q$, read as a law on $a_{\hat K}\mathbb Z^3$. (4) The transfer between two laws under one normaliser (Prop.~\YMMref{91.11}{707}) gives $|S^T_2[\tilde\omega](F_1,F_2)-S^T_2[\tilde\mu](F_1,F_2)|\le C_D\|F_1\|_\sharp\|F_2\|_\sharp$, $C_D=2\log2\,(2Q'+2)^2(2/\varrho)^2$, $\varrho$ the radius of that domain, with no separation of the supports. (5) Put
\[
 D(f,h)=S^T_2[\tilde\omega](f,h)-S^T_2[\tilde\mu](f,h).
\]
This is a bilinear form invariant under lattice translations, by (1)
and the translation invariance of the periodic law. We apply the
packing argument in the proof of Prop.~\YMMref{127.1}{848};
only these two properties and the unit-ball bound in (4) enter that
argument. In particular, it does not require the cylinder law to be a
periodic Gibbs state.

Let $r=5\mathsf d$, with $a_{\hat K}\le r\le1/20$, and suppose that
$f_1,f_2$ vanish outside one ball of radius $r$. Set
$\delta=a_{\hat K}\lceil2r/a_{\hat K}\rceil$, so that
$2r\le\delta<3r$. Translates of this ball whose centres have all
coordinates of modulus at most $0.575-r$ lie in the unit ball and
have disjoint interiors when their translation vectors lie in
$\delta\mathbb Z^3$. Each coordinate interval contains at least
$0.3/r$ points of the required translate of $\delta\mathbb Z$.
We thus obtain a set $P$ of lattice translations with
$N=\#P\ge(0.3/r)^3$. For independent signs $\epsilon_v=\pm1$ put
\[
 F_{i,\epsilon}=\sum_{v\in P}\epsilon_v\tau_vf_i,\qquad i=1,2.
\]
Their supremum and Lipschitz norms do not exceed those of $f_i$.
For the Lipschitz assertion, each function vanishes on the boundary
of its supporting ball; on a segment joining different balls,
bound the endpoint values by the distances to the respective exit
and entry points. The sum of these distances is no greater than
the length of the segment. Consequently
$\|F_{i,\epsilon}\|_\sharp\le\|f_i\|_\sharp$.
Bilinearity and sign averaging give
\[
 \mathbb E D(F_{1,\epsilon},F_{2,\epsilon})
 =\sum_{v\in P}D(\tau_vf_1,\tau_vf_2)=N D(f_1,f_2).
\]
Applying (4) and dividing by $N$ yields
$|D(f_1,f_2)|\le C_D(r/0.3)^3\|f_1\|_\sharp\|f_2\|_\sharp$.
If $\operatorname{Lip}f_i\le2\|f_i\|_\infty/\mathsf d$, then
$\|f_i\|_\sharp\le80M\|f_i\|_\infty/\mathsf d$, and hence
\[
 |S^T_2[\tilde\omega](f_1,f_2)-S^T_2[\tilde\mu](f_1,f_2)|
 \le C'_2\mathsf d\,\|f_1\|_\infty\|f_2\|_\infty,
 \qquad C'_2=C_D(50/3)^3(80M)^2.
\] (6) Let $f_+$ be the bump of radius $d_*$ about the point $x_+=(2d_*,\hat L\xi)$, the dilate of $f^\circ$, and $f_-$ its mirror image in the plane at the time $a_{\hat K}/2$, the bump about the mirror point $x_-$ of $x_+$.

When $a_{\hat K}\le d_*/4$, $3d_*\le|x_+-x_-|\le8d_*$, both bumps vanish off one ball of radius $5d_*$ and have Lipschitz constants $\le2/d_*$, and $(f_-,f_+)$ is a pair of the law of two points at $\vartheta=\frac12$. For the state $\tilde\mu$ of the torus of side $2\hat l/L$, a state at $g$, Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AV}{851}} gives, for $d_*\le\mathsf d_0(g,\frac12)$ and $s(d_*)<\hat K$, $s(\cdot)$ the witness depth (equation~\YMMref{(2321)}{843}), $S^T_2[\tilde\mu](f_-,f_+)=c_{\rm sd}\hat b^{-2}\mathcal K_{\rm free}(1+\varepsilon')$ with $|\varepsilon'|\le\frac13$, where the free kernel of the pair has $\mathcal K_{\rm free}=\mathcal K_{\rm free}(f_-,f_+)\ge\frac14\,10^{-6}$. (7) With $d_*=\min\{\mathsf d_0(g,\frac12),\,c_{\rm sd}/(24\cdot10^6C_2'\hat b^2)\}$, a number formed from $t$ and the constants, $C_2'd_*\le\frac16c_{\rm sd}\hat b^{-2}\cdot\frac14\,10^{-6}\le\frac16c_{\rm sd}\hat b^{-2}\mathcal K_{\rm free}$, and so, by (5) at $\mathsf d=d_*$,
\[ S^T_2[\tilde\omega](f_-,f_+)\ge\bigl(1-\tfrac13-\tfrac16\bigr)c_{\rm sd}\hat b^{-2}\mathcal K_{\rm free}\ge\tfrac18\,10^{-6}c_{\rm sd}\hat b^{-2} \]
at every cutoff with $\hat K>s(d_*)$ and $a_{\hat K}\le d_*/4$. Back in the original units, $\mathcal O_{\hat K}(f^{[\hat L]})=\hat L^{-1}\mathcal O_K(f)$ for $f^{[\hat L]}(x)=f(x/\hat L)$, the barycentres being multiplied by $\hat L$ and the factor $a^{-1}$ divided by it; so the covariance of $\mathcal O_K(\theta_Kf^\circ)$ and $\mathcal O_K(f^\circ)$ under $\omega_K$ is $\hat L^2$ times this one, and $\hat L^2\hat b^{-2}=b^{-2}$: the bound $\frac18\,10^{-6}c_{\rm sd}b^{-2}$ holds at all large cutoffs. A covariance does not see the centring by $e_K$, and $\theta_Kf^\circ$ is the translate of $\theta f^\circ$ by $a_K$ in the time; so the bound holds for $S_2(\theta f^\circ,f^\circ)-S_1(f^\circ)^2$ in every limit.

\emph{Step 16: even cubes (B(10)).} The reduction is arithmetic in $\ell_\sharp$ and $R$: for $t\le t_{\rm w}$ the label $b'(t)$ exists, and the cube $2L^j$ at $\beta=2L^j/t$ is the cube $\ell_\sharp(b')L^{j-\mu(t)}$ at $\beta=L^{j-\mu(t)}b'$. (a) follows for $N\ge N(t)$ from B(3), B(5) and $C^n(N)/N\to\mathscr G_n$ (Prop.~\ref{C-366-13}(e)); and up to $K_1(b')$ the cube $\ell_\sharp(b')$ has $N\le\ell_\sharp b'^{1/68}$ sites a side at $\beta=L^Kb'$, so that $N^{66}\log\beta/\beta\le2\ell_\sharp^{66}b'^{-3/68}\log b'$, which tends to $0$ as $b'\to\infty$, and Prop.~\ref{C-366-13}(g) gives the lattice value. Under (R), $\sum_{K\ge K_1(b)}c_1\ell_\sharp^\varpi L^{-\kappa K}\le C(\log b)^{r_\star\varpi}b^{-\kappa/68}\to0$, also under $\sup_{b'\ge b}$; summing from $K_1(b')$ gives the bound of (a) at every $N\in2L^{\mathbb N}$, with its lower bound on $C^n(N)/N$ the floor $ct$, and the bounded variation, $\phi_{j+1}-\phi_j$ being a difference of two consecutive cutoffs on the cubes $\ell_\sharp(b'(t))L^{j-\mu(t)}$; with the one-sided form, $\log q_K\ge\log q_{K_1(b')}-o(1)$ for $K\ge K_1(b')$ gives $ct\le r_K$, and Lem.~\ref{C-366-18} gives the bounded variation.

The proposed transport argument still requires (W) and (Window estimates). At $K_\sharp$ the lattice lies in the range of \S\ref{C-366-15}: $w_{K_\sharp}\ge c_\flat t$ and $\varsigma_{K_\sharp}\ge2^{1-L}e^{\lambda_\flat}(c_\flat t)^L$, beside which $e^{-c(\log b)^{1+\eta}}$ is $o(1)$; Lem.~\ref{C-366-12}(b) puts $w_K$ within $e^{\pm E}$ of $w_{K_\sharp}$ up to $\epsilon$, which is $o(t)$, indeed $o(t^k)$ for every $k$, as Lem.~\ref{C-366-12}(b) states ($m_K$ and $\epsilon_K$ being formed from the numbers \YMMref{(2192)--(2194)}{808} and $\mathsf R_{t_1}$ of \S\ref{sec:cutoff-calibration}), and so negligible beside $w_{K_\sharp}\ge c_\flat t$; so $\log(2^{L-1}\mathfrak q_L(K))\ge\lambda_\flat-\Lambda-o(1)>0$, and A(12) gives
\[ r_K[n_{13}]\ge w_K\,\frac{\mathfrak q_L(K)-2^{1-L}}{1-2^{1-L}}\ge c't ; \]
smaller lattices lie in the window. On the box $(\ell,\ell,i\ell)$ the same holds with $2^{i-1}\mathfrak q_i\ge0.42\cdot1.8712^i$ for $F'_t$. Under (W$'$), A(12) gives $r_K[n_{13}]\ge w_K(2\|\mathsf P_K\|/\mathrm{Tr}\,\mathsf P_K-1)\ge w_K(e^{\gamma'}-1)$, with $w_K\ge\frac12c_\flat t$ for small $t$ by Lem.~\ref{C-366-12}(b), its $\epsilon$ being $o(t)$. With $F''_t$ the same gives the quotient of the class $((1,1),0)_3$, which on the cube is $r_2$. $0.55L-1.1<0.5516L-0.7162$, and $\frac L2<0.6266L-0.873$, as $L\ge13$. In (d), the consistency is that of B(7); as $\{n(s)=n\}$ is invariant under $s\mapsto s\,\mathrm{d}\gamma$, (M) makes the unnormalised laws of each class converge, and B(2)(c) normalises them.

\emph{Step 17: Thm.~\ref{C-366-5}.} Under the hypothesis (H), at each $K\ge K_0$, Lem.~\ref{C-366-9} at $l=l_K$ gives $\theta\le0.8901$, $\mathsf e(4l_K)\le\theta^4/12.9$ and $D_2(8l_K)\le20\,\mathsf e(4l_K)^2\le0.047355$, so A(10) applies at $l_0=8l_K$; $m_*l_0\ge\log\frac1{18\cdot0.047355}\ge0.1597$, and if $m_*l_0<3$ then $l_1<6/m_*\le37.6\,l_0$ and $\sigma_*>m_*^2/6\ge0.00425\,l_0^{-2}$, while if $m_*l_0\ge3$ then $\sigma_*=m_*/l_0\ge3l_0^{-2}$; with $l_0a_K=4s_0$ this is the stated bound in physical length. The cube and loop bounds are A(10) in physical length, with $4N/l_1\le\ell/s_0$ and $N\ge4l_1$ for $\ell\ge602\,s_0$; the uniqueness of $\nu_K$ is Lem.~\ref{C-366-16}. On a cube of side $N\ge2l_K$, A(10) gives $\Phi\le\delta\le0.13736\,\theta^{N/2l_K}$ and $1-r[n]\le0.4121\,\theta^{N/2l_K}$; so $\mathfrak b\le e^{0.13736}-1<0.1473$ on that cube, and A(3) gives
\[ \sigma(N)\ge N^{-2}\log(1/0.1473)\ge1.9\,N^{-2},\qquad\text{that is}\qquad\sigma_K(\ell)\ge1.9\,\ell^{-2}. \]
For the proposed final exclusion, the following reduction requires the separate estimates (Hess) and (Flux-window). Let $s_0\le t_1b$. On the cube of physical side $s_0=2l_Ka_K$, $r_1\to v_1(s_0/b,s_0/b,s_0/b)\le C_\square t_1\le\frac15$ by B(3) and B(5), so $r_1\le\frac13$ for all large $K$, and A(13) gives $\mathsf e(l_K)\ge\log2>0.069$ there, against the hypothesis (H).
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Scope}

Thm.~\ref{C-366-3} is a statement on one lattice, for every box and every $\beta\ge0$, in lattice units; besides the periodic boxes it treats the infinite lattice at one $\beta$, in the last assertion of~(8), in~(10), under its hypothesis, one inequality between the partition functions of two periodic cubes, with its periodic Gibbs state and its loops, and in~(11), for every periodic Gibbs state, and, in~(4)(d), a slab with free boundaries in two directions. Thm.~\ref{C-366-4} concerns the periodic boxes of a fixed physical size, at a fixed label or at labels in a compact set, at every cutoff and as $K\to\infty$, the Hamiltonians $H_{l,m}$ over fixed sections, and, in~(9)(c), the cylinder over one small twisted section.

Thm.~\ref{C-366-5} concerns the infinite lattice $a_K\mathbb Z^3$ at each cutoff $K\ge K_0$: under the hypothesis~(H), the inequality $\mathsf e(l_K)\le0.069$ between the partition functions of the two periodic boxes $(l_K,2l_K,2l_K)$ and $(2l_K)^{\times3}$, it gives the uniqueness of the periodic Gibbs state $\nu_K$, an area law for the loops of every rectangle with a physical tension at least $2.65\cdot10^{-4}s_0^{-2}$, and bounds on the cubes of every physical side $\ge s_0$, resp.\ $\ge602\,s_0$, all uniform in $K$; it is a statement of the kind of confinement at each cutoff, conditional on the hypothesis~(H). Completing (Hess) and (Flux-window) would make the final exclusion show that (H) can hold only at physical sides $s_0$ of the order of the label or more.

The vacuum, the gap and the clustering of Thm.~\ref{C-366-4}(9) belong to one small twisted section, the uniqueness of $\nu_K$ is that of a Gibbs state of the lattice of one cutoff, and the tension $\sigma_K(l)$ of Thms.~\ref{C-366-4}(8) and~\ref{C-366-5} is that of a slab of fixed width $l$. Thm.~\ref{C-366-4}(10)(b)--(d) and Thm.~\ref{C-366-5} remain sketches where they use (R), (W), (W$'$) or (M), with the genuine box-inequality premise (H) retained for the area-law criterion. The window estimates specified in (10)(c), and (Hess) and (Flux-window) in the final small-side exclusion, are the remaining tasks; and Thm.~\ref{C-366-3}(7), (8) give reflection positivity for the eight sums over sets of coordinate planes and for the admissible mixtures. A box of the class $z$ is a centre sector of a periodic torus, that is, its fields of the class $z$ are the fields of the torus fixed by a group generated by the shifts by the sides of the box, each followed by the multiplication by a sign field $\chi$ on the bonds with $d\chi\equiv1$, if and only if $n_\mu n_\nu$ is even in every twisted plane $\mu\nu$ of $z$, $n_\mu$ being the side of the torus divided by that of the box.

Indeed, if it is such a sector, a fixed field is determined by its values at representatives of the bonds, which are free, its plaquette variables are periodic under the shifts, and on one copy of the box they are those, $\eta^z\partial U'$, of a field $U'$ of the box; for values in the diagonal subgroup of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, which holds $-\mathbf 1$, the product of the plaquette variables over a plane $\mu\nu$ of the torus is $\mathbf 1$, each bond entering it twice in opposite senses, and it is $(-1)^{z_{\mu\nu}n_\mu n_\nu}$, the product over the $n_\mu n_\nu$ copies of a plane of the box; the converse is the construction of Lem.~\ref{C-366-7}, read on that torus, which asks $w_{\mu\nu}=1$ only where $n_\mu$ is even.

On the tori $T_{\ell'}$, $\ell'=2L^{m+i}$ with $i\ge0$, the multiplicities of the cube $2L^m$ are $L^i$, odd, and a dilation by a power of $L$ does not change them: the cube $2L^m$ with flux is a centre sector of no torus $T_{\ell'}$, and no box of a class with a twisted plane whose two sides lie in $2L^{\mathbb Z}$ is a centre sector of a torus $T_{\ell'}$. The cube $2L^m$ of the class $z$ is a centre sector of the periodic tori with one doubled side in each twisted plane of $z$: of $(4L^m,2L^m,2L^m)$, the doubled side lying in the twisted plane, for one twisted plane, and in both twisted planes for two; of $(4L^m,4L^m,2L^m)$ or of the cube $4L^m$ for three. The chain and the two-cutoff comparison are stated on the tori $T_\ell$, and Lem.~\ref{C-366-12} on periodic cubes.

For the pairs $(U,s)$ of the mixture $\mu_{\rm mix}$ of~(M), let a chain be run with the averaging map $\mathcal M_s$ of Thm.~\ref{C-366-4}(7) and with the small-field tests applied to the signed plaquette variables, $s(p)\,\partial U(p)$ on the lattice and $s^{(d)}(P)\,\partial(\mathcal M^{K-d}_sU)(P)$ on the block lattice of depth $d$. These variables, and so the small-field and the large-field regions of this chain, do not change under $(U,s)\mapsto(\gamma U,s\,\mathrm{d}\gamma)$, $\gamma$ a sign field on the bonds: it multiplies $\partial U(p)$ and $s(p)$ by $d\gamma(p)$, and, at each depth, $\mathcal M^{K-d}_sU$ by the sign field $\bar\gamma$ on the block bonds, $\bar\gamma(c)$ the product of $\gamma$ over the straight path of the block bond $c$, and $s^{(d)}$ by $d\bar\gamma$.

When the small-field region of this chain does not wind about the torus, the closed sign field $s$ is $d\gamma$ on it for a sign field $\gamma$ on the bonds, and the change of variables $(U,s)\mapsto(\gamma U,s\,\mathrm{d}\gamma)$, under which $A_{s\,\mathrm{d}\gamma}(\gamma U)=A_s(U)$ and which the functions $H$ of~(M) do not see, makes the integrand on that region the periodic one; $s\,\mathrm{d}\gamma$ is then a closed sign field of the class $n(s)$ that is $1$ on that region, and so, for $n(s)\ne0$, $-1$ on some plaquette of the large-field region of this chain (the probability estimate for such large-field events is Prop.~\ref{prop:ward-fixed-volume-rarity}).


\section{Vanishing latent heat}\label{supp:lh:sec}

Let $P(\beta)$ be the pressure per lattice site and let
$J(\beta)=P'(\beta+)-P'(\beta-)$ be its derivative jump.
Convexity identifies $J$ with the possible variation of the mean
action among periodic Gibbs states. The normalization of the
physical action density multiplies this variation by $a_K^{-4}$.

\begin{sketch}[Decay of the pressure jump]\label{supp:lh:main}
For every $c<1/180$,
\[
 J(\beta)=O(\beta^{-4-c})\qquad(\beta\to\infty).
\]
Consequently, along the continuum cutoffs, periodic Gibbs states
have asymptotically equal one-point action densities. In particular,
\[
 3a_K^{-4}|\rho(a_p)-\nu(a_p)|\le a_K^{-4}J(\beta)
       \longrightarrow0.
\]
This does not assert that $J$ vanishes at a finite coupling.
\end{sketch}

\paragraph{Sketch of the argument.}
Compare the pressure of the infinite lattice with that on a fixed
physical torus. Reflection positivity bounds their difference,
and local source estimates control its variations in the physical
label. The part of the second derivative concentrated at one
label is precisely the rescaled latent heat. It is therefore
enough to prevent the limiting pressure response from accumulating
an atom.

Repeat the construction with two blocking factors whose logarithms
are incommensurable. They act as two translations of the logarithmic
coupling variable. The two resulting descriptions concern the same
lattice pressure. The two-period argument shows that the limiting
response cannot retain a nonconstant periodic contribution common
to both descriptions. In its quantitative form, it bounds the
mass of the response on a short logarithmic interval by its length
and an error inherited from the cutoff comparison.

The error must be estimated with its actual dependence on the
torus. For an $n$-point function the comparison has the form
\[
 |S_{K'}-S_K|\le C\ell^{3(n+1)}K^{p_n}L^{-K/10},
 \qquad K'\ge K\ge k+54m,\quad\ell=2L^m.
\]
An improved bound for the discarded large-field mass supplies this
rate. Choosing the relation between $m$ and $K$ makes the box
error decrease while retaining a sufficiently fine cutoff. For
every slope $A>90$, the two-period estimate gives
$\beta^4J(\beta)\le C_A\beta^{-1/(2A)}$. Taking $A$ sufficiently
close to $90$ yields every exponent $c<1/180$.

The derivative-jump interpretation then gives the one-point
conclusion directly. For a bounded compactly supported test,
the difference of its means is bounded by the displayed
plaquette estimate times the volume of its supporting cube and
its supremum norm. Thus conditioning on translation-invariant
events cannot leave different continuum one-point constants.

The threshold $k+54m$ grows with the box side and must remain in
the argument. Replacing it by a cutoff independent of the side
would be a stronger estimate, with a stronger conclusion about
$J$. The present reasoning controls the jump asymptotically; it
does not prove uniqueness of all finite-coupling Gibbs states.




\subsection{Latent heat and one-point constants}\label{lh:sec}

Let $P=\lim_{N\to\infty}N^{-3}\log Z_N$ be the lattice pressure and $J(\beta)=P^{\prime}(\beta+)-P^{\prime}(\beta-)$ its derivative jump. We prove $J(\beta)=O(\beta^{-4-c})$ for every $c<1/180$. The proof combines a reflection-positive lower bound, comparison with finite tori and an oscillation estimate for two incommensurable blocking factors.

The cutoff threshold depends on the size of the box. We retain this dependence: the result is a decay estimate for the jump and its continuum one-point consequences. The two-period lemma and the improved discarded-mass estimate are the main quantitative steps.

\subsubsection{Notation and hypotheses}

\emph{One lattice.} For a plaquette $p$ of $\mathbb Z^3$ with barycentre $x(p)$ and holonomy $\partial U(p)$ we put $a_p=1-\frac12\operatorname{tr}\partial U(p)\in[0,2]$, and $\mathcal O_1(f)=\sum_pf(x(p))a_p$ for bounded $f$ of compact support. For an integer $N\ge3$, $S_N$ is the sum of the $a_p$ over the $3N^3$ plaquettes of the periodic cube with $N^3$ sites, $Z_N(\beta)=\int e^{-\beta S_N}\,\mathrm{d}U$ with the Haar probability measure of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ on every bond, $\mu_{N,\beta}$ is the Wilson measure of the cube, read as a law on the configurations of $\mathbb Z^3$ that is carried by the $N\mathbb Z^3$-periodic configurations (the periodic Wilson law in equation~\YMMref{(1817)}{698}, with $\Gamma=N\mathbb Z^3$), and $P_N=N^{-3}\log Z_N$, so $P=\lim_NP_N$.

For $x\in\mathbb Z^3$ let $c_x=\frac12\sum a_p$, the sum over the six faces of the unit cube $x+[0,1]^3$. A Gibbs state of Wilson's action at the spacing $a>0$ and the coupling $\beta$ is a Borel probability measure $\nu$ on the configurations of $a\mathbb Z^3$ such that $\nu(\gamma_BF)=\nu(F)$ for every finite set $B$ of bonds and every continuous function $F$ of finitely many bonds; here the Gibbs kernel $\gamma_B$ is the normalised average over the configurations on $B$, with the Haar measure of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ on every bond of $B$ and the weight $e^{-\beta\sum_pa_p}$, the sum over the plaquettes $p$ that contain a bond of $B$, the configuration off $B$ being kept fixed (Section~\YMMref{91}{697}).

A Gibbs state is periodic if it is invariant under the translations by a subgroup of finite index of $a\mathbb Z^3$ (Section~\YMMref{91}{697}); by Prop.~\YMMref{103.4}{758} every periodic Gibbs state is invariant under all isometries of $a\mathbb Z^3$, so the periodic Gibbs states are exactly the Gibbs states that are invariant under $a\mathbb Z^3$. $\mathcal G(\beta)$ is the set of all periodic Gibbs states on $\mathbb Z^3$ at $\beta$, that is, at the spacing $1$ (the set $\mathcal G^{\rm per}_{1,\beta}$ of Section~\YMMref{91}{697}), and $e_\nu=\nu(a_p)$ for $\nu\in\mathcal G(\beta)$; this is one number for all $p$ (Lem.~\ref{lh:lat}). For a law $\mathfrak s$ that is invariant under $\mathbb Z^3$ we write $\langle f;h\rangle_{\mathfrak s}=\operatorname{Cov}_{\mathfrak s}(\mathcal O_1(f),\mathcal O_1(h))$ and $\Gamma_{\mathfrak s}(z)=\operatorname{Cov}_{\mathfrak s}(c_0,c_z)$.

\emph{Tents and the reference.} $\Lambda_\eta(u)=(1-|u|/\eta)_+$ for real $u$ and $\eta>0$. For an integer $\eta\ge1$ and $X\in\mathbb Z^3$ the tent is $\varphi^\eta_X(z)=\prod_{i\le3}\Lambda_\eta(z_i-\frac12-\eta X_i)$, the hull is $h^\eta=\sum_{|X|_\infty\le2}\varphi^\eta_X$, the sum of the $5^3$ tents nearest to $\varphi^\eta_0$, and $\varphi^\eta_{\rm c}(x)=\prod_i\Lambda_\eta(x_i)$ for $x\in\mathbb Z^3$. For a law $\mathfrak s$ invariant under $\mathbb Z^3$ we put $s^\eta_{\mathfrak s}(X)=\langle\varphi^\eta_0;\varphi^\eta_X\rangle_{\mathfrak s}$, and the near part of the specific heat is $n_\eta(\mathfrak s)=\eta^{-3}\langle\varphi^\eta_0;h^\eta\rangle_{\mathfrak s}$. For $r_1>0$ the reference is
\[
\hat n(\beta)=\liminf_{N\to\infty}n_{\lceil r_1\beta\rceil}(\mu_{N,\beta}),
\]
the lower limit along all integers $N\ge3$; it is formed from Wilson's action and $r_1$ alone. $P''(d\beta)$ is the second derivative of the convex function $P$, a positive measure, and $\mathbb M$ is the image under $s=\log\beta$ of the signed measure $\beta^4[P''(d\beta)-\hat n(\beta)d\beta]$. Thus $\mathbb M(\{s\})=e^{4s}J(e^s)$, and
\[
|\mathbb M|([s,s+\delta])=\int_{[\beta,e^\delta\beta]}x^4\,|P''(dx)-\hat n(x)\,\mathrm{d}x|\qquad(\beta=e^s).
\]

\emph{Settings.} A setting consists of a radius $\varrho>0$, a common choice $\varsigma^{\rm S}$ of the real and source construction constants and auxiliary data in Section~\YMMref{82}{665} at the radius required by Thms.~\YMMref{AJ}{673} and~\YMMref{AD}{607}, with \eqref{eq:canonical-source-quarter-room}, and the associated Wilson measures and source normalization. Write $\mathcal T^{\rm S}[2\varrho]$ for this ordered choice and $\varsigma=\pi^+(\varsigma^{\rm S})$ for its restriction to the real construction, denoted by $\mathcal T^{\rm F+}$. The numerical constants retain their values: the real hypotheses are those of Prop.~\YMMref{69.1}{595}, Prop.~\YMMref{69.3}{603} and Cor.~\YMMref{69.4}{604}; the additional source floors are imposed in their stated order. The coupling ceiling $\gamma\in(0,\frac12]$ is chosen last.

Among the constants chosen in Prop.~\YMMref{69.1}{595} are the odd block size $L\ge13$, the cell size $M$, a power of $L$, the flow bound $B_\sharp$ with $\bar B=B_\sharp L/(L-1)$, the exponent $\mathfrak p_0\in\mathbb N$ of the large-field threshold, the exponent $r$ of the cube sizes, with which the cube size at a coupling $x>1$ is $\mathcal R(x)=\min\{L^c:c\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0},\ L^c\ge(\log x)^r\}$ (equation~\YMMref{(634)}{339}; below it is read at couplings $x\ge\gamma^{-2}$ alone), and the amplitudes $A_1$ and $A_0$. A lowered choice $\varsigma'$ of a choice $\varsigma$ of $\mathcal T^{\rm F+}$ (Def.~\ref{def:rarity-choices}) keeps the values of the constants before $A_1$ and of $A_0$, has $B_\sharp'\ge B_\sharp$, and has $A_1'=\lambda'_\natural A_1$ with $\lambda'_\natural=\lambda_\natural/(2+30L)$, where $\lambda_\natural\in(0,\frac1{8\pi}]$ is a number of $\varsigma$; so the small-field thresholds $\delta_j$ of the two choices satisfy $\delta'_j=\lambda'_\natural\delta_j$.

For the ordered choices constructed in Lem.~\ref{lem:rarity-lowered-choice}, lowered choices exist: decreasing $A_1$ preserves the eight inequalities at $A_0$, and the later constants are reselected in the order proved there. Def.~\ref{def:rarity-choices} attaches to the pair $(\varsigma,\varsigma')$ a floor $\mathsf Y^\natural$ for the logarithm of the last coupling and the rate $c_2^\natural=\frac12\min\{\frac18c_1^\natural,\lambda_\natural^2A_1^2/2A_0^2\}$, with a number $c_1^\natural>0$ of the pair. We put $a_K=L^{-K}$, $\mathbb L_K=a_K\mathbb Z^3$, $\lambda=\log L$, $\ell=2L^m$ and $T_\ell=\mathbb R^3/\ell\mathbb Z^3$; the label of a pair $(K,\beta)$ is $b=a_K\beta$, and
\[
a_K^{-4}J(\beta)=b^{-4}\beta^4J(\beta).
\]

\emph{The physical scale.} For the plaquettes $p$ of $\mathbb L_K$ we put $\mathcal O_K(f)=a_K^{-1}\sum_pf(x(p))a_p$ and $r_K(f)=\frac13a_K^3\sum_pf(x(p))$, a Riemann sum of $\int f$; and $\|f\|_\sharp=\max\{\|f\|_\infty,40M\operatorname{Lip}f\}$. $\mathcal G_{K,\beta}$ is the set of all periodic Gibbs states on $\mathbb L_K$ at $\beta$, that is, at the spacing $a_K$ (the set $\mathcal G^{\rm per}_{K,\beta}$ of Section~\YMMref{91}{697}), a convex set (Props.~\YMMref{91.1}{698} and~\YMMref{103.4}{758}), and its extreme points are the pure phases (Prop.~\YMMref{106.1}{764}). $S^T_n[\nu](f_1,\dots,f_n)$ is the joint cumulant of $\mathcal O_K(f_1),\dots,\mathcal O_K(f_n)$ in a law $\nu$ on $\mathbb L_K$; for real Lipschitz $f_i$ on $T_\ell$, $S^T_{n;K,\ell,\beta}(f_1,\dots,f_n)$ is the joint cumulant under the Wilson measure of $T_\ell$ at the spacing $a_K$, that is, of the periodic cube with $\ell L^K$ sites a side. $f^{\langle\ell\rangle}=\sum_{v\in\ell\mathbb Z^3}f(\cdot-v)$ is the periodisation. The spread of $(f_1,\dots,f_n)$ is the least sup-diameter of a set of points taken one from each support; for $n=2$ it is the sup-distance of the two supports. On $T_\ell$ one has $|\mathcal O_K(f)|\le6\ell^3L^{4K}\|f\|_\infty$, so that
\[
|S^T_{n;K,\ell,\beta}(f_1,\dots,f_n)|\le\mathsf{op}_n\prod_{i\le n}6\ell^3L^{4K}\|f_i\|_\infty ,
\]
with a combinatorial number $\mathsf{op}_n$ of $n$; we call this the crude bound.

\emph{Labels and windows.} For $0<g\le\gamma$ let $X_g=L(g^{-2}+B_\sharp)$ and $I(g)=(g^{-2}+\bar B,X_g-\bar B]$ (Section~\YMMref{74}{614}), and let $\mathfrak d(g)$ be the canonical family at $g$ ({\cite[\S{}K.1]{YMM2}}), the set of the first-passage data at $g$ (Cor.~\YMMref{74.2}{616}): the pairs $(K,\beta)$, $K\in\mathbb N$, for which $K$ is the least index $k$ at which the running coupling $x_k(\beta)$, the member of index $k$ of the sequence of the increments from $x_0(\beta)=\beta$, is defined, real and at most $X_g$; in words, the running coupling arrives at the scale of $g$ at the last step. We use two facts on $\mathfrak d(g)$. By {\cite[\S{}K.1]{YMM2}}, the labels $a_K\beta$ of the pairs of $\mathfrak d(g)$ lie in the compact interval $I^{\rm lab}(g)=[g^{-2}+B_\sharp\frac{L-2}{L-1},\,L(g^{-2}+\bar B)]$ of {\cite[\S{}K.1]{YMM2}}, whose lower end is at least $g^{-2}$; so $a_K\beta\ge g^{-2}$ on $\mathfrak d(g)$. By {\cite[\S{}K.1]{YMM2}}, $(K,L^Kb)\in\mathfrak d(g)$, with the label $b$, for every $b\in I(g)$ and $K\in\mathbb N$. A window is an interval of labels; in a setting we use the window
\[
\mathsf I=[b_-,b_+],\qquad b_-=\gamma^{-2}+\bar B+\tfrac12,\qquad b_+=L(\gamma^{-2}+3\bar B+1)-2\bar B,
\]
and $g_2=(\gamma^{-2}+2\bar B+1)^{-1/2}$. $m_0\ge1$ is the least integer such that the sides $2L^m$, $m\ge m_0$, are admitted at $\gamma$ and at $g_2$ (the sides that the section of Section~\YMMref{74}{614} attaches to a reference coupling), and $\ell_0=2L^{m_0}$. With $\varepsilon=L^{-1}$, the tent $\mathsf f(y)=\prod_i\Lambda_\varepsilon(y_i-\frac12)$ and its hull $\mathsf h=\sum_{|X|_\infty\le2}\mathsf f(\cdot-\varepsilon X)$, the far part is
\[
y_{m,K}(\upsilon)=b^5\varepsilon^{-3}S^T_{2;K,\ell,L^Kb}\bigl(\mathsf f^{\langle\ell\rangle},1-\mathsf h^{\langle\ell\rangle}\bigr)\big|_{b=e^\upsilon},\qquad\ell=2L^m .
\]
When two settings $(\mathrm S_1)$, $(\mathrm S_2)$ are used, an index $i$ marks the objects of $(\mathrm S_i)$: $L_i$, $\lambda_i=\log L_i$, $M_i$, $\mathsf I_i=[b_{-,i},b_{+,i}]$, $m_{0,i}$, $\ell_{0,i}$, $\varepsilon_i$, $y^{(i)}_{m,K}$, and so on.

\emph{Tuples and functionals.} A separated tuple is $X=(f_1,\dots,f_n)$ with real $f_i\in C^1_c(\mathbb R^3)$ and pairwise disjoint supports; the empty tuple is one of them, $(f)$ is the tuple with the one entry $f$, $|X|=n$ is the number of entries, $X_A=(f_i)_{i\in A}$ for $A\subset\{1,\dots,n\}$, $(\tau_vf)(x)=f(x-v)$, $\tau_vX=(\tau_vf_i)_i$, and $X\cdot Y$ is the joined tuple, formed when its entries have pairwise disjoint supports. A symmetric functional is a map $\sigma$ on the separated tuples that is multilinear and symmetric in the entries, with $\sigma$ of the empty tuple equal to $1$. For a law $\nu$ on $\mathbb L_K$ we put
\[
X^\nu_K=\prod_{i\le n}\bigl[\mathcal O_K(f_i)-\nu(\mathcal O_K(f_i))\bigr],\qquad\sigma_\nu(X)=\nu(X^\nu_K).
\]
A Gibbs sequence at $g$ is $(K_j,\beta_j,\nu_j)_j$ with $(K_j,\beta_j)\in\mathfrak d(g)$, $K_j\to\infty$ and $\nu_j\in\mathcal G_j=\mathcal G_{K_j,\beta_j}$. A limit in its frame is $\sigma'(X)=\lim_j\rho_j(X^{\nu_j}_{K_j})$, for all separated $X$, with approximants $\rho_j\in\mathcal G_j$. The sequence converges if $\sigma(X)=\lim_j\sigma_{\nu_j}(X)$ exists for every separated $X$; then $\sigma$ is its limit, and $S^\sigma_2(f,h)=\sigma((f,h))-\sigma((f))\sigma((h))$. For separated $X^1,\dots,X^q$ the iterated plateau of a symmetric functional $\sigma$ is the iterated limit
\[
\lim_{|v_q|\to\infty}\cdots\lim_{|v_2|\to\infty}\sigma\bigl(X^1\cdot\tau_{v_2}X^2\cdots\tau_{v_q}X^q\bigr),
\]
the translations receding one after the other, $v_2$ first; at $q=1$ it is $\sigma(X^1)$, and at $q=2$ it is $\lim_{|v|\to\infty}\sigma(X^1\cdot\tau_vX^2)$. A canonical decomposition $(\mathsf X,\varpi,(\sigma_\xi)_{\xi\in\mathsf X})$ of $\sigma$ consists of (Can1) a compact metrisable space $\mathsf X$, (Can2) a Borel probability measure $\varpi$ of full support on it, (Can3) a map $\xi\mapsto\sigma_\xi$ into the symmetric functionals that is continuous for the pointwise convergence and injective, such that (Can4) $\sigma$ has iterated plateaux and $\int\prod_{i\le q}\sigma_\xi(X^i)\,\mathrm{d}\varpi$ is the iterated plateau of $(X^1,\dots,X^q)$, for all $q\ge1$ and all separated $X^1,\dots,X^q$; at $q=1$, $\sigma=\int\sigma_\xi\,\mathrm{d}\varpi$.

The $\sigma_\xi$ are the components. A symmetric functional has one vacuum if it has a canonical decomposition whose space is a point. By Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AP}{780}}, the limit $\sigma$ of a convergent Gibbs sequence at $g$ has a canonical decomposition, unique up to isomorphism; every component $\sigma_\xi$ is a limit in the frame along the full sequence, with the approximants $\nu_j(\cdot\,|B_j)$, $B_j$ invariant with $\nu_j(B_j)>0$; $\sigma_\xi((f))=\mathfrak c_\xi\int f$ with a number $\mathfrak c_\xi$; $|\sigma_\xi(X\cdot\tau_vY)-\sigma_\xi(X)\sigma_\xi(Y)|\le C^g(X,Y)/|v|$ for $|v|\ge r(X,Y)$, with the numbers $C^g$, $r$ of the paragraph on one cutoff below; and $\#\mathsf X=\dim\ker H_\sigma$, both finite and equal or both infinite, where $H_\sigma\ge0$ is the Hamiltonian of the reconstruction of $\sigma$ in any of the six coordinate directions and $H_\sigma\Omega_\sigma=0$ for its vacuum vector $\Omega_\sigma$.

So such a limit has one vacuum if and only if $\ker H_\sigma=\mathbb C\Omega_\sigma$. We put $\kappa=\int\mathfrak c_\xi^2\,\mathrm{d}\varpi$.

\emph{Limits along sequences of pairs.} A sequence of pairs is $\mathfrak p=(K_j,\beta_j)_j$ with $K_j\in\mathbb N$, $\beta_j>0$ and $K_j\to\infty$; it is at the label $b>0$ if $a_{K_j}\beta_j\to b$. $\mathsf K_{\mathfrak p}$ is the set of the functionals $\sigma$ for which there are $\nu_j\in\mathcal G_{K_j,\beta_j}$ with $\sigma(X)=\lim_j\sigma_{\nu_j}(X)$ for every separated $X$, along the full sequence; it carries the topology of pointwise convergence. $\mathsf K^\bullet_{\mathfrak p}$ is the set of its members with one vacuum. ${\rm Lim}[b]$ is the union of the sets $\mathsf K_{\mathfrak p}$ over the sequences of pairs at the label $b$, and ${\rm Lim}^\bullet[b]$ the set of its members with one vacuum; for a set $\mathfrak q$ of pairs, ${\rm Lim}_{\mathfrak q}[b]$ and ${\rm Lim}^\bullet_{\mathfrak q}[b]$ are the same unions over the sequences all of whose pairs lie in $\mathfrak q$. A sequence of pairs $\mathfrak p$ is saturated if $\mathsf K_{\mathfrak p}\ne\emptyset$ and $\mathsf K_{\mathfrak p'}=\mathsf K_{\mathfrak p}$ for every subsequence $\mathfrak p'$. For a Borel probability measure $\mu$ on a compact metrisable set of symmetric functionals, $\operatorname{bar}(\mu)=\int\psi\,\mu(\,\mathrm{d}\psi)$ is its barycentre.

\emph{Dilations; the reconstruction at every label.} For $z\in\mathbb Z$ and a separated tuple $X=(f_1,\dots,f_n)$ put $X^{[z]}=(f_i(L^z\cdot))_i$, again a separated tuple, and for a symmetric functional $\sigma$ put $\sigma^{[z]}(X)=L^{-z|X|}\sigma(X^{[z]})$. The dilation $x\mapsto L^zx$ carries a law $\nu$ on $\mathbb L_K$ to a law $\nu^{(z)}$ on $\mathbb L_{K-z}$, maps $\mathcal G_{K,\beta}$ onto $\mathcal G_{K-z,\beta}$ ({\cite[Lem.~K.1]{YMM2}}) and turns $\mathcal O_{K-z}(f)$ into $L^{-z}\mathcal O_K(f(L^z\cdot))$ ({\cite[Lem.~K.1]{YMM2}}, applied to the function $f(L^z\cdot)$: the dilated function $f^{[z]}$ of that Proposition is $f(L^{-z}\cdot)$, whereas the tuple $X^{[z]}$ above has the entries $f_i(L^z\cdot)$); so $\sigma_{\nu^{(z)}}=(\sigma_\nu)^{[z]}$, and the pair $(K-z,\beta)$ has the label $L^za_K\beta$.

Hence, if $\mathfrak p=(K_j,\beta_j)_j$ is a sequence of pairs at the label $b$ and $\sigma\in\mathsf K_{\mathfrak p}$, then $\sigma^{[z]}\in\mathsf K_{\mathfrak p'}$ for the sequence of pairs $\mathfrak p'=(K_j-z,\beta_j)_{j\ge j_0}$ at the label $L^zb$, where $K_j>z$ for $j\ge j_0$. As $\sigma^{[z]}(X\cdot\tau_vY)=L^{-z(|X|+|Y|)}\sigma(X^{[z]}\cdot\tau_{L^{-z}v}Y^{[z]})$, the conditions (Can1)--(Can4) pass through the dilation, the receding translations by $v$ becoming translations by $L^{-z}v$: $(\mathsf X,\varpi,(\sigma_\xi)_{\xi\in\mathsf X})$ is a canonical decomposition of $\sigma$ if and only if $(\mathsf X,\varpi,(\sigma_\xi^{[z]})_{\xi\in\mathsf X})$ is one of $\sigma^{[z]}$, with the same space $\mathsf X$.

For every $b>0$ there are an integer $z\ge0$ and $0<g\le\gamma$ with $g^{-2}+\bar B<L^zb<X_g-\bar B$, because $L^zb>\gamma^{-2}+\bar B$ for large $z$ and these open intervals overlap one another as $g$ decreases and cover $(\gamma^{-2}+\bar B,\infty)$; we fix such a pair $(z,g)$ for $b$, with $z=0$ if $b$ itself lies in one of these intervals. Then $L^za_{K_j}\beta_j\in I(g)$ for large $j$, so $(K_j-z,\beta_j)\in\mathfrak d(g)$ by {\cite[\S{}K.1]{YMM2}}, and $\sigma^{[z]}$ is the limit of a convergent Gibbs sequence at $g$ over these pairs, to which Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AP}{780}} applies. For $\sigma\in\mathsf K_{\mathfrak p}$ we put $H_\sigma=L^zH_{\sigma^{[z]}}$ and $\Omega_\sigma=\Omega_{\sigma^{[z]}}$, on the space of the reconstruction of $\sigma^{[z]}$, in each of the six coordinate directions, which the dilation keeps, as it commutes with the coordinate mirrors: the time $t$ of $\sigma^{[z]}$ is the time $L^{-z}t$ of $\sigma$, and the kernel is that of $H_{\sigma^{[z]}}$.

As the canonical decompositions of $\sigma$ and of $\sigma^{[z]}$ correspond to one another with the same space $\mathsf X$, which is unique up to homeomorphism (Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AP}{780}} at $\sigma^{[z]}$), $\dim\ker H_\sigma=\#\mathsf X$, both finite and equal or both infinite, and $\ker H_\sigma=\mathbb C\Omega_\sigma$ if and only if $\sigma$ has one vacuum; these statements read $\mathsf X$ alone, so they do not depend on the choice of $(z,g)$, and at $z=0$ they are those of Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AP}{780}} for $\sigma$ itself.

\emph{One cutoff.} $\mathcal I$ is the $\sigma$-field of the Borel sets invariant under the translations by $a_K\mathbb Z^3$.
