In the same way $\beta^5|n_{\lceil r_1\beta\rceil}(\nu)-\hat n|$ compares two states in a unit ball, and $\beta^5\lceil r_1\beta\rceil^{-3}s_\nu(3e_1)$ is a covariance at the distance $a_K\lceil r_1\beta\rceil\ge r_1b_-$, non-negative by Lem.~\ref{lh:rp}(a). Finally, every $\beta>Lb_-$ is $L^Kb$ with $b\in\mathsf I$ by (a); on each open interval of $(Lb_-,\infty)$ on which $\lceil r_1\beta\rceil$ is constant, Lem.~\ref{lh:rp}(b) applies with $q=\hat n-(1+870)C^{\rm ref}\beta^{-5}$; the end points of these intervals are countably many, and there $P''$ has atoms $\ge0$ while $q\,\mathrm{d}\beta$ has none.
(e) Let $\chi_k$, $k\in(\mathbb Z/\ell\mathbb Z)^3$, be the periodised products $\prod_i(1-|y_i-k_i|)_+$: they sum to $1$ on $T_\ell$, each is supported in a closed sup-ball of radius $1$, $\operatorname{Lip}\chi_k\le\sqrt3$, and so $\|\chi_kw\|_\sharp\le(40\sqrt3M+1)\|w\|_\sharp$ and $\operatorname{supp}(\chi_kw)\subset\operatorname{supp}w$. By bilinearity $S^T_2(u,w)=\sum_kS^T_2(u,\chi_kw)$, a sum of $\ell^3$ terms, each at most $C_{\rm tt}(\mathsf d)(40\sqrt3M+1)\|u\|_\sharp\|w\|_\sharp$ when $u$ is supported in a sup-ball of radius $1$ and the supports of $u$ and $w$ are at distance at least $\mathsf d$. Apply this to $u=\mathsf f^{\langle\ell\rangle}$, $w=1-\mathsf h^{\langle\ell\rangle}$, $\mathsf d=\varepsilon$, with $\|u\|_\sharp,\|w\|_\sharp\le40\sqrt3ML$ and $b^5\varepsilon^{-3}\le b_+^5L^3$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Two block sizes]\label{lh:two}
For every $\varrho>0$ and every integer $a\ge1$ there are two settings at the radius $\varrho$ with the block sizes $L_1$ and $L_2=L_1+2$ and one common value $\mathfrak p_0\ge a$. For every odd $L_1\ge3$, $\log L_1/\log(L_1+2)\notin\mathbb Q$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Use the ordered construction in the proof of Prop.~\YMMref{69.1}{595}: choose $r\ge2$, then an integer $\mathfrak p_0\ge\max\{a,6r+1\}$ and $q\ge41\mathfrak p_0+1$, followed by the reserve fractions and the other constants preceding $L$. The proof admits every sufficiently large odd $L$ with these values fixed. The additional floors in Section~\YMMref{82}{665} have the same property. Choose an odd $L_1$ above their common threshold and complete the prescribed construction separately at $L_1$ and $L_1+2$; with $\varrho$ and the associated Wilson measures and source normalization, each is a setting. If $\log L_1/\log L_2=u/v$ with positive integers, then $L_1^v=L_2^u$, and a prime factor of $L_1$ divides $L_2-L_1=2$, which is impossible for odd $L_1$. Every statement that we use is made for every radius and every choice, and no object of one choice is compared with an object of the other; the two settings meet in $P$ and $\hat n$ alone.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The lost mass on tori, without an exponential of the volume]\label{lh:lost}
Let $\varsigma'$ be a lowered choice of a choice $\varsigma$ of $\mathcal T^{\rm F+}$, and let the setting (Th) of \S\ref{sec:cutoff-calibration} hold at $\varsigma$ and at a label $b\ge\gamma^{-2}$ with $\log b\ge\mathsf Y^\natural$: $K\ge2$, $\ell=2L^m$ with $M\mathcal R(b)\le L^m$, where $\mathcal R(x)=\min\{L^c:c\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0},\ L^c\ge(\log x)^r\}$ (equation~\YMMref{(634)}{339}), the line of couplings $x_j=L^{K-j}b$, and a top level. Let $Z=\sum_h\mathsf t(h)$ be the sum of the masses $\mathsf t(h)$ of the histories (Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8}), $Z_t(h)=\Lambda_t(h)^c$ the large-field region defined by equation~\YMMref{(644)}{341}, and $N_t=\ell^3L^{3(K-t)}$. Then for $1\le t\le K$
\[
\sum_{h:\,Z_t(h)\ne\emptyset}\mathsf t(h)\le\mathsf R_tZ,\qquad\mathsf R_t=\tfrac L{L-1}M^{-3}N_t\,e^{-c_2^\natural A_0^2(\log x_t)^{2\mathfrak p_0}}.
\]
The side enters $\mathsf R_t$ only through the number $N_t$ of the sites of the level $t$; and $\mathsf R_t$ is smaller by the factor $25000$ than the number $2\cdot24^3M^{-3}N_te^{-c_2^\natural A_0^2(\log x_t)^{2\mathfrak p_0}}$ that the rarity of a large field at a point, Prop.~\ref{prop:local-large-field-rarity}, gives.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The line $x_j=L^{K-j}b$ is admissible under the stated side and coupling
conditions, by Lem.~\YMMref{118.1}{812}. Def.~\ref{def:rarity-choices}
and Lem.~\ref{lem:rarity-lowered-choice} put it in the common setting
of Prop.~\ref{prop:local-large-field-rarity}. That proposition
bounds the probability of a prescribed creation at level $t'$ by
$e^{-c_2^\natural p_0(g_{t'})^2}$.

If $Z_t\ne\emptyset$, Prop.~\YMMref{67.2}{588} gives a creation
at some level $t'\le t$. There are at most
$M^{-3}N_{t'}=M^{-3}N_tL^{3(t-t')}$ cells of that level, since
$\check R_{t'}\ge1$. Write $a=t-t'$. On this line,
$y_{t'}=y_t+a\log L$, and convexity gives
\[
 y_{t'}^{2\mathfrak p_0}-y_t^{2\mathfrak p_0}
 \ge2\mathfrak p_0y_t^{2\mathfrak p_0-1}a\log L.
\]
Condition (Y.7) of \eqref{eq:rarity-seven-conditions} therefore bounds
the contribution of level $t-a$ by $L^{-a}$ times the contribution of
level $t$. The union bound and the geometric series yield
\[
 \sum_{h:Z_t(h)\ne\emptyset}\mathsf t(h)
 \le M^{-3}N_te^{-c_2^\natural p_0(g_t)^2}Z
                 \sum_{a=0}^{t-1}L^{-a}
 \le\frac L{L-1}M^{-3}N_te^{-c_2^\natural p_0(g_t)^2}Z.
\]
Finally $L/(L-1)\le13/12<2\cdot24^3/25000$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The threshold on a torus is of exact order $\ell^{3/2\mathfrak p_0}$]\label{lh:thr}
In a setting let $K_0(\ell)=K_0(\ell,2,\mathsf I)$ and $K_1(\ell)=K_1(\ell,2,\mathsf I,\varepsilon)$ be the thresholds of the convergence on the torus $T_\ell$ (Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AS}{813}} at $s=0$, with the constants and thresholds in Thm.~\YMMref{AR}{810}) at $n=2$, for the labels of $\mathsf I$ and the spread $\varepsilon$, as they are set there. There are $c_1,c_2<\infty$ such that for all $m\ge m_0$ with $M\mathcal R(b_+)\le L^m$, $\ell=2L^m$,
\[
\frac{1800}\lambda\Bigl[\Bigl(\frac{\Xi\ell^3}{c'A_0^2}\Bigr)^{1/2\mathfrak p_0}-\log(Lb_-)\Bigr]\le K_0(\ell)\le K_1(\ell)\le c_1+c_2\ell^{3/2\mathfrak p_0},
\]
where $\Xi>0$ is the number in the factor $e^{\Xi\ell^3}$ that the bound on the lost mass, with which these thresholds are formed, carries, and $c'>0$ the number in its large-field weight $e^{-c'A_0^2(\log x)^{2\mathfrak p_0}}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The conditions that define the thresholds read the side only through $N_{[d]}=\ell^3L^{3d}$ at depths $d\le K/9+1$ and through the factor $e^{\Xi\ell^3}$. At $n=2$ the depth $u$ of the comparison of the cutoffs satisfies $K/1800\le u\le K/1800+1$. One condition asks that the bound on the lost mass, $2M^{-3}\ell^3L^{3u}\exp[\Xi\ell^3-c'A_0^2(\log(L^ub_-))^{2\mathfrak p_0}]$, be at most $\frac12$; as $2M^{-3}\ell^3\ge16$ and $\log(L^ub_-)\le K\lambda/1800+\log(Lb_-)$, it fails unless $(K\lambda/1800+\log(Lb_-))^{2\mathfrak p_0}\ge\Xi\ell^3/c'A_0^2$, which is the lower bound. For the upper bound, each condition says that a quantity $c\,\ell^3L^{-cK}$, or $c\exp[c\log K+c\log\ell+cK+\Xi\ell^3-c''K^{2\mathfrak p_0}]$ with $c''>0$ formed from $A_0$, $A_1$ and the constants that enter the definition of the thresholds, is at most a fixed number. For $K\ge c_2\ell^{3/2\mathfrak p_0}$ we have $\Xi\ell^3\le\frac12c''K^{2\mathfrak p_0}$ and $\log\ell\le\frac{2\mathfrak p_0}{3c_2}K$, and all conditions hold once also $K\ge c_1$, because $2\mathfrak p_0\ge2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[One cutoff: conditional expectations]\label{lh:cond}
Let $K\in\mathbb N$, and let $\mathcal G$ be a set of laws on $\mathbb L_K$, each invariant under the isometries of $\mathbb L_K$, such that $h\nu/\nu(h)\in\mathcal G$ for $\nu\in\mathcal G$ and every bounded $\mathcal I$-measurable $h\ge0$ with $\nu(h)>0$. For $\rho\in\mathcal G$, $e_\rho=\rho(a_p)$ is one number for all plaquettes $p$; put $e_+=\sup_{\rho\in\mathcal G}e_\rho$, $e_-=\inf_{\rho\in\mathcal G}e_\rho$, and let $\nu\in\mathcal G$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] There is one bounded $\mathcal I$-measurable $\mathsf e$ with $\mathsf e=E_\nu[a_p|\mathcal I]$ $\nu$-almost surely for every plaquette $p$; $e_-\le\mathsf e\le e_+$ $\nu$-almost surely, and $\operatorname{Var}_\nu\mathsf e\le\frac14(e_+-e_-)^2$.
\item[(b)] For bounded $f$ of compact support, $E_\nu[\mathcal O_K(f)-\nu(\mathcal O_K(f))\,|\,\mathcal I]=3a_K^{-4}r_K(f)(\mathsf e-e_\nu)$ $\nu$-almost surely.
\item[(c)] For every bounded real Borel function $F$, $E_\nu[F|\mathcal I]$ takes $\nu$-almost surely values in $[\inf_{\rho\in\mathcal G}\rho(F),\sup_{\rho\in\mathcal G}\rho(F)]$.
\item[(d)] If $\nu$ is ergodic, or $e_\nu\in\{e_-,e_+\}$, then $\mathsf e$ is $\nu$-almost surely constant.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Let $k$ be bounded and $\mathcal I$-measurable, $c=1+\sup|k|$ and $h=k+c\ge1$. The laws $h\nu/\nu(h)$ and $\nu$ lie in $\mathcal G$, so they are invariant, and the isometries act transitively on the plaquettes; so $\nu(ha_p)=\nu(ha_{p'})$ and $\nu(ca_p)=\nu(ca_{p'})$ for all $p,p'$, and subtracting, $\nu(ka_p)=\nu(ka_{p'})$: all $a_p$ have one conditional expectation given $\mathcal I$. (c): if $\{E_\nu[F|\mathcal I]>\sup_\rho\rho(F)+\epsilon\}$ had positive mass, conditioning on it would give a member of $\mathcal G$ in which the mean of $F$ exceeds $\sup_\rho\rho(F)$; likewise below. At $F=a_p$ this gives the range of $\mathsf e$, and a variable with values in an interval of length $e_+-e_-$ has variance at most $\frac14(e_+-e_-)^2$. (b): linearity, and $a_K^{-1}\sum_pf(x(p))=3a_K^{-4}r_K(f)$. (d): if $\nu$ is ergodic, $\mathcal I$ is trivial modulo $\nu$; if $\nu(\mathsf e)=e_\nu=e_+$, the function $\mathsf e\le e_+$ has the mean $e_+$, so it is constant; likewise at $e_-$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[One cutoff: the plateau for several fields]\label{lh:many}
Let $\mathcal G$ be a class at the cutoff $K$ (Section~\YMMref{100}{743}) that obeys the bound system $\mathsf C^g=(\hat C^g_1,(\hat C^g_n)_{n\ge2})$ at $g$, with the properties listed in the paragraph on one cutoff: for $n\ge2$ and every tuple $X=(f_1,\dots,f_n)$ of type $(\mathsf d;R)$, $|S^T_n[\rho](X)|\le\hat C^g_n(\mathsf d;R)\prod_i\|f_i\|_\sharp$ for $\rho\in\mathcal G$, and $|\rho(\mathcal O_K(f))-\rho'(\mathcal O_K(f))|\le\hat C^g_1(R)\|f\|_\sharp$ for $\rho,\rho'\in\mathcal G$ and $f\in C^1_c(\mathbb R^3)$ with support in a closed ball of radius $R$; the numbers $\delta(X;\bar R)$ and $\mathsf N(X;\bar R)$ are those of the plateau theorem, the second formed with this bound system. Let $\nu\in\mathcal G$. Let $X,Y$ be separated, $\bar R\in a_K\mathbb N$ with all supports in $(-\bar R,\bar R)^3$, $a_K\le2\min\{\delta(X;\bar R),\delta(Y;\bar R)\}$, $v\in a_K\mathbb Z^3$ and $|v|\ge4\sqrt3\bar R$. Then
\[
\bigl|\sigma_\nu(X\cdot\tau_vY)-\sigma_\nu(X)\sigma_\nu(Y)-\operatorname{Cov}_\nu\bigl(E_\nu[X^\nu_K|\mathcal I],E_\nu[Y^\nu_K|\mathcal I]\bigr)\bigr|\le\mathfrak k_0[\mathsf N(X;\bar R)\mathsf N(Y;\bar R)]^{1/2}\bar R/|v|,
\]
\[
\bigl|\operatorname{Cov}_\nu\bigl(E_\nu[X^\nu_K|\mathcal I],E_\nu[Y^\nu_K|\mathcal I]\bigr)\bigr|\le\tfrac14\operatorname{osc}_{\mathcal G}(X^\nu_K)\operatorname{osc}_{\mathcal G}(Y^\nu_K),\qquad\operatorname{osc}_{\mathcal G}(F)=\sup_{\rho\in\mathcal G}\rho(F)-\inf_{\rho\in\mathcal G}\rho(F);
\]
and $\operatorname{osc}_{\mathcal G}((f)^\nu_K)=3a_K^{-4}|r_K(f)|(e_+-e_-)$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Clause (b) of the plateau theorem at $\nu$ compares $\sigma_\nu(X\cdot\tau_vY)$ with 
\[
\nu(E_\nu[X^\nu_K|\mathcal I]E_\nu[Y^\nu_K|\mathcal I]),
\]
which is $\sigma_\nu(X)\sigma_\nu(Y)$ plus the covariance, as $\nu(E_\nu[A|\mathcal I])=\nu(A)$. By Lem.~\ref{lh:cond}(c) each conditional expectation lies almost surely in an interval of length $\operatorname{osc}_{\mathcal G}$, so its variance is at most $\frac14\operatorname{osc}_{\mathcal G}^2$; then the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality. At $X=(f)$, $\rho((f)^\nu_K)=3a_K^{-4}r_K(f)(e_\rho-e_\nu)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Recentring and clustering]\label{lh:rec}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[beginpenalty=10000]
\item[(a)] For laws $\rho,\nu,\nu'$ on $\mathbb L_K$ and $X=(f_1,\dots,f_n)$,
\begin{equation}\label{lh:rece}
\begin{aligned}
\rho(X^{\nu'}_K)={}&\sum_{A\subset\{1,\dots,n\}}\ \prod_{i\in A}
\bigl[\nu(\mathcal O_K(f_i))-\nu'(\mathcal O_K(f_i))\bigr]\\
&\qquad\rho\bigl((X_{A^c})^\nu_K\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
\item[(b)] Let $0<g\le\gamma$ and $B^g_n(\mathsf d;R)=\sum_\pi\prod_{A\in\pi}\hat C^g_{|A|}(\mathsf d;R)$, the sum over the partitions of $\{1,\dots,n\}$ into blocks of at least two elements ($B^g_0=1$, $B^g_1=0$). The set $\mathcal E^g$ of the symmetric functionals $\Phi$ with $|\Phi(X)|\le B^g_n(\mathsf d;R)\prod_i\|f_i\|_\sharp$ for every $X$ of type $(\mathsf d;R)$ is convex, and compact and metrisable for pointwise convergence; it contains $\sigma_\nu$ for $(K,\beta)\in\mathfrak d(g)$ and $\nu\in\mathcal G_{K,\beta}$.
\item[(c)] Let $\mathsf T$ be a compact metrisable set of symmetric functionals that are real-valued on real tuples, with pointwise convergence, such that for all separated $X,Y$ there are $r_{X,Y},c_{X,Y}<\infty$ with $\sup_{\psi\in\mathsf T}|\psi(X\cdot\tau_vY)-\psi(X)\psi(Y)|\le c_{X,Y}/|v|$ for $|v|\ge r_{X,Y}$. Then for every Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathsf T$, $(\operatorname{supp}\mu,\mu,(\psi)_{\psi\in\operatorname{supp}\mu})$ is a canonical decomposition of $\operatorname{bar}(\mu)$, and $\mu\mapsto\operatorname{bar}(\mu)$ is affine, continuous and injective.
\item[(d)] Let $0<g\le\gamma$, $(K,\beta)\in\mathfrak d(g)$, $\nu^1,\nu^2\in\mathcal G_{K,\beta}$, $0\le t\le1$, $\nu=t\nu^1+(1-t)\nu^2$, $X$ of $n$ entries and of type $(\mathsf d;R)$, and $\eta=a_K^{-4}J(\beta)(2R+1)^3$. Then
\[
\bigl|\sigma_\nu(X)-t\sigma_{\nu^1}(X)-(1-t)\sigma_{\nu^2}(X)\bigr|\le\sum_{k=1}^n\binom nk\eta^kB^g_{n-k}(\mathsf d;R)\prod_i\|f_i\|_\sharp ,
\]
and at $n=2$ exactly 
\[
\sigma_\nu((f,h))=t\sigma_{\nu^1}((f,h))+(1-t)\sigma_{\nu^2}((f,h))+9t(1-t)a_K^{-8}r_K(f)r_K(h)(e_{\nu^1}-e_{\nu^2})^2.
\]
With (C), $\eta\le(2R+1)^3g^{8+2c}c_*(c)L^{-cK}$ for $0\le c<\frac1{180}$: the defect of convexity of $\nu\mapsto\sigma_\nu$ at one cutoff falls like a power of the spacing.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(a) Write $\mathcal O_K(f_i)-\nu'(\mathcal O_K(f_i))=[\mathcal O_K(f_i)-\nu(\mathcal O_K(f_i))]+[\nu-\nu'](\mathcal O_K(f_i))$ and multiply out. (b) A centred moment $\sigma_\nu(X)$ is the sum, over the partitions without singletons, of the products of the cumulants of the blocks, which the family of bounds at $g$ bounds; the defining conditions are inequalities and equalities at finitely many tuples, so they pass to convex combinations and to pointwise limits, and Tychonoff's theorem gives compactness. Approximating each entry of a tuple in $\|\cdot\|_\sharp$ by functions from a countable family supported in finite unions of rational cubes, and using multilinearity with the bound, one finds a countable set of tuples on which two members of $\mathcal E^g$ agree only if they are equal, and on which pointwise convergence implies convergence at every tuple; so $\mathcal E^g$ is metrisable. (c) By induction on $q$, the uniform clustering shows that $\int\prod_{i\le q}\psi(X^i)\,\mathrm{d}\mu$ is the iterated plateau of $\operatorname{bar}(\mu)$ at $(X^1,\dots,X^q)$: this is (Can4); the other conditions are plain.

So $\operatorname{bar}(\mu)$ determines the integrals of the products of the functions $\psi\mapsto\psi(X)$, which are real-valued and separate the points of $\mathsf T$; their products and constants form a real unital algebra, so by the Stone--Weierstrass theorem it determines $\mu$. The barycentre is affine in $\mu$, and continuous since the integrands are continuous. (d) $\sigma_\nu(X)=t\nu^1(X^\nu_K)+(1-t)\nu^2(X^\nu_K)$, and by \eqref{lh:rece} with $\rho=\nu^i$, $\nu'=\nu$ and the centring $\nu^i$, $\nu^i(X^\nu_K)-\sigma_{\nu^i}(X)$ is a sum over $A\ne\emptyset$ of products of $|A|$ one-point differences, each at most $a_K^{-4}J(\beta)(2R+a_K)^3\|f\|_\infty\le\eta\|f\|_\sharp$ by (C), times $\sigma_{\nu^i}(X_{A^c})$, which is at most $B^g_{n-|A|}(\mathsf d;R)\prod_{A^c}\|f_i\|_\sharp$ by (b).

At $n=2$, $\operatorname{Cov}_\nu(F,H)=t\operatorname{Cov}_{\nu^1}(F,H)+(1-t)\operatorname{Cov}_{\nu^2}(F,H)+t(1-t)[\nu^1-\nu^2](F)\,[\nu^1-\nu^2](H)$ for $F=\mathcal O_K(f)$, $H=\mathcal O_K(h)$, and $[\nu^1-\nu^2](\mathcal O_K(f))=3a_K^{-4}r_K(f)(e_{\nu^1}-e_{\nu^2})$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[The one-point differences and the convexity of the limits]\label{lh:arc}
In the proof of (G)(1) the vanishing of the one-point differences, (D)(1), makes the limits of the mixtures the mixtures of the limits; the identity at $n=2$ in (d) shows, for data, what can happen without it. Let, along a sequence of pairs, the class at the $j$-th pair be the segment $\{s\nu^+_j+(1-s)\nu^-_j:0\le s\le1\}$ between two ergodic laws $\nu^\pm_j$ whose one-point functions differ by an amount that tends to $c\int f$ with $c\ne0$, and let $\sigma_{\nu^\pm_j}\to\sigma^\pm$. Then the mixtures $\nu^s_j=s\nu^+_j+(1-s)\nu^-_j$ have
\[
\sigma_{\nu^s_j}((f,h))\to\sigma_s((f,h))=s\sigma^+((f,h))+(1-s)\sigma^-((f,h))+s(1-s)c^2\int f\int h .
\]
If moreover $(f,h)\mapsto\sigma^+((f,h))-\sigma^-((f,h))$ is not a multiple of $(f,h)\mapsto\int f\int h$, the limits $\sigma_s$, $0\le s\le1$, form an arc and not a segment, and the set of the limits along the sequence, which is $\{\sigma_s:0\le s\le1\}$, does not contain the midpoint of $\sigma^+$ and $\sigma^-$: it is not convex. For the model, (D)(1) excludes such sequences among the periodic Gibbs states at first-passage data.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[What a rate on the tori gives]\label{lh:pow}
Let $(\mathrm S_1)$, $(\mathrm S_2)$ and $r_1$ be as in (A)(2); no lowered choice is given. Suppose that for $i=1,2$ there are numbers $C_i\ge1$, $c_{1,i}\ge0$, integers $m_{1,i}\ge m_{0,i}$ and, for $m\ge m_{1,i}$, $\ell=2L_i^m$ and $b\in\mathsf I_i$, real numbers $S^{(\ell,b)}$ such that for all integers $K\ge C_i\log\ell$
\[
\bigl|S^T_{2;K,\ell,L_i^Kb}(f_1,f_2)-S^{(\ell,b)}\bigr|\le C_i\ell^{c_{1,i}}L_i^{-K/C_i}\|f_1\|_\sharp\|f_2\|_\sharp\qquad\text{at the one pair }f_1=\mathsf f^{\langle\ell\rangle},\ f_2=1-\mathsf h^{\langle\ell\rangle}.
\]
Then the oscillation hypothesis of Prop.~\ref{lh:per}(b) holds for $m\ge m_{1,i}$, with $\mathsf a_i=C_i\log2$, $A_i=C_i\max\{\lambda_i,c_{1,i}\}$ and $\omega_i=2^{1+c_{1,i}}\cdot4800b_{+,i}^5M_i^2L_i^5C_i$, and the two bounds of (B)(1) hold with the power $\beta^{-1/2A}$, $A=\max_iA_i$, beyond some $\beta_1$. More generally, any oscillation bound for the far parts with thresholds $\mathsf a_i+A_im$ on all sides $m\ge m_{1,i}$ gives $\beta^4J(\beta)\le C\beta^{-1/2\max_iA_i}$ for large $\beta$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Index $i$ dropped. For $m\ge m_1$ and integers $K,K'\ge\mathsf a+Am$ we have $K\ge C\log2+C\lambda m=C\log\ell$, the same for $K'$, and $\ell^{c_1}L^{-K/C}=2^{c_1}L^{c_1m-K/C}\le2^{c_1}$, since $K/C\ge c_1m$. So the two torus functions differ by at most $2C2^{c_1}\|f_1\|_\sharp\|f_2\|_\sharp$; with $b^5\varepsilon^{-3}\le b_+^5L^3$ and $\|f_1\|_\sharp,\|f_2\|_\sharp\le40\sqrt3ML$, $\sup_{\log\mathsf I}|y_{m,K}-y_{m,K'}|\le\omega$. Enter in Prop.~\ref{lh:per}(b) as in Step~1 of the proof of Thm.~\ref{lh:main} below, with $m^0_i=m_{1,i}$; the second sentence is the same argument with the given thresholds.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[A threshold that does not grow with the side gives $J=0$ on a half line]\label{lh:cut}
Let $(\mathrm S_1)$, $(\mathrm S_2)$ and $r_1$ be as in (A)(2). Suppose that there are an integer $K_*$ and numbers $\omega_i$ such that $\sup_{\log\mathsf I_i}|y^{(i)}_{m,K}-y^{(i)}_{m,K'}|\le\omega_i$ for all integers $K,K'\ge K_*$ and all $m\ge m_{0,i}$, $i=1,2$. Then there is $\beta_*$ with $J(\beta)=0$ for $\beta\ge\beta_*$, and on $(\beta_*,\infty)$ the measure $\beta^4[P''(d\beta)-\hat n\,\mathrm{d}\beta]$ has a bounded density. In terms of one lattice: with $Y_N(\beta)=\beta^5[P_N''(\beta)-\hat n(\beta)]$, Prop.~\ref{lh:blk}(d) puts $Y_N(\beta)$ within $C^{\rm ref}$ of $y_{m,K}(\log b)$ for $N=2L^{m+K}$, $\beta=L^Kb$, $b\in\mathsf I$, $m\ge m_0$. Given lowered choices, the oscillation bound of Step~5 of the proof of Thm.~\ref{lh:main} gives $|Y_{L^kN}(L^k\beta)-Y_N(\beta)|\le\omega_A+2C^{\rm ref}$ for all $k\ge0$ at these $N$, $\beta$ with $N/\beta\le2b_+^{-1-1/A}L^{-k^{\rm rt}/A}\beta^{1/A}$; the hypothesis here asks such a bound at all of them.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Enter in Prop.~\ref{lh:per}(c) with the data of Step~1 of the proof of Thm.~\ref{lh:main} and with $\max\{K_*,k_1,k_2\}$ in the place of $K_*$: $\epsilon^{(i)}_m=c_{{\rm P},i}L_i^{-m}$ has the lower bound $0$, and the hypothesis on $Y^0$ holds at $m^0=m_{0,1}$ with $k^0=\max\{K_*,k_1\}$, since $|y^{(1)}_{m_{0,1},K}|\le|y^{(1)}_{m_{0,1},k^0}|+\omega_1$ for $K\ge k^0$. Since $P$ is the pressure, $J_P=J$. For the last sentence: $L^kN=2L^{m+K+k}$ and $L^k\beta=L^{K+k}b$, and $K\ge k^{\rm rt}+Am$ reads $N/\beta\le2b^{-1-1/A}L^{-k^{\rm rt}/A}\beta^{1/A}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The inequality of two boxes at one pair, and along a label]\label{lh:onepair}
Let $a>0$ and $\beta>0$. For the periodic boxes $\underline n=(n_1,n_2,n_3)$, $n_\mu\ge3$, of the lattice $a\mathbb Z^3$ at the coupling $\beta$ let $F(\underline n)=\log Z(\underline n)$, $|\underline n|=n_1n_2n_3$, $\Delta(\underline n)=F(\underline n)-|\underline n|P(\beta)$, write $F(N^3)$ and $\Delta(N^3)$ for the cube of side $N$, and $\mathcal E(l)=2F(l,2l,2l)-F(2l,2l,2l)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] $\Delta(\underline n)\ge0$; $\Delta(\underline n')/|\underline n'|\le\Delta(\underline n)/|\underline n|$ for $\underline n'\ge\underline n$ in each component; and $\mathcal E(N)\le8\Delta(N^3)-\Delta((2N)^3)\le8\Delta(N^3)$ for $N\ge3$.
\item[(b)] If $\mathcal E(l)\le x_0$ for one integer $l\ge3$ and one number $0<x_0\le0.069$, then, with $\theta=12.9x_0\le0.8901$: $\mathcal E(2l)\le12.9\,\mathcal E(l)^2$; $\Delta(N'^3)<0.13736\,\theta^{N'/2l}$ for every $N'\ge2l$; and $\mathcal E(l')\le0.743\,\theta^{l'/2l}$ for every $l'\ge l$.
\item[(c)] If $\mathcal E(l)\le0.069$ for one integer $l\ge3$, the lattice $a\mathbb Z^3$ has exactly one periodic Gibbs state at $\beta$; it is a pure phase, and $J(\beta)=0$.
\item[(d)] If the lattice has two periodic Gibbs states at $\beta$, then $\mathcal E(l)>0.069$ for every $l\ge3$, $\Delta(N^3)>0.0086$ for every $N\ge3$, and $\liminf_{j\to\infty}\Delta((2L^j)^3)\ge\log2$ for every odd integer $L\ge13$.
\item[(e)] At every $\beta>0$, either $\mathcal E(l)>0.069$ for every $l\ge3$, or $\mathcal E(l')\to0$ exponentially in $l'$.
\item[(f)] In a setting suppose $\mathrm{BI}[b,\ell_*,K_*;x_0]$, let $\underline K=\max\{K_*,1\}$, $\theta=12.9x_0$, and let $\nu_K$ be the one periodic Gibbs state of (c) at $a=a_K$, $\beta=L^Kb$. Let $n\ge2$, and let $X=(f_1,\dots,f_n)$ be real Lipschitz functions, none of them $0$, with pairwise disjoint supports in $(-\frac{\ell''}4,\frac{\ell''}4)^3$ for a side $\ell''=2L^{m''}\ge\ell_*$, $m''\in\mathbb N$. There is $C(X)<\infty$, formed from $X$, $\ell''$ and $b$ and from no cutoff and no further side, such that for all $K\ge\underline K$ and all sides $\ell'=2L^{m'}\ge\ell''$
\[
\bigl|S^T_n[\nu_K](X)-S^T_{n;K,\ell',L^Kb}(X^{\langle\ell'\rangle})\bigr|\le C(X)\,\theta^{\ell'/4\ell_*}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(a) Fix a direction of a box as the time and the two other sides, $n_\nu\ge3$, the section $\Sigma$, and write $F(t,\Sigma)$ and $Z(t,\Sigma)$ for the box with $t\ge3$ layers. On the Hilbert space of the configurations of the bonds of one layer (Section~\YMMref{85}{677}) let $\mathsf C_\Sigma$ be the crossing operator of Section~\YMMref{85}{677}, written $\mathsf K$ there, and $\mathsf D_\Sigma$ the multiplication by $e^{-\beta A_\Sigma}$, the weight of the plaquettes of one layer. $\mathsf C_\Sigma$ is positive (Prop.~\YMMref{85.1}{678}), and it is of trace class: the series the rank-one expansion in the proof of Prop.~\YMMref{85.1}{678} in the proof of that clause writes it as $\sum_\alpha c_\alpha|\chi_\alpha\rangle\langle\chi_\alpha|$ with $\|\chi_\alpha\|\le1$ and $c_\alpha\ge0$, $\sum_\alpha c_\alpha<\infty$ the rank-one expansion in the proof of Prop.~\YMMref{85.1}{678}.

So the transfer operator of one layer, 
\[
T_\Sigma:=\mathsf C_\Sigma^{1/2}\mathsf D_\Sigma\mathsf C_\Sigma^{1/2},
\]
is positive, as 
\[
\langle\psi,T_\Sigma\psi\rangle=\int e^{-\beta A_\Sigma}|\mathsf C_\Sigma^{1/2}\psi|^2\,\mathrm{d}V,
\]
and of trace class; like $\mathsf C_\Sigma$ and $\mathsf D_\Sigma$ it does not depend on the number of layers (Prop.~\YMMref{85.2}{679}). Integrating the variables of the bonds between two layers turns the weight of a slab into a chain of kernels: the slab operator of the function $1$ on $\vartheta\ge2$ layers is $\mathsf D_\Sigma(\mathsf C_\Sigma\mathsf D_\Sigma)^{\vartheta-1}$, so that 
\[
\mathfrak Y[1]=\mathsf C_\Sigma^{1/2}\mathsf D_\Sigma(\mathsf C_\Sigma\mathsf D_\Sigma)^{\vartheta-1}\mathsf C_\Sigma^{1/2}=T_\Sigma^\vartheta
\]
 (equation~\YMMref{(1744)}{679}).

The trace formula, Prop.~\YMMref{85.2}{679} with the function $1$ on two slabs of $2$ and $t-2$ layers, gives $Z(t,\Sigma)=\operatorname{Tr}T_\Sigma^t$ for $t\ge4$; at $t=3$ the integral over the three layers is $\operatorname{Tr}(\mathsf C_\Sigma\mathsf D_\Sigma)^3$, by the Hilbert--Schmidt kernel identity $\operatorname{Tr}(AB)=\iint A(y,x)B(x,y)\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y$ used in the proof of Prop.~\YMMref{85.2}{679}, applied to the operators $(\mathsf C_\Sigma\mathsf D_\Sigma)^2$ and $\mathsf C_\Sigma\mathsf D_\Sigma$, which have bounded kernels, and this is $\operatorname{Tr}T_\Sigma^3$ by the cyclicity of the trace. With the eigenvalues $\mu_i\ge0$ of the positive compact operator $T_\Sigma$, counted with their multiplicities, the trace of a power is the sum of the powers of the eigenvalues, by computing the trace in an orthonormal eigenbasis, and
\[
e^{F(t,\Sigma)}=Z(t,\Sigma)=\operatorname{Tr}T_\Sigma^t=\sum_i\mu_i^t\qquad\text{for every integer }t\ge3,
\]
with numbers $\mu_i\ge0$ that do not depend on $t$, odd $t$ and $t=3$ included. By the spectral argument in the proof of Prop.~\YMMref{86.5}{682}, $(\operatorname{Tr}T_\Sigma^t)^{1/t}$ does not increase in $t$; so $F/|\underline n|$ does not increase when a side grows, and as $F(N^3)/N^3\to P$ (Lem.~\ref{lh:lat}(a)), $P=\inf F/|\underline n|$, and $\Delta\ge0$ with the monotonicity per site. In particular $F(N,2N,2N)\le4F(N^3)$, so $\mathcal E(N)\le8F(N^3)-F((2N)^3)=8\Delta(N^3)-\Delta((2N)^3)$.
(b) \emph{One direction.} Fix a direction of a box as the time and the two other sides, the section $\Sigma$, and write $F(t,\Sigma)$ for the box with $t\ge3$ layers. By (a), with $\lambda_0>0$ the largest of the numbers $\mu_i$ and $\mathsf y_j\in[0,1]$ the quotients $\mu_i/\lambda_0$ of the others, $F(t,\Sigma)=t\log\lambda_0+\log(1+\mathsf r_t)$ with $\mathsf r_t=\sum_j\mathsf y_j^{\,t}$. So $\mathsf r_t$ does not increase in $t$, $\mathsf r_{2t}\le\mathsf r_t^2$, and
\[
\mathsf d(t):=2F(t,\Sigma)-F(2t,\Sigma)=2\log(1+\mathsf r_t)-\log(1+\mathsf r_{2t})\ \ge\ \log(1+\mathsf r_t)\ \ge0 .
\]
Let $\mathsf d(t)\le x<\log2$, $\eta=e^x-1<1$ and $\rho(\eta)=\eta/(1+\sqrt{1-\eta^2})$. Then $\mathsf r_t\le\eta$, and $1+2\mathsf r_t/(1+\mathsf r_t^2)\le(1+\mathsf r_t)^2/(1+\mathsf r_{2t})=e^{\mathsf d(t)}\le1+\eta$; as $r\mapsto2r/(1+r^2)$ increases on $[0,1]$ and takes the value $\eta$ at $r=\rho(\eta)$, we get $\mathsf r_t\le\rho(\eta)$, and so
\[
\mathsf d(2t)\le2\log(1+\mathsf r_{2t})\le2\log(1+\mathsf r_t^2)\le\psi(x):=2\log\bigl(1+\rho(e^x-1)^2\bigr).
\]
The function $\psi$ increases on $[0,\log2)$, and, as $(e^y-1)/y$ increases, $\psi(y)\le2\kappa(y_0)^2y^2$ for $0\le y\le y_0<\log2$, with $\kappa(y_0)=\frac{e^{y_0}-1}{y_0}\bigl(1+\sqrt{1-(e^{y_0}-1)^2}\bigr)^{-1}$; and $\kappa(0.069)\le0.51832$, $\kappa(0.14056)\le0.53995$, $\kappa(0.29264)\le0.59869$.

\emph{Doubling.} For a box $\underline n$ and a direction $\mu$ let $\mathsf d^{(\mu)}(\underline n)$ be $2F(\underline n)$ minus $F$ of the box with $n_\mu$ doubled. By the above, read in the direction $\mu$, $\mathsf d^{(\mu)}\ge0$, and $\mathsf d^{(\mu)}$ of the box with $n_\mu$ doubled is at most $\psi(\mathsf d^{(\mu)}(\underline n))$ when $\mathsf d^{(\mu)}(\underline n)<\log2$. Let $\epsilon=\mathcal E(l)\le0.069$. As $F$ does not depend on the order of the three sides, $\epsilon=\mathsf d^{(1)}(l,2l,2l)=\mathsf d^{(2)}(2l,l,2l)=\mathsf d^{(3)}(2l,2l,l)$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $\mathsf a:=\mathsf d^{(2)}(2l,2l,2l)\le\psi(\epsilon)\le2\kappa(0.069)^2\epsilon^2\le0.53732\,\epsilon^2\le0.03708\,\epsilon$;
\item[(ii)] since $F(2l,4l,l)\le2F(2l,2l,l)$ and $F(2l,4l,2l)=2F(2l,2l,2l)-\mathsf a$, we have $\mathsf d^{(3)}(2l,4l,l)\le2\,\mathsf d^{(3)}(2l,2l,l)+\mathsf a=2\epsilon+\mathsf a\le2.03708\,\epsilon\le0.14056$, so $\mathsf b:=\mathsf d^{(3)}(2l,4l,2l)\le\psi(2\epsilon+\mathsf a)\le2.41970\,\epsilon^2\le0.16696\,\epsilon$;
\item[(iii)] since $F(l,4l,4l)\le4F(l,2l,2l)$ and $F(2l,4l,4l)=2F(2l,4l,2l)-\mathsf b=4F(2l,2l,2l)-2\mathsf a-\mathsf b$, we have $\mathsf c:=\mathsf d^{(1)}(l,4l,4l)\le4\epsilon+2\mathsf a+\mathsf b\le4.24112\,\epsilon\le0.29264<\log2$;
\item[(iv)] $\mathcal E(2l)=\mathsf d^{(1)}(2l,4l,4l)\le\psi(\mathsf c)\le2\cdot0.59869^2\cdot4.24112^2\,\epsilon^2\le12.8943\,\epsilon^2$.
\end{enumerate}
So $\mathcal E(2l)\le12.9\,\mathcal E(l)^2$ when $\mathcal E(l)\le0.069$. As $12.9\cdot0.069=0.8901<1$, induction shows that $\epsilon_k=\mathcal E(2^kl)$ does not increase in $k$ and that $12.9\,\epsilon_{k+1}\le(12.9\,\epsilon_k)^2$; so $12.9\,\epsilon_k\le(12.9\,\epsilon_0)^{2^k}\le\theta^{2^k}$, that is, $\mathcal E(2^kl)\le x_k:=\theta^{2^k}/12.9\le x_0\le0.069$.

\emph{Cubes.} Put $D(N)=8F(N^3)-F((2N)^3)=8\Delta(N^3)-\Delta((2N)^3)$. At $n=2^kl$, with $\mathsf a$ and $\mathsf b$ formed at $n$ in the place of $l$, the three brackets of
\[
\begin{multlined}
D(2n)=\bigl[8F((2n)^3)-4F(2n,4n,2n)\bigr]+\bigl[4F(2n,4n,2n)-2F(2n,4n,4n)\bigr]+\bigl[2F(2n,4n, \\
4n)-F((4n)^3)\bigr]
\end{multlined}
\]
are $4\mathsf a$, $2\mathsf b$ and $\mathcal E(2n)$; so $D(2n)\le(2.14928+4.83940+12.8943)\,\epsilon_k^2\le20\,\epsilon_k^2$. By (a) the density $F/|\underline n|$ decreases to $P$ along the cubes of the sides $2^sM$, $s\to\infty$, so that $\Delta(M^3)=\sum_{s\ge0}8^{-(s+1)}D(2^sM)$. At $M=2^jl$, $j\ge1$, every $D(2^sM)$ is at most $20\,\epsilon_{s+j-1}^2\le20\,\epsilon_{j-1}^2$, and
\[
\Delta(M^3)\le\tfrac{20}7\,\epsilon_{j-1}^2\le\tfrac{20}{7\cdot12.9^2}\,\theta^{2^j}\le0.017170\,\theta^{M/l}.
\]
In particular $\Delta((2n)^3)\le\frac{20}7\,\mathcal E(n)^2\le\frac{20}7x_k^2$ at $n=2^kl$. With $\mathcal E(N)\le8\Delta(N^3)$ from (a) and $\frac{20}7\cdot64<182.9$ this gives $\Delta((2N)^3)\le183\,\Delta(N^3)^2$ when $\Delta(N^3)\le0.008625$, for then $\mathcal E(N)\le0.069$; if moreover $\Delta(N^3)>0$, the hypothesis of (b) holds at $l=N$ with $x_0=8\Delta(N^3)$, so with $\theta=103.2\,\Delta(N^3)$, as $12.9\cdot8=103.2$. For $N'\ge2l$ let $j\ge1$ with $M=2^jl\le N'<2M$; by (a), $\Delta(N'^3)\le(N'/M)^3\Delta(M^3)<8\cdot0.017170\,\theta^{M/l}\le0.13736\,\theta^{N'/2l}$, since $M/l>N'/2l$ and $0<\theta<1$.

\emph{All sides $l'\ge l$.} At $n=2^kl$, the identity $\mathcal E(n)=2\Delta(n,2n,2n)-\Delta((2n)^3)$ and the two bounds $\mathcal E(n)\le x_k$, $\Delta((2n)^3)\le\frac{20}7x_k^2$ give $\Delta(n,2n,2n)\le\frac{x_k}2+\frac{10}7x_k^2$. Let $2^kl\le l'<2^{k+1}l$. As $\Delta\ge0$, and by (a) applied to the boxes $(2^kl,2^{k+1}l,2^{k+1}l)\le(l',2l',2l')$, whose volumes have the ratio $(l'/2^kl)^3<8$,
\[
\begin{multlined}
\mathcal E(l')\le2\Delta(l',2l',2l')\le16\,\Delta(2^kl,2^{k+1}l,2^{k+1}l)\le8x_k+\tfrac{160}7x_k^2\le\Bigl(\frac8{12.9}+\frac{160\cdot0.8901}{7\cdot12.9^2}\Bigr)\theta^{2^k} \\
\le0.743\,\theta^{2^k},
\end{multlined}
\]
using $x_k^2=\theta^{2^{k+1}}/12.9^2\le0.8901\,\theta^{2^k}/12.9^2$; and $\theta^{2^k}\le\theta^{l'/2l}$, since $2^k>l'/2l$.
(c) Let $L$ be an odd integer $\ge13$, an allowed blocking factor, and $K\in\mathbb N$. Wilson's action reads the lattice only as a graph, so the dilation $x\mapsto(a_K/a)x$ carries the periodic boxes and the periodic Gibbs states of $a\mathbb Z^3$ at $\beta$ onto those of $\mathbb L_K$, with the same partition functions, and we take $a=a_K$. The cube with $(2L^j)^3$ sites, $j>K$, is then the torus $T_\ell$, $\ell=2L^{j-K}$, at the spacing $a_K$; we put $p_\ell=\ell^{-3}\log Z_{K,\ell,\beta}$. The domination theorem (Prop.~\YMMref{91.9}{705}) bounds the number $n$ of pairwise mutually singular periodic Gibbs states by $\liminf_je^{\Delta((2L^j)^3)}$. Indeed, let $\Psi$ be a function of the cell $[-\frac\ell4,\frac\ell4]^3$ of the board of $\mathbb L_K$ with the side $\frac\ell2$, half the side of $T_\ell$, and the offset $0$, and let $\nu$ be a periodic Gibbs state. Prop.~\YMMref{91.9}{705} gives $|\nu(\Psi)|\le\liminf_{\ell'\to\infty}\|\Psi\|_{{\rm ch},\ell'}$, and the comparison of two sides, {\cite[Cor.~B.1]{YMM2}}(e), gives $\|\Psi\|_{{\rm ch},\ell'}\le\|\Psi\|_{{\rm ch},\ell}\,e^{(\ell/2)^3(p_\ell-p_{\ell'})}$ for $\ell'\ge\ell$, where $(\ell/2)^3(p_\ell-p_{\ell'})\to\frac18\Delta$, $\Delta$ the excess of the cube with $\ell/a_K$ sites a side, as $p_{\ell'}\to a_K^{-3}P$; so
\[
|\nu(\Psi)|\le e^{\Delta/8}\,\|\Psi\|_{{\rm ch},\ell},
\]
and $\|\Psi\|_{{\rm ch},\ell}^8$ is the mean, in the torus measure $\tilde\mu$ of $T_\ell$, of the product of the eight mirror copies of $\Psi$ (equation~{\cite[eq.~189]{YMM2}}). Mutually singular laws $\nu_1,\dots,\nu_n$ have pairwise disjoint carriers, which local events approximate: for $\epsilon>0$ there are pairwise disjoint local events $A_i$ with $\nu_i(A_i)\ge1-n\epsilon$, and for large $\ell$ they are events of the bonds of the cell. At their indicators the last bound reads $\nu_i(A_i)\le e^{\Delta/8}\tilde\mu(E_i)^{1/8}$, where $E_i$ is the intersection of the eight mirror images of $A_i$; the $E_i$ are pairwise disjoint, so $n(1-n\epsilon)^8\le e^{\Delta}$. By (b) the right member tends to $1$ as $\ell\to\infty$; as $\epsilon$ is arbitrary, $n\le1$. Every periodic Gibbs state is an integral of ergodic periodic Gibbs states, and two different ergodic ones are mutually singular; so there is one, it is extreme, and $J(\beta)=0$ by Lem.~\ref{lh:lat}(b).
(d) The first statement is (c); the second follows from (a), as $8\cdot0.008625=0.069$; the third from the bound of (c) with $n=2$, at every odd $L\ge13$, two different ergodic periodic Gibbs states being mutually singular.
(e) is (b) and (c).
(f) Let $G$ be a product of centred $\mathcal O_K(f_i)$, $i\in I\subset\{1,\dots,n\}$, centred at the means on $T_{\ell''}$. Its chessboard seminorm $\|G\|_{{\rm ch},\ell''}$, on the board of $T_{\ell''}$ whose cell holds the supports, has as its eighth power a centred moment, on the fixed torus $T_{\ell''}$, of $8|I|$ observables with pairwise disjoint supports, the mirror copies of the $\mathcal O_K(f_i)$; it is a polynomial in cumulants of orders $\ge2$, each of which converges as $K\to\infty$ by Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AS}{813}}; so it is bounded in $K$. Let $\mu'$ be the measure of $T_{\ell'}$ at the spacing $a_K$, read on $\mathbb L_K$, $Q'=e^{\Delta'/8}$ with $\Delta'$ the excess of the cube with $\ell'/a_K$ sites a side, $Q''=e^{\Delta''/8}$ likewise at $\ell''$, $p_\ell=\ell^{-3}\log Z_{K,\ell,L^Kb}$ as in the proof of (c), and $\mathsf g=Q''\|G\|_{{\rm ch},\ell''}$. Then
\begin{equation}\label{lh:cmp}
|\nu_K(G)-\mu'(G)|\le10.7\,[Q'(Q'-1)]^{1/2}\,\mathsf g\qquad\text{if }\Delta'\le1.81 .
\end{equation}
Four facts enter. (i) For a real function $\Psi$ of the cell $[-\frac{\ell'}4,\frac{\ell'}4]^3$ of the board of $\mathbb L_K$ with the side $\frac{\ell'}2$ and the offset $0$, the coarse board, $|\nu_K(\Psi)|\le Q'\|\Psi\|_{{\rm ch},\ell'}$, by Prop.~\YMMref{91.9}{705} and {\cite[Cor.~B.1]{YMM2}}(e), as in the proof of (c); $G$ is such a function (the plaquette-support argument in {\cite[\S{}B.1]{YMM2}}). (ii) The board with the side $\frac{\ell''}2$ and the offset $0$, the fine board, has the cell $[-\frac{\ell''}4,\frac{\ell''}4]^3$, which holds the supports. As $\ell'/\ell''=L^{m'-m''}$ is odd, the coarse board is coarser than the fine one, and each of its mirror maps carries the cells of the fine board onto cells of the fine board, with the same parity (the proof of Lem.~\YMMref{104.1}{759}).

So the mirror copies $G^{[k]}$ of $G$ in the eight cells $k$ of the coarse board of $T_{\ell'}$ are mirror copies of $G$ in eight different cells of a period box of the fine board, and the chessboard estimate on the fine board of $T_{\ell'}$ ({\cite[Cor.~B.1]{YMM2}}(b), (c), which rests on Prop.~\YMMref{86.3}{681}) gives $|\mu'(\prod_{k\in S}G^{[k]})|\le\|G\|_{\rm f}^{\,|S|}$ for every set $S$ of these cells, $\|G\|_{\rm f}$ being the seminorm of $G$ at the side $\ell'$ on the fine board. (iii) By {\cite[Cor.~B.1]{YMM2}}(e) on the fine board, at the sides $\ell'\ge\ell''$, and as (a) gives $\Delta\ge0$ at the cube with $\ell'/a_K$ sites a side, that is, $p_{\ell'}\ge a_K^{-3}P$: $\|G\|_{\rm f}\le\|G\|_{{\rm ch},\ell''}\,e^{(\ell''/2)^3(p_{\ell''}-p_{\ell'})}\le\mathsf g$. (iv) $\mu'$ is invariant under the isometries of $T_{\ell'}$, so $\mu'(G^{[k]})=\mu'(G)$, and $|\mu'(G)|\le\|G\|_{\rm f}\le\mathsf g$.

Now let $t$ be real, $\Psi=1+tG$, $x=|t|\mathsf g$ and $R(x)=(1+x)^8-1-8x$. By equation~{\cite[eq.~189]{YMM2}} on the coarse board, (ii) and (iv),
\[
\|\Psi\|_{{\rm ch},\ell'}^8=\mu'\Bigl(\prod_k\bigl(1+tG^{[k]}\bigr)\Bigr)=1+8t\mu'(G)+\sum_{|S|\ge2}t^{|S|}\mu'\Bigl(\prod_{k\in S}G^{[k]}\Bigr)\le1+8t\mu'(G)+R(x),
\]
so $\|\Psi\|_{{\rm ch},\ell'}\le1+t\mu'(G)+\frac18R(x)$, as $(1+y)^{1/8}\le1+\frac y8$ for $y\ge-1$; and $1+t\nu_K(G)=\nu_K(\Psi)\le Q'\|\Psi\|_{{\rm ch},\ell'}$ by (i). Hence $t(\nu_K(G)-\mu'(G))\le(Q'-1)(1+x)+\frac18Q'R(x)$ for both signs of $t$, with $Q'\ge1$ by (a). At $\mathsf g=0$ this gives $\nu_K(G)=\mu'(G)$; at $\mathsf g>0$
\[
|\nu_K(G)-\mu'(G)|\le\mathsf g\Bigl[\frac{(Q'-1)(1+x)}x+\frac{Q'R(x)}{8x}\Bigr]\qquad\text{for every }x>0 .
\]
For $Q'>1$ and $x^2=(Q'-1)/Q'$ the bracket is $[Q'(Q'-1)]^{1/2}\bigl(1+x+R(x)/8x^2\bigr)$, and $1+x+R(x)/8x^2\le10.7$ for $x\le0.45$, that is, for $\Delta'\le1.81$; for $Q'=1$ let $x\to0$. This is \eqref{lh:cmp}. By (b) at $l=l_K=\ell_*/2a_K$, $\Delta'<0.13736\,\theta^{\ell'/\ell_*}$ and $\Delta''<0.13736$; so $Q''<1.02$, $[Q'(Q'-1)]^{1/2}\le0.14\,\theta^{\ell'/2\ell_*}$, and \eqref{lh:cmp} gives $|\nu_K(G)-\mu'(G)|\le2\,\theta^{\ell'/2\ell_*}\|G\|_{{\rm ch},\ell''}$. A cumulant of order $n\ge2$ is one polynomial in the means $\mathfrak s(G_I)$, $I\subset\{1,\dots,n\}$, for both laws $\mathfrak s\in\{\nu_K,\mu'\}$; by (iv) and the last bound these means are bounded in $K$ and $\ell'$, and as $\theta^{\ell'/2\ell_*}\le\theta^{\ell'/4\ell_*}$ this gives the display.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Proof of Thm.~\ref{lh:main}}

\emph{Step 1: (A)(1) and (A)(2).} Take two settings at one radius with $L_2=L_1+2$ (Lem.~\ref{lh:two}) and $r_1>0$ with $13r_1b_{+,i}\le1$. We enter in Prop.~\ref{lh:per}: $\beta_0=\max_iL_ib_{-,i}$; $C_{\rm low}=871C^{\rm ref}_1$; $\lambda_i=\log L_i$, so $\lambda_1/\lambda_2\notin\mathbb Q$ by Lem.~\ref{lh:two}; $\alpha_i=\log b_{-,i}$ and $\varkappa_i=\frac12[\log(b_{+,i}/b_{-,i})-\lambda_i]>0$, so that $\mathsf J_i=\log\mathsf I_i$; $k_i$ the least integer $\ge1$ with $L_i^{k_i}b_{-,i}>\beta_0$; $m^0_i=m_{0,i}$; $P^{(i)}_{m,K}=P_N$ and $n^{(i)}_{m,K}=n_{\eta_K}(\mu_{N,\beta})$ with $N=2L_i^{m+K}$ and $\eta_K=L_i^{K-1}$. By Prop.~\ref{lh:blk}(b)--(d), \eqref{lh:data} holds with $\epsilon^{(i)}_m=c_{{\rm P},i}L_i^{-m}$ and $C_N=\max_iC^{\rm ref}_i$, \eqref{lh:low} holds on $(\beta_0,\infty)$, and by \eqref{lh:far} the function $y^{(i)}_{m,K}$ of Prop.~\ref{lh:per} is the far part of the setting $(\mathrm S_i)$. By the convergence on each torus (Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AS}{813}} at $\varsigma_i$; the supports of $\mathsf f^{\langle\ell\rangle}$ and $1-\mathsf h^{\langle\ell\rangle}$ have no common point), for each $m$ the far part converges as $K\to\infty$, uniformly on $\mathsf J_i$; so there are non-decreasing integers $K^{(i)}(m)\ge k_i$, the maxima over $m_{0,i}\le m'\le m$ of the thresholds at the single sides, with
\begin{equation}\label{lh:one}
\sup_{\mathsf J_i}|y^{(i)}_{m,K}-y^{(i)}_{m,K'}|\le1\qquad(K,K'\ge K^{(i)}(m)).
\end{equation}
At $m^0=m_{0,1}$ and $k^0=K^{(1)}(m^0)$ this gives $Y^0=\sup_{\mathsf J_1}|y^{(1)}_{m^0,k^0}|+1<\infty$, the far part at one cutoff being bounded on $\mathsf J_1$. Prop.~\ref{lh:per}(a) with $\omega_i=1$, large $m_i$ and $\bar K_i=K^{(i)}(m_i)$ gives, with $\mathsf A_0$ independent of $m_1,m_2$ and for $0\le\delta\le1$,
\[
\begin{multlined}
\limsup_{s\to\infty}e^{4s}J(e^s)\le(\mathsf A_0+134)\max_i(c_{{\rm P},i}L_i^{-m_i})^{1/2},\quad\limsup_{s\to\infty}|\mathbb M|([s,s+\delta])\le(2\mathsf A_0+C_{\rm low} \\
+134)\delta+(\mathsf A_0+134)\max_i(c_{{\rm P},i}L_i^{-m_i})^{1/2}.
\end{multlined}
\]
Letting $m_1,m_2\to\infty$ gives (A)(1), and (A)(2) with $C=2\mathsf A_0+C_{\rm low}+134$, first for $\delta\le1$ and then for all $\delta>0$ by cutting $[s,s+\delta]$ into intervals of length at most $1$. The equivalent form of (A)(1) is Lem.~\ref{lh:lat}(b).

\emph{Step 2: (A)(3).} Let the two settings have one value of $\mathfrak p_0$; such pairs exist with $\mathfrak p_0\ge a$ by Lem.~\ref{lh:two}. The pair $(\mathsf f^{\langle\ell\rangle},1-\mathsf h^{\langle\ell\rangle})$ has the spread $\varepsilon$ and norms $\|\cdot\|_\sharp\le40\sqrt3ML$ (values in $[0,1]$, Lipschitz constants at most $\sqrt3L$), and $b^5\varepsilon^{-3}\le b_+^5L^3$. By the rate of the convergence on each torus and Lem.~\ref{lh:thr}, in each setting and for the sides with $M\mathcal R(b_+)\le L^m$,
\[
\sup_{\log\mathsf I}|y_{m,K}-y_{m,K'}|\le2b_+^5L^3(40\sqrt3ML)^2C'\ell^9K^{\mathsf p_2}L^{-K/10}\le1\qquad\text{for }K,K'\ge c\bigl(1+\ell^{3/2\mathfrak p_0}\bigr),
\]
with the rate constant $C'=\mathsf C'_2(\mathsf I)$ of Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AS}{813}} at $n=2$ and $s=0$, which is admitted as $b_-\ge\gamma^{-2}$ and $M\mathcal R(b_+)\le L^m$, and a number $c$ independent of $m$, because $\log\ell\le\frac{2\mathfrak p_0}3\ell^{3/2\mathfrak p_0}$. We may therefore take $K^{(i)}(m)\le c(1+(2L_i^m)^{3/2\mathfrak p_0})$ in Step~1. At a large $s$ let $m_i$ be the largest integer with $\alpha_i+2\varkappa_i+\lambda_iK^{(i)}(m_i)\le s$; then $s<c'(1+L_i^{3(m_i+1)/2\mathfrak p_0})$, so $L_i^{-m_i}\le c''s^{-2\mathfrak p_0/3}$, and Prop.~\ref{lh:per}(a) gives $e^{4s}J(e^s)\le Cs^{-\mathfrak p_0/3}$ and $|\mathbb M|([s,s+\delta])\le(2\mathsf A_0+C_{\rm low}+134)\delta+Cs^{-\mathfrak p_0/3}$ for large $s$; the second is at most $C_{\rm A}\delta$ when $C_{\rm A}\ge\max\{2\mathsf A_0+C_{\rm low}+135,C\}$ and $C_{\rm A}s^{-\mathfrak p_0/3}\le\delta$. On bounded sets of $\beta\ge3$ use $J\le6$. For a real $q_0$ choose $\mathfrak p_0\ge3q_0$; as $\log\beta\ge1$ for $\beta\ge3$, $(\log\beta)^{-\mathfrak p_0/3}\le(\log\beta)^{-q_0}$. In any setting, for $(K,\beta)\in\mathfrak d(g)$ we have $b=a_K\beta\ge g^{-2}\ge4$, so $\log\beta\ge K\lambda$ and $a_K^{-4}J(\beta)=b^{-4}\beta^4J(\beta)\le g^8C(K\lambda)^{-q_0}$.

\emph{Step 3: (A)(4).} In one of the two settings let $b\in\mathsf I$, $a=a_K$, $\beta=L^Kb$. By Prop.~\ref{lh:blk}(c) at $m=m_0$, $0\le a^{-3}[P_{N_0}(\beta)-P(\beta)]\le3C_{\rm v}$, which is $-3C_{\rm v}\le u_K\le0$. $u_K$ is the difference of a convex and a smooth function of $b$; $u_K'(b\pm)=a^{-4}[P'(\beta\pm)-P_{N_0}'(\beta)]$, and as measures on $(b_-,b_+)$, by \eqref{lh:far} at $m=m_0$,
\[
u_K''(db)=b^{-4}\mathbb M_K(db)+\vartheta_K(b)\,\mathrm{d}b,\qquad\vartheta_K=-b^{-5}\bigl[\beta^5\bigl(n_{\eta_K}(\mu_{N_0,\beta})-\hat n(\beta)\bigr)+y_{m_0,K}(\log b)\bigr],
\]
where $\mathbb M_K$ is the image of $\mathbb M$ under $s\mapsto e^{s-K\lambda}$. The far parts at $m_0$ are bounded at each cutoff and converge by \eqref{lh:one}, so $Y^*_0=\sup_{K\ge1}\sup_{\log\mathsf I}|y_{m_0,K}|<\infty$, and by Prop.~\ref{lh:blk}(d), $|\vartheta_K|\le b_-^{-5}(C^{\rm ref}+Y_0^*)$. By the last assertion of Prop.~\ref{lh:blk}(d), in the setting at hand, $P''(d\beta)\ge[\hat n(\beta)-871C^{\rm ref}\beta^{-5}]d\beta$ on $(Lb_-,\infty)$, which contains $L^K(b_-,b_+)$ for every $K\ge1$; so $\mathbb M\ge-871C^{\rm ref}ds$ on $(\log(Lb_-),\infty)$, and, as $ds=db/b$, $b^{-4}\mathbb M_K(db)\ge-871C^{\rm ref}b_-^{-5}db$ on $(b_-,b_+)$. So $u_K''\ge-C_{\rm sc}\,\mathrm{d}b$ with $C_{\rm sc}=b_-^{-5}(871C^{\rm ref}+C^{\rm ref}+Y_0^*)$, for every $K\ge1$, the numbers $C^{\rm ref}$, $b_-$ and $Y_0^*$ being those of the setting at hand.

As $\log(b+h)-\log b\le h/b_-$, (A)(2) gives $\limsup_K\sup\{|u_K''|([b,b+h]):b_-<b,\ b+h<b_+\}\le C_uh$ for every $h>0$, with $C_u=b_-^{-5}(C+C^{\rm ref}+Y_0^*)$, the upper limit of (A)(2) being over the real $s\to\infty$ and so uniform in $b$. Let $I'=[\alpha,\alpha']\subset(b_-,b_+)$. By the last bound and a covering, $\sup_{K\ge K_1}|u_K''|(I')<\infty$ for some $K_1$; the mean of $u_K'$ over $I'$ is $(u_K(\alpha')-u_K(\alpha))/|I'|$, of modulus at most $3C_{\rm v}/|I'|$, and $u_K'(\cdot\pm)$ differs from it by at most $|u_K''|(I')$; so the $u_K$, $K\ge K_1$, are bounded and have one Lipschitz constant on $I'$. The theorem of Arzel\`a and Ascoli and a diagonal sequence give the subsequence.

For $b,b+h\in I'$, $|u_K'(b\pm)-h^{-1}(u_K(b+h)-u_K(b))|\le|u_K''|([b,b+h])$; so along the subsequence $\limsup_{K,K'}\sup_{I'}|u_K'(\cdot\pm)-u_{K'}'(\cdot\pm)|\le2C_uh$ for every $h>0$: the one-sided derivatives converge uniformly on $I'$ to a function $w$, $u(b')-u(b)=\int_b^{b'}w$, and $|w(b')-w(b)|\le\limsup_K|u_K''|([b,b'])\le C_u|b'-b|$; so $u'=w$. The other properties pass to uniform limits. Last, by Lem.~\ref{lh:lat}(b) on $\mathbb L_K$, $\nu(\mathcal O_K(f))=3a^{-4}e_\nu r_K(f)$ with $-3e_\nu\in[P'(\beta-),P'(\beta+)]$; the torus measure $\tilde\mu=\tilde\mu_{K,\ell_0,\beta}$ is invariant under the isometries of $\mathbb L_K$, so $\tilde\mu(\mathcal O_K(f))=3a^{-4}e_*r_K(f)$ with $-3e_*=P_{N_0}'(\beta)$; subtract.

\emph{Step 4: (E).} (i) Let first $b'\ge\max\{\gamma^{-2},e^{\mathsf Y^\natural}\}$ and $M\mathcal R(b'')\le L^m$. Discarding (Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{115.2}{806}}, its lost-mass and cumulant bounds) holds with any number $\epsilon_{\rm R}$ that bounds the lost mass, $\sum_{h:Z_t(h)\ne\emptyset}\mathsf t(h)\le\epsilon_{\rm R}Z$, in the place of the bound on the lost mass that its statement takes from the definitions preceding Prop.~\YMMref{115.2}{806}: if $\epsilon_{\rm R}\le\frac12$, then the generating function $T$ of the kept histories is entire, $T(0)\ge\frac12Z$, and
\[
|S^T_{n;K,\ell,\beta}(\underline f)-\partial_z^n\log T(0)|\le4\,\mathsf{op}_n\epsilon_{\rm R}\prod_i6\ell^3L^{4K}\|f_i\|_\infty .
\]
Indeed, with the bare density $\rho_0$ and the weight $\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}_t\ge0$ of the definitions preceding Prop.~\YMMref{115.2}{806}, $\mathsf\Lambda(F)=\int F\rho_0\,\mathrm{d}U$ and $\mathsf\Lambda'(F)=\int F\,\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}_t\rho_0\,\mathrm{d}U$ are positive functionals on the gauge-invariant bounded Borel functions, $\mathsf\Lambda-\mathsf\Lambda'$ is positive by Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{115.2}{806}}, its positive-domination inequality, $\mathsf\Lambda(1)=Z$, and $T(z)=\mathsf\Lambda'(e^{\sum_iz_i\mathcal O_K(f_i)})$. The proof of equation~\YMMref{(2190)}{806} first bounds the lost mass by the sum of the histories with $Z_t(h)\ne\emptyset$, before estimating that sum. It therefore gives $\mathsf\Lambda(1)-\mathsf\Lambda'(1)\le\epsilon_{\rm R}\mathsf\Lambda(1)$; and the statement on two nearby positive functionals and their cumulants ({\cite[Lem.~K.2]{YMM2}}, with $|\mathcal O_K(f_i)|\le6\ell^3L^{4K}\|f_i\|_\infty$) gives $T(0)=\mathsf\Lambda'(1)\ge\frac12Z$ and the display, the cumulants of $\mathsf\Lambda$ and of $\mathsf\Lambda'$ being $S^T_{n;K,\ell,\beta}(\underline f)$ and $\partial^n_z\log T(0)$.

These are the last two steps of the proof of Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{115.2}{806}}, made with $\epsilon_{\rm R}$ in the place of that bound. The proof of Thm.~\YMMref{AR}{810} (the comparison of the cutoffs $K$ and $K+1$, with its three lemmas) uses of the bound $\epsilon_{\rm R}$ only these two facts, that it bounds the lost mass and that it is at most $\frac12$. Its error terms are of three kinds: terms exponentially small in $K$ times $N_{[d]}=\ell^3L^{3d}$ at depths $d\le K/9+1$; the term $8\,\mathsf{op}_n\epsilon_{\rm R}\prod_i6\ell^3L^{4(K+1)}\|f_i\|_\infty$; and, for $n\ge2$ and spread $\mathsf d$, a contact term at most $c\,\ell^3L^{3u}e^{-\mathsf dL^u/M}$, with the depth $u=\lceil K/180(3n+4)\rceil$.

The bound on the lost mass with which the thresholds of Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AS}{813}} are formed carries a factor $e^{{\rm const}\,\ell^3}$. We take instead $\epsilon_{\rm R}=\mathsf R_{t_1}$ of Lem.~\ref{lh:lost} at the level $t_1=K-u$: since $\log(L^ub)\ge u\lambda\ge K\lambda/180(3n+4)$ and $2\mathfrak p_0\ge2$, $\mathsf R_{t_1}\le c\,\ell^3L^{3u}e^{-c''K^{2\mathfrak p_0}}$, which beats the factor $\ell^3$ and the products of the crude bound. The most demanding of the remaining conditions is $\ell^3L^{-K/18}\le c$. Hence there is an integer $k_\flat$, free of $m$, $\ell$ and $K$, such that for $K\ge k_\flat+54m$ all conditions hold and
\[
|S_{K+1}-S_K|\le C_n\ell^{3(n+1)}K^{\mathsf p_n}L^{-K/10}\Pi .
\]
Summing over the cutoffs, with $C_n\sum_{k\ge K}k^{\mathsf p_n}L^{-k/10}\le C_n'K^{\mathsf p_n}L^{-K/10}$, which defines $C'_n$, gives (a) with $k_\flat$ and $C'_n$ in this range. For $K\le k_\flat+54m$ the crude bound and $L^{4n(k_\flat+54m)}\le L^{4nk_\flat}\ell^{216n}$ give $|S_K|\le\mathsf{op}_n6^nL^{4nk_\flat}\ell^{219n}\Pi$, and for larger $K$ (a) compares $S_K$ with $S_{k_\flat+54m}$; this gives (b) with $C^{\rm pol}_n=\mathsf{op}_n6^nL^{4nk_\flat}+C'_n\sup_kk^{\mathsf p_n}L^{-k/10}$, as $3(n+1)\le219n$. (ii) Let $\jmath\ge0$ be the least integer with $L^\jmath\ge\max\{\gamma^{-2}/b',e^{\mathsf Y^\natural}/b',b''\}$ and $L^{\jmath/2}\ge M(4r/e)^r$. For $K>\jmath$, Lem.~\YMMref{118.2}{813} gives, with $f^{(\jmath)}=f(L^{-\jmath}\cdot)$,
\[
S^T_{n;K,\ell,L^Kb}(\underline f)=L^{\jmath n}S^T_{n;K-\jmath,L^\jmath\ell,L^{K-\jmath}(L^\jmath b)}(\underline f^{(\jmath)}):
\]
both members are cumulants of the same variables on the same periodic cube with $\ell L^K$ sites a side, since $\mathcal O_K(f)=L^\jmath\mathcal O_{K-\jmath}(f^{(\jmath)})$ under the dilation by $L^\jmath$. The dilation keeps the supremum, divides the Lipschitz constant by $L^\jmath$ and multiplies the spread by $L^\jmath$, so $\|f^{(\jmath)}\|_\sharp\le\|f\|_\sharp$. The window $L^\jmath[b',b'']$ lies above both floors; and as $\mathcal R(x)<L(\log x)^r$, $\log(L^\jmath b'')\le2\jmath\lambda$ and $(2\jmath\lambda)^r\le(4r/e)^rL^{\jmath/2}$, the sides $2L^{m+\jmath}$, $m\ge1$, satisfy $M\mathcal R(L^\jmath b'')\le L^{m+\jmath}$. So (i) applies on the dilated data, with numbers $k_{\flat,\jmath}$, $C'_{n,\jmath}$, $C^{\rm pol}_{n,\jmath}$; as $n+3(n+1)+\frac1{10}\le4n+4$ and $K-\jmath\ge k_{\flat,\jmath}+54(m+\jmath)$ for $K\ge k_{\flat,\jmath}+55\jmath+54m$, this gives (a) with $k^{\rm rt}=k_{\flat,\jmath}+55\jmath$ and $C^{\rm rt}=L^{\jmath(4n+4)}C'_{n,\jmath}$, and $|S_K|\le L^{220n\jmath}C^{\rm pol}_{n,\jmath}\ell^{219n}\Pi$ for $K>\jmath$.

For $1\le K\le\jmath$ the crude bound gives $|S_K|\le\mathsf{op}_n6^nL^{4n\jmath}\ell^{3n}\Pi$; so (b) holds with $C^{\rm pol}=\max\{L^{220n\jmath}C^{\rm pol}_{n,\jmath},\mathsf{op}_n6^nL^{4n\jmath}\}$. (c): $A>30(n+1)\ge90>54$, so (a) applies for $K\ge k^{\rm rt}+Am$, and $m\le K/A$ gives $\ell^{3(n+1)}\le2^{3(n+1)}L^{3(n+1)K/A}$. (d): $K\ge C\log\ell$ with $C\ge54/\lambda+k^{\rm rt}/\log2$ gives $K\ge54m+k^{\rm rt}$, as $\log\ell\ge\log2$ and $\log\ell=\log2+m\lambda$; with $C\ge11$, $\frac1{10}-\frac1C\ge\frac1{110}$ and $K^{\mathsf p_2}L^{-K/110}\le(110\mathsf p_2/e\lambda)^{\mathsf p_2}$, so (a) gives the first bound, as $\ell^9\le\ell^{438}$; (b) gives the second.

\emph{Step 5: the far part beyond $k^{\rm rt}+Am$.} In a setting apply (E)(a) at $n=2$ to $\varsigma$ and a lowered choice $\varsigma'$, with $[b',b'']=\mathsf I$, $\mathsf d=\varepsilon$ and the pair of Step~2. With $(40\sqrt3ML)^2=4800M^2L^2$, for all $m\in\mathbb N$, $\upsilon\in\log\mathsf I$ and $K'\ge K\ge k^{\rm rt}+54m$,
\begin{equation}\label{lh:osc}
|y_{m,K'}(\upsilon)-y_{m,K}(\upsilon)|\le c_{\rm y}\ell^9K^{\mathsf p_2}L^{-K/10},\qquad c_{\rm y}=4800b_+^5M^2L^5C^{\rm rt}.
\end{equation}
For real $A>90$ and $K,K'\ge k^{\rm rt}+Am$ we have $\ell^9=2^9L^{9m}\le2^9L^{9K/A}$ and $\frac1{10}>\frac9A$; so
\[
\sup_{\log\mathsf I}|y_{m,K}-y_{m,K'}|\le\omega_A=2^9c_{\rm y}\sup_{k\ge1}k^{\mathsf p_2}L^{-(\frac1{10}-\frac9A)k}<\infty .
\]
This is the oscillation hypothesis of Prop.~\ref{lh:per}(b) with the slope $A$; and $\frac1{10}>\frac9A$ holds exactly for $A>90$. With it, $\sup_K\sup_{\log\mathsf I}|y_{m,K}|<\infty$ at each $m$, the finitely many cutoffs below the threshold being bounded one by one. (B) uses (E) here and nowhere else.

\emph{Step 6: (B).} Enter in Prop.~\ref{lh:per}(b) with the data of Step~1, $\mathsf a_i=k^{\rm rt}_i$, $A_i=A$ and $\omega_i=\omega_{A,i}$ of Step~5 at $(\varsigma_i,\varsigma'_i)$. At each single $(m,K)$, by \eqref{lh:far} and Lem.~\ref{lh:lat}(c), $|y_{m,K}|\le\beta^5(P_N''+|n_{\eta_K}(\mu_{N,\beta})|)\le(L^Kb_+)^5(9N^3+1125\eta_K^3)$. This gives (B)(1) with the constants
\begin{align}
&\begin{gathered}
k^0=\max\{k_1,\lceil k^{\rm rt}_1+Am_{0,1}\rceil\},\qquad\\
 Y^0\le(L_1^{k^0}b_{+,1})^5\bigl(72L_1^{3(m_{0,1}+k^0)}+1125L_1^{3(k^0-1)}\bigr)+\omega_{A,1},
\end{gathered}\label{lh:cst}\\
&\begin{gathered}
\mathsf M_1=(Y^0+C_N+C_{\rm low})\varkappa_1+c_{{\rm P},1}L_1^{-m_{0,1}}\bigl(15/\varkappa_1+14+12\varkappa_1\bigr),\qquad\\
\mathsf A_0=7\mathsf M_1/\varkappa_1+C_{\rm low}+4C_N+\omega_{A,1}+\omega_{A,2},
\end{gathered}\notag\\
&\begin{gathered}
c_{3,i}=|\log b_{-,i}|+2\varkappa_i+\lambda_i(k_i+k^{\rm rt}_i+1),\qquad\\
 c_6=\max_ic_{{\rm P},i}e^{\lambda_i+c_{3,i}/A},\qquad\\
 T_i(m)=\log b_{-,i}+2\varkappa_i+\lambda_i\max\{k_i,\lceil k^{\rm rt}_i+Am\rceil\},
\end{gathered}\notag\\
&\begin{gathered}
C_{\rm h}=2\mathsf A_0+C_{\rm low}+134,\qquad\\
 C_{\rm r}=(\mathsf A_0+134)c_6^{1/2},\qquad\\
\log\beta_1=\max\{0,T_1(m_{0,1}),T_2(m_{0,2}),A\log^+(4c_6/\varkappa^2)\},
\end{gathered}\notag
\end{align}
since $P$ is the pressure, $J_P=J$, and $|\mathbb M|([s,s+\delta])$ is the integral of (B)(1). (2): for $0<c<\frac1{180}$ take $A=\frac1{2c}>90$; then $\beta^{4+c}J(\beta)\le C_{\rm r}$ for $\beta\ge\beta_1$, and $\beta^{4+c}J\le6\max\{1,\beta_1\}^{4+c}$ on $[1,\beta_1]$; for $c\le0$, $\beta^{4+c}J\le\beta^{4+1/182}J$ on $[1,\infty)$. $c_*(c)$ is defined by $P$ alone. (3): $(\log\beta)^q\beta^{-1/182}$ is bounded on $[3,\infty)$. (4): enter in Prop.~\ref{lh:slope} with the data of Step~1. At $i=1$, Step~5 at $(\varsigma_1,\varsigma'_1)$ gives (i) with $\mathsf a_1=k^{\rm rt}_1$, $A_1=A$ and $\omega_1=\omega_{A,1}$, and $\sup_{K\ge k_1}\sup|y^{(1)}_{m_{0,1},K}|$ is finite, the cutoffs below the threshold being finitely many; at $i=2$, \eqref{lh:one} at $\varsigma_2$ gives (ii) with $\omega_2=1$ for every $m\ge m_{0,2}$, and $\epsilon^{(2)}_m=c_{{\rm P},2}L_2^{-m}\to0$.

Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8} is used at $\varsigma_1$ and $\varsigma'_1$ through (E), and at $\varsigma_2$ through the convergence on each torus. (5): by \eqref{lh:ident} with the data of Step~1 and $G_K=G(\cdot-K\lambda_i)$, which is supported in $\mathsf J_i+K\lambda_i\subset[s_3,\infty)$, $s_3=\log(L_i^Kb_{-,i})\ge\log\beta_1$ (and $K\ge k_i$, as $\beta_1>\beta_0$), $\int G\,y^{(i)}_{m,K}=\langle\mathbb M,G_K\rangle-r$ with $|r|\le c_{{\rm P},i}L_i^{-m}\mathsf Q(G)+C_N\|G\|_1$; by (1), the hypothesis of Prop.~\ref{lh:per}(d) holds with $s_2=\log\beta_1$ and $\epsilon_1(s)=e^{-s/2A}$, and it bounds $|\langle\mathbb M,G_K\rangle|$ by $(C_{\rm h}+C_{\rm r})(\|G\|_1+(L_i^Kb_{-,i})^{-1/2A}\|G'\|_1)$.

\emph{Step 7: (C).} By the dilation, $\rho^{(K)},\nu^{(K)}\in\mathcal G(\beta)$, and $\rho(a_p)=e_{\rho^{(K)}}$; Lem.~\ref{lh:lat}(b) gives $3|e_\rho-e_\nu|\le J(\beta)$, and invariance gives $\nu(\mathcal O_K(f))=3a_K^{-4}e_\nu r_K(f)$. For each of the three orientations the barycentres form a translate of $a_K\mathbb Z^3$, of which at most $(2R/a_K+1)^3$ points lie in $[-R,R]^3$; so $|r_K(f)|\le(2R+a_K)^3\|f\|_\infty$. On $\mathfrak d(g)$, $b=a_K\beta\ge g^{-2}\ge4$, so $\beta\ge1$, and, as $4+c>0$,
\[
a_K^{-4}J(\beta)=b^{-4}\beta^4J(\beta)\le c_*(c)\,b^{-4}\beta^{-c}=c_*(c)\,b^{-4-c}L^{-cK}\le g^{8+2c}c_*(c)L^{-cK}.
\]
The setting is used only to form $\mathfrak d(g)$; $c_*(c)$ is a number of Wilson's action.

\emph{Step 8: (D).} (1) On $\mathfrak d(g)$, $b\ge g^{-2}$ and $\beta=L^Kb\ge L^Kg^{-2}$, so $a_K^{-4}J(\beta)=b^{-4}\beta^4J(\beta)\le g^8\sup_{\beta'\ge L^Kg^{-2}}\beta'^4J(\beta')$, which tends to $0$ by (A)(1); and by (C) with $a_K\le1$ the difference of the one-point functions is at most $a_K^{-4}J(\beta)(2R+1)^3\|f\|_\infty$. (2) At $X=(f)$ a limit in the frame is $\lim_j[\rho_j(\mathcal O_{K_j}(f))-\nu_j(\mathcal O_{K_j}(f))]=0$. (3) Each component is a limit in the frame along the full sequence, with the approximants $\rho_j=\nu_j(\cdot|B_j)$ (Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AP}{780}}); by (2), $0=\sigma_\xi((f))=\mathfrak c_\xi\int f$; take $\int f=1$. As the one-point values of the component vanish, \eqref{lh:rece} with $\rho=\nu'=\rho_j$ and $\nu=\nu_j$ gives $\rho_j(X^{\rho_j}_{K_j})-\rho_j(X^{\nu_j}_{K_j})\to0$, every term with $A\ne\emptyset$ having a factor that tends to $0$ and a factor that converges; so the Gibbs sequence $(K_j,\beta_j,\rho_j)$ converges, with the limit $\sigma_\xi$.

The component clusters with the numbers $C^g$, $r$ (Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AP}{780}}); so for its own canonical decomposition $(\mathsf X',\varpi',(\sigma'_\zeta))$, (Can4) at $q=2$ gives $\int\sigma'_\zeta(X)^2d\varpi'=\lim_{|v|\to\infty}\sigma_\xi(X\cdot\tau_vX)=\sigma_\xi(X)^2=(\int\sigma'_\zeta(X)d\varpi')^2$; so $\zeta\mapsto\sigma'_\zeta(X)$ is constant on the support of $\varpi'$, which is $\mathsf X'$, and the injectivity in (Can3) makes $\mathsf X'$ a point. This argument used of (A) only that $\mathfrak c_\xi=0$; conversely, a limit of a convergent Gibbs sequence $(K_j,\beta_j,\rho'_j)$ has the one-point values $\lim_j\rho'_j((f)^{\rho'_j}_{K_j})=0$, so $\mathfrak c_\xi=0$; this is the equivalence. (4) The one-point values vanish; with (Can4) at $q=1$ and the clustering of the components,
\[
S^\sigma_2(f,\tau_vh)=\sigma((f)\cdot\tau_v(h))=\int\sigma_\xi((f)\cdot\tau_v(h))\,\mathrm{d}\varpi,\qquad|\sigma_\xi((f)\cdot\tau_v(h))|\le C^g((f),(h))/|v| .
\]

\emph{Step 9: (F).} (1) By Prop.~\YMMref{106.3}{765}, $\mathcal G_{K,\beta}$ satisfies the hypotheses of Lem.~\ref{lh:cond}, and by Lem.~\ref{lh:lat}(b) on $\mathbb L_K$, $-3e_+=P'(\beta-)$, $-3e_-=P'(\beta+)$ and $e_+-e_-=\frac13J(\beta)$. (2) The clustering inequality of the plateau theorem at $X=(f)$, $Y=(h)$ compares $\sigma_\nu((f)\cdot\tau_v(h))=S^T_2[\nu](f,\tau_vh)$ with $\nu(E_\nu[(f)^\nu_K|\mathcal I]\,E_\nu[(h)^\nu_K|\mathcal I])$, which is $9a_K^{-8}r_K(f)r_K(h)\operatorname{Var}_\nu\mathsf e$ by Lem.~\ref{lh:cond}(b), since $\nu(\mathsf e)=e_\nu$; and $\operatorname{Var}_\nu\mathsf e\le\frac14(J/3)^2$; the last bound is (C). (3) $\nu_\pm$ exist by Lem.~\ref{lh:lat}(b) on $\mathbb L_K$. By Lem.~\ref{lh:cond}(d), $\mathsf e$ is almost surely constant in $\nu_\pm$, in every $\nu$ with $-3e_\nu$ at an end of the interval, and in a pure phase, which is ergodic. For $\nu=\frac12(\nu_++\nu_-)$, which lies in the convex set $\mathcal G_{K,\beta}$, and bounded $F,F'$,
\[
\operatorname{Cov}_\nu(F,F')=\tfrac12\operatorname{Cov}_{\nu_+}(F,F')+\tfrac12\operatorname{Cov}_{\nu_-}(F,F')+\tfrac14\bigl(\nu_+(F)-\nu_-(F)\bigr)\bigl(\nu_+(F')-\nu_-(F')\bigr).
\]
Take $F=\mathcal O_K(f)$ and $F'=\mathcal O_K(\tau_vf)$, $v\in a_K\mathbb Z^3$, with $0\le f\in C^1_c((-\frac12,\frac12)^3)$ and $r_K(f)>0$, for which (2) applies at $\bar R=1$. Then $\nu_+(F)-\nu_-(F)=3a_K^{-4}r_K(f)(e_{\nu_+}-e_{\nu_-})=-a_K^{-4}J(\beta)r_K(f)$, the same for $F'$, as $r_K(\tau_vf)=r_K(f)$; (2) in the three states, with $|v|\to\infty$, gives $9a_K^{-8}r_K(f)^2\operatorname{Var}_\nu\mathsf e=\frac14(a_K^{-4}J(\beta)r_K(f))^2$. (4) Prop.~\ref{lh:many} with $\mathcal G=\mathcal G_{K,\beta}$; $X^\nu_K$ is a real continuous local function, a polynomial in finitely many $a_p$, and by Lem.~\ref{lh:lat}(b) every $\rho\in\mathcal G_{K,\beta}$ has $D^-\bar p^F(0)\le\rho(F)\le D^+\bar p^F(0)$ for such $F$; at $X=(f)$, $3a_K^{-4}|r_K(f)|(e_+-e_-)=a_K^{-4}J(\beta)|r_K(f)|$.

\emph{Step 10: (G) in a window.} Let $g^{-2}+\bar B<b<X_g-\bar B$ for some $0<g\le\gamma$. From some index on $a_{K_j}\beta_j\in I(g)$, so $(K_j,\beta_j)\in\mathfrak d(g)$; we drop the first members, which changes no set of limits. Let $\mathsf S_j=\{\sigma_\nu:\nu\in\mathcal G_{K_j,\beta_j}\}\subset\mathcal E^g$ and fix a metric of $\mathcal E^g$.

(1) $\mathsf K=\{\sigma\in\mathcal E^g:\operatorname{dist}(\sigma,\mathsf S_j)\to0\}$, a closed subset of the compact metrisable space $\mathcal E^g$ (Lem.~\ref{lh:rec}(b)). Convexity: if $\sigma^i=\lim_j\sigma_{\nu^i_j}$ and $\nu_j=t\nu^1_j+(1-t)\nu^2_j\in\mathcal G_{K_j,\beta_j}$, then
\[
\sigma_{\nu_j}(X)=t\,\nu^1_j(X^{\nu_j}_{K_j})+(1-t)\,\nu^2_j(X^{\nu_j}_{K_j}),
\]
and by \eqref{lh:rece} with the centrings $\nu^i_j$ and $\nu_j$ each bracket is at most $a_{K_j}^{-4}J(\beta_j)(2R+1)^3\|f\|_\infty\to0$ by (D)(1), while the moments $\nu^i_j((X_A)^{\nu^i_j}_{K_j})$ converge; so $\sigma_{\nu_j}\to t\sigma^1+(1-t)\sigma^2$.

(2) $(K_j,\beta_j,\nu_j)_j$ is a convergent Gibbs sequence at $g$; by (D)(3) each component is $\lim_j\sigma_{\nu_j(\cdot|B_j)}$ and has one vacuum. Components cluster at the rate $C^g(X,Y)/|v|$. A member of $\mathsf K$ that clusters, in the sense $\sigma(X\cdot\tau_vX)\to\sigma(X)^2$ for all $X$, has one vacuum, by (Can4) at $q=2$ as in Step~8; conversely, a member with one vacuum is its own component and clusters at the rate $C^g/|v|$. As $C^g$ and $r$ do not depend on the member, pointwise limits of members of $\mathsf K^\bullet$ cluster: $\mathsf K^\bullet$ is closed in $\mathsf K$, so compact.

(3) Barycentres of measures on $\mathsf K^\bullet$ lie in $\mathsf K$: for finite supports by (1), and in general by Riemann sums, the uniform continuity of $\psi\mapsto\psi(X)$ on the compact $\mathsf K^\bullet$, and the closedness of $\mathsf K$. Onto: for $\sigma\in\mathsf K$ the image of $\varpi$ under $\xi\mapsto\sigma_\xi$ is a measure on $\mathsf K^\bullet$ by (2), with the barycentre $\sigma$ by (Can4) at $q=1$. Injective: Lem.~\ref{lh:rec}(c) with $\mathsf T=\mathsf K^\bullet$. A continuous bijection of the compact $\mathrm{Prob}(\mathsf K^\bullet)$ onto the Hausdorff space $\mathsf K$ is a homeomorphism; by injectivity the image of $\varpi$ is $\mu_\sigma$; $\xi\mapsto\sigma_\xi$ is continuous and injective on the compact $\mathsf X$, and its image is the support of $\mu_\sigma$, $\varpi$ having full support. $\dim\ker H_\sigma=\#\mathsf X=\#\operatorname{supp}\mu_\sigma$ by Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AP}{780}}.

(4) One vacuum is $\ker H_\sigma=\mathbb C\Omega_\sigma$ by $\#\mathsf X=\dim\ker H_\sigma$, in each of the six directions. By (3), the extreme points of $\mathsf K$ are the barycentres of the extreme points of $\mathrm{Prob}(\mathsf K^\bullet)$, the point masses: extreme points are the members with one vacuum. The two forms of clustering are (2). \emph{Pure phases.} If $\sigma=\lim_j\sigma_{\omega_j}$ with pure phases $\omega_j$, each $\omega_j$ is ergodic, so $E_{\omega_j}[\cdot\,|\mathcal I]$ is almost surely constant, and by the statement on iterated plateaux $\int\sigma_\xi(X)^2d\varpi-\sigma(X)^2=\lim_j\operatorname{Var}_{\omega_j}(E_{\omega_j}[X^{\omega_j}_{K_j}|\mathcal I])=0$ for every $X$; so $\xi\mapsto\sigma_\xi(X)$ is constant on $\mathsf X$, and $\mathsf X$ is a point.

Conversely, let $\sigma\in\mathsf K^\bullet$ be the limit of $\sigma_{\nu_j}$. By the variance statement below, $E_{\nu_j}[X^{\nu_j}_{K_j}|\mathcal I]\to\sigma(X)$ in $L^2(\nu_j)$ for every $X$. Let $(\nu_j^U)_U$ be a regular conditional law of $\nu_j$ given $\mathcal I$; by Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{106.1}{764}} its members are, off a $\nu_j$-null set, pure phases in $\mathcal G_{K_j,\beta_j}$, and $\nu_j^U(X^{\nu_j}_{K_j})=E_{\nu_j}[X^{\nu_j}_{K_j}|\mathcal I](U)$ for $\nu_j$-almost every $U$. Take a countable family $X_1,X_2,\dots$ of tuples on which pointwise convergence in $\mathcal E^g$ implies convergence at every tuple (Lem.~\ref{lh:rec}(b)). By Chebyshev's inequality there are, for each $j$, a point $U_j$ outside the null sets and numbers $\epsilon_j\to0$, $k_j\to\infty$ with $|\nu_j^{U_j}((X_k)^{\nu_j}_{K_j})-\sigma(X_k)|\le\epsilon_j$ for $k\le k_j$.

The pure phases $\omega_j=\nu_j^{U_j}$ then have $\omega_j((X_k)^{\nu_j}_{K_j})\to\sigma(X_k)$ for every $k$; by \eqref{lh:rece} and (D)(1), $\sigma_{\omega_j}(X_k)\to\sigma(X_k)$; and as $\sigma_{\omega_j}\in\mathcal E^g$, $\sigma_{\omega_j}\to\sigma$. \emph{Variances.} By the statement on iterated plateaux, $\operatorname{Var}_{\nu_j}(E_{\nu_j}[X^{\nu_j}_{K_j}|\mathcal I])\to\int\sigma_\xi(X)^2d\varpi-\sigma(X)^2$, which does not depend on the choice of the $\nu_j$, and which vanishes for every $X$ if and only if $\mathsf X$ is a point. \emph{Faces.} For a subsequence $\mathfrak p'$, $\mathsf K\subset\mathsf K_{\mathfrak p'}$. If $\sigma\in\mathsf K$ is $t\sigma_1+(1-t)\sigma_2$ with $\sigma_i\in\mathsf K_{\mathfrak p'}$, $0<t<1$, the uniqueness of the representing measure on ${\rm Lim}^\bullet[b]$ (Lem.~\ref{lh:rec}(c), with the compact set ${\rm Lim}^\bullet[b]$ of (6)) gives $\mu_\sigma=t\mu_{\sigma_1}+(1-t)\mu_{\sigma_2}$; so the $\mu_{\sigma_i}$ live on $\operatorname{supp}\mu_\sigma\subset\mathsf K^\bullet$, and $\sigma_i\in\mathsf K$ by (3).

For the interlacing $\mathfrak p''$, $\mathsf K_{\mathfrak p''}\subset\mathsf K\cap\mathsf K_{\tilde{\mathfrak p}}$, as $\mathfrak p$ and $\tilde{\mathfrak p}$ are subsequences of $\mathfrak p''$; conversely, two Gibbs sequences that converge to $\sigma$ along $\mathfrak p$ and along $\tilde{\mathfrak p}$ interlace to one that converges to $\sigma$ along $\mathfrak p''$. \emph{One point.} Let $\mathsf K\ne\emptyset$. If $\mathsf K$ is a point, $\mathsf K^\bullet$ is not empty, as it holds the components of that point, and lies in $\mathsf K$; if $\mathsf K^\bullet$ is a point, so is $\mathrm{Prob}(\mathsf K^\bullet)$ and hence $\mathsf K$; if $\mathsf K$ is a point, $\mathsf K=\mathsf K^\bullet$; if $\mathsf K=\mathsf K^\bullet$ had two members $\sigma_1\ne\sigma_2$, then $\frac12(\sigma_1+\sigma_2)\in\mathsf K=\mathsf K^\bullet$ would be an extreme point.

By the statement on iterated plateaux, $\operatorname{Cov}_{\nu_j}(E_{\nu_j}[X^{\nu_j}_{K_j}|\mathcal I],E_{\nu_j}[Y^{\nu_j}_{K_j}|\mathcal I])\to\int\sigma_\xi(X)\sigma_\xi(Y)d\varpi-\sigma(X)\sigma(Y)$, which vanishes for all $X,Y$ if and only if $\mathsf X$ is a point; for all convergent choices this says $\mathsf K=\mathsf K^\bullet$. At single fields, Lem.~\ref{lh:cond}(b) and (F)(2) give the displayed bound, with $|r_K(f)|\le(2R+1)^3\|f\|_\infty$, and it tends to $0$ by (D)(1).

(6) The pairs $(K,L^Kb)$, $K\in\mathbb N$, lie in $\mathfrak d(g)$; as $\mathcal E^g$ is compact, a subsequence of $(\sigma_{\nu_K})$ converges, so ${\rm Lim}[b]\ne\emptyset$. ${\rm Lim}[b]=\bigcap_k\overline{\bigcup\{\mathsf S_{K,\beta}:K\ge k,\ |a_K\beta-b|\le\frac1k\}}$, with $\mathsf S_{K,\beta}=\{\sigma_\nu:\nu\in\mathcal G_{K,\beta}\}$, is compact, and ${\rm Lim}^\bullet[b]$ is closed in it by the uniform clustering. A saturated subsequence: with a countable base $(U_r)$ of $\mathcal E^g$, pass to nested subsequences along which, for each $r$, $\mathsf S_j\cap U_r$ is either non-empty for all members or empty for all members, and take the diagonal; for it and for each of its subsequences a functional is a limit if and only if each $U_r$ that holds it meets $\mathsf S_j$ for all large $j$, so all these sets of limits agree, and they are not empty by compactness. Every $\sigma\in\mathsf K_{\mathfrak p}$ lies in $\mathsf K_{\mathfrak p'}$ for a saturated subsequence $\mathfrak p'$, and the extreme points are the members with one vacuum by (4); this gives the two unions. Uniqueness of the representing measure on ${\rm Lim}^\bullet[b]$: Lem.~\ref{lh:rec}(c) with $\mathsf T={\rm Lim}^\bullet[b]$; existence: (3).

\emph{The hull.} ${\rm Lim}^\bullet[b]$ is compact and its members cluster uniformly, with the numbers $C^g$, $r$; so by Lem.~\ref{lh:rec}(c) the map $\operatorname{bar}$ is affine, continuous and injective on the compact convex set $\mathrm{Prob}({\rm Lim}^\bullet[b])$, hence an affine homeomorphism onto its image, a compact convex set. The image contains ${\rm Lim}[b]$, by the existence just shown, and it is the closure of the image of the finitely supported measures, which is the convex hull of ${\rm Lim}^\bullet[b]\subset{\rm Lim}[b]$; so it is $\overline{\rm co}\,{\rm Lim}[b]$. Its extreme points are the images of the point masses, that is, the members of ${\rm Lim}^\bullet[b]$. Hence a member of ${\rm Lim}[b]$ with one vacuum is an extreme point of $\overline{\rm co}\,{\rm Lim}[b]$, and so of ${\rm Lim}[b]$; and a member $\sigma$ that is an extreme point of ${\rm Lim}[b]$ is an extreme point of every $\mathsf K_{\mathfrak p}$ that contains it, so it has one vacuum by (4).

\emph{Convexity.} If ${\rm Lim}[b]=\mathsf K_{\mathfrak q}$, it is convex by (1). If ${\rm Lim}[b]$ is convex, it is compact and convex, so it equals $\overline{\rm co}\,{\rm Lim}[b]=\operatorname{bar}(\mathrm{Prob}({\rm Lim}^\bullet[b]))$. If this equality holds and $\psi_1,\dots,\psi_n\in{\rm Lim}^\bullet[b]$, then $\frac1n\sum_i\psi_i$ lies in some $\mathsf K_{\mathfrak p}$; by (3) it is the barycentre of a measure on $\mathsf K^\bullet_{\mathfrak p}$, which by the uniqueness on ${\rm Lim}^\bullet[b]$ is $\frac1n\sum_i\delta_{\psi_i}$, so that $\psi_1,\dots,\psi_n\in\mathsf K^\bullet_{\mathfrak p}$. If every finite subset of ${\rm Lim}^\bullet[b]$ lies in one $\mathsf K^\bullet_{\mathfrak p}$, let $\psi_1,\psi_2,\dots$ be dense in ${\rm Lim}^\bullet[b]$ and $\psi_1,\dots,\psi_n\in\mathsf K^\bullet_{\mathfrak p_n}$; for each $n$ there is a pair $(K'_n,\beta'_n)$ of $\mathfrak p_n$ with $K'_n\ge n$ and $|a_{K'_n}\beta'_n-b|\le\frac1n$ which carries, for each $i\le n$, a state $\nu$ with $\operatorname{dist}(\sigma_\nu,\psi_i)\le\frac1n$.

Along $\mathfrak q=(K'_n,\beta'_n)_n$, a sequence of pairs at the label $b$, every $\psi_i$ is a limit; so the closed set $\mathsf K_{\mathfrak q}$ contains ${\rm Lim}^\bullet[b]$, and by (3) for $\mathfrak q$ it contains $\operatorname{bar}(\mathrm{Prob}({\rm Lim}^\bullet[b]))\supset{\rm Lim}[b]\supset\mathsf K_{\mathfrak q}$. Finally, a set with one element is convex.

(5) Every $\sigma\in{\rm Lim}[b]$ lies in some $\mathsf K_{\mathfrak q}$; its components lie in $\mathsf K^\bullet_{\mathfrak q}\subset{\rm Lim}^\bullet[b]$, and $\sigma=\int\sigma_\xi\,\mathrm{d}\varpi$. If ${\rm Lim}^\bullet[b]=\{\tau\}$, all components are $\tau$ and $\sigma=\tau$; if ${\rm Lim}[b]=\{\sigma\}$, then ${\rm Lim}^\bullet[b]$ is not empty by (6) and lies in $\{\sigma\}$. The same lines serve for ${\rm Lim}_{\mathfrak q}[b]$, the components of a limit along pairs of $\mathfrak q$ being limits along the same pairs, and ${\rm Lim}_{\mathfrak q}[b]$ being non-empty by (6) applied to a sequence with pairs in $\mathfrak q$. For the third statement: a Gibbs sequence at $g$ with the label $b$ has convergent subsequences (Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AP}{780}}), whose limits lie in ${\rm Lim}[b]$; if this is one point, every subsequence has a subsequence that converges to it, so the sequence converges; conversely, interlacing two convergent Gibbs sequences with the label $b$ gives one, which converges, so their limits agree. The one limit then has one vacuum, as ${\rm Lim}^\bullet[b]\ne\emptyset$.

The clauses (1)--(4) use of (A) only that $a_{K_j}^{-4}J(\beta_j)\to0$ along $\mathfrak p$. Along $\mathfrak p=(K,L^Kb)_K$ this holds without (A) for every $b$ outside the countable set $\bigcup_KL^{-K}\{\beta:J(\beta)>0\}$, as the convex function $P$ is differentiable off a countable set; at such labels these clauses use Thms.~\YMMref{D}{8}, \YMMref{AJ}{673} and~\YMMref{AD}{607} at the choice of the setting alone.

\emph{Step 11: (G) at every label.} For $z\in\mathbb Z$ put, as in the paragraph on dilations, $X^{[z]}=(f_i(L^z\cdot))_i$ and $\sigma^{[z]}(X)=L^{-z|X|}\sigma(X^{[z]})$. The dilation $x\mapsto L^zx$ carries a law $\nu$ on $\mathbb L_K$ to a law $\nu^{(z)}$ on $\mathbb L_{K-z}$, maps $\mathcal G_{K,\beta}$ onto $\mathcal G_{K-z,\beta}$ and conditioned states to conditioned states, as it carries the invariant events to the invariant events ({\cite[Lem.~K.1]{YMM2}}), and turns $\mathcal O_{K-z}(f)$ into $L^{-z}\mathcal O_K(f(L^z\cdot))$ ({\cite[Lem.~K.1]{YMM2}}, applied to the function $f(L^z\cdot)$); so
\[
\sigma_{\nu^{(z)}}=(\sigma_\nu)^{[z]},\qquad a_{K-z}^{-4}J(\beta)=L^{-4z}a_K^{-4}J(\beta).
\]
So $\sigma\mapsto\sigma^{[z]}$ is a linear homeomorphism that carries $\mathsf K_{\mathfrak p}$, ${\rm Lim}[b]$, ${\rm Lim}^\bullet[b]$ onto the same sets at the label $L^zb$ for the pairs $(K_j-z,\beta_j)$, and canonical decompositions to canonical decompositions, component by component, with the same space $\mathsf X$. It carries the reconstruction as well. Let $(z,g)$ be a pair for $b$, that is, $z\in\mathbb Z$ and $0<g\le\gamma$ with $g^{-2}+\bar B<L^zb<X_g-\bar B$; the pair fixed for $b$ in the paragraph on dilations is one, with $z\ge0$. For $\sigma\in\mathsf K_{\mathfrak p}$, $\sigma^{[z]}$ is then, as in that paragraph, the limit of a convergent Gibbs sequence at $g$ over the pairs $(K_j-z,\beta_j)$ of large index, and Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AP}{780}} gives its reconstruction, with the Hamiltonian $H_{\sigma^{[z]}}$ and the vacuum vector $\Omega_{\sigma^{[z]}}$, in each of the six coordinate directions.

For a coordinate direction $u$, the reflection $\theta$ in the plane $\{x\cdot u=0\}$ commutes with the dilation, so that $\sigma^{[z]}(\theta X\cdot Y)=L^{-z(|X|+|Y|)}\sigma(\theta X^{[z]}\cdot Y^{[z]})$ for the tuples $X$, $Y$ in the half space $\{x\cdot u>0\}$; hence the form $\langle[X],[Y]\rangle_\sigma=\sigma(\theta X\cdot Y)$ is positive together with that of $\sigma^{[z]}$, and $W:[X]\mapsto L^{-z|X|}[X^{[z]}]$ is a unitary map of the space of the reconstruction of $\sigma^{[z]}$ onto the space that this form builds from $\sigma$, with $W[\emptyset]=[\emptyset]$. As $(\tau_vX)^{[z]}=\tau_{L^{-z}v}X^{[z]}$, $W$ carries the translations by $tu$ to the translations by $L^{-z}tu$; so, with $\hat H_\sigma$ the generator of the semigroup $e^{-t\hat H_\sigma}[X]=[\tau_{tu}X]$, $t\ge0$, in the space that the form builds from $\sigma$, $\hat\Omega_\sigma=[\emptyset]$ the class of the empty tuple there, and $e^{-tH_{\sigma^{[z]}}}[X]=[\tau_{tu}X]$, $\Omega_{\sigma^{[z]}}=[\emptyset]$ in the reconstruction of $\sigma^{[z]}$,
\[
H_{\sigma^{[z]}}=L^{-z}\,W^*\hat H_\sigma W,\qquad W\Omega_{\sigma^{[z]}}=\hat\Omega_\sigma,\qquad\ker\hat H_\sigma=W\ker H_{\sigma^{[z]}},
\]
in each of the six directions: the kernels and the vacua correspond. A linear homeomorphism carries convex sets, closed sets, extreme points, faces and one-point sets to the same, and the dilation carries the clustering numbers to dilated ones. For every $b>0$ there are pairs for $b$, already with $z\ge0$, because $L^zb>\gamma^{-2}+\bar B$ for large $z$ and the open intervals $(g^{-2}+\bar B,X_g-\bar B)$ overlap one another as $g$ decreases and cover $(\gamma^{-2}+\bar B,\infty)$. So $W$ carries the operator $L^zH_{\sigma^{[z]}}$ and the vector $\Omega_{\sigma^{[z]}}$, which are $H_\sigma$ and $\Omega_\sigma$ of the paragraph on dilations at the pair $(z,g)$ fixed for $b$, to $\hat H_\sigma$ and $\hat\Omega_\sigma$, the generator of the translations and the class of the empty tuple in the space that the form builds from $\sigma$.

These read no window, so another pair $(z,g)$ gives a unitarily equivalent operator with the corresponding vector, and $\dim\ker H_\sigma=\dim\ker H_{\sigma^{[z]}}=\#\mathsf X$, both finite and equal or both infinite. Step~10 at $(L^zb,(K_j-z,\beta_j))$ gives (1)--(6) at $(b,\mathfrak p)$. In particular the kernel clauses of (3) and (4) pass to $(b,\mathfrak p)$, with $H_\sigma=L^zH_{\sigma^{[z]}}$ and $\Omega_\sigma=\Omega_{\sigma^{[z]}}$ of the paragraph on dilations at the pair $(z,g)$ fixed for $b$: the dilation carries $\mu_\sigma$ to $\mu_{\sigma^{[z]}}$, so that $\dim\ker H_\sigma=\dim\ker H_{\sigma^{[z]}}=\#\mathsf X=\#\operatorname{supp}\mu_\sigma$, and $\ker H_\sigma=\mathbb C\Omega_\sigma$ in one, and then in each, of the six directions if and only if $\sigma$ has one vacuum.

\emph{Step 12: (G)(7).} Let $0<g\le\gamma_W$ and let $\mathfrak p$ be a sequence of pairs in $\mathfrak d(g)$ with $\mathsf K_{\mathfrak p}\ne\emptyset$; $\sigma\in\mathsf K_{\mathfrak p}$ is the limit of a convergent Gibbs sequence over $\mathfrak p$. By Prop.~\YMMref{127.8}{854}, applied with $\rho_j=\nu_j$ (see also Cor.~\textup{\YMMref{127.11}{854}}), along a convergent Gibbs sequence at $g$ the labels $a_{K_j}\beta_j$ converge, to a number $b\in I^{\rm lab}(g)$, and the two-point function of the limit, $S^\sigma_2=\lim_jS^T_2[\nu_j]$, has the displayed limit with this $b$, for every $\vartheta\in(0,1)$ and every pair of $\mathfrak T^1_{\mathbb R^3}(\mathsf d_0(g,\vartheta);\vartheta)$; this set is not empty by {\cite[Lem.~I.1]{YMM2}}(c).

The right member of the formula reads $\sigma$ alone; so the sets ${\rm Lim}_{\mathfrak d(g)}[b]$ are pairwise disjoint, and every convergent Gibbs sequence at $g$ is over a sequence of pairs with a non-empty set of limits, which has a label. An interlacing of two sequences with different labels has no label, so its set of limits is empty. Suppose that $\sigma''=t\sigma+(1-t)\sigma'$, $0<t<1$, with $\sigma\in{\rm Lim}_{\mathfrak d(g)}[b]$, $\sigma'\in{\rm Lim}_{\mathfrak d(g)}[b']$, were the limit of a Gibbs sequence over $\mathfrak p''$; then $\mathfrak p''$ has a label $b''$. The sets of the limits with one vacuum at the labels $b$ and $b'$, along sequences in $\mathfrak d(g)$, are compact, by the diagonal argument of Step~10 (6), and their members cluster uniformly, with the numbers $C^g$, $r$; with the representing measures $\mu_\sigma$, $\mu_{\sigma'}$ of (G)(6), carried by the components of $\sigma$ and of $\sigma'$, Lem.~\ref{lh:rec}(c) makes $(\operatorname{supp}\mu'',\mu'',(\psi))$, $\mu''=t\mu_\sigma+(1-t)\mu_{\sigma'}$, a canonical decomposition of $\sigma''$.

By Cor.~\textup{\YMMref{127.11}{854}}, the formula in every component of every canonical decomposition, each component of $\sigma''$ has the coefficient $b''^{-2}$, whereas the members of $\operatorname{supp}\mu_\sigma$, which are the components of $\sigma$ by (G)(3), have $b^{-2}$, and those of $\operatorname{supp}\mu_{\sigma'}$ have $b'^{-2}$; so $b=b''=b'$. \qed

\begin{proof}[Proof of Thm.~\ref{lh:box}]
(1) is Prop.~\ref{lh:onepair}(c) at $a=a_K$, $\beta=L^Kb$ and $l=l_K=L^{K+m_*}\ge L$, as $K+m_*\ge K_*+m_*\ge1$; that $P$ is differentiable at $\beta$ is $J(\beta)=0$. (2) Let first the entries be none $0$ and their supports lie in $(-\frac{\ell''}4,\frac{\ell''}4)^3$ for a side $\ell''=2L^{m''}\ge\ell_*$, $m''\in\mathbb N$; an entry $0$ makes every cumulant $0$, and every compact set lies in such a cube.
