\begin{lemma}[The third member of the stability chain as a functional of the source]\label{C-365-17}
Let $(K,\beta)\in\mathfrak d(g)$ and $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$. There are a positive $\sigma$-finite measure space $(\Xi,\mathfrak M)$ and functions $\Psi_\varpi$, $\varpi\in\Xi$, on the class of the sources, neither $\Xi$ nor $\mathfrak M$ depending on the source, such that with $h_\varpi=\operatorname{Re}\Psi_\varpi$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(T1)] for every source $w$, $\varpi\mapsto e^{\Psi_\varpi(w)}$ is measurable for the completion of $\mathfrak M$, $\widetilde Z(w)=\int e^{\Psi_\varpi(w)}\,\mathrm{d}\mathfrak M(\varpi)$, and
\[|\widetilde Z(w)|\le\mathsf T(w):=\int e^{h_\varpi(w)}\,\mathrm{d}\mathfrak M(\varpi)\le e^{C_S\ell^3};\]
\item[(T2)] $\mathsf T(u)=\widetilde Z(u)>0$ at every real source $u$;
\item[(T3)] for every $\varpi$ and every finite family $f_1,\dots,f_n$, the map $z\mapsto e^{\Psi_\varpi(\sum_qz_qf_q)}$ is holomorphic and without zeros on the convex open set $\{z:\|\sum_qz_qf_q\|_\sharp<2\varrho\}$; so $z\mapsto h_\varpi(\sum_qz_qf_q)$ is the real part of a holomorphic function there;
\item[(T4)] for real $u$, $v$ there is an $\mathfrak M$-null set, depending on the pair, off which $h_\varpi(u+\bar\zeta v)=h_\varpi(u+\zeta v)$ for all $\zeta$ with $\|u+\zeta v\|_\sharp<2\varrho$; and $(\varpi,z)\mapsto h_\varpi(w(z))$ is jointly measurable.
\end{enumerate}
The functional $\mathsf T$ is the normalized total-variation sum in equation~\YMMref{(1738)}{675}, at $k=K$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof]
Take $k=K$. By Thm.~\YMMref{AJ}{673}, there are finitely
many histories and a common source-independent null set $N_h$
for each history. Outside $N_h$, let $\mathsf D_w$ be its density:
it is zero where $\mathsf{Stay}^{\rm T}_h\chi_K(\Omega_K)=0$
and otherwise equals
$\mathsf{Stay}_h\exp(\boldsymbol\Phi_h^w+A_{K,h}^w)$.
Put $\Xi_h=\{\mathsf D_0\ne0\}$.
This set is the same for all sources, since the tests are unchanged
and an exponential has no zero. On it put
$d\mathfrak M_h=\mathsf{Stay}_h\,\mathrm{d}\mathcal M_h$.
The reference measure is a finite product of Haar and Lebesgue
measures, hence is $\sigma$-finite; multiplication by the
nonnegative finite Borel test factor preserves this property.
Neither this measure nor $\Xi_h$ depends on the source.

Histories with $\mathfrak M_h(\Xi_h)=0$ contribute zero at
every source and may be omitted. Take the disjoint union of the
remaining $\Xi_h$, with measure $\mathfrak M_h$ on each piece, and set
\[
 \Psi_{(h,\phi)}(w)=\boldsymbol\Phi_h^w(\phi)
                   +A_{K,h}^w(\phi)-E_{(K)}^w.
\]
The total variation of $\mathsf D_w\mathcal M_h$ is
$|\mathsf D_w|\mathcal M_h$. Thus the integral of
$e^{\operatorname{Re}\Psi}$ is exactly the normalized
total-variation sum in equation~\YMMref{(1738)}{675}, which proves
the two inequalities in (T1). Without moduli, the history
decomposition in Thm.~\YMMref{AJ}{673} and the vacuum splitting
in equation~\YMMref{(1737)}{675} give
$\int e^{\Psi(w)}d\mathfrak M=e^{-E_{(K)}^w}Z[w]
=\widetilde Z(w)$.

For a real source, the bare density is positive, so each
history measure is positive; the vacuum constant is real by
conjugation. This proves (T2). To prove (T3), fix a history point
and a source-independent evaluation representative, as supplied by
Thm.~\YMMref{AJ}{673}. Every argument in its exponent is fixed
as the source varies. The active action is linear in $w$, and the
regular, boundary and retained terms are finite sums of the
holomorphic families in that theorem. The whole-torus vacuum
constant has the holomorphic finite-sum splitting in
Prop.~\YMMref{83.2}{675}.

The one member that no clause covers, the constant $c_h(w)=\exp(-\mathcal E^w_{K,\mathcal S(h)})$ of the label, which does not depend on $\phi$, is holomorphic as a quotient: on measurable sets $B_n\uparrow\Xi_h$ of finite measure on which the rest $e^{\Psi^\circ_\varpi}$ of the exponential is bounded near $z_0$, the map $z\mapsto\int F_01_{B_n}\,\mathrm{d}\hat\tau^{{\rm co}\prime}_h[\rho^{w(z)}_0]$ is holomorphic by the bare-integral formula and holomorphy assertion of Prop.~\YMMref{73.5}{611}, and it equals $e^{E^{w(z)}_{(K)}}c_h(w(z))I_n(z)$ with $I_n(z)=\int_{B_n}F_0e^{\Psi^\circ_\varpi(w(z))}d\mathfrak M$ holomorphic by Morera and Fubini, and $I_n(z_0)=\int_{B_n}|e^{\Psi^\circ_\varpi(w(z_0))}|\,\mathrm{d}\mathfrak M>0$ for all large $n$ when $F_0$ is the conjugate phase of the integrand at $z_0$, because the integrand has no zero, $B_n\uparrow\Xi_h$ and $\mathfrak M(\Xi_h)>0$.

So $e^{\Psi_\varpi(w(z))}$ is holomorphic without zeros on a convex set and has a holomorphic logarithm, whose real part is $h_\varpi(w(z))$. (T4) follows from conjugation of the history measures in Thm.~\YMMref{AJ}{673} and of the vacuum splitting in Prop.~\YMMref{83.2}{675}, first at the points $\zeta$ with rational coordinates and then by continuity; joint measurability from measurability in $\varpi$ and continuity in $z$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The imaginary direction; a floor; Harnack; H\"older over several directions]\label{C-365-18}
Let $(K,\beta)\in\mathfrak d(g)$ and $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$, and let $u,v,v_1,\dots,v_n$ be real Lipschitz functions on $T_\ell$; $\|\cdot\|=\|\cdot\|_\sharp$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(P1)] If $\|u\|+\|v\|<2\varrho$: $|\widetilde Z(u+iv)|\le\mathsf T(u+iv)\le\widetilde Z(u)^{1-\vartheta}e^{\vartheta C_S\ell^3}$ with $\vartheta=2\|v\|^2/((2\varrho-\|u\|)^2+\|v\|^2)$.
\item[(P2)] If $\|u\|+\|v\|<2\varrho$: $\widetilde Z(u+v)\le\widetilde Z(u)^{1-\vartheta_1}e^{\vartheta_1C_S\ell^3}$ with $\vartheta_1=2\|v\|/(2\varrho-\|u\|+\|v\|)$.
\item[(P3)] If $\rho>0$, $\|u\|+\rho\sum_i\|v_i\|<2\varrho$ and $0\le nt\le\rho/4$: $\widetilde Z(u+t\sum_iv_i)\le\prod_i\widetilde Z(u+ntv_i)^{(1-\vartheta'')/n}e^{\vartheta''C_S\ell^3}$ with $\vartheta''=8n^2t^2/\rho^2$.
\end{enumerate}
For $\|u\|\le\varrho/2$: $\log\widetilde Z(u)\ge-(2C_g+C_S)\ell^3$ (the floor); if moreover $\|u\|+\|v\|<2\varrho$, then
\[
\begin{multlined}
\log|\widetilde Z(u+iv)|\le\log\widetilde Z(u)+C_I'\|v\|^2\ell^3\quad\text{(IM)},\qquad\log\widetilde Z(u+v)-\log\widetilde Z(u)\le\tfrac83(C_S \\
+C_g)\varrho^{-1}\|v\|\ell^3\quad\text{(the Harnack bound)},
\end{multlined}
\]
and $\partial_t^2\log\widetilde Z(u+tv)|_{t=0}\ge-2C_I'\|v\|^2\ell^3$ (semi-convexity). All of this holds for $\widetilde Z^{\rm av}$ in the place of $\widetilde Z$. $C_I'$ is free of $K$, $\beta$, $\ell$ and of the sources.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof]
For the Poisson kernel $\mathsf P_\rho(\zeta_0;\phi)=(\rho^2-|\zeta_0|^2)/|\rho e^{i\phi}-\zeta_0|^2$ one has (i) $\frac12[\mathsf P_\rho(iy;\phi)+\mathsf P_\rho(iy;-\phi)]\ge1-2y^2/(\rho^2+y^2)$ for $0\le y<\rho$; (ii) $\mathsf P_\rho(s;\phi)\ge1-2s/(\rho+s)$ for $0\le s<\rho$; (iii) $\prod_{i\le n}\mathsf P_\rho(t;\phi_i)\ge(1-8n^2t^2/\rho^2)\,n^{-1}\sum_i\mathsf P_\rho(nt;\phi_i)$ for $0\le nt\le\rho/4$; (i), (ii) are elementary, and (iii) follows from $\log\mathsf P_\rho(t;\phi)\ge\log(1-\tau^2)+2\tau\cos\phi-\tau^2/(1-\tau)$ and $n^{-1}\sum_i\mathsf P_\rho(nt;\phi_i)\le(1+\mathsf y)[1+\frac{16}3n^2\tau^2]$, $\tau=t/\rho$, $\mathsf y=2\tau\sum_i\cos\phi_i$. Thus each kernel is $(1-\vartheta)$ times the reference kernel plus $\vartheta R$ with $R\ge0$ of mean $1$. For (P1) take $1<\rho<(2\varrho-\|u\|)/\|v\|$; by (T3), (T4) of Lem.~\ref{C-365-17}, off a null set $G(\zeta)=h_\varpi(u+\zeta v)$ is harmonic near $|\zeta|\le\rho$ and $G(\bar\zeta)=G(\zeta)$. Poisson's formula at $\zeta=i$, made symmetric, gives $G(i)=(1-\vartheta)G(0)+\vartheta\int RG(\rho e^{i\phi})\,\mathrm{d}m$; Jensen's inequality, integration in $\varpi$, H\"older's inequality with the exponents $1/(1-\vartheta)$, $1/\vartheta$ and Tonelli give
\[\mathsf T(u+iv)\le\mathsf T(u)^{1-\vartheta}\Bigl(\int R\,\mathsf T(u+\rho e^{i\phi}v)\,\mathrm{d}m\Bigr)^{\vartheta}\le\widetilde Z(u)^{1-\vartheta}e^{\vartheta C_S\ell^3}\]
by (T1), (T2); let $\rho$ increase to its bound. (P2) is the same at $\zeta=1$ with (ii), and (P3) the same in $n$ variables with (iii), H\"older's inequality now with $n$ exponents $n/(1-\vartheta'')$ and one $1/\vartheta''$. The floor is (P2) at the base $u$ and the direction $-u$, where $\vartheta_1=\|u\|/\varrho\le\frac12$, with $\widetilde Z(0)\ge e^{-C_g\ell^3}$ from (M1). (IM): $\vartheta\le8\|v\|^2/(9\varrho^2)$ and $C_S\ell^3-\log\widetilde Z(u)\le2(C_S+C_g)\ell^3$ by the floor; the Harnack bound likewise with $\vartheta_1\le4\|v\|/(3\varrho)$. Semi-convexity: $\mathsf h(\zeta)=\log\widetilde Z(u+\zeta v)$ is holomorphic near $0$ and real on the real axis, and $\operatorname{Re}\mathsf h(iy)-\mathsf h(0)=-\frac12\mathsf h''(0)y^2+O(y^4)\le C_I'\|v\|^2y^2\ell^3$ by (IM). For $\widetilde Z^{\rm av}$ each inequality is one between products of powers of values of $\mathsf T$ whose exponents read norms alone; write it at the images under $\mathsf r\in\mathsf G$ and take the geometric mean, using (A1) of Lem.~\ref{C-365-14} and equality at real sources.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The walls]\label{C-365-19}
Let $b\in I(g)$, $K\ge1$, $T\ge\max\{T_0,\mathsf l\}$, $q=L^i\ge2T$, $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$ with $\ell\ge2q$, a board of $T_\ell$ of side $q$ with any offset, and $f\in\mathfrak P_T$ a profile of one of its cells, with $F$ as in Def.~\ref{C-365-4}. For real $x$ with $|x|\le\varrho/(256\mathsf c)$ and $x\le b$:
\[\log\widetilde Z^{\rm av}(xF)-\log\widetilde Z^{\rm av}(x)\le N\bigl[3C_wTq^2|x|+C_2'q^3x^2\bigr].\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof]
By the passage, $(K,L^Kb)\in\mathfrak d(g)$. Fix $o_0\in a_K\mathbb Z$ and take eight boards of side $\mathsf l$: the board $\iota\in\{0,1\}^3$ has the offset $o_\iota$ with $(o_\iota)_\mu=o_0+\iota_\mu(\mathsf l+a_K)/2$, a point of $a_K\mathbb Z^3$ as $\mathsf l/a_K$ is odd. Take the partition of unity $\Theta_\iota=\prod_\mu\mathsf t_{\iota_\mu}(y_\mu)$, $\mathsf t_1=1-\mathsf t_0$, $\mathsf t_0$ the $\mathsf l$-periodic trapezoid equal to $1$ within $\mathsf l/8$ of $o_0+\mathsf l\mathbb Z$ and to $0$ beyond $3\mathsf l/8$, with $\operatorname{Lip}\Theta_\iota\le4\sqrt3/\mathsf l$; in a cell of the board $\iota$ the support of $\Theta_\iota$ lies in a sup-ball of radius $R_0\le7\mathsf l/16$ at sup-distance $\ge\mathsf l/16$ from the walls of that board.

The walls $\mathsf g=1-F$ split as $\mathsf g\Theta_\iota=\sum_rh_r$ into pieces of the cells of the board $\iota$, with $\|h_r\|_\sharp\le\mathsf c$ and mutual sup-distances $\ge\Delta=\mathsf l/8\ge4M$; since $\mathsf g\ne0$ only within $T/2$ of a mirror of the board of side $q$, at most $n_\iota\le9NTq^2/\mathsf l^3$ pieces are non-zero. H\"older's inequality (P3) at $u=x$, $n=8$, $v_\iota=-\operatorname{sgn}(x)\mathsf g\Theta_\iota$, $t=|x|$, $\rho=\varrho/(8\mathsf c)$, with the floor, costs $\vartheta''(2C_S+2C_g)\ell^3$, $\vartheta''=32768\mathsf c^2x^2/\varrho^2$ (this is the term in $x^2$, paid on the whole torus), and leaves the eight numbers $\mathsf B_\iota=\log[\widetilde Z^{\rm av}(x+z\mathsf g\Theta_\iota)/\widetilde Z^{\rm av}(x)]$, $z=-8x$.

Write $Z_b[w]=Z_{K,\ell,L^Kb}[w]$. On the board $\iota$, the shift of the label, $Z_b[x+w]/Z_b[x]=Z_{K,\ell,\beta'}[w]/Z_{K,\ell,\beta'}$ with $\beta'=L^K(b-x)\ge0$, and the chessboard estimate at $\beta'$ give $Z_b[x+z\mathsf g\Theta_\iota]/Z_b[x]\le\prod_r\|e^{z\mathcal O(h_r)}\|_{\rm ch}$, and by the source formula $\|e^{z\mathcal O(h_r)}\|_{\rm ch}^{N_f}=Z_b[x+zh_r^{\rm per}]/Z_b[x]$, where $h_r^{\rm per}$, the sum of the $N_f=(\ell/\mathsf l)^3$ mirror copies of $h_r$, is a dense array. The energies, whose bounds grow with $K$, cancel exactly up to cross terms. Put $\mathcal E'(w)=\mathcal E^{\rm av}(x+w)-\mathcal E^{\rm av}(x)$, the function $\mathcal F'$ of Lem.~\ref{C-365-14}~(A2) for $\mathcal F=\mathcal E^{\rm av}$ at the base source $u=x$; then $Z_b[x+w]/Z_b[x]=e^{\mathcal E'(w)}\widetilde Z^{\rm av}(x+w)/\widetilde Z^{\rm av}(x)$, and so, the sums being over the $r$ with $h_r\ne0$,
\[\mathsf B_\iota\le-\mathcal E'(z\mathsf g\Theta_\iota)+\sum_rN_f^{-1}\Bigl[\mathcal E'(zh_r^{\rm per})+\log\frac{\widetilde Z^{\rm av}(x+zh_r^{\rm per})}{\widetilde Z^{\rm av}(x)}\Bigr].\]
The mirror copies of $h_r$ are its images $\mathsf rh_r$ under reflections $\mathsf r\in\mathsf G$ at mirrors of the board $\iota$, which fix the constant $x$, so that $\mathcal E^{\rm av}(x+z\mathsf rh_r)=\mathcal E^{\rm av}(\mathsf r(x+zh_r))=\mathcal E^{\rm av}(x+zh_r)$ by (A1). By Lem.~\ref{C-365-14}~(A3), applied twice with the base source $u=x$, $\mathcal E'(z\mathsf g\Theta_\iota)=\sum_r\mathcal E'(zh_r)+\mathrm{cr}_\iota$ and $\mathcal E'(zh_r^{\rm per})=N_f\mathcal E'(zh_r)+\mathrm{cr}_r$; so the terms in $\mathcal E'$ of the bound of $\mathsf B_\iota$ are $-\mathrm{cr}_\iota+\sum_rN_f^{-1}\mathrm{cr}_r$, at most $2C_\times(7/2)n_\iota|z|^2\mathsf c^2/\varrho^2$. The dense arrays are bounded by the Harnack bound, $N_f^{-1}\log[\widetilde Z^{\rm av}(x+zh_r^{\rm per})/\widetilde Z^{\rm av}(x)]\le4\mathsf c(C_S+C_g)\varrho^{-1}\mathsf l^3|z|$. Summing,
\[\mathsf B_\iota\le n_\iota\Bigl[\frac{32\mathsf c(C_S+C_g)}{\varrho}\mathsf l^3|x|+\frac{128\,C_\times(7/2)\mathsf c^2x^2}{\varrho^2}\Bigr]\le N\Bigl[3C_wTq^2|x|+\frac{1152\,C_\times(7/2)\mathsf c^2}{\varrho^2\mathsf l^3}Tq^2x^2\Bigr],\]
since $72\cdot4\mathsf c(C_S+C_g)/\varrho=3C_w$; with $Tq^2\le q^3$ and the cost of H\"older's inequality this is the claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Slabs; the walls without a term in $x^2$ for products]\label{C-365-20}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[beginpenalty=10000]
\item[(a)] \emph{The slab inequality (exact).} On a periodic box $(\mathbb Z/\mathsf N\mathbb Z)^3$ let $c(p)$ be any real weights on the plaquettes and $Z(c)=\int e^{-\sum_pc(p)a_p}\,\mathrm{d}U$. Let $\mathsf N=2k\,t$ with integers $k,t\ge1$, cut the box in one direction by the $2k$ planes of sites $x_\mu=n_0+jt$ into the closed slabs $\mathsf S_j$, and let $c_j^{\rm arr}$ be the weights that agree with $c$ on $\mathsf S_j$ and are symmetric under the reflections at all $2k$ planes. Then $Z(c)\le\prod_jZ(c_j^{\rm arr})^{1/(2k)}$; no sign of $c$ is supposed. For $c(p)=\beta-a^{-1}w(x(p))$ with $w$ real this reads $Z[w]\le\prod_jZ[w_j^{\rm arr}]^{1/(2k)}$, $w_j^{\rm arr}$ the function that agrees with $w$ on $\mathsf S_j$ and is even at all the planes.
\item[(b)] \emph{The walls for products.} Let $(K,\beta)\in\mathfrak d(g)$, $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$, $T\ge T_0$, $q=L^i\ge2T$, $\ell\ge2q$, a board of $T_\ell$ of side $q$ with mirrors $y_\mu\in s_\mu+q\mathbb Z$, and $T'$ the least power of $L$ that is $\ge2T$. Let $\varphi_\mu:\mathbb R/\ell\mathbb Z\to[0,1]$ have $\operatorname{Lip}\varphi_\mu\le16/T$ and $\varphi_\mu=1$ at distance $\ge T/2$ from $s_\mu+q\mathbb Z$, and $F(y)=\prod_\mu\varphi_\mu(y_\mu)$; let $x_0$, $x$ be real with $|x_0|+|x|\le\varrho/2$, and $C_V=16L(C_S+C_g)/\varrho+3C_\times(1)/(4\varrho T_0^3)$. Then
\[\log\widetilde Z^{\rm av}(x_0+xF)-\log\widetilde Z^{\rm av}(x_0+x)\le C_V|x|\,Tq^2N;\]
if every $\varphi_\mu$ has the period $q$ and is even at $s_\mu$ (as for the mirror copies of the centred $f_0$), the same holds for $\widetilde Z$ itself. No condition $x\le b$ is asked.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof]
(a) Cut in the direction $\mu=1$. The kernel $K_j(\phi,\phi')$ of the slab $\mathsf S_j$, with half weights on its two faces and the bonds of the faces fixed to $\phi,\phi'$, is real, continuous and positive on a compact space, so a Hilbert--Schmidt operator, and Fubini gives $Z(c)=\operatorname{Tr}(K_0K_1\cdots K_{2k-1})$. The reflection at the mid-plane of a slab shows that $K_j^T$ is the kernel of the slab with mirrored weights, so $\operatorname{Tr}((K_jK_j^T)^k)=Z(c_j^{\rm arr})$; H\"older's inequality in the Schatten classes, $|\operatorname{Tr}(A_1\cdots A_{2k})|\le\prod_i\|A_i\|_{2k}$, is the claim. In the case used it is the classical chessboard argument: $\mathsf F(C_1,\dots,C_{2k})=\operatorname{Tr}(C_1C_2^TC_3C_4^T\cdots C_{2k-1}C_{2k}^T)$ is multilinear, invariant under a cyclic shift by one place with all letters transposed, and satisfies $|\mathsf F(C)|^2\le\mathsf F(C_1,\dots,C_k,C_k,\dots,C_1)\,\mathsf F(C_{2k},\dots,C_{k+1},C_{k+1},\dots,C_{2k})$ by Cauchy--Schwarz; after the normalisation $\mathsf F(C_i,\dots,C_i)=1$, among the words that maximise $|\mathsf F|$ one with the longest run of equal letters must have a run of length $\ge k$, whence the maximum is $\le1$. (b) Three steps, one direction at a time: $u_0=x_0+x$ and $u_\mu=x_0+x\prod_{\nu\le\mu}\varphi_\nu(y_\nu)$, so that $u_3=x_0+xF$.

In the direction $\mu$ the planes $y_\mu\in s_\mu+T'/2+T'\mathbb Z$ are planes of sites, because $q/a_K$ and $T'/a_K$ are odd, and they cut $T_\ell$ into the $\ell/T'$ closed slabs $\mathsf S_j=\{|y_\mu-s_\mu-jT'|\le T'/2\}$, $j\in\mathbb Z/(\ell/T')\mathbb Z$, an even number of them; as $q/T'$ is an integer, the mirrors are the mid-planes of the $\ell/q$ \emph{wall slabs}, those with $jT'\in q\mathbb Z$. The function $u_{\mu-1}$ does not read $y_\mu$, and $u_\mu-u_{\mu-1}=-x\prod_{\nu<\mu}\varphi_\nu(y_\nu)\,(1-\varphi_\mu(y_\mu))$ vanishes at distance $\ge T/2$ from the mirrors, hence off the wall slabs and near their faces, as $T'/2\ge T$. For a wall slab $\mathsf S_j$ put
\[w_j=(u_\mu-u_{\mu-1})\mathbf 1_{\mathsf S_j}=-x\prod_{\nu<\mu}\varphi_\nu(y_\nu)\,\bigl(1-\varphi_\mu(y_\mu)\bigr)\mathbf 1_{\mathsf S_j},\]
so that $u_\mu=u_{\mu-1}+\sum_{\text{wall slabs}}w_j$, and let $w_j^{\rm arr}$, the sum of the $\ell/T'$ mirror images of $w_j$ at the planes, one in each slab, be the even continuation of $w_j$ from $\mathsf S_j$. The even continuation of $u_\mu$ from a slab is $u_{\mu-1}$ for a slab that is not a wall slab and $u_{\mu-1}+w_j^{\rm arr}$ for a wall slab $\mathsf S_j$; so (a) at the real source $u_\mu$ gives
\[\log\frac{Z[u_\mu]}{Z[u_{\mu-1}]}\le\frac{T'}{\ell}\sum_{\text{wall slabs}}\log\frac{Z[u_{\mu-1}+w_j^{\rm arr}]}{Z[u_{\mu-1}]}.\]
The normalisers cancel exactly. Let $\mathcal F=\mathcal E^{\rm av}$ for the first assertion and $\mathcal F=\mathcal E$ in the periodic even case, $\widetilde Z^{\mathcal F}=e^{-E-\mathcal F}Z$ (that is, $\widetilde Z^{\rm av}$, respectively $\widetilde Z$), and $\mathcal F'(w)=\mathcal F(u_{\mu-1}+w)-\mathcal F(u_{\mu-1})$ as in Lem.~\ref{C-365-14}~(A2) at the base $u_{\mu-1}$, so that $Z[u_{\mu-1}+w]/Z[u_{\mu-1}]=e^{\mathcal F'(w)}\widetilde Z^{\mathcal F}(u_{\mu-1}+w)/\widetilde Z^{\mathcal F}(u_{\mu-1})$. The pieces of $w_j^{\rm arr}$ are images $\mathsf rw_j$ under reflections $\mathsf r\in\mathsf G$ at the planes, which fix $u_{\mu-1}$, so $\mathcal F'(\mathsf rw_j)=\mathcal F'(w_j)$ for $\mathcal F=\mathcal E^{\rm av}$ by (A1); in the periodic even case $1-\varphi_\mu$ is even at the mid-plane of $\mathsf S_j$, the pieces are the translates of $w_j$ by $T'\mathbb Ze_\mu$, which lies in $M\mathbb Z^3$ as $T'$ and $M$ are powers of $L$ with $T'>M$, and the same holds for $\mathcal E$ itself by (M1).

Hence $\mathcal F'(w_j^{\rm arr})=(\ell/T')\mathcal F'(w_j)+\mathrm{cr}_j$ and $\mathcal F'(\sum_jw_j)=\sum_j\mathcal F'(w_j)+\mathrm{cr}$, the sum over the wall slabs, and in $\log[\widetilde Z^{\mathcal F}(u_\mu)/\widetilde Z^{\mathcal F}(u_{\mu-1})]=\log(Z[u_\mu]/Z[u_{\mu-1}])-\mathcal F'(\sum_jw_j)$ the terms $\mathcal F'(w_j)$ cancel, leaving the cross terms. These are bounded by Lem.~\ref{C-365-14}~(A3), with $x$ replaced by $\zeta$, $|\zeta|<\varrho$, in the $w_j$ alone: each support lies within $T/2$ of the mid-plane of its slab and is covered by $(\ell/T')^2$ closed sup-balls of radius $R_0=T'/2$, and different supports are at sup-distance $\ge\Delta=T'-T\ge T'/2\ge4M$, so that $R_0/\Delta\le1$.

The Harnack bound at the base $u_{\mu-1}$, with $\|u_{\mu-1}\|_\sharp\le|x_0|+|x|\le\varrho/2$, and in the direction $w_j^{\rm arr}$, with $\|w_j^{\rm arr}\|_\sharp\le|x|$ as $40M\cdot16\sqrt3/T\le1$, costs $\frac83(C_S+C_g)\varrho^{-1}|x|\ell^3$ for each wall array, and $\#\{\text{wall slabs}\}\,T'/\ell=T'/q$; a slab needs no partition of unity across it, so (P3) and its term in $x^2$ do not enter. Summing the three steps with $2T\le T'<2LT$ and $|x|\le\varrho/2$ gives the constant $C_V$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The main inequality; semi-convexity]\label{C-365-21}
Let $\ell'\in\mathfrak L(g)$ with $\ell'\ge2\mathsf l_1$ be a reference side, $T\ge\max\{T_0,\mathsf l\}$, $q=L^i\ge2T$, $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$ with $\ell\ge\max\{2q,\ell'\}$, $K\ge1$ and $b\in I(g)$, all numbers of Def.~\ref{C-365-7} being formed at $g$ with $\ell'$. Put $\omega(z)=\ell'^{-3}\log[\widetilde Z_{\ell'}(z)/\widetilde Z_{\ell'}(0)]$, let $\mu'=d'(0)$ for the $d$ of Lem.~\ref{C-365-15} at $(\ell_1,\ell_2)=(\ell,\ell')$, and for a profile $f$ let $\epsilon(z)=\mathcal E^{\rm av}_\ell(zf)+q^3[\omega'(0)-\mu']z$, a function holomorphic on $|z|<2\varrho$ with $\epsilon(0)=0$ and $\epsilon'(0)$ real.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] For every board of $T_\ell$ of side $q$, every offset and every profile $f\in\mathfrak P_T$, for $|z|\le r_1$ with $\operatorname{Re}z\le b$:
\[\Lambda(z)-\operatorname{Re}\epsilon(z)\le q^3\bigl[D_{K,\ell}(b-\operatorname{Re}z)-D_{K,\ell}(b)\bigr]+3C_wTq^2|\operatorname{Re}z|+C_Iq^3|z|^2 .\]
\item[(b)] $D''_{K,\ell}(b)\ge-C_0$ at every $b\in I(g)$. So $D_{K,\ell}+\frac12C_0y^2$ and $D_K+\frac12C_0y^2$ are convex on $I(g)$; $\mu_K=(D_K+\frac12C_0y^2)''$ and $\mu_{K,\ell}=(D_{K,\ell}+\frac12C_0y^2)''$ are positive Radon measures on $\operatorname{int}I(g)$; and for both, $\mu([y_1,y_2])\le2B'/t+C_0(y_2-y_1+t)$ whenever $[y_1-t,y_2+t]\subset I(g)$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof]
By the passage $(K,L^Kb)\in\mathfrak d(g)$, so Lems.~\ref{C-365-14}, \ref{C-365-15}, \ref{C-365-17} and Props.~\ref{C-365-18}, \ref{C-365-19} hold on both tori. The shift of the label gives on each torus, for real $|x|<2\varrho$, $\log\widetilde Z(x)-\log\widetilde Z(0)=\ell^3[p_{K,\ell}(b-x)-p_{K,\ell}(b)]-\mathcal E(x\cdot1)$; dividing by the volumes and subtracting,
\[\ell^{-3}\bigl[\log\widetilde Z_\ell(x)-\log\widetilde Z_\ell(0)\bigr]=\bigl[D_{K,\ell}(b-x)-D_{K,\ell}(b)\bigr]+\omega(x)-d(x).\]
$H(z)=\widetilde Z_{\ell'}(z)/\widetilde Z_{\ell'}(0)$ is holomorphic on $|z|<2\varrho$, $H(0)=1$ and $|H|\le e^{(C_S+C_g)\ell'^3}$ by (M1); Schwarz's lemma gives $|H-1|\le\frac12$ on $|z|\le r_2$, so $|\omega(x)-\omega'(0)x|\le C_\omega x^2$ for $|x|\le r_2/2$ and $|\omega''(0)|\le C_\omega$. For (a), with $z=x+i\tau$, the source formula gives $N\Lambda(z)=\operatorname{Re}\mathcal E^{\rm av}(w_z)+\log|\widetilde Z^{\rm av}(w_z)|-\log\widetilde Z(0)$. Then (i) (IM) for $\widetilde Z^{\rm av}$ at $u=xF$, $v=\tau(F_e-F_o)$ removes $\tau$ at the cost $C_I'\tau^2\ell^3$; (ii) the walls (Prop.~\ref{C-365-19}) replace $xF$ by the constant $x$ at the cost $N[3C_wTq^2|x|+C_2'q^3x^2]$; (iii) the identity, the bound of $\omega$ and Lem.~\ref{C-365-15} turn $\log\widetilde Z(x)-\log\widetilde Z(0)$ into at most $Nq^3\{[D_{K,\ell}(b-x)-D_{K,\ell}(b)]+[\omega'(0)-\mu']x+(C_\omega+2\mathsf A_1/h_1^2)x^2\}$; (iv) the cross terms between the cells, Lem.~\ref{C-365-14}~(A3) with $R_0=q/2$, $\Delta=T/4$, $\rho_3=\varrho$ and $C_\times(2q/T)\le M_\times(q/T)^3$, give $\operatorname{Re}\mathcal E^{\rm av}(w_z)\le N\operatorname{Re}\mathcal E^{\rm av}(zf)+NM_\times T^{-3}\varrho^{-2}q^3|z|^2$.

Adding and dividing by $N$ gives (a). For (b), semi-convexity in Prop.~\ref{C-365-18} at $u=0$, $v=1$ gives $\mathsf h''(0)\ge-2C_I'\ell^3$ for $\mathsf h(x)=\log\widetilde Z_\ell(x)$; differentiating the identity twice at $x=0$,
\[D''_{K,\ell}(b)=\ell^{-3}\mathsf h''(0)-\omega''(0)+d''(0)\ge-2C_I'-C_\omega-2\mathsf A_1/h_1^2=-C_0 .\]
$D_{K,\ell}$ is real-analytic in the label, and $D_K$ is its pointwise limit by Lem.~\ref{C-365-16}. For $\Phi=D+\frac12C_0y^2$ with $D\in\{D_K,D_{K,\ell}\}$, $\mu([y_1,y_2])=\Phi'(y_2+)-\Phi'(y_1-)$ is bounded by difference quotients over the length $t$, and $D\in[-B',0]$ by Lem.~\ref{C-365-16}~(c).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Cauchy's estimate in the chessboard seminorm; moments from the seminorm]\label{C-365-22}
On a board of $T_\ell$, at any $\beta\ge0$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] If $X=\mathcal O(f)$ is a real function of one cell and $\tilde\epsilon$ is holomorphic near the disc $|z|\le r$ with $\tilde\epsilon(0)=0$, then $\|X-\tilde\epsilon'(0)\|_{\rm ch}\le r^{-1}\max_{|z|=r}\exp[\Lambda(z)-\operatorname{Re}\tilde\epsilon(z)]$.
\item[(b)] For functions $X_1,\dots,X_n$ of $n$ different cells and complex numbers $m_i$: $|\langle\prod_i(X_i-m_i)\rangle|\le\prod_i\|X_i-m_i\|_{\rm ch}$; $|\langle X_i\rangle-m_i|\le\|X_i-m_i\|_{\rm ch}$; $|\operatorname{Cov}(X_1,X_2)|\le2\|X_1-m_1\|_{\rm ch}\|X_2-m_2\|_{\rm ch}$; and the centred moments satisfy $|\langle\prod_i(X_i-\langle X_i\rangle)\rangle|\le\prod_i2\|X_i-m_i\|_{\rm ch}$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof]
(a) Pointwise on the configurations, $X-\tilde\epsilon'(0)=(2\pi i)^{-1}\oint_{|z|=r}e^{zX-\tilde\epsilon(z)}z^{-2}\,\mathrm{d}z$; the Riemann sums converge uniformly since $X$ is bounded; the triangle inequality and the homogeneity of the seminorm, with $\|F\|_{\rm ch}\le\sup|F|$ for the remainder, give $\|X-\tilde\epsilon'(0)\|_{\rm ch}\le r^{-1}\max_{|z|=r}\|e^{zX-\tilde\epsilon(z)}\|_{\rm ch}$, and $\|e^{zX-\tilde\epsilon(z)}\|_{\rm ch}=e^{-\operatorname{Re}\tilde\epsilon(z)}(Z[w_z]/Z)^{1/N}$ by the source formula. (b) The first inequality is the chessboard estimate; the second is the first with one factor and $\|1\|_{\rm ch}=1$; the third follows from $\operatorname{Cov}(X_1,X_2)=\langle(X_1-m_1)(X_2-m_2)\rangle-(\langle X_1\rangle-m_1)(\langle X_2\rangle-m_2)$; and $\|X_i-\langle X_i\rangle\|_{\rm ch}\le\|X_i-m_i\|_{\rm ch}+|\langle X_i\rangle-m_i|\le2\|X_i-m_i\|_{\rm ch}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[From a bound on increments of the pressure to the cube means, on a torus]\label{C-365-23}
In the setting of Prop.~\ref{C-365-21}, let $\mathsf s$, $\delta_2$, $\tilde C$, $\eta_+$, $x_0$ be real numbers with $\delta_2\ge0$, $\tilde C\ge0$, $\eta_+\ge0$ and $0<x_0\le b$, such that
\[D_{K,\ell}(b-x)-D_{K,\ell}(b)\le\mathsf sx+\delta_2|x|+\tilde Cx^2+\eta_+\qquad\text{for all real }|x|\le x_0 .\]
Put $\delta=3C_wT/q+\delta_2$, and let $q\ge\max\{(\tilde C+C_I)/(9C_w^2T^2),\,(3C_wT\min\{r_1,x_0\})^{-1/2}\}$. Then on every board of $T_\ell$ of side $q$, $\|x_c-m'\|_{\rm ch}\le e^{2+q^3\eta_+}\delta$ with the real number $m'=q^{-3}\epsilon'(0)+\mathsf s$, which depends on $\ell$ and on the profile. Hence, for profiles of $\mathfrak P_T$ in distinct cells,
\[|\operatorname{Cov}_{K,\ell,L^Kb}(x_c,x_{c'})|\le2e^{4+2q^3\eta_+}\delta^2,\qquad\Bigl|\bigl\langle\textstyle\prod_{i=1}^n(x_{c_i}-\langle x_{c_i}\rangle)\bigr\rangle_{K,\ell,L^Kb}\Bigr|\le\bigl(2e^{2+q^3\eta_+}\delta\bigr)^n .\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof]
Put $\tilde\epsilon(z)=\epsilon(z)+q^3\mathsf sz$. For $|z|=r\le\min\{r_1,x_0\}$, so that $\operatorname{Re}z\le x_0\le b$, the main inequality and the hypothesis at $x=\operatorname{Re}z$ give, since $\delta_2\ge0$ and $\tilde C\ge0$ allow $\delta_2|x|\le\delta_2r$ and $\tilde Cx^2\le\tilde Cr^2$,
\[\Lambda(z)-\operatorname{Re}\tilde\epsilon(z)\le q^3\delta r+q^3(\tilde C+C_I)r^2+q^3\eta_+ .\]
Take $r=1/(q^3\delta)$; since $\delta\ge3C_wT/q$, $r\le1/(3C_wTq^2)\le\min\{r_1,x_0\}$ by the second floor; $q^3\delta r=1$; and $q^3(\tilde C+C_I)r^2=(\tilde C+C_I)/(q^3\delta^2)\le(\tilde C+C_I)/(9C_w^2T^2q)\le1$ by the first. Lem.~\ref{C-365-22}~(a) gives $\|\mathcal O(f)-\tilde\epsilon'(0)\|_{\rm ch}\le q^3\delta e^{2+q^3\eta_+}$; divide by $q^3$; for a profile of another cell the same holds with its own $\epsilon$ and $m'$; Lem.~\ref{C-365-22}~(b) gives the rest.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The window inequality, in one frame, at every cutoff]\label{C-365-24}
In the setting of Prop.~\ref{C-365-21}, let $b$ be a label with $I_q(b)\subset\operatorname{int}I(g)$, $q\ge q_1=\max\{2T,\,C_I/(9C_w^2T^2),\,(3C_wTr_1)^{-1/2}\}$, $K\ge1$, and
\[\delta_K(q,b)=3C_wT/q+\mu_K(I_q(b)).\]
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] For all $\nu,\nu'\in\mathcal G^{\rm per}_{K,L^Kb}$, every board of $\mathbb L_K$ of side $q$ with any offset and profiles of $\mathfrak P_T$ in distinct cells $c,c',c_1,\dots,c_n$:
\[
\begin{multlined}
|\operatorname{Cov}_\nu(x_c,x_{c'})|\le2e^4\delta_K(q,b)^2,\qquad|\nu(x_c)-\nu'(x_c)|\le2e^2\delta_K(q,b),\qquad\Bigl|\nu\Bigl(\prod_i(x_{c_i} \\
-\nu(x_{c_i}))\Bigr)\Bigr|\le(2e^2\delta_K(q,b))^n .
\end{multlined}
\]
\item[(b)] The same holds with $\delta=3C_wT/q+C_0x_q+x_q^{-1}\Delta^2_{x_q}D_K(b)$, which is $\le\delta_K(q,b)$; and for every $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$ with $\ell\ge\ell'$,
\[
\begin{multlined}
x_q^{-1}\Delta^2_{x_q}D_K(b)\le x_q^{-1}\Delta^2_{x_q}D_{K,\ell}(b)+6C_wC_{\rm FS}Tq^2/\ell\le x_q\sup_{|y-b|\le x_q}D''_{K,\ell}(y) \\
+6C_wC_{\rm FS}Tq^2/\ell,\qquad C_{\rm FS}=3\ell'B':
\end{multlined}
\]
the bounds in every periodic Gibbs state are governed by the pressures of the two tori $T_\ell$, $T_{\ell'}$ at a side $\ell$ of the order $q^3$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof]
(a) \emph{A window gives the hypothesis of Prop.~\ref{C-365-23}.} $\Phi=D_K+\frac12C_0y^2$ is convex on $\operatorname{int}I(g)\supset I_q(b)$; with $\sigma_0=\Phi'(b-)$, for $0<x\le x_q$, $\Phi(b+x)-\Phi(b)\le\sigma_0x+x\mu_K([b,b+x))$ and $\Phi(b-x)-\Phi(b)\le-\sigma_0x+x\mu_K((b-x,b))$; since $D_K(b-x)-D_K(b)=\Phi(b-x)-\Phi(b)+C_0bx-\frac12C_0x^2$, the function $D_K$ has the hypothesis with $\mathsf s=C_0b-\sigma_0$, $\delta_2=\mu_K(I_q(b))\ge0$, $\tilde C=0$, $\eta_+=0$, $x_0=x_q$. \emph{From the tori to the states.} By Lem.~\ref{C-365-16}, $D_{K,\ell}=D_K+\mathsf w_\ell$ with $0\le\mathsf w_\ell\le\bar\eta(\ell)$, so $D_{K,\ell}$ has it with the tolerance $\eta_+=\bar\eta(\ell)$, and Prop.~\ref{C-365-23} gives $\|x_c-m'_\ell\|_{{\rm ch},\ell}\le e^{2+q^3\bar\eta(\ell)}\delta_K(q,b)$ for all $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$, $\ell\ge\max\{2q,\ell'\}$. The real numbers $m'_\ell$ are bounded at fixed $K$, since $|m'_\ell-\langle x_c\rangle_\ell|\le e^3\delta_K$ for large $\ell$ and $|x_c|$ is bounded. For finitely many profiles choose $\ell_k\to\infty$ with $m'_{\ell_k,i}\to m_{*,i}$; then $\limsup_k\|x_{c_i}-m_{*,i}\|_{{\rm ch},\ell_k}\le e^2\delta_K$, and the domination gives
\[\Bigl|\nu\Bigl(\prod_i(x_{c_i}-m_{*,i})\Bigr)\Bigr|\le(e^2\delta_K)^n\qquad\text{for every }\nu\in\mathcal G^{\rm per}_{K,L^Kb};\]
at $n=1$, $|\nu(x_c)-m_*|\le e^2\delta_K$ for $\nu$ and for $\nu'$, one common centre serving both; expanding as in Lem.~\ref{C-365-22}~(b) gives the three bounds. (b) In Prop.~\ref{C-365-23} the hypothesis enters only at $|x|\le r=1/(q^3\delta)\le x_q$. On $[b-r,b+r]$ the convex $\Phi$ lies below its chord, so $\Phi(b-x)-\Phi(b)\le-\mathsf s_rx+\frac12\Delta^2_r\Phi(b)$ with the slope $\mathsf s_r$ of the chord; and $\Delta^2_r\Phi(b)/r=r^{-1}\int_0^r\mu_K((b-u,b+u))\,\mathrm{d}u$ does not decrease in $r$, so $\frac12\Delta^2_r\Phi(b)\le r\,x_q^{-1}\Delta^2_{x_q}\Phi(b)$, which is $r(C_0x_q+x_q^{-1}\Delta^2_{x_q}D_K(b))$ and at most $r\mu_K(I_q(b))$. The comparison with the torus follows from $D_K\le D_{K,\ell}\le D_K+\bar\eta(\ell)$, $2\bar\eta(\ell)/x_q=6C_wC_{\rm FS}Tq^2/\ell$, and $\Delta^2_sD\le s^2\sup D''$ for the real-analytic $D_{K,\ell}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[A sum rule; near and far parts; a pile recurs at all large cutoffs]\label{C-365-25}
Let one frame, $0<g\le\gamma$, a compact interval $W\subset I(g)$ of positive length and $\ell'\in\mathfrak L(g)$ with $\ell'\ge2\mathsf l_1$ be given, let $k_7\ge1$ be an integer with $\varsigma_7=L^{-k_7}\le2/(3\sqrt3)$, and let $\chi$, $\eta$, $\mathsf c_7$, $c_T$, $c_N$ be formed with this $\varsigma_7$ as in Def.~\ref{C-365-7}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{Exact.} For $K\ge k_7$, every side $\ell>6\varsigma_7$ and $b\ge0$:
\[
\begin{multlined}
p''_{K,\ell}(b)=\varsigma_7^{-3}S^T_{2;K,\ell,L^Kb}(\chi,1)=V^{\rm near}_{K,\ell}(b)+V^{\rm far}_{K,\ell}(b),\qquad V^{\rm near}=\varsigma_7^{-3}S^T_2(\chi,\eta),\quad V^{\rm far} \\
=\varsigma_7^{-3}S^T_2(\chi,1-\eta).
\end{multlined}
\]
\item[(ii)] $|V^{\rm near}_{K,\ell}-V^{\rm near}_{K,\ell'}|\le c_N$ on $I(g)$ for all $K\ge k_7$ and $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$; and for each side $\ell$, $\omega_\ell(K,K'')=\sup_W|V^{\rm far}_{K,\ell}-V^{\rm far}_{K'',\ell}|\to0$ as $K,K''\to\infty$.
\item[(iii)] For every closed interval $I$ and $\delta>0$ with $I^{+\delta}=[\min I-\delta,\max I+\delta]\subset\operatorname{int}W$, all $K,K''\ge k_7$ and all $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$ with $\ell\ge\ell'$:
\[\mu_K(I)\le\mu_{K''}(I^{+\delta})+(|I|+2\delta)\bigl[2c_N+\omega_\ell(K,K'')+\omega_{\ell'}(K,K'')\bigr]+\frac{24\ell'B'}{\delta\ell}.\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof]
(i) 
\[
p''_{K,\ell}=\ell^{-3}L^{2K}\operatorname{Var}(\sum_pa_p)=a_K^{-5}\mathsf N^{-3}\operatorname{Var}(\sum_pa_p),
\]
while $S^T_2(\chi,1)=a_K^{-2}\sum_p\chi(x(p))\operatorname{Cov}(a_p,\sum_{p'}a_{p'})$. By translation invariance the covariance depends on the orientation of $p$ alone, the three orientations summing to $\mathsf N^{-3}\operatorname{Var}(\sum_pa_p)$, and for each orientation $\sum_p\chi(x(p))=(\varsigma_7/a_K)^3$, the sums of tents of the integer half-width $\varsigma_7/a_K$; the splitting is $1=\eta+(1-\eta)$. (ii) The supports of $\chi$ and $\eta$ lie in a ball of radius $3\sqrt3\varsigma_7\le2$, and $\|\chi\|_\sharp,\|\eta\|_\sharp,\|1-\eta\|_\sharp\le\mathsf c_7$, so the transfer (M7) at $n=2$ between the two tori, at the first-passage data given by the passage, bounds the near parts; the supports of $\chi$ and $1-\eta$ are at sup-distance $\varsigma_7$, so the convergence on fixed tori (M8) gives the far parts. (iii) Take a $C^2$ function $1_I\le\eta_I\le1_{I^{+\delta}}$ with $\|\eta_I''\|_1\le8/\delta$, the indicator of $[\min I-\delta/2,\max I+\delta/2]$ smoothed by the kernel $\frac{15}{16}(1-t^2)_+^2$ at the scale $\delta/2$. Since $\mu_K\ge0$, $\mu_K(I)\le\int\eta_I\,\mathrm{d}\mu_K$ and $\int\eta_I\,\mathrm{d}\mu_{K''}\le\mu_{K''}(I^{+\delta})$, and
\[\int\eta_I\,d(\mu_K-\mu_{K''})=\int\eta_I''\bigl[(D_K-D_{K,\ell})-(D_{K''}-D_{K'',\ell})\bigr]+\int\eta_I\,\bigl(D''_{K,\ell}-D''_{K'',\ell}\bigr),\]
where the bracket lies in $[-\bar\eta(\ell),\bar\eta(\ell)]$ by Lem.~\ref{C-365-16}, and by (i) $D''_{K,\ell}=(V^{\rm near}_{K,\ell}-V^{\rm near}_{K,\ell'})+V^{\rm far}_{K,\ell}-V^{\rm far}_{K,\ell'}$, so that $|D''_{K,\ell}-D''_{K'',\ell}|\le2c_N+\omega_\ell+\omega_{\ell'}$ on $W$. In words: a concentration of $\mu_K$ at one large cutoff recurs at all large cutoffs.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Dilations by real factors]\label{C-365-26}
For real $s>0$, $a>0$ and $\beta>0$ the image under $\mathrm{dil}_s$ maps the periodic Gibbs states at $(a,\beta)$ onto the periodic Gibbs states at $(sa,\beta)$, and $S^T_n[\nu](f_1,\dots,f_n)=s^n\,S^T_n[(\mathrm{dil}_s)_*\nu](f_1(\cdot/s),\dots,f_n(\cdot/s))$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof]
The exponent $H_B=-\beta\sum_{p\in\mathrm{Pl}[B]}a_p$ of a Gibbs kernel contains no spacing. By the exact dilation facts (M9), $\mathrm{dil}_s$ carries $\mathrm{Pl}[B]$ onto $\mathrm{Pl}[\mathrm{dil}_sB]$, $a_{\mathrm{dil}_sp}(\mathrm{dil}_sU)=a_p(U)$, the product Haar measure on the bonds of $B$ to that on the bonds of $\mathrm{dil}_sB$, and the configuration that is $V$ on $B$ and $U$ off $B$ to the one that is $\mathrm{dil}_sV$ on $\mathrm{dil}_sB$ and $\mathrm{dil}_sU$ off it; hence
\[\mathrm{dil}_s(\gamma_BF)=\gamma_{\mathrm{dil}_sB}(\mathrm{dil}_sF),\]
and $((\mathrm{dil}_s)_*\nu)(\gamma_{\mathrm{dil}_sB}\mathrm{dil}_sF)=\nu(\gamma_BF)=\nu(F)$; as $B\mapsto\mathrm{dil}_sB$ and $F\mapsto\mathrm{dil}_sF$ are onto, the image is a Gibbs state. Invariance under the translations by a subgroup $\Gamma$ of finite index passes to $s\Gamma$, of the same index; $\mathrm{dil}_{1/s}$ is the inverse. The formula for the cumulants follows from $\mathcal O_a(f)(U)=s\,\mathcal O_{sa}(f(\cdot/s))(\mathrm{dil}_sU)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[One pressure for both frames; the reference tori compared]\label{C-365-27}
In a Setting, let $K\ge k_7$, $\hat K\ge1$, $\lambda=L^K/\hat L^{\hat K}$ and $J$ a closed interval with $J\subset W_1$ and $\lambda J\subset\hat W$, so that $\lambda\in[\lambda_-,\lambda_+]$. Then $p''_{K,\infty}(J)=\lambda^4\hat p''_{\hat K,\infty}(\lambda J)$ and
\[D_K''(J)\le\lambda^4\hat D''_{\hat K}(\lambda J)+c_2|J| .\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof]
By Lem.~\ref{C-365-16}~(b), $p_{K,\infty}(b)=L^{3K}P(L^Kb)$ and $\hat p_{\hat K,\infty}(\hat b)=\hat L^{3\hat K}P(\hat L^{\hat K}\hat b)$ with one convex $P$; for $J=[y_1,y_2]$, $p''_{K,\infty}(J)=L^{4K}[P'(L^Ky_2+)-P'(L^Ky_1-)]=\lambda^4\hat p''_{\hat K,\infty}(\lambda J)$, since $\hat L^{\hat K}\lambda=L^K$. With $\mathsf r_1=p''_{K,\ell'}$, $\mathsf r_2=\hat p''_{\hat K,\hat\ell'}$ this gives $D''_K(J)-\lambda^4\hat D''_{\hat K}(\lambda J)=\int_J[\lambda^5\mathsf r_2(\lambda b)-\mathsf r_1(b)]\,\mathrm{d}b$, and both $\mathsf r_1(b)$ and $\lambda^5\mathsf r_2(\lambda b)$ are $a_K^{-5}(\text{box})^{-3}$ times a variance of the action at the one coupling $\beta=L^Kb=\hat L^{\hat K}\lambda b$. In the units of the second frame the tent becomes $\chi(\cdot/\lambda)$, $\hat{\mathcal O}=\lambda^{-1}\mathcal O$ and $S_2=\lambda^2\hat S_2$; the sum rule of Lem.~\ref{C-365-25} holds on both reference boxes, as $6\lambda\varsigma_7<\hat\ell'$.

The far parts are bounded by $c_F$ and $\hat c_F$, the bound of (M8) reading of the functions only the spread $\lambda\varsigma_7\ge\lambda_-\varsigma_7$ and the norms $\le\hat{\mathsf c}_8$. For the near parts take $\nu\in\mathcal G^{\rm per}$ at $(a_K,\beta)$, which exists by (M9), and its image $\hat\nu$ under the dilation by the real factor $\lambda$, a periodic Gibbs state at $(\hat a_{\hat K},\beta)$ by Lem.~\ref{C-365-26}, with $S_2[\nu](\chi,\eta)=\lambda^2\hat S_2[\hat\nu](\chi(\cdot/\lambda),\eta(\cdot/\lambda))$; by the passage in each frame both pairs are first-passage data, and the transfer in each frame between the reference torus and the state ($3\sqrt3\lambda\varsigma_7\le2$) gives
\[|\lambda^5\mathsf r_2(\lambda b)-\mathsf r_1(b)|\le\varsigma_7^{-3}\bigl[c_T\mathsf c_7^2+\lambda_+^2\hat c_T\hat{\mathsf c}_8^2+c_F+\lambda_+^2\hat c_F\bigr]=c_2 .\qedhere\]
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[No pile of specific heat]\label{C-365-28}
In a Setting, with $(g_1,W_1,W')$ and $\operatorname{dist}(W',\partial W_1)=\varepsilon$: for every $0<\delta\le\delta_{\max}$ there is an integer $K^\circ$ with
\[\mu_K(I)\le C_\flat(|I|+\delta)\qquad\text{for all }K\ge K^\circ\text{ and all closed intervals or points }I\subset W'.\]
So $K_1(\delta)$ of Def.~\ref{C-365-7} exists, and it does not increase in $\delta$. Of the convergence on fixed tori (item (M8)) the proof reads two clauses, both at $n=2$, for pairs with disjoint supports and without a rate: (1) the convergence in the cutoff, uniformly in the label, of the cumulant $S^T_2$ at the pair $(\chi,1-\eta)$ on the tori $T_\ell$, $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g_1)$, $\ell\ge\ell'$, over $W_1$, and at the pair of the tent and the plateau of half-width $1/\hat L$ on the tori $T_{\hat\ell}$, $\hat\ell\in\hat{\mathfrak L}(\hat g)$, $\hat\ell\ge\hat\ell'$, over $\hat W$; (2) the bound clause, which gives $c_F$, for the one pair $(\chi,1-\eta)$ on $T_{\ell'}$ over $W_1$, and $\hat c_F$ on $T_{\hat\ell'}$, uniformly in $\hat K\ge1$, in $\hat b\in\hat W$ and in the pairs $(\chi(\cdot/\lambda),1-\eta(\cdot/\lambda))$, $\lambda\in[\lambda_-,\lambda_+]$, whose spread $\lambda\varsigma_7\ge\lambda_-\varsigma_7$ and whose norms $\le\hat{\mathsf c}_8$ are all that the clause reads of them. Thus on $T_{\hat\ell'}$ two kinds of pairs are read: the pair of half-width $1/\hat L$ through the convergence, and the family of the dilated pairs through the bound.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof]
\emph{Thresholds.} In the first frame Lem.~\ref{C-365-25} is used with $g_1$, $W_1$, $\ell'$ and $k_7$ of Def.~\ref{C-365-7}. Take $\ell(\delta)\in\mathfrak L(g_1)$, $\ell(\delta)\ge\ell'$, with $24\ell'B'/(\delta\ell(\delta))\le\delta/2$, and an integer $K^\circ\ge k_7$ with $\omega_{\ell(\delta)}(K,K'')+\omega_{\ell'}(K,K'')\le1/6$ for all $K,K''\ge K^\circ$ (Lem.~\ref{C-365-25}~(ii)). In the second frame Lem.~\ref{C-365-25} is used with $\hat g$, $\hat W$, $\hat\ell'$ and $\hat k_7=1$, so that the tent and the plateau have the half-width $1/\hat L\le2/(3\sqrt3)$ there and the constant of the near parts is $\hat c_N$. Put $\hat\delta=\lambda_+\delta$; take $\hat\ell\in\hat{\mathfrak L}(\hat g)$, $\hat\ell\ge\hat\ell'$, with
\[\frac{24\hat\ell'\hat B'}{\hat\delta\hat\ell}\le\frac\delta2,\]
and an integer $\hat K_*\ge1$ with $\hat\omega_{\hat\ell}(\hat K,\hat K'')+\hat\omega_{\hat\ell'}(\hat K,\hat K'')\le1/(10\lambda_+)$ for all $\hat K,\hat K''\ge\hat K_*$. \emph{One interval.} Let $I=[y-\delta/2,y+\delta/2]$, $y\in W'$, $J=I^{+\delta}\subset\operatorname{int}W_1$, $K\ge K^\circ$. Let $R=\lfloor|\hat W|/(12\lambda_+\delta)\rfloor\ge|\hat W|/(24\lambda_+\delta)$ and $t_r=\hat w_-+|\hat W|/4+(r-\frac12)6\lambda_+\delta$, $r=1,\dots,R$. As $\log L/\log\hat L$ is irrational, Kronecker's theorem gives integers $K''_r\ge K^\circ$ and $\hat K_r\ge\hat K_*$ with
\[\bigl|\lambda_ry-t_r\bigr|<\lambda_+\delta/2,\qquad\lambda_r=L^{K''_r}/\hat L^{\hat K_r};\]
then $\lambda_r\in[\lambda_-,\lambda_+]$, and the intervals $\mathsf I_r=(\lambda_rJ)^{+\hat\delta}$ are pairwise disjoint and lie in the middle half of $\hat W$. \emph{The chain.} Lem.~\ref{C-365-25}~(iii) in the first frame, for $I$ with the margin $\delta$ and the side $\ell(\delta)$, from $K$ to $K''_r$: $\mu_K(I)\le\mu_{K''_r}(J)+3\delta(2c_N+\frac16)+\frac\delta2=\mu_{K''_r}(J)+(6c_N+1)\delta$. Lem.~\ref{C-365-27} between the frames, with $\hat D''\le\hat\mu$ (as $\hat C_0\ge0$), $\hat\mu\ge0$ and $\lambda_r\le\lambda_+$: $\mu_{K''_r}(J)=D''_{K''_r}(J)+3C_0\delta\le\lambda_+^4\hat\mu_{\hat K_r}(\lambda_rJ)+3(c_2+C_0)\delta$. Lem.~\ref{C-365-25}~(iii) in the second frame, for the interval $\lambda_rJ$, of length $3\lambda_r\delta\le3\lambda_+\delta$, with the margin $\hat\delta$ and the side $\hat\ell$, from $\hat K_r$ to the one cutoff $\hat K_*$, whose added terms are at most $5\lambda_+\delta\,(2\hat c_N+\frac1{10\lambda_+})+\frac\delta2=10\lambda_+\hat c_N\delta+\delta$: $\hat\mu_{\hat K_r}(\lambda_rJ)\le\hat\mu_{\hat K_*}(\mathsf I_r)+10\lambda_+\hat c_N\delta+\delta$. Together:
\[\mu_K(I)\le\lambda_+^4\bigl[\hat\mu_{\hat K_*}(\mathsf I_r)+10\lambda_+\hat c_N\delta+\delta\bigr]+\bigl[6c_N+3(c_2+C_0)+1\bigr]\delta\qquad\text{for every }r.\]
Take the mean over $r$: the $\mathsf I_r$ are pairwise disjoint and lie in the middle half of $\hat W$, whose mass for $\hat\mu_{\hat K_*}$ is at most $8\hat B'/|\hat W|+\frac34\hat C_0|\hat W|\le\hat{\mathfrak m}$ by the mass bound of Prop.~\ref{C-365-21}~(b) in the second frame at $t=|\hat W|/4$; so $R^{-1}\sum_r\hat\mu_{\hat K_*}(\mathsf I_r)\le\hat{\mathfrak m}/R\le24\lambda_+\hat{\mathfrak m}\delta/|\hat W|$. This is $\mu_K(I)\le C_\flat\delta$. \emph{Any closed $I\subset W'$} is covered by at most $|I|/\delta+1$ such intervals. The property at $\delta$ implies it at every $\delta'>\delta$, so $K_1$ does not increase.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The labels; the exact dilation]\label{C-365-29}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[beginpenalty=10000]
\item[(i)] If $W\subset I(g)$ is nonempty and compact, then $W\subset\operatorname{int}I(g_1)$ for every $g_1<g$ with $g_1^{-2}+\bar B<\min W$, and such $g_1$ exist.
\item[(ii)] Every $b>\gamma^{-2}+\bar B$ lies in $\operatorname{int}I(g_2)$ for some $g_2\le\gamma$; hence for every $b_\infty>0$ there are an integer $s\ge0$ and $g_2\le\gamma$ with $L^sb_\infty\in\operatorname{int}I(g_2)$.
\item[(iii)] For integers $0\le s\le K$ the dilation $x\mapsto L^sx$ carries $\mathbb L_K$ onto $\mathbb L_{K-s}$, $\mathcal G^{\rm per}_{K,\beta}$ onto $\mathcal G^{\rm per}_{K-s,\beta}$, $T_\ell$ at the cutoff $K$ with its law onto $T_{L^s\ell}$ at the cutoff $K-s$, boards of side $q$ onto boards of side $L^sq$, $\mathfrak P_T(\square_c)$ onto $\mathfrak P_{L^sT}(L^s\square_c)$ by $\tilde f=f(\cdot/L^s)$, and the label $b$ into $L^sb$; and $x_c=L^{4s}\tilde x_c$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof]
(i) $I(g)$ is open on the left and $W$ is compact, so $\min W>g^{-2}+\bar B$; for $g_1^{-2}\in(g^{-2},\min W-\bar B)$ one has $g_1<g$, $g_1^{-2}+\bar B<\min W$ and $X_{g_1}-\bar B>X_g-\bar B\ge\max W$. (ii) Put $g_2^{-2}=b-\bar B-\epsilon$ with $\epsilon=\min\{1,b-\bar B-\gamma^{-2}\}$; then $g_2\le\gamma$ and $g_2^{-2}+\bar B<b$, and since $L(\bar B-B_\sharp)=\bar B$,
\[X_{g_2}-\bar B>b\iff(L-1)b>2\bar B+L\epsilon;\]
as $b>4+\bar B$ (because $\gamma\le\frac12$), $(L-1)b>4(L-1)+(L-1)\bar B\ge L+2\bar B\ge L\epsilon+2\bar B$. For $b_\infty>0$ take $s$ with $L^sb_\infty>\gamma^{-2}+\bar B$. (iii) The dilation is a graph isomorphism of the lattices, the Wilson weight reads the graph and $\beta$ alone, so the laws of the tori correspond, and the periodic Gibbs states correspond by (M9); $\beta=L^Kb=L^{K-s}(L^sb)$; $\tilde{\mathcal O}_{K-s}(\tilde f)=a_{K-s}^{-1}\sum_pf(x(p))a_p=L^{-s}\mathcal O_K(f)$, hence $\tilde x_c=(L^sq)^{-3}\tilde{\mathcal O}(\tilde f)=L^{-4s}x_c$; the collars and the Lipschitz constant scale with $L^s$, and offsets in $a_K\mathbb Z^3$ go to offsets in $a_{K-s}\mathbb Z^3$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The K\"all\'en--Lehmann form]\label{C-365-30}
Let $\sigma'$ be the limit $\sigma$ of a convergent Gibbs sequence or a component $\sigma_\xi$ of it, and $\mathbf s$ its radial kernel.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] $\mathbf s$ is completely monotone on $(0,\infty)$; so $\mathbf s\ge0$ does not increase, and $\kappa'=\lim_{r\to\infty}\mathbf s(r)\in[0,\infty)$ exists.
\item[(b)] $r\mapsto r(\mathbf s(r)-\kappa')$ is completely monotone; there is exactly one positive Borel measure $\rho$ on $[0,\infty)$ with $\mathbf s(r)=\kappa'+\int e^{-mr}(4\pi r)^{-1}\,\mathrm{d}\rho(m)$.
\item[(c)] $\rho(\{0\})=\lim_{r\to\infty}4\pi r(\mathbf s(r)-\kappa')$, and $\rho([0,m])\le4\pi e\,m^{-1}(\mathbf s(1/m)-\kappa')$ for $m>0$.
\item[(d)] \emph{Cube means, with no further hypothesis.} Let $T\ge\max\{T_0,\mathsf l\}$, $q=L^i\ge2T$, a board of $\mathbb R^3$ of side $q$ (a partition of $\mathbb R^3$ into the cubes $\square_c$ of side $q$ centred at the points $o+qc$, $c\in\mathbb Z^3$, with an offset $o\in\mathbb R^3$; $c$ is the index of the cell) and profiles $f_c\in\mathfrak P_T(\square_c)$, $f_{c'}\in\mathfrak P_T(\square_{c'})$ of two distinct cells be given. For every $0<r_0\le T/4$
\[0\le q^{-6}\Bigl[\sigma'(f_c,f_{c'})-\kappa'\int f_c\int f_{c'}\Bigr]\le24\pi\,r_0\bigl(\mathbf s(r_0)-\kappa'\bigr)/q,\]
and if the two cells share a face, the middle member is $\ge\rho(\{0\})(1-T/q)^6/(4\sqrt6\,\pi q)$. So $q$ times the middle member tends to $0$ as $q\to\infty$, uniformly in the pairs of distinct cells and in the profiles, if and only if $\rho(\{0\})=0$.
\item[(e)] \emph{The converse; the measure that attains the bounds.} The following are equivalent: (i) there are $T\ge\max\{T_0,\mathsf l\}$, $C$ and $j_0$ with $L^{j_0}\ge2T$ and $\sigma'(\theta w_i,w_i)\le C(T/q_i)^2$ for all $i\ge j_0$, the $w_i$ of Def.~\ref{C-365-4}~(7) being formed with this $T$; (ii) $\mathbf s(r)=O(r^{-2})$ as $r\to\infty$; (iii) $\kappa'=0$ and $\rho([0,m])=O(m)$ as $m\to0$; (iv) there are $A_\mu$ and $r_*>0$ with $\mu_h(Q_r)\le A_\mu\|h\|_1^2r^2$ for every real $h\in C^1_c(\mathbb E_+)$ and $0<r\le r_*$, $\mu_h$ formed in $\mathcal H(\sigma',e_3)$. Under them $\rho(\{0\})=0$, so that $\rho\ge\mathsf Z\delta_0$ with $\mathsf Z>0$ is excluded, and so is $\rho([0,m])\ge c_\rho m^\vartheta$ for all small $m$ with $c_\rho>0$ and $\vartheta<1$; the measure $\rho=c_\rho\,\mathrm{d}m$ on $[0,\infty)$, $c_\rho>0$, whose kernel is $\mathbf s(r)=c_\rho/(4\pi r^2)$, satisfies (ii) and (iii) and attains both bounds in order.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof]
We use Bernstein's theorem (a function on $(0,\infty)$ is completely monotone if and only if it is $\int e^{-tE}\,\mathrm{d}\mu(E)$ with a unique positive $\mu$), that $-c'$ is completely monotone with $c$, and that a pointwise finite limit of completely monotone functions is completely monotone (Helly's theorem applied to the measures $e^{-t_0E}d\mu_n$). (a) By (M10), $\sigma'$ is invariant under $\mathbb R^3\rtimes\mathrm O(3)$ and reflection positive, so the reconstruction applies: for $f_\epsilon(x)=\eta_\epsilon(x_3)\mathsf g(x_1,x_2)$ with $0\le\eta_\epsilon\in C^1_c((s-\epsilon,s+\epsilon))$ of mass $1$ and real $\mathsf g\in C^1_c(\mathbb R^2)$, $c_\epsilon(t)=\sigma'(\theta f_\epsilon,\tau_{te_3}f_\epsilon)=\int e^{-tE}d\mu_{f_\epsilon}$ is completely monotone, and by the kernel it tends to $\mathsf P_{\mathsf g}(2s+t)$, $\mathsf P_{\mathsf g}(u)=\iint\mathsf g(y)\mathsf g(y')\mathbf s((u^2+|y-y'|^2)^{1/2})\,\mathrm{d}y\,\mathrm{d}y'$; letting $\mathsf g$ tend to a point mass gives (a). (b) For a radial $\mathsf g\ne0$ put $G=\mathsf g*\mathsf g$, with radial profile $\hat G$, and $\mathsf g_R=R^{-1}\mathsf g(\cdot/R)$, so that $\mathsf P_R(u)=2\pi\int_0^\infty\hat G(\varrho'/R)\mathbf s((u^2+\varrho'^2)^{1/2})\varrho'd\varrho'$; with $\partial_u\mathbf s((u^2+\varrho'^2)^{1/2})=(u/\varrho')\partial_{\varrho'}\mathbf s((u^2+\varrho'^2)^{1/2})$ one integration by parts gives
\[-\mathsf P_R'(u)=2\pi u\Bigl[\hat G(0)\mathbf s(u)+\int_0^\infty\hat G'(v)\,\mathbf s((u^2+R^2v^2)^{1/2})\,\mathrm{d}v\Bigr]\ \longrightarrow\ 2\pi\hat G(0)\,u\,(\mathbf s(u)-\kappa')\qquad(R\to\infty),\]
and $-\mathsf P_R'$ is completely monotone; Bernstein's theorem gives $\rho$, normalised so that $4\pi r(\mathbf s(r)-\kappa')=\int e^{-mr}\,\mathrm{d}\rho(m)$. (c) Monotone convergence, and $\int e^{-mr}\,\mathrm{d}\rho(m)\ge e^{-1}\rho([0,1/r])$. (d) As $\mathbf s\ge\kappa'$ and $f_c,f_{c'}\ge0$, the middle member is $q^{-6}\iint f_c(x)f_{c'}(y)(\mathbf s(|x-y|)-\kappa')\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y\ge0$. The supports are at distance $\ge T/4\ge r_0$, where $\mathbf s(|x-y|)-\kappa'\le r_0(\mathbf s(r_0)-\kappa')/|x-y|$, since $r(\mathbf s(r)-\kappa')$ does not increase by (b); and with $0\le f_c,f_{c'}\le1$ on the cells, $u=(y-x)/q$ and the tent $\chi_{\mathbf d}(u)=\prod_\mu(1-|u_\mu-d_\mu|)_+$ about the difference $\mathbf d\ne0$ of the indices of the two cells, $q^{-6}\iint_{\square_c\times\square_{c'}}|x-y|^{-1}\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y=q^{-1}\int\chi_{\mathbf d}(u)|u|^{-1}\,\mathrm{d}u$, which is $\le q^{-1}$ if $|\mathbf d|_\infty\ge2$ and $\le q^{-1}\int_{|u|\le2\sqrt3}|u|^{-1}du=24\pi/q$ otherwise.

For cells that share a face, $4\pi r(\mathbf s(r)-\kappa')=\int e^{-mr}\,\mathrm{d}\rho\ge\rho(\{0\})$, the profiles are $1$ on the concentric cubes of side $q-T$, and two points of these cubes are at distance $\le\sqrt6q$. If $\rho(\{0\})=0$, then $r(\mathbf s(r)-\kappa')\le\epsilon_1$ for $r\ge r_{\epsilon_1}$, and the pairs of points of $\square_c\times\square_{c'}$ at distance $<r_{\epsilon_1}$ have measure $\le8\pi q^2r_{\epsilon_1}^4$; so $q$ times the middle member is $\le24\pi\epsilon_1+8\pi(\mathbf s(T/4)-\kappa')r_{\epsilon_1}^4q^{-3}$, for every $\epsilon_1>0$. (e) (i) gives (ii): $\theta w_i,w_i\ge0$ have disjoint supports in a box of diameter $\sqrt6q_i$, $\int w_i\ge(1-3T/(4q_i))^3$, and $\mathbf s$ does not increase, so $C(T/q_i)^2\ge\sigma'(\theta w_i,w_i)\ge\mathbf s(\sqrt6q_i)(1-3T/(4q_i))^6$; for $\sqrt6q_i\le r<\sqrt6q_{i+1}$, $\mathbf s(r)\le\mathbf s(\sqrt6q_i)$ and $q_i^{-2}<6L^2/r^2$. (ii) gives (i): if $\mathbf s(r)\le A_{\mathbf s}r^{-2}$ for $r\ge r_0$, take $T\ge\max\{T_0,\mathsf l,4r_0\}$; the supports of $\theta w_i$ and $w_i$ are at distance $\ge T/4\ge r_0$, so $\sigma'(\theta w_i,w_i)\le A_{\mathbf s}q_i^{-2}\int\chi_{e_3}(u)|u|^{-2}\,\mathrm{d}u\le3\pi A_{\mathbf s}q_i^{-2}$, as $\chi_{e_3}(u)\le u_3$ on its support, which lies in $\{|u|\le\sqrt6,\ u_3>0\}$. (ii) gives (iii) by (c). (iii) gives (ii): if $\kappa'=0$ and $\rho([0,m])\le C_\rho m$ for $0<m\le m_0$, then $e^{-mr}=e^{-m_0r}+r\int_m^{m_0}e^{-ur}du$ and Fubini give $\int_{[0,m_0]}e^{-mr}d\rho(m)\le C_\rho m_0e^{-m_0r}+C_\rho/r$, and for $r\ge1$ the rest of $4\pi r\mathbf s(r)$ is $\le e^{-m_0(r-1)}4\pi\mathbf s(1)$. (iii) and (iv): for real $h\in C^1_c(\mathbb E_+)$ the kernel, the form (b) and the formula
\[\frac{e^{-m\sqrt{\tau^2+|w|^2}}}{4\pi\sqrt{\tau^2+|w|^2}}=\int_{\mathbb R^2}e^{i\mathsf q\cdot w}\,\frac{e^{-\tau\omega_m(\mathsf q)}}{2\omega_m(\mathsf q)}\,\frac{d^2\mathsf q}{(2\pi)^2},\qquad\omega_m(\mathsf q)=(m^2+|\mathsf q|^2)^{1/2},\ \tau>0,\ w\in\mathbb R^2,\]
give for $t\ge0$ and $v\perp e_3$
\[\langle\psi_h,e^{-tH}\mathcal U(v)\psi_h\rangle=\sigma'(\theta h,\tau_{te_3+v}h)=\kappa'\Bigl(\int h\Bigr)^2+\int \,\mathrm{d}\rho(m)\int e^{-t\omega_m(\mathsf q)-iv\cdot\mathsf q}\,\frac{|\hat h_m(\mathsf q)|^2}{2\omega_m(\mathsf q)}\,\frac{d^2\mathsf q}{(2\pi)^2},\]
with $\hat h_m(\mathsf q)=\int h(y)e^{-\omega_m(\mathsf q)y_3+i\mathsf q\cdot y_\perp}\,\mathrm{d}y$; as a finite measure on $[0,\infty)\times\mathbb R^2$ is determined by its transform, $\mu_h$ is $\kappa'(\int h)^2\delta_{(0,0)}$ plus the images under $\mathsf q\mapsto(\omega_m(\mathsf q),-\mathsf q)$ of the measures $|\hat h_m|^2(2\omega_m)^{-1}d^2\mathsf q/(2\pi)^2$, integrated in $d\rho(m)$. As $|\hat h_m|\le\|h\|_1$ and $\int_{\omega_m(\mathsf q)\le r}(2\omega_m(\mathsf q))^{-1}d^2\mathsf q/(2\pi)^2=(r-m)_+/(4\pi)$, this gives $\mu_h(Q_r)\le\kappa'\|h\|_1^2+(4\pi)^{-1}r\,\rho([0,r])\|h\|_1^2$, so (iii) gives (iv). Conversely, take $0\le h\ne0$ with support in $\{y_3\le R_h,\ |y_\perp|\le R_h\}$ and $r\le\min\{r_*,1/(2R_h)\}$: the points $(\omega_m(\mathsf q),-\mathsf q)$ with $m\le r/2$ and $|\mathsf q|\le r/2$ lie in $Q_r$, and there $|\hat h_m(\mathsf q)|\ge e^{-1}\cos(\frac12)\|h\|_1$; so $A_\mu\|h\|_1^2r^2\ge\mu_h(Q_r)\ge\kappa'\|h\|_1^2+e^{-2}\cos^2(\frac12)(32\pi)^{-1}r\,\rho([0,r/2])\|h\|_1^2$, which gives (iii). Under (iii), $\rho(\{0\})\le\rho([0,m])\to0$ as $m\to0$; and $\int_0^\infty e^{-mr}c_\rho\,\mathrm{d}m/(4\pi r)=c_\rho/(4\pi r^2)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Three mirrors; the spectral form]\label{C-365-31}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[beginpenalty=10000]
\item[(a)] Let $\sigma'$ be a real, symmetric, normalized functional on $\mathfrak S(\mathbb R^3)$, multilinear on products of test spaces with disjoint closures, whose one-point function is $\sigma'(f)=c\int f$ and whose connected functions obey a bound table as in Section~\YMMref{90}{695}. Assume that $\sigma'$ is invariant under the translations of $\mathbb R^3$ and reflection positive at the three coordinate mirrors through $0$; let $X,Y\in\mathfrak S(\mathbb R^3)$ have their supports in $\{|x|_\infty<R\}$ and $G(a)=\sigma'(X\cdot\tau_aY)$. Then $G(a)$ converges as $\min_\mu a_\mu\to\infty$, jointly in the three coordinates, to $\langle[\theta X_0],\mathcal P(\{0\})[Y_0]\rangle$ in $\mathcal H(\sigma',e_3)$, with $X_0=\tau_{-(R+\frac12)e_3}X$ and $Y_0=\tau_{(R+\frac12)e_3}Y$; likewise in each of the eight orthants, $X$ and $Y$ being exchanged in the directions in which $a_\mu\to-\infty$.
\item[(b)] Let $\sigma'$ obey a bound table with one-point constant $0$, be invariant under the translations of $\mathbb R^3$ and reflection positive at $(e_3,0)$, and let $\sigma'(\theta w_i,w_i)\le C_{\rm LH}(T/q_i)^2$ for $i\ge j_0$, with $q_{j_0}\ge2T$. Then for real $h\in C^1_c(\mathbb E_+)$
\[\mu_h(Q_r)\le12.46\,(1-3T/(4q_{j_0}))^{-6}L^2C_{\rm LH}\|h\|_1^2T^2r^2\quad(0<r\le1/q_{j_0}),\qquad\mathcal P(\{0\})\psi_h=0 .\]
\end{enumerate}
Neither the cubic group nor $\mathrm O(3)$ nor a kernel is used.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof]
(a) In the picture $e_3$, for $t=a_3-2R-1\ge0$, translation invariance and the reconstruction give $G(a)=\langle[\theta X_0],e^{-tH}\mathcal U(a_\perp)[Y_0]\rangle=\int e^{-tE+ia_\perp\cdot\mathsf q}\,\mathrm{d}m_3$, $m_3=\langle[\theta X_0],\mathcal P(\cdot)[Y_0]\rangle$, so $\sup_{a_\perp}|G(a)-G_3(a_\perp)|\le\varepsilon_3(t)=\int_{E>0}e^{-tE}d|m_3|\downarrow0$, with $G_3(a_\perp)$ the part at $E=0$; the same in the pictures $e_1$, $e_2$. Changing one coordinate at a time between two points with all coordinates $\ge A$,
\[|G(a)-G(a')|\le2\sum_\mu\varepsilon_\mu(A-2R-1)\to0,\]
so $G$ converges; its limit is the limit of the Ces\`aro means $A^{-3}\int_{[A,2A]^3}G$, whose three brackets in the picture $e_3$ tend to $1_{E=0}$, $1_{\mathsf q_1=0}$, $1_{\mathsf q_2=0}$, giving $m_3(\{(0,0,0)\})$. In the other orthants write $G(a)=\sigma'(\tau_{-a}X\cdot Y)$. (b) Let $w=w_i$, $q=q_i$, $i\ge j_0$; $w\ge0$ has its support in $\{T/4\le x_3\le q-T/4\}$. The convolution $w*h=\int w(y)\tau_yh\,\mathrm{d}y=\int h(y)\tau_yw\,\mathrm{d}y$ is read twice, the Riemann sums converging in $\|\cdot\|_\sharp$ and $h\mapsto\psi_h$ being linear and bounded by the bound table:
\[
\begin{multlined}
\psi_{w*h}=\mathsf G_w(H,P)\psi_h,\quad\mathsf G_w(E,\mathsf q)=\int w(y)e^{-y_3E+iy_\perp\cdot\mathsf q}\,\mathrm{d}y,\qquad\psi_{w*h} \\
=\int h(y)e^{-y_3H}\mathcal U(y_\perp)\psi_w\,\mathrm{d}y .
\end{multlined}
\]
The operators $e^{-tH}\mathcal U(v)$ are contractions, so 
\[
\int|\mathsf G_w|^2d\mu_h=\|\psi_{w*h}\|^2\le\|h\|_1^2\sigma'(\theta w,w)\le\|h\|_1^2C_{\rm LH}(T/q)^2.
\]
On $Q_{1/q}$, as $\varphi_0$ is even, 
\[
\mathsf G_w=q^{-3}\int\varphi_0(y_3-\frac q2)e^{-y_3E}\,\mathrm{d}y_3\prod_{k=1,2}\int\varphi_0(y_k)\cos(y_k\mathsf q_k)\,\mathrm{d}y_k\ge e^{-1}\cos^2(\tfrac12)(1-3T/(4q))^3;
\]
and $e^2/\cos^4(\frac12)\approx12.4577$. For $1/(Lq_i)<r\le1/q_i$, $\mu_h(Q_r)\le\mu_h(Q_{1/q_i})$ and $q_i^{-2}<L^2r^2$. Finally $\|\mathcal P(\{0\})\psi_h\|^2=\mu_h(\{0\})\le\mu_h(Q_r)\to0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Limits of Gibbs sequences, with free constants]\label{C-365-32}
Let a frame, $0<g'\le\gamma$, $T\ge\max\{T_0,\mathsf l\}$ and numbers $C_{\rm LH},c_{\rm LH},q_{\rm LH}>0$ be given, and let $(K_j,\beta_j,\nu_j)$ be a convergent Gibbs sequence at $g'$ with the following property: for every $q=L^i\ge\max\{2T,q_{\rm LH}\}$ there is $j(q)$ such that for all $j\ge j(q)$, all $\nu,\nu'\in\mathcal G^{\rm per}_{K_j,\beta_j}$, every board of $\mathbb L_{K_j}$ of side $q$ with any offset and profiles of $\mathfrak P_T$ in two distinct cells $c,c'$: $|\operatorname{Cov}_\nu(x_c,x_{c'})|\le C_{\rm LH}(T/q)^2$ and $|\nu(x_c)-\nu'(x_c)|\le c_{\rm LH}T/q$. Then the conclusions 1--9 of Thm.~\ref{C-365-8}~(c) hold for $\sigma$ and every $\sigma_\xi$, with $C_{\rm LH}$ in the place of $C_2$, $L^{j_0}\ge\max\{2T,q_{\rm LH}\}$, $r_0=\sqrt6L^{j_0}$ and $C_{\mathbf s}=6L^2(1-3T/(4L^{j_0}))^{-6}C_{\rm LH}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof]
\emph{The pair of cells.} Fix $q=q_i\ge\max\{2T,q_{\rm LH}\}$. On the board of $\mathbb L_{K_j}$ of side $q$ with the offset $(0,0,\frac12q+\frac12a_{K_j})$, which lies in $a_{K_j}\mathbb Z^3$ because $q/a_{K_j}$ is odd, the two cells with the centres $(0,0,\pm\frac12q+\frac12a_{K_j})$ have a common face, and $f_0(\cdot\mp\frac12qe_3)$ is moved from them by $\frac12a_{K_j}\le T/8$ for large $j$; so, $\varphi_0$ being even, $\mathcal O(w_i)$ and $\mathcal O(\theta w_i)$ are cube means $x_c$, $x_{c'}$ of two distinct cells. \emph{The lattice bounds pass to $\sigma$ and to every $\sigma_\xi$}, because they name the pair $(K_j,\beta_j)$ alone and so hold for the $\nu_j$ and for the approximants $\rho_j$ of $\sigma_\xi$:
\[\mathfrak c_\xi\int w_i=\sigma_\xi((w_i))=\lim_j(\rho_j-\nu_j)(x_c),\qquad|(\rho_j-\nu_j)(x_c)|\le c_{\rm LH}T/q,\qquad\int w_i\ge(1-\tfrac{3T}{4q})^3\ge(\tfrac58)^3,\]
for every $q$ above the floor, so $\mathfrak c_\xi=0$; this is shown before the kernel is used, so that $S^{\sigma'}_2(f,h)=\sigma'(f,h)$. Further $S^\sigma_2(\theta w_i,w_i)=\lim_j\operatorname{Cov}_{\nu_j}(x_{c'},x_c)$ and $\sigma_\xi(\theta w_i,w_i)=\lim_j[\operatorname{Cov}_{\rho_j}(x_{c'},x_c)+(\rho_j-\nu_j)(x_{c'})(\rho_j-\nu_j)(x_c)]$, whose second term tends to $0$; this is conclusion 2. \emph{From two cells with a common face to the kernel.} By Prop.~\ref{C-365-30}, $\mathbf s\ge0$ does not increase; $\theta w_i$, $w_i\ge0$ have disjoint supports in a box of diameter $\sqrt6q$, so $C_{\rm LH}(T/q_i)^2\ge\sigma'(\theta w_i,w_i)\ge\mathbf s(\sqrt6q_i)(1-3T/(4q_i))^6$; for $r\ge r_0$ take $i\ge j_0$ with $\sqrt6q_i\le r<\sqrt6Lq_i$, so $q_i^{-2}<6L^2/r^2$ and $\mathbf s(r)\le C_{\mathbf s}T^2/r^2$.

Hence $\kappa'=0$, conclusion 3 is Prop.~\ref{C-365-30}~(b), conclusion 5 follows from $|x-y|\ge|a|-R_f-R_h\ge r_0$ on the supports, and 6, 7 from Prop.~\ref{C-365-30}~(c). \emph{One field.} For real $h\in C^1_c(\mathbb E_+)$, $\|e^{-tH}\psi_h\|^2=\sigma'(\theta h,\tau_{2te_3}h)\le\|h\|_1^2\mathbf s(2t)$, the supports being at distance $\ge2t$; so $e^{-tH}\psi_h\to0$, which kills the projection on $\ker H$; $\int_0^\infty\langle\psi_h,e^{-tH}\psi_h\rangle\,\mathrm{d}t=\|H^{-1/2}\psi_h\|^2$ is finite by the bound at large $t$; and $e^{-2}\langle\psi_h,1_{[0,\epsilon]}(H)\psi_h\rangle\le\|e^{-H/\epsilon}\psi_h\|^2$. For conclusion 9 rotate $a$ to the $e_3$ axis by $\mathrm O(3)$ and put $X_0=\tau_{-(R_X+1)e_3}X$, $h_0=\tau_{(R_h+1)e_3}h$, $t=|a|-R_X-R_h-2$:
\[\sigma'(X\cdot\tau_ah)=\langle[\theta X_0],e^{-tH}\psi_{h_0}\rangle,\qquad|\sigma'(X\cdot\tau_ah)|\le\|[\theta X_0]\|\,\|e^{-tH}\psi_{h_0}\|\le\mathsf N(X)\|h\|_1C_{\mathbf s}^{1/2}T/(2t),\]
where $\|[\theta X_0]\|^2=\sigma'(X\cdot\theta_{e_3}X)\le\mathsf N(X)^2$, finite by the bound tables since the supports of $X\cdot\theta_uX$ lie in one ball and those of $X$ and $\theta_uX$ are at distance $\ge2$;
in the moment--cumulant formula for $S^{\sigma'}_{n+1}(f_1,\dots,f_n,\tau_ah)$ exactly one factor holds $\tau_ah$, and it is $\sigma'(X_J\cdot\tau_ah)$ for a subtuple $X_J$ or $\sigma'((\tau_ah))=0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Growing tori, with free constants]\label{C-365-33}
Let a frame, $0<g'\le\gamma$, $T\ge\max\{T_0,\mathsf l\}$, numbers $C_{\rm LH},q_{\rm LH}>0$ and $j_0$ with $L^{j_0}\ge\max\{2T,q_{\rm LH}\}$ be given, and let $S$ be a continuum limit at $g'$ along growing tori with a defining sequence $(K_j,\ell_j,\beta_j)$ that has the following property: for every $q=L^i\ge\max\{2T,q_{\rm LH}\}$ there is $j(q)$ such that for all $j\ge j(q)$, $\ell_j\ge2q$ and $|\operatorname{Cov}_{K_j,\ell_j,\beta_j}(x_c,x_{c'})|\le C_{\rm LH}(T/q)^2$ for profiles of $\mathfrak P_T$ in two distinct cells of every board of $T_{\ell_j}$ of side $q$. Then the conclusions 1--3 of Thm.~\ref{C-365-8}~(d) hold with $C_{\rm LH}$ in the place of $C_2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof]
By (M10), $\sigma_S$ obeys a bound table with one-point constant $0$, is invariant under the translations and the cubic group, and is reflection positive at the coordinate mirrors, so Lem.~\ref{C-365-31} applies at $u=e_1,e_2,e_3$. For $q=q_i$ and large $j$, as in the proof of Lem.~\ref{C-365-32} on the board of $T_{\ell_j}$ of side $q$ with the offset $(0,0,\frac12q+\frac12a_{K_j})$ ($2q$ divides $\ell_j$, and the supports lie in $(-\ell_j/4,\ell_j/4)^3$), $\theta w_i$ and $w_i$ are $q^{-3}$ times profiles of two distinct cells, so
\[\sigma_S(\theta w_i,w_i)=S_2(\theta w_i,w_i)=\lim_jS^T_{2;K_j,\ell_j,\beta_j}(\theta w_i,w_i)\le C_{\rm LH}(T/q_i)^2;\]
the cubic group carries this to the mirrors $(e_1,0)$, $(e_2,0)$. The spectral clauses are Lem.~\ref{C-365-31}~(b). For conclusion 3, Lem.~\ref{C-365-31}~(a) at $Y=(h)$ gives the limit $\langle[\theta X_0],\mathcal P(\{0\})\psi_{h_0}\rangle=0$, $h_0=\tau_{(R+\frac12)e_3}h\in C^1_c(\mathbb E_+)$, and $0$ likewise in the other orthants; in the moment--cumulant formula exactly one factor holds $\tau_ah$, and it is $\sigma_S(X_J\cdot\tau_ah)\to0$ or $\sigma_S((\tau_ah))=0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Thm.~\ref{C-365-8}]
\emph{Step 1: the Setting is consistent.} $g_1$ exists by Lem.~\ref{C-365-29}~(i), hence $\varepsilon$ exists; Prop.~\ref{C-365-28} is applied to $(g_1,W_1,W')$, with $\operatorname{dist}(W',\partial W_1)=\varepsilon$. Since $C_w^-\le C_w$, $r_1^-\le r_1$, $C_I\le C_I^+$ and $T\ge T_0$, the floor $q\ge q_0$ gives
\[\text{(f1)}\quad q\ge\frac{4C_\flat+C_I}{9C_w^2T^2},\qquad\text{(f2)}\quad x_q=\frac1{3C_wTq^2}\le\min\{r_1,\varepsilon/2\},\]
so $I_q(b)\subset W'\subset\operatorname{int}I(g_1)$ for $b\in W$, and $\delta=\delta^\circ(q)\le\delta_{\max}$ has $C_\flat\delta\le\frac32C_w^-T_0/q\le\frac32C_wT/q$. The number $C_\flat$ is formed from $\lambda_+$, $\hat{\mathfrak m}$, $\hat c_N$, $c_N$, $c_2$ and $C_0$, none of which depends on $T$.

\emph{Step 2: clause (a).} Let $b\in W$ and $K\ge K_0(q)=K_1(\delta)$. Prop.~\ref{C-365-28} gives $\mu_K(I_q(b))\le C_\flat(2x_q+\delta)$, and $2C_\flat x_q\le\frac32C_wT/q$ is (f1); so
\[\delta_K(q,b)=3C_wT/q+\mu_K(I_q(b))\le6C_wT/q .\]
Prop.~\ref{C-365-24}~(a) at $g_1$ applies, as $q\ge q_1$ by $q\ge2T$, (f1) and (f2): $2e^4\cdot36=72e^4$ and $2e^2\cdot6=12e^2$. The clause names the states at $(K,L^Kb)$, which do not depend on the reference coupling.

\emph{Step 3: clause (b).} Let $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$, $\ell\ge\ell_0(q)\ge\ell'$; as $\mathfrak L(g_1)$ is closed upward, $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g_1)$. $\Psi=D_K+\frac12C_0y^2$ and $\Phi=D_{K,\ell}+\frac12C_0y^2$ are convex on $W_1$ and $0\le\Phi-\Psi\le\bar\eta=\bar\eta(\ell)$. With $\sigma_0=\Psi'(b-)$, $t=(\bar\eta/C_\flat)^{1/2}\le\varepsilon/2$ (this is $\ell\ge12\ell'B'/(C_\flat\varepsilon^2)$) and $0<x\le\varepsilon/2$, the slopes of a convex function do not decrease:
\[\frac{\Phi(b+x)-\Phi(b)}x\le\frac{\Phi(b+x+t)-\Phi(b+x)}t\le\frac{\Psi(b+x+t)-\Psi(b+x)+\bar\eta}t\le\sigma_0+C_\flat(x+t+\delta)+\frac{\bar\eta}t,\]
by Prop.~\ref{C-365-28} on $[b,b+x+t]\subset W'$, and the mirror bound holds on the left; $C_\flat t+\bar\eta/t=2(C_\flat\bar\eta)^{1/2}$. So $D_{K,\ell}$ has the hypothesis of Prop.~\ref{C-365-23} with $\mathsf s=C_0b-\sigma_0$, $\delta_2=2(C_\flat\bar\eta)^{1/2}+C_\flat\delta\ge0$, $\tilde C=C_\flat\ge0$, $\eta_+=0$, $x_0=\varepsilon/2<b$. Its floors are (f1), (f2); $2(3C_\flat\ell'B'/\ell)^{1/2}\le\frac32C_wT/q$ is $\ell\ge\frac{16}3C_\flat\ell'B'q^2/(C_wT)^2$; so $\delta_2\le3C_wT/q$, $\delta\le6C_wT/q$, and the bounds follow as in Step 2.

\emph{Step 4: clause (c).} Take $g'=g$ in Lem.~\ref{C-365-32}. For $q=L^i\ge\max\{2T,q_0\}$ and large $j$ we have $K_j\ge K_0(q)$ and $b_j\in W$; clause (a), which names the pair $(K_j,\beta_j)$ alone, gives the hypothesis of Lem.~\ref{C-365-32} with
\[(C_{\rm LH},c_{\rm LH},q_{\rm LH})=(C_2,\ 12e^2C_w,\ q_0),\]
and its conclusions are clause (c).

\emph{Step 5: clause (d).} Take $g'=g$ in Lem.~\ref{C-365-33}. For $q=L^i\ge\max\{2T,q_0\}$ and large $j$: $K_j\ge K_0(q)$, $b_j\in W$, and $\ell_j\in\mathfrak L(g)$, $\ell_j\ge\ell_0(q)\ge2q$. The two floors do not depend on each other, so no relation between $K_j$ and $\ell_j$ is used, and clause (b) gives the hypothesis of Lem.~\ref{C-365-33} with $(C_{\rm LH},q_{\rm LH})=(C_2,q_0)$; its conclusions are clause (d).

\emph{Step 6: clauses (e)\,1 and (e)\,2.} (e)\,1 is Lem.~\ref{C-365-29}~(ii). For (e)\,2, Lem.~\ref{C-365-29}~(iii) carries the states at $(K,L^Kb)$ and their boards of side $q$ to states at $(K-s,L^{K-s}\cdot L^sb)$ and boards of side $L^sq$, with
\[\operatorname{Cov}_\nu(x_c,x_{c'})=L^{8s}\operatorname{Cov}_{\tilde\nu}(\tilde x_c,\tilde x_{c'}),\qquad\nu(x_c)-\nu'(x_c)=L^{4s}(\tilde\nu-\tilde\nu')(\tilde x_c),\]
and $n$-cell moments carrying $L^{4ns}$; $(L^sT)/(L^sq)=T/q$; apply (a), (b) in the Setting built on $(g_2,W^{(2)})$ at $(L^sT,L^sq,K-s,L^s\ell)$.

\emph{Step 7: clause (e)\,3.} Each $b_\infty\in\mathsf B$ has, by (e)\,1, a pair $(s,g_2)$ and a compact interval $W^{(2)}\subset\operatorname{int}I(g_2)$ holding $L^sb_\infty$ in its interior; finitely many of the open sets $L^{-s}\operatorname{int}W^{(2)}$ cover $\mathsf B$, say $(s_i,g^{(i)},W^{(i)})$, $i\le n_{\mathsf B}$, each with its Setting in the frame $L$ and one second frame for all. Put
\[C_{\mathsf B}=\max_iL^{8s_i}72e^4\bigl(C_w^{+,(i)}\bigr)^2,\quad q_{\mathsf B}=\max_iL^{-s_i}q_0^{(i)},\quad K_{\mathsf B}(q)=\max_i\bigl[s_i+K_0^{(i)}(L^{s_i}q)\bigr],\]
and let $\ell_{\mathsf B}(q)$ be the maximum over $i$ of $L^{-s_i}$ times $\ell_0^{(i)}(L^{s_i}q)$ formed with $C_w^{-,(i)}T_0$ in the place of $C_wT$, which bounds $\ell_0^{(i)}(L^{s_i}q)$ at the width $L^{s_i}T$ because $(L^{s_i}q)^2/(C_wL^{s_i}T)^2=q^2/(C_wT)^2$. None of these depends on $T$. A side $L^{s_i}\ell=2L^{m+s_i}\ge\ell'^{(i)}$ lies in $\mathfrak L(g_1^{(i)})\subset\mathfrak L(g^{(i)})$ by (M5), so (b) at $g^{(i)}$ speaks of it; $T\ge\max\{T_0,\mathsf l\}$ gives $L^{s_i}T\ge\max\{T_0,\mathsf l\}$; and $(2C_{\mathsf B})^{1/2}\ge L^{4s_i}12e^2C_w^{(i)}$. Step 6 gives (e)\,3.

\emph{Step 8: clause (e)\,4.} At $g'\le\gamma$ the labels of every Gibbs sequence, and of every defining sequence of a limit along growing tori, lie in the compact set $\mathsf B=I^{\rm lab}(g')$ by (M5). For $q=L^i\ge\max\{2T,q_{\mathsf B}\}$ and large $j$, $K_j\ge K_{\mathsf B}(q)$ and $\ell_j\ge\ell_{\mathsf B}(q)\ge2q$, so (e)\,3 gives the hypotheses of Lems.~\ref{C-365-32} and~\ref{C-365-33} with
\[(C_{\rm LH},c_{\rm LH},q_{\rm LH})=\bigl(C_{\mathsf B},(2C_{\mathsf B})^{1/2},q_{\mathsf B}\bigr),\]
and these lemmas, in which the theorems on limits are taken at $g'$ itself, give (c) and (d) at $g'$. The lemmas with free constants are needed here: no single window, dilated or not, holds $I^{\rm lab}(g')$, whose ends have a quotient $\ge L$, while the quotient of the ends of $I(g)$ is at most $L$ with the lower end open; so (e)\,4 does not follow from (c), (d) applied to the sequence taken whole, and the only lattice input of (c), (d) is a bound expressed through $(K_j,\beta_j)$ and $\ell_j$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Mean actions are slopes of the pressure; both ends are taken; the plateau]\label{C-365-34}
Let $a>0$ and $\beta>0$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] For $\nu\in\mathcal G^{\rm per}_{a,\beta}$ the number $\mathsf a(\nu)=\nu(a_p)$ is the same for all plaquettes $p$, and $P(\beta+t)-P(\beta)\ge-3\mathsf a(\nu)t$ for all $t>-\beta$; so $-3\mathsf a(\nu)\in[P'(\beta-),P'(\beta+)]$.
\item[(ii)] There are $\nu_\pm\in\mathcal G^{\rm per}_{a,\beta}$ with $-3\mathsf a(\nu_\pm)=P'(\beta\pm)$; so $3\sup\{|\mathsf a(\rho)-\mathsf a(\nu)|:\rho,\nu\in\mathcal G^{\rm per}_{a,\beta}\}=J(\beta)$.
\item[(iii)] At $a=a_K$, for $(K,\beta)\in\mathfrak d(g)$ and $\nu\in\mathcal G^{\rm per}_{K,\beta}$, the function $\mathsf e$ of Thm.~\ref{C-365-9}~(e) exists, takes its values $\nu$-almost surely in $[\inf_\rho\mathsf a(\rho),\sup_\rho\mathsf a(\rho)]$, an interval of length $J(\beta)/3$, and $3a_K^{-4}\operatorname{Rie}_K(f)(\mathsf e-\mathsf a(\nu))$ is a conditional expectation of $\mathcal O_K(f)-\nu(\mathcal O_K(f))$ given $\mathcal I$, for every bounded $f$ with compact support.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof]
(i) The lattice isometries act transitively on the plaquettes, carry $a_p$ to $a_{\mathsf rp}$, and leave every periodic Gibbs state invariant (M9); so $\nu(a_p)$ is one number. The tangent inequality (M9) for the function $A=-(a_{p_{12}(0)}+a_{p_{13}(0)}+a_{p_{23}(0)})$ of the three plaquettes at one site, whose array over the periodic box of $N$ sites a side is $-\sum_pa_p$, reads
\[\log Z_N(\beta+t)-\log Z_N(\beta)\ge-3\mathsf a(\nu)\,tN^3-144\,\beta N^2-72\,|t|N^2,\]
where $Z_N$ is the partition function of that box, which does not depend on the spacing; divide by $N^3$ and let $N\to\infty$ (Lem.~\ref{C-365-16}). (ii) Take points $\beta_k\downarrow\beta$ at which $P$ is differentiable and $\nu_k\in\mathcal G^{\rm per}_{a,\beta_k}$, which exist by (M9); by (i), $-3\mathsf a(\nu_k)=P'(\beta_k)$; a subsequence converges weakly, its limit is a periodic Gibbs state at $\beta$ by the closedness in (M9), and $a_p$ being continuous, $-3\mathsf a(\nu_+)=\lim_kP'(\beta_k)=P'(\beta+)$; likewise $\beta_k\uparrow\beta$ gives $\nu_-$. (iii) By Prop.~\YMMref{106.3}{765} (M9), at a first-passage datum the set $\mathcal G^{\rm per}_{K,\beta}$ is a class at the cutoff $K$ that obeys the bound system at $g$, and with $\nu$ it contains $k\nu/\nu(k)$ for every bounded $\mathcal I$-measurable $k\ge0$ with $\nu(k)>0$; with the invariance used in (i) this gives $\nu(ka_p)=\nu(ka_{p_0})$ for all plaquettes $p$, so one $\mathcal I$-measurable $\mathsf e$ serves all plaquettes, and the statements on conditional expectations given $\mathcal I$ (M9) place its values between the infimum and the supremum of the $\mathsf a(\rho)$, an interval of length $J(\beta)/3$ by (ii); linearity gives the conditional expectation of $\mathcal O_K(f)$, since $a_K^{-1}\sum_pf(x(p))=3a_K^{-4}\operatorname{Rie}_K(f)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Thm.~\ref{C-365-9}]
\emph{Step 1: clause (a).} The first bound is Prop.~\ref{C-365-28}; $|D_K''|(I)\le\mu_K(I)+C_0|I|$. For the convex $\Phi=D_K+\frac12C_0y^2$,
\[\Delta^2_s\Phi(b)=\int(s-|y-b|)_+\,\mathrm{d}\mu_K(y)=\int_0^s\mu_K((b-u,b+u))\,\mathrm{d}u\le C_\flat(s^2+\delta s),\]
and $\Delta^2_sD_K=\Delta^2_s\Phi-C_0s^2\ge-C_0s^2$ because $\mu_K\ge0$. Since $K_1$ does not increase, the bounds hold for every $\delta>\delta_0(K)$, hence at $\delta_0(K)$, and $\delta_0(K)\le\delta$ once $K\ge K_1(\delta)$. For the tent $\phi_{\delta'}$, $\mathsf p''(b)=\int\phi_{\delta'}(b-y)\,\mathrm{d}\mu_K(y)-C_0$, and the layer-cake formula with the bound on the open intervals $(b-\delta'(1-\delta't),b+\delta'(1-\delta't))$ gives $\int\phi_{\delta'}(b-y)\,\mathrm{d}\mu_K(y)\le C_\flat(1+\delta_0/\delta')$; and $\mathsf p(b)-D_K(b)=\int_0^{\delta'}\phi_{\delta'}(t)\Delta^2_tD_K(b)\,\mathrm{d}t$ with $\int_0^{\delta'}\phi_{\delta'}(t)t^2\,\mathrm{d}t=\delta'^2/12$ and $\int_0^{\delta'}\phi_{\delta'}(t)t\,\mathrm{d}t=\delta'/6$.

\emph{Step 2: clause (b).} $p_{K,\ell'}$ is real-analytic, so the atom of $\mu_K=(D_K+\frac12C_0y^2)''$ at $b$ is the jump of $p'_{K,\infty}$ there, and $p_{K,\infty}(b)=L^{3K}P(L^Kb)$ by Lem.~\ref{C-365-16}:
\[\mu_K(\{b\})=p'_{K,\infty}(b+)-p'_{K,\infty}(b-)=L^{4K}J(L^Kb)\le C_\flat\delta .\]
For the limit of $\beta^4J(\beta)$: by Lem.~\ref{C-365-29}~(ii) every point of $[1,L]$ has a dilate $L^{s}b_\infty$ in the interior of a window $W^{(\iota)}\subset\operatorname{int}I(g^{(\iota)})$; finitely many of the sets $L^{-s_\iota}\operatorname{int}W^{(\iota)}$ cover $[1,L]$, each window with its Setting. Every $\beta\ge L^{1+\max s_\iota}$ is $L^{K'}y$ with $y\in W^{(\iota)}$ for some $\iota$ and an integer $K'$ that tends to $\infty$ with $\beta$; so $\beta^4J(\beta)=y^4\mu^{(\iota)}_{K'}(\{y\})\le(\max W^{(\iota)})^4C_\flat^{(\iota)}\delta$ once $K'\ge K_1^{(\iota)}(\delta)$, for every $\delta$.

\emph{Step 3: clause (c).} Lem.~\ref{C-365-34}~(i), (ii) at $a=a_K$, $\beta=L^Kb$. With $e(\nu)=3a_K^{-4}\mathsf a(\nu)$: $\nu(\mathcal O(f))=a_K^{-1}\mathsf a(\nu)\sum_pf(x(p))=\operatorname{Rie}_K(f)e(\nu)$, and the tangent inequality in the label reads
\[p_{K,\infty}(b')-p_{K,\infty}(b)=L^{3K}\bigl[P(L^Kb')-P(L^Kb)\bigr]\ge-3\mathsf a(\nu)L^{4K}(b'-b)=-(b'-b)e(\nu),\]
since $p'_{K,\infty}(b\pm)=L^{4K}P'(L^Kb\pm)$; the end points are taken by $\nu_\pm$.

\emph{Step 4: clause (d).} By (c), $\nu(x_c)-\nu'(x_c)=q^{-3}\operatorname{Rie}_K(f)(e(\nu)-e(\nu'))$, and for $0\le f\le1$ vanishing off a cube of side $\le q-a_K$, each of the three orientations contributes at most $(q/a_K)^3$ plaquettes, so $0\le q^{-3}\operatorname{Rie}_K(f)\le1$:
\[|\nu(x_c)-\nu'(x_c)|\le|e(\nu)-e(\nu')|\le J_K(b)=\mu_K(\{b\}) .\]
Uniformity in $b\in W\subset W'$ follows from (b) at every $\delta$.

\emph{Step 5: clause (e).} Prop.~\YMMref{100.1}{744}, applied to $\nu$ and the tuples $(f)$, $(h)$, bounds the difference between $S^T_2[\nu](f,\tau_vh)$ and $\nu(E_\nu[\mathcal O(f)-\nu(\mathcal O(f))\,|\,\mathcal I]\,E_\nu[\mathcal O(h)-\nu(\mathcal O(h))\,|\,\mathcal I])$ by the right member; by Lem.~\ref{C-365-34}~(iii) the latter is $9a_K^{-8}\operatorname{Rie}_K(f)\operatorname{Rie}_K(h)\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\mathsf e)$, and a random variable with values in an interval of length $J(\beta)/3$ has variance $\le\frac14(J(\beta)/3)^2$, so $9a_K^{-8}\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\mathsf e)\le\frac14(a_K^{-4}J(\beta))^2=\frac14J_K(b)^2$. As $-3\mathsf a(\nu_\pm)=P'(\beta\pm)$ and $P'(\beta+)\ge P'(\beta-)$, $\mathsf a(\nu_+)=\inf_\rho\mathsf a(\rho)$ and $\mathsf a(\nu_-)=\sup_\rho\mathsf a(\rho)$; the mean of $\mathsf e$ in a state $\nu$ is $\nu(a_p)=\mathsf a(\nu)$. So at $\nu_+$ the function $\mathsf e$ is $\ge$ its mean, and at $\nu_-$ it is $\le$ its mean; in both cases the mean is an end of the interval, so $\mathsf e$ is almost surely constant. An ergodic $\nu$ makes the $\mathcal I$-measurable $\mathsf e$ constant. At $\nu=\frac12(\nu_++\nu_-)$, a periodic Gibbs state,
\[\operatorname{Cov}_\nu(F,F')=\tfrac12\operatorname{Cov}_{\nu_+}(F,F')+\tfrac12\operatorname{Cov}_{\nu_-}(F,F')+\tfrac14\bigl(\nu_+(F)-\nu_-(F)\bigr)\bigl(\nu_+(F')-\nu_-(F')\bigr);\]
at $F=\mathcal O(f)$, $F'=\mathcal O(\tau_vf)$ with $\operatorname{Rie}_K(f)>0$ the covariances in $\nu_\pm$ are $O(1/|v|)$ by the plateau at $\nu_\pm$, $\nu_+(F)-\nu_-(F)=-a_K^{-4}J(\beta)\operatorname{Rie}_K(f)$, and $|v|\to\infty$ gives the equality.

\emph{Step 6: clause (f).} (M14) is taken with what the clause supposes, which is what (M14) asks: two frames at one radius with the block sizes $L_1$ and $L_2=L_1+2$, Thms.~\YMMref{AJ}{673} and~\YMMref{AD}{607} granted at both, Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8} at the choices of its constants that they determine and at a lowered choice of each, and, in each frame $i$, the rate of the far part, that is, numbers $\mathsf k_i\ge0$ and $\mathsf c_{{\rm y},i}<\infty$, free of $m$, $K$ and $b$, with $|\mathsf y^{(i)}_{m,K'}(b)-\mathsf y^{(i)}_{m,K}(b)|\le\mathsf c_{{\rm y},i}\,\ell^9K^{\mathsf p_{2,i}}L_i^{-K/10}$ for all integers $m\ge1$, $\ell=2L_i^m$, all $b\in\mathcal W_i$ and all integers $K'\ge K\ge\mathsf k_i+54m$.

The power of (M14) is derived, in \S\ref{lh:sec} on the latent heat of the $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Wilson model on $\mathbb Z^3$, from these data, the rate among them; so (M14) gives for every real $A>90$ numbers $\mathsf C_{\rm r}$ and $\beta_1$ with $\beta^4J(\beta)\le\mathsf C_{\rm r}\beta^{-1/(2A)}$ for $\beta\ge\beta_1$. That proof, measured on the physical scale, compares the specific heats of the Wilson model at the block sizes $L_1$ and $L_2=L_1+2$, whose logarithms are rationally independent (Lem.~\ref{C-365-6}), through the exact finite-size bounds, a common near part and the far parts $\mathsf y^{(i)}_{m,K}$, as in Prop.~\ref{C-365-28} made quantitative. The rate enters at the cutoffs $K\ge\mathsf k_i+Am$: there $\ell^9=2^9L_i^{9m}\le2^9L_i^{9K/A}$, so that for $K'\ge K$
\[\sup_{b\in\mathcal W_i}\bigl|\mathsf y^{(i)}_{m,K'}(b)-\mathsf y^{(i)}_{m,K}(b)\bigr|\le2^9\mathsf c_{{\rm y},i}\sup_{k\ge1}k^{\mathsf p_{2,i}}L_i^{-(\frac1{10}-\frac9A)k},\]
a number free of $m$ and $K$, finite as $A>90$. With $A=1/(2\alpha)$ for $0<\alpha<1/180$, and $J\le6$ (the difference quotients of $P$ lie in $[-6,0]$, since $0\le\sum_pa_p\le6$ per site), $\mathsf c_*(\alpha)<\infty$; for $\alpha=0$ use $\alpha=1/182$. On $\mathfrak d(g)$ the label is $b=a_K\beta\ge g^{-2}$ by (M5), so $\beta\ge1$ and
\[a_K^{-4}J(\beta)=b^{-4}\beta^4J(\beta)\le b^{-4}\mathsf c_*(\alpha)\beta^{-\alpha}=\mathsf c_*(\alpha)\,b^{-4-\alpha}L^{-\alpha K}\le g^{8+2\alpha}\mathsf c_*(\alpha)L^{-\alpha K}.\]
