By (c) at $b$, $3a_K^{-4}|\rho(a_p)-\nu(a_p)|=|e(\rho)-e(\nu)|\le a_K^{-4}J(\beta)$; for $f$ with support in $[-R,R]^3$ each orientation has at most $(2R/a_K+1)^3$ barycentres there, which gives the bound for $\mathcal O_K(f)$; and (d) gives the bound for the cube means.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Thm.~\ref{C-365-10}]
\emph{Step 1: clause (a) and the limit at the label.} By the passage, $(K,L^K\mathsf b)\in\mathfrak d(g)$ for $K\ge1$, so $(K,L^K\mathsf b,\nu_K)_{K\ge\max\{K_\circ,1\}}$ is a Gibbs sequence at $g$, with the constant label $\mathsf b$. By (M13)\,(ii) and (v), $\nu_K$ is the one periodic Gibbs state at $(K,L^K\mathsf b)$, the sequence converges, its limit $\sigma$ is its own single component with $\ker H=\mathbb C\Omega$, and the spectrum of $H$ lies in $\{0\}\cup[m_*,\infty)$; $\sigma$ is invariant under $\mathbb R^3\rtimes\mathrm O(3)$, as every limit of a convergent Gibbs sequence (M10). We use two terms. A \emph{limit at the label $\mathsf b$} is a limit, for $n\ge2$ and $X\in\mathfrak S_n(\mathbb R^3)$, of $S^T_{n;K,\ell,L^K\mathsf b}(X^{\langle\ell\rangle})$ as $K$ and $\ell=2L^m$ tend to infinity, together or in either order, the bare coupling being $L^K\mathsf b$ at every cutoff $K$.

A \emph{continuum limit along growing tori at the label $\mathsf b$} is a continuum limit at $g$ along growing tori (Def.~\ref{C-365-5}~(5)) whose defining sequence $(K_j,\ell_j,\beta_j)$ has $\beta_j=L^{K_j}\mathsf b$, that is, all its labels equal to $\mathsf b$, from an index on. Let $X=(f_1,\dots,f_n)\in\mathfrak S_n(\mathbb R^3)$, $n\ge2$ (an entry $0$ makes both sides $0$), and take a side $\ell_1=2L^{m_1}\ge\ell_\circ$ with the supports in $(-\ell_1/4,\ell_1/4)^3$. By (M13)\,(iv), for all $K\ge\max\{K_\circ,1\}$ and all sides $\ell\ge\ell_1$,
\[\bigl|S^T_{n;K,\ell,L^K\mathsf b}(X^{\langle\ell\rangle})-S^T_n[\nu_K](X)\bigr|\le C(X)\,\theta_\circ^{\ell/(2\ell_\circ)},\]
a bound free of $K$, while $S^T_n[\nu_K](X)\to S^\sigma_n(X)$ as $K\to\infty$, the Gibbs sequence converging. So $S^T_{n;K,\ell,L^K\mathsf b}(X^{\langle\ell\rangle})\to S^\sigma_n(X)$ when $K$ and $\ell$ tend to infinity together; in the order $\ell$ first the inner limit is $S^T_n[\nu_K](X)$; in the order $K$ first the inner limit exists at every fixed side $\ell\ge\ell_1$ by (M8), the supports of the periodised functions being disjoint, and it lies within $C(X)\theta_\circ^{\ell/(2\ell_\circ)}$ of $S^\sigma_n(X)$. Along a defining sequence with $\beta_j=L^{K_j}\mathsf b$ from an index on, $K_j\to\infty$ and $\ell_j\to\infty$, the same bound gives $S_n(X)=\lim_jS^T_{n;K_j,\ell_j,\beta_j}(X^{\langle\ell_j\rangle})=S^\sigma_n(X)$ for $n\ge2$; as $\sigma_S$ and $\sigma$ are formed from their connected functions with the one-point functions $0$ ($S_1=0$, and $\sigma((f))=0$ by Def.~\ref{C-365-5}~(2)), $\sigma_S=\sigma$.

So every limit at the label $\mathsf b$, in any order of cutoff and volume, and every continuum limit along growing tori at the label $\mathsf b$ is $\sigma$. The class $[\varnothing]$ of the empty tuple has norm $\sigma(\varnothing)^{1/2}=1$ and is fixed by every $e^{-tH}$, so it spans $\ker H$; take $\Omega=[\varnothing]$. For $X,Y\in\mathfrak S(\mathbb E_+)$, $\langle[X],\Omega\rangle=\sigma(\theta X)=\sigma(X)$ by the invariance, and $P_\Omega$ commutes with $H$, so
\[\sigma(\theta X\cdot\tau_{te_3}Y)-\sigma(X)\sigma(Y)=\bigl\langle(1-P_\Omega)[X],e^{-tH}(1-P_\Omega)[Y]\bigr\rangle,\]
and $\|e^{-tH}(1-P_\Omega)\|\le e^{-m_*t}$ by the spectral theorem; the rotations carry this to every direction. By Thm.~\ref{C-365-8}~(e)\,4 at $g$, clause (c) of that theorem applies to $\sigma$: $\sigma((f))=0$, the kernel $\mathbf s\ge0$ does not increase, and
\[4\pi r\,\mathbf s(r)=\int e^{-mr}\,\mathrm{d}\rho(m),\qquad\rho\ge0,\qquad\rho(\{0\})=0 .\]

\emph{Step 2: the gap passes to the kernel.} For real $f\in C^1_c(\mathbb E_+)$ the vector $\psi_f$ is orthogonal to $\Omega$, as $\langle\Omega,\psi_f\rangle=\sigma((f))=0$; so by the gap $\sigma(\theta f,\tau_{te_3}f)=\langle\psi_f,e^{-tH}\psi_f\rangle\le e^{-m_*t}\|\psi_f\|^2$. With $f_\epsilon(x)=\eta_\epsilon(x_3)\mathsf g(x_1,x_2)$ as in the proof of Prop.~\ref{C-365-30}, this reads $c_\epsilon(t)\le e^{-m_*t}c_\epsilon(0)$; letting $\epsilon\to0$ and then $\mathsf g$ tend to a point mass,
\[\mathbf s(2s+t)\le e^{-m_*t}\,\mathbf s(2s)\qquad(s>0,\ t\ge0),\]
that is $\mathbf s(r)\le e^{-m_*(r-r')}\mathbf s(r')$ for $0<r'\le r$.

\emph{Step 3: no spectral mass below the gap.} Fix $r'>0$. For $0\le m<m_*$ and $r\ge r'$, $\int e^{-m''r}\,\mathrm{d}\rho(m'')\ge e^{-mr}\rho([0,m])$, so
\[\rho([0,m])\le e^{mr}\,4\pi r\,\mathbf s(r)\le4\pi r\,e^{-(m_*-m)r}e^{m_*r'}\mathbf s(r')\to0\qquad(r\to\infty),\]
and $\rho([0,m_*))=0$.

\emph{Step 4: the sharper decay.} As $\rho$ is carried by $[m_*,\infty)$, for $0<r'\le r$
\[4\pi r\,\mathbf s(r)=\int_{[m_*,\infty)}e^{-m''r}\,\mathrm{d}\rho(m'')\le e^{-m_*(r-r')}\int e^{-m''r'}\,\mathrm{d}\rho(m'')=e^{-m_*(r-r')}\,4\pi r'\mathbf s(r');\]
so $\mathbf s(r)=O(r^{-3})$, and $\rho([0,m])=0$ for $m<m_*$ gives $\rho([0,m])=O(m^2)$.

\emph{Step 5: cube means in the limit.} Profiles of distinct cells have supports at distance $\ge T/4$; as $\sigma((f))=0$, $S^\sigma_2=\sigma$ on pairs, and with $0\le f_c,f_{c'}\le1$ and $\int f_c\le q^3$,
\[\bigl|S^\sigma_2(q^{-3}f_c,q^{-3}f_{c'})\bigr|\le q^{-6}\int f_c(x)\int_{|y-x|\ge T/4}\mathbf s(|x-y|)\,\mathrm{d}y\,\mathrm{d}x\le q^{-3}\,4\pi\int_{T/4}^\infty r^2\mathbf s(r)\,\mathrm{d}r,\]
which is finite by Step 4 and the continuity of $\mathbf s$ on $[T/4,\infty)$. The cells $\square_c$ and $\square_{c'}$ are centred at $o+qc$ and $o+qc'$, $c,c'\in\mathbb Z^3$, as in clause (c); let $\mathbf d=c'-c$ be the difference of their indices, as in the proof of Prop.~\ref{C-365-30}~(d). If the two cells have no common point, that is $|\mathbf d|_\infty\ge2$, then the cells are at sup-distance $q(|\mathbf d|_\infty-1)\ge q$, each support lies at sup-distance $\ge T/8$ from the boundary of its cell, so the supports are at distance $\ge q+T/4$, and as $\mathbf s$ does not increase the left member is at most $q^{-6}\|f_c\|_1\|f_{c'}\|_1\mathbf s(q)\le\mathbf s(q)$, which by Step 4 is at most $(r'/q)\,e^{-m_*(q-r')}\mathbf s(r')$ for $0<r'\le q$. For the $26$ cells with $|\mathbf d|_\infty=1$, which share a face, an edge or a corner with the first, the bound is $\chi_\circ q^{-3}$ of the display.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[A derivative from the values on a diameter]\label{C-365-35}
Let $\mathsf u$ be holomorphic on $|z|<r$ with $|\mathsf u|\le M$ there, and $|\mathsf u(x)|\le o$ for real $|x|\le r/2$, where $o>0$. Then $|\mathsf u'(0)|\le(4o/r)[1+\log_2^+(M/o)]$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof]
Write $\mathsf u(z)=\sum_mc_mz^m$ with $|c_m|\le Mr^{-m}$. If $o\ge M$, $|\mathsf u'(0)|\le M/r\le o/r$. Otherwise let $N=\lceil\log_2(M/o)\rceil\ge1$ and $Q(x)=\sum_{m\le N}c_mx^m$; for real $|x|\le r/2$, $|\mathsf u(x)-Q(x)|\le M\sum_{m>N}2^{-m}\le o$, so $|Q|\le2o$ there. Bernstein's inequality for a real polynomial $Q_1(t)=\sum_{k\le N}c'_kt^k$ with $|Q_1|\le1$ on $[-1,1]$ gives $|Q_1'(0)|\le N$; applied to $Q_1(t)=\operatorname{Re}[e^{i\varphi}Q(rt/2)]/(2o)$ with the phase $\varphi$ that makes $e^{i\varphi}Q'(0)\ge0$, it gives $|\mathsf u'(0)|=|Q'(0)|\le4oN/r$.
\end{proof}

The comparison of two cutoffs stops before the terminal scale. We
therefore need the vacuum constant of the steps already performed,
with the stopping index retained in the two-torus estimate.

\begin{lemma}[Vacuum constants before the terminal scale]
\label{lem:vacuum-prefix}
Fix the common construction choice and the real regular progression
of Thm.~\YMMref{Y}{438} for one admissible sequence
$x_0,\ldots,x_K$. Let $T_{\ell_1}$ and $T_{\ell_2}$ be admitted
tori for this sequence, where $\ell_i=2L^{m_i}$, and assume
\[
 LM R(x_K)\le L^{m_i},\qquad \ell_i\ge C_LM,\qquad
 \kappa\ge2\log9216+5,\qquad \delta_NM\ge\kappa,
 \qquad E_0\ge2E_N.
\]
Here $C_L$ is the room constant of Prop.~\YMMref{74.5}{617},
and $E_N,\delta_N$ are the normalizer constants of
equations~\YMMref{(1399)--(1401)}{573}.
At step $j+1$ put
\[
 \mathsf{vl}^{(j+1)}(X,z)=E^{(j+1)}(X,\mathbf1,z),
 \qquad \mathsf{vn}^{(j+1)}(X,z)=\mathsf n^{(j+1)}(X,z).
\]
The second family is the local Gaussian constant in
equation~\YMMref{(1399)}{573}. Both families are real and bounded
by $E_0e^{-\kappa d_{j+1}(X)}$. With the extensive term
$\mathsf N^{(j)}$ of equations~\YMMref{(1402), (1405)}{574}, define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:vacuum-prefix-definition}
\begin{split}
 \mathsf E^{(j)}(T_\ell,T_\ell)
   &=\mathsf N^{(j)}(T_\ell,T_\ell)
     +\sum_X\sum_{z\in X}
       \bigl(\mathsf{vl}^{(j+1)}(X,z)
                    +\mathsf{vn}^{(j+1)}(X,z)\bigr),\\
 E_{(n)}[T_\ell]&=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}
                      \mathsf E^{(j)}(T_\ell,T_\ell),
                    \qquad 0\le n\le K.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
The domains and sites in the first sum have level $j+1$.
These are the constants in equations~\YMMref{(1406)--(1407)}{574}:
on a whole torus there is no boundary layer to remove from the
set of base points.

The normalizing factor of each real step satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:vacuum-step-normalization}
 \log\bigl(\mathsf{pf}_j(x_j)\mathsf Z^{(j)}_{\mathbf1}\bigr)
   =\mathsf N^{(j)}(T_\ell,T_\ell)
            +\sum_X\sum_{z\in X}\mathsf{vn}^{(j+1)}(X,z).
\end{equation}
Consequently the constant accumulated by the zero-source chain
through step $n$ is $E_{(n)}[T_\ell]$.

Put $\ell_* =\min(\ell_1,\ell_2)$ and
$C_{\rm tt}=4096\sum_{q\ge0}e^{-q}$, as in
Prop.~\YMMref{74.5}{617}. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:vacuum-prefix-comparison}
 \left|\frac{E_{(n)}[T_{\ell_1}]}{\ell_1^3}
       -\frac{E_{(n)}[T_{\ell_2}]}{\ell_2^3}\right|
 \le2C_{\rm tt}E_0
       \sum_{s=K-n}^{K-1}L^{3s}e^{-\kappa\ell_*L^s/(5M)}.
\end{equation}
The sum is empty when $n=0$. For every integer $u\ge0$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:vacuum-prefix-tail}
 \sum_{s\ge u}L^{3s}e^{-\alpha L^s}
       \le2L^{3u}e^{-\alpha L^u},
       \qquad \alpha=\frac{\kappa\ell_*}{5M}>4.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
We first identify the constant of one step. Write
$N_j=\#\mathbb T^{(j)}$, $D=N_j-N_{j+1}$ and
$\nu=\frac32\log(2\pi)$. There are $3D$ positive nonpivot
bonds and $3N_{j+1}$ pivot bonds. At the trivial triple the
fluctuation matrix $\mathsf A_{\mathbf1}$ is positive on a real
space of dimension $9D$, and the elimination map at every pivot
is $L^{-3}\mathrm{id}$ on the three-dimensional colour space.
The real Gaussian integral and these pivot determinants give
\[
 \log\mathsf Z^{(j)}_{\mathbf1}
   =27N_{j+1}\log L+3D\nu
                        -\tfrac12\log\det\mathsf A_{\mathbf1}.
\]
The Haar prefactor of the step, at $t=x_j$, is
\[
 \log\mathsf{pf}_j(t)
 =-D\log\mathsf z(t,\varepsilon(t))
   +3D\bigl(\log\sigma_{\rm H}-\tfrac32\log t\bigr)
   -9N_{j+1}\log L.
\]
Since $D=(L^3-1)N_{j+1}$, the definition of
$\mathsf N^{(j)}$ yields
\[
 \log\bigl(\mathsf{pf}_j(t)\mathsf Z^{(j)}_{\mathbf1}\bigr)
 =\mathsf N^{(j)}(T_\ell,T_\ell)
       +18N_{j+1}\log L-\tfrac12\log\det\mathsf A_{\mathbf1}.
\]
It remains to identify the last two terms with the local Gaussian
constants. The logarithm series defining the local normalizer in
the proof of Prop.~\YMMref{50.2}{386} has
$T=1-c_N^{-1}\mathsf A_{\mathbf1}$, with $\|T\|<1$.
Adding its diagonal terms over the nonpivot bonds gives
\[
 \sum_b f_b(T_\ell)
 =9D\log c_N-\sum_{q\ge1}\frac1q\operatorname{Tr}T^q
 =\log\det\mathsf A_{\mathbf1}.
\]
The series is absolutely convergent. The last equality follows
by applying $-\sum_{q\ge1}(1-v)^q/q=\log v$ to each positive
eigenvalue $v$ of $c_N^{-1}\mathsf A_{\mathbf1}$, which lies
in $(0,2)$. Summing the local finite differences of $f_b$ recovers
$f_b(T_\ell)$, and the tents sum to one for each bond. Thus the
nonpivot constants sum to $-\frac12\log\det\mathsf A_{\mathbf1}$.
Each of the $3N_{j+1}$ pivot bonds contributes $6\log L$, by
equation~\YMMref{(1399)}{573}. This proves
\eqref{eq:vacuum-step-normalization}. The chain identity in
Prop.~\YMMref{114.2}{801} adds to this logarithm the values
$E^{(j+1)}(X,\mathbf1,z)$ of the new local terms. Summing over
the steps proves the assertion about its accumulated constant.

For the comparison, we retain the level in the proof of
Prop.~\YMMref{74.5}{617}. At level $j$, the localization
cubes have side $ML^{j-K}$. A domain is common if it has a lift
contained in an axis-parallel box of side less than $\ell_*/2$.
The regular families have the same value on these lifts by
Thm.~\YMMref{Y}{438}. The Gaussian constants have the same
property: the local logarithm series, pivot bond and tent are
transported by the same chart, as in the proof following
equation~\YMMref{(1400)}{573}. Thus both families define one
function over the common lifts.

The sum of this function over a period of either torus, divided
by its volume, has the same value. Indeed, the larger side is
an integer multiple of the smaller one; a period of the larger
torus contains that multiple cubed of the lifts of each site
of the smaller torus. The extensive term also cancels, since
\[
 \ell_i^{-3}\mathsf N^{(j-1)}(T_{\ell_i},T_{\ell_i})
 =L^{3(K-j)}\bigl[3(L^3-1)
       (\mathsf{co}^{\rm b}_{j-1}+\mathsf{co}^{\rm i}_{j-1})
                         +\mathsf{co}^{\rm s}_{j-1}\bigr]
\]
depends only on the common sequence. Therefore, writing
$\mathsf S_i^{(j),\rm nc}$ for the sum of the two local families
over the non-common domains on $T_{\ell_i}$, we have
\[
 \frac{E_{(n)}[T_{\ell_1}]}{\ell_1^3}
 -\frac{E_{(n)}[T_{\ell_2}]}{\ell_2^3}
 =\sum_{j=1}^n
    \left(\ell_1^{-3}\mathsf S_1^{(j),\rm nc}
                     -\ell_2^{-3}\mathsf S_2^{(j),\rm nc}\right).
\]

The lifting argument in that proof gives
$d_j(X)\ge\ell_*L^{K-j}/(2M)-2$ for each non-common domain.
For a fixed site $z$, its domain-counting estimate is
\[
 \sum_{\substack{X\ni z\,;\ d_j(X)\ge D_0}}e^{-\kappa d_j(X)}
 \le2048\sum_{q\ge D_0}e^{-(\kappa-\log9216)q}
 \le\frac{C_{\rm tt}}2 e^{-\kappa D_0/2}.
\]
The hypotheses give $t_j=\ell_*L^{K-j}/M\ge2L^2\ge338$,
so $\frac12(t_j/2-2)\ge t_j/5$. Multiplying the last bound by
$2E_0$ and by the number $\ell_i^3L^{3(K-j)}$ of level-$j$
sites gives
\[
 \ell_i^{-3}|\mathsf S_i^{(j),\rm nc}|
   \le C_{\rm tt}E_0L^{3(K-j)}
                    e^{-\kappa\ell_*L^{K-j}/(5M)}.
\]
Sum only over $1\le j\le n$ and put $s=K-j$ to obtain
\eqref{eq:vacuum-prefix-comparison}. Finally the ratio of
successive terms in \eqref{eq:vacuum-prefix-tail} is
\[
 \exp\bigl(3\log L-\alpha L^s(L-1)\bigr)\le\tfrac12,
\]
because $L\ge13$, $\alpha\ge4$ and $\log L\le L-1$.
Summing this geometric majorant from $s=u$ proves the tail bound.
\end{proof}


\begin{proof}[Proof of Prop.~\ref{C-365-11}]
\emph{Step 1: the identity.} The translations by $a_K\mathbb Z^3$ and the permutations of the axes act on $T_\lambda$, preserve the weight and the Haar measure and are transitive on the plaquettes, so $\langle a_p\rangle_{K,\lambda,L^Kb}=\mathsf a_\lambda$ is one number; there are $3(\lambda/a_K)^3$ plaquettes, and $p'_{K,\lambda}(b)=-\lambda^{-3}L^K\langle\sum_pa_p\rangle=-3a_K^{-4}\mathsf a_\lambda$. As each plaquette of $\mathbb L_K$ has exactly one image on the torus, $\sum_{p\subset T_\lambda}f^{\langle\lambda\rangle}(x(p))=\sum_{p\subset\mathbb L_K}f(x(p))$, so
\[\langle\mathcal O(f^{\langle\lambda\rangle})\rangle_{K,\lambda,L^Kb}=a_K^{-1}\mathsf a_\lambda\sum_pf(x(p))=-\operatorname{Rie}_K(f)\,p'_{K,\lambda}(b);\]
subtract the two sides; for the tent $\chi_0$ of half-width $1/L$ about a site, $\operatorname{Rie}_K(\chi_0)=L^{-3}$.

\emph{Step 2: the bound.} By the passage both laws are at a first-passage datum, and the transfer (M7) at $n=1$, for $f$ with support in a ball of radius $2$, gives $|A_K(f;b)|\le2\log2\,(2\mathsf Q_1+2)\varrho^{-1}\|f\|_\sharp$; at $f=\chi_0$, $\|\chi_0\|_\sharp\le\mathsf c_\chi$. For a cube mean, $0\le q^{-3}\operatorname{Rie}_K(f)\le1$ as in the proof of Thm.~\ref{C-365-9}~(d).

\emph{Step 3: the read-out at the order $0$ on one torus.} Let $\lambda\in\{\ell,\ell'\}$, $b\in\mathsf J$ and $K\ge K_{\rm bf}(\lambda,\mathsf J)$. The theorem on two consecutive cutoffs (Thm.~\YMMref{AR}{810}) compares on $T_\lambda$, at the label $b$, the run $\mathrm A$ at the cutoff $K^{\mathrm A}=K$ with the run $\mathrm B$ at the cutoff $K^{\mathrm B}=K+1$; the mark $\bullet$ stands for $\mathrm A$ or $\mathrm B$. Its objects are taken at the order $1$, the tuple being any one real Lipschitz function on $T_\lambda$ that is not $0$, and at the source $0$, where no object reads that function (\S\ref{sec:cutoff-calibration} and Section~\YMMref{116}{807}); its conditions hold at every such $K$ (Cor.~\textup{\ref{IV-62-66}}~(a)).

The objects are: the depth $u=\lceil K/1260\rceil$ and the level $t_1^\bullet=K^\bullet-u$ of $\bullet$ at this depth; the space of the configurations at the depth $u$, one space for both runs, with its Haar measure $dV$ and its inner ball $\mathsf{In}$, an open set that holds the trivial configuration $\mathbf 1$; the chain of $\bullet$, with its exponent $\Phi^\bullet$ on $\mathsf{In}$, the sum $c^\bullet(0)$ of the constants split off along it at the steps $1,\dots,t_1^\bullet$, the integral $I^\bullet=\int_{\mathsf{In}}e^{\Phi^\bullet}dV$ and the mass $T^\bullet=e^{c^\bullet(0)}I^\bullet$; and the classical start of $\bullet$ at the depth $\lceil K/9\rceil$, with its exponent $\hat\Phi^\bullet$ on $\mathsf{In}$, the sum $\hat c^\bullet(0)$ of its constants, $\hat I^\bullet=\int_{\mathsf{In}}e^{\hat\Phi^\bullet}dV$, its measure $\hat\nu^\bullet=e^{\hat c^\bullet(0)}e^{\hat\Phi^\bullet}dV$ on $\mathsf{In}$ and its mass $\hat T^\bullet=\hat\nu^\bullet(\mathsf{In})=e^{\hat c^\bullet(0)}\hat I^\bullet$ (the form of the theorem, the proof of Prop.~\YMMref{116.1}{808}).

The small numbers $\epsilon_{\rm fg}\le\frac18$, $\epsilon_{\rm cl}\le\frac1{20}$, $\epsilon_{\rm sh}\le\frac1{20}$ and $\mathsf R_{t_1}\le\frac12$ are those of \S\ref{sec:cutoff-calibration} on $T_\lambda$, and $\epsilon_3=4\epsilon_{\rm cl}+6\epsilon_{\rm sh}$. We write $\mathsf R_K[T_\lambda]$ for the number $\mathfrak o_K$ of (M12) on the torus $T_\lambda$ (Def.~\textup{\ref{IV-62-62}}~(4)); with its bound of Cor.~\textup{\ref{IV-62-66}}~(a),
\[\mathsf R_K[T_\lambda]=\mathfrak o_K=8\mathsf R_{t_1}+12\epsilon_{\rm fg}+8\epsilon_{\rm cl}+12\epsilon_{\rm sh}\le\mathsf C_{\rm bf}\lambda^3K^{\mathsf p_0}L^{-K/10}.\]
The links (i)--(iv) below are the four statements of Subsection~\ref{C-365-13} that the proof of clause (c) uses, each derived here from the cited construction estimates. The links (i)--(iii) give
\[\bigl|\log Z_{K+1,\lambda,L^{K+1}b}-\log Z_{K,\lambda,L^Kb}-\operatorname{Re}(c^{\mathrm B}-c^{\mathrm A})(0)\bigr|\le\mathsf R_K[T_\lambda]\le\mathsf C_{\rm bf}\lambda^3K^{\mathsf p_0}L^{-K/10},\]
so that $\mathsf R_K[T_\lambda]$ bounds the error of the read-out at the order $0$ on the torus $T_\lambda$; the link (iv) identifies $c^\bullet(0)$ for Step~4.

(i) \emph{The read-out at the order $0$}, from the discarding estimate, the form and the data of the read-out at $z=0$. With $Z^\bullet=Z_{K^\bullet,\lambda,L^{K^\bullet}b}$, the discarding estimate (Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{115.2}{806}}, at the level $t_1^\bullet$) gives $(1-\mathsf R_{t_1})Z^\bullet\le T^\bullet\le Z^\bullet$. The data of the read-out at $z=0$ (Section~\YMMref{116}{807}; the proofs of Props.~\YMMref{116.1}{808} and~\YMMref{116.3}{809}) give $|I^\bullet/\hat I^\bullet-1|\le2\epsilon_{\rm fg}$, and $\hat T^{\mathrm A}>0$, $\hat T^{\mathrm B}>0$ with $|\hat T^{\mathrm B}/\hat T^{\mathrm A}-1|\le\epsilon_3\le\frac12$. As $T^\bullet=e^{(c^\bullet-\hat c^\bullet)(0)}\,(I^\bullet/\hat I^\bullet)\,\hat T^\bullet$ with $T^\bullet>0$ and $\hat T^\bullet>0$, moduli and logarithms, with $-\log(1-t)\le2t\log2$ for $0\le t\le\frac12$ and $\log\frac{1+y}{1-y}\le\frac{32}{15}y$ for $0\le y\le\frac14$, give
\[
\begin{multlined}
\Bigl|\log\frac{Z^{\mathrm B}}{Z^{\mathrm A}}-\operatorname{Re}\bigl[(c^{\mathrm B}-\hat c^{\mathrm B})-(c^{\mathrm A}-\hat c^{\mathrm A})\bigr](0)\Bigr|\le1.39\,\mathsf R_{t_1}+4.27\,\epsilon_{\rm fg}+1.39\,\epsilon_3=1.39\,\mathsf R_{t_1}+4.27\,\epsilon_{\rm fg} \\
+5.56\,\epsilon_{\rm cl}+8.34\,\epsilon_{\rm sh}.
\end{multlined}
\]

(ii) \emph{The two classical starts are comparable as measures on the inner ball}, from the proof of the comparison of their masses. Let $Y$ run through the configurations at the depth $\lceil K/9\rceil$, with the Haar measure $dY$, $Y_{t_1}$ being the block average of $Y$ at the depth $u$, and let $\mathsf k^\bullet\ge0$ and $\hat F^\bullet\ge0$ be the weights and the starts of Section~\YMMref{116}{807} at the source $0$, so that $\int_{\mathsf{In}}H\,\mathrm{d}\hat\nu^\bullet=\int H(Y_{t_1})\,\mathsf k^\bullet\hat F^\bullet\,\mathrm{d}Y$ for every bounded Borel function $H$ on the configurations at the depth $u$ (\S\ref{sec:block-field-laws}). The positive-kernel argument in the proof of Prop.~\YMMref{116.1}{808} runs with a bounded Borel function $H\ge0$ of the block field at the depth $u$ as a further factor, since its kernel inequalities hold against every bounded nonnegative Borel function; it gives
\[
\begin{gathered}
\int H(Y_{t_1})\,\mathsf k^\bullet\,\mathbf 1\{\mathsf k^\circ=0\}\,\hat F^\bullet\,\mathrm{d}Y\le\epsilon_{\rm sh}\int_{\mathsf{In}}H\,\mathrm{d}\hat\nu^\bullet\qquad\\
\bigl(\{\bullet,\circ\}=\{\mathrm A,\mathrm B\}\bigr).
\end{gathered}
\]
Where both weights are positive they are equal and 
\[
\hat F^{\mathrm B}/\hat F^{\mathrm A}\in[e^{-\epsilon_{\rm cl}},e^{\epsilon_{\rm cl}}]
\]
 (Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{116.1}{808}}). Dropping from $\int_{\mathsf{In}}H\,\mathrm{d}\hat\nu^{\mathrm B}$ the part where $\mathsf k^{\mathrm A}=0$, comparing the starts where both weights are positive, and using the display for $(\bullet,\circ)=(\mathrm A,\mathrm B)$, and then the same with $\mathrm A$ and $\mathrm B$ exchanged, one obtains for every bounded Borel $H\ge0$
\[
\begin{gathered}
e^{-\epsilon_{\rm meas}}\int_{\mathsf{In}}H\,\mathrm{d}\hat\nu^{\mathrm A}\le\int_{\mathsf{In}}H\,\mathrm{d}\hat\nu^{\mathrm B}\le e^{\epsilon_{\rm meas}}\int_{\mathsf{In}}H\,\mathrm{d}\hat\nu^{\mathrm A},\qquad\\
\epsilon_{\rm meas}=\epsilon_{\rm cl}-\log(1-\epsilon_{\rm sh})\le\epsilon_{\rm cl}+1.06\,\epsilon_{\rm sh}.
\end{gathered}
\]
At the real source $0$ the density $\mathsf D^\bullet=e^{\hat c^\bullet(0)}e^{\hat\Phi^\bullet}$ of $\hat\nu^\bullet$ is positive at every point of $\mathsf{In}$ (the positive classical density in the proof of Prop.~\YMMref{116.1}{808}), so $\log\mathsf D^\bullet=\operatorname{Re}\hat c^\bullet(0)+\operatorname{Re}\hat\Phi^\bullet$; taking for $H$ the indicator functions of the sets where $\mathsf D^{\mathrm B}<e^{-\epsilon_{\rm meas}}\mathsf D^{\mathrm A}$ or $\mathsf D^{\mathrm A}<e^{-\epsilon_{\rm meas}}\mathsf D^{\mathrm B}$, the display gives
\[\bigl|[\operatorname{Re}\hat c^{\mathrm B}(0)+\operatorname{Re}\hat\Phi^{\mathrm B}]-[\operatorname{Re}\hat c^{\mathrm A}(0)+\operatorname{Re}\hat\Phi^{\mathrm A}]\bigr|\le\epsilon_{\rm meas}\qquad\text{Haar-almost everywhere on }\mathsf{In}.\]

(iii) \emph{The constants of the two classical starts cancel}, from the value $0$ and the continuity of the exponent of the classical start at the trivial configuration. At the source $0$ the exponent $\hat\Phi^\bullet(V)$ of the classical start of $\bullet$ at the level $t_1^\bullet$ is the action of its bare array at a background $U(V)$ over $V$ less the Wilson action at that background weighted by the coupling of the level (Prop.~\YMMref{114.2}{801}). It vanishes at $V=\mathbf 1$ and is continuous there. Indeed the trivial configuration of the bare lattice has the action $0$ and the block average $\mathbf 1$, so it lies on the minimal orbit over $\mathbf 1$, on which both terms take one value (the gauge-invariance argument preceding equation~\YMMref{(2133)}{790}, Props.~\YMMref{114.2}{801} and~\YMMref{113.13}{799}); the weighted action vanishes at it, and so does the action of the bare array, every member of which enters less its value at the trivial pair (equation~\YMMref{(874)}{412}).

The actual analytic-background argument in the proof of Prop.~\YMMref{52.3}{433} supplies a continuous representative $\Upsilon(V)$ near $\mathbf 1$. The weighted action is the finite sum $\eta_t^{-1}\sum_pc(p)a_p(\Upsilon(V))$ of continuous plaquette functions; gauge invariance identifies this sum with the action of the background. Thus it is continuous at $\mathbf 1$. The action of the array is continuous there as well: its members are local terms, holomorphic in the pair that they read (Lem.~\ref{lem:analytic-open-pairs}), the pair being a polynomial map of the configuration (\S\ref{sec:analytic-core-complements}, \YMMref{(70)}{38}, \YMMref{(69)}{38}); so the action of the array is continuous at $\mathbf 1$ along the continuous choice of Thm.~\YMMref{E}{10} and its real-analytic continuation. So for every $\delta>0$ there is an open set $\mathcal N\subset\mathsf{In}$ with $\mathbf 1\in\mathcal N$ on which $|\operatorname{Re}\hat\Phi^{\mathrm A}|\le\delta$ and $|\operatorname{Re}\hat\Phi^{\mathrm B}|\le\delta$.

The comparison (ii) holds Haar-almost everywhere, so the argument reads the open set $\mathcal N$, which has positive Haar measure: at a point of $\mathcal N$ off the null set of (ii), $|\operatorname{Re}\hat c^{\mathrm B}(0)-\operatorname{Re}\hat c^{\mathrm A}(0)|\le\epsilon_{\rm meas}+2\delta$. As $\delta>0$ is arbitrary, $|\operatorname{Re}(\hat c^{\mathrm B}-\hat c^{\mathrm A})(0)|\le\epsilon_{\rm meas}$, and with (i)
\[\bigl|\log Z^{\mathrm B}-\log Z^{\mathrm A}-\operatorname{Re}(c^{\mathrm B}-c^{\mathrm A})(0)\bigr|\le1.39\,\mathsf R_{t_1}+4.27\,\epsilon_{\rm fg}+6.56\,\epsilon_{\rm cl}+9.40\,\epsilon_{\rm sh}\le\mathsf R_K[T_\lambda],\]
which is the display above.

(iv) \emph{The constants at zero source.} We claim that
\[
 c^\bullet(0)=E_{(n)}[T_\lambda],\qquad
 n=t_1^\bullet=K^\bullet-u,
\]
where the right side is the vacuum constant of the first $n$ steps of the actual progression at cutoff $K^\bullet$. The hypotheses at $K\ge\max\{K_{\rm bf}(\ell,\mathsf J),K_{\rm bf}(\ell',\mathsf J)\}$ give the admitted setting of \S\ref{sec:cutoff-calibration} on both tori.

The couplings $x_j^\bullet=L^{K^\bullet-j}b$ have zero increments and form an admissible finite sequence. With either side $2L^m$ they give admitted data, by the proof of Lem.~\YMMref{118.1}{812}. The stronger room required in Lem.~\ref{lem:vacuum-prefix} follows from
$LMR(b)\le LMR(L(g^{-2}+\bar B))\le L^{m_{\mathfrak L}(g)}\le L^m$; its proof above also gives $2L^m\ge C_LM$.

At zero source, the family of level $j$ in the chain is the family of the canonical progression of the cut $(x_0^\bullet,\ldots,x_{K^\bullet-1}^\bullet)$, by the same proof of Lem.~\YMMref{118.1}{812}. Thm.~\YMMref{Y}{438} identifies these with the first $K^\bullet$ families of the progression of the full line, with their common companions on all admitted tori. They are real at the trivial configuration and satisfy the bound in Lem.~\ref{lem:vacuum-prefix}; the common choice retains $\delta_NM\ge\kappa$, $E_0\ge2E_N$ and $\kappa\ge2\log9216+5$.

By Prop.~\YMMref{114.2}{801}, step $i$ adds the logarithm of its normalizing factor and the sum of the local values $E^{(i)}(X,\mathbf1,z)$. Equation~\eqref{eq:vacuum-step-normalization} identifies the logarithm with $\mathsf N^{(i-1)}$ and the sum of $\mathsf{vn}^{(i)}$. Since a whole torus has no boundary, every site in each domain is a base point. Thus the constant added at step $i$ is exactly $\mathsf E^{(i-1)}(T_\lambda,T_\lambda)$. Summation over $1\le i\le n$ proves the claimed identity. In particular these accumulated constants are real.

\emph{Step 4: two tori.} Equation~\eqref{eq:vacuum-prefix-comparison} gives, per volume, \[
 \left|E_{(n)}[T_\ell]\ell^{-3}-E_{(n)}[T_{\ell'}]\ell'^{-3}\right|
 \le2C_{\rm tt}E_0\sum_{s=K-n}^{K-1}L^{3s}
       \exp[-\kappa\ell'L^s/(5M)];
\] divide Step 3 by the volumes and subtract the two tori:
\[|U_{K+1}(b)-U_K(b)|\le\ell^{-3}\mathsf R_K[T_\ell]+\ell'^{-3}\mathsf R_K[T_{\ell'}]+2\mathsf v_K\le2\mathsf C_{\rm bf}K^{\mathsf p_0}L^{-K/10}+2\mathsf v_K .\]
The right member is summable in $K$, so $U_K$ converges uniformly on $\mathsf J$: clause (c).

\emph{Step 5: a holomorphic extension free of the cutoff.} For $\lambda\in\{\ell,\ell'\}$, $\phi_\lambda(z)=\widetilde Z_\lambda(z)/\widetilde Z_\lambda(0)$ is holomorphic on $|z|<2\varrho$ with $\phi_\lambda(0)=1$ and $|\phi_\lambda|\le e^{(C_S+C_g)\lambda^3}\le e^{(C_S+C_g)\ell^3}$ by (M1); by Schwarz's lemma $|\phi_\lambda-1|\le\frac12$, so $\log\phi_\lambda$ is holomorphic with modulus $\le\log2$, on $|z|<\varrho/(e^{(C_S+C_g)\ell^3}+1)$. By the shift of the label, $\lambda^{-3}\log\phi_\lambda(x)=p_{K,\lambda}(b-x)-p_{K,\lambda}(b)-\lambda^{-3}\mathcal E_\lambda(x\cdot1)$ for real $x$, the logarithm being real there by the conjugation in (M1); so, with $d$ of Lem.~\ref{C-365-15},
\[\mathsf u_{K,b}(z)=\ell^{-3}\log\phi_\ell(z)-\ell'^{-3}\log\phi_{\ell'}(z)+d(z)\]
is holomorphic on $|z|<r_3$, bounded there by $M_3$, and equals $U_K(b-x)-U_K(b)$ for real $|x|<r_3$; Cauchy's estimate gives $|\partial_b^nU_K(b)|\le n!M_3r_3^{-n}$.

\emph{Step 6: the derivative.} For $b\in\mathsf W$ the function $\mathsf h=\mathsf u_{K+1,b}-\mathsf u_{K,b}$ is holomorphic on $|z|<r_3$ with $|\mathsf h|\le2M_3$, and for real $|x|\le r_3/2$ both $b$ and $b-x$ lie in $\mathsf J$, so by Step 4, with the number $\mathsf o_K=4\mathsf C_{\rm bf}(\mathsf J)K^{\mathsf p_0}L^{-K/10}+4\mathsf v_K$ of (d),
\[|\mathsf h(x)|=\bigl|(U_{K+1}-U_K)(b-x)-(U_{K+1}-U_K)(b)\bigr|\le\mathsf o_K .\]
Lem.~\ref{C-365-35} gives $|U'_{K+1}(b)-U'_K(b)|=|\mathsf h'(0)|\le(4\mathsf o_K/r_3)[1+\log_2^+(2M_3/\mathsf o_K)]$. As $\mathsf o_K$ decays like $K^{\mathsf p_0}L^{-K/10}$ and its logarithm grows like $K$, the series $\sum_KK\sup_{\mathsf W}|U'_{K+1}-U'_K|$ converges; this gives the uniform convergence of $U'_K$ and the bound of $\sup_K\sup_{\mathsf W}|U'_K|$.

\emph{Step 7: the contact terms.} The read-out of the theorem on two consecutive cutoffs at the order $1$ in the source (Thm.~\YMMref{AR}{810}, equation~\YMMref{(2202)}{810}, at $n=1$), on each torus with $f^{\langle\lambda\rangle}$, gives $S^T_{1;K+1}(f)-S^T_{1;K}(f)$ up to the derivative at zero source of the difference of the contact terms at the cutoffs $K+1$ and $K$ and an error that is summable in $K$; subtracting the two tori, by Step 1, $A_{K+1}(f)-A_K(f)=-\operatorname{Rie}_{K+1}(f)(U'_{K+1}-U'_K)(b)-[\operatorname{Rie}_{K+1}(f)-\operatorname{Rie}_K(f)]U'_K(b)$, with $|\operatorname{Rie}_{K+1}(f)-\operatorname{Rie}_K(f)|\le\sqrt3a_K\operatorname{Lip}(f)(2R+2)^3$ for $R$ the radius of a ball about the origin that holds the support of $f$, and $|U'_K|$ bounded; so the difference between the two tori of the derivatives of the contact terms is summable in $K$, uniformly on $\mathsf W$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Prop.~\ref{C-365-12}]
\emph{Step 1: characteristic functions from the imaginary axis.} In (a), by the passage $(K,L^Kb)\in\mathfrak d(g)$. For real $y$ and $t$ the function $e^{ityX_\kappa}$ of the cell $\kappa$ has, by the source formula, $\|e^{ityX_\kappa}\|_{{\rm ch},\ell}^N=Z[ity(F_e-F_o)]/Z$, a number $\ge0$, the same for both parities of $\kappa$; with $v=y(F_e-F_o)$, $\|v\|_\sharp=|y|$, and (IM) for $\widetilde Z^{\rm av}$ at $u=0$,
\[\|e^{ityX_\kappa}\|_{{\rm ch},\ell}\le\exp\bigl[N^{-1}\operatorname{Re}\mathcal E^{\rm av}_\ell(itv)+C_I't^2y^2q^3\bigr].\]
The Taylor coefficients of $s\mapsto N^{-1}\mathcal E^{\rm av}_\ell(s(F_e-F_o))$ are real by (A1) of Lem.~\ref{C-365-14}, and bounded uniformly in $\ell$ at fixed $K$, by the count of domains, which bounds the energies of the domains that meet one cell; so $N^{-1}\operatorname{Re}\mathcal E^{\rm av}_\ell(itv)=-\frac12t^2y^2\mathsf e_\ell+O(t^4)$ uniformly in $\ell$, and $\bar{\mathsf e}$ is finite.

\emph{Step 2: the variance from below.} Choose sides $\ell_k\to\infty$ with $\mathsf e_{\ell_k}\to\bar{\mathsf e}$. The domination, for the functions $e^{ity_\kappa X_\kappa}$ of different cells, gives
\[\bigl|\nu\bigl(e^{it\sum_\kappa y_\kappa X_\kappa}\bigr)\bigr|\le\exp\Bigl[-\tfrac12t^2(\bar{\mathsf e}-2C_I'q^3)\sum_\kappa y_\kappa^2+O(t^4)\Bigr],\]
while $|\nu(e^{itY})|\ge\operatorname{Re}\nu(e^{it(Y-\nu(Y))})\ge1-\frac12t^2\operatorname{Var}_\nu(Y)$; letting $t\to0$ gives (a).

\emph{Step 3: covariances by variances.} Apply (a) to $X_\kappa\pm X_{\kappa'}$: 
\[
\operatorname{Var}_\nu(X_\kappa)+\operatorname{Var}_\nu(X_{\kappa'})\pm2\operatorname{Cov}_\nu(X_\kappa,X_{\kappa'})\ge2(\bar{\mathsf e}-2C_I'q^3),
\]
which is the second assertion of (a).

\emph{Step 4: Cauchy's estimate with the chord.} In (b), for $z=x+i\tau$ with $|z|=r\le\varrho/2$, the source formula gives 
\[
N\Lambda(z)=\operatorname{Re}\mathcal E^{\rm av}(w_z)+\log|\widetilde Z^{\rm av}(w_z)|-\log\widetilde Z(0).
\]
(IM) at $u=xF$, $v=\tau(F_e-F_o)$ costs $C_I'\tau^2\ell^3$. By semi-convexity, $\mathsf g(t)=\log\widetilde Z^{\rm av}(tF)$ has $\mathsf g''\ge-2C_I'\ell^3$ on $[-r,r]$, so $\mathsf g+C_I'\ell^3t^2$ lies below its chord:
\[\mathsf g(x)\le\tfrac12[\mathsf g(r)+\mathsf g(-r)]+C_I'\ell^3r^2+\mathsf m_rx,\qquad\mathsf m_r=[\mathsf g(r)-\mathsf g(-r)]/(2r).\]
The cross terms between the cells give $\operatorname{Re}\mathcal E^{\rm av}(w_z)\le N\operatorname{Re}\mathcal E^{\rm av}(zf)+NM_\times T^{-3}\varrho^{-2}q^3|z|^2$, as in Prop.~\ref{C-365-21}. With $\tilde\epsilon(z)=\mathcal E^{\rm av}(zf)+N^{-1}\mathsf m_rz$, holomorphic with $\tilde\epsilon(0)=0$ and $\tilde\epsilon'(0)$ real, $\Lambda(z)-\operatorname{Re}\tilde\epsilon(z)\le\frac12\mathsf S_f(r)+(2C_I'+M_\times T^{-3}\varrho^{-2})q^3r^2$ on $|z|=r$, and Lem.~\ref{C-365-22}~(a) gives the bound, with $m=q^{-3}\tilde\epsilon'(0)$; Lem.~\ref{C-365-22}~(b) gives the covariance. At $r=\hat rq^{-3+p/2}$ one has $(rq^3)^{-2}=\hat r^{-2}q^{-p}$ and $q^3r^2=\hat r^2q^{p-3}\le\hat r^2$.

\emph{Step 5: the cost from below.} By semi-convexity at the bases $\pm tF$, $|t|\le r\le\varrho/2$,
\[\mathsf g(r)+\mathsf g(-r)-2\mathsf g(0)=\int_0^r(r-t)\bigl[\mathsf g''(t)+\mathsf g''(-t)\bigr]dt\ge-2C_I'\ell^3r^2,\]
and $\ell^3/N=q^3$.

\emph{Step 6: the cost from above.} In (c), the walls (Prop.~\ref{C-365-19}) at $x=\pm r$ ($r\le b$, $r\le\varrho/(256\mathsf c)$), the identity in the proof of Prop.~\ref{C-365-21}, the bounds $\omega(r)+\omega(-r)\le2C_\omega r^2$ and $|d(r)+d(-r)|\le4\mathsf A_1r^2/h_1^2$ give
\[\mathsf S_f(r)\le q^3\Delta^2_rD_{K,\ell}(b)+6C_wTq^2r+2q^3r^2\bigl[C_2'+C_\omega+2\mathsf A_1/h_1^2\bigr]\le q^3\Delta^2_rD_{K,\ell}(b)+6C_wTq^2r+2C_Iq^3r^2 .\]
At $r=\hat rq^{-3/2}$: $q^3\Delta^2_rD_{K,\ell}(b)\le q^3[\Delta^2_rD_K(b)+2\bar\eta(\ell)]$ by Lem.~\ref{C-365-16}, $q^3\Delta^2_rD_K(b)\le C_\flat\hat r^2+C_\flat\hat rq^{3/2}\delta\le2C_\flat$ by Thm.~\ref{C-365-9}~(a) with $\delta\le q^{-3/2}$ and $[b\pm r]\subset W'$, and $2q^3\bar\eta(\ell)=6\ell'B'q^3/\ell\le1$; the lower bound is Step 5.

\emph{Step 7: a power of $q$.} In (d) the proof of Lem.~\ref{C-365-32} applies with $C_pq_i^{-p}$ in the place of $C_{\rm LH}(T/q_i)^2$: $C_pq_i^{-p}\ge\sigma'(\theta w_i,w_i)\ge\mathbf s(\sqrt6q_i)(1-3T/(4q_i))^6$, and for $\sqrt6q_i\le r<\sqrt6Lq_i$, $q_i^{-p}<(\sqrt6L)^pr^{-p}$; then $\rho([0,m])\le4\pi e\,m^{-1}\mathbf s(1/m)$ by Prop.~\ref{C-365-30}.

\emph{Step 8: one frame and a growth bound.} In (e), Prop.~\ref{C-365-24}~(b) at the side $\ell_q$, which lies below $6LC_{\rm FS}q^3$, gives
\[\delta\le\frac{3C_wT}q+C_0x_q+x_qY_0\ell_q^{1/3}+\frac{6C_wC_{\rm FS}Tq^2}{\ell_q}\le\frac{3C_wT}q+C_0x_q+\frac{Y_0(6LC_{\rm FS})^{1/3}q}{3C_wTq^2}+\frac{C_wT}q,\]
which is the display; the window inequality gives the three bounds. Only one frame enters.

\emph{Step 9: the variances from above.} In (f), by the passage $(K,L^Kb)\in\mathfrak d(g)$. Let $\nu$ and $0<r\le\varrho/2$ be given, and on $T_{\ell_k}$, with $N_k$ cells, let $\tilde\epsilon_k(z)=\mathcal E^{\rm av}_{\ell_k}(zf)+N_k^{-1}\mathsf m_{r,k}z$, $\mathsf m_{r,k}$ the slope of the chord of Step~4. For $z=x+i\tau$ with $|z|=r$, the source formula, (IM) at $u=xF$, $v=\tau(F_e-F_o)$, the chord of Step~4, and the cross terms between the cells (Lem.~\ref{C-365-14}~(A3) with $R_0=q/2$, $\Delta=T/4$, $\rho_3=3\varrho/2$, so that $C_\times(2q/T)\le c_X$) give
\[\log\|e^{zX}\|_{{\rm ch},\ell_k}-\operatorname{Re}\tilde\epsilon_k(z)\le\tfrac12\mathsf S_{f,\ell_k}(r)+2C_I'q^3r^2+\tfrac49c_X\varrho^{-2}r^2\le\mathsf S_{f,\ell_k}(r)+c_3r^2,\]
the last step by $\mathsf S_{f,\ell_k}(r)\ge-2C_I'q^3r^2$ (Step~5). The functions $\tilde\epsilon_k$ are holomorphic on $|z|<2\varrho$, real on the real axis and $0$ at $0$, and they are bounded uniformly in $k$, by the count of domains for the domains that meet one cell and by (M1) and the floor for the slopes; along a subsequence they converge, locally uniformly, to such a function $\tilde\epsilon$. The domination gives $|\nu(e^{zX})|\le\liminf_k\|e^{zX}\|_{{\rm ch},\ell_k}$, so $G(z)=\nu(e^{zX})e^{-\tilde\epsilon(z)}$ is holomorphic on $|z|<2\varrho$, $G(0)=1$, and $|G|\le\exp[\limsup_k\mathsf S_{f,\ell_k}(r)+c_3r^2]$ on $|z|=r$. The coefficient of $z^2$ in $G$ is $\frac12[\nu((X-\tilde\epsilon'(0))^2)-\tilde\epsilon''(0)]$, and Cauchy's estimate gives
\[\operatorname{Var}_\nu(X)\le\nu\bigl((X-\tilde\epsilon'(0))^2\bigr)\le\tilde\epsilon''(0)+2r^{-2}\exp\Bigl[\limsup_k\mathsf S_{f,\ell_k}(r)+c_3r^2\Bigr].\]
Finally $\tilde\epsilon''(0)$ is the limit of $\partial_s^2\mathcal E^{\rm av}_{\ell_k}(sf)|_{s=0}$ along the subsequence. By (A1) of Lem.~\ref{C-365-14} and the cross terms at $\rho_3=\varrho$, $N^{-1}\mathcal E^{\rm av}_\ell(s(F_e-F_o))=\frac12[\mathcal E^{\rm av}_\ell(sf)+\mathcal E^{\rm av}_\ell(-sf)]+N^{-1}\mathrm{cr}(s)$ with $|\mathrm{cr}(s)|\le Nc_X|s|^2/\varrho^2$ for complex $|s|<\varrho$, so Cauchy's estimate gives $|\mathrm{cr}''(0)|\le2Nc_X/\varrho^2$, hence $\partial_s^2\mathcal E^{\rm av}_\ell(sf)|_{s=0}\le\mathsf e_\ell+2c_X\varrho^{-2}$ and $\tilde\epsilon''(0)\le\bar{\mathsf e}+2c_X\varrho^{-2}$. The second assertion of (f) is (a): $|\operatorname{Cov}_\nu(X_\kappa,X_{\kappa'})|\le C_{\rm var}q^{6-p}+2C_I'q^3\le(C_{\rm var}+2C_I')q^{6-p}$, as $p\le3$; divide by $q^6$.

\emph{Step 10: the walls and the cost.} In (g), for $t$ between $0$ and $x$ the source $xF+t(1-F)=t+(x-t)F$ has the norm $\le|x|\le\varrho/2$, and $\|1-F\|_\sharp\le1$; so semi-convexity gives $\partial_t^2\log\widetilde Z^{\rm av}(xF+t(1-F))\ge-2C_I'\ell^3$, and at $t=x$
\[\log\widetilde Z^{\rm av}(x)\ge\log\widetilde Z^{\rm av}(xF)+xN\upsilon_f(x)-C_I'\ell^3x^2,\]
which divided by $N$ is the first assertion. Next, by (A1) of Lem.~\ref{C-365-14} at constant sources,
\[\mathsf S_f(r)=\Upsilon_f(r)+\Upsilon_f(-r)+N^{-1}\bigl[\log\widetilde Z(r)+\log\widetilde Z(-r)-2\log\widetilde Z(0)\bigr];\]
the first two terms are $\le2C_\Upsilon$; by the identity in the proof of Prop.~\ref{C-365-21} and the bounds of $\omega$ and of $d$ there, the bracket is $q^3[\Delta^2_rD_{K,\ell}(b)+\omega(r)+\omega(-r)-d(r)-d(-r)]\le q^3[\Delta^2_rD_{K,\ell}(b)+2(C_\omega+2\mathsf A_1/h_1^2)r^2]$, as $r\le r_1\le\min\{r_2/2,h_1/2\}$; and $\Delta^2_rD_{K,\ell}(b)\le\Delta^2_rD_K(b)+2\bar\eta(\ell)$ by Lem.~\ref{C-365-16}, while $\Delta^2_rD_K(b)\le C_\flat r^2+C_\flat\delta r$ by Thm.~\ref{C-365-9}~(a), since $[b-r,b+r]\subset W'$.
\end{proof}


\section{The Haag net of the action density}\label{supp:C-363-1}

Write $\phi(f)$ for the reconstructed action-density field on
Minkowski space $\mathbb R^{1+2}$, and $\Omega$ for its vacuum
vector. The polynomial energy bound gives a common invariant
domain and closed smeared fields $\bar\phi(f)$. For an open
region $O$, let $\mathcal C(O)$ be the bounded weak commutant
of these local fields and their adjoints, and set
$\mathcal A(O)=\mathcal C(O)'$. Here weak commutation is tested on
their common energy domain. Write $O^\times$ for the open spacelike
complement of $O$, and generate $\mathcal A(O^\times)$ from the
algebras of regions contained in that complement.

\begin{sketch}[Local algebras and wedge duality]\label{supp:C-363-4}
For a volume-first limit and each of its components,
$O\mapsto\mathcal A(O)$ is an isotonic, covariant local net.
The field $\bar\phi(f)$ is affiliated with $\mathcal A(O)$ when
$\operatorname{supp}f\subset O$. For a wedge $W$ and its
spacelike complement $W'$, the vacuum is cyclic and separating,
and
\[
 \mathcal A(W)'=\mathcal A(W'),\qquad
 \Delta^{it}=U(B(-2\pi t)).
\]
Here $U$ implements Poincar\'e transformations, $B(s)$ is the
wedge-preserving boost of rapidity $s$, and $\Delta$ is the vacuum
modular operator of $\mathcal A(W)$. For a double cone $O$, the dual
completion $\mathcal A^d(O)=\mathcal A(O^\times)'$, extended to other
open regions by joining the double-cone algebras, is a local Haag-dual net. Equality of $\mathcal A$ and
$\mathcal A^d$ for all double cones is not asserted.
\end{sketch}

\paragraph{Sketch of the argument.}
The reconstruction supplies local unbounded fields. Passing from
their commutation relations to commutation of bounded operator
algebras requires an additional argument: weak commutation on a
common domain does not by itself identify the commutants of the
closures. The lattice provides bounded operators with which to
make this passage.

Use the algebra of bounded operators on the right half of the
lattice time-zero plane. Reflection positivity embeds its
vectors in the lattice Hilbert space. A quarter turn relates the
two Euclidean quadrants. In the continuum this relation becomes
the quarter power $\Delta^{1/4}$ of the boost modular operator.
Convergence of the reflection-positive forms and functional
calculus then carry the lattice modular translations to the
boost group.

Every bounded weak limit from the lattice half-plane algebra
commutes with the fields in the opposite wedge. To show that
there are enough such limits, regularize the lattice insertion
of a field and use the quarter-turn relation. The resulting
bounded approximants reach a dense family of vectors
$\phi(f)\Omega$ in the closure of the opposite-wedge commutant
acting on $\Omega$. Their error is controlled by a separated
Euclidean four-point function. The modular relation
\[
 J\Delta^{1/2}Y\Omega=Y^*\Omega
\]
identifies the two wedge algebras and yields locality and wedge
duality. The weak-commutant definition then gives affiliation
of the closed local fields. Intersecting the containing wedge
algebras produces the stated dual completion.

The argument also passes to components. Translation-invariant
weights can be approximated by distant averages, so they preserve
the relevant positivity forms. The reconstructed Hilbert space
and wedge algebra decompose over the component measure; their
fibres agree with the component wedge algebras almost everywhere.

The periodic lattice approximants are essential to this supply
of bounded operators. For a general limit of periodic Gibbs
states the source establishes a supply of half-plane operators,
but does not assert the whole locality theorem by this argument.
Nor should wedge duality be renamed Haag duality of the original
net on arbitrary bounded regions.




\subsection{Local nets and duality}\label{C-363-1}

We construct the local net of the action density from the continuum limits and their components. The lattice quarter turn determines the modular data of a wedge. Passing its bounded operators to the limit gives wedge duality and the affiliation of the closed field operators with their local algebras.

We distinguish the original net from its dual completion: the latter is Haag dual, while equality with the original net is an additional assertion. Energy bounds, Gaussian examples and the lattice ring calculation clarify the scope of this distinction. The fixed-depth block-loop arguments use \S\ref{C-372-1}.

\subsubsection{Notation and hypotheses}

\paragraph{Constants.} We fix the radius $\varrho>0$ and the constants $(\sigma^-,\gamma)$ of the list $\mathcal T^{\rm S}[2\varrho]$ of the common sourced construction in Section~\YMMref{82}{665}, among them the integers $L,M,\mathfrak p_0$ and the number $B_\sharp\ge0$ that bounds the increments of the flow of the running coupling (see the objects below), and a coupling $0<g\le\gamma$; $\bar B=B_\sharp L/(L-1)$ is formed from $\sigma^-$ alone, with no radius, $\gamma$ or $g$, and $\bar B\le\frac{13}{24}\gamma^{-2}<\gamma^{-2}$ (indeed, $B_\sharp\gamma^2\le\frac12$ and $L\ge13$ give $\bar B\gamma^2\le L/[2(L-1)]\le13/24$). $C^g_{\rm pt}$ is the constant of the point bound at $g$ of equation~\YMMref{(2097)}{779} among the construction results, and $\bar{\mathfrak c}(\mathsf C^g)$, with the bound system $\mathsf C^g$ at $g$ of equation~\YMMref{(2030)}{765}, is the bound of the one-point constants of the components of equation~\YMMref{(1993)}{749}. The short-distance law of the two-point function among the construction results, the law of two points of Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AV}{851}} as it holds in every component (Cor.~\textup{\YMMref{127.11}{854}}), holds at the couplings $0<g\le\gamma_{\rm sd}$, where $\gamma_{\rm sd}=\gamma_W\in(0,\gamma]$ is its ceiling equation~\YMMref{(2346)}{850}, a number formed from $(\sigma^-,\gamma)$ alone. For $0<g\le\gamma_{\rm sd}$ we put
$$c_{\rm sd}=c_{\rm sd}(g)=4.6\cdot10^{-9}L^{-2}\bigl(g^{-2}+\bar B\bigr)^{-2},\qquad r_{\rm sd}=r_{\rm sd}(g)=2.2\,\mathsf d_0\bigl(g,\tfrac1{10}\bigr),$$
with $\bar B=B_\sharp L/(L-1)$ and the threshold $\mathsf d_0$ of the law, equation~\YMMref{(2350)}{851}: two numbers that depend on $g$ and on no sequence, limit, decomposition or $\xi$, and $c_{\rm sd}(g)\le4.6\cdot10^{-9}g^4$. Then for every component $\sigma'_\xi$ of a limit of periodic Gibbs states at $g$ the kernel $\mathsf s$ of its two-point function, $\sigma'_\xi((f,h))=\iint f(x)h(y)\,\mathsf s(|x-y|)\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y$ for $f,h$ of disjoint supports, is $\ge0$ and non-increasing, and $\mathsf s(r)\ge c_{\rm sd}r^{-6}$ for $0<r\le r_{\rm sd}$. Indeed, with the point vectors $\Psi_1$ of the reconstruction recalled below and $0<\epsilon<r/2$, $\mathsf s(r)=\|e^{-(r/2-\epsilon)H}\Psi_1(\epsilon e_3)\|^2$, and the truncated kernel, $\mathsf s$ minus the square of the one-point constant, is $\|e^{-(r/2-\epsilon)H}(1-|\Omega\rangle\langle\Omega|)\Psi_1(\epsilon e_3)\|^2$, the vacuum of a component being unique; both are $\ge0$ and non-increasing in $r$.

For $0<d\le\mathsf d_0(g,\frac1{10})$ let $f\ge0$ be of class $C^1$, equal to $1$ on the ball of radius $0.3d$ about $2de_3$ and to $0$ off the ball of radius $0.9d$ about it, with $\sup f=1$ and ${\rm Lip}\,f<3/d$: then $(\theta f,f)$ is a test pair at the scale $d$ with the shape parameter $\frac1{10}$ ({\cite[Lem.~I.1]{YMM2}}), its two supports lie at distances between $2.2d$ and $5.8d$, and $\int f<3.06\,d^3$. The lower bound of Cor.~\textup{\YMMref{127.11}{854}} makes the truncated two-point function at this pair at least $\frac23\,10^{-8}\mathsf c_2\mathsf b^{-2}$, with $\mathsf c_2=9/16\pi^2$ \YMMref{C}{7} and the label $\mathsf b\le L(g^{-2}+\bar B)$ (equation~\YMMref{(1854)}{710}); as the truncated kernel is non-increasing, its value at $2.2d$ is at least $\frac23\,10^{-8}\mathsf c_2\mathsf b^{-2}(3.06\,d^3)^{-2}$, and $\frac23\,10^{-8}\,\mathsf c_2\,(2.2)^6(3.06)^{-2}>4.6\cdot10^{-9}$ gives the bound at $r=2.2d$, for the truncated kernel and so for $\mathsf s$.

\paragraph{Space-time.} In $\mathbb R^3\ni x=(x_1,x_2,x_3)=(\vec x,x_3)$ the coordinate $x_3$ is Euclidean time and $\mathbb E_+=\{x_3>0\}$; $\theta,\theta_1$ are the reflections at $x_3=0$ and at $x_1=0$, $\tau_v$ is the translation by $v$, $\mathsf d(x_1,x_2,x_3)=(x_3,x_2,x_1)$, and $R_\tau x=(x_1\cos\tau-x_3\sin\tau,\,x_2,\,x_1\sin\tau+x_3\cos\tau)$, also on $\mathbb C^3$, with $R=R_{\pi/2}=\theta_1\mathsf d$; $\mathsf I=\{x_1>0,x_3>0\}$ and $\mathsf{II}=R\,\mathsf I=\{x_1<0,x_3>0\}$. An isometry $\mathsf r$ acts on functions by $\mathsf rh=h\circ\mathsf r^{-1}$ and on tuples entry by entry. In $\mathbb R^{1+2}\ni x=(x^0,x^1,x^2)$, $t=x^0$: $V_+=\{x^0>|\vec x|\}$, $W=\{x^1>|x^0|\}$, $W'=-W$, $\mathsf j(x)=(-x^0,-x^1,x^2)$, and $B(s)(t,x^1,x^2)=(t\cosh s+x^1\sinh s,\,t\sinh s+x^1\cosh s,\,x^2)$ are the boosts that keep $W$. A wedge is a region $\mathfrak gW$, $\mathfrak g$ in the Poincar\'e group; a double cone is a Poincar\'e image of $\{|x^0|+|\vec x|<r\}$, upright if it is a translate of one; $O^\times$ is the union of the open sets that are spacelike separated from $O$; $\mathcal F(O)=C^\infty_c(O;\mathbb C)$, $\mathcal F_{\mathbb R}(O)$ its real elements, $\mathcal S=\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{1+2})$, $\hat f$ the Fourier transform, and $f^{(a,\Lambda)}=f\circ(a,\Lambda)^{-1}$.

\paragraph{Data (Rec) and the reconstruction.} A separated tuple is a tuple of real $C^1_c$ functions on $\mathbb R^3$ with pairwise disjoint supports; $F,F'$ denote finite complex combinations of separated tuples, over a set if all supports lie in it, and $\bar F$ has the conjugate coefficients. Data (Rec) with a triple $(C_\wp,\wp,c_0)$ are the symmetric functionals $\sigma$ on separated tuples, $\sigma(\varnothing)=1$, with the following conditions (Section~\YMMref{107}{765}): (Rec1) $\sigma$ is invariant under the isometries of $\mathbb R^3$; (Rec2) $\sigma$ is reflection positive at $x_3=0$, the classes $[F]$ of the combinations over $\mathbb E_+$ span the Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, $\Omega=[\varnothing]$, and $e^{-tH}[F]=[\tau_{te_3}F]$ with $H\ge0$; (Rec3) the joint spectrum of $H$ and the momenta lies in $\{E\ge|q|\}$; (Rec4) $|\sigma(\theta\bar F\cdot(h)\cdot F')|\le C_\wp\eta^{-\wp}\|h\|_{L^1}\|[\tau_{-\eta e_3}F]\|\|[\tau_{-\eta e_3}F']\|$ for $0<\eta\le1$, $F,F'$ over $\{x_3>\eta\}$ and $h\in C^1_c(\{|x_3|<c_0\eta\})$. (Rec5) is the uniqueness of the vacuum, $\ker H=\mathbb C\Omega$.

The reconstruction in Sections~\YMMref{109}{772} and~\YMMref{110}{776} gives $N=1+H$, $\mathcal D_\infty=\bigcap_kD(H^k)$, a representation $U$ of the Poincar\'e group, and the field $\phi(f)$, $f\in\mathcal S$, on $\mathcal D_\infty$, with $\phi(f)^\dagger=\phi(\bar f)$ and $[H,\phi(f)]=i\phi(\partial_tf)$ on $\mathcal D_\infty$, and with Lorentz covariance and locality on the span $\mathcal D_0$ of the vectors $\phi(f_1)\cdots\phi(f_n)\Omega$ ($\mathcal D_0(O)$: all $f_k\in\mathcal F(O)$); for $Y=\phi(f_1)\cdots\phi(f_n)$ we write $Y^\dagger=\phi(\bar f_n)\cdots\phi(\bar f_1)$. It gives the field $\mathsf B(s,s')$ at the point $0$ between the Euclidean times $s,s'>0$, with $e^{-tH}\mathsf B(s,s')e^{-t'H}=\mathsf B(s+t,s'+t')$, $\mathsf B(s,s')^*=\mathsf B(s',s)$ and
\begin{equation}\label{C-363-2}
\|\mathsf B(s,s')\|\le C_\wp\min\{s,s',1\}^{-\wp},\qquad e^{-sH}\phi(f)e^{-sH}=\int f(x)\,U(x)\mathsf B(s,s)U(x)^{-1}\,\mathrm{d}x,
\end{equation}
the insertion operators of Lem.~\YMMref{107.1}{766}: for $0<\eta\le1$ and $h\in L^1(\{|x_3|<c_0\eta\})$, $\mathsf B^{\rm in}_\eta(h)$ is the bounded operator, linear in $h$ and of norm $\le C_\wp\eta^{-\wp}\|h\|_{L^1}$, with $\langle[\tau_{-\eta e_3}F],\mathsf B^{\rm in}_\eta(h)[\tau_{-\eta e_3}F']\rangle=\sigma(\theta\bar F\cdot(h)\cdot F')$ for $F,F'$ over $\{x_3>\eta\}$ when $h\in C^1_c(\{|x_3|<c_0\eta\})$, and by the insertion formula \YMMref{(2039)}{767} $\langle\psi,\mathsf B^{\rm in}_\eta(h)\psi'\rangle=\int h(x)\langle\psi,U(\vec x)\mathsf B(\eta+x_3,\eta-x_3)U(\vec x)^{-1}\psi'\rangle\,\mathrm{d}x$; the form $q_0$ of the field at the point $0$ and the time $0$, $q_0(e^{-sH}\psi',e^{-s'H}\psi)=\langle\psi',\mathsf B(s,s')\psi\rangle$, and point vectors $\Psi_n(z)$, holomorphic on the tube $\mathsf{Tb}^{(n)}=\{z\in(\mathbb C^3)^n:d(z_1)>0,\ d(z_{k+1}-z_k)>0\}$, $d(z)={\rm Re}\,z_3-|{\rm Im}(z_1,z_2)|$, of norm $\le(C_\wp\eta^{-\wp})^n$ where these numbers are $\ge2\eta$, $\eta\le1$, with $[G]=\int\prod_kh_k(x_k)\Psi_n(x)\,\mathrm{d}x$ for ordered tuples $G=(h_k)$ in $\mathbb E_+$ whose supports lie in balls of radii below $c_0$ times the gaps of the heights.

With the continued translations $\mathcal T(\mathfrak w)$, $\mathcal T(\eta e_3)=e^{-\eta H}$, and $\iota(t,\vec x)=(\vec x,-it)$, Lem.~\YMMref{109.2}{773}, which links the field operators with the point vectors, reads
$$\text{(Br)}\qquad\mathcal T(\mathfrak w_1)\phi(f_1)\cdots\mathcal T(\mathfrak w_n)\phi(f_n)\Omega=\int\prod_kf_k(x_k)\,\Psi_n\bigl((\iota x_k+\textstyle\sum_{i\le k}\mathfrak w_i)_k\bigr)\,\mathrm{d}x\qquad(d(\mathfrak w_i)>0),$$
and the products of fields are the limits of these vectors as the $\mathfrak w_i$ tend to $0$.

\paragraph{The net and the conditions.} $P_n=\mathbf 1_{[n,n+1)}(H)$, $b_{mn}(f)=\|P_m\phi(f)P_n\|$, $\bar\phi(f)$ is the closure of $\phi(f)$, $\mathcal P$ is the joint spectral measure of the translations, $U(B(s))=e^{isK}$ and $\Delta^s=e^{-2\pi sK}$. For open $O$
$$\mathcal C(O)=\{Q\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H):\langle\phi(\bar f)\psi,Q\psi'\rangle=\langle\psi,Q\phi(f)\psi'\rangle\ \ \forall f\in\mathcal F(O),\ \psi,\psi'\in\mathcal D_0\},\qquad\mathcal A(O)=\mathcal C(O)';$$
$\mathcal L(O)=\mathcal A(O)\cap\mathcal C(O^\times)$; $\mathcal H_0$ is the closure of $\mathcal C(W)\Omega$; for bounded open convex $O$, $\mathcal A^d(O)=\bigcap\{\mathcal A(\mathfrak gW):\mathfrak gW\supset O\}$, and for other open $G$, $\mathcal A^d(G)=\bigvee\{\mathcal A^d(O):O\subset G\ \text{a double cone}\}$. $\mathfrak P$ is the unital $*$-algebra generated linearly by $\mathcal F(\mathbb R^{1+2})$, with $f^*=\bar f$ and $gh=hg$ for real spacelike separated $g,h$; $\pi$ is its representation by the fields on $\mathcal D_0$ and $\mathcal W(f_1\cdots f_n)=\langle\Omega,\phi(f_1)\cdots\phi(f_n)\Omega\rangle$ its Wightman functional; for a subalgebra $\mathfrak A$, $\mathfrak A^+$ is the set of the finite sums $\sum Z_i^*Z_i$, $Z_i\in\mathfrak A$; $\mathfrak P(W)$ is generated by $1$ and $\mathcal F(W)$.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(W)] $\mathcal C(O_1)'\subset\mathcal C(O_2)$ for all non-empty open spacelike separated $O_1,O_2$.
\item[(CP)] For every upright double cone $K$, real $f\in\mathcal F(K)$ and $Y_0,\dots,Y_r$ in the algebra $\mathfrak A$ generated by $1$, $f$ and $\mathcal F(K^\times)$: if $\sum_n\lambda^nY_n\in\mathfrak A^+$ for all real $\lambda$, then $\mathcal W(\sum_nf^nY_n)\ge0$.
\item[(QCP$_f$)] For real $f\in\mathcal F(K)$, $K$ an upright double cone with $\bar K\subset W'$, and $\eta=\phi(f)\Omega$: if $Y_0,Y_1,Y_2\in\mathfrak P(W)$ and $Y_0+\lambda Y_1+\lambda^2Y_2\in\mathfrak P(W)^+$ for all real $\lambda$, then $\langle\Omega,Y_0\Omega\rangle+\langle\Omega,Y_1\eta\rangle+\langle\eta,Y_2\eta\rangle\ge0$. This is the second order of (CP) at $f$; its first order is the same statement with $Y_2=0$.
\item[(LB$_{u,c}$)] $|\langle\psi,\phi(u)\psi\rangle|\le c\langle\psi,N\psi\rangle$ on $\mathcal D_0$; (LB$^\pm_{u,c}$) are its halves $\pm\langle\psi,\phi(u)\psi\rangle\le c\langle\psi,N\psi\rangle$; (LB$_u$) holds if (LB$_{u,c}$) holds for some $c$, and $c_*(u)\in[0,\infty]$ is the least such $c$.
\item[(QA$_f$)] $\sum_n\|\phi(f)^n\Omega\|^{-1/n}=\infty$.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{The objects.} For a state $\nu$ on $L^{-K}\mathbb Z^3$ or on a torus and a tuple $X=(f_i)$ let $(X)^\nu_K=\prod_i(\mathcal O_K(f_i)-\nu(\mathcal O_K(f_i)))$, extended linearly to combinations; $\theta$ and the bar act on lattice functions by reflection and conjugation. A pair $(K,\beta)$ is admitted at $g$ if it lies in the canonical family $\mathfrak d(g)$ of equation~\YMMref{(1843)}{708} ({\cite[\S{}K.1]{YMM2}}), that is, if it is a first-passage datum at $g$ (Cor.~\YMMref{74.2}{616}), formed at the fixed $(\sigma^-,\gamma)$: along the flow $x_0=\beta$, $x_k=L^{-1}x_{k-1}-b_k$ of the inverse squared running coupling, whose increments obey $|b_k|\le B_\sharp$, $K$ is the least index with $x_K\le X_g=L(g^{-2}+B_\sharp)$.

Then $x_0>x_1>\dots>x_K\ge\gamma^{-2}$, and the label $L^{-K}\beta$ lies in the outer interval of the labels $I^{\rm lab}(g)=[g^{-2}+B_\sharp-L^{-1}\bar B,\,L(g^{-2}+\bar B)]$ of (equation~\YMMref{(1854)}{710}) (Cor.~\YMMref{74.2}{616}). A periodic Gibbs state at $(K,\beta)$ is a Gibbs state of the Wilson weight $e^{-\beta\sum_pa_p}$ on $L^{-K}\mathbb Z^3$ that is invariant under the translations of a subgroup of finite index of $L^{-K}\mathbb Z^3$; a torus state at $(K,\beta)$ is a weak limit point, as $m\to\infty$, of the Wilson measures of the tori $L^{-K}\mathbb Z^3/2L^m\mathbb Z^3$ (Section~\YMMref{91}{697}), and it is a periodic Gibbs state (Prop.~\YMMref{91.2}{699}). A volume-first limit at $g$ ({\cite[\S{}K.1]{YMM2}}) has a defining sequence $(K_j,\beta_j,\nu_j)$: $K_j\to\infty$, pairs $(K_j,\beta_j)$ admitted at $g$, and torus states $\nu_j$ at $(K_j,\beta_j)$ whose connected functions converge; its centred functional is $\sigma(X)=\lim_j\nu_j((X)_j)$, $(X)_j=(X)^{\nu_j}_{K_j}$.

A limit of periodic Gibbs states at $g$ is $\sigma'(X)=\lim_j\rho_j((X)^{\rho_j}_{K_j})$ for periodic Gibbs states $\rho_j$ of the Wilson weight at admitted pairs $(K_j,\beta_j)$, $K_j\to\infty$. In general $(\cdot)_j$ is the product at $K_j$ centred by the $j$-th state of the sequence at hand: $(X)_j=(X)^{\nu_j}_{K_j}$ for the centred functional, $(X)_j=(X)^{\rho_j}_{K_j}$ for a limit of periodic Gibbs states $\rho_j$, also where the periodic Gibbs states $\rho_{j,\xi}$ that approximate a component integrate, the $\rho_j$ giving the centring, and, in Steps~2--7 of the proof of Thm.~\ref{C-363-4}, the product on the torus $\Lambda_j$ centred by the Wilson measure $\mu_j$ there. A canonical decomposition $(\mathsf X,\lambda,(\sigma_\xi))$ of $\sigma$ has $\mathsf X$ compact metrisable, $\lambda$ a probability measure of full support, $\xi\mapsto\sigma_\xi(X)$ continuous, $\xi\mapsto\sigma_\xi$ injective, and iterated cluster limits $\lim_{|v_q|\to\infty}\cdots\lim_{|v_1|\to\infty}\sigma(X^0\cdot\tau_{v_1}X^1\cdots\tau_{v_q}X^q)=\int\prod_i\sigma_\xi(X^i)\,\lambda(\,\mathrm{d}\xi)$; the $\sigma_\xi$ are its components, and objects of $\sigma_\xi$ bear the index $\xi$.

\paragraph{Lattice, norms, slabs.} On $\Lambda=a\mathbb Z^3/\ell\mathbb Z^3$, $\ell/a$ even and $\ge4$: $G=\mathrm{SU}(2)$ with Haar measure, $t_p=\frac12{\rm tr}\,\partial U(p)$, $a_p=1-t_p$, the Wilson measure $\mu_\beta\propto e^{-\beta\sum_pa_p}dU$, and $\mathcal O(f)=a^{-1}\sum_pf(x(p))a_p$, $x(p)$ the barycentre of $p$ ($\mathcal O_K$ at $a=L^{-K}$). $\|h\|_\sharp=\max\{\sup|h|,40M\,{\rm Lip}\,h\}$ and $\|h\|_{\sharp,\mathsf l}=\max\{\sup|h|,40M\mathsf l\,{\rm Lip}\,h\}$; on $\mathbb R^2$, $|h|_{C^1}=\sup|h|+\sup|\nabla h|$; $\|f\|_\star=\int \,\mathrm{d}t\sum_{\kappa\in\mathbb Z^2}\sup_{\vec x\in\kappa+[-1,1]^2}(|f|+|\nabla_{\vec x}f|)(t,\vec x)$. A board $(i,o)$ of $L^{-K}\mathbb Z^3$, $i\le K-1$ and $o$ a site of $L^{-K}\mathbb Z^3$, is its partition into the cells $\square_{\mathbf k}=o+\mathsf l\mathbf k+[-\frac{\mathsf l}2,\frac{\mathsf l}2]^3$, $\mathbf k\in\mathbb Z^3$, cubes of side $\mathsf l=L^{-i}$ centred at the sites $o+\mathsf l\mathbf k$; the middle of $\square_{\mathbf k}$ is $\{|x-o-\mathsf l\mathbf k|_\infty\le\frac{\mathsf l}4\}$; for odd $L$ the walls of the cells lie midway between sites and the middle planes of the cells pass through sites; and $\|\cdot\|_{\rm ch}$ is the seminorm of the chessboard estimate.

For $h\in L^1(\mathbb R^2)$, $\mathsf B_h(s,s')=\int h(\vec x)U(\vec x)\mathsf B(s,s')U(\vec x)^{-1}d^2x$ is the field at time $0$ smeared in space; $T_{mn}(h)=P_me^{sH}\mathsf B_h(s,s')e^{s'H}P_n$ does not depend on $s,s'$, and $\mathsf T(h)=\sum_{m,n}T_{mn}(h)$ is the form of the field at time $0$ on the vectors of bounded energy. With $\rho_{\mathsf l}(\varsigma)=\frac5{\mathsf l}\cos^2\frac{5\pi\varsigma}{2\mathsf l}$ on $|\varsigma|\le\frac{\mathsf l}5$ and $0$ elsewhere, the plate is $\mathsf I_{\mathsf l}(h)=\int\rho_{\mathsf l}(\varsigma)\mathsf B_h(\frac{\mathsf l}2+\varsigma,\frac{\mathsf l}2-\varsigma)\,\mathrm{d}\varsigma$.

\subsubsection{From fields to bounded local operators}

There are two locality questions in this argument. The reconstructed
field satisfies a commutation relation on its common invariant domain.
A local net requires commuting algebras of bounded operators. Passing
from the first statement to the second requires control of closures
and their commutants. The energy estimates make the closures
available; the lattice approximation supplies the bounded operators.
Keeping these two tasks separate explains why reconstruction alone
does not end the argument.

For an open region $O$ in Minkowski space, write
$\mathcal F(O)=C_c^\infty(O;\mathbb C)$ and let $\mathcal D_0$ be the
span of field polynomials applied to the vacuum. A bounded operator
$Q$ belongs to the weak commutant $\mathcal C(O)$ when
\[
 \langle\phi(\bar f)\psi,Q\psi'\rangle
   =\langle\psi,Q\phi(f)\psi'\rangle,
 \qquad f\in\mathcal F(O),\quad \psi,\psi'\in\mathcal D_0.
\]
Thus the definition involves bounded $Q$, although the field on either
side is initially defined on $\mathcal D_0$. The proposed local algebra
is $\mathcal A(O)=\mathcal C(O)'$. To establish locality one must show
that these algebras commute for spacelike separated regions. The
relation of field polynomials on $\mathcal D_0$ does not itself give
that assertion about their bounded commutants.

The construction first uses the wedges
\[
 W=\{(t,x^1,x^2):x^1>|t|\},\qquad W'=-W.
\]
Their Euclidean antecedents are quadrants. A quarter turn exchanges
the two boundaries of a quadrant, so the two Euclidean reflection
forms put a finite-lattice operator on the two sides of the same
Hilbert-space pairing. The finite-lattice four-square construction
in \cref{C-363-14} is the source of the required bounded
approximation. It retains the operator norm bound while keeping
track of what the quarter turn does to vectors. Both pieces of
information are needed: convergence of correlation functions
would retain the vectors without supplying a bounded operator in
the desired commutant.

In the limit, the quarter-turn operator is identified with
$\Delta^{1/4}$, where the boost generator $K$ is normalized by
$\Delta^s=e^{-2\pi sK}$. This is an assertion about functional
calculus, rather than a substitution of an imaginary angle into an
unbounded operator. First prove convergence for the
quarter turn, applies bounded functions of it, and only then reads
off the corresponding bounded functions of $K$. This order permits
the approximation to pass through the lattice Hilbert spaces.

Write $\mathsf I=\{x_1>0,x_3>0\}$ in Euclidean space. For real
$u\in C_c^\infty(\mathsf I)$, define the Schwartz function
\[
 f_u(B(s)(0,\rho,x_2))
   =\int_0^{\pi/2}u(\rho\cos\alpha,x_2,\rho\sin\alpha)
          e^{-(s+i(\pi/4-\alpha))^2}\,\mathrm{d}\alpha
\]
on $W$, and set it to zero off $W$. Here $\rho>0$ and $s$ is the
boost parameter. This Gaussian smoothing is the bounded functional
calculus just described. Let $\theta_1$ reflect the first Euclidean
coordinate. The construction gives bounded
$T_u^{(\epsilon)}\in\mathcal C(W')$ such that
\[
 \|T_u^{(\epsilon)}\Omega-\phi(f_u)\Omega\|
 \le \frac{\sqrt\epsilon}{2}\pi e^{5\pi^2/8}
          \|[\theta_1u\cdot u]\|.
\]
The norm on the right is determined by a separated Euclidean four-point
function. It is finite before $\epsilon$ is sent to zero. Hence the
field vectors $\phi(f_u)\Omega$ lie in
$\overline{\mathcal C(W')\Omega}$. The Fourier transforms of the $f_u$ have no common real zero,
which gives density. This is the point at which a supply of bounded
lattice limits becomes sufficient to determine the wedge algebra.

Let $J$ be the antiunitary implementing the wedge reflection in the
modular construction. The modular relation on this dense family is
\[
 J\Delta^{1/2}Y\Omega=Y^*\Omega.
\]
Boost invariance makes the family a core for the operator on the
left. Thus a smaller algebra generated by the lattice limits and
the candidate wedge algebra have the same modular conjugation.
The inclusion between the algebras gives the reverse inclusion
between their commutants; conjugation by $J$ closes the inclusion
back on the algebras. The detailed argument below uses this to
identify the wedge algebra, prove wedge duality, and obtain
\[
 \mathcal A(W)'=\mathcal A(W'),\qquad
 \Delta^{it}=U(B(-2\pi t)).
\]

Double cones require a further distinction. For a bounded convex
region $O$, intersect the wedge algebras containing $O$; for general
open regions, take joins over contained double cones. This defines
the dual completion $\mathcal A^d$. The argument establishes its
locality and duality, but does not identify it with $\mathcal A$ on
every double cone. Wedge equality supplies the construction of
$\mathcal A^d$ without settling that additional equality.

Finally, the component argument has two levels. Positivity
inequalities pass to every component through the continuous
decomposition of the Euclidean functional. The identification of
the fibre of a decomposable wedge algebra is a direct-integral
statement and holds almost everywhere. In particular, a fibre identity is not
promoted to an identity at every point of the component space.

\subsubsection{Principal results}

\begin{theorem}[The net of data (Rec)]\label{C-363-3}
Let $\sigma$ be data (Rec) with the triple $(C_\wp,\wp,c_0)$; uniqueness of the vacuum is not assumed. Every statement holds also with $W$ and $W'$ exchanged.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] \emph{Frame.} For every $n$ the spaces $N^n\mathcal D_0$ and $N^n\mathcal D_0(O)$, $O\ne\emptyset$ open, are dense, and $\phi(f)$ on $\mathcal D_0$ and on $\mathcal D_\infty$ have one closure $\bar\phi(f)$. $\mathcal C(O)=\{Q:Q\bar\phi(f)\subset\bar\phi(f)Q,\ f\in\mathcal F(O)\}$ is a von Neumann algebra, $U(\mathfrak g)\mathcal C(O)U(\mathfrak g)^{-1}=\mathcal C(\mathfrak gO)$, and $\mathcal A$ is isotonous and covariant. For $O\ne\emptyset$, $\Omega$ is separating for $\mathcal C(O)$ and cyclic for $\mathcal A(O)$; $\bar\phi(f)$, $f\in\mathcal F(O)$, is affiliated with $\mathcal A(O)$, and $\mathcal A$ is the least net with this property; $\mathcal C(\bigcup_iO_i)=\bigcap_i\mathcal C(O_i)$ and $\mathcal A(\bigcup_iO_i)=\bigvee_i\mathcal A(O_i)$. $\mathcal L$ is isotonous, covariant and local; (W) holds if and only if $\mathcal L=\mathcal A$, and if and only if it holds for spacelike separated upright double cones.
\item[(b)] \emph{The order $\wp$.} For $f\in\mathcal S$ and $m,n\in\mathbb N_0$:
(b1) $b_{mn}(f)\le eC_\wp\|f\|_{L^1}(m+n+2)^\wp$;
(b2) $(|m-n|-1)^kb_{mn}(f)\le b_{mn}(\partial_t^kf)$ if $|m-n|\ge2$, $k\in\mathbb N$;
(b3) for $\epsilon\in(0,1]$, $k_1=\max\{0,\lceil(\wp-1)/\epsilon\rceil\}$ and $|m-n|>(m+n+2)^\epsilon$: $b_{mn}(f)\le3^{k_1}eC_\wp\|\partial_t^{k_1}f\|_{L^1}(m+n+2)$, so that the blocks are linearly bounded off every band $|m-n|\le(m+n+2)^\epsilon$, $\epsilon>0$;
(b4) $b_{mn}(h*f)\le\|h\|_{L^1}b_{mn}(f)$ for $h\in L^1(\mathbb R^{1+2})$ with $h*f\in\mathcal S$;
(b5) with $\mathsf s_0(q)=1+2\cdot2^q+2\cdot3^q$ and $\mathsf s(q,k)=\sum_{l\ge1}(l+3)^ql^{-k}$, for real $j\ge0$ and $\psi,\psi'\in\mathcal D_\infty$:
$$\|N^j\phi(f)\psi\|\le2^je^2C_\wp\bigl[\mathsf s_0(\wp+j)\|f\|_{L^1}+2\mathsf s(\wp+j,k_j)\|\partial_t^{k_j}f\|_{L^1}\bigr]\|N^{\wp+j}\psi\|,\qquad k_j=\lfloor\wp+j\rfloor+2,$$
$$|\langle\psi',\phi(f)\psi\rangle|\le e^2C_\wp\bigl[\mathsf s_0(\tfrac\wp2)\|f\|_{L^1}+2\mathsf s(\tfrac\wp2,k_\flat)\|\partial_t^{k_\flat}f\|_{L^1}\bigr]\|N^{\wp/2}\psi'\|\,\|N^{\wp/2}\psi\|,\qquad k_\flat=\lfloor\tfrac\wp2\rfloor+2,$$
and $D(H^\wp)\subset D(\bar\phi(f))$; at $\wp=4$ the two brackets are bounded above by $195\|f\|_{L^1}+537.82\|\partial_t^6f\|_{L^1}$ and $27\|f\|_{L^1}+37.20\|\partial_t^4f\|_{L^1}$.
\item[(c)] \emph{Wedge relation.} There is exactly one antiunitary $J$ with $J\Omega=\Omega$, $J\mathcal D_0=\mathcal D_0$ and $J\phi(f)\psi=\phi(\bar f\circ\mathsf j)J\psi$ for $\psi\in\mathcal D_0$; $J^2=1$, $JU(a)J=U(\mathsf ja)$, $JU(B(s))J=U(B(s))$ and $J\mathcal C(O)J=\mathcal C(\mathsf jO)$. For $f_1,\dots,f_n\in\mathcal F(W)$ and $Y=\phi(f_1)\cdots\phi(f_n)$: $Y\Omega\in D(\Delta^{1/2})$ and $J\Delta^{1/2}Y\Omega=Y^\dagger\Omega$; every boost-invariant dense subspace of $D(\Delta^{1/2})$ is a core of $\Delta^{1/2}$, and $\mathcal D_0(W)$ is one. For $Q\in\mathcal C(W)$: $JQ\Omega\in D(\Delta^{1/2})$ and $\Delta^{1/2}JQ\Omega=Q^*\Omega$. Moreover $\mathcal C(W')\subset\mathcal C(W)'$ on all of $\mathcal H$; hence $O\mapsto\mathcal C(O^\times)$ is isotonous, covariant and local on double cones, $\mathcal C(O^\times)\subset\mathcal A^d(O)$, and (W) holds if and only if $\mathcal C(O^\times)=\mathcal A^d(O)$ for all double cones $O$.
\item[(d)] \emph{What locality says.} For every $\epsilon>0$ there is a real $f_*\in C^\infty_c(\mathbb R^{1+2})$, $f_*\ge0$, $\int f_*=1$, even in each coordinate, with support in $[-\epsilon,\epsilon]^3$ and $\hat f_*(p)>0$ for all real $p$; it may be chosen with $\|\partial_t^kf_*\|_{L^1}\le A_0R_0^k(k!)^2$ for all $k$, $A_0=\frac{e^3\pi}2$, $R_0=\frac{3e\pi^2}{2\epsilon}$. The following are equivalent: (W); $\mathcal C(W)\Omega$ is dense; $\mathcal C(W)'=\mathcal C(W')$; $J\mathcal A(W)J\subset\mathcal C(W)$; (CP); $\phi(f)\Omega\in\mathcal H_0$ for all $f\in\mathcal F(W)$; $\phi(f)\Omega\in\mathcal H_0$ for all $f$ in a set $\mathfrak F\subset\mathcal S$ whose Fourier transforms have no common real zero (for instance $\mathfrak F=\{f_s\}$, one real $f_s$ with $\hat f_s$ free of real zeros); $\inf_{s\in\mathbb R}{\rm dist}(U(B(s))\phi(f_s)\Omega,\mathcal H_0)=0$ for one such $f_s$; for one real $f_0\ge0$, $f_0\ne0$, in $C^\infty_c$, every Lorentz transformation $\Lambda$ has a translation $a_\Lambda$ with $\phi(f_0^{(a_\Lambda,\Lambda)})\Omega\in\mathcal H_0$; (QCP$_{f_s}$) for one such $f_s$ with support in an upright double cone $K$, $\bar K\subset W'$.

The first order of (QCP$_f$) holds for all data (Rec), and (QCP$_f$) gives operators $Q_n\in\mathcal C(W)$ with $\|Q_n\|\le n$ and $Q_n\Omega\to\phi(f)\Omega$. $\mathsf D(f)={\rm dist}(\phi(f)\Omega,\mathcal H_0)$ is a seminorm on $\mathcal S$, invariant under translations and under the boosts $B(s)$, with $\mathsf D(h*f)\le\|h\|_{L^1}\mathsf D(f)$; (W) holds if and only if $\mathsf D\equiv0$. Under (W), $\mathcal A(W)=\mathcal C(W')$, $\Omega$ is cyclic and separating for it, its modular group is $\Delta^{it}=U(B(-2\pi t))$ and its modular conjugation is $J$. (CP) implies, for real $f,g_1,g_2$ with pairwise spacelike separated compact supports,
$$|\mathcal W(fg_1g_2)|^4\le\mathcal W(f^2g_1^2)\,\mathcal W(f^2g_2^2)\,\mathcal W(g_1^2g_2^2),$$
and $\mathcal W(p(f_1,f_2))\ge0$ for every real polynomial $p\ge0$ on $\mathbb R^2$ and real spacelike separated $f_1,f_2$; Motzkin's polynomial $x^4y^2+x^2y^4-3x^2y^2+1$, which is no sum of squares, is among them.
\item[(e)] \emph{Dual net.} Assume (W), and let $O,O_1,O_2$ be bounded, open and convex. Then $\mathcal A^d(O)=\mathcal C(O^\times)=\mathcal A(O^\times)'\supset\mathcal A(O)$ is a von Neumann algebra; $\mathcal A^d$ is isotonous and covariant, $J\mathcal A^d(O)J=\mathcal A^d(\mathsf jO)$, $\Omega$ is cyclic and separating for $\mathcal A^d(O)$, and $\bar\phi(f)$, $f\in\mathcal F(O)$, is affiliated with it; $\mathcal A^d(O_1)\subset\mathcal A^d(O_2)'$ for spacelike separated $O_1,O_2$; $\mathcal A^d(O)'=\mathcal A(O^\times)=\mathcal A^d(O^\times)=\bigvee\{\mathcal A(\tilde W'):\tilde W\supset O\text{ a wedge}\}$; every family $O\mapsto\mathfrak F(O)$ of bounded operators with $\mathfrak F(O)\subset\mathcal A(O_1)'$ for all double cones $O_1\subset O^\times$ has $\mathfrak F(O)\subset\mathcal A^d(O)$; $\mathcal A^d(\tilde W)=\mathcal A(\tilde W)$ for wedges $\tilde W$, so $(\mathcal A^d)^d=\mathcal A^d$; and $\mathcal A(O)=\mathcal A^d(O)$ if and only if $\mathcal C(O^\times)\subset\mathcal C(O)'$. $\mathcal A^d$ is outer regular: for a double cone $O=(a+V_+)\cap(b-V_+)$ and $O_\epsilon=(a-\epsilon e_0+V_+)\cap(b+\epsilon e_0-V_+)$, $\mathcal A^d(O)=\bigcap_{\epsilon>0}\mathcal A^d(O_\epsilon)$. Without (W): $O\mapsto\bigcap_{\mathfrak gW\supset O}\mathcal A(\mathfrak gW)$ is local if and only if (W) holds.
\item[(f)] \emph{Sufficient conditions.} Let $k_0=\max\{1,\lceil\wp\rceil\}$. If $f$ is real and $|\langle\psi,\phi(\partial_tf)\psi\rangle|\le c\langle\psi,N\psi\rangle$ on $\mathcal D_0$, then $\phi(f)$ is essentially self-adjoint on $\mathcal D_0$; if besides $\sup_{m,n}b_{mn}(\partial_t^jf)/(m+n+2)<\infty$ for $1\le j\le k_0+3$, the resolvents of $\bar\phi(f)$ keep $D(H^k)$, $k\le k_0$, off a strip about $\mathbb R$, and all of them lie in $\mathcal C(O)$ for every open $O$ spacelike separated from ${\rm supp}f$. Each of the following implies (W) and (CP).
(f1) There are real $f_i\in C^\infty_c$, ${\rm supp}f_i\subset\{|x|\le\delta_i\}$, $\delta_i\to0$, $\int f_i=1$, $\sup_i\|f_i\|_{L^1}<\infty$, and numbers $c_i,\epsilon_i>0$, nothing uniform in $i$, with $b_{mn}(\partial_tf_i)\le c_i(m+n+2)(1+\log(m+n+2))$ for $|m-n|\le(m+n+2)^{\epsilon_i}$.
(f2) There is a real $f_0\in C^\infty_c$, $f_0\ge0$, $f_0\ne0$, even in $t$, with $\langle\psi,\phi(\partial_tf_0)\psi\rangle\le c\langle\psi,N\psi\rangle$ on $\mathcal D_0$.
(f3) (QA$_{f_0}$) holds for one real $f_0\in C^\infty_c$, $f_0\ge0$, $f_0\ne0$.
(f4) $\wp\le1$, or $\|\mathsf B(s,s)\|\le Cs^{-1}(1+\log s^{-1})$ for $0<s\le1$; then every $\phi(f)$, $f\in\mathcal S$ real, is essentially self-adjoint on $\mathcal D_0$, and the closures commute strongly at spacelike separation.
(f5) There are bounded operators $\mathsf B^e_h(s,s')$, $s,s'>0$, real linear in $h\in C^1_c(\mathbb R^2)$, with $e^{-tH}\mathsf B^e_h(s,s')e^{-t'H}=\mathsf B^e_h(s+t,s'+t')$, $\mathsf B^e_h(s,s')^*=\mathsf B^e_h(s',s)$ and $\|\int\rho_e(\varsigma/\eta)\mathsf B^e_h(\eta+\varsigma,\eta-\varsigma)\,\mathrm{d}\varsigma\|\le C_e|h|_{C^1}$ for all $\eta=\frac1{4(k+2)}$, $k\in\mathbb N_0$, for one measurable $\rho_e\ge0$ on $[-\frac12,\frac12]$ with $\bar\rho_e=\int\rho_e>0$; and with the time average $\mathsf e(f)=\int q_{f_t}(e^{-itH}\cdot,e^{-itH}\cdot)\,\mathrm{d}t$ of the sharp-time forms $q_h$ of $\mathsf B^e$ (Lem.~\ref{C-363-20}), the boosts $B_j(s)$ in the direction $e_j$, one $s>0$ and real $\mathsf c,\mathsf c'$:
$$\langle\psi,\phi(f)\psi\rangle=\mathsf c\Bigl[(1+2\coth^2s)\,\mathsf e(f)(\psi,\psi)-\frac1{2\sinh^2s}\sum_{j=1,2}\sum_\pm\mathsf e\bigl(f\circ B_j(\pm s)\bigr)(\psi_{j,\pm},\psi_{j,\pm})\Bigr]+\mathsf c'\int f\,\|\psi\|^2$$
for real $f\in C^\infty_c$ and $\psi\in\mathcal D_0$, $\psi_{j,\pm}=U(B_j(\pm s))^{-1}\psi$. Then (LB$_f$) holds for every real $f\in C^\infty_c$.
If the bound of (f2) holds at $f_0=f_*$, the function of (d), then (f1) holds with the functions $f_i=f_**\mu_i$, $\mu_i\in\mathcal S$; this route to (W) does not use the wedge relation (c).
\item[(g)] \emph{Mixtures and limits.} Let $(\mathsf X,\lambda,(\sigma_\xi))$ be a canonical decomposition of $\sigma$ with all $\sigma_\xi$ data (Rec) with one triple. For real $u\in\mathcal S$ and $c\ge0$, (LB$_{u,c}$), and each of (LB$^\pm_{u,c}$), holds for $\sigma$ if and only if it holds for every $\sigma_\xi$; so do (CP) and (W); and every inequality $\mathcal W(a)\ge0$, $a\in\mathfrak P$ fixed, passes from all $\sigma_\xi$ to $\sigma$. If data (Rec) $\sigma_j$ with one triple converge to $\sigma$ on separated tuples, then $\mathcal W^{\sigma_j}(f_1\cdots f_n)\to\mathcal W^\sigma(f_1\cdots f_n)$ for all $f_k\in\mathcal S$: the real-time functions converge; every inequality $\mathcal W(a)\ge0$, $a\in\mathfrak P$, passes to $\sigma$, and (LB$^\pm_{u,c}$), (CP) and (W) pass from all $\sigma_j$ to $\sigma$.
\item[(h)] \emph{Two bounds towards a linear one.} (h1) Let $\mathsf l,r>0$, $Q\ge1$, $c_2\ge0$, $\mathfrak m\in\mathbb R$, $h'\in C^\infty_c(\mathbb R^2)$ real, $\rho_1\ge0$ even, of class $C^1$, carried by $(-\frac14,\frac14)$, $\int\rho_1=1$, and let $\hat D(x)$, $x\in[-r,r]$, be bounded operators with: (i) $x\mapsto\hat D(x)$ is the restriction of a function holomorphic in norm on a complex neighbourhood of $[-r,r]$; (ii) $\hat D(x)=\hat D(x)^*\ge0$ and $\|\hat D(x)\|\le Q$; (iii) $\hat D(0)=e^{-\mathsf lH}$; (iv) $\hat D'(0)=\mathsf I-\mathfrak me^{-\mathsf lH}$ with $\mathsf I=\int\mathsf l^{-1}\rho_1(\varsigma/\mathsf l)\mathsf B_{h'}(\frac{\mathsf l}2+\varsigma,\frac{\mathsf l}2-\varsigma)\,\mathrm{d}\varsigma$; (v) for every $\Lambda<\infty$ and every $\psi$ in $\mathcal H_\Lambda=\mathbf 1_{[0,\Lambda]}(H)\mathcal H$: $\limsup_{\epsilon\downarrow0}\sup_{|x|\le r}\frac{d^2}{dx^2}\langle\psi,-\log(\hat D(x)+\epsilon)\psi\rangle\le c_2\langle\psi,N\psi\rangle$. Then for $\psi\in\mathcal D_\infty$
$$\bigl|\langle\psi,\phi(g_{\mathsf l}\otimes h')\psi\rangle-\mathfrak m\|\psi\|^2\bigr|\le\frac{\mathsf l\langle\psi,H\psi\rangle+\log(Q+1)\|\psi\|^2}r+\frac r2\,c_2\langle\psi,N\psi\rangle,$$
where $\hat g_{\mathsf l}(E)=\mathsf G(\mathsf lE)$, $\mathsf G(y)=\int\rho_1(s)\cosh(sy)\,\mathrm{d}s\,\frac{y/2}{\sinh(y/2)}$. No injectivity of $\hat D(x)$ is assumed, and under (i)--(iv) the slope is the real-time average of the field: $\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}\frac d{dx}\langle\psi',\log(\hat D(x)+\epsilon)\psi\rangle|_{x=0}=\langle\psi',\phi(g_{\mathsf l}\otimes h')\psi\rangle-\mathfrak m\langle\psi',\psi\rangle$ for $\psi,\psi'\in\mathcal H_\Lambda$. If such bounds hold at all $\mathsf l=L^{-i}$ with constants $\le C\mathsf l^{-N_0}$, then (LB$_{k\otimes h'}$) holds for every real $k\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R)$. (h2) Let $\wp<6$. For a unit timelike vector $n\in V_+$, $\mu\ge1$, Borel sets $\Delta,\Delta'\subset\{p\in\bar V_+:n\cdot p\le\mu\}$ and $u\in\mathcal S$: $\|\mathcal P(\Delta')\phi(u)\mathcal P(\Delta)\|\le e^2C_\wp\|u\|_{L^1}\mu^\wp$. For $\mu\ge1$, $u\in\mathcal S$ and vectors $\psi,\psi'$ of bounded energy in the spectral subspace of $\{p\cdot p\le\mu^2\}$:
$$|\langle\psi',\phi(u)\psi\rangle|\le C_{\rm L}\bigl(\|u\|_{L^1}+\|\mathcal L^4u\|_{L^1}\bigr)\mu^\wp\|\psi'\|\|\psi\|,\qquad\mathcal L=-\partial_t^2-\partial_1^2-\partial_2^2,$$
with $C_{\rm L}=100e^2C_\wp\max\{18^\wp,6^\wp c\,\Sigma_\wp\}$, $\Sigma_\wp=\sum_{r\ge1}(r+1)r^{-8}(2r+3)^\wp$ and a numeral $c$, formed from $C_\wp,\wp$ alone; for the following two consequences assume additionally $\wp>0$. Then for all $m,n$, with $\mathcal P_<$ the spectral projection of $\{p\cdot p\le(m+n+2)^{2/\wp}\}$: $\|\mathcal P_<P_m\phi(u)P_n\mathcal P_<\|\le C_{\rm L}(\|u\|_{L^1}+\|\mathcal L^4u\|_{L^1})(m+n+2)$. With $\Pi$ the spectral projection of $\{p:p\cdot p\le(1+p^0)^{2/\wp}\}$, $\|\Pi e^{-sH}\phi(u)e^{-sH}\Pi\|\le c(u)s^{-1}$ for $0<s\le1$, $c(u)$ formed from $C_{\rm L}$ and the norms $\|\partial_t^ju\|_{L^1}+\|\mathcal L^4\partial_t^ju\|_{L^1}$, $j\le2$. For data (Rec) of any order $\wp$ and real $f\in\mathcal S$, energy and invariant mass together bound the field: $\pm\phi(f)\le c(f)(1+H+M^2)^{\wp/2}$ as forms on the vectors of bounded energy, $M^2=\int(E^2-|q|^2)\,\mathrm{d}\mathcal P$ the operator of the invariant mass squared, $c(f)$ formed from $C_\wp$, $\wp$ and finitely many of the norms $\|\partial_\nu^kf\|_{L^1}$, $\nu=0,1,2$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Locality of the continuum limits]\label{C-363-4}
Let $0<g\le\gamma$, let $\sigma$ be the centred functional of a volume-first limit at $g$, and let $\tau$ be $\sigma$ or a component of a canonical decomposition of $\sigma$; every such limit, decomposition and component is admitted. On $\mathcal H(\tau)$:
\begin{enumerate}
