2\int(1-e^{-t\lambda})\,\mathrm{d}\nu=2t\int\lambda\,\mathrm{d}\nu-2\int(t\lambda-1+e^{-t\lambda})\,\mathrm{d}\nu,
\]
with 
\[
\mathbb E|\int_0^t\mathcal L_KF(U_s)\,\mathrm{d}s|^2=2\int(t\lambda-1+e^{-t\lambda})\,\mathrm{d}\nu\le t^2\|\mathcal L_KF\|^2
\]
 by stationarity, $\nu$ the spectral measure of $F$.

The generators $X_\alpha$ of the rotations at $y$ act on six bonds, $\sum_\alpha|X_\alpha F|^2\le6|\partial F|^2$, and the first non-zero eigenvalue $3$ of the Laplacian of the unit sphere $S^3=G$ gives $\int\sum_\alpha|X_\alpha F|^2\,\mathrm{d}\mu^K\ge3\|F-\Pi_yF\|^2$. The commuting projections $\Pi_y$ split $L^2(\mu^K)$ into joint eigenspaces invariant under $P^K_t$, on which $\frac d{dt}\|P^K_tF\|^2=-2\mathcal E_K(P^K_tF)$. Since $v$ is the field of $\Phi$, $v(G\circ\Phi_\sigma)(U)=\frac d{ds}G(\Phi_\sigma\Phi_sU)|_{s=0}$.

(b) The laws of the block fields at rational times lie in a compact set of measures on the compact metrisable space $\mathcal Y^{\mathbb Q}$. The means $\langle\Psi_0,P^K_{s_1}\Psi_1\cdots P^K_{s_n}\Psi_n\rangle$ extend holomorphically and boundedly to $\mathrm{Re}\,s_i>0$, so normal families carry convergence from rational to all times and give the real analyticity; convergence in total variation of the laws of the block fields carries it from continuous to Borel functions. Stationarity, reversibility and positivity under reflection hold at every cutoff, where $\mathbb E[\overline{\theta\mathsf F}\mathsf F]$ is the square of a norm by the Markov property, and pass to the limit.

By (a) the non-invariant parts decay in a time $O(a_K)$; this gives the independent gauges and $Q_t=\Pi Q_t\Pi$. Since $1$ and the $e^{-t\lambda}$ span a dense algebra of $C([0,\infty])$, the spectral measures converge; $\frac1t(1-e^{-t\lambda})\uparrow\lambda$ gives $\mathcal E_\star(F)=\int\lambda\,\mathrm{d}\nu_F$, lower semicontinuity and closedness, and $(F,(1-Q_t)F)=\frac12\mathbb E(F(Y_t)-F(Y_0))^2$ the Markov property of the form. $\|Q_tF\|^2\le(F,Q_{2t}F)$ is Cauchy--Schwarz at the cutoff; recovery sequences are $\Lambda(\Lambda-\mathcal L_{K_j})^{-1}G_j$ with $\Lambda\to\infty$ slowly. In the equivalences, weak convergence with convergence of the norms is strong convergence, and $\|P^K_t\Psi_K\|^2=(\Psi_K,P^K_{2t}\Psi_K)$; the strong convergence of $P^{K_j}_t\Psi_{K_j}$ gives (M1) through the quadratic forms $\langle H,(1-P^{K_j}_t)H\rangle\ge2\langle H,(1-P^{K_j}_t)G_j\rangle-\langle G_j,(1-P^{K_j}_t)G_j\rangle$, and the non-invariant parts are handled by (a).

For the last statement, the form $\mathbb E[\overline{\theta\mathsf F}\,\mathsf G]$ is hermitian and positive; $\mathcal K$ is its completion, $JF=[F(Y_0)]$, $R_s$ the shift of the times by $s$, self-adjoint because $\theta$ reverses the shift and contractive by repeated Cauchy--Schwarz; $(F,Q_tF')=\langle JF,R_tJF'\rangle$, and Pythagoras gives the identity.

(c) The weight defined before Prop.~\YMMref{115.2}{806} of the chain with top depth $n$ vanishes unless all $\pi_{K,d}U$, $n\le d\le K$, lie in their cuts, and by the comparison of the chain with the bare density (Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{115.2}{806}}, domination and lost-mass bounds) its integral against $e^{-\beta A_K}dU$ falls short of $Z_K$ by at most $\mathsf R_nZ_K$; so off a $\mu^K$-mass $\le\mathsf R_n$ all $\pi_{K,d}U$ lie in the cuts, and $\varpi(\pi_{K,d}U)<\theta_d$; for $\mu$ by total variation at finitely many depths (Cor.~\textup{\ref{IV-62-66}}) and a monotone limit. Four statements among the construction results on the averaging map $\mathcal M$ enter: its gauge covariance $\mathcal M(U^u)=\mathcal M(U)^{u|}$, $u|$ the restriction of a gauge transformation $u$ to the sites of the coarser lattice (Prop.~\YMMref{4.5}{20}, \YMMref{(40)}{20}); $\mathcal M$ is Borel, and on the small fields, where the plaquette variables of the double block of a coarse bond lie within $(200L^2)^{-1}$ of $\mathbf 1$, it is given at that bond by the first of the three formulas of its definition and is real-analytic (Prop.~\YMMref{4.5}{20}); its linear part at $\mathbf 1$ (Lem.~\YMMref{4.6}{22}, \YMMref{(42)}{22}) is the straight average along the bonds plus the difference of the averages along the contours at the two ends of the coarse bond, which is the coarse gradient of a site function; and the bound for rearranged paths (Lem.~\YMMref{4.1}{17}), which gives on the triple block of a coarse bond $c$, the union of the blocks of $c_-$, of $c_+$ and of the end point of the next bond $c^+$ in the direction of $c$, a gauge in which every bond variable is $e^{iA_b}$ with $A_b\in\mathfrak g$, $|A_b|\le15L^2\epsilon$, if all plaquette variables there lie within $\epsilon\le(200L^2)^{-1}$ of $\mathbf 1$.

With them the averaging map acts on gradients of invariant functions as follows: if $\varpi(\mathcal M^jU)\le\epsilon'_j\le(48000L^4)^{-1}$ for $j<k$, then $\mathcal M^k$ is real-analytic near $U$ and
\[
\Gamma_{d+k}(\Psi\circ\mathcal M^k)(U)\le\prod_{j<k}(1+C_D\epsilon'_j)^2\,\Gamma_d(\Psi)(\mathcal M^kU),\qquad C_D=C_D(L),
\]
for invariant $\Psi\in C^1(\Omega_d)$: the transpose of the differential of $\mathcal M$ maps horizontal vectors to horizontal vectors with norm at most $L^{-1/2}(1+C_D\epsilon)$, because the linear average is the straight average along the bonds, of norm $L^{-1/2}$ by Cauchy--Schwarz, plus the coarse gradient of the contour averages, which is a gauge direction of the block field and is orthogonal to the horizontal vectors, and the rest has norm at most $37L^2C_L\epsilon$, by the gauge covariance in the gauge of the triple block and the mean value inequality on the ball $\{|A_b|\le(3200L^2)^{-1}\}$, $C_L$ the largest norm there of the differentials of $A\mapsto\mathcal M(e^{iA})(c)$ and of the rest, so that $C_D=37L^{5/2}C_L$ depends on $L$ alone; and $a_{d+k}^{-1}L^{-k}=a_d^{-1}$.

The cutoffs: $|\partial(\varpi_p^2)|\le4\varpi_p$ by the computation of Lem.~\ref{C-367-13}(a) on $\Omega_d$, so each factor of $\chi_d$ has a gradient of norm at most $4\varpi_p/(2\theta_d)^2\le4/\theta_d$, which vanishes unless $2\theta_d\le\varpi_p\le4\theta_d$, and there are $3(\ell L^d)^3$ plaquettes; this gives $\Gamma_d(\chi_d)^{1/2}\le\mathsf k_d\mathbf 1\{\varpi\ge\theta_d\}$. $F_K$ is smooth: by induction from the depth $K$ down, the closure of the set where $\prod_{e<e'\le K}\chi_{e'}\circ\pi_{K,e'}\ne0$ lies in $\{\varpi(\pi_{K,e'}U)\le4\theta_{e'}$ for $e<e'\le K\}$, where $4\theta_{e'}\le(48000L^4)^{-1}$ as $e'>e\ge n\ge n_1$, so that $\pi_{K,e}$ is real-analytic near it; on that open neighbourhood the product with $\chi_e\circ\pi_{K,e}$ is smooth, it is $0$ on the open complement of the closure, and the two open sets cover $\Omega_K$; the same holds for the factor $\Phi\circ\pi_{K,n}$.

This is the role of the cutoffs: they keep every block field that enters $F_K$ where $\mathcal M$ is given by its real-analytic formula. By the product rule and the averaging bound at $\epsilon'_j=4\theta_{K-j}$, with $\prod_j(1+C_D\epsilon'_j)\le\mathsf c_*=\exp(4C_D\sum_{e\ge n_1}\theta_e)$,
\[
\Gamma_K(F_K)^{1/2}\le\mathsf c_*\Bigl[\sup\Gamma_n(\Phi)^{1/2}+\sup|\Phi|\sum_{n\le d\le K}\mathsf k_d\,\mathbf 1\{\varpi(\pi_{K,d}U)\ge\theta_d\}\Bigr],
\]
and the event in the sum has $\mu^K$-mass $\le\max\{\mathsf R_d,\mathsf R_{d-1}\}$, by the first statement of (c) at the depth $d$, or at the depth $d-1$ if $d=K$. Minkowski's inequality and the decay of $\mathsf R_d$ faster than every exponential, against $\mathsf k_d=O(L^{4d})$, bound every $L^p$ norm uniformly in $K$, and $\|\Gamma_K(\chi^K_n)^{1/2}\|_{L^{2p}(\mu^K)}\le\mathsf c_*\sum_{d\ge n}\mathsf k_d\max\{\mathsf R_d,\mathsf R_{d-1}\}^{1/2p}\to0$ as $n\to\infty$. Density: a bounded Borel invariant function of a small depth is $\mu$-almost surely a Borel function of a large depth, it is approximated in $L^2(\mu_d)$ by invariant polynomials, and the cutoffs change it by $\le\mathsf R_d^{1/2}$.

Then $\mathcal E_\star(F)\le\liminf_K\mathcal E_K(F_K)$, $\|Q_tF-F\|^2\le2(F,(1-Q_t)F)\le2t\sup_K\mathcal E_K(F_K)$, and $\nu_F(\{\infty\})=\|F\|^2-\lim_{t\to0}(F,Q_tF)$. Each property of $(Y_t)$ and of $\mathcal E_\star$ stated in (b) and (c) is shared by the frozen process, which keeps $Y_0$ up to gauge transformations of the threads drawn from the Haar measure independently at different times, so that $Q_t=\Pi$ for $t>0$ and $\mathcal E_\star=0$ on $L^2_{\rm inv}$: motion is the content of (A1).
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The limiting process on the common core]\label{C-367-17}
Assume (E); let $\mathcal C$ and $F_K$ be as in Lem.~\ref{C-367-6}(c), and $T>0$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] (Paths.) For $F\in\mathcal C$ and $1\le p<\infty$, $\mathbb E|F_K(U_t)-F_K(U_s)|^{2p}\le C_p(F)|t-s|^p$ uniformly in $K$; the processes $(F_K(U_t))_{t\le T}$ are tight in $C[0,T]$, and along every limit $F(Y_t)$ has a continuous modification, locally H\"older continuous of every exponent $<\frac12$. For $d\ge n_1$ there is $\mathsf p_d(T)$, which does not depend on $K$ and tends to $0$ faster than every exponential in $d$, such that for all $K>d$, with probability at least $1-\mathsf p_d(T)$, $\varpi(\pi_{K,e}U_t)<2\theta_e$ for all $d\le e\le K$ and all $t\in[0,T]$.
\item[(b)] (Energies.) For $F\in\mathcal C$ the limit $\mathcal E_\infty(F)=\lim_K\mathcal E_K(F_K)$ exists along the full sequence of cutoffs, and $\mathcal E_\infty(F)=\int\Gamma_\infty(F)\,\mathrm{d}\mu$ with
\[
\Gamma_\infty(F)(Y)=\lim_{d\to\infty}a_d^{-1}\,\mathsf t[\tfrac23,\tfrac16;Y_d]\bigl(\partial F^{[d]}(Y_d)\bigr)\quad\mu\text{-almost surely and in }L^1(\mu),
\]
where $F^{[d]}$ is the lattice form of $F$ at depth $d$ and 
\[
\mathsf t[\alpha,\beta;V](B)=\alpha\|B\|^2+2\beta\sum_c\langle B(c),\mathrm{Ad}(V(c))B(c^+)\rangle,
\]
$c^+$ the bond that follows $c$ in its direction. $\mathcal E_\infty(F)$ depends only on the class of $F$ in $L^2(\mu)$, $\mathcal E_\star\le\mathcal E_\infty$ on $\mathcal C$ for every limit, and for $F=\Phi(Y_d)\prod_{e\ge d}\chi_e(Y_e)$ with $\mathsf R_d<1$
\[
\mathcal E_\infty(F)\ge\bigl(\tfrac13-\tfrac12\bar\eta_d\bigr)(1-\mathsf R_d)\,e^{-\mathsf o_d}\,a_d^{-1}|\mathsf I_d|^{-1}\int_{\mathsf I_d}|\partial\Phi|^2dV,\qquad\bar\eta_d\to0 .
\]
\item[(c)] (The laws of the block fields.) For an integer $d\ge1$ with $L^d\mathsf b\ge\mathsf t_\natural$ and every bounded Borel invariant $f\ge0$ on $\Omega_d$,
\[
\begin{multlined}
(1-\mathsf R_d)\,e^{-\mathsf o_d}|\mathsf I_d|^{-1}\!\int_{\mathsf I_d}f\,\mathrm{d}V\le\int f(Y_d)\,\mathbf 1\{\varpi(Y_e)<\theta_e\text{ for all }e\ge d\}\,\mathrm{d}\mu\le\int f\,\mathrm{d}\mu_d \\
\le e^{\mathsf o_d}|\mathsf I_d|^{-1}\!\int_{\mathsf I_d}f\,\mathrm{d}V+\mathsf R_d\sup f,
\end{multlined}
\]
and the same at every cutoff $K>d$, with $\mu^K_d$ in the place of $\mu_d$ and with the middle member $\int f(\pi_{K,d}U)\,\mathbf 1\{\varpi(\pi_{K,e}U)<\theta_e\text{ for }d\le e\le K\}\,\mathrm{d}\mu^K$. So an invariant Haar-null set has $\mu_d$- and $\mu^K_d$-mass $\le\mathsf R_d$; and if $\mathsf R_d<1$, every non-empty open subset of $\mathsf I_d$ has positive $\mu_d$-mass and $\mu^K_d$-mass bounded below uniformly in $K$.
\item[(d)] (Square field and martingales.) Let $(K_j)$ be a limit and $F\in\mathcal C$. There is $\Gamma_\star(F)\in L^2_{\rm inv}$ with $(2t)^{-1}\mathbb E[\phi(Y_0)(F(Y_t)-F(Y_0))^2]\to\int\phi\,\Gamma_\star(F)\,\mathrm{d}\mu$ as $t\to0$ for bounded invariant $\phi$; $0\le\Gamma_\star(F)\le\Gamma_\infty(F)$, $\int\Gamma_\star(F)\,\mathrm{d}\mu=\mathcal E_\star(F)$, and $\mathcal E_\star(\psi(F))=\int\psi'(F)^2\Gamma_\star(F)\,\mathrm{d}\mu$ for $\psi\in C^2(\mathbb R)$. Along a further subsequence the lattice martingales converge, and $F(Y_t)=F(Y_0)+M^F_t+D^F_t$, with a continuous martingale $M^F$ with $\langle M^F\rangle_t=2\int_0^t\Gamma_\infty(F)(Y_s)\,\mathrm{d}s$, and a continuous process $D^F$ with stationary increments, $\mathbb E|D^F_t|^2=2[t\,\mathcal E_\infty(F)-(F,(1-Q_t)F)]$, $\mathbb E[D^F_t(F(Y_t)-F(Y_0))]=0$, and $\lim_{t\to0}t^{-1}\mathbb E|D^F_t|^2=2[\mathcal E_\infty(F)-\mathcal E_\star(F)]$; in reversed time, $F(Y_t)-F(Y_0)=\frac12M^F_t-\frac12(\hat M^F_T-\hat M^F_{T-t})$ with a martingale $\hat M^F$ of the law of $M^F$.

The following are equivalent: $\mathcal E_\star(F)=\mathcal E_\infty(F)$; $\Gamma_\star(F)=\Gamma_\infty(F)$ $\mu$-almost everywhere; $D^F$ has zero energy; $\lim_{\Lambda\to\infty}\limsup_j\int_{(\Lambda,\infty)}\lambda\,\mathrm{d}\nu^{K_j}_F=0$, $\nu^K_F$ the spectral measure of $F_K$. And $F$ is frozen ($Q_tF=F$ for all $t$) if and only if $D^F=-M^F$.
\item[(e)] (Motion from fields with a divergence.) A vector field with a divergence at the cutoff $K$ is a $\zeta\in L^2(\mu^K;\mathfrak g^{\rm bonds})$ with $\delta_K\zeta\in L^2(\mu^K)$ such that $a_K^{-1}\int\langle\zeta,\partial H\rangle\,\mathrm{d}\mu^K=-\int H\,\delta_K\zeta\,\mathrm{d}\mu^K$ for $H\in C^\infty(\Omega_K)$. If $a_{K_j}^{-1}\int|\zeta_j|^2\,\mathrm{d}\mu^{K_j}\le\mathsf A^2$, $\|\delta_{K_j}\zeta_j\|\le\mathsf D$ and $\delta_{K_j}\zeta_j\to g$ weakly, then for $F\in L^2(\mu)$ and $t>0$
\[
\mathcal E_\star(F)\ge\frac{(F,g)^2}{\mathsf A^2},\qquad(F,(1-Q_t)F)\ge\frac{t\,(F,g)^2}{\mathsf A^2+t\,\mathsf D^2};
\]
conversely, if $\mathcal E_\star(F)>0$, such fields with $(F,g)\ne0$ exist. A field that does not depend on the configuration pairs to zero with every invariant gradient: $\int\langle\partial F,z\rangle\,\mathrm{d}\mu^K=0$ for constant $z$ and invariant $F$.
\item[(f)] (An example.) In a limit of reversible diffusions observed through a block variable whose law converges in total variation, the inequality $\mathcal E_\star\le\mathcal E_\infty$ can be strict: for the reversible diffusion on $\mathbb R^2$ with the weight $e^{-\frac\kappa2(x-w)^2-\frac12w^2}$, the form $\int(|\partial_xF|^2+s^2|\partial_wF|^2)$ with fixed $s>0$ and the block variable $x$, as $\kappa\to\infty$ the law of $x$ converges in total variation, the square field of $x$ is $1$, the limit is an Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process, Markov and moving, and $\mathcal E_\star(x)=s^2/(1+s^2)<1=\mathcal E_\infty(x)$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(a) At every cutoff, for $H\in C^\infty(\Omega_K)$ and $0\le t\le T$, $H(U_t)-H(U_0)=\frac12M_t-\frac12(\hat M_T-\hat M_{T-t})$ with forward and backward martingales of brackets $2\int\Gamma_K(H)$ (the drift drops out, and the square field alone enters); the martingale moment inequalities and stationarity give $\mathbb E|H(U_t)-H(U_s)|^{2p}\le c_p2^p|t-s|^p\int\Gamma_K(H)^pd\mu^K$, and $\mathbb P(\sup_{t\le T}|H(U_t)-H(U_0)|\ge\lambda)\le10T\lambda^{-2}\mathcal E_K(H)$. With the bounds of Lem.~\ref{C-367-6}(c) this is uniform in $K$, and the criterion of Kolmogorov and Chentsov gives tightness and H\"older continuity. For the small fields apply the maximal bound to $H=\prod_{d\le e\le K}\chi'_e\circ\pi_{K,e}$, built from a second family of cutoffs, $\chi'_e=\prod_p\varphi_{\rm cut}(\varpi_p^2/\theta_e^2)$ on $\Omega_e$ with the function $\varphi_{\rm cut}$ of Lem.~\ref{C-367-6}(c): $\chi'_e$ is $1$ where $\varpi\le\theta_e$ and $0$ where $\varpi\ge2\theta_e$, and, as there, each factor has a gradient of norm at most $4\varpi_p/\theta_e^2\le8/\theta_e$, so that $\Gamma_e(\chi'_e)^{1/2}\le\mathsf k_e\mathbf 1\{\varpi\ge\theta_e\}$ with the same numbers $\mathsf k_e=24L^{e/2}\theta_e^{-1}(\ell L^e)^3$, which thus bound $\Gamma_e^{1/2}$ of both families.

As in the proof of Lem.~\ref{C-367-6}(c), the energy of $H$ is at most $\mathsf c_*^2\Sigma_d^2$, $\Sigma_d=\sum_{e\ge d}\mathsf k_e\max\{\mathsf R_e,\mathsf R_{e-1}\}^{1/2}$, with $\mathsf c_*=\exp(4C_D\sum_{e\ge n_1}\theta_e)$; $H(U_0)=1$ off a mass $\le\mathsf R_d$, and $H(U_t)>0$ forces $\varpi(\pi_{K,e}U_t)<2\theta_e$ for $d\le e\le K$; so $\mathsf p_d(T)=\mathsf R_d+10T\mathsf c_*^2\Sigma_d^2$.

(b) On the small fields $F_K=F^{[d]}\circ\pi_{K,d}$, $\partial F_K=\mathcal D^{(k)}(U)^*\partial F^{[d]}$ with $\mathcal D^{(k)}$ the differential of $\mathcal M^k$, and the transpose of the differential carries the quadratic forms along: $L^k\mathsf t[\alpha,\beta;U](\mathcal D^{(k)*}B)=\mathsf t[\mathsf A_L^k(\alpha,\beta);V](B)+O(\sum_j\epsilon'_j)\|B\|^2$ for horizontal $B$ at $V=\mathcal M^kU$, where $\mathsf A_L$ is the linear map of the flat average, with the eigenvector $(\frac23,\frac16)$ of eigenvalue $1$ (the Gram matrix of the kernels that are a tent along the bond and a box across it) and $(\frac13,-\frac16)$ of eigenvalue $L^{-2}$.

So $\Gamma_K(F_K)$ is close in $L^1(\mu^K)$, uniformly in $K$, to $a_d^{-1}\mathsf t[\frac23,\frac16;\cdot](\partial F^{[d]})\circ\pi_{K,d}$, and total variation gives the limit along the full sequence; the same estimate between two depths along a thread gives $\Gamma_\infty$. A function of $\mathcal C$ that vanishes $\mu$-almost everywhere has a gradient that vanishes off an invariant Haar-null set, whose mass is controlled by (c); this gives the dependence on the class. $\mathcal E_\star\le\mathcal E_\infty$ is the lower semicontinuity of Lem.~\ref{C-367-6}(b). The lower bound: on the threads with $\varpi(Y_e)<2\theta_e$ for all $e\ge d$, where all cutoffs $\chi_e$ equal $1$ near $Y_e$ and $F^{[e]}=\Phi\circ\mathcal M^{e-d}$, the same estimate between the depths $d$ and $e\to\infty$ gives $|\Gamma_\infty(F)(Y)-a_d^{-1}\mathsf t[\frac23,\frac16;Y_d](\partial\Phi(Y_d))|\le\frac12\bar\eta_da_d^{-1}|\partial\Phi(Y_d)|^2$, with $\bar\eta_d=4C_{\rm T}\mathsf c_*^2\sum_{e>d}\theta_e$, $C_{\rm T}=C_{\rm T}(L)$ the constant of the term $O(\sum_j\epsilon'_j)$ above and $\mathsf c_*$ that of the proof of Lem.~\ref{C-367-6}(c), so $\Gamma_\infty(F)(Y)\ge(\frac13-\frac12\bar\eta_d)a_d^{-1}|\partial\Phi(Y_d)|^2$ as $\mathsf t[\frac23,\frac16;V]\ge\frac13\|\cdot\|^2$; elsewhere $\Gamma_\infty(F)\ge0$.

The event of the middle member of (c) lies in that set of threads, and (c) at the invariant function $f=|\partial\Phi|^2$ gives the bound.

(c) At the top depth $d$ the chain from level $0$ has the density $e^{\Sigma+\Phi_t}$ with respect to Haar measure on $\mathsf I_d$, $\Sigma$ a constant (Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{115.2}{806}}, image identity, Prop.~\YMMref{114.2}{801}), its non-classical part bounded by $C_{\rm nl}\frac L{L-1}E_0(\ell L^d)^3$ (equation~\YMMref{(2180)}{803}) and the classical part between $0$ and $\frac32c_\rho^2A_0^2(\log L^d\mathsf b)^{2\mathfrak p_0}(\ell L^d)^3$ (by \YMMref{(2161)}{796} at the weight $x_t$); its mass lies in $[1-\mathsf R_d,1]$; the comparison of the chain with the bare density (Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{115.2}{806}}, domination and lost-mass bounds) gives the sandwich for $\mu^K_d$, and total variation (Cor.~\textup{\ref{IV-62-66}}) for $\mu_d$.

The middle member: the weight of the chain with top depth $d$ vanishes unless $\pi_{K,e}U$ lies in its cut, so in $\{\varpi<\theta_e\}$, for $d\le e\le K$; the function $f(\pi_{K,d}U)\mathbf 1\{\varpi(\pi_{K,e}U)<\theta_e$ for $d\le e\le K\}$ is invariant, by the gauge covariance of $\mathcal M$; so, $\sigma^K$ being at most $\mu^K$ on invariant functions (Lem.~\ref{C-367-7}(i)), $\int f\,\mathrm{d}\sigma^K_d=\int f(\pi_{K,d}U)\mathbf 1\{\cdots\}\,\mathrm{d}\sigma^K\le\int f(\pi_{K,d}U)\mathbf 1\{\cdots\}\,\mathrm{d}\mu^K$, and $\int f\,\mathrm{d}\sigma^K_d\ge(1-\mathsf R_d)e^{-\mathsf o_d}|\mathsf I_d|^{-1}\int_{\mathsf I_d}f\,\mathrm{d}V$ by the lower bound of the density of $\sigma^K_d$ (Lem.~\ref{C-367-7}(iii)).

For $\mu$: at a depth $D>d$ the event $\{\varpi(Y_e)<\theta_e$ for $d\le e\le D\}$ is an event of the block field of depth $D$, it contains the event at the cutoff $K>D$, and total variation at the depth $D$ carries the bound to $\mu$; then $D\to\infty$, a monotone limit. Positivity: for a non-empty open $O\subset\mathsf I_d$ and a smaller non-empty open $O'$ with closure in $O$, the gauge orbit of $O'$ is open, invariant and of positive Haar measure, and it is covered by finitely many gauge translates of $O$, which all have the mass of $O$.

(d) For bounded invariant $\phi$, the forward--backward decomposition gives $(2t)^{-1}\mathbb E[\phi(U_0)(F_K(U_t)-F_K(U_0))^2]\le\int\phi\,\Gamma_K(F_K)+c\,\langle\phi,(1-P_t)\phi\rangle^{1/2}$ for $\phi\ge0$; the limit in $K$ and then in $t$ gives $\Gamma_\star\le\Gamma_\infty$, and, with $\mathsf e_t(\phi;F)=(2t)^{-1}\mathbb E[\phi(Y_0)(F(Y_t)-F(Y_0))^2]$, the identity $2t\,\mathsf e_t(\phi;F)=2\langle\phi F,(1-Q_t)F\rangle-\langle\phi,(1-Q_t)F^2\rangle$ gives the existence. The chain rule follows from fourth moments of the increments, which are $O(t^2)$. The lattice processes $F_K(U_t)$, their martingales $M^{K,F}$ and brackets are tight in $C[0,T]$, limits of $L^4$-bounded martingales are martingales, and the brackets converge to $2\int\Gamma_\infty(F)(Y_s)\,\mathrm{d}s$ by (b).

At the cutoff, with the spectral measure $\nu$ of $F_K$, $\mathbb E|\int_0^t\mathcal L_KF_K(U_s)\,\mathrm{d}s|^2=2\int(t\lambda-1+e^{-t\lambda})\,\mathrm{d}\nu=2[t\,\mathcal E_K(F_K)-(F_K,(1-P^K_t)F_K)]$ and the drift is orthogonal to the increment; these pass to the limit. The equivalences: $\mathcal E_\infty(F)-\mathcal E_\star(F)=\lim_\Lambda\lim_j\int(\lambda-\Lambda)_+\,\mathrm{d}\nu^{K_j}_F$, the energy that escapes to infinite frequency, is the energy of the drift and the integral of $\Gamma_\infty-\Gamma_\star$.

(e) Let $H_j\to F$ strongly with $\mathcal E_{K_j}(H_j)\to\mathcal E_\star(F)$; then $|\langle H_j,\delta_{K_j}\zeta_j\rangle|\le\mathsf A\,\mathcal E_{K_j}(H_j)^{1/2}$, and the left side tends to $|(F,g)|$. At a positive time, $1-e^{-x}\ge\frac x{1+x}$ for $x\ge0$ (as $e^x\ge1+x$) and $\int\frac{t\lambda}{1+t\lambda}\,\mathrm{d}\nu=\min_G\{\|H-G\|^2+t\,\mathcal E_K(G)\}$, which is bounded below, for every real $s$, by $2s\langle H,\delta_K\zeta\rangle-s^2(\|\delta_K\zeta\|^2+t^{-1}a_K^{-1}\int|\zeta|^2)$. Conversely, $\zeta_j=\partial(1-\mathcal L_{K_j})^{-1}H_j$ has $\delta_{K_j}\zeta_j=(1-\mathcal L_{K_j})^{-1}H_j-H_j\to(1+A_\star)^{-1}F-F$ by (A3), and $(F,(1+A_\star)^{-1}F-F)=-\int\frac\lambda{1+\lambda}d\nu_F\ne0$. For constant $z$, $\int\partial_bF\,\mathrm{d}\mu^K$ is invariant under $\mathrm{Ad}(g)$ for all $g$, hence $0$.

(f) The operator of the diffusion on linear functions has the trace $\kappa(1+s^2)+s^2$ and the determinant $\kappa s^2$; its eigenvalues are $\lambda_+\sim\kappa(1+s^2)$ and $\lambda_-\to s^2/(1+s^2)$, and the spectral measure of $x$ puts a mass asymptotic to $\frac1{1+s^2}\lambda_+^{-1}$ at $\lambda_+$, so $\int\lambda\,\mathrm{d}\nu^\kappa_x=1$ for all $\kappa$ while $\mathcal E_\star(x)=s^2/(1+s^2)$.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Conditional fluctuation laws and transport estimates}

\begin{lemma}[Conditional laws along the renormalisation chain]\label{C-367-7}
Assume (E), let $n\ge1$ be an integer with $L^n\mathsf b\ge\mathsf t_\natural$, and let $K>n$. (i) $1-\mathsf R_n\le\sigma^K(\Omega_K)\le1$, and $\int f\,\mathrm{d}\sigma^K\le\int f\,\mathrm{d}\mu^K\le\int f\,\mathrm{d}\sigma^K+\mathsf R_n\sup f$ for bounded Borel invariant $f\ge0$. (ii) For $0\le k<t$, $d=K-k$, and every $W\in\mathsf{Cut}_{k+1}$, $p_W$ is a probability measure with a positive continuous density on the box; $\sigma^K_{d-1}$ is carried by $\mathsf{Cut}_{k+1}$, and
\[
\int\Bigl[\int f(V_W(B))\,p_W(\,\mathrm{d}B)\Bigr]\sigma^K_{d-1}(\,\mathrm{d}W)=\int f\,\mathrm{d}\sigma^K_d\qquad\text{for every Borel }f\ge0\text{ on }\Omega_d ;
\]
so the images of the $p_W$ under the $V_W$ form a regular conditional law of $V_k$ given $V_{k+1}=W$ under $\sigma^K$, and under $\sigma^K$ the sequence $V_t,\dots,V_0$ is a Markov chain from coarse to fine whose kernel at every $W\in\mathsf{Cut}_{k+1}$ is the image under $V_W$ of $p_W$; the kernels carry bounded continuous functions on $\mathsf{Cut}_k$ to continuous functions on $\mathsf{Cut}_{k+1}$, that is, $W\mapsto\int h(V_W(B))\,p_W(\,\mathrm{d}B)$ is continuous on $\mathsf{Cut}_{k+1}$ for every bounded continuous $h$ on $\mathsf{Cut}_k$; kernels and towers do not depend on the top level; $h_k(V_k)$ is the conditional mean of $H$ given $V_k$; the tower of an invariant $H$ is invariant at every point of $\mathsf{Cut}_k$, with $\inf H\le h_k\le\sup H$; and a density that is a function of the first member $V_t$ changes no kernel and no tower.

(iii) $\sigma^K_n=\mathsf g\,\mathrm{d}V$ on $\mathsf I_n$, $\sup\mathsf g\le e^{\mathsf o_n}\inf\mathsf g$, and $(1-\mathsf R_n)e^{-\mathsf o_n}\le\mathsf g\,|\mathsf I_n|\le e^{\mathsf o_n}$ at every point. (iv) For $n\ge n_2$, $0\le k<t$, $W\in\mathsf{Cut}_{k+1}$: $p_W=e^{-\Psi_W}dB$ with $\Psi_W$ real-analytic and $\frac14\gamma_{\rm r}\le D^2\Psi_W\le\Lambda_+$; every tangent vector $X$ of the fibre $\{\mathcal MV=W\}$ at $V_W(B)$ has $\|X\|^2\le C_{\rm ch}\sum|X(b)|^2$, the sum over the bonds that are not pivot bonds; and for bounded $g\in C^1(\mathsf{Cut}_k)$
\[
\mathrm{Var}_{p_W}(g\circ V_W),\ \ \tfrac12\mathrm{Ent}_{p_W}\bigl((g\circ V_W)^2\bigr)\ \le\ C_{\rm P}\frac{a_d^2}{\mathsf b}\int\Gamma_d(g)(V_W(B))\,p_W(\,\mathrm{d}B),
\]
with $C_{\rm P}=4C_{\rm ch}/\gamma_{\rm r}$, which depends only on the constants of the construction, and not on $K$, $k$, $W$, $\ell$ or $\mathsf b$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(i) is Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{115.2}{806}}, domination and lost-mass bounds, the comparison of the small-field chain with the bare density, with the weight $\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}_t$ and the bound $\mathsf R_n$ of the definitions preceding Prop.~\YMMref{115.2}{806}; (ii): the weight defined before Prop.~\YMMref{115.2}{806} vanishes unless every $V_j$ lies in its cut, so $\sigma^K_{d-1}$ is carried by $\mathsf{Cut}_{k+1}$. Positivity at every point, by induction over the scales: with $\Sigma_k$ the sum of the constants of the steps $1,\dots,k$ at the source $0$, $e^{\Sigma_0}F_0=F_0$ is the bare density on $\mathsf{Cut}_0$ (the definition preceding Prop.~\YMMref{114.2}{801}), and if $e^{\Sigma_k}F_k>0$ on $\mathsf{Cut}_k$, then $e^{\Sigma_{k+1}}F_{k+1}=\mathsf I[e^{\Sigma_k}F_k]>0$ on $\mathsf{Cut}_{k+1}$ \YMMref{(2174)}{801}, because the prefactors of the chart integral are positive, $G_W$ and $\mathsf J_W$ are real ({\cite[Lem.~B.3]{YMM2}}) and the chart carries the box into $\mathsf{Cut}_k$ (Lem.~\YMMref{113.10}{796}); so the density of $p_W$, a positive multiple of $e^{-x_kG_W+\mathsf J_W}(e^{\Sigma_k}F_k)\circ V_W$, is positive at every point of the box, and it is continuous, as $(W,B)\mapsto V_W(B),G_W(B),\mathsf J_W(B)$ are continuous and the chart integral of a continuous function is continuous ({\cite[Lem.~B.3]{YMM2}}), which makes every $F_k$ continuous on $\mathsf{Cut}_k$ by the same induction.

The kernels carry bounded continuous functions to continuous functions, in the whole range $L^n\mathsf b\ge\mathsf t_\natural$: at a bounded continuous $h$ on $\mathsf{Cut}_k$ the kernel at $W$ is $\mathsf I[hF_k](W)/\mathsf I[F_k](W)$, the normalised chart integral {\cite[eq.~191]{YMM2}} of the integrand of the chain; $\mathsf{Cut}_{k+1}$ lies in the set $\mathsf O^{\rm im}$ (Lem.~\YMMref{113.10}{796}), where the chart, its gauge-fixing form and the exponent of its Jacobians are continuous in $(W,B)$ ({\cite[Lem.~B.3]{YMM2}}), and $F_k$ is continuous on $\mathsf{Cut}_k$, into which the chart carries the box; so the chart integrals of the non-negative functions $(\sup|h|\pm h)F_k$ integrate over the fixed box functions that are continuous in $(W,B)$, Fatou's lemma on the box makes them lower semicontinuous in $W$, and as their sum $2\sup|h|\,\mathsf I[F_k]=2\sup|h|\,e^{\mathsf c_{k+1}(0)}F_{k+1}$ is continuous by the induction above, both are continuous; the denominator $\mathsf I[F_k]$ is continuous and positive.

The identity: the factors of the weight of the levels $>k$ are functions of $V_{k+1}$; the measure of the chain of the level $k$ is $\nu_k=e^{\Sigma_k}\mathbf 1_{\mathsf{Cut}_k}F_k\,\mathrm{d}V$ the measure recursion in Prop.~\YMMref{114.2}{801}, \YMMref{(2175)}{802}; and by the identity of measures of the step ({\cite[Lem.~B.3]{YMM2}}) the image under $\mathcal M$ of $\mathfrak G_k[x_k]\chi^{\rm sf}_{x_k}\,h\,\nu_k$ has the density $e^{\Sigma_k}\mathsf I[h\mathbf 1_{\mathsf{Cut}_k}F_k]$ on the open set $\mathsf O^{\rm im}$, which contains $\mathcal W_{k+1}(x_k;\alpha_0,\alpha_1)\supset\mathsf{Cut}_{k+1}$ (Lem.~\YMMref{113.10}{796}), for every bounded Borel $h$ on $\Omega_d$, and on $\mathsf{Cut}_{k+1}$ this density is $e^{\Sigma_k}\mathsf I[hF_k]$, the chart carrying the box into $\mathsf{Cut}_k$; dividing by $e^{\Sigma_k}\mathsf I[F_k]$ gives the identity for bounded Borel $f\ge0$, and monotone convergence for every Borel $f\ge0$.

As $V_{k+2},\dots,V_t$ are functions of $V_{k+1}$, the identity at $f=h\cdot(g\circ\mathcal M)$ is the Markov property with the kernel $p_W$. The tower of an invariant $H$ is invariant at every point by the covariance of the chain under the gauge transformations that are constant on blocks; (iii) follows from the statements on the iteration from a level: by Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{115.2}{806}}, image identity and Prop.~\YMMref{114.2}{801}, at the top the density is $e^{\Sigma+\Phi_t}$ on $\mathsf I_n$, $\Sigma$ a constant, with a non-classical part bounded by $C_{\rm nl}\frac L{L-1}E_0(\ell L^n)^3$ (equation~\YMMref{(2180)}{803}) and a classical part between $0$ and $\frac32c_\rho^2A_0^2(\log L^n\mathsf b)^{2\mathfrak p_0}(\ell L^n)^3$ (by \YMMref{(2161)}{796} at the weight $x_t$), so it oscillates by at most $\mathsf o_n$, and its mass is that of (i).

(iv): at every $W\in\mathsf{Cut}_{k+1}$, which lies in the class $\mathcal W_{k+1}(x_k;\alpha_0,\alpha_1)$ of the sum rule (Lemma \YMMref{113.10}{796}), the sum identities in equations~\YMMref{(828)}{395}--\YMMref{(830)}{395} and their preceding Jacobian calculation and the step (Prop.~\ref{prop:source-entry}) give the density of $p_W$ the form $e^{\mathcal E(P_W;B)}$, normalised, of Prop.~\ref{C-367-8}(b). This form holds at every depth, at every $W$ of the class of the sum rule, where the restrictions of $P_W$ to the polymers lie in the analyticity cores and the sum rules hold, so that every term of $\mathcal E(P_W;\cdot)$ is formed and holomorphic in $B$ on $\{|B(b)|<C_A\mathfrak b(x_k)\}$ (Thm.~\YMMref{W}{423}, Prop.~\YMMref{51.4}{393} and its proof, the potential definitions in Section~\YMMref{51}{389}, and \S\ref{sec:step-input-conventions}); the conditions of $n_3$ enter Prop.~\ref{C-367-8} only through the ball of complex triples of (a) and through the response.

So the form holds for every integer $n\ge1$ with $L^n\mathsf b\ge\mathsf t_\natural$, from $n_2$ on in particular, as Prop.~\ref{C-367-8}(b) states. The density being positive by (ii), $e^{\mathcal E(P_W;\cdot)}$ is a constant multiple of a positive function, so the imaginary part of $\mathcal E(P_W;\cdot)$ is constant on the connected box, and $\Psi_W=-\mathcal E(P_W;\cdot)+\log\int e^{\mathcal E(P_W;B')}\,\mathrm{d}B'$, with the branch of the logarithm that makes it real, is real-analytic near the closed box. Its Hessian is $D^2\Psi_W=\mathsf A_W-D^2\sum_Yv_Y$, with the form $\mathsf A_W=\sum_Y\mathsf b_Y(P_W)+\sum_\square\hat{\mathsf G}_\square(P_W)$ of the Gaussian integral of one step at $P_W$, whose inverse is the whole covariance of the step at $P_W$.

It lies within $\frac12\mathsf u_{\rm G}(LM)^{-3}\le\frac12\gamma_{\rm r}$, in the $\ell^2$ operator norm, of a real reference form whose floor and ceiling are $\gamma_{\rm r}$ and $c_{\rm r}$ (the completeness (St4) of Def.~\YMMref{47.2}{359}, Thm.~\YMMref{W}{423}, the proof of Prop.~\YMMref{113.4}{791}), so $\frac12\gamma_{\rm r}\le\mathsf A_W\le c_{\rm r}+\frac12\gamma_{\rm r}$. The potentials are bounded by a constant times $\delta(x_k)\mathfrak b(x_k)^2e^{-\lambda d(Y)}$ on the whole product of the cores and the polydisc of radius $C_A\mathfrak b(x_k)$, so at $P_W$ for every $W$ of the class of the sum rule (Thm.~\YMMref{W}{423}, Prop.~\YMMref{51.4}{393} and its proof, as in the proof of Prop.~\ref{C-367-8}(d)), and by Cauchy's estimate their Hessians are at most $C_{\rm Hs}\delta(x_k)\le\frac14\gamma_{\rm r}$ for $n\ge n_2$; hence $\frac14\gamma_{\rm r}\le D^2\Psi_W\le c_{\rm r}+\frac34\gamma_{\rm r}\le\Lambda_+$.

The log-Sobolev inequality $\mathrm{Ent}_p(f^2)\le\frac2\kappa\int|\nabla f|^2\,\mathrm{d}p$ of a probability measure $p=e^{-\Psi}dx$ on an open convex set with $D^2\Psi\ge\kappa$, at $\kappa=\frac14\gamma_{\rm r}$ on the convex box, gives $\mathrm{Ent}_{p_W}(F^2)\le\frac8{\gamma_{\rm r}}\int|\nabla_BF|^2\,\mathrm{d}p_W$, and its linearisation the Poincar\'e inequality with $\frac4{\gamma_{\rm r}}$; since $x_k^{-1}=a_d/\mathsf b$, the chart gives $|\nabla_B(g\circ V_W)|^2\le C_{\rm ch}x_k^{-1}|\partial g|^2=C_{\rm ch}\frac{a_d^2}{\mathsf b}\Gamma_d(g)\circ V_W$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Log-concavity of the fluctuation law]\label{C-367-8}
Assume (E). For $0\le k<K$, lengths at the level $k+1$ are measured in its units, in which the bare spacing is $\eta_{k+1}=L^{-(k+1)}$; $J^{(k+1)}(U)=\eta_{k+1}^{-3}\partial A_K(U)=L^{-3(K-k-1)}J(U)$ is the current (\YMMref{9.2}{38}) formed with this spacing; for a $1$-form $A$ and a configuration $U$, $(\nabla^U_\mu A_\nu)(x)=\eta_{k+1}^{-1}[\mathrm{Ad}(U(\langle x,x+\eta_{k+1}e_\mu\rangle))A_\nu(x+\eta_{k+1}e_\mu)-A_\nu(x)]$, and $|\nabla_UA|(b)=\max_\mu|(\nabla^U_\mu A_\nu)(x)|$ at the bond $b=\langle x,x+\eta_{k+1}e_\nu\rangle$. $\pi^M_k$ is the partition of the torus into the cubes of side $M$ in the units of level $k$ (the partition $\pi_k$ of Section~\YMMref{72}{607} (the definitions of $\mathcal D_j$ and $d_j$ at its beginning)); $\mathcal D_k$ is the set of its localisation domains, the unions of cubes of $\pi^M_k$ that are connected through their faces, which we call polymers; $d(Y)=d_k(Y)$ is the linear size \YMMref{72}{607} (the definitions of $\mathcal D_j$ and $d_j$ at its beginning) of a polymer $Y$, the least number of edges of a tree of edges of its cubes that meets all of them; $\mathrm{Bd}(Y)$ is the set of the bare bonds with an end point in $Y$; and for a function $f$ of triples and a pair $(a,\mathbf j)$ of complex $1$-forms, $D_{(a,\mathbf j)}f(P_W)=\frac d{dz}f(U_+,za,\mathbf J_++z\mathbf j)|_{z=0}$.

There are $r_{\rm c}\in(0,\alpha_0/256]$, determined by the fixed radii $\alpha_0<\alpha_1$ of the notation and the constants of Prop.~\YMMref{51.10}{403}, and $C_{\rm mx}<\infty$, depending only on the constants of the construction, such that for $K>n\ge n_3$, $0\le k<K-n$ ($k=0$ included), $W\in\mathsf{Cut}_{k+1}$, any background $U_+$ over $W$, $\mathbf J_+=J^{(k+1)}(U_+)$ and $P_W=(U_+,0,\mathbf J_+)$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] for every polymer $Y\in\mathcal D_k$ and complex $1$-forms $A'$, $\mathbf j$ on $\mathrm{Bd}(Y)$ with $|A'|,|\nabla_{U_+}A'|,|\mathbf j|<r_{\rm c}$ there, the triple $(U_+,A',\mathbf J_++\mathbf j)$ on $\mathrm{Bd}(Y)$ lies in the analyticity core $\mathcal U^\circ_{k+1}(Y;\alpha_0,\alpha_1)$ (Def.~\YMMref{49.1}{374}, Prop.~\YMMref{51.10}{403}, first assertion);
\item[(b)] $p_W\propto e^{\mathcal E(P_W;B)}dB$, where
\[
\mathcal E(P;B)=\sum_{Y\in\mathcal D_k}\bigl[-\tfrac12(B,\mathsf b_Y(P)B)+v_Y(P;B)\bigr]-\tfrac12\sum_{\square\in\pi^M_k}(B,\hat{\mathsf G}_\square(P)B),
\]
$\mathsf b_Y=x_kD_B^2\Psi^{\rm A}(Y;P,0)$ with $\Psi^{\rm A}$ of equations~\YMMref{(815)}{393} and~\YMMref{(816)}{393}, $v_Y$ the potentials of Thm.~\YMMref{W}{423} and of the fourth family at zero source (Prop.~\ref{prop:source-entry}), $\hat{\mathsf G}_\square$ of \S\ref{sec:step-input-conventions}; the quadratic form, too, is a sum of local terms; and $(A',\mathbf j,B)\mapsto\mathcal E$ is holomorphic on the product of the ball of (a) with $\{|B(b)|<C_A\mathfrak b(x_k)\}$, $C_A\ge3$, which contains the closed box. The formula for $p_W$, the locality of its quadratic form and the holomorphy of $B\mapsto\mathcal E(P_W;B)$ on $\{|B(b)|<C_A\mathfrak b(x_k)\}$ hold as well for every integer $n\ge1$ with $L^n\mathsf b\ge\mathsf t_\natural$, so from $n_2$ on, with $K>n$, $0\le k<K-n$, at every $W\in\mathsf{Cut}_{k+1}$ and any background $U_+$ over $W$: they need of $W$ only that it lies in the class $\mathcal W_{k+1}(x_k;\alpha_0,\alpha_1)$ of the sum rule (Lem.~\YMMref{113.10}{796}), at which the restrictions of $P_W$ to the polymers lie in the analyticity cores;
\item[(c)] for $W$ at a depth $\ge n_{\rm a}$, with $\mathcal H^+$ the response of $U_+$ at level $k+1$ (\S\ref{sec:background-step-complements}), $\mathbf U_\xi=e^{iL^{-k-1}\mathcal H^+(\xi)}U_+$, $W'_\xi=\mathcal M^{k+1}\mathbf U_\xi$ and $P_\xi=(U_+,\mathcal H^+(\xi),J^{(k+1)}(\mathbf U_\xi))$, there is $r_0>0$, which may depend on $W$ and $K$, such that for real $\xi$ with $\sup|\xi|<r_0$: $W'_\xi\in\mathsf{Cut}_{k+1}$ is a gauge transform of $e^{i\xi}W$, and $\mathbf U_\xi$ lies in the minimal orbits over $W'_\xi$ and over $\mathcal M^k\mathbf U_\xi$; there is a chart $\check V_\xi(B)$ of the fibre over $W'_\xi$, real-analytic in $(\xi,B)$ near the closed box, $\check V_0=V_W$, with values in a compact invariant subset of $\mathsf{Cut}_k$; for every bounded Borel invariant $H$, $h_{k+1}(e^{i\xi}W)=\int h_k(\check V_\xi(B))\,\check p_\xi(\,\mathrm{d}B)$, where $\check p_\xi$ has the density $e^{\mathcal E(P_\xi;B)}/\int e^{\mathcal E(P_\xi;B')}\,\mathrm{d}B'$, real-analytic in $\xi$ uniformly on the closed box, and $\check p_0=p_W$; the frame, $\check p_\xi$ and $\psi_\xi=\frac d{ds}\mathcal E(P_{s\xi};\cdot)|_{s=0}$ do not depend on the choice of the axial element;
\item[(d)] for real $\zeta$ on the box and every pair $(a,\mathbf j)$ of complex bare $1$-forms, with $\mu_y(a,\mathbf j)$ the largest of $|a|$, $|\nabla_{U_+}a|$, $|\mathbf j|$ at the bare bonds with an end point in the block of $y\in\Lambda_{K-k-1,\ell}$,
\[
\bigl|\partial_\zeta D_{(a,\mathbf j)}\mathcal E(P_W;B)\bigr|\le C^\sharp_{\rm mx}(x_k)\,\mathfrak b(x_k)\,\|\zeta\|\Bigl(\sum_y\mu_y(a,\mathbf j)^2\Bigr)^{1/2},
\]
with $C^\sharp_{\rm mx}$ depending on $x_k$ only through $\delta(x_k)\le1$; and for every real $\xi$ on $\Lambda_{K-k-1,\ell}$, $\sup_B|\partial_\zeta\partial_s\mathcal E(P_{s\xi};B)|_{s=0}|\le C_{\rm mx}\mathfrak b(x_k)\|\zeta\|\|\xi\|$, $C_{\rm mx}=\mathsf B\mathsf S\sup_{\mathsf t\ge\mathsf t_\natural}C^\sharp_{\rm mx}(\mathsf t)$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(a) Prop.~\YMMref{52.3}{433} holds for free radii $b_0,b_1\in(0,1]$, with the threshold $\varepsilon_{\mathcal W}b_0$ for $\varpi(W)$; the threshold that enters $n_3$ is the one at the radii $b_0=\frac12\alpha_0$, $b_1=\frac12\alpha_1$, that is, $2\theta_d\le\varepsilon_{\mathcal W}\alpha_0$ for $d\ge n_3$. So every $W\in\mathsf{Cut}_{k+1}$ with $K-k-1\ge n\ge n_3$ has $\varpi(W)<\theta_{K-k-1}\le\frac12\varepsilon_{\mathcal W}\alpha_0$, and by the plain-core verification in its proof $P_W$ lies in the core $\mathcal U^\circ_{k+1}(Y;\frac12\alpha_0,\frac12\alpha_1)$ with half the radii. The outer substitution from half the radii (Prop.~\YMMref{51.10}{403} (first assertion) at the radii $\alpha_0,\alpha_1$) carries this triple, moved by $(A',\mathbf j)$ with $|A'|,|\nabla_{U_+}A'|,|\mathbf j|<r_{\rm c}$, into the core with the radii $\alpha_0,\alpha_1$: the halved radii leave the room $r_{\rm c}$.

(b) The density in the chart comes from the sum identities in equations~\YMMref{(828)}{395}--\YMMref{(830)}{395} and their preceding Jacobian calculation and the step (Prop.~\ref{prop:source-entry}); the quadratic form is a sum of local terms, obtained by subtracting polynomials that agree on an open set. The formula for $p_W$, the locality of its quadratic form and the holomorphy of $B\mapsto\mathcal E(P_W;B)$ on $\{|B(b)|<C_A\mathfrak b(x_k)\}$ need of $W$ only that it lies in the class $\mathcal W_{k+1}(x_k;\alpha_0,\alpha_1)$ of the sum rule (Lem.~\YMMref{113.10}{796}), where the restrictions of $P_W$ to the polymers lie in the analyticity cores and the sum rules hold, so that every term of $\mathcal E(P_W;\cdot)$ is formed and holomorphic in $B$ there (Thm.~\YMMref{W}{423}, Prop.~\YMMref{51.4}{393} and its proof); so they hold for every integer $n\ge1$ with $L^n\mathsf b\ge\mathsf t_\natural$, from $n_2$ on in particular.

Only the joint holomorphy in $(A',\mathbf j)$ on the ball of (a) uses (a), and with it the condition $2\theta_d\le\varepsilon_{\mathcal W}\alpha_0$ of $n_3$. (c) Moving $W$ along the response keeps the background in the minimal orbit, so no control of the axial gauge is needed. With the residual gauge $h_\xi$ such that the background over $W'_\xi$ is $\mathbf U_\xi^{h_\xi}$, $\check V_\xi(B)$ is $V_{W'_\xi}(\mathrm{Ad}(h_\xi)B)$ carried back by $h_\xi$; its values at the pivots follow from the contraction there (the contraction leading to \YMMref{(800)}{391}, with the inverse of the one-step pivot derivative bounded by $2L^2$ in \YMMref{(798)}{390}) and the implicit function theorem. Every term of $\mathcal E$ is invariant under $(P,B)\mapsto(P^u,\mathrm{Ad}(u)B)$ and depends on $P=(U,A',\mathbf J)$ only through $(e^{iL^{-k-1}A'}U,\mathbf J)$ (Thm.~\YMMref{W}{423}, Def.~\YMMref{52.1}{415}, Prop.~\YMMref{51.4}{393} and its proof, \S\ref{sec:step-input-conventions}, and the pair and gauge covariance of Prop.~\ref{prop:source-entry}), and $\mathrm{Ad}(h_\xi)$ keeps $dB$ and the box: so the density depends on $P_\xi$ alone, and no derivative of $h_\xi$ enters.

The values lie in a compact subset because the regularity number of the backgrounds stays strictly below the cut. (d) Each local term is bounded on the whole product of the core and the polydisc (Prop.~\YMMref{51.4}{393} and its proof, Thm.~\YMMref{W}{423}), for instance $|v_Y|\le32C_V\delta(x_k)(d(Y)+1)C_A^2\mathfrak b(x_k)^2e^{-\lambda d(Y)}$ with constants $C_V$, $\lambda$ of the step; Cauchy's estimate on a bidisc, the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality and the sum over polymers {\cite[eq.~320]{YMM2}} give the first bound. At $s=0$, the derivative of $P_{s\xi}$ near $y$ is at most $\mathsf B\,m_y(\xi)$ by Lem.~\ref{lem:response-current-zero}, which also gives $\sum_ym_y(\xi)^2\le\mathsf S^2\|\xi\|^2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[One-step transport of the Dirichlet energy]\label{C-367-9}
For a level $j$ and a $\mathfrak g$-valued function $w$ of the bare bonds let $[w]_j^2=\sum_y(L^j\max\{|w(b)|:b_-\in B^j(y)\})^2$, $B^j(y)$ the cube of $L^{3j}$ bare sites centred at $y\in\Lambda_{K-j,\ell}$; then $L^{j/2}[w]_j\le L^{(j+1)/2}[w]_{j+1}$, $\|w\|^2\le3L^j[w]_j^2$, $[w]_0\le\|w\|$, and $[\mathrm{Ad}(g)w]_j=[w]_j$. For $V\in\mathsf{Cut}_j$ at a depth $\ge n_{\rm a}$, $U$ in the minimal orbit over $V$ and a real $1$-form $X$ on $\Lambda_{K-j,\ell}$, let $N^\flat_V(X)=L^{j/2}\min_\lambda[L^{-j}D\mathcal H_U(0)X-\mathrm{d}_U\lambda]_j$ for $j\ge1$, $N^\flat_V(X)=\min_\lambda[X-\mathrm{d}_V\lambda]_0$ for $j=0$, and $\Gamma^\flat_{K-j}(g)(V)=L^K\sup_{X:\,N^\flat_V(X)>0}\langle X,\partial g(V)\rangle^2/N^\flat_V(X)^2$.

$N^\flat_V$ is a seminorm that does not depend on the choice of $U$ and vanishes exactly on the gauge directions; $N^\flat_V(X)\le L^{j/2}\mathsf M\|X\|$, so $\Gamma_d\le\mathsf M^2\Gamma^\flat_d$; $\Gamma^\flat_K(H)\le3\Gamma_K(H)$ for invariant $H$; and $\Gamma^\flat_d(g)$ is Borel for invariant $g\in C^1$. There are $n_{\rm a}$ as in the notation and $C_\flat$, depending only on $L$, $C_Q$, $\mathsf M$ and the constants of \S\ref{sec:background-step-complements}, such that, with $C_{\rm cov}=\frac4{\gamma_{\rm r}}C_{\rm ch}^{1/2}\mathsf M\sqrt6C_QL^{-1/2}C_{\rm mx}$, for $K>n\ge n_{\rm a}$, $0\le k<K-n$, $W\in\mathsf{Cut}_{k+1}$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] every real $\xi'$ on $\Lambda_{K-k-1,\ell}$ has a representative $\xi$ modulo gauge at $W$, depending on $W$, $U_+$, $\xi'$ and not on $B$, with $\|\xi\|\le\sqrt6C_QL^{-(k+1)/2}N^\flat_W(\xi')$ and $N^\flat_{V_W(B)}(\check{\mathsf d}_k(W,B)\xi)\le(1+C_\flat\delta(x_k))N^\flat_W(\xi')$ for all $B$ in the box, $\check{\mathsf d}_k(W,B)\xi=\frac d{ds}\check V_{s\xi}(B)|_{s=0}$; more precisely, for every bare velocity $w$ of backgrounds at $U_+$ of level $k+1$ and $\xi=D\mathcal M^{k+1}(U_+)w$, $N^\flat_{V_W(B)}(\check{\mathsf d}_k(W,B)\xi)\le(1+C_\flat\delta(x_k))L^{(k+1)/2}[w]_{k+1}$;
\item[(b)] for real invariant $H\in C^1(\Omega_K)$ the tower has $h_k\in C^1(\mathsf{Cut}_k)$, and for $W\in\mathsf{Cut}_{k+1}$ and real $\xi$, with $\psi_\xi$ of Prop.~\ref{C-367-8}(c),
\[
\langle\xi,\partial h_{k+1}(W)\rangle=\int\langle\check{\mathsf d}_k(W,B)\xi,\partial h_k(V_W(B))\rangle\,p_W(\,\mathrm{d}B)+\mathrm{Cov}_{p_W}(h_k\circ V_W,\psi_\xi),
\]
\[
\Gamma^\flat_{d-1}(h_{k+1})(W)^{1/2}\le(1+C_\flat\delta(x_k))\int\Gamma^\flat_d(h_k)^{1/2}\circ V_W\,\mathrm{d}p_W+C_{\rm cov}\,\delta(x_k)\Bigl(\int\Gamma^\flat_d(h_k)\circ V_W\,\mathrm{d}p_W\Bigr)^{1/2},
\]
so $\Gamma^\flat_{d-1}(h_{k+1})(W)\le(1+\epsilon^\flat_d)\int\Gamma^\flat_d(h_k)\circ V_W\,\mathrm{d}p_W$ at every $W$; the same holds for $\phi_k=f_k^{1/2}$, $(f_k)$ the tower of $G^2+\epsilon$, $G$ real invariant, $\epsilon>0$;
\item[(c)] for $0\le k\le K-n$,
\begin{equation}\label{C-367-10}
\int\Gamma_{K-k}(h_k)\,\mathrm{d}\sigma^K_{K-k}\le3\mathsf M^2\Pi^\flat_n\int\Gamma_K(H)\,\mathrm{d}\sigma^K ,
\end{equation}
and, pointwise, $\Gamma_e(g_{t'})(W)\le3\mathsf M^2\Pi^\flat_e\int\Gamma_K(G)\,\mathrm{d}\mathsf P_W$ for the law $\mathsf P_W$ of (B3) and every $W\in\mathsf{Cut}_{t'}$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(a) Three facts: the monotonicity of $L^{j/2}[w]_j$ in $j$, with constant one; $\|D\mathcal M^j(U)w\|\le\sqrt6C_Q[w]_j$ when the plaquettes of $U$ lie within $a_QL^{-2j}$ of $\mathbf 1$ (equation~\eqref{eq:plain-average-l2-derivative}); and 
\[
[L^{-j}D\mathcal H_V(\zeta)X]_j\le\mathsf B\mathsf S\|X\|
\]
 (\S\ref{sec:background-step-complements}). The key is that the gauge compensator is bounded pointwise: every bare velocity $w=L^{-j}D\mathcal H_U(0)X-\mathrm{d}_U\lambda$ is also $L^{-j}D\mathcal H_U(0)X^w+\mathrm{d}_U\nu$, $X^w=D\mathcal M^j(U)w$, with
\[
|\nu(x)|\le(k_6+\tfrac32)\,\mathsf B\,m^j_y(X^w)+\tfrac32L^j\max_{b_-\in B^j(y)}|w(b)|\qquad(x\in B^j(y)),
\]
at the block centres by equation~\YMMref{(996)}{446}, with $k_6=4\kappa_{\rm av}$ as fixed in \S\ref{sec:background-step-complements}, and inside a block along a path, by $|\lambda(x)|\le|\lambda(y)|+\frac32L^j\max_{B^j(y)}|\mathrm{d}_U\lambda|$. Lift the velocity of level $k+1$ to a bare velocity $w$; the fluctuation $B$ moves the background of level $k$ by $O(\delta(x_k))$, so there is a curve of backgrounds of level $k$ over $\check V_{s\xi}(B)$, up to a gauge, whose bare velocity differs from $w$ by at most $C_\flat\delta(x_k)L^{1/2}[w]_{k+1}$ in $[\cdot]_k$; the monotonicity then costs nothing. The minimum in $N^\flat_W(\xi')$ is attained at some $w$; $\xi=X^w$ is the representative, and $\|\xi\|\le\sqrt6C_Q[w]_{k+1}$.

The argument of (a) is deterministic. The properties of $N^\flat_V$: a curve of backgrounds whose block field moves with velocity $X$ has a bare velocity $w$ with $L^{j/2}[w]_j\ge N^\flat_V(X)$; $\Gamma^\flat_K\le3\Gamma_K$ because $\langle X,\partial H\rangle^2=\langle X-\mathrm{d}_V\lambda,\partial H\rangle^2\le\|X-\mathrm{d}_V\lambda\|^2|\partial H|^2\le3[X-\mathrm{d}_V\lambda]_0^2|\partial H|^2$ for invariant $H$ and every $\lambda$; upper semicontinuity of $(V,X)\mapsto N^\flat_V(X)$ gives the Borel property.

(b) Differentiate Prop.~\ref{C-367-8}(c) at $\xi=0$; domination holds on the closed box, as the moving chart takes its values in a compact subset of $\mathsf{Cut}_k$. The left side depends on $\xi$ only modulo gauge: take the representative of (a); the first term is then at most $L^{-K/2}(1+C_\flat\delta(x_k))N^\flat_W(\xi')\int\Gamma^\flat_d(h_k)^{1/2}\,\mathrm{d}p_W$. For the plain tower, the Poincar\'e inequality of $p_W$ used twice gives $|\mathrm{Cov}_p(f,\psi)|\le\frac4{\gamma_{\rm r}}\|\nabla_Bf\|_{L^2(p)}\sup|\nabla_B\psi|$. For the square roots, the log-Sobolev inequality of $p_W$ with $\kappa=\frac14\gamma_{\rm r}$ gives $\log\int e^{s(\psi-\int\psi)}\,\mathrm{d}p\le s^2l^2/2\kappa$ when $|\nabla_B\psi|\le l$, and the variational formula of the entropy at $\phi^2$ and $s(\psi-\int\psi)$, optimised in $s$, gives
\[
|\mathrm{Cov}_p(\phi^2,\psi)|\le\frac{2l}\kappa\,\|\phi\|_{L^2(p)}\|\nabla_B\phi\|_{L^2(p)},
\]
with equality for a Gaussian $p$, $\phi=e^{ax/2}$, $\psi=x$. By Prop.~\ref{C-367-8}(d), $\sup|\nabla_B\psi_\xi|\le C_{\rm mx}\mathfrak b(x_k)\|\xi\|$; the chart factor $x_k^{-1/2}$ turns $\mathfrak b(x_k)$ into $\delta(x_k)$, and $L^{K/2}L^{-d/2}L^{-(k+1)/2}=L^{-1/2}$. Directions with $N^\flat_W(\xi')=0$ contribute zero by gauge invariance; for the other directions divide by $L^{-K/2}N^\flat_W(\xi')$ (for the square roots by $2\phi_{k+1}(W)=2\|\phi_k\circ V_W\|_{L^2(p_W)}$) and use Jensen's inequality for the probability $p_W$.

(c) Integrate the one-step bound against $\sigma^K_{d-1}$ (Lem.~\ref{C-367-7}(ii)) and iterate, using $\Gamma_d\le\mathsf M^2\Gamma^\flat_d$ at the top and $\Gamma^\flat_K\le3\Gamma_K$ at the bottom; for the pointwise form iterate at the fixed block field along the kernels. The constant does not depend on $K$ because $\sum_d\delta(L^d\mathsf b)<\infty$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Transport in the $\ell^2$ metric]\label{C-367-19}
Assume (E). For $V\in\mathsf{Cut}_j$ with $\varpi(V)$ below the radius of \S\ref{sec:background-step-complements}, $U$ in the minimal orbit over $V$ and $\mathsf Z=L^{-j}D\mathcal H_U(0)$, let $N_V(\xi)=\min_\lambda\|\mathsf Z\xi-\mathrm{d}_U\lambda\|$ ($N_V(\xi)=\min_\lambda\|\xi-\mathrm{d}_V\lambda\|$ at $j=0$). $N_V$ is a seminorm that does not depend on the choice of $U$ and vanishes exactly on the gauge directions; $N_V(\xi)^2\le\|\mathsf Z\xi\|^2\le C_{\rm rs}L^j\|\xi\|^2$, with $C_{\rm rs}$ depending only on $L$ and the constants of \S\ref{sec:background-step-complements}. Every real $\xi$ is $\xi_*+\mathrm{d}_V\phi$ with exactly one horizontal datum $\xi_*$, that is, with $\mathrm{d}_U^{\mathsf T}\mathsf Z\xi_*=0$; on horizontal data $N_V(\xi_*)=\|\mathsf Z\xi_*\|$; every real $\xi$ has $\|\xi\|\le C_{\mathcal Q}L^{-j/2}\|\mathsf Z\xi\|$, so $\|\xi_*\|\le C_{\mathcal Q}L^{-j/2}N_V(\xi_*)$, with $C_{\mathcal Q}=34(L^3+2)$ as in Lem.~\ref{lem:constant-frame-row} (a number other than the $C_Q$ and $C'_Q$ of Lem.~\ref{lem:plain-average-remainder}); and the two metrics are equivalent: $3^{-1/2}N_V\le N^\flat_V\le\mathsf MC_{\mathcal Q}N_V$.

There are $C_\sharp$ and a depth $n_4\ge n_3$, depending only on $\mathsf b$ and the constants of the construction, such that for $K-k>n_4$, $W\in\mathsf{Cut}_{k+1}$ and $U_+$ a background over $W$ the following hold. All clauses of Prop.~\ref{C-367-8}(c) hold at $W$, with the frame $\check V_\xi(B)$ real-analytic in $(\xi,B)$ on $\{\sup|\xi|<r_0\}$ times the open box and with first derivatives in $\xi$ that are bounded there. For every horizontal datum $\xi$ at $W$, that is, every real $\xi$ on $\Lambda_{K-k-1,\ell}$ with $\mathrm{d}_{U_+}^{\mathsf T}\mathsf Z_{k+1,U_+}\xi=0$, $\mathsf Z_{k+1,U_+}=L^{-k-1}D\mathcal H^+(0)$, and all $B$ in the box, $s\mapsto\check V_{s\xi}(B)$ is defined and real-analytic near $0$ and
\[
N_{V_W(B)}\bigl(\check{\mathsf d}_k(W,B)\xi\bigr)\le\bigl(1+C_\sharp\,\delta(L^{K-k}\mathsf b)\bigr)N_W(\xi).
\]
Consequently Prop.~\ref{C-367-9}(b), (c) hold as well in the metric $N$ for $K>n\ge n_4$, (B3) for $K>e\ge n\ge n_4$, and (B2) in (a)--(c) for $n\ge\max\{n_4,n_{\rm c}\}$, in the proposed variant (d), still requiring the multiscale gauge estimate, for $n\ge\max\{n_4,n_{\rm e}\}$ with $\mathsf R_n<1$, and in (e) for $n\ge n_4$, with $C_{\rm rs}\Pi_n$, $\Pi_n=\prod_{d>n}(1+\epsilon_d)$, $1+\epsilon_d=[1+(C_\sharp+\frac4{\gamma_{\rm r}}(C_{\rm ch}C_{\rm rs})^{1/2}C_{\mathcal Q}L^{-1/2}C_{\rm mx})\delta(L^d\mathsf b)]^2$, in the place of $3\mathsf M^2\Pi^\flat_n$ (in (B3): $C_{\rm rs}\Pi_e$ in the place of $3\mathsf M^2\Pi^\flat_e$).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
\emph{The range of $\mathsf Z$.} The response is in the Landau gauge on the kernel of the site averages: by equation~\YMMref{(837)}{398}, $\mathsf R^{\rm La}D^{\mathsf T}\mathcal H=0$, $D=\mathrm{d}_U$, $\mathsf R^{\rm La}$ the orthogonal projection onto $D^{\mathsf T}D\mathcal N$ and $\mathcal N$ the site functions whose site averages $Q'_q$ vanish at the tops (\S\ref{sec:response-step-conventions}); so $\mathsf R^{\rm La}\mathrm{d}_U^{\mathsf T}\mathsf Z\xi=0$ for every $\xi$. The response is covariant, as the averaging map is, so $\mathsf Z$ carries the gauge directions $\mathrm{d}_V\psi$ of the block field to gauge directions at $U$; these meet $\mathrm{d}_U\mathcal N$ only in $0$ (a $\mathrm{d}_U\mu$, $\mu\in\mathcal N$, in the range of $\mathsf Z$ has $\mathsf R^{\rm La}\mathrm{d}_U^{\mathsf T}\mathrm{d}_U\mu=0$ while $\mathrm{d}_U^{\mathsf T}\mathrm{d}_U\mu$ lies in the range of $\mathsf R^{\rm La}$, so $\mathrm{d}_U\mu=0$), and by the count of dimensions the two together span all the gauge directions at $U$.

A horizontal velocity of backgrounds at $U$, $h=\mathsf ZX-\mathrm{d}_U\lambda$ with $\mathrm{d}_U^{\mathsf T}h=0$, is then $\mathsf ZX'-\mathrm{d}_U\nu$ with $\nu\in\mathcal N$, and $\mathsf R^{\rm La}\mathrm{d}_U^{\mathsf T}\mathrm{d}_U\nu=\mathsf R^{\rm La}\mathrm{d}_U^{\mathsf T}\mathsf ZX'=0$: so $\mathrm{d}_U\nu=0$ and $h=\mathsf ZX'$. The range of $\mathsf Z$ holds every horizontal velocity of backgrounds, with no compensator.

\emph{The decomposition.} The part $h$ of $\mathsf Z\xi$ orthogonal to the range of $\mathrm{d}_U$ is a horizontal velocity of backgrounds, $h=\mathsf Z\xi_*$; $\mathsf Z(\xi-\xi_*)$ is a gauge direction at $U$, so $\xi-\xi_*$ is a gauge direction at $V$; $\xi_*$ is unique, as $\mathsf Z$ is injective (below) and a horizontal vector that is a gauge direction vanishes.

\emph{The bound.} Lem.~\ref{lem:constant-frame-row} applies in the constant frame, with bare spacing $L^{-j}$ and terminal spacing one. It gives $\mathcal Q(\mathcal H_U(\zeta))=\zeta$, and hence $L^jK_0\mathsf Z\xi=\xi$, together with $\|K_0\|\le2L^{-3j/2}\le C_{\mathcal Q}L^{-3j/2}$ on counting-measure $\ell^2$. Thus $\|\xi\|\le C_{\mathcal Q}L^{-j/2}\|\mathsf Z\xi\|$; on horizontal data $\|\mathsf Z\xi_*\|=N_V(\xi_*)$. The equivalence follows from $\|w\|^2\le3L^j[w]_j^2$ and $N^\flat_V(\xi)=N^\flat_V(\xi_*)\le L^{j/2}\mathsf M\|\xi_*\|$.

\emph{The estimate.} $U_+$ is a background of the level $k$ as well, and the same argument at the level $k$ shows that the velocity of a horizontal datum $\xi$ at $W$ is a response one level finer, with no compensator: $\mathsf Z_{k+1,U_+}\xi=\mathsf Z_{k,U_+}\zeta$, $\zeta=D\mathcal M^k(U_+)\mathsf Z_{k+1,U_+}\xi$; the fluctuation moves the background of level $k$ by $O(\delta(x_k))$, which costs the factor $1+C_\sharp\delta$.

\emph{The frame from the depth $n_4$ on.} As $n_4\ge n_3$, $\theta_d$ lies below the radius of \S\ref{sec:background-step-complements}; $U_+$ is a reference of the levels $k+1$ and $k$; for small real $\xi$, $W'_\xi$ is a gauge transform of $e^{i\xi}W$ in $\mathsf{Cut}_{k+1}$, $\mathbf U_\xi$ lies in the minimal orbits over $W'_\xi$ and over $\mathcal M^k\mathbf U_\xi$, and $\xi\mapsto\mathcal M^k\mathbf U_\xi$, $\xi\mapsto W'_\xi$ are real-analytic. The value of $\mathcal M(V)$ at a bond $c$ of $\Lambda_{K-k-1,\ell}$ reads $V$ on the bonds of the double block of $c$ alone, of the pivot bonds the pivot bond of $c$ alone, and its derivative in the value at that pivot bond is invertible, with an inverse bounded by $2L^2$, on the compact closure of the set of the restrictions of the $V_W(B)$, $B$ in the box.

The implicit function theorem, with radii that are uniform over this compact set, gives about every base point $V_W(B)$ exactly one solution at each pivot near the value of the base point, real-analytic in the data, with bounded first derivatives. The frame $\check V_\xi(B)$ is $e^{ix_k^{-1/2}B(b)}(\mathcal M^k\mathbf U_\xi)(b)$ at the bonds that are not pivot bonds and this solution at the pivots; by the uniqueness at the pivots and continuation in $B$ along $\tau B$, $\tau\in[0,1]$, from $B=0$, it is $V_{W'_\xi}(\mathrm{Ad}(h_\xi)B)$ carried back by $h_\xi$. Hence, as in Prop.~\ref{C-367-8}(c): the tower identity; the density $e^{\mathcal E(P_\xi;B)}/\int e^{\mathcal E(P_\xi;B')}\,\mathrm{d}B'$ of $\check p_\xi$, which reads the depth only through $n_3$; the values in a compact invariant subset of $\mathsf{Cut}_k$; analyticity on small $\xi$ times the open box, with $\xi$-derivatives bounded there, which carries the domination in the differentiation of Prop.~\ref{C-367-9}(b); and at the depths $\ge n_{\rm a}$ the frame is that of Prop.~\ref{C-367-8}(c).

In the differentiated step the representative is used only through $\|\xi\|\le c\,L^{-(k+1)/2}N_W(\xi)$, which the horizontal datum of the class satisfies with $c=C_{\mathcal Q}$; the rest of the proof of Prop.~\ref{C-367-9} is unchanged, with the square field $\Gamma^N$ built from $N$ as $\Gamma^\flat$ is built from $N^\flat$, $N_V(X)\le C_{\rm rs}^{1/2}L^{j/2}\|X\|$ at the top and $\Gamma^N_K\le\Gamma_K$ at the bottom.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Connected regions at the coarse scale]\label{C-367-11}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[beginpenalty=10000]
\item[(a)] Let $\mathsf n\ge\lambda_{{\rm BG},3}$, $0<\kappa'\le\kappa_0$, $\mathsf n\ge\kappa'^{-1/2}$, and $V$ a configuration on $(\mathbb Z/\mathsf n)^3$ with $\varpi(V)\le\kappa'$. Some gauge has $|V^u(b)-\mathbf 1|\le C_{\rm BG}\sqrt{\kappa'}$ at every bond; $\{\varpi<\kappa'\}$ lies in the path component of $\mathbf 1$ in $\{\varpi<C''\kappa'\}$; so, at $\kappa'=r/C''$, for $0<r\le C''\kappa_0$ and $\mathsf n\ge\max\{\lambda_{{\rm BG},3},(C''/r)^{1/2}\}$, every other component of $\{\varpi<r\}$ lies in the shell $\{r/C''\le\varpi<r\}$.

The estimate involving $J$ block levels remains to be proved, as described under \textup{(Multiscale gauge)}. The proposed estimate requires finite constants; no numerical values for them are asserted here.
\item[(b)] For a finite set $E$ of bonds, $0<\alpha<\pi$, $\mathsf K\subset\{A\in\mathfrak g^E:|A(b)|<\alpha\}$ open and convex and $V_0\in G^E$, $A\mapsto e^{iA}V_0$ maps $\mathsf K$ diffeomorphically onto its image $\mathsf B$; there Haar measure is $\prod_b(2\pi^2)^{-1}\mathsf j(A(b))\,\mathrm{d}A(b)$, $\mathsf j(X)=(\sin|X|/|X|)^2$; $-\log\prod_b\mathsf j$ has Hessian $\ge\frac23$; and $\mathrm{Ent}_{dV|\mathsf B}(\psi^2)\le3\int_{\mathsf B}|\partial\psi|^2dV$ for bounded locally Lipschitz $\psi$, whatever the number of bonds.
\item[(c)] If $\nu|_{S_i}$ have log-Sobolev constants $c_i$ on open $S_1,S_2$ with $\nu(S_1\cap S_2)>0$, then $\nu|_{S_1\cup S_2}$ has $2\max_ic_i(1+16\nu(S_1\cup S_2)/\nu(S_1\cap S_2))$. If Haar measure on an open $S'$ has the constant $c$, $\rho(V)=\int\mathbf 1_{S'}(V^g)\,\mathrm{d}g$, $\rho_0>0$ and $w=\min\{1,\rho/\rho_0\}$, then $\mathrm{Ent}_{w\mathsf g\,\mathrm{d}V}(\phi^2)\le\frac{c\,\mathsf g_+}{\rho_0\mathsf g_-}\int|\partial\phi|^2w\,\mathsf g\,\mathrm{d}V$ for invariant $\phi$ and Borel $0<\mathsf g_-\le\mathsf g\le\mathsf g_+$, whatever the boundary of $S'$. For an open invariant $\mathcal O$, a component $\mathsf C$ of it and a compact invariant $\mathcal K\subset\mathsf C$ there is a connected finite union $S'$ of sets $\{e^{iA}V_i:|A(b)|<\delta_i\}$ with $\mathcal K\subset S'\subset\mathsf C$.
\item[(d)] The set $\mathcal N\subset(0,2)$ of the $r=\varpi(V)$ at which $\sum_pc_p\partial a_p(V)=0$ for some $c\ge0$, $c\ne0$, carried by the plaquettes with $\varpi_p(V)=r$, is Lebesgue-null; for $r\notin\mathcal N$, $\{\varpi<r\}$ has finitely many components, each a connected open set with a Lipschitz boundary. The abelian fields whose $(1,2)$ plaquettes all equal $e^{if\sigma_3}$, $f=2\pi m/\mathsf n^2$, and whose other plaquettes are $\mathbf 1$, are such critical points: $2\sin(\pi m/\mathsf n^2)\in\mathcal N$ for integers $0<m<\mathsf n^2/2$.
\item[(e)] For $0<r<2$, every connected component of $\{\varpi<r\}$ is open, invariant, and contains a local minimiser of $\varpi$. For $\phi_1\in C^2[0,c)$, $c=\frac12r^2$, with $\phi_1'>0$ and $\phi_1\to\infty$ at $c$, the function $\Phi=\sum_p\phi_1(a_p)$ has compact sublevel sets in $\{\varpi<r\}$, every component contains a point where $\Phi$ restricted to it is least, and there $\sum_p\phi_1'(a_p)\,\partial a_p=0$ with weights $\phi_1'(a_p)>0$ at all plaquettes and $\nabla^2\Phi\ge0$; $\{\varpi<r\}$ is connected if and only if every local minimiser of $\Phi$ lies in the component of $\mathbf 1$; and $\{\varpi<r\}$ is the increasing union of the sets $\{\sum_pa_p^q<c^q\}$, $q\to\infty$.
\item[(f)] Let $0<\alpha\le\frac1{32}$, $r'=64\alpha^2$, $N$ the number of sites along an axis, and $\mathscr D=\{A:|A(b)|<\alpha\ \forall b,\ |Y_p(A)|<r'\ \forall p\}$, $e^{iY_p(A)}=\partial(e^{iA})(p)$, $|Y_p|\le\pi$. Then $\mathscr D$ is star-shaped, $\mathscr D=\{s\omega:|\omega|=1,\ 0\le s<\varrho(\omega)\}$ with $\frac12r'\le\varrho\le\rho_{\max}=\alpha\sqrt{3N^3}$ and $|\varrho(\omega)-\varrho(\omega')|\le\frac{4\pi\rho_{\max}^2}{r'}|\omega-\omega'|$; $A\mapsto e^{iA}$ maps $\mathscr D$ diffeomorphically onto $\exp\mathscr D=\{V:\mathsf d(V(b),\mathbf 1)<\alpha,\ \mathsf d(\partial V(p),\mathbf 1)<r'\}$, and $\mathrm{Ent}_{\mathbf 1_{\exp\mathscr D}dV}(\phi^2)\le C_{\mathscr D}\int_{\exp\mathscr D}|\partial\phi|^2dV$ for bounded locally Lipschitz $\phi$, with $C_{\mathscr D}$ of (B1)(e) at $\alpha_n=\alpha$.

With $w(V)=\int\mathbf 1\{\mathsf d(V^u(b),\mathbf 1)<\alpha\ \forall b\}\,\mathrm{d}u$ and $\mathsf{In}=\{V:\mathsf d(\partial V(p),\mathbf 1)<r'\ \forall p\}$: $\int_{\mathsf{In}}f\,w\,\mathrm{d}V=\int_{\exp\mathscr D}f\,\mathrm{d}V$ for invariant Borel $f\ge0$; $w(V)\ge[(\frac12\alpha-\sin\frac12\alpha)/2\pi]^{N^3}$ if some gauge brings all bonds of $V$ within $\frac14\alpha$ of $\mathbf 1$; and $\mathsf{In}\cap\{w>0\}$ is path connected.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(a) The gauge is built cell by cell on a periodic grid of mesh $\kappa'^{-1/2}$, along the proof of Prop.~\ref{prop:uniform-box-gauge}; along the ray to $0$ in exponential coordinates, $\bigl||\partial e^{itA}(p)-\mathbf 1|-|t\,\mathrm{d}A(p)|\bigr|\le10\alpha^2$, with $dA(p)=A(b_1)+A(b_2)-A(b_3)-A(b_4)$ the plain sum of the bond function $A$ around $p$, its bonds $b_1,\dots,b_4$ taken with the signs $(+,+,-,-)$ of Lem.~\ref{C-367-13}, when $|A|\le\alpha\le\frac18$, which keeps the ray in $\{\varpi<C''\kappa'\}$. The multilevel estimate \textup{(Multiscale gauge)} is a separate task; this construction concerns one scale.

For $\mathrm U(1)$ the flux sectors are distinct components. (b) The radial function $h(\rho)=-2\log(\sin\rho/\rho)$ on $\mathbb R^3$ has
\[
h''(\rho)=2\sum_{m\ge1}\bigl[(m\pi-\rho)^{-2}+(m\pi+\rho)^{-2}\bigr]\ge4\sum_{m\ge1}(m\pi)^{-2}=\tfrac23,\qquad\frac{h'(\rho)}\rho=4\sum_{m\ge1}(m^2\pi^2-\rho^2)^{-1}\ge\tfrac23 ;
\]
$|\nabla(\psi\circ\exp)|\le|\partial\psi|$ since $\frac d{ds}e^{i(X+sY)}=iZe^{iX}$ with $Z=\int_0^1\mathrm{Ad}(e^{iuX})Y\,\mathrm{d}u$, $|Z|\le|Y|$; then the log-Sobolev inequality on a convex set, and locally Lipschitz $\psi$ by the dilations $A_0+\vartheta(A-A_0)$, $\vartheta\to1$. (c) The first bound by comparing means on the overlap $S_1\cap S_2$; the second by applying the inequality on $S'$ in each orbit through the orbit average $\rho$, capped at $\rho_0$, and the bounded change of density $\mathsf g$; the cover of $\mathcal K$ by chart balls inside $\mathsf C$ is joined along paths in $\mathsf C$. (d) Sard's theorem on the strata indexed by the set of the maximal plaquettes; off $\mathcal N$ Gordan's alternative gives a common descent direction of all maximal plaquettes, which makes the boundary locally a Lipschitz graph.

At the abelian flux fields $\sum_p\partial a_p$ over the $(1,2)$ plaquettes vanishes. (e) Compactness of sublevel sets in the open set; a component is closed in $\{\varpi<r\}$, so a minimising sequence in it has its limit points in it. (f) Along rays the plaquette angle grows: $\frac d{dt}|Y(t)|\ge|Y|-32\alpha^2$, which gives the star shape and the Lipschitz radial function; the log-Sobolev inequality on a star-shaped domain with Lipschitz radial function follows by mapping it to a ball, at the cost of the Jacobian and of the Lipschitz constant, which is $C_{\mathscr D}$. The identity is Fubini over the gauge group; the lower bound counts, at each site, the gauge transformations within $\frac14\alpha$ of the given one, a ball of normalised volume $(\frac12\alpha-\sin\frac12\alpha)/2\pi$.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Completion of the limit and flow arguments}

\emph{Step 1: compactness, motion and the Markov property, (A1)--(A3).} Let $K>n\ge n''$ and let $H\in C^1(\Omega_K)$ be real and invariant, with tower $(h_k)$. Under $\sigma^K$, $h_k(V_k)$ is a martingale from the top to the bare level (Lem.~\ref{C-367-7}(ii)), so $\int|H-h_t(V_t)|^2\,\mathrm{d}\sigma^K=\sum_{k<t}\int\mathrm{Var}_{p_W}(h_k\circ V_W)\,\sigma^K_{d-1}(\,\mathrm{d}W)$; Lem.~\ref{C-367-7}(iv) at $g=h_k$, \eqref{C-367-10}, $\sigma^K\le\mu^K$ on invariant functions, $\sum_{d>n}a_d^2=\frac{a_n^2}{L^2-1}$, and Lem.~\ref{C-367-7}(i) for the passage to $\mu^K$ give
\[
\|H-(\mathbf 1_{\mathsf I_n}h_t)\circ\pi_{K,n}\|^2_{L^2(\mu^K)}\le\frac{C^\sigma C_{\rm P}}{L^2-1}\frac{a_n^2}{\mathsf b}\,\mathcal E_K(H)+4\mathsf R_n\sup|H|^2,\qquad\int\Gamma_n(h_t)\,\mathrm{d}\sigma^K_n\le C^\sigma\mathcal E_K(H).
\]
(A2): after replacing $H_j$ by smooth invariant functions with the same bounds (closure, a smooth contraction, the gauge average), let $c=\sup_j\sup|H_j|$, $e=\sup_j\mathcal E_{K_j}(H_j)$, and for $n\ge n''$ and $K_j>n$ let $h^j_n$ be the top of the tower of $H_j$ at $t=K_j-n$ and $g^j_n=\mathbf 1_{\mathsf I_n}h^j_n$. The tops are bounded by $c$ and, by the display and Lem.~\ref{C-367-7}(iii), have Dirichlet integrals on $\mathsf I_n$ for Haar measure bounded uniformly in $j$. Rellich's theorem on compact subsets of the open set $\mathsf I_n$, which needs no regularity of its boundary, the bound $c$, and diagonal sequences over an exhaustion of $\mathsf I_n$ by compact sets and over $n$, give one subsequence along which $h^j_n\to\phi_n$ in $L^2(\mathsf I_n,dV)$ for every $n\ge n''$.

The limit $\phi_n$ is a Haar class; as a function under $\mu_n$ we take a representative: let $\Psi_n$ be $\mathbf 1_{\mathsf I_n}$ times the gauge average of a Borel function in the class of $\phi_n$ with values in $[-c,c]$; it is Borel, invariant at every point, $|\Psi_n|\le c$, and $\Psi_n=\phi_n$ Haar-almost everywhere on $\mathsf I_n$, as $\phi_n$ is invariant almost everywhere. Prop.~\ref{C-367-17}(c) for $\mu^{K_j}_n$ at $f=|\Psi_n-g^j_n|^2\le4c^2$, which vanishes off $\mathsf I_n$, gives $\int f\,\mathrm{d}\mu^{K_j}_n\le e^{\mathsf o_n}|\mathsf I_n|^{-1}\int_{\mathsf I_n}|\phi_n-h^j_n|^2\,\mathrm{d}V+4c^2\mathsf R_n$, so with the display
\[
\limsup_j\|H_j-\Psi_n\circ\pi_{K_j,n}\|_{L^2(\mu^{K_j})}\ \le\ 2c\,\mathsf R_n^{1/2}+\Bigl(\frac{C^\sigma C_{\rm P}}{L^2-1}\frac{a_n^2}{\mathsf b}\,e+4\mathsf R_nc^2\Bigr)^{1/2}=:\epsilon_n,\qquad\epsilon_n\to0 .
\]
Total variation enters only here: $\|\Psi_n(Y_n)-\Psi_{n'}(Y_{n'})\|_{L^2(\mu)}=\lim_j\|\Psi_n\circ\pi_{K_j,n}-\Psi_{n'}\circ\pi_{K_j,n'}\|_{L^2(\mu^{K_j})}\le\epsilon_n+\epsilon_{n'}$, so the invariant cylinder functions $\Psi_n(Y_n)$ converge in $L^2(\mu)$ to some $G$, $|G|\le c$, and $\lim_n\limsup_j\|H_j-\Psi_n\circ\pi_{K_j,n}\|_{L^2(\mu^{K_j})}=0$: $H_j\to G$ strongly. This holds along every sequence of cutoffs. (A1): let $H_j\to\Phi(Y_n)$ be a recovery sequence of Lem.~\ref{C-367-6}(b), smooth, invariant, $\sup|H_j|\le\sup|\Phi|$ (truncation and the gauge average do not raise the energy). The conditional mean under $\sigma^K$ given $V_t$ is an $L^2(\sigma^K)$-contraction that fixes $\Phi(V_t)$, so the tops converge to $\Phi$ in $L^2(\sigma^K_n)$, hence in $L^2(\mathsf I_n,dV)$ by the lower bound of the density; the bound on $\int\Gamma_n(h_t)\,\mathrm{d}\sigma^K_n$, $\inf\mathsf g\ge(1-\mathsf R_n)e^{-\mathsf o_n}/|\mathsf I_n|\ge e^{-\mathsf o_n}/2|\mathsf I_n|$ and the lower semicontinuity of the Dirichlet integral give \eqref{C-367-3}.

As $\Gamma_n(a_p)=4a_n^{-1}|\mathsf s_p|^2$, by the computation of Lem.~\ref{C-367-13}(a) on $\Omega_n$, is positive at the fields of $\mathsf I_n$ with $\varpi_p>0$, $\mathcal E_\star(a_p(Y_n))>0$; since $\nu_\Psi(\{\infty\})=0$ for invariant $\Psi$, $(\Psi,(1-Q_t)\Psi)=\int(1-e^{-t\lambda})d\nu_\Psi>0$. (A3): for an invariant cylinder function $\Psi$ and $t>0$, $H_j=P^{K_j}_t\Psi_{K_j}$ is invariant, $|H_j|\le\sup|\Psi|$, $\mathcal E_{K_j}(H_j)\le\sup|\Psi|^2/2et$ (Lem.~\ref{C-367-6}(a)), and $H_j\to Q_t\Psi$ weakly; by (A2) every subsequence has a strongly convergent subsequence, whose limit is the weak limit; so $H_j\to Q_t\Psi$ strongly, which is one of the equivalent properties of Lem.~\ref{C-367-6}(b), and with it all of them, (M1), and the convergence of $P^{K_j}_tH_j$ for all $H_j\to F$.

With (M2) of Lem.~\ref{C-367-6}(b) the forms converge in the strong and weak sense, which gives the strong convergence of the resolvents by the theorem on the convergence of resolvents under convergence of forms in the strong and weak sense; Lem.~\ref{C-367-6}(c) gives a dense domain and strong continuity. Compactness: fix a countable dense set $(\Phi_i)$ of invariant cylinder functions; for $G_m$ in the set choose a cylinder function $\Psi_m$ with $\|\Psi_m-G_m\|\le\frac1m$ and, by (M2), truncation at $\pm1$ and the gauge average, smooth invariant $H_m$ on $\Omega_{K_{j(m)}}$ with $|H_m|\le1$, $\mathcal E_{K_{j(m)}}(H_m)\le1+\frac1m$ and $\|H_m-\Psi_{m,K_{j(m)}}\|\le\frac1m$, where $j(m)$ increases so fast that $\|\Psi_{m,K}-\Phi_{i,K}\|$ is within $\frac1m$ of $\|\Psi_m-\Phi_i\|$ for $i\le m$ and $K\ge K_{j(m)}$; by (A2) a subsequence of $(H_m)$ converges strongly to some $G$, then $G_m\to G$ in $L^2(\mu)$ along it, and $|G|\le1$, $\mathcal E_\star(G)\le1$ by (M1).

The criterion without a cutoff: $W_j=(1-\mathcal L_{K_j})H_j$ is bounded in $L^2$, so a subsequence converges weakly to some $W$ (a diagonal sequence over a countable dense set of cylinder functions); for invariant cylinder $\Psi$, $\int H_j\Psi_{K_j}\,\mathrm{d}\mu^{K_j}=\int W_j(1-\mathcal L_{K_j})^{-1}\Psi_{K_j}\,\mathrm{d}\mu^{K_j}\to(W,(1+A_\star)^{-1}\Psi)$, the resolvents being symmetric and strongly convergent, so $F=(1+A_\star)^{-1}W\in D(A_\star)$; the weak limit $F-W=-A_\star F$ of $\mathcal L_{K_j}H_j$ does not depend on the subsequence, and $\mathcal E_{K_j}(H_j)=\langle H_j,W_j\rangle-\|H_j\|^2\to(F,W)-\|F\|^2=\mathcal E_\star(F)$. The bilinear forms: with $T^\alpha_j=\alpha(\alpha-\mathcal L_{K_j})^{-1}$ and $T^\alpha=\alpha(\alpha+A_\star)^{-1}$, $\mathcal E_{K_j}(T^\alpha_ju_j,v_j)=\alpha\langle u_j-T^\alpha_ju_j,v_j\rangle\to\alpha(u-T^\alpha u,v)=\mathcal E_\star(T^\alpha u,v)$, as $u_j-T^\alpha_ju_j\to u-T^\alpha u$ strongly; by the spectral theorem $\mathcal E_{K_j}(u_j-T^\alpha_ju_j)\le\mathcal E_{K_j}(u_j)-\alpha\langle u_j,u_j-T^\alpha_ju_j\rangle$, whose limit $\mathcal E_\star(u)-\int\frac{\alpha\lambda}{\alpha+\lambda}d\nu_u$ tends to $0$ as $\alpha\to\infty$; with $|\mathcal E_{K_j}(u_j-T^\alpha_ju_j,v_j)|\le\mathcal E_{K_j}(u_j-T^\alpha_ju_j)^{1/2}\mathcal E_{K_j}(v_j)^{1/2}$, $\mathcal E_\star(v)\le\liminf_j\mathcal E_{K_j}(v_j)$ by (M1) and $\mathcal E_\star(T^\alpha u,v)\to\mathcal E_\star(u,v)$ this gives the convergence.

\emph{Step 2: the connected coarse-scale law, (B1).} The regularity number of a background $U$ of level $k$ is $L^{2k}\max_p|\partial U(p)-\mathbf 1|$, the maximum over the bare plaquettes ({\cite[Def.~B.2]{YMM2}}), and $\mathsf{Cut}_k$ is the set of the block fields over which it is $<c_\rho\varepsilon(x_k)$ (the definitions preceding Lem.~\YMMref{113.10}{796}). By the curvature comparison in the proof of Lem.~\YMMref{113.10}{796}, these numbers contract from level to level, by the factor $L^{-2}$ up to $C_H\delta(x_k)$: for $W\in\mathsf{Cut}_{k+1}$ and $B$ in the box, the regularity number of every background over $V_W(B)$ is at most $L^{-2}$ times that of a background over $W$ plus $C_H\delta(x_k)$; starting the chain $j_1$ levels higher, at every $U$ in the support of its small-field weight,
\[
\varpi(V_t)\le2\vartheta\varepsilon_n,\qquad\vartheta=\vartheta_\infty+L^{-3j_1/2}c_\rho<1 .
\]
The set $\mathcal K_0=\{\varpi\le2\vartheta\varepsilon_n\}$ is compact and lies in $\mathsf I_n$; as $\mathsf D_n$ and $\mathsf I_n\setminus\mathsf D_n$ are open, it is the disjoint union of the compact invariant sets $\mathcal K_1=\mathcal K_0\cap\mathsf D_n$ and $\mathcal K_2=\mathcal K_0\setminus\mathsf D_n$, which are free of $K$. The convexity of one box joins $V_W(B)$ to $V_W(0)$ at a fixed $W$ only; the $j_1$ levels are passed with the tower of a continuous function. Let $\mu_{t+j_1}=c_\rho\varepsilon(x_{t+j_1})$ and $\mu_k=L^{-2}\mu_{k+1}+C_H\delta(x_k)$ for $t\le k<t+j_1$, so that $\mu_t\le\vartheta\varepsilon_n$, and let $\mathsf D'_k$ be the set of the $W\in\mathsf{Cut}_k$ over which the regularity number is $<\mu_k$: $\mathsf D'_{t+j_1}=\mathsf{Cut}_{t+j_1}$, $V_W(B)\in\mathsf D'_k$ for $W\in\mathsf D'_{k+1}$ and every $B$ in the box (Lem.~\YMMref{113.10}{796}, the curvature comparison in the proof of Lem.~\YMMref{113.10}{796}), and $\mathsf D'_t\subset\mathcal K_0$ (the small-curvature averaging bound of Prop.~\YMMref{14.1}{61}).

Let $h$ be continuous on $\Omega_n$ with values in $[0,1]$, $h=1$ on $\mathcal K_1$ and $h=0$ on $\mathcal K_2$ (Urysohn), and let $h_t=h$, $h_{k+1}(W)=\int h_k(V_W(B))\,p_W(\,\mathrm{d}B)$, be its tower upward from the level $t$ in the chain from the depth $n-j_1$. The kernels carry bounded continuous functions on $\mathsf{Cut}_k$ to continuous functions on $\mathsf{Cut}_{k+1}$ (as in the proof of Lem.~\ref{C-367-7}(ii), where the integrands $F_k$ are shown continuous on the cuts): the kernel at $W$ is the normalised chart integral {\cite[eq.~191]{YMM2}} of the integrand $F_k$ of the chain at the level $k$; on $\mathsf{Cut}_{k+1}$, which lies in the set $\mathsf O^{\rm im}$ of the chart (Lem.~\YMMref{113.10}{796}), the chart, its gauge-fixing form and the exponent of its Jacobian are continuous in $(W,B)$, and the chart integral of a continuous function is continuous ({\cite[Lem.~B.3]{YMM2}}); $F_k$ is continuous on $\mathsf{Cut}_k$, into which the chart carries the box (Lem.~\YMMref{113.10}{796}), and dominated convergence on the box applies.

By induction on $k$, $h_k$ is continuous on $\mathsf{Cut}_k$ and takes on $\mathsf D'_k$ the values $0$ and $1$ alone: for $W\in\mathsf D'_{k+1}$ the function $B\mapsto h_k(V_W(B))$ is continuous on the convex box with values in $\{0,1\}$, hence constant, and as $p_W$ is a probability, $h_{k+1}(W)=h_k(V_W(B))$ for every $B$ in the box. Take all the fluctuations $0$: for $W\in\mathsf{Cut}_{t+j_1}$ let $W^{(t+j_1)}=W$ and $W^{(k)}=V_{W^{(k+1)}}(0)=\mathcal M^kU^{(k)}_+$, $U^{(k)}_+$ a background over $W^{(k+1)}$. The backgrounds are nested: $U^{(k)}_+$ is a background over $W^{(k)}$ as well ({\cite[Lem.~B.4]{YMM2}}(2)), so the regularity number over $W^{(k)}$ is exactly $L^{-2}$ times that over $W^{(k+1)}$ (the identity $\mathsf m_k=L^{-2}\mathsf m_{k+1}$), with no $C_H\delta(x_k)$; hence $\varpi(W^{(t)})<2L^{-2j_1}c_\rho\varepsilon(x_{t+j_1})\le2L^{-3j_1/2}c_\rho\varepsilon_n\le2\varepsilon_n/C''$, $W^{(t)}\in\mathsf D_n$ by Lem.~\ref{C-367-11}(a), so $W^{(t)}\in\mathcal K_1$ and $h_{t+j_1}(W)=h(W^{(t)})=1$.

On the support of the small-field weight of the chain from the depth $n-j_1$, $V_{t+j_1}\in\mathsf{Cut}_{t+j_1}$ and $V_k=V_{V_{k+1}}(B_k)\in\mathsf D'_k$, so $h(V_t)=h_{t+1}(V_{t+1})=\dots=h_{t+j_1}(V_{t+j_1})=1$; as $V_t\in\mathcal K_0$ and $h=0$ on $\mathcal K_2$, $V_t\in\mathcal K_1$. Of the dependence on $W$ this argument uses the continuity of the kernels alone. So $\sigma^K_n(\Omega_n\setminus\mathcal K_1)\le\mathsf R_{n-j_1}$ by Lem.~\ref{C-367-7}(i) for the chain from depth $n-j_1$. Glue finitely many chart balls in $\mathsf D_n$ to a connected $S'\supset\mathcal K_1$ (Lem.~\ref{C-367-11}(b), (c)), put $w_n=\min\{1,\rho/\rho_0\}$, $\rho_0=\min_{\mathcal K_1}\rho>0$, so that $w_n=1$ on $\mathcal K_1$ and $w_n=0$ off $\mathsf D_n$: this is (a).

Lem.~\ref{C-367-11}(c) with the density of $\sigma^K_n$, $\sup\mathsf g\le e^{\mathsf o_n}\inf\mathsf g$ (Lem.~\ref{C-367-7}(iii)), and $\Gamma_n=a_n^{-1}|\partial\cdot|^2$ give (b) with $C^{\rm t}_n=a_nc(S')e^{\mathsf o_n}/\rho_0$. (c): the linearisation of (b) gives $\int(\phi-c)^2w_n\,\mathrm{d}\sigma^K_n\le\frac12C^{\rm t}_n\int\Gamma_n(\phi)w_n\,\mathrm{d}\sigma^K_n$, and the part where $w_n<1$ costs at most $\mathrm{osc}(\phi)^2\mathsf R_{n-j_1}$. (d): $\mathrm{Ent}_{\sigma^K_n}(\phi^2)\le\int\Xi(\phi^2,c')\,\mathrm{d}\sigma^K_n=\mathrm{Ent}_{w_n\sigma^K_n}(\phi^2)+\int\Xi(\phi^2,c')(1-w_n)\,\mathrm{d}\sigma^K_n$. (e): the explicit-top sketch still requires the multiscale gauge estimate. The conditions of $n_{\rm e}$ are those of \textup{(Multiscale gauge)} at $J=J_n$; a field of $\mathsf I_n$ whose block fields $\mathcal M^jV$, $j\le J_n$, lie in the cuts has a gauge with all bonds within $44\pi L^2\sum_{j<J_n}\theta_{n-j}+C_{\rm S}L^{-J_n}\le\frac14\alpha_n$ of $\mathbf 1$, so $w^{\rm e}_n\ge c_n$ there by Lem.~\ref{C-367-11}(f), $\chi_n=1$, and $\sigma^K_n(\chi_n<1)\le\mathsf R_{n-J_n}$ by Lem.~\ref{C-367-7}(i) for the chain from depth $n-J_n$.

Since $r'_n=2\arcsin\varepsilon_n=64\alpha_n^2$ is the angle of the radius $2\varepsilon_n$, $\mathsf I_n=\{\mathsf d(\partial V(p),\mathbf 1)<r'_n\ \forall p\}$, and the identity of Lem.~\ref{C-367-11}(f) carries the log-Sobolev inequality of Haar measure on $\exp\mathscr D$ to invariant functions under $w^{\rm e}_ndV$, then to $\chi_ndV$ at the cost $c_n^{-1}$, and to $\chi_n\sigma^K_n$ at the cost $e^{2\mathsf o_n}/(1-\mathsf R_n)$ of the density: this is $C^\flat_n$. The set $\{\chi_n>0\}\cap\mathsf I_n$ is the path connected set of Lem.~\ref{C-367-11}(f); it contains $\mathbf 1$, so it lies in $\mathsf D_n$. For the block-field laws, $\mathrm{Var}_{\mu^K_n}(\Phi)\le\int(\Phi-c)^2\,\mathrm{d}\mu^K_n\le\int(\Phi-c)^2\,\mathrm{d}\sigma^K_n+\mathsf R_n\mathrm{osc}(\Phi)^2$ by Lem.~\ref{C-367-7}(i), then (c) with $\chi_n$ and $\int\Gamma_n(\Phi)\,\mathrm{d}\sigma^K_n\le\int_{\mathsf I_n}\Gamma_n(\Phi)\,\mathrm{d}\mu^K_n$; for $\mu_n$ by total variation.

\emph{Step 3: weak Poincar\'e bounds and mixing, (A4).} Let $c$ be the mean of $H$ under $\varsigma^K$. The density $w_n(V_t)$ is a function of the first member of the chain, so it changes no kernel and no tower, and
\[
\int(H-c)^2\,\mathrm{d}\varsigma^K=\int(H-h_t(V_t))^2\,\mathrm{d}\varsigma^K+\int(h_t-c)^2w_n\,\mathrm{d}\sigma^K_n\le\mathsf C_n\mathcal E_K(H),
\]
the first term by the martingale sum of Step~1, the second by (B1)(b) linearised and \eqref{C-367-10} at $k=t$; passing to $\mu^K$ costs $\mathsf r_n\mathrm{osc}(H)^2$ by (B2)(a). This is (a), first for smooth $H$ and then by closure. (b): $\frac d{dt}\mathrm{Var}(P^K_tH)=-2\mathcal E_K(P^K_tH)\le-\frac2{\mathsf C_n}[\mathrm{Var}(P^K_tH)-\mathsf r_n\mathrm{osc}(H)^2]$, as $\mathrm{osc}(P^K_tH)\le\mathrm{osc}(H)$, and $\mathrm{Var}(H)\le\frac14\mathrm{osc}(H)^2$. (c): truncated and gauge-averaged recovery sequences and (a); if $\mathcal E_\star(F)=0$, then $\mathrm{Var}_\mu(F)\le\mathsf r_n\mathrm{osc}(F)^2$ for all admitted $n$. For non-constant bounded $F\in L^2_{\rm inv}$ the spectral measure $\nu_F$ is not carried by $\{0\}$, as else $\mathcal E_\star(F)=0$, and $\nu_F(\{\infty\})=0$ (Lem.~\ref{C-367-6}(c)); so $(F,(1-Q_t)F)=\int(1-e^{-t\lambda})\,\mathrm{d}\nu_F>0$.

(d): $\varphi(t)=\|Q_{t/2}(F-\int F)\|^2$ has $\varphi'(t)=-\mathcal E_\star(Q_{t/2}(F-\int F))\le-\mathsf C_n^{-1}[\varphi(t)-\mathsf r_n\mathrm{osc}(F)^2]$ by (c) and spectral calculus, and $\varphi(0)\le\frac14\mathrm{osc}(F)^2$.
