For all large $N=2\mathsf L^j$, $A$ is an event of the bonds inside one cell of side $N/2$, and Lem.~\ref{lem:exc}, applied to $s$ and to $\nu$, gives $|s(A)-\nu(A)|\le\sqrt\epsilon+\epsilon$ with $\epsilon=22.3(e^{\delta_{\rm c}(N)/7}-1)$, which tends to $0$ as $\delta_{\rm c}(N)<0.1324\,\theta^{N/2l}$ (Prop.~\ref{prop:rec}(d)). So $s=\nu$. Prop.~\YMMref{103.4}{758} gives reflection positivity at every lattice mirror. By Prop.~\YMMref{106.2}{764}, the ergodic components of $\nu$ are periodic Gibbs states; uniqueness makes them equal to $\nu$, so $\nu$ is ergodic.

\emph{Step 4 (all boxes).} Let the three sides of boxes $\underline n^{(k)}$ tend to infinity. Their laws on $\Omega$ lie in a compact set; every limit point satisfies the Gibbs equations, as in Step 2, and is invariant under all translations, as every box law is; so it is a periodic Gibbs state, that is $\nu$, and the whole sequence converges.

\emph{Step 5 (twisted cubes).} Let $n\ge2\mathsf ql$ be an integer, $j$ the largest integer with $4^j\le n/2\mathsf ql$, $w=2^j$, $l'=l_j=2wl$ and $M=n/l'$, a real number with $w\mathsf q\le M<4w\mathsf q$ and $M^2<2\mathsf qn/l$. Lem.~\ref{lem:vort}(a) from the box $(l',n,l')$ to the cube, with $\kappa=M^2$, and Prop.~\ref{prop:tub}(d) give
\[
z_-(n,n,n)\le\bigl[Me^{-\varsigma w^2+0.01655\,M\theta^{2w}}\bigr]^{M^2},\qquad M^2\varsigma w^2=\sigma^+n^2 ,
\]
and $0.01655\,M\theta^{2w}<4\mathsf q\cdot0.01655\,we^{-2w\Lambda}\le\frac{4\cdot0.01655}e(\frac1{2\Lambda}+\frac{1.67}{4\Lambda^2})\le0.855$ and $\log M<\frac12\log\frac{2\mathsf qn}l$: the first bound of (d). The bound for all seven $z\ne0$ then follows from Lem.~\ref{lem:tr}(c).

\emph{Step 6 (flux sectors, static charges).} With the time $1$ over $n\times n$ and $e\in\{01,11\}$, $\Lambda_e^n\le W_n(01;0)+W_n(11;0)=a_-(n,n,n)=z_-\lambda_0^n(1+\mathsf r_n(n,n))$; for $e=10$ the same holds because $Z^{(1,0,0)}=Z^{(0,1,0)}$ on the cube (Lem.~\ref{lem:tr}(iii)). So $\log(\lambda_0/\Lambda_e)\ge\frac1n[-\log z_-(n,n,n)-\log(1+\mathsf r_n(n,n))]$, and $\log(1+\mathsf r_n(n,n))$ is at most $\mathsf r_n(n,n)\le0.001615\,\theta^{n/l}\le0.0017$ at $n=2^il$, and in general, with $n_0=2^il\le n<2n_0$, at most $\delta_{\rm c}(n)\le8\delta_{\rm c}(n_0)\le8\cdot0.01655\cdot0.792279\le0.105$ (Lem.~\ref{lem:seq}(f), Prop.~\ref{prop:rec}(d)). With Step 5 this is the first statement of (e); the second is Lem.~\ref{lem:two}(d) on the cube with $n_3=n$, and Step 5. For any two sites $o\ne r$ it is Lem.~\ref{lem:two}(e) on the cube, with the time $1$ or $2$, whichever direction of the section realises $|r-o|_\infty$, and Step 5; for fixed $o$, $r$ and $n=2^il$, $i\to\infty$, the factor $[8(1+\mathsf r_n(n,n))]^{1/n}$ tends to $1$ and the correction $\frac{2\mathsf qR}{ln}(\frac12\log\frac{2\mathsf qn}l+0.86)$ to $0$, while $R=|r-o|_\infty$ once $n>2|r-o|_\infty$.

\emph{Step 7 (rectangles).} By the symmetries of $\nu$ and of the cube laws it suffices to take $C$ in a $(1,3)$-plane with the side $R$ along $e_1$. On the cube of an integer side $n\ge2\mathsf ql$ with $R\le n/2$, $T\le n-1$, Lem.~\ref{lem:two}(d) gives $0\le\langle W_C\rangle_{(n,n,n)}\le8^{T/n}z_-(n,n,n)^{RT/n^2}$, and Step 5 gives the bound on the cube. Along $n=2^kl$ the left side tends to $\nu(W_C)$ by Step 1, while $8^{T/n}\to1$ and $(\log n)/n\to0$: this is \eqref{eq:area}. The bound by the perimeter is Lem.~\ref{lem:bond}(b).

\emph{Step 8 (closed paths).} Let $C$ and $(\rho',\rho)$ be as in (c); by symmetry $(\rho',\rho)=(1,3)$. On the cubes $n=2^kl$, which are even, Lem.~\ref{lem:sev}(c) applies for large $k$: the sum of the $\ell_j$ is $\mathsf A_{13}(C)$, $\sum_j(\mathsf v_j+1)/n\to0$, the thermal factors tend to $1$, and $z_-(n,n,n)^{\mathsf A/n^2}\le e^{-\sigma^+\mathsf A+o(1)}$ by Step 5. For the general form let $\rho=3$: by the symmetry of the cube that exchanges the directions $1$ and $2$, Lem.~\ref{lem:sev}(b) holds with the direction $2$ in the place of the direction $1$, the two twisted pairs having one quotient on the cube (Lem.~\ref{lem:tr}(c)), and in the proof of Lem.~\ref{lem:sev}(c) each norm $\|\hat{\mathsf T}_{D_j}\|$ is bounded by (b) on its own; so in each gap $\ell_j$ may be taken as the larger of the two counts $\ell^1_j(C)$, $\ell^2_j(C)$, whose sum over the gaps is $\mathsf A_3(C)$, and Lem.~\ref{lem:sev}(d) carries all this to $D$, with $d^{\,c_3(C)-1}$ in front and $\sum_j\mathsf v_j\log d/n\to0$.

For a staircase loop the senses of its runs of the direction $\rho$ are up in $T$ consecutive gaps and then down in the same gaps, so $c_\rho=1$, and $\mathsf A_{\rho'\rho}(C)=\sum_j|r_j-o_j|$. For a simple closed curve of a coordinate plane each passage from down to up and each from up to down holds at least one bond of the other direction, and between two such passages there is at least one bond of the direction $\rho$; so $|C|\ge4c_\rho(C)$ and $2^{c_\rho-1}\le\frac12e^{(\log2/4)|C|}$.

\emph{Step 9 (gap).} Let $N=N_1\le N_2$ (by (T1)), $n_0\le N<2n_0$, and $i$ with $t_i\le N_2<2t_i$ in Prop.~\ref{prop:slab}(b): for $a\ge1$, $(\lambda_a/\lambda_0)^{t_i}\le\mathsf r_{t_i}(N_2,N)\le0.28\,\chi'^{2^i}\le\chi'^{t_i/n_0}$, so $\log(\lambda_0/\lambda_a)\ge\frac1{n_0}\log\frac1{\chi'}\ge\frac\Lambda l+\frac{1.021}{n_0}$. The vacuum is simple and its eigenvector lies in the sector $00$ (Lem.~\ref{lem:tr}); the tops of the sectors with electric flux are among the $\lambda_a$, $a\ge1$. For $N=n=2^kl$ and an integer $N_2\ge n$, with $t_i=2^in\le N_2<2t_i$, Prop.~\ref{prop:slab}(a), (c) give $\log(1+\mathsf r_{t_i}(N_2,n))\le\frac{N_2}{t_i}\delta^{(n)}(t_i,t_i)\le0.3652\,\chi^{2^i}$, so $(\lambda_a/\lambda_0)^{t_i}\le0.367\,\chi^{2^i}\le\chi^{t_i/n}$ and $\log(\lambda_0/\lambda_a)\ge\frac1n\log\frac1\chi\ge\frac\Lambda l+\frac{3.5065}n$. Over $n\times n$, $(\lambda_a/\lambda_0)^n\le\mathsf r_n(n,n)\le0.001615\,\theta^{n/l}$, and $\log\frac1{0.001615}\ge6.42$. Finally, for $N_1,N_2\ge n$, Lem.~\ref{lem:seq}(f) gives $\log(1+\mathsf r_n(N_1,N_2))\le\delta(n,N_1,N_2)\le\frac{N_1N_2}{n^2}\delta_{\rm c}(n)\le0.01655\,\frac{N_1N_2}{n^2}\theta^{n/l}=:u\le\log2$, and $e^u-1\le u/\log2$, $\log2/0.01655\ge41.8$.

\emph{Step 10 (flux lines of dyadic length).} $2\sigma^+N^2/\log\frac1\chi=2\varsigma w^2/(-\log0.03+2w\Lambda)$ increases in $w$, is $\ge3.83$ at $w=2$ and $<2\mathsf qw=\mathsf qN/l$: the bounds on $\hat N$. With the time $1$ over $(N_2,N)$, Lem.~\ref{lem:tr}(d) gives $\Lambda_-^t\le a_-(t,N_2,N)=z_-(t,N_2,N)\lambda_0^t(1+\mathsf r_t(N_2,N))$ for every $t$. Take $t=t_i=2^iN$ with $i$ the largest integer such that $\mathsf M=N_2/t\ge\hat N/2$, so that $\hat N/2\le\mathsf M<\hat N$. The first inequality of Lem.~\ref{lem:vort}(b) at the time $N_2$, Prop.~\ref{prop:slab}(c), $\mathsf r_{N_2}(t,N)\le\mathsf r_t(t,N)^{\mathsf M}\le e^{-2^i\sigma^+N^2}$ and $\log(1+\mathsf r_t(N_2,N))\le\mathsf M\delta^{(N)}(t,t)\le0.1826\,\mathsf M\chi^{2^i}$ give
\[
\log\frac{\lambda_0}{\Lambda_-}\ge\frac1t\Bigl[2^i(\sigma^+N^2-\mathsf g)-\log\mathsf M-0.1826\,\mathsf M\chi^{2^i}\Bigr]\ge\sigma^+N-\frac{2\log\hat N+1.86}N,
\]
as $\hat N\chi\le0.7936$. As $N_2\to\infty$, $i\to\infty$, and the bounded last two terms are divided by $2^iN$: the lower limit. For $\max\{N,2\mathsf ql\}\le N_2<\hat NN/2$ let $w'$ be the largest power of two with $w'\le w$ and $2\mathsf qw'^2l\le N_2$, and $l'=2w'l\le N$, so that $N_2\ge\mathsf ql'^2/2l$; Prop.~\ref{prop:tub}(e) with $N_3=N$, $n_2=N_2$ and $M=N_2/l'$ applies. If $w'<w$, then $8\mathsf qw'^2l>N_2$, so $N/l'^2<2\mathsf qN/N_2l\le2\mathsf q/l$ and $M<4\mathsf qw'$; if $w'=w$, then $N/l'^2=1/N\le2\mathsf q/l$ and $M<\hat N/2<4\mathsf qw$. In both cases $\log M<\log\frac{2\mathsf qN}l$ and $0.01655\,M\theta^{l'/l}<4\mathsf q\cdot0.01655\,w'e^{-2w'\Lambda}\le0.855$, which gives the second floor. For $N\le N'<2N$: with the time $1$, Lem.~\ref{lem:vort}(a) in the third side gives $\Lambda_-(N_2,N')^t\le a_-(t,N_2,N')\le a_-(t,N_2,N)^{N'/N}$, and $a_-(t,N_2,N)^{1/t}\to\Lambda_-(N_2,N)$; so $\log\Lambda_-(N_2,N')\le\frac{N'}N\log\Lambda_-(N_2,N)$. Also $\log\lambda_0(N_2,N')\ge N_2N'P$ and $\log\lambda_0(N_2,N)\le\frac1NF(N,N_2,N)\le N_2NP+\frac{N_2}{N^2}\delta_{\rm c}(N)$ (Lem.~\ref{lem:seq}(f)). Hence $\log\frac{\lambda_0}{\Lambda_-}(N_2,N')\ge\frac{N'}N[\log\frac{\lambda_0}{\Lambda_-}(N_2,N)-\frac{N_2}{N^2}\delta_{\rm c}(N)]$, and the first floor, $\delta_{\rm c}(N)\le0.01655\,\theta^{N/l}$ and $N'/N<2$ give the third.

\emph{Step 11 (flux lines of every integer length; the slabs).} Let $N\ge4l$. Prop.~\ref{prop:lines} gives $t_i\varepsilon_{\rm v}(t_i,N)\le e^{-E'_i}$ with $2^{-i}E'_i\ge\mathsf E_0-\mathsf g'$. As in Step 10, with $i$ the largest integer such that $\mathsf M=N_2/t_i\ge\hat N'/2$, the first inequality of Lem.~\ref{lem:vort}(b) at the time $N_2$, with $\mathsf r_{N_2}(t_i,N)\le\chi_0^{2^i\hat N'/2}\le e^{-2^i\mathsf E_0}$, gives $z_-(t_i,N_2,N)\le\hat N'e^{-E'_i}$, and Prop.~\ref{prop:slab}(b) gives $\log(1+\mathsf r_{t_i}(N_2,N))\le\mathsf M\delta^{(N)}(t_i,t_i)\le\frac14\xi'_i$; so $\log(\lambda_0/\Lambda_-)\ge\frac1{t_i}[E'_i-\log\hat N'-\frac14\xi'_i]\ge(\mathsf E_0-\mathsf g')/n_0=\sigma^+N-\kappa\mathsf g'/N$. The penultimate inequality uses the unused positive recurrence tail displayed in the proof of Prop.~\ref{prop:lines}.

As $\kappa\mathsf g'=\kappa^2\log\hat N'+\kappa[3.22+(3\kappa+0.68)\mathsf h]$ and $\mathsf h\le0.4274\kappa+0.0208$, $\kappa\mathsf g'$ increases in $\kappa$, and at $\kappa=2$ it is at most $4\log\hat N'+18.14$. The window $\max\{N,2\mathsf ql\}\le N_2<\hat N'n_0/2$ is treated as in Step 10, with $l'=2w'l\le n_0$. For the closed form, $\hat N'n_0/2<(\mathsf qN/l+2)N/2\le(\frac{\mathsf q}2+\frac14)N^2/l$ and $\hat N'<(\mathsf q+\frac12)N/l$, as $N\ge4l$; so $C(\theta)N^2/l\ge\hat N'n_0/2$ and $4\log\hat N'+18.2\le4\log\frac Nl+4\log(\mathsf q+\frac12)+18.2\le C(\theta)(1+\log\frac Nl)$; and $4\log8.673+18.2\le26.85$ at $\mathsf q\le8.173$. If $w\ge4$ and $\tau\le0.087$, the same road, with the slab of the thickness $N$ started from $\mathsf e^{(N)}(n_0)\le2\delta(n_0,2n_0,N)\le8\cdot0.01655\,\tau\le0.0116$, where $\omega(Y_1(x))\le2.06x^2$, so that $2.06\,\mathsf e^{(N)}(t_i)\le(0.2728\,\tau)^{2^i}$, and with the start from Prop.~\ref{prop:tub}(d) at $l'=n_0$ carried to the thickness $N$ by Lem.~\ref{lem:vort}(a) at the real factor $N/n_0$, gives the floor with $\hat N''$ and $10.8$. (g3) is Lem.~\ref{lem:road} with $L_2=N_2$, $L_3=N$ and $\phi\ge\sigma^+N-(4\log\hat N'+18.2)/N$.

\emph{Step 12 (boxes of every shape, cylinders, twisted boxes).} A cube of $N/2$ layers is a cell $\mathsf C_{N/2}(c)$, and all box laws are invariant under translations. For a real function $A$ of the cell, Prop.~\ref{prop:shape} gives $|\langle A\rangle_{\underline n}-\langle A\rangle_{(N,N,N)}|\le2.71\,\theta^{N/4l}|\!|\!|A|\!|\!|_N$ for every box with sides $\ge N$. If $A$ is continuous, let the sides of a second box tend to infinity: by Step 4, $|\nu(A)-\langle A\rangle_{(N,N,N)}|\le2.71\,\theta^{N/4l}|\!|\!|A|\!|\!|_N$, so $|\langle A\rangle_{\underline n}-\nu(A)|\le5.42\,\theta^{N/4l}|\!|\!|A|\!|\!|_N\le5.42\,\theta^{N/4l}\sup|A|$ by Lem.~\ref{lem:mir}(b). For a bounded real Borel $A$, take continuous $A_k$ with $|A_k|\le\sup|A|$ and $A_k\to A$ in $L^8$ of the mean of the images of $\langle\cdot\rangle_{(N,N,N)}$, $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\underline n}$ and $\nu$ on the bonds of the cell; both sides of the bound pass to the limit, the seminorm because $|\!|\!|A_k-A|\!|\!|_N\le\langle|A_k-A|^8\rangle_{(N,N,N)}^{1/8}$ (Lem.~\ref{lem:mir}(b)).

For an event take $A=\mathbf 1_E-\frac12$. For the cube of side $m\ge2l$ take $N=2\lfloor m/2\rfloor\le m$. The cylinder over $\Sigma$ is the limit of Prop.~\ref{prop:long}, and the bound passes to it; with $\Sigma=(n,n)$ and $M\to\infty$, Lem.~\ref{lem:vort}(a) in the third side gives $z_-(n,n,Mn)\le[z_-(n,n,n)\lambda_0^n(1+\mathsf r_n(n,n))]^M\lambda_0^{-Mn}=[(1+\mathsf r_n(n,n))z_-(n,n,n)]^M$, and Lem.~\ref{lem:two}(d) on the box $(n,n,Mn)$ gives the area bound on the cylinder, as $8^{T/Mn}\to1$. Twisted boxes: let the columns recede. For a finite set $\mathfrak A$ of bonds the plaquettes that meet $\mathfrak A$ carry no twist in all but finitely many members, so every limit point satisfies the Gibbs equations, as in Step 2.

The translate by $e_\mu$ of a twisted box law is the twisted law with the columns moved by one step, and by the proof of Lem.~\ref{lem:tr}(iii) this is the image of the law under $U(b)\mapsto-U(b)$ on a set of bonds next to the columns; a fixed local function depends on none of these bonds in all but finitely many members. So every limit point is a periodic Gibbs state, that is $\nu$; the two equations are linear in the law, so they hold for finite mixtures. If a column passes through $p_0$ for all members, one flip moves it off $p_0$ and changes the sign of $\operatorname{tr}\partial U(p_0)$, and the column so moved recedes after further flips that do not touch $p_0$; so the law of $\operatorname{tr}\partial U(p_0)$ tends to that of $-\operatorname{tr}\partial U(p_0)$ under $\nu$, which differs because $\nu(\operatorname{tr}\partial U(p_0))=2\nu(W_p)>0$ by Cor.~\ref{cor:pot}(a).

\emph{Step 13 (the pressure).} By Thm.~\ref{thm:crit}(b), $\mathsf e(2l)\le\theta^2/12.9\le0.0615<0.069$ at $\beta$. Each $F(\underline n;\beta')$ is a smooth function of $\beta'$, so there is an open interval $\mathsf U$ containing $\beta$ on which $\mathsf e(2l;\beta')\le0.069$: the criterion holds on $\mathsf U$ at the side $2l$ with $x_0=0.069$, so that what is proved above holds at each $\beta'\in\mathsf U$, with the state $\nu_{\beta'}$ and with $\delta_{\rm c}(N;\beta')<0.1324\cdot0.8901^{N/4l}$ for $N\ge4l$, uniformly on $\mathsf U$. Let $N_m=2\mathsf L^m$ and $f_m(\beta')=F(N_m,N_m,N_m;\beta')/N_m^3$: these are smooth, tend to $P$ pointwise, and $f_m'(\beta')=-3\langle a_p\rangle_{(N_m,N_m,N_m)}$ by the invariance of the cube under translations and permutations of the axes. As $0\le a_p\le2$ is a function of one cell of the torus, Lem.~\ref{lem:exc} gives $|\langle a_p\rangle_{(N_m,N_m,N_m)}-\nu_{\beta'}(a_p)|\le\sqrt{\epsilon_m}+\epsilon_m$, with $\epsilon_m\to0$ uniformly on $\mathsf U$. So the $f_m'$ converge uniformly on $\mathsf U$ to $-3\nu_{\beta'}(a_p)$, which is therefore continuous, and $P(\beta_2)-P(\beta_1)=\lim_m\int_{\beta_1}^{\beta_2}f_m'=\int_{\beta_1}^{\beta_2}(-3\nu_{\beta'}(a_p))\,\mathrm{d}\beta'$. Finally $\nu(a_p)=1-\nu(W_p)\le1-\frac\beta{4(\beta+1)}$ by Cor.~\ref{cor:pot}(a).
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Thm.~\ref{thm:crit}]
(a) is Prop.~\ref{prop:rec}(a); if $\beta>0$, $\mathsf e(l_0)\le X(l_0)\le\frac1{20}\le0.069$, and $12.9/20=0.645$. (b) By Prop.~\ref{prop:rec}(b), (c), $12.9\,\mathsf e(2n)\le(12.9\,\mathsf e(n))^2$ as long as $\mathsf e(n)\le0.069$, and the induction keeps $\mathsf e(2^kl)\le\theta^{2^k}/12.9$. For $k\ge3$, $\mathsf e(2^{k-1}l)\le\theta^4/12.9\le0.04866\le\frac1{20}$, so
\[
X(2^kl)\le17.71\,\mathsf e(2^{k-1}l)^2\le\frac{17.71}{166.41}\,\theta^{2^k}\le0.10643\,\theta^{2^k}\le0.10643\cdot0.394013 .
\]
$\Phi(\Psi(x))=\frac1{20}$ at $x=0.065062\ldots$ and $\Phi(x)=\frac1{20}$ at $x=0.052727\ldots$; both functions increase, $X(2l)\le\Phi(x_0)$, $X(4l)\le\Phi(\Psi(x_0))$, and $\Phi(\Psi^k(x_0))$ does not increase in $k$ because $\Psi(x)\le x$ there. (c) $\mathsf m_{\mathsf e}(2n)\ge\mathsf m_{\mathsf e}(n)$ is $12.9\,\mathsf e(2n)\le(12.9\,\mathsf e(n))^2$. For $k\ge3$, $\mathsf e(n)\le X(n)\le\frac1{20}$ gives $X(2n)\le17.71\,\mathsf e(n)^2\le18X(n)^2$, so $\mathsf m_X$ does not decrease. $X(n)\ge\mathsf e(n)$ gives $\mathsf m_X(n)\le\mathsf m_{\mathsf e}(n)-\frac1n\log\frac{18}{12.9}$, with $\log\frac{18}{12.9}\ge0.3331$; $X(n)\le17.71\,\mathsf e(n/2)^2$ gives $18X(n)\le1.91563\,(12.9\,\mathsf e(n/2))^2$, so $\mathsf m_X(n)\ge\mathsf m_{\mathsf e}(n/2)-\frac1n\log1.91563$, with $\log1.91563\le0.6501$. Both rates being monotone and squeezed, they have one limit, and $\mathsf m_{\mathsf e}(l)\ge\Lambda/l$ is the criterion. (d) $Y_2(0.0740538)\approx0.3156<\log2$; for $0<x<0.0740538$ the iterates $\Psi^k(x)$ decrease, and to $0$, since a positive limit would be a fixed point below $0.0740538$; so $\mathsf e(2^kl)\le\Psi^k(\mathsf e(l))\to0$ and $X(2^{k+1}l)\le\Phi(\Psi^k(\mathsf e(l)))\to0$; and $\beta>0$ because $\mathsf e(l)>0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Thm.~\ref{thm:phys}]
Apply Thms.~\ref{thm:one} and~\ref{thm:crit} at $l=l_*L^K$ and $\beta=L^K\mathsf b$, with the one $x_0$ of the uniform criterion; then $\theta$, $\Lambda$, $\mathsf q$, $C(\theta)$ do not depend on $K$. By \eqref{eq:sigma}, $\sigma^+l^2=\frac12\log\frac1\theta+0.4175$ depends on $\theta$ alone. A rectangle of physical sides $R,T$ has $RL^K\times TL^K$ bonds, and $\sigma^+\cdot RL^K\cdot TL^K=\frac{\sigma^+l^2}{l_*^2}RT=\sigma_*RT$. For $R,T\ge2a_K$, Lem.~\ref{lem:bond}(b) with $\#B=2(R+T)/a_K-4$ and $\beta=\mathsf b/a_K$ gives $\nu_K(W_C)\le\exp[-3(|C|_{\rm ph}-4a_K)/(8\mathsf b+3a_K)]$, and the smaller of two bounds is at most their geometric mean: (a). For $n=\ell/a_K$: $\sigma^+n^2=\sigma_*\ell^2$, $n/l=\ell/l_*$, $a_K^{-1}\sigma^+n=\sigma_*\ell$, $a_K^{-1}/l=1/l_*$ and $a_K^{-1}/n=1/\ell$; this turns Thm.~\ref{thm:one}(d), (e), (f) and (g) into (b), (c) and (d), with $\hat N\le\mathsf q\ell/l_*+1$ and $C(\theta)\le27$. (e) is Thm.~\ref{thm:crit}(b) at $k=3$, with $18\cdot\frac{17.71}{166.41}\le1.91563\le1.9157$, and Thm.~\ref{thm:crit}(a); finally $4\cdot0.4757=1.9028$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Cor.~\ref{cor:pot}]
\emph{Step 1 (symmetry).} The symmetries of $\nu$ carry a rectangle to every other one with the same sides, or with the sides exchanged and run backwards.

\emph{Step 2 (two Hankel forms).} At a site mirror orthogonal to $e_\mu$ that contains a site $x$, let $\gamma_h$ run from $x$ up $h$ steps along $e_\mu$, $R$ steps along $e_\lambda$, and down to $x+Re_\lambda$ ($\gamma_0$ lies in the mirror). Then $\sum_{j,k}U(\gamma_{h'})_{jk}\overline{U(\mathfrak r\gamma_h)_{jk}}=2W$ of a rectangle $R\times(h+h')$, and the reflection positivity of $\nu$ at this mirror (Prop.~\YMMref{103.4}{758}; $\nu$ is a periodic Gibbs state), applied to $A_{jk}=\sum_hc_hU(\gamma_h)_{jk}$, gives $\sum_{h,h'}c_hc_{h'}m(R,h+h')\ge0$. At a bond mirror, take the paths $\gamma'_h$ from a site $x_p$ next to the mirror up $h$ steps, along $R$ steps and down to $x_q=x_p+Re_\lambda$; then $\sum\overline{(\mathsf z_p)_{ji}}(\mathsf z_q)_{kl}A_{jk}\overline{\mathfrak rA_{il}}$ with $A_{jk}=\sum_hc_hU(\gamma'_h)_{jk}$ is $2\sum_{h,h'}c_hc_{h'}W$ of rectangles $R\times(h+h'+1)$. Its mean is $\ge0$ on the cubes of sides $2^kl$, which are even, by Lem.~\ref{lem:mir}(c) after a translation that brings the mirror between the layers $0$ and $1$, and it passes to $\nu$ by Thm.~\ref{thm:one}(a): $\sum_{h,h'}c_hc_{h'}m(R,h+h'+1)\ge0$.

\emph{Step 3 (log-convexity).} The $2\times2$ minors of the two forms give $m(R,T)^2\le m(R,T-1)m(R,T+1)$ for all $T\ge1$.

\emph{Step 4 ($w>0$).} Given the other bonds, $U(b)$ has the density proportional to $\exp[\beta\mathsf k\frac12\operatorname{tr}(U(b)g)]$, $\mathsf kg$ the sum of the four staples of $b$, $0\le\mathsf k\le4$; so, by the Gibbs equation and Lem.~\ref{lem:bond}(a), $4w=\nu(\mathsf k\,r(\beta\mathsf k))\ge\nu(\beta\mathsf k^2/(\beta\mathsf k+4))\ge\beta\nu(\mathsf k^2)/(4\beta+4)$. Two different staples of $b$ are mirror images at a mirror that contains $b$, a site mirror if they lie in one plane and a diagonal mirror if they lie in two; so $\nu(\mathsf k^2)=4+\sum_{s\ne s'}\nu(\frac12\operatorname{tr}ss'^{-1})\ge4$ by reflection positivity, and $w\ge\beta/(4(\beta+1))$.

\emph{Step 5 (positivity).} From $m(1,0)=1$, $m(1,1)=w>0$ and Step 3, $m(1,T)>0$ for all $T$; then $m(R,1)=m(1,R)>0$ and $m(R,T)>0$. As $T\mapsto-\log m(R,T)$ is concave and vanishes at $0$, $m(R,T)\ge m(R,1)^T\ge w^{RT}$; the upper bound of (a) is Thm.~\ref{thm:one}(b).

\emph{Step 6 (the potential).} The increments of a concave sequence do not increase; their limit is their infimum and also the limit of $-\frac1T\log m(R,T)$; summing the increments from $T_1$ to $T_2$ gives $m(R,T_2)\le e^{-(T_2-T_1)V(R)}m(R,T_1)$; if a number $v$ has this property for infinitely many $T_2$, dividing by $T_2$ gives $v\le V(R)$; and the increasing slopes of the convex function $\log m(R,\cdot)$ give the inequality of four rectangles.

\emph{Step 7 (the measure).} Let $\Lambda$ be the linear functional on the real polynomials with $\Lambda(\lambda^T)=m(R,T)$. Step 2 says $\Lambda(p^2)\ge0$ and $\Lambda(\lambda p^2)\ge0$. With $s_r=\Lambda(\lambda^rp^2)\ge0$, Schwarz's inequality gives $s_r^2\le s_0s_{2r}$, and, $|m|\le1$ bounding every $s_r$, iteration gives $s_2\le s_0$ and then $s_1\le s_0$: $\Lambda((1-\lambda)p^2)\ge0$; and $\Lambda(\lambda(1-\lambda)p^2)=\Lambda((1-\lambda)(\lambda p)^2)+\Lambda(\lambda((1-\lambda)p)^2)\ge0$. Writing $\lambda^T(1-\lambda)^k$ as $\lambda^\epsilon(1-\lambda)^{\epsilon'}q^2$ with $\epsilon,\epsilon'\in\{0,1\}$ gives $\sum_i(-1)^i\binom kim(R,T+i)\ge0$ for all $k,T\ge0$: the sequence is completely monotone, and Hausdorff's moment theorem gives the one measure $\varrho_R$. Since $m(R,T)\le(\max\operatorname{supp}\varrho_R)^T$ and $m(R,T)\ge(\lambda_*-\varepsilon)^T\varrho_R([\lambda_*-\varepsilon,1])$ for $\lambda_*=\max\operatorname{supp}\varrho_R>0$, $m(R,T)^{1/T}\to\lambda_*$, so $\lambda_*=e^{-V(R)}$; for $T\ge1$ the point $0$ gives nothing, and the substitution $\lambda=e^{-E}$ gives the representation, with the mass $\varrho_R((0,1])\ge m(R,1)>0$.

\emph{Step 8.} (d) follows from (a): $V(R)\ge\sigma^+R$ from the upper bound, $V(R)\le-R\log w$ from the lower one. (e) At $l=l_*L^K$, $\sigma^+=\sigma_*a_K^2$, so $a_K^{-1}V(R/a_K)\ge a_K^{-1}\sigma^+R/a_K=\sigma_*R$; and $M_K(R,T_2)/M_K(R,T_1)=e^{2\kappa(T_2-T_1)}m(R/a_K,T_2/a_K)/m(R/a_K,T_1/a_K)$, to which (c) applies; in the inequality of four rectangles the factors $e^{2\kappa(T'-T)}$, raised to the powers $1/(T'-T)$, give one and the same factor on both sides. Along a sequence, $M_j(R,T_2)\le e^{-(T_2-T_1)v_j(R)}M_j(R,T_1)$ at each $j$, as just shown with $\kappa=\kappa_j$; so $v_j(R)\le\frac1{T_2-T_1}\log\frac{M_j(R,T_1)}{M_j(R,T_2)}$, whose right member converges, and $v_j(R)\ge B$ for infinitely many $j$ gives $B\le\limsup_jv_j(R)$; and $V_{K_j}(R)\ge\sigma_*R$ gives $v_j(R)\ge\sigma_*R-2\kappa_j$.

The symmetry, the inequality of three rectangles, which is the log-convexity of (b) in the form of chords, and that of four rectangles hold for each $M_j$, the factors $e^{2\kappa_j(R+T)}$ cancelling in both inequalities, and pass to the limits. With $\mathsf F(T)=-\log\mathsf W(R,T)$, the inequality of three rectangles says that the slope $(\mathsf F(T')-\mathsf F(T_1))/(T'-T_1)$ does not increase in $T'>T_1$; so it has a limit in $[-\infty,\infty)$ as $T'\to\infty$, $\mathsf F(T')/T'$ tends to this limit for every $T_1$, and $V_{\rm ren}(R)$ is the infimum of all these slopes. (f) A rectangle with an even side $2h$ is $\gamma(\mathfrak r\gamma)^{-1}$ for the site mirror halfway along that side, and a square is $\gamma(\mathfrak r\gamma)^{-1}$ for a diagonal mirror through two of its corners; as in Step 2, Prop.~\YMMref{103.4}{758} gives $s(W_C)\ge0$.

\emph{Step 9 (no criterion).} (g) Steps 1--7 use of $\nu$ only that it is a periodic Gibbs state, invariant under the symmetries of the lattice and reflection positive at every lattice mirror (Prop.~\YMMref{103.4}{758}), and, for the second Hankel form, that it is positive at the bond mirrors on the functions of two crossing bonds. With the hypothesis of (g) they hold for $s$, but for the upper bound of (a), in whose place $m_s\le1$ stands; and $m_s(R,T)\ge w^{RT}$ gives $V_s(R)\le-R\log w\le R\log\frac{4(\beta+1)}\beta$. On site mirrors alone the first Hankel form, with all $c$ but two equal to $0$, gives $m_s(R,h+h')^2\le m_s(R,2h)\,m_s(R,2h')$. At $(h-1,h+1)$, and from $m_s(R,0)=1$ and $m_s(R,2)>0$, induction gives $m_s(R,2h)>0$ for all $h$, and $\psi(h)=-\log m_s(R,2h)$ is concave, $\ge0$, with $\psi(0)=0$; so $\psi(h)/h$ tends to $2V_{\rm e}(R)=\inf_h(\psi(h+1)-\psi(h))\ge0$, and $\psi(h_2)-\psi(h_1)\ge2(h_2-h_1)V_{\rm e}(R)$ is the inequality for even $T_1$ and $T_2$. For an odd $T_2=2h_2+1>T_1$, the pair $(h_2,h_2+1)$ gives $m_s(R,2h_2+1)\le[m_s(R,2h_2)\,m_s(R,2h_2+2)]^{1/2}$, and the even case twice gives the inequality. For even $R$: the pair $(0,1)$ gives $m_s(1,2)\ge m_s(1,1)^2=w^2>0$, by Step 4, and $m_s(2,2)\ge m_s(2,1)^2=m_s(1,2)^2>0$; the induction at the width $2$ gives $m_s(2,2h)>0$, and $m_s(2h,2)=m_s(2,2h)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Prop.~\ref{prop:where}]
(a) $F(l,2l,2l)\le0$ and $-F(2l,2l,2l)\le6\beta(2l)^3$, so $0\le\mathsf e(l)\le48\beta l^3\le x_0$. (b) For $\mathsf k\in\mathbb R^4$ let $\pi_{\mathsf k}$ be the law on $G\simeq S^3$ with the density proportional to $e^{\langle U,\mathsf k\rangle}$. Every linear component $\langle U,\mathsf e\rangle$, $|\mathsf e|=1$, has variance $\le\frac14$ under $\pi_{\mathsf k}$: with $\kappa=|\mathsf k|$ and $x=\langle U,\mathsf k\rangle/\kappa$, the mean $A(\kappa)$ of $x$ satisfies $A'=\operatorname{Var}x$ and, by an integration by parts, $\langle1-x^2\rangle=3A/\kappa$, so $A'=1-3A/\kappa-A^2$; a comparison with the positive root $\mathsf B(\kappa)$ of $1-3a/\kappa-a^2=\frac14$, whose derivative is $<\frac14$, together with $A\le\kappa/4$, which follows from $3A=\kappa\langle1-x^2\rangle$ and $\langle x^2\rangle\ge\frac14$, the two identities in the proof of Lem.~\ref{lem:bond}(a), $x$ having the law of $x_0$ under $\langle\cdot\rangle_\kappa$, gives $A\ge\mathsf B$ and so $\operatorname{Var}x\le\frac14$, while the components orthogonal to $\mathsf k$ have the variance $A/\kappa\le\frac14$.

So two such laws differ in total variation by at most $\frac14|\mathsf k-\mathsf k'|$. The conditional law of one bond given the others is $\pi_{\beta\mathsf h}$, $\mathsf h$ the sum of the four unit vectors of its staples, and changing one of its $12$ neighbouring bonds moves $\mathsf h$ by at most $2$. For a bounded Borel function $f$ of finitely many bonds let $\delta_b(f)$ be its oscillation in the single bond $b$, and $\Delta(f)=\sum_b\delta_b(f)$. The conditional expectation $E_b$ in the bond $b$ gives $\delta_b(E_bf)=0$, $\delta_{b'}(E_bf)\le\delta_{b'}(f)+\frac\beta2\delta_b(f)$ for the $12$ neighbours $b'$ of $b$, and $\delta_{b'}(E_bf)\le\delta_{b'}(f)$ for the other bonds; so after any sequence of updates the oscillations are, bond by bond, at most the entries of the vector $v$ that arises from $(\delta_b(f))_b$ by the linear rules $v_b\to0$, $v_{b'}\to v_{b'}+\frac\beta2v_b$ for the neighbours $b'$ of the updated bond $b$.

Let $S_0$ be the set of the bonds of $f$, $S\supset S_0$ a finite set of bonds, $d(b)$ the distance of $b$ from $S_0$ in the graph of neighbouring bonds, $r=\min\{d(b):b\notin S\}$, $\alpha=6\beta<1$, and $f_k$ the function that $k$ sweeps of updates through $S$, each bond of $S$ once in a sweep, make of $f$. An update at $b$ takes $v_b\alpha^{-\min\{d(b),r\}}$ from the weighted sum $\sum_{b'}v_{b'}\alpha^{-\min\{d(b'),r\}}$ and adds at most $\frac\beta2\cdot12\,v_b\,\alpha^{-\min\{d(b),r\}-1}=v_b\,\alpha^{-\min\{d(b),r\}}$, as $d(b')\le d(b)+1$; so the weighted sum does not increase, it equals $\Delta(f)$ at the start, when $v$ lives on $S_0$, where $d=0$, and the bonds outside $S$ carry the weight $\alpha^{-r}$: $\sum_{b\notin S}v_b\le\alpha^r\Delta(f)$ at all times.

An update at $b\in S$ changes $\sum_{b'\in S}v_{b'}$ by at most $-(1-\alpha)v_b$, and in a sweep the entries of the bonds of $S$ at the times of their updates add up to at least the sum at the beginning of the sweep; so $\sum_{b\in S}v_b\le\alpha^k\Delta(f)$ after $k$ sweeps. As $f_k$ is a function of the bonds of $S$ and of their neighbours, and two configurations of these bonds are joined by changing one bond at a time, $\sup f_k-\inf f_k\le(\alpha^k+\alpha^r)\Delta(f)$. Now let $l\ge4$ be even, $S$ the set of the bonds with both ends in the cube $\{0,\dots,l-3\}^3$, and $f=a_p$ for the plaquette $p=p_{12}(c_0,c_0,c_0)$, $c_0=\frac{l-4}2$. The ends of the bonds at distance $\le j$ from the four bonds of $p$ lie in $[c_0-j,c_0+1+j]^3$, which lies in $[0,l-3]^3$ for $j\le c_0$; so every bond not in $S$ has $d\ge c_0+1=\frac l2-1$, that is $r\ge\frac l2-1$; and $\Delta(a_p)\le8$.

The bonds of $S$ and their neighbours lie in a cube of $l$ sites a side, which the projections modulo $l$ and modulo $2l$ map one to one into the tori of sides $l$ and $2l$, the plaquettes at the bonds of $S$ onto plaquettes; so on both tori the conditional laws of the bonds of $S$ are those used above, the functions $f_k$ are the same, and both means of $a_p$ equal means of $f_k$, which lie in $[\inf f_k,\sup f_k]$. Letting $k\to\infty$: $|\bar a_{2l}(b)-\bar a_l(b)|\le8(6b)^{l/2-1}$, $\bar a_n(b)$ the mean of $a_p$ on the cube of side $n$ at the coupling $b$. As $\frac d{d\beta}F(n,n,n)=-3n^3\bar a_n(\beta)$ and $X=0$ at $\beta=0$,
\[
X(l)=24\,l^3\int_0^\beta\bigl(\bar a_{2l}(b)-\bar a_l(b)\bigr)\,\mathrm{d}b\le64\,l^2(6\beta)^{l/2}.
\]
At each of the four pairs of a coupling and a side named in (b), $64\,l^2(6\beta)^{l/2}\le\frac1{20}$; and $l\mapsto l^2(6\beta)^{l/2}$ decreases for $l>4/\log\frac1{6\beta}$, which lies below each of the four sides. Thm.~\ref{thm:crit}(a) gives the criterion. (c) The same contraction, with $S$ the set of the bonds at the distance $<r$ from the bonds of $f$, applied to two Gibbs states $s$, $s'$, for which $s(E_bF)=s(F)$ by the Gibbs equation of one bond, gives $|s(f)-s'(f)|=|s(f_k)-s'(f_k)|\le(\alpha^k+\alpha^r)\Delta(f)$; let $k\to\infty$ and then $r\to\infty$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Prop.~\ref{prop:says}]
(a) Lem.~\ref{lem:seq}(a), (b) with $\kappa_i=\lambda_i(2l,2l)^l$, so that $D=\mathsf e(l)$ and $\eta=\mathsf r$: $2\log1.0351\le0.069$, and $\varpi(e^{0.069}-1)\le0.0357638$. The tops $\Lambda_e$, $e\ne00$, are among the $\lambda_i$, $i\ge1$ (Lem.~\ref{lem:tr}), so $(\Lambda_e/\lambda_0)^l\le\mathsf r$, and $\log\frac1{0.0357638}\ge3.33$; and $\mathsf r\ge\sum_{e\ne00}(\Lambda_e/\lambda_0)^l$ gives the last statement. (b) With the time $1$ over $(2l,2l)$ let $w_f=W_{2l}(f;0)/Z$ on the cube of side $2l$. Inside each sector $(\sum_i\mu_i^l)^2\ge\sum_i\mu_i^{2l}$, so
\[
\mathsf e(l)=2\log Z(l,2l,2l)-\log Z(2l,2l,2l)\ge2\log\sum_f\sqrt{w_f}.
\]
By Lem.~\ref{lem:tr}(c), $w_{00}=\frac14(1+2r_1+r_2)$, $w_{10}=w_{01}=\frac14(1-r_2)$, $w_{11}=\frac14(1-2r_1+r_2)$, and $w_{11}\ge0$, $r_2\le r_1$ give $2r_1-1\le r_2\le r_1$; here $r_1\le1$ by Lem.~\ref{lem:tr}(c), and $r_1>0$ because, with the time the direction that is not in the twisted pair, $Z^-=\operatorname{Tr}\mathsf T_1^{2l}$ is the integral over the diagonal of a kernel with values $>0$ (Lem.~\ref{lem:tr}(i), (ii)). The sum of the square roots is concave in $r_2$, so on this interval it is at least the smaller of its two end values; with $x=1-r_1\in[0,1)$ these are $\sqrt{1-x}+\sqrt{2x}$ at $r_2=2r_1-1$ and $\frac12\sqrt{4-3x}+\frac32\sqrt x$ at $r_2=r_1$, and the first is the smaller, as $\frac14(4-3x)\ge1-x$ and $\frac32>\sqrt2$.

The function $\mathsf f$ increases on $[0,\frac23]$ and decreases on $[\frac23,1]$, with $\mathsf f(1)=\log2$; and $\mathsf f(0.00063)>0.069$, $\mathsf f(0.0039)\ge0.16567$. (c) Let $\mathsf e(l)\le0.069$ and $N\ge16l$, and let $\bar N=2^jl\le N<2\bar N$, $j\ge4$. By Lem.~\ref{lem:seq}(f), $\log(1+\mathsf r_N(N,N))\le\log(1+\mathsf r_{\bar N}(N,N))\le\delta(\bar N,N,N)\le4\delta_{\rm c}(\bar N)\le4\bar\delta_4\le0.0029221$ (Prop.~\ref{prop:rec}(e)); and by Lem.~\ref{lem:tr}(c), $1-Z^-/Z=1-r_1\le\frac43(1-e^{-0.0029221})\le0.0038905<0.0039$. For an integer $l'\ge16l$ with $\bar N=2^jl\le l'<2\bar N$, $j\ge4$: $\mathsf e(l')\le2\log(1+\mathsf r_{l'}(2l',2l'))\le2\delta(\bar N,2l',2l')\le2(2l'/\bar N)^2\delta_{\rm c}(\bar N)<32\,\bar\delta_4\le0.02338$.

The last sentence is the contrapositive of the first, at $l\le N/16$. (d) Thm.~\ref{thm:one}(b) at $R=T=1$ gives $\sigma^+\le\log(1/\nu(W_p))$, and $\sigma^+l^2\ge0.4757$.
\end{proof}

\noindent\emph{The numbers of Remark~\ref{rem:free}.} Over a torus of side $2l$ the momenta are $\frac\pi lm$, $m\in\mathbb Z^2$; three fields with one mode for each momentum $m\ne0$ give the Fock levels whose sum at the time $l$ is the product displayed, and the same at the time $2l$; in the notation of Lem.~\ref{lem:seq}, $1+\eta=1+\mathsf r$ and $1+s_2=1+\mathsf r'$. Summing $-3\log(1-e^{-\pi|m|})$ over the shells $|m|^2=1,2,4,5,8,9,10,13,\dots$ gives approximately $0.72010$, and $-3\log(1-e^{-2\pi|m|})$ gives approximately $0.02415$; so $D\approx1.416$.

\begin{proof}[Proof of Prop.~\ref{prop:small}]
\emph{The exact part.} On every periodic cube of an even side $N$, at every $\beta$, take as time a direction of the twisted pair, let $\nu$ be the other direction of that pair, let $\vartheta\ge2$ and $k\ge2$ be integers with $2k\vartheta=N$, and cut the cube into $2k$ slabs of $\vartheta$ layers. The transfer operator over $\vartheta$ layers, $\mathsf Y=\mathsf T'^{\,\vartheta}$ in the notation of the proof of Lem.~\ref{lem:mir}, commutes with the flip $\mathsf J$ of one layer, the operator $\mathsf J_i$ of Lem.~\ref{lem:tr} that changes the sign of the bonds of the direction $\nu$ that cross one plane $\{x_\nu=c\}$, $c\in\mathbb Z+\frac12$; $Z=\operatorname{Tr}\mathsf Y^{2k}$ and $Z^-=\operatorname{Tr}(\mathsf J\mathsf Y^{2k})$ (Lem.~\ref{lem:tr}(ii), (c)); so $P_\pm=\frac12(1\pm\mathsf J)$ have $\operatorname{Tr}(P_\pm\mathsf Y^{2k})=\frac12(1\pm r_1)Z$: the weights of the two sectors of the flip are $\frac12(1\pm r_1)$.

A function of the bonds is \emph{odd under the flip} if it changes its sign when the bonds of the direction $\nu$ that cross the plane $\{x_\nu=c\}$ change their signs in all layers. Let $D$, $D'$ be bounded Borel functions of the bonds with both ends in one and the same slab of $\vartheta$ layers, $D'$ odd under the flip; of $D$ no parity is asked. For $1\le j\le2k-1$ let $\mathsf t_j$ be the translation by $j\vartheta$ along the time, and $\mathsf t=\mathsf t_k$ the translation by $N/2$. With the slab operators $\mathsf Y_D$, $\mathsf Y_{D'}$ of the proof of Lem.~\ref{lem:mir}, $Z\langle D\cdot\mathsf t_jD'\rangle=\operatorname{Tr}(\mathsf Y^{2k-j-1}\mathsf Y_{D'}\mathsf Y^{j-1}\mathsf Y_D)$.

The weights of the layers and of the crossings do not change when all layers are flipped (proof of Lem.~\ref{lem:tr}); so $P_\sigma\mathsf Y=\mathsf YP_\sigma$ and, $D'$ being odd, $\mathsf J\mathsf Y_{D'}\mathsf J=-\mathsf Y_{D'}$, that is $P_\sigma\mathsf Y_{D'}=\mathsf Y_{D'}P_{-\sigma}$. Splitting the trace over the two sectors, the sector changes between $D$ and $D'$:
\[
Z\langle D\cdot\mathsf t_jD'\rangle=\sum_{\sigma=\pm1}\operatorname{Tr}\bigl((P_\sigma\mathsf Y)^{2k-j-1}\,\mathsf Y_{D'}\,(P_{-\sigma}\mathsf Y)^{j-1}\,\mathsf Y_D\bigr),
\]
a trace of $2k$ Hilbert--Schmidt operators. H\"older's inequality for it (Lem.~\YMMref{86.1}{680}), with $\|P_\sigma\mathsf Y\|_{2k}^{2k}=\operatorname{Tr}(P_\sigma\mathsf Y^{2k})$ and $\|\mathsf Y_D\|_{2k}^{2k}=\operatorname{Tr}(\mathsf Y_D^*\mathsf Y_D)^k\le\sup|D|^{2k}Z$ (the norm definition preceding Lem.~\YMMref{86.1}{680}; the trace is $Z$ times the mean of a product of $2k$ copies of $D$ and of its mirror image), gives
\[
|\langle D\cdot\mathsf t_jD'\rangle|\le\sup|D|\,\sup|D'|\sum_{\sigma=\pm1}\Bigl(\frac{1+\sigma r_1}2\Bigr)^{\frac{2k-j-1}{2k}}\Bigl(\frac{1-\sigma r_1}2\Bigr)^{\frac{j-1}{2k}}
\]
(with $0^0=1$), and at $j=k$, where the two summands are equal,
\[
|\langle D\cdot\mathsf tD'\rangle|\le2\sup|D|\,\sup|D'|\,\Bigl[\frac{1-r_1^2}4\Bigr]^{\frac12-\frac1{2k}} .
\]

\emph{The calibrated construction.} The constants are chosen as in (Th1), (Th2) of \S\ref{sec:cutoff-calibration}, the setting in which Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8} is used; among them are the cube size $M=\mathsf L^{m'}$, with $m'\ge5$ (the setting preceding equation~\YMMref{(634)}{339} has $M\ge L^4M_1$ and $M_1\ge L$), the exponents $r\ge2$ and $\mathfrak p_0$, the constant $A_0>0$ of the thresholds (equation~\YMMref{(634)}{339}), $\gamma\in(0,\frac12]$, and the numbers $c'>0$, $\mathsf C^\Sigma_{\rm maj}$, $c_{\rm low}$ of (Th2). The setting (E) of \S\ref{sec:cutoff-calibration} gives besides a label $\mathsf b\ge\gamma^{-2}$ and an integer $m\ge1$ with $M\,R(\mathsf b)\le\mathsf L^m$, $R(x)=\min\{\mathsf L^i:i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0},\ \mathsf L^i\ge(\log x)^r\}\ge1$, and $\ell=2\mathsf L^m$. At the cutoff $K$ the coupling is $\beta=\mathsf L^K\mathsf b$, and the cube has $N=\ell\mathsf L^K=2\mathsf L^{m+K}$ sites a side. For an integer $0\le d<K$ the block field of the depth $d$ is $V=\mathcal M^{K-d}U$, $\mathcal M$ the block-averaging map of equations~\YMMref{(37)--(39)}{20}; it lives on a periodic cube of
\[
\mathsf n=\ell\mathsf L^d=2\mathsf L^{m+d}
\]
blocks a side, each block having $\vartheta=\mathsf L^{K-d}$ sites a side, so that $N=\mathsf n\vartheta$; its law is $\mu^K_d$ (Def.~\textup{\ref{IV-62-62}}). As $R\ge1$, $\mathsf L^m\ge M=\mathsf L^{m'}\ge\mathsf L^5$, and with $d\ge1$ and $\mathsf L\ge13$:
\[
\mathsf n\ge2\cdot13^6 .
\]
Let $|\partial V-\mathbf 1|_\infty$ be the largest $|\partial V(p)-\mathbf 1|$ over the plaquettes of the block lattice, $x_d=\mathsf L^d\mathsf b$, $\varepsilon=A_0x_d^{-1/2}(\log x_d)^{\mathfrak p_0}$ the threshold of equation~\YMMref{(634)}{339} at the coupling $x_d$, $\delta=\exp[7\mathsf n^2\varepsilon]-1$, and $\mathsf R_d$ the number $\mathsf R_t$ of the definitions preceding Prop.~\YMMref{115.2}{806} at the level $t=K-d$; as there $N_t=\ell^3\mathsf L^{3d}$ and $x_t=x_d$, $\mathsf R_d$ does not depend on $K$. The hypotheses (H) are: $d\ge1$; $x_d\ge\mathsf t_\natural$, the fixed calibration of \S\ref{sec:cutoff-calibration}; $\delta\le\frac1{20}$; and $\mathsf R_d\le\frac1{40}$.

\emph{Step 1: under (H) the block field is nearly flat with probability at least $\frac{39}{40}$, at every cutoff $K>d$.} The data $K$, $\mathsf b$, $m$ and the top level $t=K-d$ make the setting (Th) of \S\ref{sec:cutoff-calibration}, as $1\le t\le K-1$ and $x_t=x_d\ge\mathsf t_\natural$; Lem.~\YMMref{118.1}{812} gives what Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{115.2}{806}} asks of it. Let $F=\mathbf 1_{\mathsf{In}_t}(\mathcal M^tU)$, $\mathsf{In}_t=\{|\partial V-\mathbf 1|_\infty<2\varepsilon\}$ the inner ball of the definitions preceding Lem.~\YMMref{113.10}{796}: a bounded gauge-invariant Borel function, by Prop.~\YMMref{4.5}{20}, \YMMref{4.5}{20} and~\YMMref{113.10}{796}. The weight $\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}_t$ of the definitions preceding Prop.~\YMMref{115.2}{806} carries the factor $\mathbf 1_{\mathsf{In}_t}(\mathcal M^tU)$, so $\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}_t=F\,\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}_t$, and the right inequality of Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{115.2}{806}}, domination and lost-mass bounds gives $Z-\int F\rho_0\,\mathrm{d}U\le Z-\int\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}_t\rho_0\,\mathrm{d}U\le\mathsf R_dZ$, $\rho_0=e^{-\beta A}$ at $\beta=\mathsf L^K\mathsf b$. That is
\[
\mu^K_d\bigl(|\partial V-\mathbf 1|_\infty\ge2\varepsilon\bigr)\le\mathsf R_d\le\tfrac1{40}.
\]
Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8} enters here, through Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{115.2}{806}}.

\emph{Step 2: a winding loop of the block field, its parity and its translate.} Fix a block site $\xi$; let $\Gamma_1$, $\Gamma_2$, $\Gamma_{12}$ be the closed paths of the block lattice from $\xi$ with the step sequences $(e_1^{\mathsf n})$, $(e_2^{\mathsf n})$, $(e_1^{\mathsf n},e_2^{\mathsf n})$, $P_i=V(\Gamma_i)$, and for each of them $D_\Gamma(U)=W_\Gamma(V)=\frac12\operatorname{tr}V(\Gamma)$. Take the direction $3$ as time, the flip of the bonds of the direction $1$ that cross the plane $\{x_1=c\}$, $c=\xi_1+\frac12\vartheta$, and $\mathsf t$ the translation by $N/2$ along $e_3$. Then: (i) $D_\Gamma$ is a real Borel function with $|D_\Gamma|\le1$ (Prop.~\YMMref{4.5}{20}); (ii) it is a function of the bonds with both ends in one slab of $\vartheta$ layers, the slab of the blocks of the sites of $\Gamma$, by the locality of $\mathcal M^{K-d}$ (Prop.~\YMMref{4.5}{20}); (iii) $D_{\Gamma_1}$ and $D_{\Gamma_{12}}$ are odd under the flip: as $\mathsf L$ is odd, the plane $\{x_1=c\}$ separates blocks at every level from $d$ to $K$, on each double block the flip is the gauge transformation that is $-\mathbf 1$ on one side of the plane, so by Prop.~\YMMref{4.5}{20} the averaging map carries the flip of the bonds that cross the plane at one level to the flip at the next level; and $\Gamma_1$, $\Gamma_{12}$ run exactly one block bond that crosses the plane, $\Gamma_2$ none; (iv) $\mathsf tD_\Gamma=W_{\mathsf t\Gamma}(V)$, as $\mathsf t$ is the translation by $\frac{\mathsf n}2$ blocks and $\mathcal M^{K-d}$ commutes with it ({\cite[Lem.~G.1]{YMM2}}).

And $\mathsf m_\Gamma:=\langle D_\Gamma\cdot\mathsf tD_\Gamma\rangle=\int W_\Gamma W_{\mathsf t\Gamma}\,\mathrm{d}\mu^K_d$ has $\mathsf m_{\Gamma_2}=\mathsf m_{\Gamma_1}$: the exchange of $e_1$ and $e_2$ about $\xi$ keeps the law of the cube, commutes with $\mathsf t$ and with $\mathcal M^{K-d}$ ({\cite[Lem.~G.1]{YMM2}}), and carries $\Gamma_1$ to $\Gamma_2$.

On $\mathsf B=\{|\partial V-\mathbf 1|_\infty<2\varepsilon\}$ the two winding holonomies nearly commute: the step sequences $(e_1^{\mathsf n},e_2^{\mathsf n})$ and $(e_2^{\mathsf n},e_1^{\mathsf n})$ are rearrangements of one another, of the length $2\mathsf n$, and Lem.~\YMMref{4.1}{17} gives
\[
|P_2P_1P_2^{-1}P_1^{-1}-\mathbf 1|\le(1+|\partial V-\mathbf 1|_\infty)^{\mathsf n(2\mathsf n-1)}-1<e^{4\mathsf n^2\varepsilon}-1\le\delta .
\]
As $|g-\mathbf 1|^2=2-\operatorname{tr}g$ for $g\in G$, $\frac12\operatorname{tr}(P_2P_1P_2^{-1}P_1^{-1})\ge1-\frac12\delta^2$. The trace identity of Fricke, $\operatorname{tr}(ABA^{-1}B^{-1})=(\operatorname{tr}A)^2+(\operatorname{tr}B)^2+(\operatorname{tr}AB)^2-\operatorname{tr}A\,\operatorname{tr}B\,\operatorname{tr}AB-2$ for $A,B\in\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb C)$, at $A=P_2$, $B=P_1$, gives with $x_i=W_{\Gamma_i}(V)$ and $x_{12}=W_{\Gamma_{12}}(V)$
\[
x_1^2+x_2^2+x_{12}^2-2x_1x_2x_{12}\ge1-\tfrac14\delta^2,\qquad\text{so}\qquad2x_1^2+2x_2^2+x_{12}^2\ge1-\tfrac14\delta^2,
\]
as $|x_{12}|\le1$ gives $-2x_1x_2x_{12}\le x_1^2+x_2^2$. On $\mathsf B$ a winding loop is also close to its translate: with $\epsilon$ the path of $\frac{\mathsf n}2$ steps $e_3$ from $\xi$ to $\mathsf t\xi$ and $g=V(\epsilon)$, the step sequences of $\Gamma$ followed by $\epsilon$ and of $\epsilon$ followed by $\mathsf t\Gamma$ are rearrangements of one another, of the length $\le\frac52\mathsf n$, and Lem.~\YMMref{4.1}{17} gives $|gV(\mathsf t\Gamma)g^{-1}-V(\Gamma)|\le(1+|\partial V-\mathbf 1|_\infty)^{\frac{25}8\mathsf n^2}-1<e^{6.25\,\mathsf n^2\varepsilon}-1\le\delta$, so that $|W_{\mathsf t\Gamma}-W_\Gamma|\le\delta$. As $W_\Gamma W_{\mathsf t\Gamma}\ge W_\Gamma^2-|W_\Gamma-W_{\mathsf t\Gamma}|$ and $|W_\Gamma-W_{\mathsf t\Gamma}|\le2$ off $\mathsf B$, Step~1 gives $\mathsf m_\Gamma\ge\mu^K_d(W_\Gamma^2)-\delta-2\mathsf R_d$; with the weights $2,2,1$ and $\mathsf m_{\Gamma_2}=\mathsf m_{\Gamma_1}$,
\[
4\mathsf m_{\Gamma_1}+\mathsf m_{\Gamma_{12}}\ge\bigl(1-\tfrac14\delta^2\bigr)\bigl(1-\mathsf R_d\bigr)-5\bigl(\delta+2\mathsf R_d\bigr)\ge\tfrac{1599}{1600}\cdot\tfrac{39}{40}-\tfrac12=\tfrac{30361}{64000}>0.4743,
\]
the middle member decreasing in $\delta$ and in $\mathsf R_d$ on $[0,1]$. So $\mathsf m_\Gamma\ge0.0948>0.09$ for $\Gamma=\Gamma_1$ or for $\Gamma=\Gamma_{12}$; both loops give real functions of modulus $\le1$ that are odd under the flip and are functions of one slab of the thickness of a block.

\emph{Step 3: the ceiling.} The exact part at $D=D'=D_\Gamma$, with that $\Gamma$, $\vartheta=\mathsf L^{K-d}\ge2$ and $2k=\mathsf n$, so that $2k\vartheta=N$ and $\frac1{2k}=\frac1{\mathsf n}=\frac{a_d}\ell$, the ratio of the block size $a_d=\mathsf L^{-d}$ at the depth $d$ to the side $\ell$, gives $0.09\le\mathsf m_\Gamma\le2[\frac14(1-r_1^2)]^{\frac12(1-2/\mathsf n)}$, that is, with $\mathsf x=(0.045)^{2/(1-2/\mathsf n)}$,
\[
r_1^2\le1-4\mathsf x,\qquad r_1\le1-2\mathsf x=1-2\,(0.045)^{2/(1-2/\mathsf n)},
\]
the second because $(1-2\mathsf x)^2\ge1-4\mathsf x$, $1-2\mathsf x>0$ and $r_1>0$. The right member of the second inequality decreases in $\mathsf n$ to the limit $0.99595$, and it is $\le0.99596$ if and only if $\mathsf n\ge5020$; at $\mathsf n=2\cdot13^6$ it is $\le0.99595002$. So under (H), $r_1\le0.99596$ on the cube of $2\mathsf L^{m+K}$ sites a side at $\beta=\mathsf L^K\mathsf b$, for every $K>d$.

\emph{Step 4: the range of (H); the numbers $t_\circ$ and $m_t$; (a).} Let $\mathsf C_+=\max\{0,\mathsf C^\Sigma_{\rm maj}+2+c_{\rm low}\}$, and let $y_\circ\ge2$ be the least real number such that for all $y\ge y_\circ$
\[
\begin{multlined}
28\mathsf L^{11/2}M^2A_0\,y^{2r}(y+\log\mathsf L)^{\mathfrak p_0}e^{-y/2}\le\log\tfrac{21}{20},\qquad\log\bigl(16\mathsf L^9y^{3r}\bigr)+\bigl(\mathsf C_++\tfrac92y\bigr)(2\mathsf L^2M)^3y^{3r} \\
-c'A_0^2y^{2\mathfrak p_0}\le-\log40 ;
\end{multlined}
\]
it exists, as the first left member tends to $0$ and, in the second, $2\mathfrak p_0>3r+2$ at the chosen constants (the choice $\mathfrak p_0\ge6r+1$ in Prop.~\YMMref{69.1}{595}) and $c'A_0^2>0$. Put $t_\circ=\min\{2\mathsf L\gamma^2,\ 2\mathsf L^2/\mathsf t_\natural,\ 2\mathsf Le^{-y_\circ}\}$. For $0<t\le t_\circ$ let $m_t$ be the least integer $m\ge1$ with $M\,R(2\mathsf L^m/t)\le\mathsf L^m$, which exists as $R(x)\le\max\{1,\mathsf L(\log x)^r\}$; let $\ell_t=2\mathsf L^{m_t}$, $\mathsf b_t=\ell_t/t$ and $y=\log\mathsf b_t$. Then (E) holds for the label $\mathsf b_t$ and the integer $m_t$, as $\mathsf b_t\ge2\mathsf L/t_\circ\ge\gamma^{-2}$; $y\ge\log(2\mathsf L/t_\circ)\ge y_\circ$; and $\ell_t\le2\mathsf L^2My^r$, as $m_t=1$ or $\mathsf L^{m_t-1}<M\,R(\mathsf b_t/\mathsf L)\le M\mathsf Ly^r$.

At $d=1$: $x_1=\mathsf L\mathsf b_t\ge2\mathsf L^2/t_\circ\ge\mathsf t_\natural$; $\mathsf n=\mathsf L\ell_t\le2\mathsf L^3My^r$ and $x_1=\mathsf Le^y$ give $7\mathsf n^2\varepsilon\le\log\frac{21}{20}$ by the first inequality, that is $\delta\le\frac1{20}$; and $\log x_1\ge y$, $2M^{-3}\ell_t^3\mathsf L^3\le16\mathsf L^9y^{3r}$ and $\ell_t^3\le(2\mathsf L^2M)^3y^{3r}$ give $\mathsf R_1\le\frac1{40}$ by the second. So (H) holds for $(\mathsf b_t,m_t)$ at $d=1$. At the cutoff $K\ge2$ the cube has $N=2\mathsf L^{m_t+K}$ sites a side and $\beta=\mathsf L^K\mathsf b_t=N/t$; by Step~3, $r_1\le0.99596$ on the cube of $2\mathsf L^j$ sites a side at $\beta=2\mathsf L^j/t$, for every $j\ge m_t+2$. Then $1-r_1\ge0.00404\ge0.0039$, and Prop.~\ref{prop:says}(b), (c) give $\mathsf e(\mathsf L^j)\ge\mathsf f(0.0039)\ge0.16567$ and $\mathsf e(l)>0.069$ for $3\le l\le\mathsf L^j/8$: (a).

(b) The cube of the criterion at the cutoff $K$ has $2l_*\mathsf L^K=2\mathsf L^{m_0+K}$ sites a side and $\beta=\mathsf L^K\mathsf b=2\mathsf L^{m_0+K}/t$ with $t=\ell_0/\mathsf b\le t_\circ$; apply (a) with $j=m_0+K$, for all $K\ge m_t+2-m_0$. (c) Let $\bar y=\frac43[\log(2\mathsf L^2M)+r\log(4r)+\log(\mathsf L/t_\circ)]$ and $\beta_\flat=2\mathsf L^5M\bar y^r/t_\circ$. For $\beta\ge\beta_\flat$ choose $j$ with $2\mathsf L^j\le t_\circ\beta<2\mathsf L^{j+1}$ and put $t=2\mathsf L^j/\beta\in(t_\circ/\mathsf L,t_\circ]$. With the numbers of Step~4 at this $t$, $y\le\log\ell_t+\log(\mathsf L/t_\circ)$ and $\ell_t\le2\mathsf L^2My^r$; with $r\log y\le\frac y4+r\log(4r)-r$ this gives $y\le\bar y$, so $2\mathsf L^{m_t+2}=\mathsf L^2\ell_t\le2\mathsf L^4M\bar y^r=\frac{t_\circ}{\mathsf L}\beta_\flat\le\frac{t_\circ}{\mathsf L}\beta<t\beta=2\mathsf L^j$, that is $j\ge m_t+2$; and (a) gives $\mathsf e(l)>0.069$ for $3\le l\le\mathsf L^j/8$, while $\mathsf L^j/8>t_\circ\beta/16\mathsf L$. For the uniform criterion at a label $\mathsf b$ take $K\ge K_0$ with $L^K\mathsf b\ge\beta_\flat$: the criterion at $l=l_*L^K$ forces $l_*L^K>\frac{t_\circ}{16\mathsf L}L^K\mathsf b$.

(d) Put $\mathsf G_N=\log(Z(N,N,N)/\lambda_0(N,N)^N)=\log(1+\mathsf r_N(N,N))$. By Prop.~\ref{prop:says}(a), and as $\mathsf r_t$ decreases in $t$, $\mathsf e(N/2)\ge\log(1+\mathsf r_{N/2}(N,N))\ge\mathsf G_N$; and for every integer $q\ge2$, $Z(N,N,qN)\ge\lambda_0(N,N)^{qN}$ gives $\mathsf G_N\ge\mathsf d_q(N)/q$, $\mathsf d_q(N)=qF(N,N,N)-F(N,N,qN)$. Three facts bound $e^{-\mathsf d_q(N)}=Z(N,N,qN)/Z(N,N,N)^q$ from above: a swap on the long box, which bounds it through the largest probability on the cube $(N,N,N)$ that the five invariants of the pair of the winding holonomies at one site lie in one small cell; a bound of that probability on a bare cube (Lem.~\ref{lem:anti}); and a comparison of the laws of the block fields at two consecutive cutoffs in which the errors that bound quotients of densities enter as factors (Lem.~\ref{lem:cut}), which carries the bound from one low cutoff $K_1$ to all higher ones. Besides Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8} and the statements among the construction results named for this clause, (d) rests on Lem.~\ref{lem:toron-weaker-floor} and these two lemmas, which give the estimate \eqref{eq:wind} and, with the chain from a low cutoff, the estimate \eqref{eq:lowcut}, and are stated below with their proofs.

\emph{A swap on the long box.} For $g\in G$ write $g=\cos\alpha(g)\,\mathbf 1+i\sum_j\mathsf v_j(g)\tau_j$, $\tau_1,\tau_2,\tau_3$ the Pauli matrices, with the class angle $\alpha(g)=\arccos\frac12\operatorname{tr}g\in[0,\pi]$ and the vector part $\mathsf v(g)\in\mathbb R^3$, $|\mathsf v(g)|=\sin\alpha(g)$. To a pair $(g_1,g_2)$ of elements of $G$ attach the real $3\times2$ matrix $\mathsf v$ with the columns $\mathsf v(g_1)$, $\mathsf v(g_2)$, the matrix $\mathsf s=(\mathsf v^{\rm t}\mathsf v)^{1/2}$, and the five invariants $\mathsf a(g_1,g_2)=(\alpha(g_1),\alpha(g_2),\mathsf s_{11},\mathsf s_{12},\mathsf s_{22})\in\mathbb R^5$: they do not change under a simultaneous conjugation of the pair, and if $|g_i-hg'_ih^{-1}|\le\delta\le1$ for $i=1,2$ and one $h\in G$, then $|\mathsf a(g_1,g_2)-\mathsf a(g'_1,g'_2)|_\infty\le2\delta$, as $|\mathsf v(g)-\mathsf v(g')|\le|g-g'|$, $|g-g'|\ge2\sin\frac12|\alpha(g)-\alpha(g')|$, and $\mathsf v\mapsto(\mathsf v^{\rm t}\mathsf v)^{1/2}$ has the Lipschitz constant $\sqrt2$ for the Hilbert--Schmidt norm.

Let $V$ be either the bare field, with $\mathsf n=N$, or the block field of the depth $0$, on a lattice of $\mathsf n=\ell$ sites a side in the section, formed on the long box by the same local formulas; let $\omega\in(0,1]$ with $\delta_q=(1+\omega)^{q\mathsf n^2}-1\le1$. To a site $\xi$ attach $\mathsf a(V,\xi)=\mathsf a(P_1(\xi),P_2(\xi))$, the five invariants of the pair of its winding holonomies in the directions $1$ and $2$. Cut $\mathbb R^5$ into half-open cubes $c_k$ of a side $w\ge2\delta_q$, and let $c^+_k$ be the half-open cube of side $3w$ with the same centre and the same choice of included faces, so that every point lies in exactly $3^5$ of them. On the event that every plaquette of $V$ on the box $(N,N,qN)$ is within $\omega$ of $\mathbf 1$, let $\xi'=\xi+ke_3$, $0\le k<q\mathsf n$, and $\mathsf t$ the transport of $V$ from $\xi$ to $\xi'$ along the line of the direction $3$: for $\mu=1,2$ the transports $\mathsf tP_\mu(\xi')$ and $P_\mu(\xi)\mathsf t$ run along the step sequences $(e_3^k,e_\mu^{\mathsf n})$ and $(e_\mu^{\mathsf n},e_3^k)$, which pass into one another by $k\mathsf n\le q\mathsf n^2$ exchanges of adjacent entries, and each exchange multiplies the transport by a conjugate of $\partial V(p)^{\pm1}$ for one plaquette $p$, as in the proof of Lem.~\YMMref{4.1}{17}; so $|\mathsf tP_\mu(\xi')\mathsf t^{-1}-P_\mu(\xi)|\le\delta_q$, with one $\mathsf t$ for both $\mu$, and $\mathsf a(V,\cdot)$ stays within $2\delta_q$ of $\mathsf a(V,\xi)$ at all the sites of that line.

Cut the box by walls into $q$ slabs of $N$ layers, with the mirrors $\theta_i$ in their middle planes and sites $\xi^-_i$ of one line of the direction $3$ just below these planes; then the indicator of the event is at most $\sum_k\prod_ig^k_i\,(g^k_i\circ\theta_i)$, $g^k_i=\mathbf 1\{\mathsf a(V,\xi^-_i)\in c^+_k\}$, a function of the bonds of the lower half of the slab $i$ (for the block field, whose walls of the blocks contain these planes, as $N=\mathsf n\mathsf L^K$ with $\mathsf n$ even, by the locality of the averaging map and its covariance under the lattice isometries, Prop.~\YMMref{4.5}{20}, {\cite[Lem.~G.1]{YMM2}}). The slab operator of $g^k_i\,(g^k_i\circ\theta_i)$ is $\mathsf Y^*\mathsf Y\ge0$, $\mathsf Y$ that of the lower half with $g^k_i$, as in the proof of Lem.~\ref{lem:mir}; and $|\operatorname{Tr}(\mathsf O_1\cdots\mathsf O_q)|\le\prod_i\operatorname{Tr}\mathsf O_i$ for positive operators of trace class.

So every slab closes into a cube: $Z(N,N,qN)\langle\prod_ig^k_i\,(g^k_i\circ\theta_i)\rangle\le\prod_iZ(N,N,N)\langle g^k_i\rangle_{(N,N,N)}$. The plaquettes off the event are bounded by Schwarz's inequality at a mirror (Lem.~\ref{lem:mir}(a)) and the same closing. With $P_\ast$ the largest probability on the cube $(N,N,N)$ that $\mathsf a(V,\xi)$ lies in one $c^+_k$, and $\rho$ the largest probability on it that one plaquette of $V$ is not within $\omega$ of $\mathbf 1$, this gives $x\le243\,P_\ast^{q-1}+3q\mathsf n^3(\rho x)^{1/2}$ for $x=e^{-\mathsf d_q(N)}$, whence
\[
e^{-\mathsf d_q(N)}\le486\,P_\ast^{q-1}+9q^2\mathsf n^6\rho .
\]

\emph{Anticoncentration on a bare cube.} For an integer $N'\ge4$ and a coupling $\beta'>0$ let $\mu_{N',\beta'}$ be the law $Z^{-1}e^{-\beta'\sum_pa_p}dU$ of the periodic cube of $N'$ sites a side, $Z=Z(N',N',N')$, and $|\partial U-\mathbf 1|_\infty$ the largest $|\partial U(p)-\mathbf 1|$ over its plaquettes.

\begin{lemma}[Anticoncentration on a bare cube]\label{lem:anti}
Let $N'\ge4$ be an integer, $\beta'\ge C_{\rm T}N'^{68}$ and $0<\omega\le1.6\cdot10^{-7}N'^{-13}$, with $C_{\rm T}$ of Lem.~\ref{lem:toron-weaker-floor}, enlarged to be at least $1.1\cdot10^9$. For every site $\xi$, every $w'$ with $(N'^5/2\beta')^{1/2}\le w'\le\frac1{20}$ and every closed cube $\mathsf Q$ of the half side $w'$ in $\mathbb R^5$,
\[
\mu_{N',\beta'}\bigl(\mathsf a(U,\xi)\in\mathsf Q,\ \max_p|\partial U(p)-\mathbf 1|<\omega\bigr)\le C_{\rm a}\,N'^{29.5}\,\beta'^{1/2}\,w'^3 .\qedhere
\]
\end{lemma}

Here $C_{\rm a}$ is an absolute constant. Thus the bound
$C_{\rm a}N'^{c_{\rm a}}\beta'^{1/2}w'^3$ of
\eqref{eq:wind} holds with $c_{\rm a}=29.5$,
$c'_{\rm a}=C_{\rm T}$ and $c''_{\rm a}=68$.

\emph{Sketch of the proof of Lem.~\ref{lem:anti}.} Write $\mathsf V=N'^3$, take $\xi=0$, let $|\cdot|_2$ be the Euclidean norm of a family indexed by bonds or by plaquettes, and $Z[F]=\int F\,e^{-\beta'\sum_pa_p}\,\mathrm{d}U$. (i) \emph{The gauge of a maximal tree.} Let $T$ be the tree of the bonds $\langle x,x+e_3\rangle$ with $x_3\le N'-2$, $\langle x,x+e_2\rangle$ with $x_3=0$, $x_2\le N'-2$, and $\langle x,x+e_1\rangle$ with $x_2=x_3=0$, $x_1\le N'-2$. A bounded Borel function that the gauge transformations do not change has the same integral against $dU$ as against the Haar measures of the bonds off $T$ at $U=\mathbf 1$ on $T$; there the winding holonomies at $0$ are the values $P_\mu$ of $U$ at the three bonds $b^*_\mu$ from $(N'-1)e_\mu$ to $0$.

On the set $S_0$ of the other $2\mathsf V-2$ bonds write $U(b)=V^P(b)\,e^{a(b)}$, $a(b)\in\mathfrak{su}(2)$, $|a(b)|<\pi$, where $V^P(b)=P_\mu$ if $b$ is a bond of the direction $\mu$ that starts in the plane $x_\mu=N'-1$, and $V^P(b)=\mathbf 1$ else; in $a(b)$ the Haar measure has a density at most $(2\pi^2)^{-1}$. (ii) \emph{Small fields.} Along the tree every bond $b\in S_0$ is rebuilt from at most $2N'^2$ plaquettes, none of them a corner plaquette $p_{\mu\nu}(x)$ with $x_\mu=x_\nu=N'-1$: $|U(b)-V^P(b)|\le2N'^2|\partial U-\mathbf 1|_\infty$. The same rebuilding, linearised, gives $|a|_2\le2N'^{5/2}|d_Pa|_2$ for every triple $P$ and every family $a$ on $S_0$, $d_P$ being the linearisation at $V^P$ of $a\mapsto(\partial U(p))_p$, a covariant lattice curl.

So on $\{|\partial U-\mathbf 1|_\infty<\omega\}$ every $|a(b)|\le\pi N'^2\omega$, and at the corner plaquettes, where $\partial U(p)$ is the commutator $C_{\mu\nu}=P_\mu P_\nu P_\mu^{-1}P_\nu^{-1}$ up to four factors $e^{\pm a(b)}$, $|C_{\mu\nu}-\mathbf 1|\le9N'^2\omega$. Stokes' formula over the $N'^2$ plaquettes $p_{\mu\nu}(x)$ with $x_\rho=0$, $\rho$ the third direction, gives $2|\mathsf v(P_\mu)\times\mathsf v(P_\nu)|=|C_{\mu\nu}-\mathbf 1|\le\sum_p|\partial U(p)-\mathbf 1|$, and Schwarz's inequality then $\sum_pa_p\ge2N'^{-2}\sum_{\mu<\nu}|\mathsf v(P_\mu)\times\mathsf v(P_\nu)|^2$. (iii) \emph{The ceiling at a fixed triple.} Let $\kappa$ be the family of the logarithms of the $C_{\mu\nu}$, placed at the corner plaquettes of the planes $\mu\nu$.

With $|e^{X_1}\cdots e^{X_k}-e^{X_1+\dots+X_k}|\le\frac12(\sum_i|X_i|)^2$ for $X_i\in\mathfrak{su}(2)$, (ii) gives on $\{|\partial U-\mathbf 1|_\infty<\omega\}$ that $2\sum_pa_p\ge(1-\eta_1)^2|d_Pa+\kappa|_2^2$, $\eta_1=39\pi N'^{9/2}\omega\le2\cdot10^{-5}N'^{-8.5}$; keeping the fraction $N'^{-3}$ of the action for the holonomies,
\[
\sum_pa_p\ge\tfrac12(1-N'^{-3})(1-\eta_1)^2|d_Pa+\kappa|_2^2+\frac2{N'^5}\sum_{\mu<\nu}|\mathsf v(P_\mu)\times\mathsf v(P_\nu)|^2 .
\]
At a fixed triple the Gaussian integral over the $6\mathsf V-6$ real coordinates of $a$ is at most $(2\pi/\beta'')^{3\mathsf V-3}D(P)^{-1/2}$, with $\beta''=\beta'(1-N'^{-3})(1-\eta_1)^2$ and $D(P)$ the determinant of $d_P^*d_P$ on the families on $S_0$, the shift by $\kappa$ only lowering it; and $(\beta'/\beta'')^{3\mathsf V-3}\le(1-N'^{-3})^{-3N'^3}(1-\eta_1)^{-6N'^3}\le e^{3.2}$. (iv) \emph{Determinants.} A triple whose three commutators lie within $\epsilon$ of $\mathbf 1$ lies within $(2\epsilon)^{1/2}$ of a triple $P'$ with one axis, $P'_\mu=\cos\alpha_\mu\,\mathbf 1+i\sin\alpha_\mu\sum_j\hat n_j\tau_j$, and $D(P)\ge(1-48N'^{5/2}\delta)^{12\mathsf V}D(P')$ for $\max_\mu|P_\mu-P'_\mu|\le\delta$; at $\epsilon=9N'^2\omega$, $\omega\le1.6\cdot10^{-7}N'^{-13}$, this gives $D(P)^{-1/2}\le e^{0.5}D(P')^{-1/2}$.

At $P'$ the families split into the colour along $\hat n$, on which $d_{P'}$ is the lattice curl, and the complex colour across $\hat n$, on which it is the curl twisted by the phases $e^{-2i\alpha_\mu}$ at the bonds where $V^{P'}=P'_\mu$: $D(P')=D(0)\,D(2\alpha)^2$, where $D(\theta)$, for $\theta\in\mathbb R^3$, is the determinant of the curl twisted by the phases $e^{i\theta_\mu}$ on the families on $S_0$, an even function, $2\pi$-periodic in each $\theta_\mu$. For every momentum $k\in(\frac{2\pi}{N'}\mathbb Z/2\pi\mathbb Z)^3$ the twisted curl has the eigenvalue $\sum_\mu(2-2\cos(k_\mu+\theta_\mu/N'))$ twice, besides the gradients; let $\mathfrak d(\theta)$ be the product of these numbers over all $k$, and $\mathfrak d'$ their product over $k\ne0$ at $\theta=0$.

Then $D(0)=\mathfrak d'$, the change of coordinates along the tree being unimodular, and $D(\theta)\ge\mathfrak d'/(1.5\cdot10^{10}N'^{24})$ for every $\theta$: by $2\pi$-periodicity first take $\theta\in[-\pi,\pi]^3$; for $|\theta|_\infty\le\frac1{64}N'^{-11/2}$ by a comparison of the forms that uses the bound $|a|_2\le2N'^{5/2}|d_Pa|_2$ of (ii), and else by Cauchy's interlacing from the determinant $|1-e^{i\theta_\mu}|^2\mathfrak d(\theta)$ on the families that vanish on $T$ and at $b^*_\mu$ alone, $|\theta_\mu|=|\theta|_\infty$, together with $\mathfrak d(\theta)\ge4\sin^2\frac{\theta_\mu}2\,N'^{-2}\mathfrak d'$, which the product formula $\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}(2\cosh m-2\cos\frac{2\pi j+\vartheta}n)=2\cosh nm-2\cos\vartheta$ gives. This covers the triples near $P_\mu=\pm\mathbf 1$ as well.

Together, for every Borel set $\mathcal P$ of triples that the simultaneous conjugations carry onto itself,
\[
\begin{multlined}
Z\bigl[\mathbf 1_{\mathcal P}(P)\,\mathbf 1\{|\partial U-\mathbf 1|_\infty<\omega\}\bigr]\le10^{12}N'^{24}\,\mathsf X_0\int_{\mathcal P}\exp\Bigl[-\frac{2\beta'}{N'^5}\sum_{\mu<\nu}|\mathsf v(P_\mu)\times\mathsf v(P_\nu)|^2\Bigr]dP,\qquad\mathsf X_0 \\
=(2\pi^2)^{-(2\mathsf V-2)}\Bigl(\frac{2\pi}{\beta'}\Bigr)^{3\mathsf V-3}\mathfrak d'^{-3/2},
\end{multlined}
\]
$dP$ is Haar measure on $G^3$. (v) \emph{The normalizing lower bound.}
Lem.~\ref{lem:toron-weaker-floor} gives
$Z\ge c_{\rm T}N'^2\mathsf X_0/\beta'^2$
throughout the stated range, by the quantitative periodic
Laplace estimate.

(vi) \emph{The toron integral.} Let $B=2\beta'/N'^5$, so that $B^{-1/2}\le w'\le\frac1{20}$. The triples with $\mathsf a(P_1,P_2)\in\mathsf Q$ carry at most $261\,w'^3B^{-3/2}$ of the integral of $\exp[-B\sum_{\mu<\nu}|\mathsf v(P_\mu)\times\mathsf v(P_\nu)|^2]$. Integrate $P_3$ first: with the singular values $s_1\ge s_2$ of the matrix $\mathsf v$ of the pair $(P_1,P_2)$, in the eigenframe of $\mathsf v\mathsf v^{\rm t}$, $\sum_{i=1,2}|\mathsf v(P_i)\times\mathsf v(P_3)|^2\ge s_2^2x_1^2+s_1^2(x_2^2+x_3^2)$, $x=\mathsf v(P_3)$, so that this integral is at most $\min\{1,(Bs_1^2)^{-1}\}\min\{1,3.81(Bs_2^2)^{-1/2}\}$; and $|\mathsf v(P_1)\times\mathsf v(P_2)|=s_1s_2$.

If $|\mathsf v(P_i)|<0.9$ for $i=1,2$ on the whole set, the Haar measure of the pair has in the coordinates $\mathsf s$ a density at most $\frac2{0.19\pi^2}\,4s_1s_2(s_1+s_2)$, the product of $4s_1s_2(s_1+s_2)$ with the bound of the $P_3$-integral is at most $30.5\,B^{-3/2}$, and the projection of $\mathsf Q$ onto the three coordinates $(\mathsf s_{11},\mathsf s_{12},\mathsf s_{22})$ has volume $8w'^3$. Else $\sin\alpha(P_i)\ge0.8$ on the set for one $i$, and the two angles alone give $12.6\,w'^2B^{-2}\le12.6\,w'^3B^{-3/2}$: in general the triples whose two angles lie in a set $\mathcal A$ carry at most $2.52\,B^{-2}\int_{\mathcal A}\min\{B^{1/2}\mathsf m,\mathsf m^{-1}\}\,\mathrm{d}\alpha_1d\alpha_2$, $\mathsf m=\max_i\sin\alpha(P_i)$. (vii) By (iv) and Lem.~\ref{lem:toron-weaker-floor},
\[
 \mu_{N',\beta'}(P\in\mathcal P,\ |\partial U-\mathbf1|_\infty<\omega)
 \le \frac{10^{12}}{c_{\rm T}}N'^{22}\beta'^2
       \int_{\mathcal P}
       e^{-B\sum_{\mu<\nu}|\mathsf v(P_\mu)\times
                                  \mathsf v(P_\nu)|^2}\,\mathrm{d}P.
\]
Using (vi) proves the lemma with any absolute
$C_{\rm a}\ge261\cdot10^{12}/(2^{3/2}c_{\rm T})$,
enlarged to be at least $1$.

\emph{From one cutoff to the next.} In the setting (E) of \S\ref{sec:cutoff-calibration}, with the side $\ell=2\mathsf L^m$ and the label $\mathsf b$, take at every integer $K\ge2$ the numbers of \S\ref{sec:cutoff-calibration} at $n=1$: the depths $u=\lceil K/1260\rceil$ and $s=\lceil K/9\rceil$, $t_1=K-u$, and, with $N_{[d]}=\ell^3\mathsf L^{3d}$ and $\mathsf y_{[d]}=(\log(\mathsf L^d\mathsf b))^{2\mathfrak p_0}$, the four errors
\[
\begin{gathered}
\epsilon_{\rm fg}=C_{\rm old}C_{\rm fg}\tfrac{\mathsf L}{\mathsf L-1}E_0\,N_{[u]}\mathsf L^{-(s-u)},\qquad\\
\epsilon_{\rm cl}=4\mathsf K_{\rm w}c_\rho^2A_0^2\bigl(1+\tfrac{2\varrho}{\mathsf b}\bigr)\mathsf y_{[K]}N_{[s]}K^{1/2}\mathsf L^{-(K-s)/2},\\
\epsilon_{\rm sh}=3(s-u)N_{[s]}\exp\bigl[C_{\rm sh}-\tfrac14\kappa_{\rm b}A_1^2\mathsf y_{[u]}\bigr],\qquad\\
\mathsf R_{t_1}=2M^{-3}N_{[u]}\exp\bigl[-c'A_0^2\mathsf y_{[u]}+\bigl(\mathsf C^\Sigma_{\rm maj}+2+c_{\rm low}+\tfrac92\log\mathsf b\bigr)\ell^3\bigr],
\end{gathered}
\]
with the constants named there. The first two fall like powers of $\mathsf L^{-K}$, up to factors that are powers of $K$, $\ell$ and $\log\mathsf b$; the last two are exponentially small in $(\log(\mathsf L^u\mathsf b))^{2\mathfrak p_0}$. Cor.~\textup{\ref{IV-62-66}}(a) bounds the difference of the means of a gauge-invariant function at two consecutive cutoffs by $\mathfrak o_K=8\mathsf R_{t_1}+12\epsilon_{\rm fg}+8\epsilon_{\rm cl}+12\epsilon_{\rm sh}$ times its supremum; here its comparison is run with the errors that bound quotients of densities kept as factors, so that an event of a probability of the order of $t$ keeps this order.

\begin{lemma}[One step between consecutive cutoffs]\label{lem:cut}
In the setting (E), let $K\ge2$ be an integer at which the conditions (k0)--(k4) and (k6) of \S\ref{sec:cutoff-calibration} hold at $n=1$, and put
\[
\epsilon^\times_K=4\epsilon_{\rm fg}+2\epsilon_{\rm cl}+1.06\,\epsilon_{\rm sh}+1.39\,\mathsf R_{t_1},\qquad\epsilon^+_K=\mathsf R_{t_1}+1.29\,\epsilon_{\rm sh}.
\]
Then for every integer $0\le d\le u$ and every Borel set $E$ of block fields of the depth $d$ that the gauge transformations carry onto itself (Def.~\textup{\ref{IV-62-62}}(3)),
\[
\mu^{K+1}_d(E)\le e^{\epsilon^\times_K}\mu^K_d(E)+\epsilon^+_K,\qquad\mu^K_d(E)\le e^{\epsilon^\times_K}\mu^{K+1}_d(E)+\epsilon^+_K .
\]
\end{lemma}

\emph{Sketch of the proof of Lem.~\ref{lem:cut}.} It suffices to take $d=u$: for $d<u$ replace $E$ by its preimage under the averaging maps from the depth $u$ to the depth $d$, which are the same on the two lattices (Section~\YMMref{116}{807}) and keep it Borel and gauge invariant (Prop.~\YMMref{4.5}{20}, \YMMref{4.5}{20}). Take the lattices $\mathrm A=(\ell,K)$ and $\mathrm B=(\ell,K+1)$ with the top levels $t_1$ and $t_1+1$, the objects of Section~\YMMref{116}{807} with $n=1$ and $f_1=1$, at the source $0$, and $\mathsf R=\mathsf R_{t_1}$, which is the same number on both (\S\ref{sec:cutoff-calibration}). For a bounded Borel function $F\ge0$ of the block fields of the depth $u$ that the gauge transformations do not change, and for each lattice $\bullet$, of the cutoff $K^\bullet$ and the top level $t^\bullet$, let $\langle F\rangle^\bullet_0$ be the mean of $F(\mathcal M^{K^\bullet-u}U)$ at the cutoff $K^\bullet$, $\langle F\rangle^\bullet_1$ the normalised integral of $F$ against the measure of the chain on the inner ball $\mathsf{In}_{[u]}$, and $\langle F\rangle^\bullet_2$ that against the classical start on it. (1) \emph{The discarded mass, a remainder.} The measure of the chain is the image of $\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}_{t^\bullet}\rho_0\,\mathrm{d}U$ under the averaging, with $\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}_{t^\bullet}\ge0$ (Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{115.2}{806}}, image identity); the right inequality of Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{115.2}{806}}, domination bound, for $F$ and for $\sup F-F$ composed with the averaging, which are gauge invariant (Prop.~\YMMref{4.5}{20}), and Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{115.2}{806}}, lost-mass bound, by which the discarded mass is at most $\mathsf R$ times the partition function, give $\langle F\rangle^\bullet_0\le\langle F\rangle^\bullet_1+\mathsf R\sup F$ and $\langle F\rangle^\bullet_1\le(1-\mathsf R)^{-1}\langle F\rangle^\bullet_0$. (2) \emph{Forgetting, a factor.} On $\mathsf{In}_{[u]}$ the two measures have the densities $e^{c^\bullet(0)}e^{\Phi^{\bullet,0}}$ and $e^{\hat c^\bullet(0)}e^{\hat\Phi^{\bullet,0}}$ (the proof of Prop.~\YMMref{116.1}{808}), both positive almost everywhere, as both measures are positive (Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{115.2}{806}}, image identity, Prop.~\YMMref{116.1}{808}); and the real parts of the two exponents differ by at most $\epsilon_{\rm fg}$ at every point of $\mathsf{In}_{[u]}$ (equation~\YMMref{(2180)}{803}).

So the quotient of the densities lies in $\varkappa^\bullet[e^{-\epsilon_{\rm fg}},e^{\epsilon_{\rm fg}}]$ with one number $\varkappa^\bullet>0$, which cancels between the numerator and the normaliser: $e^{-2\epsilon_{\rm fg}}\langle F\rangle^\bullet_2\le\langle F\rangle^\bullet_1\le e^{2\epsilon_{\rm fg}}\langle F\rangle^\bullet_2$. (3) \emph{The two classical starts, a factor and a remainder.} Both are integrals of $F(\mathcal M^{s-u}W)$ over the block fields $W$ of the depth $s$ against $\mathsf k^\bullet(W)\hat F^\bullet_0(W)\,\mathrm{d}W$, $\mathsf k^\bullet\ge0$ (\S\ref{sec:block-field-laws}); where $\mathsf k^{\rm A}$ and $\mathsf k^{\rm B}$ are both positive they are equal and $\hat F^{\rm B}_0=\hat F^{\rm A}_0e^{\mathsf q_0}$, $|\mathsf q_0|\le\epsilon_{\rm cl}$ (Prop.~\textup{\YMMref{116.1}{808}}, density comparison in the proof); and for $(\bullet,\circ)=(\mathrm A,\mathrm B)$ and $(\mathrm B,\mathrm A)$ the fields at which $\mathsf k^\circ$ vanishes carry at most the fraction $\epsilon_{\rm sh}$ of the mass of the start of $\bullet$ (\S\ref{sec:block-field-laws}).

So $\langle F\rangle^\bullet_2\le e^{2\epsilon_{\rm cl}}(1-\epsilon_{\rm sh})^{-1}\langle F\rangle^\circ_2+\epsilon_{\rm sh}\sup F$. Chaining (1), (2), (3), (2), (1),
\[
\langle F\rangle^\bullet_0\le\frac{e^{4\epsilon_{\rm fg}+2\epsilon_{\rm cl}}}{(1-\epsilon_{\rm sh})(1-\mathsf R)}\langle F\rangle^\circ_0+\bigl(\mathsf R+e^{2\epsilon_{\rm fg}}\epsilon_{\rm sh}\bigr)\sup F,
\]
and (k2), (k3), (k6) give $e^{2\epsilon_{\rm fg}}\le e^{1/4}<1.29$, $-\log(1-\epsilon_{\rm sh})\le1.06\,\epsilon_{\rm sh}$ and $-\log(1-\mathsf R)\le2\log2\cdot\mathsf R\le1.39\,\mathsf R$. At $F=\mathbf 1_E$ this is the lemma.

\emph{The chain from a low cutoff.} Let $p=2\mathfrak p_0$, $y=\log\mathsf b$, $\bar\ell(y)=2\mathsf L^2My^r$, $\mathsf k(y)=\bar\ell(y)^3y^{p+1}$, $\mathsf N(y)=\mathsf L\,\bar\ell(y)^{31}y^{10(p+1)}$, and let $K_1=K_1(y)$ be the least integer $K\ge10$ with $\mathsf L^{K/10}\ge\mathsf k(y)$. With the constants of \S\ref{sec:cutoff-calibration} and the number $\mathsf C_+$ of Step~4 put
\[
\begin{gathered}
a_1=C_{\rm old}C_{\rm fg}\tfrac{\mathsf L}{\mathsf L-1}E_0\mathsf L^4,\qquad\\
 a_2=4\mathsf K_{\rm w}c_\rho^2A_0^2(1+2\varrho)\mathsf L^{7/2},\qquad\\
 a_3=\sum_{K\ge1}(1+K\log\mathsf L)^pK^{1/2}\mathsf L^{-K/90},\\
a_4=529200\,e^{C_{\rm sh}}\sum_{i\ge1}i\,\mathsf L^{420i}e^{-\frac14\kappa_{\rm b}A_1^2(i\log\mathsf L)^p},\qquad\\
 a_5=2520\,M^{-3}\sum_{i\ge1}\mathsf L^{3i}e^{-c'A_0^2(i\log\mathsf L)^p},\qquad\\
 a_6=\frac{256\,\mathsf K_uc_\rho^2A_0^2\mathsf L^4}{\gamma_{\rm r}A_1^2},\\
\mathsf R(y)=1.29\,\bar\ell(y)^3\Bigl[\\
a_4e^{-\frac14\kappa_{\rm b}A_1^2y^p}\\
+a_5e^{(\mathsf C_++\frac92y)\bar\ell(y)^3-c'A_0^2y^p}\Bigr];
\end{gathered}
\]
these are formed from the constants alone, and the three series converge, as $p\ge2$, $\kappa_{\rm b},c'>0$ (Prop.~\YMMref{114.4}{803} and \S\ref{sec:cutoff-calibration}) and $A_0,A_1>0$ (equation~\YMMref{(634)}{339}). Suppose that (E) holds, $\ell\le\bar\ell(y)$, $\mathsf b\ge\Theta_\star$, the number of the condition (k1), $y\ge\max\{8a_1,20a_2a_3,a_6\}$ and $\mathsf R(y)\le e^{-3y^2}$. Then (k0)--(k4) and (k6) hold at every integer $K\ge K_1$, and the sums $\mathsf S=\sum_{K\ge K_1}\epsilon^\times_K$ and $\mathsf R_\Sigma=\sum_{K\ge K_1}\epsilon^+_K$ satisfy
\[
\mathsf S\le\frac{17.72\,a_1+2a_2a_3}y+1.39\,\mathsf R(y),\qquad\mathsf R_\Sigma\le\mathsf R(y)\le e^{-3y^2},\qquad\ell\mathsf L^{K_1}<\mathsf N(y).
\]
Indeed, for $K\ge K_1$ one has $u<\frac K{1260}+1$ and $\frac K9\le s<\frac K9+1$, so $4u-s\le4-\frac K{10}$, $\frac{7s-K}2\le\frac72-\frac K{10}-\frac K{90}$ and $4s-K\le4-\frac K{10}$; and $\ell^3\mathsf L^{-K/10}\le\ell^3/\mathsf k(y)\le y^{-p-1}$. Hence $\epsilon_{\rm fg}\le a_1\ell^3\mathsf L^{-K/10}$, $\epsilon_{\rm cl}\le a_2y^p(1+K\log\mathsf L)^pK^{1/2}\mathsf L^{-K/90}\ell^3\mathsf L^{-K/10}$, and the left member of (k4) is at most $a_6\gamma_{\rm r}A_1^2\ell^3\mathsf L^{-K/10}$. Summed over $K\ge K_1$, as $(1-13^{-1/10})^{-1}\le4.43$, these give $\sum_{K\ge K_1}(4\epsilon_{\rm fg}+2\epsilon_{\rm cl})\le(17.72\,a_1+2a_2a_3)/y$. (k0) holds as $K\ge10$, (k1) as $\mathsf b\ge\Theta_\star$, and $y\ge\max\{8a_1,20a_2a_3,a_6\}$ gives (k2), (k4) and the first half of (k3).

For the two other errors, $(y+u\log\mathsf L)^p\ge y^p+(u\log\mathsf L)^p$, $s-u\le140u$, $N_{[s]}\le\ell^3\mathsf L^{420u}$, and at most $1260$ cutoffs have the same $u$: $\sum_{K\ge K_1}\epsilon_{\rm sh}\le a_4\ell^3e^{-\frac14\kappa_{\rm b}A_1^2y^p}$ and $\sum_{K\ge K_1}\mathsf R_{t_1}\le a_5\ell^3e^{(\mathsf C_++\frac92y)\ell^3-c'A_0^2y^p}$. So $\mathsf R_\Sigma\le\mathsf R(y)$, which gives the second half of (k3) and (k6), and $\sum_{K\ge K_1}(1.06\,\epsilon_{\rm sh}+1.39\,\mathsf R_{t_1})\le1.39\,\mathsf R(y)$. Finally $\mathsf k(y)>\mathsf L$, so $K_1\ge11$ and $\mathsf L^{(K_1-1)/10}<\mathsf k(y)$: $\mathsf L^{K_1}<\mathsf L\,\mathsf k(y)^{10}$ and $\ell\mathsf L^{K_1}<\mathsf N(y)$. Lem.~\ref{lem:cut} at $d=0$ and an induction on $K$ give $\mu^K_0(E)\le e^{\mathsf S_K}(\mu^{K_1}_0(E)+\mathsf R_K)$, with $\mathsf S_K$ and $\mathsf R_K$ the sums of the $\epsilon^\times_{K'}$ and of the $\epsilon^+_{K'}$ over $K_1\le K'<K$; so \eqref{eq:lowcut} holds: for every integer $K\ge K_1$ and every Borel set $E$ of block fields of the depth $0$ that the gauge transformations carry onto itself
\[
\mu^K_0(E)\le e^{\mathsf S}\bigl(\mu^{K_1}_0(E)+\mathsf R_\Sigma\bigr).
\]

\emph{The parameters.} Let $\mathsf y_\star$ be the least real number 
\[
y_0\ge\max\{122,\log\gamma^{-2},\log\Theta_\star,8a_1,20a_2a_3,a_6,2(17.72\,a_1+2a_2a_3)\}
\]
 such that at every $y\ge y_0$
\[
\begin{gathered}
\textup{(y1)}\ \mathsf R(y)\le e^{-3y^2};\qquad\\
\textup{(y2)}\ \log\mathsf L+30\log\bar\ell(y)+10(p+1)\log y\le y;\qquad\\
\textup{(y3)}\ 26\,\mathsf N(y)^{28}\,\bar\ell(y)\,y^4e^{-y}\le2.5\cdot10^{-14};\\
\textup{(y4)}\ 26\,\mathsf N(y)^6\,\bar\ell(y)\,y^2e^{-y}\le(c^{\rm SO}_2)^2;\qquad\\
\textup{(y5)}\ 31\,(y+1)^2\,\mathsf N(y)^6\le e^{2y^2};\qquad\\
\textup{(y6)}\ C_{\rm T}\bar\ell(y)\mathsf N(y)^{67}e^{-y}\le1,
\end{gathered}
\]
$c^{\rm SO}_2$ the number of Lem.~\ref{lem:background-iterated-average}. It exists: $\bar\ell$ and $\mathsf N$ are powers of $y$, so the left member of (y2) is $O(\log y)$, those of (y3) and (y4) tend to $0$, that of (y5) is a power of $y$, that of (y6) tends to zero, and the two exponents in $\mathsf R(y)e^{3y^2}$ are $-\frac14\kappa_{\rm b}A_1^2y^p+3y^2+O(\log y)$ and 
\[
-c'A_0^2y^p+(\mathsf C_++\frac92y)\bar\ell(y)^3+3y^2+O(\log y),
\]
which tend to $-\infty$, as $p=2\mathfrak p_0>3r+2$ at the chosen constants (the choice $\mathfrak p_0\ge6r+1$ in Prop.~\YMMref{69.1}{595}) and $r\ge2$; each condition compares continuous functions, so the numbers $y_0$ at which all hold on $[y_0,\infty)$ form a closed half line. Put $t_\star=2\mathsf Le^{-\mathsf y_\star}$. Now let $j\ge1$ and $\beta>0$ with $t=2\mathsf L^j/\beta\le t_\star$, and $N=2\mathsf L^j$; let $m$ be the least integer $m\ge1$ with $M\,R(2\mathsf L^m/t)\le\mathsf L^m$, $\ell=2\mathsf L^m$, $\mathsf b=\ell/t$, $y=\log\mathsf b$ and $K=j-m\in\mathbb Z$, so that $N=\ell\mathsf L^K$ and $\beta=\mathsf L^K\mathsf b$; and $q=\lceil y\rceil$.

Then $y\ge\log(2\mathsf L/t)\ge\mathsf y_\star$; as in Step~4, (E) holds for $(\mathsf b,m)$ and $\ell\le\bar\ell(y)$; by (y2), $\log\ell\le y/30$, so that $\log\frac1t\le y\le2\log\frac1t$, and $y\le q<y+1$, $q\ge122$; $e^{-y}\le t=\ell e^{-y}\le\bar\ell(y)e^{-y}$; the chain holds from $K_1=K_1(y)$, with $e^{\mathsf S}\le e^{0.53}<1.7$ and $\mathsf R_\Sigma\le e^{-3y^2}$; and $\beta_1=\mathsf L^{K_1}\mathsf b=\ell\mathsf L^{K_1}/t$ has $\log\beta_1=y+K_1\log\mathsf L<y+\log\mathsf L+10\log\mathsf k(y)\le2y$, by (y2).

\emph{Bare cubes.} Let $(N',\beta')$ be $(\ell\mathsf L^{K_1},\beta_1)$, the bare cube at the cutoff $K_1$, or $(N,\beta)$ if $N<\ell\mathsf L^{K_1}$. Then $N'$ is of the form $2\mathsf L^{j'}$, $j'\ge1$, so even, $26\le N'<\mathsf N(y)$, $\beta'=N'/t$, and $\log\beta'\le2y$. Put $\Lambda'=3N'^3\log(8e^8\beta'^{3/2})+\log(3N'^3)+3y^2$, $\omega_0=(2\Lambda'/\beta')^{1/2}$ and $\upsilon=N'^2\omega_0$. The Haar measure of $\{g\in G:|g-\mathbf 1|\le\beta'^{-1/2}\}$ is at least $\frac18\beta'^{-3/2}$, and $\beta'\sum_pa_p\le24N'^3$ when all bonds lie in this set; so $Z(N',N',N')\ge(8e^8\beta'^{3/2})^{-3N'^3}$, every plaquette has $|\partial U(p)-\mathbf 1|\ge\omega_0$ with a probability at most $Z^{-1}e^{-\beta'\omega_0^2/2}$, and
\[
\mu_{N',\beta'}\bigl(|\partial U-\mathbf 1|_\infty\ge\omega_0\bigr)\le3N'^3\,(8e^8\beta'^{3/2})^{3N'^3}e^{-\Lambda'}=e^{-3y^2}.
\]
Further $N'^3\le\Lambda'\le13N'^3y^2$, so $\upsilon^2\le26N'^6y^2t\le26\,\mathsf N(y)^6\bar\ell(y)y^2e^{-y}$; and (y3), (y4) give $\omega_0\le1.6\cdot10^{-7}N'^{-13}$, $q\upsilon\le1.7\cdot10^{-7}$, $\beta'\ge N'e^y/\bar\ell(y)\ge C_{\rm T}N'^{68}$ by (y6) and $\upsilon\le c^{\rm SO}_2$. With $w=2.03\,q\upsilon$ and $w'=\frac32w+1.03\,\upsilon$ one has $(N'^5/2\beta')^{1/2}\le3\upsilon\le w'\le4q\upsilon\le\frac1{20}$, and Lem.~\ref{lem:anti} at $\omega=\omega_0$ gives, for every site $\xi'$ and every closed cube $\mathsf Q$ of the half side $w'$,
\[
\mu_{N',\beta'}\bigl(\mathsf a(U,\xi')\in\mathsf Q,\ |\partial U-\mathbf 1|_\infty<\omega_0\bigr)\le C_{\rm a}N'^{29.5}\beta'^{1/2}(4q\upsilon)^3\le P^{\rm b}:=C_{\rm b}\,q^3y^3\,\mathsf N(y)^{39}\,t,
\]
where $C_{\rm b}=8500C_{\rm a}$, since $(2\Lambda')^{3/2}\le132.6\,N'^{4.5}y^3$ and $N'^{40}/\beta'=N'^{39}t$.

\emph{The cutoffs $K\ge K_1$.} Take the swap with the block field $V=\mathcal M^KU$ of the depth $0$, $\mathsf n=\ell$, and $\omega=\theta_{\mathsf L}\mathsf L^{2K_1}\omega_0$, with $\omega_0$ and $\upsilon$ those of $(\ell\mathsf L^{K_1},\beta_1)$ and the number $\theta_{\mathsf L}=\exp\frac1{2(\mathsf L^2-1)}<1.003$ of Lem.~\ref{lem:background-iterated-average}: $\mathsf n^2\omega=\theta_{\mathsf L}\upsilon$, so $\delta_q\le e^{q\theta_{\mathsf L}\upsilon}-1\le1.015\,q\upsilon$, $2\delta_q\le w$ and $\omega\le1$. The sets $E_p=\{|\partial V(p)-\mathbf 1|\ge\omega\}$ and $\{\mathsf a(V,\xi')\in c^+_k\}$ are Borel sets of block fields of the depth $0$ that the gauge transformations carry onto themselves, as these conjugate $\partial V(p)$, and the two winding holonomies at $\xi'$ by one element; so the chain gives $\mu^K_0(E)\le1.7\,(\mu^{K_1}_0(E)+e^{-3y^2})$ for each of them.

At the cutoff $K_1$, where $|\partial U-\mathbf 1|_\infty<\omega_0$ on the bare cube: $\mathsf L^{2K_1}\omega_0\le\upsilon\le c^{\rm SO}_2$, so $|\partial V-\mathbf 1|_\infty<\omega$, and the winding holonomies of $V=\mathcal M^{K_1}U$ differ from the bare ones along the same lines by at most $13.3\,\ell\mathsf L^{2K_1}\omega_0=13.3\,\upsilon/\ell\le0.512\,\upsilon$ (Lem.~\ref{lem:averaged-line-holonomy}), so that $|\mathsf a(V,\xi')-\mathsf a(U,\xi')|_\infty\le1.03\,\upsilon$; and $c^+_k$ lies in a closed cube of the half side $\frac32w$. With the bounds on the bare cube $(\ell\mathsf L^{K_1},\beta_1)$ this gives, for the swap, $\rho\le3.4\,e^{-3y^2}$ and
\[
P_\ast\le1.7\bigl(P^{\rm b}+2e^{-3y^2}\bigr)\le\Pi(y)\,t,\qquad\Pi(y)=C_\Pi y^6\,\mathsf N(y)^{39},\qquad C_\Pi=2C_{\rm b}+4,
\]
as $q^3\le1.025\,y^3$ and $e^{-3y^2}\le e^{-y}\le t$; and $9q^2\mathsf n^6\rho\le30.6\,(y+1)^2\bar\ell(y)^6e^{-3y^2}\le e^{-y^2}$, by (y5).

\emph{The cutoffs $K<K_1$}, among them those with $K\le0$. Take the swap with the bare field on the cube of $N<\ell\mathsf L^{K_1}$ sites a side, $\mathsf n=N$, and $\omega=\omega_0$ of $(N,\beta)$: $\mathsf n^2\omega=\upsilon$, $2\delta_q\le w$, $\rho\le e^{-3y^2}$, $P_\ast\le P^{\rm b}+e^{-3y^2}$, and $9q^2N^6\rho\le e^{-y^2}$; the same bounds hold.

\emph{The end.} As $\Pi(y)\ge1$, $t\ge e^{-y}$ and $q-1\le y$, $(\Pi(y)t)^{q-1}\ge e^{-y^2}$; so in all cases $e^{-\mathsf d_q(N)}\le486\,P_\ast^{q-1}+9q^2\mathsf n^6\rho\le487\,(\Pi(y)t)^{q-1}$. Where $\Pi(y)t<1$, as $q\ge y\ge\log\frac1t$ and $q\ge122$,
\[
\mathsf G_N\ge\frac{\mathsf d_q(N)}q\ge\frac{q-1}q\Bigl(\log\frac1t-\log\Pi(y)\Bigr)-\frac{\log487}q\ge\log\frac1t-\log\Pi(y)-1.06,
\]
that is $\lambda_0(N,N)^N/Z(N,N,N)=e^{-\mathsf G_N}\le2.89\,\Pi(y)\,t$. As $\mathsf N(y)^{39}=\mathsf L^{39}(2\mathsf L^2M)^{1209}y^{1209r+390p+390}$ and $y\le2\log\frac1t$, this is the bound of (d), with
\[
\mathsf p_\star=1209\,r+780\,\mathfrak p_0+396,\qquad\mathsf C_\star=3C_\Pi\,\mathsf L^{39}(2\mathsf L^2M)^{1209}\,2^{\mathsf p_\star},
\]
formed from $\mathsf L$, $M$, $r$ and $\mathfrak p_0$, and with $t_\star$, formed from the constants. Where $\Pi(y)t\ge1$ the bound holds as well, as $\mathsf C_\star(\log\frac1t)^{\mathsf p_\star}\ge2.89\,\Pi(y)$ and $\lambda_0(N,N)^N\le Z(N,N,N)$.
