The mean of the two cells $d$ slabs apart is $\operatorname{Tr}(\mathsf T'^nY^*\mathsf T'^nY)/Z$; write $\mathsf T'^n=\lambda_0^n(|e_0\rangle\langle e_0|+\mathsf R_{(n)})$ with $\|\mathsf R_{(n)}\|=\varrho^n$ and $\operatorname{Tr}|\mathsf R_{(n)}|=\mathsf r_n$, and $\lambda_0^{-\vartheta}\langle e_0,Ye_0\rangle=(1+\mathsf r_N)\mu_N(\Phi_{\tau_0})-\lambda_0^{-\vartheta}\operatorname{Tr}(\mathsf R_{(N-\vartheta)}Y)$ from the mean of one cell; expanding, the term $|\langle e_0,Ye_0\rangle|^2$ gives the square, and the others are bounded by $\varrho^n$ and $\mathsf r_n$ times $\|Y\|^2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Contraction of the seminorm]\label{C-361-12}
Let $L'\ge13$ be an odd integer, $k\in\mathbb N$, $\beta>0$, on the lattice $L'^{-k}\mathbb Z^3$ with the sides $2L'^{\mathbb N}$. Let $\ell_f,\ell_c\in2L'^{\mathbb N}$ with $d=\ell_c/\ell_f\ge L'$, $\mathsf h=\ell_fL'^k/2$ the number of layers of a fine cell, and let $\mathsf e(l)\le x_0$ at $\beta$ with $24l\le\mathsf h$. Then for every real $G$ of the bonds of the cell $[-\ell_f/4,\ell_f/4]^3$,
\[
\bigl\|G-\mu_{k,\ell_c,\beta}(G)\bigr\|_{\mathrm{ch},\ell_c}\le1.343\,\theta^{(d-1)\mathsf h/8l}\,\bigl\|G-\mu_{k,\ell_f,\beta}(G)\bigr\|_{\mathrm{ch},\ell_f},
\]
where on the left $G$ is regarded as a function of the cell $[-\ell_c/4,\ell_c/4]^3$, which holds the cell $[-\ell_f/4,\ell_f/4]^3$. The constant $1.343$ depends on none of $G$, $k$, $\beta$, $d$, $L'$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let $X=G-\mu_{k,\ell_c,\beta}(G)$, $B_1=X$, $B_{2p}=B_p\cdot\Theta_iB_p$ with $\Theta_i$ the reflection in the coarse wall plane of the direction $i$, and $m_p=\mu_{k,\ell_c,\beta}(B_p)$; then $m_1=0$, and $m_8$ is the eighth power of the left member. In the direction $i$, $B_p$ is a function of one slab of $\mathsf h$ layers, and $\Theta_iB_p$ lies $n=(d-1)\mathsf h$ layers further, on the cube of $N=2d\mathsf h$ sites. Lem.~\ref{C-361-29} with $Y$ the slab operator of $B_p$, the gap of Prop.~\ref{C-361-19}(a), and $\lambda_0^{-\mathsf h}\|Y\|\le\mathsf c\,u^p$, $\mathsf c=(1+\mathsf r_N)^{1/2d}$, $u=\|X\|^{(\ell_f)}_{\mathrm{ch},\ell_c}$, the seminorm of $X$ on the torus $\ell_c$ for the fine board, of side $\ell_f/2$ (the array form of this board, applied to the pile of $2d$ copies of $B_p$, which are $2dp$ copies of $X$ in cells of the fine board, with the factor $1$ in the other cells, bounds the $\mathsf p$ of Lem.~\ref{C-361-29} by $u^{2dp}$), give
\[
0\le m_{2p}\le\bigl[(1+\mathsf r_N)\,m_p+\mathsf r_{N-\mathsf h}\,\mathsf c\,u^p\bigr]^2+(2+\mathsf r_n)\,\theta^{n/l}\,\mathsf c^2u^{2p}.
\]
With the bounds of Prop.~\ref{C-361-8} on the $\mathsf r$, three steps give $m_8\le3.68\,u^8\theta^{n/l}$. To bound $u$, put $G_0=G-\mu_{k,\ell_f,\beta}(G)$ and $Q_f=e^{\delta((2\mathsf h)^3)/8}$, $2\mathsf h=\ell_fL'^k$ being the number of sites of a side of the torus $\ell_f$. The fine-to-coarse form gives $u\le Q_f\|X\|_{\mathrm{ch},\ell_f}$; as $X=G_0-\mu_{k,\ell_c,\beta}(G_0)$ and $\|1\|_{\mathrm{ch},\ell_f}=1$, $\|X\|_{\mathrm{ch},\ell_f}\le\|G_0\|_{\mathrm{ch},\ell_f}+|\mu_{k,\ell_c,\beta}(G_0)|$; and Prop.~\ref{C-361-9}(c) at $\ell'=\ell''=\ell_f$, with $\mathfrak s=\mu_{k,\ell_c,\beta}$ and $\mu_{k,\ell_f,\beta}(G_0)=0$, gives $|\mu_{k,\ell_c,\beta}(G_0)|\le4.84\,[Q_f(Q_f-1)]^{1/2}\|G_0\|_{\mathrm{ch},\ell_f}$. By Prop.~\ref{C-361-19}(c) at $N=2\mathsf h\ge48l$, $\delta((2\mathsf h)^3)\le0.5892\,\theta^{48}\le0.0022046$, so $Q_f\le1.000276$ and $u\le Q_f(1+4.84\,[Q_f(Q_f-1)]^{1/2})\|G_0\|_{\mathrm{ch},\ell_f}\le1.0807\,\|G_0\|_{\mathrm{ch},\ell_f}$. As $m_8$ is the eighth power of the left member and $n=(d-1)\mathsf h$, the left member is at most $3.68^{1/8}\cdot1.0807\,\theta^{(d-1)\mathsf h/8l}\|G_0\|_{\mathrm{ch},\ell_f}\le1.272\,\theta^{(d-1)\mathsf h/8l}\|G_0\|_{\mathrm{ch},\ell_f}$, and $1.272\le1.343$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[A second blocking factor; dense labels]\label{C-361-28}
(a) For every integer $L\ge2$ there are an odd prime $L'\ge13$ with $L'>L$ and an admissible choice of the constants with the blocking factor $L'$; for such $L'$, $\alpha=\log L/\log L'\in(0,1)$ is irrational. (b) Let $\mathsf b>0$, $k(K)=\lfloor K\alpha\rfloor$ and $\mathsf c_K=\mathsf b\,L'^{K\alpha-k(K)}\in[\mathsf b,L'\mathsf b)$. Then $L^K\mathsf b=L'^{k(K)}\mathsf c_K$; $k$ does not decrease, $k(K+1)-k(K)\in\{0,1\}$ and $k(K)\to\infty$, so every integer $k>k(K_1)$ is $k(K)$ for some $K>K_1$; and $\{\mathsf c_K:K\ge K_1\}$ is dense in $[\mathsf b,L'\mathsf b]$ for every $K_1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(a) is (M6) with the infinitude of primes; $L^q=L'^p$ is impossible for a prime $L'\nmid L$. (b) is arithmetic; the density is that of $\{K\alpha\}$ modulo $1$ for irrational $\alpha$.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Statements uniform in the cutoff}

\begin{proposition}[Products of action densities on one torus]\label{C-361-30}
Let $\ell''\in\mathfrak L$, $J'=[\mathsf b_-,\mathsf b_+]\subset(0,\infty)$ and $\mathsf d>0$. For $k\ge2$ let $\mathsf B_k(\ell'',J',\mathsf d)$ be the bound of (M4)(i) on the $k$-th cumulants on the torus $\ell''$ at the labels of $J'$, for supports at pairwise sup distances $\ge\mathsf d$ and unit norms, and $\mathsf M_k=\sum_\pi\prod_{B\in\pi}\mathsf B_{|B|}$ over the partitions of $\{1,\dots,k\}$ into blocks of at least two members. Let $K\in\mathbb N$, $\mathsf b'\in J'$, $\beta=L^K\mathsf b'$, $\square$ a cell of a board of side $\ell''/2$ with any offset, $f_1,\dots,f_r$ real Lipschitz functions, none $0$, with supports in $\square$ at sup distance $\ge\mathsf d/2$ from its walls and pairwise $\ge\mathsf d$ apart, and $X_i=\mathcal O_K(f_i)-\mu_{K,\ell'',\beta}(\mathcal O_K(f_i))$. Then for $\emptyset\ne I\subset\{1,\dots,r\}$, $X_I=\prod_{i\in I}X_i$ is a real function of the bonds of $\square$ and
\[
\|X_I\|_{\mathrm{ch},\ell''}\le\mathsf M_{8|I|}^{1/8}\prod_{i\in I}\|f_i\|_\sharp .
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The walls of the board lie between lattice sites. Thus a plaquette whose centre lies strictly inside $\square$ has all its corners in the closed cell; the supports lie inside the cell, so $X_I$ depends only on its bonds. By the array form of (M2), $\|X_I\|^8_{\mathrm{ch},\ell''}$ is the mean on the torus $\ell''$ of the product of the eight mirror copies of $X_I$; the mirror copy of $\mathcal O_K(f)$ is $\mathcal O_K(f\circ\hat{\mathsf r})$ for the mirror map $\hat{\mathsf r}$, with the same mean. So it is a moment of $8|I|$ centred fields with pairwise disjoint supports on one torus, at distances $\ge\mathsf d$ inside one cell and across the walls, hence a sum over the partitions into blocks of at least two members of products of joint cumulants; (M4)(i) bounds each by $\mathsf B_{|B|}$ times the norms.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The vacuum constants of two tori; the cube number]\label{C-361-13}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[beginpenalty=10000]
\item[(a)] Let $\mathsf b\ge\gamma^{-2}$, $\ell\in\mathfrak L$ with $LM\,R(\mathsf b)\le\ell/2$, and $K\ge10$ with $L^{\lceil K/1260\rceil}\mathsf b\ge\Theta_\star$, a number of the constants, so that the auxiliary sequence of renormalization steps is formed. At every level of the auxiliary sequence started from zero families with zero counterterms, the local numbers on the tori $\ell$ and $L\ell$ are equal on every region that lifts to both. Consequently
\[
|L^3\mathfrak K_K(\ell,\mathsf b)-\mathfrak K_K(L\ell,\mathsf b)|\le C\,(L\ell)^3\exp\bigl[-\kappa_1\ell L^{\lceil K/1260\rceil}\bigr]
\]
with numbers $C,\kappa_1>0$ of the constants.
\item[(b)] For every $\mathsf b>0$, $\ell\in2L^{\mathbb Z}$ and $K\ge K_\star(\mathsf b,\ell)$: $|X_{K+1}(\mathsf b,\ell)-X_K(\mathsf b,\ell)|\le L^3\mathfrak o_K(\ell/L)+\mathfrak o_K(\ell)+C\ell^3e^{-\kappa_1\ell L^{\lceil K/1260\rceil-1}}$ after the dilation of (c), and $\sum_{k\ge K}|X_{k+1}-X_k|\le\eta_K(\mathsf b,\ell)$, with the $\eta_K$ of Thm.~\ref{C-361-5}(1).
\item[(c)] The dilation $(\mathsf b,\ell,K)\mapsto(L^z\mathsf b,L^z\ell,K-z)$ names the same lattices at the same couplings, so $X_K(\mathsf b,\ell)=X_{K-z}(L^z\mathsf b,L^z\ell)$, and it brings every label and side into the range of (a).
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(a) The zero initial families and zero counterterms have a common
infinite-lattice companion and satisfy the input size bound. The
induction in Thm.~\YMMref{Y}{438}, applied to the auxiliary
sequence, therefore constructs the same family on each common
lift. Its proof transports the entire local input through the
chart at every step, including its domain. The floor
$L^{\lceil K/1260\rceil}\mathsf b\ge\Theta_\star$ is the
coupling floor needed for this auxiliary run. The Gaussian
numbers also agree under these charts, by the local normalizer
construction in equations~\YMMref{(1399)--(1400)}{573}.

To estimate the contact terms, we keep the stopping depth in
their vacuum constants. Put $u=\lceil K/1260\rceil$, and mark
the cutoffs $K^{\mathrm A}=K$ and $K^{\mathrm B}=K+1$.
The zero-source chain identity proved in Step~3(iv) of
Prop.~\ref{C-365-11}, or directly
\eqref{eq:vacuum-step-normalization} summed over its steps, gives
\[
 c^\bullet_\lambda(0)=
 E^{\bullet}_{(K^\bullet-u)}[T_\lambda],\qquad
 \mathfrak K_K(\lambda,\mathsf b)
       =c^{\mathrm B}_\lambda(0)-c^{\mathrm A}_\lambda(0).
\]
Here $E^\bullet$ is built from the line
$x_j^\bullet=L^{K^\bullet-j}\mathsf b$ on $T_\lambda$.
These constants are real. The identity uses the actual chains;
it does not require the error estimate comparing their masses.
The line has zero increments and is admissible by the proof of
Lem.~\YMMref{118.1}{812}. The assumed room
$LMR(\mathsf b)\le\ell/2$ admits it on both tori. It also
implies the side floor $\ell\ge C_LM$: the retained room condition
{\cite[eq.~215]{YMM2}} gives
$C_L\le2LR(\gamma^{-2})\le2LR(\mathsf b)$.

Apply \eqref{eq:vacuum-prefix-comparison} at each cutoff, with
$n=K^\bullet-u$, to the sides $\ell$ and $L\ell$. Both lower
summation indices are $u$. The triangle inequality gives
\[
 \left|\frac{\mathfrak K_K(\ell,\mathsf b)}{\ell^3}
       -\frac{\mathfrak K_K(L\ell,\mathsf b)}{(L\ell)^3}\right|
 \le4C_{\rm tt}E_0\sum_{s\ge u}
                   L^{3s}e^{-\kappa\ell L^s/(5M)}
 \le8C_{\rm tt}E_0 L^{3u}e^{-\kappa\ell L^u/(5M)}.
\]
The last inequality is \eqref{eq:vacuum-prefix-tail}. Since
$\kappa\ell/(5M)>4$, the factor $L^{3u}$ can be absorbed in
half the exponent. For example, take
\[
 \kappa_1=\frac{\kappa}{10M},\qquad
 C=8C_{\rm tt}E_0\sup_{v\ge1}v^3e^{-2v}<\infty.
\]
Multiplication by $(L\ell)^3$ proves (a).

(b) The zero-source read-out (M4)(ii) gives
\[
 |\log Z_{K+1,\ell}-\log Z_{K,\ell}
                   -\mathfrak K_K(\ell,\mathsf b)|
       \le\mathfrak o_K(\ell,\mathsf b).
\]
Apply this on the sides $\ell/L$ and $\ell$, multiply the first
identity by $L^3$, and subtract. The contact terms cancel up to
the error in (a), giving the asserted bound for $X_{K+1}-X_K$.
The two read-out errors have the summable rate in (M4)(ii).
With $\varsigma=\sum_{j\ge0}(1+j)^{\mathsf p_0}L^{-j/10}$,
their tail is bounded by $\eta_K$ once $K$ is above the
thresholds where (M4)(ii) and (a) apply and where the exponential
term is at most
$\mathsf C_{\rm bf}\ell^3K^{\mathsf p_0}L^{-K/10}$.
After the dilation in (c), these requirements are imposed on
$K-z$ and on both sides $L^{z-1}\ell$, $L^z\ell$, at label
$L^z\mathsf b$, including their thresholds $K_{\rm bf}$.
This is the choice of $K_\star$ in
Thm.~\ref{C-361-5}(1).

(c) The dilation leaves both the bare lattice and its coupling
unchanged. This proves the identity for $X_K$ and permits the
fixed dilation used in (b).
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Two cutoffs on boxes with mixed sides]\label{C-361-14}
The following comparison remains a sketch at the full interacting Hessian estimate described with Thm.~\ref{C-366-4}. Its intended conclusion is: for every compact set $J$ of labels, every class $z\in\{0,1\}^3$, all sides $s_\mu\in L^{\mathbb Z}\cup2L^{\mathbb Z}$ such that each twisted plane has a side in $L^{\mathbb Z}$, and every $l\in2L^{\mathbb Z}$, there are $C$ and $K_*$ such that
\[
\Bigl|\log Z^z_{K+1}(\underline s;\mathsf b)-\log Z^z_K(\underline s;\mathsf b)-\frac{|\underline s|}{l^3}\bigl(\log Z_{K+1,l}-\log Z_{K,l}\bigr)\Bigr|\le C\,L^{-K/10}\qquad(\mathsf b\in J,\ K\ge K_*),
\]
where $Z^z_K(\underline s;\mathsf b)$ is the partition function of the box with $s_\mu/a_K$ sites along the side $\mu$ and the twist $z$, at $\beta=L^K\mathsf b$, and $|\underline s|=s_1s_2s_3$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The box $\underline s$ is mixed for $z$ in the sense of Lem.~\ref{C-366-7}. After a common dilation by a power of $L$, choose a periodic covering cube $\ell_C\in2L^{\mathbb Z}$ for both this box and the reference cube $l^3$. The latter is mixed for class $0$. Thm.~\ref{C-366-4}(4), under \textbf{(Hess)}, gives the two comparisons with the same extensive term $\Delta_K[\ell_C,\mathsf b]$.

Subtract $|\underline s|/l^3$ times the comparison for $l^3$ from the comparison for $(\underline s,z)$. The coefficients $|\underline s|/\ell_C^3$ of $\Delta_K$ cancel. The two errors are bounded by $C_1L^{-K/10}$ and $(|\underline s|/l^3)C_2L^{-K/10}$, uniformly on $J$, after increasing the common threshold. This proves the stated estimate.





















The errors are $\le CL^{-K/10}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[A summable bound closes the criterion]\label{C-361-26}
Let $(\mathsf e_K)_{K\ge K_*}$ be real numbers with $|\mathsf e_{K+1}-\mathsf e_K|\le\mathsf q_K$ and $Q_K=\sum_{k\ge K}\mathsf q_k<\infty$. Then (a) $\mathsf e_\infty=\lim\mathsf e_K$ exists and $|\mathsf e_K-\mathsf e_\infty|\le Q_K$; (b) if $\mathsf e_{K_1}\le x_0-Q_{K_1}$ at one $K_1\ge K_*$, then $\mathsf e_K\le x_0$ for all $K\ge K_1$; (c) if $\mathsf e_K\le x_0'<x_0$ for all large $K$, then $\mathsf e_{K_1}\le x_0-Q_{K_1}$ at every large $K_1$; (d) $\mathsf e_\infty<x_0$ if and only if $\mathsf e_{K_1}<x_0-Q_{K_1}$ at one $K_1$, and $\mathsf e_\infty>x_0$ if and only if $\mathsf e_{K_1}>x_0+Q_{K_1}$ at one $K_1$, and then $\mathsf e_K>x_0$ for all $K\ge K_1$; at $\mathsf e_\infty=x_0$ neither holds.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
$|\mathsf e_K-\mathsf e_{K'}|\le Q_K$ for $K'\ge K$, and $Q_K\to0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Small tori]\label{C-361-15}
For an integer $N\ge3$ let $\lambda_N(k,u)=\sum_\mu(2-2\cos\frac{2\pi k_\mu+u_\mu}N)$ for $k\in(\mathbb Z/N)^3$, $u\in\mathbb R^3$; $\mathrm{Det}'(N)=\prod_{k\ne0}\lambda_N(k,0)$; $\Upsilon_N(u)=N^2\prod_k\lambda_N(k,u)/\mathrm{Det}'(N)$; $\mathscr J_N=\int_{[-\pi,\pi]^3}du/\Upsilon_N(u)$; $f_\Delta=(2\pi)^{-3}\int_{[-\pi,\pi]^3}\log\sum_\mu(2-2\cos p_\mu)\,\mathrm{d}p$; and $c'_N=\log(\mathscr J_N/8\pi^2)-\frac32(\log\mathrm{Det}'(N)-f_\Delta N^3-2\log N)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] There are absolute numbers $c_3>0$ and $x_*\in(0,\frac12]$ with the following two properties. On one bare periodic cube: for every integer $N\ge3$ and every real $\beta\ge3$ with $\mathsf{er}_N=c_3(N^{66}\log\beta/\beta)^{1/8}\le x_*$,
\[
\begin{multlined}
\Bigl|\frac{\beta^{3N^3-1}Z(N^3)}{\mathcal Z(N)}-1\Bigr|\le\mathsf{er}_N,\qquad\mathcal Z(N)=\frac{(2\pi)^{3N^3-1}\,N^2\mathscr J_N}{(2\pi^2)^{2N^3}\,4\pi\,\mathrm{Det}'(N)^{3/2}},\qquad\log\mathcal Z(N) \\
=N^3z_\infty-\log N+c'_N,
\end{multlined}
\]
$Z(N^3)$ the partition function at $\beta$ and $z_\infty$ the number of (d). Consequently, for all integers $N\ge3$, $q\ge2$ and real $\beta\ge3$ with $\mathsf{er}=c_3((qN)^{66}\log\beta/\beta)^{1/8}\le x_*$:
\[
\bigl|D_q(N)-(q^3-1)\log(\beta/N)-q^3c'_N+c'_{qN}-\log q\bigr|\le2(q^3+1)\,\mathsf{er}.
\]
\item[(b)] There are numbers $t_0\in(0,\frac1{36}]$ and $C_B$ of the constants such that for every integer $i\ge1$, $N=2L^i$, and every real $\beta$ with $t=N/\beta\le t_0$: $|D_L(N)-(L^3-1)\log(1/t)-L^3c'_N+c'_{LN}-\log L|\le C_Bt^{1/1500}$.
\item[(c)] With $t_1=t_0^2$ and a number $C_C$ of the constants: $|\delta(N^3)-\log(1/t)-c'_N|\le C_Ct^{1/1500}$ for $N=2L^i$, $t=N/\beta\le t_1$. Moreover $c'_N\to c'$ and $|c'_N-c'|\le C_AN^{-2}(\log N)^{5/2}$ with an absolute $C_A$.
\item[(d)] With $z_\infty=\log\frac2\pi-\frac32f_\Delta\approx-2.96167$ there are numbers $\beta_1$, $C$ of the constants with $|P(\beta)+3\log\beta-z_\infty|\le C\beta^{-1/1500}$ for every real $\beta\ge\beta_1$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(a) \emph{The value.} As $\beta\to\infty$ the measure of the bare cube concentrates on the flat fields. Up to gauge these are the commuting triples of holonomies; at a generic triple the orbit is that of a maximal torus, parametrised by $u\in[0,2\pi]^3$, and the transverse fluctuations are Gaussian with the quadratic form of the lattice Laplacian twisted by $u$, whose lowest eigenvalue $\lambda_N(0,u)$ is of the order $|u|^2/N^2$. The volume of the orbits, the Haar measure near them and the Gaussian integral give $\beta^{3N^3-1}Z(N^3)\to\mathcal Z(N)$ and $\log\mathcal Z(N)=(3N^3-1)\log2\pi-2N^3\log2\pi^2-\log4\pi-\frac32\log\mathrm{Det}'(N)+2\log N+\log\mathscr J_N=N^3z_\infty-\log N+c'_N$, by $3\log2\pi-2\log2\pi^2=\log\frac2\pi$, $\log2\pi+\log4\pi=\log8\pi^2$ and the definition of $c'_N$.

\emph{The error, with all its powers of $N$.} (1) \emph{The cut.} In the gauge in which the bonds of a maximal tree carry $\mathbf 1$, which removes the gauge group exactly, with no gauge copies and no Jacobian, the field is bounded by its curvature: with $A=\sum_pa_p$, every other bond variable lies within $2NA^{1/2}$ of $\mathbf 1$ or, at a bond that crosses the boundary of the fundamental cube, of the holonomy $h_\mu$ of its direction, and $|h_\mu h_\nu h_\mu^{-1}h_\nu^{-1}-\mathbf 1|\le N(2A)^{1/2}$. The fields with $A\ge\alpha_\beta=4N^3\log\beta/\beta$ carry at most $\beta^{-4N^3}$, which is $(C/\beta)^{N^3}$ times $\mathcal Z(N)\beta^{1-3N^3}$: this cut is the source of $\log\beta$. (2) \emph{The generic stratum.} On $\{A<\alpha_\beta\}$ the integral is squeezed between two Gaussian integrals: in $d_\nu\le6N^3$ transverse variables $\nu$ with $\|\nu\|^2\le\Lambda_\delta A$ and $|A-Q|\le43N^2|\nu|_\infty\|\nu\|^2$, $Q$ the quadratic part of $A$ and $43N^2$ the bound of the cubic remainder of the plaquettes, the integral of $e^{-\beta A}$ over $\{A<\alpha_\beta\}$ lies between $e^{\mp(d_\nu\epsilon+C\rho_\delta)}$ times the Gaussian integral of $Q$, $\rho_\delta=(\Lambda_\delta\alpha_\beta)^{1/2}$, $\epsilon=43N^2\Lambda_\delta\rho_\delta$; the Gaussian determinants need not be computed, as the limit $\mathcal Z(N)$ names them.

Where some holonomy has $1-(\frac12\operatorname{tr}h_\mu)^2\ge\delta^2$, the base is the commuting triple, there are $6N^3-2$ transverse variables, and the softest of them costs of the order $\delta^2/N^2$: $\Lambda_\delta\le2\pi^2N^5+\frac{\pi^2}4N^2\delta^{-2}$. (3) \emph{The eight points} at which every $h_\mu$ is $\pm\mathbf 1$: there the stabiliser is all of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, the nine constant modes $c=(c_\mu)$ have the quartic action $N^3|c\wedge c|^2$, $|c\wedge c|^2=\sum_{\mu<\nu}|c_\mu\times c_\nu|^2$, and the Gaussian picture fails for $|u|\lesssim(N/\beta)^{1/4}$. An upper bound suffices there. In Landau's gauge the action is at least $\frac12(1-\epsilon')\|d_1Y'\|^2+N^3|c\wedge c|^2$ for the non-constant part $Y'$ of the field, $d_1$ the lattice exterior derivative of $1$-forms, the Jacobian is at most $(\mathrm{Det}'(N)/N^3)^{3/2}(1+7N^2r_\delta)^{3N^3}$ (Kirchhoff's theorem), $r_\delta^2=6\pi^2N^2\delta^2+24N^5\alpha_\beta$, and the integral over the constant modes is at most $48\pi^3r_\delta N^{-3/2}(\beta N^3)^{-2}$; measured against $\mathcal Z(N)\beta^{1-3N^3}$, in which $\mathscr J_N=\int \,\mathrm{d}u/\Upsilon_N(u)$ lies between two absolute numbers, as $c_0|u|^2\le\Upsilon_N(u)\le c_0^{-1}$ with an absolute $c_0>0$ and $|u|^{-2}$ is integrable in three dimensions, the weight of these fields is at most $C\,N^{-1/2}r_\delta\,e^{CN^5r_\delta}$. (4) \emph{The balance.} The error of (2) is of the order of $N^8\delta^{-3}(N^3\log\beta/\beta)^{1/2}$, that of (3) of the order of $N^{1/2}\delta$; with $\delta=N^{-6}(N^{66}\log\beta/\beta)^{1/8}$ both, and the cut, are at most an absolute multiple of $(N^{66}\log\beta/\beta)^{1/8}$: the exponent $\frac18$ is the balance of $\delta^{-3}\beta^{-1/2}$ against $\delta$, all the dependence on $N$ sits in $N^{66}$, and $c_3$, $x_*$ are absolute.

\emph{The consequence.} With $|\log(1+x)|\le2|x|$ for $|x|\le\frac12$, the bound at $N$ and at $qN$ (the condition at $qN$ implies the one at $N$) gives $\log Z(N^3)=-(3N^3-1)\log\beta+\log\mathcal Z(N)+O(2\mathsf{er})$ and the same at $qN$; as $-q^3(3N^3-1)+(3q^3N^3-1)=q^3-1$, the terms in $N^3$ cancel in $D_q(N)=q^3F(N^3)-F((qN)^3)$, and $-q^3\log N+\log(qN)=-(q^3-1)\log N+\log q$. (b) Let $t\le t_0$. \emph{The frame.} Let $j_t$ be the least integer $j\ge1$ with $L^j\ge LM\,R(2L^j/t)$. As $R(Lx)\le L\,R(x)$ once $\log x\ge r$, the exponent of $R(2L^j/t)$ grows by at most one when $j$ grows by one, so equality holds at $j_t$: $\ell'=2L^{j_t}$, $\mathsf b'=\ell'/t$ and $y'=\log\mathsf b'$ satisfy $\ell'=2LM\,R(\mathsf b')$, which is $L$ times the least side at which (M4)(ii), (iii) apply at the label $\mathsf b'$, and $2LMy'^r\le\ell'<2L^2My'^r$, $\log\frac1t<y'<2\log\frac1t$ for small $t$.

Every pair $(N,\beta)$ with $N=2L^i$ and $N/\beta=t$ is the pair $(\ell'/a_K,L^K\mathsf b')$ of the cutoff $K=i-j_t$, of either sign, on the line of $\mathsf b'$ (Def.~\ref{C-361-2}). Write $D_K=D_L(\ell'/a_K)$ at $\beta=L^K\mathsf b'$, which is $X_K(\mathsf b',L\ell')$. \emph{Two cutoffs, uniformly in the label.} The number $\mathfrak o_K$ of (M4)(ii) is $8\mathsf R_{t_1}+12\epsilon_{\rm fg}+8\epsilon_{\rm cl}+12\epsilon_{\rm sh}$ (\textup{(\ref{IV-62-64})}), with the explicit numbers of \S\ref{sec:cutoff-calibration} at $n=1$: with $y=\log\mathsf b$, $u=\lceil K/1260\rceil$, $s=\lceil K/9\rceil$ and the top level $t_1=K-u$ of (M4)(ii) in $\mathsf R_{t_1}$, $\epsilon_{\rm fg}\le c\,\ell^3L^{-34K/315}$ and $\epsilon_{\rm cl}\le c\,(y+K\log L)^{2\mathfrak p_0}K^{1/2}\ell^3L^{-K/9}$, while $\mathsf R_{t_1}$ carries the factor $e^{-c'A_0^2(y+u\log L)^{2\mathfrak p_0}}$ against $e^{(C+\frac92y)\ell^3}$, and $\epsilon_{\rm sh}$ the factor $e^{-\frac14\kappa_{\rm b}A_1^2(y+u\log L)^{2\mathfrak p_0}}$.

On the sides $2MR(\mathsf b)\le\ell\le2L^3My^r$ one has $\ell^3\le8L^9M^3y^{3r}$ and $y^{2\mathfrak p_0}\le(\ell/2M)^{2\mathfrak p_0/r}$, and the condition $2\mathfrak p_0>3r+2$ of the list of (H3) lets $e^{-c'A_0^2y^{2\mathfrak p_0}}$ beat $e^{(C+\frac92y)\ell^3}$. So there are numbers $y_\sharp$, $C_{\mathfrak o}$ of the constants such that at every label with $y\ge y_\sharp$, on every such side $\ell$ and at every $K\ge11(5+2\mathfrak p_0/r)\log_L\ell$, the conditions (k0)--(k4), (k6) of \S\ref{sec:cutoff-calibration} hold and $\mathfrak o_K(\ell)\le C_{\mathfrak o}\,\ell^{3+2\mathfrak p_0/r}L^{-K/11}$, uniformly in the label; this is the form needed here, as $\mathsf b'\to\infty$ when $t\to0$, while the constant $\mathsf C_{\rm bf}$ of (M4)(ii) is formed on bounded sets of labels.

The two sides $\ell'$, $L\ell'$ lie in this range, and (M4)(ii) on both, with Prop.~\ref{C-361-13}(a), gives
\[
\begin{multlined}
|D_{K+1}-D_K|\le L^3\mathfrak o_K(\ell')+\mathfrak o_K(L\ell')+C\ell'^3L^{-K}\le C\,\ell'^{\,3+2\mathfrak p_0/r}L^{-K/11}\qquad\bigl(K\ge11(5 \\
+2\mathfrak p_0/r)\log_L(L\ell')\bigr).
\end{multlined}
\]
\emph{The base.} Let $K_\circ$ be the least integer with $N_\circ=\ell'L^{K_\circ}\ge t^{-1/130}$, so that $t^{-1/130}\le N_\circ<Lt^{-1/130}$; as $\ell'$ is a power of $\log\frac1t$, $K_\circ$ lies above the bound on $K$ of the display once $t\le t_0$. Let $N=2L^i$ and $\beta=N/t$. (1) If $N\le N_\circ$, then $(LN)^{66}\log\beta/\beta=L^{66}N^{65}t\log\frac Nt\le L^{131}t^{1/2}(\log L+\frac{131}{130}\log\frac1t)$, and (a) at $q=L$ applies for $t\le t_0$ and bounds the left member of (b) by $2(L^3+1)c_3L^{17}t^{1/16}(\log L+\frac{131}{130}\log\frac1t)^{1/8}$. (2) If $N>N_\circ$, then $K=i-j_t>K_\circ$, and with $\mathsf k_M=L^3c'_M-c'_{LM}+\log L$,
\[
D_L(N)-(L^3-1)\log\tfrac1t-\mathsf k_N=\bigl[D_K-D_{K_\circ}\bigr]+\bigl[D_L(N_\circ)-(L^3-1)\log\tfrac1t-\mathsf k_{N_\circ}\bigr]+\bigl[\mathsf k_{N_\circ}-\mathsf k_N\bigr]:
\]
the first bracket is at most $C(1-L^{-1/11})^{-1}\ell'^{\,3+2\mathfrak p_0/r+1/11}t^{1/1430}$ by the display, as $L^{-K_\circ}\le\ell't^{1/130}$; the second is case (1) at $N_\circ$; the third is at most $2(L^3+1)C_AN_\circ^{-2}(\log N_\circ)^{5/2}\le2(L^3+1)C_At^{1/65}(\log L+\frac1{130}\log\frac1t)^{5/2}$ by the rate of (c), whose proof does not use (b). The exponents $\frac1{16}$, $\frac1{1430}$, $\frac1{65}$ exceed $\frac1{1500}$, and the powers of $\log\frac1t$ are absorbed into $C_B$; $t_0$ is fixed by $\log\frac1{t_0}\ge y_\sharp$, by the place of $K_\circ$ and by the condition of (a) in case (1). (c) By Prop.~\ref{C-361-7}(c) and $\delta(M^3)\le3(M/N)^2\delta(N^3)$, $(1-3L^{-S-1})\delta(N^3)\le\sum_{s=0}^SL^{-3(s+1)}D_L(L^sN)\le\delta(N^3)$, and with $Y(M)=\log(\beta/M)+c'_M$ the main terms of (b) telescope:
\[
\sum_{s=0}^{S}L^{-3(s+1)}\bigl[(L^3-1)\log(\beta/L^sN)+L^3c'_{L^sN}-c'_{L^{s+1}N}+\log L\bigr]=Y(N)-L^{-3(S+1)}Y(L^{S+1}N);
\]
choosing $L^S$ of the order $t^{-1/2}$ gives (c). The limit $c'$ and the rate are those of Riemann sums for lattice determinants, written through heat kernels: $\log\mathrm{Det}'(N)$, $f_\Delta N^3$ and $2\log N$ are integrals $\int_0^\infty[\cdots]\frac{d\tau}\tau$ of one-dimensional heat kernels, which converge to those of $\vartheta(\tau,\cdot)$. (d) At $N=2L$ and $\beta\ge2L/t_1$, (a) gives $F(N^3)=-(3N^3-1)\log\beta+N^3z_\infty-\log N+c'_N+O((\log\beta/\beta)^{1/8})$ and (c) gives $\delta(N^3)=\log(\beta/N)+c'_N+O(\beta^{-1/1500})$; the difference is $N^3P=-3N^3\log\beta+N^3z_\infty+O(\beta^{-1/1500})$.\qedhere
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The flux quotient of small cubes at every cutoff]\label{C-361-16}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[beginpenalty=10000]
\item[(a)] There are numbers $t_2>0$, $C_\flat$ of the constants, and $\mathsf a=\frac92r+\mathfrak p_0$, such that for every integer $j\ge1$ and every real $\beta$ with $t=2L^j/\beta\le t_2$: $r_1(2L^j)\le\eta_\flat(t)=C_\flat(\log\frac1t)^{\mathsf a}t^{1/500}$ at $\beta$. Equivalently: for every side $\ell=2L^m$, $m\in\mathbb Z$, every real label $\mathsf b$ with $\ell/\mathsf b\le t_2$, and every cutoff $K\ge1-m$.
\item[(b)] To obtain the following sharper bound, one must establish the \textbf{(Heaviest class)} probability estimate. The intended conclusion is that there are numbers $t_4>0$, $C$ of the constants, and $\mathsf q=1116\,r+720\,\mathfrak p_0+366$, such that for every integer $j\ge1$ and every real $\beta$ with $t=2L^j/\beta\le t_4$, over the cross-section $(N,N)$, $N=2L^j$: $\lambda_0^N/Z(N^3)\le C\,t\,(\log\frac1t)^{\mathsf q}$.\qedhere
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(a) \emph{On one lattice.} (i) Multiplying by $-1$ the bonds of a sheet (a half-plane of bonds bounded by two columns) moves a twisted column; so $Z^z$ does not depend on the place of its column, and reflection positivity across two layers with the column in the cut gives $0\le Z^z[\chi\chi']\le Z[\chi]^{1/2}Z[\chi']^{1/2}$ for $[0,1]$-valued $\chi,\chi'$ of the two halves. On configurations whose block plaquettes at a level $q$ (or the bare plaquettes) lie within $\omega$ of $\mathbf 1$, a twist forces the holonomies $P_1,P_3$ of the block field around the twisted plane to anticommute up to $\varpi=(1+\omega)^{\mathsf n^2}-1\le\frac1{20}$, $\mathsf n$ the number of block sites a side; hence $|W_1|\le\varpi/2$ and $W_2^2\ge1-0.52\,\varpi^2$ for the half-traces $W_\mu(y)$ of the straight closed lines of the block field through a site, and
\[
r_1(N)\le\max_y\mu_{N^3}\bigl(\mathcal C^\varpi(y)\bigr)+3\mathsf n^3\mathsf R^{1/2},\qquad\mathcal C^\varpi(y)=\bigl\{|W_1(y)|\le\tfrac\varpi2,\ W_2(y)^2\ge1-0.52\,\varpi^2\bigr\},
\]
$\mathsf R$ the largest probability of a rough block plaquette. (ii) On a bare cube small against $\beta$: with $\Xi_\beta=3N^3\log(8e^8\beta^{3/2})+2\log(3N^3\beta)$ and $\omega_0=(2\Xi_\beta/\beta)^{1/2}$, $Z\ge(8e^8\beta^{3/2})^{-3N^3}$, so a plaquette is rough, $|\partial U(p)-\mathbf 1|\ge\omega_0$, with probability $\le(3N^3\beta)^{-2}$. Then the angle of $P_1$ is shifted along the seam: with $P_1(y_0)=e^{i\alpha_0\hat n\cdot\sigma}$ at the site $y_0$ of the event, $0<\alpha_0<\pi$, $\sigma$ the Pauli matrices, $\mathsf N(x)$ the matrix $\hat n\cdot\sigma$ carried to $x$ along a path from $y_0$ that uses no seam bond $\langle x,x+e_k\rangle$, $x_k=0$, $k=1,2$, and $V(b)\mapsto V(b)e^{-is_k\mathsf N(b_+)}$ on the seam bonds of the direction $k$, this map, defined for $|s|_\infty\le\frac1{10}$, commutes with gauge transformations, turns $P_1(y_0)$ by $-s_1$ and $P_2(y_0)$ by $-s_2$ about $\hat n$, changes the action by at most $131N^4\beta\omega_0^2|s|_\infty$ on the fields whose plaquettes all lie within $\omega_0$ of $\mathbf 1$, and changes the Haar measure by the factor $\sin^2(\alpha_0-s_1)/\sin^2\alpha_0$.

Let $D$ be the event $\mathcal C^\varpi(y_0)$ intersected with that of no rough plaquette. For $s\in2\varpi\mathbb Z^2$ with $|s|_\infty\le s_0=(131N^4\beta\omega_0^2)^{-1}$, which is $<\frac1{10}$, the action rises by at most $1$, so the image of $D$ has the measure $\ge e^{-1}\cos^2(0.13)\,\mu_{N^3}(D)\ge0.36\,\mu_{N^3}(D)$; on $D$ the angles of $P_1(y_0)$ and $P_2(y_0)$ about $\hat n$ fix $s$ up to $1.02\varpi$ and $1.46\varpi$, so the images of distinct points of the grid are disjoint, and there are at least $(s_0/2\varpi)^2$ of them. Hence $\mu_{N^3}(D)\le\frac4{0.36}\varpi^2(131N^4\beta\omega_0^2)^2$, which is of the order $N^{12}\Xi_\beta^3/\beta$, as $\beta\omega_0^2=2\Xi_\beta$ and $\varpi\le2.1N^2\omega_0$; with the rough plaquettes, $\mu_{N^3}(\mathcal C^\varpi)\le[6.8\cdot10^6N^{12}\Xi_\beta^3+1]\beta^{-1}$, for the block field of a bare lattice that is not too large against $\beta$ as well, by (M4)(v). (iii) \emph{Through the cutoffs.} Write $2L^j=\ell L^K$ with $\ell=2L^m$ the least side at which (M4) applies at the label $\mathsf b=\ell/t$, $y=\log\mathsf b$, $\ell\le2L^2My^r$.

At the cutoffs $K\le K_1=\lceil y/(25\log L)\rceil$ the lattice is a bare cube small against $\beta$, and (ii) applies. Above $K_1$ we use (M4)(iii) at the depth $d=0$: at the cutoff $K$ the block field is $\mathcal M^KU$, on the unit lattice of the torus $\ell$, with $\ell$ sites a side at every cutoff; the roughness $\omega$ and the width $\varpi$ are chosen at $K_1$ and do not depend on $K$. The events $\mathcal C^\varpi(y')$ of this block field and the events that one of its plaquettes lies at a distance $\ge\omega$ from $\mathbf 1$ are closed and gauge invariant, and the same at all cutoffs; so by (M4)(iii) their probabilities move by at most $\mathfrak o_K$ from one cutoff to the next, and $\sum_{K\ge K_1}\mathfrak o_K\le Q(y)e^{-y/250}$, $Q$ a polynomial formed from the constants; (i) at the cutoff $K$ then gives $r_1\le4\bar\ell(y)^3Q(y)^{1/2}e^{-y/500}$, $\bar\ell(y)=2L^2My^r$, which is $\le C_\flat(\log\frac1t)^{\mathsf a}t^{1/500}$. (b) The proposed sharper estimate still requires \textbf{(Heaviest class)}; the remaining reduction uses another label of a layer and a multiplicative comparison through the cutoffs.

\emph{The top level against the heaviest cell of a label.} Let $\Phi$ map the configurations on the bonds of the directions $1,2$ of one layer into a set $\mathsf X$, let $\mathcal P$ be a finite partition of $\mathsf X$ into cells whose preimages are Borel, $\sim$ a reflexive and symmetric relation on $\mathcal P$ with at most $\nu$ neighbours to each cell, and $\iota_k$ the cell of the label of the layer $x_3=k$. Then over the cross-section $(N,N)$ of an even cube $N=2h$
\[
e^{-\mathsf G_N}=\frac{\lambda_0^N}{Z(N^3)}\le\bigl(\nu^2\sqrt{p^\sharp}+\nu\sqrt{\varepsilon_2}+\sqrt{\varepsilon_1}\bigr)^2\le2\nu^4\bigl(p^\sharp+\max\{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2\}\bigr)\quad(\nu\ge2),
\]
$p^\sharp=\max_I\mu_{N^3}(\iota_1=I)$, $\varepsilon_1=\mu_{N^3}(\iota_1\not\sim\iota_{\mathsf n/2-1})$, $\varepsilon_2=\mu_{N^3}(\iota_{\mathsf n/2-1}\not\sim\iota_{\mathsf n/2+1})$, in two cases: ($\alpha$) the label of a bare layer, $\mathsf n=N$; ($\beta$) the label of a layer of the block field $\mathcal M^qU$ of the bare cube, with $\mathsf n\ge8$ block sites a side. Indeed, let the first slab be the bare layers $1,\dots,s$, with $s=2$ in ($\alpha$), $s=\frac12(3L^q-1)$ in ($\beta$), and $2s<h$, which in ($\beta$) follows from $\mathsf n\ge8$. The label $\iota_1$ is a Borel function of the bonds with both ends in the first slab: in ($\alpha$) it reads the layer $x_3=1$ alone, and in ($\beta$), by the locality of the averaging map (Prop.~\YMMref{4.5}{20}), only the bare bonds of the blocks of the block layer $1$, which, centred at the height $L^q$, lie in the bare layers $\frac12(L^q+1),\dots,\frac12(3L^q-1)$.

The reflection in the plane $x_3=\frac h2$, the translation by $he_3$ and the reflection in the plane $x_3=0$ carry the first slab onto the layers $h-s,\dots,h-1$, the layers $h+1,\dots,h+s$ and the layers $N-s,\dots,N-1$; the layers $0$ and $h$ lie in none of these four slabs. The three maps are isometries of the bare lattice and, in ($\beta$), as $h=\frac{\mathsf n}2L^q$ is a multiple of $L^q$, of the block lattices, and the averaging maps commute with them ({\cite[Lem.~G.1]{YMM2}}); so the label $\iota_1$, read on the configuration moved by them, is $\iota_{\mathsf n/2-1}$, $\iota_{\mathsf n/2+1}$, $\iota_{\mathsf n-1}$ respectively. Let $\chi_I$ be the indicator function of the label $I$ on the first slab, $\mathfrak Y[\chi_I]$ its slab operator of (M1), and $Y_I=\mathfrak Y[\chi_I]\,\mathsf T'^{\,1/2}$, the operator $\mathsf T'=\mathsf K^{1/2}\mathsf m\,\mathsf K^{1/2}$ being $\ge0$; then $\sum_IY_I=\mathsf T'^{\,s+1/2}$, $R=\mathsf T'^{\,h-2s-1}\ge0$ and $\mathsf T'^{\,h}=\sum_{I,J}Y_J^*RY_I$.

The conjugated mirror image $\chi_J^\Theta$ of (M1), placed on the layers $h-s,\dots,h-1$, is $\chi_J$ read on the configuration mirrored in the plane $x_3=\frac h2$ midway between these layers and the first slab, that is the indicator of $\iota_{\mathsf n/2-1}=J$; placed on the layers $N-s,\dots,N-1$, it is $\chi_J$ read on the configuration mirrored in the plane $x_3=h$, which on the box of $N=2h$ layers is the reflection in the plane $x_3=0$, that is the indicator of $\iota_{\mathsf n-1}=J$; and $\chi_{I'}$ placed on the layers $h+1,\dots,h+s$ is the indicator of $\iota_{\mathsf n/2+1}=I'$. So the trace formula of (M1), in which the first slab stands rightmost, for the functions $\chi_I^{+(h-2s-1)}$, $(\chi_J^\Theta)^{+1}$, $\chi_{I'}^{+(h-2s-1)}$, $(\chi_{J'}^\Theta)^{+1}$ on the consecutive slabs of $h-s-1$, $s+1$, $h-s-1$, $s+1$ layers from the layer $1$ on, with $\mathfrak Y[\Phi^{+j}]=\mathsf T'^{\,j}\mathfrak Y[\Phi]$ (the $j$ added layers lying above those of $\Phi$), $\mathfrak Y[\chi_J^\Theta]=\mathfrak Y[\chi_J]^*$ and the cyclicity of the trace, gives $\operatorname{Tr}(Y_{J'}^*RY_{I'}\,Y_J^*RY_I)=\operatorname{Tr}(\mathsf T'\mathfrak Y[\chi_{J'}^\Theta]\,R\,\mathfrak Y[\chi_{I'}]\,\mathsf T'\mathfrak Y[\chi_J^\Theta]\,R\,\mathfrak Y[\chi_I])=Z(N^3)\,\mu_{N^3}(\iota_1=I,\iota_{\mathsf n/2-1}=J,\iota_{\mathsf n/2+1}=I',\iota_{\mathsf n-1}=J')$: probabilities of one and the same cube.

The terms with $I\not\sim J$ have together the Hilbert--Schmidt norm $\le(Z\varepsilon_1)^{1/2}$. The terms with $I\sim J$ are $\mathbb X\mathbb B\mathbb X^*$, with $\mathbb X(\varphi_I)_I=\sum_IY_I^*R^{1/2}\varphi_I$ and the neighbour matrix $\mathbb B$ of norm $\le\nu$ (Schur's test); $\mathbb X^*\mathbb X$ is the matrix of the $R^{1/2}Y_IY_J^*R^{1/2}$, whose Hilbert--Schmidt norms are $(Z\mu_{N^3}(\iota_1=\iota_{\mathsf n/2-1}=I,\ \iota_{\mathsf n/2+1}=\iota_{\mathsf n-1}=J))^{1/2}$, so Schur's test on the neighbouring entries and the Hilbert--Schmidt norm of the others give $\|\mathbb X^*\mathbb X\|\le\nu(Zp^\sharp)^{1/2}+(Z\varepsilon_2)^{1/2}$. Hence $\lambda_0^h=\|\mathsf T'^{\,h}\|\le Z^{1/2}[\nu(\nu\sqrt{p^\sharp}+\sqrt{\varepsilon_2})+\sqrt{\varepsilon_1}]$.

\emph{The label: the class of the pair of holonomies.} For pairs $P=(P_1,P_2)$, $Q$ in $\mathrm{SU}(2)^2$ let $\mathsf D(P,Q)=\min_g\max_{i=1,2}|P_i-gQ_ig^{-1}|$, a distance between the classes under simultaneous conjugation, $\mathcal O_w(Q)=\{P:\mathsf D(P,Q)\le w\}$, and $\mathsf v(r)$ the volume of a ball of radius $r$ of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$. For $0<w\le\frac2{35}$ a maximal family of points $Q^{(k)}$ at mutual class distances $>w$ gives a finite partition of $\mathrm{SU}(2)^2$ into Borel cells $I_k\subset\mathcal O_w(Q^{(k)})$, invariant under simultaneous conjugation; with $I_k\sim I_l$ if and only if $\mathsf D(Q^{(k)},Q^{(l)})\le3w$, two pairs at the class distance $\le w$ lie in neighbouring cells, and $\nu\le\mathsf v(\frac72w)^2/\mathsf v(\frac12w)^2\le1.21\cdot10^5$.

The label of a layer is the cell of the pair $(P_1,P_2)$ of the holonomies of its straight closed lines through one site, and $E_k$ is the event that this pair lies in $I_k$. The label is rigid across the layers: if all plaquettes of a lattice of $\mathsf n$ sites a side lie within $\varpi$ of $\mathbf 1$, one conjugation carries both holonomies at $a+ke_3$ to within $k\mathsf n\varpi$ of those at $a$, so that $\mathsf D\le k\mathsf n\varpi$. \emph{No class is heavy on a bare even cube.} Let $\rho_\omega$ be the density, against the Haar measure of $\mathrm{SU}(2)^3$, of the three holonomies $(P_1,P_2,P_3)$ through a site on the event that all plaquettes lie within $\omega$ of $\mathbf 1$; it vanishes unless $|[P_\mu,P_\nu]|\le N^2\omega$, and it is greatest at $(\mathbf 1,\mathbf 1,\mathbf 1)$, as follows.
Choose a pointwise version of $\rho_\omega$ by solving one seam bond on each of the three straight winding loops for $P_\mu$ and integrating over all other bonds. The loops have no bonds in common, and these substitutions preserve product Haar measure. Fix $\mu$ and cut at the site planes $x_\mu=0,h$, where $N=2h$. Let $B$ be their tangential bonds and $X_+,X_-$ the private bonds in the two halves, identified by reflection. No plaquette crosses a site plane, so the cut Wilson weight factors as $w_0(B)w_+(B,X_+)w_+(B,X_-)$, with $dU=dB\,\mathrm{d}X_+\,\mathrm{d}X_-$ and nonnegative factors bounded by one. The plaquette indicators factor in the same way. At fixed $B$, solve one private bond on the half-path from $0$ to $he_\mu$ for its transport. Its weighted Haar density $k_B$ is bounded and hence belongs to $L^2(G)$. If the two half-transports from $0$ to $he_\mu$ are $g_+,g_-$, then $P_\mu=g_+g_-^{-1}$ and its unnormalised conditional density is $q_B(p)=\int k_B(pg)k_B(g)\,\mathrm{d}g\le\int k_B(g)^2\,\mathrm{d}g=q_B(\mathbf1)$ by Schwarz and Haar invariance. The other two loops lie in $x_\mu=0$, so their holonomies and their solved seam bonds are functions of $B$. Integrating this inequality over the remaining boundary bonds with those holonomies fixed proves $\rho_\omega(P)\le\rho_\omega(P_1,\ldots,P_{\mu-1},\mathbf1,P_{\mu+1},\ldots,P_3)$ in the pointwise version just specified. Apply it for $\mu=1,2,3$. The factorization is also the site-mirror case of the proof of Prop.~\YMMref{91.4}{700}, which keeps the boundary bonds as separate Haar variables.
To complete \textbf{(Heaviest class)}, one must establish the following quantitative class-probability estimate; the subsequent calculation describes its use. Take $\Xi'=\beta\omega_0^2\ge1$ with $\Xi' N^5\omega_0\le3/640$ and $N^2\omega_0\le w\le1/10$.

The estimate required here is, for every pair $Q$ and every site $y$,
\[
\mu_{N^3}\bigl(\mathsf D((P_1,P_2)(y),Q)\le w,\ \text{no rough plaquette}\bigr)\le10^{11}\,\Xi'^5N^7w^6\omega_0^{-4}.
\]
Given this estimate, on the bare cube with $\omega_0$ and $\Xi_\beta$ of (a)(ii), $\Xi'=2\Xi_\beta$ and $w=N^2\omega_0$, as long as $2\Xi_\beta N^5\omega_0\le\frac3{640}$: where no plaquette is rough, $\mathsf D$ between the labels of the layers $1$ and $\frac N2-1$ is $<w$ and between those of the layers $\frac N2\mp1$ it is $\le2N\omega_0\le w$, so $\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2$ are at most the probability, $\le\beta^{-2}$, that some plaquette is rough, $p^\sharp\le10^{11}(2\Xi_\beta)^6N^{19}\beta^{-1}+\beta^{-2}$, and, the bound increasing with $\nu$, with $1.21\cdot10^5$ for $\nu$ and $2\nu^4=4.2872\cdot10^{20}$: $e^{-\mathsf G_N}\le2.8\cdot10^{33}\Xi_\beta^6N^{18}\,t$ on the bare cube. \emph{Through the cutoffs.} With $y=\log\mathsf b$ and the side $\ell$ of (a)(iii), this serves at the cutoffs below the cutoff $K_1(y)$ of (M4)(vi), Prop.~\ref{C-361-23}(c), which in (b) we call $K_1$: the least $K\ge10$ with $L^{K/10}\ge\bar\ell(y)^3y^{2\mathfrak p_0+1}$, so that $L^{K_1}<L\,(\bar\ell(y)^3y^{2\mathfrak p_0+1})^{10}$ and the bare cube has $N_1=\ell L^{K_1}<\mathsf N(y)=L\,\bar\ell(y)^{31}y^{10(2\mathfrak p_0+1)}$ sites a side, a fixed power of $y$; at the bare cubes $N\le N_1$ one has $\Xi_\beta\le10N^3y$, and the condition $2\Xi_\beta N^5\omega_0\le\frac3{640}$ holds once $y$ is large, as $t\le\bar\ell(y)e^{-y}$.

Above $K_1$ the additive transport of (a) does not serve: even summed from the higher cutoff $\lceil y/(25\log L)\rceil$ of (a)(iii), its error $\sum_K\mathfrak o_K\le Q(y)e^{-y/250}$ is of the order of $t^{1/250}$ up to powers of $\log\frac1t$, and swamps the first power of $t$; summed from $K_1$ it is only of the order $1/y$. We use instead the comparison with a factor of (M4)(vi), Prop.~\ref{C-361-23}(c): from $K_1$ on its factors multiply to at most $e^{0.53}<1.7$, the sums from $K_1$ on of the numbers of \S\ref{sec:cutoff-calibration} being of the order $1/y$, and its remainders add up to at most $e^{-4y}$. At $K_1$ take $\omega_0$ of (a)(ii) at $\beta_1=N_1/t$, $w=N_1^2\omega_0$, the cells $I_k$ of this $w$, and for the block field the roughness $\omega=1.003\,L^{2K_1}\omega_0$; none of these reads $K$.

By (M4)(v), where all bare plaquettes lie within $\omega_0$ of $\mathbf 1$ (for large $y$, $L^{2K_1}\omega_0\le N_1^2\omega_0$ lies below the number of $L$ that (M4)(v) asks), the block plaquettes of $\mathcal M^{K_1}U$ lie within $\omega$ of $\mathbf 1$ and its holonomies within $13.3\,N_1L^{K_1}\omega_0\le0.512\,w$ of the bare ones; so the bound on the classes of the bare cube $N_1$, taken at $1.52\,w$, gives for each of the finitely many events $E_k$ of the block field of depth $0$ at a site $\mu^{K_1}_0(E_k)\le\beta_1^{-2}+7.9\cdot10^{19}N_1^{36}y^6\,t$, and for the event $\mathfrak R$ of a rough block plaquette $\mu^{K_1}_0(\mathfrak R)\le\beta_1^{-2}$. By (M4)(vi), in the form of Prop.~\ref{C-361-23}(c), used for each of these gauge-invariant events apart (nothing is summed over the cells: $p^\sharp$ is a maximum), at every $K\ge K_1$ each has a probability at most $1.7$ times its probability at $K_1$ plus $1.7\,e^{-4y}$.

At the cutoff $K$ the label ($\beta$) of the block field of depth $0$, on the torus $\ell$ with $\mathsf n=\ell$ block sites a side, is rigid with $\omega$ for $\varpi$: between the layers $1$ and $\frac{\mathsf n}2-1$ the class distance is $<\frac12\ell^2\omega<w$, between $\frac{\mathsf n}2\mp1$ it is $\le2\ell\omega<w$, so $\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2\le\mu^K_0(\mathfrak R)$. As $\beta_1^{-2}\le t$ and $e^{-4y}\le t$, the bound of the top level by the heaviest cell gives $e^{-\mathsf G_N}\le6\cdot10^{40}N_1^{36}y^6\,t$, which is at most $C\,t\,(\log\frac1t)^{\mathsf q}$, as $N_1<\mathsf N(y)$ and $\log\frac1t\le y\le2\log\frac1t$; the bound $2.8\cdot10^{33}\Xi_\beta^6N^{18}t\le2.8\cdot10^{39}\mathsf N(y)^{36}y^6t$ of the bare cubes below $K_1$ is smaller.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Proof of the theorems}

\emph{Step 1: Thm.~\ref{C-361-3}(1).} BI is the hypothesis $\mathsf e(l)\le x_0$ of Props.~\ref{C-361-8}, \ref{C-361-19}, \ref{C-361-10}, \ref{C-361-11} and of Lem.~\ref{C-361-20} at $l=l_K$, $\beta=L^K\mathsf b$, with one $x_0$ for all $K$. For $N=\ell/a_K$,
\[
\frac N{2l_K}=\frac\ell{\ell_0},\qquad\theta^{1/l_K}=e^{-m_*a_K},\qquad N\ge2l_K\iff\ell\ge\ell_0 .
\]
(a) is Prop.~\ref{C-361-8}(b), (c) and Prop.~\ref{C-361-19}(c), with $X_K(\mathsf b,\ell)\le L^3\delta((\ell/La_K)^3)$ (Prop.~\ref{C-361-7}(c)). (b) is Prop.~\ref{C-361-10}(a), (b). (c): with $y=\theta^{\ell/\ell_0}\le0.8901$, convexity gives $\varepsilon\le22.3(e^{0.13736/7}-1)\,y\le0.441912\,y$ in Prop.~\ref{C-361-9}(b), and $\frac12(\sqrt\varepsilon+\varepsilon)\le0.540843\sqrt y$; with $y=\theta^{\ell'/\ell_0}$, $Q',Q''\le e^{0.13736/8}\le1.017319$ and $Q'(Q'-1)\le0.0176182\,y$, so Prop.~\ref{C-361-9}(c) gives $4.84\cdot0.132734\cdot1.017319\le0.66$. The boxes are Prop.~\ref{C-361-10}(c) with $\theta^{N/4l_K}=\theta^{\ell/2\ell_0}$, the twisted boxes Prop.~\ref{C-361-10}(d). (d) is Prop.~\ref{C-361-19}(a), (b) with $A=l_1/a_K$, $B=l_2/a_K$ and $t/a_K$ for $t$: $\frac A{2(t/a_K)}=\frac{l_1}{2t}$, $\frac{AB}{4l_K^2}=\frac{l_1l_2}{\ell_0^2}$, $\theta^{(t/a_K)/l_K}=e^{-m_*t}$, $\frac{1.4239}{A}=a_K\frac{1.4239}{l_1}$, and $\sum_{i\ge1}(\lambda_i/\lambda_0)^{t/a_K}=e^{\mathsf G}-1$; at $l_1=\ell_0$, $(2.42x_0)^{1/l_K}=\exp[-a_K\frac2{\ell_0}\log\frac1{2.42x_0}]$, and $2\log(1/(2.42\cdot0.069))\approx3.5798$.

For the square, $n=s_\ell/a_K=2^kl_K$ and $(\lambda_i/\lambda_0)^n\le i^{-1}\mathsf r_n\le0.20395\,i^{-1}\theta^{n/l_K}$, which is the bound on $E_i$ and on their number; $\log(1/0.20395)\ge1.5898$. The vortex line: Prop.~\ref{C-361-19}(d) and Prop.~\ref{C-361-11}(e), at $\ell=2^j\ell_0$, $\ell/a_K=2^{j+1}l_K$, $\sigma^+a_K^{-2}=\sigma_*$. (e) is Prop.~\ref{C-361-10}(f) at $n_0=0$; Lem.~\ref{C-361-20}(b) with $\theta^{(j-1)\mathsf w/l_K}=e^{-m_*(j-1)\ell''/2}$ and $Q''^2\le1.0350$; and Prop.~\ref{C-361-10}(b$'$), $\theta^{(2n-1)/6l_K}=e^{-m_*(2n-1)a_K/6}$, $n\ge\frac12(3l_K+1)$ being $na_K\ge\frac34\ell_0+\frac12a_K$. (f) With the time $e_3$, the lattice $\Gamma$ is the box $(\ell/2a_K;2\ell/a_K,\ell/a_K)$ closed up with the translation by $\frac\ell2e_1$ (its periods are also $2\ell e_1$, $\ell e_2$, $\frac\ell2(e_1+e_3)$).

With $l'=\ell/2a_K$, Prop.~\ref{C-361-7}(f) over the cross-section $(4l',2l')$ gives $\lambda_0^{l'}(1-\mathsf r)\le Z_\Gamma\le Z(l',4l',2l')$, $\mathsf r=\mathsf r_{l'}(2l',4l')$. Above: $F(l',4l',2l')\le2F(l',2l',2l')$ (Prop.~\ref{C-361-7}(b)), so $E\le\mathsf e(l')$. Below: $\log\lambda_0=8l'^2P+\varepsilon(2l',4l')\ge8l'^2P$ and $\log Z((2l')^3)=8l'^3P+\delta_K(\ell)$, so $E\ge\log(1-\mathsf r)-\delta_K(\ell)$; by Prop.~\ref{C-361-19}(b) in the zone $2t\le A$, $\mathsf r\le e^c-1$ with $c=0.54526\,y$, $y=\theta^{\ell/\ell_0}$; as $c\mapsto\log(2-e^c)$ is concave and vanishes at $0$, $\log(2-e^c)\ge-2.0196\,c$ for $0\le c\le0.54526\cdot0.8901$; with $\delta_K(\ell)<0.13736\,y$ the sum is $\ge-1.24\,y$.

The sign $E\ge0$ is Prop.~\ref{C-361-7}(g) at $N=\ell/a_K$, the lattice $\Gamma$ being $\Gamma^\diamond$ in physical units.

\emph{Step 2: Thm.~\ref{C-361-3}(2).} Fix $K\ge\max\{K_0,1\}$, $\beta=L^K\mathsf b$, boards of the offset $0$. The $X_i$ and $G_I$ are real functions of the cell $[-\ell''/4,\ell''/4]^3$ at every cutoff. \emph{(i)} $M_I<\infty$: $\|G_I\|^8_{\mathrm{ch},\ell''}$ is a moment of $8|I|$ centred fields with disjoint supports on the single torus $\ell''$, a polynomial in their cumulants of orders $\ge2$, which converge as $K\to\infty$ by (M4)(i) (Prop.~\ref{C-361-30}). \emph{(ii) One factor.} With $y=\theta^{\ell'/\ell_0}$, by Step~1, $[Q'(Q'-1)]^{1/2}\le0.132734\sqrt y$ and $Q''\le1.0174$; Prop.~\ref{C-361-9}(a), (c) give $|\nu_K(G_I)|,|\mu_{K,\ell',\beta}(G_I)|\le1.0174\,M_I$ and $|\nu_K(G_I)-\mu_{K,\ell',\beta}(G_I)|\le0.65\,\sqrt y\,1.0174\,M_I$. \emph{(iii) The cumulant.} A cumulant of order $n\ge2$ does not see the centring, nor, for $n=1$, does the difference of the means of two laws; and
\[
\kappa_n=\sum_\pi(-1)^{|\pi|-1}(|\pi|-1)!\prod_{I\in\pi}\mathbb E\Bigl(\prod_{i\in I}X_i\Bigr),\qquad\Bigl|\prod_I\mathsf a_I-\prod_I\mathsf b_I\Bigr|\le\sum_I|\mathsf a_I-\mathsf b_I|\prod_{I'\ne I}\max\{|\mathsf a_{I'}|,|\mathsf b_{I'}|\},
\]
so the bound holds with $C(X)$. \emph{(iv) Limits.} As the torus cumulants converge at each fixed $\ell'$ by (M4)(i), $\limsup_K-\liminf_K$ of $S^T_n[\nu_K](X)$ is at most $2C(X)\theta^{\ell'/2\ell_0}$ for every $\ell'$, hence $0$; letting $K\to\infty$ in the bound gives the iterated limit, and along $(K_j,\ell_j)$ the difference is $\le C(X)\theta^{\ell_j/2\ell_0}$. \emph{(v) Every shape.} At $N'=\ell'/a_K$ the corner $c'=\frac{\ell'}4(1,1,1)$ has $\mathsf C_{N'/2}(c')=[-\frac{\ell'}4,\frac{\ell'}4]^3$, and $\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{ch};N'}=\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{ch},\ell'}$ there; by Lem.~\ref{C-361-21}(b), (c) with $\delta(N'^3)<0.13736\,y\le\frac12$: $|\langle G_I\rangle_{\underline n}|\le e^{0.1717}\,1.0174\,M_I\le1.208\,M_I$ and $|\langle G_I\rangle_{\underline n}-\mu_{K,\ell',\beta}(G_I)|\le7.31\cdot0.370622\sqrt y\,1.0174\,M_I$; with (ii), $|\langle G_I\rangle_{\underline n}-\nu_K(G_I)|\le3.36\sqrt y\,1.0174\,M_I$, and (iii) gives $C^{\rm sh}(X)$.

For boxes of any shape with $a_{K_j}\min_\mu n^{(j)}_\mu\to\infty$ take $\ell_j$ the greatest member of $\mathfrak L$ below that length. \emph{(vi) A constant free of label, side and place.} For $\mathsf b\in I(g)$ the pairs are first-passage data at $g$. Put the supports by a corner of the cell, $c_\mu=\lfloor z_\mu+R\rfloor+\frac32$, $z$ the centre of the ball: one corner serves all cutoffs because $L$ is odd; the cell $c+[-\frac{\ell'}2,0]^3$ holds the supports farther than $\frac12$ from its walls; and the $8n$ mirror images of the $f_i$ in the planes $x_\mu=c_\mu$ have the same norms, supports each in a ball of radius $R$, pairwise $\ge\mathsf d'$ apart (two images on the two sides of a wall are more than $1$ apart), all in $c+[-(2R+\frac32),2R+\frac32]^3$, which a lattice translation carries into $(-\frac{\ell'}4,\frac{\ell'}4)^3$.

So the expansion of Prop.~\ref{C-361-30}, with the bounds (M5)(i) in the place of (M4)(i), gives $\|G_I\|_{\mathrm{ch},\ell'}\le\mathsf m^\flat_I$, centring by the mean on the torus $\ell'$ itself (the floor $128n(R+1)$ is the floor $16k(R+1)$ of (M5)(i) at $k=8n$). Then (ii), (iii) at $\ell''=\ell'$, where $4.84\cdot0.132734=0.642433$ and no factor $Q''$ enters, give $C^\flat(X)$, for $\nu_K$ and for a torus $\ell^+\ge\ell'$ alike, both being states $\mathfrak s$ of Prop.~\ref{C-361-9}; for the boxes $(q_\mu N)$, Lem.~\ref{C-361-21}(b), (c) give $1.86\cdot0.370622=0.68936$ in the place of $0.642433$; for every box, Lem.~\ref{C-361-21}(b), (c) and (ii) give $|\langle G_I\rangle_{\underline n}-\nu_K(G_I)|\le(2.70925+0.642433)\sqrt y\,\mathsf m^\flat_I$ and $e^{\frac54\cdot0.13736}\le1.19$.

For $n\ge2$, $|S_n(X)|\le C^g_n\prod\|f_i\|_\sharp$ is the limit of (M5)(i) along the tori.

\emph{Step 3: Thm.~\ref{C-361-3}(2$'$).} For bounded $Y,X_1,\dots,X_n$, with $X_I=\prod_{i\in I}X_i$,
\[
\begin{multlined}
\kappa(Y,X_1,\dots,X_n)=\sum_{\emptyset\ne I\subset[n]}\operatorname{Cov}(Y,X_I)\,\mathsf c([n]\setminus I),\qquad\mathsf c(S)=\sum_{\pi\in\mathrm{Part}(S)}(-1)^{|\pi|}|\pi|!\prod_{B\in\pi}\mathbb E[X_B], \\
\mathsf c(\emptyset)=1 .
\end{multlined}
\]
Take a board of side $\ell''/2$ with a cell $\square$ about the tuple and a cell $\square'$ about the support of $h$; centring by the means on the torus $\ell''$, Prop.~\ref{C-361-30} bounds the seminorms of the products of the centred fields in each cell, Prop.~\ref{C-361-9}(a) bounds the means $\mathbb E[X_B]$, and Lem.~\ref{C-361-20}(b) bounds $\operatorname{Cov}(Y,X_I)$ by $e^{-m_*(j-1)\ell''/2}$ times the seminorms, the indices of $\square$, $\square'$ differing by $j\ge2(|v|_\infty-\ell'')/\ell''+1$ in some direction; on a torus both ways around enter. The constants depend on the label only through the compact set of Prop.~\ref{C-361-30}. For $W$ in the place of $h$ the same argument runs with $Y=W$, whose centred seminorm in its cell takes the place of the bound of Prop.~\ref{C-361-30} for $h$. Summing over the plaquettes of a far region with a partition of unity by translates of a fixed bump gives the absolute convergence and the decay: with the tents $\chi_v$, $v\in\rho\mathbb Z^3$, of (2$'$) and $u$ vanishing on $\{|x|_\infty<r\}$, $r\ge\ell''+\rho$, the bound for $h=u\chi_v$, which vanishes unless $|v|_\infty\ge r-\rho\ge\ell''$, summed over $v$, gives
\[
\sum_{v\in\rho\mathbb Z^3}\bigl|S^T_{n+1}[\nu_K](u\chi_v,X)\bigr|\le\mathsf C_n\,\sup_v\|u\chi_v\|_\sharp\prod_i\|f_i\|_\sharp\sum_{v\in\rho\mathbb Z^3,\ |v|_\infty\ge r-\rho}e^{-m_*(|v|_\infty-\ell'')},
\]
On the torus use $V$ and $\chi_v^{\rm per}$ from (2$'$). The conditions $\ell\ge L\ell''$ and $\ell''\ge8\rho+4\mathsf d+4$ give $2\rho<\ell$, so each periodized tent is a single local tent in its torus chart and $\sum_{v\in V}\chi_v^{\rm per}=1$. Choose half-open representatives of $V$ with minimal sup norm. They form a subset of $\rho\mathbb Z^3$ and satisfy $|v|_\infty=|v|_{\infty,\ell}$. The one-far-insertion bound summed over this finite set, for $r\ge\frac32\ell''+\rho$, is therefore bounded by the displayed infinite-grid tail, with the same $3.44\,\mathsf C_n$.

\emph{Step 4: Thm.~\ref{C-361-3}(3), the vacuum and the Euclidean group.} For $\mathsf b\in I(g)$ all pairs $(K,L^K\mathsf b)$ are first-passage data, and by Step~1 the only periodic Gibbs state there is $\nu_K$. The moments of the centred fields under $\nu_K$ are polynomials in the cumulants $S^T_{|I|}[\nu_K]$, $|I|\ge2$, which converge by Step~2; so $(\nu_K)$ converges, and $S^\sigma_n=S_n$. By (M5)(ii) each ergodic component of $\sigma$ is a limit along the full sequence whose approximants are periodic Gibbs states at the same pairs, that is $\nu_K$; so $\sigma$ is its own component, and Thm.~\YMMref{AP}{780} gives the invariance under $\mathbb R^3\rtimes\mathrm O(3)$, reflection positivity at every plane, $\ker H_\sigma=\mathbb C\Omega_\sigma$ and the Wightman theory with a unique vacuum. Step~2 (iv), with its iterated limit and its bound along every pair of sequences $K_j\to\infty$, $\mathfrak L\ni\ell_j\to\infty$, identifies every continuum limit at $g$ along growing tori with the pairs $(K_j,L^{K_j}\mathsf b)$ with $(S^\sigma_n)_{n\ge2}$, the limits with the spacing removed first among them; so each of them has the Schwinger functions of $\sigma$, and with them its invariance under $\mathbb R^3\rtimes\mathrm O(3)$, its reflection positivity, its reconstruction with a unique vacuum and, by Step~5, its gap.

\emph{Step 5: Thm.~\ref{C-361-3}(3), the gap.} Let $F=\sum_i\zeta_iX_i$ be a finite combination of separated tuples of fields supported in $\{\epsilon<x_3<\mathsf h'\}$, $\Theta$ the reflection $x_3\mapsto-x_3$, $\tau_t$ the translation by $te_3$ with $t\in a_K\mathbb N$, and $F_K$ the same combination of the lattice fields $\mathcal O_K(f)$, centred by their means in $\nu_K$, a function of one slab above the plane $x_3=0$, with $n_0$ layers between the slab and its mirror image. By translation invariance $\nu_K(\overline{\Theta F_K}\,\tau_tF_K)$ is $h_{F_KF_K}(n_0+t/a_K)$, the mirror being moved to the plane $x_3=-t/2$; so Prop.~\ref{C-361-10}(f) with $A=B=F_K$, $n=n_0+t/a_K$ and $l=l_K$ gives
\[
\nu_K\bigl(\overline{\Theta F_K}\,\tau_tF_K\bigr)-|\nu_K(F_K)|^2\le e^{-m_*t}\bigl[\nu_K\bigl(\overline{\Theta F_K}\,F_K\bigr)-|\nu_K(F_K)|^2\bigr],
\]
with a rate that does not depend on $K$ and a prefactor that converges. Fix $t\in a_{K_*}\mathbb N$. It belongs to every finer time grid, so we may let $K\to\infty$ at this fixed time. With $\psi=(1-P_\Omega)[F]\in\mathcal H(\sigma)$: $\langle\psi,e^{-tH_\sigma}\psi\rangle\le e^{-m_*t}\|\psi\|^2$ on the unbounded set $\bigcup_Ka_K\mathbb N$ of times; so the spectral measure of $\psi$ gives mass at most $e^{-\eta t}\|\psi\|^2$ to $[0,m_*-\eta]$ for arbitrarily large $t$, that is none, and such $\psi$ are dense in $\Omega_\sigma^\perp$. The bilinear bound is the spectral theorem on $\Omega_\sigma^\perp$; the other directions follow by the invariance.

\emph{Step 6: Thm.~\ref{C-361-3}(4).} Prop.~\ref{C-361-11} at $l=l_K$, lengths in units of $a_K$: $\sigma^+a_K^{-2}=(2\Lambda+1.67)/4l_K^2a_K^2=\sigma_*$, and $\sigma_*\ge(2\cdot0.116421+1.67)/\ell_0^2$ at $\theta\le0.8901$; the areas become physical areas. For the flux quotient, $N/l_K=2\ell/\ell_0$ turns $2.2\cdot10^{-4}(N/l_K)^2$ into $8.8\cdot10^{-4}\ell^2/\ell_0^2$, $1.4268\cdot10^{-3}$ into $5.707\cdot10^{-3}$ at $N\ge256l_K$, that is $\ell\ge128\ell_0$, and $2\mathsf qN/l_K$ into $4\mathsf q\ell/\ell_0$. For the potential, $V_K(r)=a_K^{-1}V(r/a_K)$ with the $V$ of Prop.~\ref{C-361-11}(d), whose slopes are $\ge\sigma^+=\sigma_*a_K^2$.

\emph{Step 7: Thm.~\ref{C-361-4}(1).} By Lem.~\ref{C-361-28} take a second admitted blocking factor $L'>L$, a prime with $\alpha=\log L/\log L'$ irrational; Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8} holds in the scheme of $L'$ (spacings $L'^{-k}$, sides $2L'^{\mathbb N}$), and $L^K\mathsf b=L'^{k(K)}\mathsf c_K$ with the labels $\mathsf c_K\in[\mathsf b,L'\mathsf b)$ dense. In the scheme of $L'$ let $\ell_f\in2L'^{\mathbb N}$, $\ell_f\ge24L'\ell_0$, $w_0=\ell_f/2L'$, $f(x)=\prod_i\max\{0,1-|x_i|/w_0\}$ (the tent), and $\mathsf M_k(\ell;c)=\|\mathcal O_k(f)-\mu_{k,\ell,L'^kc}(\mathcal O_k(f))\|_{\mathrm{ch},\ell}$. (i) $\mathsf M_k(\ell;\cdot)^8$ is a polynomial in torus cumulants of orders $2$ to $8$, which by (M4)(i) at $L'$ converges, uniformly on $[\mathsf b,L'\mathsf b]$, to a continuous function; so $\mathsf M_f=\sup_{k\in\mathbb N,\ c\in[\mathsf b,L'\mathsf b]}\mathsf M_k(\ell_f;c)<\infty$. (ii) At the labels $\mathsf c_K$, BI gives $\mathsf e(l_K)\le x_0$ at $\beta=L'^{k(K)}\mathsf c_K$ with $l_K=\ell_0L^K/2$, and a fine cell has $\mathsf h=\ell_fL'^{k(K)}/2$ layers with $\mathsf h/l_K\ge\ell_f/L'\ell_0\ge24$; Lem.~\ref{C-361-12} with $\ell_c=d\ell_f$, $d=L'^j$, gives
\[
\mathsf M_{k(K)}(\ell_c;\mathsf c_K)\le\epsilon_\star(d)=1.343\,\mathsf M_f\,\theta^{(d-1)\ell_f/8L'\ell_0}.
\]
(iii) Let $x(c)=L'^{-3}D_{L'}(N)$, $N=\ell_cL'^k$, at $\beta=L'^kc$. Since $\partial_\beta\log Z(n^3)$ is $-3n^3$ times the mean plaquette variable, which is the same for all plaquettes of a torus, and the translates of the tent are a partition of unity,
\[
x'(c)=-(\ell_c/w_0)^3\bigl[\mu_{k,\ell_c,\beta}(\mathcal O_k(f))-\mu_{k,L'\ell_c,\beta}(\mathcal O_k(f))\bigr],\qquad\ell_c/w_0=2L'd .
\]
Wherever $x\le0.0064$, $\delta(N^3)\le(L'/(L'-1))^3x\le0.0086$ by Thm.~\ref{C-361-6}(1), and Prop.~\ref{C-361-9}(c) bounds the bracket by $0.16\,\mathsf M_k(\ell_c;c)$; so $|x'|\le0.0058/((L'-1)\mathsf b)$ there as soon as $\mathsf M_k(\ell_c;c)\le\epsilon_{\rm req}(d)=0.036/[(2L'd)^3(L'-1)\mathsf b]$. The required smallness shrinks with $d$ like $d^{-3}$, while $\epsilon_\star(d)/\epsilon_{\rm req}(d)$ is a constant times $d^3\theta^{(d-1)\ell_f/8L'\ell_0}$, which tends to $0$ as $d=L'^j\to\infty$: fix $d$ with $\epsilon_\star(d)\le\frac12\epsilon_{\rm req}(d)$. By (i) the functions $\mathsf M_k(\ell_c;\cdot)$ converge uniformly on $[\mathsf b,L'\mathsf b]$ to a continuous limit; at the labels $\mathsf c_K$, $K\ge K_0$, which are dense, with $k(K)\to\infty$, they are at most $\frac12\epsilon_{\rm req}(d)$; so the limit is at most $\frac12\epsilon_{\rm req}(d)$ everywhere, and there is $\bar k\ge k(K_0)$ with $\mathsf M_k(\ell_c;c)\le\epsilon_{\rm req}(d)$ for all $c\in[\mathsf b,L'\mathsf b]$ and all $k\ge\bar k$. (iv) At each $k\ge\bar k$ there is $K$ with $k(K)=k$, and Prop.~\ref{C-361-8}(b) gives $x(\mathsf c_K)<0.000514$; by the mean value theorem the component of $\{x\le0.0064\}$ that contains $\mathsf c_K$ carries $x\le0.006314$, so it is all of $[\mathsf b,L'\mathsf b]$.

Hence $\delta(N^3)\le0.008625$ for all $c$ and all $k\ge\bar k$, and every $\beta\ge\beta_0=L'^{\bar k}\mathsf b$ equals $L'^kc$ with $l=N\le C_+\beta$, $C_+=\ell_c/\mathsf b$. Of $L$ the argument uses only that $\log L/\log L'$ is irrational.

\emph{Step 8: Thm.~\ref{C-361-4}(2), (2$'$), (3).} At $\beta=L^K\mathsf b'\ge\beta_0$ there is $l\le C_+\beta$ with $\mathsf e(l)\le0.069$, and Prop.~\ref{C-361-8}(b) gives $\delta(N'^3)\le0.13736\cdot0.8901^{24}<0.008625$, so $\mathsf e(N')\le0.069$, for all $N'\ge48l$. Since $L^{m+K}\ge48C_+\mathsf b'L^K\ge48l$, the cube of BI at the side $2L^m$ qualifies; on $[\mathsf b_-,\mathsf b_+]$ take $L^m\ge48C_+\mathsf b_+$ and the threshold of $\mathsf b_-$. If BI holds at one label, it holds at all: the set of the labels is empty or $(0,\infty)$. (2$'$): $\mathsf M<\infty$ by Prop.~\ref{C-361-30} and (M4)(i). Fix $K\ge\max\{K_0,1\}$ and write $\delta(s)$ for $\delta_K(\ell_1)$ at the label $s$. The derivative of the excess in the label is $L^K$ times the sum over the plaquettes of the torus of the differences between the mean plaquette variable on the torus and in the periodic Gibbs state at the label $s$ (Prop.~\ref{C-361-10}(a)); all plaquettes having one such difference, by the symmetries of both laws, it is a multiple $R_K$, $|R_K|\le1458$, of the difference of the means of $\mathcal O_K(f)$ on the torus and in that state:
\[
\delta(\mathsf b_2)-\delta(\mathsf b_1)=-\int_{\mathsf b_1}^{\mathsf b_2}R_K\bigl[\mu_{K,\ell_1,L^Ks}(\mathcal O_K(f))-\nu_{K,s}(\mathcal O_K(f))\bigr]\,\mathrm{d}s .
\]
While $\delta(s)\le0.008625$, Prop.~\ref{C-361-9}(c) bounds the bracket by $0.17516\,\mathsf M$, with constants free of $K$. At $s=\mathsf b$, $\delta(\mathsf b)<0.13736\,\theta^{\ell_1/\ell_0}\le0.13736\cdot0.8901^{75}<0.000025$; so $\delta$ cannot reach $0.008625$ within $\eta$ of $\mathsf b$, at every cutoff. The continuity and the limits along labels follow from Step~2, made with a supremum over the labels of $[\mathsf b-\eta,\mathsf b+\eta]$ (one side $2\ell_1$, one threshold, $\theta=0.8901$), and the continuity in the label of (M4)(i). For the second form put $N=\ell_1^\flat/a_K$. At $\mathsf b$, Prop.~\ref{C-361-8}(b) gives $D_L(N)<L^3\,0.13736\,\theta^{\ell_1^\flat/\ell_0}\le0.03$.

At a label $s$ with $D_L(N)\le0.069$, $\delta(N^3)\le0.069/(L-1)^3$ by Thm.~\ref{C-361-6}(1), and the derivative of $D_L(N)=L^3F(N^3)-F((LN)^3)$ in the label is $-L^3R_K$ times the difference of the means of $\mathcal O_K(f^\flat)$ on the tori $\ell_1^\flat$ and $L\ell_1^\flat$, with the number $R_K$ of the first form, now for $f^\flat$, $|R_K|\le1458$; Prop.~\ref{C-361-9}(c) bounds that difference by $4.84\,[Q'(Q'-1)]^{1/2}\mathsf M^\flat\le0.010813\,\mathsf M^\flat$. So $D_L(N)$ rises by at most $0.03$ within $r$ of $\mathsf b$ and stays below $0.06$; then $\mathsf e(N)\le\frac8{L^3}D_L(N)<0.48/L^3<2.2\cdot10^{-4}$ by Thm.~\ref{C-361-6}(1), and Prop.~\ref{C-361-8}(b) at $l=N$, with $\theta_1=12.9\cdot2.2\cdot10^{-4}$, gives $\mathsf e(L^zN/2)<0.3702\,\theta_1^{L^z/4}\le6.1\cdot10^{-9}$, which is the inequality of BI at the side $L^z\ell_1^\flat$. (3): Prop.~\ref{C-361-10} at this $l$: the rate $\theta^{n/l}$ with $\theta=0.8901$ and $l\le C_+\beta$ is at most $e^{-c_*n/\beta}$; the transfer operator is the operator $T_\nu$ of the setting, whose matrix elements are the numbers $h_{AB}(n)$ of Prop.~\ref{C-361-10}(f): at $\theta=0.8901$ and $l\le C_+\beta$, $\ker(1-T_\nu)=\mathbb C\Omega$ and $\|T_\nu\|\le0.8901^{1/l}\le e^{-c_*/\beta}$ on $\Omega^\perp$; and Prop.~\ref{C-361-11}(a) with $l\le C_+\beta$ gives the flux quotient; Prop.~\ref{C-361-11}(d) gives the slopes, $\sigma^+l^2=\frac12\log\frac1{0.8901}+0.4175\ge0.4757$.

The labels $a_K\beta$ of all first-passage data $(K,\beta)$ at $g$ lie in the window $\bigl(g^{-2}+B_\sharp\frac{L-2}{L-1},\,L(g^{-2}+\bar B)\bigr]$ (\YMMref{(1531)}{615} in Prop.~\YMMref{74.1}{615}), so at a datum with $\beta\ge\beta_0$ the cube of the side $2la_K\le2C_+\beta a_K\le2C_+L(g^{-2}+\bar B)=\ell_0^g$ satisfies the inequality: Thm.~\ref{C-361-3}(1) and Step~2 hold there with $\ell_0^g$ for $\ell_0$ and $0.8901$ for $\theta$, uniformly over these data, the seminorms of Prop.~\ref{C-361-30} being bounded over the window.

\emph{Step 9: Thm.~\ref{C-361-4}(4).} On $a\mathbb Z^3$ the weight does not contain $a$, and $\mathcal O_a(f(\cdot/t))=t^{-1}\mathcal O_{a/t}(f)$; hence
\[
\kappa_n\bigl(\beta,a/t;X\bigr)=t^n\,\kappa_n\bigl(\beta,a;X_t\bigr)
\]
for the cumulants in the unique periodic Gibbs state at $\beta\ge\beta_0$. By Step~8, BI holds near every label with one side and one threshold, and Step~2, taken with a supremum over a compact set of labels and of dilations of $X$, gives one limit along every sequence of pairs whose labels converge, continuous in the label and the dilation. The supremum over the dilations is had through the rate of (M4)(i): by~the Cauchy estimate in the proof of Thm.~\YMMref{AS}{813} in Thm.~\textup{\YMMref{AS}{813}}, on one torus and on a compact interval of labels, $|S^T_{n;K',\ell,L^{K'}\mathsf b}(Y)-S^T_{n;K,\ell,L^K\mathsf b}(Y)|\le C\,K^{2\mathfrak p_0(n+1)+\frac12}L^{-K/10}\prod_i\|y_i\|_\sharp$ for all $K'\ge K$ above a threshold, where $C$ and the threshold depend on $n$, the side, the interval and a floor of the spread of the supports of $Y=(y_1,\dots,y_n)$, and on $Y$ otherwise only through these norms.

For $Y=X_{t'}$ with $t'$ in a compact interval $J''\subset(0,\infty)$, 
\[
\|f_i(\cdot/t')\|_\sharp\le\max\{\sup|f_i|,40M(\inf J'')^{-1}\operatorname{Lip}f_i\}
\]
 and the spread is at least $\inf J''$ times that of $X$; so the torus cumulants converge uniformly in the label and the dilation. At a fixed cutoff they are continuous in both, being finite sums with the coefficients $f_i(x(p)/t')$; so the limit is jointly continuous, and the seminorms $M_I$ of Step~2 are bounded uniformly in $t'\in J''$ in the same way. In the scheme of $L'$ the lattices of the line of $\mathsf b$ are the lattices of the dense labels $\mathsf c_K$, dilated by $\mathsf b/\mathsf c_K$; so the limit of the scheme of $L'$ at every label $c$ is the dilation of $\sigma_{\mathsf b}$ by $c/\mathsf b$.

The dilations by $L$ and by $L'$, which are trivial in their own schemes, generate a dense subgroup of $(0,\infty)$, and by continuity $\sigma_{tc}$ is the dilation of $\sigma_c$ for every real $t$; the identity above reduces arbitrary real spacings to the scheme of $L$, and $H_n$ is $S^{\sigma_1}_n$, so $S^{\sigma_c}_n(X)=c^{-n}H_n(X_{1/c})$. At $c\in I(g)$, Step~4 identifies $\sigma_c$; the gap of $\sigma_{tc}$ is that of $\sigma_c$ divided by $t$.

\emph{Step 10: Thm.~\ref{C-361-4}(5).} For $\varphi$ vanishing outside $v+[-\rho,\rho]^3$ the insertion of the rotation weighted by $\varphi$ depends only on the bonds within $2a_K$ of that cube and is bounded by $3402(1+|v|_\infty)\rho^4L^{4K}|\omega|\sup|\varphi|$, and $\sup|\mathcal O_K(f)|\le162\rho^3L^{4K}\sup|f|$ for $f$ vanishing outside $v+[-\rho,\rho]^3$; so in every state, for $\chi$ vanishing outside $v+[-\rho,\rho]^3$ and the $f_i$ outside $v+[-R,R]^3$, $|\mathfrak U|\le\mathsf c_n(1+\mathsf b)(1+|v|_\infty)\rho^4R^{3n}L^{(4n+5)K}|\omega|\sup|\chi|\prod\sup|f_i|$, with $\mathsf c_n=3402\cdot162^n\,\mathsf F_{n+1}$ and $\mathsf F_m=\sum_\pi|\pi|!$, the sum over the partitions $\pi$ of $\{1,\dots,m\}$; in the theorem $\rho=R$. (i) \emph{Torus against state.} The bulk term is a polynomial in means of products of local functions of one cube; by Thm.~\ref{C-361-3}(1)(c), in total variation, on all tori $\ell\ge\ell''$ and in $\nu_K$ it agrees up to $2.164\,\mathsf c_n(1+\mathsf b)(1+|v|_\infty)\rho^4R^{3n}L^{(4n+5)K}e^{-m_*\ell''/4}$ times the sup norms, which is $\le$ the same expression with $L^{-K}$ for $L^{(4n+5)K}e^{-m_*\ell''/4}$ once $\ell''\ge\Lambda_0K$, $\Lambda_0=4(4n+6)\log L/m_*$. (ii) \emph{The place.} For a state invariant under $a_K\mathbb Z^3$, translating the tuple by $v$ adds the translation $\omega v=\sum_\lambda v_\lambda\,\omega e_\lambda$ to the generator of the insertion, and the insertion of the translation by the vector $\omega e_\lambda$ is the difference of the bulk terms of the tuple moved by $e_\lambda$ and of the tuple, both carried by $[-R-1,R+1]^3$; summed over the components of $v$ this gives the factor $1+2|v|_1$. (iii) So it suffices to bound the bulk term of tuples carried by a fixed cube about the origin on one side in $[\Lambda_0K,L\Lambda_0K]$ of $\mathfrak L(g)$, which by (i) serves for $\nu_K$ and all larger sides, and on the sides $\ell\le L\Lambda_0K$ a power of $\ell$ is a power of $K$.

There $\mathfrak U$ of~\YMMref{(2108)}{782} is split as follows, with the objects of (M8). A joint cumulant with the $\mathcal O_K(f_i)$ is the derivative in the $z_i$ of a mean at the source $w_z=\sum_iz_if_i$, so the bulk term of~\YMMref{(2107)}{782} in equation~\YMMref{(2107)}{782} and the source calculation in the proof of Prop.~\YMMref{112.1}{782} is $-\partial^n_z$ at $z=0$ of the mean at the source $w_z$ of the bulk insertion $(\mathfrak S_{\omega,\chi}+\mathfrak K_{\omega,\chi})[\beta-a_K^{-1}w_z]$ (equation~\YMMref{(2107)}{782} and the source calculation in the proof of Prop.~\YMMref{112.1}{782}). With the orbital potential $\Psi_\rho(p)$ and the remainder of third order $\mathfrak r^\sharp_\rho(p)=\mathfrak r_\rho(p)-\Psi_\rho(p)+\Psi_\rho(p_-)$ of {\cite[\S{}H]{YMM2}}, the summation by parts of {\cite[Prop.~H.1]{YMM2}} writes this insertion as the sum of three members, affine in $z$: the spin part $\mathfrak S_\omega[\phi_z]$, $\phi_z=\beta\chi-a_K^{-1}w_z$; the member $-\sum_p\sum_\rho\tilde c_\rho(x(p))\Psi_\rho(p)$, $\tilde c_\rho(y)=(\omega y)_\rho\,a_K^{-1}[\phi_z(y+a_Ke_\rho)-\phi_z(y)]$, of order $2$ in the curvature with the weight $\beta$; and the cubic member $\mathfrak K^\sharp[\phi_z\,\omega y]$ of~{\cite[eq.~297]{YMM2}}, of order $3$ with the weight $\beta/a_K=\mathsf bL^{2K}$.

Accordingly $\mathfrak U=\mathfrak U^\sharp+(\mathfrak U-\mathfrak U^\sharp)$ with
\[
\mathfrak U^\sharp_{\omega,\chi}(f)=-\beta\bigl\langle\mathfrak K^\sharp[\chi\,\omega y];\mathcal O_K(f_1);\dots;\mathcal O_K(f_n)\bigr\rangle+a_K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\bigl\langle\mathfrak K^\sharp[f_i\,\omega y];(\mathcal O_K(f_l))_{l\ne i}\bigr\rangle .
\]
\emph{All but the cubic member.} Use the exact lattice decomposition in Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(b,c,e,f), as in Step~8 of the proof of Thm.~\ref{C-360-4}. For $\varphi\in\{\chi,f_1,\dots,f_n\}$, antisymmetry of $\omega$ rewrites $a_K^{-1}\mathfrak S_\omega[\varphi]$ as an order-$2$ entry with weights $k^\varphi_{b,p,\rho}=a_K^{-1}(\varphi(x(p))-\varphi(x_b))\sum_\lambda\omega_{\rho\lambda}a_K^{-1}(x_b-x(p))_\lambda$, bounded by $|\omega|\operatorname{Lip}\varphi/4$. The bilinear orbital entry has the vector weight $\mathsf k^{\varphi,\rho}(y)=(\omega y)_\rho\nabla^+_\rho\varphi(y)$, whose Lipschitz norm is at most $5|\omega|(1+\ell)\|\varphi\|_{C^{1,1}}$. Lem.~\ref{C-360-8}(c) gives $\mathfrak J^{\rm bl}[\mathsf k]=-\mathfrak N[\mathsf k]/4+\sum_{v=1}^5\mathfrak J_v[\mathsf k]-c_{\mathsf k}/4$: the five entries have orders $2,2,2,3,4$, and only the last two carry $\beta$. The null term is evaluated by the contact formulas (N3), (N4) of that lemma. They leave numbers, action densities and order-$2$ entries without a factor $\beta$; the numbers drop from the cumulants. Terms absorbing all the sources vanish, and merging the absorbed supports leaves spread at least $\mathsf d-3a_K\ge\mathsf d/2$. Thus Lem.~\ref{C-360-18}, applied in its spread form, bounds every remaining term.

For the dependence on $\ell$, use the proof of Lem.~\ref{C-360-18} before its constants are collected. A local insertion of order $m$ is carried to depth $u=\lceil\phi K\rceil$, $\phi=(\frac12-c_1)/(3n+4)$. The entry contributes at most a factor $\ell^3$ from its sites, and the source radii are $(2nN_t\mathsf C_t\|f_q\|_\sharp)^{-1}$, with $N_t=\ell^3L^{3u}$ and $\mathsf C_t\le CK^{2\mathfrak p_0}$. Their Cauchy cost contributes $\ell^{3n}$; the powers of $L$ are $L^{(3n+4)u-\mathsf g_mK}$, where $\mathsf g_2=1$ and $\mathsf g_m=3/2$ for $m\ge3$. The factors $\beta$ in the orders $3,4$ leave the decay $L^{-c_1K}$. The discarded mass of the definitions preceding Prop.~\YMMref{115.2}{806} has the form $2M^{-3}\ell^3L^{3u}\exp[-c\{\log(L^u\mathsf b')\}^{2\mathfrak p_0}+C_g\ell^3]$. Since $\mathfrak p_0\ge13$, the labels lie in a compact first-passage interval and $\ell\le L\Lambda_0K$, this mass and its fixed-order moment factors decay faster than every $L^{-AK}$, uniformly in these sides. The locality remainders have the same property. Collecting the weights from the preceding paragraph gives, times the norms, $|\mathfrak U-\mathfrak U^\sharp|\le C\ell^{3(n+1)}(R+5)|\omega|K^{(2n+1)\mathfrak p_0}L^{-c_1K}$ for every $0<c_1<\frac12$ on $2R+4\le\ell\le L\Lambda_0K$, uniformly over first-passage data at $g$, with $C$ free of the side.

\emph{The cubic member} obeys an estimate on all the sides at once, the bound (M7), which is Lem.~\ref{C-360-19} of the section on plane fields and the stress tensor (\S\ref{C-360-1}) taken at the field $\chi\,\omega y$: for $n\ge2$, $\mathsf d>0$ and $\rho_0\ge1$ there are $C_\sharp$ and a threshold, depending on $g$, $n$, $\mathsf d$, $\rho_0$ and the constants and on no side, such that for all real $\chi,f_i\in C^{1,1}$ vanishing outside $[-\rho_0,\rho_0]^3$, $\chi$ covering the $f_i$, the supports of the $f_i$ at pairwise sup distances $\ge\mathsf d$,
\[
|\mathfrak U^\sharp_{\omega,\chi}(f)|\le C_\sharp|\omega|L^{-K/16}\|\chi\|_{C^{1,1}}\prod_i\|f_i\|_{C^{1,1}}
\]
at all first-passage data at $g$ with $K$ above the threshold, on all sides $\ell\ge2\rho_0+2$ of $\mathfrak L(g)$. It is proved in three steps, as in the idea of the proof of (M7). On one torus, the conditional mean of the cubic insertion given the block field of the level $K-\lceil\phi'K\rceil$, $\phi'>0$ small, under the small-field chain of Thm.~\YMMref{D}{8}, differs from a constant by at most a power of $K$ times $L^{-cK}$, for every $c<\frac1{14}$ (Lem.~\ref{C-360-9}(b)): the density is of third order, $|\mathfrak r^\sharp_{\rho(p)}(p)|\le C_{\rm orb}\,\bar a(p)^{3/2}$ ({\cite[eq.~295]{YMM2}}), plain power counting against the weight $\mathsf bL^{2K}$ falls short by the factor $a_K^{-1/2}$, and the parity under the lattice mirrors, the covariance of the renormalisation step and a Hölder bound of a background against its mirror image win this factor back.

The joint cumulants of the insertion with the sources then obey the same bound, for every $c<\frac1{14}$, by the two-constants inequality of Lem.~\YMMref{116.2}{809} in the source variables; this is the bound of one torus, Lem.~\ref{C-360-10}. Last, the bound on one torus serves on the finitely many sides of $\mathfrak L(g)$ from $2\rho_0+2$ up to a fixed side $\ell'$, where (M7) is Lem.~\ref{C-360-10}, and it passes from $\ell'$ to every larger side (Lem.~\ref{C-360-19}) by the chessboard estimate (M2) on the board of side $\ell'/2$, which writes the difference of a cumulant on the torus $\ell$ and on the torus $\ell'$ through cumulants on the torus $\ell'$ of mirror copies of the entries that join cells, every block that holds a copy of the cubic insertion carrying the small factor, at the cost of the factor $e^{(\ell'/2)^3(p_{\ell'}-p_\ell)}\le e^{\delta_K(\ell')/8}$ of the fine-to-coarse form, which Thm.~\ref{C-361-6}(5)(a), (6) bound at the fixed side $\ell'$, uniformly in the cutoff and over the window of the labels at $g$.

With $\rho_0=R+1$ the sum is $\le C|\omega|K^{p'}L^{-\kappa K}$ times the norms for every $\kappa<\frac1{16}$. The condition $|v|_\infty+R+2\le\ell/4$ keeps the moved tuples and the insertion away from the seam of the torus, the planes $x_\mu=\pm\ell/2$ along which the cube $[-\ell/2,\ell/2]^3$ is closed up.

\emph{Step 11: Thm.~\ref{C-361-5}(1)--(4).} (1) is Prop.~\ref{C-361-13}(b), (c); the statements on a height $y$ follow from $|X_{K'}-X_K|\le\eta_K$ for $K'\ge K\ge K_\star$ and $\eta_K\to0$. (2) If $D_L(N)\le\frac{L^3}8x$ with $x\le0.069$, then $\mathsf e(N)\le D_2(N)\le\frac8{L^3}D_L(N)\le x$, because $D_L(N)-\frac{L^3}8D_2(N)=\frac{L^3}8\delta((2N)^3)-\delta((LN)^3)\ge0$ by the monotone density; Prop.~\ref{C-361-8} at $l=N$ gives $\mathsf e(2^kN)\le(12.9x)^{2^k}/12.9=\epsilon$, and since $2^kN\le LN/2<2^{k+1}N$,
\[
\mathsf e(LN/2)\le2\,\delta(\tfrac{LN}2,LN,LN)\le\Bigl(\frac L{2^{k+1}}\Bigr)^3\bigl[\epsilon+\tfrac{20}7\epsilon^2\bigr]=\Phi_L(x),\qquad D_L(2l)\le L^3\delta((2l)^3)\le\tfrac{20}7L^3\mathsf e(l)^2 .
\]
At $N=\ell/La_K$ we have $LN/2=\ell/2a_K$, and by (1) $X_K\le X_{K_1}+\eta_{K_1}\le y_1$ for all $K\ge K_1$; as $\Phi_L(x_1)\le x_0$, this gives BI$[\mathsf b,\ell,K_1;x_0]$; with $y_0$, $\mathsf e(\ell/La_K)\le x_0$, which is BI at the side $2\ell/L$ with $c=2$, and Thm.~\ref{C-361-3} holds at every side $2cL^{m_0}$. Conversely BI at the side $2\ell/L$ has $l_K=\ell/La_K$, and $X_K(\mathsf b,L\ell)=D_L(Ll_K)\le L^3\delta((Ll_K)^3)\le L^3\bar\delta_{x_0}(L)$ by the proof of Prop.~\ref{C-361-8}(b). The bracket: the upper members are Thm.~\ref{C-361-6}(1) at $l=\ell/2a_K$, $2l/L=\ell/La_K$; the lower member is the contrapositive of $D_L(2l)\le\frac{20}7L^3\mathsf e(l)^2$ for $\mathsf e(l)\le0.069$, at $2l=\ell/a_K$.

So BI gives $X_K(\mathsf b,L\ell)\le\frac{20}7L^3x_0^2$, and (1) excludes this for $K\ge K_1$ when $X_{K_1}(\mathsf b,L\ell)>\frac{20}7L^3x_0^2+\eta_{K_1}$; the members of the bracket are continuous and monotone in $X_K$, and $X_K\to X_\infty$, which gives the bracket for $\liminf_K\mathsf e_K$ and $\limsup_K\mathsf e_K$. (3) At the single cutoff $K_1$, Prop.~\ref{C-361-8}(b) at $l=l_{K_1}$ gives $X_{K_1}(\mathsf b,L^i\ell_0)=D_L(2L^{i-1}l_{K_1})\le L^3\bar\delta_{x_0}(2L^{i-1})$; with the margin, (1) gives $X_K\le y_1$ for all $K\ge K_1$, and (2) applies. At $i=2$, $\bar\delta_{x_0}(2L)<8\mathsf c_0\theta^{L}\le0.13736\,\theta^L$, which at $x_0=0.069$ and $L\ge33$ is at most $0.0030$; and for $L\ge33$, $2^k\ge16$, so $\Phi_L(0.05)\le8\cdot1.01\,(0.645)^{16}/12.9<0.069$ and $x_1\ge0.05$, $\frac18x_1\ge0.00625$: the margin condition holds once $\eta_{K_1}\le0.003L^3$.

At $i=1$ it never holds at $x_0=0.069$, as $\bar\delta_{0.069}(2)=\frac{20}7\cdot0.069^2>\frac18\cdot0.069$. (4) (iii) and (1) give $X_K\le y_0$ for $K\ge K_1$, hence $\mathsf e(\ell/La_K)\le x_0$, which is BI at the side $\ell_0=2\ell/L\in2\cdot2L^{\mathbb Z}$; (i) gives $X_K(\mathsf b,\ell)\le L^3\bar\delta_{x_0}(2\ell/L\ell_0)<0.13736L^3\theta^{\ell/L\ell_0}$ for $\ell\ge L\ell_0$ by Prop.~\ref{C-361-8}(b), hence (iv); (iv) implies (ii); and (ii) implies (iii) by (1).

\emph{Step 12: Thm.~\ref{C-361-5}(5), (6).} (5): the reduction, requiring the interacting Hessian estimate, applies Prop.~\ref{C-361-14} at $\underline s=(\ell_0/2,\ell_0,\ell_0)$, $z=0$, $l=\ell_0$, where $|\underline s|/l^3=\frac12$, gives
\[
\mathsf e_{K+1}-\mathsf e_K=2\Bigl[\log Z_{K+1}(\underline s;\mathsf b)-\log Z_K(\underline s;\mathsf b)-\tfrac12\bigl(\log Z_{K+1,\ell_0}-\log Z_{K,\ell_0}\bigr)\Bigr],
\]
so $|\mathsf e_{K+1}-\mathsf e_K|\le2CL^{-K/10}$ uniformly on $J$, and Lem.~\ref{C-361-26} gives the rest. (6): $D_L(\ell/a_K)=X_K(\mathsf b,L\ell)$ converges uniformly on compact sets of labels by (1), with the rate of Prop.~\ref{C-361-13}(b); the pairs $(\ell/a_K,L^K\mathsf b)$ depend on $(\ell,\mathsf b)$ only through $\ell/\mathsf b$ up to the index of the cutoff, so $D_\infty$ is a continuous function of $t$. The series for $\delta_K(\ell)$ of Prop.~\ref{C-361-7}(c) at $q=L$, $\delta_K(\ell)=\sum_sL^{-3(s+1)}D_L(L^s\ell/a_K)$, has the majorant $L^{-3(s+1)}D_L(L^s\ell/a_K)\le L^{-3s}\delta_K(L^s\ell)\le C(t)\,L^{-s}$, uniformly in the large $K$, with $C(t)$ bounded on compact sets, by the bounds at a fixed cutoff of Thm.~\ref{C-361-6}(5)(a) and (6), whose proofs do not use the present clause; dominated convergence gives $\delta_K(\ell)\to\delta_\infty(t)$, locally uniformly, and $L^3\delta_\infty(t)-\delta_\infty(Lt)=D_\infty(t)$; the inequalities $(L-1)^3\delta\le D_L\le L^3\delta$ of Thm.~\ref{C-361-6}(1) pass to the limit.
