\emph{One function for all block sizes.} Let $L'$ be a second admitted blocking factor with $\log L/\log L'$ irrational. At one coupling, cubes $N\le M$ with $M/N\le\rho$ have $\delta(M^3)\le\rho^3\delta(N^3)$ by the monotone density. Pass to a subsequence of the lattices $(N,\beta)$ that converge to $\delta_\infty^{(L)}(t)$, and choose along it cubes $M=2L'^{j}$ with $M/N\to\rho_0\in[1,\rho]$, which the density of $\{L'^j/L^i\}$ allows; the lattices $(M,\beta)$ are lattices of the scheme of $L'$ whose labels converge, so $\delta^{(L')}_\infty(\rho_0t)\le\rho^3\delta^{(L)}_\infty(t)$. Letting $\rho\to1$ and using the continuity, $\delta^{(L')}_\infty\le\delta^{(L)}_\infty$, and by symmetry the two are equal. The same comparison of nearly equal cubes, now with the lattice inequalities of Prop.~\ref{C-361-7}(c) and Thm.~\ref{C-361-6}(1),(2) between the cubes $N$ and $M=\lfloor\rho N\rfloor$, gives that $t^{-3}\delta_\infty(t)$ does not increase, the bound $(3\rho^2-3\rho+1)$ for real $\rho$, and the alternative for real $t\ge2t_0$.

\emph{Positivity.} $\delta_\infty\ge0$ from the series. At every $t$, choosing by a dilation a label in $I(g_1)\cup I(g_2)=(\gamma_W^{-2}+\bar B,\kappa_0]$ and the side $\ell=t\mathsf b$, Thm.~\ref{C-361-6}(1), (3) give $8\delta_K(\ell)\ge\mathsf e(\ell/a_K)\ge\min\{0.069,0.0775\,e^{-2.6\ell/\mathsf d_\circ}\}$ at all large $K$, so $\delta_\infty(t)>0$; this uses Thms.~\YMMref{AJ}{673} and~\YMMref{AD}{607} through (M5)(iii). \emph{The case of BI.} If BI holds at $(\mathsf b,\ell_0)$, then $\delta_\infty(\ell/\mathsf b)\le0.13736\,\theta^{\ell/\ell_0}$ for large $\ell$ by Thm.~\ref{C-361-3}(1); conversely, $\delta_\infty(t_0)<0.008625$ and $\ell/\mathsf b=t_0$ give $\delta_K(\ell)\le0.008625$ for all large $K$, hence $\mathsf e(\ell/a_K)\le0.069$: BI at the side $2\ell$.

If $D_{q,\infty}(t_0)<(q-1)^3x_0/8$ for an admitted $q$, then $\delta_\infty(t_0)<x_0/8\le0.008625$, as $(q-1)^3\delta_\infty\le D_{q,\infty}$. In the second case $\delta_\infty<0.008625$ on a whole interval $[t_2',Lt_2']$, and the uniform convergence on the compact set of labels $[\mathsf b,L\mathsf b]$ at one side gives, for every real $\beta$ above a threshold, a cube $N\le C\beta$ with $\delta(N^3)\le0.008625$: Thm.~\ref{C-361-4}(1) a second time.

\emph{Step 13: Thm.~\ref{C-361-5}(7).} The conditions of the list (H3), each attached to its constant, are inequalities between numbers; the one that binds $L$ alone, with its constant $4096$, is $L>48\cdot4096^2e^{24}\approx21\,331\,858\,733\,892\,671\,081.7\ldots$, and every odd integer above it is admitted. The list also forces floors on the other constants that enter $K_\star$ and $\eta_K$: $r\ge2$, $\mathfrak p_0\ge13$ (so $\mathsf p_0\ge26.5$), $M\ge L^7$, $\gamma^{-2}\ge(2L)^{1602}$, $A_0\ge256L^5A_1$, and three constants: $\mathsf c_{\rm a}=\mathsf C_{\rm ex}$, the expansion constant preceding equation~\YMMref{(705)}{360}, with $\mathsf C_{\rm ex}\ge8e^8$; $\mathsf c_{\rm c}=\kappa>0$, the constant of the list that enters $\lambda_{\rm out}=(1+4\beta_{\rm s})\kappa$ of~\YMMref{(889)}{415}; and $\mathsf c_{\rm b}=\lambda_1=\lambda_{\rm out}+2^3c_{\rm w}+\mathsf C_{\rm ex}+\lambda_{\rm s}$ of~\YMMref{(705)}{360}, where $c_{\rm w}=c_{\rm v}+3$, $c_{\rm v}=2+\mathsf C_{\rm ex}c_G(LM)^3u$ with $c_G=\mathsf C_{\rm ex}(\gamma_{\rm r}^{-1}+c_{\rm r}^2)\ge2\mathsf C_{\rm ex}$ and $(LM)^3u=\mathsf u^*_{\rm S}=3+c_{\rm r}+\mathsf u_{\rm G}>4$ by~\YMMref{(889)}{415}, so that $\mathsf c_{\rm b}>\mathsf c_{\rm c}+64\,\mathsf c_{\rm a}^2\ge\mathsf c_{\rm c}+4096\,e^{16}$, where $4096\,e^{16}\approx3.6397\cdot10^{10}$.

The threshold $K_\star$ is the least cutoff at which the conditions of (M4)(ii)--(iii) on the construction constants hold for both tori, with the thresholds $K_{\rm bf}$ of (M4)(ii) on both after the dilation by $z$, as in Thm.~\ref{C-361-5}(1), together with the comparison of Prop.~\ref{C-361-13}. At their floors these conditions give $(K-z)\log L>9\,\mathsf c_{\rm b}>36864\,e^{16}\approx3.2757\cdot10^{11}$ for every $K\ge K_\star(\mathsf b,\ell)$. Indeed, at the dilated data $(L^z\mathsf b,L^z\ell)$, whose cutoff $K-z$ is written $K$ in this sentence: the number $\kappa_{\rm b}$ of~\YMMref{(2181)}{803} is $w_\star e^{-\lambda_V}/32M^3$ with $w_\star=w_0e^{-4\lambda_1}/(\mathsf C_{\rm ex}(L+2)^3S_{\rm s})$, $w_0=(4S_{\rm s}L^3)^{-1}$ (equation~\YMMref{(705)}{360}), so $\kappa_{\rm b}^{-1}>L^6M^3e^{4\mathsf c_{\rm b}}$; the condition $\epsilon_{\rm sh}\le\frac1{20}$ of (k3) forces $\exp[\frac14\kappa_{\rm b}A_1^2\mathsf y_{[u]}]\ge60$, so $A_1^2\mathsf y_{[u]}>16/\kappa_{\rm b}$ and $A_0^2\mathsf y_{[u]}>L^{16}M^3e^{4\mathsf c_{\rm b}}$; then $\epsilon_{\rm cl}\le\frac1{20}$ forces $L^{(K-s)/2}\ge80A_0^2\mathsf y_{[u]}>e^{4\mathsf c_{\rm b}}$, $s=\lceil K/9\rceil$, and as $K-s\le\frac89K$, $K\log L>9\,\mathsf c_{\rm b}$.

So the small cube of the criterion of (2) has $2L^{m+K-1}\ge2L^{K-z+1}$ sites a side, as $m+z\ge2$, hence more than $e^{9\mathsf c_{\rm b}}>10^{1.4226\cdot10^{11}}$. Where the margin $\eta_K$ is below the height of the criterion, as the margin condition of (3) requires of $\eta_{K_1}(\mathsf b,L^2\ell_0)$, the same conditions, with $\mathsf C_{\rm bf}\ge64\mathsf K_{\rm w}c_\rho^2A_0^2\mathsf y_{[1]}L^{7/2}$ from~\textup{(\ref{IV-62-65})} and $\mathsf y_{[1]}(K-z)^{2\mathfrak p_0}\ge\mathsf y_{[u]}$, make $L^{(K-z)/10}$ larger than $e^{4\mathsf c_{\rm b}}\ge e^{4(\mathsf c_{\rm b}-\mathsf c_{\rm c})}$ times a power of $L$ and of $M$, and $e^{4(\mathsf c_{\rm b}-\mathsf c_{\rm c})}>e^{256\,\mathsf c_{\rm a}^2}\ge e^{16384\,e^{16}}$; so $(K-z)\log L>163840\,e^{16}\approx1.4559\cdot10^{12}$.

At the cutoff of (3) the half side $l=\ell_0/2a_{K_1}$ of the cube of BI is then $>10^{6.3228\cdot10^{11}}$, and the two boxes $(l,2l,2l)$ and $(2l)^3$, of $4l^3$ and $8l^3$ sites, have more than $10^{1.8968\cdot10^{12}}$ sites each. For the floor of $\eta_K$: $\varsigma\ge\varsigma_\flat(L)$ as $\mathsf p_0\ge\frac52$, $\mathsf C_{\rm bf}\ge2$, and $L^z\ell=2L^{m+z}\ge2L^2$ as $m+z\ge2$; so $\eta_K\ge3\varsigma_\flat\cdot2\cdot8L^6(K-z)^{5/2}L^{-(K-z)/10}$. An inequality $X_{K_1}\le y-\eta_{K_1}$ with $X_{K_1}\ge0$, $y\le y_0$, forces $\eta_{K_1}\le\frac{L^3}8\,0.069$, hence $K_1-z\ge K_\flat(L)$ for the least $K_\flat$ at which the floor drops below that number, and the small cube then has $2L^{m+K_1-1}\ge2L^{1+K_\flat}$ sites a side; at every admitted $L$ this exceeds $10^{152}$ (already at $L=13$, $2L^{1+K_\flat}>10^{152.9}$).

\emph{Step 14: Thm.~\ref{C-361-6}(1)--(4).} (1): $D_2(N)=4\mathsf d^{(3)}(N,N,N)+2\mathsf d^{(2)}(N,N,2N)+\mathsf d^{(1)}(N,2N,2N)$, three doubling defects $\ge0$ by Prop.~\ref{C-361-7}(b), the last being $\mathsf e(N)$; $D_2\le8\delta$ and $D_q-\frac{q^3}8D_2=\frac{q^3}8\delta((2N)^3)-\delta((qN)^3)\ge0$ by Prop.~\ref{C-361-7}(c); $(q-1)^3\delta(N^3)\le D_q(N)$ is $\delta((qN)^3)\le(3q^2-3q+1)\delta(N^3)$, and the box and cube bounds are Prop.~\ref{C-361-7}(c); $\mathsf e(l)\le2\delta(l,2l,2l)\le16(l/N)^2\delta(N^3)$. For $l=Ll'$, $n=2l/L$, with the time along a side of the cube $Ln=2l$: $D_L(n)\ge LF(n,2l,2l)-F(2l,2l,2l)=L\mathsf G(n)-\mathsf G(2l)\ge L\mathsf G(l)-\mathsf G(2l)\ge\frac L2\mathsf e(l)$ over the cross-section $(2l,2l)$, as $n\le l$ and $\mathsf e(l)=2\mathsf G(l)-\mathsf G(2l)$, the two other thermal defects of $D_L$ being $\ge0$; this is $\mathsf e(l)\le\frac2LD_L(2l/L)$.

The cube criterion and $D_L(2l)\le\frac{20}7L^3x^2$ are Step~11; $\mathsf e\le8\delta$; and $0.13736\cdot0.8901^{24}\le0.0084022$. Finally $F\le0$ and, by Jensen's inequality for the Haar measure, $F\ge-3\beta|\underline n|$, so $\mathsf e(l)\le-F((2l)^3)\le24\beta l^3$. (2) is Prop.~\ref{C-361-8} with $x_0=8\delta(N^3)$, $\theta=103.2\,\delta(N^3)$ (if $\delta(N^3)=0$ the excess vanishes for all larger cubes), $\delta((2N)^3)\le\frac{20}7\mathsf e(N)^2\le\frac{20}7\cdot64\,\delta(N^3)^2$, and Prop.~\ref{C-361-8}(e) for $0.07489$. Two periodic Gibbs states exclude the first alternative by Prop.~\ref{C-361-10}(a); by (M3) each is an integral of ergodic ones, two different ergodic ones are mutually singular, and Prop.~\ref{C-361-9}(d) gives $2\le\liminf e^{\delta}$.

The last sentence is Prop.~\ref{C-361-9}(d), the sides being chosen with $\delta$ tending to its lower limit and the laws converging, by the compactness of the laws on a compact space. (3): if $\mathsf e(l)>0.069$ there is nothing to prove; otherwise let $\nu$ be the state of Prop.~\ref{C-361-10}, $f$ the bump of (M5)(iii) at radius $\mathsf d_\circ$ and height $2\mathsf d_\circ$, and $C(n)$ the covariance under $\nu$ of $\mathcal O_K(f\circ\Theta)$ and $\mathcal O_K(f(\cdot-na_Ke_3))$, $\Theta$ the reflection $x_3\mapsto-x_3$. For $0\le n\le N_4$ the pair is a test pair at $(\mathsf d_\circ;\vartheta_1)$ and two points of the supports are between $2\mathsf d_\circ+na_K$ and $6\mathsf d_\circ+na_K$ apart; so (M5)(iii) gives $C(n)>0$ and
\[
\frac{C(0)}{C(N_4)}\le\frac{4/3}{2/3}\Bigl(\frac{10\,\mathsf d_\circ}{2\,\mathsf d_\circ}\Bigr)^6=2\cdot5^6=31250 .
\]
By translation invariance $C(n)$ is the covariance of $\mathcal O_K(f)$ and its mirror image in the plane $x_3=-\frac n2a_K$, so Prop.~\ref{C-361-10}(f) with $A=B=\mathcal O_K(f)$, as in Step~5, gives $C(n)\le\theta^{n/l}C(0)$, $C\ge0$, and $C$ is log-convex, so all $C(n)>0$ and the quotients $C(n+1)/C(n)$ do not decrease: $C(n)\ge C(N_4)\,31250^{-(n-N_4)/N_4}$. Taking $n$-th roots, $\theta^{1/l}\ge31250^{-1/N_4}$, with $\theta=12.9\,\mathsf e(l)$; and $\log31250<10.35\le2.6\,N_4a_K/\mathsf d_\circ$ as $a_K/\mathsf d_\circ\le\frac1{52}$. With $\mathsf d_\circ=\mathsf d_0$, $l=\ell/2a_K$; (1) carries the floor to $D_2$, $8\delta$, $\frac8{L^3}D_L$; and $\frac1{12.9}31250^{-l/N_4}>0.069$ if and only if $l/N_4<\log(1/(12.9\cdot0.069))/\log31250$, which $la_K<0.0449\,\mathsf d_\circ$ gives, as $N_4>4\mathsf d_\circ/a_K-1$ and $\mathsf d_\circ/a_K>4L^3M$. (4): dilating by $L^z$, the label enters the period $(\gamma_W^{-2}+\bar B,\kappa_0]$, which $I(g_1)\cup I(g_2)$ covers by the form of the intervals $I(g)$ in (M5); there (3) at the side $L^z\ell_0$ gives $L^{-z}m_*\le2.6/\mathsf d_0^\star$, and $L^z\le\kappa_0/\mathsf b$, so $m_*\le2.6\kappa_0/(\mathsf d_0^\star\mathsf b)$, which is the bound since $\log(1/\theta)/1.3\ge0.0895$.

On the cube $(2l)^3$, Prop.~\ref{C-361-7}(d), (e) give $w_{00}=\frac14(1+2r_1+r_2)$, $w_{10}=w_{01}=\frac14(1-r_2)=u$, $w_{11}=\frac14(1-2r_1+r_2)=v$; with $x=1-r_1=2(u+v)$ the sum $\sum_fw_f^{1/2}=(1-u-\frac x2)^{1/2}+2u^{1/2}+(\frac x2-u)^{1/2}$ is concave in $u$ on the range $\frac x4\le u\le\frac x2$ allowed by $r_2\le r_1$ and $v\ge0$, so least at an end of it, which is $u=\frac x2$ for $x\le\frac12$; this gives $\mathsf e(l)\ge2\log(\sqrt{1-x}+\sqrt{2x})$, which exceeds $0.069$ for $x>0.00062714$ and is at least $\log2$ for $\frac19\le x\le\frac12$; for $x>\frac12$ both end values of the sum are at least $\sqrt2$, so $\mathsf e(l)\ge\log2$ there; and $\mathsf e(l)\ge\mathsf G_{2l}\ge\log\frac1{w_{00}}\ge\log\frac4{1+3r_1}$.

Then Prop.~\ref{C-361-7}(d) for $r_2,r_3$, Prop.~\ref{C-361-8}(b) for $\delta((2l)^3)\le\frac{20}7\cdot0.069^2\le0.0136029$, and Prop.~\ref{C-361-7}(b) for $\mathsf r_{l}(2l,2l)\le\varphi(e^{0.069}-1)\le0.0357638$, $\log(1/0.0357638)\approx3.33082$, $l_Ka_K=\ell_0/2$.

\emph{Step 15: Thm.~\ref{C-361-6}(5), (6).} (5)(a) is Prop.~\ref{C-361-15}(c) at $N=\ell/a_K$, $\beta=L^K\mathsf b$, where $N/\beta=\ell/\mathsf b$, with $|c'_N-c'|\le C_AN^{-2}(\log N)^{5/2}$; and the limit $K\to\infty$ by Thm.~\ref{C-361-5}(6). (b) Prop.~\ref{C-361-16}(a) and Prop.~\ref{C-361-7}(d), (e): as $r_2\le r_1$, $w_{00}$ is the largest weight and $\frac14\le w_{00}\le\frac14(1+3r_1)$, $|4w_f-1|\le3r_1$; $\delta_K(\ell)\ge\mathsf G_N\ge\log\frac1{w_{00}}\ge\log\frac4{1+3r_1}$, and $\mathsf e(\ell/2a_K)\ge\mathsf G(\ell/2a_K;N,N)\ge\mathsf G_N$; the last assertion follows from (4): $\eta_\flat(\ell_0/\mathsf b)<0.99937$ gives $1-r_1>0.000628$ on the cube $\ell_0/a_K$ at every cutoff. (c) Completing the \textbf{(Heaviest class)} probability estimate would make the reduction in Prop.~\ref{C-361-16}(b) give $\mathsf G_N=\log(Z/\lambda_0^N)\ge\log\frac1t-\mathsf q\log\log\frac1t-\log C$. (d) Choose $t_\circ>0$ with $16Lt_\circ\le t_2$ and $\eta_\flat(t)\le0.9961$ for $t\le16Lt_\circ$, and $\beta_\flat=1/8t_\circ$.

For $\beta\ge\beta_\flat$ there is $j\ge1$ with $2L^j/\beta\in(16t_\circ,16Lt_\circ]$; then $1-r_1(2L^j)\ge0.0039$ by (b), and Prop.~\ref{C-361-8}(d), by contraposition, excludes $\mathsf e(l)\le0.069$ for every $l\le2L^j/16$, which includes $3\le l\le t_\circ\beta$. For BI take $K$ with $L^K\mathsf b\ge\beta_\flat$: $l_K=\ell_0L^K/2>t_\circ L^K\mathsf b$. The exact statement on one lattice is the contrapositive of Prop.~\ref{C-361-8}(d). (e) is Prop.~\ref{C-361-15}(d). (6): with $N=L^{-j}\ell/a_K$ at the same $\beta$, (a) at the side $L^{-j}\ell$, where $t_1/L<L^{-j}t\le t_1$, bounds $\delta(N^3)$ by $\log(L/t_1)+c'+C$, and Thm.~\ref{C-361-6}(1) gives $\delta_K(\ell)\le3L^{2j}\delta(N^3)$ with $L^j\le Lt/t_1$; then $\mathsf e\le8\delta$ and $D_L\le L^3\delta$.

\begin{remark}[Scope]\label{C-361-17}
The theorems do not assert BI at any label; by Thm.~\ref{C-361-6} it fails at every cutoff on cubes small against the label, and it can hold only on cubes of side at least $0.0895\,(\mathsf d_0^\star/\kappa_0)\,\mathsf b$. Thm.~\ref{C-361-4}(2) carries BI from one label to every other label at other sides and from other thresholds, with numbers $\beta_0$, $C_+$ that are not explicit. Uniqueness in Thm.~\ref{C-361-3}(1)(b) is uniqueness among the periodic Gibbs states; of Gibbs states without periods it says only that $\nu_K$ is extreme and trivial at infinity. The area law bounds the loops in the state $\nu_K$ at each cutoff. Thm.~\ref{C-361-4}(5) concerns tuples carried by a cube that keeps away from the seam of the torus.
\end{remark}

Derivatives of continuum tests act on $\R^3$; bond derivatives and
covariant lattice differences act on the cutoff lattice. Stochastic
time, gradient-flow time and real time in the reconstructed quantum
field are distinct. Constants have the dependencies stated in each
sketch. A bound uniform in the fine cutoff need not be uniform in
the physical volume.
